issues.body:
Environment
- Windows, ChatGPT/Codex desktop app, auto-updated 26.1111.2228.0 -> 26.1111.9664.0 on 2026-11-19 (UTC+8)
- One connected computer ("ShrimpF"); dispatch is done by an external agent through the connected-computer feature
- Before the update, dispatch worked: the agent could send messages to an existing local Codex conversation and create new local tasks

What happened
- 2026-11-19 20:21 and 20:51 local: the computer went offline twice; ~20:55 the client switched to the new version
- 2026-11-19 20:56:06.802 local (12:56:06.802Z) log: codex-app-tools status check failed, reason=status_check_failed, bundledVersion=26.1111.71704, installedLocalVersion=26.1111.71704, installedPluginSourcePath=C:\Users\Fangdaq\.codex\.tmp\bundled-marketplaces\openai-bundled\plugins\codex-app-tools, marketplaceName=openai-bundled, sourceType=local
- A later log (2026-11-19 23:29:17.701) shows bundled_plugin_install_skipped_current for codex-app-tools (install skipped as current; not a functional pass)

Symptoms since the update (still current)
- The computer is online and readable: conversation history and execution results of the existing local Codex conversation can be read normally
- The two dispatch capabilities never came back: sending a message to an existing local Codex conversation (the documented "continue an existing local Codex task") and creating a new native Local conversation
- Capability enumeration is unstable: it completed once (2026-11-20 10:51 check) and returned only the plugin/skill registry; codex-app-tools showed as "discovered" with no version returned, not confirmed enabled/active, and exposed no callable tools. At other times, including after a full re-registration, enumeration returns deadline_reached
- A read-only test message (report hostname and current directory) cannot even be submitted: there is no send entry point, so no execution record exists
- Retried with the target conversation open and the app in the foreground (2026-11-20 11:02:45): no change
- Scan results only expose summary fields scan_warnings: 5 and unreadable_entries: 0, with no per-item detail

Directory integrity check (2026-11-20 13:25, read-only)
- .codex\.tmp\bundled-marketplaces\openai-bundled contains .agents, plugins, .materialization-key; .agents\plugins\marketplace.json is present
- plugins contains browser, chrome, codex-app-tools, computer-use, latex, unified-computer-use, visualize; codex-app-tools contains .codex-plugin\plugin.json, .mcp.json, server.mjs and scripts
- No .staging leftovers under bundled-marketplaces; plugin cache holds versions 26.1111.71704 and 26.1117.31558
- So this does not appear to be the partial-marketplace state described in #26501

Already tried, none of it helped
- Full quit and reopen of the desktop app (multiple times)
- Windows Settings "Repair" (not Reset)
- Removing the duplicate computer entry left by the update
- Clicking "Allow access" for the computer
- Opening the target conversation and keeping the app in the foreground
- Full re-registration: forced the computer offline (home router powered off), deleted it from the account device list on a phone over cellular, then re-added it fresh. After re-registration, enumeration still returns deadline_reached and dispatch is still absent

Possibly related
- #40852: after a Desktop update, read tools (list_threads / read_thread / wait_threads) remain while send_message_to_thread, create_thread, fork_thread, handoff_thread and automation_update are omitted from the callable catalog
- #40865: same read/write split for remote tasks; effectful codex_app tools omitted with no replacement exposed

Questions
1. Are the effectful codex_app tools intentionally filtered for connected-computer / remote dispatch in current builds, or is this a regression?
2. If it is a regression, is there a fixed build or an ETA?
3. Is there any supported workaround to restore dispatch to a local Codex conversation without downgrading?

No API keys, tokens or credentials are included in this report; I can provide full local logs on request.

issues.body:
## Problem

Commands requesting execution outside the sandbox fail even though I click Allow. The tool returns `aborted by user`. An affected Work conversation also displayed “That approval request is no longer active. Please retry the action if you still want ChatGPT to continue with it.”

This blocks document creation and downloads. A harmless command reproduces the failure.

## Environment

- Observed: 27 October 2026, Australia/Sydney.
- Windows version reported by PowerShell: `Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0`.
- Running desktop executable package version: `OpenAI.Codex_26.1021.3705.0_x64`.
- PowerShell: `7.6.5`.
- Reproduced with GPT-6.1 Sol and again after switching the conversation to GPT-6 Astra.

## Minimal reproduction

1. In a Windows-connected ChatGPT Work conversation, run an ordinary shell command and verify it succeeds.
2. Request the following through `exec_command` with `sandbox_permissions: require_escalated` and an approval justification:

```powershell
Write-Output 'Approved command execution: OK'
```

3. Click Allow when prompted.
4. The tool returns:

```text
aborted by user after 0.1s
```

There is no command output or successful exit status. I explicitly confirmed the prompt appeared and I approved it; I did not intentionally cancel that request. The duration above is tool-reported and should not be interpreted as independently measured approval waiting time.

## Latest Full Access test

I enabled Full Access and requested another test in the same conversation.

- Ordinary `Write-Output 'Standard command execution: OK'` succeeded with exit code 0.
- The same explicit `require_escalated` test again returned `aborted by user after 0.1s`.

Whether the changed Full Access setting propagated to this existing conversation has not been independently verified. This does not establish that Full Access fails in every execution mode.

## What works

- Ordinary PowerShell execution.
- Creating, reading back and deleting a temporary file in the permitted workspace.
- Reading local files.
- Computer-use app/window discovery and screenshot capture.
- Connected-browser navigation and reading pages.

## Separate sandbox startup issue was resolved

Earlier, commands could not start because of:

```text
helper_sandbox_lock_failed
lock sandbox bin dir <USER_PROFILE>\.codex\.sandbox-bin failed
NtCreateFile: Access is denied. (os error 5)
```

Closing the app, renaming `.sandbox-bin` to a backup, and reopening resolved that startup failure. Ordinary execution and file read/write/delete tests then passed. The approval failure persisted afterwards.

Prior troubleshooting also included restarting Windows, reinstalling the app, changing the projectless chat folder and testing on a phone hotspot. The approval issue remained. A comparison with a newly created task explicitly configured for Local execution has not yet been performed.

## Expected behaviour

An approved command should execute and return output and exit status, or report an accurate execution/approval-delivery error. It should not be attributed to intentional user cancellation without evidence.

## Related reports

- #50512 — Windows file operations fail after approval.
- #57345 — Windows file-writing operations return cancellation and an expired-approval error.
- #53560 — Work approvals immediately fail after clicking Allow on macOS.
- #51996 — Accepted command approvals followed by connection failures and cancellation results on macOS.

A shared root cause has not been established. Please investigate the approval lifecycle for this minimal command and advise on a supported recovery path.

This report omits business content, private conversation links, personal filesystem paths, account details and raw logs.

Version obtained from the running application's package path, not the About dialog.

### What subscription do you have?

Not included in this report; the investigation did not inspect billing/account credentials.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64 desktop, controlling remote Linux hosts through saved SSH connections. The same remote thread IDs also have catalog entries under Remote Control connection IDs.

### What issue are you seeing?

Several pinned Codex chats in the ChatGPT desktop app show disconnected even though the same chats remain readable through the app's thread tools when an explicit SSH host ID is supplied.

Read-only investigation found duplicate `local_thread_catalog` entries for each affected thread: one under an SSH host ID and another under a Remote Control host ID. For the four affected pinned chats examined, the Remote Control row had an older recency value. Both rows were eligible (`missing_candidate = 0`, non-ChatGPT source).

The installed renderer contains a deterministic duplicate-selection inconsistency: it sorts catalog entries newest first, then constructs a thread-ID-only map with unconditional `Map.set`. Later, older entries overwrite the newer entries. The backend host lookup instead selects the newest eligible row.

This is a suspected explanation for the visible disconnected cards, not a confirmed capture of their current in-memory host selection.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed configuration / reproduction candidate (not yet validated from a clean profile):

1. Have one remote thread represented under both SSH and Remote Control host IDs.
2. Let the SSH catalog row have newer recency than the Remote Control row.
3. Load both catalog entries into the renderer and display the thread as a pinned row.
4. If no eligible manager summary or live-conversation state supersedes the catalog summary, the thread-ID-only catalog map selects the older Remote Control entry.
5. The hover card prefers that summary's host ID when looking up connection status. If that Remote Control connection is disconnected, the card can show disconnected despite the thread being accessible through SSH.

Minimal illustration of the confirmed map-reduction behavior:

```js
const entries = [
  { threadId: "example", hostId: "ssh-example", sourceRecencyAt: 200, sourceCreatedAt: 100 },
  { threadId: "example", hostId: "remote-control-example", sourceRecencyAt: 150, sourceCreatedAt: 100 },
];
entries.sort((a, b) =>
  b.sourceRecencyAt - a.sourceRecencyAt ||
  b.sourceCreatedAt - a.sourceCreatedAt ||
  a.hostId.localeCompare(b.hostId) ||
  a.threadId.localeCompare(b.threadId)
);
const byThread = new Map();
for (const entry of entries) byThread.set(entry.threadId, entry);
console.log(byThread.get("example").hostId); // remote-control-example
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Host resolution should be consistent between the sidebar, hover card, navigation, and thread tools. A stale alternate-transport catalog entry should not silently override the intended usable host.

If multiple host identities for one thread are ambiguous, preserve host-qualified identity or resolve them through an explicit consistent policy. A supported way to repair/reassociate stale host references would also help.

### Additional information

Static evidence from the installed `app.asar`:

- `webview/assets/app-shared-c568b0b98683.js`: `XPr` deduplicates by host/thread pair, sorts via `nFr`, then calls `eFr` to build `entriesByConversationId`. `eFr` unconditionally overwrites each non-ChatGPT thread ID. The last duplicate wins: lowest recency, then lowest creation time, then the last host under `localeCompare`. `sourceUpdatedAt` is not used by this comparator.
- `.vite/build/main-DAwJoFgo.js`: `Khe.readThreadHostId` filters missing/ChatGPT rows and selects highest recency, then highest creation time, then the first host under `localeCompare` (after a SQL limit of 100).
- `webview/assets/app-initial-ff48311587c5.js`: the catalog selector feeds `FA`/`B4t`; summary-backed rows pass their summary through to `x2i`. The hover-card host precedence is `threadSummary?.hostId ?? hoverCardHostConfig?.id ?? generalThreadHostResolver(threadId)`.

Observed state:
- Two affected chats already had SSH project assignments; one had a Remote Control assignment; one had no assignment.
- All four lacked per-thread membership-host entries.
- The chat-list tool reported the intended SSH host for all four, and explicit SSH-host thread reads succeeded. This confirms access through that tool path, not successful UI resume or the transport state used by the hover card.
- A separate affected chat began showing connected without an investigative settings/database edit. Another comparison chat had a single SSH catalog row and consistent SSH assignments.

Limitations:
- The renderer's currently loaded catalog subset, manager summaries, live-conversation host set, runtime override, and actual hover-card props have not been captured.
- The catalog overwrite behavior is confirmed by static code; its causal role in each visible disconnected card remains unproven.
- No settings, database rows, session files, or host assignments were changed during this investigation.

Related but not confirmed duplicates: openai/codex#42628 (catalog reconciliation) and openai/codex#41214 (multi-host sidebar state). Neither examined report establishes this specific duplicate-host reduction behavior.

Private chat titles, thread IDs, host/environment IDs, account identifiers, local paths, credentials, and raw logs are intentionally omitted.

issues.body:
### App version

Desktop bundle manifest: **26.1029.61003**. Windows package: **OpenAI.Codex 26.1029.7803.0, x64**. These are separate version identifiers, not a claimed mismatch.

### Subscription

Not collected for this report.

### Platform

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19045.0, x64.

### Problem and reproduction

After the desktop app has been running for a long time, clicking conversations and switching between them becomes very slow. The user captured a built-in performance trace while performing only a few conversation switches. This concerns local UI responsiveness, not model generation speed.

Reproduction shape:
1. Use the desktop app for an extended period.
2. Switch between existing conversations using the sidebar.
3. Observe multi-second pauses and delayed click feedback.
4. Record a short built-in performance trace.

A precise time-to-degradation threshold and minimal conversation fixture have not yet been established. No post-restart control or mitigation was tested in this environment.

### Expected behavior

Conversation navigation and input remain responsive during prolonged application use, without periodically restarting the app or discarding conversation history.

### Sanitized trace evidence

Analyzed locally with official Perfetto Trace Processor v59.1. The raw trace and conversation contents are not attached.

The entire trace spans 76.65 s, but the main renderer's synchronous task track is observable for **55.20 s**. Its RunTask wall duration totals **52.80 s**. One **3.925 s CpuProfiler::StartProfiling** event is recording startup overhead.

Excluding that startup interval leaves **48.86 s of RunTask work in a 51.25 s window (95.34%)**, with **45.91 s thread CPU time** and **93 tasks above 50 ms**. These percentages describe one UI thread, not whole-machine CPU utilization. Ongoing profiling overhead is not quantified, so these are measurements under instrumentation.

| Main-renderer event | Count | Total wall duration | Maximum |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| UpdateLayoutTree | 413 | 35,851 ms | 830 ms |
| Layout | 231 | 937 ms | 97 ms |
| Paint | 756 | 216 ms | 8 ms |
| MajorGC | 4 | 465 ms | 256 ms |
| MinorGC | 39 | 431 ms | 24 ms |

UpdateLayoutTree consumed **34.02 s of thread CPU time**. The longest RunTask lasted **5.155 s**, including **23 style updates totaling 4.535 s (~88%)**; Layout was only 38 ms, minor GC 21 ms, and Paint 6 ms in that task.

ForcedStyleAndLayout.UpdateTime totaled 26.85 s. This overlaps the style measurements; nested event totals must not be added. Same-name nested RunTask/UpdateLayoutTree slices were checked and did not cause double counting. Perfetto reported no nonzero error/data_loss stats.

### Input delays

Selected Chromium EventTiming click records, relative to trace start:

| Time | Event latency | Input queue | Click handler processing |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 28.769 s | 4,829 ms | 5 ms | 2,753 ms |
| 34.779 s | 2,026 ms | 252 ms | 1,213 ms |
| 38.262 s | 5,062 ms | 314 ms | 3,554 ms |
| 46.266 s | 1,828 ms | 1,785 ms | 2 ms |
| 66.186 s | 3,633 ms | 1,281 ms | 2 ms |
| 67.076 s | 2,743 ms | 2,708 ms | 1 ms |

EventTiming is input-to-presentation-related latency, not completion of all conversation loading. The trace lacks semantic markers mapping every click to a particular navigation action. Pointer-over processing also reached 1.56 s.

### Concrete investigation leads

CPU samples and a read-only inspection of the same installed bundle identified these paths. Positions below are one-based generated source line/column, with local installation paths removed.

- **Sidebar visibility scan:** `assets/async/968918.7aa8e43105.js:1:46352`. Navigation-state and MutationObserver callbacks enumerate registered sidebar regions and check `[data-sidebar-cycle-item]` visibility. The helper at `:1:55845` reads `getClientRects()` and computed visibility. Mutation observation includes subtree/ancestor and class/style/visibility-related changes. Six style updates directly under this callback totaled **1.862 s**.
- **Viewer header measurement:** `assets/async/265651.3442ea834c.js:2:823179`. ResizeObserver measurement changes display/flex and reads offsetWidth to select collapsed header items. Fourteen style updates under this callback totaled **1.507 s**.
- **Composer focus after ResizeObserver:** `assets/async/1975.61532a3aaf.js:1:34146`; associated style updates totaled **0.612 s**.
- **Browser selection-bound update:** style updates under WidgetBase::UpdateSelectionBounds totaled **14.463 s**.
- A React scheduling microtask at `assets/async/142457.27811297d7.js:2:132362` enclosed **13.777 s** of style updates.

These are triggering/call-context observations, not proof that any one observer or React itself owns the underlying defect. Selection and geometry reads may flush style invalidation caused earlier.

Expensive individual style updates processed roughly **6,600-7,200 elements**. The field is the number affected by that update, not total DOM count or leaked objects.

### Limits and request

The immediate bottleneck is sustained main-thread style work. A memory leak, accumulated observers, retained inactive UI, or a particular CSS selector has **not** been proven. V8 GlobalConsumedBytes ranged about 608-854 MiB and ended below its first value; this is not process RSS.

Please investigate broad style invalidation and repeated synchronous geometry reads during navigation, sidebar observation, header sizing, and focus updates, and whether their cost grows with application lifetime. A targeted cold-versus-long-running comparison and selector/retainer instrumentation would help isolate the underlying defect.

Potentially related: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/59614 (same package version, style-heavy long-chat/sidebar lag). This capture adds prolonged-use navigation/input-queue measurements; it does not establish the PDF/preview-specific trigger in that report. Please consolidate if engineering confirms a shared cause.

### Privacy

This report contains only sanitized reproduction details, platform/build identifiers, aggregate timings, relative timing samples, and application asset locations. Usernames, machine names, project paths/names, conversation titles/IDs/content, network destinations, credentials, screenshots, absolute timestamps, and raw traces have been omitted. The original trace remains local and unchanged.

labels.name: bug

labels.name: TUI
labels.description: Issues related to the terminal user interface: text input, menus and dialogs, and terminal display

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

issues.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

Source-level production-component probe at commit `05ae1b0fdd5ab412d24248acc76c5d9f6f275440`; no packaged CLI binary was run. The same removal path is present in the 0.170.0 release source and current `main`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not applicable; no account or provider was used.

### Which model were you using?

None; no model or API call was made.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux x86_64 isolated probe environment; Git 2.43.0.

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Not applicable; the production crate probe was non-interactive.

### Codex doctor report

Not run; the probe did not install a packaged CLI.

### What issue are you seeing?

On the source commit above, Codex cannot remove a managed worktree when it contains an initialized Git submodule, even when the superproject and submodule are clean. The worktree browser reports Git's removal error and leaves the checkout on disk.

`WorktreeManager::remove` checks ignored files from the superproject, then runs `git worktree remove <path>` without `--force`. Git rejects this operation for a worktree with an initialized submodule. The production crate probe reproduced the failure in 3/3 runs; removing an otherwise equivalent worktree without a submodule succeeded. When an ignored file was placed inside the submodule, the failed removal preserved both the checkout and that file.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Create a local Git repository whose branch includes a Git submodule.
2. Use Codex's worktree browser to create a managed checkout of that branch, then initialize the submodule inside the managed checkout. Keep both repositories clean.
3. Switch to another checkout and ask the worktree browser to remove the managed checkout.
4. Observe that removal fails with a Git error similar to `working trees containing submodules cannot be moved or removed`, and the checkout remains on disk.

The same result was reproduced by calling the production `WorktreeManager::remove` API against temporary local repositories. The no-submodule control succeeded; the initialized-submodule case failed in 3/3 trials. The complete TUI interaction was not run.

### What is the expected behavior?

A clean managed worktree with an initialized submodule should be removable. A failed removal should continue to preserve local data inside submodules.

### Additional information

The removal code is present in the [0.170.0 release source](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.170.0/codex-rs/worktree/src/lib.rs) and [current `main`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/worktree/src/lib.rs); these were source checks, not packaged-binary runs. The tested path is [`WorktreeManager::remove`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/05ae1b0fdd5ab412d24248acc76c5d9f6f275440/codex-rs/worktree/src/lib.rs#L285-L330), called by the [worktree browser](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/05ae1b0fdd5ab412d24248acc76c5d9f6f275440/codex-rs/tui/src/worktree_browser.rs).

[Issue #62410](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/62410) concerns automatic cleanup of worktrees still used by active chats and workers. This report concerns an explicit removal that Git rejects for a clean initialized-submodule worktree; the reproduction retained its files.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

issues.body:
### What version of Codex is running?

`@openai/codex` 0.153.4 (npm dist, `codex-win32-x64` payload), driven as `codex app-server --stdio`.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Plus (signed in via ChatGPT auth; `auth_mode=Chatgpt`).

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro Insider Preview, build 29708, x86_64.

### What issue are you seeing?

A read-only Codex session cannot read files at all: every `exec_command` is rejected before process creation, including pure read commands like `type`/`Get-Content`.

The session is started through `thread/start` with `approvalPolicy: "never"` and no sandbox override, so it resolves to the read-only sandbox. The resolved policy appears in the log as:

```
approval_policy=Never sandbox_policy=ReadOnly { network_access: false }
```

When the model then calls the shell tool to inspect a file, the tool fails immediately with:

```
exec_command failed: CreateProcess { message: "Rejected(\"\`\\\"C:\\\\Program Files\\\\PowerShell\\\\7\\\\pwsh.exe\\\" -Command \\\"type C:\\\\...\\\\a.txt\\\"\` rejected: blocked by policy\")" }
```

Because Codex reads files through the shell tool, the rejection removes file-reading capability entirely. A read-only session therefore cannot inspect a repository, so an unattended review task is impossible without switching the session to `workspace-write` (which also permits writes).

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start `codex app-server --stdio` on Windows.
2. `initialize` → `initialized`, then `thread/start` with `{ "approvalPolicy": "never", "cwd": "<any existing directory>" }` (no `sandbox` field), which resolves to the read-only sandbox.
3. `turn/start` with a task that requires reading a file, e.g. "read `C:\tmp\probe\a.txt` and reply with its contents".
4. Observe the model's `exec_command` call fail with `Rejected(... rejected: blocked by policy)` before any process is created.

### What is the expected behavior?

A read-only sandbox should still allow commands that only read: `type`, `Get-Content`, `Get-ChildItem`, `rg`, `git status`/`git diff`, and similar. Read-only means "no writes, no network", not "no process creation".

If running any process under the read-only sandbox is intentional on Windows, please provide a sandbox-compatible file-read tool (or document an equivalent) so a read-only session can still inspect files. Right now the only working configuration is `workspace-write`, which grants write access a review-only session must not have.

### Additional information

- Related reports that may share a root cause: #51644, #58550, #57623, #60191. None of them cover "read-only sandbox blocks *read* commands on Windows".
- Second observation from the same test matrix, possibly a separate issue: with `approvalPolicy: "on-request"` + auto review, an `exec_command` requesting `sandbox_permissions: "require_escalated"` was approved automatically and successfully wrote a file **outside** the session's `cwd` — the session was not confined to its workspace. Worth confirming whether Windows sandbox confinement is expected to hold there.
- Reproducible with an empty `config.toml`; no `sandbox_mode` key is set, so the read-only default applies.

issues.body:
## Summary
ChatGPT Work on macOS is unable to use the built-in browser and cannot complete network-dependent development/deployment work. Read-only diagnostics on October 20 and 21, 2026 reproduced missing browser availability and restricted shell networking. A shared root cause has not been established.

## Environment
- ChatGPT desktop: 26.1013.40934, build 20770
- macOS: 27.0.1
- Surface: Work/local tasks on a connected, attached, authorized Mac
- User reports public internet access is enabled in Work settings.

## Observed results
1. Browser inventory returns an empty list. Selecting the built-in browser returns `Browser is not available: iab`, before any website can be inspected.
2. The shell environment reports `CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED=1`. On October 20, DNS lookups for github.com and learn.chatgpt.com failed with `[Errno 8] nodename nor servname provided, or not known`.
3. Existing development-task results also recorded loopback `EPERM` and database-host `ENOTFOUND`. These denied operations were not repeated in the read-only diagnostic.
4. A documentation fetch on October 20 returned `Client error: exec-server transport disconnected`. This particular error did not recur during the October 21 check; permanent recovery is not established.
5. Basic shell commands/file reads, desktop artifact listing, and an authenticated GitHub connector lookup succeeded. This is not evidence of a Mac-wide internet outage. The network-disabled environment variable alone does not establish that every managed network route is unavailable.

## Troubleshooting already performed
- User reports quitting/restarting the app and enabling public internet access.
- A fresh local diagnostic task was started on October 20; missing IAB and shell networking problems persisted.
- Rechecked that diagnostic on October 21 at approximately 13:28 UTC: browser inventory still empty, same IAB error, network-disabled flag still present, app version unchanged. Public HTTPS was not retried under the reported restriction.
- No destructive reset, access-control bypass, deployment, or database mutation was performed.

## Expected behavior
Authorized Work tasks should expose the supported built-in browser and accurately reflect effective network access. If workspace or execution policy overrides an enabled setting, the UI should clearly identify that restriction and provide a supported resolution.

## Impact
Browser-based verification and network-dependent coding/deployment workflows are blocked. Ordinary chat and some read-only tools still work.

## Related reports
- #51290: matching built-in-browser availability failure, including an October 20 comment on this exact app version/build.
- #53278: similar network-setting/effective-policy mismatch on Windows; related symptoms, not proof of the same cause.
- https://community.openai.com/t/chatgpt-work-on-mac-chrome-file-access-blocked-operation-not-permitted-new-threads-temporarily-help/1407805

Please investigate browser-provider availability and the discrepancy between the enabled network setting and actual execution behavior, or route these symptoms to the appropriate team. A supported recovery path that preserves existing chats, files, and project work would be appreciated.

This report was prepared with assistant help and submitted with the user's explicit approval. Private project names, file paths, account details, chat history, credentials, and raw logs have been omitted.

## Description

Opening an affected cloud-managed chat from the Codex Desktop sidebar on Windows can show this error before a new message is submitted.

```text
Failed to resume chat
Invalid request: AbsolutePathBuf deserialized without a base path
```

Reading the stored conversation can still succeed while resuming it fails.

Existing chats should open and resume from the sidebar with their complete conversation history intact.

## What to investigate

Check how Desktop resolves workspace paths when resuming cloud-managed chats from Windows. The error indicates that a path could not be resolved as absolute without a base path. Which field triggers the error remains unknown.

On macOS (Apple Silicon), scripted `codex exec` runs can no longer use the ChatGPT Chrome extension. Every browser call fails with:

```
Browsers: Error: The browser access host is unavailable
```

The same Chrome, extension and account work from Codex threads started inside the ChatGPT desktop app. Until about November 3 the same `codex exec` setup listed Chrome profiles and tabs.

Please provide a **supported way for the Codex CLI (including non-interactive `codex exec`) to use the desktop app's browser access**, for example pairing the CLI or the shared app-server daemon with the signed-in desktop app, or at least a clear error that says the CLI is not supported.

### Versions

- Codex CLI 0.166.0 (Homebrew cask)
- ChatGPT desktop 26.1029.61003
- Chrome plugin cache 26.1029.61003, extension `hehggadaopoacecdllhhajmbjkdcmajg` 1.26.1102.11740
- macOS 26.6.2, Apple Silicon (arm64)
- Google Chrome 157.0.8103.38

### Timeline

1. Nov 4, CLI 0.163.0: `codex exec --approve-for-me` + Computer Use (`cua_repl`) listed both Chrome profiles and their tab hosts, and `createBrowserTab` worked, but `goto`, `evaluate` and `close` failed with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'timeoutMs')` (same as #59437).
2. Nov 5: updated the CLI to 0.166.0, updated and restarted the desktop app, fully quit and restarted Chrome.

A documented way for CLI and `codex exec` runs to get browser access through the signed-in desktop app (with the same approvals and Work settings), or a CLI error that says browser use is desktop-only.

#59456 (same versions, macOS Intel), #59437, #57641, #59300, #59334, #56928, #26820, #22164, #57779

issues.title: Codex sandbox installation corrupts ACL on AppData

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.313.5234

### What subscription do you have?

Free

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19045.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

#### Description

After installing Codex on Windows 10 and subsequently enabling/installing its sandbox component, Opera, Opera GX, and Opera Developer fail to launch entirely. The browsers flash a black screen 2–3 times and silently close. The issue appears specifically after the sandbox setup step, not immediately after the initial Codex installation. Chrome (stable) and Brave are unaffected.

#### Root Cause

Codex creates a local Windows group `CodexSandboxUsers` and local users `CodexSandboxOffline` / `CodexSandboxOnline` during installation, and modifies ACL permissions on `AppData\Local`.

This breaks the Chromium sandbox for any browser installed under `AppData\Local` (Opera, Opera GX, Chrome Canary), because the GPU process requires the `ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES (S-1-15-2-1)` permission on that path to launch in sandboxed mode.

Browsers installed in `Program Files` (Chrome stable, Brave, Edge) are unaffected because their `AppData\Local` path is not involved in the same way.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Install Codex on Windows 10
2. Go through the sandbox setup/activation step within Codex
3. Launch Opera, Opera GX, or Opera Developer → browser closes immediately

### What is the expected behavior?

The sandbox installation step should not modify ACL permissions on `AppData\Local` in a way that affects other applications, or should at minimum restore them on uninstall/rollback.

Codex Desktop 26.1117.31558 (bundled app version), Windows MSIX package OpenAI.Codex 26.1117.3838.0.

### What subscription do you have?

Pro 100$

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 10 Pro. PowerShell output: Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19045.0 x64.

### What issue are you seeing?

After latest updating Codex Desktop, I noticed that opening some local Markdown files from links in chat makes the file path bar flicker continuously, roughly 5–10 times per second. The flicker persists while the window is idle. I reproduced it in two local projects.

With the same file tab open, narrowing the window until more of the path is truncated stops the flicker. Restoring the previous width starts it again. Switching to View source and restarting the app did not resolve it.

Video:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4e2e5b6-dc9e-42ce-9612-16c9ca421622

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Save the attached `codex-repro-b.md` as `docs/plans/codex-repro-b.md` in any local workspace.
2. Open that workspace in Codex Desktop. Ask Codex to reply with a clickable link to `docs/plans/codex-repro-b.md`, then click the link to open the built-in file viewer.
3. Adjust the window width until the file path bar flickers. Release the window edge and observe that the flicker continues.
4. Without closing the tab, make the window narrower until the path is truncated further and the flicker stops.
5. Restore the width from step 3. The flicker starts again.

Attached file: [codex-repro-b.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35127737/codex-repro-b.md)

### What is the expected behavior?

At any fixed window width, the path bar should settle on a stable display. If the path needs to be truncated, it should stay truncated until the available space changes.

### Additional information

The attached file contains 44,875 bytes of plain text with no Markdown formatting. A 73-byte version at the same path was stable at the tested width. Some longer filenames were stable as well.

The file path component uses `ResizeObserver` to decide which path segments fit. The repeatable stop and resume when resizing suggests a possible layout feedback loop around a truncation threshold. The exact width and root cause are still unconfirmed.

issues.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

In a long-lived ChatGPT Work thread, the user repeatedly experienced turns making no visible progress under GPT-6 Astra. Repeated requests to continue did not reliably resume useful work. The user reports that switching to GPT-6.1 Sol restored progress. This is a user-observed correlation, not proof of a model-serving root cause.

The affected task combined connected-app retrieval, attachment materialization, local calculations and optional subagents. Private task contents and connected data are intentionally omitted.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The incident occurred in an existing long-lived Work conversation with many prior turns and subagents:
1. Continue an analysis task under GPT-6 Astra.
2. The thread stops delivering useful progress despite repeated continuation messages.
3. Switch the conversation to GPT-6.1 Sol; ordinary connected-app reads and local execution proceed.

No deterministic minimal reproduction is available yet. We cannot establish whether automatic compaction, collaboration scheduling or another host state was active at every stall.

### What is the expected behavior?

A turn should complete, expose the operation it is waiting on, or return a cancellable bounded error. A failed optional collaborator should not indefinitely block the parent thread. Switching models should not be required to recover an otherwise executable task.

### Additional information

- Surface: ChatGPT Work, managed cloud runtime. Exact client/app-server build and client OS were not exposed to the agent.
- Incident observed: 2026-10-20 through early 2026-10-21, UTC+08.
- A prior visible `collaboration.send_message` operation was aborted after approximately 278.4 seconds. This does not account for all user-reported unresponsiveness.
- An agent-authored script also raised `TypeError` while dereferencing an undefined temporary-store value. That script error is a separate workflow defect and is not asserted to be the platform root cause.
- After the model switch, two workout-data queries returned in approximately 2.24 and 2.94 seconds; six targeted heart-rate queries returned in approximately 1.60–2.50 seconds. Attachment reads, local calculations and saving completed.
- No approval prompt was observed in the visible affected operations. Client session logs and backend traces are not available in the managed runtime.
- A local workflow instruction unnecessarily required an Astra review before delivery. That dependency is being removed as a mitigation; it does not repair the host or prove the platform incident resolved.
- Potentially related, but not confirmed duplicates: #43062 (compaction), #33777 (spawn lifecycle), #32756 (message scheduling). Those reports concern specific app/CLI paths; applicability to this Work incident is unknown.

Please advise which Work diagnostic/session identifier and private channel are needed to correlate the stalled turns with backend traces. No raw conversation, account identifiers, credentials or private connected-app data are included.

## Summary

On Windows, keeping Codex Desktop in a maximized/full-screen window for some time can cause severe system-wide slowdown and eventually make the entire PC unresponsive. This is not limited to the Codex window becoming sluggish: the host computer itself becomes difficult or impossible to use.

The report is specifically about the apparent relationship between the maximized/full-screen window state and the system-wide freeze. The exact mechanism is unknown; this report does not assume whether the cause is rendering, GPU composition, memory growth, or another subsystem.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Launch Codex Desktop on Windows.
2. Put the main window into a maximized/full-screen state.
3. Continue using Codex for some time.
4. Observe whether system-wide responsiveness degrades, potentially progressing to a full PC freeze.

The exact time-to-failure and whether the trigger is the native Windows maximize state or F11-style full screen have not yet been isolated.

## Actual behavior

The entire Windows PC becomes severely laggy or unresponsive after Codex has been maximized/full-screen for a while. This is more severe than a renderer-only or window-only freeze.

## Expected behavior

Codex Desktop should remain responsive without degrading the host operating system, regardless of whether its window is restored, maximized, or full-screen.

## Environment

- Platform: Windows
- Codex Desktop version: not yet recorded
- Windows edition/build: not yet recorded
- CPU, GPU, memory, and graphics driver: not yet recorded

## Related reports

These reports describe adjacent symptoms, but do not establish the same trigger or root cause:

- #25513 — maximized-window rendering freeze/transparency
- #16374 — Windows shell/UI freezes associated with Codex
- #40531 — system-wide Windows desktop stutter after extended Codex use

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

OpenAI.Codex_26.818.8289.0

### What subscription do you have?

Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26100.0, x64

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex Desktop repeatedly launches complete or near-complete sets of configured stdio MCP servers during ordinary task activity. Older MCP process trees remain alive instead of being reclaimed, causing `cmd.exe` and `node.exe` processes and their memory usage to accumulate over the lifetime of the Desktop session.

The affected configuration contained five Node/npx-based MCP servers: Context7, Sequential Thinking, Memory, Playwright, and Chrome DevTools. Some were configured directly, while Playwright and Chrome DevTools were supplied by plugins, so the behavior does not appear specific to one MCP package.

The observed Windows process chain was:

```text
codex.exe app-server
  -> cmd.exe /c npx ...
     -> npx.cmd
        -> cmd.exe /d /s /c ...
           -> node.exe
```

The child processes appeared in distinct start-time batches: one around 13:56 and several more around 15:56–15:59.

A process-tree snapshot attributable to the live Codex app-server contained approximately:

* 30 `cmd.exe` processes
* 34 `node.exe` processes
* ~3.7 GB combined working-set memory

The same MCP server names occurred repeatedly across the batches. Completing or closing the visible task did not reclaim the older process trees. The wrappers also caused visible `cmd.exe` console-window flashes on Windows.

Disabling MCP entries in `config.toml` did not terminate already-running children. A full Codex Desktop tray exit/restart was required before the reduced MCP configuration took effect.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start Codex Desktop on Windows with multiple stdio MCP servers configured. In my case these included Context7, Sequential Thinking, Memory, Playwright, and Chrome DevTools.
2. Use Codex Desktop normally across multiple tasks/session activity while leaving the Desktop app running.
3. Inspect the process tree of the active `codex.exe app-server` in Task Manager or PowerShell.
4. Observe multiple start-time batches containing repeated instances of the same MCP servers under `cmd.exe` / `npx.cmd` / `node.exe`.
5. Complete or close the visible Codex task and inspect the process tree again.
6. The older MCP process trees remain alive rather than being reclaimed.
7. Disable manually configured MCP entries in `config.toml`.
8. Observe that already-running MCP children remain alive.
9. Fully exit Codex Desktop from the system tray and restart it.
10. The stale processes from the previous app-server generation are finally removed.

In my observed incident, the live app-server process tree accumulated approximately 30 `cmd.exe` processes and 34 `node.exe` processes, using about 3.7 GB of combined working-set memory.


### What is the expected behavior?

Codex Desktop should keep the number of MCP server processes bounded.

When an MCP connection manager/runtime generation is replaced, the previous MCP server set should be shut down and the complete Windows process tree should be reaped, including `cmd.exe`-wrapped `node.exe` grandchildren.

Completing tasks or disabling MCP servers should not leave stale MCP process trees alive.

Background MCP wrappers should also launch without visible `cmd.exe` console windows.


### Additional information

This appears closely related to #32797, #34614, and #38825.

I am filing this as a separate current-build reproduction because the same process-batch accumulation and incomplete cleanup behavior is still reproducible on the newer Codex Desktop package `OpenAI.Codex_26.818.8289.0`.

Unlike #32797, which reports a much larger MCP configuration, my affected setup contained only five Node/npx-based MCP servers (`Context7`, `Sequential Thinking`, `Memory`, `Playwright`, and `Chrome DevTools`). Despite the smaller configuration, the live Codex app-server process tree still accumulated approximately 30 `cmd.exe` processes and 34 `node.exe` processes, using about 3.7 GB of combined working-set memory.

The processes appeared in distinct start-time batches, with the same MCP server names recurring across batches. Completing the visible task did not reclaim the older process trees. Disabling MCP entries in `config.toml` also did not terminate already-running children; a full Codex Desktop tray exit/restart was required before the reduced configuration took effect.

The bundled Codex version observed from the Desktop process was `0.149.0-alpha.4.3`. A separate `codex` executable exists on my `PATH`, but it is not the Desktop-bundled binary and was not used as the Desktop version reported above.

I can provide a fresh sanitized process snapshot containing `PID`, `PPID`, process name, sanitized command line, start time, and working-set memory if useful for identifying which app-server/runtime generation owns each stale MCP process tree.

I have intentionally not attached my full `config.toml` for security reasons.

Documents attached directly to chats in the ChatGPT macOS desktop app are repeatedly unavailable to the assistant. This affects PDF, DOCX, TXT files and virtually all other files, including files uploaded using the + file picker.

The assistant responds with messages such as:

However, the corresponding assistant execution histories showed the text requests without a usable attachment reference or document contents. The assistants searched unsuccessfully for the files and then reported that no attachment was visible.

In a separate desktop session with local file access, providing explicit local file paths successfully allowed the assistant to read the TXT file and extract and summarize the PDF. This bypasses ordinary attachment delivery and does not resolve the failure in the affected chats.

The observations suggest an attachment handoff or availability problem, but the underlying cause has not been confirmed.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

2. Open a new chat in the macOS desktop app.

6. Repeat with PDF and DOCX files and request a summary; the same problem occurs.
7. Upload the same files through ChatGPT in a web browser; the assistant reads them successfully.

The exact selected model and execution mode for each failed test were not recorded.

### What is the expected behavior?

A supported document attached directly to a chat should be made available to the assistant so it can read, quote, or summarize its contents.

If attachment processing or transfer fails, the app should display an actionable error rather than accept the request while leaving the assistant without access to the document.

### Additional information

Troubleshooting completed:

- Tested PDF, DOCX, and TXT documents, including a tiny TXT file.
- Tested uploading through the + file picker.

- Checked for available app updates; none were shown.
- Enabled Full Disk Access while the app was closed, then reopened it.
- Independently verified during the diagnostic session that ChatGPT’s Full Disk Access and iCloud Drive access were enabled.
- Checked Files & Folders; no individual Downloads/Desktop/Documents permission switches were available.
- Tested with the VPN enabled and disabled; neither resolved the issue.
- Tested using a phone hotspot; the desktop failure persisted.
- Confirmed network proxies were off.
- Looked for Profiles/Device Management and Network Filters in System Settings and found none.
- Checked reported ChatGPT storage usage: 2.3 GB. No storage-cap or upload-limit error was reported.
- Successfully read the test TXT and PDF using explicit local file paths in a desktop session with local file access.

No cache reset or deletion of local Library/Codex data was performed. Signing out and back in was suggested but is not confirmed as completed.

issues.title: Windows Computer Use: capture access and gold/yellow display border remain open after screenshot-producing turn completes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Incident package: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1021.3705.0`, Windows x64 MSIX. This version was obtained from the installed package path, not the About dialog.
Computer Use / unified-computer-use plugin: `26.1021.31345`.
Bundled CUA runtime directory identifier: `1fb7137c46617d50`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not collected for this report.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64, OS-reported version `Microsoft Windows 10.0.26200`.

### What issue are you seeing?

A gold/yellow border remained around the user's display after a Codex chat had finished its native desktop capture work. Investigation found the Windows Computer Use helper still running and its Windows capture-access record still open approximately five hours after the screenshot-producing turn completed.

The request is for capture resources to be released when their owning work ends, while preserving Computer Use for other chats that actually need it.

#### Verified incident timeline

Times below are UTC, with America/New_York (UTC-04:00) equivalents. Incident date was October 25, 2026 locally.

| UTC | Local time | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-10-25 19:58:05.097 | Oct 25, 15:58:05 | The originating chat called `driveClient.getScreenshot()` on a Google Drive desktop window during an authorized backup/restore verification. |
| 2026-10-25 19:58:07.456 | Oct 25, 15:58:07 | Windows CapabilityAccessManager's entry for this helper records capture-access start. |
| 2026-10-25 20:02:51.338 | Oct 25, 16:02:51 | Another `driveClient.getScreenshot()` call occurred in the same turn. |
| 2026-10-25 20:04:50.622 | Oct 25, 16:04:50 | The local transcript records `task_complete` for that screenshot-producing turn. |
| Before 2026-10-26 01:04:26 | Before Oct 25, 21:04:26 | The user reported the persistent gold display border. The helper remained running; its capture-access stop time was still zero. Latest inspected turns of active chats were using files, APIs, or browser automation, with no current native desktop-capture calls found in those turns. |
| 2026-10-26 01:04:26.466 | Oct 25, 21:04:26 | Only the positively identified stale `codex-computer-use.exe` helper was terminated. Windows then recorded a nonzero capture-access stop time. |

The completion timestamp comes from the original transcript's lifecycle event, not an assumption based on the chat appearing idle.

#### Process and Windows evidence

- The retained process was `codex-computer-use.exe`, PID 34140, directly parented by the main `ChatGPT.exe` process, PID 48532.
- Its command line was the bundled helper path followed by `--parent-pid 48532`.
- Loaded modules included `GraphicsCapture.dll`, `Windows.Graphics.dll`, `d3d11.dll`, and `dwmapi.dll`.
- A separate `codex-computer-use-swift.exe` helper was present and was left untouched.
- The relevant Windows record was under:
  `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\CapabilityAccessManager\ConsentStore\graphicsCaptureWithoutBorder\NonPackaged\<encoded-helper-path>`.
- Before cleanup: `LastUsedTimeStart = 134374318874561759`, `LastUsedTimeStop = 0`.
- After cleanup: `LastUsedTimeStop = 134374502664667304`, corresponding to `2026-10-26T01:04:26.4667304Z`.
- After cleanup, the old helper was absent; no replacement `codex-computer-use.exe` was observed in the follow-up checks. The main app and both checked Codex agent-server processes remained running, and ongoing chats continued.
- No app restart, broad process kill, plugin disablement, or Windows permission change was used.

The user-visible border was reported by the user. The verified post-cleanup result is helper termination plus Windows recording capture access as ended; no new desktop screenshot was taken merely to verify the border.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is one observed incident sequence, not a verified deterministic minimal reproduction:

1. Run multiple chats in the Windows desktop app with Computer Use enabled.
2. Have one chat capture a native application window using Computer Use.
3. Let the screenshot-producing chat turn complete, and continue ordinary work in other chats.
4. Observe whether the gold/yellow capture border and native helper persist after native desktop work has ended.
5. Check the helper's Windows capture-access record for an unset stop time.
6. In this incident, terminating only the identified stale native capture helper caused Windows to record the end of capture access while the app and other chat agents remained running.

Please do not use a blanket helper-killing rule as the product fix: another chat may legitimately be using the same helper.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Release native capture sessions, cached frames, and associated graphics resources promptly when the owning chat finishes or relinquishes desktop use.
- Remove the Windows capture indicator when no capture remains needed.
- Preserve any other chat's active native operation.
- Allow a later authorized Computer Use task to acquire a fresh session normally.
- Handle ordinary completion, interruption, errors, disconnects, and concurrent chats.

### Additional information

#### Existing cleanup and a possible lifecycle ordering gap

Local, read-only inspection found that cleanup mechanisms are already present:

- User configuration already had a `notify = [<bundled codex-computer-use.exe>, "turn-ended"]` entry.
- The installed unified-computer-use MCP configuration included its hidden `turn_ended` tool.
- The shipped Windows client registers an `addTurnEndedHandler` and sends an `end_turn` request.
- The shipped desktop JavaScript tracks active turns by native-pipe socket. Its `end_turn` path removes matching active-turn entries. Separately, `closeActiveTurn` first checks that tracking map and returns without closing the helper transport if the turn is no longer present.

**Hypothesis, not a confirmed root cause:** if the end-turn request removes ownership tracking before the outer `turn/completed` cleanup checks it, the later cleanup could skip closing the helper transport, allowing cached capture resources to outlive the turn. Please investigate the interaction between the end-turn callback, socket/turn ownership tracking, helper transport closure, and the native capture cache.

This was static inspection of the installed JavaScript plus process/registry observations. No instrumented race reproduction or native decompilation established the exact defect.

#### Scope and limitations

- The persistent border, retained graphics-capture helper, original turn-completion timestamp, open Windows access record, and successful targeted cleanup are the evidence being reported.
- The registry record alone does not prove continuous frame acquisition, video recording, uploading, or continuous model access to the display. No such claim is made here.
- Later native activity in other turns is not exhaustively ruled out. At diagnosis, no current native capture calls were found in the latest turns inspected.
- No full transcripts, screenshots, credentials, account email addresses, personal usernames, or unrelated project content are included.

Related, but a different primary symptom: #56941 reports a retained helper after Computer Use on the same desktop package version, with system-wide UI lag. This report concerns the lingering capture indicator and capture-access lifecycle; a common cause is not established.

Also related: #46675 describes the takeover overlay remaining until the entire agent turn ends on an older build. The present incident includes a verified completed screenshot-producing turn and Windows capture access remaining open afterward, rather than only an overlay persisting during the same active turn.

This is unacceptable behavior for a developer tool.

Codex Desktop repeatedly initiates massive background Git operations against my workspace without my permission, without meaningful resource limits, and without providing a way to disable them.

These operations repeatedly process large files, cause extreme disk I/O, and frequently make my entire computer freeze or become unresponsive.

I am not asking Codex to stage files, create Git snapshots, package datasets, or perform repository-wide operations. I am simply trying to use an AI coding assistant.

Why is a coding assistant allowed to consume enough system resources to make the user's entire machine unusable just to support an optional background feature?

The problem

  1. Codex periodically initiates expensive Git snapshot and packing operations without any explicit user request.

  2. Large files are repeatedly processed, even though .gitignore explicitly excludes them.

  3. There is no reliable setting to disable this behavior.

  4. These operations repeatedly restart, even when no Git-related functionality is requested.

  5. The resulting disk I/O frequently freezes my entire computer and interrupts my work.

This is not a minor performance issue. It is a critical reliability problem.

This has already been reported repeatedly. Why is it still happening?

Multiple issues have documented closely related problems:

  • #28750 — Repeated background Git operations.

  • #29388 — Excessive disk usage from automatic snapshots.

  • #50920 — Canceled snapshots leaving over 774 GiB of temporary files.

  • #59156 — Background checkpointing expanding Git storage to 385 GB.

How many more reports of frozen computers, exhausted disks, and disrupted workflows are needed before this gets fixed?

Why is such a resource-intensive background feature enabled by default with no effective opt-out?

Why are users expected to restructure their projects just to work around a problem caused by Codex itself?

What I expect from the maintainers

  • Provide a real OFF switch for all automatic Git snapshots and background packing.

  • Respect .gitignore and stop unnecessarily processing large files.

  • Enforce resource limits so background operations cannot freeze the entire system.

  • Stop repeatedly retrying failed or canceled snapshot operations.

These operations repeatedly process large files, generating extremely heavy disk I/O. 7. After some time, the entire system becomes severely unresponsive or freezes. 8. The behavior repeats periodically, with no available option to disable it. ### Expected behavior Codex should not perform resource-intensive repository-wide Git operations without explicit user consent. issues.title: Goal mode sends `function_call_output` input item without required `call_id`, breaking custom Responses API providers

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: custom-model
labels.description: Issues related to custom model providers (including local models)

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

issues.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

Codex CLI 0.169.0 / 0.170.0

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### Which model were you using?

custom

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Kitty

### Codex doctor report

```json

```

### What issue are you seeing?

• Goal active Objective: This is a test
■ stream disconnected before completion: stream closed before response.completed

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Configure a custom provider with `wire_api = "responses"`:

```toml
model_provider = "dashscope"

[model_providers.dashscope]
name = "dashscope"
base_url = "https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1"
wire_api = "responses"
env_key = "DASHSCOPE_API_KEY"
```

2. Start codex with this provider, set a goal (any objective, e.g. `/goal 这是一个短goal测试`).
3. The goal continuation turn starts automatically. Every sampling request fails immediately; after 5 retries codex shows:

```text
stream disconnected before completion: stream closed before response.completed
```

Goal becomes "stalled". Without a goal, the same session/model/endpoint works fine.
## Root cause

When a goal is active, codex injects the goal objective into the request `input` as a custom item:

```json
{
  "type": "function_call_output",
  "id": "fco_01a1f6d0-b42b-7051-ace5-1a3ae4be459a",
  "name": "goal_objective",
  "namespace": "agent",
  "output": "这是一个短goal测试"
}
```

Per the Responses API schema, `function_call_output` requires a `call_id` referencing a preceding `function_call`. This item has none (and there is no matching `function_call` in the input). Providers that validate the schema reject the request.

The injection is **unconditional** with goal mode: it happens for short and long objectives alike, regardless of content. Short objectives are additionally inlined in the `user_goal` context message; long ones are redacted from the rollout, but the malformed item is always sent.

This is a regression: goals completed successfully on 2026-11-17 with the previous binary; the 0.169.0 binary was installed on 2026-11-18; all goal sessions fail from 2026-11-19 onward.

## Observed provider error

DashScope returns HTTP 200 with an SSE error event (also see secondary issue below):

```text
event:error
:HTTP_STATUS/400
data:{"code":"InvalidParameter","message":"Invalid 'call_id': call_id is required for function_call_output.","request_id":"0a6f00a1-cbe4-9d27-928a-cea5d65b1c77"}
```

## Minimal reproduction (no codex needed)

POST to `/v1/responses` on any strictly validating provider:

```json
{
  "model": "glm-5.3-prime",
  "stream": true,
  "input": [
    {"type": "function_call_output", "name": "goal_objective", "namespace": "agent", "output": "这是一个短goal测试"}
  ]
}
```

Result: `InvalidParameter: call_id is required for function_call_output`.

Control: the same text as a regular user message completes normally. Deleting only the `function_call_output` item from a captured 335KB real codex goal request and replaying it unchanged also completes normally — this isolates the single offending item.

## Secondary issue: SSE `event:error` not surfaced

Codex does not parse the provider's in-stream error event (`event: error` with `:HTTP_STATUS/400`), so a protocol-level rejection is reported as a connectivity problem:

```text
stream disconnected before completion: stream closed before response.completed
```

This misleads users toward network/moderation/upstream-outage hypotheses (our investigation spent several wrong turns on exactly those). Surfacing the in-stream error payload would make the real cause visible immediately.


### What is the expected behavior?

- Goal-mode requests should only contain schema-valid input items (e.g. inject the objective as a message, or a well-formed tool-call pair).
- In-stream `event: error` payloads should be surfaced to the user instead of being reported as a stream disconnect.


### Additional information

_No response_

issues.title: Codex Desktop on Windows: existing coding chat returns HTTP 400 'Audio input is not available' for text-only messages, while new chats work

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

issues.body:
## Summary

An existing Codex Desktop coding conversation on **Windows 11** fails with **HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error`** and the message **`Audio input is not available.`**, even though the user is sending **plain text**, not an audio message.

The problem appears limited to **one previously active conversation**: newly created Codex conversations can accept text normally. The affected conversation contains work on an in-progress coding task, including partially completed edits, so losing the ability to continue the same thread interrupts the workflow and makes it difficult to preserve the task's context.

This may be related to #62212, which documents an earlier unsupported audio tool result poisoning later text-only turns. **However, unlike that report, the user did not intentionally submit audio in the failing turn, and we have not established whether any historical message or tool output contains audio.** Please do not assume the cause is the same.

## Environment

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Product | Codex Desktop |
| Operating system | Windows 11 |
| Date observed | November 18, 2026 |
| Codex app version/build | Not yet collected |
| Model / reasoning level | Not verified |
| Interface language | Chinese (based on the available UI screenshot) |
| Authentication/subscription | Not verified |
| Affected scope | One existing conversation; new conversations work |
| Input in failing turn | Plain text; no intentional voice/audio input |

## Steps to reproduce (observed workflow)

1. Open Codex Desktop on Windows 11.
2. Open an **existing coding conversation** in which Codex has already performed some project modifications and the development task is not yet complete.
3. Type and send a **plain-text** follow-up message in that existing conversation.
4. Observe the HTTP 400 error shown below, referring to unavailable audio input.
5. Create a **new conversation** in Codex Desktop and send plain text. The new conversation works normally, suggesting the issue is specific to the original conversation/history rather than a general loss of service.

**Important limitation:** We can reproduce/observe the failure in the affected historical conversation but do not yet have a minimal synthetic transcript that produces the failure from a fresh conversation. The original conversation's complete message/tool-output history has not been inspected.

## Actual behavior

Codex rejects a text-only turn with:

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": null,
    "message": "Audio input is not available.",
    "param": "input"
  },
  "status": 400
}
```

No useful recovery path is provided in this error. The user cannot readily continue the ongoing development task within the original conversation, despite the new text message containing no audio. A new conversation works but does not automatically preserve the full conversational context and prior decisions from the blocked thread.

## Expected behavior

- A plain-text follow-up should be accepted in an otherwise usable coding conversation.
- If a historical tool result/message contains an unsupported audio content item, Codex should validate and handle that item at the appropriate boundary instead of continuing to pass it in a way that breaks all subsequent text-only turns.
- If some historical content cannot be replayed to the selected model, the application should gracefully recover, omit/replace the unsupported item where safe, compact around it, or provide an explicit recoverable error.
- Users should be able to resume a conversation with an in-progress coding task without needing to abandon its history.

## Impact / severity

- **Session-blocking:** a previously productive development thread becomes unusable for further work.
- **Interrupted development:** the repository contains partially completed changes, while the task instructions, decisions, and progress are in the affected conversation.
- **Loss of continuity:** creating a fresh thread is a workaround for sending messages, but it is not equivalent to resuming the original development context.
- The error misleadingly refers to audio when the visible user input is text.

## What has and has not been verified

**Confirmed by the reporter:**
- Plain-text input was used when the error occurred.
- The error has the exact JSON payload above.
- The failure is specific to the old conversation; new conversations work.
- The affected conversation was being used for a partially completed coding task.

**Not yet verified:**
- Whether the conversation history includes audio embedded by a tool, a prior attachment, or a malformed/unsupported content part.
- Codex Desktop version/build, model, and exact thread identifier.
- Whether `codex resume`, forking, or compaction can recover this particular thread.
- Whether the source of the problem is client-side history serialization, request construction, or server-side validation.

## Potential area to investigate

This symptom is **consistent with**, but does not prove, unsupported content from an earlier turn being included in a new text-only request. Please consider checking:
1. How old `input` content parts and tool responses are serialized/replayed on the next request.
2. Whether unsupported `input_audio` entries can remain in saved conversation history and invalidate all later turns.
3. Whether the error is surfaced with enough information to identify the offending historical item.
4. Whether Codex can automatically sanitize/recover a thread instead of making the user start over.

**Related issue:** #62212 (same exact error string following known audio tool output; different platform and known trigger).

## Additional information

A screenshot of the HTTP 400 JSON error is available. Full private project contents, session history, and any potentially sensitive attachments are intentionally not included in this public report. I can provide sanitized diagnostic details if needed.
