prs.title: docs(auto-memory): fix dead anchor to skills discovery tiers section
prs.body:
## Summary

The Auto Memory guide's final "reviewing proposals" paragraph links "skill discovery precedence" to `./skills.md#skill-discovery-tiers`, but `docs/cli/skills.md` has no such anchor — its relevant heading is `## Discovery tiers`, whose anchor is `#discovery-tiers` (the file contains no explicit `<a id>`/`{#...}` anchors, so GitHub's auto-slug applies). Readers clicking the link land at the top of the Agent Skills page instead of the section that describes the discovery order.

This is a one-line docs fix: point the fragment at the existing `#discovery-tiers` anchor.

## Details

Verified against current `main` (`acfb42d0`):

```
$ grep -n "skill-discovery-tiers\|Discovery tiers" docs/cli/skills.md
35:## Discovery tiers

$ grep -n "skills.md#" docs/cli/auto-memory.md
110:[skill discovery precedence](./skills.md#skill-discovery-tiers). Applied memory
```

A full-repo link/anchor scan of `docs/` (382 internal links) flags exactly this one broken fragment; after the change, the auto-memory entry disappears from the scan and every other link in the two files is unchanged.

Note: PR #29230 proposed the same anchor correction (among seven pages in one PR) but was closed by the lifecycle bot without merging; the anchor is still broken upstream. This PR intentionally scopes the fix to a single page, per the repo's preference for small, atomic PRs.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30371

## How to Validate

1. `grep -n "Discovery tiers" docs/cli/skills.md` — heading exists at line 35; its GitHub anchor is `#discovery-tiers`.
2. Before: `grep -n "skill-discovery-tiers" docs/cli/auto-memory.md` matches line 110 (dead anchor). After: the line reads `./skills.md#discovery-tiers`.
3. `npx prettier --check docs/cli/auto-memory.md` — passes.
4. `git diff --check` — clean; repo `pre-commit` hook (prettier) passed at commit time.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [ ] Added/updated tests (if needed) — documentation-only change
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (if any) — none

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with the help of an AI coding agent: the agent ran a link/anchor integrity scan over `docs/`, verified the anchor mismatch against the target file's headings, made the one-line edit, and ran the local verification shown above (link scan red→green, prettier, `git diff --check`). A human reviewed and approved the final diff before submission.

prs.title: fix(core): keep a tier alias's config when the tier resolves to its first model
prs.body:
## Summary

A custom alias defined on a tier (`flash-lite`, `flash`, `pro`) now keeps its `generateContentConfig`. Previously, `applyModelSelection` re-resolved the config whenever the selected model's name differed from the resolved name. For a tier the selected name is always the concrete model, so every request used that model's stock settings: temperature 1, thinking HIGH, and no output cap. The alias's own settings were silently ignored, even though no fallback had happened.

## Details

- `applyModelSelection` now re-resolves only when the selected model differs both from the resolved name and from the head of that name's policy chain (`resolvePolicyChain(config, model)[0]`). That head is the model the tier resolves to, so it is the model the alias config was written for.
- A real availability fallback, where the pick is some other model in the chain, still takes that model's config exactly as before.
- Aliases on concrete models are unaffected, because for them the chain head is the model itself.

## Documented behavior

[Advanced Model Configuration](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/docs/cli/generation-settings.md) (`docs/cli/generation-settings.md`) describes behavior that `main` does not follow for an alias on a tier:

- **Step 1: Alias Resolution.** The docs say the requested model string is looked up in the alias map, its `extends` chain is merged, and *"this results in a base `ResolvedModelConfig`."* On `main`, that config is thrown away whenever the selected model's name differs from the resolved name. A tier alias such as `flash-lite` always resolves to a different, concrete name, so the request is re-resolved under that name and gets that model's stock settings.
- **Overrides.** The docs say an override's `match.model` *"matches the requested model name or alias."* The re-resolution uses the concrete model name, so an override that matches the alias, or the tier name, does not apply either.
- **The docs' own example.** The `precise-mode` example (`extends` a chat alias with `temperature: 0.0`) depends on this too. If the model it ends up on is resolved or promoted to another name, `temperature: 0.0` is dropped the same way.

This PR makes the runtime match the documented resolution. The alias's resolved config is kept unless an availability fallback moves the request to a different model in the chain. Only that fallback, which the docs do not describe as a config change, takes the other model's config.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30238

## How to Validate

1. Unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/availability/
   ```
   The new test fails on `main`. It defines `my-lite` on `flash-lite` with `temperature: 0.2` and `maxOutputTokens: 256`, then checks that the selected concrete model keeps both. The existing fallback test still passes.
2. Add this to `settings.json`:
   ```json
   "modelConfigs": { "customAliases": { "my-lite": { "modelConfig": {
     "model": "flash-lite",
     "generateContentConfig": { "temperature": 0.2, "maxOutputTokens": 256 } } } } }
   ```
   Then run `gemini -m my-lite -p "Reply with the single word ok."` with a local proxy via `CODE_ASSIST_ENDPOINT` that records `generationConfig`:

   | Build | `model` | `generationConfig` |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | main `e5d88fb2c` | `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` | `temperature: 1`, `thinkingLevel: HIGH`, no `maxOutputTokens` |
   | this PR | `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` | `temperature: 0.2`, `maxOutputTokens: 256` |

- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)

Updates `esbuild` from 0.25.0 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

    This should match <span class="a"><span class="b"><span class="b">yes</span></span></span> but not <span class="a"><span class="b">no</span></span>. The old output incorrectly matched both.

  • Avoid overwriting input files without --allow-overwrite (#4484)

    For example: esbuild input.js --outfile=input.js tells esbuild to overwrite input.js with the output of running esbuild on it. This was supposed to already be prevented by default, but it accidentally regressed in version 0.17.0 and apparently didn't have any test coverage. The error message was being printed but the input file was still being overwritten. Oops.

    This release puts the original behavior back. With this release, esbuild should now actually avoid overwriting input files unless --allow-overwrite is explicitly present. This is done by not writing out any files when a build error is encountered.

  • Fix incorrect code generated when using top-level await (#4498)

    Previously esbuild could generate code containing a syntax error in complex scenarios involving top-level await used in a dependency cycle. The problem was a missing async on one or more module wrapper closures. With this release, esbuild now uses a fixed-point iteration algorithm to correctly annotate all dependencies in the cycle as needing an async module wrapper.

  • Fix a minification bug with lowered logical assignment operators (#4508)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to generate incorrect code for logical assignment operators when lowering them to an older target environment. Specifically the lowering process requires duplicating the left-hand side, but esbuild incorrectly failed to count the duplicate as a new usage when the left-hand side is an identifier. That then caused the minifier to believe that the left-hand side was only used once and could attempt to incorrectly inline an initializer into the first usage. This bug has now been fixed:

    // Original code
function foo() {
  let x
  bar(x ||= {})

Changelog

Sourced from esbuild's changelog.

Changelog: 2025

This changelog documents all esbuild versions published in the year 2025 (versions 0.25.0 through 0.27.2).

0.27.2

  • Allow import path specifiers starting with #/ (#4361)

    Previously the specification for package.json disallowed import path specifiers starting with #/, but this restriction has recently been relaxed and support for it is being added across the JavaScript ecosystem. One use case is using it for a wildcard pattern such as mapping #/* to ./src/* (previously you had to use another character such as #_* instead, which was more confusing). There is some more context in nodejs/node#49182.

    This change was contributed by @​hybrist.

  • Automatically add the -webkit-mask prefix (#4357, #4358)

    This release automatically adds the -webkit- vendor prefix for the mask CSS shorthand property:

    /* Original code */
main {
  mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat
}

    /* Old output (with --target=chrome110) */
    
main {
    
mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}
    

    /* New output (with --target=chrome110) */
    
main {
    
-webkit-mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}

    This change was contributed by @​BPJEnnova.

  • Additional minification of switch statements (#4176, #4359)

    This release contains additional minification patterns for reducing switch statements. Here is an example:

    // Original code
switch (x) {
  case 0:
    foo()
    break
  case 1:
  default:
    bar()
}

Updates `express` from 5.1.0 to 5.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

v5.3.0

Highlights

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by @​YuryShkoda in #4893

    Fixed the behavior of res.send() to prevent conflicts between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding HTTP headers in responses. The Content-Length header in res.send() is now only added when a Transfer-Encoding header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a Transfer-Encoding header - by @​cuishuang in #7459

  • Upgrade qs to ^6.16.0, which fixes CVE-2026-2391 (GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883), CVE-2026-82417 (GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) and CVE-2026-82562 (GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx): arrayLimit bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled isBuffer - by @​davetashner in #7057 and #7478, and @​cyphercodes in #7305

  • Upgrade proxy-addr to ^2.0.8, which fixes CVE-2026-90711 - by @​lazerg in #7474

🚀 Improvements

  • Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. req.fresh previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by @​Cherry in #7366

    // QUERY /reports with If-None-Match: "12345"
app.query('/reports', (req, res) => {
  res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
  res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
});

  • Improve HTML structure in res.redirect() responses when HTML format is accepted by adding <!DOCTYPE html>, <title>, and <body> tags for better browser compatibility - by @​Bernice55231 in #5167

  • When calling app.render with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by AkaHarshit in #6903

    app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected

  • Upgrade content-type to ^2.0.0, bringing a faster parser (~1.5x quicker Content-Type parsing/formatting in res.send()) along with a behavior change: res.send() now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a Content-Type that fails to parse. type-is is upgraded to ^2.1.0 as part of the same change - by @​blakeembrey in #7234

    res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
// -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8

  • The default error handler now logs the full error object instead of only its stack trace, so nested details such as Error.cause and library-specific properties (e.g. Sequelize's parent/original) are no longer swallowed - by @​Nitin-Mohapatra in #6464

  • Upgrade content-disposition to ^2.0.1, which changes the Content-Disposition header emitted by res.download(), res.attachment(), and res.sendFile(): file names that are valid HTTP tokens are no longer wrapped in quotes. This is equivalent per RFC 6266, but applications asserting on the exact header bytes should update their expectations - by @​blakeembrey in #7233

    res.attachment('user.html');
// before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"
// after  -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=user.html

... (truncated)

issues.title: Model and context-window changes are applied non-deterministically; session sat on `auto` for ~12 minutes while the client showed another model

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In a long-running Copilot agent session hosted by VS Code's agent host (harness mode), an explicit model change is not applied to the session reliably. Selections are silently dropped, the session keeps running on the model it was already on, and at one point the session sat on `auto` for ~12 minutes while the VS Code picker displayed a completely different model. Auto routing then chose an expensive model for every turn.

I have never seen a deterministic side effect from any of my attempts. Some interrupts did nothing, some did; nothing I did reliably changed which model served the next message. The one time the change finally landed, the event log revealed the session had been on `auto` the whole time.

**Expected behaviour is simple and should be deterministic: when I change the model, or the context-window size, the very next message I send is served by that model with that context setting.** Not sometimes. Not after a window reload, an agent host restart, and a VS Code restart.

### Environment

- Windows 11, VS Code Stable, Copilot in agent host ("harness") mode; one shared Local Agent Host for all windows
- Copilot CLI 1.0.114 (updated from 1.0.113 earlier in the same session)
- One very long-lived session: ~236 MB session log, ~133k events, 100+ compactions, context display showing 654.3K / 328K tokens (100%)

### Evidence from the session event log (times UTC, 2026-11-20)

Earlier in the same session a model change worked normally (`session.model_change` gemini-4-neon → gpt-6.2-sol at 02:33:53). After that, nothing applied:

| Time | Model I selected in the picker | What the session did |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 03:34–03:45 | Claude Sonnet 5.5, across several stop/interrupt retries and a Reload Window | No `session.model_change` at all. Every `assistant.message` and every `session.usage_record` was `gpt-6.2-sol`, and the response footer confirmed "GPT-6.2 Sol". |
| 03:48:55 | Claude Haiku 5.5, after `Developer: Restart Local Agent Host` | One model change arrived — but as **`auto`**, not Haiku (`source: "sdk"`, `newModel: "auto"`), and the context tier was reset from `long_context` to `null`. |
| 03:49:00–03:51:09 | Haiku / Sonnet | `session.fusion_resolved` (`hydrafusion`, critique pattern), then `session.auto_mode_resolved` → "Copilot Fusion selected Claude Opus 5.5 since the task has high complexity." One of those turns billed **170.6 credits**. |
| 03:52:10, 03:53:11 | Sonnet 5.5, after a full VS Code restart | Both user messages were recorded, **no assistant reply was produced at all**. |
| 03:55:42 | Local custom-endpoint model | No model change. Compaction and every reply ran on `claude-opus-5.5`. |
| 04:00:53.479 → .512 | Same local model, after one more interrupt | The change finally landed: `session.model_change` `newModel: customendpoint/Strata (local dual RTX 5090)/strata`, **`previousModel: "auto"`**. |
| 04:02:45 | — | `assistant.message model: Strata (local dual RTX 5090)/strata` — finally the model I had chosen. |

That `previousModel: "auto"` is the key datum: for roughly 12 minutes the session's stored model was `auto` while the picker displayed Haiku, then Sonnet, then a local model. Auto routing scored every turn "high complexity" and selected Opus 5.5, so I was billed for a model I had explicitly rejected — on a session where I had switched models specifically to reduce cost.

Across the reloads and restarts there are many `session.shutdown` / `session.resume` pairs, and every later resume reports `selectedModel: "auto"`, which suggests the resume path restores a defaulted model rather than the model the client currently holds.

### Things I tried, with no reliable effect

Stop/interrupt (repeatedly, with a pause before resending), `Developer: Reload Window`, `Developer: Restart Local Agent Host`, and a full VS Code quit and relaunch. Individually some of these happened to coincide with a change landing and most did not, which is the real problem: there is no deterministic recovery action, and the picker keeps displaying a model that is not serving the session.

### Suggested fixes

1. Make an explicit model / context-window change land deterministically: the next user message must be served by the selected model, or the request must fail with a visible error rather than silently continuing on the previous model.
2. Never let auto or Fusion routing silently replace an explicit user selection. If the session is auto-routed, the client must know that, and it must be visually distinct from an explicit choice. (I saw "Copilot Fusion selected Claude Opus 5.5" rendered under a picker that said Sonnet 5.5.)
3. Preserve `contextTier` across a model change instead of resetting it to `null`.
4. Have `session.resume` restore the client's actual current model rather than defaulting to `auto`.
5. Expose the model actually serving the turn so the client footer can't lie about it.

### Related

- Filed in parallel as [microsoft/vscode#349375](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/349375) because the symptom is visible in VS Code's agent-host UI and it is unclear which layer owns the stale model state. Cross-linked from there.
- Similar area, distinct symptoms: #3998 (wrong model billed under auto), #5213 (explicit startup model selection replaced by `auto`).

I can supply the relevant event-log slices (`session.model_change`, `session.auto_mode_resolved`, `session.fusion_resolved`, `session.usage_record`, `session.resume`) privately, plus UI screenshots showing the picker/footer mismatch and the 170.6-credit turn.

### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

With reasoning shown ( showReasoning  / ctrl+t), every "Thought for…" block stays expanded after the model finishes thinking. In long agent sessions, this pushes answers, tool calls and results off-screen, and I have to scroll past old reasoning to find them. Today the choice is all or nothing: keep every block expanded, or hide reasoning entirely and lose the live view of what the agent is doing.

### Proposed solution

Proposal
Add an auto-collapse mode, for example  showReasoning: "auto" :

• Show the block expanded while the model is thinking.
• When the thought finishes, collapse it to a single "Thought for Ns" line.
• Let me expand one collapsed block (by clicking it or with a key) without expanding all of them.
• Keep ctrl+t as the toggle for all blocks, and save the mode across sessions like  showReasoning .

Current workaround
ctrl+t hides all reasoning, and ctrl+o toggles the whole timeline, but neither collapses only the finished thoughts.

issues.body:
**Problem**
When a task needs the user to act (for example approving a device-login URL/code in a browser), the instruction is often printed only inside a collapsed bash/tool output block. In autopilot or long-running sessions the user does not see it and the flow stalls until the login times out.

**Expected**
- Any step that needs human action (open a URL, enter a code, approve a prompt, run a command manually) should be surfaced prominently in the visible assistant message or as a notification, not only in collapsed tool output.
- Ideally the CLI could detect/flag such prompts (URLs + codes from background commands) and raise them to the timeline or a desktop notification.

**Impact**
Interactive login flows (OAuth device flow) silently wait on the user, who never saw the prompt.

Version: 1.0.114, macOS.

issues.title: Remote control: sessions are read-only on GitHub Mobile/web since legacy remote steering was removed (1.0.110)

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Since 1.0.110 ("Remove legacy remote steering; cloud sessions and remote connections now require an AHP environment"), sessions shared with `/remote on` can no longer be steered from GitHub Mobile or github.com. The session shows up in the Agents list but is read-only ("Steering disabled"). The only way to steer it now is from another Copilot CLI via `/environments`.

That breaks the feature as documented and announced as GA in May (https://github.blog/changelog/2026-05-18-remote-control-for-copilot-cli-sessions-now-generally-available-on-mobile-web-and-vs-code): "monitor or steer it from the GitHub Mobile app or github.com". The docs (https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli/steer-remotely) still describe phone/web steering and still mention `copilot --remote`, which now errors with "--remote was removed".

### Affected version

1.0.114 (also 1.0.110+). Works on 1.0.108 with `COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Copilot Pro account (personal, no org policy), Linux.
2. Run `copilot` (1.0.114), type `/remote on`. Output: "Sharing this session through Mission Control".
3. Open the session in GitHub Mobile or at github.com/copilot/agents.
4. It's view-only, "Steering disabled", and you can't send a prompt.

For comparison:
1. `COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false npx -y @github/copilot@1.0.108`
2. `/remote on`. Output: "Remote steering enabled" plus a github.com/copilot/tasks/... link.
3. Prompts sent from GitHub Mobile are received and answered.

### Expected behavior

`/remote on` on the current version should let me steer the session from GitHub Mobile and github.com, as documented. If not, mobile/web should support AHP sessions before legacy steering is removed, and the docs and the mobile hint should be updated.

### Additional context

- OS: Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu), plus a second machine with the same result
- Pinning 1.0.108 works around it, but auto-update silently upgrades unless `COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false` is set
- GitHub Mobile still suggests "start it with copilot --remote", which no longer works

issues.title: Prompt cache expires during synchronous `task` sub-agent runs on `gemini-4-carbon` (94% miss rate / 20x input cost penalty on resume)

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When using `gemini-4-carbon` as an orchestrator that delegates work to synchronous `task` sub-agents (e.g., researchers, workers, code reviewers), the parent agent's prompt cache almost always expires while waiting for the sub-agent tool call to complete.

Because uncached input tokens on `gemini-4-carbon` bill at **20x the cached rate** (`200 AIU/1M` uncached vs `10 AIU/1M` cached), every sub-agent return forces the parent thread to re-ingest its entire 300K–500K token context from scratch—costing **75–100 AIU for a single post-tool resume call**.

Across 3,100+ main-thread API calls (>80K prompt tokens) in local `events.jsonl` / `assistant_usage_events` telemetry:

| Metric (Prompts > 80K Tokens) | `gemini-4-carbon` | `gemini-4-argon` | `gpt-6-luna` | `claude-opus-5 / 5.5` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **Cache hit rate after a `task` sub-agent** | **5.6%** *(2 / 36)* | **80.0%** *(24 / 30)* | **100%** | **100%** *(when < 5m)* |
| **Cache hit rate after a 3–15 min wait (`180s–900s`)** | **6.8%** *(4 / 59)* | **58.1%** *(61 / 105)* | **100%** *(5 / 5)* | **100% <= 5m** / **0% > 5m** |
| **Cache hit rate at 2–3 min (`121s–180s`)** | **62.8%** *(19 / 30)* | **87.8%** *(42 / 47)* | **96.7%** *(5 / 5)* | **99.0%** *(5 / 5)* |
| **Unexpected `0` cache-read misses under 90s** | **4.8%** *(21 / 440)* | **5.0%** *(41 / 822)* | **0.0%** *(0 / 105)* | **0.7%** *(1 / 150)* |

In a multi-step plan + implementation session where the parent `gemini-4-carbon` thread accumulated ~400K–500K tokens and spawned 10–19 synchronous `task` sub-agents:
- Main-thread cache misses alone consumed **~2,210 AIU across just 31 missed calls** (~75% of the main agent's total credit spend).
- The exact same workflow on `gemini-4-argon` cost **3x less** because the parent context stayed cached while sub-agents ran.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI `1.0.111-0` (via VS Code Copilot Agent Host)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start an agent session with `gemini-4-carbon` selected and build up a conversation context (>100K–300K tokens).
2. Have the main agent invoke a synchronous `task` sub-agent (`mode: "sync"`) that runs for 2–10 minutes.
3. Inspect the `session.usage_record` and `session.usage_checkpoint` events in `~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/events.jsonl` for the main agent call immediately following `subagent.completed`.
4. Observe that `usage.cacheReadTokens` drops to `0` on the parent's resume call (94.4% of the time across 36 sub-agent runs), billing the full `usage.inputTokens` at the uncached rate (`200 AIU/1M` instead of `10 AIU/1M`).

### Expected behavior

1. **Parent prompt cache stays warm while synchronous `task` sub-agents execute:** When the harness blocks a parent agent on a long-running `task` call, the parent turn is still active and guaranteed to resume with the same prefix as soon as the sub-agent completes.
2. **Explicit cache pinning / consistent KV-cache TTL on Gemini:** Enable explicit context caching / cache markers (`marks_system_prompt` / `marks_conversation`) for Gemini models, or match `gemini-4-carbon`'s backend KV-cache retention to `gemini-4-argon` (which retains cached prefixes across 10–15 minute sub-agent runs).

### Additional context

- **OS / Environment:** Windows 11 (x86_64), PowerShell, VS Code Copilot Agent Host (`producer: "copilot-agent"`, `copilotVersion: "1.0.111-0"`).
- **No explicit cache pinning on Gemini (`/chat/completions`) in `session.usage_checkpoint`:**
  - `gpt-6-*` uses `ws:/responses` with `incremental_input: true`, `marks_system_prompt: true`, and `modelCacheState: [{ cacheTtlSeconds: 1800 }]`.
  - `claude-*` uses `/v1/messages` with explicit `cacheWriteTokens` and `modelCacheState: [{ cacheTtlSeconds: 300 }]`.
  - `gemini-4-*` uses stateless `/chat/completions` with `modelCacheState: []`, `cacheWriteTokens: 0`, and `cache_config: { arm: "control", marks_system_prompt: false, marks_conversation: false }`, relying entirely on best-effort implicit prefix caching.
- **Sub-90s same-host evictions:** Even without sub-agents, `gemini-4-carbon` frequently reports `cacheReadTokens: 0` on 250K–425K token contexts after gaps of just **20s–79s** (e.g., while waiting on a build/test command), even when consecutive requests land on the **exact same backend host prefix** in `providerCallId`.

issues.title: Windows MCP authentication fails for guest-tenant resources despite discovering the correct tenant

labels.name: area:authentication

issues.body:
## Description

Authenticating an Entra-protected remote MCP server fails when my Windows account is a guest in the tenant hosting the API.

Copilot supplies the resource tenant's authority to OneAuth, but the subsequent Windows broker request uses /common and Entra evaluates the API resource in my home tenant. Authentication fails with AADSTS500011, surfaced by Copilot as a generic ENTRA_CONFIG error.

## Environment

- Copilot CLI: **1.0.114**
- Windows: **10.0.26300**, x64
- OneAuth: **12.1.0**
- Remote MCP server hosted on Azure Functions
- Windows account belongs to tenant A and is a guest in resource tenant B

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use Windows with an account from tenant A.
2. Have guest access to tenant B, where an Entra-protected MCP API is registered.
3. Configure the MCP server to advertise tenant B's authorisation server and API scope.
4. Add the remote MCP server to Copilot CLI and authenticate.

## Expected behaviour

Copilot acquires a token for the MCP API in tenant B using the account's guest identity, prompting for interaction or consent if necessary.

## Actual behaviour

Authentication fails:

```text
ENTRA_CONFIG: the authenticator rejected the configuration
[code 2002, tag 4usqa]
```

## Diagnostic evidence

Identifiers below are replaced with placeholders.

Copilot's native authentication log initially shows the correct authority:

```text
Initializing authority from URI
'https://login.microsoftonline.com/<RESOURCE_TENANT_ID>'
```

However, Windows AAD Operational events show:

```text
TokenEndpoint:
https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/token

AADSTS500011: The resource principal named
api://<MCP_API_APPLICATION_ID_URI>
was not found in the tenant named <HOME_TENANT_ID>.
```

Broker telemetry also reports:

```json
{
  "server_error_code": 500011,
  "oauth_error_code": "invalid_resource",
  "authority": "organizations",
  "is_guest_resource_scenario": false,
  "ui_visible": false
}
```

## Additional observations

- Setting COPILOT_ENTRA_DISABLE_ONEAUTH=1 does not enable browser authentication; it instead fails with ENTRA_UNAVAILABLE.
- The UI hides the actionable AADSTS500011 error behind the generic configuration error.
- The evidence suggests resource-tenant targeting is lost or overridden between OneAuth's initial request and WAM token acquisition. The exact cause is not yet confirmed.

issues.title: MCP: dynamic headers helper for remote MCP servers (parity with Claude Code `headersHelper`)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Remote (HTTP) MCP servers can only get static `headers`. `${VAR}` expansion happens once when the config loads, and plugin-shipped remote servers get no expansion at all. That doesn't work for short-lived credentials in a custom header, such as a token that expires after an hour or two. When the token expires, the server fails until the user restarts the CLI with a fresh environment variable. `/mcp` reload doesn't help, because the process environment is unchanged. Hooks can't change MCP request headers.

A common case is a server that needs a short-lived token from a local credential CLI in a custom header, while Copilot CLI's built-in MCP OAuth keeps handling `Authorization`. Today the only options are restarting every session before the token expires, running a local proxy that adds the header, or swapping the remote server for a stdio bridge. The bridge loses Copilot's built-in OAuth.

### Proposed solution

Add an optional `headersHelper` field to remote MCP server configs (`http`/`sse`, in user, workspace and plugin config), matching Claude Code's [`headersHelper`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp#use-dynamic-headers-for-custom-authentication):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "issues": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
      "headersHelper": "/usr/local/bin/mcp-headers",
      "tools": ["*"]
    }
  }
}
```

Suggested behaviour:

1. The command writes a JSON object of string headers to stdout and runs with a timeout (e.g. 10 s).
2. It runs on every connect and reconnect. On a `401`/`403` the CLI runs it again, reconnects and retries the request once.
3. Its headers override static `headers` with the same name.
4. Its headers are added to **every** request to the server, including the first `initialize` after an OAuth login.
5. If the helper outputs no `Authorization` header, the built-in MCP OAuth flow stays on and keeps sending its own `Authorization`.
6. The helper receives the server name and URL as environment variables (e.g. `COPILOT_MCP_SERVER_NAME`, `COPILOT_MCP_SERVER_URL`), so one helper can serve several servers.
7. The helper's output is never logged, and `copilot mcp get` shows it masked.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. A long autopilot session (`/goal ...`) calls tools on a remote MCP server for 4 hours. The short-lived token is refreshed silently by the helper; no restart is needed.
2. An organisation ships a plugin with its remote MCP servers and a `headersHelper` pointing to its credential CLI. Users install the plugin and don't need to export any token.
3. `copilot -p "summarise open bugs in PROJ"` in a cron job uses the helper to get a fresh token on each run, without a wrapper script that exports environment variables.
4. Several remote servers need the same custom header. One helper serves all of them, and each server still has its own OAuth sign-in.

### Additional context

- Related: #4681, which reports that custom headers from `mcp-config.json` are not sent on the `initialize` request after an OAuth login. A dynamic header has the same requirement: it must be sent on every request.
- Related: #3100 (static `Authorization` header and OAuth discovery).
- A precedent for refreshable auth parity with Claude Code: #3477 (OTel headers helper, completed).
- Copilot CLI version: 1.0.112, macOS. The behaviour described is from the CLI command reference and the plugin reference.

issues.title: Hook for user-invoked skills (slash commands), or a matcher on `userPromptTransformed`

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

We run a plug-in marketplace with a central, force-enabled plug-in that uses `preToolUse` (matcher `skill|task`) to deny a skill when the plug-in's prerequisites are missing (e.g. a required CLI or environment variable).  When the user starts a skill with a slash command (`/my-skill`), the runtime injects the skill directly into the prompt (`skill.invoked` with `trigger: "user-invoked"`, `<skill-context name="my-skill">` in the model-facing content). No `skill` tool call happens, so `preToolUse`/`postToolUse` never fire and the skill runs even though its prerequisites are not met.

### Proposed solution

**Request** (any of these would solve it)

1. Fire `preToolUse`/`postToolUse` with `toolName: "skill"` (or a dedicated event such as `skillInvoked`) for user-invoked skills too, with the ability to deny and give a reason.
2. Support a `matcher` on `userPromptTransformed`/`userPromptSubmitted` (e.g. on the invoked skill name), so the hook only runs when a slash-command skill is used.
3. Document the shape of user-invoked skill context in the hook payload (e.g. an `invokedSkill` field), so hooks don't have to parse the prompt.

### Example prompts or workflows

_No response_

### Additional context

**What we tried**

A `userPromptTransformed` command hook can detect the `<skill-context>` block and replace it via `modifiedTransformedPrompt`. That works (Copilot CLI runtime 1.0.111, VS Code Copilot harness), but:

- `userPromptTransformed` has no matcher, so the hook runs for every prompt of every user. Starting the shell alone costs ~0.5 s (pwsh) to ~1.3 s (Windows PowerShell 5.1), and the hook blocks the turn.
- It depends on the undocumented `<skill-context>` prompt format.

**Environment**

- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.110 (terminal), runtime 1.0.111 in the VS Code Copilot harness
- Windows 11, pwsh 7.5 and Windows PowerShell 5.1

issues.title: Linux: Perforce depot wildcards are misclassified as UNC paths and blocked by content exclusion

labels.name: area:platform-linux
labels.description: Linux-specific: Wayland, X11, Ubuntu, Fedora, Alpine, ARM, terminal emulators

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On Linux, Copilot CLI rejects a read-only Perforce command containing a depot filespec such as `//depot/project/dir/*` before invoking `p4`. It reports that the path is excluded by organization content policy, even though no configured exclusion rule matches that depot path.

A concrete depot filename succeeds in the same session, while a depot filespec containing `*` is denied. Perforce uses `//depot/...` as a server-side namespace; this is not a Windows UNC share or a local filesystem path.

The examples below use synthetic depot names in place of private paths. The original wildcard failure and concrete-filename success were observed in real Copilot CLI sessions on 2026-11-18; these placeholder paths have not themselves been executed against a server.

### Affected version

```text
GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.114
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Use Linux with a working Perforce CLI/client and an organization account with content exclusions enabled. Have at least one exclusion rule for an unrelated path, for example `**/unrelated-private-area/**`. The depot path used below must not match any exclusion rule.
2. Verify that a read-only listing of an authorized depot directory works directly in bash:

   ```bash
   p4 files "//depot/project/dir/*"
   ```

3. Ask Copilot CLI to run that exact command through its bash/shell tool. It is rejected during preflight, before `p4` starts:

   ```text
   Access denied: "//depot/project/dir/*" is excluded by organization content policy. Do not attempt to access this file.
   ```

4. Compare with a command using a concrete, authorized depot filename, such as `p4 files "//depot/project/dir/example.txt"`. Concrete depot filenames were accepted in the affected session; the denial is sensitive to filespec syntax, not just the leading `//`.

### Expected behavior

Recognize Perforce depot filespecs in `p4` commands and do not classify them as Windows UNC shares merely because they begin with `//`, especially on Linux.

Continue enforcing applicable content-exclusion rules. This report is **not** a request to disable content exclusions or to exempt every `//` argument from security checks. If a target genuinely cannot be evaluated, distinguish that failure from a positive match against an organization exclusion rule.

### Additional context

- OS: AlmaLinux 8.10, Linux x86_64.
- Shell: bash.
- Observed with CLI 1.0.114; no claim about other releases.
- The configured organization exclusions were checked during the investigation. None matched the failing depot path. Private policy contents, credentials, depot names, session transcripts, and server addresses are intentionally omitted.
- Running Perforce metadata listings directly in bash succeeds. No file-content reads or repository modifications are needed to demonstrate this failure.

#### Suspected cause

Inspection of the installed Linux native runtime suggests two interacting checks. This is an analysis of the shipped artifact, not a source-level fix or a maintainer-confirmed diagnosis:

1. The shell argument classifier associated with `src/native/primitives/shell_paths.rs` appears to omit some `//` tokens from `possiblePaths` when they contain `:`, end with `...`, or consist solely of nonempty slash-separated components using `[A-Za-z0-9+\-.@_]`. A Perforce `*` wildcard fails that last test and the token is treated as a filesystem path instead.
2. The content-exclusion path associated with `src/runtime/src/session_permissions/content_exclusion.rs` appears to classify the resulting `//depot/project/...` argument as a Windows UNC path on Linux. The runtime contains this more specific diagnostic:

   ```text
   Content exclusion cannot evaluate UNC paths. Blocking access to protect excluded content.
   ```

   The user-facing error instead says the path *is excluded by organization policy*, which misdirects troubleshooting toward an organization rule that does not match it.

Perforce revision syntax such as `#head` appears affected by the same classifier limitation. That extension follows from the runtime analysis; it has not been separately reproduced through Copilot preflight.

#### Scope and regression tests

Suggested regression coverage: ordinary depot filenames, single-directory `*`, recursive `...`, revision-qualified `*#head` and `...#head`, and genuinely excluded targets. Preserve correct handling of real Windows UNC paths and Bazel `//package:target` syntax.

Perforce `*` and `...` are not interchangeable: `*` matches within a directory, while `...` is recursive. Substituting `...` to avoid the denial changes the requested scope and is not a general workaround. Runtime analysis suggests that tokens ending in `...` take a different classification path, but that is not claimed here as a newly verified end-to-end Copilot workaround.

issues.title: Extension host hangs forever in `process.exit` after app quit (macOS): orphan keeps its listening port

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

After I quit the GitHub Copilot app, one extension host process did not exit. Its parent CLI process was force-stopped by the app, the bootstrap watchdog in `extension_bootstrap.mjs` then called `process.exit(0)`, and that call never returned. The main thread is blocked in `uv_thread_join` inside libuv's threadpool cleanup, while all four libuv worker threads sit idle in `uv_cond_wait`. The process uses 0% CPU, has PPID 1, and still holds its listening TCP socket.

The extension was a canvas extension that serves a local dashboard on `127.0.0.1:7927`. Because the orphan still owns that port but its event loop is dead, the canvas fails to open on every later app launch:

```
RPC error -32603: Request session.canvas.open failed with message: Port 7927 is in use and not answering. Stop that program, or set SWARM_DASHBOARD_PORT to a free port for the Copilot app and restart it.
```

The extension code does not call `process.exit`; the exit came from the runtime's bootstrap watchdog. The hang is inside Node/libuv shutdown in the embedded runtime. The app's shutdown also has a gap: it force-stopped the host's parent, logged `survivors=0`, and never checked or signalled the extension host itself.

I have seen this once. The other extension hosts that were running at the same quit exited normally.

### Affected version

- GitHub Copilot app 1.4.2 (commit `aa666576`), macOS arm64
- Embedded runtime `copilot-sdk-runtime-1.0.106-8.unstable.r43566476370.g869eef3`: Node v24.22.1, libuv 1.52.1
- Runtime image `LC_UUID 6CAF9C5B-1E60-382D-B33C-06521A6AEB0F`
- macOS 27.2.1 (26B131)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

I can't reproduce this on demand. What happened:

1. The app was running with a session whose canvas extension (the `swarm-dashboard` canvas from the `wintermute` plugin) served HTTP and SSE on `127.0.0.1:7927`. Its extension host was pid 80226, started 2026-11-18 13:14:15 UTC. Its parent CLI was pid 75796.
2. About 20 hours later I quit the app at 2026-11-19 09:19:22 UTC.
3. The app force-stopped CLI pid 75796. Within about a second the bootstrap watchdog in pid 80226 saw the parent was gone and called `process.exit(0)`.
4. Pid 80226 never exited. `ps` shows PPID 1, state `S` and 0.0% CPU. Its CPU time was `21:33.95` at 09:38 UTC and was still `21:33.95` at 09:56 UTC, about 37 minutes after the quit.
5. On the next app launch, opening the canvas failed with the error above, because pid 80226 still holds the `LISTEN` socket on port 7927.

### Expected behavior

- `process.exit(0)` in an extension host ends the process.
- If a host does not exit, the app should not leave it running after quit. An orphaned host should never keep holding ports or other resources for the next app launch.

### Additional context

#### Main-thread stack (from `sample`, identical at 09:26:27 and 09:38:11 UTC)

```
    +             2601 node::Environment::RunTimers(uv_timer_s*)  (in copilot) + 536  [0x102190120]
    +               2601 v8::Function::Call(v8::Isolate*, v8::Local<v8::Context>, v8::Local<v8::Value>, int, v8::Local<v8::Value>*)  (in copilot) + 492  [0x1024d2754]
    +                 2601 ???  (in copilot)  load address 0x1020e4000 + 0x579dd0  [0x10265ddd0]
    +                   2601 ???  (in copilot)  load address 0x1020e4000 + 0x57a46c  [0x10265e46c]
    +                     2601 ???  (in copilot)  load address 0x1020e4000 + 0x105e570  [0x103142570]
    +                       2601 ???  (in copilot)  load address 0x1020e4000 + 0x105e8cc  [0x1031428cc]
    +                         2601 ???  (in <unknown binary>)  [0x12b07c070]
    +                           2601 ???  (in <unknown binary>)  [0x12afc29a8]
    +                             2601 ???  (in copilot)  load address 0x1020e4000 + 0x10616e0  [0x1031456e0]
    +                               2601 ???  (in copilot)  load address 0x1020e4000 + 0x1060bec  [0x103144bec]
    +                                 2601 ???  (in copilot)  load address 0x1020e4000 + 0x1062818  [0x103146818]
    +                                   2601 node::Environment::Exit(node::ExitCode)  (in copilot) + 392  [0x102191cbc]
    +                                     2601 node::DefaultProcessExitHandlerInternal(node::Environment*, node::ExitCode)  (in copilot) + 68  [0x1020fb9cc]
    +                                       2601 ???  (in copilot)  load address 0x1020e4000 + 0x103ac34  [0x10311ec34]
    +                                         2601 uv_thread_join  (in copilot) + 20  [0x103131934]
    +                                           2601 _pthread_join  (in libsystem_pthread.dylib) + 620  [0x19eb56fd8]
    +                                             2601 __ulock_wait  (in libsystem_kernel.dylib) + 8  [0x19eb11af4]
```

All four `libuv-worker` threads:

```
2601 Thread_12128792: libuv-worker
+ 2601 thread_start  (in libsystem_pthread.dylib) + 8  [0x19eb4fcd0]
+   2601 _pthread_start  (in libsystem_pthread.dylib) + 136  [0x19eb54ce4]
+     2601 ???  (in copilot)  load address 0x1020e4000 + 0x103b4a4  [0x10311f4a4]
+       2601 uv_cond_wait  (in copilot) + 40  [0x1031320a0]
+         2601 _pthread_cond_wait  (in libsystem_pthread.dylib) + 980  [0x19eb551b4]
+           2601 __psynch_cvwait  (in libsystem_kernel.dylib) + 8  [0x19eb1350c]
```

(Threads `12128793`, `12128794` and `12128795` are the same.)

#### What the unnamed frames are

`atos` names the two unnamed offsets `_uv_barrier_destroy +0x11c` and `_uv_cancel +0x304`, but those are only the nearest exported symbols. Disassembly of the runtime binary (same `LC_UUID` as the live image) shows:

| Frame | Real location |
|---|---|
| `DefaultProcessExitHandlerInternal + 68` | Return address of `bl _uv_library_shutdown` (`uv_library_shutdown` ends with a tail call, so it has no frame) |
| `+ 0x103ac34` | Inside `uv__threadpool_cleanup`: return address of `bl _uv_thread_join` in the `for (i = 0; i < nthreads; i++)` join loop |
| `+ 0x103b4a4` | Inside libuv's `worker()`: return address of `bl _uv_cond_wait`, in the idle wait between `idle_threads += 1` and `idle_threads -= 1` |

The code just before the join loop locks the threadpool mutex, queues `exit_message`, calls `uv_cond_signal` if `idle_threads != 0`, and unlocks. So the main thread posted the exit message and then blocked joining a worker, and no worker woke up. This matches libuv 1.52.1 `src/threadpool.c` (`uv__threadpool_cleanup`, `post`, `worker`) and Node v24.22.1 `src/api/environment.cc` (`DefaultProcessExitHandlerInternal`).

#### The watchdog that called `process.exit`

`preloads/extension_bootstrap.mjs`, lines 27-38:

```js
const parentWatch = setInterval(() => {
    try {
        if (process.ppid !== parentPid) {
            process.exit(0);
        }
        if (!sandboxed) {
            process.kill(parentPid, 0);
        }
    } catch {
        process.exit(0);
    }
}, 1000);
```

The sample shows a timer callback (`RunTimers` → JS) calling `Environment::Exit`. The JS frames have no names, so the sample alone can't name the timer. This watchdog is the only timer I found that calls `process.exit`; the extension's own code has no `process.exit`, `reallyExit` or `abort`.

#### App log at quit (`github-app.<pid>.log`, owning app pid 72566)

```
2026-11-18T13:12:13.727933Z  INFO ... github_copilot_sdk: copilot CLI client ready pid=Some(75796)
2026-11-19T09:19:22.541748Z  INFO github_app::session::manager::process_teardown: terminated agent processes owned by ending sessions scope="app_exit" session_count=23 runtime_outcome="parallel" runtime_cancelled=0 verified=0 already_gone=700 unverified=4 force_killed=0 survivors=0
2026-11-19T09:19:22.633731Z  INFO github_copilot_sdk: force-stopping CLI process pid=Some(75796)
```

No line in that log mentions pid 80226. The app does not seem to log extension hosts by pid.

#### System log at quit (UTC)

```
2026-11-19 09:19:22.630 Df analyticsd[495:f3e317] [com.apple.xpc:connection] [0x7865268a00] invalidated because the client process (pid 75796) either cancelled the connection or exited
2026-11-19 09:19:23.234 I  loginwindow[439:f3eba4] [com.apple.launchservices:quitsupport] applicationDeath: app=0x0-0x13d63d5 "GitHub Copilot", has non-application coalition pids [ ... 80218/copilot, 80219/copilot, 80221/copilot, 80224/copilot, 80225/copilot, 80226/copilot, ... ], so this application stays in the running list.
```

That list has 64 pids. When I checked afterwards, 80226 was the only one still alive.

#### Other details

- `lsof` on pid 80226: `TCP localhost:7927 (LISTEN)` plus three accepted sockets in state `CLOSED`. No database files open.
- `lldb process attach --pid 80226` is refused ("Not allowed to attach to process"). The binary uses the hardened runtime without `get-task-allow`, so I could not read the threadpool state or take a core dump.
- `PSYNCH` kernel messages: none found, but the unified log has no kernel lines for that time window at all, so this proves nothing.

#### Analysis and confidence

- **Certain (high confidence):** the host called `process.exit(0)` after its parent was force-stopped. Node ran `uv_library_shutdown`. `uv__threadpool_cleanup` posted the exit message and is blocked joining a pool thread, while all four pool threads are still parked in the idle `uv_cond_wait`. The event loop is gone, so the socket stays open and nothing answers on it.
- **Not caused by the extension's code (high confidence).** The dashboard extension is where it showed up because it binds a fixed port.
- **Why the workers never woke: unproven.** I read libuv's `post` and `worker` code and the compiled loop and could not find a lost-wakeup window in libuv itself: the insert and signal happen under the mutex, and a worker tests the queue under the mutex before it waits. That leaves two candidates:
  1. A wakeup lost below libuv: `pthread_cond_signal` did not wake a blocked waiter (libpthread or the kernel's psynch code). My estimate: about 60%.
  2. Corrupted threadpool state: `idle_threads` was 0 although four threads were waiting, or `wq`, `cond` or `mutex` were damaged. My estimate: about 25%.
  Telling these apart needs the values of `idle_threads`, `wq` and `exit_message` from a debugger.
- An unrelated project reports the same stack on macOS with Node 22 and 24, also unsolved: [mhismail3/tron#729](https://github.com/mhismail3/tron/issues/729) and [mhismail3/tron#1120](https://github.com/mhismail3/tron/issues/1120). libuv also already works around an older Apple condition-variable bug (libuv/libuv#4165), so that layer has had defects before; that does not prove the same cause here.
- Possibly related, different trigger: github/copilot-cli#4468 (`--server --stdio` never releases extension-host processes).

#### Asks

1. **Runtime / Node shutdown hang.** Please look into the `process.exit` hang in `uv__threadpool_cleanup` on macOS in the embedded Node v24.22.1 / libuv 1.52.1. Whatever its root cause, the watchdog's last resort is `process.exit`, which runs Node's full teardown with no time limit, and a JS timer can't recover once the main thread blocks. When the parent is gone, the host could end without Node's teardown (for example a self-`SIGKILL`, or a native exit with a deadline).
2. **App robustness on quit.** The app should make sure extension hosts are actually dead on quit, not only their parent CLI: for example send `SIGKILL` after a grace period, or kill the whole process group, and then verify. Today the app logs `survivors=0` while an extension host it started is still alive, so a hung exit leaves an orphan holding ports and other resources.

If it helps, the unslid addresses of libuv's threadpool statics in this build are: `nthreads` `0x10590e5c0`, `idle_threads` `0x10590e5c4`, `slow_io_work_running` `0x10590e5c8`, `threads` `0x10590e5d0`, `exit_message` `0x10590e5d8`, `wq` `0x10590e608`, `cond` `0x10590e638`, `mutex` `0x10590e668` (add `0x20e4000` for this process). With a debuggable build, `idle_threads == 4` with `exit_message` in `wq` would point to a lost wakeup; `idle_threads == 0` would point to corrupted state.

#### Workaround

`kill -9 <pid>` of the orphaned host. A plain `kill` (SIGTERM) is unlikely to work: the extension installs a `SIGTERM` listener, so the signal goes to libuv's handler, which only queues it for an event loop that no longer runs. (Not tested.)

#### Attachments

All files are in this gist: https://gist.github.com/ncksol/8a29f1eda274b13daa142cf566dfa82a

Paths are redacted (home directory replaced with `~`, project path with `~/<project-worktree>`).

- `01-sample-pid80226-0926Z.txt`: full `sample` output at 09:26:27 UTC
- `02-sample-pid80226-0938Z.txt`: full `sample` output at 09:38:11 UTC (same call graph)
- `03-disasm-exit-path.txt`: disassembly of `DefaultProcessExitHandlerInternal`, `uv_library_shutdown`, `uv__threadpool_cleanup` and `worker`
- `04-symbols.txt`: `atos`-style names for the unnamed frames (nearest exported symbol only)
- `05-lsof-pid80226.txt`: open files and sockets of the hung host
- `06-lldb-attach-refused.txt`: the refused debugger attach
- `07-app-log-quit.txt`: app log lines at the quit
- `08-app-log-next-launch-canvas-error.txt`: the canvas open failure on the next launch
- `09-system-log-quit.txt`: `analyticsd` and `loginwindow` lines at the quit, including the full coalition pid list
- `10-extension_bootstrap-excerpt.mjs`: `extension_bootstrap.mjs` lines 1-38
- `11-ps-pid80226.txt`: `ps` status of the host about 37 minutes after the quit

issues.title: Gemini 4 Neon and Hydrogen: Usage records report medium for xhigh task requests

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Copilot CLI 1.0.114 lists `gemini-4-neon` and `gemini-4-hydrogen` under `xhigh` in its `task` tool schema (`reasoning_effort` extras). However, two observations show `xhigh` unavailable or reported as `medium`:

- In the `/model` picker's interactive reasoning-effort switcher for `gemini-4-neon`, `high` is the highest available option (`xhigh` is absent).
- In four synchronous `explore` sub-agent runs (one `xhigh` request and one `high` control per model), three relevant records from each `xhigh` run's event chain reported different `reasoningEffort` values: `"reasoningEffort": "medium"` in `subagent.configured`, `"reasoningEffort": "xhigh"` in `session.model_change`, and `"reasoningEffort": "medium"` in `session.usage_record`. Neither `xhigh` run logged a warning event. In both `high` control runs, all three records reported `"reasoningEffort": "high"`.

Google documents an `xhigh` thinking level for these models (labeled `Extra` in the Antigravity model selector): the [Gemini 4 Neon announcement](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-neon/), the [Gemini 4 Hydrogen announcement](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-hydrogen/), and the [Antigravity model documentation](https://antigravity.google/docs/models/).

Related issue: #3823 reports a silent downgrade from `xhigh` to `medium` for models not advertising `xhigh` in CAPI capabilities. Here, `gemini-4-neon` and `gemini-4-hydrogen` appear under `xhigh` in the CLI's own `task` tool schema. These records do not establish whether CAPI advertises `xhigh` for either model or which effort Copilot sent to the provider.

### Affected version

`GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.114`

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Interactive picker check: In Copilot CLI 1.0.114, open `/model` and highlight `gemini-4-neon`, then step through its reasoning-effort levels with the left and right arrow keys. A separate interactive check for `gemini-4-neon` showed `high` as the highest available option in the picker, and `xhigh` was absent.
2. Sub-agent check: In a Copilot CLI 1.0.114 session already running `gemini-4-neon` at `long_context` (the recorded parent session state; fresh-launch setup for `long_context` was not separately verified), prompt Copilot to dispatch four synchronous `explore` sub-agents via the `task` tool (asking each to reply with `OK` without calling tools), giving each a distinct `name` and omitting `context_tier` on both `gemini-4-hydrogen` calls:
   - `name: "probe-neon-xhigh"`, `model: "gemini-4-neon"`, `reasoning_effort: "xhigh"`, `context_tier: "long_context"`
   - `name: "probe-neon-high"`, `model: "gemini-4-neon"`, `reasoning_effort: "high"`, `context_tier: "long_context"`
   - `name: "probe-hydrogen-xhigh"`, `model: "gemini-4-hydrogen"`, `reasoning_effort: "xhigh"` (omit `context_tier`; inherited `long_context` from the parent session)
   - `name: "probe-hydrogen-high"`, `model: "gemini-4-hydrogen"`, `reasoning_effort: "high"` (omit `context_tier`; inherited `long_context` from the parent session)
3. Obtain the session ID with `/session id` and open `~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/events.jsonl` (under `$COPILOT_HOME` when set). Use `agentId` to link each run's `subagent.started` event to three records: `subagent.configured`, `session.model_change`, and `session.usage_record`. Confirm `"contextTier": "long_context"` in each `subagent.configured` record before comparing results.

Observed field excerpts from the four runs:

```text
probe-neon-xhigh (gemini-4-neon, requested xhigh):
  subagent.configured:  {"model": "gemini-4-neon", "reasoningEffort": "medium", "contextTier": "long_context"}
  session.model_change: {"source": "agent", "contextTier": "long_context", "newModel": "gemini-4-neon", "reasoningEffort": "xhigh"}
  session.usage_record: {"model": "gemini-4-neon", "responseModel": "gemini-4-neon", "initiator": "sub-agent", "reasoningEffort": "medium", "maxPromptTokens": 983040}

probe-neon-high (gemini-4-neon, requested high):
  subagent.configured:  {"model": "gemini-4-neon", "reasoningEffort": "high", "contextTier": "long_context"}
  session.model_change: {"source": "agent", "contextTier": "long_context", "newModel": "gemini-4-neon", "reasoningEffort": "high"}
  session.usage_record: {"model": "gemini-4-neon", "responseModel": "gemini-4-neon", "initiator": "sub-agent", "reasoningEffort": "high", "maxPromptTokens": 983040}

probe-hydrogen-xhigh (gemini-4-hydrogen, requested xhigh):
  subagent.configured:  {"model": "gemini-4-hydrogen", "reasoningEffort": "medium", "contextTier": "long_context"}
  session.model_change: {"source": "agent", "contextTier": "long_context", "newModel": "gemini-4-hydrogen", "reasoningEffort": "xhigh"}
  session.usage_record: {"model": "gemini-4-hydrogen", "responseModel": "gemini-4-hydrogen", "initiator": "sub-agent", "reasoningEffort": "medium", "maxPromptTokens": 983040}

probe-hydrogen-high (gemini-4-hydrogen, requested high):
  subagent.configured:  {"model": "gemini-4-hydrogen", "reasoningEffort": "high", "contextTier": "long_context"}
  session.model_change: {"source": "agent", "contextTier": "long_context", "newModel": "gemini-4-hydrogen", "reasoningEffort": "high"}
  session.usage_record: {"model": "gemini-4-hydrogen", "responseModel": "gemini-4-hydrogen", "initiator": "sub-agent", "reasoningEffort": "high", "maxPromptTokens": 983040}
```

### Expected behavior

For `gemini-4-neon`, if Copilot CLI supports interactive `xhigh`, the `/model` picker's interactive reasoning-effort switcher should offer `xhigh`.

For each model (`gemini-4-neon` and `gemini-4-hydrogen`), if `task` supports `xhigh`, Copilot CLI should honor and record it across three points: request `xhigh` from the provider, log `"reasoningEffort": "xhigh"` in `subagent.configured`, and report `"reasoningEffort": "xhigh"` in `session.usage_record` when the provider applies that level.

If `task` does not support `xhigh` for a model, the `task` tool schema should omit that model from `xhigh`. In that case, Copilot CLI should reject the request or warn the caller.

### Additional context

- Operating system: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.6 (Linux 5.14.0-570.19.1.el9_6.x86_64)
- CPU architecture: x86_64
- Verbatim `task` tool `reasoning_effort` extras on 1.0.114: `xhigh='claude-fable-5','claude-fable-5.1','claude-fable-5.2','claude-haiku-5.5','claude-opus-4.8-fast','claude-opus-5.5','claude-sonnet-5','claude-sonnet-5.5','gemini-4-hydrogen','gemini-4-neon','gpt-5.3-codex','gpt-5.6-luna','gpt-5.6-sol','gpt-6-astra','gpt-6-luna','gpt-6-sol','gpt-6.1-sol','gpt-6.1-terra','gpt-6.2-astra','gpt-6.2-sol','grok-4.6','grok-4.7','mai-code-2','mai-code-2-flash'`

issues.title: Remote MCP (OAuth): expired access token forces interactive re-auth instead of silent refresh_token grant

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
## Summary

When a remote OAuth-protected MCP server's cached **access token** is expired at session start, the Copilot CLI treats the server as needing a fresh **interactive** OAuth login and drops its tools — even though a valid **refresh token** is cached. It never attempts an [RFC 6749 §6](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6749#section-6) `refresh_token` grant. In non-interactive/automation sessions the interactive flow can't complete, so the server's tools silently never load.

## Environment

- GitHub Copilot CLI `1.0.71`, running inside VS Code
- macOS (Darwin); credential store = Apple Keychain (`copilot-mcp-oauth`)
- MCP transport: `rmcp` streamable HTTP (`rmcp::transport::worker` / `::streamable`), `reqwest 0.13.4`

## Configuration

- Remote HTTP MCP server in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`:
  ```json
  "notion": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.notion.com/mcp" }
  ```
- Cached grant in Keychain (`service copilot-mcp-oauth`, account `<hash>`) and `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/<hash>.tokens.json` — contains `accessToken`, `expiresAt`, `refreshToken`.
- Server authorization-server metadata ([RFC 8414](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8414)) advertises refresh support:
  `token_endpoint: https://mcp.notion.com/token`, `grant_types_supported: ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"]`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Authenticate a remote OAuth MCP server (e.g. Notion) so a valid access+refresh grant is cached.
2. Let the **access** token expire while the **refresh** token stays valid (Notion access tokens last ~8h — e.g. leave it overnight).
3. Start a new Copilot CLI session (especially a non-interactive/scheduled one).
4. Observe: the server's tools are absent from the session.

## Observed behavior

From `~/.copilot/logs/process-<...>.log` (redacted):

```
[ERROR] Starting remote MCP client for notion with url: https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
[ERROR] Connecting MCP client for notion...
        -> connects to mcp.notion.com:443 using the cached (expired) access token
[ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed,
        when Client(OAuthChallenge { www_authenticate_header:
        "...OAuth, resource_metadata=\".../.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp\",
        error=\"invalid_token\", error_description=\"Mis...\"" })
[ERROR] Server notion requires authentication, initiating OAuth flow
[ERROR] OAuth authentication required for notion
```

The runtime then reads the cached OAuth entry from Keychain but still ends at **"OAuth authentication required."**

### Evidence that no refresh was attempted

Grep of the entire session-start process log:

```
POSTs to mcp.notion.com/token : 0
```

Zero `refresh_token` grants were sent, despite a valid refresh token being cached.

## Expected behavior

On a `401` / `WWW-Authenticate: … error="invalid_token"` for a server that has a cached refresh token:

1. Silently POST `grant_type=refresh_token` (+ `client_id`) to the discovered `token_endpoint`.
2. Persist the rotated access/refresh tokens.
3. Reconnect and load the server's tools.
4. Only fall back to the interactive OAuth flow if the refresh itself fails (`invalid_grant`, expired/revoked).

## Impact

- Any remote OAuth MCP server silently loses its tools once the access token expires, until a manual re-auth — even though the refresh token is valid and the whole point of storing it is to avoid exactly this.
- Breaks unattended/scheduled sessions (e.g. a daily automation), where the interactive prompt can never be completed.

## Likely root cause / where to look

- The `rmcp` streamable transport surfaces the OAuth challenge as a **fatal** transport error ("worker quit with fatal … `OAuthChallenge`"), and the CLI's handler maps "auth required" directly to the interactive flow without first attempting a token refresh.
- Secondary: the session's tool list appears to be snapshotted at startup, so even a later successful (re)auth doesn't surface the tools into an already-running session.

## Suggested fix

- Insert a refresh step in the auth-challenge path: if a `refresh_token` is cached for the server, perform the refresh grant against the discovered `token_endpoint`, persist rotated tokens, and reconnect **before** considering interactive auth.
- Optionally refresh **proactively** when `expiresAt` is at/near expiry before the first connect.
- Consider re-syncing tools into active sessions after a late auth success.

## Workaround

- Manually perform the `refresh_token` grant against the `token_endpoint`, write the rotated tokens back into the cache; or re-run the CLI's interactive auth for the server before starting the session.

---

cc @connor4312 (VS Code team)

<sub>Filed with assistance from GitHub Copilot CLI.</sub>

issues.title: Allow /fork to open a new terminal and add copilot --fork

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

The interactive /fork command moves the current terminal into the fork, and Copilot CLI has no startup option for creating a fork from an existing session. This makes parallel terminal workflows unnecessarily manual.

### Proposed solution

Support both of these entry points:

1. Add `copilot --fork=<session-id> --name=<new-session-name>`. It should create a new fork of the supplied session, apply the optional name to the new fork, and start the fork in the process that invoked the command. The source session name should remain unchanged.
2. Add an option such as `/fork --new-terminal [name]`. It should create the fork in a new terminal window or tab while the current terminal remains in the original session.

The command line option provides a portable building block when automatic terminal launching is unavailable. Users can combine it with their preferred terminal application.

If `/fork --new-terminal` cannot identify or launch the current terminal application, it should return the new session ID and a ready-to-run `copilot --resume=<new-session-id>` command instead of silently changing behavior.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. Run `/fork --new-terminal investigate-auth` during a task. The fork opens separately, and the original session remains visible and interactive.
2. Run `wt new-tab copilot --fork=<session-id> --name=investigate-auth` to create and name a fork in a new Windows Terminal tab.
3. Run `copilot --fork=<session-id> --name=alternative-design` from another shell to create, name, and enter a fork of a specific session.
4. Run `!wt new-tab copilot --fork=<session-id> --name=side-investigation` inside Copilot CLI to launch the fork without abandoning the current session.

### Additional context

This replaces #4578, which was submitted without the Feature Request form.

This is a focused follow-up to #2058. That issue requested the core `/fork` command and mentioned a new terminal window or tab in its proposed solution. The core command now exists, but terminal selection and process startup interfaces are still missing.

Related issue #1697 also describes working with forked sessions in separate terminals.

Confirmed with GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.81-8: both `copilot --fork=<session-id>` and `copilot --branch=<session-id>` are rejected as unknown options.

issues.title: store_memory offers user scope when user-level memory is unavailable; every user-scoped store fails with 404

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`store_memory` offers `scope: "user"` even when user-level preferences are not available for my account. Every user-scoped store then fails with HTTP 404, while repository-scoped stores work. The only client-side switch, `/memory off`, turns off both scopes, so I can't keep repository memory and turn off only the user scope that fails.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.113; also the runtime embedded in the VS Code 1.146.0 agent host (1.0.108-0)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Use an account where user-level Copilot Memory preferences are not available, and work in a repository where repository memory is.
2. Start a session with memory enabled (VS Code agent host, or `copilot --enable-memory`).
3. Note that the `store_memory` tool's `scope` parameter allows `["repository","user"]`; `copilot -p "..." --enable-memory` reports the same.
4. Have the agent store a personal preference, so it calls `store_memory` with `scope: "user"`. It fails within about a second:
   > Unable to store memory: the memory endpoint was not found. User-scoped memories may not be enabled.

   Tool telemetry: `operation=storeMemory`, `source=service_api`, `scope=user`, `httpStatus=404`.
5. With the same account and host, `store_memory` with `scope: "repository"` succeeds (HTTP 201), and repository memories load into the prompt normally.

### Expected behavior

When user-level preferences are not available, the runtime should:

- Leave `user` out of `store_memory`'s `scope` values and out of the memory guidance in the system prompt. It already does this for repository scope when there is no repository context ("Memory storage correctly limits available scopes when no repository context is present").
- Show user scope as unavailable in `/memory show`, as 1.0.107 does for repository scope.

Separately, it would help to be able to turn off only one scope (for example user scope) in `/memory` or `/settings`, rather than all memory with `/memory off`.

### Additional context

- macOS 27.0.1, arm64.
- The client can't tell me why user scope is unavailable (my personal scope choice, my plan, or organization policy); it only infers "may not be enabled" from the 404.
- Workaround: a personal custom instruction telling agents not to call `store_memory` with user scope. This relies on the model following it.
