issues.title: Pasted PDF is counted at its encoded size in the context estimate and triggers an unnecessary compaction (620k estimated vs 31k real)

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Pasting a PDF into the prompt triggers an immediate automatic compaction because the context estimate counts the PDF at roughly its encoded file size, not what it costs the model. A 1.9 MB PDF added ~620k to the estimate but ~31k real input tokens.

Similar to #2936 (images), closed in April; this is the PDF/document case.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.114-0

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start a session on `gpt-6.2-astra` with the `long_context` tier (tokenLimit 922000).
2. Work until the context is ~200k (estimate `conversationTokens` ~202k).
3. Paste a 1.9 MB PDF into the prompt (attachment type `file`) and submit.
4. `session.compaction_start` fires 10 ms after `user.message`:
   `trigger "threshold"`, `currentTokens 845092`, `conversationTokens 821857`, `tokenLimit 922000`.
5. Compaction is applied: 276 of 283 messages removed, ~41k tokens left.
6. `session.usage_record` for the call carrying the PDF: `inputTokens 234816` (previous call `204065`), so the PDF cost ~31k real tokens.

### Expected behavior

The compaction threshold uses the attachment's model token cost (~31k here), not an estimate from the raw or base64 file size. No compaction at ~235k of 922k.

### Additional context

- macOS (Darwin), arm64, zsh; terminal: xterm.js inside tmux
- The ~620k estimate ≈ the base64 size of the file (1.9 MB × 4/3 ÷ 4 chars per token)
- Evidence is in the session's `events.jsonl`: `user.message`, `session.compaction_start`, `session.compaction_complete`, `session.usage_record`

issues.title: Linux/WSL: Entra MCP browser sign-in stalls silently when `xdg-open` is missing, and `/mcp` Authenticate shows a URL that fails with "State mismatch"

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

This issue was split out of #4017 at a maintainer's request. It isn't #5250 either: there's no OS broker here, and the CLI logs `Entra broker not eligible; using the browser OAuth flow {"broker_available":false}`.

I retested on **CLI 1.0.114** on WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 with an Entra-protected remote HTTP MCP server (the Azure DevOps remote MCP, `https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>`) and no stored token. The browser flow itself now works. When a browser opens, Entra SSO completes, the loopback callback reaches the CLI, and the CLI logs `MCP OAuth tokens saved`. The token falls back to file storage under `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/` because there's no Secret Service, and a restart reuses it. Device code (Ctrl+G) now shows a code. Each flow uses a per-flow random loopback port, so the "fixed callback port" I described in #4017 doesn't apply on 1.0.114.

Two problems remain, plus one on the app side.

**1. When `xdg-open` is missing, sign-in stalls with no URL and no visible error**

A stock WSL Ubuntu install has no `xdg-utils`, though `wslview` is installed. The launch fails, and the failure is logged only at DEBUG:

```
[DEBUG] [rust:mcp_client::oauth_flow] Entra broker not eligible; using the browser OAuth flow {"server_url":"https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>","broker_available":false,"force_device_code":false}
[ERROR] Opening browser for ado-direct authentication...
[DEBUG] [rust:mcp_client::oauth_flow] failed to open OAuth browser {"error":"Spawn { command: \"xdg-open\", source: Os { code: 13, kind: PermissionDenied, message: \"Permission denied\" } }"}
[ERROR] Requesting access token for ado-direct...
```

The `PermissionDenied` error is misleading because no `xdg-open` exists on `PATH`. I suspect `execvp` returns EACCES from a Windows-interop `PATH` entry. The CLI doesn't print the authorize URL or fall back to `$BROWSER` or `wslview`. The user sees only:

```
! MCP server 'ado-direct' is taking longer than expected to connect.
! Gave up waiting for MCP server to finish starting: ado-direct. Startup continued without it; it may still connect.
```

After that, the CLI contacts `login.microsoftonline.com` about every 6 s indefinitely, and the server stays `pending`.

**2. `/mcp` → server → Authenticate shows a URL whose callback is rejected**

While the startup flow is pending, choosing **Authenticate** shows:

```
A browser authorization is already in progress for this server. Open the URL below to complete it.
If your browser didn't open, copy this URL manually: https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/oauth2/v2.0/authorize?...
```

The displayed URL is identical to the startup flow's URL, including `state` and `nonce`. But the action also starts a new flow: `session.mcp.oauth.prepareFlow` runs again. When I complete the displayed URL in the browser, Entra and the `vscode.dev/redirect` hop succeed, and the loopback callback reaches the CLI. The CLI then rejects it:

- With a working browser opener: the callback page shows **"Authorization Failed — State mismatch - possible CSRF attack"**.
- After the `xdg-open` failure in (1): the callback returns **HTTP 404 Not Found**. Replaying the same callback URL from inside WSL with `curl` also returns 404, which rules out WSL localhost forwarding. Nothing is logged.

If I skip Authenticate and open the startup URL directly, sign-in succeeds, even about 70 s after startup "gave up waiting". So the only URL the UI ever shows is one that can't complete. Without a working `xdg-open`, the user has no way to sign in from the UI. That matches my original #4017 symptom: the browser reports success, but no token is stored.

**3. App sessions on a WSL host have no sign-in path**

In GitHub Copilot app 1.4.2 (Windows) with sessions on a WSL host, the host was still running bundled CLI **1.0.104-0** (`copilotd` 1.0.5) and didn't update to 1.0.114. A new session lists the server's tool names, which may come from the tool snapshot cache. Every call fails:

```
MCP server 'ado-direct': MCP server "ado-direct" requires authentication. Sign in through your MCP client's authentication settings.
```

No browser opens on Windows, and I found no sign-in action for the server in the app. The Windows app log shows only `session/mcpServerStateChanged` actions with `translated_event_count=0` and no auth-related action. If this is already fixed in a newer host, please say which `copilotd` or CLI version to wait for.

### Expected behavior

- If launching the browser fails, show the authorize URL in the session immediately, log the failure at WARNING, and fall back to `$BROWSER` or `wslview` on WSL.
- When Authenticate runs while a flow is pending, either keep the pending flow's `state`/`nonce` valid or display the new flow's URL. Never show a URL the callback will reject.
- App sessions on Linux/WSL remote hosts should surface MCP OAuth-required in the app with a Sign in action that completes the flow. Opening the Windows browser works: WSL localhost forwarding delivers the callback to the host process.

### Affected version

- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.114 (linux-x64 release tarball, `--no-auto-update`)
- GitHub Copilot app 1.4.2 (Windows), with its WSL host serving sessions using bundled CLI 1.0.104-0

### Environment

- Windows 11 + WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04.5, kernel 6.18 (microsoft-standard-WSL2)
- No `xdg-open` (`xdg-utils` not installed); `wslview` present; `BROWSER` unset
- No Secret Service (`org.freedesktop.secrets`), so MCP tokens fall back to `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/`
- Server: Azure DevOps remote MCP, `type: http`, no `oauthClientId`

### Steps to reproduce

1. On WSL Ubuntu without `xdg-utils`, with no stored MCP token, run:
   `copilot --log-level debug --additional-mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{"ado-direct":{"type":"http","url":"https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>","tools":["*"]}}}'`
2. Observe "taking longer than expected" and no URL. The log shows the `xdg-open` spawn failure.
3. Open `/mcp` → `ado-direct` → **Authenticate**. Copy the displayed URL into a Windows browser and complete sign-in.
4. The callback returns 404 (or "State mismatch" if an opener exists), and the server stays unauthenticated.
5. Control: put an `xdg-open` shim on `PATH` that hands the URL to the Windows browser, and restart without clicking Authenticate. Sign-in completes and the server connects.

**Workaround:** install `xdg-utils`, or put an `xdg-open` shim on `PATH` that calls `wslview`, and don't click Authenticate while the startup flow is pending. That fixes the standalone CLI only. For app sessions on a WSL host, I still use a local stdio proxy that adds a bearer token from `az account get-access-token`.


(These details we created using GHCP attempting to repro another bug/fix.)

issues.title: MCP OAuth (interactive): authorization code is received and the success page is served, but the code->token exchange never runs — server stuck "Connecting"

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

For a remote HTTP MCP server using Entra ID OAuth (Azure DevOps remote MCP,
`https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>`), the interactive CLI completes the browser
round-trip but never exchanges the authorization code for a token.

Observed with Copilot CLI running **inside WSL2** (Ubuntu 26.04 on a Windows 11
host). I have not tested native Windows or native Linux, so I cannot say whether
this is WSL-specific — see the note at the end.

Observed sequence:

1. On startup the CLI auto-connects, gets the expected `401` with
   `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.dev.azure.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/<org>"`.
2. Metadata discovery and dynamic client registration succeed — a registration
   record is written to `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/<key>.json`, with
   `authorizationServerUrl`, `clientId: aebc6443-996d-45c2-90f0-388ff96faa56`,
   `redirectUri: http://127.0.0.1:41003/`.
3. The CLI logs `Opening browser for <server> authentication...` then
   `Requesting access token for <server>...`.
4. I complete the sign-in. The browser lands on
   `http://127.0.0.1:41003/?nonce=<nonce>&code=<code>` and **the CLI's own
   callback page renders** ("Authorization Successful"). So the code reaches
   the CLI's listener.
5. Nothing further happens. The TUI stays on "Authenticating: <server>" /
   "Connecting to <server>...". No `<key>.tokens.json` is ever written, and no
   log line is emitted after this point.

The `<key>.verifier` file is **not** removed. Per the runtime's own state
machine (`MCP OAuth token exchange completed; saving tokens` ->
`MCP OAuth tokens saved; clearing code verifier`), a surviving verifier means
the exchange never completed successfully.

The MCP transport worker meanwhile keeps cycling:

```
[ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed,
  when Client(OAuthChallenge { www_authenticate_header: "...oauth-protected-resource/<org>",
  response: McpOAuthHttpResponse { status_code: 401, ... } })
```

### The failure is in the CLI, not the environment

I reproduced the identical flow manually with a small script — **same client ID,
same scope, same `vscode.dev` relay, same loopback pattern** — and it succeeds
on the first attempt:

```
TOKEN EXCHANGE: HTTP 200 SUCCESS
  scope        : https://mcp.dev.azure.com/Ado.Mcp.Tools https://mcp.dev.azure.com/.default
  token_type   : Bearer
  expires_in   : 4102
  refresh_token: present
```

Driving the MCP server with that token also works:

```
[initialize] HTTP 200   serverInfo: {"name": "AzureDevOps.Mcp", "version": "1.0.0.0"}
[tools/list] HTTP 200   tool count: 43
```

Writing that token into `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/<key>.tokens.json` in the
CLI's own schema (`accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `expiresAt`, `requestedScope`,
`scope`) makes the server connect normally. `grant_type=refresh_token` renewal
against the same endpoint also works.

So tenant config, consent, scopes, app registration, the `vscode.dev` relay,
loopback reachability and the MCP server are all confirmed working. The only
step that fails is the CLI's own code->token exchange.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`:
   ```json
   {"mcpServers":{"ado-remote-mcp":{"type":"http","url":"https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>"}}}
   ```
2. Start `copilot`. It auto-connects and begins the OAuth flow.
3. Run `/mcp auth ado-remote-mcp`, press `c`, open the URL, complete sign-in.
4. Browser shows the CLI's "Authorization Successful" page.
5. `ls ~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/` — no `.tokens.json`; the `.verifier`
   remains. The TUI never leaves the connecting state.

### Expected behavior

After the callback is received, the CLI proceeds to `exchanging_code`, stores
the tokens, clears the verifier, and connects the server.

### Additional context

- **No diagnostics are available for this step.** `RUST_LOG` is accepted but
  produces no additional output, and the process log contains nothing at all
  between the callback and the stall. The runtime has specific failure strings
  (`ExchangeResponseFailure`, `failed to clear OAuth code verifier after
  authorization failure`) but none reach the log file. Surfacing the token
  endpoint's response on failure would make this self-diagnosable.
- `ctrl+g` (device code) does not help: `mcp.dev.azure.com` advertises no
  device-code support, so the CLI logs `Server does not support device code
  flow - falling back to browser` and retries the browser path.
- The callback arrives as `?nonce=<nonce>&code=<code>` with **no `state`
  parameter** — `vscode.dev/redirect` consumes `state` (the CLI encodes the
  nonce in the state fragment). If the handler validates `state`, that may be
  relevant. Unverified.
- Possibly related: #4994, #5192, #4695 — all ACP-mode or cross-session reuse.
  This one is plain interactive mode on first sign-in.
- **Environment caveat (WSL2).** This was only observed with the CLI running
  inside WSL2; I have not reproduced it on native Windows or native Linux, so I
  cannot confirm whether the platform matters. Two WSL-specific points, both
  ruled out as causes:
  - WSL has no browser launcher by default (`xdg-open`/`wslview` absent), so the
    CLI's `Opening browser...` step is a silent no-op until `BROWSER` is set.
    That produces a *separate* earlier symptom (no prompt at all). After adding a
    launcher the browser opens correctly, and the stall described above persists.
  - Windows→WSL loopback forwarding works. An independent listener inside WSL
    received the browser's redirect on `127.0.0.1` (including the follow-up
    `favicon.ico` request), so the callback path itself is sound.

issues.title: MCP OAuth (Copilot Desktop app): non-first-party HTTP servers cancel host-token then never launch the "runtime browser flow" they deferred to — no auth, no error, no popup

labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

labels.name: area:mcp

issues.body:
Describe the bug
In the GitHub Copilot Desktop app, remote MCP servers configured with "type": "http" that are non-first-party (e.g. Atlassian, incident.io) fail to authenticate. Toggling the server off/on in Settings produces no browser popup and no visible error — the server simply never connects.

Affected version
Desktop app shell: v1.0.15 (latest, confirmed via in-app update check)
Bundled Copilot CLI engine: v1.0.69-0 (AppData\Local\github-copilot-sdk\cli\1.0.69-0\copilot.exe)

Steps to reproduce
Add a non-first-party remote MCP server with "type": "http" and a url in mcp-config.json (e.g. https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2)
Enable it via Settings → MCP servers in the Desktop app
Toggle it off, then on again
Observe: no browser window ever opens; the server stays disconnected with no user-facing error

Expected behavior
A browser window should open for OAuth consent, as it does for the raw copilot CLI and for local-type servers wrapped in npx mcp-remote.

Actual behavior
~/.copilot/logs/github-app.<pid>.log shows this single log line and nothing further:

github_app::session::manager::mcp_status: MCP OAuth non-first-party server; cancelling host-token so runtime browser flow runs server_name=<server>
```

This line repeats on every toggle attempt (confirmed 43 occurrences across multiple sessions for both atlassian and incident.io), but there is no subsequent log entry anywhere indicating the "runtime browser flow" it defers to is ever actually invoked — no browser-launch attempt, no OAuth URL, no error surfaced to the user.

## Root cause hypothesis
This behavior appears tied to the MCP host token-injection OAuth rework shipped in copilot-cli v1.0.66 (2026-06-30 changelog entry: "Added runtime telemetry for the MCP host token-injection OAuth flow, recording when an OAuth broadcast is emitted to the host and how the host responds (token or cancelled)"). For non-first-party servers, the host correctly identifies it should defer to a client-side browser flow and cancels its own token injection — but that deferred browser flow is never triggered inside the Desktop app shell.

## Workaround
Reconfiguring the server as a local type wrapping npx mcp-remote bypasses the broken Desktop-app host/browser-flow handoff entirely, since mcp-remote runs its own independent OAuth implementation:

```json
"atlassian": {
  "type": "local",
  "command": "npx",
  "args": ["--yes", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp"]
}
```

This works reliably. Native "type": "http" does not, for any non-first-party server, in the Desktop app.

## Additional context
Possibly related to #2536, but distinct: that issue is about the raw copilot CLI's "Opening browser for X authentication..." log line firing and a browser genuinely opening, just re-registering (DCR) on every launch. In this Desktop-app case, the browser-flow deferral log line fires but no browser-launch attempt is ever logged afterward — a different failure point entirely (host→client handoff, not CLI OAuth caching).

issues.title: Bad default: engine falls back to 128K token budget for model

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

labels.name: area:models
labels.description: Model selection, availability, switching, rate limits, and model-specific behavior

issues.body:
## Summary

When a routed model has no capability limits installed (or reports a zero context window), the agent engine silently falls back to a hardcoded **128,000**-token prompt budget and drives context compaction against it. For large-context models (e.g. 1M-token Anthropic models) whose ids don't match a host-provided capabilities entry, this makes compaction fire ~8x too early (at ~102K tokens instead of ~800K+), causing avoidable summarization churn, latency, token cost, and quality loss.

We hit this integrating the SDK/engine into a host app. We can work around it host-side by always installing capabilities, but the engine's default is not sane and the fallback operator makes it worse.

## Where it lives

In the bundled engine (`@github/copilot`, observed in `1.0.63` and `1.0.73`; `app.js`, minified). The relevant compiled forms:

```js
// module init
sen = .8, aen = .95, Nk = 128e3;            // Nk == 128000
class LM { static DEFAULT_TOKEN_LIMIT = Nk; /* ... */ }

// CompactionProcessor.preRequest
s = r.capabilities?.limits?.max_prompt_tokens
    || r.capabilities?.limits?.max_context_window_tokens
    || Nk;                                   // <-- falsy fallback to 128000
u = promptTokens + toolTokens;
d = u / s;                                   // utilization
// compaction triggers when d >= 0.8 (background) / 0.95 (buffer exhaustion)
```

The same `... || Nk` fallback is repeated in the `session.usage_info` emit, `contextInfo`, and `getTokenLimits` paths.

## Two distinct problems

1. **Falsy fallback (`||`) instead of nullish (`??`).**
   A model that reports `max_context_window_tokens: 0` (a legitimately "unknown" signal) collapses to `128000` rather than being treated as unknown. This is compounded upstream: the `@github/copilot-sdk` client's `models.list` handler backfills missing limits with `{ max_context_window_tokens: 0 }`, so an un-capped model arrives at the engine with `0` and `|| Nk` turns it into 128K. `0` should not be coerced to the default via a truthiness check.

2. **No model-aware default.**
   Every un-registered model — including known large-window models — gets the same 128K budget. There is no per-family/default table and no way to distinguish "small model, 128K is right" from "1M-window model, 128K is catastrophically low."

## Impact

- Large-context models compact at ~0.8 * 128000 ≈ 102K tokens regardless of their true window.
- Symptoms: premature/repeated context compaction, extra summarization round-trips, higher token spend and latency, degraded answer quality on long tasks.
- Silent: nothing in the default event payload surfaces the *effective* window that was used, so the "capped at 128K" cause has to be inferred from the model id. (We had to add host-side telemetry — reconstructing `max_prompt_tokens ?? max_context_window_tokens ?? 128000` — to see it.)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a session with a large-context model whose id is **not** matched by any host-installed capabilities entry (so no `limits` reach the engine, or they arrive as `max_context_window_tokens: 0`).
2. Send a turn whose prompt+tool tokens exceed ~102K but are well under the model's real window (e.g. 300K on a 1M-window model).
3. Observe `session.compaction_start` firing even though the real window is nowhere near exhausted.

## Expected

- `0` / missing limits should be treated as "unknown," not coerced to 128K (use `??`, or validate `> 0`).
- Provide a sane, model-aware default (or at minimum a host-configurable default budget) so large-window models are not capped at 128K.
- Surface the effective token limit the engine used in the compaction / `usage_info` telemetry so the applied budget is observable without host-side reconstruction.

## Suggested fixes

- Change the fallback chain from `a || b || Nk` to nullish/`> 0` validation so a real `0` isn't silently replaced.
- Add a model-aware default table, or accept an explicit host-supplied default token budget on session config.
- Emit the resolved effective prompt-token limit alongside compaction and `session.usage_info` events.

## Environment

- Engine: `@github/copilot` `1.0.63` (also reproduced against `1.0.73` via `@github/copilot-next`).
- SDK: `@github/copilot-sdk` `1.0.0` (zero-window backfill also present in `1.0.7`).

## Related

The SDK-side zero-window backfill (`@github/copilot-sdk` `models.list` handler) contributes to problem (1). Happy to cross-file there if the SDK is the preferred owner for that half.

issues.title: Copilot CLI prompts excessively for authorization during a single request (“authorization fatigue”)

labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### **Summary**

The GitHub Copilot CLI is prompting for authorization far too frequently during a single high‑level request, resulting in significant “authorization fatigue.” A single prompt such as:

    PR 727 needs some work. Investigate and see why it's failing

produced **more than a dozen consecutive approval prompts**, interrupting the workflow repeatedly.

This greatly degrades usability and makes multi‑step analysis scenarios difficult to use in practice.

### **What’s happening**

When Copilot CLI executes a high‑level task, it often chains together multiple tool invocations (e.g., GitHub API calls, log loading, local file reads, JSON parsing). For each of these internal steps, the CLI repeatedly asks for permission—sometimes multiple times in a row for the exact same file path or the same type of action.

In this scenario, the CLI:

*   Retrieved PR metadata
*   Checked CI status
*   Loaded workflow run lists
*   Retrieved workflow logs
*   Loaded multiple large log blobs saved to the user’s temp directory
*   Queried/tested multiple log patterns
*   Checked test files under the repository

Each of these steps resulted in additional authorization dialogs. Over a dozen confirmations were required before the task finished.

### **Why this is a problem**

*   **User friction:** Excessive prompting interrupts flow and makes complex tasks painful.
*   **Redundant prompts:** The CLI often asks for permission to read **files it just wrote**, or to perform the same type of action multiple times.
*   **Expected behavior:** A single high‑level user action should not require constant re‑authorization, especially when the operations are clearly part of one cohesive workflow initiated by a single command.

### **Expected behavior**

*   The CLI should **batch or scope authorization** for the duration of a single high‑level request (e.g., “Analyze PR 727”).
*   After the user approves the initial action, subsequent internal steps of that same chain should proceed without further prompts, unless:
    *   a new permission category is needed, or
    *   a clearly risky action is about to take place.

### **Actual behavior**

*   The CLI prompts repeatedly—sometimes every few seconds—to confirm routine file reads, tool invocations, or GitHub queries, even when they are:
    *   safe
    *   expected
    *   part of the same chain
    *   previously approved during the same command

### **Impact**

This drastically reduces the usability of Copilot CLI for multi‑step reasoning tasks, PR analysis, or anything involving workflow logs or large outputs.

### **Suggested improvements**

1.  **Single approval per top-level request.** Treat everything triggered by a single line of user input as one execution context.
2.  **Permission caching.** Cache permission acknowledgements for:
    *   specific file paths or glob patterns
    *   categories of actions (e.g., “read GitHub workflow logs”)
3.  **Smarter grouping of tool invocations.** Instead of prompting for each intermediate step, provide a single consolidated summary of what the CLI intends to do.
4.  **User-configurable trust policies.**
    *   Per‑session trust
    *   Per‑repo trust
    *   Per‑action-category trust (e.g., allow all read‑only operations)

### **Environment**

*   GitHub Copilot CLI (latest version as of Jan 2026)
*   Running on Windows (Temp directory prompts especially problematic)
*   Repository: public GitHub repo (uBPF), but issue is general to all repos

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When the `.well-known/openid-configuration` is behind an http redirect, authentication fails with:

```
Authentication failed: MCPOAuthError: Incompatible authorization server: authorization server advertised an issuer that does not match the URL its metadata was discovered from (RFC 8414 §3.3); refusing to connect
```

I believe that `copilot-cli` checks the issuer against the original URL instead of the redirected URL. Note that RFC 8414 states that the issuer must match "_the URL used to retrieve the metadata,_" which strictly speaking is the redirection target, not the source.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.83.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Run an MCP server on a different server from its OAuth authorization server, e.g. https://my.mcp.server vs https://my.oauth.server
2. Configure the MCP server so that https://my.mcp.server/.well-known/openid-configuration returns an HTTP 301 redirect to https://my.oauth.server/.well-known/openid-configuration
3. Configure the OAuth server so that https://my.oauth.server/.well-known/openid-configuration specifies https://my.oauth.server as the issuer
4. In `copilot-cli`, type `/mcp add FooBar`, select type HTTP, remote server URL https://my.mcp.server, and the client ID when asked


### Expected behavior

Copilot should ask to authenticate, then open the authentication URL in my browser (or display the authentication code and URL so that I can copy-paste them in my browser), then complete the authentication flow.

### Additional context

This may be related to #4480 except that in #4480, the Atlassian MCP server gave the wrong issuer, whereas here the issuer is correct for the real URL and copilot-cli is checking against the wrong URL.

issues.title: Windows: Backspace in $EDITOR=vim.exe launched via Ctrl+G inserts ⌂ (0x7F) instead of deleting

labels.name: area:input-keyboard
labels.description: Keyboard shortcuts, keybindings, copy/paste, clipboard, mouse, and text input

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

issues.body:
### Repro
- Windows 11, PowerShell (conhost or Windows Terminal)
- Copilot CLI v1.0.49-1
- Vim 9.2 (console build) at `C:\Program Files\Vim\vim92\vim.exe`

```powershell
$Env:EDITOR = "$Env:ProgramFiles\Vim\vim92\vim.exe"
copilot
# Press Ctrl+G (or Ctrl+X then e) to edit the prompt in $EDITOR
# In Vim, press `i` for insert mode, type some text, press Backspace
```

### Expected
Backspace deletes the previous character.

### Actual
Backspace inserts the `⌂` glyph (CP437 rendering of byte `0x7F` / DEL).

### Notes
- Vim launched directly from the same PowerShell session (`& $Env:EDITOR`) works correctly — Backspace deletes as expected. The bug only reproduces when Vim is spawned by Copilot CLI's external-editor feature.
- Apparent root cause: Copilot CLI puts the Windows console into VT input mode (ConPTY) for its own TUI. With `ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT` set, Backspace is delivered as `0x7F` (`^?`, xterm style). Vim's Windows console build defaults to `t_kb=^H` (`0x08`), so it does not recognize `0x7F` as Backspace and inserts it as a literal character (displayed as `⌂`).
- The editor is spawned via plain stdio inheritance (no PTY bridge), so the parent's VT input mode leaks into the child.

### Possible fixes? (Unverified)
- Allocate a PTY for the editor subprocess, or
- Temporarily clear `ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_INPUT` on the console before spawn and restore after, or
- Set `TERM=win32` in the spawned editor's environment so Vim picks compatible termcap defaults.

### Environment
- OS: Windows 11
- Shell: PowerShell
- Copilot CLI: 1.0.49-1
- Vim: 9.2 (console build, `vim.exe`)

prs.title: fix: extension bootstrap path mismatch in launchExtension() (#2890)
prs.body:
## Summary

Extensions fail to load on both macOS and Windows because the forked child process's security check in `index.js` expects the bootstrap path under `dirname(process.execPath)` (the SEA binary directory), but `app.js` passes a path from the pkg cache (`universal/<ver>/preloads/`).

This affects **all** extensions — both user-level and project-level — on CLI v1.0.34 and v1.0.35.

Fixes #2890

## Root Cause

| | macOS | Windows (npm) |
|---|---|---|
| SEA dir (`index.js`) | `darwin-arm64/<ver>/` | `npm/.../copilot-win32-x64/` |
| Bootstrap from (`app.js`) | `universal/<ver>/preloads/` | `universal/<ver>/preloads/` |
| `preloads/` exists in SEA dir? | No | No |

The security check in the embedded `index.js`:
```js
var z = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));  // SEA binary dir
var q = Q?.startsWith(resolve(z, "preloads") + sep) ? Q : undefined;
// q is always undefined → falls through → "Invalid command format"
```

## Proposed Fixes

**Option A (smallest change):** In `launchExtension()`, resolve bootstrap path from `dirname(process.execPath)` instead of `cliDistDir`, and ship `preloads/` in platform npm packages.

**Option B (no package changes):** Expand the `index.js` security check to also trust the `cliDistDir` pkg cache path (passed via env var from parent).

See `fix-extension-bootstrap-path.md` in this PR for full details and code samples.

## Verification

Option A tested locally on Windows 11 (npm install, CLI 1.0.35):
1. Copied `preloads/` to SEA binary directory
2. Patched minified `app.js` to prefer `dirname(process.execPath)`
3. Both user-level and project-level extensions loaded successfully

issues.body:
**Version:** opencode v2.3.0, Linux x86_64, local ext4/btrfs-class disk (not a network filesystem)

## Problem
Running many `opencode run --format json` processes at once against the same `opencode.db` makes a large share of them die mid-session with:

```json
{"type":"error","sessionID":"ses_…","error":{"type":"unknown","message":"Failed to execute statement"}}
```

The message carries no SQLite error code, so callers cannot tell a transient `SQLITE_BUSY` from a real failure and cannot retry sensibly.

## Observed
- 100 short-lived worker processes launched by an orchestrator, cap raised from 20 to 50 concurrent.
- Within ~90 s of the cap change, 17 of the first ~35 launched workers failed or had to be requeued; the supervisor classified them as `sqlite_other`. Several exhausted their retries.
- At 20 concurrent the same workload had no failures.
- Database: `opencode.db` ≈ 5.5 GB with a WAL file (~17 MB) and `-shm`; all processes share the default data dir.
- Failures hit processes that were already running (not only boot), so this is different from #53879 (first-start `CREATE TABLE` race). It looks closer to the write contention described in #56282, but happens on a local disk.

## Likely causes
1. Each process opens its own connection and writes message/part rows on every streamed step, so N processes = N concurrent writers on one WAL database. WAL allows only one writer; the rest rely on the busy handler.
2. Busy handling appears to be absent or too short. A write that cannot acquire the lock immediately surfaces as a generic "Failed to execute statement".
3. With a multi-GB DB, checkpoints and the WAL index are slower, widening the window in which writers collide.

## Suggested fixes
- Set `PRAGMA busy_timeout` (for example 5–10 s) on every connection, and `PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL` with WAL.
- Retry statements that fail with `SQLITE_BUSY` / `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT` with bounded jittered backoff instead of failing the session.
- Use `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` for write transactions so a lock conflict fails at the start of the transaction, where it is safe to retry, instead of at upgrade time, which is not retryable.
- Batch part updates (write the final part, or coalesce streamed deltas) so a step costs one write transaction, not many.
- Include the SQLite result code and extended code in the error (`SQLITE_BUSY`, `SQLITE_LOCKED`, …) so wrappers can classify it.
- Optionally allow a per-run database (`OPENCODE_DB=…` or an ephemeral session store) for headless `run` invocations that do not need to share history.

## Repro sketch
```sh
for i in $(seq 1 50); do
  opencode run --format json -m <any-fast-model> "reply with OK" >/tmp/o$i.log 2>&1 &
done
wait
grep -l 'Failed to execute statement' /tmp/o*.log | wc -l
```
(Failure count rises with concurrency and with database size.)

Related: #56282, #53879

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Plugin API: `permission.reply` hook to adjust the decline message before the reply settles the request
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

Add a `permission.reply` plugin hook, the counterpart of `permission.evaluate`, that runs when a client replies to a pending permission request and lets a plugin adjust the decline message.

#### Motivation

In v2, `Permission.reply` decides how a rejection reaches the session:

- A rejection with a message fails the request with `Permission.CorrectedError`. Tools convert it into a `ToolFailure`, `toSessionError` maps it to `permission.rejected` with the feedback text, and the model continues in the same step.
- A rejection without a message fails the request with `Permission.DeclinedError`. It travels as a defect and ends the step.

The outcome therefore depends on whether the user typed text. Users and organizations that want every decline to be reported back to the model, with a standard explanation, have no supported way to configure that:

- V1's `experimental.continue_loop_on_deny` is not supported in v2 (see `migrate-v1.mdx`).
- `permission.evaluate` runs before the request is created, so it cannot see the user's reply.
- Subscribing to `Permission.Event.Replied` and sending a follow-up message starts a new turn after the step has ended. The declined tool call stays recorded as aborted, and the model does not receive the explanation as that call's result.

#### Proposal

Trigger a `permission.reply` hook in `Permission.reply` before the `reject` branch decides between `CorrectedError` and `DeclinedError`:

```ts
interface PermissionReplyEvent {
  readonly sessionID: Session.ID
  readonly requestID: Permission.ID
  readonly action: string
  readonly resources: ReadonlyArray<string>
  readonly metadata?: Record<string, unknown>
  readonly source?: Permission.Source
  readonly reply: "once" | "always" | "reject"
  message?: string
}
```

- The hook runs once per client reply, for the request the client answered.
- When the final `reply` is `reject` and `message` is non-empty, the existing code creates `CorrectedError`. The same message applies to the whole batch of pending requests in the session, as it does today.
- The `reply` field is read-only, so a plugin can adjust the message and cannot turn a rejection into an approval.
- `PluginHooks.Service` is already available in the `Permission` layer, and the plugin side only needs a new entry in `PermissionHooks` next to `evaluate`.

With this hook, a plugin can fill in a default message for plain rejections:

```ts
hook.reply((event) => {
  if (event.reply === "reject" && !event.message) {
    event.message = "The user declined this tool call. Choose a different approach or ask what they prefer."
  }
})
```

The model then receives the text as the tool failure in the same step, which is the behavior users already get when they type a reason.

issues.body:
## Summary

Background shell tasks launched through OpenCode are now cancelled when the OpenCode server restarts. Until an update about 2026-11-18/19, these tasks routinely survived server restarts. Long-running work (a data pipeline loop, a heartbeat script) is now killed on every restart, with the harness reporting `Command cancelled because the server restarted`.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.2 (from the runtime diagnostics snapshot; the `opencode` CLI is not on PATH in the shell, so this could not be re-verified from the terminal)
- OS: Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.19044.0 (Windows 10 IoT Enterprise LTSC, win32 x64)
- Terminal: OpenCode-managed PTY; `TERM=xterm-256color`, `TERM_PROGRAM` and `COLORTERM` unset
- Shell: `C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe` (`ComSpec`); tool calls are wrapped in Windows PowerShell 5.1
- Install/channel: latest release (2.3.2). New `opencode-pty` component cached at version `0.6.0-3ca87f140ff90483` (installed 2026-11-19 17:54); previous version `0.5.2-11340688cb76d2ba` dated 2026-11-17
- Active plugins: none found in `C:\Users\user\.config\opencode\opencode.jsonc` (only an MCP `browser-bridge` server is configured)

## Reproduction

1. Start a long-running task as an OpenCode background shell, e.g. a PowerShell loop that appends `timestamp tick=N pid=PID` to a log file every 5 seconds and never exits.
2. Confirm several ticks are written and note the process ID.
3. Restart the OpenCode server.
4. Inspect the log file and process list after the server is back.

## Expected Behavior

The background task continues running across the server restart and keeps appending ticks, as it did before the update two days ago.

## Actual Behavior

The task is cancelled by the server restart. The log stops immediately (8 ticks, last write `2026-11-20 07:13:35`, PID 15976), the process is gone, and the harness reports:

```
Command cancelled because the server restarted
```

A second long-running data pipeline script was killed the same way on an earlier restart (its own log stopped at `2026-11-20 07:08:15`). This has now happened on two consecutive restarts, so it is consistent rather than intermittent.

## Additional Context

- The user reports background tasks did **not** close with OpenCode before the update roughly two days ago, so this looks like a regression rather than intended behavior.
- Likely related change: a new `opencode-pty` binary, `C:\Users\user\.cache\opencode\bin\opencode-pty\0.6.0-3ca87f140ff90483\opencode-pty.exe`, appeared on 2026-11-19 and replaces `0.5.2-11340688cb76d2ba` from 2026-11-17. This component appears to own child-process lifetime, but that has not been confirmed.
- Initial investigation assumed the harness had always killed background tasks on restart; the user corrected that. No config, plugin, or terminal change was made in that interval.
- Existing related issues found by search but not duplicates: #64080 (PTY daemon reconnect failure), #60876 (stale PTY session dir), #64317 (orphaned PTY shell on Windows).
- Workaround not yet applied: run long-lived work under Windows Task Scheduler so it lives outside the OpenCode process tree.

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something is broken

labels.name: area/core
labels.description: Agent loop, tools and config

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/macos
labels.description: macOS

issues.body:
## Problem

A session moves into a worktree, the worktree is removed, and the next `opencode reload` fails with `ServiceUnavailableError` — it rebuilds nothing, so config and MCP changes stay unapplied. Removing a worktree should leave the server reloadable.

## Evidence

1. `worktree_create` a worktree, e.g. `/Users/oscar/.worktree/v2-api-fixes`.
2. `session_move` the session into it. The server boots that location (its MCP clients connect with `directory=/Users/oscar/.worktree/v2-api-fixes`).
3. `worktree_remove` the worktree.
4. Run `opencode reload`.

```
ServiceUnavailableError: FileSystem.DirectoryNotFoundError: Directory not found: /Users/oscar/.worktree/v2-api-fixes
    at LocationServiceMap.reload
  [cause]: PlatformError: NotFound: FileSystem.realPath (/Users/oscar/.worktree/v2-api-fixes)
      at rm
  [cause]: Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '/Users/oscar/.worktree/v2-api-fixes'
```

`Worktree.remove` (`packages/core/src/worktree.ts:257`) deletes the directory and the row but leaves the location cached in `LocationServiceMap`. `reload` (`packages/core/src/location-service-map.ts:20`) invalidates and re-boots every cached key, and its second pass collects exits but still fails the effect — so one directory that no longer exists fails the entire reload.

Workaround: `DELETE /api/debug/location?location[directory]=<path>` (which correctly does nothing for a missing directory) and reload again, or restart the server.

Version 2.3.2, macOS arm64. Present on main as of 3508a0e31a.

## Impact

Anyone who deletes a worktree a session had moved into: every later reload fails until the server is restarted or the location is evicted by hand. One stale location, but the reload is all-or-nothing, so it blocks config, plugin, and MCP reloads for every location on the server.

issues.body:
### Summary

In OpenCode Desktop (Windows), when a shell command is still running in the background, the session still signals turn completion: the notification sound plays, the input is released and the assistant message arrives, while the background indicator in the bottom-left corner (e.g. **"1 Shell"**) keeps counting. The transcript contains no hint that a job is still running.

Users read the finished-looking answer as final, copy it, and only later notice that the command was still in flight.

### Environment

- opencode desktop **2.3.2** (packaged, Windows 11 x64)
- background service 2.3.2 on the same port
- shell tool used for long-running commands (polling, verification runs)

### Reproduction

1. Ask the agent to start a long command in the background, e.g. a 10-minute poll loop that writes into a log.
2. The status area at the bottom left shows `1 Shell` and keeps it while the command runs.
3. The agent finishes its turn and writes a normal assistant message.
4. Observe: the completion notification/sound fires and the prompt is available again, while `1 Shell` is still shown.
5. The transcript shows nothing about the running job — no row, no badge, no state.

### Expected

- While a background job is running, the session should not present itself as finished (no "done" signal, or an explicit "background work running" state), OR
- the transcript should show the background job as a visible, stateful row (like a tool call), so a reader can see at a glance that work is still in progress.

Either fix removes the ambiguity; ideally both.

### Actual

- Completion signal fires immediately after the assistant message, independent of the running background command.
- The only indication is the small counter in the corner, which is easy to miss and is not part of the transcript.

### Relation

- #65057: desktop session looks idle / shows no working indicator while a **subagent** is still running — same class of problem, different background work.
- #65014: background shell tasks cancelled on server restart.

issues.title: desktop: idle GPU helper + WindowServer ~28% CPU even when the window is fully occluded (Intel MacBookPro15,1, macOS 15.8.2, v2.2.6)
issues.body:
### Description

OpenCode Desktop 2.2.6 on macOS 15.8.2 (Intel) keeps a fully idle UI rendering continuously: `OpenCode Helper (GPU)` sits at ~29% CPU and `WindowServer` at ~28% CPU with no interaction at all.

The load does **not** drop when the window is completely occluded by another full-screen window, but drops to ~0-1% as soon as the window is hidden or minimized. This points to a permanent `requestAnimationFrame`/compositor loop rather than to cost proportional to what is visible.

Hardware acceleration is working on this machine, so this is **not** the OCLP software-rendering case in #55786: the GPU process is not launched with `--use-gl=disabled`, `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passes, and the iGPU reports 26-34% device utilization.

### Environment

- OpenCode Desktop 2.2.6 (bundled `opencode-cli` 2.2.6), Electron
- macOS 15.8.2 (24H232), x86_64
- MacBookPro15,1 - Core i9-9880H, 16 GB RAM, Radeon Pro 560X + Intel UHD 630
- Internal 2880x1800 panel, default "looks like 1680x1050" HiDPI (3360x2100 backing)
- No plugins, no MCP servers enabled
- Reproduces right after a fresh reboot

### Reproduction

1. Launch the desktop app and open a session.
2. Leave it idle (no prompt running), window visible, do not interact.
3. Measure WindowServer and the GPU helper.

### Measurements

`ps -p <pid> -o %cpu=`, 1 s samples over 10 s windows:

| State | WindowServer | GPU helper | Renderer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Window visible, app frontmost | 27-28% | 28.7% | 6.0% |
| Window visible but fully covered by a full-screen Safari window | 24-28% | - | - |
| Window hidden (Cmd+H) | 0.0-1.9% | ~0% | ~0% |
| Window shown again | 27.9-28.3% | - | - |
| Window resized to 500x350 | 28% (vs 31% at 1034x705) | - | - |

The cost is independent of visible area and survives full occlusion, which is why this looks different from a normal "big window" repaint cost.

### Ruled out on this machine

- Memory pressure: `kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level = 1`, no pageouts
- Thermal throttling: `CPU_Speed_Limit = 100`
- SSD: SMART Verified, no I/O errors
- Network / proxy: disabled system proxy, no change
- Wallpaper: switching from the dynamic aerial 4K HEVC wallpaper to a static image did not change WindowServer load at all (still 28-30% with the app visible)
- ResizeObserver storm (#52706): `renderer.log` contains only 0-6 occurrences per session, not a storm

### Related issues

- #52927 - same "idle app pins a CPU core" symptom, closed as a duplicate of #55786 (OCLP software rendering). This report is a different case: hardware acceleration is active and the app still repaints forever.
- #31664 - identifies the class of cause: `clip-path` progress-bar animation plus a `mix-blend-mode: soft-light` avatar loader forcing full-window mask/shader recalculation every frame; minimizing suspends `requestAnimationFrame` and drops load to 0%.
- #52706 - ResizeObserver loop (fixed in 2.2.1), not the cause here.

### Workaround being tested

The `--force-prefers-reduced-motion` launch flag was reported in #52927 to drop total CPU from 243-294% to 0-1% on Windows. I am verifying it on this Intel Mac and will report the result here.

### Separate note (auto-update)

The built-in updater has failed repeatedly on this machine. `ShipIt_stderr.log` shows the downloaded bundle failing validation:

```
Code signature at URL .../OpenCode.app did not pass validation
SecComponentPath=Helpers/chrome_crashpad_handler
NSLocalizedDescription=invalid signature (code or signature have been modified)
```

The installed app signature itself verifies fine. Currently stuck on 2.2.6 while 2.2.7 is out.

issues.body: ### Description A ```math block renders as a plain code block with its raw LaTeX when the formula contains "\ " (backslash-space, the standard control space). This does not render: ~~~md ```math \forall \varepsilon>0\ \exists K\in\mathbb{N} ``` ~~~ Without `\ ` it renders (`\forall \varepsilon>0\exists K\in\mathbb{N}`, or with `\;` instead), the control space is the trigger. `packages/latex` implements `\,`, `\:`, `\;`, `\quad`, `\qquad`, `\enspace`, and `\thinspace`, but not `\ `. issues.title: tui: indeterminate progress indicator with active stage and elapsed time for long-running tools and subagents

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New behaviour or an improvement

labels.name: area/tui
labels.description: Terminal interface

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/macos
labels.description: macOS

issues.body:
## Summary

During long-running tool executions or subagent tasks, users cannot tell whether work is actively progressing or stalled. Adding an indeterminate progress indicator displaying the current phase/tool/subagent, a concise user-facing rationale for the step, and elapsed time will provide critical visibility into active execution state.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.2
- OS: Darwin 27.2.0 (arm64)
- Terminal: Ghostty (TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor)
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: None found in config

## Reproduction

1. Initiate a task requiring extended computation, deep file/system operations, or subagent delegation (e.g., multi-step analysis or codebase exploration).
2. Observe the terminal UI feedback while the tool or child agent runs.
3. Attempt to determine the active subtask or whether the operation has hung.

## Expected Behavior

A native visible activity indicator should display the active context—specifically identifying the running subagent or tool name, a concise user-facing task purpose/rationale explaining *why* the step is being performed, and elapsed execution time.

Example format:
- `Researching CLI settings — to determine whether a native progress indicator exists (01:42)`
- `Running subagent: researcher — synthesizing competitor features across docs (02:15)`
- `Executing tool: execute — running unit test suite to verify changes (00:43)`

This provides immediate visual confirmation of forward progress and context without requiring arbitrary percentage-based completion estimates or exposing raw chain-of-thought / private reasoning.

## Actual Behavior

The existing spinner and notifications confirm that the process is technically alive, but they do not communicate the current stage, which specific tool or subagent is active, why the active step is being executed, or elapsed activity time. As a result, users cannot distinguish between legitimate long-running tasks and silent hangs or timeouts.

## Additional Context

- **Why avoid percentage estimates:** Model generation time, external APIs, and open-ended tool loops have unpredictable lifecycles; indeterminate progress with live stage, brief rationale, and elapsed duration provides reliable feedback without misleading completion metrics.
- **Privacy & clarity:** The step rationale should be a short, user-facing summary of intent rather than verbose internal monologue or raw reasoning tokens.
- **Scope:** Primarily impacts TUI and interactive CLI workflows during nested tool calls and background child sessions.

issues.title: Provider `claude-agent`: system messages in history are dropped, so keyed instruction updates never reach Claude
issues.body:
### Description

On the `claude-agent` provider, `system` messages in the conversation history never reach Claude.
The keyed session instructions API delivers every update after the first request as exactly such a
message, so a plugin's later `ctx.session.instructions.entry.put` or `remove` never reaches Claude.

- `ctx.session.instructions.entry.put` / `remove` (experimental): the first value goes into the
  request's system parts. Every later change is appended at the next step boundary as a stored
  `system` message, "Instructions updated: …"
  (`packages/core/src/session/message-updater.ts:154`, `instruction-state.ts`,
  `runner/to-llm-message.ts`).
- The connector skips `system` messages, both when it converts the prompt for Claude and when it
  fingerprints history:
  - `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/claude-agent/language-model/convert-to-claude-message.ts:13`
  - `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/claude-agent/sync/fingerprint.ts:91`
  - `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/claude-agent/sync/decide.ts:47`

On other providers the update message is part of the request. On `claude-agent` the model keeps the
first value for the rest of the session.

This is related to #61248 / #61273 but not the same: those cover system *parts* that a plugin
pushes into `event.system`, which the provider snapshots too early. This one covers system-role
*messages* in history. #61273 does not touch the conversion above.

**Expected:** an instruction update reaches Claude without changing the system prompt (a change
there restarts the Claude process, per the provider spec). One option is to render it into the user
content, the way other notices are.

Found by reading the source at v2.2.5 (`9bbb8ce`); the lines above are unchanged on `dev`. It was
not reproduced against a live Claude account.

### Plugins

A custom server plugin (any plugin that uses `ctx.session.instructions.entry`)

### OpenCode version

2.2.5

### Steps to reproduce

1. In a server plugin, call `ctx.session.instructions.entry.put({ sessionID, key: "repro.state", value: "A" })` before the session's first request.
2. After the first step, call it again with `"B"`.
3. Run the session on `claude-agent/<model>` and on `openai/<model>`, and ask the model for the current value.
4. Expected from the source: OpenAI sees the "Instructions updated" message with `B`; Claude still answers `A`.

### Operating System

Windows 11

issues.title: desktop: sessions from unrelated folders merge into a shared "global" project
issues.body:
## Summary

In the desktop app, sessions from unrelated folders are merged into one shared project when those folders do not have an independently resolvable project identity (they are not a git repo, or are a git repo with no commits yet / unborn HEAD). Selecting one folder in the sidebar shows sessions created in other folders too.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.26
- OS: Darwin 27.2.0 (darwin arm64)
- Terminal: Unavailable: terminal environment variables are not set (observed in the desktop app)
- Shell: /bin/zsh
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: None found in config

## Reproduction

1. Create two or more separate folders that are either (a) not a git repository, or (b) a git repository created with `git init` but with **no commits** (unborn `HEAD`).
2. Open each folder as its own project in the desktop app and start/run a session in each.
3. In the sidebar, select one of those folders and look at its session list.

## Expected Behavior

The session list for a selected project/folder should only contain sessions that belong to that folder.

## Actual Behavior

The session list contains sessions from **all** folders that lack an independent project identity, i.e. sessions from unrelated folders are mixed into the selected one. It is intermittent in practice only because most folders are real git repositories with commits (those get their own stable project id and stay isolated); the problem appears whenever such "identity-less" folders are opened together.

## Additional Context

Root cause appears to be that OpenCode cannot derive a project id for a folder when it is not a VCS repo, or is a repo with an unborn `HEAD`, and falls back to a single shared catch-all project (`project_id = "global"`). Because the session list is filtered by `project_id` (with no fallback to `directory`), every folder that maps to `global` shares one session pool.

Evidence from local storage at `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (names redacted):

**1. One `global` bucket holds far more sessions than any real project, spanning many distinct directories**

```
session_v2 grouped by project_id (top rows):
  global                                 156
  <hash-A>                                38
  <hash-B>                                35
  ...
```

**2. The `worktree` table maps several different directories to the same `project_id = global`**

```
project_id | directory
global     | <home>/.../folderA
global     | <home>/.../folderB
global     | <home>/.../folderC
```

**3. Sessions shown under the wrong project all carry `project_id = global` while their `directory` differs**

```
title                | project_id | directory
<session-in-folderA> | global     | <home>/.../folderA
<session-in-folderB> | global     | <home>/.../folderB
<session-in-folderC> | global     | <home>/.../folderC
```

**4. Correlation: folders that fall back to `global` have no commits; folders with their own project id have commits**

```
directory | git toplevel | HEAD commits | resulting project_id
folderA   | yes          | unborn/fatal | global
folderB   | yes          | unborn/fatal | global
folderC   | no           | n/a          | global
repoX     | yes          | 30           | <unique hash>
repoY     | yes          | 11           | <unique hash>
```

### Workaround

Give each affected folder a real git repository with at least one commit:

```sh
cd <folder> && git add -A && git commit -m "init"
```

After that OpenCode assigns it a unique project id and its sessions no longer mix. For non-repo folders, `git init` followed by one commit achieves the same.

### Suggested fix

When a folder has no resolvable project identity, either generate a per-directory project id, or fall back to filtering sessions by `directory` instead of collapsing everything into a single `global` project.

issues.body:
### Description

# Summary

After upgrading the desktop app from 1.19.5 to 2.3.2, all projects disappeared from the sidebar. Sessions were still present in the database but were attributed to the legacy `global` project, and opening a session showed a wrong project in the breadcrumb (e.g. `proj-a / proj-b / title`). Re-adding a directory did not create a project; the server only inserted a `worktree` row under `global`.

Root cause (observed): in 2.x the project identity for a git repository is derived from the repository itself — the root commit SHA when there is no remote, or a hash of the remote URL. If the repository has **no commits at all** (`git init` without any commit, unborn HEAD), no identity can be derived and the location falls back to the legacy `global` project. A V1 install commonly has several such directories, so after migration they all merge into `global`.

# Environment

```
opencode v2.3.2 (desktop, Windows)
opencode-cli.exe serve --service
service status: http://127.0.0.1:<port>
upgraded from desktop 1.19.5 (DB at ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db)
```

# Steps to reproduce

Minimal, on a clean 2.3.2 install:

1. Create three directories that are git repositories with no commits:

   ```bash
   mkdir proj-a proj-b proj-c
   git -C proj-a init
   git -C proj-b init
   git -C proj-c init
   ```

2. Resolve each directory through the API:

   ```bash
   opencode api GET /api/location -H "x-opencode-directory:<abs path to proj-a>"
   opencode api GET /api/location -H "x-opencode-directory:<abs path to proj-b>"
   ```

3. Observe that every directory resolves to `project.id = "global"` and that a `global + <directory>` row is added to the `worktree` table.

4. Add one commit to a repository and retry:

   ```bash
   git -C proj-a -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t commit --allow-empty -m init
   opencode api GET /api/location -H "x-opencode-directory:<abs path to proj-a>"
   ```

   Now it resolves to `project.id = <root commit SHA>`.

# Expected

- A directory that is a git repository but has no commits should get its own project, or at least the migration should preserve the directory → project mapping from V1 (`session.directory`).
- Adding a project directory from the desktop UI should create a project, not append a worktree to `global`.

# Actual

| Directory type | `location.get` result |
|---|---|
| non-git directory | own project, id derived from path |
| git repo, no commits (unborn HEAD) | `global` |
| git repo, 1 commit, no remote | own project, id = root commit SHA |
| git repo, 1 commit, with remote | own project, id = hash(remote URL) |

Additional desktop behavior observed after V1→V2 migration:

- `kv.migration.v1-v2 = {"phase":"completed"}`.
- All legacy sessions had `project_id = 'global'`; V1 stored project attribution only in `session.directory`.
- `project_directory` stayed empty and `project` contained only the legacy `global` row plus a few rows created during migration.
- Adding a directory from the UI only wrote `worktree(project_id='global', directory=<dir>)`. `project` gained no row.
- The sidebar only lists project IDs present in the desktop state `usedProjectIDs` (`drafts.sqlite`, scope `opencode.global.dat`, key `server`). Inserting rows into `project` alone does not make them visible.
- The service caches location resolution: after changing identities, `opencode service restart` is required, and directories that were already opened keep resolving to `global` until then.
- Breadcrumb uses the resolved location's project, so a session in `proj-b` can render as `proj-a / proj-b / title` and new sessions are created under `proj-a` (`global`).

# Root cause

V1→V2 migration imports sessions but does not create V2 projects per directory. V2 project identity is repository-based, not path-based. Repositories with no commits yield no identity, and the resolver falls back to `global`.

Note: identical empty commits also produce identical root SHAs, so "add an empty commit" only works if the commit message/date differs per repository. Worth handling explicitly (e.g. reject identity-less repos with a clear error, or key them by canonical path).

# Workaround (validated locally)

1. Give every affected repository a unique identity, e.g. an empty commit with a unique message:

   ```bash
   git -C <dir> -c user.name=opencode -c user.email=opencode@localhost \
     commit --allow-empty -m "init: <unique name>"
   git -C <dir> rev-parse HEAD   # this SHA becomes the project id
   ```

   (Alternative: add a unique remote, which uses the remote URL hash as identity. Reversible: `git remote remove origin`.)

2. Insert matching `project` rows (`id = root commit SHA`, `worktree = <dir>`), move sessions by `session.directory` to those IDs, remove `global + <dir>` worktree rows, and set `global.worktree` to a neutral parent path so it no longer collides with a real project.

3. Add the new project IDs to `usedProjectIDs` in `drafts.sqlite` (desktop must be closed or the state is overwritten on exit).

4. `opencode service restart`, then re-check `/api/location` for every directory.

5. Restart the desktop app; the sidebar and breadcrumbs are correct afterwards.

Data was preserved throughout: all sessions were kept and redistributed to their projects.

# Related issues

- #64569 desktop: project panel loses pre-update projects after migration (empty project_directory, NULL names)
- #49827 migrate-v1: non-git sessions in "global" project hidden after V1→V2 upgrade
- #57858 desktop: home screen renders without projects or New session action on first launch after V1 migration
- #52501 project: Windows path case sensitivity silently splits project identity

# Logs

Relevant server log lines (no sensitive data):

```
WARN message="worktree discovery failed" directory="<path>" strategy=git error=Worktree.DirectoryUnavailableError
INFO message="location services booted" directory="<path>" workspaceID=undefined
```

The `worktree discovery failed` warning appears for git repositories without commits. Paths and IDs in this report are anonymized.


### Plugins

None

### OpenCode version

opencode v2.3.2 (desktop, Windows)

### Steps to reproduce

Minimal, on a clean 2.3.2 install:

1. Create three directories that are git repositories with no commits:

   ```bash
   mkdir proj-a proj-b proj-c
   git -C proj-a init
   git -C proj-b init
   git -C proj-c init
   ```

2. Resolve each directory through the API:

   ```bash
   opencode api GET /api/location -H "x-opencode-directory:<abs path to proj-a>"
   opencode api GET /api/location -H "x-opencode-directory:<abs path to proj-b>"
   ```

3. Observe that every directory resolves to `project.id = "global"` and that a `global + <directory>` row is added to the `worktree` table.

4. Add one commit to a repository and retry:

   ```bash
   git -C proj-a -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t commit --allow-empty -m init
   opencode api GET /api/location -H "x-opencode-directory:<abs path to proj-a>"
   ```

   Now it resolves to `project.id = <root commit SHA>`.


### Screenshot

_No response_

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Terminal

_No response_
