issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, the background service got stuck installing a `github:` plugin from a private repo that needs a GitHub sign-in. Plugin activation never finished, so `/api/model` and `/api/provider` returned 503. The desktop app showed no models and said "Connect an integration to send prompts", which pointed at the provider login instead of the plugin. The service stayed stuck after `opencode service restart`. Only removing the plugin from the config fixed it.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.3.2 (CLI and background service; the problem started right after updating to it)
- OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200.9974)
- Git: 2.55.0.windows.3, Git Credential Manager 2.9.0
- Terminal: OpenCode desktop app; CLI commands run from MSYS2
- Shell: zsh (MSYS2)
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: a local file plugin in `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`, `superpowers@git+https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git`, and `github:<org>/<repo>` (a private repo behind GitHub org SAML SSO; this is the one that got stuck)

## Reproduction

I have not reproduced this from a clean setup. These steps are inferred from the logs below.

1. On Windows with Git Credential Manager, add a plugin `github:<org>/<repo>` where the repo needs authentication (org SAML SSO here), and GCM has no valid cached credential for it.
2. Start the background service when there is no usable cached install of that plugin. Here this happened right after updating to 2.3.2; the log reports `Package is not installed` for the plugin's cache directory.
3. Open the desktop app, or run `opencode models`.

## Expected Behavior

- A plugin install started by the background service runs git without interactive prompts and fails quickly with an authentication error that names the plugin.
- A plugin that fails or is still installing appears in `/api/plugin` with its state and the reason.
- The app names the plugin that is blocking startup, rather than saying "Connect an integration to send prompts".
- `opencode service restart` recovers once the credential problem is fixed.

## Actual Behavior

- Desktop app: "Connect an integration to send prompts" and an empty `/models`. Later it showed:
  ```
  ServiceUnavailableError: Location plugins did not finish activating
      at MFt (oc://renderer/assets/main-CJInpv21.js:686:34398)
  ```
- `opencode models` failed with the same `ServiceUnavailableError: Location plugins did not finish activating`.
- `GET /api/plugin` first returned `{"location":{...},"data":[]}`. After a service restart it listed every built-in plugin, the local plugin and `superpowers` as `active`. The private plugin was missing entirely, shown neither as failed nor as pending, and `/api/model` still returned 503.
- The service log showed the install giving up only after about 300 s (`http.span=300613`):
  ```
  level=ERROR message="unhandled rejection" cause="ServiceUnavailableError: Location plugins did not finish activating" role=cli
  level=WARN message="failed to load plugin" target=github:<org>/<repo> cause=Cause([Fail(LockTimeoutError)]) http.span=300613 role=server
  level=WARN message="failed to check plugin update" target=github:<org>/<repo> cause="Cause([Fail(NpmInstallFailedError: Failed to install C:\\Users\\<user>\\.cache\\opencode\\npm\\git-<repo>-<hash>: Package is not installed: github:<org>/<repo> (cause: Error: Package is not installed: github:<org>/<repo>))])" http.span=300617 role=server
  ```
- Running `git ls-remote https://github.com/<org>/<repo>` by hand printed `info: please complete authentication in your browser...` from Git Credential Manager, then succeeded after the browser sign-in. I believe the service's git process was waiting on the same prompt, which a background service cannot show. I have not confirmed this directly.
- After that manual sign-in, `opencode service restart` did not recover. About 2 minutes after the restart, activation still had not finished and `opencode models` still returned the 503.
- Removing the plugin from `opencode.jsonc` fixed everything right away.

## Additional Context

- Happened on both service starts we checked, until the plugin was removed.
- Re-authenticating GitHub Copilot (`/connect`) did not help; the provider was fine the whole time. The "Connect an integration" message sent troubleshooting in the wrong direction for a long time.
- Related:
  - #63814 (merged after 2.3.2) stops model and provider handlers from waiting on plugins, so models would stay visible. The stuck plugin would still silently never load, though, and nothing would say why.
  - #61131: `LockTimeoutError` from concurrent installs of the same plugin.
  - #63816: another case of a stuck plugin missing from `/api/plugin` while activation hangs.
  - #64408 (closed): a plugin activation timeout was rejected, so the fix probably belongs in the install step. For example, run git with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `GCM_INTERACTIVE=never` and fail fast.

prs.title: fix(browser): show saved tabs at once when the app reopens, and hold them while they load
prs.body:
Quit the app with browser tabs open in a session's side panel and open it again. On `dev` the strip has no browser tab until the desktop has attached to the session's server. Then each tab draws its address, then Chromium's name for the page while it loads, then its title. Tabs are as wide as their label, so every change resizes the tab and moves the tabs after it.

- **Now:** from the first frame after the reopen until every restored page has loaded, each restored tab keeps its box: same x, same width, same label, same icon. Only the page area changes.
- **Overlap:** #64742 (main keeps its saved `{ id, url }` record when a window detaches) and #63271 (retry the attach while the server's browser RPC loads) shorten or protect the wait; neither holds the strip during it. This PR does not touch `pane-machine.ts`, `restore.ts` or `ipc.ts`, and its `machine.ts` hunks are apart from #63271's.

## Per phase

One restored tab, saved as `Preview` at `http://localhost:4173/`. Widths are measured in the component fixture's strip; `808a2c4` is this PR's earlier head, which the owner rejected.

| Phase | Main sends for the tab | `dev` | `808a2c4` | Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Reopened, not attached | nothing | not drawn | `Preview`, saved icon, 87.03 px | `Preview`, saved icon, 87.03 px |
| 2. First inventory, page not loaded | `title: ""` | the address, globe | `Preview`, 87.03 px | `Preview`, 87.03 px |
| 3. Page committed, still loading | before: `title: "localhost:4173"`, no icon. Now: `title: ""`, no icon | `localhost:4173`, globe | `localhost:4173`, globe, **126.52 px**; the next tab moves **39.48 px** | `Preview`, saved icon, 87.03 px |
| 3b. Committed where the address redirected | `title: ""`, the new address | the new address | the new address, **192.23 px** | `Preview`, saved icon, 87.03 px |
| 4. Title parsed, icon loaded, stopped | `title: "Preview"`, the icon | `Preview`, icon | `Preview`, icon, 87.03 px | `Preview`, icon, 87.03 px |
| A tab never selected (its page never loads) | `title: ""` for good | its address | `Docs`, 69.59 px | `Docs`, saved icon, 69.59 px |
| The server has no browser | closes the binding, `unsupported` | not listed | a loader with no end | same box; "The browser couldn't open", Try again |

Red lines mark each tab's left and right edge, with its measured x and width.

| | `808a2c4` | Now |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Reopened | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8609c541-4eda-408c-967b-dc8eed582349) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a965c8bb-b750-4617-8301-9d981e2638ac) |
| 2. Attached | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab735765-9fb5-4ae3-8f7c-4959d219985d) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fdc68810-5f0c-492d-984b-292302e69195) |
| 3. Loading | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28dd1bbd-8488-4b70-a3e7-f29e3b6f4437) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa8b3a87-dedb-4bd0-9eb7-49d040927c83) |
| 4. Loaded | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5c4c379-9e69-49d9-9048-981596dae675) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b4d4f19-c692-4fcf-b772-8f8572a7fca8) |

The whole restore, now:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a3e16d9c-e8f7-40cf-b9f1-a76c4a5baff4

On `dev`, reopened and then attached: ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b35480c-47db-4d03-88c1-9f9aa258f693) ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d7408b47-afc5-4c03-9702-c138b6595fba)

## Cause

- **Nothing to draw:** the window had the tab ids, their order and the selection (`Layout.stored`), but a stored tab stayed `hidden` until the model's chunk had loaded and main's inventory named it (`renderer.tsx:522` and `model-machine.ts:84` on `dev`), and its title came only from that inventory. Main saves `{ id, url }` (`restore.ts:11`) and restores with `title: ""` (`pane-machine.ts:488`).
- **The width change:** a restored page is a document with no origin, so its first commit was never "the same site" and took Chromium's name for the page as its title (`page-machine.ts:251`, fed by `contents.getTitle()` at `chromium.ts:782`). In real Electron that is `127.0.0.1:52433/saved` until the `<title>` parses. The label drew any non-empty title, in a content-sized `max-w-40 truncate` span.
- **Left the strip:** `sessionTabs` returned `[]` outside `sessionPending` (`machine.ts:397-400`): in backoff, or while the server had no browser yet.

## Fix

- **Main:** a restored document keeps the title it was restored with through its first commit, as a navigation on the same site already does, until it names itself or stops loading.

  ```ts
  // page-machine.ts, committed()
  title: same || state.status === "restoring" ? state.title : event.title,
  ```

- **Saved tabs:** a window store `tabs` (`Store.global`, loaded before setup) keeps each session's `{ id, url, title?, icon? }` from every inventory and page icon (`saved-tabs.ts`; icons bounded as in the history).
- **Label:** the page's own title, else the saved one at the same address or while the tab loads. The page's own icon, else the saved one on the same site. An empty title or a missing icon never replaces a saved one.
- **Strip:** a saved tab is not `hidden`, and `Panel.list` keeps the stored ids until an inventory names the desktop's tabs, so the same tab objects stay and no trigger remounts.
- **Content, every wait ends:** a `Loader` only while an inventory is on its way (registering, the Ipc starting, the first 4 retries). After that, or when the server has no browser, the existing "The browser couldn't open" view with Try again (`session.retry`); the retries go on behind it. A paused pane says so. The tabs keep their box in each state.
- **Before the attach:** the attachment machine remembers a saved tab the person closed or picked (`strip.dismissed`, `strip.selected`) and sends `tabs.close` or `tabs.focus` with the first inventory that has it.

## Unchanged

- A session with no saved tabs, the web app, and a pane that was closed at quit.
- A session another window took, one the server lacks, and one on a server whose version does not work with this app list no tabs, as before.

## Tested

| | On `808a2c4` | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| `browser-pane-restore.spec.ts` "holds every restored tab's box, label and icon…" | fails: `Preview` becomes the redirected address, 87.03 → 192.23 px | Ipc pending, inventory with the titles main sends, loading, commit at a redirected address without title or icon, title, icon, loaded, and a tab never selected. At every step: x, width, label and icon of all three tabs equal the first frame, and the tab elements are the same nodes |
| same file, "a restored tab on a server without a browser…" | fails: loader with no end | the view, Try again, the boxes |
| `electron-restore.test.ts` (real Electron, a page whose title arrives late) | fails: publishes `127.0.0.1:…/saved` | a restored page publishes `Saved title`, or none, then `Real title` |
| `page-machine.test.ts`, `machine.test.ts`, `saved-tabs.test.ts` | fail | the commit rule; listing, pending, unavailable and retry in every binding state; close and pick before the first inventory; titles, icons, pruning, a stored record without title or icon |

## Limits

- **First launch after the update:** nothing is saved yet. The tabs appear with the first inventory, as on `dev`, each drawn by its address; a tab changes once, to its title, when its page has loaded.
- **A redirect to another site during the restore:** the title holds, the icon is the globe until the new site's icon arrives. The icon slot has one size, so nothing moves.
- **A page that changed its title, or has none:** the label changes once, when the page says so or stops loading.
- **A page that asks for the person, or a tab the agent used:** the dot beside the label adds its width, as before. A restore does not raise it.
- **A cold start that attaches before the server has loaded its browser** shows "The browser couldn't open" until the server reports its plugins, then opens by itself. #63271 turns that into retries, which wait with the loader.
- **Not run:** the whole app in a real Electron window. The real-Electron test covers one restored page, not the pane's attach. The component fixture draws the strip with content-sized buttons, not the host's trigger; the host is untouched.

No feature flag: a fix.

prs.title: feat(core): opt-in sqlite full-text index of session history
prs.body:
Adds an opt-in SQLite FTS5 index of session history that SQLite keeps current itself, plus a one-time background build over existing history. Off by default in every build: `experimental.sqlite_fts: true` or `OPENCODE_FLAGS=sqlite_fts` (an opt-in-only flag, like `todo`). This PR only builds and maintains the index. Nothing queries it yet: the search API (ranked results, excerpts, cursors), its endpoint, tools and a progress UI come in follow-ups.

Public API added: the `sqlite_fts` flag. Nothing else in HTTP, the SDK or plugins. The index lives in `opencode.db` as `session_search*` tables, a view and triggers, created at runtime when the flag is first on.

### Problem

Agents can't search past sessions. Scanning history without an index takes minutes per search on a large database (~2.5 min on a 37.5 GB one), so search needs an index that stays current without app code having to remember to update it on every write path.

### Change

```text
sqlite_fts on in a loaded location
  (the server forks SessionSearchBuild.run next to Automation.run, where it waits; a small internal config
   plugin calls build.start once a loaded location's flags have it on, so global config turns it on everywhere.
   Config is per location, so this plugin is how a per-location flag starts one database-wide job; it goes away
   with the flag, when the server just starts the build)
  ─► ensure (once): pick a layout for this SQLite, create the FTS5 table, the source view and triggers
       SQLite 3.43+ ─► compact: contentless, contentless_delete      (163 MB on a 37.5 GB DB)
       older        ─► text: FTS5 over session_search_document text  (352 MB) e.g. macOS 13, 14.0-14.1
       no FTS5 / JSON functions ─► unsupported, nothing created
  ─► one-time build in the background (never blocks readiness), like the V1 import:
       newest first, <= 50 messages and <= 1 MiB stored bytes per transaction, cursor in kv,
       resumes after restart, waits out SQLITE_BUSY, skips rows that fail alone, records done/failed
  ─► afterwards SQLite maintains it: source triggers reindex changed rows directly from the
       session_search_source view (and delete triggers remove entries directly)
flag turned off mid-build ─► the build keeps going until done or the process exits; the next process with the
  flag off doesn't start it, and it resumes from its cursor once the flag is on again. The index and triggers stay.
```

Indexed: session titles, user text, finished assistant text (part rows, then inline), completed compaction summaries, each capped at 64 KiB. Never indexed: tool calls and output, reasoning, files, synthetic/system/skill messages, running or failed compactions. Every message type is listed as indexed or not, so a new type fails typecheck until decided. Tokenizer `porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`, plus ASCII folding for letters it leaves alone (`đ->d`, `ł->l`, `ø->o`, `ß->ss`, `æ->ae`, `œ->oe`, `þ->th`, ..., as Lucene's `asciifolding` does), so "hoa don" finds "hóa đơn". The follow-up query has to fold its words the same way.

```text
packages/core/src/session/search-index.ts          # layouts, view, triggers, ensure, build chunks, state
packages/core/src/session/search-build.ts          # one-time background build
packages/core/src/config/plugin/session-search.ts  # starts the build once a location has the flag on (temporary, goes with the flag)
packages/server/src/process.ts                     # forks the build next to Automation.run
packages/schema/src/config/flag.ts                 # sqlite_fts, opt-in only
packages/schema/src/session-message.ts             # notes on fields read by search-index.ts SQL
```

### Trade-offs and behavior to know about

Things that are true once someone has opted in:

- **Turning the flag off doesn't remove anything.** It only keeps a not-yet-started build from starting on the next run. The triggers keep indexing every write, and there's no command to drop the index yet; today that takes manual SQL.
- **Writes cost more.** Measured on a copy of a 37.5 GB database (19,587 sessions, 703,859 messages): user message +0.05 ms, streaming assistant +0 ms (skipped until finished), finishing a 200 KB assistant +1.3 ms, deleting a 1,370-message session 4.8 -> 22.3 ms. Bulk writes (imports, forks, large project deletes) pay proportionally more.
- **A corrupt index breaks session writes.** If the FTS tables get corrupted, writes that touch indexed rows fail until the index is removed by hand. Planned follow-up before default-on: when a session write fails with `SQLITE_CORRUPT` and search triggers exist, drop them, mark the index failed and retry the write once; the next start rebuilds the index from scratch.
- **Migrations keep triggers attached.** Normal migrations (`CREATE TABLE`, `ADD COLUMN`, `DROP COLUMN` on unindexed columns, data updates) leave the index and `done` state untouched. A future migration that drops and renames `session_v2`, `session_message`, or `session_part` must drop the `session_search*` objects and clear `kv['session.search']` so `ensure` rebuilds cleanly; the migration replay test (`PRAGMA legacy_alter_table = OFF`) fails CI if forgotten.
- **It's one index for the whole database**, not per project; project filtering belongs to the follow-up query.
- **Index gaps:** forks re-index copied `session_part` text once per copied part, assistants that never finish are never indexed, and CJK text isn't split into words by `unicode61`.
- **Progress is only in the logs** (`session search build started/finished`, skipped rows), until the follow-up adds a status API.
- **Failed builds:** three consecutive non-busy failures (disk full, I/O) mark the build failed; a later process retries it once.
- **Changing what's indexed needs a `Version` bump**, enforced by a SHA-256 test over the `sqlite_master` SQL of both layouts.
- **Tables are created at runtime, not in a migration**, because the index is flag-gated and the layout depends on the machine's SQLite.
- **Durable Objects:** nothing forks the build there, so it never runs.

### Measured (29.2 GB compacted copy of a 37.5 GB `opencode.db`: 19.6k sessions, 704k messages)

| | |
|---|---|
| Index size | 162.6 MB compact (0.55% of DB) / 352 MB text |
| One-time build (compact, SQLite 3.51) | 227 s wall (105 s of it is 5 ms pauses), chunk p50 4.4 ms / p99 16.8 ms / max 47.6 ms, event-loop lag p99 13.7 ms / max 43.8 ms, 0 skipped |
| One-time build (text, forced) | 310 s wall, chunk p99 66.9 ms / max 583 ms |
| Extra cost per write, compact (p50) | user message 0.02 -> 0.07 ms, finishing a 200 KB assistant 0.25 -> 1.55 ms, deleting a 1,370-message session 4.8 -> 22.3 ms |
| Search latency, compact (p50, `bm25` top 20) | rare word 0.04 ms, phrase 1.4 ms, 3-word OR 14.5 ms, common word (23k hits) 24 ms |
| Agent benchmark: 27 questions x 12 models | 93.7% pass, 18k median tokens, vs 91.5% / 31k for a no-index search and 57% / 99k for a page-by-page scan |

### Verification

- `bun run check`, `packages/protocol` `bun run check:generated`, `packages/client` `bun run check:generated`: pass.
- `packages/core`: `bun run typecheck:tsc` and `bun run script/test.ts test/session-search-index.test.ts test/session-search-build.test.ts test/config/session-search.test.ts test/flag.test.ts test/database-migration.test.ts`: pass (also 10x randomized reruns). Covers both layouts across edits, renames, reverts and cascade deletes (verifying session delete skips per-part re-indexing), streaming assistants indexed once finished, every message type decided, SQL hash pinned to `Version`, every migration since `session_part` with `legacy_alter_table = OFF`, `SQLITE_BUSY` retry during `ensure`, cursor resume, failed-build retry, ASCII folding, byte cap and skipped rows.
- Tested across compiled SQLite 3.32.3, 3.37.0, 3.39.4 (with and without FTS5), 3.42.0, 3.43.0, 3.47.2, 3.51.0, and 3.54.1, plus Node 25 (`node:sqlite`).
- Not run on Windows in PR CI (`unit (windows)` runs after merge to `dev`).

prs.title: feat(browser): import browsing history and complete the address bar from it
prs.body:
## What a person gets - An import from another browser now brings its **browsing history** with its sign-ins: Chromium family, Firefox family, Safari. - The address bar completes from it and from pages opened in OpenCode: `rune` finds `github.com/anomalyco/rune-desktop`, `anom rune` finds it too, `gith` completes `github.com`. - **Clear history** and **Sign out everywhere** remove all of it. One switch, Settings › Browser › Advanced › **Import browsing history**, turns the import off. | Typing `rune` (made-up history) | Measured | | --- | --- | | ![The address field with "rune" typed and five suggestions, github.com/anomalyco/rune-desktop first](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d3f52bbb-d25a-4d27-a2f2-d4f89112b72a) | ![The same drop-down with red guide lines: icons, row edges and text columns have 0 px drift](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d8b58d8-73ec-4f58-b0ad-e5a6204ad0f3) | | Import dialog, before | Import dialog, after | | --- | --- | | ![Copies cookies for all 12 sites. The other browser keeps its own.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16894b2d-157f-4fa9-a0f3-4d618c16ceae) | ![Copies cookies for 12 sites and your history. Nothing is removed.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e4a7d8d1-6780-4832-8e6b-100197829696) | ![Imported 10 cookies and 4,210 pages from Google Chrome](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23a121f0-6cd6-435e-ab3b-d6de3913e829) - The dialog keeps its size and one line. The sentence with history is shorter than the old one plus "and history", which wrapped at 430 px. - The drop-down row is unchanged. Imported pages have no icon: the globe stands in, and none is fetched. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph window field[address field] -->|"input: ask(attempt, text)"| machine[address-machine.ts] list[last 30 pages
new tab page, icons] --> machine machine -->|suggestions| dropdown[drop-down] end subgraph main ipc[["Ipc browser.history
prepare · search · visit · retitle · remove · clear"]] --> store[(history.sqlite
one row per page)] store --> index[in-memory index
search text per page] profile[profile import] -->|"readHistory → add"| store end machine -->|"search(text, 8)"| ipc ipc -->|"answered(attempt, pages)"| machine other[(other browser
History · places.sqlite · History.db)] -->|private copy, deleted after the read| profile ``` - **Store** (`browser/history/store.ts`): `/browser-history/history.sqlite` through `node:sqlite`, in the main process only. One row per page: host without `www.`, path without a trailing slash, query and fragment, so `http`/`https`, `www.` and a trailing slash are one row. At most 50,000 pages; past that the least visited and oldest go. - **Index** (`history/search.ts`): the first focus of the address field reads every page into memory as one search text per page. A keystroke is one pass over it, no database read. Opening the store reads nothing, and a visit before the first search only writes its row. - **Window**: the list of the last 30 pages stays, for the new tab page and for icons, and answers at once. Main takes it over once, the first time the store opens (`history/earlier.ts`), so no visit is lost. - **A keystroke never waits**: each change of the text takes the next attempt number, and `answered` with any other number returns the same state. The previous answer stays, matched against the new text, so the list narrows instead of blinking. ```ts case "answered": { if (state.status !== "editing" || event.attempt !== state.asked) return unchanged(state) ``` ### What is imported | Browser | File, table | Read | Left behind | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Chromium family | `History`, `urls` | `url`, `title`, `visit_count`, `typed_count`, `last_visit_time` (µs since 1601) | `hidden` rows, rows never visited | | Firefox family | `places.sqlite`, `moz_places` | `url`, `title`, `visit_count`, `typed`, `last_visit_date` (µs since 1970) | `hidden` places, bookmarks never visited; `frecency` is not read, its meaning changed in Firefox 147 | | Safari | `History.db`, `history_items` ⋈ `history_visits` | `url`, `visit_count`, latest visit's `title` and `visit_time` (s since 2001) | needs Full Disk Access, as its cookies do; without it, 0 pages and no error | - Every read goes through `snapshotDatabase`: a private copy, deleted after the read. The other browser's files are never written or locked. - A missing column reads as a default (`PRAGMA table_info`); a value of the wrong type reads as no title, no visit or no time. - **Choose sites** limits history to the chosen sites, with the same filter as cookies. **Import all** brings the whole history, up to 50,000 pages: the most used and most recent. - History never fails an import: one that cannot be read is 0 pages, and the result names only what came. ### Matching and ranking 1. Every typed word must be in the address or the title, case-insensitively. 2. Words that all start a word, a host label or a path segment rank before words found only inside a longer word. 3. Then `log2(1 + visits + typed) × recency`: recency is 1 for the last 4 days and falls to 0.7 at 14 days, 0.5 at 31, 0.3 at 90 and 0.1 at a year. 4. Text that begins a host also brings that site's front page, scored with the sum of the site's pages that begin so. When it leads, it is the inline completion. | Taken from | What | | --- | --- | | Chrome (`ScoredHistoryMatch`, `HistoryURLProvider`) | Word-boundary matches beat mid-word ones. The recency curve above. Typed visits weigh more (1.5× there; a typed visit counts twice here). Frequency saturates (the last 10 visits there; a logarithm here). A typed host prefix promotes the host itself. Duplicates collapse by scheme, `www.` and trailing slash. `hidden` rows stay out. | | Firefox (Places frecency) | One number per page from frequency and recency buckets (100/70/50/30/10 at 4/14/31/90 days). All words must match, at a boundary first, then anywhere. Origin autofill scores an origin by the sum of its pages. Bookmarks never visited are not history. | ## Privacy - **On this machine only**: one SQLite file in the app's profile data. Nothing sends it to a server, and no remote server's partition receives it. - **Not reachable by the agent**: the only door is the `browser.history` Ipc between a window and main. `packages/plugin-browser`, the pane and its RPC are untouched, so no browser tool lists or searches it and no tool result carries it. - **Never stored**: addresses that are not `http(s)`, addresses with a user name or password, addresses over 2,048 characters. Titles are cut to 200 characters. - **Clearing leaves nothing in the file**: `secure_delete`, then `VACUUM` and a truncating checkpoint. A test reads the bytes. - The other browser's private windows never reach its files, so nothing of them is read. ## Measured Pinned Electron 44.9.1 (V8 15.2, SQLite 3.53.4) on Windows, a 50,000-page store of made-up pages, three process runs. `dev` has no store to compare with: it searches 30 visits in the window. | | 50,000 pages | | --- | --- | | Search in main, 10 queries × 200 runs | median 1.2–6.1 ms per query, worst single run 8.7 ms | | … `gith` / `rune` / `anom rune` / `e` / no match | 2.4 / 4.7 / 4.5 / 6.0 / 1.2 ms | | Open the store | 1.3 ms | | Record a visit | 0.02 ms | | First read into memory, once per run, on focusing the address field | 143–149 ms | | Import 50,000 rows: read a copy of a Chromium `History` + write | 140–142 ms + 307–324 ms = 449–464 ms | | Store file, index in memory | 12.4 MB, about 15 MB | ## Changed on purpose - **Enter on a phrase searches.** On `dev`, typed text that reads as a search preselects the first match, so Enter opens it. With 50,000 pages nearly every word matches something, and Enter would stop searching. Now only an address that begins with the typed text is preselected; a step down chooses a match. - **Sign out everywhere** also clears the history, in main and in the window. - The offer bar and card say "sign-ins and history" while history import is on. - **Shift+Delete** forgets the chosen suggestion. ## Unchanged - The drop-down row, its 5 rows and its styles; the new tab page's recent pages; deleting never completes. - The cookie import, its results and its messages for locked, protected and failed cookies. - `packages/core`, `server`, `protocol`, `schema`, `plugin`, `plugin-browser`, `desktop`: no change. In `packages/app` only tests changed. ## Limits and follow-ups - **No feature flag**: the GUI SDK still gives a plugin no way to read `Flag.enabled`; the only gate it has is `ctx.app.channel`. - **Not run**: Safari on macOS (reader built from the documented schema and a fixture), Chromium and Firefox profiles on macOS and Linux, and the feature inside a running desktop window. Real `History` (version 70, Edge and Helium) and `places.sqlite` schemas were checked on Windows from private copies. - An import writes its rows in one synchronous transaction in main: about 0.3 s for 50,000. - The store is a plain SQLite file, as other browsers keep theirs. It is not encrypted at rest. - Visits made in OpenCode are not marked as typed yet. - Shift+Delete on a site's front-page row: the row returns while other pages of the site remain. - A restored tab counts one visit when it loads. ## Tests - `history/store.test.ts`: the ranking table (`rune`, `anom rune`, `gith`, …), one row per page, the 50,000 cap, clear leaves no bytes, the one-time takeover of the window's list and its storage keys, no read of a full history before the first search. - `history/match.test.ts`: which addresses are kept (schemes, credentials, length) and their keys. - `profile/history.test.ts`: each reader against a database built with the browser's own `CREATE TABLE`: filters, damaged rows, missing columns, chosen sites, the 50,000 cap. - `address-machine.test.ts`: late, stale and failed answers, answers after the edit ended, completion, Shift+Delete. - `profile/electron-import.test.ts`: the read, the store and a search in the pinned Electron's SQLite. - Component specs: the drop-down with a seeded history (story `plugins-browser--imported-history`), the dialog's one line, the result line, the Settings switch.

prs.title: feat(core): machine keys and one-use join strings
prs.body:
**The server can now invite another computer with a one-use join string, and remember that computer by its own key.**
Core only: no network code, no endpoint, no command. Nothing calls it yet, so nothing changes for anyone. The callers arrive with the encrypted link, behind the `machines` flag. Builds on #64997 (the machine list).

💡 **Why**
Today the machine list serves whatever connection it is handed and believes the name in its hello. Before a real worker can dial in over a network, three facts have to exist: who the home is, who each machine is, and a way to introduce one to the other exactly once.

🆕 **What it adds**

```ts
machines.invite("gpu", { reach: [{ type: "url", url: "https://…" }] })
// → "ocjoin_eyJ2IjoxLCJob21lIjoi…"   one use, five minutes

machines.join({ secret, key })   // the worker presents the secret and its public key → "gpu"
machines.identify(key)           // every later connection → "gpu"
machines.list()                  // each machine now says whether it is paired
```

- **A key for the home.** A 32-byte Ed25519 seed in a file only the user can read, outside the database. It is created the first time a machine is invited, never at startup, and never regenerated: every paired machine trusts it. Like `ssh`, a key file other users can read is refused, with the `chmod` to run.
- **A key per machine.** One new nullable column on the `machine` table, unique when set.
- **A join string**, `ocjoin_<base64url(JSON)>`: the home's public key, a one-use secret, an expiry, and a list of ways to reach the home. A worker can check it is talking to the right home before it sends the secret. Ways to reach the home that a worker does not recognise are dropped, not rejected, so new carriers can be added later.
- **The home picks the name.** The secret is bound to the name it was issued for; the worker never chooses.
- **Only a hash of the secret is kept**, in memory, one pending invitation per name. A second invite replaces the first; removing the machine cancels it.
- **Every refused join is the same error**, whatever the reason.

It does not reuse the existing device pairing, which hands out sessions on the server; a worker's join string must never be able to do that.

🚦 **How it ships:** unreachable until the link calls it. Building the server does nothing new: no file is written and the existing single query gains one column.

```diff
+ invite "gpu"   -> secret made, its hash kept for 5 minutes; join string returned
+ join(secret, key), all under the name's lock:
+     still the current invitation for that name?  not expired?  not already paired (unless replace)?
+     key not on another machine?   -> key saved; the secret is spent whether or not this succeeded
+ identify(key)  -> the machine's name, from memory
```

📊 **Proof**

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Join string round trip; a fixed string decodes to fixed values (a vector for the worker) | ✅ |
| Wrong prefix, version, key or secret length, over 4,096 characters, sloppy base64url, a nonsense expiry | ✅ all rejected |
| A way to reach the home that this build does not know | ✅ dropped, the others kept |
| Home key: created on first use with mode 600; same key after a rebuild; a signature verifies | ✅ |
| Home key truncated, or readable by other users | ✅ refused with the reason, file untouched |
| A failed key load, then the file fixed | ✅ works without a restart |
| Same secret twice; expired; wrong | ✅ the same error each time |
| A second invite, or removing the machine, while the first join string is out | ✅ the first no longer works |
| A join already in flight when the name is re-invited or removed | ✅ exactly one key lands; the removed name pairs nothing |
| Inviting a paired machine | ✅ refused without `replace`; with it, the old key stops identifying the machine once the new one joins |
| One key on two machines | ✅ refused |
| Keys after a rebuild on the same database | ✅ still identify their machines |

Each test that guards a property fails with the property broken.

👀 **Read:** `invite` and `join` in `machine/machines.ts`, about 45 lines: everything `join` decides is decided inside the name's lock, and `invite` does not pause between its checks and registering the secret. Then `load` in `machine/identity.ts`. Two things are left as they are, with a comment where it matters: two different names presenting the same key at the same instant are stopped by the unique index and that call fails as an internal error instead of the uniform one (the link will turn every failure into one refusal); and pending invitations, like the list itself, are per process.

<sub>🔍 First of four pieces of pairing a computer with the server · no user reports · an independent security review before the first push reproduced six problems (two races between invite and join, key file permissions, a cached failure, a runtime-only API, a loose decoder); all fixed here</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `bun typecheck` in `packages/core`: clean; oxlint and prettier on the changed files: clean
- `test/machine-join.test.ts`, `test/machines.test.ts`, `test/machine.test.ts`, `test/machine-path.test.ts`, `test/machine-instructions.test.ts`: 134 pass
- `bun script/migration.ts --check`: no changes; `check:generated` in `packages/client` and `packages/protocol`: no diff

</details>

prs.title: fix(ai): stop empty Gemini replies after a session moves to the Interactions API
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR No linked issue. Reported internally: Gemini 4 Neon sessions accept a message, then go idle with no reply. ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? `recommended_api` moved `gemini-4-neon` from generateContent to the Interactions API. A session that began on generateContent then gets empty replies: the step ends with `finish: stop` and nothing is shown. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["generateContent stores
thoughtSignature"] --> B["Interactions request reads
only interactionSignature"] B --> C["209 of 210 tool calls sent with
skip_thought_signature_validator"] C --> D["Gemini: status completed,
one thought step, no output"] D --> E["recorded as a
successful empty reply"] ``` - **Signatures follow the conversation to Interactions.** Each generateContent signature moves to the `thought` step before the part that carried it, which is the shape Interactions returns itself. - **A `completed` response with no output is a retryable `incomplete-stream` error.** generateContent ends the same generation with `MALFORMED_RESPONSE`, which already retries. - **The switch back keeps signatures too.** An Interactions signature moves to the generateContent part after the thinking. ```diff // stored by a generateContent step { type: "tool", name: "shell", native: { thoughtSignature: "EvQD…" } } // sent to Interactions - { type: "function_call", name: "shell", signature: "skip_thought_signature_validator" } + { type: "thought", signature: "EvQD…" } + { type: "function_call", name: "shell" } ``` The Interactions route only runs under the `recommended_api` flag, so this adds no flag. Not fixed here: a history with no signatures at all (after a model switch) still gets these empty generations from Gemini, and no placeholder signature changes that. It now shows as a retried error instead of silence. ### How did you verify your code works? Live `gemini-4-neon`; each cell is replies with output / attempts. `dev` and this branch ran as isolated servers behind a recording proxy, on forks of the real sessions that went silent. | | dev | this PR | |---|---|---| | Session A: a follow-up after 191 generateContent steps | 0/5 | 6/6 | | Session B: the question that got 3 empty replies in a row | 0/6 | 6/6 | | 6 other prompts in sessions B, C and D, where dev also replies | 25/25 | 28/28 | | Session A's 325k-token request sent directly, signatures dropped vs kept, 4 thinking levels | 12/41 | 30/30 | | New Interactions session: 142 steps, 154 tool calls, up to 480k tokens | | 0 empty | | That session switched back to generateContent, 122 signatures carried | 13/13 | 10/10 | | A captured empty `completed` injected by the proxy | empty reply, idle | 2 retries, then the answer | Unit tests cover both lowerings and the empty `completed`. ### Screenshots / recordings ![Replies with output, before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4c3f3578-0f77-4931-a8f5-31678ad8c40d) ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR --- _Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._ Related: #55378

The `models` tool hides older versions of a model family unless `all` is set. prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

I wrapped shell, subagent, Code Mode, image, and video results in one tag. Each kind keeps its original attributes and body. I escape opening and closing tags for both `<background-result>` and `<system-update>` in the body.

```diff
- <subagent sessionID="ses_child" state="running" description="Run tests">
+ <background-result kind="subagent" sessionID="ses_child" state="running" description="Run tests">
  Started tests

  Background work still running:
  - shell (sh_1): bun test
- </subagent>
+ </background-result>
```

prs.title: feat(core): rotate Claude Agent accounts with selectable strategies
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #60793

Builds on #62514, which is still a draft. Its commit is kept as-is, with its authorship, and rebased onto current `dev`.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`settings.configDir` on the `claude-agent` provider takes one Claude Code config folder or a list. With a list, a request refused by a subscription limit before any output retries on the next folder. That part is #62514. On top of it:

- **Limit memory.** A limit refusal reports `resetsAt` in its `rate_limit_event`. The folder is stored as limited until then and skipped, so later requests don't spend a failed attempt on it first. If every folder is limited, they are all still tried, so the user sees Claude's own error.
- **`settings.strategy`** picks the folder a request starts on:

| Strategy | New chats | Existing chats |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ordered` (default) | First folder with room left | Stay on their folder until it hits a limit |
| `ordered-strict` | First folder with room left | Go back to an earlier folder as soon as it resets |
| `round-robin` | Next folder in turn | Stay on their folder until it hits a limit |

- Round-robin turns are stored per list of folders. This replaces the single `last-account` key, which models with different lists kept overwriting for each other (the bot pointed this out on #62508).
- An unknown `strategy` falls back to `ordered`, the same way `configDir` skips values it can't use. Throwing inside the `sdk` hook would break every request on the provider.

Moving a chat to a folder it hasn't used before resends the whole conversation as a checkpoint, without the prompt cache. Moving it back to a folder it used before resumes that transcript and only catches up the turns it missed, because records are already kept per session and folder. That is what makes `ordered-strict` affordable.

Also updates two tests from #62514 that expected compaction to stop the chat's Claude process, which #63025 removed.

No feature flag: nothing changes unless `configDir` is a list.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `test/plugin/provider/claude-agent/claude/accounts.test.ts`: new cases for skipping a limited folder, each strategy, a strict chat returning after the reset, and round-robin turns kept per list. With the strict branch disabled, its test fails.

- Running it locally with two subscription logins. I haven't hit a real limit with it yet, so the fallback itself is only covered by the replayed tests.

prs.title: feat(core): auto-update @latest, range and Git branch plugins
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Follows https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64764

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Since https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64764, a plugin written as `name@latest` updates itself: checked on startup and every 24 hours, installed, then hot reloaded, with the previous version kept if the new one fails to load. This PR extends that to the other targets that say what to follow: a version range, a Git branch and a Git `semver:` range. Every other target behaves as before.

```diff
 plugin                                            stays on the installed version
 plugin@latest                                     updates itself
-plugin@^1.2.0, @~1.2.0, @1.x, @>=1.2.0 <2         notify only
+plugin@^1.2.0, @~1.2.0, @1.x, @>=1.2.0 <2         updates itself, within the range
 plugin@next (other tags)                          notify only
 plugin@1.2.0                                      pinned
 github:acme/plugin (no ref)                       stays on the installed commit
-github:acme/plugin#main, #main::path:pkg          notify only
+github:acme/plugin#main, #main::path:pkg          updates itself
 github:acme/plugin#v1.2.0 (tag)                   notify only
-github:acme/plugin#semver:^1.0.0                  notify only
+github:acme/plugin#semver:^1.0.0                  updates itself, within the range
 github:acme/plugin#<short or full hash>           pinned
```

"Stays" and "notify only" both mean the plugin doesn't update itself. `plugin check` still reports a newer version and `plugin update` still installs it.

**A range never leaves its constraint.** `Npm.check` asks pacote for the newest version that satisfies the spec, and `Npm.update` installs the spec with Arborist, so `^1.2.0` can move to `1.9.0` but not to `2.0.0`. A Git `semver:` range resolves to the newest matching tag the same way.

**How a plugin qualifies.** The supervisor used to filter with `target.endsWith("@latest")`. It now asks a new `Npm.follows(target)` once per interval, for plugins whose check found a newer version:

- Registry and Git range targets are decided from the spec `Npm` already parses with npm-package-arg: `@latest` written out, a range written out (a bare name parses as `*`, so it's excluded), or a Git `semver:` range.
- A Git ref such as `#main` could be a branch or a tag. Only the remote knows, so `Npm.follows` resolves the spec with pacote's `GitFetcher` and reads the ref type pacote already records (`resolvedRef.type === "branch"`). The update check runs `git ls-remote` just before this, and `@npmcli/git` keeps that ref list for 5 minutes, so this normally doesn't contact the remote again. A tag, a short hash or a pull ref isn't a branch, so it doesn't qualify. `::path:` subdirectories don't affect the ref.

There's no new setting, and core doesn't parse specs itself.

Unchanged: one attempt per plugin per 24-hour interval (from https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65056), rollback when a new version fails to load, and disabled plugins aren't checked.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/core/test/npm.test.ts`:
  - A table for `Npm.follows` that covers bare, `@latest`, `@next`, the four range forms, an exact version, Git with no ref, a `::path:` without a ref, a full hash and `semver:`. It also covers a local repository's branch, the branch with `::path:`, a tag and a short hash, resolved through pacote.
  - "updates a range only within it": with `1.0.0` installed from `^1.0.0` and `2.0.0` published as `latest`, update installs `1.1.0`, and the next check finds nothing newer.
- `packages/core/test/plugin/supervisor.test.ts`: `@latest`, a range and a Git branch install once per interval, and again at the next interval's scheduled check. A bare name, `@next` and a Git repository without a ref don't install, even though their checks report a newer version. The 24-hour check regression test is unchanged.
- Both files passed 5 runs in a row. All of `packages/core/test/plugin/` plus `test/npm.test.ts` pass (654 tests). `bun typecheck` passes in `packages/util`, `packages/core` and `packages/server`, and `bun run check` passes from the root.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR


---
<!-- opencode-github-bot:pr-section -->
_Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._

Public API: npm range, Git branch and Git `semver:` range plugins now auto-update instead of only reporting an update (behaviour change; pin an exact version or commit to opt out)

prs.title: feat(app): support building the web app under a base path
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #7624

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Lets the web app be built to run under a path prefix, e.g. behind a reverse proxy at `https://host/opencode/`:

```sh
bun --cwd packages/app build --base=/opencode/
```

It uses Vite's own [`base`](https://vite.dev/config/shared-options#base) option, from the CLI flag or the config. There's no new env var.

Picks up the idea from #18209 (thanks @Ark-kun), ported to `dev`, where a straight port would break the PWA and the routes:

- **Vite `base`:** the icons plugin (manifest, favicons) and the service worker (through vite-plugin-pwa's `configureOptions`) read the resolved `base`. A small plugin adds the trailing slash if it's missing, so `--base=/opencode` works too.
- **Routing:** Solid Router's own `base` leaves the prefix in `useLocation().pathname` (under `base="/opencode"`, `navigate(useLocation().pathname)` goes to `/opencode/opencode/...`), which breaks every place that compares or navigates to it (current route, tabs, cursor hash nav, titlebar history…). Builds with a base use a small `BasePathRouter` that maps browser paths to and from base-free app paths, so no call site needs to know about the prefix. Root builds keep the stock `Router`.
- **Server URL** is `location.origin + base`, so the API is reached through the same prefix.
- **PWA:** service worker registered at `${base}sw.js` (so its scope is the base), `navigateFallback` and the denylist get the prefix, the manifest's `id`/`start_url`/`scope`/icons get it, and PWA route restore strips and adds it.
- **index.html:** the manifest link and `twitter:image` use `%BASE_URL%`, because Vite doesn't rewrite those.

The default build (no `--base`) produces the same `index.html`, `site.webmanifest` and service worker routes as before, apart from chunk hashes.

Also fixed: attachment uploads and request-queue classification assumed the API sat at the origin root (see review thread).

Not covered: the server's pairing redirect (`/auth/connect/…` → `/`) is still absolute, so pairing through a prefix needs the proxy to rewrite `Location`. That's a server-side follow-up.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Unit tests for the base path helpers, request classification under a prefix, and a `vite.icons` test that builds under `/opencode/`.
- Built with and without `--base=/opencode` and diffed the output. Under `/opencode`, `index.html`, CSS font URLs, the manifest, the SW registration and the SW fallback/denylist all carry the prefix. The root build is unchanged.
- Served the `--base=/opencode` build behind a proxy that strips the prefix, in front of a real `opencode serve`, and drove it in Chromium: home loads and calls `/opencode/api/*`, the SW registers with scope `/opencode/`, opening a new session goes to `/opencode/new-session?draftId=…` with the tab active, and back returns to `/opencode/`. No requests escape the prefix.
- `bun run typecheck` and `bun run lint:changed`. The only remaining findings are the existing `as any` and conditional spread in `vite.config.ts`.

prs.title: fix(core): cap retries when the connection drops mid-response
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Related: #59291, #64484, #56344. Follow-up to #65043, which adds diagnostics for these drops.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A connection that dies while the response is being read (ECONNRESET / EPROTO,
"Connection lost while reading the response") is almost always the network path -
a proxy, load balancer, or VPN - closing a healthy connection, usually on an idle
or read timeout. Re-running the step does not change the path, but today it
re-runs the whole step (re-billing it) up to 10 times: about 11 attempts when the
middlebox has a 60s timeout.

- cap those failures at 2 retries, the same pattern as the existing timeout cap;
  pre-request drops, read timeouts, and unreachable hosts keep their current budgets
- when a mid-response drop surfaces as the session error, name the cause and point
  at what to check: "The provider dropped the connection while sending the response.
  Check the idle or read timeout of any proxy, load balancer, or VPN on the path."

prs.title: fix(claude-agent): deliver keyed instruction updates to Claude
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #62916

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

On the claude-agent provider, system messages in the conversation history never reached Claude, so keyed instruction updates (`ctx.session.instructions.entry.put` / `remove`) were lost after the first request.

Background: the first instruction value goes into the request's system parts and becomes the Claude system prompt. Every later change is appended to history as a stored system message ("Instructions updated: ...") at the next step boundary (`message-updater.ts`). The connector skips system messages when it converts the prompt (`convert-to-claude-message.ts`) and when it fingerprints history (`fingerprint.ts`), so the update was never grouped, never detected as new, and never rendered, and the model kept the first value for the rest of the session. Putting the update back into the system prompt is not an option because changing it restarts the Claude process.

Fix: instead of special casing system messages in each of those spots, the connector turns them into user content once, at its entry (`liftInstructionUpdates` in `convert-to-claude-message.ts`, called from `claude-agent-language-model.ts`). This is safe because the only system messages OpenCode appends after the first turn come from the instruction updater, which is the single producer of `SessionMessage.System` (`message-updater.ts:157`). The leading system message(s) are the system prompt itself and are kept as system, so they still flow into `request.system` and the running process is not restarted. Once an update is a user message, the existing grouping, decide and catch-up logic carry it as a normal turn and it reaches Claude.

Why it works: a lifted update merges with the next user turn into one group, so decide returns a continue/catch-up that starts at the update, and catch-up renders it as user content. The system prompt is built from the leading system messages only, so the update never leaks into it and no restart happens.

### How did you verify your code works?

Added tests and ran them on a clean checkout of dev:

- `convert.test.ts`: `liftInstructionUpdates` turns a mid-conversation system message into a user turn and leaves the leading system prompt in place; `utility()` still returns only the leading system text; `content()` renders the update but not the system prompt. A prompt with no updates is returned unchanged. The existing "utility calls keep system instructions separate" test still passes.
- `sync.test.ts`: an end to end case that mirrors the issue's repro. After the first reply an instruction update is appended, then a new user turn arrives. `decide` returns `{ kind: "continue", start: 4 }` and `CatchUp.content` includes the update text, so it is delivered to the running process.

Full runs:
- `bun test test/plugin/provider/claude-agent`: 84 pass, 0 fail
- `turbo typecheck`: clean across all 34 tasks

I did not test against a live Claude account (the issue was also found by reading the source, not reproduced live), but the behavior is covered by the unit and sync tests above.

prs.title: fix(core): check plugins for updates every 24 hours, not every 48
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Follows https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/64764

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Plugin update checks were meant to run every 24 hours but in practice ran about every 48. The supervisor's 24-hour timer starts when plugins load, while the check cache and the `@latest` auto-update throttle each measured 24 hours from their own timestamps, which come a little later because startup, checks and installs take time. When the timer fired, slightly under 24 hours had passed by their clocks, so the cached result was reused and the update skipped until the next tick.

```diff
-PluginSupervisor: sleep 24h, then reload
-PluginUpdate.check: reuse the result if checked less than 24h ago
-@latest auto-update: skip if the last attempt was less than 24h ago
+PluginUpdate: one 24h timer numbers each interval and announces the new one
+PluginUpdate.check: reuse the result only if it was checked in the current interval
+PluginSupervisor: reload when a new interval starts
+@latest auto-update: skip if already attempted in the current interval
```

What still holds:

- Reloads within an interval reuse the checks and don't reinstall.
- The timer is shared by every location, so each target is still checked once per interval.
- `plugin check` still forces a fresh check.
- Which plugins auto-update (`name@latest` only), pinned versions and rolling back a version that fails to load are unchanged.

No CI changes.

### How did you verify your code works?

New test in `packages/core/test/plugin/supervisor.test.ts`, on the test clock, with each check taking 10 seconds:

- The `@latest` plugin installs once at startup. Another reload in the same interval makes no new checks or installs.
- Moving the clock to exactly 24 hours after startup fires the production timer, with no manual reload, and the plugin is checked and installed again.

Without the source change the test fails at that last step ("condition never became true within 15s"; it reaches the timer with 1 install and never gets a second). With it, the test passed 10 runs in a row. I also ran all of `packages/core/test/plugin/` plus `test/npm.test.ts` (652 tests), `bun typecheck` in `packages/core`, and `bun run check` from the root.

### Checklist

- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

The composer's attachment upload built `/api/experimental/fs/write` by hand: it set up the query string and auth header itself and cast the response. It now calls `client.experimental.file.write`. prs.title: fix(install): retry the download when curl cannot see /tmp
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #65044

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`curl | bash` creates the staging directory with the host shell and then hands that path to curl. A snap-confined curl bind-mounts its own `/tmp` over the host one, so the path does not exist for it: the write fails with exit 23 and the installer reports a full disk.

The download now retries in `$HOME/tmp` when curl exits 23 and `TMPDIR` is unset, after a line that names the directory it could not write. A `TMPDIR` the user set is left alone, so a full disk or a deliberate tmpfs still gets the #59312 hint. `$HOME/tmp` is removed again when the script created it, so a fallback install leaves the home directory as it found it. A normal install keeps using `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}` and never touches `$HOME/tmp`. If the retry fails too, the error names the path it actually tried and keeps curl's exit code.

The download and its non-TTY/windows fallback moved into a `download` helper so both attempts share one implementation. Nothing else changes.

### How did you verify your code works?

`bash -n install` passes.

I ran the installer end to end with a stand-in `curl` on `PATH` that cannot write into the host `/tmp` (the property a snap gives it) and a local package tarball for `cli-darwin-arm64-9.9.9.tgz`. Five cases:

- hidden `/tmp`, `TMPDIR` unset: the first write fails with 23, the retry installs from `$HOME/tmp`, `~/tmp` is gone afterwards. Exit 0.
- plain curl: installs through `/tmp` as before and never creates `$HOME/tmp`. Exit 0.
- every write failing, `TMPDIR` unset: exits 23, names `$HOME/tmp/opencode_install_<pid>`, removes the `~/tmp` it created.
- every write failing, `TMPDIR` set: exits 23, names the `TMPDIR` path, no retry and no `~/tmp`.
- `~/tmp` already exists with a file: installs, the existing directory and file are untouched.

The same harness on the current `dev` script fails the hidden-`/tmp` case with exit 23 and names `/tmp/opencode_install_<pid>`, so it is red without the change. I did not run the report's `unshare` reproduction here (macOS); the stand-in curl takes the same exit path.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none">
  <style>
    .tmp { opacity: 0; }
    .home { opacity: 1; }
    .fill { width: 168px; }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
      .tmp { animation: tmp 5s ease-in-out infinite; }
      .home { animation: home 5s ease-in-out infinite; }
      .fill { animation: fill 5s ease-in-out infinite; }
    }
```

prs.title: fix(core): skip directory watches instead of hanging when inotify is exhausted
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

When no inotify instance can be created (for example when `fs.inotify.max_user_instances` is reached), the service stops responding once a Location loads, and logs nothing. `@parcel/watcher`'s `subscribe` starts its inotify backend synchronously. When `inotify_init1` fails, the backend waits forever for a start signal that never comes. This blocks the JS thread, so `SUBSCRIBE_TIMEOUT_MS` never fires and logs never flush. The bug is still in the latest upstream release (2.6.0).

Before each inotify directory subscribe, the watcher now creates and closes an inotify instance through `bun:ffi`. If that fails, it logs a warning that names the limit and skips the watch. That reuses the existing path for an unavailable watch: the streams end and boot continues. Without Bun FFI, the check is skipped and behavior is unchanged.

### How did you verify your code works?

New Linux-only test in `watcher.test.ts` runs a child with `ulimit -n 256` that uses up its descriptors, then subscribes to a directory. This makes `inotify_init1` fail without using up the user's shared inotify budget. On `dev` the child blocks until the spawn timeout. With this change, it prints the warning and returns. `watcher.test.ts` and `file-watch.test.ts` pass, and so do `bun run check` and `typecheck:tsc` in core.

Also checked by hand with all inotify instances in use: on `dev`, a client command against the managed service hung until a 40s timeout with nothing logged. With this change, it finished in 1.5s and logged the warning.

### Screenshots / recordings

prs.title: feat(core): switch Claude Agent accounts by config folder
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Builds on #62514 (feature request #60793). Stacked on #64579, which only merges `dev`; the three commits to review are the last three.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

I have a personal and a work Claude plan and wanted to switch between them the way I can for providers whose token opencode holds. Today two saved Claude Agent accounts are identical records, because opencode holds no token for Claude, so switching changes nothing. #62514 lets config pick a folder, but that means a model alias per account and no use of the account switch.

Three commits:

1. The Claude Code login method gets an optional "Claude config folder" field, stored as credential metadata, the way the Bedrock AWS profile login stores its profile.
2. The active account's folder is used for the login check, the model list and chats when no `settings.configDir` is set. It is read per request rather than projected into provider settings, so a retry right after an account switch cannot run on the old account before a provider reload lands. A configured `settings.configDir` still wins.
3. A plan limit is raised as a quota error with the time until reset. It currently has no HTTP status and Claude Code's wording matches none of the text patterns, so it ends up as `provider.unknown` and a `session.retry` hook that switches accounts on a limit cannot recognise it. The provider's own retry hook leaves quota errors alone, since hooks run in load order and it would otherwise undo that plugin's retry.

No feature flag, same as the PR this builds on. Happy to add one, or to split commit 3 out as its own PR.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun run check` from the root, and `bun test test/plugin test/integration.test.ts test/session/to-session-error.test.ts` in `packages/core` (666 pass). New tests cover the folder following an account switch on the same model object, the quota type and its wait, and the retry hook.
- Live, on a build of these commits: connected two accounts with `auth login claude-agent --method claude-login --answer configDir=...` pointing at two real subscription logins. A chat ran in the first folder, and after `auth switch claude-agent` the next chat ran in the other, checked by where Claude Code wrote each transcript.

prs.title: fix(core): record where a dropped provider stream died
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Related: #59291, #64484, #56344, #57875.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

When a provider stream dies mid-generation, the server log only shows the raw socket error
("Failed to drain Session", ECONNRESET). The user has no way to tell where in the stream the
connection died, and that is exactly what triage of the linked issues keeps asking for
("always around 60s in?", "had output started before the reset?") - people currently count
log lines by hand.

This records it at the failure point, once per attempt:

- a `Warn` line `provider stream failed` with session, model, transport code (ECONNRESET,
  EPROTO, ...), operation (request vs read), `elapsedMs` since the attempt started, whether
  output had started, how many stream events were received, and the retry attempt number
- span `opencode.llm.stream_elapsed_ms` next to the existing `opencode.llm.first_output_ms`

So a user's log now answers "the stream lived Ns and died after M events, output had started"
for each attempt without anyone reconstructing it.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New test in packages/core/test/session-step.test.ts: drops the stream mid-generation with
  an ECONNRESET TransportError; asserts the warning carries the right context (code,
  operation, outputStarted, event count) and the step still returns its retry outcome.
- Session runner suite: 329 tests pass (6 files).
- tsc and oxlint on the touched files: clean.
