prs.title: feat(core): run OpenTUI on the shared agent loop by default
prs.body:
## What this PR does

OpenTUI now runs on the shared agent loop by default: each model round and tool batch of a live turn runs on the loop the other surfaces use. To switch back, set `"experimental": { "unifiedAgentLoop": false }` or `QWEN_CODE_ENABLE_UNIFIED_AGENT_LOOP=opentui=0`. This is OpenTUI's step 2 of #17045: the `opentui` entry of the per-surface default table turns on, next to headless, the Ink TUI and AgentCore. ACP (its own PR), speculation and the Hosted Harness keep their current loop, and the event-bus kernel stays off for every surface.

The setting's description, the settings reference, the VS Code schema and the Web Shell's Chinese text now say that both TUIs default to the shared loop, and the design docs record OpenTUI's default. The OpenTUI output tests' fake client gains the two calls the shared loop makes, so the two cases there that resolve the default now run on the shared loop.

### Intended differences

With the shared loop, an OpenTUI turn differs from before in the ways the unified-loop design lists for OpenTUI, which bring it in line with the Ink TUI:

- a call the model replays from history is answered in place instead of running again, and answers alone go out as the next round; a model that replays an answered call again is stopped as a loop;
- every tool batch is finalized, so results that together exceed the tool output budget are trimmed to it (before, only a batch the Mod tool middleware touched was);
- each completed call counts toward the session's completed tool calls, except a cancelled one and those the Mod tool middleware counted;
- a tool that ends the turn ends it, with the results in history;
- any stop reason, a detected loop included, keeps the round's calls from running;
- `experimental.eventBusAgentLoop` (off by default) now takes effect for OpenTUI on its own: before, OpenTUI ignored it unless the shared loop was also turned on; now a session with it set runs on the event-bus kernel.

OpenTUI still starts no turns of its own (no Goal continuation, background-notification or cron turns) on either loop, and a tool a slash command runs keeps the current path.

### How to switch back

Either of these keeps OpenTUI on its current loop:

- the setting `"experimental": { "unifiedAgentLoop": false }` (this turns the shared loop off for every surface);
- the environment variable `QWEN_CODE_ENABLE_UNIFIED_AGENT_LOOP=opentui=0` (OpenTUI only), or `=0` (every surface).

The current loop stays until OpenTUI's step 5, at least 14 days from this change.

## Why it's needed

#17045 opens the shared loop one surface at a time; OpenTUI's default is due 12-01. This PR is opened ahead of its date to be reviewed; it must not merge before 11-28, when every step-2 condition holds. Still pending:

- the nightly OpenTUI job with the shared loop on: it joined the nightly with #17050 (merged 11-13) and has passed every night since 11-14, so its 14 nights end on 11-27; OpenTUI's last non-fix change to its shared path is #17055 (merged 11-14), and the seven nights after it end on 11-21.

Already met:

- the setting has shipped in stable releases since v0.26.2;
- the TUI parity suite on OpenTUI compares the current loop, the shared loop and the shared loop on the kernel, with each arm forced explicitly; it passed 20 runs in a row with retries off on main at 0fe8b7fc9e under Bun 1.4.4 (22 tests each), with the strict renderer check so no run fell back to Ink;
- OpenTUI has no open row in the design's table of send options a host owns;
- the intended differences and the way back are listed above, so the release notes carry them.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- With nothing set, an OpenTUI session (`QWEN_TUI_RENDERER=opentui` under Bun) runs on the shared loop: with `QWEN_DEBUG_LOG_FILE=1` its debug log shows `[LOOP] opentui shared`. With `QWEN_CODE_ENABLE_UNIFIED_AGENT_LOOP=opentui=0`, or `"experimental": { "unifiedAgentLoop": false }`, it shows `[LOOP] opentui legacy`.
- The config tests pin headless, both TUIs and AgentCore on by default and every other surface off, both ways back for each, the loop path each resolves to, and that the event-bus default does not move with them.

```
cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/config
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/config src/ui/opentui
cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/settings.test.ts client/settings
QWEN_E2E_RENDERER=opentui QWEN_SANDBOX=false npx vitest run --root ./integration-tests ./interactive/tui-agent-loop-parity.test.ts --retry=0   # 20 times, on main
```

Results: typecheck clean for core, CLI and the Web Shell; core config tests passed (1427); CLI config and OpenTUI tests passed (5260, 12 skipped); Web Shell settings tests passed (167); the OpenTUI parity suite passed 20 runs in a row with `--retry=0` on main at 0fe8b7fc9e (its arms are forced, so the flip does not change it). Linux, Node 22, Bun 1.4.4.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A: no visible change in the common case; the differences are listed above.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Node 22 and Bun 1.4.4, no sandbox; fake OpenAI server for the parity suite.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: every OpenTUI session moves at once. The differences above are intended; a regression attributed to the new path restarts OpenTUI's wait before its next step, and either switch above brings the current loop back.
- Not validated / out of scope: the other surfaces' defaults (ACP's is in its own PR); the kernel's default (OpenTUI's step 4, 12-04); removing OpenTUI's current loop (step 5). This PR and ACP's both edit the same setting texts; whichever lands second merges main.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: the behavior differences above; `experimental.unifiedAgentLoop: false` now also keeps OpenTUI on its current loop.

Design doc: [English](docs/design/2026-10-23-unified-agent-loop.md) · [中文](docs/design/2026-10-23-unified-agent-loop.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Part of #17045 (OpenTUI's step 2).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

OpenTUI 现在默认运行在共享 agent loop 上：live 回合的每个模型轮和工具批都在其他入口使用的同一个 loop 上运行。切回方式：设置 `"experimental": { "unifiedAgentLoop": false }`，或设 `QWEN_CODE_ENABLE_UNIFIED_AGENT_LOOP=opentui=0`。这是 #17045 中 OpenTUI 的第 2 步：按入口默认值表中的 `opentui` 一项改为开启，与 headless、Ink TUI 和 AgentCore 并列。ACP（在单独的 PR 中）、speculation 和 Hosted Harness 保持现有 loop，事件总线内核在所有入口上仍默认关闭。

设置说明、设置参考文档、VS Code schema 和 Web Shell 的中文文案现在写明两个 TUI 默认使用共享 loop，设计文档记录了 OpenTUI 的默认值。OpenTUI 输出测试的假 client 补上了共享 loop 会调用的两个方法，因此其中两个按默认值解析 loop 的用例现在运行在共享 loop 上。

### 有意差异

使用共享 loop 时，OpenTUI 回合与以前的差异见统一 loop 设计文档中 OpenTUI 的部分，这些差异让它与 Ink TUI 一致：

- 模型从历史中重放的调用就地应答，不再重新执行，一轮里只剩应答时，应答作为下一轮发出；模型再次重放已应答的调用会被当作循环停止；
- 每个工具批都会收尾，合计超出工具输出预算的结果会被裁剪到预算内（以前只有 Mod 工具中间件处理过的批才会）；
- 每个完成的调用计入会话的已完成工具调用数，被取消的调用和 Mod 工具中间件已计数的调用除外；
- 结束回合的工具会结束回合，结果保留在历史中；
- 任何停止原因（包括检测到循环）都会让这一轮的调用不再执行；
- `experimental.eventBusAgentLoop`（默认关闭）现在单独设置就对 OpenTUI 生效：以前除非同时开启共享 loop，OpenTUI 会忽略它；现在设置了它的会话运行在事件总线内核上。

两种 loop 下 OpenTUI 都不会自己发起回合（没有 Goal 续跑、后台通知或 cron 回合），斜杠命令运行的工具仍走现有路径。

### 如何切回

下面任意一种方式都能让 OpenTUI 回到现有 loop：

- 设置 `"experimental": { "unifiedAgentLoop": false }`（这会对所有入口关闭共享 loop）；
- 环境变量 `QWEN_CODE_ENABLE_UNIFIED_AGENT_LOOP=opentui=0`（只关 OpenTUI），或 `=0`（关闭所有入口）。

现有 loop 保留到 OpenTUI 的第 5 步，距本次改动至少 14 天。

## 为什么需要

#17045 一次开放一个入口的共享 loop；OpenTUI 的默认开启定在 12-01。这个 PR 提前提出以便评审；在 11-28 第 2 步的所有条件满足之前不得合入。尚未满足：

- 开共享 loop 的 OpenTUI nightly 任务：由 #17050（11-13 合入）加入，从 11-14 起每晚通过，14 晚在 11-27 满；OpenTUI 共享路径上最后一次非修复改动是 #17055（11-14 合入），它之后的 7 晚在 11-21 满。

已经满足：

- 该设置自 v0.26.2 起已在 stable 版本中发布；
- OpenTUI 上的 TUI 对拍套件比较现有 loop、共享 loop 和内核上的共享 loop，每个 arm 都显式强制；它在 main 0fe8b7fc9e 上用 Bun 1.4.4、关闭重试连续通过 20 次（每次 22 个测试），并开启严格渲染器检查，确认没有一次退回 Ink；
- 设计文档的宿主持有发送选项表中没有 OpenTUI 未关闭的行；
- 有意差异和切回方式已在上面列出，release notes 会带上它们。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

- 什么都不设置时，OpenTUI 会话（Bun 下 `QWEN_TUI_RENDERER=opentui`）运行在共享 loop 上：开启 `QWEN_DEBUG_LOG_FILE=1` 时调试日志显示 `[LOOP] opentui shared`。设 `QWEN_CODE_ENABLE_UNIFIED_AGENT_LOOP=opentui=0` 或 `"experimental": { "unifiedAgentLoop": false }` 时显示 `[LOOP] opentui legacy`。
- 配置测试固定 headless、两个 TUI 和 AgentCore 默认开启、其他入口关闭，每个入口的两种切回方式、各自解析出的 loop 路径，以及事件总线默认值不随它们变化。

结果：core、CLI 和 Web Shell 的 typecheck 无错误；core 配置测试通过（1427）；CLI 配置和 OpenTUI 测试通过（5260，跳过 12）；Web Shell 设置测试通过（167）；OpenTUI 对拍套件在 main 0fe8b7fc9e 上以 `--retry=0` 连续通过 20 次（它的 arm 是强制的，所以这次翻转不影响它）。Linux、Node 22、Bun 1.4.4。

### 前后对比

不适用：常见情况下没有可见变化；差异已在上面列出。

### 环境

Node 22 和 Bun 1.4.4，无沙箱；对拍套件使用 fake OpenAI server。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：所有 OpenTUI 会话一起切换。上面的差异是有意的；归因于新路径的回归会让 OpenTUI 在下一步之前重新等待，上面任意一种开关都能切回现有 loop。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：其他入口的默认值（ACP 在单独的 PR 中）；内核的默认开启（OpenTUI 第 4 步，12-04）；删除 OpenTUI 的现有 loop（第 5 步）。本 PR 与 ACP 的 PR 修改同一段设置说明，后合入的一方合并 main 解决。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：上面的行为差异；`experimental.unifiedAgentLoop: false` 现在也会让 OpenTUI 保持现有 loop。

设计文档：[English](docs/design/2026-10-23-unified-agent-loop.md) · [中文](docs/design/2026-10-23-unified-agent-loop.zh-CN.md)

## 关联 Issue

属于 #17045（OpenTUI 的第 2 步）。

</details>

prs.title: fix(sdk-python): wait for process startup before closing a query
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Wait for in-flight Python SDK process startup before closing a query, then stop the resulting child and its background work. Control calls that resume after shutdown stop before registering a new request. Initialization failures retain their original error type and exit code; repeated calls keep traceback depth bounded.

A clean process exit ends pending control waits and cancels incoming permission callbacks before iteration ends. Already queued messages remain readable, and later explicit shutdown completes input-generator cleanup.

## Why it's needed

Closing during process creation can otherwise return before the child exists, allowing startup to leave a live child behind. The related shutdown paths also need to preserve the correct error and stop work whose peer has exited.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start a public control call, close while process creation is pending, then allow startup to finish. Close must return only after the child exits, and the waiting caller must receive exactly `Query is closed`, with no pending request.
2. Repeat with two close callers, close before startup, and close after a startup error. Cleanup must remain safe, including an input generator that calls close from its own cleanup.
3. Make the peer stop reading stdin after initialization, send a message larger than the pipe buffer, and close. The child must exit; new control calls after close must report `Query is closed`.
4. Exit with code 1 or 9 before initialization responds. Repeated control calls must preserve `ProcessExitError` and its exit code, with a bounded traceback.
5. Exit cleanly before initialization responds, for both a single-turn prompt and streaming input. The input task must complete without writing into the dead pipe.
6. Send an incoming permission request, wait for its callback to start, then exit cleanly. The callback must finish cancellation and leave no incoming request registered before iteration ends. Repeat with the callback closing the query from its own cleanup; callback close, iteration and the surrounding context must all finish.
7. Exit with messages already queued. Those messages must remain readable, and later close must finish suspended input cleanup.

### Critical follow-up after review round 5

Current head: `763f146cce1de7c3b2c633e41d1f7e91012d572b`. Permission callback cleanup can now close the query without waiting on the router that is waiting for that callback. Ordinary external close still waits for the router, and cancellation still finishes before terminal delivery.

The independent real-subprocess probe reproduced the old hang on Python 3.12.14: the peer exited 0, but callback close, iteration and context exit remained unfinished after five seconds, with one incoming request registered. The same probe completes on Python 3.11.18, 3.12.14 and 3.13.5 with the fix. The new reentrant regression exceeds a bounded 15-second subprocess run against the previous source and passes with this guard.

- Startup/close regressions: **17 passed** on both Python 3.11.18 and 3.12.14.
- Complete Python 3.12 SDK suite: **212 passed, 26 skipped**.
- Official SDK Ruff lint/format and mypy checks, isolated source/wheel build, independent diff review and diff checks: passed.
- The published Git tree matches the tested candidate. New-head results are tracked in [SDK Python](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44591016184) and [Qwen Code CI](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44591016473).

The two round-5 Suggestions, R5-1 and R5-2, are deferred to #17872 under the repository's convergence guidance. This critical fix does not change the shared exception-object policy or consolidate terminal-state handling.

### Earlier SDK fix verification

SDK fix commit: `dee7f05dbee233af401880576803ace957096829`. The results in this section refer to that fix commit; the current branch head is recorded above, and the earlier main-branch sync is recorded below.

The follow-up addresses R3-1, R3-2 and R3-4:

- Reset the traceback at all four sites that re-raise the stored close reason, preserving its type and payload.
- Cancel and await incoming callbacks on clean EOF before queuing the terminal marker.
- Exercise clean exit before initialization with real subprocesses for both input modes, then await the input task and inspect the peer's received request log.

Before the production fix, the same 16-case startup/shutdown module gives **3 failed, 13 passed**. The two exit-code cases retain progressively deeper tracebacks (6, 10, 14, ... frames across 20 calls), and the clean-exit permission case leaves the callback registered. With the fix, **16 passed**; an independent rerun also passed all 16.

The clean-EOF guard regressions were checked separately: restoring the single-turn guard to `if self._closed` fails only the single-turn case; deleting the clean-EOF cancellation flag fails only the streaming case. Each mutation gives **1 failed, 1 passed**, with `ConnectionResetError` from the attempted post-exit write. Production was restored before final verification.

Linux, Python 3.12.14:

- Complete Python SDK suite: **211 passed, 26 skipped**.
- Configured Ruff lint/format and mypy: passed.
- Normal isolated wheel/source build: passed.
- Changed documentation formatting, independent diff review and `git diff --check`: passed.
- The published Git tree matches the locally validated tree.

The [Python SDK workflow for this fix commit](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44477618698) passed on Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12. Its [main CI](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44477618742) failed in two Linux shards: a standalone-runtime archive download timed out, and an SSE test's temporary-directory cleanup raised `ENOTEMPTY`. The latter is addressed by the upstream fix included in the sync below.

### Earlier main-branch sync

Previous synchronized head: `d31538768524568fb9e329319a3ab1830a39ad51`, an ordinary merge of `main` at `9cc77eb58e804e848938c0a8e7acc17dae59162c`. This incorporates the upstream SSE cleanup fix [#17764](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17764) (`f1d4abd247b9ad4a3c65e7ddf48b235373e1bcc7`), which closes the daemon before removing its log directory. The original four-file PR patch and entire Python SDK subtree are unchanged.

On the merged tree, the 16 startup/close regressions pass. Ruff lint and formatting (19 files) and mypy (9 source files) pass using the official SDK CI commands and Ruff 0.17.5; staged and working-tree diff checks also pass. The full SDK suite was not rerun locally for this sync. The [SDK Python](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44499620572) workflow passed. [Qwen Code CI](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44499620512) also completed successfully on this same head after the failed Playwright-install shard was rerun; its aggregate smoke gate passed at 18:08 UTC on 2026-11-19.

### Retained regression evidence

The earlier blocked-pipe follow-up reproduced **1 failed / 12 passed** before its fix and **13 passed** afterward. Removing either shutdown-reason safeguard restored the failure. This branch also retains the startup-lock, original-error, clean-EOF, buffered-message and initialization-cancellation coverage, including upstream #17499.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Not tested locally |
| Windows | Not tested locally |
| Linux | Complete local Python SDK suite and package checks passed |

## Risk & Scope

Shutdown waits for process creation already in progress. Indefinitely stalled startup, cancellation of shutdown itself, official CLI/model end-to-end behavior and complete repository preflight remain outside this verification.

For a query that has not already failed, the exact closed-query error applies to new control calls after close completes. A control call already writing when shutdown starts may raise its transport error. Clean EOF preserves queued messages; explicit close or the context manager completes input-task cleanup. No public signature or protocol changes.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17493.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 修改内容与原因

Python SDK 查询在进程创建期间关闭时，现在会等待创建完成，再终止子进程并清理后台任务，避免关闭返回后留下新启动的子进程。初始化失败保留原始异常类型和退出码，重复控制调用的 traceback 长度保持有界。

干净退出会立即结束待处理的控制请求，并在迭代结束前取消、等待入站权限回调。已入队消息仍可读取，后续显式关闭继续负责输入生成器的清理。

## 审查者验证计划

1. 在子进程创建尚未完成时关闭查询。关闭返回前子进程必须已退出；等待中的控制调用精确收到 `Query is closed`，没有残留请求。
2. 覆盖两个并发关闭调用、启动前关闭、启动失败后关闭，以及输入生成器在自身清理时再次关闭查询。
3. 初始化后让子进程停止读取 stdin，发送超过管道缓冲区的内容后关闭。子进程必须退出；关闭后新的控制调用精确返回查询已关闭错误。
4. 初始化答复前以退出码 1 或 9 退出。重复调用保留 `ProcessExitError` 和退出码，traceback 长度不再增长。
5. 初始化答复前干净退出，同时覆盖单次和流式输入。输入任务应正常结束，不得向已退出的管道写入。
6. 发出权限请求，确认回调开始，再干净退出。迭代结束前回调必须完成取消，入站请求表为空。另覆盖回调在自身清理时关闭查询，确保回调关闭、消息迭代和外层上下文均完成。
7. 干净退出后继续读取已经入队的消息；后续关闭完成挂起输入生成器的清理。

## 第 5 轮关键缺陷修复

当前 head：`763f146cce1de7c3b2c633e41d1f7e91012d572b`。权限回调在取消清理中关闭查询时，不再等待正在等待该回调的路由任务。普通外部关闭仍会等待路由任务，终止通知仍在回调取消完成后发送。

独立真实子进程探针在 Python 3.12.14 复现旧问题：对端已以 0 退出，但 5 秒后回调中的关闭、消息迭代和上下文退出仍未完成，入站请求表仍有 1 项。修复后，同一探针在 Python 3.11.18、3.12.14、3.13.5 均完成，入站请求表为空。新增重入回归搭配旧源码超过 15 秒的有界子进程观察窗口，搭配修复后通过。

Python 3.11.18 和 3.12.14 的启动／关闭回归各 **17 通过**；Python 3.12 完整 SDK 套件 **212 通过、26 跳过**。官方 Ruff lint／格式、mypy、隔离源码包／wheel 构建、独立 diff 审查及 diff 检查通过，发布的 Git tree 与验证候选一致。新 head 的托管结果见 [SDK Python](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44591016184) 和 [Qwen Code CI](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44591016473)。

按仓库第 5 轮收敛规则，R5-1、R5-2 两项建议已记录到后续 issue #17872；本次关键修复没有改变共享异常对象策略或合并终止状态处理。

## 先前 SDK 修复验证

SDK 修复提交：`dee7f05dbee233af401880576803ace957096829`。本节结果对应此修复提交；当前分支 head 见上文，先前主分支同步见下文。本次处理 R3-1、R3-2 和 R3-4：四处重抛保留异常的站点重置 traceback；干净 EOF 在终止标记入队前取消并等待入站回调；增加真实子进程的单次／流式输入退出用例。

同一组 16 项启动／关闭测试，在生产修复前为 **3 失败、13 通过**：退出码 1 和 9 的 traceback 在 20 次调用中按 6、10、14……帧增长；干净退出后权限回调仍残留。修复后为 **16 通过**，独立复核也通过全部 16 项。

分别恢复单次输入旧守卫、删除干净 EOF 取消标记，会各自使对应输入用例因退出后写入的 `ConnectionResetError` 失败，每次为 **1 失败、1 通过**。最终验证前已恢复生产源码。

Linux、Python 3.12.14：该修复提交的完整 Python SDK 套件 **211 通过、26 跳过**；配置的 Ruff lint／格式、mypy、正常隔离 wheel／源码包构建、文档格式、独立 diff 审查和 `git diff --check` 均通过。发布的 Git tree 与本地验证树一致。该修复提交的[托管 Python SDK 工作流](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44477618698)已在 Python 3.10、3.11 和 3.12 通过。

保留先前启动锁、堵塞管道关闭、原始错误、干净 EOF、缓冲消息及初始化取消的回归，包括上游 #17499。该修复提交的主 CI 两个 Linux 分片分别遇到独立运行时归档下载超时，以及 SSE 测试清理临时目录时的 `ENOTEMPTY`；后者由下述主分支同步带入的上游修复处理。

## 先前主分支同步

先前同步 head 为 `d31538768524568fb9e329319a3ab1830a39ad51`，普通合并 `main` 快照 `9cc77eb58e804e848938c0a8e7acc17dae59162c`。其中包含上游 [#17764](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17764) 的 SSE 清理修复（`f1d4abd247b9ad4a3c65e7ddf48b235373e1bcc7`）：先关闭 daemon，再删除其日志目录。原 PR 四个文件的补丁与整个 Python SDK 子树均原样保留。

合并树上的 16 项启动／关闭回归通过；按官方 SDK CI 命令及 Ruff 0.17.5 执行的 lint、格式检查（19 个文件）、mypy（9 个源文件）和 staged／working-tree diff 检查均通过。本次同步未在本地重跑完整 SDK 套件。该 head 的 [SDK Python](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44499620572) 已通过；[Qwen Code CI](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44499620512) 在同 head 重跑 Playwright 安装失败分片后也已通过，smoke 聚合门禁于 2026-11-19 18:08 UTC 通过。

## 风险与范围

关闭会等待已开始的进程创建。无限期停滞的创建、关闭操作自身被取消、官方 CLI／模型端到端行为、macOS、Windows 和完整仓库 preflight 未在本轮验证。精确的关闭错误适用于此前未失败、且关闭完成后新发起的控制调用；关闭开始时已在写入的调用仍可能抛出传输错误。没有公共签名或协议变更。

修复 #17493。

</details>

prs.title: fix(ci): recover durable Runtime in long-answer restart E2E
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The Linux long-answer persistence scenario starts both Broker instances with durable local Runtime identity and keeps the worker alive when the original Spring process is killed. The replacement Broker can verify and adopt the worker before admitting the second Workspace Turn.

## Why it's needed

The scenario kills its original Spring and Harness processes and submits another Turn for the same Workspace from a clean replacement. The old test also killed the worker by signaling the entire Spring process group. With in-memory worker ownership, the replacement cannot observe the old Runtime conclusively. With durable identity alone, it can establish that the worker died, but recovery still requires stop evidence. Both paths timed out preparing the second Turn.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the existing long-answer persistence scenario with the same Linux and MySQL setup as Hosted failover CI. Confirm both Turns complete, the full first answer is read back from durable storage and included in the replacement model context, and the short answer still stays inline. On macOS, confirm this mode reports its Linux requirement before starting test services.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (CI fixture). [Main baseline failure](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44602073150/job/135835841137). The [Linux/MySQL long-answer, session owner, in-flight owner, and continuation owner failover steps](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44667032585/job/136058719820) passed at `f6ba3d7ae1`. Local build and bundle, typecheck, formatting, lint, and 181 script tests passed. The macOS platform guard returned the expected error.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :---: |
| macOS | Build, typecheck, script tests and platform guard passed |
| Windows | Pending CI |
| Linux | Long-answer and three owner failover E2E steps passed with MySQL |

## Risk & Scope

- The long-answer fixture now requires Linux for durable worker adoption. Workspace admission and answer-persistence assertions still run. Dedicated failure scenarios continue to cover worker loss.
- The separately failing Hosted MySQL process fault tests are tracked in #16371.

## Linked Issues

Refs #17851 and #11220.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 改动

Linux 长回答持久化用例为两个 Broker 启用可恢复的本地 Runtime 身份，并在终止原 Spring 进程时保留独立 worker。替换 Broker 可以在接收第二个 Workspace Turn 前验证并接管该 worker。

## 背景

用例终止原 Spring 和 Harness 进程，再从全新的替换实例向同一 Workspace 提交 Turn。原脚本向整个 Spring 进程组发出信号，worker 也随之退出。只有内存记录时，替换 Broker 无法确认原 Runtime 的状态。仅启用持久身份后，可以确认 worker 已退出，但回收绑定仍需要写入方已停止的证据。两种配置下的第二个 Turn 都在准备阶段超时。

## 验证

使用与 Hosted failover CI 相同的 Linux 和 MySQL 环境运行现有长回答持久化用例。确认两次 Turn 均完成，第一条完整回答能从持久化存储读回并进入替换实例的模型上下文，第二条短回答继续使用内联存储。在 macOS 上，该模式应在启动测试服务前提示需要 Linux。

[主分支失败基线](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44602073150/job/135835841137)。`f6ba3d7ae1` 的 [Linux/MySQL 长回答、会话 owner、执行中 owner 和 continuation owner 故障转移步骤](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/44667032585/job/136058719820)全部通过。本地构建与打包、类型检查、格式检查、lint 和 181 个脚本测试已通过。macOS 平台检查返回预期错误，Windows 待 CI。

## 范围

- 长回答用例现在要求 Linux，以使用可验证的 worker 接管路径。现有 Workspace 准入与回答持久化断言继续执行。专门的故障场景继续覆盖 worker 丢失。
- Hosted MySQL 进程故障测试的独立失败由 #16371 跟踪。

关联 #17851 和 #11220。

</details>

prs.title: perf(web-shell): render large workspace PDFs on demand
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Web Shell renders workspace PDFs from 4 MiB through 100 MiB one page at a time. It lazily loads a PDF.js viewer and reads byte ranges through the existing authenticated workspace API. Users can page through the preview or open the complete PDF in the browser's native viewer. Workspace PDFs below 4 MiB and PDF attachments use the native viewer.

## Why it's needed

The existing preview waits for the entire PDF to be fetched in serial 256 KiB chunks before handing it to the browser. For a 20 MiB file, this puts all 80 reads on the critical path to showing page one.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Open a large multipage workspace PDF from Files. Check that page one is visible while data used only by later pages is still outstanding. Navigate to the next page and verify that it loads and renders.
2. Choose **Open full PDF** and check that the native viewer opens and the downloaded copy matches the workspace file. Confirm that a small workspace PDF or a PDF attachment opens in the native viewer.
3. Replace a PDF while the paged preview is open. Verify that the preview reports the change when it reads another range and **Open full PDF** opens the latest file. A PDF that needs a built-in CMap should offer the full viewer with a clear message.

### Evidence (Before & After)

| PDF | Click to visible page one (median) | Raw PDF bytes before page one | File and renderer response bodies before page one |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 20 MiB | 11.107 s → 2.237 s | 20 MiB → 3.25 MiB | 26.68 MiB → 6.50 MiB |
| 5 MiB | 3.522 s → 1.530 s | 5 MiB → 1 MiB | 6.67 MiB → 3.49 MiB |
| 300 KiB | 595.5 ms → 588 ms | 300 KiB in both builds | 409,870 bytes in both builds |

The 20 MiB test held a range used by page two. Page one appeared while the range was held, page two rendered after release, and the downloaded PDF matched the fixture's SHA-256. The 300 KiB result is from six alternating pairs, with both builds using Chromium's native viewer.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Untested locally |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Untested locally |

### Environment (optional)

Chromium 149 with a token-protected local daemon and production Web Shell builds. The benchmark used 40 ms simulated latency and 4 MiB/s download throughput. The baseline Web Shell was built from `ac4ae44c`.

## Risk & Scope

- The first large-PDF preview fetches the PDF.js renderer and worker. The transfer figures above include that cold load.
- The paged viewer renders to a canvas. Use **Open full PDF** for search, printing, text selection, and documents that require an external font map.
- The feature uses the existing workspace file API and configuration.
- Design documents in [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/web-shell-pdf-range/docs/design/web-shell/web-shell-pdf-range-preview.md) and [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/web-shell-pdf-range/docs/design/web-shell/web-shell-pdf-range-preview.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

Web Shell 对 4 MiB 至 100 MiB 的工作区 PDF 提供逐页预览。PDF.js 查看器按需加载，通过现有的工作区鉴权接口读取字节范围。用户可以在预览里翻页，也可以用浏览器原生查看器打开完整 PDF。低于 4 MiB 的工作区 PDF 和 PDF 附件使用原生查看器。

## 为什么需要

现有预览要串行读取所有 256 KiB 分片，才能把 PDF 交给浏览器。打开 20 MiB 的文件时，第一页显示前要等完全部 80 次读取。

## 审阅测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 从「文件」打开大体积、多页工作区 PDF。确认仅后续页需要的数据尚未返回时，第一页已可见。切换到下一页，确认它可以加载并显示。
2. 选择「打开完整 PDF」，确认原生查看器能打开文件，下载的副本与工作区文件一致。较小的工作区 PDF 和 PDF 附件也应由原生查看器打开。
3. 在按页预览打开时替换 PDF。检查预览在读取下一个字节范围时提示文件已变更，且「打开完整 PDF」能打开最新文件。依赖预定义 CMap 的 PDF 应显示清晰提示，并提供完整预览入口。

### 优化前后对照

| PDF | 点击到第一页可见（中位数） | 首屏前收到的 PDF 原始数据 | 首屏前文件及渲染器响应体 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 20 MiB | 11.107 秒 → 2.237 秒 | 20 MiB → 3.25 MiB | 26.68 MiB → 6.50 MiB |
| 5 MiB | 3.522 秒 → 1.530 秒 | 5 MiB → 1 MiB | 6.67 MiB → 3.49 MiB |
| 300 KiB | 595.5 ms → 588 ms | 均为 300 KiB | 均为 409,870 字节 |

20 MiB 测试挂起了第二页依赖的一个字节范围。挂起时第一页已可见，放行后第二页正常绘制，下载文件的 SHA-256 与样本一致。300 KiB 来自 6 对交替复测，两版都使用 Chromium 原生查看器。

### 已验证系统

| 系统 | 状态 |
| --- | --- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ 已验证 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 本地未验证 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 本地未验证 |

### 测试环境（可选）

Chromium 149、启用令牌鉴权的本地 daemon 和 Web Shell 生产构建。模拟延迟 40 ms、下载速率 4 MiB/s。基线 Web Shell 构建于 `ac4ae44c`。

## 风险与范围

- 第一次打开大 PDF 会加载 PDF.js 渲染器和 worker。上面的传输量计入了这次冷加载。
- 按页查看器在画布上渲染。搜索、打印、选择文本或查看依赖外部字体映射的文档时，可选择「打开完整 PDF」。
- 此功能使用现有的工作区文件 API 和配置。
- 设计文档提供 [英文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/web-shell-pdf-range/docs/design/web-shell/web-shell-pdf-range-preview.md) 和 [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/web-shell-pdf-range/docs/design/web-shell/web-shell-pdf-range-preview.zh-CN.md) 两个版本。

## 关联 Issue

无。

</details>

### Review follow-up / 审查跟进

- Regenerated the VS Code companion’s PDF.js license notice in `8ca05af768`. Both CI generators now reproduce the tracked files locally. 已补齐 VS Code 插件的 PDF.js 许可证声明，本地运行 CI 的两个生成器均能复现提交中的文件。 [R1-1](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17899#discussion_r4638857919)
- Deferred VS Code webview support for the inline JBIG2 and JPEG 2000 decoders. This requires validation in the companion host, whose existing PDF iframe is also restricted by CSP. VS Code Webview 的内联解码器兼容性留待插件宿主专项验证，现有 PDF iframe 也受 CSP 限制。 [R1-2](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17899#discussion_r4638857936)
- Deferred direct automated tests for the range viewer. The browser run reported above exercised paging, file replacement, and closing a preview while a read was pending. 分页查看器的自动化覆盖留待后续补齐，已有浏览器实测覆盖翻页、读取期间替换文件和关闭预览。 [R1-3](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17899#discussion_r4638857943)
- Deferred preserving full-view mode across Retry. After a failed full load, Retry returns to the paged view, where the user can select **Open full PDF** again. 「重试」保留完整预览模式留待后续修复，目前可在返回分页预览后再次选择「打开完整 PDF」。 [R1-4](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17899#discussion_r4638857948)
- Deferred password messaging in the paged viewer. **Open full PDF** remains available to use the native viewer’s password prompt in the browser. 分页模式的密码提示留待后续完善，浏览器中可通过「打开完整 PDF」使用原生查看器的密码提示。 [R1-5](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17899#discussion_r4638857953)

prs.title: fix(ci): gate the Teams channel on its npm publishing bootstrap (#17898)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Holds the Microsoft Teams channel out of the npm release until a maintainer completes its one-time public bootstrap publish, using the same repository-variable gate the Mem0 extension already uses. The gate lives in the release package selection, so it rides the workflow-pinned checkout and applies even when the selected release ref predates this change; the release workflow contributes a single orchestration line exposing the variable, guarded to the upstream repository so a fork can never publish into the `@qwen-code` scope. The already-shipped guard and the release versioning behaviour are deliberately left untouched: Teams is still probed for an existing version, and its package and extension manifests still follow the release version. The developer documentation now names both bootstrap-gated packages and the variables that enable them.

## Why it's needed

The nightly `v0.28.0-nightly.20261119.f8d4f706ea` failed in its publish job (#17898). The Teams channel merged the same day and was the only new workspace in the release window since the last good nightly. Because it merged without `private`, it opted straight into the main npm release — but the publish job authenticates with npm trusted publishing alone, carrying no npm token, and npm only lets a maintainer bind a trusted publisher to a package that already exists. Teams has never been published, so the workflow cannot authenticate for it, and since the whole selection goes out through one recursive publish invocation under a fail-fast shell, that single package takes down the entire release rather than being skipped. This repository already documents both halves of that trap: the pnpm release design warns that a new non-private workspace opts into the release and its npm permissions and trusted publisher must be reviewed before merging, and the Mem0 extension design records the bootstrap-variable remedy for exactly this constraint. Teams was merged without either. Gating it defaults the release back to a working state immediately, while preserving the intent to distribute it once the bootstrap is done.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm that the default release selection no longer contains `@qwen-code/channel-msteams`, while `@qwen-code/audio-capture` and `@qwen-code/external-context-mem0` keep their existing behaviour, and that enabling the new variable on the upstream repository puts Teams back into the selection while a fork still never publishes it. Confirm the already-shipped guard still lists Teams among the packages it probes, so a partial release cannot be overwritten by a retry. The focused suites below cover all of this; each new clause was also mutation-probed by deleting or negating it and watching the corresponding test fail. After merge, a maintainer still needs to perform the one-time public bootstrap publish of Teams, bind it to the release workflow in the `production-release` environment, and then set `NPM_CHANNEL_MSTEAMS_TRUSTED_PUBLISHING_ENABLED` to `true`. Until then Teams is intentionally not distributed through npm; its documented local-extension install path is unaffected.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — release-pipeline behaviour, no user-visible UI change. Before: the publish selection handed a never-published package to a tokenless trusted-publishing invocation, failing the whole job. After: that package is skipped by default and re-enters the selection only when a maintainer enables its variable.

### Tested on

|     OS     |    Status    |
| :--------: | :----------: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅ tested   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit and meta-test suites only (`scripts/tests` via the repository's Vitest config), plus the full build, typecheck and lint. The sandbox runs as a non-owner uid, so `COREPACK_HOME` and `npm_config_cache` were pointed at writable temporary directories for those commands; no repository file was changed to accommodate that.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Teams' npm distribution is deferred until a maintainer completes the bootstrap publish and sets the variable. That is the intended trade — a skipped package is recoverable in one release, whereas an unauthenticatable one fails every nightly. If Teams had already been bootstrapped and bound, this change would only delay its distribution by one release rather than break anything.
- Not validated / out of scope: the release workflow itself and a real npm publish were not run. This environment has no GitHub credentials, so the failed run's log could not be fetched, and publishing is a networked write that is out of bounds here. The diagnosis rests on the release-window diff, the publish job's tokenless trusted-publishing configuration, and the repository's own documented constraint and precedent; the regression witness is the selection gate and its mutation probes. The bootstrap publish, the trusted-publisher binding, and setting the repository variable remain maintainer actions. No change to Teams' runtime, its ingress, or its version alignment.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No published package is removed or renamed, and no consumer-facing contract changes. Teams was never available on npm, so nothing that users could have installed is affected.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #17898

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

在维护者完成 Microsoft Teams 渠道的一次性公开 bootstrap 发布之前，把它挡在 npm 发布之外，使用的是 Mem0 扩展已有的同一套仓库变量开关。开关逻辑位于发布包选择处，因此它随 workflow 固定（pinned）的 checkout 一起生效，即使所选发布 ref 早于本次改动也依然有效；发布工作流只贡献一行编排代码来暴露该变量，并限定在上游仓库，使 fork 永远无法向 `@qwen-code` scope 发布。"已发布"守卫与发布版本行为刻意保持不变：Teams 仍会被探测是否已存在该版本，其包清单与扩展清单也仍跟随发布版本。开发者文档现在列出了两个受 bootstrap 开关控制的包，以及启用它们的变量。

## 为什么需要它

 nightly `v0.28.0-nightly.20261119.f8d4f706ea` 在其 publish 任务失败（#17898）。Teams 渠道当天合并，是自上一个成功 nightly 以来发布窗口内唯一新增的 workspace。由于它合并时没有设置 `private`，就直接进入了主 npm 发布 —— 但 publish 任务仅使用 npm trusted publishing 认证，不携带任何 npm token，而 npm 只允许维护者为已经存在的包绑定 trusted publisher。Teams 从未发布过，因此工作流无法为它完成认证；又因为整个选择集是在 fail-fast shell 下通过一条递归 publish 命令发出的，这一个包就会拖垮整个发布，而不是被跳过。本仓库已经记录了这个陷阱的两个方面：pnpm 发布设计文档警告新增的非 private workspace 会进入主发布，合并前必须检查其 npm 权限与 trusted publisher；Mem0 扩展设计文档则记录了针对该约束的 bootstrap 变量补救方式。Teams 合并时两者都没有做。加上开关后，发布立即恢复到可用状态，同时保留了 bootstrap 完成后继续分发它的意图。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

确认默认发布选择中不再包含 `@qwen-code/channel-msteams`，而 `@qwen-code/audio-capture` 与 `@qwen-code/external-context-mem0` 的既有行为保持不变；并确认在上游仓库启用新变量会让 Teams 重新进入选择集，而 fork 仍然永远不会发布它。确认"已发布"守卫探测的包列表中仍包含 Teams，因此部分发布的版本不会被重试覆盖。下面的聚焦套件覆盖了以上全部；每个新增子句还做了变异探针验证 —— 删除或取反它，然后观察对应用例失败。合并之后，维护者仍需完成 Teams 的一次性公开 bootstrap 发布，在 `production-release` 环境中把它绑定到发布工作流，然后把 `NPM_CHANNEL_MSTEAMS_TRUSTED_PUBLISHING_ENABLED` 设为 `true`。在此之前 Teams 有意不通过 npm 分发；其文档中的本地扩展安装路径不受影响。

### 证据（改动前后）

N/A —— 发布流水线行为，没有用户可见的 UI 变化。改动前：发布选择把一个从未发布过的包交给无 token 的 trusted publishing 命令，导致整个任务失败。改动后：该包默认被跳过，只有维护者启用其变量时才重新进入选择集。

### 测试平台

|     OS     |    状态    |
| :--------: | :----------: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅ 已测试   |

### 环境（可选）

仅单元与元测试套件（通过仓库的 Vitest 配置运行 `scripts/tests`），外加完整的 build、typecheck 与 lint。沙箱以非所有者 uid 运行，因此这些命令把 `COREPACK_HOME` 与 `npm_config_cache` 指向了可写的临时目录；没有为此改动任何仓库文件。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：Teams 的 npm 分发被推迟，直到维护者完成 bootstrap 发布并设置变量。这正是预期的权衡 —— 被跳过的包可以在一个发布周期内恢复，而无法认证的包会让每个 nightly 都失败。即便 Teams 其实已经完成 bootstrap 并绑定，本改动也只会把它的分发推迟一个发布周期，而不会破坏任何东西。
- 未验证 / 范围之外：没有运行发布工作流本身，也没有做真实的 npm 发布。本环境没有 GitHub 凭据，因此无法拉取失败运行的日志；而发布属于联网写操作，在此处越界。诊断依据是发布窗口的差异、publish 任务无 token 的 trusted publishing 配置，以及仓库自身记录的约束与先例；回归见证是选择开关及其变异探针。bootstrap 发布、trusted publisher 绑定以及设置仓库变量仍是维护者动作。没有改动 Teams 的运行时、其 ingress 或其版本对齐逻辑。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。没有删除或重命名任何已发布的包，也没有消费者可见的契约变化。Teams 从未在 npm 上可用过，因此用户可能安装过的任何东西都不受影响。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #17898

</details>

prs.title: fix(web-shell): keep the model sheet's rows and search field touch-sized
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Gives the model picker's bottom sheet the same touch sizing the rest of the mobile composer already uses. Rows in the sheet — model rows and the reasoning controls — get a 44px minimum height, and the sheet's search field gets a 44px height, a 16px font floor at every breakpoint, and the mobile input hints the add menu's search fields already carry (autocapitalize and autocorrect off, spellcheck off, a Search enter key). The section row that expands the model list keeps its own taller 48px floor. The desktop popover is not touched: every new attribute is gated on the sheet being active.

## Why it's needed

The bottom sheet added in #17401 fixed the real complaint — opening the picker no longer focuses the search field, so iOS no longer raises the keyboard over the model list. What it carried over unchanged is the desktop sizing. The sheet is portaled outside the composer shell, so the mobile composer's 44px overrides never reach its rows, leaving them at 34px. The search field is the shared input primitive, which is 32px tall and drops to 14px at the `md` breakpoint. The sheet's media query matches coarse pointers with no upper width bound, so a tablet in landscape gets the sheet *and* the 14px field — and iOS zooms the whole page when a focused field is under 16px.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Open the Web Shell on a touch device (or a coarse-pointer emulation) and tap the model chip in the composer. The sheet should open without the keyboard, its model rows and reasoning rows should be comfortably tappable, and the section row that expands the model list should look no smaller than before. Then widen the viewport past 768px while keeping touch emulation on — a landscape tablet — and tap the search field: the page must not zoom, and the field must be at least 44px tall. On a desktop browser at normal width the model picker is still the upward popover with its original compact search field.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Screenshots below are real runs of the same scenario against the mock daemon, captured on this branch and on its parent commit, under `mobile-chromium` (Pixel 7) touch emulation. The model list is expanded in both frames.

### Real daemon, real browser

These are runs against a real `node dist/cli.js serve` on loopback with an isolated `QWEN_HOME`, a real session, and a model catalog derived from real `modelProviders` settings — no mock daemon. The browser is a real Chromium; the two arms are this head and the PR's base, each built and bundled separately.

**Phone (Pixel 7, coarse pointer)**

Before:

![Model sheet on a real daemon before the change, phone width](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17892-touch-targets/pr17892-real/before-phone.png)

After:

![Model sheet on a real daemon after the change, phone width](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17892-touch-targets/pr17892-real/after-phone.png)

**Landscape tablet (1024×768, still coarse pointer) — where the 14px field shows up**

Before:

![Model sheet search field on a real daemon before the change, tablet width](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17892-touch-targets/pr17892-real/before-tablet.png)

After:

![Model sheet search field on a real daemon after the change, tablet width](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17892-touch-targets/pr17892-real/after-tablet.png)

**Narrow desktop window (600×800, mouse) — the surface that must not change**

Before:

![Model sheet on a real daemon before the change, narrow mouse-driven window](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17892-touch-targets/pr17892-real/before-narrow-desktop.png)

After:

![Model sheet on a real daemon after the change, narrow mouse-driven window](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/pr17892-touch-targets/pr17892-real/after-narrow-desktop.png)

Those last two files are **byte-identical** — same git blob `1a70061f4f7f4768ae92d5e8e4be9c0e3025067c`, same 15498 bytes. The pointer gate leaves the mouse-driven window pixel-for-pixel alone.

Measured in those runs, in CSS pixels:

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Phone: model row height | 34 | 44 |
| Phone: Done button height | 32 | 44 |
| Phone: refresh icon | 28×28 | 44×44 |
| Phone: search field height | 32 | 44 |
| Phone: Thinking switch `::after` inset | -8px | -13px |
| Tablet: search font size | **14px** | **16px** |
| Model-list section row height | 48 | 48 |
| Narrow desktop: row / Done / search / refresh | 34 / 32 / 32 / 28 | 34 / 32 / 32 / 28 |
| Narrow desktop: `spellcheck` attribute | absent | absent |

The tablet font line is the iOS page-zoom trigger; it only appears once the viewport crosses `md`, which is why a phone-width screenshot alone would not show it. The section row is unchanged in both arms, which is the point of excluding it from the row rule. Both arms exited 0 and neither left anything under the real `~/.qwen/projects`.

### CI-style suites

Browser coverage, `mobile-chromium` (Pixel 7) plus the desktop `chromium` project, whole mobile composer spec including the new cases:

```
npx playwright test --config playwright.config.ts \
  --project=chromium --project=mobile-chromium \
  web-shell.composer.mobile.spec.ts web-shell.model-sheet-pointer-gate.spec.ts
  31 passed (7.4m)
```

The added case measures, in a real browser: reasoning effort rows ≥44px, the model-list section row still ≥48px, model rows ≥44px after expanding the list, and then — after widening the viewport to 1024×768 with touch still emulated — a search field whose computed font size is ≥16px and whose height is ≥44px. The width change is what makes the font assertion load-bearing: at the Pixel 7 width the `md:` breakpoint never applies, so the old code would have passed there too.

The compiled CSS was read back from the dev server to confirm the exclusion survives CSS-module hashing:

```
[data-web-shell-model-sheet] ._dropdownItem_vt00s_422:not(._sheetSectionRow_vt00s_516),
[data-web-shell-model-sheet] ._reasoningThinkingRow_vt00s_517,
[data-web-shell-model-sheet] ._reasoningEffortRow_vt00s_518 {
  min-height: 44px;
}
```

Unit coverage, run from `packages/web-shell`:

```
npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts \
  client/components/ChatEditor.test.tsx client/components/ChatEditor.css.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  323 passed (323)
```

Three cases were added: the sheet's search field carries the touch height, the `md:text-base` floor and the mobile input hints; the desktop popover's search field carries none of them; and a narrow mouse-driven window that still gets the sheet keeps the compact field. The last two are the negative controls for the gating.

Mutation witnesses — each applied alone, run, then reverted, with the tree re-checked afterwards:

| Mutation | Result | Killed by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Drop the sheet field's class entirely | KILLED, `1 failed \| 14 passed` | the touch-height unit case (`expected 'h-8 …' to contain 'h-11'`) |
| `h-11` → `md:h-11` (the regression R1-6 describes) | KILLED, `1 failed \| 14 passed` | the same case, now comparing whole tokens |
| Gate on `mobileSheet` alone, dropping the pointer check | KILLED, `1 failed \| 14 passed` | `keeps the compact field when the sheet stands in for a narrow desktop window` |
| Switch `::after` inset back to the primitive's 8px | KILLED in the browser | the e2e pad assertion, `Expected: >= 13, Received: 8` |

Round 2 added four more, each targeting a probe rather than the styling:

| Mutation | Result | Killed by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hoist the switch `::after` rule out of the `@media` block | KILLED, `1 failed / 322 passed` | `keeps every sizing rule inside the shared touch query` (stylesheet parse, no browser) |
| Drop `.reasoningThinkingRow` from the floor | KILLED, `1 failed / 322 passed` | `covers the rows, the footer button, the refresh icon and the switch` |
| Drop `coarse &&` from the shared media helper | KILLED, `1 failed / 322 passed` | the narrow-desktop unit control |
| `size="sm"` on the reasoning switch | KILLED in the browser | the hit-rect sum, `Expected: >= 44, Received: 40` |

In every unit mutation the rest of the suite stayed green, so each one is isolated to the clause it targets.

The desktop negative control is tagged `@smoke`: the pull-request lane runs `--grep @smoke`, and an untagged control would only ever run after merge. Listing confirms it — the smoke set went from 589 tests in 94 files to **590 in 95**, with the pointer-gate case present under `chromium` only.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Vite dev server with the Playwright mock daemon; no real daemon, no model calls. Unit tests under vitest/jsdom.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: taller rows inside the model list's existing 250px cap mean fewer models are visible at once (roughly five instead of seven). That is the usual touch-target tradeoff; the cap itself is left alone because changing it is a separate layout decision.
- The sheet is not only a touch surface. `MODEL_SHEET_QUERY` also matches `(max-width: 639px)`, so a narrow **desktop** window uses the sheet too. The sizing is therefore gated on `(hover: none) and (pointer: coarse)` — in CSS via a media query, and in the input's class and hints via `isCoarsePointerDevice()` — so a mouse-driven narrow window keeps the compact field, its spell-check, and the original row heights. A desktop e2e case pins that.
- The floor covers the sheet's own controls: model rows, reasoning rows, the Done button and the refresh icon. The Thinking row is a plain `div`, so the switch inside it gets the enlarged hit rect instead of the row alone. Host-injected picker content (`modelPicker.mountHeader` / per-row mounts) keeps whatever sizing the host gives it.
- Not validated / out of scope: the real iOS soft keyboard and the `mobile-webkit` (iPhone 13) project were not exercised locally — WebKit cannot start on this host. The 16px floor is verified as a computed font size under Chromium touch emulation at 1024px, not as an observed absence of iOS page zoom. The sheet's list height cap, its reasoning section layout and its focus handling are all unchanged from #17401.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The change is purely additive and gated on the sheet; the desktop popover renders exactly as before.

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to #17401.

prs.title: feat(core): add local notes compaction with a strategy selector
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds an opt-in local notes compaction strategy. Users can select **Summary** or **Notes and History** under **Chat Compression Strategy** in `/settings`, or set `model.chatCompression.strategy` to `summary` or `notes` in `settings.json`. Summary remains the default; changing the selection requires restarting Qwen Code.

Eligible main sessions gain `session_notes`, `session_history`, `get_context_remaining`, and `new_context`. The model can persist a bounded working checkpoint, start a smaller context from that checkpoint and the latest consumed user request, and recover omitted evidence from the active branch of its local session log. Successful notes rollovers make no summarization request. Notes revisions live in the existing JSONL transcript, with a generated Markdown projection for inspection; checkpoint persistence must succeed before active history changes. Resume, fork, rewind, archive, and deletion handle the matching notes state.

Missing, stale, or unusable notes fall back to summary for automatic and ordinary manual compression. An explicit `new_context` requires a fresh revision and reports an error if it cannot commit. `/compress <instructions>` continues to summarize, and `/compress-fast` keeps its existing behavior. The notes tool bundle respects recording availability and tool policy and is excluded from subagents, teammates, and nested code-mode calls. Ink and OpenTUI display a notes-specific transition notice.

## Why it's needed

Repeated full-history summaries can lose constraints, decisions, and tool evidence that a long task needs later. A local working checkpoint plus bounded history retrieval gives the model a way to carry forward its current state and recover details on demand. Storage and retrieval use the existing session log and require no additional memory backend. Selected notes and retrieved history still go to the configured model provider as normal inference input. Real-model quality, total token cost, and latency remain to be measured before considering a default change.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start the local build with no strategy configured and confirm summary behavior. Open `/settings`, search for `compression`, switch to **Notes and History**, and confirm the saved value is `model.chatCompression.strategy: "notes"` and the restart notice appears. Restart and check that the four notes tools are available. Repeat with `summary`, including activation through `settings.json`.
2. In an isolated recorded session, have the model write notes and request a new context in separate tool-only responses using the returned revision. Repeat three times. Each new context should retain the checkpoint and current user constraints, with no summarizer request. Deliberately omit an earlier identifier from the notes, then recover it through history search/read. Resume the session and check that its latest notes revision and old history reference still work.
3. Check that missing/stale revisions, oversized notes, and notes/reset calls mixed with ordinary text or tools cannot install a new context. Disabling recording or denying a required notes tool should disable the complete bundle. After switching to a smaller model window, existing bounded notes should remain readable, while an oversized checkpoint must be shortened before it can authorize a reset.
4. Compare compression commands: `/compress` with fresh notes should use notes; missing/stale notes should fall back to summary; `/compress <instructions>` should forward those instructions to the summarizer even with fresh notes; `/compress-fast` should retain its current tool-output clearing behavior. Check that the next model request uses the committed context and that notes transitions show the notes-specific notice.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Actual tmux captures of `/settings`, with the search set to `compression`:

**Before — global `qwen` `0.23.3-nightly.20260913.faa395885e`:**

```text
No settings match your search.
```

**After — local bundle `0.24.1`:**

```text
Chat Compression Strategy                                                   Notes and History*
Choose summary compression or local notes with history recovery. Restart Qwen Code to apply.
To see changes, Qwen Code must be restarted. Press r to exit and apply changes now.
```

The fresh-notes `/compress` case displayed `Started a new context from local notes` in the actual TUI. The complete deterministic headless/tmux run passed settings persistence, tool availability, history recovery/resume, six rejection cases, and all six manual-compression cases. After the final fixes, the rebuilt handoff rerun again committed **three distinct notes windows in 15 main requests with zero summarizer requests**; resume took three requests and restored the same notes revision and historical reference.

`npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, and `npm run bundle` passed. Relevant core, ACP, settings/schema/i18n, and Ink/OpenTUI regression tests passed. The final focused rerun passed 23 core tests and 54 event-adapter tests; the commit hook also passed formatting and ESLint. A separate comment contains the E2E matrix and coverage limits.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested locally |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ Not tested locally |

### Environment (optional)

macOS arm64, Node.js `v26.8.2`; local bundled CLI `0.24.1`; isolated temporary settings and runtime directories; deterministic localhost OpenAI-compatible provider; headless CLI and real tmux interaction. The user's normal settings and sessions were not modified by the tests.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: This changes core recording, compaction, and replay paths. Correctness depends on fresh notes, successful checkpoint persistence, and branch-correct recovery; note completeness still depends on the model. The Markdown file is a generated view, so editing it directly does not update canonical notes.
- Not validated / out of scope: Real-model task quality, token/cost/latency comparisons, full ACP/Web Shell E2E, other provider wire protocols, process-crash/disk/lease fault injection, and Windows/Linux execution. The deterministic E2E suite does not cover automatic/hard-overflow triggers, nested code mode, or fork/rewind/archive lifecycle operations; focused regression tests cover relevant runtime paths, without claiming end-to-end coverage. Cross-session memory, multi-file notes, and a notes editor are out of scope.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: No settings migration is required. `summary` remains the default, existing transcripts remain supported, and enabling or disabling `notes` requires a restart. Ordinary compression can use summary fallback; an explicit `new_context` never silently summarizes.

Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/158a0511ddcdd465e14083c56d0f9c7cc8ac629a/docs/design/2026-09-19-local-notes-compaction.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/158a0511ddcdd465e14083c56d0f9c7cc8ac629a/docs/design/2026-09-19-local-notes-compaction.zh-CN.md). Both versions are complete and synchronized, including decisions, constraints, acceptance criteria, and follow-up validation.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #12257

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的内容

增加可选的本地 notes 压缩策略。用户可以在 `/settings` 的 **上下文压缩方式** 中选择 **摘要** 或 **笔记与历史**，也可以在 `settings.json` 中把 `model.chatCompression.strategy` 设为 `summary` 或 `notes`。默认仍为摘要；修改选项后需要重启 Qwen Code。

符合条件的主会话获得 `session_notes`、`session_history`、`get_context_remaining` 和 `new_context` 四个工具。模型可以保存有大小限制的工作笔记，从笔记和最近已消费的用户请求启动更小的上下文，再从本地 session log 的有效分支找回遗漏证据。成功的 notes 换窗口不发起摘要请求。笔记版本保存在现有 JSONL transcript 中，并生成方便查看的 Markdown 文件；只有恢复 checkpoint 持久化成功后才替换当前历史。恢复、分叉、回退、归档和删除操作会处理对应的笔记状态。

自动压缩和普通手动压缩在笔记缺失、过期或不可用时回退到摘要。显式调用 `new_context` 必须提供新鲜的笔记版本，无法提交时返回错误。`/compress <instructions>` 继续生成摘要，`/compress-fast` 保持现有行为。笔记工具组遵循录制可用性及工具策略，并对 subagent、teammate 和嵌套 code-mode 调用关闭。Ink 和 OpenTUI 会显示专门的 notes 换窗口提示。

## 为什么需要

反复生成全历史摘要可能丢失长任务后续需要的约束、决策和工具证据。本地工作笔记加上有界历史检索，使模型能够保留当前工作状态并按需找回细节。存储和检索复用现有 session log，不需要新增 memory 后端。选中的笔记和检索出的历史仍会作为正常推理输入发送给配置的模型 provider。在考虑修改默认策略前，仍需评估真实模型的任务质量、总 token 成本和延迟。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 使用本地构建启动，不配置策略时确认仍使用摘要。打开 `/settings`，搜索 `compression`，切换到 **Notes and History**，确认保存的值为 `model.chatCompression.strategy: "notes"` 并显示重启提示。重启后检查四个笔记工具可用。再切回 `summary`，并验证通过 `settings.json` 启用的行为一致。
2. 在隔离且开启录制的会话中，让模型先写笔记，再用返回的 revision 请求新上下文；两次调用分别放在独立且只含该工具的回复中。重复三次。每个新上下文都应保留 checkpoint 和当前用户约束，且不发起摘要请求。故意不把某个早期标识符写入笔记，再通过历史搜索和读取找回。恢复会话后，检查最新笔记版本和旧历史引用仍可用。
3. 检查缺失或过期的 revision、超限笔记，以及混入普通文本或其他工具的笔记/换窗口调用，都不能安装新上下文。关闭录制或拒绝任一必需工具后，整个笔记工具组应被关闭。切换到窗口更小的模型后，已有且满足固定大小上限的笔记仍应可读，但超过当前模型预算的 checkpoint 必须缩短后才能用于换窗口。
4. 对比压缩命令：笔记新鲜时 `/compress` 应使用笔记；笔记缺失或过期时应回退到摘要；即使有新鲜笔记，`/compress <instructions>` 也应把指定要求转交摘要模型；`/compress-fast` 应保留现有清理工具输出的行为。检查下一次模型请求使用已提交的上下文，且 notes 换窗口显示对应提示。

### 证据（前后对比）

以下为真实 tmux 捕获的 `/settings` 画面节选，搜索词为 `compression`：

**修改前：全局 `qwen` `0.23.3-nightly.20260913.faa395885e`：**

```text
No settings match your search.
```

**修改后：本地 bundle `0.24.1`：**

```text
Chat Compression Strategy                                                   Notes and History*
Choose summary compression or local notes with history recovery. Restart Qwen Code to apply.
To see changes, Qwen Code must be restarted. Press r to exit and apply changes now.
```

使用新鲜笔记执行 `/compress` 时，真实 TUI 显示 `Started a new context from local notes`。完整的确定性 headless/tmux 测试通过了设置持久化、工具可用性、历史找回与会话恢复、六项拒绝场景以及全部六项手动压缩场景。最终修复后重新构建并复测交接，再次在 **15 次主模型请求中提交了三个不同的 notes 窗口，摘要请求为零**；恢复过程使用三次请求，恢复了相同的笔记版本和历史引用。

`npm run build`、`npm run typecheck` 和 `npm run bundle` 均通过。相关 core、ACP、设置/schema/国际化、Ink/OpenTUI 回归测试均通过。最后的针对性复测通过了 23 个 core 测试和 54 个 event-adapter 测试；提交钩子的格式和 ESLint 检查也通过。另附评论列出 E2E 场景矩阵和覆盖范围。

### 测试平台

| 平台 | 状态 |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未在本地测试 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 未在本地测试 |

### 环境（可选）

macOS arm64、Node.js `v26.8.2`、本地 CLI bundle `0.24.1`；使用隔离的临时设置和 runtime 目录、确定性的 localhost OpenAI 兼容模型服务、headless CLI 和真实 tmux 交互。测试未修改用户日常使用的设置和会话。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：涉及 core 的录制、压缩和回放路径。正确性依赖笔记新鲜度、checkpoint 成功持久化以及有效分支恢复；笔记内容是否完整仍依赖模型。Markdown 文件只是生成视图，直接编辑不会更新权威笔记。
- 未验证或不在范围内：真实模型任务质量、token/成本/延迟对比、完整 ACP/Web Shell E2E、其他 provider 的通信协议、进程崩溃/磁盘/写入租约故障注入，以及 Windows/Linux 运行。确定性 E2E 未覆盖自动/硬溢出触发、嵌套 code mode 或分叉/回退/归档生命周期操作；针对性回归测试覆盖了相关运行时路径，但不代表完成了这些场景的端到端验证。跨会话记忆、多文件笔记和笔记编辑器不在本次范围内。
- 破坏性变更或迁移说明：无需迁移设置。默认仍为 `summary`，继续支持已有 transcript；开启或关闭 `notes` 需要重启。普通压缩可以回退到摘要；显式 `new_context` 绝不会悄悄改用摘要。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/158a0511ddcdd465e14083c56d0f9c7cc8ac629a/docs/design/2026-09-19-local-notes-compaction.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/158a0511ddcdd465e14083c56d0f9c7cc8ac629a/docs/design/2026-09-19-local-notes-compaction.zh-CN.md)。两个版本完整同步，包括决策、约束、验收标准和后续验证。

prs.title: perf(serve): shorten daemon startup and readiness waits
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Routes a leading `qwen serve` through the existing lightweight parser in workspace and bundled installs. Help, version, unsupported arguments, and managed updates retain their existing handling. The listener uses the current health, authenticated request, and fallback triggers to start the runtime.

Loads webhook authentication configuration on demand and overlaps independent handler imports with telemetry initialization. Queued reads of branding, voice settings, and workspace-scoped file status can use the mounted app once required channel startup succeeds. They retain the same authorization and workspace selection as later requests.

## Why it's needed

The general CLI dispatcher and webhook configuration previously loaded before a typical `serve` launch could accept connections. Moving these loads out of the startup path lets the listener accept connections sooner. Releasing queued metadata reads at app readiness avoids waiting for Live Host publication.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Launch a packaged daemon. Verify that shallow health responds during bootstrap, followed by deep health and a successful stat for the target workspace. Verify that the fallback timer can start the daemon without an initial health probe.
- Check that an early authorized stat request reaches the selected workspace and that a missing workspace returns `workspace_mismatch`. Check early webhook requests still need a valid secret.
- Confirm `serve --help`, `serve --version`, and an unknown option retain their output and exit status. Stop the daemon with SIGTERM and confirm it exits cleanly.

### Evidence (Before & After)

The packaged entry dependency check, CLI tests, and loopback daemon tests cover the changed startup paths. The earlier revision's paired staging run compared the default trigger with starting the runtime at listen. With warm compile cache and initial 50 ms polling, starting at listen saved 49 ms on workspace readiness and added 163 ms to shallow health, measured as medians of paired differences. The revised PR keeps the default trigger.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Tested on arm64 with Node 22.23.5 for packaged startup |
| Windows | Pending CI |
| Linux | Pending CI |

## Risk & Scope

- Timing and failure handling during cold boot matter. Keep the existing runtime readiness checkpoint and authentication, with a narrower wait for the specified read-only routes.
- Startup measurements depend on polling cadence and available CPU. The paired staging run used seven fixture workspaces with affinity to one CPU.
- Design [English](https://github.com/callmeYe/qwen-code/blob/codex/serve-startup-latency/docs/design/serve-startup-latency.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/callmeYe/qwen-code/blob/codex/serve-startup-latency/docs/design/serve-startup-latency.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 变更内容

工作区版和打包版的 `qwen serve` 均优先使用现有轻量解析器。帮助、版本、不支持的参数与托管更新沿用现有处理。监听后沿用现有的健康检查、已鉴权请求及兜底触发条件启动运行时。

Webhook 鉴权配置按需加载，独立的处理模块与遥测初始化并行。必需的 Channel 启动成功后，等待中的品牌、语音设置和作用域文件状态读取可使用已挂载的应用，沿用后续请求的鉴权与工作区选择。

## 背景

一般的 `serve` 启动在接受连接前会加载通用 CLI 分发和 webhook 配置。把这两项加载移出启动路径后，监听器可以更早接受连接。等待中的元数据读取在应用就绪后即可返回，无需等待 Live Host 发布。

## 评审验证

- 启动打包版，验证引导阶段浅探活可响应，随后深探活通过且目标工作区 stat 成功。验证尚未收到探活请求时，兜底定时器也能启动运行时。
- 验证早到的已鉴权 stat 请求进入所选工作区，未知工作区返回 `workspace_mismatch`，启动期间的 webhook 仍要求正确的密钥。
- 验证 `serve --help`、`serve --version` 和非法参数的输出和退出码。发送 SIGTERM 后确认守护进程正常退出。

bundle 入口依赖检查、CLI 测试和本机回环测试覆盖了启动链路的改动。此前在预发用同一版产物配对比较了默认触发和监听后立即启动。在热编译缓存、初期每 50 ms 探活的条件下，监听后立即启动相对默认路径让工作区就绪提前 49 ms，首次浅探活延后 163 ms，均为配对差值的中位数。本次更新采用默认触发。macOS arm64 上使用 Node 22.23.5 验证了打包产物。Windows、Linux 等待 CI。

## 风险与范围

- 重点是冷启动时的时序及失败处理。保留现有运行时就绪检查点和鉴权，仅缩短指定只读路由的等待。
- 启动耗时取决于探活节奏和可用 CPU。预发配对测试使用了七个测试工作区，进程绑定一个 CPU。
- 设计同上。无关联 Issue。

</details>

prs.title: feat(web-shell): commit only the selected files from the commit view
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The Web Shell commit view can now commit a subset of the dirty files. It lists every uncommitted file with a checkbox, preselects all of them, and sends the selection with the commit. Unchecked files stay in the working tree, and work the user had already staged outside the selection stays staged instead of being swept in.

Underneath, the shared commit helper and the daemon commit route gained a `paths` option next to the existing `all` flag. The dialog sends an explicit selection whenever the listing is complete; a click while the first listing is still in flight is refused with a "list is still loading" message instead of committing the whole tree, and a listing the daemon capped commits everything, which the legend says.

Renames are handled explicitly: either half of a rename selects the pair, because git only records the rename when the deletion and the addition land in the same commit.

## Why it's needed

The commit view always committed everything. A single session that produced two unrelated changes (a bug fix and a refactor, say) could only be split into clean commits from a terminal, which defeats the point of having the dialog. The issue asks for per-file checkboxes so the Web Shell git workflow matches what the CLI already allows.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Unit and route tests cover the new behavior; no manual UI session was run. Reproduce the original gap by opening the commit view with two dirty files and pressing Commit — before this change both files are in the commit, after it only the checked ones are, and unchecking all of them surfaces a "select at least one file" error instead of a daemon call.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no screenshot or recording was captured for this run.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Tests and lint run locally on macOS from a linked worktree; no `npm run dev` session.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the dialog now depends on the diff listing to build a selection. A listing the daemon caps or cannot produce falls back to committing every change (``all: true``), which the dialog discloses in its legend; only the not-yet-loaded state is refused, so a slow diff route delays a commit from the dialog but a broken one does not block it (the CLI is unaffected).
- Not validated / out of scope: no manual UI verification on a running daemon, and no full `npm run build`. `packages/cli` typecheck was not run (fresh worktree reports unrelated TS6305 on unbuilt workspace dependencies); `packages/core` typecheck passes. `packages/web-shell` typecheck reports only the 12 known stale-SDK errors, which are identical on `origin/main`.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. `all: true` keeps its previous semantics.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #8446

prs.title: perf(web-shell): load xterm on demand
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Loads xterm, FitAddon, and the terminal stylesheet together when a workspace terminal is enabled or a managed terminal is opened. The tab or dialog opens immediately and shows a loading indicator until the runtime is ready. Workspace terminals can still release a detached PTY while the runtime is loading or while a restored tab is inactive.

## Why it's needed

Opening a chat currently loads xterm JavaScript and CSS even if the user never opens a terminal. On Chromium with a fresh cache, the production comparison moves about 337 kB of raw JS and CSS off the startup path, or 86 kB after local gzip compression.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Open a chat in a fresh Chromium context and check the Network panel. The terminal runtime should be absent from the chat and Files views.
2. Open Terminal from the panel's add menu. The runtime should load, the terminal should show output, and scrolling or switching away and back should preserve the live connection. Closing the tab should release it.
3. Reload with Files selected and an inactive restored terminal tab. Closing that terminal tab should release the existing PTY without fetching the runtime.
4. Open a managed terminal inside an embedded Web Shell. Its xterm styles should apply within the Web Shell, including inside a shadow root.

### Evidence (Before & After)

| Chromium, cold chat | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| JavaScript and CSS, raw | 8.53 MB | 8.19 MB |
| JavaScript and CSS, local gzip | 2.40 MB | 2.31 MB |
| xterm on chat startup | Present in entry JS and CSS | Absent |

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Chromium production-build A/B and focused unit tests |
| Windows | Pending CI |
| Linux | Pending CI |

## Risk & Scope

- The first terminal open waits for the runtime chunk. Further opens reuse the loaded browser module.
- Existing workspace and managed PTY connection, replay, reconnect, and release rules still apply.
- Design documents [English version](docs/design/2026-11-19-web-shell-lazy-terminal.md) and [简体中文版](docs/design/2026-11-19-web-shell-lazy-terminal.zh-CN.md).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 改动

启用工作区终端或打开托管终端时，才一起加载 xterm、FitAddon 和终端样式。标签或对话框立即打开，运行时就绪前显示加载状态。运行时仍在加载或恢复的标签处于未激活状态时，工作区终端仍能释放已挂起的 PTY。

## 背景

当前打开聊天会同时加载 xterm 的 JavaScript 和 CSS，即使用户从未打开终端。Chromium 冷缓存生产构建对照显示，启动路径少加载约 337 kB 原始 JS 和 CSS，本地 gzip 后约少 86 kB。

## 审查测试计划

### 验证步骤

1. 在新的 Chromium 浏览器上下文中打开聊天并检查网络面板。聊天和文件视图都不应请求终端运行时。
2. 从面板的添加菜单中打开终端。运行时应成功加载，终端应显示输出。滚动或切换回终端时，现有连接仍可使用。关闭标签应释放终端。
3. 在选中文件且存在未激活终端标签时重新加载。关闭恢复的终端标签应释放已有 PTY，期间不请求终端运行时。
4. 在嵌入式 Web Shell 中打开托管终端。xterm 样式应在 Web Shell 范围内生效，包括 Shadow DOM。

### 前后对照

| Chromium 冷缓存聊天 | 优化前 | 优化后 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| JavaScript 和 CSS 原始体积 | 8.53 MB | 8.19 MB |
| JavaScript 和 CSS 本地 gzip 体积 | 2.40 MB | 2.31 MB |
| 聊天启动时的 xterm | 包含在入口 JS 和 CSS | 未加载 |

### 测试环境

| 系统 | 状态 |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Chromium 生产构建 A/B 和相关单元测试 |
| Windows | 等待 CI |
| Linux | 等待 CI |

## 风险与范围

- 首次打开终端需要等待运行时 chunk。后续打开复用浏览器已加载的模块。
- 工作区和托管终端继续沿用现有的 PTY 连接、回放、重连和释放规则。
- 设计文档见[英文版](docs/design/2026-11-19-web-shell-lazy-terminal.md)和[简体中文版](docs/design/2026-11-19-web-shell-lazy-terminal.zh-CN.md)。

</details>

prs.title: feat(serve): add daemon restart recovery inbox
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a daemon restart recovery inbox. After a daemon restart, `POST /sessions/recovery` lists workspace sessions whose newest prompt did not settle, and `POST /sessions/recovery/continue` resumes a selected batch without opening or switching conversations. The scan reads the bounded tail of the existing prompt terminal ledger; session enumeration reads only the transcript head for project membership. Session ids are validated against the persisted file shape before deriving a ledger path, and continuation cold-loads through the existing restore core and the live session-owner continuation path. The routes are advertised by a new `restart_recovery` capability, exposed as `DaemonClient.getRestartRecoveries` / `continueRestartRecoveries`, and surfaced in Web Shell as a sidebar panel above the session list.

## Why it's needed

After a restart, recovery was only reachable after opening each interrupted conversation: the recovery summary is produced after a cold load, and the Continue button lives inside the chat surface. With several workspaces and interrupted tasks, users had to find every conversation in the sidebar and click Continue one by one. This change gives one place to see the interrupted tasks and resume them, while keeping the existing per-conversation recovery behavior unchanged.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the focused daemon, SDK, and Web Shell suites from the repository root:

```bash
(cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/restart-recovery-scan.test.ts src/serve/routes/session-restart-recovery.test.ts src/serve/routes/session-restart-recovery-continue.test.ts src/serve/server/telemetry-catalog.test.ts src/serve/server/telemetry.test.ts src/serve/rest-integration-docs-contract.test.ts src/serve/capabilities-docs-contract.test.ts src/serve/capability-parity.test.ts)
(cd packages/sdk-typescript && npx vitest run test/unit/daemon-public-surface.test.ts)
(cd packages/sdk-typescript && npx vitest run test/unit/DaemonClient.test.ts -t 'restart recovery')
(cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/components/RestartRecoveryPanel.test.tsx client/i18n.test.ts)
npm run build && npm run bundle
(cd integration-tests && QWEN_SANDBOX=false npx vitest run cli/qwen-serve-restart-recovery.test.ts)
```

Expected: the scanner classifies `in_flight`, interrupted terminals, and the normal-shutdown `error`/`daemon_shutdown` terminal, and skips settled ones; the query route enforces workspace trust, per-member errors, the 30-day clamp, and omits live active sessions; the continuation route cold-loads, requires `confirmToolTurn` for tool turns, and refuses degraded history; the sidebar panel lists interrupted sessions, continues one or all, stays hidden when the capability is absent, and routes cancellation confirmations to the conversation. The integration test starts a real daemon and runs both scenarios: SIGKILL → `in_flight`, and SIGTERM → `daemon_shutdown`, each followed by restart, scan, continuation, and transcript/ledger checks.

To exercise the real flow manually: start a daemon, start a long turn, kill the daemon process, restart it, call `POST /sessions/recovery` with the workspace, then `POST /sessions/recovery/continue` and confirm a new turn appears in the persisted transcript. Two daemon-level runs passed in this worktree against the built daemon and a loopback fake model: the SIGKILL run reported `interruption: in_flight`; the SIGTERM run reported `interruption: daemon_shutdown`. In both cases `POST /sessions/recovery/continue` returned `accepted` with a `promptId`, the persisted transcript contained the new assistant output and its `turn_result`, the prompt ledger reached `completed`, and a second scan no longer listed the session.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A for screenshots. Daemon-level evidence comes from the restarted session's persisted transcript: the continuation `promptId` appears in a new `turn_result` followed by assistant output, and the prompt ledger records the matching completed terminal.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

Linux covers the focused unit, contract, component, and committed daemon restart integration suites, plus local SIGKILL and SIGTERM daemon runs. macOS and Windows were not run.

### Environment (optional)

Focused vitest suites and a built daemon in this worktree; no Docker or sandbox.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the scan reads a persisted sidecar ledger, so a missing or unreadable ledger fails closed and that session is not listed. The continuation route loads selected sessions into memory; the batch is capped at 10 and workspaces per scan at 20.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS and Windows, standalone conversation coverage, and automatic continuation. Tool-turn continuations require `confirmToolTurn: true`; `degraded_history` is never continued.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The new `restart_recovery` capability is additive; older daemons do not advertise it, and Web Shell hides the panel when it is absent.

Design documents: [English](docs/design/2026-11-17-daemon-restart-recovery-inbox.md) · [简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-17-daemon-restart-recovery-inbox.zh-CN.md)

prs.title: fix(extensions): load extension manifests saved with a UTF-8 BOM
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Extension manifests saved with a UTF-8 BOM now load. The extension manager strips a leading BOM before `JSON.parse`, the same way the LSP config and TOML readers in core already do. The CLI command loader, which re-reads the manifest for a custom `commands` path, now uses the existing `stripUtf8Bom` helper. Three other readers of the same files strip it too: the mods loader (`mods/discovery.ts` `readManifest`), the classic hook loader (`hooks/hooks.json`), and Agent Plugins v1 `plugin.json` (`getAgentPluginSchemaStatus` and `loadAgentPluginManifest`).

## Why it's needed

Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes a BOM by default (`'{"name": "bomext", "version": "1.0.0"}' | Out-File -Encoding utf8 qwen-extension.json`). `JSON.parse` throws on U+FEFF, so the extension is skipped without a warning and `qwen extensions list` says `No extensions installed.` Same class as #13595 / #13944.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

`npx vitest run src/extension/extensionManager.test.ts -t "UTF-8 BOM"` in `packages/core`, and `npx vitest run src/services/FileCommandLoader.test.ts -t "UTF-8 BOM"` in `packages/cli`. Both new tests fail on main (`expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0`).

### Evidence (Before & After)

0.26.2 on Windows 11, BOM manifest in `~/.qwen/extensions/bomext`:

```
before: No extensions installed.
after:  ✓ bomext (1.0.0)
```

Manifest without the BOM lists on both. A BOM manifest missing `name` is still skipped.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ✅   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Linux (node:24): prettier, eslint `--max-warnings 0`, `tsc --noEmit` for core, vitest `core/src/extension` (1022 passed) and `cli/src/services` + `src/config` (2896 passed), same as main plus the 2 new tests. Windows: the new core test, `tsc --noEmit` for cli (same 3 unbuilt `@qwen-code/web-templates` errors as main), and the CLI repro above.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: low. Only a leading BOM is removed before parsing, in `qwen-extension.json`, `plugin.json`, `hooks/hooks.json` and the mods manifest reader. User-visible: extensions, Agent Plugins and hooks saved with a BOM, which were silently skipped, now load.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS. `managed-package.ts` left alone.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15785
