## What this PR does

Microcompaction now treats a Part carrying producer-attached recovery metadata with at least one persisted output file as protected before falling back to the model-visible stub string. The string fallback remains for resumed histories because JSON serialization intentionally drops the non-enumerable recovery handle.

Regression coverage now runs the real `enforceFunctionResponseBudget` output shape through real `microcompactHistory` for both the singular finalizer artifact and the `web_fetch` metadata/`Full extracted text saved to` shape. It also covers JSON round-trip fallback, empty `persistedOutputFiles`, and an ordinary control result.

## Why it's needed

Before this change, a live finalized tool result could carry `/tmp/tool-results/...` in `part.functionResponse.response.output` while its durable artifact list lived only in recovery metadata. Idle microcompaction only recognized older string envelope spellings, so it replaced those previews with `[Old tool result content cleared]` and destroyed the only model-visible path back to the saved bytes. After this change, any producer that records a non-empty persisted-file recovery handle is protected without adding another producer-specific text spelling.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

From `packages/core`, run:

```text
npm test -- src/services/microcompaction/microcompact.test.ts src/tools/tool-response-finalizer.test.ts src/tools/truncation.test.ts
```

Expected: all 219 tests pass. The new recovery regressions were also checked against the pre-fix predicate with `npm test -- src/services/microcompaction/microcompact.test.ts -t 'real finalized|recognized string fallback|only non-empty recovery'`; the two real-finalized shapes and the non-empty recovery list failed by being cleared, while the resumed string fallback remained covered.

Additional verification on the final source:

```text
npx prettier --check src/services/microcompaction/microcompact.ts src/services/microcompaction/microcompact.test.ts
npx eslint src/services/microcompaction/microcompact.ts src/services/microcompaction/microcompact.test.ts
npm run typecheck
npm run build
```

All passed locally.

Local review gate: `qwen review run --effort high --json --timeout-minutes 15 --quiet` returned no verdict within its bounded run; it printed only the admission warning that a 15-minute timeout could not fit the 20-minute reserve plus 30-minute audit round. Review-gate status: UNVERIFIED (timeout/no verdict), not clean. The branch instead received a self-review over the full candidate diff plus the verification commands above.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — this fixes internal core microcompaction classification. UI verification cannot distinguish whether these recovery metadata handles were protected before building the clearing plan.

### Environment (optional)

macOS arm64, Node.js 22.23.4, lockfile-matched `pnpm install`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: any Part whose in-process recovery metadata contains a non-empty `persistedOutputFiles` list is retained during microcompaction; that is the intended producer-agnostic protection, and empty lists remain clearable.

prs.title: perf(web-shell): gzip serve responses for large transcript loads (#6181)
prs.body:
# perf(web-shell): gzip serve responses for large transcript loads

> Fixes part of #6181 (serve-layer item: "load 响应加 gzip" / add gzip to load responses)
> Branch: `perf/web-shell-gzip-transcript-6181` · base: `main` @ `92a8a8d17`

## Problem / 问题

Web Shell session loads (`POST /session/:id/load`) return the full transcript replay as a single JSON document — typically 1–5 MB for long sessions. The serve layer had **no response compression at all** (middleware chain is CORS → host → traceId → auth → rateLimiter; no `Content-Encoding` anywhere in the repo), so mobile / bandwidth-constrained clients pay the full uncompressed transfer on every session switch. This is one of the remaining root-cause layers of the mobile session-switch jank tracked in #6181.

Web Shell 的 session load（`POST /session/:id/load`）把整段 transcript 回放作为单个 JSON 返回，长会话通常 1–5 MB。serve 层此前**完全没有任何响应压缩**（中间件链为 CORS → host → traceId → auth → rateLimiter，全仓无 `Content-Encoding` 输出），移动端/弱网客户端每次切换会话都要裸传全量数据。这是 #6181 移动端切会话卡顿剩余根因层中的服务端一项。

## Solution / 方案

Add a dependency-free `gzipJsonResponses()` middleware (`packages/cli/src/serve/gzip-response.ts`) built on `node:zlib`, mounted in `server.ts` **after auth + rate limiter, before route registration**:

新增零依赖的 `gzipJsonResponses()` 中间件（基于 `node:zlib`），挂载在 `server.ts` 中 **auth + rate limiter 之后、路由注册之前**：

- Compress only when the client negotiates gzip via `Accept-Encoding` (full RFC 9110 token/q-value parsing — `gzip;q=0` is honored, so a plain substring check is not used).
- Only `application/json` bodies **≥ 1 KiB** (the `compression` middleware's default threshold — the gzip header/trailer costs more than it saves below that).
- Explicitly skips: SSE / streamed `res.write` responses, attachment (`Content-Disposition`) and range (`Content-Range`) downloads (byte-exact semantics), HEAD, 204/304/1xx, and responses that already carry a `Content-Encoding`.
- Falls back to identity when the gzip output is not smaller than the input (incompressible payloads).
- Sets `Content-Encoding: gzip`, rewrites `Content-Length` to the compressed size, appends `Vary: Accept-Encoding` on every gzip-capable response (cache correctness), and drops the identity `ETag` on the compressed path (one resource now legitimately has two representations).
- Compression runs on the **async `zlib.gzip` callback path** (`Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION` level 6) so the daemon's event loop keeps serving SSE frames while a large transcript is being compressed — no `gzipSync` blocking.

Design choices / 设计取舍:

- **No new dependency.** The repo has no `compression` package; a ~90-line middleware reading like the rest of `serve/` keeps the dependency surface unchanged. (If maintainers prefer the standard `compression` middleware, the tests here would transfer almost verbatim.)
- **Mounted after auth.** 401/403/429 bodies are tiny and must not spend CPU on unauthenticated callers.
- **Client needs zero changes.** Browser `fetch` + `res.json()` decompresses transparently; the SDK/CLI clients that do not send `Accept-Encoding: gzip` keep getting identity responses.

## Measured impact / 实测效果

Real-HTTP probe (express + this middleware, transcript-shaped replay JSON with realistic prose/code/tool-output diversity, deterministic PRNG), `curl --raw`:

| Payload | Identity | Gzip (wire) | Ratio | Saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.42 MB session load | 1,486,587 B | 235,430 B | 15.8% | **84.2%** |
| 4.73 MB session load | 4,955,284 B | 776,866 B | 15.7% | **84.3%** |

- Response headers verified: `Content-Encoding: gzip`, `Vary: Accept-Encoding`, `Content-Length` = compressed size; gunzip round-trips to the exact original JSON.
- Loopback CPU cost: ~5.5 ms per 4.7 MB compression (identity 1.4 ms/req vs gzip 6.9 ms/req). On Fast 3G (~1 Mbps) the same response drops from ~40 s to ~6.3 s of transfer — the CPU cost is negligible by comparison, and the async path keeps SSE unaffected.

真实 HTTP 探针（express + 本中间件、形状贴近真实的 transcript 回放 JSON）实测：1.42 MB → 235 KB（省 84.2%）、4.73 MB → 777 KB（省 84.3%）；响应头三项齐全，gunzip 可无损还原；回环压缩 CPU 开销约 5.5 ms/4.7 MB，Fast 3G 下传输时间从约 40 s 降到约 6.3 s，且异步压缩不阻塞 SSE。

## Tests / 测试

- `packages/cli/src/serve/gzip-response.test.ts` (new, 30 tests):
  - `acceptsGzip` parsing matrix: 16 header shapes (`gzip`, `GZIP`, `gzip;q=0`, quoted q-values, mixed codings, absent/non-string headers …).
  - Middleware behavior: compresses large JSON; identity when gzip not offered / below threshold; `Vary` on pass-throughs; HEAD skipped; no double-encode; SSE and `res.write` streaming untouched; attachments untouched; non-JSON untouched; 204/304 untouched; ETag dropped on compressed path; Buffer bodies; incompressible-payload fallback; custom threshold; error-status JSON still functional.
- `packages/cli/src/serve/server.test.ts`: new integration test in the `POST /session/:id/load and /resume` group — real `createServeApp` + fake bridge, asserts `content-encoding`/`vary`/rewritten `content-length` and byte-exact JSON equivalence after decompression.
- Regression: full `server.test.ts` **1227/1227 passed**; `routes/session-prompt-terminals.test.ts` 5/5; repo-root `npm run typecheck` clean; prettier/eslint clean on touched files.

测试覆盖：中间件单测 30 例（协商解析 16 例矩阵 + 行为 14 例：压/不压各情形、SSE/下载/HEAD/预编码跳过、不可压回退、ETag/Vary 语义、gunzip 还原等价）；server 集成测试 1 例（真实 app + load 路径）；全量 `server.test.ts` 回归 1227/1227；根 typecheck 通过；prettier/eslint 干净。

## Notes for reviewers / 审阅备注

- Out of scope here (follow-up layers of #6181): client-side session-switch caching, Shiki viewport gating, non-virtualized `content-visibility`, and the `rawOutput`/`details` duplication reduction.
- Two `tsc` errors that appear in a fresh checkout (`BundledSkillLoader.ts` / `SkillCommandLoader.ts` importing `applySkillSideEffects`) are pre-existing on `main` until `@qwen-code/qwen-code-core` is rebuilt (`npm run build -w @qwen-code/qwen-code-core`); they are unrelated to this change and disappear after the rebuild.

Refs #6181

auto_merge.commit_message:
Serve-layer compression for JSON API responses. Web Shell session
loads return multi-megabyte transcript JSON; on mobile /
bandwidth-constrained clients the uncompressed transfer dominates
the cost of switching sessions (#6181).

Adds a dependency-free middleware (node:zlib, async callback path)
mounted after auth + rate limiter:
- compress only when Accept-Encoding negotiates gzip (q-values
  honored) and the body is application/json at or above 1 KiB
- skip SSE/streaming, attachments/ranges, HEAD, no-body statuses,
  pre-encoded responses; fall back to identity when gzip would not
  shrink the body
- set Content-Encoding: gzip + Vary: Accept-Encoding, rewrite
  Content-Length, drop the identity ETag

Browser fetch decompresses transparently; the client is unchanged.

Refs #6181

prs.title: ci(managed-agent): stabilize required gate name
prs.body:
## What this PR does

- Stabilizes the merge-relevant Managed Agent check context as `Managed Agent gate` for touched PR fast/full runs, untouched runs, main pushes, and merge groups.
- Keeps touched review runs that select no full suite on the non-required `Managed Agent review (no full run)` context; non-approval and closed-PR reviews still skip, so a no-suite or skipped review cannot overwrite a real fast/full result. A rerun or reopen on a head with an earlier full report also preserves that full result instead of replacing it with fast.
- Extracts tier selection into `.github/scripts/managed-agent-gate-tier.sh`, keeps that script inside the managed-path matcher, and fixes fork review runs whose `pull_requests` list is empty: rerun suppression is SHA-scoped while approval dedup verifies the current PR head SHA/ref against the candidate run branch.
- Updates the workflow meta-test matrix and both Managed Agent gate design documents; the full-run dedup tests now explicitly account for fast-tier runs sharing the required name and fork runs omitting PR metadata.

## Why it's needed

A tier-dependent job name cannot be added safely to the main ruleset: a touched PR reported `Managed Agent fast tier`, while untouched and full-run paths reported `Managed Agent gate`. The change makes the merge-relevant context stable without letting a review that ran no Java publish or overwrite the required context.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Run `npx prettier --check .github/workflows/managed-agent-gate.yml .github/scripts/managed-agent-gate-scope.mjs scripts/tests/managed-agent-gate-workflow.test.js docs/design/2026-10-16-managed-agent-gate.md docs/design/2026-10-16-managed-agent-gate.zh-CN.md`; expect all matched files to pass.
2. Run `bash -n .github/scripts/managed-agent-gate-tier.sh` and `shellcheck .github/scripts/managed-agent-gate-tier.sh`; expect both to pass.
3. Run `WORKFLOW_SIZE_BASE_SHA="$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)" bash .github/scripts/check-workflow-size.sh`; expect the managed gate to stay within its baseline allowance.
4. Run `npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/managed-agent-gate-workflow.test.js scripts/tests/sdk-java-workflow.test.js scripts/tests/workflow-size.test.js`; expect 450 passed and 28 skipped tests (85 in the Managed Agent gate suite).
5. On this PR, confirm the Managed Agent workflow reports the fast-tier result as `Managed Agent gate`, not `Managed Agent fast tier`. A later review that selects no full run must not replace that context.

<!-- pr-evidence -->

| Evidence | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Formatting | `prettier --check` passed for the changed workflow, matcher, meta-test, and both docs |
| Shell | `bash -n` and `shellcheck` passed for `.github/scripts/managed-agent-gate-tier.sh` |
| Workflow-size gate | `check-workflow-size.sh` passed; `managed-agent-gate.yml` is within its baseline allowance |
| Focused meta-tests | 450 passed / 28 skipped across `managed-agent-gate-workflow`, `sdk-java-workflow`, and `workflow-size` |
| Live gate | pending on `4db5731`; its `Select the Managed Agent tier` job passed and the quoted workflow invocation passed full yamllint locally |

N/A for UI screenshots — this changes GitHub Actions check naming and has no CLI, TUI, Web UI, or Web Shell surface.

|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

### Environment (optional)

Local Node 22/pnpm test environment; no Java suite was run locally because the PR's own Managed Agent workflow is the discriminating CI witness.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the fast tier now satisfies the stable required context before the first maintainer approval; the first approval still starts the full suite, and no-suite reviews remain non-required.
- Not validated / out of scope: this PR does not edit the main ruleset; the ruleset now requires `Managed Agent gate`, and this PR's live run is the check-name witness.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## 这个 PR 做了什么

- 对改到路径 PR 的 fast/full 运行、未改到运行、main push 和 merge group，把与合并相关的 Managed Agent check context 稳定为 `Managed Agent gate`。
- 改到路径但未选择全量运行的 review 仍使用非必需的 `Managed Agent review (no full run)` context；非 approve 和 PR 关闭后的 review 继续跳过，因此没跑套件的或 skipped review 不能覆盖真实 fast/full 结果。同一 head 已有全量报告时，重新运行或重新打开 PR 也会保留该全量结果，而不是用 fast 结果替换。
- 把层级选择提取到 `.github/scripts/managed-agent-gate-tier.sh`，将该脚本纳入 managed-path matcher，并修复 fork review 运行中 `pull_requests` 为空的问题：重跑抑制按 SHA 判断，approve 去重则校验当前 PR 的 head SHA/ref 与候选运行分支。
- 更新 workflow 元测试矩阵以及英文、中文 Managed Agent 门禁设计文档；全量去重测试现在显式覆盖 fast 层级与必需名字相同、以及 fork 运行缺少 PR 元数据的情况。

## 为什么需要

层级相关的 job 名无法安全加入 main ruleset：改到路径的 PR 报告 `Managed Agent fast tier`，而未改到路径和全量运行报告 `Managed Agent gate`。这次修改让与合并相关的 context 保持稳定，同时不允许没跑 Java 的 review 发布或覆盖必需 context。

issues.title: execpolicy: minor over/under-marks in stdin_piped propagation
issues.body:
Round-10 correctness review (execpolicy-c1a55fdcbe) residual findings, non-blocking. Assess each for accept-as-is vs narrow fix:

1. `x || ssh host` denies: the `|` arm fires on each `|` of `||`, marking the next line stdin_piped though nothing is piped. Over-mark.
2. `ssh host 3< f` denies: any `<`-family descriptor marks stdin_piped; fd-3 redirection is not stdin. `0<` vs `3<`/`{fd}<` not distinguished.
3. `ssh host ls <<EOF ... EOF` denies: heredoc body parsed as commands though it feeds the remote command's stdin. Over-deny unless the remote command evals it.
4. `echo 'rm x' | find . -exec ssh host \;` allows: record_find_exec builds its payload line with stdin_piped=false, but -exec children inherit find's stdin. Narrow under-mark.
5. `{ a; ssh h; }` after a pipe: only the first brace-member line gets stdin_piped; group stdin sharing not modeled. Narrow under-mark.
6. numactl spec still lists `strict` in long_values — latent table defect (bare `numactl --strict rm` allowed; destructive forms self-mitigate via head+1 emit).

See reviews/execpolicy-c1a55fdcbe-corr-devin.md for the full traces.

issues.title: execpolicy: tmux execution verbs beyond the modeled set (display-popup, confirm-before, command-prompt, bind-key, source-file)
issues.body:
Round-10 correctness review (execpolicy-c1a55fdcbe) residual finding.

The tmux VerbLauncher models run-shell/run/send-keys/send/if-shell/if/pipe-pane/pipep, but tmux has more command-executing verbs:

- `tmux display-popup 'rm x'` — runs the command in a popup immediately
- `tmux confirm-before 'rm x'` — runs after a confirm prompt
- `tmux command-prompt -I 'rm x'` — user-editable command line
- `tmux bind-key k run-shell 'rm x'` — command bound to a key, executes on press
- `tmux source-file f` — reads commands from a file (file-content launchers may be a separate class)

Mechanism: execpolicy shell_expand.rs VERB_LAUNCHER_SPECS table — evaluate which verbs execute a command tail vs. which are inert, and model the executing ones with the operand-consumption rules each verb needs.

Discovered during execpolicy hardening review; see reviews/execpolicy-c1a55fdcbe-corr-devin.md for the full trace.

issues.title: tui: second Enter gate re-absorbs /command Enter after command-context release

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

issues.body:
## Why this matters
There are two Enter gates in the composer path, and only the first checks command context. Gate 1 (`handle_paste_burst_key`) releases a bare Enter when the draft looks like a slash/$ command, but gate 2 (`handle_composer_enter`) re-runs `newline_should_insert_instead_of_submit` with no command-context check — so whenever paste-suppression evidence is live, the released Enter is re-absorbed as a pasted '\n' and the command does not run.

Pre-existing for the burst band (chars <8ms): a fast-typed `/new` + Enter already swallows within the 120ms window. The slow-paste stream heuristic (#7398) widened the same hole to all ≤60ms-cadence typing: a short muscle-memory command (`/new`, `/quit`, `/model`) typed at 30–60ms/keypress + Enter ≤60ms after the last char lands "/new\n" in the composer instead of executing.

## Current behavior
`event_loop.rs` → `submit_decided_composer_input` → `handle_composer_enter(protect_paste)` in `crates/tui/src/tui/app/composer.rs` — `protect_paste` is just `is_plain_enter`; no `in_command_context` check. `flush_before_modified_input` drains the buffer without clearing `burst_window_until`, so the second gate still sees live evidence.

## Desired behavior
- Decide contract: either accept-and-document that live-evidence command Enters absorb (data-loss-safe default — a pasted `/cmd\nrest` must insert the newline), or pass a release reason into `handle_composer_enter` so gate 2 honors gate 1's command-context release.
- Careful: a naive `looks_like_slash_command_input` check at gate 2 re-breaks pasted slash commands (the original Y-7 data loss).
- Recoverable today: a second Enter submits (`/new\n` trims to `/new`).

Refs #7398; found in adversarial review `pastefix-24b13f4a6f-adv-devin.md` (F1).

issues.title: execpolicy: static script payloads in awk/sed programs are not scanned

labels.name: area:sandbox
labels.description: Sandbox, container, or OS-level isolation behavior

issues.body:
## Why this matters
`awk 'BEGIN{system("rm x")}'` and `sed 's/x/rm y/e'` execute a deny-listed command from inside a fully static program text. The scanner inspects argv words only, so the payload never reaches a deny target. (The runtime-resolved sibling — `awk \$PROG`, `sed -e \$PROG` — was closed in the same audit round by `script_operands_dynamic`; the static case is the remaining half.)

## Current behavior
`crates/execpolicy/src/shell_expand.rs` records awk/sed heads and their operand words; the program text is opaque. Deny `rm` + `AskForApproval::Never` still allows the command.

## Desired behavior
- Scan awk program text for `system(`/`getline … | `getline`-pipe coprocess command strings and sed script text for the `e` flag on `s///`, `e`/`w`-with-command forms; emit any command payload through `code_payload`.
- Where the program text is dynamic, the existing `script_operands_dynamic` fail-closed already applies — keep that path.
- Deny-matrix rows for static `awk 'BEGIN{system("rm x")}'`, `sed 's/a/rm x/e'`, and allow-list rows for ordinary `awk '{print}`/`sed -n '/x/p'`.

Refs #7397

issues.title: execpolicy: find -delete is not treated as a destructive payload

labels.name: area:sandbox
labels.description: Sandbox, container, or OS-level isolation behavior

issues.body:
## Why this matters
`find` arguments are scanned for `-exec`/`-execdir` command payloads, but `-delete` removes every matched file with no command words at all — a deny rule on `rm` does not cover the equivalent deletion.

## Current behavior
`crates/execpolicy/src/shell_expand.rs` handles `-exec`/`-execdir` in `record_find_exec`; `-delete` is an ordinary predicate to the scanner, so `find . -name '*.bak' -delete` emits no deny target even where a same-repo policy denies `rm`.

## Desired behavior
- Decide policy semantics first (deny-list parity vs a dedicated destructive-action rule): either emit `-delete` as an `rm`-equivalent deny target or document that deletion-by-find needs its own rule name.
- If treated as rm-equivalent, add `-delete` (and GNU `-fls`/exec-shaped variants if any) to the find handling and add deny-matrix rows.

Refs #7397

issues.title: execpolicy: unmodeled execution launchers (oc, vagrant, op, opam, helm)

labels.name: area:sandbox
labels.description: Sandbox, container, or OS-level isolation behavior

issues.body:
## Why this matters
Deny rules (e.g. prefix-deny `rm`) only hold for launchers the scanner models. Adversarial review of the execpolicy hardening branch verified that several common launchers run a deny-listed command with no deny target emitted: `oc rsh pod rm x` / `oc exec pod rm x`, `vagrant ssh -c 'rm x'`, `op run -- rm x`, `opam exec -- rm x`, `helm plugin`/post-render hooks and similar verb-bearing tools. `kubectl exec` and `docker container|compose` were closed in the same audit round; these remain.

## Current behavior
`crates/execpolicy/src/shell_expand.rs` models verb launchers through `VerbLauncher` + `launcher_verb_targets`. Unlisted programs treat their words as ordinary command words, so `oc exec pod -- rm x` emits no deny target for `rm`.

## Desired behavior
- Add spec tables + `VerbLauncher` entries for each launcher with a documented operand layout (pod/service consumed before the command words).
- Where a launcher accepts shell strings or hooks (helm post-renderer, op run env), emit the payload through `code_payload` or fail closed when the value is runtime-resolved.
- Deny-matrix rows in `crates/execpolicy/tests/shell_parse_policy.rs` for each new spelling, plus allow-list rows for inert verbs (`oc get pods`, `helm list`).

Refs #7397

issues.title: execpolicy: whole-word dynamic flag/verb names bypass option scanners
issues.body:
Follow-up from the 0.10.3 execpolicy hardening review (PR #7397, round 6).

A word whose ENTIRE flag or verb text is runtime-resolved slips every scanner: `su $(echo -c) 'rm x'`, `nix $(echo develop) -c rm x`, `docker $(echo run) --entrypoint rm alpine`, `ssd --start $(echo --exec) rm -- x`. Verified `denied=false` on both the merge-base and the hardened head.

Mechanism: substitution contributes no text to the word, so it parses as empty + dynamic; every scanner arm requires `token.starts_with('-')` or a static flag/verb name, so the dynamic empty word matches nothing and its bit is dropped.

Proposed direction: in `command_heads`/scanner entry, an empty word with `dynamic=true` at a flag position should emit an unresolved marker (same ('',true) fail-closed shape as the option_payloads fix), and verb-resolution should treat a dynamic verb word as unresolvable rather than positional.

Not a regression — pre-existing on main. Severity: same deny-bypass class as the rest of the round.

issues.body:
## Why this matters
`true -- a -- b -- …` on one command line makes `expand_command` re-run `record_extra_deny` per `--` with a fresh expander — ~2^m redundant work. An attacker-supplied or pathological pasted command can burn the analysis budget (found during adversarial review of the audit fix; a probe test SIGTERM'd on it).

## Current behavior
`crates/execpolicy/src/shell_expand.rs` `record_extra_deny` (~:2018) is invoked once per `--` slice from the parent `--` loop; each child rescans its own tail. No memo/short-circuit on repeated segment structure.

## Desired behavior
- Linear (or linear-bounded) work for a line with many `--` separators, e.g. short-circuit once `extra_deny` hits `MAX_COMMANDS`, or share one expander/scan.
- Behavior contract unchanged: deny targets emitted and `dynamic` set on caps, exactly as today.

## Repro or evidence
Adversarial-review probe: `caps()`-style input `true -- a1 -- a2 -- a3 …` (> ~28 segments) did not finish inside a test timeout. Code path: `shell_expand.rs` `emit_extra_deny`/`record_extra_deny` (~:1414-1427, :2018-2025).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `expand_command` on a 512-segment `--` line completes in bounded time (assert in test, e.g. < 1s)
- [ ] `cargo test -p codewhale-execpolicy` passes including new bound test

issues.title: opencode-zen: free model rows are dead ends in Codewhale — the gateway checks an exact payload and TLS cipher list (429 FreeUsageLimitError)

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: os:linux
labels.description: Linux-specific behaviour

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
### Before you start
- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. Closest closed issue: #6705 (different problem — stale curated wire list).

### What happened?

`opencode-zen` lists Zen's free model ids in the model list — `codewhale model list --provider opencode-zen` returns 50 rows, 11 of them `*-free` (`hy4-flash-free`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, `beam-free`, …) — and `docs/PROVIDERS.md:998` documents the free rows as supported `/chat/completions` models. Every request to one of them fails with the provider's client-scoped refusal:

```
Rate limit exceeded: Free usage limit reached. Free models work in OpenCode (https://opencode.ai);
subscribe to OpenCode Go to keep going: https://opencode.ai/go; … automatic retry stopped
```

The same key and the same model id work in the official OpenCode CLI at the same minute, so this is not a credential or account problem: the entitlement is scoped to the first-party client. Codewhale already recognises the message (`opencode_go_hint`, `crates/engine/src/llm_client/mod.rs:469`), but the catalog surface still offers the rows, so the user selects a model and hits a dead end after the turn has started.

Expected: the free rows work from Codewhale the way they work in the OpenCode CLI with the same key.

### Request

Please make the free OpenCode Zen models work from Codewhale on the `opencode-zen` route.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the Zen route with a key via `OPENCODE_API_KEY` (documented fallback env var, `crates/config/assets/provider_descriptors.json` → `opencode-zen.env_vars`).
2. `codewhale exec --provider opencode-zen --model hy4-flash-free "hi"` (same in the TUI: `/provider` → OpenCode Zen, `/model` → a `*-free` row).
3. The turn ends with the quota-window error quoted above (classified `llm_quota_window`).

Plain curl, same key, outside Codewhale — the same refusal, so it is not a Codewhale request-shape bug:

```bash
curl -s https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCODE_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"hy4-flash-free","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}],"max_tokens":8}'
# HTTP 429
# {"type":"error","error":{"type":"FreeUsageLimitError","message":"Free usage limit reached.
#  Free models work in OpenCode (https://opencode.ai); subscribe to OpenCode Go to keep going: https://opencode.ai/go"}}
```

Control — same key, same model id, same minute, official CLI:

```
opencode run -m opencode/hy4-flash-free "hi"    # normal answer; the session row records
                                               # {"id":"hy4-flash-free","providerID":"opencode"}
```

`GET https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models` with the same key returns 200 and lists the free ids, so the key is valid and the catalog is reachable.

### Verified 2026-11-18: what actually gates the free rows

#### How it was measured

The `opencode` provider's `baseURL` was pointed at a local HTTP capture server through `provider.opencode.options.baseURL`, and one `opencode run -m opencode/hy4-flash-free` was made through it. The captured request (all headers and the full body) was saved and then replayed byte-for-byte against the real endpoint with three clients, using the same key and no proxy:

| Client | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `bun` `fetch` | captured request, byte-for-byte | **HTTP 200**, streamed answer from `hy4-flash-free` |
| `curl` 8.23.0 with OpenSSL defaults | captured request, byte-for-byte | HTTP 429 `FreeUsageLimitError` |
| Node 26 `fetch` (OpenSSL) | captured request, byte-for-byte | HTTP 429 `FreeUsageLimitError` |
| `bun` `fetch` | same headers, simplified body (short system prompt) | HTTP 429 `FreeUsageLimitError` |

#### Correction to the first hypothesis

The first reading of that table was "a TLS fingerprint that only Bun can pass". That was wrong. A second round of measurements with a plain `curl` isolated three independent conditions, all reproducible with standard command-line flags:

1. **Payload.** The system prompt (61 901 characters) and the `tools` array (11 870 characters) must be the client's own, byte for byte. Only the user message (`messages[1].content`) and the model id may change. Truncating the system prompt, dropping `tools`, or keeping a single tool returns 429; changing only the user message returns 200.
2. **TLS cipher list.** The gateway checks both the order and the exact set of suites: TLS 1.3 in the order `AES128 → AES256 → CHACHA`, then this exact TLS 1.2 list:

   ```
   ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-SHA:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-SHA:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA:AES128-GCM-SHA256:AES256-GCM-SHA384:AES128-SHA:AES256-SHA
   ```

   With OpenSSL's default order the request returns 429 even with a valid payload; with the lists below it returns 200. The two curl flags are `--tls13-ciphers` and `--ciphers`. Set separately, either flag alone still returns 429 — both are required.
3. **Session id.** A real `x-opencode-session` id captured from the CLI (`ses_` + 24 characters) is required. A randomly generated id of the same shape returns 429.

Not required: the API key, an `Authorization` header, a proxy, `x-opencode-client`, `x-opencode-project`, `x-session-affinity`, `x-session-id`, or a particular header order. The free tier answers anonymous requests. `wget`, Python `ssl`, `openssl s_client` and 11 `curl-impersonate` profiles (Chrome 100-136, Safari, Firefox, Edge) all return 429 with an otherwise identical request, which is why the first hypothesis looked like a transport fingerprint; the cipher-list comparison shows the check is narrower than that.

#### Working example

The payload is captured once from a real CLI request via the `baseURL` override described above and saved as `free-payload.json` (about 104 KB on disk, about 32 KB gzipped). Replace the session id with a freshly captured one. Note that this route is `https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1/chat/completions`, different from the `/zen/v1` route used in the original reproduction above.

```bash
jq -c --arg q 'Say hi in one word' '.messages[1].content = $q' free-payload.json \
| curl -sN https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'User-Agent: opencode/latest/2.2.0/cli' \
    -H 'x-opencode-session: <real-session-id-from-cli>' \
    --tls13-ciphers 'TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256:TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256' \
    --ciphers 'ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-SHA:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA:ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-SHA:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA:AES128-GCM-SHA256:AES256-GCM-SHA384:AES128-SHA:AES256-SHA' \
    --data-binary @- \
| sed -n 's/^data: //p' | grep -v '^\[DONE\]$' \
| jq -r 'select(.choices[0].delta.content != null) | .choices[0].delta.content' | tr -d '\n'
```

Observed on 2026-11-18 with curl 8.23.0, no key and no proxy: `hy4-flash-free` answered with a single-word greeting, `glm-5.3-flash-free` answered `pong`. A control request with the same payload and the same session id, but with neither cipher flag, returned HTTP 429 with `Retry-After: 78867` seconds. The 429 is the per-IP free-tier limit, so wait for that window instead of retrying in a loop; this is a rate limit, not a ban.

#### Caveats

The payload is tied to client version `2.2.0`: if the server-side prompt changes, a fresh capture is needed. The session id may expire and needs to be captured again. These measurements describe an intentional client gate; whether Codewhale should reproduce a first-party client is a maintainer decision.

#### Implication for the fix

Codewhale has to reproduce the exact payload, carry a valid session id, and present a matching cipher list. Changing the User-Agent or adding `x-opencode-*` headers alone is not enough.

### Codewhale version
`codewhale 0.10.3 (dev)` (built from a git checkout)

### Where did it happen?
TUI (terminal interface), CLI command (`codewhale exec`)

### Operating system
Linux

### How did you get Codewhale?
Built from a git checkout

### Provider and model
`opencode-zen` / `hy4-flash-free` (also `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, `glm-5.3-flash-free`, `beam-free`, … — 11 free rows in total)

### Possible cause (not verified)
`client_user_agent()` (`crates/engine/src/client.rs:331`) sends `Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; codewhale/<version>; +https://github.com/codewhale-hq/CodeWhale)` on every route, so the provider can distinguish Codewhale from the OpenCode app. I did not test whether a different User-Agent changes the result: that would mean impersonating the first-party client, and whether this project should do that is the maintainers' decision, not mine.

Update 2026-11-18: verified above — sending the first-party User-Agent alone does not change the result. The exact request body, a real session id and the matching TLS cipher list are all required. Whether Codewhale should impersonate the first-party client remains the maintainers' decision.

issues.body:
Before each model request, `prepare_model_bound_request` (`crates/engine/src/client.rs`) passes every tool result in the conversation through `redact_model_bound_secrets` again, so the redaction cost is paid on every call and grows with the session. Redaction itself is slow on ordinary text: on a 2.8 MB mix of this repo's source, `Cargo.lock` and JSON files, one pass takes about 317 ms here (release build, Windows 11, i7-9700), roughly 9 MB/s.

I have a change ready in `crates/sanitize/src/redact.rs` that brings that pass to about 127 ms (about 2.5x) without changing any masking rule or any output. The old and new code give byte-identical results on every text file in the repo and on fuzzed input, and the existing sanitize tests pass.

Since this sits next to the credential handling that CONTRIBUTING asks to discuss first: would you take a PR for it?

prs.title: feat(web): add SearchApi as a web search provider
prs.body:
Disclosure first: I work at [SearchApi](https://www.searchapi.io) (developer advocate), so I have a vendor interest in this change.

## What and why

Adds **SearchApi** as an opt-in `[search]` provider for the Web tool, next to Serply and the other keyed SERP backends. It calls `GET https://www.searchapi.io/api/v1/search?engine=google&q=...` with `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and returns Google organic results (title, URL, snippet). Nothing changes for anyone who does not set `provider = "searchapi"`: the default stays keyless Firecrawl, the provider order and the degradation chain are untouched, and `searchapi` is appended at the end of every enumeration.

Configuration:

```toml
[search]
provider = "searchapi"   # also accepts "search-api" and "search_api"
api_key = "..."          # or the SEARCHAPI_API_KEY env var
```

Recency and locale are forwarded, since the Google engine documents them: `time_period=last_day|last_week|last_month|last_year`, `hl` (language) and `gl` (country). `num` is honored by the API up to 10 and clamped above that, which matches the shared tool's 10-result cap.

## Where this came from

Provider addition, no issue (CONTRIBUTING.md lists providers as a standing project that needs no issue first). Same shape as the Serply provider in #6100, brought up to today's tree where the request plan and the response parse also run through the TypeScript Web Host adapter.

## Checking the description against the code

- Provider enum, aliases, `parse`/`as_str`, `names_hint`: `SearchProvider::SearchApi` in `crates/runtime/src/config/search.rs` (serde `rename = "searchapi"`, aliases `search-api`, `search_api`).
- Backend id: `BackendId::SearchApi` in `crates/engine/src/tools/web/contract.rs`; the configured-backend mapping, the `(recency, locale) = (true, true)` capability row and the configuration hint (`searchapi accepts SEARCHAPI_API_KEY`) in `crates/engine/src/tools/web/backend.rs`.
- Request and parse: `SEARCHAPI_ENDPOINT`, `WebSearchTool::run_searchapi_search`, `searchapi_search_url`, `parse_searchapi_results` in `crates/engine/src/tools/web_search.rs`. The key is sent as a Bearer header, never as a query parameter. Fail-closed gate when no key is configured (`not_configured(...)` arm), host allowlist entry `www.searchapi.io`, network-policy check before the request, probe target for `codewhale doctor --probe-search`.
- Web Host adapter: `case 'searchapi'` in `provider()` (reads `organic_results[]`, `link`, `snippet`) and in `request()` (keyless pairs `q`, `engine=google`, `num`, optional `time_period`, `hl`, `gl`) in `crates/engine/extension-host/src/builtin/shared/web-adapters.ts`. The Rust-side plan validator in `host_request` admits `searchapi` with the GET-pair providers and the two new keys `engine` and `time_period`. `dist/` is rebuilt from source and the `harness` digest in `crates/engine/src/extension_host/tier.rs` is updated to match (`BUILTIN_MODULES` test passes).
- TUI / command contract: `CommandSearchProvider::SearchApi` in `crates/command-contract/src/config.rs`, both mapping functions in `crates/tui/src/commands/config_host.rs`, `SEARCHAPI_API_KEY` recognised as a workspace `.env` credential key in `crates/tui/src/lib.rs`, and added to `PRODUCT_RESERVED_ENV_VARS` in `crates/config/src/cloud_facts/registry.rs`.
- Docs: `config.example.toml`, `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` and `docs/zh_hans/CONFIGURATION.md` (recency/locale table row, provider paragraph, provider list in the example). `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/CONTRIBUTORS.md` are deliberately untouched per CONTRIBUTING.md.

Things a reviewer should know:

- **Zero results are not an error.** When Google returns nothing, SearchApi answers HTTP 200 with `search_metadata` plus `error: "Google didn't return any results."` and no `organic_results`. The parser reads that as an empty list, so the existing empty-result degradation (DuckDuckGo then Bing) applies, same as the other API providers.
- **`google.com/goto?url=...` links.** Some lower-ranked rows carry a Google redirect as their link. They are passed through unchanged, like any other URL; the parser does not unwrap them.
- **Bad key** is a plain HTTP 401 `{"error":"Invalid API key."}`, surfaced through the existing non-2xx path with the truncated body.
- `num` above 10 is clamped by the API (verified live: `num=15` is echoed back as `num: 10`), so no client-side clamp was added beyond the tool's own cap.

## How I tested it

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-runtime search`: `test result: ok. 18 passed; 0 failed` (16 before, +2 new: explicit `provider = "searchapi"` is preserved; aliases parse and the value round-trips through serde).
- `cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib -- searchapi tools::web::backend extension_host::tier search_host_tests serply`: `test result: ok. 38 passed; 0 failed`. New tests: `searchapi_search_url_encodes_query_engine_and_result_count`, `parse_searchapi_results_reads_link_and_snippet_and_treats_no_organic_rows_as_empty` (sample with a `goto` row, a row without link, a non-object row, `max_results` cut, the no-results body and an error body), `searchapi_missing_key_is_fail_closed_inside_the_backend_chain`, `searchapi_provider_without_api_key_surfaces_clear_error_not_silent_fallback`, `searchapi_url_carries_recency_language_and_country`; plus a `searchapi` row in the Rust-vs-Host parity test (`search_host_tests.rs`) and in the backend mapping, locale-capability and configuration-hint tests.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-config reserved`: `2 passed; 0 failed`.
- `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-config -p codewhale-command-contract`: finished without warnings from the touched files.
- `cargo clippy -p codewhale-runtime -p codewhale-engine --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings -A clippy::uninlined_format_args -A clippy::too_many_arguments -A clippy::unnecessary_map_or`: finished, no warnings in the touched crates (only the pre-existing `codewhale-ratatui` manifest lints note).
- `crates/engine/extension-host`: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` (the rebuilt `dist/` is committed; a rebuild of the untouched tree before my change reproduced the committed bundle byte for byte), `npm test`: `tests 528, pass 521, fail 0` (rest skipped as before). New: a `searchapi` row in the alias/whitespace table, `searchapi` in the keyless-plan loop, two request-pair assertions (`q`, `engine`, `num`, `time_period`, `hl`, `gl`), and a parse test with a `goto` row plus the no-results body.
- Live call (key from env, not in the repo): `GET /api/v1/search?engine=google&q=ratatui+rust+terminal+ui&num=3&hl=en&gl=us` returned HTTP 200, `search_metadata.status: "Success"`, 3 `organic_results` with `title`, `link`, `snippet`, `domain`, `displayed_link`, `position` (one row also had `date`). `time_period=last_week` was echoed back in `search_parameters` and narrowed the result set; `num=15` was echoed back as `num: 10`. A bogus key returned HTTP 401 `{"error":"Invalid API key."}`. The end-to-end Codewhale request path was not exercised against the live API; it is covered by the unit and host tests above.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [x] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — docs updated; no new feature row, the existing `web-search` feature already covers configured search providers (same as the Serply PR)

prs.title: 0.10.3 lane 8 batch 2: stop the repeated `--` stall in command policy
prs.body:
## What and why `f553b4a033` **repeated `--`**: each unquoted `--` makes `record_extra_deny` expand the suffix after it, and each child `Expander` then walked every later `--` again. Expansion time grew about 2.7× per pair of `--`: `npm` followed by 24 `--` took about 14 s, and 50 still hadn't finished after 20 minutes. Found by the adversarial review of #7385 ([comment](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7385#issuecomment-7004281767)); main `c5b484aa6` has the same problem. `record_extra_deny` now shares a map from each suffix (words, dynamic/odd/quoted flags, `literal_backslashes`) to the shallowest depth it was expanded at. The map is moved into each child and taken back afterwards. A suffix already expanded at the same or a shallower depth is skipped. Every suffix is still expanded at its shallowest depth, and its deny lines still reach the top expander. This is the first slice of lane 8's second batch, cut from `main`. More execpolicy follow-ups will stack here; the ones that touch the launcher arm wait for #7385. ## Where this came from Bug fix. Refs #7283, #7284 ## How I tested it On Linux x86_64: - `cargo test --locked -p codewhale-execpolicy`: 268 passed, 0 failed (246 unit, 1, 11, 9, 1 doctest). - The new test `repeated_double_dash_expands_in_bounded_time` runs `echo` and `npm` with 40 `--` and checks that `rm -rf /` is still a deny command. It passes in under 5 s. With the skip disabled, it was still running when `timeout` killed it at 120 s. - `cargo clippy --locked -p codewhale-execpolicy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p codewhale-execpolicy -- --check` and `sh scripts/sync-changelog.sh --check` are clean. ## Checklist - [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves) - [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior - [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (n/a) ---

prs.title: feat(tui): CW-8264 settle flash, plus the two v3 TUI fixes main lacks
prs.body:
## What and why This PR targets `main` (`c5b484aa6`, which has release-prep v2 squashed in as #7386). It contains three commits: 1. `fe717a57b` fix(tui): fold plain `task_shell_wait` polls into the shell's own row (carried from v3 `66699e11e7`) 2. `172f6b352` fix(tui): hold the composer border still while the transcript is scrolled away (carried from v3 `394d88c951`; the measured cause of the Terminal.app flicker from CW-8264 `ef51913d63`) 3. `8d7945310` feat(tui): flash a tool row's outcome once when it settles (CW-8264, new) v3's third commit, `4bee24fd7d` (Terminal.app scrollbar inset), is deliberately left out. codewhale-ops CURRENT_DECISIONS §231 drops it and keeps the scrollbar flush with the right edge. Commit 3: CW-8264 asks for color-coded running → done/failed transitions with a brief flash. `ef51913d63` (now on main) added the running-row sweep and breathing composer border. A finished row still switched to `done` in one silent repaint, though. `apply_settle_flash` runs on the visible lines after the transcript cache, so it invalidates nothing. It reads the existing `active_tool_entry_completed_at` timestamps and adds no new state. For 680 ms (2 × `MOTION_DURATION_PANEL_MS`, ease-out from `ACTIVITY_SWEEP_PEAK`), a row's status mark, family glyph and outcome word blend toward `tool_success` or `tool_failed`. A failed row whose ink is already `tool_failed` lifts toward `text_body` and back. Shell rows flash only the mark and, on failure, the `failed` word. The summary, path and command never flash. The contrast guard in `activity_sweep_ink` still applies. The `activity_sweep_allowed` gate turns the flash off under Reduced/Still, `fancy_animations = false`, sub-truecolor terminals, `NO_COLOR` and non-RGB themes. A visible flash keeps the 66 ms tier for its 680 ms only; activity motion requests no frames at idle. Design note with frames, reduced-motion path and perf budget: codewhale-ops `design/TUI-ACTIVITY-MOTION-20261119.md` ([ops #37](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/codewhale-ops/pull/37)). ## Where this came from Linear CW-8264 (TUI: a working session looks dead). `ci/cw-8264-motion-v3` and `claude-CW-8264-motion` are earlier versions of `ef51913d63` and do not contain the settle flash. ## How I tested it These runs were on `5d870582f`, which has the same settle-flash patch on the v3 base. - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean. `sh scripts/sync-changelog.sh --check`: up to date (this head). - `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- settled_tool_rows`: 1 passed, 0 failed (new regression test; renders real generic success and failed rows and a failed shell row, and checks that the summary or command never changes and nothing is left behind at 680 ms) - `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- tui::widgets:: tui::history tui::transcript tui::ui::motion`: 479 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored - Two independent exact-SHA LAND reviews and a live TUI recording are in progress. ## Checklist - [x] Focused change on current `main` - [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior - [x] No new feature flag or command, so no `docs/features.toml` row ---

prs.title: fix(tui): large pastes no longer freeze the composer
prs.body: ## Summary - **O(n²) raw-char path:** non-ASCII `KeyCode::Char` input (CJK paste on a terminal without bracketed-paste) ran ~10 O(n) passes per char through `insert_char`. Those chars now feed the existing `PasteBurst` state machine — `rapid_chars >= 2` starts buffering, same as the ASCII path. - **Trusted-gate correction:** gate now requires `bracketed_paste_seen || (bracketed_paste_trusted && use_bracketed_paste)`. - **O(n) re-wrap ×3 per frame:** `desired_height` now counts rows only up to the layout cap via `native_composer_wrap_text_bounded`/`source_row_count`; `plan` computes the source once and reuses it (`plan_with_source`) for the clipped submit-hint re-plan; the dead O(n) text copy in plan removed (`Cow::Borrowed`). - Known pre-existing bound (unchanged): `PASTE_BURST_MAX_BYTES` = 64 KiB still caps the burst buffer for raw pastes — filed for follow-up. ## Test plan - [x] paste filters: 59 + wrap: 61 + composer: 166 + widgets: 295 + tui-kit: 222 + ratatui: 153 — all green - [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean Generated with [Devin](https://devin.ai) ---

prs.title: feat(acp): file tool calls carry their absolute location and the requested diff
prs.body:
## Summary Refs #7280 (ACP server lane for 0.10.3). I checked #7280's four gaps against the code. One code gap was still open: - **Session load/resume:** already on this branch (`session/list`, `session/load` with prefix match, durable replay, checkpoint after each turn). - **Permission dial:** already on this branch. The editor gets `session/request_permission` tied to the Runtime approval, with responder `ApprovalResponder::Acp`. The posture is server-owned and read-only, and remembered grants are never given. That is the documented contract. - **Plugins in ACP sessions:** already on this branch (CW-7941 and CW-8050: extension host plus configured MCP servers, and nested approvals). - **File/terminal tool updates:** this was the gap, and this PR fixes it. A tool call carried only a title and `rawInput`, so an editor could not follow the agent to the file or show the change. `tool_call_start(call, workspace)` now: ``` kind ∈ {Read, Edit} && input.path → locations: [{ path: workspace.join(path) }] kind == Edit → content: [diff { path, newText: content }] // write [diff { path, oldText: search, newText: replace }] // edit (+ old_string/new_string… aliases) ``` - The live projection gets the workspace from `ThreadRecord.workspace`. - `session/load` replay gets it from `SessionMetadata.workspace`. - `apply_patch` gets no diff. - Shell output is still text content: editor-owned ACP `terminal` content is not used. `docs/RUNTIME_API.md` now says so. - CHANGELOG has a new 0.10.3 line, and `scripts/sync-changelog.sh` was run. ## Tests (Linux, bubblewrap installed) - `cargo test -p codewhale-app-server --lib acp_server`: **44 passed; 0 failed**. This includes the new `file_tool_start_names_absolute_location_and_requested_diff`. - `cargo test -p codewhale-app-server --test integration acp`: **4 passed; 0 failed**. These are `acp_conformance::every_frame_the_acp_server_writes_is_an_official_v1_shape` and the 3 `acp_journey` tests. - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean. Not run: a real-editor (Zed) journey. ---

auto_merge.commit_message:
* docs: remove the ten Indonesian redirect stubs

docs/*.id.md were added on 2026-08-18 as redirects to docs/id/ "for one
release cycle". Three releases have shipped since and no tracked file
links any of them. The translated pages in docs/id/ and
docs/i18n/README.id.md are untouched.

docs/README.md line 5 still describes `*.id.md` as a translation
location; that file belongs to another in-flight slice and is corrected
by the docs index rewrite.

Check: the docs link checker reports the same 13 broken links and 1 bad
anchor as before the removal (none new).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci(docs): add a warn-only Markdown link check

No job checked Markdown links. scripts/docs/check-links.py reads every
tracked Markdown file and reports relative links, repository URLs and
anchors that resolve to nothing; it does not fetch external URLs. It
prints findings and exits 0, with --strict to fail and --orphans to list
docs pages nothing links, in the style of scripts/check-lexicon.py.

scripts/docs/run-checks.sh runs every scripts/docs/check-* file, so a
later docs check is one new file and no workflow edit. The Lint job runs
it as one step.

Today's output on this tree: 376 Markdown files, 13 broken links, 0
missing anchors. Eight of the 13 are in the generated
crates/tui/CHANGELOG.md, four are the moved skills-catalog-matrix.json
path and one is in docs/id/INSTALL.md. The Hindi README anchor an
earlier audit script reported was that script's error: its slug rule
dropped Devanagari vowel signs.

Checks: sh scripts/docs/run-checks.sh (exit 0), check-links.py --strict
(exit 1, as expected with findings), ci.yml parses as YAML.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: fix the skills matrix link, a moved config path and hook mode labels

- docs/SKILLS.md and its zh_hans peer linked
  crates/tui/assets/skills-catalog-matrix.json; the file is at
  crates/skills/assets/. Two broken links fixed.
- docs/LSP_PHP_CUSTOM.md and its peer named crates/tui/src/config.rs for
  LspConfigToml; it is in crates/runtime/src/config.rs.
- docs/HOOKS.md and its peer said hooks receive `OPERATE` / `Operate` in
  DEEPSEEK_MODE. AppMode has two values: UI-fired events send
  hook_label() (`ACT`, `PLAN`) and tool_call_before sends the Debug
  spelling (`Agent`, `Plan`). The page now says so and says why the
  pre-rename names stay.

MCP.md and MEMORY.md needed no path fix. The vocabulary sweep of these
pages is not in this commit; it waits for the docs vocabulary decision.

Checks: link checker 13 -> 11 broken links, none new;
scripts/check-tui-product-vocabulary.sh passes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: fix moved code paths and a retired mode row on eight pages

- LIVE_SMOKE.md (+ zh_hans): skills-catalog-matrix.json is in
  crates/skills/assets/. Two broken links fixed.
- TOOL_SURFACE.md (+ zh_hans): subagent_limits.rs is in
  crates/runtime/src/config/.
- LEGACY_PATHS.md (+ zh_hans): workspace_trust.rs is in crates/runtime/src/.
- THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md: credential_resolve.rs is in
  crates/runtime/src/config/.
- web/README.md: derive-facts.mjs is web/scripts/derive-facts.mjs, and it
  reads the provider list from
  crates/config/assets/provider_descriptors.json, not
  crates/tui/src/config.rs (checked against web/scripts/facts-lib.mjs).
- CACHE.md (+ zh_hans): the mode-change row listed operate and yolo;
  AppMode has Plan and Work.

Not changed: BUILD_PERFORMANCE.md names crates/tui/src/config.rs inside a
dated refactoring plan whose status needs its owner, and its
dev-test.test.sh mentions already say the file was removed.
zh_hans/ENVIRONMENTS.md is still missing the Fleet placement section.
WEB.md, PET_MODE.md and RECEIPTS.md needed no path fix.

Check: link checker 13 -> 11 broken links, none new.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: add the voice input page and fix the voice charter's stale terms

docs/VOICE.md is the writing charter, and /voicecontrol and /voicesend
appeared in no doc. docs/VOICE_INPUT.md is the user page: recorders per
system, the three commands and their aliases, how a recording ends, the
send phrases, what voice control sends, the backend order and the
CODEWHALE_ASR_MODEL values, CODEWHALE_DISABLE_VOICE, and the messages a

from the CLI help of this tree (crates/cli, crates/account-cli) and

`account-login` has no docs path (features-rows,

Needs a privacy review before landing, as the audit asks.

prs.body:
## What and why The CNB Cool (`cnb.cool/codewhale.net/codewhale`) and GitCode (`gitcode.com/HunterBown/Codewhale`) mirrors must stay current so users can always install and test the latest build. `main` pushes and `release.yml` already sync both mirrors, and both match `main` and `v0.10.2` today. Two gaps remain: a release published outside `release.yml` (its `GITHUB_TOKEN` publication fires no event), and a push or release whose sync never ran or failed. - `sync-cnb.yml` and `sync-gitcode.yml` now also run on `release: published`. Prereleases are skipped, as in `release.yml`. - Both workflows also run at :17 and :47 each hour. This backstop re-mirrors `main` and copies the **latest published GitHub Release** tag when a mirror lacks it, then verifies it with `verify-remote-tag.sh`. - On CNB the tag starts CNB's release build, so the run checks the release with `verify-release-inventory.js` before pushing. - If the CNB tag is already there, the run also requires its `codewhale-artifacts-sha256.txt` to be downloadable. - Tags are never forced, and prereleases or tags still awaiting publication are never copied. Nothing creates a tag or release. A tag that differs on a mirror fails the run. `CNB_MIRROR` and `GITCODE_MIRROR` still switch the mirrors off. - `docs/CNB_MIRROR.md` (+ zh_hans) now describes these triggers. It no longer claims `fix/*`, `rebrand/*` or `work/v*` branches are mirrored, and it names GitCode as the second mirror, which carries source only. - No changelog hunks: per CONTRIBUTING.md, the entry is written on `main` at merge time. ## Where this came from Founder request to keep the CNB and GitCode mirrors updated in real time. This is a CI and docs change with no issue. The app mirror and the setup doc are in [codewhale-app#3577](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/codewhale-app/pull/3577) and [codewhale-ops#24](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/codewhale-ops/pull/24). ## How I tested it - `actionlint` on `sync-cnb.yml`, `sync-gitcode.yml` and `release.yml`: exit 0. - `node .github/scripts/release-workflows.test.js`: exit 0 ("17 checks passed"). - `verify-remote-tag.sh` for `v0.10.2` against cnb.cool and gitcode.com: OK (`ff466b2ed0`). The CNB `v0.10.2` manifest returns HTTP 200, and a wrong SHA exits 1. - Not verified: the first scheduled run and a `release: published` run on GitHub. These can only run after merge. ## Checklist - [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves) - [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior - [x] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) ---

auto_merge.commit_title: ci(mirror): sync CNB and GitCode on every published release, with a half-hourly backstop (#7380)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* ci(mirror): re-check CNB and GitCode mirrors every half hour

The founder wants the CNB Cool and GitCode mirrors current at all times so
users can install and test the latest build. Push and release syncs already
existed; nothing caught a main push that started no workflow (pushes made
with GITHUB_TOKEN, an Actions outage, an expired mirror token) or a release
whose mirror job failed.

- sync-cnb.yml and sync-gitcode.yml also run at :17 and :47 each hour. The
  schedule takes the existing main path (a no-op push when already in sync)
  and honours CNB_MIRROR / GITCODE_MIRROR like a main push.
- A scheduled run then resolves the latest GitHub Release and checks its tag
  on the mirror with scripts/release/verify-remote-tag.sh; on CNB it also
  requires the release's codewhale-artifacts-sha256.txt. It never pushes a
  tag, so it cannot start CNB's release pipeline.
- docs/CNB_MIRROR.md (and zh_hans) no longer claim fix/*, rebrand/* and
  work/v* branches are mirrored; push syncs cover main only. GitCode is
  named as the source-only second mirror.

Evidence:
- actionlint sync-cnb.yml sync-gitcode.yml release.yml: exit 0.
- node .github/scripts/release-workflows.test.js: exit 0 (17 hermetic
  invocation checks passed, 11 wrapper event cases).
- verify-remote-tag.sh v0.10.2 against cnb.cool and gitcode.com: OK
  (ff466b2ed0); CNB v0.10.2 manifest: HTTP 200; a wrong SHA exits 1.
- sh scripts/sync-changelog.sh --check: up to date.
- Not verified: the first scheduled run on GitHub.

* ci(mirror): sync CNB and GitCode on every published release

Real time means a release reaches the mirrors when it is published, not at
the next schedule. Both workflows now also run on release: published (for a
release published outside release.yml, whose GITHUB_TOKEN publication fires
no event); prereleases are skipped as in release.yml. The half-hourly run is
the backstop and now repairs instead of only reporting: CNB pushes the latest
GitHub Release tag when missing (after verify-release-inventory.js, since the
tag starts CNB's release build), GitCode pushes every v* tag as a manual
dispatch already did. Tags are never forced and nothing creates a tag or
release; a tag that differs on a mirror still fails the run.

Evidence: actionlint sync-cnb.yml sync-gitcode.yml release.yml exit 0;
node .github/scripts/release-workflows.test.js exit 0 (17 hermetic checks
passed); sync-changelog.sh --check up to date.

* chore: strip changelog hunks (written on main at merge time)

* ci(mirror): GitCode backstop copies only the latest published release

The schedule pushed every v* tag, including prereleases and tags whose
release was still being built. It now pushes only the latest GitHub Release
tag when GitCode lacks it and then verifies it, like CNB.

Evidence: actionlint sync-*.yml release.yml exit 0;
release-workflows.test.js exit 0.

## What and why Keep indexless Gemini parallel calls separate without changing other providers’ indexed routing. Preserve late thought signatures, require a signature only on the first call in each replayed batch, and reject ambiguous continuations rather than attaching arguments to the wrong tool. Honor Hydrogen’s `xhigh`, the published `low` floor, and `auto`. Extract messages, quota codes, and retry delays from singleton-array provider errors. ## Where this came from Provider bug fix: transplants [`a05ce3c0695`](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/a05ce3c0695743feb6890ad33f292133ec6e7430) without its unrelated branch history. Rebased on `main` after [0.10.3 release prep](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7386) merged. ## How I tested it - Rust 1.100.0, locked nextest for Engine and Models: 7,876 passed, 0 failed, 13 skipped by the test profile. Six focused regressions also passed. - Rust 1.100.0 Engine Clippy passed with all targets and features, warnings denied, and the three existing CI allowances. - Formatting, changelog synchronization, and `scripts/preflight.sh --check --base origin/main` passed. - Independent reviews and exact-SHA hosted CI are pending. ---

prs.body:
## Summary Lands Hunter's `ci/dsh-plugin-parity-0103` WIP (`c04c9952f`, `5a25bda4e`), rebased onto main `c5b484aa6`, plus the fixes found while qualifying the pinned DSH rows (#7278) and CW-8288. Refs #7278, #7284. From the WIP: - `codewhale plugins import dsh ` / `import dsh approve ` - read-only `tools/post-execute` observers (they see `{is_error, duration_ms}` only) - `plugins.item` / `plugins.detail.actions` / `plugins.detail.badge` seats - reviewed static CSS/SVG/image/font assets (SVG served under a sandbox CSP) - pnpm-style confined `node_modules` symlinks materialized at install Added here: - **fix(app-server):** DSH static assets returned 404. The grant's `ui_prefix` is `source/` (taken from `source/package.json`), but DSH asset paths are already relative to the bundle root, so the lookup became `source/source/lib/style.css`. DSH grants now resolve against the bundle root, as `verify_dsh_closure` already does. Non-DSH bundles still use `ui_prefix`. `plugin_ui_dsh_serves_reviewed_static_assets_and_detail_slots` failed before this fix and passes after it. - **fix(app-server), CW-8288:** in `DSH_BOOTSTRAP_TAIL`, `resolve(from, id)` used `from.slice(0, lastIndexOf("/"))`. For an entry at the root (`client.js`) it got `-1`, so `./helper` became `client./helper`. The directory part is now empty when `from` has no `/`. Regression test: `dsh_bootstrap_resolves_relative_requires_from_a_root_level_entry`. - **test(dsh-acceptance):** added `--allow-host` (repeatable). It writes `[network] allow` into the isolated `CODEWHALE_HOME` and records the hosts as `network_allow` in the receipt. Without it, every row with npm deps was refused at admission with "Network approval required for registry.npmjs.org". - `crates/tui/CHANGELOG.md` sync and rustfmt for the WIP files. ## Evidence (local, Linux x86_64) - `cargo test -p codewhale-app-server --lib -- plugin_ui`: `test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed` (before the asset fix: 3 passed; 1 failed, CSS HTTP 404) - `cargo test -p codewhale-plugins --lib -- npm_deps dsh`: `test result: ok. 30 passed; 0 failed` - `node --test test/*.test.mjs` in `crates/engine/extension-host`: 519 pass, 0 fail, 6 skipped - `dsh_acceptance.py selftest`: 15 passed, 0 failed - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `scripts/sync-changelog.sh --check` up to date - Acceptance driver against a source build of `5a25bda4e`: 26 of 33 rows pass the full Engine lifecycle. Rows 14/19/29 are refused as pinned. Rows 11/22/25 are refused by the 2 MiB DSH source scan limit. Row 4's pinned artifact is unavailable. No row is PASS, because `journey.core` has no scripted journey and provider calls were off. The per-row list is in [codewhale-ops#38](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/codewhale-ops/pull/38). Exact-SHA CI is not run yet. ---

prs.body: ## Summary Fixes from the overnight 0.10.3 audit (see artifacts report), one commit per finding: - **V4:** ACP external-agent tool calls never left `pending` — the completion arm required `metadata/execution_id`; now falls back to `metadata/external_agent/tool_call_id` + regression test. - **V5:** ACP shell calls ran operator `shell_env` hooks despite the documented no-hooks contract — `collect_shell_env` now gated on `acp_host.is_none()` (covers profile + per-turn narrowing; native path unchanged). - **V6:** mobile kept one stream ticket per session (two tabs invalidated each other) — bounded 32-ticket vec mirroring the web surface + test. - **V7:** LSP HTTP mixed 1-based input with 0-based output — additive `position_base` field on responses, documented. - **S3:** a contained pnpm `node_modules` **directory** link was accepted then silently skipped — now a named refusal (file links/.bin shims still fine). - **S4:** external-agent locations dropped `line` — now carried in item metadata (bounded); diff bodies stay summarized per the deliberate MAX_DETAIL_BYTES bound. - **S2 verified-not-a-bug:** the ACP SDK dispatches same-connection requests serially; no interleaving possible. ## Test plan - [x] app-server lib: 895/903 (7 load flakes pass serially; 1 pre-existing base failure unrelated) - [x] integration 28/28, plugins 283/283, engine+lsp check clean Generated with [Devin](https://devin.ai) ---

prs.title: fix(execpolicy): nix --command= attached forms hide payloads from deny rules
prs.body: ## Summary - **Audit V1 (HIGH, verified):** `nix develop --command='rm -rf /'` and `nix shell --command=...` were allowed under a deny-`rm` ruleset with `AskForApproval::Never` — the `nix` launcher arm only matched separated `-c`/`--command` tokens. Attached long (`--command=CMD`), attached short (`-cCMD`) and clustered (`-ic CMD`) forms now flow through `code_payload` AND are recorded as argv[0] over the remaining tokens, covering both nix's argv and shell-string interpretations. - **Audit S1 (LOW):** `emit_extra_deny`/`record_extra_deny` now set `dynamic = true` when caps drop deny targets — fail closed, matching `emit()`'s existing behavior. - Regression rows prove all three spellings denied pre-fix and post-fix; 269/269 execpolicy tests pass. The suggested `option_payloads` shape was deliberately not used (it would regress existing argv coverage — documented in the commit). Found by the overnight 0.10.3 audit (deepseek-v4.1-flash). ## Test plan - [x] `cargo test -p codewhale-execpolicy` — 269 pass - [x] Negative check: fix stashed → new spellings bypass deny (reproduced) - [x] clippy + fmt clean Generated with [Devin](https://devin.ai) ---

prs.title: build(npm,ci): Node.js 22 floor for the npm wrapper and a weekly floating-stable check (CW-8205)
prs.body:
## What and why Finishes the Engine part of the 0.10.3 release updates (CURRENT_DECISIONS §189): - **Node.js 22 floor (§189.3):** the founder decided the `codewhale` npm package requires Node.js 22 or newer. `npm/codewhale/package.json` `engines.node` and the install-time check in `scripts/install.js` move from 18 to 22. On Node.js 18 or 20 the install now stops and asks you to upgrade. `docs/INSTALL.md` (en, zh), `web/lib/content/install.ts` and the generated web facts and agent docs follow. CHANGELOG line added. - **Weekly floating-stable check (§189.4, critic note on PLAN RU-01):** new `.github/workflows/toolchain-drift.yml` runs the Lint job's clippy command on `stable` every Monday (and on dispatch). It reports only: it is not required and it never moves the `rust-toolchain.toml` 1.100.0 pin, so a new Rust release's breaks show up before someone moves the pin. `release-workflows.test.js` lets this one workflow select `stable`, and every other workflow must still equal the pin or MSRV. Already on main and not touched here: the 1.100.0 pin, the MSRV 1.89 job, RU-02 runner and tool pins, and the RU-03 lock stack (clipboard-win 5.4.3, rustls-webpki 0.103.17, tokio 1.54.1, aws-lc-sys 0.47.0). `cargo audit` on main shows 0 vulnerabilities; the remaining warnings are unmaintained notices (bincode, chrono, humantime, zbus family). ## Where this came from Linear CW-8205 (0.10.3 release updates). No GitHub issue. ## How I tested it - `node .github/scripts/release-workflows.test.js`: OK - `npm test` in `npm/codewhale`: 104 passed, 0 failed - `npx vitest run lib/facts.test.ts lib/check-facts.test.ts lib/facts-drift.test.ts` in `web`: 30 passed - `npm run prebuild` then `node scripts/check-facts.mjs` in `web`: OK - `python3 scripts/test_ci_migration_wiring.py`: OK - `actionlint` 1.7.9 on `toolchain-drift.yml`: clean - Not run: hosted CI on this SHA, and the drift workflow itself (it starts on its schedule or by dispatch after merge). ## Checklist - [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves) - [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior (no Rust changed) - [x] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (no feature row applies) ---

prs.title: 0.10.3 lane 8: execpolicy launcher panic and payload-hiding fixes
prs.body: ## Summary Lane 8 batch, rebased onto `main` `c5b484aa6` after #7386 landed release-prep (range-diff against the earlier `25e73276b5` base: all 10 commits identical). Replaces #7375 (closed). - `66bb715829` **guard launcher verb index on flag-only commands**: `npm --version`, `docker --version`, `nix --version` and similar inputs panicked in `Expander::record_launcher_commands`. The cause: `resolve_wrapper_targets` returns `tokens.len()`, and that index was used unchecked. This is #7375's `03aee41843` restacked, source patch identical; it had two LAND reviews ([correctness](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7375#issuecomment-7003153077), [adversarial](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7375#issuecomment-7003163147)). - `38ab7d8f13` + `cd141de8bc` **empty words**: in `npm '' [--silent] exec -c 'rm -rf /'` (and the same for docker and nix), the empty word took the verb slot and hid the payload. `launcher_verb_targets` now re-walks the options after each empty landing, so candidates only grow. - `0f1a3168a1`, `1965a7a1ed`, `0d75cf4312`, `ce76c13d1c` **`--entrypoint`**: `docker|podman run --entrypoint X IMAGE ARGS` is now also checked as `X ARGS`. Every `--entrypoint` value before the image becomes a candidate, including one that sits in another option's value position; an `--entrypoint` after the image is a container argument. - `5760dd1bcc` + `f2974ff8e0` **512-state limit**: when a launcher option walk hits `MAX_HEAD_STATES`, the line is now marked dynamic instead of silently dropping the nested payload. - `d4c0ead146` **docs/MODES.md**: the `Shift+Tab to change` hint stands down after two presses, except on Auto-Review and Full Access. This was found in the CLI terminal walk of #7283. Earlier LAND reviews at `ce76c13d1c` ([correctness](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7385#issuecomment-7003721556), [adversarial](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7385#issuecomment-7003744156)). Checks on Linux x86_64: `cargo test --locked -p codewhale-execpolicy` passes 270 with 0 failed. Every new test row fails without its fix. Clippy `-D warnings`, rustfmt and `sync-changelog.sh --check` are clean. Refs #7283, #7284 --- 🟢 Devin Review found nothing to fix · [View findings](https://app.devin.ai/review/codewhale-hq/codewhale/pull/7385)

prs.body:
## Summary Running a launcher with only global flags (`npm --version`, `docker --version`, `nix --version`, `launchctl --help`, …) panicked the turn during command-policy expansion. `resolve_wrapper_targets` returns `tokens.len()` as the "verb" index when no subcommand follows the global flags, and `Expander::record_launcher_commands` indexed `tokens[verb_idx]` unchecked in four arms (nix, npm, launchctl, `VERB_LAUNCHERS`). ```rust - let verb = tokens[verb_idx].as_str(); + let Some(verb) = tokens.get(verb_idx).map(String::as_str) else { continue; }; ``` New test `launcher_flag_only_commands_do_not_panic` covers the flag-only forms and checks that the guarded arms still surface nested payloads (`npm --silent exec --call 'rm -rf /'`, `nix --offline develop -c rm -rf /`, `docker -D run alpine rm -rf /`). This is Mac commit `0d0c625791c` (`ci/execpolicy-launcher-panic-0103`) cherry-picked with `-x` onto main `e1364cabc`, without the unlanded scroll-flicker commit `c006d3f4e` it was stacked on. The changelog conflict was resolved to keep only this entry, and `scripts/sync-changelog.sh` re-synced `crates/tui/CHANGELOG.md`, which also restores the Muse Code line main had left out of the TUI copy. Checks (Linux x86_64): `cargo test --locked -p codewhale-execpolicy` 268 passed / 0 failed; without the guards the new test fails (`index out of bounds: the len is 2 but the index is 2`); clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p codewhale-execpolicy --check`, `sync-changelog.sh --check` clean. issues.title: ci: attribute iOS comparison preparation delays and sampling gaps
issues.body:
## Summary

The iOS release comparison proof records incomplete simulator measurements and a single composite preparation duration, but does not retain enough timing information to explain either delay.

## Observed evidence

[Run 44578202675](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44578202675), using OpenClaw `cd2ae19272a3ee7be456385fa7efc56d6e2109a6` and upstream SimSlim 0.11.0, completed four matched pairs. All sixteen UI test executions passed, but seven of eight footprint traces were incomplete: eighteen internal gaps and three measurement timeouts left zero complete pairs.

The recorded full-arm median regression was 27.96%. Preparation accounts for 95.95% of the aggregate extra wall time, but its timer combines cold boot, SimSlim activation, readiness and verification. Measurement failures lack per-call timestamps, so the proof cannot distinguish scheduling delay from command duration.

## Requested change

Add bounded scheduled/start/end timings and sanitized outcomes for measurement calls, both test boundaries, and elapsed wall time/exit status for the four existing preparation commands. Preserve the stock default, upstream version and profile, sampling schedule, timeout/cancellation behavior and qualification thresholds. This requests diagnostics, not another comparison run, a performance claim or a Rust port.

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

issues.body:
**Environment:** OpenClaw 2026.9.7, `@openclaw/codex` 2026.9.7 (Codex app-server harness).

**What happens**
A parent agent spawns native Codex children (`spawn_agent`). A child finishes its first task normally. Later, in a
**new** parent turn, the parent sends that same (now idle) child a new task through the collaboration message path.
The child's new turn starts and its **first model request** is rejected:

```
unexpected status 403 Forbidden: Codex cannot verify the owner of this model request. Start a fresh request before retrying.
```

The child turn ends immediately. The parent is not told in a way it can act on, so from the parent's point of view the
task was delegated and nothing happens. In our case work silently stalled for ~25 minutes until someone checked.

**Evidence (10 of 10 cases over 4 days)**
- Every real failure (we excluded the error string quoted inside later context) happened in a **child thread whose turn
  number was ≥ 2**, and that turn was **triggered by an inter-agent message**.
- It never happened on a child's first turn.
- It happened with and without our local relay patches, so it is not caused by them.

**Where it comes from**
`extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-dispatch.ts` → `createCodexInferenceModelBinding`. For a child request,
`captureModelSource({ threadId, turnId, parentThreadId, parentTurnId, rootTurnId })` fails or returns no source, and the
binding throws `CodexInferenceAuthorizationError("owner")`, which becomes a 403 `model_permission_denied`. Our reading
is that the re-tasked child's model custody is still tied to the parent turn that originally spawned it. That turn is
over, so there is no current owner to bind to.

**Expected**
One of these:
- (a) Re-tasking an idle child from the current parent turn re-binds its model custody to the current parent turn.
- (b) The send or re-task call is rejected **up front**, with a clear error to the parent ("child is bound to an
  ended turn; spawn a new child").

Either way, the failure should not be silent for the parent.

**Workaround we use:** always spawn a fresh child for each new task, and never re-task children from earlier parent
turns. Since adopting it, no recurrences.
