issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs) — also a regression: the same deployment started fine on pre-2026.9 images.

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a containerized deployment (image default entrypoint, inside a podman pod), after upgrading to **2026.11.5** the Gateway **never starts**. The container reports `Up`, the reverse proxy answers, but every request is `502`.

The image entrypoint runs a pre-start `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` pass. That pass finishes with:

```
Doctor: maintenance finish
└  Doctor finished with plugin load errors.
Doctor: maintenance release
```

and exits non-zero. The entrypoint treats a non-zero Doctor exit as fatal and **returns without ever exec'ing the Gateway**, so with `--restart always` the container loops forever (~60–90 s per round) and the instance is silently down.

Two things make this undiagnosable in a container:

1. **`Doctor finished with plugin load errors.` names no plugin and gives no reason.** I captured a full failing pass (123,130 bytes of stdout/stderr) and searched it exhaustively — the only match for the error is the summary line itself. There is no plugin id, no package, no cause, no remediation hint.
2. The condition **persists even when every plugin is already current and loaded**, so each restart re-enters the same "needs fixing" state — a livelock rather than a one-time repair.

### Actual behavior

`podman top` on the stuck container shows **only Doctor, never a Gateway**:

```
tini -s -- node /app/docker-entrypoint.mjs node openclaw.mjs gateway
node /app/docker-entrypoint.mjs node openclaw.mjs gateway
/usr/local/bin/node /app/openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive
```

Relevant logic in `/app/docker-entrypoint.mjs` (≈ lines 112–140):

```js
child = spawn(process.execPath,
  [path.join(root, "openclaw.mjs"), ...invocation.rootOptions, "doctor", "--fix", "--non-interactive"],
  { stdio: "inherit", env });
...
const signal = interrupted ?? outcome.signal;
if (signal || outcome.code !== 0) {
  process.exitCode = signal ? 128 + os.constants.signals[signal] : (outcome.code ?? 1);
  return;                       // ← Gateway is never exec'd
}
```

Result: HTTP 502 through the in-pod nginx sidecar, endless restart loop, sustained CPU load on the host.

### What I verified is *not* the cause

`openclaw plugins list --json` on the stuck instance (parsed with the image's own `node`, no `jq` assumed):

* 85 plugins total, 41 enabled; **every enabled plugin reports `status: "loaded"`**
* `dependencyStatus`: `installed` / `requiredInstalled` / `optionalInstalled` all `true`, `missing: []`, `missingOptional: []`
* 0 entries "configured but not installed", 0 anomalous entries
* Diffed against a healthy instance in the same fleet — same shape, no differences

`openclaw plugins update --all --dry-run` — everything already current:

```
brave is up to date (2026.11.5).            dingtalk-connector is up to date (0.8.27).
feishu is up to date (2026.11.5).           openclaw-qqbot is up to date (2.0.4).
openclaw-weixin is up to date (2.4.10).     qwen is up to date (2026.11.5).
tavily is up to date (2026.11.5).           wecom-openclaw-plugin is up to date (2026.10.30).
```

Read-only Doctor (`openclaw doctor --json`, no `--fix`) on the same mounted state reports **no plugin findings at all** — only 4 unrelated warnings (legacy Browser Relay auth, plaintext secret-bearing config fields, two channel `groupPolicy="open"` notices), and a healthy database inventory:

```
ok=false, checksRun=42, checksSkipped=30
databaseStores: state/openclaw.sqlite observed=sqlite schema.version=36 expectedVersion=36 pending=0 issues=[]
```

So the failure appears **only on the `--fix` path**, and only as an unnamed summary line.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw with the **default image entrypoint** inside a podman pod, state on a named volume mounted at `/home/node/.openclaw`, `--restart always`, plus a reverse-proxy sidecar pointing at `127.0.0.1:18789`.
2. Upgrade the image from an older release (our instance had been on a pre-2026.9 state) and restart the pod.
3. Doctor completes its migration pass, prints `Doctor finished with plugin load errors.`, exits non-zero; the entrypoint exits without starting the Gateway; the restart policy loops it.

Note: 7 of 9 instances in the same batch upgrade came up normally, so this is state/plugin-set dependent — but the affected instance is stuck **regardless of plugin currency**, which is the part that looks wrong.

### Expected behavior

1. `doctor --fix --non-interactive` should print **which** plugin(s) failed and why (id, package, error, remediation), and surface them as `findings` in `doctor --json` — not only a bare summary line.
2. A plugin load error that does not prevent the Gateway from serving should not be a **hard startup failure**. At minimum provide an opt-out (e.g. `--tolerate-plugin-errors`, or an env var the container image can set) so a container cannot livelock on it.
3. The entrypoint should fail **fatally and legibly**: a distinct exit code plus a one-line cause and the exact next command, instead of exiting in a way that is indistinguishable from a normal restart.

### Workaround currently in use

Start the Gateway while skipping the pre-start Doctor pass (safe here because Doctor had already completed migrations against the same mounted state):

```bash
podman rm -f <app-container>
podman run -d --pod <pod> --name <app-container> --restart always \
  -e TZ=Asia/Shanghai -v <state-volume>:/home/node/.openclaw:Z \
  --entrypoint node ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:latest /app/openclaw.mjs gateway
```

With this, the instance is fully healthy: dashboard 200, all configured channels `running`/`connected`, and the Gateway's own post-ready maintenance reports `cleaned 5 retained npm plugin generation(s)` / `cleaned 1 retired native plugin capture(s)`. That the instance works perfectly when Doctor is skipped is further evidence Doctor is failing on a phantom condition.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5 (e13cf15) — image `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:latest`, image ID `405dcc682726`

### Operating system

Linux x64, kernel 6.8.0-147-generic

### Install method

Container image (podman 4.9.3), default entrypoint, inside a podman pod with a named state volume

### Model

n/a — the Gateway process never reaches model runtime

### Provider / routing chain

n/a (qwen provider plugin is installed and reported `up to date`)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Not relevant to this failure; Doctor exits before the Gateway starts.

### Logs

One full failing `doctor --fix --non-interactive` pass (123,130 bytes) is available to attach. The repeating tail:

```
Doctor: Configured plugin repair
Doctor: Plugin registry
◇  Plugin registry ───────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  Plugin registry refreshed: 41/85 enabled plugins indexed.  │
Doctor: Legacy plugin captures
...
Doctor: maintenance ready
Doctor: retained runtimes
[state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: verification-missing; agent=<agent-a>
[state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: verification-missing; agent=<agent-b>
[state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: verification-missing; agent=<agent-c>
Doctor: maintenance finish
└  Doctor finished with plugin load errors.
Doctor: maintenance release
```

Grepping the whole capture for the failing plugin yields nothing but the summary line:

```bash
grep -inE "plugin" fix-loop.log | grep -iE "error|fail|unable|cannot|missing|invalid|not found|✖"
# → only: "Doctor finished with plugin load errors."
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

* Full captured stdout/stderr of one failing Doctor pass (123,130 bytes) — happy to attach.
* `doctor --json` (read-only) output; `plugins list --json` for both the stuck and a healthy instance.
* `podman top` / `podman inspect` output above.

### Impact and severity

Hard outage of one instance in a 9-instance fleet, with **no actionable error message**. `--restart always` converts it into an endless loop that also burns CPU. Worse, it was invisible at fleet level: our deploy script's readiness gate reported success (see below), so a batch announced "8/8 upgraded" while 2 instances were down.

### Additional information

1. **A separate, already-reported lease problem was the *first* blocker on this instance.** Doctor could not enter maintenance because of a lease from a long-dead Gateway (`holder 2 at unknown host, last renewed 3656001 s ago` — ≈42 days). Explicit `openclaw gateway recover-lock --confirm <fingerprint>` fixed that instance completely. This appears to be the same class as #201472 (dead Gateway lock without `processNamespace` blocks maintenance) and #196846 (Doctor in a one-off container fails with `GatewayLockNamespaceError` and no reason; docs should say to run it inside the Gateway container) — filing this only for the **plugin-load-livelock** part, not the lease part. One extra data point for those threads: the docs' recommended recovery path `podman run --rm -v <state>:/home/node/.openclaw <image> openclaw doctor --fix` is unverifiable by construction (no shared PID namespace), so a lease recorded from inside the pod can never be cleared that way.

2. **Secondary observation (can be split into its own issue if useful):** `openclaw gateway status` exits **0** even when the Gateway is not running at all. On the dead instance it printed config-derived text and returned success:

   ```
   Service: no supported service manager detected (diagnostic only, not the check target)
   Gateway: bind=loopback (127.0.0.1), port=18789 (env/config)
   Check target: ws://127.0.0.1:18789
   rc=0
   ```

   Any script or supervisor that uses `gateway status` as a readiness probe will report success on a dead Gateway. Suggested: exit non-zero when the check target is unreachable, or state explicitly in the docs that only `/healthz`, `/startupz`, `/readyz` (and `gateway status --deep`) are fit for readiness gating. We have switched to probing `/healthz` with `node fetch` inside the container.

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

openclaw update migration-plan always returns a refused plan with candidate-artifact-digest-required because the command provides no way to supply the required candidate artifact digest.

### Steps to reproduce

Install OpenClaw 2026.11.5.
2. Create an isolated snapshot directory containing an `openclaw.json` file with `{}` and an empty state directory.
3. Run:

openclaw update migration-plan --dry-run --json --snapshot-home <snapshot-home> --snapshot-config <snapshot-home>\openclaw.json --snapshot-state <snapshot-home>\state

4. Observe exit code 1 and `outcome: "refused"` with `refusal.code: "candidate-artifact-digest-required"`.

### Expected behavior

For a valid isolated snapshot, the command should return a usable read-only migration plan with a bound candidate artifact identity, or expose a documented option for supplying the required digest.

### Actual behavior

The command exits with code 1 and returns an `openclaw.legacyStateMigrationPlan.v1` document with `mutationAllowed: false`, `outcome: "refused"`, no warnings, and `refusal.code: "candidate-artifact-digest-required"`. The candidate artifact is reported as `outcome: "deferred"`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5 (e13cf15)

### Operating system

Microsoft Windows 11 Home, version 10.0.26300, build 26300

### Install method

npm package install in the OpenClaw-managed Node runtime

### Model

N/A

### Provider / routing chain

N/A

### Additional provider/model setup details

No model or provider request is involved. The failure occurs entirely in the local update CLI before inference.

### Logs

```shell
{
  "schemaVersion": "openclaw.legacyStateMigrationPlan.v1",
  "mutationAllowed": false,
  "outcome": "refused",
  "warnings": [],
  "refusal": {
    "code": "candidate-artifact-digest-required",
    "message": "Candidate artifact content identity must be supplied by the staged-candidate owner."
  },
  "candidate": {
    "version": "2026.11.5",
    "artifact": {
      "outcome": "deferred",
      "refusal": {
        "code": "candidate-artifact-digest-required"
      }
    }
  }
}

Process exit code: 1
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Attached: IMP-137-upstream-migration-plan-bug.pdf. It contains the reproduction, expected and actual behaviour, and source comparison for the published OpenClaw 2026.11.5 and 2026.11.6 packages.

[IMP-137-upstream-migration-plan-bug.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35129263/IMP-137-upstream-migration-plan-bug.pdf)

### Impact and severity

Affected: Operators using the standalone migration-plan command to preflight update repair.
Severity: High — blocks the read-only safety gate before a mutating repair.
Frequency: 1/1 directly observed attempt on 2026.11.5; the published 2026.11.6 package contains the same relevant implementation.
Consequence: Operators cannot obtain an accepted migration plan before running update repair.

### Additional information

The published OpenClaw 2026.11.6 package contains the same relevant migration-plan implementation. The command passes only the candidate root and version, while the planner requires a candidate artifact digest and refuses when none is supplied. The CLI exposes no candidate-digest option. No supported workaround was identified. No production repair or live-state mutation was performed during reproduction.

issues.body:
I reproduced this in a Debian 12.12 ARM64 VM with a global npm install and the Gateway running as a systemd user service. I verified that the 2026.9.37 Gateway answered a health request, then ran `openclaw update` against the published 2026.11.6 tarball. To exercise rollback, I forced Doctor to exit with code 1 after the new package was in place.

The rollback worker hit the SQLite maintenance lock held by the updater itself. The update reported “Database rollback could not finish” and exited with code 1. The CLI still reported 2026.11.6, the Gateway service was inactive, and the health request got a connection refusal.

I expected the update to report the failure, restore 2026.9.37 and its databases, and bring the Gateway back up.

I ran the same forced failure against a local build with the rollback patch. The update still exited with code 1, but it restored the pre-migration databases and 2026.9.37. The Gateway restarted and answered a health request. I also upgraded from 2026.10.33 to the patched build without forcing a failure. That update exited with code 0, and the Gateway was healthy afterward.

issues.body:
### Summary

I'd like to move a conversation that started without a project into a registered project, and keep working in the same conversation.

### Problem to solve

I often start a conversation without picking a project, because I don't know yet that it will turn into code. Then the agent clones a repo into its workspace and starts changing it there. Once I want that work in the project, I can't give the conversation a project after it started: the conversation menu has nothing for it. My only option is a new session in the project, which leaves this conversation behind and its work sitting in a folder of the old workspace.

### Proposed solution

- A "Move to project…" item in the conversation menu, for conversations that aren't in a project yet.
- It opens a dialog that lists the projects I can use. If the conversation's workspace has a clone of the chosen project, the dialog says that work comes along and shows its last commit and how many files have unsaved changes.
- After the move, my next message opens the project the same way a session created in it would: its own branch and checkout, with the project's AGENTS.md and skills. The branch starts at the clone's commit, and my uncommitted changes are still there, still uncommitted.
- The conversation keeps its earlier messages.

### Alternatives considered

Starting a new session in the project and asking the agent to redo or copy the work. That leaves the conversation behind and is easy to get wrong when there are uncommitted changes.

### Impact

Affected: anyone who starts a conversation before deciding it belongs in a project.
Severity: blocks the workflow; the work has to be moved by hand.
Frequency: every time a conversation turns into code after it started.
Consequence: a second session, repeated context, and a manual copy of uncommitted changes.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Control UI **Desktop** for a paired macOS app node disconnects about 2–4 seconds after a successful macOS (ARD) login with `Desktop disconnected: desktop stream failed`. The node host forwards each loopback socket read as a single attach WebSocket message, while the Gateway's node-stream attach server rejects messages larger than 64 KiB, so the stream closes with 1009.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a Gateway on `2026.11.2` (official Docker image).
2. Pair **OpenClaw.app 2026.11.5** on macOS 26.7.3 as a node over direct `wss://` (its node worker runs on Bun; node logs report `runtime: "bun"`, `bun/1.4.4`).
3. Enable **System Settings → General → Sharing → Screen Sharing** on that Mac (observed with a 5120×2880 Retina display).
4. In the Control UI (desktop browser or iOS), open **Desktop**, select the Mac node, enter the macOS account credentials, and connect.

### Expected behavior

The desktop stream stays connected and renders the Mac screen, with the node respecting the Gateway's documented attach frame limit (or the Gateway accepting the node's own stream payload size).

### Actual behavior

- macOS `screensharingd` logs `authResult = 0` / `good authentication`, then the viewer connection reaches EOF ~2–4 s later.
- Node host log (`node-host/stream`): `node stream closed {"streamKind":"desktop","trigger":"websocket-close","closeCode":1009}`
- Gateway log (`gateway/node-stream`): `node stream closed {"streamKind":"desktop","trigger":"websocket-error","closeCode":1006}`, followed by `gateway/desktop`: `desktop observer closed {"trigger":"stream-error","cleanupCode":1011,"closeCode":1011}`
- UI: `Desktop disconnected: desktop stream failed`. Reproduced on every attempt (5/5).

**Root cause (code references):**

- `src/node-host/node-stream-transport.ts` forwards every loopback read unsplit: `socket.on("data", (chunk) => { ... streamWs.send(chunk, { binary: true }, ...) })`. The node's own client `maxPayload` is 1 MiB (`MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 1048576`).
- `src/gateway/desktop/node-stream-broker.ts`: `const MAX_ATTACH_FRAME_BYTES = 64 * 1024;` is used both for the attach-metadata check and for `new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true, maxPayload: MAX_ATTACH_FRAME_BYTES })`, so every post-metadata stream frame is also capped at 64 KiB.
- Node.js TCP reads are capped at 64 KiB, so Node-runtime node hosts stay within the limit. The macOS app bundles only Bun, whose reads exceed 64 KiB during large framebuffer updates, and the Gateway's `ws` server rejects them (1009 to the node, local error/1006 on the Gateway).
- Both files are unchanged on `main`, `v2026.11.6`, and `v2026.11.10-beta.1`. The same attach server also carries node **portal** streams, so Bun-based nodes can hit the same limit there.

**Confirmation:** raising only the Gateway attach server's `maxPayload` to 1 MiB (keeping the 64 KiB attach-metadata check) makes the paired Mac desktop stream connect and stay connected, from both desktop and iOS Control UI.

**Suggested fix:** split outbound chunks in `node-stream-transport.ts` to at most the Gateway attach frame limit (for example, loop over `chunk.subarray(offset, offset + 64 * 1024)`), and/or let the Gateway accept the node transport's 1 MiB payload for stream frames after metadata while keeping the 64 KiB metadata limit.

### OpenClaw version

Gateway 2026.11.2 (b556fdf); macOS app 2026.11.5 (build 2611000590), node worker bun/1.4.4

### Operating system

Gateway: Ubuntu 24.04 (Docker); node: macOS 26.7.3 (Mac Pro, 5120×2880 display)

### Install method

Gateway: official Docker image (digest-pinned); node: OpenClaw.app

### Model

N/A (desktop transport)

### Provider / routing chain

N/A

### Logs

See "Actual behavior" above (node host, Gateway, and `screensharingd` excerpts; identifiers redacted).

### Impact and severity

- Affected: paired macOS app nodes (Bun runtime) using Control UI Desktop; likely also portal streams.
- Severity: blocks the paired-desktop workflow entirely.
- Frequency: always on the affected setup.
- Workaround: patch the Gateway's attach `maxPayload` to 1 MiB.

### Additional information

"The failing node is the OpenClaw.app 2026.11.5 node worker, which runs on Bun. A Node.js-runtime node host was not tested against the same Mac, so the Bun read-size explanation is inferred from the 1009 close plus the confirmed 1 MiB Gateway-side fix."

issues.body:
### Description
After upgrading to 2026.11.6 (06afb10), an active session goal kept running after the context budget was exhausted. Each continuation produced an assistant reply that was delivered to the bound Discord channel, so the same automated reminder appeared in the channel repeatedly, roughly every 5 to 10 seconds, for about six minutes. The loop stopped only when the gateway was stopped. The goal stayed `active` the whole time.

This is related to, but distinct from, #186928, #187898, #192988, and #196175. Those report goals that stall or lose continuation ownership. In this report the goal does the opposite: it keeps continuing with no terminal condition. It is also distinct from #120116 (closed), which had a different trigger (a missing native hook relay), and no Discord delivery.

### Environment
- **OpenClaw Version**: `2026.11.6 (06afb10)`
- **OS**: Linux x86_64 (WSL2, systemd user service)
- **Runtime**: Node.js 26.13.1
- **Channel**: Discord, bound to the main agent session
- **Model**: `claude-haiku-5.5` via LiteLLM (provider `litellm`)

### Reproduction Steps
1. Run OpenClaw 2026.11.6 with a Discord channel bound to the main agent.
2. Create a session goal in that channel. Do not set a token budget.
3. Let the session grow until the prompt exceeds the context budget (about 80,000 prompt tokens before reserve). The route switches to compaction only.
4. Observe that the goal stays `active` and continuation prompts keep being injected, each followed by an assistant reply in the channel.

### Expected Behavior
When the context budget is exhausted and no further progress is possible, the goal should stop, pause, or ask for input. Continuation replies should not be posted to the channel repeatedly.

### Actual Behavior
The goal stayed `active` with `continuationTurns` at 107 and no token budget set. During the window, the session recorded 54 internal continuation prompts and 58 assistant replies. Per-minute counts of internal prompts were 9, 9, 4, 11, 10, 8, and 3 (12:46 to 12:52 local time). The gateway log shows the context budget at the time of the last snapshot:

```text
[context-pressure-diagnostic] admitted provider attempt ... route=compact_only estimatedPromptTokens=95712 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=80000
remainingPromptBudgetTokens=0, overflowTokens=15712, shouldCompact=true
```

The loop ended at SIGTERM. Log coverage for this window is confirmed: the file ends at 12:52:29 local time.

Impact: channel spam that continued until the gateway was manually stopped.

### What is confirmed and what is not
- Confirmed from the session store: continuation prompts carry the internal-system marker, the goal stayed `active`, and the counts above.
- Confirmed from the gateway log: the context budget was exhausted and the route stayed on compaction only during the window.
- Not confirmed at runtime: that each continuation reply was delivered to the channel. This is inferred from the installed code, which routes follow-up replies to the session's origin channel, and from the matching counts. I did not run the gateway to observe delivery.
- Not confirmed: why the goal's last-updated time did not change during continuation turns.
- Not confirmed: whether a cron job was involved. None was linked to this loop.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary

In a Telegram direct chat, a turn finished normally and its reply was delivered with the `message` tool. About 3 seconds later OpenClaw posted the generic failure notice into the same chat:

> ⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this request. Check the conversation before trying again. For details, open Settings → Logs in the Control UI or run `openclaw logs --follow`.

Nothing had failed: the run is recorded as succeeded and the reply as delivered. The Gateway file log and the service journal contain no error, warning or cause for the notice, so the owner is told to "check the logs" and the logs have nothing.

### Observed (2026.11.3 847611d, Telegram DM, embedded runner, anthropic/claude-fable-5-2, `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`)

UTC 2026-11-15, one user turn in the owner's DM session (run `213d61d4…`), then the notice:

```text
03:10:36.300  audit  tool.action.started   message   (send, reply to the triggering message, final)
03:10:37.551  [telegram] outbound send ok … messageId=<N> operation=sendRichMessage deliveryKind=text replyToMessageId=<trigger>
03:10:38.050  audit  tool.action.finished  message   status=succeeded
03:10:38.627  audit  agent.run.finished    status=succeeded   run=213d61d4…
03:10:38.763  [auto-reply/message-tool-outcome] recorded message-tool-only run outcome  outcome="tool_delivered" runStatus="completed"
03:10:41.534  [telegram] outbound send ok … messageId=<N+1> operation=sendRichMessage deliveryKind=text      <- the failure notice, no replyTo
```

Between 03:10:38.763 and 03:10:41.534 the journal has no line for this session, and for the whole turn there is no `Embedded agent failed before reply`, no `lane task error`, no `incomplete turn detected`, no `empty response` line. The session transcript holds the delivery mirror of the reply (`openclawDeliveryMirror.kind = "message-tool-source-reply", final: true`) and no assistant error entry.

What else was happening in that window (correlation only, not shown to be the cause):

- A hidden subagent spawned by this turn with `completionTarget: "parent"` had finished 4 minutes earlier. Its private completion turn in the same session (`announce:v1:…`) began preparing about 0.45 s after the user turn finished (its `prep stages` line at 03:10:48.690 reports `totalMs=9612`), i.e. the notice was sent while that turn was being set up.
- Earlier in the same user turn the model had called `sessions_yield`, which returned `already_pending` (an unrelated child from two days before, `state: completing, wakeArmed: false`; see #189980), and the turn went on with tool calls and ended with the `message` send.

### Shipped code

Three places can produce this exact sentence. Two of them log before sending (`agent-runner` writes `Embedded agent failed before reply: …`; the incomplete-turn path writes `incomplete turn detected`). The third does not, and by elimination it is the one that fired:

`src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.execute.ts`, the `.catch` of the reply resolver (v2026.11.3 lines 500-516; unchanged on `main` at lines 546-562 and in v2026.11.5-beta.3):

```ts
// Gate collection, not just printing: diagnostic subscribers can export this cause.
if (isFileLogLevelEnabled("debug")) {
  replyResolverError = truncateUtf16Safe(formatErrorWithRedactor(error, { redact: redactToolPayloadText }), 2_048);
}
failDispatchReplyOperation(error, "failed");
if (!didDeliverVisiblePartialReply) {
  return adopted &&
    isRequiredReplyExpectation(state.replyOperationRunState.replyCompletion?.expectation) &&
    state.replyOperationRunState.replyCompletion?.outcome !== "blocked" &&
    !state.suppressDelivery &&
    !state.getObservedReplyDelivery()
    ? { text: GENERIC_EXTERNAL_RUN_FAILURE_TEXT, isError: true }
    : undefined;
}
```

Two things follow from the source:

1. The error that reaches this `catch` is kept only when the file log level is `debug`. At the default level the notice is sent and the cause is discarded, which matches the empty log.
2. The only delivery check is `getObservedReplyDelivery()`, which is set from the agent runner when it resolves the terminal reply completion. An error thrown after the run has ended and the message-tool reply has been delivered, but before that callback, leaves the flag false, so a delivered turn is treated as unanswered. The same run was recorded as `tool_delivered` / `completed` by `recordMessageToolRunOutcome` 2.8 s before the notice.

### Expected

1. A turn whose source reply was delivered (message-tool receipt for the current source, run finished ok) never gets the generic failure notice afterwards, whatever fails later in dispatch bookkeeping.
2. Whenever this notice is sent, its cause is written to the log at `warn` (redacted), not only collected at `debug`. The notice itself sends the owner to the logs.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d), Linux x86_64, Node 26.12.1, systemd user service. Telegram DM, embedded agent runner, `anthropic/claude-fable-5-2`, `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`, `messages.queue.mode: "collect"`, file log level default (no `logging` block).

### Evidence scope

- Observed once with complete records (above). The run id, audit rows, journal lines and transcript entries were read after the fact; nothing was induced.
- Not reproduced on demand, and the thrown error is unknown because it was not logged. That the `dispatch-from-config` catch is the sender is an inference from the absence of the other two paths' log lines, not a captured stack.
- Whether the starting private completion turn or the earlier `already_pending` yield result plays a part is not established.
- Related but different: #192688 (same notice in groups after an empty final or a provider 429), #169229 (closed; successful Codex final replaced by this notice, also without a logged cause), #176330 (closed; `ActiveTurnClaimError` surfacing as this notice, with log lines).

issues.body:
### Description
After upgrading to the latest stable release, the gateway posts the same automation reminder to a Discord channel repeatedly, several times per minute, over about six minutes. Each repeat is an assistant reply to an internal system prompt that the gateway injects as a user message. The injected prompt is a goal-continuation prompt ("advance the active goal; keep it active until fully achieved"), not a human message. The loop stopped only when the gateway was stopped. Message content is intentionally omitted.

### Environment
- **OpenClaw Version**: `2026.11.6 (06afb10)`
- **OS**: Linux x86_64 (systemd user service)
- **Runtime**: Node.js 26.13.1
- **Channel**: Discord (main agent session bound to a Discord channel)
- **Model**: `litellm/claude-haiku-5.5` (via LiteLLM)

### Reproduction Steps
1. Run OpenClaw gateway 2026.11.6 with an active goal in a session bound to a Discord channel, and a few cron automations configured.
2. Let the session run for several minutes with a large prompt history.
3. Observe internal goal-continuation prompts being injected at a rate of roughly one every 5–10 seconds.
4. Observe a matching assistant reply for each injection, with the reminder text repeated in the channel.

### Expected Behavior
The goal loop ends when the goal is complete or its budget is exhausted. Only meaningful replies reach the channel. Repeated internal prompts do not produce repeated channel messages.

### Actual Behavior
From about 12:46 to 12:52 (local time), the session produced about 54 internal goal-continuation prompts and 58 assistant replies. The channel received the same reminder repeatedly. Gateway logs during the same window show:

```text
[context-pressure-diagnostic] admitted provider attempt ... route=compact_only estimatedPromptTokens=81112 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=80000
... (estimatedPromptTokens rose steadily from about 81k to about 95k, above the 80k budget)
[compaction-safeguard] Compaction safeguard: found 0 of 1 configured sections in AGENTS.md; check postCompactionSections.
cron: automation has no recorded inference account; run openclaw doctor --fix before its next scheduled run ...   (2 jobs)
```

The loop did not end on its own. It stopped when the gateway received a stop signal.

Impact: channel spam that users cannot stop from the channel.

### What is confirmed and what is not
- Confirmed from the session store: the repeated user messages carry the internal-system provenance and the goal-continuation text, and they are interleaved with assistant replies.
- Confirmed from the gateway logs: prompt size stayed above the budget and the route stayed on compaction only, during the same window.
- Not confirmed: whether the goal loop is what caused the prompt size to grow, or whether the growth caused the loop. The two are correlated in the logs. The goal's completion or budget state was not found in the logs.
- Not confirmed: the exact path by which each assistant reply reached the channel.

### Related
- #186043 and #194274 describe session binding errors. They do not describe repeated goal-continuation replies in a channel.

issues.body:
### Summary

On 2026.11.6, a node client connecting with a setup-code bootstrap token authenticates and then fails in the hello phase with `duplicate column name: setup_id`, because the post-connect bookkeeping runs `ALTER TABLE device_bootstrap_tokens ADD COLUMN setup_id` against a table that already has that column.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (the connect is rejected with `UNAVAILABLE`; the gateway keeps running)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run 2026.11.6 against a state DB where `device_bootstrap_tokens` already contains `setup_id`. On mine the column was added by an earlier boot of the same release: `PRAGMA table_info(device_bootstrap_tokens)` lists it and the stored `CREATE TABLE` text in `sqlite_master` includes it.
2. Mint a setup code (`openclaw qr --json`) and connect a node client with `connect.params.auth.bootstrapToken`, device identity, `role: "node"`, `mode: "node"`.
3. The handshake authenticates (`[ws] client connected … auth=bootstrap-token`), then fails with `UNAVAILABLE: Error: duplicate column name: setup_id: code=ERR_SQLITE_ERROR`.

### Expected behavior

The bootstrap-token connect completes with `hello-ok` and the device pairs, which is what happens on a DB where the column is absent and `ensureColumn` performs the ALTER once.

### Actual behavior

The connect fails in the hello phase:

```
[gateway] bootstrap token post-connect bookkeeping failed device=…: Error: duplicate column name: setup_id: code=ERR_SQLITE_ERROR
[gateway] frame handler failed conn=…: Error: duplicate column name: setup_id: code=ERR_SQLITE_ERROR
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ connect … failurePhase=hello failureCause=handler-error
```

The client receives `{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Error: duplicate column name: setup_id: code=ERR_SQLITE_ERROR"}`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.6 (06afb10), image `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw@sha256:ccb0d04f14edd04c201b85bcee4612e7c084158a3d8fafa77a3c78554587edca`

### Operating system

Linux (NixOS 25.11 host, Docker container)

### Install method

docker. `/app/dist` is an overlay built from v2026.11.6; the schema helper code involved here is unpatched in that overlay.

### Model

openai/gpt-6.1-terra

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> codex runtime (ChatGPT subscription)

### Additional provider/model setup details

This is a node connect; no model call happens before the failure, so model routing is not involved.

### Logs

```
[gateway] bootstrap token post-connect bookkeeping failed device=271abb657bc8b956…: Error: duplicate column name: setup_id: code=ERR_SQLITE_ERROR
    at createError (file:///app/dist/openclaw-state-worker-error-DFc1hTOR.mjs:318:24)
    at decodeSqliteWorkerReplyError (file:///app/dist/sqlite-worker-store-CD_VeKwI.mjs:436:10)
[gateway] frame handler failed conn=b3ca8665…: Error: duplicate column name: setup_id: code=ERR_SQLITE_ERROR
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ connect 26ms bytes=174 failurePhase=hello failureCause=handler-error
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The column is present in the live DB:

```
$ sqlite3 openclaw.sqlite "SELECT count(*) FROM pragma_table_info('device_bootstrap_tokens') WHERE name='setup_id';"
1
$ sqlite3 openclaw.sqlite "SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE name='device_bootstrap_tokens';"
CREATE TABLE "device_bootstrap_tokens" (
  token_key TEXT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  …
  last_used_at_ms INTEGER
, setup_id TEXT) STRICT
```

### Impact and severity

- Affected: gateways whose state DB already contains `setup_id` when a client pairs with a setup code (Android app, QR onboarding)
- Severity: blocks workflow — pairing fails every time
- Frequency: 4/4 observed attempts across restarts
- Consequence: setup codes and QR pairing unusable; clients using the gateway token or an already-paired device are unaffected

### Additional information

Suspected cause: `ensureColumn()` (`openclaw-state-db-schema-helpers-*.mjs`) guards the ALTER with `tableHasColumn()`, which reads admitted schema facts and caches the parsed column set in a `WeakMap` keyed by that facts object. The connection that runs the bookkeeping still reports `setup_id` as missing, so it issues the ALTER and SQLite rejects it. Dropping the column, checkpointing the WAL, and restarting all reproduced the same failure on the next connect.

Workaround I applied locally: treat a `duplicate column name` error from that ALTER as success. Setup-code pairing then completes with `hello-ok`.

Related closed issues on the same column: #125771, #127463, #126899 (different failure modes — migration deadlock and first-use-only assertions).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When agent A sends a message to agent B's main session with sessions_send (mode followup, timeoutSeconds 0) and agent B runs on the plugin CLI backend agy-cli, B receives the message and produces a full assistant reply. Right after that, post-reply CLI transcript compaction fails with "agent tool caller authority is no longer active". B's run is then marked run-failed-before-reply even though the reply completed, and sender A receives a false "sessions_send delivery failed ... target may not have received the message; retry" notice.

This looks like the same family as #158070 / #188437 (fixed per #159353, shipped in 2026.11.5-beta.1), but it still reproduces on 2026.11.6 when the target runs on a CLI backend (agy-cli), so the CLI transcript compaction path may not be covered by that fix. Possibly related: #162941, #194403, #201190.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Windows 11, local Gateway. Agent A runs on claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5. Agent B main session runs on CLI backend agy-cli (models gemini-pro-orchestrator-neon and gemini-4-hydrogen-high; both fail).
2. From A call sessions_send to B's main session with mode followup, timeoutSeconds 0.
3. Read B history with sessions_history: a full assistant reply is present.
4. Observe a run-failed-before-reply custom entry appended after the reply, and the delivery-failure notice delivered to A.
Observed 5 times on 2026-11-20.

### Expected behavior

After a completed reply, CLI transcript compaction should run with valid authority (or not fail the run). The run must not be marked failed, and the sender must not get a delivery-failure notice.

### Actual behavior

B's transcript gets a run-failed-before-reply custom entry: "Your request couldn't be completed: CLI transcript compaction failed for agy-cli/<model>: agent tool caller authority is no longer active". A then receives an inter-session notice: "sessions_send delivery to <B> failed: ... The target may not have received the message; retry ...". Impact: false delivery-failure notices make senders retry and duplicate work, and completed replies are marked failed.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.6 (06afb10)

### Operating system

Windows 11

### Install method

npm global

### Model

agy-cli/gemini-pro-orchestrator-neon, agy-cli/gemini-4-hydrogen-high

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> agy-cli (plugin CLI backend)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Default CLI backend agy-cli for agent B; agent A on claude-cli.

### Logs

```shell
CLI transcript compaction failed for agy-cli/<model>: agent tool caller authority is no longer active
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: multi-agent setups using sessions_send into sessions on a CLI backend.
Severity: Medium (reply completes, but run marked failed and false delivery-failure notice)
Frequency: 5/5 observed sends on 2026-11-20
Consequence: sender retries and duplicate messages.

### Additional information

Workaround: sender checks the target's sessions_history before retrying. Separately, in the same session an ask_user call through the MCP bridge timed out after 3m0s (context deadline exceeded); possibly related, not confirmed.

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows with 20 registered agents, the gateway child process sustains ~100-170% of one CPU core while completely idle on **2026.10.10**, after the watch-target refresh machinery named in #191612 was removed by PR #170341. The reported symptom persists in the replacement code path.

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.10.10** (7dc3350), npm global install
- Windows 10.0.26200 x64, 20 logical CPUs, Node v24.22.1
- 20 agents under `agents.entries`, shared skills dir via `skills.load.extraDirs`
- Gateway launched by Windows Scheduled Task -> gateway.cmd -> `node dist/index.js gateway --port 18789 --task-supervisor`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Register 19-20 agents on Windows with a shared skills directory.
2. Start the gateway and leave it idle: no chat, no commands, no channel traffic.
3. Observe the `--task-supervisor-child` node process: sustained ~100-170% of one core indefinitely.
4. Kill it, upgrade 2026.10.7 -> 2026.10.10, rerun `openclaw doctor --fix` to completion, restart, wait past startup.
5. Observe: identical CPU consumption on the new release.

Scale dependence on one host (agent count is the only variable changed):

```
 0 agents ->   3.0% of one core
 2 agents ->  30.5%
 6 agents ->  79.7% average, decaying to 18-38%
17 agents -> 143.4%
19 agents -> 150-226%, never settles
```

## Expected behavior

An idle gateway consumes near-zero CPU.

## Actual behavior

Measured **after** upgrading to 2026.10.10, with `doctor --fix` completed at exit 0 and the gateway restarted on the new code:

```
run 1: 1,433 CPU-seconds in 14 minutes  (~170% of one core)
run 2:   518 CPU-seconds in  6 minutes  (~143% of one core)
4-second instantaneous sample: 168.6%
```

No errors, no warnings, no crash; the process stays functional. Per-second CPU deltas show no idle gaps.

## Confirmation that PR #170341 landed in this install

Grepped the installed `dist`:

```
refresh-watch-targets               -> 0 files
nativeWatchCapacityFailed           -> 0 files
addTrustedSymlinkSkillWatchTargets  -> 0 files
scanDirtySources (replacement)      -> present (refresh-epILD946.mjs)
```

So the owning refresh boundary and its sticky capacity machinery are genuinely gone, and the coalesced discovery replacement is present. The idle scan still re-enters.

## Where the remaining hot path may be

`ensureSkillsWatcher` survives in 2026.10.10 and is still referenced from the session-snapshot, workspace-worker, and server-startup-post-attach surfaces (5 dist files). It is called on every session snapshot when `watch !== false`, which would explain continuous re-entry independent of the removed watch-target resolver.

## Prior evidence

#191612 (closed as already-implemented) carries the original 2026.10.7 profile, the syscall-counting harness results, and the post-upgrade measurements:
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191612#issuecomment-6620744886

Filed separately because the author cannot reopen an issue closed by a maintainer/bot, and a comment on a closed issue is not re-triaged.

## Impact

One of 20 cores permanently unavailable (~5% of machine capacity) on an idle gateway, with continuous heat and added latency when preparing sessions. No data risk.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Sandboxed agent runs (cron and dashboard) intermittently fail with "Aborted | sandbox_provisioning" about 5 to 12 s into the run lane, before any tool call, on the native Podman backend. Observed repeatedly on 2026.9.2, 2026.9.6 and 2026.9.7.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

The sandbox is provisioned and the run proceeds, as it does for the same scheduled jobs and the same agents in most runs (for example the same email job succeeded on 2026-09-30 20:13 UTC and 2026-10-01 11:00 and 15:00 UTC on 2026.9.7, using the same containers).

### Actual behavior

The run ends with error "Aborted | sandbox_provisioning" (SandboxProvisioningError) about 5 to 12 s after the lane starts, before any tool call. Gateway log shows only "lane task error ... error="Aborted"". No Podman lifecycle event is recorded in podman events for the failure windows, and no Podman command is logged at debug level; this does not show that no Podman command ran, because read only commands such as podman info do not produce events. Dashboard turns show "This turn ended before a reply: Aborted". An immediate manual retry succeeded; cron applied a 60 s error backoff and did not rerun the slot. Later occurrences are listed in the comments.

Occurrences (UTC):
2026-09-27 05:45 Gemini worker probe (2026.9.2)
2026-09-27 15:00 scheduled email job (2026.9.2)
2026-09-29 15:00 scheduled email job (2026.9.2), cron nested lane 5400 ms
2026-09-30 02:50 Gemini worker probe (2026.9.2), lane 5301 ms; provider call returned 200
2026-09-30 11:00 scheduled email job (2026.9.6), cron nested lane 6237 ms
2026-09-30 21:00 scheduled email job (2026.9.7), run 7043 ms
2026-10-01 06:00 scheduled email job (2026.9.7), run 6775 ms, cron nested lane 5663 ms
2026-10-01 12:20 dashboard turn, Codex runtime agent (2026.9.7), lane main 6362 ms

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.7 (also observed on 2026.9.2 and 2026.9.6)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (VPS, 6 vCPU, 12 GB RAM)

### Install method

npm global with bundled Node 24.19.0, Gateway as systemd user service

### Model

openai/gpt-5.6-sol (also seen with a Codex runtime agent and a Google Gemini worker agent)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw → openai (ChatGPT OAuth, Codex endpoint)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Sandbox: rootless Podman via the Docker compatible backend, image openclaw-sandbox:bookworm-slim, network none, sandbox required for all agents. Tools profile coding. Cron jobs run isolated with a pinned model. A custom router plugin is installed but the failure occurs with all three agents and different providers (OpenAI OAuth, Codex runtime, Google Gemini).

### Logs

```shell
Captured with logging.level debug, 2026-10-01 (UTC):
12:20:15 message received
12:20:19 "slow session lifecycle operation" (about 4 s)
12:20:21 turn created
12:20:26 child process spawns (git x1, one other)
12:20:27 lane task error, error="Aborted", SandboxProvisioningError
12:20:28 Codex app server spawn; stderr "Refusing to create helper binaries under temporary dir" (PATH aliases)

No sandbox or Podman subsystem log lines appear before the abort, even at debug level. No memory pressure lines for the 2026.9.7 occurrences.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: scheduled cron jobs and dashboard turns on three agents
Severity: annoying; runs fail closed (no host fallback), no data loss
Frequency: intermittent, 8 observed between 2026-09-27 and 2026-10-01, about once or twice a day
Consequence: missed scheduled job slots until the next run or a manual retry

### Additional information

No known good version: first seen on 2026.9.2, unchanged after upgrading to 2026.9.6 and 2026.9.7.

Ruled out by observation: disk space (ample), gateway restarts (same process before and after the 2026.9.7 failures), container recreation (same containers used by failing and succeeding runs), memory pressure on 2026.9.7.

Code locations read in 2026.9.7: dist/context-C8b8jL6J.mjs around line 843, resolveSandboxContext wraps errors from resolveProvisionedSandboxContext via toSandboxProvisioningError (dist/provisioning-error-BtcXlI7q.mjs), keeping the original message "Aborted". The run classifier (dist/worker/worker.mjs around line 9746) checks sandbox_provisioning before caller_signal_aborted.

Questions: is there a fixed deadline of roughly 5 to 6 s that can abort a run during sandbox context resolution or session lifecycle work? Can the original abort reason and stack be logged?

Possibly related: #160144 (same SandboxProvisioningError wrapper, different message and timing, browser sidecar involved; we have none).

A payload free diagnostics export is available on request.

issues.body:
# Content-safety refusals are never classified — and the two transports do opposite things with them

> **Edited 2026-07-29.** The original version of this issue argued that refusals should be made non-fallback-eligible. That was written without knowledge of #98976, which argues the opposite and cites Anthropic's own guidance recommending a fallback model for refusals. I've rewritten this around what the two reports actually share — the missing classification — and around a behavioural inconsistency that neither report on its own makes visible. The policy question is now presented as an open decision rather than a recommendation. Original text is preserved in the edit history.

## Relationship to existing issues

- **#98976** (open) — Anthropic `refusal` stop reason / OpenAI `content_filter`: the request returns HTTP 200 with a completed stream, so no error classification happens, `failoverReason` is `null`, and the fallback chain is **never consulted**. The turn dies with a generic `LLM request failed.`
- **#27975** (closed, not planned) — generic "An unknown error occurred" surfaced to chat on Anthropic refusal / sensitive stop reasons.

This issue reports the **`claude-cli` provider path**, where the same class of refusal produces the **opposite** behaviour. It is not a duplicate of #98976, and the two together describe a single underlying gap.

## The core defect

**A refusal never gets a reason.** There is no `refusal` / `content_refusal` value anywhere in the failover reason set. What happens next depends entirely on which transport the refusal arrives through:

| | how the refusal arrives | classified as | fallback chain |
|---|---|---|---|
| API transport (#98976) | HTTP 200, `stopReason: "refusal"` | `failoverReason: null` — no classification runs | **never consulted** |
| `claude-cli` transport (this issue) | thrown error, `API Error: … safety measures …` | `"unknown"` | **advances to the next candidate** |

Same refusal, same user-visible cause, opposite outcome — and neither outcome was chosen deliberately. Both are the default that falls out of a missing classification. Any fix for one path that doesn't address the other leaves the inconsistency in place.

## Observed behaviour (claude-cli path)

Structured record from `model-fallback/decision`, fields trimmed:

```json
{
  "event": "model_fallback_decision",
  "decision": "candidate_failed",
  "requestedProvider": "claude-cli",
  "requestedModel": "claude-opus-5",
  "reason": "unknown",
  "errorPreview": "API Error: claude-opus-5 has safety measures that flagged this message for a cybersecurity topic. To learn about the Cyber Verification Program and apply for access, visit our help center: ...",
  "fallbackStepFromFailureReason": "unknown",
  "fallbackStepToModel": "<third-party-provider>/<model>",
  "fallbackStepFinalOutcome": "next_fallback"
}
```

The API returned a specific, actionable message naming a named access program. It is preserved verbatim in `errorPreview` but plays no part in classification, so `reason` degrades to `unknown` and the chain advances to a different vendor.

Two such events in one day on one host, both during ordinary systems/log analysis work. In both cases an immediate retry on the **same** model succeeded (13:49:11 refused → 13:49:22 succeeded; 18:35:08 refused → 18:35:22 succeeded), confirming this is a per-message classifier result, not a model- or account-level block.

## Source references

Verified against installed `openclaw@2026.7.1-2` (bundled `dist/`, mapped back to the `src/` paths in the region comments):

- `src/agents/model-fallback.ts` — `recordFailedCandidateAttempt` and `appendFailedCandidateAttempt` both do `reason: described.reason ?? "unknown"`. When the classifier has no opinion, the attempt is recorded as `unknown`.
- The candidate loop in `runWithModelFallbackInternal` advances on a thrown candidate error; there is no reason-aware gate that could hold a refusal back, because no reason distinguishes it.
- `src/agents/failover-policy.ts` — `shouldAllowCooldownProbeForReason` and `shouldUseTransientCooldownProbeSlot` both list `"unknown"` alongside `rate_limit` / `overloaded` / `timeout`, i.e. `unknown` is positively treated as a **transient** failure. A refusal is deterministic and content-dependent, not transient.
- `src/shared/anthropic-refusal.ts` (`applyAnthropicRefusal`, `provider_refusal`) is present in the build and is the #98976 path — it converts the refusal into an assistant message rather than a classified error, which is why that path never reaches failover at all.

## What should change

**Uncontested, and the part I'd like to see regardless of the policy decision:**

1. **Classify refusals.** Introduce a distinct reason (`refusal` / `content_refusal`), populated from both transports — the API `stopReason: "refusal"` / `finish_reason: content_filter` path *and* the CLI error-string path. Today neither produces one. #98976 asks for the same field.
2. **Stop treating them as transient.** Whatever the fallback policy ends up being, a refusal should not be sharing a code path with `rate_limit` in `failover-policy.ts`. Retrying does not help, and cooldown-probe accounting is meaningless for it.
3. **Surface the provider's own message.** The refusal text is specific and frequently actionable. Both this issue and #27975 report operators being shown a generic unavailable/unknown error while the real explanation sits unused in the payload.

**The open policy question — I don't think this issue should decide it:**

Should a classified refusal be fallback-eligible?

- **#98976 argues yes**, on the grounds that from the user's perspective the prompt simply didn't get processed, classifier false positives are real (a music track titled "Species Filter" tripping the `bio` category), and Anthropic's own error copy explicitly recommends configuring a fallback model.
- **The counter-argument**, from the behaviour observed here: the current claude-cli path already does fall back, and does it **silently and cross-vendor**. An operator who has consented to one provider handling their content has not necessarily consented to a different one receiving the same content, and gets no signal that the substitution occurred. An automatic retry-elsewhere-until-accepted loop is also, mechanically, classifier shopping — which is a strong thing to have as an undocumented default.

These are reconcilable. Falling back on a refusal is defensible **when the operator can see it happened**; what's hard to defend is that it currently happens invisibly, under a reason label that says `unknown`. So the ask is that the behaviour becomes deliberate and observable — configurable if that's the maintainers' preference — rather than an accident of which transport the refusal arrived through.

Genuine provider failures — `timeout`, `overloaded`, capacity, billing — should be untouched by any of this.

## Secondary finding (happy to split out)

`warn` / `error` / `fatal` console logs are emitted via `console.warn` / `console.error` to **stderr**. Any deployment that routes the process's stderr to `/dev/null` — a launchd plist with `StandardErrorPath` set that way, for instance — silently discards **all** warn-and-above console output gateway-wide. The structured JSONL file logger is unaffected, but an operator grepping the process's captured stdout will find nothing and reasonably conclude the events never occurred. That is how the fallbacks above went unnoticed here.

issues.body:
## What happens today

On a new install the dashboard's first-run card says "Connecting your AI..." and "Checking a real conversation. This may take a minute or more." It picks an AI on its own and tests it, with no way to see or choose what it is doing. Its only choice is "Sign in with ChatGPT", plus buttons for whatever else the Gateway happened to find. When that fails, the card prints the Gateway's raw error text. One real example from a failed ChatGPT sign-in:

> Credentials saved; default unchanged. OAuth token refresh failed for openai: Auth profile credential authority is unavailable; retry after owner recovery. Please try again or re-authenticate. Choose the saved sign-in in Model Setup to retry without signing in again. Choose whether OpenClaw can use your ChatGPT plan for eligible Responses API requests. Token sharing does not grant access to conversations, Codex history, or connected apps.

The Mac app's own welcome window does this better: Welcome, then "Where should your assistant run?", then "Connect your AI", where you pick an AI and set it up. Its errors are one short sentence, with the full message behind "Show details".

## What should happen

The dashboard's first-run setup uses the same steps as the Mac welcome:

1. Welcome to OpenClaw
2. Where should your assistant run? (shows the Gateway this page is connected to)
3. Connect your AI: a short list with one row per provider. Picking a row replaces the list with that provider's own card, with a way back to the list:
   - ChatGPT, first, working as it does today: an existing Codex login on the Gateway is tested when ChatGPT is picked; otherwise, or when that test fails, the card shows one "Sign in with ChatGPT" button.
   - Claude: one "Use my Claude Code login" button when the Gateway found one, otherwise a Claude API key.
   - Run a model locally: local models the Gateway found, local model servers such as LM Studio, and downloads such as Ollama.
   - Another provider: every other sign-in and API key.
   A small refresh control checks again for newly installed apps and logins. Nothing is tested or saved until the user picks a provider. Plugin approvals and sign-in codes are answered on the provider's card.
4. You're all set!

The list shows only provider names, with no model ids such as `openai/default` and no explanatory text; everything about setting one up lives on its card.

Errors on this screen are one short sentence. The Gateway's own text stays under "Show details".

## Notes

- The sign-in failure itself (the token refresh error above) is a separate problem.
- OpenClaw has no browser sign-in for Claude, so the Claude card uses a Claude Code login or an API key.

issues.body:
## Problem

Expose compaction reserve or an equivalent trigger threshold under agents.defaults.compaction, preserving current defaults.

Confirmed investigation on deployed npm OpenClaw 2026.9.7: automatic compaction uses contextTokens > contextWindow - reserveTokens with a 20,000-token reserve floor. A 258,400-token window therefore compacts around 238k. Embedded worker sessions often end at 140–220k, never reaching this point while resending growing history each call.

Gateway evidence, 2026-11-08→11-11, 17,053 Codex calls: input p50 73,239; p90 119,842; p95 146,481; p99 198,425; max 264,174. Only 0.12% exceed 238k. Eight fresh sessions start at 47,697–47,725 input and grow ~1.5k/call. Previously confirmed measurements, not a claim about current upstream main.

## Request

Expose the reserve or equivalent explicit trigger configuration so operators can compact earlier (~120–150k here) without patching core. Keep behavior unchanged when unset. Cover schema, runtime wiring, documentation and tests, including interaction with model context and reserve floor.

keepRecentTokens controls retention. maxActiveTranscriptBytes on the investigated version covers auto-reply preflight, not embedded/subagent runs. truncateAfterCompaction only rotates after compaction fires; neither moves the embedded trigger earlier. Daily reset is a separate mitigation.

Implementation will check current upstream compatibility and avoid duplicating any existing feature. No replacement of the running npm install or silent downstream fork. Related TF operational investigation: grox2012/TokenFactory#146.

issues.body: ### Bug type Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary On a physical Apple Watch, Talk on Watch consistently fails after talk.client.create succeeds, showing “Voice changed its remote network address” and never establishing realtime audio. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure OpenClaw Gateway 2026.9.6 Talk with OpenAI Realtime Voice, model gpt-live-1-codex, transport: webrtc, and a valid OpenAI OAuth login for the selected agent. 2. Complete standalone Apple Watch setup against the reachable HTTPS/WSS Gateway. 3. On a physical Apple Watch running the OpenClaw companion app from iPhone version 2026.9.2 (1), open Talk on Watch, tap Start, and select the Home Assistant agent. 4. Observe Call unavailable with: Voice changed its remote network address. 5. Confirm in Gateway logs that talk.client.create completed successfully immediately before the Watch failure. ### Expected behavior Per the standalone Apple Watch voice documentation, after tapping Start with a supported WebRTC provider/auth configuration, the Watch should establish the realtime call and show Connected, allowing two-way Opus audio with the provider. ### Actual behavior The Watch never reaches Connected. It shows Call unavailable for the selected Home Assistant agent with the error Voice changed its remote network address. Gateway logs show talk.client.create completed successfully immediately before the Watch-side failure. ### OpenClaw version Gateway: 2026.9.6; iOS/watchOS app: 2026.9.2 (1) ### Operating system Ubuntu 24.04 (Gateway); watchOS 27 (physical Apple Watch Ultra 2); iOS 27 (paired iPhone) ### Install method Docker (Gateway); OpenClaw iOS/watchOS companion app ### Model gpt-live-1-codex ### Provider / routing chain Apple Watch -> OpenClaw Gateway -> OpenAI Realtime (gpt-live-1-codex, ChatGPT OAuth); WebRTC/Opus media flows directly between Watch and OpenAI ### Additional provider/model setup details Talk realtime provider: OpenAI Realtime model: gpt-live-1-codex Voice: cove Transport: webrtc Brain: agent-consult OpenAI authentication is ChatGPT OAuth configured for the Home Assistant agent. The Home Assistant agent itself continues to use its configured backend model (Groq/Qwen); GPT-Live is used only for the realtime voice session. Gateway talk.catalog reports OpenAI realtime as ready and supports webrtc. The failure occurs after talk.client.create succeeds. ### Logs ```shell Watch UI immediately after the failed call: Call unavailable Home Assistant Voice changed its remote network address Gateway log from the same test: 2026-09-25T11:01:47.071-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ talk.client.create 191ms conn=dcaeb596…6fe6 id=C24EF2CE…4E00 Additional Gateway checks: 2026-09-25T11:03:02.412-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ talk.catalog 50ms conn=9d638fe0…c888 id=72:c0ad14c8-…ade7 2026-09-25T11:03:10.419-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ talk.catalog 50ms conn=9d638fe0…c888 id=77:8737789d-…35e9 talk.catalog reports the OpenAI realtime provider as ready, with: - activeProvider: openai - model: gpt-live-1-codex - transport support: webrtc - voice: cove Source/version comparison: The Watch-side check producing this error is present unchanged in both OpenClaw v2026.9.2 and v2026.9.6: guard destination == requested.destination else { throw WatchRealtimeMediaError.unavailable( String(localized: "Voice changed its remote network address.") ) } ``` ### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence Gateway logs for the same attempt show talk.client.create succeeded before the Watch-side failure. ### Impact and severity Affected: Physical Apple Watch user using standalone “Talk on Watch” with OpenAI Realtime Voice over WebRTC. Severity: High for the affected feature. The standalone Watch voice call cannot be established at all. No crash or data loss was observed. Frequency: Reproduced on every observed attempt with this configuration, including a repeat test with iPhone Bluetooth disabled. Consequence: “Talk on Watch” is unusable because the call terminates before reaching Connected or establishing realtime audio. ### Additional information No known-good physical-Watch version has been established. The failure reproduces with the iPhone Bluetooth disabled, so it is not dependent on the normal Watch-to-iPhone Bluetooth path. A DNS64 check on the same home network (`dig +short AAAA ipv4only.arpa`) returned no result. The Watch-side `readyRoute()` check that emits `Voice changed its remote network address` is unchanged between OpenClaw v2026.9.2 and v2026.9.6, so this specific behavior does not appear to be explained by the iOS/watchOS app being on 2026.9.2 while the Gateway is on 2026.9.6.

### Bug type

### Beta release blocker

### Summary
The main-session subscription test discards a rejected chat.send RPC's error payload and can leave its session.message waiter unhandled when the assertion fails.

### Steps to reproduce
Observed in the Bun agentic-control-plane-agent-chat-hosted-2 shard in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44566158760/job/135709313435. A standalone reproduction of the initial RPC rejection is not yet established.

### Expected behavior
The test should preserve the failed RPC's error and observe both asynchronous results, including when the socket closes during fixture cleanup. Listener registration must still precede chat.send, and the existing session visibility assertions must remain intact.

### Actual behavior
server.chat-main-session-narrow.test.ts fails at the ownerTurn chat.send assertion with `expected false to be true`. The same file reports an unhandled `closed 1012: service restart` rejection. The helper creates onceMessage before awaiting the RPC, but only awaits that promise after a successful assertion.

### OpenClaw version
0eb6488cd3ce5918c4d1fe48d0a4bb4cd2d290a2 (main CI); the test is unchanged at cd2ae19272a3ee7be456385fa7efc56d6e2109a6.

Gateway test fixture.

## Summary
Reuse the existing synchronous filesystem counter helper in the two sandbox preparation benchmarks.

## Problem to solve
`sandbox-mount-preparation-measure.ts` and `sandbox-tool-preparation-measure.ts` duplicate the same filesystem wrapping and restoration code. This is the next bounded cleanup in the maintainer-requested sloppiness audit, following #201832.

Replace both copies with `countSyncFsCalls`, keeping the four instrumented methods, the `realpathNative` output key, the instrumented run boundary, and cleanup in `finally`. No production sandbox behavior changes.

Internal benchmark maintenance only; no user-visible behavior change.

The current production snapshot identifies this shared block as clone group `da1f674db5c3`. Both copies remain in the verified source baseline. A real-filesystem parity check confirms matching counts, return values, ENOENT errors, native calls, named ESM exports, and restoration for both callers.

Yes. The scoped change removes 42 lines across the two callers and reuses the helper already merged in #201832.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The managed-service registry in `src/agents/provider-local-service.ts` is per process. Any second OpenClaw process with the same config (for example `openclaw memory status --deep`, `openclaw memory search`, `openclaw agent exec`) acquires the same configured `--port`:

- If nothing is listening, it spawns its own llama-server there, and on exit SIGKILLs that process group.
- If something is listening, `startAndWaitForLocalService()` treats a healthy probe as its own service and uses it without owning it.

So the Gateway can adopt a server owned by a short-lived CLI process, which then kills it on exit while Gateway embedding requests are in flight (transport failure -> provider degraded -> index dirty until the next successful sync). A CLI can likewise adopt the Gateway server. Found by code reading; adoption was observed (a headless `agent exec` run used the Gateway warm server instead of starting one), the kill-during-request sequence was not separately reproduced.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Managed local embeddings; wait until the Gateway managed llama-server idle-stops.
2. Start a long-running CLI memory operation (for example `openclaw memory index --agent <id>`), which spawns llama-server on the configured port.
3. While it runs, trigger a Gateway memory sync: the Gateway health probe succeeds against the CLI server, so the Gateway does not spawn its own.
4. Let the CLI exit: its process group is killed; in-flight Gateway embedding requests fail.

### Expected behavior

One owner per configured managed service: for example a lock or pid file next to the preset, verifying that a healthy listener belongs to this process before adopting it, or routing non-Gateway embedding use through a running Gateway.

### Actual behavior

Ownership is decided by a health probe only; a process can borrow, or kill, a service it does not own on the shared port.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.6 (fe06181). The relevant code is unchanged on `main` (checked 2026-10-24).

### Operating system

Linux x64 (Arch-based), Node 24.22.1

### Install method

npm global; `@openclaw/llama-cpp-provider` from the official channel; managed CPU llama.cpp b10809

### Model

Embeddings: `hf:ggml-org/embeddinggemma-300m-qat-q8_0-GGUF/embeddinggemma-300m-qat-Q8_0.gguf`

### Provider / routing chain

`memory.search.provider: "local"`, `fallback: "none"` -> managed llama-cpp router on 127.0.0.1 (`--models-preset <absolute path>`, `--models-max 2`, embedding-only setup, no chat models)

### Impact and severity

Transient Gateway embedding failures whenever CLI memory commands or headless runs overlap with Gateway indexing. Workaround: avoid CLI memory commands while the Gateway is indexing; use the in-Gateway memory tools.

Related: #182518 (the preset failure that made this sequence worth closing).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary

If the Control UI tab's Gateway WebSocket drops during a Talk session (realtime mode, `agent-consult` brain, WebRTC transport), Talk keeps running directly against the realtime provider and keeps delegating turns to the agent. Those delegated turns still carry the operator authority captured from the dead connection but no longer have a Gateway context. Every Gateway-backed tool call in them fails with:

```
operator run authority requires its admitted Gateway
```

Local tools (exec, other MCP servers) in the same turns keep working, so the agent looks healthy and retries. The user isn't told that anything is wrong.

### Steps to reproduce

1. OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (b556fdf). The agent runs on the `claude-cli` backend, with OpenClaw tools exposed through the MCP loopback bridge.
2. Open the Control UI and start a Talk session (realtime, `talkBrain: agent-consult`, `talkTransport: webrtc`, provider `openai`).
3. Let the Control UI's Gateway WebSocket drop while the WebRTC audio stays up, for example by backgrounding the browser or locking a phone screen. The Gateway logs `webchat disconnected code=1006` and the connection does not come back.
4. Keep talking. Ask for something that makes the delegated agent turn call `sessions_list`, `sessions_history` or `sessions_search`.

### Actual behavior

- Every call to `sessions_list`, `sessions_history` and `sessions_search` in the delegated turns returns `operator run authority requires its admitted Gateway`. In the observed incident, all failures fell in the ~3 minutes after the `code=1006` disconnect and none before it.
- Non-Gateway tools in the same turns succeed.
- The Gateway emits no log line for the refusal. The throw happens caller-side in `callAgentToolGatewayRequestBound` (dist `in-process-gateway-*.mjs`), when the caller identity has `operatorAuthority` but `getInProcessGatewayRequestContext(...)` resolves nothing.
- Talk gives the user no sign that tools are unavailable.

Controls on the same build and the same Gateway process:
- The same tools succeed from channel-originated turns (e.g. a chat-channel message) in the same session. Those turns have no operator authority, so they take the ordinary Gateway client fallback.
- The same tools succeed from an operator-authority turn whose Gateway connection is still live (`openclaw agent ...` → `sessions_list: OK`, `sessions_history: OK`).

### Expected behavior

One of these:
- Talk/Control UI re-establishes the Gateway connection and rebinds delegated turns to it, or
- once the operator connection that admitted the Talk session is gone, Talk stops delegating and tells the user that agent tools are offline until the tab reconnects, rather than silently running turns whose Gateway tools are guaranteed to fail.

At minimum, the Gateway should log once when it admits (or continues) a delegated run that carries operator authority with no resolvable Gateway context.

### Related

- #187535 shows the same error string with a different trigger: a queued follow-up runner with no `resolveGatewayContext`. It is closed, and this path is still present in 2026.11.2.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.2 (b556fdf)

### Operating system

macOS (Gateway as a LaunchAgent), Control UI in a mobile browser

### Install method

npm global

issues.body:
### Summary

Expose `workboard.cards.archive` and `workboard.cards.move` as Workboard dashboard
action verbs, so a granted HTML widget can archive or move a card with
`openclaw.action.run` instead of posting a prompt to the session.

### Problem to solve

I keep a pinned HTML dashboard widget that renders a Workboard board (one card per
upstream issue or PR I follow) with an Archive button on each card. Today the
Workboard plugin declares only `workboard.dispatch` as a dashboard action verb
(docs/plugins/reference/workboard.md). A widget therefore cannot archive a card
directly. The only route is `openclaw.prompt.send`, which posts a visible chat
message, starts an agent turn and asks the agent to run the Gateway call. A
one-click board action becomes a model turn and a confirmation in the chat.

`openclaw.cron.trigger(jobId)` does not help either: it takes no parameters, so
a job cannot know which card to act on.

### Proposed solution

Add these to the Workboard plugin's `dashboard.actionVerbs`, mapped to the
existing `operator.write` methods:

- `workboard.cards.archive` with `{ id, archived?, expectedUpdatedAt? }`
- `workboard.cards.move` with `{ id, status, expectedUpdatedAt? }`

Grants stay per widget and per verb as today, so an operator approves "this
widget may archive cards" once. Optionally, allow a grant to be scoped to one
board (for example `workboard.cards.archive:<boardId>`), as
`github.actions.runs:<owner>/<repo>` is scoped to a repository.

### Alternatives considered

- `openclaw.prompt.send` (current): works, but every click becomes a chat
  message and an agent turn, and needs a confirmation unless the prompt grant
  is given.
- A third-party plugin that registers its own archive RPC and action verb: it
  duplicates a method Workboard already has, only to make it reachable.
- `openclaw.cron.trigger`: no parameters, so one job per card would be needed.

### Impact

Affects anyone who builds a board-backed dashboard widget. Without this, simple
card actions such as archive, done or move back to backlog have to go through
the chat and the model. The methods and scopes already exist; this only makes
them reachable from granted widgets.

### Evidence/examples

- docs/plugins/reference/workboard.md: "Dashboard action verbs: `workboard.dispatch`"
- docs/tools/show-widget.md: `openclaw.action.run(actionId, params?)` invokes an
  operator-granted plugin dashboard action verb; `openclaw.cron.trigger(jobId)`
  takes only a job id.
- docs/plugins/workboard.md: `workboard.cards.archive` and `.move` accept
  `expectedUpdatedAt`, which fits widget-initiated writes.

- Builds on #112083 (plugin-declared widget data bindings and action verbs) and
  #127314 (granted widgets can run actions).

Seen on OpenClaw 2026.10.5.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No.

issues.title: Plugin metadata snapshot rescans the entire plugin tree on every startup: runtimePluginMs 58s on a 6,495-file tree, 7× per-file cost on Docker/NAS
