### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On Linux with OpenClaw 2026.11.4, `backup create --verify` wrote a 32.8 GB archive before rejecting two distinct workspace files whose names differ only by capitalization. The predictable path-policy failure was surfaced only after roughly 40 minutes of backup work.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on an existing installation (no minimal isolated reproduction was run):

1. Have two different regular files in the same included workspace directory whose names differ only by case. For privacy, refer to the observed names as `Example_0.json` and `example_0.json`.
2. Run `openclaw backup create --output <backup-directory> --verify --json`.
3. Observe the full archive being written and published, then verification exiting 1 with `Archive contains a portable path collision` naming the two entries.

### Expected behavior

Apply the verifier's existing portable-path policy during creation preflight, before expensive database snapshot/compression work, and identify the conflicting paths with actionable guidance. Preserve both source files and retain strict final verification. This is a requested behavior improvement; no known-good earlier version was tested on this installation.

### Actual behavior

The archive reached 32,841,185,743 bytes and 786,311 entries before the command reported a portable path collision. The two files contain different data, so silently choosing a winner or deduplicating them would lose information.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.4 (d843d6a)

### Operating system

Linux x64, kernel 7.0.0-43-generic, case-sensitive source filesystem; Node.js 26.13.1.

### Install method

npm global; systemd user Gateway. Backup executed on the host as the installation owner.

### Model

Not applicable: local backup command.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable: local backup command.

### Logs

Paths and filenames below are anonymized; error wording is preserved:

```text
Backup archive verification failed: <backup-directory>/<timestamp>-openclaw-backup.tar.gz.
Archive contains a portable path collision:
<archive-root>/payload/posix/home/<user>/.openclaw/workspace/<agent>/artifacts/<directory>/Example_0.json and
<archive-root>/payload/posix/home/<user>/.openclaw/workspace/<agent>/artifacts/<directory>/example_0.json
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- Exit code: 1, JSON error type `cli_error`.
- `gzip -t` on the completed archive exited 0.
- Python `tarfile` streamed all 786,311 entries successfully.
- Both offending files were present, with sizes 36,610 and 34,170 bytes respectively. Each archived file's SHA-256 matched its original source file.
- These checks establish archive readability and preservation of that pair; they do NOT establish OpenClaw restore compatibility. No restore was attempted and no guard was bypassed.
- No raw archive, credentials, configuration, file contents, or private paths are attached.

### Impact and severity

Observed once on this installation. It blocked the verified-backup prerequisite for an upgrade after writing 32.8 GB and spending roughly 40 minutes. A separate `--no-include-workspace --verify` attempt is in progress; its success is not yet established. Both source files and the rejected archive have been preserved.

### Additional information

Related: #136159 (closed, includes late case-collision detection), #148020 (closed, case-only credential filenames), and #196334 (open, documentation of this policy). This report specifically requests early, actionable detection by the creator, not relaxed cross-platform restore validation. Please link/close as duplicate if that creation-preflight behavior is already tracked elsewhere.

issues.body:
### Summary

The Active Memory timeout circuit breaker (#74054) should pause recall after `circuitBreakerMaxTimeouts` consecutive timeouts (default 3) for `circuitBreakerCooldownMs` (default 60 000). It never opens when timed-out turns arrive more than `circuitBreakerCooldownMs` apart, which is the normal case in a chat:

- A recall has already used its whole budget by the time its timeout is recorded. Two back-to-back timeouts in one conversation are therefore at least `timeoutMs + setupGraceTimeoutMs` apart, plus however long the user takes to reply.
- Since PR #105316, `recordCircuitBreakerTimeout()` drops a key whose last timeout is older than the cooldown before incrementing it. With a budget of 60 s or more, every timeout restarts the count at 1. With the default 15 s budget, the breaker opens only if each timed-out turn lands within 60 s of the previous one.

So when the recall model can't finish inside its budget, every turn waits the full budget, then runs without memory context, and the in-flight model stream is aborted. Recall is never paused.

### Where (main @ cf2558f5639e)

- `extensions/active-memory/recall-state.ts:62-77`: `recordCircuitBreakerTimeout()` deletes every entry with `now - lastTimeoutAt >= cooldownMs`, including the key being recorded (loop at 64-68). It then sets `consecutiveTimeouts: (entry?.consecutiveTimeouts ?? 0) + 1`. `recall-state.test.ts:51` ("restarts an expired key before adding a new timeout") pins this behavior.
- `extensions/active-memory/recall-state.ts:45-60`: once the breaker is open, the first check after the cooldown deletes the record ("reset and allow one attempt through"). A probe that times out starts again from 1 instead of re-opening. PR #100176 proposed a half-open fix but was closed for inactivity without review.
- `extensions/active-memory/recall.ts:216-238`: the breaker check. `recall.ts:366` and `:382` already reset the key after any non-timeout result, so expiring the count is not what keeps it from going stale.
- `extensions/active-memory/types.ts:28-29`: defaults 3 / 60 000 ms. The schema allows a cooldown up to 600 000 ms, but a longer cooldown also widens the window that counts as "consecutive".

### Steps to reproduce

Unit level, with the same fake-timer setup as `recall-state.test.ts`:

```ts
const key = buildCircuitBreakerKey("main", "local", "slow-model");
for (let turn = 0; turn < 5; turn++) {
  vi.advanceTimersByTime(150_000); // each timed-out turn spends its full budget first
  recordCircuitBreakerTimeout(key, 60_000);
}
expect(isCircuitBreakerOpen(key, 3, 60_000)).toBe(true); // fails on main: the count is back to 1
```

End to end:
1. Enable Active Memory for direct chats with `logging: true` and the breaker defaults. Point recall at a model that can't answer within `timeoutMs`, such as a local reasoning model with `thinking` raised, or an endpoint that stalls.
2. In one chat, send five messages, each after the previous reply arrives.
3. Every turn logs `done status=timeout elapsedMs≈<budget>` and starts its reply only after the full budget. The breaker's skip line never appears (`skipped (recall paused after consecutive timeouts)` on main, `skipped (circuit breaker open after consecutive timeouts)` in 2026.10.6).

### Observed (one host, 2026.10.5 and 2026.10.6, 2026-10-16 to 2026-10-22)

Active Memory config: `mode: always`, `queryMode: full`, `promptStyle: recall-heavy`, `thinking: xhigh`, `timeoutMs: 120000`, `setupGraceTimeoutMs: 30000` (both at the schema maximum), `logging: true`, breaker defaults. Recall runs on the agent's own model, a local reasoning model served through oMLX (OpenAI-compatible, one inference slot). Counts come from the gateway log's `active-memory: … start` and `done status=…` lines:

| Outcome | Recalls | Elapsed |
|---|---:|---|
| completed | 211 | p50 63 s, p75 90 s, p90 113 s, max 148.5 s |
| timed out | 106 (30%) | 150.0–150.2 s, `summaryChars=0` every time |
| failed (unrelated errors, first three days only) | 41 | — |

- Timeouts came in runs of up to 13 with no completed recall in between. Run lengths: 1 (×36), 2 (×8), 3 (×5), 4, 6, 8 (×2), 13.
- Back-to-back timeouts were a median 643 s apart. 6 of the 52 back-to-back pairs were under 60 s apart, and 4 of those came from one burst of five concurrent recalls that timed out together.
- The breaker's skip line was logged 0 times in seven days (`skipped (circuit breaker open after consecutive timeouts)` in 2026.10.6; main logs `skipped (recall paused after consecutive timeouts)`).
- Raising `circuitBreakerCooldownMs` does not work around this. Replaying these 358 recalls through the 2026.10.6 breaker logic (outcomes as logged, state cleared at each gateway restart) with the maximum cooldown of 600 000 ms would have paused 3 recalls with `circuitBreakerMaxTimeouts: 3` and 8 with `2`. With the default 60 000 ms the replay pauses none, matching the log.
- The 106 timeouts held replies for about 4.4 h in total and returned nothing. Each one also aborted the in-flight stream. The provider logged a cancelled request, and the single inference slot spent 150 s on work that was discarded.

### Expected

- Count consecutive timeouts by outcome: a new timeout should not expire its own key. Pruning other stale keys and the 1000-key cap from PR #105316 already keep the map bounded, and a completed recall already resets the key.
- Keep the tripped state across the cooldown (half-open), as PR #100176 proposed. Let one probe through, re-open at once if it times out, and clear on success.
- Make the pause outlast the gap between turns, for example by skipping the next N recalls or by deriving the default cooldown from the recall budget. A 60 s pause expires before a human sends the next message, even with the default 15 s budget.

### Data for #86065

#86065 (raise the 120 000 ms `timeoutMs` ceiling) was closed as not planned because longer waits make the reply feel hung. The decision asked for live local-model measurements, and the table above is one, taken at the current ceiling:

- 17 of the 211 completed recalls finished between 120 s and 150 s, inside `setupGraceTimeoutMs`.
- 30% of recalls still reached the ceiling, so the user waited the full 150 s and got nothing back.

This issue doesn't ask to change the ceiling. A breaker that actually opens is what bounds that cost for slow deployments today, and any longer opt-in budget would depend on it.

### Related

#74054 and PR #74158 (breaker added), PR #105316 (expiry when a timeout is recorded), PR #100176 (half-open fix, closed as stale), #86065 and PR #87606 (ceiling), #90082 (the opposite failure mode, before these changes), #72015.

### Version

OpenClaw 2026.10.6 (fe06181), Linux arm64, npm global install. The breaker code is the same on main @ cf2558f5639e (2026-10-22).

Version: OpenClaw 2026.11.5.

## Summary
A cron `agentTurn` job on an agent whose fallback chain contains a CLI-backend provider (plugin-registered `cliBackends` id,
catalog stub `baseUrl` = `http://127.0.0.1:9/`, `api: openai-completions`) fails. The CLI-backend candidate is sent through the
HTTP transport instead of the CLI backend, throws `TypeError` in 1 ms, and that is the error the job reports
("Couldn't connect to the AI service"). The error of the first hop (here an API billing 400) is only visible in debug log lines.

## Repro
1. Agent with `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks` = `[claude-cli/<m>, <cli-backend-id>/<m>]` and a provider `<cli-backend-id>` declared as an
   `openai-completions` stub (the plugin registers the same id as a CLI backend).
2. `openclaw cron add --agent <agent> --session session:x --every 6h --disabled --no-deliver --model anthropic/<m> --message 'reply OK'`
3. `openclaw cron run <id>`; `openclaw cron runs <id>` -> `status: error`, `provider: <cli-backend-id>`.
4. Gateway log (subsystem `provider-transport-fetch`): `[model-fetch] error provider=<cli-backend-id> api=openai-completions elapsedMs=1 name=TypeError causeName=Error`.
   Same run, earlier hops: `anthropic` candidate `status=400 failoverReason=billing`; `claude-cli` candidate `candidate_failed` (attempt 2 of 3).

## Expected
The CLI-backend candidate runs through the CLI backend (as in chat turns, where `isCliProvider` is true), or the job reports the
first non-fallback error (billing) rather than the last hop's transport TypeError.

`TypeError` from the stub transport; `All models failed (3)` lists the CLI hop as "Connection error. (timeout)" (failoverReason is
classified `timeout` for the TypeError).

issues.body:
### Summary

Let curated memory files other than `MEMORY.md` / `USER.md` opt into the existing per-entry chunking, so that list-style memory files under `memory/` are indexed one entry per chunk.

### Problem to solve

memory-core already has a per-entry chunking mode (`chunkMarkdown(..., { perEntry: true })` via `curatedMarkdownEntrySpans`). It keeps each curated bullet/entry in its own chunk with its own recall metadata. Today it is enabled only for the root `MEMORY.md` and `USER.md` (`manager-index-preparation.ts`).

Many workspaces split curated memory into topic files under `memory/` (for example one file per person, project or decision log) that use the same "one fact per bullet" style as `MEMORY.md`. Those files go through the size-based chunker instead. Unrelated facts get merged into ~400-token chunks, so:

- one query hit pulls in neighboring, unrelated facts;
- the embedding of a mixed chunk is diluted, so specific facts rank lower than they do in `MEMORY.md`;
- entry-level recall metadata (annotation spans, project scope) is not applied per fact.

In practice, moving facts from `MEMORY.md` into topic files makes recall worse, which pushes users to keep everything in one growing root file.

### Proposed solution

Make per-entry chunking selectable for additional curated memory files. `memory.search.chunking` was intentionally removed from config, so I'd rather not reintroduce a chunking knob without maintainer direction. Possible shapes, smallest first:

1. **File-level opt-in marker**: a curated file under `memory/` that starts with frontmatter such as `memory: { chunking: entries }` (or an equivalent HTML-comment carrier, like the existing annotation carriers) is chunked per entry. No config change; the choice travels with the file.
2. **Config list**: a `memory.search.perEntryPaths` glob list (relative to the workspace), defaulting to `["MEMORY.md", "USER.md"]`, included in the index fingerprint so changes trigger a reindex.
3. **Convention**: treat a reserved directory (for example `memory/curated/`) as per-entry.

The change in the indexer is small in all three cases: the `perEntry` predicate in `prepareMemoryIndexChunks` gets one more input. The open question is which contract maintainers want.

### Alternatives considered

- Keep all curated facts in `MEMORY.md`: works, but the file grows without bound and is injected into context.
- Local patch of the `perEntry` predicate in the built `dist` file: works, but breaks on every update and needs a forced reindex.
- One fact per file: per-file overhead and noisy paths in search results.

### Impact

- Affected: users who keep curated memory in topic files under `memory/`
- Severity: recall quality, no crash
- Frequency: every memory search over those files
- Consequence: facts that are clearly written down are missed or ranked below unrelated content

### Evidence/examples

Prior art is in-tree: `perEntry` chunking for `MEMORY.md`/`USER.md` and its entry-scoped recall metadata. Running the same predicate for an extra path prefix locally fixed our ranking problem without other changes.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes. I'd like a maintainer to choose a shape first (my preference is option 1, the file-level opt-in, because it adds no config surface); I'll then open a small PR with tests.

issues.body:
## Summary

Keep utility-generated progress narration grounded in observed activity when the latest request refers to earlier conversation that the narrator does not receive.

## Problem to solve

The main assistant and the progress narrator do not see the same context, but their messages appear to users as one assistant. A status line that treats an unresolved reference in its own input as a lack of understanding by the main assistant can make an otherwise successful turn look confused.

For example, after earlier numbered choices, a follow-up such as `Use option 3` may be fully understood by the main assistant. The narrator receives that short follow-up and compact activity summaries, not those earlier choices. It should describe the work that is actually recorded rather than speculate about what the assistant knows or what the reference means.

This proposal was prompted by a user observation of a context-disconnected intermediate status followed by a correct final answer. We have not captured the exact transient status or proven which status producer emitted it. That production observation is not presented as a deterministic reproduction or an established release regression.

## Proposed solution

Within the existing narration prompt:

- Explain that the request and activity summaries are a partial view, not the main assistant's complete conversation.
- Ground status claims in the supplied activity. Do not infer that the main assistant lacks context merely because a number, pronoun, or earlier selection is not explained in the narrator's input.
- Keep the narrator in its status-reporting role rather than interpreting or answering the user request. Preserve legitimate, explicitly recorded failures and blockers.
- Use neutral progress wording when the available evidence cannot support a more specific claim.

Keep narration enabled. Do not send full conversation history, expand the input data surface, add a configuration option, or change model selection/scheduling as part of this change.

## Alternatives considered

- Disable narration: loses useful visibility during longer turns.
- Use a larger utility model: does not supply missing conversation context.
- Send full history: increases cost and data exposure for a small status task.

## Impact

Affected: users of utility-generated progress drafts, including Discord. This is an intermittent clarity/trust issue rather than a demonstrated failure of task execution. Frequency and affected-provider distribution are unknown.

## Evidence

Reviewed current main at `3b15369945`:

- `src/auto-reply/reply/progress-narrator-model.ts` builds the narration input from at most 500 request characters, the latest 15 activity notes, and the previous status.
- The system prompt asks for a short description of what the assistant is doing but does not explicitly explain the partial-context boundary.
- `docs/concepts/progress-drafts.md` documents this bounded input and the separation between model preambles and utility-generated status narration.

Searched open and closed issues/PRs for narrator/narration plus context, hallucination, misleading, grounded, and prompt. Related but different work: #103463 (original feature), #112553 (activity-note pipeline), #177098 (scheduler benchmark), #179092 (Gateway narration subscriber payloads). No equivalent proposal found in that search.

## Generation-validated implementation

The comparison requested in review is now complete. A prompt-only candidate and opt-in live regressions are prepared; the original production observation remains unattributed.

Four fixed synthetic cases (English/Korean earlier-choice followups, ordinary review, recorded access blocker) ran three times each for the base and final prompt through the source narrator and utility completion owner. Every output was retained. Unsupported missing-context claims fell from 4/6 to 0/6; invented access blockers from 3/3 to 0/3; recorded blockers remained reportable in 3/3 samples for both. An intermediate candidate still failed two Korean samples and was revised rather than counted as success.

Example base output: “I can’t identify options 2 and 4 or the earlier constraints from the available context.” Final candidate: “I’m reviewing the project notes related to options 2 and 4.”

The committed opt-in live regression was run against exact base prompt bytes: the referential case failed on the intended unsupported context claim, the ordinary case failed on an unexpected native tool-call item (not wording evidence), and the blocker passed. The identical final-candidate run passed all three cases. Focused narrator/prefix tests (41), targeted typecheck/lint/format, and fresh scoped autoreview passed.

Limits of the function-level evaluation above: it used the configured utility model with task-local native-user authentication and a 60-second budget, not the original agent-scope route or scheduler deadline. That evaluation did not exercise the Gateway/channel entry point; the separate Gateway and Discord-protocol follow-up below adds bounded evidence for that path. The installed app-server version differed from the checkout bundle (0.163.0 vs 0.162.1). This is sampled prompt-behavior evidence, not a universal guarantee. One final Korean output still overstated progress and 3/12 raw outputs exceeded the length instruction; those broader quality issues remain. No production configuration, authentication, or install was changed.

## Follow-up: exact-head Gateway and Discord-protocol evidence

The issue review above predates the later October 23 proof update on #181609. This section links that existing evidence; it does not claim a new October 31 execution.

- Candidate: `4440107fc93bb82c737345b339588d6f2763b07f`; baseline: `3b153699457f0f51c6d84d3e5ad8ddd29780b9ef`.
- The [PR evidence section](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181609) and [follow-up comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181609#issuecomment-6365156905) document isolated shipped-Gateway entry-point runs through the Discord handler and the repository's Discord protocol fixture. They used real main/utility completions, actual file/command activity, English/Korean earlier-choice follow-ups, and the unchanged ten-second narration deadline.
- Four emitted baseline draft edits claimed missing context; none of the four emitted candidate edits did. Both revisions' main assistants completed the selected inspection. Candidate utility completions took 2.461–3.484 seconds and were correlated with accepted fixture draft PATCH requests. These are small retained samples, not universal behavior guarantees.
- The [subsequent exact-head PR review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181609#issuecomment-6364418350) assessed the routing/deadline proof gap as resolved for this prompt change, found no actionable code defects, and marked the PR ready for maintainer review. This is an automated review, not maintainer approval or a merge.

Limits remain explicit: the Discord fixture is not the hosted Discord service or a real client; the original transient production status remains uncaptured and unattributed. The native-user authentication adaptation, app-server version difference, an additional baseline output-shape failure, candidate harness cleanup recovery, and other wording-quality limits remain documented in the PR. No new runtime, authentication, scheduling, model-selection, or data-surface changes are proposed here.

issues.body: ### Bug type Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary A long tool-using turn on a local model hit a context overflow. Auto-compaction succeeded, and the turn was aborted 30 ms later. The chat showed only "Unable to finish this reply. Your request couldn't be completed: The operation was aborted. | 20" with a "Try again" button. Nothing said why the turn was stopped, and nothing said that the task had already applied its changes (a plugin update, with a config backup). I had to read the Gateway log and the plugin list to learn that the work was done and that "Try again" would have repeated it. Related to #201576 (closed by #201928) but with a different signature: no "Reply operation stalled", no "caller_signal_aborted", no chat.abort; compaction succeeded in 99 s; the abort was classified reason=timeout. #201928 may already cover the abort itself. This report is mainly about what the user is told when a turn ends this way. One occurrence, not reproduced. ### Steps to reproduce Observed once; not minimized and not rerun. 1. Mac app with app-managed Gateway; chat model on the managed llama.cpp provider, 65,536-token context. 2. In a chat already holding about 50k tokens, ask the agent for a multi-step admin task (check for a compatible plugin version, back up the config, update the plugin, verify). 3. The agent makes 44 tool calls. The task's changes are applied about 2.5 minutes in. 4. 322 s in, the next model request overflows the context. Auto-compaction succeeds 99 s later. 5. 30 ms after "auto-compaction succeeded; retrying prompt" the turn ends with AbortError. ### Expected behavior 1. A turn that recovers from an overflow by compacting continues, or the abort is logged with its source. 2. When the system stops a turn, the chat says why (for example a time or stall limit) instead of "The operation was aborted. | 20". 3. The chat states which actions the turn had already completed, or at least warns that changes may have been applied, so "Try again" is an informed choice. ### Actual behavior The turn ended with a generic abort message and a retry button. The completed actions were visible only as a collapsed list of tool calls marked "Interrupted", with no summary. The reason for the stop appeared nowhere in the UI, and no log line names the source of the abort. ### OpenClaw version 2026.11.4 (d843d6a), app and Gateway ### Operating system macOS 27.2.1, Apple silicon (Mac Studio, 64 GB) ### Install method OpenClaw.app (app-managed Gateway, bundled runtime) ### Model llama-cpp/muse-glimmer-30b-q4_k_m (Muse Glimmer 30B, Q4_K_M) ### Provider / routing chain Managed llama.cpp provider on the same Mac (loopback); no fallbacks ### Additional provider/model setup details Context window 65,536 at the time. agents.defaults.compaction was { "mode": "safeguard" }; no compaction.timeoutSeconds and no agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds set. Thinking level High. ### Logs ```shell Gateway log, 2026-11-18, US Eastern. Ids removed. 18:47:15.258 [agent/embedded] [context-pressure-diagnostic] admitted provider attempt for llama-cpp/muse-glimmer-30b-q4_k_m route=compact_only estimatedPromptTokens=50831 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=49152 18:52:37.216 [agent/embedded] embedded run agent end: isError=true ... rawError=Context window exceeded: estimated input 63560 leaves only 1975 output tokens within the 65536-token context. 18:52:37.232 [agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for llama-cpp/muse-glimmer-30b-q4_k_m 18:54:16.314 [compaction-safeguard] Compaction safeguard: finalized artifact truncated; loss=preserved-turn-head,suffix-head 18:54:16.333 [agent/embedded] auto-compaction succeeded for llama-cpp/muse-glimmer-30b-q4_k_m; retrying prompt 18:54:16.363 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=421330 error="The operation was aborted." errorName=AbortError taskKind=turn 18:54:16.368 [model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed ... reason=timeout next=none detail=The operation was aborted. 18:54:16.429 Embedded agent failed before reply: The operation was aborted. | 20 18:54:16.515 [diagnostic] message dispatch completed: channel=webchat ... outcome=error duration=421522ms Session transcript, same turn (timestamps only): 18:47:14.975 user message 18:47:27.207 first assistant message (thinking + tool call) 18:47:27 to 18:52:37: 44 assistant messages, each thinking + one tool call, none with user-visible text; 44 tool results; largest gap between assistant messages 16.1 s 18:52:37.155 last assistant tool call; 18:52:37.208 assistant error (overflow) 18:54:16.315 compaction entry written ``` ### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence ### Impact and severity Slower local models are where long tool-using turns overflow, and those are the turns that change things. Risks a blind retry of commands that already ran. Seen once. ### Additional information Timing: the turn was 322 s old at the overflow and 421 s old when compaction returned, so it crossed 360 s inside the compaction. Model output had been continuous until the overflow, but none of it was user-visible text. Contrast, same machine and version, 2026-11-19: a user message overflowed at the start of its turn (10:37:46 "context overflow detected (attempt 1/3)"), compaction took 205 s (10:41:11 "auto-compaction succeeded; retrying prompt"), and the turn continued and replied. A separate 846 s tool-using turn with no compaction was not aborted either. User stops on this install log "chat.abort requested" and "reason=caller_signal_aborted"; neither appears on Nov 18. The "Reply operation stalled" message from #201576 is not in the 2026.11.4 build, so its absence here does not rule that watchdog out. If #201928 already prevents the abort, points 2 and 3 under Expected behavior still stand.

issues.body:
### Summary
On macOS (polling mode, Bot API routed through an HTTP proxy via env), transient network failures on Telegram `sendMessage` result in **permanent dead-lettering after exactly one attempt**, with no real retry, no user-visible error, and no alert. This silently drops high-value messages — especially subagent completion announces (follow-up agent calls with `deliver=true`), whose final reply is a single-shot delivery: when it fails, the user never receives the agent's work report.

### Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.7.2-beta.3 (npm), macOS arm64, node 26
- Telegram channel, long-polling accounts (11 bots), egress via HTTP proxy env (`HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`)
- State evidence: `delivery_queue_entries` table

### Observed behavior
1. **223 historical failed rows, all identical**: `lastError = "Network request for 'sendMessage' failed!"` (grammY wording), all failures resolving in **7.4–9.3s** (timeout-type, not instant connection refused), `retry_count = 1`, `recovery_state = send_attempt_started`, then permanent `failed`.
2. Failed payloads include complete assistant replies of completion-announce turns (queue entry payload == the full reply text, target routing correct) — i.e. the message body was produced fine and lost on the delivery leg.
3. Subagent completion announces (`sessions_spawn` → announce step, follow-up agent call `deliver=true`) fail **completely silently**: only a `[warn]` in gateway log; user gets nothing, not even a typing indicator (typing appears suppressed for internal-source turns).
4. Docs promise (`docs/tools/subagents.md`, Announce section): *"queue routing, then to a short exponential-backoff retry of the announce before final give-up"* — for network-level failures this does not happen in practice.

### Source analysis (2026.7.2-beta.3 dist)
- Telegram adapter does not declare `capabilities.reconcileUnknownSend = true`.
- Delivery drain path: send fails → `failDelivery` → drain sees `needsUnknownSendReconciliation` (send_attempt_started) → `reconcileUnknownQueuedDelivery` returns null (no adapter reconciliation) → *"refusing blind replay without adapter reconciliation"* → `moveToFailed`. **`DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES=5` is effectively bypassed — only 1 real attempt is made.**
- Announce layer: `runAnnounceDeliveryWithRetry` TRANSIENT regex matches "network error" but the actual error string is "Network request ... failed" (case/wording mismatch), so no retry classification; and by then the agent call already returned (reply text produced), so `getGatewayAgentCommandDeliveryFailure` only logs a warn.

### Impact
- Any completion/event-driven turn's final reply can be permanently lost on a single transient network hiccup, with zero user feedback and zero alerting. In a long-lived gateway process behind a proxy this is not rare (223 occurrences over ~4 weeks in one deployment).

### Suggested fixes
1. Implement `reconcileUnknownSend` for the Telegram adapter (e.g. short-lived `getChat`/`sendMessage` probe or send-with-dedupe), enabling safe replay instead of dead-lettering.
2. Alternatively/additionally: real retry with backoff for transient network errors at the queue level, honoring `DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES`.
3. Widen the TRANSIENT classification regex to cover grammY's "Network request for 'X' failed!" wording.
4. Surface announce delivery failure to the user (or at minimum a delivery-failure hook/flag) instead of silent `[warn]`.

### Repro
Route Bot API through a proxy, briefly cut/timeout egress (~8s) right when a subagent completion announce fires; observe single-attempt dead-letter in `delivery_queue_entries` and no user-visible message or indicator.

---

## Second issue (mention in same report or separate)
- Announce follow-up call (`deliver=true`) external delivery failure is silent; typing indicator suppressed for internal-source turns — combined effect: user sees literally nothing (no message, no typing) while an agent turn ran and completed.

issues.body:
### Feature type

Behavior/configuration tuning (not a bug)

### Summary

First and upfront: **Skill Workshop auto-sedimentation is a great design, and we fully support it.** Turning repeated multi-step work into reusable skills is exactly why we keep it enabled on our daily-driver deployment — several auto-generated skills have already paid for themselves. This issue is *not* asking to nerf or disable the feature; it asks for **a dial on the sedimentation rate**, because at current default behavior the generation volume outpaces what an operator can reasonably curate.

### Context (daily-driver observations, v2026.10.5)

Over the past three days of ordinary use, the background experience review produced three auto-sedimentation events (two new skills, one update to an existing skill). Our workshop library has grown to 20+ skills in ~6 weeks. Of the three recent events:

- one was a genuinely reusable runbook (kept, gratefully);
- one read like **session-history narration** — a chronological account of a single troubleshooting afternoon rather than a "when X happens, do Y" procedure (we archived it);
- one was a beneficial patch, but surfaced mid-work as another notification awaiting a keep/undo verdict.

The friction, concretely:

1. **Volume vs. curation capacity**: roughly one skill per significant work session means the library grows faster than the human can review it. Left alone, this accumulates exactly the kind of low-signal entries that skill search then has to filter through.
2. **Content shape**: some auto-generated SKILL.md bodies are operation logs ("what happened on day X: first we tried..., then we tried...") rather than distilled procedures (trigger → steps → red lines). These then require *manual* compression and cleanup — which partly defeats the purpose of auto-sedimentation. Ironically, the curation work the workshop tries to save is transformed, not removed.
3. **Attention cost**: every generation/update lands as a notification expecting a keep/undo decision, usually mid-task. We have instituted a local operating rule ("batch-report workshop events to the operator at end of turn; never interrupt active work") to keep sedimentation from derailing ongoing tasks — i.e., the operator ends up absorbing the filtering load that the feature was supposed to remove.

### Proposal (any of these would help; they compose)

1. **A temperature knob**, e.g. `skillWorkshop.sedimentation: conservative | balanced | aggressive` (default `balanced`):
   - `conservative`: only generate a skill after the *same task pattern* recurs N≥2 times in a window;
   - `balanced`: current behavior;
   - `aggressive`: for teams that want maximal capture.
2. **A review-queue digest mode**: auto-sedimented candidates land in a pending queue and surface once per session (or on demand via `skill_workshop` status) instead of interrupting per-notification.
3. **A content gate**: require generated SKILL.md bodies to be procedure-shaped (clear triggers, steps, red lines); chronological session narrative gets demoted to a scratch/appendix section or excluded. From our sample, the best auto-generated skills already satisfy this shape naturally — the worst are pure narrative.

Option 3 resonates most with what we observe: the gap between useful and useless sediment isn't frequency alone, it's whether the artifact is a *procedure* or a *diary*.

### Additional context

- OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (stable), daily driver, multi-channel deployment.
- No sedimentation-rate configuration entry exists in the configuration reference today (checked before filing), so this would be net-new surface.
- Related prior art in the tracker: #159570 (opt-in review for automation contexts) suggests we're not the only deployment interested in more control over when the workshop engages; #173605 (move out of core) is a stronger form of the same underlying friction.
- Reiterating the framing: we like the feature and want it to stay — the ask is a dial, not an off switch. Happy to provide our archived narrative-style skill as a concrete before/after example if useful for calibrating a content gate.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The repetition guard on `main` (`820c30a3a010`, #173844) stopped a real runaway reply only at char 192,000 of 212,412. The reply came from a 27B local model (a `qwen3.8-27b` variant behind vLLM), so it is inside the guard's size class.

The loop cycled through a handful of short lines with no tool call: "Let me do it now." x410, "Let me write the response." x409, "Let me write it now." x204, and a few others. That's 2,899 lines and 238 distinct overall, ending with `stopReason=length` at 65,536 output tokens.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Take a reply whose tail is a few short lines cycling in varying order (above).
2. Feed it through `RepetitionWatch` from `main`'s `packages/agent-core/src/repetition-guard.ts` in 16-, 64- or 1,024-char deltas.
3. It stops at char 192,000 (192,512 with 1,024-char deltas).
4. Control: one repeated line stops at 15,936.

### Expected behavior

Stop at the 64k or 128k check, once the 64k tail is a few short lines repeating.

### Actual behavior

At each check, against the 64k tail:

| check at | lines | distinct | best single line (count x length) | half the tail | all lines repeated 5+ times, summed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16,000 | 109 | 105 | 0 | 8,000 | 0 |
| 32,000 | 271 | 233 | 130 | 16,000 | 349 |
| 64,000 | 740 | 238 | 4,600 | 32,000 | 32,720 |
| 128,000 | 935 | 23 | 15,345 (144x "Let me do it now.") | 32,000 | 62,069 |
| 192,000 | 929 | 22 | 17,820 | 32,000 | fires |

At 128k the tail is down to 23 distinct lines across 935, and it still passes:
- No single line covers half the tail.
- The 60-char window test needs 534 non-overlapping repeats of one window (`ceil(32000 / 60)`).
- No exact period covers half the tail.

Summing every line that repeats at least 5 times would have crossed half the tail at the 64k check. I know the PR keeps lines separate on purpose, so boilerplate in distinct records doesn't add up. A narrower rule could still catch this one, for example summing only when distinct lines are under 10% of the tail's lines (23 of 935 here). That would have fired at 128k instead of 192k.

This matters beyond the GPU time. Without the guard (this host runs 2026.10.5), the whole 212k chars stayed in session history, and the next turn started at 230,664 prompt tokens with the loop in it. A stop at 64k or 128k would have left `[Repetitive output stopped]` in its place much earlier.

### OpenClaw version

`main` `820c30a3a010` for the guard test (`repetition-guard.ts` unchanged on main since). The runaway itself happened on 2026.10.5 (`1b58cb9`) plus backports, which doesn't have the guard.

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2 (arm64)

### Install method

Source build

### Model

qwen3.8-27b (27B; uncensored variant)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> self-hosted OpenAI-compatible gateway -> vLLM (`openai-completions`)

### Additional provider/model setup details

Happy to run any candidate threshold against this text. I can't attach the text itself (private conversation), but the per-check numbers above come straight from it.

issues.body:
## Bug

After a `config.patch` reload, a later ordinary turn in the same session rebuilds the prompt:

- skills that were added mid-session move into the system prompt's skill list;
- the "System prompt update" messages (Tooling, Skills) that carried them as appended deltas drop out of the history.

The prompt-caching contract (`docs/reference/prompt-caching.md`) sends mid-session skill changes as appended deltas and allows the system prompt to change only at rebuild points (compaction, `/new`, a model, provider or tool-surface switch). This turn is none of those, so the provider sees a different system prompt and a rewritten history: a full cache miss.

## Repro

The randomized prefix journey in #201723 (`test/prompt-cache-prefix-randomized.anthropic-messages.e2e.test.ts`, fake Anthropic transport, Tool Search on), seed 6:

1. Step 2 (`toolsChanged`) changes `tools.deny` through `config.patch`.
2. Steps 9 and 12 (`skillAdded`) add `probe-skill-9` and `probe-skill-12` to the workspace; each arrives as a "System prompt update" delta.
3. Step 14 switches the model, an allowed rebuild point. The rebuilt system prompt does not list the two skills, which is fine since they arrived as deltas.
4. Step 21 is an ordinary user turn. Its request lists both skills in the system prompt and drops the four "System prompt update" messages from the history.

Controls:

- The same seed passes with the ad1cd95 test code, and on the #201723 head when the step writes the config file instead of calling `config.patch`.
- The journey records this as a known break (`skills-refresh-after-config-reload`); the entry fails once this is fixed, so remove it then.

## Lead

`refreshConfigReloadSkills` (`src/gateway/config-reload-skills.ts`) -> `refreshSkillsDiscovery` with reason `config-change` (`src/skills/runtime/refresh.ts:533`) -> `bumpSkillsSnapshotVersion`. After that refresh, a later turn appears to adopt the new skills snapshot as a session rebuild instead of keeping the pinned prompt and sending deltas.

issues.body:
## Summary

On 2026.11.5, a plugin page opened by direct link or reload (`/plugin?plugin=<id>&id=<page>`) can stay empty when a plugin has selected a `workspace` replacement that mounts the default workspace with `context.mountDefault(...)`. The routed `<openclaw-plugin-view kind="pages">` is created, but the page's `mount()` is never called. The result is a blank page under the top bar. Navigating to the same page from the menu works.

It reproduces every time in Chrome (macOS) and in Safari on iPhone. 2026.11.3 was not affected in our setup.

## Reproduce

1. Use a plugin that:
   - registers a page with `host.ui.registerPage({ id: "projects", mount })`;
   - registers a `workspace` replacement whose `mount()` appends a container and calls `context.mountDefault(pane)` (in our case from a `queueMicrotask` after `mount()` returns);
   - calls `host.ui.selectReplacement("workspace", ...)`.
2. Open `/plugin?plugin=<id>&id=projects` directly, or reload while on it.
3. The sidebar renders, but the page area stays empty. The page's `mount()` never runs and nothing is reported.

## What we see

- `document.querySelector('openclaw-plugin-view')`, filtered to `kind === "pages"`:
  - it exists, with `contributionKey` `<id>/projects`;
  - it is connected;
  - its inner `display:contents` container has 0 children.
- No console error and no "Retry view" card.
- Changing the element's `contributionKey` to another value and back makes the view re-create its inner mount node and mount the page. The page then renders correctly:
  ```js
  const v = [...document.querySelectorAll("openclaw-plugin-view")].find((e) => e.kind === "pages");
  const k = v.contributionKey; v.contributionKey = k + "#"; v.contributionKey = k;
  ```

## Likely cause (from the 2026.11.5 control-ui bundle)

In the plugin view component, the mount function run from the inner node's mount effect starts with:

```js
if (!host.isConnected || disposed || !registration || registration.signal.aborted) return;
```

When the routed page is built inside the default workspace that a replacement mounts via `mountDefault`, the view's effect seems to run before the subtree is inserted into the document. So `isConnected` is false, the function returns, and nothing re-runs it:
- the later "connected/props changed" path (`T()`) only calls `update` on an existing view;
- the remount key only changes when the registration or the contribution key changes.

## Expected

The view mounts once it is connected, for example by retrying the mount on connect when no view was mounted, instead of staying empty with no error.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15), Docker image, Control UI over HTTPS (tailnet) and http://127.0.0.1.
- Clients: Chrome on macOS, Safari on iOS.

Workaround on our side: the plugin watches for an empty `kind="pages"` view of its own and toggles `contributionKey` (at most 3 times).

issues.body:
## Summary

On the same host, two maintenance commands (`doctor --fix` on **2026.10.6**, `update repair` on **2026.11.3**) entered an unbounded loop in the **update-run admission** machinery. Both times the Gateway service was **stopped** at entry (the doctor flow stops it itself; `update repair` was run manually with the service down).

Signature (Incident A): the admission reader (`createUpdateRunAdmissionReader`) re-evaluates admission on every call — "no grant is cached" — and each evaluation spawns `sqlite-source-revision.worker.js --openclaw-sqlite-readonly-child content-version <state/openclaw.sqlite>` workers that re-hash the **same, unchanged** state database. Observed rate: ~33 workers/min, ~310 MB/s sustained reads, **~1.26 TB cumulative reads**, ~2 % CPU spread over workers, **zero writes** for ~52 minutes. The process never reaches a terminal state; SIGTERM exits cleanly.

Incident B shows the same storm via a second entry point (`update repair` → `update finalize:doctor`), plus a second hang mode: after the per-agent database pass the process idles in `ep_poll` (0 % CPU, flat I/O) for minutes before the storm starts.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: **2026.10.6 (fe06181)** (Incident A) / **2026.11.3** (Incident B)
- Node.js v24.22.1 (patched line), npm global install at `~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.22.1/lib/node_modules/openclaw`
- Ubuntu 22.04, ZFS root, systemd user service `openclaw-gateway.service` (port 28789)
- State DB `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite` ≈ 166 MB; agent DBs up to ≈ 888 MB (large-state checks are in scope per the 11.1 notes)

## Reproduction

### Incident A — `openclaw doctor --fix`, 2026.10.6 (2026-11-13)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 13:59 | `openclaw doctor --fix` started (interactive) |
| 14:02:45 | doctor stops the managed Gateway (expected) |
| 14:10:43 | pre-repair recovery capture completes (2.2 GB, SHA-256) — `~/.openclaw.update-captures/doctor-d21f43d4-8219-40a1-8b3c-929a1ae53879/manifest.json` |
| 14:15:44 | **last doctor output** |
| 14:16:44 | **last DB write**; afterwards: update-activation recovery loop |
| 14:16→15:09 | livelock: `sqlite-source-revision.worker.js` respawned ~33×/min, re-hashing `content-version` of the unchanged state DB; ~1.26 TB reads at ~310 MB/s; no writes, no further output |
| 15:09 | SIGTERM (clean exit) |
| 15:10:02 | Gateway restarted manually → symptoms stop |

### Incident B — `openclaw update repair --yes`, 2026.11.3 (2026-11-13)

Context: fresh `npm install -g openclaw@2026.11.3` completed; Gateway intentionally stopped; `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive < /dev/null` had **also** hung minutes earlier (see "Hang modes" below) and was killed.

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 18:04:55 | `openclaw update repair --yes` reaches `[update finalize] {"step":"finalize:doctor","status":"in_progress"}`; log shows `operation=update.run elapsedMs=1337` on the state DB |
| 18:06:13–18:06:18 | per-agent DB inspection completes (`mr-review elapsedMs=14494`, then `mr-summary`, `tutor-package`) |
| 18:06:18→18:09 | idle: process in `ep_poll`, 0 % CPU, zero I/O growth (no workers) |
| 18:09:48 | log: `core/doctor/native-status - fs-safe: loaded`, `proc-safe: loaded` |
| 18:09:48→ | storm: child worker 100.7 % CPU (one core, 17 threads), **5.95 GB read per 10 s (~595 MB/s)**, cumulative `rchar` **226 GB**, no progress logs. Killed. |

## Observed hang modes

1. **Re-hash storm** (both incidents): unbounded `sqlite-source-revision` work over the same unchanged state DB, driven by repeated admission evaluation. IO-bound, sustained hundreds of MB/s.
2. **Idle deadlock** (Incident B, also `doctor --fix` on 2026.11.3 at `state.admission.fast-path`): event loop parked in `ep_poll`, 0 % CPU, flat I/O, no output — appears to wait on something that never resolves (both times while the Gateway service was stopped).

## Evidence

- Log excerpts (host log `/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-2026-11-13.log`): timestamps above; `operation=update.run`, `state.admission.fast-path`, `core/doctor/native-status` lines quoted verbatim in the timeline.
- `/proc/<storm-pid>/io` samples: rchar 220,519,096,461 → 226,467,236,978 in 10 s (Incident B); cumulative ~1.26 TB (Incident A).
- Worker cmdline: `sqlite-source-revision.worker.js --openclaw-sqlite-readonly-child content-version <state/openclaw.sqlite>` (Incident A, ~33/min).
- Module pointers from dist inspection: `createUpdateRunAdmissionReader` (`update-run-reader-26jSfn0A.mjs`), `package-update-activation-recovery.mjs`, `doctor-maintenance-admission-D7tIXhlB.mjs`, `sqlite-snapshot-source-Dd_uWirj.mjs`.

## Relation to previous fixes

Several changelog entries look like they target this family — but the loop still reproduces in 2026.11.3 through `update repair`:

- 2026.10.7: "post-activation Doctor waits are bounded", "stale receipts cannot veto a valid repair" (#181166, #181307, #173862, #167459, #172768, #172769, #181389)
- 2026.10.8: "an orphaned maintenance worker no longer blocks every CLI command and Gateway start" (#180668, #181695)
- 2026.10.10: "bound Doctor inspection"
- 2026.11.1: "resolve pending package steps **without repair loops**", "avoids repeated full-database copying during large-state checks" (#177932, #186787, #189647, #182632, #187921)
- 2026.11.2: "avoid update self-fencing", "Keep unavailable environments out of admission budgets" (#189321, #174735)

Hypothesis: the bounded paths cover `doctor --fix`'s update-activation loop, but the same admission reader is reachable from `update repair`'s `finalize:doctor` step and is still unbounded there (or the bounding only applies when the Gateway is up).

## Related issues

- #176112 — same command (`doctor --fix`) livelock on Windows, different mechanism (state-owner lock renewal); ours is the admission / `sqlite-source-revision` re-hash storm and reproduces cross-version and via `update repair`.
- #184516 — `update repair` misbehaving under maintenance contention (2026.10.7); may share the `finalize:doctor` path described here.

## Impact

- Gateway (and thus bots/cron integrations) down for ~1 h in Incident A; maintenance commands unusable in Incident B.
- ~1.4 TB of aggregate useless reads in two days (I/O wear, ARC/page-cache pressure) plus burned CPU.
- Operator risk: these are the *repair* commands users run when something is already wrong.

## Workarounds

- SIGTERM exits cleanly; restart the Gateway to clear symptoms.
- Avoid `doctor --fix` / `update repair` **while the Gateway service is stopped**; on this host, plain `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` (no `--fix`) completed fine (exit 0, ~13 min) with the Gateway running.
- Targeted `openclaw plugins install <name>` replaced `update repair` for provider restoration without side effects.

## Suggested fix direction

- Cache the admission grant for the lifetime of a maintenance run instead of re-evaluating per call (the reader comment admits "no grant is cached").
- Put an overall bound/wall-clock budget on `finalize:doctor` database work, and make it fail loudly instead of spinning.
- In both hang modes, emit periodic progress with the current admission decision and DB revision so a stalled loop is diagnosable from logs.

## Additional context

- Reproduced twice in one day on one host after a storage cleanup that shrank DBs (state DB 166 MB, largest agent DB 888 MB); DB sizes don't appear to be the trigger.
- Host logs and the update capture manifest are retained and can be attached on request.

issues.body:
> **Correction (2026-11-19):** an earlier version of this report said "15 marker hits". That count was
> taken from lines matching the marker, and one of those 15 lines is the wrapper's own terminal message.
> The diagnostic occurrences are **14**, comprising **8 distinct diagnostics**, and the two trees compared
> below produce an identical distinct set. The substance of the report is unchanged; the number was wrong.

## Summary

`scripts/tsdown-build.mts` converts a **successful** tsdown build into `rc=1` whenever the output contains `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]`. That marker is pre-existing at the commit we built, so any branch that touches those modules can never produce a green build — and a real compile failure is indistinguishable from this veto, because both just exit 1.

## Where

- `scripts/tsdown-build.mts:59` — `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT_MARKER`
- `scripts/tsdown-build.mts:782`, `:787` — detection: `hasIneffectiveDynamicImport ||= combined.includes(INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT_MARKER)`
- `scripts/tsdown-build.mts:1406-1410` — the veto:

```ts
if (result.status === 0 && result.hasIneffectiveDynamicImport) {
  console.error(
    "Build emitted [INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]. Replace transparent runtime re-export facades with real runtime boundaries.",
  );
  return 1;
}
```

`result.status === 0` means tsdown itself succeeded. The wrapper then returns failure.

## Evidence that the marker is pre-existing, not caused by the change under test

Same checkout, `bff0b597d`, same build command, two runs:

| run | tree state | marker hits | exit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | four-file patch applied | 15 | `TSD_APPLIED_RC=1` |
| B | same four files stashed | 15 | `TSD_STASHED_RC=1` |

Identical marker count with the change removed. The veto is a property of the base tree at this commit.

(The base `pnpm build` path is not a useful comparison: it dies earlier in `plugins:assets:build` with `BUILD_RC=1`, before reaching this phase. The veto only surfaces through the tsdown script path.)

## Expected

A build that succeeds should exit 0, or the wrapper should fail in a way that distinguishes "new diagnostic introduced by this change" from "diagnostic already present at the base commit". Right now neither is possible.

## Suggested shape

- Build the base commit once, record its marker set, and veto only markers that are **new** relative to that baseline; or
- downgrade to a warning that prints the marker count and continues; or
- keep the veto but make it explicit in the exit contract (for example a distinct exit code and a line CI can grep), so a post-success veto is never mistaken for a compile failure.

Any of the three unblocks CI-based validation of changes to these modules.

## Impact

We could not use CI as a gate for a four-file change to the state/admission path: the build reported failure on a diagnostic that was already there. We verified by stashing the change and re-running, which is exactly the manual work a maintainer should not have to repeat per branch.

Environment note: reported from a third-party operator testing a patch against `bff0b597d` (`2026.11.5`), Node 24.22.3, Ubuntu Linux x64.

issues.body:
## Summary

A source build of this repo produces a `dist` that **cannot boot**: `dist/extensions/<name>/` gets the extension JavaScript but not its `openclaw.plugin.json` manifest and not its `assets/` directory. `openclaw.json` `plugins.entries.*` resolves against those manifest paths, so config validation fails and the gateway exits `status=78/CONFIG` before it ever binds its port.

Nothing in the build output or the docs says the source build is not bootable.

## Environment

- Source checkout at `bff0b597d` (package version `2026.11.5`), built with the repo's own `scripts/tsdown-build.mts`
- Node 24.22.3, Ubuntu Linux x64
- Comparison target: the published npm install of `2026.9.37` (`81da850`) on the same host

## Observed

Manifest coverage across `dist/extensions`:

| tree | extension dirs | dirs with `openclaw.plugin.json` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| source build, `bff0b597d` | 83 | **3** |
| published npm install, `2026.9.37` | 65 | **64** |

One extension, `a2a`, side by side:

| source build | published install |
| --- | --- |
| `api.js`, `channel-plugin-api.js`, `index.js`, `runtime-api.js`, `setup-entry.js`, `setup-plugin-api.js` | `api.d.ts`, `api.js`, `assets/`, `channel-plugin-api.js`, `index.d.ts`, `index.js`, **`openclaw.plugin.json`**, `package.json` |

`openclaw.json` on this host lists 51 `plugins.entries.*`. Validation resolves those entries against the manifest paths, which do not exist in the source build.

## Reproduction

1. Build from a source checkout of `bff0b597d` using the repo's build script.
2. Point a gateway at the built `dist` (`node <checkout>/dist/index.js gateway --port <port>`).
3. Observe config validation fail and the process exit `status=78/CONFIG` with no listener on the port.

Journal in our run: service started 22:01:47 MST, state upgrade completed 22:02:13, config validation failed 22:06:26, process gone, port never bound.

## Why this is worse than a plain startup failure

The failure happens *after* the upgrade path runs. In our attempt the new binary had already:

- copied 7.3 GB of state across 58,337 files,
- migrated the agent databases v19 → v24,
- stamped `lastTouchedVersion` / `lastRunVersion = 2026.11.5` into `openclaw.json`.

So reverting the binary alone does not recover the host: the older release then refuses to start with *"this OpenClaw binary is older than the config last written by OpenClaw 2026.11.5"*. Recovery required restoring `openclaw.json` and the pre-upgrade database copies as well. A packaging error that fires before the port binds still costs a state migration and a full restore.

## Expected

Either the build produces a bootable install-style layout (copy each extension's `openclaw.plugin.json` and `assets/` into `dist/extensions/<name>/`), or the build/docs state explicitly that a source build is not bootable without a separate packaging step.

Manually staging the manifests into `dist/extensions/` is a workaround, not a fix: it changes the artefact, so any hash recorded before staging no longer describes what boots.

## Impact

Anyone validating a branch from source on a real host hits a non-obvious exit after a state migration, and the natural conclusion ("my change broke boot") is wrong. We lost an apply window to it.

Environment note: this report is from a third-party operator testing a patch, not a maintainer.

issues.body:
`openclaw setup` can fail with `Unknown model: openai/gpt-6.1-terra` even though the connected account offers that model. I reproduced it with the model's agent runtime pinned to `openclaw`.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Use fresh state with valid account credentials.
2. Configure `openai/gpt-6.1-terra` and pin its agent runtime to `openclaw`, without manually registering a provider model row.
3. Run:

   ```bash
   openclaw setup --message "Reply exactly OK. Do not change any settings or call tools." --json
   ```

**Expected:** Setup completes its inference check and shows the system overview.

**Actual:** Setup reports `Unknown model` before sending an inference request.

**Reproduced on:** macOS, OpenClaw 2026.11.6 and main `7d6f2b9`.

**Workaround:** A completed `openclaw models list --refresh --provider openai --json` resolves it. A refresh stopped before it completes does not.

**Cause:** The setup inference check resolves the model against a cold static catalog without first loading the account's model listing.

**Proposed fix:** Load the missing provider catalog before the setup inference check, wait for it, and keep setup's read-only config and auth behaviour and its cancellation cleanup.

**Evidence:** A regression test with a synthetic provider fails with the same error on main and passes with the fix.

issues.body:
## Problem

`~/.openclaw/media/outgoing/originals/` accumulates reply-generated media (TTS voice notes, images) indefinitely. There is no config knob to clean it up.

Measured on a single-agent instance over ~10 weeks (Sep 1 to Nov 20): **954 MB / 706 files**, growing ~10-20 files per day (voice-note replies are the bulk). Multiplied across agents and channels, this grows unbounded on disk.

## What I checked before filing

- Config reference: no retention/cleanup/max-age knob anywhere. The `agents.defaults.media` namespace only configures media **generation** models (template variables), not storage lifecycle.
- Docs (`web/control-ui/chat.md`, `web/control-ui/security-model.md`): describe the media serving model and graceful rendering, but no retention.
- Source: the only `cleanup` CLI (`openclaw update cleanup`) targets update-rollback recovery files - unrelated to chat media.

## Why this is safe to implement

Per `docs/web/control-ui/security-model.md`, media that fails to load already renders gracefully as an **"Unavailable" card with Retry** - no hard errors. Deleting files past a retention window therefore does **not** break loading older sessions; old transcripts just show an unavailable media card.

## Proposal

- Retention config, e.g. `media.retentionDays` (or per-direction: `media.outgoing.retentionDays` / `media.incoming.retentionDays`), applied to generated media under `media/outgoing/` **and** to received attachments stored on disk (same lifecycle question on the inbound side).
- A periodic cleanup sweep (daily or on gateway start) deleting files older than the retention window; disabled/very generous default for safety.
- Optionally log removed bytes for visibility.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.5-beta.4 (2c173a3), Linux x64, single gateway, 20 agents.

## Summary

The Workboard "Run Claude" / "Run OpenAI" card buttons use hardcoded models and ignore the agent's configured default model and the user's model policy. There is no config knob to override them.

## Location

`extensions/workboard/browser/lib/workboard/execution.ts` (checked at `cdc1b7f292d`):

```ts
const WORKBOARD_ENGINE_MODELS = {
  codex: "openai/gpt-6-astra",
  claude: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6",
} as const;
```

Documented in `docs/plugins/workboard.md` under "Starting work from a card".

History: the constant was introduced in #134943 (`6a97159ece`); the `codex` entry was set to Astra in #145646 (`f9ccd07ded`).

## Impact

- Run Claude starts on Sonnet 4.6 even when the agent's default is a newer model (e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`).
- Run OpenAI starts on `gpt-6-astra`, the most expensive OpenAI tier, regardless of the user's cost/model policy.
- Users cannot change this without patching the source.

## Suggested fix

Resolve the model for Run buttons from the assigned agent's (or the default agent's) configured model, falling back to the provider default. Optionally add a plugin config override, e.g. `plugins.entries.workboard.config.engineModels` (`{ codex?: string, claude?: string }`). Keep the current values only as the last-resort fallback, if at all.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A Control UI stable update from 2026.11.3 to 2026.11.4 spent hours validating/activating, left the Gateway unavailable during the incident, and recorded a SQLite-lock failure publishing the predecessor-stop receipt; SSH intervention was needed to finish recovery.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Actual behavior

This is one observed incident, not a minimal or repeatable reproducer. The operator started the stable update through Control UI → Settings → Updates on an existing npm-global installation with a systemd user service. After more than three hours, the Gateway was unavailable and update status showed `offline-maintenance` blocked.

The failure report records `validating` for 9027.67 seconds (~150 minutes) and `activating` for 4468.76 seconds (~74 minutes). Candidate admission checks passed. Candidate Doctor lint exited 0 with 14 deferred advisory inspections; the subsequent `openclaw doctor` exited 1 with `Predecessor stop receipt publication could not be verified. database is locked`.

Rollback refused because the shared SQLite database had changed since its snapshot and restoring it would discard later writes. Package recovery was marked unverified. These failure records coexist with later recovery/readiness records; they should not be interpreted as a single instantaneous health status.

### OpenClaw version

Starting CLI: 2026.11.3 (`847611d`). Target and candidate safety-check updater: 2026.11.4. After recovery, CLI and live Gateway RPC were verified as 2026.11.4, build `d843d6af39a42cd3c30084edbeabeece732fd93a`.

### Operating system

Ubuntu/Linux; incident OS release was not captured in the supplied evidence.

### Install method

User npm-global installation (`~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw`), systemd user Gateway service. Update initiated through Control UI Settings → Updates, stable channel. Approximately 253 GiB available at snapshot-space preflight; this was not a disk-full failure.

Current shell Node: `v24.22.3` (read-only `node --version`, 2026-11-16). Incident Node version is not independently established by the retained local evidence inspected for this report; candidate node-runtime admission passed.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Additional provider/model setup details

The reported failure is in the updater/Gateway handoff, not an observed model request. Later model-login trouble was restored through unspecified steps; credential deletion and any causal connection to this update are unproven.

### Logs

Minimal excerpts from the retained update report and bounded failure JSON (private paths omitted):

```text
Update safety checks ran in the candidate updater (2026.11.4).
Admission checks: config: ok, database-schema: ok, node-runtime: ok, plugin-availability: ok.
Phases: requested (38.12s) → staging (499ms) → validating (9027.67s) → activating (4468.76s)
candidate-doctor-lint: exitCode=0; errors=0; warnings=14
openclaw doctor: exitCode=1
Predecessor stop receipt publication could not be verified. database is locked
SQLite contention call site: Error: database is locked
  at runExistingOpenClawStateWriteTransaction
Databases changed after snapshot capture: $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite;
restoring the backup would discard later writes. Current databases were preserved.
package-backup-retention: exitCode=1
Installation recovery is unverified
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No raw log attachments. The excerpts above were checked against the retained update report and bounded diagnostic JSON. Additional timing/process observations below come from the operator's incident/recovery summary, not a new reproduction.

### Impact and severity

One observed affected Ubuntu installation; the update blocked normal Gateway use and required SSH recovery. One incident is documented; recurrence rate and broader prevalence are unknown. No database loss is established. The rollback guard explicitly preserved later writes.

### Additional information

#### Observed activity and uncertainty

Earlier samples showed filesystem traversal through retained workspace/build artifacts, then a SQLite-header worker doing disk reads. A later sample showed the main updater using approximately 99% of one CPU core while other cores were idle. The last reported handoff messages concerned previous-Gateway verification and service-command ownership, but the last message is not proof of the blocking location.

The scanning hypothesis is unconfirmed. The recorded SQLite-lock error does not establish the cause of the earlier hours of CPU activity. This report does not conflate the incident with the separate `Invalid string length` SQLite-classification issue.

#### Recovery (operator-reported, not instructions)

The operator sent exactly one SIGINT to the updater and confirmed the updater/controller and direct children had exited. Status was then `publication-complete` but still failed with `post-update-failed`. SIGINT may have contributed to the final outcome; the available evidence does not exclude that possibility.

Backup existence was checked, but verification details were not recorded. The operator ran `openclaw update repair --no-restart` once as the installation owner, without sudo. Recovery reported Gateway restart/verification and finalization with warnings. Subsequent CLI and live Gateway RPC checks verified 2026.11.4. No raw SQL, database restoration, lock deletion, forced kill, or manual npm replacement was reported. Retained incomplete captures are not claimed as verified backups.

Recovery warnings included unfinished Codex data/settings migration with old data retained, deferred agent database-path repair, retained runtimes because an unrelated process's cwd was inaccessible, an unavailable tool-allowlist entry, and unresolved auth identity with the profile unchanged. Latest status reported repair finalization succeeded and superseded some warnings; not every warning was independently rechecked.

#### Desired outcome and investigation request

No grounded known-good timing baseline or deterministic reproducer is available, hence the `NOT_ENOUGH_INFO` fields above. The desired behavior is bounded update completion/failure, useful progress diagnostics, and restored availability without SSH rescue. `publication-complete` should not be confused with end-to-end success.

Please investigate prolonged validation/activation CPU activity; writer contention while publishing the predecessor-stop receipt; handoff/cancellation behavior while maintenance blocks Gateway access; and progress reporting. This report does not establish a full root cause or a released fix.

#### Related reports checked

- #193094 documents prolonged validation on 2026.10.8 → 2026.10.9 with SIGKILL; this incident instead reached 2026.11.4 activation and includes the predecessor-stop receipt error and a single operator SIGINT.
- #197083 documents a WAL-publication witness failure on 2026.11.1 → 2026.11.3, not the same recorded receipt-publication error.
- #200022 is a closely related 2026.11.3 → 2026.11.4 automated package-backup-retention report with matching build and generic failure/recovery shape; it does not include the timing, receipt-lock excerpt, or intervention sequence here. Whether it represents the same underlying defect or incident has not been established.

issues.body:
## Summary

When a plugin-owned helper session ends (here: every Active Memory recall), `session.lifecycle.artifacts-prepare` runs a full orphan-transcript sweep inside the exclusive SQLite session writer. On our store it holds the writer for 8.6–13.0 s per call. The Active Memory recall has already produced its answer, but the plugin only sees completion after this cleanup, so recalls that answered at 22–25 s are reported as `done status=timeout elapsedMs=30002` and the reply waits the full 31.5 s with nothing injected. Other session writes queue behind the same hold (8–11 s), and some fail with `Activity recap lifecycle or utility model changed`.

## Where the time goes

`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-lifecycle-artifacts.ts` (same shape on v2026.11.5 and main 416b357cb2b1):

- `planSqliteOrphanLifecycleTranscriptStateDeletes` pages through **every** orphan `session_windows` row (`session_id not in session_nodes.current_session_id`), not only those of the plugin or key prefix being cleaned up.
- For each reclaimable orphan without a foreign `plugin_owner_id` (null owner passes), `sqliteTranscriptStateHasMarker` reads the session's complete `transcript_events` JSON and does `event_json.includes(transcriptContentMarker)`.
- Orphans that do not contain the marker are never deleted by this path, so the same windows are rescanned on every call: the cost is O(all orphan transcript rows) per helper-session cleanup and never shrinks.

## Evidence (one call, from the built-in diagnostics)

```
operation: session.lifecycle.artifacts-prepare, isMainThread: true
elapsedMs 11161, queueWaitMs 0, writerExecutionMs 11161
artifactPreparation: nodeInventoryMs 16, referencePlanningMs 91, orphanPlanningMs 4778, markerScanMs 6273,
  nodeRows 1683, windowRows 7465, referenceIds 8382, selectedEntries 1,
  markerWindows 870, markerRows 66671, deletePlans 1
```

`markerWindows 870 / markerRows 66671` is identical in all 18 calls of the day: the same non-matching orphans are rescanned each time.

Timeline of one timed-out recall (UTC, 2026-11-19):

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 15:14:53.994 | `active-memory ... start timeoutMs=30000` |
| 15:15:19.475 | recall model's final assistant message (stopReason `stop`, 1,270 chars; from `persistTranscripts`) |
| ~15:15:19.9 | `artifacts-prepare` starts (ends 15:15:32.834 with elapsedMs 12895) |
| 15:15:24.507 | `done status=timeout elapsedMs=30002 summaryChars=0` |
| 15:15:25.494 | `before_prompt_build recall timed out after 31500ms; skipping memory lookup` |
| 15:15:32.849 | `SQLite session write failed` session-entry.patch, queueWaitMs 10160, error `Activity recap lifecycle or utility model changed` |

Same pattern at 13:51 (answer at +22.6 s, cleanup 8.6 s, timeout) and 15:29 (answer at +24.4 s, cleanup 11.0 s, timeout). Successful recalls show the same lag: answer at +17.6 s, `done status=ok elapsedMs=29420` right after a 11.2 s cleanup; answer at +13.9 s, `done ok elapsedMs=25443`.

Day counts (one agent, `always` mode on a few chats): 14 recall starts, 5 timeouts; 18 slow `artifacts-prepare` writes (max 13,049 ms, p50 8,568 ms); 12 `SQLite session write failed` (session-entry.patch) queued behind them. The day before, with almost no recalls, there were 4 such writes: the cost scales with helper-session count.

## Expected

A helper session's cleanup must not make a finished plugin run miss its deadline or stall other session writes. The answer Active Memory already produced reaches the reply within `timeoutMs`, and per-call cleanup cost does not grow with the number of unrelated orphan transcripts. For example: restrict the per-call sweep to the plugin's own windows / key prefix (or to the sessions being removed), remember or tombstone orphans already checked as non-matching, move the full orphan sweep to periodic maintenance, or deliver the plugin result before the cleanup instead of after it.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d), npm global install, Linux x64, Node 26.12.1, single Gateway.
- Per-agent store `openclaw-agent.sqlite` 9.0 GB, WAL.
- Active Memory: mode `always`, model claude-sonnet-5-5, `timeoutMs` 30000, `persistTranscripts` true.

## Evidence scope

Observed in the Gateway log with the shipped diagnostics; not induced. Not reproduced on 2026.11.5, but the relevant source is unchanged there and on main. Related umbrella: #119720 (synchronous persistence holds); #180978 (Active Memory timeout handling) is a different cause.

# Candidate Doctor blocks 2026.11.3 → 2026.11.5 with migration-input conflict and `changed=[]`

## Summary

A managed npm update from OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (`847611d`) to 2026.11.5 fails during candidate validation, before activation. Candidate Doctor reports that plugin migration obligations changed during input publication, but its diagnostic says `changed=[]` and displays the same truncated expected/current plugin IDs.

## Environment

- macOS 26.4.1, Apple Silicon Mac mini; LaunchAgent Gateway, loopback binding.
- Installed/running OpenClaw: 2026.11.3; candidate updater: 2026.11.5.
- Homebrew Node v24.22.3; Gateway service explicitly uses this runtime.
- Managed update handoff invokes `openclaw update --yes`.
- An earlier SQLite STAT4 snapshot incompatibility was resolved by selecting the verified Homebrew runtime. This attempt successfully completed all eight SQLite snapshots; this report concerns the subsequent, different failure.

## Observed sequence

1. Start the normal managed update with the existing configured plugins and migration state. A minimal clean fixture is not yet available.
2. Admission: `config: warn`, `database-schema: ok`, `node-runtime: ok`, `plugin-availability: ok`.
3. Candidate snapshot succeeds for all eight databases (about 4.2 GiB total); plugin files about 409 MiB. Available space about 121 GiB; estimated required space 18 GiB.
4. Candidate invokes `doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` against its temporary copy.
5. Doctor exits 1 (about 47 seconds). Overall validating phase reported about 513 seconds.

Saved failure excerpt:

```text
Plugin migration obligations changed during migration input publication.
expected=[apple-pim-cli, codex, llama-cpp, parallel, +1 more],
current=[apple-pim-cli, codex, llama-cpp, parallel, +1 more], changed=[].
Retained inputs remain protected; run "openclaw doctor --fix" after the other repair finishes.
```

The compact `failureFacts` message is truncated; the saved stderr tail retains `changed=[]`. The fifth plugin is not identified in the saved summary, so identical displayed lists do not prove identical full sets.

## Result and impact

- Update blocked at `candidate-doctor` / `doctor-failed`, not activation.
- Live Gateway remains reachable on 2026.11.3 with the same PID; no outage observed.
- Native updater log confirms temporary candidate copy cleanup after failure.
- No standalone mutating Doctor, manual database edit, guard bypass, or retry was used to address this new failure.
- Only one attempt with the corrected runtime is documented; reproducibility is not yet established.

## Source observations, not a proven root cause

In tag `v2026.11.5`, `src/infra/deferred-plugin-migrations.ts` compares complete arrays with `isDeepStrictEqual` in `assertPendingGeneration`. `formatConflictIds` sorts/deduplicates and truncates IDs to four; `formatChangedObligationFields` compares fields of matching IDs, but does not report added/removed IDs or list order. Thus `changed=[]` does not establish a real concurrent repair, nor prove equivalent full inputs. Ordering, omitted membership changes, and structural differences remain investigation candidates.

Related but not established as identical: #180350 (conflict diagnostics), #190658 / #190665 (reason/command changes). This incident has no reported changed fields, unlike #190658.

## Requested outcome

Please investigate the candidate Doctor publication path with pending obligations, preserving generation protection and retained inputs. Improve safe diagnostics to distinguish set/order/structural differences without exposing configuration values or conversations. Please identify a supported workaround applicable before activation, or the fixing PR and first released version containing it. A generic live `doctor --fix` recommendation does not establish that it addresses this specific candidate-only failure.

No raw configuration, credentials, database, or conversation content is attached.
