### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

WebChat progress sent through `message(action="send", final=false)` remains visible after the final reply with **Keep commentary** off; the **Tool calls** toggle works.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Turn **Keep commentary** off in WebChat on 2026.10.10.
2. Run a task that sends intermediate progress to the source conversation through `message(action="send", final=false)`, followed by a final reply.
3. After final completion, observe that progress prose remains visible.
4. Toggle **Tool calls**: tool visibility changes, but completed progress prose remains.

These describe the user's observed existing session, not an independent fresh-profile or current-main reproduction.

### Expected behavior

Completed routine progress should be hidden with **Keep commentary** off. Substantive nonfinal answers and explicitly delivered updates must remain visible: `final=false` alone is not a safe commentary classification. The reference is the existing UI setting and its filtering of completed streaming-fallback commentary; message-tool progress does not receive the same visible treatment.

### Actual behavior

The user confirmed persistence after the final response with Keep commentary off. Tool-call visibility responds to its own toggle. This is retained progress prose, not duplicate rendering of one streamed item.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10

### Operating system

Gateway: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS. Browser/client OS and browser version: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Install method

npm global

### Model

gpt-6-astra

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw -> native Codex route -> gpt-6-astra

### Additional provider/model setup details

`messages.visibleReplies` was already `automatic` when inspected.

### Logs

Sanitized investigation summary, not raw logs:

- Installed UI filtering requires `openclawStreamFallback.itemId`.
- Inspected message-tool progress history lacks that marker.
- Source-reply persistence preserves `final=false` in `deliveryMirror` without setting that streaming-fallback marker.
- Installed source-reply instructions direct progress through `message` with `final=false`, including in automatic mode.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Local investigation inspected installed bundles `control-ui-boot-shared-C5EXU5eX.js`, `control-ui-boot-shared-BLdIbmDQ.js`, `internal-source-reply-persistence-DaYaIgkL.mjs`, and `source-reply-delivery-mode-CC4nGK9E.mjs`. These observations identify metadata paths to inspect, not a proven root cause or current-main failure. User confirmation establishes persistence after final completion. No independent browser reproduction is claimed; private transcripts/screenshots are not attached.

### Impact and severity

Affected: the observed WebChat session. Severity: readability/UI annoyance; completed conversations retain unwanted progress prose. Frequency: observed in the reported session, without controlled attempt counts or cross-profile measurement. Final responses still arrive.

### Additional information

Related, but not established exact duplicates:

- #134276 (closed) concerned repeated streamed commentary; closure cited run/item-keyed reconciliation. Here the route is message-tool `final=false` progress without the streaming-fallback item marker.
- #164443 (open) addresses streamed commentary repeating in live replies. That PR has not been tested for this report.
- #161052 (closed), “keep routine progress in commentary, not message sends,” provides delivery-route context.

No known-good version or regression boundary is established. No native code, settings, or transcripts were changed during this investigation.

## Review clarification

The [source review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192460#issuecomment-6620444157) identifies a shared route for disposable progress and durable side answers. The open decision is whether routine progress should use the existing commentary lane or receive an explicit classification separate from finality. A fix must cover completion and reload while preserving substantive nonfinal replies, with streaming-fallback commentary as a control. No new reproduction, passing regression, or implemented fix is claimed by this clarification.

issues.body:
I found that a worker failure can reach the caller as:

```text
Native worker task channel closed
```

That tells me the connection disappeared, but hides the useful part: whether the worker threw an exception, hit its memory limit, or exited with a particular code.

## What I reproduced

I ran isolated fault cases through OpenClaw’s real worker pool and supervisor on Node 24.20.0 and the pinned Bun 1.4.4 fork:

| Injected failure | Before the fix | With the local fix |
|---|---|---|
| Exception with a custom code and nested cause | Generic channel-closed error | Original exception, code, and nested cause preserved |
| Explicit exit with code 77 | Generic channel-closed error | Exit code 77 preserved |
| Worker memory exhaustion | Generic channel-closed error | Out-of-memory reason and `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` preserved |

I also checked channel-only closure, worker cleanup, synchronous failure handling, and a refused shutdown. Replacement tasks completed successfully after cleanup.

## Why the cause gets lost

I traced this to two separate message paths. The task channel can close before the supervisor delivers the worker’s actual error or exit result. The pool rejects the task with the first channel error and starts cleanup, so the later cause no longer reaches that task’s caller.

I found a second loss point on Bun: its native out-of-memory error inherits its `code` property, while OpenClaw’s serializer only copied an own property.

## Local fix and verification

I have a local fix that keeps the native failure until the existing shutdown path settles, then reports the actual exception or observed exit code. It also preserves inherited error codes without invoking getters.

I verified four targeted regression failures against main’s matching worker sources at `b8cd64b`. With the patch, 91 focused tests pass, along with typecheck, lint, and formatting.

I have not added sleeps, automatic retries, or higher memory limits. The patch covers active task failures; queued startup refusals retain their existing generic wording.

**This fixes the hidden diagnosis, not the underlying worker crash.**

### Bug type

Behavior bug / provider-routing classification needs verification (incorrect or ambiguous user-facing route notice; no crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A successful run selected and retained `github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol-fast` as its terminal model, while the provider response recorded `responseModel: "gpt-5.6-sol"`. The visible runtime notice said:

```text
Model route changed: github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol-fast → github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol.
```

This looks like a fallback or route change even though the observed OpenClaw target/effective model remained `gpt-5.6-sol-fast`. One plausible explanation is that Copilot's `-fast` catalog selector is served by the base `gpt-5.6-sol` model and reports that base identity in the response. That alias hypothesis is **not proved** by this observation: the provider may genuinely route the request to a different backend, and no provider contract for this pair was found in OpenClaw.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Select `github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol-fast` for a run.
2. Complete a successful response for which the terminal receipt records the selected/effective model as `github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol-fast` and the provider response identity as `gpt-5.6-sol`.
3. Observe the runtime-authored route notice.

Sanitized observed facts:

```json
{
  "selectedProvider": "github-copilot",
  "selectedModel": "gpt-5.6-sol-fast",
  "terminalProvider": "github-copilot",
  "terminalModel": "gpt-5.6-sol-fast",
  "responseModel": "gpt-5.6-sol",
  "outcome": "success",
  "notice": "Model route changed: github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol-fast → github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol."
}
```

No prompt, response text, account identifier, session identifier, credential, or raw diagnostic bundle is included.

### Expected behavior

The notice should distinguish a provider-declared response-model alias from a genuine fallback:

- If GitHub Copilot confirms `gpt-5.6-sol-fast` → response identity `gpt-5.6-sol` as equivalent, keep the concrete `responseModel` for diagnostics but set `rerouted: false` and emit no `Model route changed` notice.
- If the pair is not equivalent, preserve the route-change signal (or describe it specifically as a provider response-identity change) rather than implying an OpenClaw fallback that was not established.
- A real fallback/effective-model change must still set `rerouted: true` and remain visible.

Please do not implement this as a generic `-fast` suffix heuristic without a provider-owned contract.

### Actual behavior

Raw response-model inequality is sufficient to produce the visible route-change notice for this Copilot pair. The successful run's selected/terminal model still shows `github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol-fast`; only `responseModel` is `gpt-5.6-sol`.

This observation does not prove whether the provider used an alias or performed a genuine backend reroute. It does show that the current notice presents the distinction as settled when OpenClaw has no Copilot equivalence rule for it.

### OpenClaw version

OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (`b556fdf457b026574bf0f1e7b4914b15f3f179ce`)

### Operating system

Linux x64; Node.js 24.22.1

### Install method

Packaged Gateway environment; exact installation method was not captured.

### Model

Selected/effective: `github-copilot/gpt-5.6-sol-fast`

Provider-reported response identity: `gpt-5.6-sol`

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw → bundled `github-copilot` provider → GitHub Copilot model endpoint

### Logs

The sanitized receipt fields and exact notice are included above. No private transcript or raw logs are attached.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Source review at the observed build:

- [`isProviderModelRerouted`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b556fdf457b026574bf0f1e7b4914b15f3f179ce/src/agents/provider-model-route.ts) compares `responseModel` with the selected model, then consults the provider's `isResponseModelEquivalent` hook. If the IDs differ and the hook does not return true, it classifies the run as rerouted.
- The bundled [GitHub Copilot provider policy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b556fdf457b026574bf0f1e7b4914b15f3f179ce/extensions/github-copilot/provider-policy-api.ts) exposes thinking-profile behavior but no `isResponseModelEquivalent` rule.
- Current main showed the same relevant shape during review: Copilot has no response-equivalence rule, while core supports provider-owned equivalence.

This verifies why the observed tuple is classified as a route change. It does **not** verify that Copilot treats `gpt-5.6-sol-fast` and `gpt-5.6-sol` as the same route.

Related prior work:

- #169976 reported the same class of false notice for an OpenAI pair that OpenAI explicitly declared equivalent.
- #169977 fixed core route detection to consume provider-owned `isResponseModelEquivalent`; it did not add a Copilot policy for this pair.
- #184810 concerns ClawRouter upstream IDs and downstream compaction/fallback effects; those effects were not observed or claimed here.

Suggested verification and regression coverage:

1. Establish the Copilot contract from a provider-owned fact or a controlled transport fixture: does selecting `gpt-5.6-sol-fast` legitimately return `model: "gpt-5.6-sol"` as the same served route?
2. If yes, add a narrow Copilot policy test for requested `gpt-5.6-sol-fast` / response `gpt-5.6-sol` and an end-to-end terminal-receipt test asserting:
   - selected/effective model remains `gpt-5.6-sol-fast`;
   - concrete `responseModel` remains `gpt-5.6-sol`;
   - `rerouted: false`;
   - no route-change notice.
3. Add a negative control with an unrelated response identity (for example `gpt-5.6-luna`) that remains `rerouted: true` and emits the notice.
4. Add a genuine-fallback control where the effective provider/model changes after the selected candidate fails; it must remain `rerouted: true` and preserve the fallback/route notice even if the successful response has an otherwise equivalent alias.
5. Avoid assuming reverse equivalence unless Copilot documents it.

### Impact and severity

Low-to-medium UX/diagnostic impact. A successful Copilot run is presented as having changed routes, which can mislead users and parent-agent completion summaries into reporting a fallback or model substitution. No inference failure, data loss, or confirmed wrong-model execution is claimed.

### Additional information

Issue searches for the exact model and Copilot route notice found no open matching report. This is intentionally a provider-contract investigation rather than an assertion that the source is definitely wrong. The actionable boundary is to verify the Copilot response identity and then make alias handling differ from genuine fallback handling in tests.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On 2026.10.8, the WebChat `/clear` state check ("Checking OpenClaw state" → "Update history" note) renders recorded warnings attributed to a five-week-old update run — including `Plugin "codex" state migration is pending` — although the codex completion receipt exists, `openclaw update status --json` reports `migrationWarnings: []`, and a fresh CLI `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` renders the note from the actual latest run without the codex line. The stale chat rendering survives Gateway service restarts and a full host reboot; the CLI rendering from the same boot is correct. Filed per the closure instruction in #166766.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed path (after a 2026.9.8 → 2026.10.8 update with successful recovery):

1. Complete recovery: `openclaw update repair` + `openclaw doctor --fix` with the Gateway stopped. All `deferred-plugin-migration:*` receipts (including codex) show `status=completed` with `finished_at` recorded.
2. Verify: `openclaw update status --json` → `lastRun.status: succeeded`, `migrationWarnings: []`, `packageActivation: null`, no `activeRun`.
3. Fresh CLI process: `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` → the "Update history" note names the latest run (created the same day) and the codex warning is retired — receipt-based retirement (#166668) demonstrably works.
4. In a WebChat direct chat, run `/clear` → the state-check block names a run created five weeks earlier and includes the codex `state migration is pending` line with repair instructions.
5. Restart the Gateway service, then reboot the whole host; repeat `/clear` → identical stale rendering each time (rules out warm-read/process-lifetime caching).
6. Immediately after, run `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` again in the same boot → still renders the current run correctly. The divergence is repeatable at will: CLI correct, chat surface stale.

### Expected behavior

The chat-side state check renders the same current data as CLI doctor: recorded warnings from the latest run (`readUpdateRuns` orders `created_at_ms DESC`), with deferred-plugin-migration warnings retired via completion receipts.

### Actual behavior

The chat surface deterministically renders a five-week-old run and the unretired codex warning. Local cache artifacts were ruled out:

- Full table scans of the shared state DB and the affected agent DB found no persisted copy of the banner text or the stale run identifier outside `update_runs`.
- The rendering survives a cold host reboot (all processes fresh).
- In the same boot, CLI doctor renders the correct latest run through the same note code (`inspectStaleUpdateRuns` → `readRetiredDeferredPluginMigrationWarnings`), so the data layer and the retirement filter are functional.

Chat rendering (after full reboot; run id redacted):

```
◇  Update history
│  Recorded warnings from update <run-id created 2026-09-23> (a later repair may have resolved them):
│  core/doctor/skill-workshop-tool-policy: agents.entries.test.tools.allow does not include "skill_workshop".
│  Deferred model retirement repair completed after plugin convergence.
│  Plugin "codex" state migration is pending: The plugin has not reported completion of its retained state
│  migration. State and legacy config inputs are preserved. Run "openclaw update repair", then "openclaw doctor --fix".
```

CLI rendering (same day, same boot; run id redacted):

```
◇  Update history
│  Recorded warnings from update <run-id created same day 16:50> (a later repair may have resolved them):
│  core/doctor/skill-workshop-tool-policy: agents.entries.test.tools.allow does not include "skill_workshop".
│  channels.whatsapp.accounts.default contains only shared policy and has no detected credentials. …
│  Deferred model retirement repair completed after plugin convergence.
```

The codex line contradicts the completion receipt (`deferred-plugin-migration:codex`, `status=completed`, `finished_at` = same day 17:00:55 local) and the empty `migrationWarnings`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.8 (dc2523e), stable channel

### Operating system

Linux x64 (Ubuntu-based cloud VM, kernel 7.0.x), Node v24.22.1

### Install method

npm global install; Gateway as a systemd user unit; `OPENCLAW_HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` on a non-default data volume; WebChat/Control-UI surface; 9 agents; all plugins converged to 2026.10.8

### Model

Not relevant to the display defect (state reads only; no model involvement in rendering the state check itself)

### Provider / routing chain

Not relevant

### Additional provider/model setup details

None

### Logs

Timeline (local time, 2026-10-28):

- 16:50 `openclaw update repair` run recorded `succeeded`
- 16:59–17:00 `openclaw doctor --fix` completed all eight `deferred-plugin-migration:*` receipts (codex 17:00:55)
- 17:1x Gateway started; verification green (`migrationWarnings: []`, `packageActivation: null`)
- 18:0x WebChat `/clear` → stale banner (run from 2026-09-23, codex line present)
- 18:3x Gateway service restart → `/clear` → identical stale banner
- 19:16 full host reboot
- 19:2x WebChat `/clear` → identical stale banner; CLI `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` in the same boot → correct current run, no codex line

### Related issues and delimitation

- #166766 (closed): same visible symptom on 2026.9.8; fixed by #166668 (receipt-based retirement). Retirement demonstrably works in the CLI path on 2026.10.8; the chat state-check surface still selects/renders the stale run. Filed per #166766's closure instruction: if the defect persists in a release containing the fix, open a new issue with the doctor output and link #166766.
- #161728 (closed): similar symptom, different root cause per its resolution.
- #178121/#178122 (closed): migration recovery coverage warnings rendered on every update — different mechanism (coverage declarations), not stale-run selection.

### Impact

Cosmetic but user-facing: an apparently pending migration with repair instructions is shown after every `/clear` although everything completed, misleading operators into repeating repair/doctor loops (done here before proving data-layer completion). No functional impact observed; channels, plugins, and agents all work. Severity: low-moderate (operator confusion, ux-friction). Frequency: deterministic on this installation since the recovery; reach unknown.

issues.body:
### Summary

A managed npm upgrade from 2026.11.1 to 2026.11.3 activated the new core, then post-install Doctor failed with `SQLite WAL commit publication could not be verified`. The updater refused rollback as `state-migrated-no-rollback`, recovered a serving 11.3 Gateway, but left external plugin convergence unfinished. Offline `update repair` subsequently completed.

### Environment

- Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie), Linux/x64
- Managed Node 24.22.1
- npm package installation, systemd user Gateway, existing operator service overrides preserved
- Target/serving version: 2026.11.3, commit `847611d`
- Source 2026.11.1 had a local header-probe deadline workaround for the already-fixed large-tree timeout. The target retained that override for recovery but replayed **zero** local overrides. Target dist inspection during repair reported no content mismatches or extra paths.

### Observed sequence

1. Candidate snapshot, Doctor/lint/config/plugin/startup checks passed.
2. The old Gateway was stopped and 11.3 was installed.
3. Post-install Doctor failed. Bounded diagnostic:

```text
SQLite read-only worker SQLite WAL commit publication could not be verified:
$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/openclaw.sqlite
```

   Immediately preceding diagnostics reported two slow `update.run` transactions in the Doctor process: about 1650 ms on the main thread, then about 1653 ms on worker thread 4.
4. Run outcome: `state-migrated-no-rollback`. The protected rollback refusal preserved changed state; the native recovery started the 11.3 Gateway and verified readiness.
5. External official plugins remained on 11.1 until repair.

This is one observed production occurrence, **not a deterministic reproduction**. Read-only diagnostic observers had been used during the original update. A connection/SHM or write-publication interaction is a hypothesis, not an established cause; the second logged transaction could also be failure bookkeeping.

### Recovery evidence

After stopping the Gateway through its existing service owner, with no concurrent OpenClaw CLI/direct SQLite observers:

```sh
OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external openclaw update repair --yes --json
```

Exit 0, final status `warning`; all finalization phases completed:
- Doctor ~229 s
- plugin convergence ~94 s
- final configuration/Doctor convergence ~290 s
- seven official external plugins updated from 11.1 to 11.3
- post-plugin error-level Doctor lint: exit 0, no findings

The same user service was started afterward: authenticated read RPC reports 11.3, `readyz` reports `ready:true`, `coreReady:true`, no failing components; plugin version drift is empty. Existing recovery artifacts were retained. No database restore, manual state edits, lease deletion, or guard bypass was used.

### Expected behavior / investigation request

The updater should finish its own post-install Doctor without losing its stable WAL-publication witness, or safely converge/recover with actionable diagnostics. Please distinguish which witness predicate failed (generation changed, WAL-index header copies differed, or nonempty WAL had no initialized index) without exposing private state.

The installed implementation checks this in `update-doctor-migration-attribution` / `update-physical-database-generations`. The current message does not identify the predicate, so this report does **not** establish database corruption or justify relaxing the consistency guard.

### Scope

This failure occurred after header probing passed. It is separate from the configurable header deadline proposal #197079 and the previously fixed all-path 10-second timeout. No current-main acceptance test or targeted code fix for this WAL failure has been produced.

Private paths, database contents, credentials, recording contents, and internal session identifiers are omitted.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug — prompt assembly / runtime-context injection; user-visible phantom reply + wasted model work.

### Summary

On a long-running Control UI webchat session, a continuation turn (runtime-context injection arriving between plan steps of a live run) received conversation data presenting an **already-answered request from ~10 minutes earlier** as if it were new input. The agent re-fetched the referenced internal system and emitted a second, user-visible answer to a message the user never (re-)sent. The projected transcript contains **no duplicate user record**: between the two terminal assistant messages there are only assistant/tool records, and the next real user message arrived ~80 s later as the genuine next step.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9), stable npm channel, Debian 13 arm64 VM, gateway as `systemd --user` service — process **never restarted** in the window (same MainPID, `NRestarts=0`).
- Control UI webchat, single tab; custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving a reasoning model (assistant records persist `openclawDelivery.textPhaseRequiresTerminal: true`, `responseModel: "keepalive"`).

### What happened (verified in the persisted transcript, UTC)

- 08:11:30 — user question Q lands (single `:user` record). Run R begins; first model call delayed by ~152 s (`slow chat send … stage=startup`); client WS dies at 08:13:19 `code=1006`.
- 08:18:45 — run R emits terminal answer A1 to Q (`stopReason: "stop"`), delivered while the client is disconnected.
- 08:18–08:21 — continuation turns of run R arrive with runtime-context injections. Per that turn's reasoning as persisted in the transcript, one injection's conversation data echoed a ~07:10 request ("check this task …") that had already been answered at 07:24. The turn treated the echo as fresh work: re-fetched the referenced system and emitted a **second terminal message A2 at 08:21:25** ("Re-checked — nothing new since my earlier pass …").
- 08:21:47+ — client reconnects (two more 1006 flaps) and reloads history. The card for Q now renders A2 — content unrelated to Q — as the visible bubble, with the correct A1 collapsed into the tool steps (see #177094, filed the same day from the same install). User-visible symptom: *"you answered twice; the first correct answer was hidden in the tools block, the second isn't related to any question."*

### Expected behavior

Continuation assembly must never treat echoed conversation data as a new request. A turn should start substantive work only from an unconsumed user input (a fresh `idempotencyKey`, or a transcript seq greater than what the run has already answered). Stale `lastUserMessage`-style echoes must be informational and provably inert.

### Proposed fix direction

- Stamp injected conversation echoes with the transcript seq of the message they repeat; runs track `answeredThroughSeq`; suppress new work when an echo's seq ≤ that watermark.
- Refuse to launch work from injection-only turns when the session queue/`pendingInputs` reports nothing unconsumed.
- Also relevant: the ~150 s `chat.send stage=startup` preparation stalls observed on this large session (~300 k tokens) widen the client-offline window during which these phantom artifacts get created and then become visible on reconnect.

### Relation to existing issues

- #177094 — same install, same day: the rendering displacement that subsequently hides the real answer when a stray settle exists in the open card. This issue supplies how the stray settle gets created.
- #143714 — closest sibling (phantom behavior driven by injected context: heartbeat `HEARTBEAT_OK` retry produces a bogus "resend request"); different trigger and artifact.
- #150202 — empty-outbox republish forcing transcript rebuild; #165433 — reconnect-queued `chat.send` envelope rejected: adjacent reconnect-state family.
- #55792 — inverse symptom (catch-up on *missed* messages after restart).

### Notes

Repro is intermittent and correlated with abnormal WS closes (`1006`) during live long runs plus slow startup-stage send preparation. Sketch: start a long multi-step task in webchat; drop the WS abnormally mid-run; while the client is away, the run continues via runtime-context injections; if an injection's conversation echo repeats an already-answered request, the run can answer it a second time, and the stray reply displaces the real one on the next history reload.

issues.body:
## Summary

The active-memory escalation gate only starts the deep-recall sub-agent when `hasRecallIntent(message)` matches. The shipped patterns cover English, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese and Korean, but not German. With the default `mode: "escalate"`, German-speaking users effectively never get deep recall. This includes `memory.search.rememberAcrossConversations` (cross-conversation recall), which goes through the same escalation decision.

Same root cause as #135085 (PT-BR) and #117338 (CJK). Adding a German group would help. Since each language keeps coming up as a separate bug, please consider an extensible or configurable pattern mechanism (see "Suggested fix").

## Where

`extensions/active-memory/escalation.ts` (shipped as `dist/escalation-*.mjs` in 2026.9.4):

- `RECALL_INTENT_PATTERNS`: EN plus one ES group
- `LOCALIZED_RECALL_INTENT_PATTERNS`: zh, ja, ko
- no German group

`resolveRecallEscalationDecision()` returns `no-recall-intent` for German messages, so `extensions/active-memory/index.js` never starts the recall sub-agent.

## Verification (2026.9.4, shipped module)

```js
const m = await import('<openclaw>/dist/escalation-B0r0wGN-.mjs');
const hasRecallIntent = m.t;
hasRecallIntent("Weißt du noch, was wir zu dem Upgrade entschieden haben?");       // false
hasRecallIntent("Erinnerst du dich an das Codewort aus unserem anderen Gespräch?"); // false
hasRecallIntent("Was haben wir gestern über das Backup besprochen?");               // false
hasRecallIntent("Worüber haben wir letzte Woche gesprochen?");                      // false
hasRecallIntent("Wie war das nochmal mit dem Neustart neulich?");                   // false
hasRecallIntent("Hatten wir nicht schon mal entschieden, das Plugin zu sperren?");  // false
hasRecallIntent("Do you remember what we decided about the upgrade?");              // true
```

End-to-end on a personal install (builtin memory, `rememberAcrossConversations: true` for the agent, Active Memory `mode: "escalate"`):

- The German question produced no `active-memory: … start` log line and no recall.
- The same question in English produced `status=ok` and correct cross-conversation recall.

## Impact

Deployments whose users write in German silently get no deep recall and no cross-conversation recall in the default mode. The only workaround is `mode: "always"`. That adds a blocking recall pass of several seconds to every eligible private reply, which is often not acceptable on chat channels.

## Suggested fix

1. Add a German group. Include umlaut and `ae`/`oe`/`ue`/`ss` spellings, and a future-guard like the CJK groups:
   - intent:
     - `\b(?:wei(?:ß|ss)t|erinnerst)\s+du\s+(?:noch|dich)\b`
     - `\bkannst\s+du\s+dich\s+erinnern\b`
     - `\b(?:hatten|haben)\s+(?:wir|du|ich)\b.{0,48}\b(?:besprochen|entschieden|vereinbart|beschlossen|abgemacht|ausgemacht|gesagt|erw(?:ä|ae)hnt|gesprochen)\b`
     - `\b(?:fr(?:ü|ue)heren?|vorherigen?|letzten?|anderen?)\s+(?:gespr(?:ä|ae)ch|unterhaltung|chat)\b`
     - `\b(?:letztes\s+mal|neulich|vorhin|gestern|vorgestern|letzte\s+woche|letzten\s+monat|vor\s+\w+\s+(?:tagen|wochen|monaten))\b`
   - future (do not treat as recall unless also retrospective):
     - `\b(?:morgen|(?:ü|ue)bermorgen|n(?:ä|ae)chste[nrs]?\s+(?:woche|monat|mal)|sp(?:ä|ae)ter|demn(?:ä|ae)chst)\b`
     - `\berinnere?\s+mich\b` (a reminder request, not recall)
   Checked locally (JS, `u` flag) against the six German phrases above plus two future-tense negatives ("Erinnere mich morgen an …", "Lass uns nächste Woche über … sprechen"): 8/8 as expected.
2. Longer term: let operators extend the patterns without a release, for example `plugins.entries.active-memory.config.recallIntentPatterns` (a list of regex strings or locale ids), or a small model-free multilingual classifier. The per-language issues (#117338, #135085, this one) suggest the hard-coded table will keep lagging behind.

## Related (probably a separate issue)

Cross-conversation recall (`rememberAcrossConversations`) only works when the Active Memory recall model runs on the embedded OpenClaw runtime:

- **CLI backends (claude-cli):** `runCliAgent()` does not receive `conversationRecall`. The embedded CLI dispatch forwards it only in the embedded attempt path.
- **Codex harness:** the recall sub-agent's `memory_search` also runs without the authorization.
- **Consequence:** `memory_search` with `corpus: "sessions"` returns "Session transcript search is not enabled". Private transcript recall silently yields nothing when the agent's model runs on claude-cli or Codex.
- **Workaround:** set a model with `agentRuntime.id: "openclaw"` as `plugins.entries.active-memory.config.model`.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (`3a9d69d`), macOS, builtin memory (`memory-core`), OpenAI embeddings
- Active Memory `mode: "escalate"`, `queryMode: "recent"`, `promptStyle: "balanced"`

issues.body:
# Telegram poller never starts after boot while `channels status` reports connected (offset queued, never committed)

**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.10.2 (b8952d4) · Linux (systemd user unit) · single gateway, 10 agents / 9 Telegram accounts

## Summary

After a boot, every Telegram account reports `enabled, configured, running, connected, mode:polling`, but
**no polling occurs at all**: zero `update spooled` lines, zero `isolated polling` lines, zero Telegram
errors, zero new `channel_ingress_events` rows for 8+ minutes, while Telegram's
`pending_update_count` stays frozen (22). `channels.stop` returns `stopped: true` and
`channels.start` returns `status: "handed-off"` — and nothing starts behind it. The `handed-off`
state is not persisted anywhere in the state DB, so there is no row to clear.

A related, earlier presentation of the same fault is a **re-spool storm**: one update id re-spooled
~32,000 times/minute while `offset queued` lines accumulate (~38k) and **not one**
`offset committed/applied/advanced` line appears — i.e. the poller processes and re-polls the same
update forever instead of committing its offset.

## Reproduction (observed twice)

1. Run a gateway with several Telegram accounts until a crash / unclean boot occurs (the crash-loop
   breaker is a reliable precursor).
2. Restart the service, then issue `channels.start` per account. All return `status: "handed-off"`.
3. Observe: `channels status` shows `running, connected, mode:polling` for 9/9 accounts; journal
   contains **no** polling/spool lines; `pending_update_count` does not move; no new ingress rows are
   written.

## Evidence (8 minutes of clean uptime, no errors)

```
state=active  uptime=07:24  health=200  connected=9
spool_lines_since_boot=0
polling_lines_since_boot=0
telegram_errors_since_boot=0
pending = 22 · 22 · 22
last ingress row: 05:36:05 (written by the previous process)
```

Storm variant, 20-minute window:

```
updateId=30739880 occurrences: 112,679
update spooled: 38,391   offset queued: 38,674   offset committed: 0
channel_ingress_events row: event_id=...0739880 status=completed attempts=0
```

## Ruled out

- **Not a duplicate poller**: `terminated by other getUpdates` = 0, no `409 Conflict`.
- **Not a failed insert**: the dedupe row exists and reads `completed`; deleting it causes it to be
  re-created as `completed` within a minute while the loop continues.
- **Not Telegram-side backlog**: draining the queue with `getUpdates?offset=<max+1>` takes
  `pending_update_count` to 0 and the storm continues unchanged.
- **Not disk/DB contention**: WAL checkpoint `0|12|12` in ~10 ms, single writer, `busy_timeout=0`;
  fsync p50 2.5 ms.
- **Not a blocked event loop**: `/health` answers in ~1 ms, `eventLoopDelay p99` 32–54 ms.
- **Not signal handling**: `SigCgt` includes SIGTERM; `SigIgn` is SIGPIPE only.
- **Not persisted handoff state**: `worker_session_placements` all `state='local'`;
  `plugin_state_entries` has no channel/telegram/handoff keys; `update_runs` all terminal.

## Impact

- All Telegram lanes go silent while the status API reports them healthy — the failure is invisible to
  local health checks.
- Messages accumulate unconfirmed at Telegram (22 in the observed incident).
- In the storm variant, ~1.5 CPU cores burn continuously and the process reached a 20 GB RSS peak.

## Suggested direction

The `isolated polling` offset queue needs a commit/ack step with a bounded retry and a visible failure
counter; a queued offset that is never applied should surface as an error state rather than a
per-update re-spool storm. Separately, `channels.start` should not return `handed-off` while leaving no
running poller — either start the worker or return an error. A defensive guard that drops and warns on
N re-spools of the same update id within a minute would bound the damage.

*(Report from a fleet operator; host names, paths and credentials removed.)*

issues.body:
## Summary
`openclaw infer audio transcribe --model <provider/model>` and `openclaw infer video describe --model <provider/model>` do not use the requested provider/model. When `tools.media.models` has an entry for the capability, the flag is ignored and the file is uploaded to that configured entry instead (often a different provider). With no configured entry, audio still swaps the requested model for the provider's transcription default, so `--model openai/whisper-1` uploads with `model=gpt-4o-transcribe`. `docs/cli/infer.md` says "Use `--provider` or `--model provider/model` to pin a specific backend", and `infer image describe --model` already does pin.

## Environment
- Commit: ca5ac6f5b69aa8704b653fade36e2fa59937c7fb (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: `openclaw infer audio transcribe` and `openclaw infer video describe` (local transport), `src/cli/capability-cli/media-understanding-command.ts`

## Steps to reproduce
1. Configure providers `openai`, `deepgram` and `moonshot` with API keys, and set `tools.media.models` to `[{ provider: "deepgram", model: "nova-3", capabilities: ["audio"] }, { provider: "moonshot", model: "kimi-k2.5", capabilities: ["video"] }]`.
2. Run `openclaw infer audio transcribe --file tone.wav --model openai/whisper-1 --json`.
3. Run `openclaw infer video describe --file clip.mp4 --model moonshot/kimi-k2.6 --json`.
4. Remove `tools.media.models` and run step 2 again.

## Expected
Each run uses the provider and model named by `--model`: OpenAI `whisper-1` for steps 2 and 4, Moonshot `kimi-k2.6` for step 3.

## Actual
- Step 2 uploads the audio to Deepgram with `nova-3` and reports `provider: deepgram, model: nova-3`.
- Step 3 runs on Moonshot with `kimi-k2.5` and reports `model: kimi-k2.5`.
- Step 4 uploads to OpenAI with `model=gpt-4o-transcribe` and reports that model.
No warning is printed; the flag is silently dropped.

## Root cause
`src/cli/capability-cli/media-understanding-command.ts:48-49` forwards `--model` only as `activeModel`:

```ts
const activeModel = requireProviderModelOverride(opts.model);
const input = { filePath: path.resolve(file), cfg, agentId, agentDir, activeModel };
```

In the media runner, `activeModel` means "the active chat model" of the reply pipeline. When `resolveModelEntries` (`src/media-understanding/resolve.ts:208`) finds configured `tools.media.models` entries for the capability, `activeModel` is never consulted. When there are none, audio deliberately replaces the chat model id with the provider's transcription default via `resolveAutoProviderModelEntry` (`src/media-understanding/runner.ts:436`), because a chat model id is not a valid STT model. Both behaviors are right for channel replies, but the CLI reuses the field to carry an explicit user override, so the override is lost.

## Sibling surfaces
`infer image describe --model` already pins through `describePreparedImageWithModel` and is unaffected. Audio and video both go through the one command file above.

## Open question for maintainers
Closed PR #172409 fixed this by running the command with a request-local `tools.media.models` narrowed to one entry for the requested provider/model (keeping a matching configured entry's `baseUrl`, `headers` and auth settings). Review flagged one policy question: should `--model` disable the other configured media entries as fallbacks for that one invocation (strict pin, as the docs describe), or keep them as fallbacks the way image describe does?

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: `infer audio transcribe --model` and `infer video describe --model` send the upload to the configured `tools.media.models` entry, or to the provider transcription default, instead of the requested provider/model.
Real environment tested: the real `openclaw` CLI entry (`src/entry.ts`, run from source with node 26.9) at origin/main ca5ac6f5b69, with isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. Config loading, agent and auth resolution, the media-understanding runner, entry selection and the real deepgram, openai and moonshot media providers ran unmodified (moonshot loaded from the tree's `extensions/moonshot` via `plugins.load.paths`). The only replaced seam is the provider HTTP endpoint: every `baseUrl` points at a local HTTP listener that logs the route, the `model` sent and the `x-entry` header. The configured deepgram entry has its own `baseUrl` (`/deepgram-entry/v1`) and header `x-entry: kept`. For the EXPECTED half, the source change from closed PR #172409 was applied to `media-understanding-command.ts` only, the same commands were rerun on identical inputs, and the change was reverted.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts infer <args> --json` with `<args>` = `audio transcribe --file tone.wav --model openai/whisper-1`, `video describe --file clip.mp4 --model moonshot/kimi-k2.6`, `audio transcribe --file tone.wav` (no `--model`, control), and the first command again with `tools.media.models` removed; the listener log was read after each run.
Evidence after fix:
```
# OBSERVED (origin/main ca5ac6f5b69)
$ openclaw infer audio transcribe --file tone.wav --model openai/whisper-1 --json
  "provider": "deepgram",
  "model": "nova-3",
      "text": "reply from deepgram-entry",
[deepgram-entry] POST /deepgram-entry/v1/listen model=nova-3 x-entry=kept
$ openclaw infer video describe --file clip.mp4 --model moonshot/kimi-k2.6 --json
  "provider": "moonshot",
  "model": "kimi-k2.5",
      "text": "reply from moonshot",
[moonshot] POST /moonshot/v1/chat/completions model=kimi-k2.5 x-entry=-
$ openclaw infer audio transcribe --file tone.wav --json
  "provider": "deepgram",
  "model": "nova-3",
      "text": "reply from deepgram-entry",
[deepgram-entry] POST /deepgram-entry/v1/listen model=nova-3 x-entry=kept
# no tools.media.models configured
$ openclaw infer audio transcribe --file tone.wav --model openai/whisper-1 --json
  "provider": "openai",
  "model": "gpt-4o-transcribe",
      "text": "reply from openai",
[openai] POST /openai/v1/audio/transcriptions model=gpt-4o-transcribe x-entry=-

# EXPECTED (same inputs, PR #172409 source change applied locally)
$ openclaw infer audio transcribe --file tone.wav --model openai/whisper-1 --json
  "provider": "openai",
  "model": "whisper-1",
      "text": "reply from openai",
[openai] POST /openai/v1/audio/transcriptions model=whisper-1 x-entry=-
$ openclaw infer video describe --file clip.mp4 --model moonshot/kimi-k2.6 --json
  "provider": "moonshot",
  "model": "kimi-k2.6",
      "text": "reply from moonshot",
[moonshot] POST /moonshot/v1/chat/completions model=kimi-k2.6 x-entry=-
$ openclaw infer audio transcribe --file tone.wav --model deepgram/nova-3 --json
  "provider": "deepgram",
  "model": "nova-3",
      "text": "reply from deepgram-entry",
[deepgram-entry] POST /deepgram-entry/v1/listen model=nova-3 x-entry=kept
$ openclaw infer audio transcribe --file tone.wav --json
  "provider": "deepgram",
  "model": "nova-3",
      "text": "reply from deepgram-entry",
[deepgram-entry] POST /deepgram-entry/v1/listen model=nova-3 x-entry=kept
# no tools.media.models configured
$ openclaw infer audio transcribe --file tone.wav --model openai/whisper-1 --json
  "provider": "openai",
  "model": "whisper-1",
      "text": "reply from openai",
[openai] POST /openai/v1/audio/transcriptions model=whisper-1 x-entry=-
```
Observed result after fix: on main, `--model openai/whisper-1` reaches the configured Deepgram entry with `model=nova-3`, `--model moonshot/kimi-k2.6` runs with `model=kimi-k2.5`, and with no configured entry `--model openai/whisper-1` is sent as `model=gpt-4o-transcribe`; the requested provider/model is never used. With the PR #172409 change, each run reaches the requested provider with the requested model, `--model deepgram/nova-3` still reaches the entry's own base URL with its header, and the no-flag control is unchanged.
What was not tested: no requests to the real OpenAI, Deepgram or Moonshot APIs (a local listener stands in for them); the CLI ran from source, not a built or published package; `infer image describe` was read but not run; fallback behavior when the pinned provider fails was not exercised.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In a Control UI chat on the Claude CLI runtime, the short notes the agent writes before a tool call ("Checking the config before I run the command.") show as normal replies instead of progress. When a turn writes such a note and then ends without a final answer, the note sits at the bottom of the chat and reads as the agent's answer.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a Control UI (dashboard) chat whose model runs on the Claude CLI runtime.
2. Ask for something that makes the agent write one line of text and then call a tool, for example "Say you're checking, then run `pwd`."
3. Reload the chat, or open it in another browser.
4. Look at the pre-tool line, and at the `stopReason` of that message in `chat.history`.

### Expected behavior

The pre-tool line is imported with `stopReason: "toolUse"`, the same value native runs store, and the Control UI shows it as progress/commentary.

### Actual behavior

The line is imported with `stopReason: "tool_use"` (Anthropic's raw value). The Control UI only treats `toolUse` as commentary (`assistantMessageKind` in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-assistant-reply.ts`), so the line renders as a reply.

Cause: `parseClaudeCliHistoryEntry` in `src/gateway/cli-session-history.claude.ts` copies `stop_reason` unchanged. The same function already converts Claude's `tool_use` content blocks to the provider-neutral form, so this looks like a missed case rather than intent.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.6 (latest stable) and main at 8a6d3a04ee7 (code read and unit repro). Observed live on 2026.11.2.

### Operating system

macOS 26.3.1 (arm64)

### Install method

npm global

### Model

claude-opus-5-5

### Provider / routing chain

claude-cli runtime (Anthropic subscription login), Control UI webchat

### Additional provider/model setup details

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO; not provider-setup dependent. Any Claude CLI session imported into chat history is affected. Codex/GPT sessions store `toolUse` and are not affected.

### Logs

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO. No error is logged; the effect is the stored `stopReason` value.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

On a clean main worktree, a new unit test that imports an assistant entry with `stop_reason: "tool_use"` fails (`stopReason` is `tool_use`, expected `toolUse`). Stock `assistantMessageKind` returns `reply` for `tool_use` and `commentary` for `toolUse`. On a live 2026.11.2 install, after normalizing at import, all 137 imported pre-tool notes in one session read `toolUse`; final answers kept `end_turn`/`stop`.

### Impact and severity

Medium for Control UI users on the Claude CLI runtime. Progress notes look like answers, and a silent background turn can leave a progress note as the newest "reply", so users think the agent answered with a non-answer or ignored them.

### Additional information

A PR with the one-line normalization and a regression test follows.

issues.body:
### Summary

Accept `gpt-live-1.1` as a public API GPT-Live model, next to `gpt-live-1`.

### Problem to solve

OpenAI released `gpt-live-1.1` to the API on 2026-11-19 ([changelog](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog), [model page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-live-1.1)). It runs on the same endpoint (`v1/live/sessions`) and, per OpenAI's docs, uses the same events as `gpt-live-1`.

OpenClaw recognizes the public API model only by the exact name `gpt-live-1` (`isOpenAIGptLiveApiModel` in `extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver.ts`). Any other `gpt-live-*` name is handled as a GPT-Live model that is not the public API one:

- the API voice list is not applied (only `marin` and `cedar` are offered),
- the frameless event names and schemas are used instead of the `session.*` ones,
- the public projection drops the model and reports `gatewayRelaySupported: false`.

So Talk over the Gateway relay with an OpenAI API key cannot be moved to `gpt-live-1.1`.

### Proposed solution

Treat `gpt-live-1.1` as a public API model: add it to `OPENAI_GPT_LIVE_MODELS` and have `isOpenAIGptLiveApiModel` accept it, so it gets the same voices, events and Gateway relay as `gpt-live-1`. `gpt-live-1` can stay the default.

### Alternatives considered

Staying on `gpt-live-1`, which works but leaves out the newer model's better transcription and accent consistency.

### Impact

- Affected: anyone using Talk, voice calls or meetings on GPT-Live with an OpenAI API key.
- Severity: blocks moving to the newer model; nothing breaks for people who stay on `gpt-live-1`.
- Frequency: always, for that model name.
- Consequence: the realtime voice stays on `gpt-live-1`.

### Evidence/examples

- OpenAI's API changelog entry of 2026-11-19 and the `gpt-live-1.1` model page linked above.
- Checked in the published packages 2026.10.8, 2026.11.6 and 2026.11.10-beta.1, and on `main`: the model check is the exact match described above.
- Not verified by running: I have not run a `gpt-live-1.1` session through OpenClaw. The behaviour above is from reading the source.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes

issues.body:
## Summary

`group:openclaw` is documented as "all built-in OpenClaw tools (excludes provider plugins)" across multiple docs pages, but is missing the entire `group:fs` (`read`, `write`, `edit`, `apply_patch`) and `group:runtime` (`exec`, `process`) tool sets.

## Impact

- `allow: ["group:openclaw"]` in subagent or HTTP tool policy silently excludes filesystem and execution tools
- `deny: ["group:openclaw"]` leaves `read`, `write`, `exec`, `process` unblocked — the opposite of the documented intent

## Steps to reproduce

```ts
import { TOOL_GROUPS } from "./src/agents/tool-policy-shared.js";
console.log(TOOL_GROUPS["group:openclaw"].includes("read")); // false — should be true
console.log(TOOL_GROUPS["group:openclaw"].includes("exec")); // false — should be true
```

## Fix

Add `read`, `write`, `edit`, `apply_patch`, `exec`, `process` to `group:openclaw`.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Stable 2026.10.8 still keeps every temporary update runtime when an unrelated Node process runs a standalone script with no `package.json` anywhere up to `/`. This is the failure reported in #177706, which was closed because #177407 (`8b78b230`) fixed it on `main`. That commit is not in `v2026.10.8`: comparing `8b78b230...v2026.10.8` returns `diverged`. Stable users who update keep accumulating retained runtimes. On this host, about 2.9 GB of `openclaw-update-runtime-*` directories had to be removed by hand.

In the same update, `update.run` reported `status=skipped`, and the restart sentinel logged `remained pending after retry window` twice. The second warning came after the update had already been installed by a later restart.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On 2026.10.7, npm global on macOS arm64, keep a long-lived unrelated `node /path/to/server.cjs` process running. The script's directory and all its ancestors have no `package.json`.
2. Run `update.run` from the Control UI to 2026.10.8.
3. Read the `infra:temp-artifacts` warnings and `ls /opt/homebrew/lib | grep openclaw-update-runtime`.

### Expected behavior

- Retained runtimes are reclaimed when the only unclassifiable process is unrelated and has a readable cwd and no manifest (the #177407 behavior). This should hold on the stable channel too.
- `update.run` and the restart sentinel should not report `skipped` for an update that a later restart applies. A sentinel that has already been satisfied should not warn again.

### Actual behavior

```
2026-10-28T18:00:33.766Z WARN infra:temp-artifacts Runtime retained at /opt/homebrew/lib/openclaw-update-runtime-Ax1pgx: Could not inspect OpenClaw processes: Error: Could not classify PID 982: could not read package identity
2026-10-28T18:00:33.925Z WARN infra:temp-artifacts Runtime retained at /opt/homebrew/lib/openclaw-update-runtime-DgiIk1: Could not inspect OpenClaw processes: Error: Could not classify PID 982: could not read package identity
2026-10-28T18:00:34.060Z WARN infra:temp-artifacts Runtime retained at /opt/homebrew/lib/openclaw-update-runtime-V0Drj2: Could not inspect OpenClaw processes: Error: Could not classify PID 982: could not read package identity
2026-10-28T18:23:38.848Z INFO gateway update.run completed actor=gateway-client … restartReason=update.run status=skipped
2026-10-28T18:47:45.673Z WARN gateway/restart-sentinel Gateway restart update skipped (npm): update restart sentinel remained pending after retry window {"reason":"managed-service-handoff-started"}
  … second Gateway restart ~19:03Z; update finalize runs; installed version is 2026.10.8 (dc2523e) …
2026-10-28T19:57:32.924Z WARN gateway/restart-sentinel Gateway restart update skipped (npm): update restart sentinel remained pending after retry window
```

PID 982 is a non-OpenClaw `node <home>/…/server.cjs`. Its cwd is readable, and no `package.json` exists from that directory up to `/`.

### Source (v2026.10.8, dc2523e)

- `src/infra/gateway-process-argv.ts`: `classifyOpenClawEntrypointPath` calls `readProcessPackageIdentity(root, true)`. That walks up on `ENOENT` and, at `/`, throws `could not read package identity`. The result is `{ kind: "unclassified", cause: "package-identity" }` instead of `other`.
- `src/infra/openclaw-process-census.ts`: when `classifyProcessArtifactCustody` returns `unresolved`, it throws `Could not classify PID ${pid}`. The outer catch then turns the whole census into an error, so `temp-artifact-cleanup.ts` keeps every runtime.
- `src/gateway/server-restart-sentinel.ts`, `scheduleRestartSentinelWake`: after `CONTROL_PLANE_UPDATE_PENDING_MAX_ATTEMPTS` it logs `remained pending after retry window`. Here the pending owner was a managed-service handoff (`managed-service-handoff-started`) that outlived the window. The run is finalized as skipped even though the handoff later completed.

issues.body:
## Summary

On `openai-completions` (OpenRouter/DeepSeek), the **system prompt section set changes between consecutive requests inside a single session**. A section appearing or disappearing renumbers the sections after it, so the system prompt suffix digest changes on every such turn. That invalidates the provider prompt cache for the whole prefix even when the message history is byte-identical.

The built-in cache diagnostic misreports this: it emits `historyRewrite` ("history must be append-only") while the message history has not changed.

Observed on OpenClaw **2026.11.6 (06afb10)**, Linux, provider `openrouter`, `modelApi: openai-completions`.

## Evidence A - section churn between two requests 5.6s apart

Same session (`agent:...:main`), one model, no model change, no restart between them:

```
ts=2026-11-19T18:46:15.224Z  dropCause=tracked-input-change  requestGapMs=5617
previousCacheRead=150912  cacheRead=142976
changes[0] = system…ffix
  "system prompt suffix digest changed (sections: section[13], section[14],
   section[15], section[16], section[18], section[19], Silent Replies,
   section[17], +1 more)"
```

## Evidence B - same class, earlier, 7.3s apart

```
ts=2026-11-19T18:29:38.374Z  dropCause=tracked-input-change  requestGapMs=7247
previousCacheRead=83968  cacheRead=0
changes: system…ffix (sections included "Tooling, section[13], ...")
       + message-level diff
```

## Evidence C - separate observation: provider served zero on a byte-identical prefix

Six requests where the diagnostic's `changes` array is **empty** - identical prefix, identical messages - and the provider still returned no cached tokens:

```
18:00:56 prevCacheRead=17266   cacheRead=0  gap=30s   cause=provider-cache-reuse-lost:unchanged-prefix
18:05:22 prevCacheRead=32256   cacheRead=0  gap=2s    cause=provider-cache-reuse-lost:unchanged-prefix
18:39:24 prevCacheRead=190976  cacheRead=0  gap=5s
18:40:12 prevCacheRead=46080   cacheRead=0  gap=5s
18:42:26 prevCacheRead=117632  cacheRead=0  gap=9s
18:46:04 prevCacheRead=149632  cacheRead=0  gap=82s
```

Flagged separately because it may be provider-side reuse behaviour rather than the same cause.

## Evidence D - diagnostic tolerates envelope metadata inconsistently

`envelope.other["provenance"]` (stamped on inter-session sends and delivery mirrors) is not in the tracker's tolerated-envelope set, so a provenance-only change is reported as a history rewrite, although it is envelope metadata and is not part of the serialised request bytes. Is that intended? If it is tolerated by design, the comparison should ignore it.

## Impact

Measured on one host over ~86 minutes: **25 cache-read drops**, ~2.4M cache tokens re-read at full input price instead of the cached rate. With the fleet on a cheap model this is cents; on a premium model the same rate is roughly $32 lost per 86 minutes (~$50 at full re-bill).

## Reproduction

1. One `openai-completions` session, no model change, no restart.
2. Log the system-prompt suffix digest and the list of included sections per request.
3. Send two requests a few seconds apart.
4. If the section set differs between them (e.g. a `Silent Replies` block appears or disappears), the provider cache is invalidated for the entire prefix even though message history is append-only.

## Questions

1. Is the system prompt section set intended to be stable for the life of a session? If yes, this is a bug.
2. If it is intentionally dynamic, should the cache diagnostic report section churn separately from `historyRewrite`, so a history rewrite is distinguishable from prompt composition churn?

Related: #58779 (system prompt section caching with static/dynamic boundary, closed) describes the static/dynamic split that would fix this class.

### Summary

All PR `check` workflows fail with `401 Unauthorized` from `oven-sh/setup-bun`. This affects **every open PR** including commits to `main`.

### Evidence

- main CI: [failure at 01:29 UTC](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/22122805052), [failure at 01:18](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/22122564288), success at 01:09 (intermittent)
- All 30+ open PRs show `check=FAILURE` regardless of code changes
- The failure is in the bun setup step, not in the actual `pnpm check` task

### Impact

- Contributors cannot get green CI
- Maintainers must merge with red `check` status (some already doing this)
- New contributors may be confused by failures unrelated to their code

### Suggested fix

- Pin `oven-sh/setup-bun` to a known-good version
- Or switch to `npm install -g bun` as fallback
- Or add a retry step around bun setup

### Workaround

PRs can be validated locally or in clean sandboxes: `pnpm check` passes on clean Ubuntu with Node 20 + pnpm 10.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With `gateway.roles` configured, an isolated `agentTurn` cron job created from a Slack conversation fails at run time, before the agent starts, with `user profile not found: <slack-user-id>`, because the creator's channel identity is looked up as a user-profile ID.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start OpenClaw 2026.9.5 with the Slack channel enabled, `cron.enabled: true`, and any valid `gateway.roles` block (config below).
2. Make a Slack user an owner (`commands.ownerAllowFrom: ["slack:<slack-user-id>"]`) so its turns get the scheduling tool.
3. From that Slack user, in a channel the agent answers, ask the agent to schedule a one-time job that runs as its own agent turn a few minutes from now. The agent creates a job with `payload.kind: "agentTurn"`, `sessionTarget: "isolated"`, `schedule: { kind: "at", ... }` and `delivery: { mode: "announce", channel: "slack", to: "channel:<channel-id>", threadId: "<thread-ts>" }`.
4. Wait for the scheduled time and inspect the job's last run status and diagnostics.

Minimal config (redacted, relevant keys only):

```json5
{
  gateway: {
    roles: {
      default: "limited",
      definitions: {
        admin: { /* ... */ },
        limited: { /* ... */ },
      },
    },
  },
  commands: { ownerAllowFrom: ["slack:<slack-user-id>"] },
  cron: { enabled: true },
}
```

### Expected behavior

The job runs an isolated agent turn and announces its result in the Slack thread. It behaves as on the same setup without `gateway.roles`, where this works. A creator with no user profile, such as a channel sender, should resolve to "no role assignment", so that `resolveOperatorRolePolicyForAssignment` applies `roles.default` (or the denied role) as it already does for a missing assignment.

### Actual behavior

The run fails in setup, about 176 ms after start, before any model call. It is classed as a permanent error, and the one-shot job does not run:

```
cron: job failed: user profile not found: <slack-user-id>
lastDiagnostics.entries[0]: { source: "cron-setup", severity: "error", message: "user profile not found: <slack-user-id>" }
```

Observed:
- The failure occurs whichever role the sender is meant to have. We reproduced it for a sender intended to have the admin role as well as for the default role.
- On the same host, fixed-text (non-agent) cron jobs from the same sender run normally.
- A host with the same OpenClaw version but no `gateway.roles` runs the same agent-turn job normally.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS

### Install method

npm global (Node v24.16.0), run as a systemd service (`openclaw gateway run --bind loopback`)

### Model

fireworks/accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4p1-flash (not reached: the run fails before the agent starts)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> fireworks

### Additional provider/model setup details

Not relevant: the failure is in cron setup, before model selection. Channel: Slack (`@openclaw/slack`, Socket Mode).

### Logs

```shell
# cron run receipt (IDs redacted)
status=error duration_ms=176 error_text="user profile not found: <slack-user-id>"
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Code path (identical in the v2026.9.5 tag and in `main` at a0bf24c0c85842e94eb267925912c87f13a5ab4c; 2026.9.5 dist: `isolated-agent-*.mjs` line 901, `operator-role-policy-*.mjs`):

1. `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prepare.ts:231`: `resolveCreatorSandbox(runtimeCfg, { actor: input.job.createdActor })`. For a job created from a Slack conversation, `createdActor` is `{ type: "human", id: "<slack-user-id>" }`, taken from the creator session in `src/gateway/server-methods/cron.ts` (around line 672).
2. `src/gateway/operator-role-policy.ts`, `resolveCreatorSandbox` (line 142): for a human actor with an `id`, it calls `resolveOperatorRolePolicyForProfile(actor.id, cfg)`. When `gateway.roles` is set, that calls `readOperatorRoleAssignment(profileId)` (line 45).
3. `readOperatorRoleAssignment` calls `getUserProfileRole(profileId)` (`src/state/user-profiles.ts:153`), which calls `requireResolvedUserProfileMetadataById`. That function throws `UserProfileNotFoundError` (`src/state/user-profiles-internal.ts:260`) because the Slack user ID is not a user-profile ID.
4. `resolveOperatorRolePolicyForAssignment` (line 112) already falls back to `roles.default` or the denied role when the assignment is null (line 138), but the throw happens before that code runs.

Suggested fix: in `readOperatorRoleAssignment`, or in `resolveCreatorSandbox` for creator actors, treat an unknown profile ID as "no assignment". That could mean using the non-throwing `selectResolvedUserProfileMetadataById`, or catching `UserProfileNotFoundError`, so the existing `roles.default` and denied-role logic applies. An alternative is to resolve a channel identity to its linked profile first, when one exists. Either way, one unknown creator ID should not fail the whole cron run permanently.

We have not opened a PR.

### Impact and severity

Affected: deployments that set `gateway.roles` and let chat-channel users (Slack, in our case) schedule agent-turn cron jobs.
Severity: blocks the workflow. Scheduled agent turns created from chat never run.
Frequency: every agent-turn job created by a channel sender on a roles-enabled host, in all our attempts.
Consequence: scheduled reminders and follow-ups silently never happen. The user was told the job was scheduled.

### Additional information

Workaround: we leave `gateway.roles` unset on hosts where channel users schedule agent-turn jobs. Last known good and first known bad versions were not tested; 2026.9.5 is the only version we have observed.

Gateway logs show the history is not append-only between requests: previously stored assistant messages come back with **regenerated tool-call ids**.

## Environment

### Actual behavior

Assistant messages are re-sent with new ids in `content[1].id` / `content[2].id`, so the prefix diverges mid-conversation and every subsequent request is a cache miss. Practical effect: ~1–3% cache hit rate instead of ~90%.

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, a non-elevated `openclaw gateway install` cannot register the S4U Scheduled Task, so it falls back to a Startup-folder login item. On such a host, `openclaw gateway status` and `openclaw doctor` misreport the service in two ways:

1. **Wrong service label.** `gateway status` prints `Service: Scheduled Task (registered)`, although no Scheduled Task exists. A few lines further down, the runtime line says `Startup-folder login item installed; …`.
2. **False warning on every run.** `gateway status` always prints `Service definition inspection incomplete: Service definition inspection could not be completed.` `openclaw doctor` shows the same sentence in its "Gateway service definition" box. Nothing is wrong with the installed service: there is simply no Scheduled Task definition to inspect.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Home x64, build 10.0.26200, non-elevated user
- `openclaw@2026.11.5` (e13cf15) from npm, Node 24.19.0
- Current main (98a00f48e455) has the same code paths

## Steps to reproduce

1. From a non-elevated shell, run `openclaw gateway install`. The output reports `Installed Windows login item: …\Startup\OpenClaw Gateway.vbs` and `Startup mode: Per-user desktop (requires interactive logon)`.
2. Run `openclaw gateway status`.
3. Run `openclaw doctor --non-interactive`.

## Actual

```text
Service: Scheduled Task (registered)
…
Service definition inspection incomplete: Service definition inspection could not be completed.
…
Runtime: running (pid <pid>, Startup-folder login item installed; matching gateway process detected for port <port>.)
```

`doctor`:

```text
o  Gateway service definition ------------------------------+
|  - Service definition inspection could not be completed.  |
```

## Expected

- `gateway status` names the login item it actually found (`Startup-folder login item`).
- Neither command reports a definition inspection failure when the service is a login item and no task exists.
- Real inspection failures, such as Task Scheduler being unreadable while no login item is installed, are still reported.

## Cause

- **Label:** the win32 service label is the static `"Scheduled Task"` (`src/daemon/service.ts`), and `isScheduledTaskInstalled` also returns true for a Startup entry (`src/daemon/schtasks-runtime.ts`). `formatServiceLabel` has no fact telling it which mechanism is installed.
- **Warning:**
  - `auditGatewayServiceConfig` calls `auditScheduledTaskDefinition` whenever a service command exists (`src/daemon/service-audit.ts`).
  - On a login-item install, `schtasks /Query /TN <task> /XML` exits non-zero because the task does not exist.
  - The audit therefore throws, and the catch turns that into the generic `definitionDriftError`.
  - This has been the behavior since #151777.

## Not in scope

Update-owned service refresh deliberately rejects the Startup fallback (`UPDATE_NATIVE_AUTHORITY: … startup fallback is unsupported`). Update publication reads the fallback separately, through `readWindowsStartupFallbackRuntimeForUpdate`. This report does not change that.

## Summary

On a Windows installation running 2026.11.5-beta.2, two attempts to update to 2026.11.5-beta.3 failed during validation with `gateway-stop-unverified`. The failure diagnostics report an invalid response while inspecting the Windows Scheduled Task, so the updater could not verify that the Gateway had stopped.

## Steps and observed result

1. Start a managed update from 2026.11.5-beta.2 to 2026.11.5-beta.3 on Windows.
2. Candidate package installation completes; validation remains quiet for several minutes and fails with `gateway-stop-unverified` and a Scheduled Task inspection invalid response.
3. Between attempts, `openclaw gateway status --deep --json` successfully observed the task as registered and running and connected to the Gateway. The connection did not have operator scopes, so this was not a privileged health check.
4. Retry the update: the same validation failure occurs. Automatic triage timed out on the retry.

No package replacement was attempted according to the failure report. The service definition was left unchanged; recovery did not automatically restart the service because a Gateway process still held the state. The installed CLI remained beta.2; the Gateway was accepting connections after the first failure. No beta.3 startup is claimed.

## Expected

The updater should inspect the managed task reliably and complete the update, or provide actionable underlying inspection diagnostics while preserving service safety.

## Environment and evidence limits

Windows, managed Scheduled Task; source version 2026.11.5-beta.2, target 2026.11.5-beta.3. Exact Windows and Node versions and the underlying command response are not yet confirmed. Updater transcript, Gateway log snapshot, and failure diagnostics were saved locally; raw logs are not included pending privacy review. Earlier beta.2 logs contained event-loop stalls and slow SQLite reservations, but their relationship to this failure has not been established.

## Related

- #170956 concerns Windows update/restart reliability and a Scheduled Task access-denied error; an access-denied cause has not been established here.
- #164639 concerns an aborted update leaving the task disabled; that outcome has not been observed here.

This is a possible distinct inspection failure, not a confirmed root cause or confirmed beta.3 regression.

### Bug type

### Beta release blocker

### Summary
The owner reports that switching the sidebar from My sessions to All owners narrows the conversation list to the selected agent, despite the broader owner selection.

### Steps to reproduce
Prior synthetic rendered-menu diagnostic on commit 81ca4f4d712a67c012c7dc0311e0fa37ac576490, not a live installation reproduction:
1. Provide synthetic sessions owned by the current user on agents A and B, and another owner's session on agent A.
2. Select agent A and My sessions: both A and B appear.
3. Switch to All owners without changing agent: only A's two sessions appear.

### Expected behavior
An All owners selection would not silently reduce the agent scope relative to My sessions, or the retained agent scope would be made explicit. This is an expectation about filter semantics, not an established documented contract.

### Actual behavior
The synthetic diagnostic showed the agent B session disappearing on the owner-filter transition. The owner separately reports different sidebar sessions under different selected agents with All owners selected. Live query parameters and reproducibility have not been independently verified.

### OpenClaw version
Gateway status: 2026.11.3; local dist build metadata: 17db2476982fcc05f59e36c16ce60195899e74dd, built 2026-11-13. The exact currently served UI bundle has not been independently verified.

### Operating system
Debian GNU/Linux 13, x64.

### Install method
Git checkout launch; installation history unknown.

### Model
N/A

### Provider / routing chain
N/A

### Logs
No private logs published. Existing logs do not establish the live query parameters.

### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
When the Android chat catalog is cleared, the composer chip replaces the model alias with the raw model id. The selected model does not change.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Install Android `ai.openclaw.app.debug` built from `54b059c478f39289fba83fb361271dd72ccc963f` (versionName `2026.8.2-debug`, versionCode `2026080201`).
2. Connect it to a Gateway that has two configured models with aliases. This run used `lab/alpha` alias Alpha and `lab/beta` alias Beta.
3. Open a loaded chat whose composer chip shows `Beta`.
4. Turn on airplane mode so the app shows Gateway offline.
5. Read the composer chip.

A second observation, from an induced 10 second hold of the `chat.metadata` or `models.list` response after New session: the chip shows `alpha` or `beta` for the whole hold, then returns to `Alpha` or `Beta` when the catalog is published. The induced hold is a transport delay in a disposable proxy. The payload bytes were unchanged. It is a separate setup from the airplane-mode steps.

### Expected behavior
The chip keeps the alias already shown for that selection. With the catalog loaded, the same sessions show `Alpha` and `Beta`, which is `selectedCatalogModel.name`.

### Actual behavior
The chip text changes to the raw id, `beta` while offline and `alpha` or `beta` during the catalog gap. The picker selection and the session model do not change.

`ChatScreen.kt` `selectedModelLabel` uses the catalog name when that entry exists, and otherwise `selected.substringAfterLast('/')`. Clearing the catalog on disconnect, and at a new chat scope before `models.list` returns, makes that fallback visible.

### OpenClaw version
Android `2026.8.2-debug` from `54b059c478f39289fba83fb361271dd72ccc963f`. Gateway CLI `2026.11.1 (4ffdd20)`, Node 24.22.1.

### Operating system
Android 16, API 36, `sdk_gphone64_x86_64` emulator. Gateway on Linux, Node 24.22.1.

### Install method
Local play debug APK. Gateway from the npm global CLI, disposable state directory.

### Model
`lab/beta` (alias Beta). Also observed for `lab/alpha` (alias Alpha).

### Provider / routing chain
Android app to a disposable local Gateway. Models came from a configured `lab` provider. No inference call was made.

### Additional provider/model setup details
`models.mode` merge. Provider `lab`, two text models, aliases Alpha and Beta. Both reported `available`.

### Logs
Airplane-mode observation is the UI change from alias `Beta` to raw `beta` when the app shows Gateway offline. No model-selection RPC is required for that change.

Induced catalog-gap example, `chat.metadata` held 10 seconds: Gateway handler `chat.metadata` 23 ms, 24670 bytes, id `2e0b969b…`. `models.list` was not requested until 10.060 seconds later, id `52419e97…`, 1043 bytes. The chip showed `alpha` until that catalog publish, then `Alpha`.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Observed on the emulator during the #192252 reproduction. Offline frame: header New chat, body Gateway offline, chip `beta`. Induced frame: body Ready when you are, picker only Default model, chip `alpha`, then alias `Alpha` after the catalog returned.

### Impact and severity
Affected: Android chat composer while the catalog is empty.
Severity: annoying. The selected model stays the same. The label is the raw id.
Frequency: every observed disconnect in this run, and for the full duration of each induced catalog gap (3 seconds and 10 seconds, both `chat.metadata` and `models.list`).
Consequence: the chip disagrees with the alias shown in the picker and with the chip text from a moment earlier.

### Additional information
Related to #192252, which is the delayed picker. This report is only the label fallback. The regression baseline is unknown. This was not compared with an older Android build.
