issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With memory-lancedb `autoCapture` on, the `[System]` retry turn that OpenClaw sends after a stranded `message_tool` final is stored as a user memory when the reply it quotes contains a capture trigger.

### Steps to reproduce

1. main at `eef407423d4`, `pnpm build`.
2. Add the qa scenario below (`qa/scenarios/memory/memory-lancedb-system-turn-capture.yaml`). It sets `messages.visibleReplies: message_tool` and enables memory-lancedb with `autoCapture: true`, `autoRecall: false`, mock-provider embeddings (`dimensions: 16`) and `customTriggers: [QA-STRANDED-85714]`.
3. `node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario memory-lancedb-system-turn-capture --concurrency 1 --fast`

The scenario sends `qa stranded final recovery check. Remember the marker QA-STRANDED-85714.` The mock answers without the message tool, the gateway logs `source-reply/private-final` and runs one retry turn, and the retry delivers through `message(action=send)`. The scenario then reads the store with `openclaw ltm query --agent qa`.

### Expected behavior

Only the user's message is stored. Turns OpenClaw writes itself carry the `[System]` prefix from `formatSystemTurnPrompt` (`src/sessions/system-turn-prompt.ts`). They are not something the user said, the same reason capture already drops envelope metadata and injected memory blocks.

### Actual behavior

The scenario fails. `openclaw ltm query --agent qa --filter "text LIKE '[System]%'"` returns:

```
[System] Your previous reply was not delivered because you did not call message(action=send). Your reply text was: "QA-STRANDED-85714：近 7 日營收較前期增加 5.09%，... 我尚未取得該線的回覆。". If the user should see a reply, send it now with message(action=send). If no reply is needed, answer exactly NO_REPLY.
```

The user's own turn is stored too, so capture ran normally. Nothing filters the row on the way back out: `cleanMemorySearchResults` and `findCleanDuplicateMemory` accept it, so with `autoRecall` on it can return as a relevant memory.

The policy check reproduces without a gateway. On main, `shouldCapture(sanitizeForMemoryCapture(text))` is:
- `true` for the stranded-reply retry text when the quoted reply contains "remember" or "always";
- `true` for `sessions_send`'s restart note followed by a dispatched message containing "Remember ...";
- `false` for the restart note alone, since main reworded it and it no longer hits a trigger.

### OpenClaw version

main `eef407423d4`. In 2026.10.10-beta.4 and beta.5, memory-lancedb's `shouldCapture` has no system-turn check either.

### Operating system

macOS 26 (Apple silicon) for the qa run.

### Install method

Source checkout, `pnpm build`, qa-lab suite.

### Model

qa-lab mock-openai.

### Provider / routing chain

qa-lab mock-openai -> qa-channel. Embeddings come from the same mock.

### Additional provider/model setup details

memory-lancedb `embedding: { model: text-embedding-3-small, dimensions: 16 }`, because the mock returns 16-dimensional vectors. Without `dimensions` every capture fails with `No vector column found to match with the query vector dimension: 16`.

### Logs

Gateway stderr shows the `[source-reply/private-final]` warning followed by the retry, and no capture errors.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

<details>
<summary>qa scenario</summary>

The full YAML is in the linked PR, which adds it as the regression check. The parts that matter:

```yaml
gatewayConfigPatch:
  messages:
    visibleReplies: message_tool
  plugins:
    slots:
      memory: memory-lancedb
    entries:
      memory-lancedb:
        enabled: true
        config:
          embedding:
            model: text-embedding-3-small
            dimensions: 16
          autoCapture: true
          autoRecall: false
          captureMaxChars: 4000
          customTriggers:
            - QA-STRANDED-85714
```

Updated 2026-11-03 to match the PR's current scenario: the flow sends a first prompt that is not capturable, waits for the recovered reply, then sends a later turn in the same conversation (`QA-MEMORY-BARRIER ...`) and waits until that turn is stored. Captures for one session run in order, so the retry's capture has settled by then. It then checks that no stored row contains the retry instruction `send it now with message(action=send)`, with or without its `[System]` line. (The first version slept 8 s and looked for rows starting with `[System]`.)

</details>

### Impact and severity

Deployments using `messages.visibleReplies: message_tool` with memory-lancedb `autoCapture` store OpenClaw's own retry instructions as user facts. The stored text includes "send it now with message(action=send)", and recall can feed that back into later turns.

We hit an earlier form of this on 2026.9.6. The restart-recovery note then ended "never claim completion or success", "never" is a default trigger, and after recall agents told users the gateway had restarted when it had not. main has since reworded that note. The stranded-reply retry and `sessions_send` paths still reach capture.

### Additional information

Fix: #189956. It adds the scenario as a regression check in a sturdier form. The first prompt is not capturable, and the store is read only after a later turn in the same conversation has been captured, so a slow capture cannot read as a pass. On main it fails the same way, with the `[System]` row stored.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add progress drafts to WhatsApp, starting with an `edit` action for the bot's own messages.

### Problem to solve

Progress drafts work on Discord, Telegram, Slack, Mattermost, Matrix and Teams. On WhatsApp you only see typing at most, so a long run looks silent until the final answer.

### Proposed solution

Two small PRs, in this order:

1. **`edit` message action for the bot's own messages.** Baileys already supports it. No revoke or delete (#14344), and no handling of inbound user edits.
2. **`streaming.mode: "progress"` for WhatsApp**, on the shared `createChannelProgressDraftCompositor`, `createFinalizableDraftLifecycle` and `createLivePreviewLifecycle`. Opt-in, off by default. Same rows as Telegram and Discord.

WhatsApp-specific behaviour for PR 2:

- WhatsApp allows edits for about 15 minutes. At 12 minutes the draft stops editing and continues in a new message.
- At most one edit per 5 seconds, on state change only.
- The final answer is always a normal new message, so a failed edit cannot lose it.
- The typing indicator stays off while a draft is showing, because the draft already shows the run is active.
- Nothing in the shared code handles a maximum message age today. It can start in the WhatsApp draft stream, or move to shared code if you prefer.

### Alternatives considered

A third-party plugin works, but it has to reach into the WhatsApp socket because the channel has no edit action.

### Impact

Anyone running long tasks over WhatsApp gets the same progress view as on the other channels. Nothing changes unless progress mode is turned on.

### Evidence/examples

I tested the idea as a third-party plugin on a live account. The status message updates in place and the final answer arrives as a new message.

Not tested yet: what an edit past 15 minutes does. The draft avoids that case by design.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

### Additional information

Known risks:

- I found no reports of bans tied to edits, and no documented rate limit. The throttle is a cautious choice, not a proven safe value.
- Baileys resolves before the server accepts an edit, so a rejected edit can be silent. The action reports `submitted: true, confirmed: false` for this reason.
- Each edited message shows WhatsApp's "edited" label.

Question: is this split acceptable, and should the 12-minute rollover stay in the WhatsApp draft stream or move to shared code?

Related: #70813 (edit plus unsend, closed), #107741 (closed), #80612 (WhatsApp status reactions, merged).

issues.body:
## Summary
On Telegram, auto-delivered final replies (direct-chat agent finals) and native command replies (e.g. `/model`) are sent without the `telegram/send` "telegram outbound send ok … messageId=…" INFO line. `message` tool sends and cron direct-delivery do log that line.

## Impact
Operators and agents use that log line to confirm delivery. When it's missing, a delivered reply looks lost. That leads to false "message lost" diagnoses and duplicate resends. It happened to us after a gateway restart: the final had been delivered, but because there was no log line we assumed it was lost, and Michael got the answer twice.

## Evidence (2026.10.9, Telegram, streaming=partial, cli backend)
- A DM final at 23:31 UTC has no send line, but the user replied confirming its content.
- The Telegram message ids between the user's inbound ids (bot messages in the same private-chat id space) match the finals and `/model` replies, and none of those ids appear anywhere in the log.
- The session transcript has a `channel-final` delivery-mirror for the `/model` reply, but the log has no matching send line.

## Ask
Log the same `outbound send ok` line, with `messageId` and `operation`, for the final and preview-finalise delivery path and for native command replies. A sessionKey or runId on the line would make delivery auditable.

issues.body:
## Observed

After a Gateway container restart (OpenClaw 2026.10.7, Docker, Linux x64), the gateway log repeatedly shows:

```
[agents/subagent-registry] sessions.delete failed during collector group sweep; keeping group
runId=swarm_... groupId=swarm:agent:main:discord:channel:...
error="Agent main has not completed startup inspection and preparation. Inspection ..."
```

Timestamp was ~1 h after container start; the sweep attempt ran while the agent had not finished startup DB inspection, so the cleanup could not complete and the group was kept (cleanup presumably retried/lingered).

## Expected

Collector group sweep (startup cleanup of stale collector groups) should either wait for/trigger on agent-ready, or retry with backoff until the agent completed startup inspection, instead of failing with this error.

## What went wrong

Speech integrations cannot reliably distinguish an HTTP provider rejection from a transient failure using TTS results alone. The shared HTTP helper supplies status, provider error code and Retry-After metadata, but failed TTS attempts retain only coarse `provider_error`/`timeout` classification and formatted text.

## Expected behavior

Keep optional structured failure fields on the existing TTS attempt result. Do not change provider selection, fallback or retry policy, and do not copy response bodies or headers.

## Reproduction / source evidence

On main `3f2791e7b620d5023877090e56e265df3f3cfa47`, return a `ProviderHttpError` with HTTP 429, code `quota_exceeded` and Retry-After from a registered speech provider, then call `synthesizeSpeech`, `textToSpeechStream` or `textToSpeechTelephony`. The shared `executeTtsProviderAttempts` catch returns a failed attempt without those structured fields, although the existing error text is preserved.

This is source-level confirmation; no real provider failure was induced. A focused regression is being submitted for CI and initial review. Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/57954

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior / recovery UX bug (Goal state remains paused; no crash or data loss established)

### Summary
In a built-in local session with an existing Goal paused after a terminal run error, work on the objective continued through same-session scheduled/delegated turns. The operator tried **Resume** in the Control UI. The UI showed an unconfirmed Goal update and told the operator to retry the same request. During this Resume recovery episode the Gateway returned quick `Goal is being admitted; retry the same request.` responses; an overlapping long attempt eventually returned `This session still has active or queued work. Wait for it to finish, then retry the Goal.`. A subsequent Goal read still reported `paused` with the original Goal ID. Repeated ongoing work in the same session makes the operator's requested Goal continuation hard to admit, even though work on that objective is visibly occurring.

### Observed sequence (one live incident; not an isolated reproduction)
1. A pre-existing built-in OpenClaw Goal became `paused` after a terminal model/tool request error. Its objective, ID and progress remained intact.
2. The same conversation continued handling user messages, a periodic agent-turn watchdog, and a delegated worker for that unfinished objective. These are not evidence that the Goal became active again.
3. The operator used the Control UI **Resume** control during this activity. A screenshot showed: `Goal update not confirmed. Check its outcome before making another change. Goal is being admitted; retry the same request.`
4. Sanitized Gateway responses on 2026-10-30, local UTC+04:

```text
22:35:52 sessions.goal.update 56ms UNAVAILABLE: Goal is being admitted; retry the same request.
22:36:07 sessions.goal.update 45ms UNAVAILABLE: Goal is being admitted; retry the same request.
22:36:08 sessions.goal.update 46ms UNAVAILABLE: Goal is being admitted; retry the same request.
22:37:33 sessions.goal.update 133456ms UNAVAILABLE: This session still has active or queued work. Wait for it to finish, then retry the Goal.
```

5. A read-only Goal check after these attempts still showed the same Goal as `paused`. No committed Resume or accepted continuation was verified. The session's separate scheduled/delegated work continued. The reporter did not verify a later successful idle Resume.

### Expected behavior
A paused Goal should have an actionable, unambiguous recovery path that preserves the Goal and the currently running work. If Resume cannot be admitted while another turn is active, the UI should distinguish an in-flight same-operation retry from a definitive busy refusal, reconcile the saved operation, and tell the operator when/how to safely resume. Alternatively, a single idempotent Resume could be admitted behind current work under the existing session authority and start only once it settles. Do not interrupt existing work, create duplicate Goal turns, or blindly clear recovery on an outcome that could have committed.

### Actual impact and limits
- The Goal stayed `paused` while independent same-session work on the objective ran. The user could not use the Goal's automatic-continuation semantics and received a confusing unconfirmed state followed by a busy refusal.
- Only one live incident is established. This does **not** prove a permanent Gateway deadlock, that the Control UI still retained its recovery record after the final busy response, or that a retry during a genuinely idle interval would fail. No isolated reproduction or patch is included.
- This is distinct from the closed #174656: that issue concerned UI classification of an immediate typed `goal-session-busy` refusal and was closed by #174683. Here the observed sequence began with the distinct `Goal is being admitted` response, included a long overlapping admission, and left the operator without a successful Resume while same-session work continued. Please link/merge if maintainers determine it is the same remaining edge case.

### Environment
- OpenClaw `2026.10.7 (44dd89b)`, built-in local runtime, Control UI and Gateway RPC `sessions.goal.update`.
- Linux x64 Gateway host; Node `v24.22.1`. Browser version was not captured.
- Model/provider are not material to these observed Resume RPC errors; the prior terminal run error only supplied the paused Goal precondition.
- Screenshot and raw logs are not attached because the session contains private material. The excerpt above omits identifiers, hostnames, account names and conversation content.

### Regression coverage suggested
Exercise an existing paused Goal with same-session queued/active work; exercise the in-flight `UNAVAILABLE: Goal is being admitted` response and the definite busy response during an overlapping Resume recovery episode. Assert that the UI never creates duplicate Goal turns, does not leave an ambiguous recovery fence for a definite non-admission, and offers an actionable path to activate the original Goal once the session is idle. Keep genuinely unknown transport/ACK outcomes recoverable by the original operation ID.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary

On Linux/Docker (2026.10.8, single Gateway) the SQLite snapshot reclaimer logs `Skipped SQLite snapshot reclamation: Unrecognized snapshot artifact` on every maintenance tick and has never reclaimed a single artifact. First observed 2026-10-28, still firing now: **572 occurrences, 304 in the last 24 h, ~14/hour**. It keeps firing even when the only files present are the live database and its own sidecar files — there are no snapshot artifacts left to misidentify.

### Environment

- version 2026.10.8, Docker, Linux (Synology NAS)
- state directory contents at time of report:
```
157,724,672  openclaw.sqlite
 10,431,872  openclaw.sqlite-wal
     32,768  openclaw.sqlite-shm
     20,480  openclaw-quarantine.sqlite
        219  openclaw.sqlite.cron-authority.lock
          0  *.bak
```

### Evidence

Every skip carries an **empty structured payload** — no artifact name, no path, no reason:

```json
{"0":"{\"subsystem\":\"infra/sqlite-snapshot\"}","1":{},"2":"Skipped SQLite snapshot reclamation: Unrecognized snapshot artifact"}
```

Before manual cleanup, two doctor-created snapshots had sat unreclaimed for roughly two weeks:

```
openclaw.sqlite                          151M
openclaw.sqlite.doctor-cron-...4eaa.bak  107M   (Oct 16)
openclaw.sqlite.doctor-cron-...4fa7.bak  101M   (Oct 13)
openclaw.sqlite-wal                       10M
```

After archiving and removing both `.bak` files by hand, the warning rate did not change. That rules out "an unknown file is present" as the trigger: the matcher appears to reject the live set it is supposed to recognise.

### Expected

- The reclaimer recognises its own artifacts — including the live database and the sidecar files it must not touch — and reclaims genuinely stale snapshots without operator intervention.
- When a skip occurs, the structured payload names the rejected artifact and the reason. An empty object makes the message undiagnosable from logs.

### Impact

- Silent, unbounded growth of orphaned snapshots: 217 MB accumulated here on the same volume as the session database.
- ~14 WARN/hour of indistinguishable noise. In the same window the log also holds 1,905 `slow SQLite` WARN lines, so real failures are effectively invisible.

### Related

#188586 (main-thread session-sqlite maintenance/reclamation commits blocking the event loop).

issues.body:
### Summary

Let the Control UI image viewer step through all images in the chat and show a thumbnail strip for jumping between them.

### Problem to solve

Opening an image fullscreen in Control UI chat shows only that image with zoom (− / 100% / +), Download image, and close. Previous/next controls and the position counter (#151981, #152027) only appear when the opened message itself has several images. When the images are spread across messages (the common case: one screenshot per message), there is no way to move to the next or previous image without closing the viewer, scrolling, and opening the next one. With several images there is also no overview or way to jump directly to a specific one.

### Proposed solution

Use the Telegram desktop media viewer as the reference UX (screenshot below):

- Previous/next arrow buttons on the left and right edges that step through the images in the current chat (session), not only within one message. Left/Right arrow keys do the same.
- When there are several images, a caption such as "Photo 4 of 5".
- A small strip of thumbnails at the bottom, with the current image highlighted; clicking a thumbnail jumps to it.
- Existing zoom, download, close, swipe, and focus-return behavior stays as is.

### Alternatives considered

Keeping navigation scoped to a single message (current behavior) doesn't help when each image arrives in its own message. Grouping consecutive images into one row (#153222) reduces scrolling in the transcript, but the fullscreen viewer still can't move between messages.

### Impact

Affected: Control UI users reviewing several screenshots or generated images in a chat
Severity: Annoying (repeated close/scroll/open)
Frequency: Every time images are compared across messages
Consequence: Extra steps and lost context when going through a set of images

### Evidence/examples

Reference: Telegram desktop media viewer, with side arrows, a "Photo 4 of 5" caption, and a thumbnail strip at the bottom (personal details blurred):

![Telegram media viewer as reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw-pr-proofs/5f409f7a002b4712bf61c901a08b9d139f666381/2026-10-30/control-ui-lightbox-telegram-reference-viewer.png)

issues.body:
## Environment

- Windows Server 2022, 4 vCPU / 8 GB RAM, virtual disk (~4 MB/s write)
- OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (dc2523e), npm-global install, Gateway under a Windows Scheduled Task
- Node 26.12.1, 10 configured agents, SQLite WAL mode
- Single-user deployment, no control UI in use

## Summary

One agent has a session window stuck in `status = running` that has had no activity for ~25 days. It still holds 13,290 rows in `session_transcript_active_events` (13,454 events in `transcript_events`, 93.3 MB plaintext / 29.6 MB zstd, largest single event 10.75 MB).

The same `session_key` has five windows stacked under it, and the retired ones are not consistently marked ended:

| session | status | last update | active rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `59d82361-...` (current) | done | 2026-10-30 19:58 | 2,355 |
| `119e8cfa-...` (orphan) | **running** | 2026-10-05 04:04 | **13,290** |
| `967b2361-...` | null | 2026-09-26 01:22 | 0 |
| `17ae482e-...` | done | 2026-09-07 02:59 | 0 |
| `373f4ff5-...` | null | 2026-09-06 02:59 | 0 |

This looks like a `/reset` or session-rebuild path that creates a new window without ending the old one.

## Why it matters (measured)

Maintenance work runs on the Gateway main thread (`isMainThread: true`) and gets expensive on this agent's database:

```
cron-cleanup              n=33   median 10.06 s   max 90.2 s   total 457 s
session.maintenance.plan  n=148  median  0.72 s   max 66.9 s
compact                   n=1                    max 55.7 s
```

During those stalls, unrelated lanes wait - which matches user-visible `sessions_send gateway timeout` and multi-minute queueing on a different chat with the same agent. **I have not run an A/B (same copy, orphan rows removed), so I am not claiming the orphan window is the sole cause**; the correlation is what I can show. On an isolated copy the same cleanup operation took ~8 s versus ~2.7 s live, so cost does scale with database content.

Additional data point: the agent database also reports 453 missing canonical transcript archive copies, so per-event canonical validation may be part of the cost.

## What I tried (all read-only, 2026.10.8)

- `openclaw sessions archive <session_key>` - resolves the key to the **current** session and sends `sessions.patch { key, expectedSessionId, archived: true }`. It cannot address the orphan window.
- `openclaw sessions delete <session_key>` - same key-level resolution; removes the current session and its live state, not the orphan.
- `openclaw sessions cleanup --dry-run` - reports 152 store entries, all `keep`; the orphan window does not appear in that inventory at all (0 occurrences).
- `sessions.storage.run` RPC - invoked with `{}`; triggers generic maintenance, no way to target a `session_id`.
- Lowering `session.maintenance.maxDiskBytes` to 600-800 MB on a copy: `archived=0, pruned=0, capped=0`, all entries still `keep`.

So there appears to be **no supported entry point** that can transition a stale non-current window from `running` to `ended`/archived, and cleanup does not consider it.

## Reproduction shape

1. Long-lived deployment, one chat with a large active transcript.
2. Force a session reset/rebuild for that chat so a new window becomes the current one.
3. Use the agent normally for weeks.
4. Observe: old window stays `running` with its full active transcript retained; `sessions cleanup` never revisits it; no CLI/RPC command accepts the orphan `session_id`.

## Ask

1. A supported way to end/archive a specific historical window (`session_id`), not just the key's current session.
2. Cleanup should consider windows that are `running` but have no activity for N days, or windows superseded by a newer window on the same key.
3. If (1) is not intended, a documented, safe procedure for operators, or a clear statement that only a manual DB edit can fix it.

## Related

- #160719 sessions.delete silently keeps a run
- #160744 session controller / stuck-session watchdog
- #167602 restart recovery tombstones the orphan
- #161719 gateway restart tombstones a whole main session

Happy to provide additional measurements (query timings, dbstat, per-window payload sizes) or to run an isolated A/B if a maintainer wants a specific command exercised.

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a Gateway whose shared state is in PostgreSQL, request paths that load plugins synchronously fail with `Cannot open PostgreSQL connection: PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker`. Talk never leaves "Talk catalog is warming" in the Control UI, `talk.config` fails, and the same error appears for cron provider-auth preparation at startup. 2026.11.3 (`636454ee16a`) does not do this; 2026.11.5 (`475fccddc2a`) and current `main` (`b23642c2330`) do.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Disposable PostgreSQL 17 with `vector` and `unaccent`; isolated `HOME` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.
2. Config: `database.families.{state,agent,workboard}.engine = "postgres"`, `database.postgres.connection` = env SecretRef to a Unix-socket DSN, unique `schemaPrefix`.
3. `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --auth-choice apiKey --token-provider anthropic --anthropic-api-key <synthetic>`.
4. `openclaw gateway run --port 18977 --token <t>`.
5. `openclaw gateway call talk.catalog --json` (twice).

### Expected behavior

`talk.catalog` warms and returns the catalog, as on 2026.11.3. Gateway logs show no main-thread PostgreSQL refusals.

### Actual behavior

Every `talk.catalog` call returns `UNAVAILABLE: Talk catalog is warming; retry shortly`, and each refresh logs `talk.catalog refresh failed ... phases={"realtimeConfig":…,"speech":…}`. Gateway startup also hits the guard in `describeCronInferenceMigration` → `resolveProviderPreferredProfileId`.

The guard fires from the same frame in every case (stack captured with a diagnostic print at the guard; abridged):

```
assertEngineStoreExecutionAllowed
new PostgresSyncConnection
openExistingStatePostgresConnection
withExistingOpenClawStateDatabaseReadOnly
readDeferredPluginMigrations
readPluginStateMigrationReadiness            <- sync fallback in the loader
loadOpenClawPluginsSteps
loadOpenClawPlugins
resolveRuntimePluginRegistry
loadCapabilityProviderEntries / resolveProviderRuntimePluginLookup
listSpeechProviders (talk.catalog) / resolveProviderPreferredProfileId (cron startup)
```

Cause: `selectReadiness()` in `src/plugins/plugin-state-migration-readiness.ts` caches settled readiness only under the deferred-migration receipt. #197510 (`2c4413a6abb`) changed `readDeferredPluginMigrationReceipt()` in `src/infra/deferred-plugin-migrations.ts` from `getOrLoadSqliteDatabaseAdmissionForPath(…, () => ({}))` to `peekSqliteDatabaseAdmissionForPath(…)`. That removed the filesystem lookup, but the receipt is now absent until a migration write publishes one, which a normal Gateway run never does. The worker's async readiness read at startup is therefore never cached, and every later synchronous plugin load (`pending ??= readPluginStateMigrationReadiness(...)` in `src/plugins/loader-runtime-core.ts`) reads the ledger again on the Gateway thread. SQLite accepts that read; PostgreSQL refuses it.

A diagnostic print in `selectReadiness` shows `receipt=true, hit=true` for the synchronous loads on 2026.11.3, and `receipt=false, hit=false` followed by the guard on 2026.11.5/main.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5 (`475fccddc2a`); also current `main` `b23642c2330`

### Operating system

macOS 27.2.1

### Install method

git checkout (pnpm build)

### Model

anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 (not involved; fails before any model call)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> anthropic (not involved)

### Logs

Production Gateway (all three families on PostgreSQL), since the 2026.11.5 update on 2026-11-18:

```
[gateway] talk.catalog refresh failed elapsedMs=6 phases={"realtimeConfig":5} waiting=…
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ talk.config 23ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Error: Cannot open PostgreSQL connection: PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker; only synchronous admission, migrations, and CLI one-shots may run on the main thread; verify database.postgres.connection and server availability.
```

1,178 `talk.catalog refresh failed` lines and 239 failed `talk.config` responses in about 16 hours, none before the update. The same error also appears on that Gateway for `sessions.create`, `chat.metadata` ("prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for main"), cron script automations, and `[reload] gateway restart preflight failed`. Those were not reproduced in the disposable setup above, so their exact stack is unconfirmed.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: Gateways with the state family on PostgreSQL.
- Severity: Talk unusable in the Control UI/native apps; other synchronous plugin-loading request paths fail intermittently.
- Frequency: always, from Gateway start.

### Additional information

Related but separate: #196174 (config hot reload fails through the synchronous installed-plugin index read), #201058 / #201063 (secrets preparation), #201876 (plugin tools on agent turns). #201063 and #201876 fix their own callers by moving them to the async loader. The readiness cache gap described here affects every synchronous loader caller.

prs.title: fix(state): keep shared workers serving until active leases release
prs.body:
## Summary

When a caller reuses a shared-state worker entry and then fails its own admission check, the owner retires the shared entry even though other callers still hold live leases on it. This change defers that retirement until the last lease is released. Canonical `close()` still retires straight away, and it now tells the retained leases first so they stop before the client closes.

## What Problem This Solves

`open()` in `src/state/openclaw-state-worker-owner.ts` can return an existing shared entry that other callers are using through `retainOperation` (`activeOperations > 0`). A long-lived example is the cron scheduler's lease. If the reusing caller's own `admission.assertCurrent()` (or binding) then fails, `retireAfterFailure` calls `retire(entry)`. That removes the shared entry from `stores` and closes it while the other leases are still in use. The results:

- The live leases are closed under their holders, or lose their owner.
- Every later `open()` on that database finds a retiring entry whose actor is still in use and throws `Shared-state worker is retiring while its actor is in use; close its leases first`. This lasts until the stranded leases release, which for a long-lived lease can be the life of the process.

On a multi-agent Gateway this shows up as follows: `secrets.reload` hangs until the client times out, background state readers (device-pair notify poll, session upstream links) fail on every tick, and Gateway shutdown waits on the hung request. In the run below it was still pending 45 seconds after SIGTERM.

Canonical `close()` had the opposite gap. It closed the client without notifying the retained leases' `nativeLostListeners`, so a retained lease could keep running against a closed worker.

The fix:

- `retire(entry, closeLeases = false)`: when leases are not being closed, the entry is still in use (`activeOperations !== 0`) and it is not already retiring, the entry is added to `retireWhenReleased` and the call returns. The caller that failed admission still gets its own error.
- The final lease release retires a deferred entry.
- `close()` passes `closeLeases = true`, which notifies `nativeLostListeners` before closing.

## Evidence

### Real Gateway, before and after

There are two disposable local Gateways, both built with `pnpm build` and run through the shipped CLI (`node openclaw.mjs gateway run`). Each uses its own state root, a config file outside the state directory, and a unique port, with `gateway.port` rewritten before any client call. Both use plain SQLite state and need no model.

- BEFORE: `OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (18c6b79)`, plain `main` at 18c6b79f44789439fabea7d98fcb822fb3eebcaa.
- AFTER: `OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (10eff8c)`, this branch.

**Trigger (instrumented, to be clear):** I could not find a request flow on `main` that makes a reusing caller's admission fail on demand. The window is a few microtasks between joining the shared open and re-checking admission. Both throwaway builds therefore carry the same temporary hook, which is not part of this PR. When a flag file exists, the next caller that reuses an entry with `activeOperations > 0` fails its own `admission.assertCurrent()` once with the real `StateDatabaseReadAdmissionInvalidatedError("OpenClaw state database read admission changed")`. The flag file is then deleted. The hook only creates the precondition. The live lease is the real cron scheduler lease (`activeOperations=1`), and everything that follows is unmodified Gateway behavior seen through ordinary CLI requests.

<details><summary>Temporary hook applied identically to both throwaway builds (not in this PR)</summary>

```diff
       const store = await (ownsOpening ? entry.opening : wait(entry.opening));
       try {
+        // TEMPORARY PROOF HOOK - throwaway build only, never part of the PR.
+        const proofFlag = process.env.OPENCLAW_PROOF_FAIL_REUSED_ADMISSION_FILE;
+        if (proofFlag && !ownsOpening && entry.activeOperations > 0 && proofExistsSync(proofFlag)) {
+          proofRmSync(proofFlag, { force: true });
+          log.warn("PROOF HOOK: failing one reusing caller's admission", {
+            path: admission.databasePath,
+            activeOperations: entry.activeOperations,
+          });
+          throw new ProofAdmissionError("OpenClaw state database read admission changed");
+        }
         admission.assertCurrent();
```

</details>

Sequence on each Gateway: `secrets reload` as a baseline, then arm the flag, then `secrets reload` (the hook fires inside this request), then `gateway call exec.approvals.get`, `secrets reload`, `cron status`, and SIGTERM.

**BEFORE (18c6b79):**

```text
$ node openclaw.mjs --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (18c6b79)

### baseline
[21:49:31] $ openclaw secrets reload
Secrets reloaded.

### arm the flag
[21:49:33] $ openclaw secrets reload
OpenClaw took too long to respond.
(hook fired: flag consumed)

### afterwards (flag already consumed)
[21:50:05] $ openclaw secrets reload
OpenClaw took too long to respond.

### SIGTERM the Gateway
Gateway still running 45s after SIGTERM:
[gateway] shutdown pending: count=1 shutdown.received-connection-work=45007ms
(SIGKILLed)
```

Gateway log:

```text
21:49:32.483 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 102ms
21:49:34.090 [state/worker] PROOF HOOK: failing one reusing caller's admission path=<state>/state/openclaw.sqlite activeOperations=1
21:49:35.681 [plugins] device-pair: notify poll failed: Failed to open the plugin state database. | Shared-state worker is retiring while its actor is in use; close its leases first
21:49:40.817 [sessions/upstream-links] failed to list watched session upstream links: Error: Shared-state worker is retiring while its actor is in use; close its leases first
21:50:04.079 [ws] → close code=1005 durationMs=29997 lastFrameMethod=secrets.reload
21:50:35.674 [ws] → close code=1005 durationMs=30000 lastFrameMethod=secrets.reload
21:50:35.702 [plugins] device-pair: notify poll failed: ... Shared-state worker is retiring while its actor is in use; close its leases first
```

The retiring error was logged 10 times in about 60 seconds and never cleared. In an earlier exploratory run on the same build, a direct request returned the error to the client:

```text
$ openclaw gateway call exec.approvals.get --params '{}'
Gateway call failed: Error: Shared-state worker is retiring while its actor is in use; close its leases first
```

**AFTER (10eff8c):**

```text
$ node openclaw.mjs --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (10eff8c)

### baseline
[21:51:47] $ openclaw secrets reload
Secrets reloaded.

### arm the flag
[21:51:48] $ openclaw secrets reload
Could not reload secrets because the Gateway did not respond: secrets.reload failed.
(hook fired: flag consumed)

### afterwards (flag already consumed)
[21:51:50] $ openclaw secrets reload
Secrets reloaded.
[21:51:51] $ openclaw gateway call exec.approvals.get --params {}
{ ... "askFallback": "deny", "autoAllowSkills": false } }
[21:51:52] $ openclaw cron status
"jobs": 2

### SIGTERM the Gateway
Gateway exited cleanly after SIGTERM
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 532ms
```

Gateway log:

```text
21:51:47.885 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 94ms
21:51:49.445 [state/worker] PROOF HOOK: failing one reusing caller's admission path=<state>/state/openclaw.sqlite activeOperations=1
21:51:49.448 [gateway] secrets.reload failed: OpenClaw state database read admission changed
21:51:49.448 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ secrets.reload 7ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE
21:51:51.108 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 93ms
```

After the fix, only the caller whose admission failed sees an error, and it gets that error straight away. The cron lease keeps serving, the next `secrets.reload` succeeds, the retiring error never appears (0 occurrences), and shutdown completes.

### Tests: red, then green

I added the two tests in `src/state/openclaw-state-worker-lease.test.ts` first, without the fix:

```text
× keeps concurrent leases serving after a reused entry loses only its caller's admission
  Error: Shared-state worker is retiring while its actor is in use; close its leases first
× retires retained leases before closing their shared worker and permits a fresh open
  AssertionError: promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting
Tests  2 failed | 9 passed (11)
```

With the fix:

```text
$ pnpm exec vitest run src/state/openclaw-state-worker*.test.ts
Test Files  4 passed (4)
     Tests  76 passed (76)

$ pnpm exec vitest run src/infra/sqlite-worker-shared-state.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-shared-state-idle.test.ts \
    src/infra/sqlite-worker-terminal-admission.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-existing-schema.test.ts \
    src/infra/device-pairing-worker.test.ts src/infra/restart-intent.test.ts \
    src/infra/telemetry-store.worker.test.ts src/transcripts/store.test.ts
Test Files  8 passed (8)
     Tests  120 passed (120)
```

### Checks

- `pnpm tsgo:core`: pass
- `pnpm check:test-types`: pass
- `oxlint` on the changed files: pass
- Test-lines ratchet: `Test lines OK. Net test lines: +68; allowance: 400; allocation credit: 68.`

## Scope

- `src/state/openclaw-state-worker-owner.ts`: deferred retirement (`retireWhenReleased`), retirement on the final release, and lease notification in canonical `close()`.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-worker-lease.test.ts`: two regression tests.
- `config/test-lines-allocations/shared-worker-lease-retirement.txt`: test-lines allocation for those tests.

No other callers, contracts or worker code change. This is separate from #197468. That PR stops a worker-level native open refusal from retiring a SQLite Worker. This one stops the host-side owner from retiring a shared entry under live leases after one reusing caller's admission fails.

## Risk

Low and contained to the shared-state worker owner.

- A retirement that is deferred because of a failed reuse now waits for the last lease to release. The failing caller still gets its own error right away. A worker that has actually become unavailable keeps the existing path, which retires the actor on the final release when the native store is no longer available.
- Canonical `close()` behaves as before, except that retained leases are told before the client closes. Lease holders already handle that signal, which is the same `nativeLostListeners` path that native loss uses.
- An entry in `retireWhenReleased` stays in `stores` until it is released, so later compatible opens keep reusing the healthy worker instead of being refused.

prs.title: fix: list ChatGPT models with a Codex client version
prs.body:
Related: #201130, #201493

## What Problem This Solves

ChatGPT subscription model discovery sends OpenClaw's calendar version to a Codex-maintained API. The backend's client-version gates therefore receive a version from the wrong release stream.

## User Impact

Subscription discovery reports a stable Codex client version independently of OpenClaw releases. The first discovery after cache expiry can wait up to five seconds for npm; a registry failure still allows discovery using the bundled Codex version.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve npm's latest stable `@openai/codex` version, cache successful lookups for six hours, and use bundled Codex `0.169.0` as both the minimum and registry-failure fallback. Failed lookups are retried on the next discovery attempt. Responses attribution and Codex binary selection/update behavior remain independent.

This removes the calendar-version/`99.0.0` selection and reuses the existing guarded HTTP transport and catalog cache. A contract test keeps the floor aligned with the bundled dependency; test planning schedules that contract for pin changes. The existing Responses wrapper fixture moves into its existing support module to satisfy the line-cap ratchet, with its assertions preserved.

## Evidence

- Regression tests failed on the original behavior: discovery used OpenClaw `2026.11.5` where the Codex version was expected. The corrected discovery and provider contracts pass.
- 132 focused tests passed across discovery, provider listing, auth ordering, prompt stability, and the bundled-version contract. After the fixture move, all 33 provider tests and all 8 token-sharing tests passed again.
- Targeted typecheck, extension/core/script lint, formatting, and commit-hook checks passed. Targeted planner routing was verified; the broad planner suites were not completed locally.
- Authenticated live proof through an isolated foreground Gateway: npm lookup HTTP 200; `/backend-api/codex/models?client_version=0.171.0` HTTP 200; 10 available models; a real OpenClaw-runtime turn returned `CODEX_DISCOVERY_OK`. Responses used `originator=openclaw` and `version=2026.11.5`. The test Gateway was stopped after validation.
- Local autoreview of the working-tree candidate based on `140e6bf92c820eb9d7592c285106b62668319d50` reported scoped-clean at P0–P2. The subsequent change only relocates the existing test fixture. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its source checkout lacks dependencies and build output; a hosted ClawSweeper review was requested on this ready PR.

Broad coverage remains with PR CI.

<details>
<summary>Scope and simplification</summary>

Against the merge base: production +72/-14 lines; tests, fixtures, and planning +187/-76; docs and guide +11/-11. The new resolver contains the Codex version lookup, cache policy, and fallback; it adds no new cache or transport owner.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ui): keep Review visible when sending a message
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Sending a message can leave the Control UI's open Review panel showing its empty placeholder even though the session checkout still has changes.

## User Impact
Sending a message should no longer blank the open diff for a viewer whose workspace-read access is confirmed.

## Why This Change Was Made
The send event carries `workspaceReadDisabledReason: null` to explicitly allow reads. Session-row reconciliation interpreted that value as a tombstone and removed the field. Review then saw `undefined` (no known decision) and stopped rendering the diff. Preserve the explicit null for this field only. Denials and Gateway authorization checks are unchanged.

## Evidence
- Reproduced on a running Control UI (2026.11.5, `92d147da1552`) using two chat panes and a synthetic Git checkout with one modified file. Review blanked on send, while `git diff --stat` was unchanged; reloading recovered the view.
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/lib/sessions/reconcile.test.ts`: on base `b4ddf4b30fc`, the new allowed-read case fails (expected null, received undefined); with the fix, **19/19** pass, including explicit denial. Targeted format and lint checks pass.

- **Real Gateway, compiled Control UI:** an isolated local Gateway handled browser sends against a deterministic loopback model provider, using a synthetic Git checkout. The browser showed the diff before sending in both runs. After the assistant reply, without reloading, the UI built with the base reconciler (`b4ddf4b30fc`) showed the empty Review placeholder; the UI built from the PR head (`fb668991137`) still showed all three changed files. Same Gateway runtime and browser fixture in both runs. No production deployment.
- Both UI builds reported the same four CSS/JS budget warnings.

**Base UI — Review is empty after the reply**

![Base UI: empty Review after the reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b0d99e6-238e-4b70-b895-8de2d26d6d97)

**PR head — Review retains the diff after the reply**

prs.title: fix: let Docker config and channel commands work while the Gateway runs
prs.body:
Fixes #202040

## What Problem This Solves

With the shipped Docker Compose file, `openclaw-cli` cannot change config or add a channel once the Gateway is running. Those commands first check that the running Gateway owns the shared state, and `openclaw-cli` runs in a different PID namespace from the Gateway, so the check cannot verify the owner and the write is refused. The documented `docker compose run --rm openclaw-cli channels add ...` step hits this. So does `./scripts/docker/setup.sh`, which writes config through `openclaw-cli` after starting the Gateway: it can print `WARNING: Failed to reset agents.defaults.sandbox.mode to off`, and with `OPENCLAW_SANDBOX=1` it cannot turn sandbox mode on.

## User Impact

User impact: with the default Compose stack, `openclaw-cli` config commands and `channels add` reach the running Gateway instead of being refused, and `setup.sh` can apply its sandbox settings. One behavior change to know about: stopping or recreating the Gateway container now also ends any `openclaw-cli` container that is still running. Anyone who defines their own `openclaw-cli` service needs both `network_mode` and `pid` set to `service:openclaw-gateway`. This has not been run against a real Docker host yet; see Evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

`openclaw-cli` already shared the Gateway's network, and with it the hostname, so the PID namespace was the only part of the ownership check that could not match. The service now sets `pid: "service:openclaw-gateway"`, the same line the Compose operations guide already told people to add in an override.

The CLI service also drops `init: true`. In the shared namespace the Gateway's docker-init is PID 1 and reaps orphaned processes. A second docker-init would not be PID 1 and would print a warning on every command.

Once the CLI can see the Gateway as the owner, its writes go to the Gateway's listener. `setup.sh` issued them right after `docker compose up -d`, before the listener accepts connections. It now runs the image's own health check through `docker compose exec` and waits up to 180 seconds before those writes. If the Gateway never reports healthy, it prints a warning with the logs command and continues, so a slow Gateway does not abort setup.

The Docker docs now describe the shared PID namespace. The security note now says the CLI container can see and signal Gateway processes; it already receives the same Gateway token and state mounts. The `compose-setup` Docker E2E gains a config write through `openclaw-cli` while the Gateway runs, read back from inside the Gateway.

Compose has resolved `pid: service:<name>` since v2.1.0. The file's `env_file` `required:` entries already need a later Compose release, so this adds no new version requirement.

## Evidence

Checked locally, without a Docker daemon:

- A new `setup.sh` test asserts the health wait runs after the Gateway starts and before the first runtime `openclaw-cli config set`. The Compose alignment test now requires `pid` and no `init` on `openclaw-cli`. Before the change both fail: the health-wait index is `-1` and the `pid` property is missing. After the change, 22 of 27 tests in `test/scripts/docker-setup.test.ts` pass, and the new test takes about 2.2 s.
- The other 5 tests in that file (the sandbox paths) could not run locally. They bind a Unix socket to stand in for the Docker socket, my environment blocks that bind, and they fail with `listen EPERM` before reaching `setup.sh`. I read their assertions against the new log line: the health check is a `docker compose exec`, with no ` run ` or ` up -d`, so their compose-policy and Gateway-start checks see the same lines as before. CI runs them.
- `bash -n` and `shellcheck -S warning` are clean on `scripts/docker/setup.sh` and `scripts/e2e/compose-setup.sh`. `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- I checked the namespace behavior in the upstream sources. Docker copies the target container's hostname for `network_mode: container:` (moby `daemon/container_operations.go`). Compose resolves `pid: service:<name>` to `container:<id>` (docker/compose `pkg/compose/service_containers.go`; v2.0.1 still passed it to Docker unresolved). Docker's docker-init is tini v0.19.0, which warns when it is neither PID 1 nor a subreaper.

Not run: `setup.sh` against a real Docker Compose stack (plain or with `OPENCLAW_SANDBOX=1`), `pnpm test:docker:compose-setup`, an actual `channels add` (it goes through the same ownership check as `config set`), and Docker Desktop on macOS or Windows.

prs.title: fix(acp): keep active coding replies alive across tool calls
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Codex reply in an ACP session can disappear after six minutes even while tools are returning results. On OpenClaw 2026.11.5, two interrupted replies had tool results just 14 and 17 seconds before cancellation.

Related to #195520 and #195584. This PR covers replies dispatched through the ACP session manager. #195584 addresses liveness ownership in the ACPX harness attempt.

## User Impact

An active ACP reply can finish after six minutes. A stalled reply still times out when the backend only repeats a completed tool update or emits empty text, usage, or an in-progress status.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ACP manager already receives output before projecting it into chat. It now reports nonblank text deltas, including thoughts, and the first terminal event for each tool call to the watchdog on the current reply operation. The reporter runs after the actor check and ignores events after cancellation. It remembers up to 4,096 completed call IDs per backend attempt. Once full, only new text advances the watchdog.

## Evidence

- On upstream base `e62a1a37a`, all three new dispatch cases reproduced the missing progress timestamp. With the fix, the tool-result and thought cases stay active past six minutes of virtual time. The case with only repeated or non-semantic events reaches the stop decision.
- All 72 focused tests passed across the ACP dispatcher, turn stream, and session watchdog. The final single-worker run took 32 seconds locally, including about 6.4 seconds for the changed test file. Core and messaging-test type checks, lint, formatting, and the test-line budget passed.
- On a locally patched 2026.11.5 Gateway, a separate Codex session through ACPX completed nine sequential tools and returned its final answer after 7 minutes 18 seconds. The final answer matched in the Codex rollout and Gateway chat history.
- Local Codex review of the staged patch against `e62a1a37a` reported no actionable findings.

prs.title: fix: show app update guidance instead of a failing Update button on app-managed Macs
prs.body:
Closes #198506

Prior work: #198562 tried this and was closed without merging because the update handlers it edited have since moved. This PR is written against current main.

## What Problem This Solves

On a Mac where OpenClaw.app owns the Gateway, Settings > Updates still shows an enabled "Update Gateway..." button and an "Update status unavailable" row. Clicking the button gets a refusal from the Gateway ("Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway."). The page then keeps that refusal as an update error with a "Retry update" button, and the error stays until the page is reloaded. A healthy install looks like it failed an update, and Retry cannot succeed because the Gateway marks the refusal as not retryable.

## User Impact

User impact: on an app-managed install, Settings > Updates now says "Managed by OpenClaw.app" in the status row and shows the app's own guidance ("Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway.") where the update button used to be. There is no button to click, so no error appears and nothing is left to retry. Other installs (package, Git checkout, separately managed Gateways) look and behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already knew the install was app-owned, but `update.status` dropped that fact, so the page had no way to tell this install from any other and offered the normal action. The Gateway now sends the owner under `schedule.install.host`, and the Settings page uses it. Ownership comes from the same install marker the Gateway's refusal already uses, so a Mac connected to a separately managed Gateway still gets the normal update flow.

The protocol schema gains an optional `install.host` object and a `host` install kind, and the generated validators were regenerated from it. The Control UI adds four English strings. The updating doc notes where the owner is reported.

## Evidence

I ran the same Settings > Updates steps in Chromium against disposable Gateways built from the merge base (`d119c6b`) and from this PR (`0f678cb`). Both used the exact ownership marker written by the Mac packaging script, with fresh Gateway state and no model or credentials.

- Before: Settings showed "Update status unavailable" and offered "Update Gateway…". Confirming it left "Couldn’t update OpenClaw. Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway." in the status row. `update.status` returned `schedule.install: null`.
- After: Settings shows "Managed by OpenClaw.app" and the guidance "Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway." There is no Gateway update button. `update.status` returned `schedule.install: {"kind":"host","host":{"owner":"macos-app","displayName":"OpenClaw.app","updateHint":"Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway."}}`.
- I also built the changed Updating guide with the same docs site renderer on both sides. The new version explains that Settings shows the owner's guidance instead of a Gateway update action.

That run is the before/after Settings proof with real app-owned `update.status` data that ClawSweeper listed as missing end-to-end coverage. The rest of that item is still open: the native OpenClaw.app updater and an upgrade from the latest stable release with settings intact were not exercised. A separately managed Gateway was not run in a browser either; the existing `updates.test.ts` cases for the "Update Gateway…" action still pass.

With main's sources and this PR's tests, the new Settings test fails the way the issue describes: the status row reads "Update status unavailable" where it should say "Managed by OpenClaw.app". The Gateway cases that expect the owner fail the same way. With this change, all of them pass.

Tests run locally on this branch after rebasing it onto main (Node 26, macOS arm64):

- `ui/src/pages/config/updates.test.ts`: 43 passed, including the app-managed case, which takes about 6 ms. With main's sources it fails ("expected 'StatusUpdate status unavailable' to contain 'Managed by OpenClaw.app'") and the other 42 pass.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/config.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-install-status.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-startup-host-owned.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server-methods/update-status-schedule.test.ts`: 50 passed. With main's sources, the 9 cases that expect the owner fail. The new schema case takes about 1 ms.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/update-status.test.ts`: 21 passed with a 60 second test timeout. At the default 5 seconds, 3 history reconciliation cases timed out in my environment at 6 to 8 seconds each.
- `generate-gateway-validators --check` and `generate-control-ui-validators --check` report no drift. `predicates.js` was regenerated on top of main instead of merged by hand.
- `ui:i18n:verify` passes. `ui:i18n:check` reports fallback baseline drift from the four new English strings; the locale refresh workflow owns those generated files, so this PR does not touch them.
- `oxfmt --check` on the 13 changed files and `git diff --check` are clean.

Not verified:

- No run inside OpenClaw.app itself. The browser run above used a Gateway built from source with the Mac packaging marker. The issue's reporter offered to check a fix on their Mac.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/update-host-owned.test.ts` has one failure ("refuses an immutable surface discovered after initial admission before campaign adoption"), a SQLite offline maintenance lock in the test's temp state. It fails the same way with main's sources, so this change does not cause it.
- `pnpm install` and the full `pnpm check:changed` were not run. Dependencies came from a scratch npm install using the versions in `package.json` (npm resolved the transitive ones), with the repository's Solid patches applied.

prs.title: fix(sessions): let an optional human correction steer the active turn
prs.body:
Fixes #196358

## What Problem This Solves

A turn with a **required** reply contract already owns the reply path. When an optional human correction arrives while that turn is finishing, `resolveReplyBackendQueueMessageMismatch` used to queue it as a separate reply because the optional contract's `queueMessage` did not match the active required contract. The correction was then dropped or delivered late instead of steering the active turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mismatch resolver now lets an **optional** inbound inherit the active **required** contract, so the correction steers the turn instead of spawning a queued reply. Required-vs-required and optional-vs-optional mismatches keep the previous behaviour.

## Evidence

Head `441f1d8d46` (rebased on main `1c5c3adb5a`; the earlier head `af7e3e610a` was 2600+ commits behind).

$ pnpm exec vitest run src/sessions/session-controller.steer.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  35 passed (35)

prs.title: fix: reclaim cache left by completed Linux commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completed host commands can leave empty Linux session cgroups holding file cache for hours. That cache competes with the Gateway's working set even though the commands that populated it have finished.

## User Impact

OpenClaw now attempts to reclaim cache when session exec processes finish, then removes the empty session cgroup. Live groups, aggregate resource limits, and the shared fallback remain intact. There is no new configuration or database migration; other platforms remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The delegated cgroup owner created session leaves but had no teardown operation. Broker command closure, supervisor extinction, and standalone PTY completion now call one serialized cleanup operation. It checks both process membership and descendant population, writes current usage to `memory.reclaim`, and handles a concurrent arrival through the kernel's `EBUSY` result. Missing reclaim support logs a fallback warning before removal. If cleanup removes a prepared leaf before a new command joins, the existing placement owner recreates its policy and retries the join once.

Reclaim runs asynchronously with 50 ms pauses and a 250 ms retry budget. One kernel write can exceed that budget; this is not a hard reclaim deadline or a measured bound on kernel CPU/IO. Live leaves are skipped and pre-existing orphaned leaves are not swept. Real reclaim behavior on btrfs and the reported production deployment is unverified locally.

## Evidence

The supervisor regression failed on base `e62a1a37a6e0a4727a402db3d26640ceab93a9b7` because neither reclaim nor removal happened, and passed after the fix. All 35 owner tests pass, including live processes, populated descendants, `EBUSY`, absent reclaim, partial reclaim, serialization, and non-Linux no-op. The final owner/supervisor run passed 78 tests in 50.10 s including worker preparation; test bodies are measured in milliseconds.

The committed `scripts/perf/agent-exec-cgroup-teardown-measure.mts` replays 48 synthetic cgroups, 46 empty, with 29.5 GB modeled charge and a 17.9 GB largest leaf. Five alternating before/after pairs plus five A/A pairs show 0 → 46 reclaim/removal operations, both live groups unchanged, and one maximum concurrent reclaim. Median elapsed owner time is 0.023 → 2350.391 ms (including deliberate pauses), CPU 0.032 → 8.686 ms, and sampled allocation 10,448 → 810,720 bytes. Candidate A/A elapsed medians are 2381.618 / 2409.475 ms. Baseline is the previously absent cleanup operation, independently proven by the red regression. These are fake-cgroupfs scheduling/contract measurements, not actual reclaimed RAM or kernel performance. No large database or workspace is materialized because this owner never reads them.

Codex autoreview of the complete local diff is scoped-clean at P0–P2. Production grows 115 lines because cleanup ownership was missing; no scan, cache, schema, or configuration is added. Transport callbacks share the existing cgroup owner. Focused sibling tests passed: 72 passed / 54 runtime skips on the default runtime (39.36 s wrapper), and 60 passed / 3 platform skips on Node (38.79 s wrapper), covering broker raw/execa/file-output and PTY lifecycles. `pnpm check:changed` completed its full check set. Initial lane-caused typing/lint issues were fixed; its second run retained an early line-cap failure, repaired during that run and then verified by a passing targeted line-cap check. All other checks passed, including core/test/script types, lint, formatting, dead exports, and import boundaries. No inherited failure exception is claimed. Exact-head CI and ClawSweeper are required before merge.

prs.title: fix(msteams): replies with lists, headings, or tables post twice in personal chats
prs.body:
Related: #158103

## What Problem This Solves

In a Teams 1:1 chat, when the agent's answer has a list, a heading, or a table, the user gets the answer twice. The second copy has its bullet points squashed onto one line.

## User Impact

Users get the answer once, and it still streams in as it is written. List items and line breaks each show on their own line, in normal Teams messages too.

## Why This Change Was Made

Teams only accepts a streaming update that adds to the text already shown. Today the plugin streams the raw text, then at the end swaps in a formatted version. Teams rejects the swap, so the plugin sends the whole answer again as a new message.

The fix has two parts:

1. **Stream the formatted text from the start.** The end of the stream then only adds text, so Teams accepts it.
2. **Keep line breaks.** The formatter writes list items as plain `• item` lines (its mobile-safe style, unchanged), but Teams joins single line breaks, so the items ran together on one line. It now adds a Markdown line break at the end of those lines, and of the author's own line breaks.

The two parts belong together: without part 2, the single streamed answer would show the run-together list.

## Evidence

The same question to the same bot, before and after:

| Before: the answer arrives twice | After: once |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ahamilton454/openclaw/pr-proof/double-reply-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ahamilton454/openclaw/pr-proof/after.png) |

What Teams answered to each streaming update (from our network log):

```text
before  202 202 201 202 403 403 201   <- two updates rejected, then the answer is sent again
after   202 202 201 202 202 202       <- every update accepted
```

- **Tests:** all 1,088 Teams plugin tests pass. With the old code, 15 of the 58 tests touched here fail, including one whose fake Teams server rejects updates exactly like real Teams does.
- **Checks:** format, typecheck, lint, and the SQLite check pass. The dead-code scan lists 103 old entries in other files; this PR adds no exports.
- **Code review:** OpenClaw's autoreview tool (Claude engine on Opus, since Codex isn't installed here and the default Claude model was over its limit) rated it correct. Its one finding, a half-written line that later becomes a table header, is fixed. An earlier independent review found eight issues, all fixed with tests.
- **How often it happens:** across our bots, Teams rejected 47 streaming updates in 14 days, in 4 customer workspaces.
- **Not checked:** the Teams mobile apps (tested on Teams web, including at phone size), and the `progress` streaming mode, which this PR does not change.

## Merge Danger

Easy to revert. No settings or stored data change. It affects how the Teams plugin formats and streams messages.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep the prompt series when the bounded window drops an old compaction
prs.body:
## Problem

The prompt owner keys each system prompt series on its history: the newest compaction or reset. Each run hydrates a bounded transcript window. When the history after a compaction outgrows that window (large prompt checkpoints count toward it), the window can start after the compaction. The history id then read as `null`, the series restarted as `restarted:history`, and the system prompt, prompt suffix and tool descriptions were re-rendered. The next run could see the compaction again and flip back. Each flip misses the whole provider prefix.

## Solution

- Port of a local fix (first commit, kept with its author): when the window starts after the boundary, the newest `openclaw.system-prompt` checkpoint in the window names the history.
- Close the stale-checkpoint edge: a checkpoint written before a later compaction still names the earlier history. Each checkpoint now records the transcript boundary count (`sessionManager.getBoundaryCount()`). A checkpoint is evidence of the current history only when its count matches the current count. A checkpoint whose count matches names the history even when the boundary is also in the window. Otherwise the visible boundary names it; with neither, the history is unknown. An unknown history is named `unknown:<boundaryCount>`: the count changes only at a compaction or reset on the active path, so a checkpoint that recorded `unknown:N` at count N belongs to the same history. The series restarts at most once when nothing in the window names the history. A restored checkpoint without a count is rewritten with the count on the next persist. `null` stays valid only for a session that never compacted or reset.
- Compaction leaves `System prompt update` messages out of the summary input (`compaction-planning.ts`, one predicate used by the prepared plan and the array path). A pinned series carries every update since its history began, each repeating the whole changed section; the summarizer had to read them all. Compaction starts a new prompt history, and that restart renders every section current, so the updates carry nothing the next request lacks. Provider requests outside compaction are unchanged.

## Impact

- Sessions that outgrow their bounded window after a compaction keep their system prompt series and provider cache across runs.
- Compaction summaries no longer re-read prompt updates; long pinned sessions that edit workspace files compact on a smaller input.
- Existing checkpoints do not record a boundary count. In a session that has compacted, the first run after deploy whose window does not contain the compaction restarts the series once. A legacy checkpoint read while the compaction is in the window is rewritten with the count instead. Never-compacted sessions are not affected.

## E2E (head `af7ee63f5b61`, merge base `b4ddf4b30fc5`; the final head `dfb4d5bce649` only reshapes a test fixture)

Isolated scratch Gateways from source (`env -i`, own state, random ports), same driver on both sides, OpenAI Responses (`gpt-6.2-astra`, `contextTokens: 24000`, `maxTokens: 2048`). Journey `gate-h`: three story turns, `/compact` asking for a very long summary, then workspace `AGENTS.md` edits each followed by a follow-up turn (the history after the compaction outgrows the bounded window), then a **Gateway restart** on the same state and three more edit/follow-up pairs. An unrelated chat (`gate-other`) runs ordinary turns and `/compact` every second turn throughout. Numbers are provider usage per request (cacheRead / cacheWrite).

Long workspace rules, two runs per side:

| | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| Req 13 (edit after the window drops the compaction) | `restarted:history`, **0 / 11096** (run 2); `restarted:history` at req 14, 0 / 11459 (run 1) | pinned, **12336 / 484** (run 2); pinned 12332 / 484 (run 1) |
| History restarts without a compaction | 2 and 3 | 0 and 0 |
| Automatic compaction after the restart | run 2: 1 failed attempt, then succeeded; one turn failed ("Couldn't finish this reply") | run 2: 2 failed attempts, then succeeded; every turn answered. Run 1: every turn answered |
| Live prompt updates at the compaction (peak) | 34 KB | 88 KB in history, none in the summary input |

Before the compaction change (head `dd58eb1`, two runs) the same journey failed automatic compaction three times in a row after the restart and the last turn failed in both runs. The remaining failed attempts on both sides are `summary truncated at the output token limit` and come from the journey itself: the `/compact` message asks for "at least 3000 words" and stays in the history the next automatic compaction summarizes. With a plain `/compact`, base and head match request for request and both compact twice without a failure.

Short workspace rules (control, 9 edits): neither window loses the compaction, so both sides stay pinned and match (req 22: 14398 / 664 head, 14336 / 662 base); both compact automatically after the restart and every turn answers.

Side effects:
- Ordinary chat (`gate-other`): every turn and every `/compact` returned `ok` on both sides in all runs.
- Cron, tool and session paths (run on head `dd58eb1`, unchanged by the compaction commit except the summary input): cron starting a chat, exec background wake, subagent completion, steer, `sessions_send`, cron surviving new/reset/edited chats, Stop and reset gave identical results on base and head, then a Gateway restart.

UI: Control UI on the head scratch Gateway renders the history across both compactions and answers every turn after the restart; screenshots in the PR comments.

## Evidence

Tests (merge base vs head):
- `attempt-session-runtime-prepare.history-boundary.test.ts`, real SQLite hydration, one bounded view per run; every case pushes the boundary out of the window so it reaches the count rule:
  - three runs whose byte window includes, then drops, then includes an old compaction keep one series (base: `restarted:history` on run 2);
  - eviction: the newest checkpoint leaves the window with the compaction, the series restarts once as `unknown:1`, then stays pinned when the boundary returns beside that checkpoint (previous head `3df7c53`: second restart);
  - a legacy checkpoint that names the visible boundary is rewritten with the count and stays pinned when the boundary leaves (previous head: two restarts);
  - a legacy checkpoint with `historyId: null` restarts once, then stays pinned (base: pinned on the wrong history);
  - rewind to a checkpoint written at count 1 (stored as `unknown:1`, `boundaryCount: 1`) past a later compaction: the series stays pinned to that checkpoint (fails if the count were store-wide);
  - a counted reset restarts the series although the window holds a checkpoint of the earlier history (fails if resets were not counted);
  - a visible compaction after a counted checkpoint restarts the series (fails if any counted checkpoint outranked the visible boundary);
Each of the last three cases was checked with a local mutation of the behavior it guards (store-wide count, uncounted reset, checkpoint always outranking the boundary): each fails under its mutation and passes after revert.
- `prepared-compaction-plan.test.ts`: prompt updates between turns are left out of the summary selection, the turns stay (red on `7a698fb`: the updates were selected).
- The rewind case reads the same SQLite bounded context through `SessionManager.openBoundedAsync`; the separate SQLite reader case was dropped after main grew that file past the line cap.
- `session-prompt-state.test.ts`:
  - a checkpoint that predates a compaction outside the window restarts the series, and the request carries the re-rendered prompt (base: pinned);
  - a never-compacted session stays pinned (passes on both);
  - the ported unit test for a window that starts after the compaction, now passing the boundary count as production does (base: restart).
- The earlier prefix-stability journey step was removed: it passed on the merge base, so it could not catch this defect.

Real route on head `3df7c5332e81` vs merge base (re-run on `3677e9f`: OpenAI requests 13/15 pinned at 9474/484 and 12048/484, 0 history restarts without a compaction; Claude request 15 pinned at 18150/988, only restart at a real compaction with `boundaryCount: 2`), isolated scratch Gateways, same script on both sides, an unrelated second chat running turns and compacting throughout. Script: 3 story turns, `/compact` with a long summary, then workspace edits each followed by a follow-up turn, so the history after the compaction outgrows the bounded window.

OpenAI Responses (`gpt-6.2-astra`, minimal tool profile, `contextTokens: 24000`):

| Request | Base series, cacheRead / cacheWrite | Head series, cacheRead / cacheWrite |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | `restarted:history` (historyId -> null), **2700 / 3876** | pinned, 9432 / 484 |
| 15 | pinned, 7061 / 484 | pinned, 12005 / 484 |
| 16 | `restarted:history` (flips back), 7545 / 485 | real automatic compaction (allowed rebuild) |
| History restarts without a compaction | 2 | 0 |

cliproxy Claude (`claude-opus-5-5`, `contextTokens: 30000`):

| Request | Base series, cacheRead / cacheWrite | Head series, cacheRead / cacheWrite |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | `restarted:history` (historyId -> null), **1394 / 16782** | pinned, 18263 / 988 |
| 20/21 | restart at a real automatic compaction | restart at a real automatic compaction (checkpoint `boundaryCount: 2`) |
| History restarts without a compaction | 1 | 0 |

Upgrade (one state dir: base builds a compacted chat with legacy checkpoints, stop, start head on the same state, OpenAI route):
- target chat: one `restarted:history` on the first turn after the upgrade, then pinned through 6 edit/follow-up pairs (cacheRead 2432 -> 10213); `/compact` on head restarts once and writes `boundaryCount: 2`; later checkpoints stay pinned at count 2;
- never-compacted chat: pinned across the upgrade (legacy checkpoint `historyId: null`, then `boundaryCount: 0`);
- unrelated chat: restarts only at its own compactions (counts 2-5 recorded);
- cron created on base: still enabled on head and fired on schedule in the target chat; with the scratch model at `maxTokens: 2048`, that turn failed in automatic compaction (summary output budget exhausted); the merge base fails the same way on the same setup. With `maxTokens: 8192` the cron turn passes on head, the target chat restarts once after the upgrade and then stays pinned (cacheRead 2297 -> 10078), and `/compact` restarts once with `boundaryCount: 3`.

Follow-ups (not blockers):
- A session fork loses its pinned prefix while the source series is `unknown:N` (the fork view carries no checkpoint data); this costs cache until the next compaction.
- `removeTrailingEntries` can delete a boundary through the plugin compatibility surface; core does not reach that path today.
- A legacy session gets one extra checkpoint append after the upgrade, when its count is first written.

Gates on `af7ee63`, plus lint, format, the touched test and test-lines on `dfb4d5b`: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxlint and oxfmt on touched files, the baseline ratchets (mock-exports, test-lines +400 of 400, line-cap, max-lines, database-worker), the focused tests above, the prompt-cache prefix-stability suites, and the compaction, safeguard and memory-flush tests. Production lines vs main: +102 / -34 (compaction change: +33 / -14).
