prs.title: fix: tell the model why a stringified tool argument was rejected
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Models sometimes send an object or array tool argument as a JSON string, for example `dispatch_action` with `args: "{\"title\":…}"`. OpenClaw converts these strings back into objects. When that conversion failed, the model only saw `args: must be object` and had no way to tell what was wrong. In one design session, six `show_widget` calls failed this way. Each one was a stringified `args` with a single extra trailing `}`, so the failures looked random and appeared to depend on the embedded images. Separately, valid strings over 64 KiB were never converted at all and failed with the same message, far below `show_widget`'s documented 262,144-character `widget_code` limit.

## User Impact

When an agent sends a malformed stringified object or array, the rejection now includes the JSON parse error and tells the model to pass the value itself, so it can correct the call on its next attempt. Valid stringified objects and arrays of any size are now converted, as smaller ones already were.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Size cap removed.** The 64 KiB cap on this conversion came from a review concern in #96922 about running `JSON.parse` without a bound on model output. That concern doesn't hold here: the transport has already parsed the complete tool-call argument buffer, these string bytes included, without any bound. A second parse of a value that is already in memory adds no new exposure, and the cap rejected legitimate large widget payloads.
- **Real reason in the error.** For a TypeBox `type` error that expects an object or array and received a string, the message now explains what was received:
  - the string is not valid JSON: `args: must be object (received a string that is not valid JSON: <parse error>; pass the value itself, not a string)`
  - the string is valid JSON of the wrong kind: `(received a JSON string; pass the value itself, not a string)`

  This work runs only on the error path.
- **No automatic repair.** Malformed strings, such as one with a stray brace, are not repaired. Reporting the error accurately is enough for the model to fix the call itself.

## Evidence

- I recovered the six failed calls from the stored session transcript. In each one, `args` was a string, and `JSON.parse` failed at the last character because of the extra `}`. With that brace removed, the widget HTML in two of the calls was byte-for-byte identical to the source file, base64 included. Every call ended normally with a tool-use stop reason, so no output was truncated.
- I added two regression tests to `packages/llm-core/src/validation.test.ts`, both run under the dynamic-execution and embedded-aot profiles. One checks that a stringified object over 64 KiB is converted. The other checks that a malformed stringified object reports its parse error. Both fail on `main` (4 failures) and pass with the fix (76/76).
- Consumer suites pass: `tool-search`, `tool-search-runtime`, `provider-tools`, `tool-error-summary` and `agent-tools.schema`. `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- An independent review of the diff reported no P0–P2 findings.
- Gap: I did not rerun the original failure end to end through a live Gateway and model. The defect and the fix are both inside the validator, so I proved them at that boundary.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: feat(plugin-sdk): add repository sources with a bundled GitLab consumer
prs.body:
Related: #185864

## What Problem This Solves

Repository integrations cannot join OpenClaw's new-session picker, managed checkout and worktree preparation through a public plugin contract. Supporting a second forge such as GitLab (#185864) would therefore need changes in core.

## User Impact

- **GitLab users** can enable the new bundled `gitlab` plugin, search public GitLab projects in **New session**, and start a session on a managed checkout or a new worktree. Self-managed GitLab works through `plugins.entries.gitlab.config.baseUrl`.
- **Plugin authors** can offer repositories from any Git host with `api.registerRepositorySource` and `openclaw/plugin-sdk/repository-sources`.
- **Everyone else:** no change. Built-in GitHub, existing plugins, existing sessions and existing configuration keep working, and nothing needs migrating. The GitLab plugin is off by default.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the smaller, consumer-backed stage that the first review of this PR recommended. The earlier revision proposed four SDK families at once (repository sources, execution environments, caller-bound plugin tools, Control UI V2) with no production consumer. This revision keeps **only repository sources** and adds a real consumer, the bundled GitLab plugin. The other families come back later, each together with the feature that uses it.

Plugins supply vendor policy (URL rules, transport, search). OpenClaw keeps custody of checkout storage, leases, worktree preparation, session state and authorization.

### How this relates to #192349 and #192350

This remains an **alternative** to the SDK foundation in #192349 and the GitHub migration in #192350, not an addition to them. Those PRs add GitHub-only SDK entry points (`native-github-account-host`, `native-github-publication-host`, `native-github-session-read`). Those entry points hand a plugin core's existing GitHub account records, publication receipts and `sessions.github.*` methods, which a GitLab plugin cannot use, and which keep that GitHub code in core.

The planned order. Everything #192349 and #192350 delivered has a stage:

1. **This PR:** repository sources (picker, managed checkout, base resolution) plus a GitLab consumer.
2. **GitLab merge requests:** general account, publishing and status contracts, replacing the GitHub-only bridges from #192349, used by GitLab. It brings the execution-environment, plugin-tool and Control UI pieces GitLab needs. To be coordinated with #185928 first.
3. **GitHub as a plugin:** GitHub moves onto the same contracts, and Doctor migrates its settings. This stage also carries every piece GitHub needs that GitLab did not:
   - cloud-worker support for plugin sources (GitHub sessions already run on cloud workers; if stage 2 gives GitLab cloud support, it arrives there instead);
   - execution identity: Git identity, credential stripping, sandbox setup, co-author lines and secret exclusions;
   - caller-bound plugin tools and how sub-agents inherit tool policy;
   - Board (GitHub Actions) bindings and plugin Doctor checks;
   - PR badges that survive a reload, and publishing that keeps running after the pane closes;
   - `owner/repo#123` references, and keeping the read-only `github` plugin independent;
   - the scheduled PR auto-fix job.

   Unlike #192350, which kept GitHub's account records, publication receipts and `sessions.github.*` methods in core, this stage would move them to the general contracts. That changes stored data and public Gateway methods, so it needs owner approval and will likely be split into two PRs.

## Repository sources: the SDK contract

**Purpose:** let a plugin offer repositories from any Git host (GitLab, Gitea, Bitbucket, a self-hosted forge) in the new-session picker. Sessions can then check out and work on them through the same project and worktree flow that built-in GitHub uses. Plugin sources run sessions on the Gateway; cloud workers come in a later stage.

### How a plugin wires it up

**1. Declare the source in `openclaw.plugin.json`.** The search method is a normal Gateway method the plugin registers:

```json
{
  "repositorySources": [
    { "id": "repositories", "label": "Example Forge", "searchMethod": "example.repositories.search" }
  ]
}
```

**2. Register the search method** with `api.registerGatewayMethod`. It returns the existing remote-project search shape:
- `projects`: name, clone and web URLs, visibility, and an optional description and default branch.
- `credential`: whether a credential is available. It never contains the credential itself.

Discovery is backend metadata only. It needs no browser module.

**3. Register the source** with `api.registerRepositorySource(source)`. The type is `RepositorySourceV1`:

| Member | Required | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | Matches the manifest contribution ID. The host qualifies it as `pluginId/id`. |
| `resolve(url)` | yes | Accepts and normalizes a supported URL, returning `{ url, name, display? }`, or returns `undefined` to decline. `display` is presentation only and never grants access. |
| `prepare({ url, agentId, requiredCommit?, signal, assertCurrent })` | yes | Prepares a local project. Returns `{ project, assertCurrent, resolveBase(ref?) }`, where `project` is `{ id, repoRoot, source }`. `resolveBase` returns `{ commit, ref }`. With no ref, it observes the current remote default branch (including a renamed one) and returns `origin/<branch>`. An explicit branch, tag or full commit resolves to that ref. |

Registration fails visibly, as a plugin registration error, when the ID is not declared in the manifest, `resolve` or `prepare` is missing, or the same ID registers twice.

The bundled GitLab plugin is a complete source in about 450 lines: `extensions/gitlab/index.ts` (registration), `src/url.ts` (URL rules), `src/source.ts` (the source), `src/transport.ts` (Git transport) and `src/search.ts` (search).

### Managed checkout: `createManagedProjectCheckoutV1(source)`

The plugin supplies a `ManagedProjectSourceV1`: `resolveUrl` and `invalidUrlMessage` for URL rules, plus the Git transport operations `clone`, `ensureCommit`, `resolveBase` and `refresh`. The host supplies everything else:
- **Reused from the host:** checkout leases, on-disk layout and the project registry. The plugin does not pick storage paths or keep its own registry.
- **What you get back:** `materialize`, `resolveBase` and `refresh` operations. Call them from inside the plugin's managed invocation, so the host can bind the current Gateway config and plugin authority. Called outside that context, they throw.
- **The host checks the plugin's answer:** it verifies the returned base commit locally, keeps safe fast-forward checks, and records the chosen ref and exact commit before setup. Retries reuse that pinned commit instead of fetching a new base.
- **Credentials stay with the plugin:** they live in the transport closure and never become host state.
- **Only its own clones:** `resolveBase` and `refresh` refuse a managed clone whose saved origin the source does not admit, so one source cannot run its transport on another source's checkout.
- **Lease checks per command:** each transport call receives `ManagedProjectTransportOptions`, including an optional `startRun`. Running every Git command through it re-checks the host's checkout leases right before the command starts.

`executeGitCommand`, `requireGitCommandOutput`, `runProjectGitCommand`, `projectCheckoutGitEnvironment` and `configureProjectCheckoutMaintenance` in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime` let a transport reuse the host's bounded Git runner, cancellation and maintenance settings.

### How sessions choose a source

- `sessions.create` gains an optional `repositorySource: "<pluginId>/<id>"`, sent alongside `projectGitUrl`. Combined with a cloud `repository` workspace, it is rejected with a message that asks for a local placement.
- **Field absent:** the existing built-in path runs unchanged. It accepts GitHub URLs only, as it does today.
- **Field present:** the host resolves exactly that source. It **never falls back** to another plugin or to the built-in source. These cases fail with an actionable error:
  - the source is disabled, withdrawn or does not accept the URL;
  - the source's answer for the URL changed between selection and preparation;
  - an existing session is asked to switch to a different source.
- **Control UI:** the new-session picker reads plugin sources from the plugin catalog (`plugins.controlUi.list` → `repositorySources`), shows them beside the built-in search, and sends `repositorySource` for a plugin result.
- **Sticky selection:** the session records the source as `repositorySourceId`. Deferred preparation, including after a restart, resolves that same source again, and forked sessions keep it.

### What the SDK exports

`openclaw/plugin-sdk/repository-sources` adds one entry point with one function, `createManagedProjectCheckoutV1`, and seven types: `RepositorySourceV1`, `RepositorySourceProject`, `RepositorySourcePreparation`, `ManagedProjectSourceV1`, `ManagedProjectOptions`, `ManagedProjectTransportOptions` and `ManagedProjectBaseV1`. Plugins register with `api.registerRepositorySource`. Full guide: `docs/plugins/sdk-repository-sources.md`.

## The bundled GitLab plugin

`extensions/gitlab` is the first consumer, and is meant as a reference implementation:

- **Manifest:** declares one repository source (`gitlab/repositories`) and the `gitlab.repositories.search` Gateway method. Config takes an optional `baseUrl` (an HTTPS origin, default `https://gitlab.com`).
- **Search:**
  - queries `/api/v4/projects` anonymously for public projects through the SDK's SSRF-guarded fetch, limited to the configured host with no redirects;
  - ranks by stars, so canonical projects come before forks;
  - maps results into the existing remote-project shape.
- **Source:** admits only HTTPS project URLs on the configured server and normalizes them to `https://host/group[/subgroup]/project.git`.
- **Transport:**
  - runs Git through the host runner (`process-runtime`) with credential helpers disabled, HTTPS only, no redirects and no prompts;
  - routes every command through the host's lease-checking `startRun`;
  - error messages name the failed step and never echo transport output.
- **Off by default.** Enable it in **Plugins** or with `plugins.entries.gitlab.enabled: true`.
- **Docs:** `docs/plugins/gitlab.md`; the plugin inventory and reference pages are regenerated.

## Evidence

### End to end in a real Gateway and Control UI

- **Setup:** a Gateway built from this branch, with isolated state, token auth on loopback, and the `gitlab` plugin enabled.
- **Discovery:** `plugins.controlUi.list` returned `repositorySources: [{ id: "repositories", label: "GitLab", searchMethod: "gitlab.repositories.search", pluginId: "gitlab" }]`.
- **Search and selection:** the picker showed a **GitLab** group beside GitHub. Choosing `gitlab-org/project-templates/express` set the chip to that project.
- **Session creation:** I called `sessions.create` with the same parameters the picker sends (`projectGitUrl` and `repositorySource: "gitlab/repositories"`), once for the current checkout and once with `worktree: true`. Both returned `repositorySourceId: "gitlab/repositories"`.
- **Clone:** the managed clone has origin `https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/project-templates/express.git` at `d10a6ca`, matching `git ls-remote ... HEAD`.
- **Worktrees:** both sessions received worktrees (`openclaw/kind-crab`, `openclaw/fresh-prawn`) based on `d10a6ca`, with project `express`.
- **No model:** the test Gateway had no model credentials, so the first turn reported "OpenAI didn't accept the saved credentials". Repository preparation completes before the turn, so this does not affect the proof.

Screenshots (user and device names blacked out):

| Before: plugin disabled, GitHub results only | After: GitLab group in the picker |
|---|---|
| ![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raw-labs/openclaw/f959e0164b4c74feb7de1d316aac54daca211a71/before-picker-github-only.png) | ![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raw-labs/openclaw/f959e0164b4c74feb7de1d316aac54daca211a71/after-picker-gitlab-group.png) |

| GitLab project selected | GitLab-backed session (project `express`, branch `fresh-prawn`) |
|---|---|
| ![Selected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raw-labs/openclaw/f959e0164b4c74feb7de1d316aac54daca211a71/after-selected-gitlab-project.png) | ![Session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raw-labs/openclaw/f959e0164b4c74feb7de1d316aac54daca211a71/after-gitlab-session.png) |

### Upgrade from the latest stable release (2026.11.4)

- **Before:** `openclaw@2026.11.4` from npm ran a Gateway on fresh isolated state (loopback, token auth). It created a plain session and a GitHub project session (`octocat/Hello-World`, project `hello-world`, worktree `openclaw/cool-lobster`).
- **Upgrade:** a Gateway built from this branch started on the same state. It ran its normal state upgrade, and `sessions.list` returned both sessions unchanged.
- **After:** with the `gitlab` plugin enabled, the upgraded Gateway created a GitLab worktree session (`express`, `openclaw/crisp-claw`) and a new GitHub session (`hello-world`, `openclaw/dawn-langoustine`). In the agent database, the GitLab row holds `repositorySourceId: "gitlab/repositories"`, the other rows have no source, and all four entries are valid.
- **Cloud placement:** `sessions.create` with `repository` and `repositorySource: "gitlab/repositories"` returned `INVALID_REQUEST`: "Plugin repository sources run sessions on this Gateway; cloud workers do not support them yet. Choose a local placement."
- **Downgrade:** 2026.11.4 refuses to start on the upgraded state because `main` already moved the state database to a newer schema (40, against 22 supported by 2026.11.4). This PR changes no schema, so a downgrade to 2026.11.4 is refused for any current `main` build, with or without it.

### Checks

- **Typecheck:** every `tsgo` lane (core, UI, extensions, extension tests, all core test lanes) reports 0 errors.
- **Lint and ratchets:** `oxlint` is clean on changed files, and the export-name-collision, assertion-safety, mock-exports, max-lines, line-cap and test-lines ratchets pass.
  - `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/plugins.ts` was already over its line cap. Its Control UI catalog schemas move to `schema/plugin-control-ui-catalog.ts` so the new field causes no growth.
  - No baseline changes.
  - `plugin-sdk:surface:check` already fails on the base commit (163 public entrypoints against a budget of 162, among others). This PR adds 1 entrypoint, 8 exports and 1 callable export to that existing overrun.
- **Tests on the current head (after merging `main`):** the PR's 86 test files and the New session UI suites pass (946 tests across the gateway, plugins, UI, UI browser and extensions shards). All `tsgo` lanes, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, `protocol:check`, `config:docs:check`, `check:control-ui-controllers` and the ratchets above pass. The one `oxlint` warning on a changed file (`chat-message-group.solid.test.tsx:347`) is already on `main`.
- **Test lines:** net +707 test lines, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/200166-repository-sources.txt` (307 beyond the 400-line allowance). Most of it is contract tests for the new public SDK surface.
- **New test files** (`--maxWorkers=1` wall time, including about 2 s of runner startup):

| File | Tests | Wall |
|---|---|---|
| `src/plugins/repository-sources.test.ts` | 3 | 8.2 s |
| `src/plugins/manifest-repository-sources.test.ts` | 8 | 6.1 s |
| `extensions/gitlab/src/url.test.ts` | 10 | 1.6 s |
| `extensions/gitlab/src/transport.test.ts` | 1 | 8.2 s |

### Data compatibility

- **New fields are optional:** `sessions.create.repositorySource`, the session entry's `repositorySourceId`, and the manifest `repositorySources`. The worker snapshot is no longer changed.
- **Old data keeps the old path:** an existing session or saved preference without them takes the unchanged built-in path. Tests cover requests without the field, and saved repository preferences with and without a source.
- **No migrations:** nothing is migrated and no SQLite schema changes.
- **Upgrade:** a real upgrade from 2026.11.4 is above. The published-driver × candidate Docker cell was not run locally. Saved New Session preferences live in browser storage; tests cover them with and without a source, but a browser upgrade was not run.

## Size

- **Total:** 93 files, +5,523 / −2,917 against the merge base with `main`.
- **Generated protocol and validator files:** +2,580 / −2,462. Excluding them, the change is about +2,940 / −455.
- **Tests:** +709 / −2.
- **Docs:** +202 / −5.
- **UI (excluding tests and generated validators):** +302 / −29.
- **GitLab plugin, with its tests:** +646.
- **`src/plugin-sdk`:** +114.

## Known gaps

- **Owner decisions:** whether this local repository-source SDK is the first public stage (see the planned order above), and SecOps approval of the new plugin's dependencies for the current head.
- **Startup bundle (needs a maintainer decision):** measured with `ui:check-performance:base` against the merge base, Control UI startup grows by **+464 B** gzipped on chat boot (1,325,122 → 1,325,586 B) and **+991 B** on New Session boot (816,023 → 817,014 B). The base is already over these caps, so the check allows no growth beyond 64 B.
  - **Already moved out of startup:** the plugin search client (1.3 KiB gzipped) and its result validator now load only when the user searches with a plugin source present.
  - **What remains:** the picker logic that lists plugin source groups and their status, plus the catalog field.
  - **The choice:** accept the measured growth with a budget adjustment, or ask for a follow-up that restructures the picker.
- **Cloud workers:** plugin sources run sessions on the Gateway only, and the GitLab plugin is local only. A cloud `repository` workspace with a plugin source is rejected with a clear message. In the Control UI, the picker still offers plugin results when a cloud placement is selected; submitting shows that message.
- **Public projects only:** the plugin sends no GitLab credentials. Private repositories need the account contracts planned for the next stage.
- **Pasted URLs:** pasting a GitLab URL into the picker still selects the built-in GitHub path, which ignores non-GitHub URLs, as on `main`. Pick GitLab projects from search; the docs say so.
- **Stale selection while disabled:** if the source's plugin is disabled after a project is chosen, the saved draft keeps the chip. Submission is blocked, but the chip itself shows no warning.
- **Rollback:** sessions created with a plugin source save `repositorySourceId`. A downgrade to 2026.11.4 is refused before any session is read, because the base `main` already uses a newer state schema.
- **Not run:** the published-driver × candidate Docker cell, the full test suite, and the UI e2e suites. This PR relies on CI for those.

<details>
<summary>Review history (four ClawSweeper reviews, all findings addressed)</summary>

- **First review:** took the smaller stage it recommended (repository sources only, with GitLab as the consumer). Removed the unimplemented co-author hook and the uncited `extensions/AGENTS.md` rule, rebuilt on `main`, and added real Gateway proof.
- **Second review:** GitLab resolves explicit tags and commits (`transport.test.ts`), a failed plugin clone cleans up its target, and the unused `createRepositorySources` facade is gone.
- **Third review:** dropped the unconsumed worker contract as recommended, rejected plugin sources on cloud workspaces with a clear message, and added the upgrade proof from 2026.11.4.
- **Fourth review:** replaced the cached import flagged by the UI guard with an awaited import, and merged `main`.

Open decisions from these reviews are under Known gaps. Each fix is also explained in its re-review comment.
</details>

prs.title: fix(agents): long conversations get stuck when the primary model's explicit auth order has no usable profile
prs.body:
Related #194689

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long conversation gets stuck with "This conversation is too long, and OpenClaw couldn't shorten it" on every message when the session model's explicit `auth.order` has no usable profile, even though ordinary turns already answer from the configured fallback model.

## User Impact

User impact: when the primary model's ordered credentials are all unusable, compaction now summarizes with the next model in `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`, the same chain ordinary turns already use, so long sessions keep working until the operator signs in again. Ordinary turns behave as before (the primary is tried, fails, and the "Model switched from … to …" notice is posted, now with `(auth)` instead of `(unknown)`). With no fallback configured, the reply names the cause, "This saved login isn't available. Choose another login…", instead of "Your request couldn't be completed." A user-pinned login with no stored credential, which the rate-limit pre-check used to move behind the fallbacks silently, is now tried first, then the turn switches with the notice.

Accepted edge case: the message is the same whatever made every ordered login unusable (missing, expired, permanently disabled); it names the login rather than the underlying reason, which the operator's auth status already shows.

Accepted edge case: a refused route stays in the reordered chain, so the candidate before it still sees a later fallback. With a chain like `primary/main → backup/fast → primary/other`, a missing login for `primary` and a replay-safe 429 on `backup/fast` whose retry floor exceeds the 15-second fallback window, `backup/fast` moves on instead of waiting, and the turn fails when `primary/other` is refused too; `main` marked the route unavailable and kept the longer wait. It needs all three conditions; separating notice ordering from fallback eligibility is a follow-up if a maintainer wants it.

Not changed, on purpose: the reporter's second case, an explicit `agents.defaults.compaction.model` that cannot authenticate on the embedded path. That override stays exact and has no fallback chain, as `docs/concepts/compaction.md` documents; checking at config time whether a compaction model can work is not part of this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Auth preparation refused the explicit-order case with a plain `Error`. Turns fall back on any candidate error, but compaction moves to the next model only for a classified failover error, so it stopped after one attempt (`attempt=1 maxAttempts=1 outcome=failed reason=unknown`). The refusal is now a `FailoverError` with the existing `selected_auth_profile_unavailable` code (reason `auth`, no HTTP status): it is a local refusal, not a provider response, so it gets that code's "saved login isn't available" copy and no re-authenticate hint. Compaction already forwards the failure code to its fallback classification, which maps this code to `auth`.

The rate-limit pre-check that reorders fallback models before each turn treats an auth-preparation `FailoverError` as "skip this candidate" and records nothing for it. It now leaves `selected_auth_profile_unavailable` to the fallback runner, which attempts the primary, logs `candidate_failed`, and posts the notice, as on `main`. This keeps the shared token-rate-limit pre-check's purpose (bound same-model recovery when a usable fallback exists) for every other refusal; only this local saved-login refusal is left in place, because demoting it silently skipped the failure record and the switch notice.

Docs: `docs/concepts/compaction.md` lists this case beside the cooldown case, and `docs/auth-credential-semantics.md` (Explicit auth order filtering) says what happens when no ordered profile is usable.

Not changed: the turn fallback order and policy, compaction's failover classification, `compaction.model` exactness, the other route refusals (`configured-auth`, `required-profile`).

## Evidence

### Live run: full-product repro on `main` and the same runs on this change

Built Gateway (`openclaw.mjs gateway run`, bench tree at `main` `3d172a63470`; this change = `89d82d887f1`, whose later amendments added only doc lines) in a no-network container. Config: `primary/main-model` with `auth.order.primary: ["primary:revoked"]` (declared, no stored credential), fallback `backup/backup-model`, both 16k-token windows, served by a local Responses model that reports request size as usage. The shipped CLI sends long messages with `gateway call chat.send` and reads `gateway call chat.history`.

With the fallback configured, `main`:

```
turn 1-3: Model switched from primary/main-model to backup/backup-model (unknown).
          log: lane task error "Explicit auth order for primary has no usable profiles." / candidate_failed primary / candidate_succeeded backup
turn 4:   [compaction-diag] end ... trigger=budget provider=primary/main-model attempt=1 maxAttempts=1 outcome=failed reason=unknown
          preflight compaction failed: Explicit auth order for primary has no usable profiles.
          ⚠️ This conversation is too long, and OpenClaw couldn't shorten it. ...
summary requests to backup-model: 0
```

This change:

```
turn 1-4: Model switched from primary/main-model to backup/backup-model (auth).
          log: candidate_failed primary / candidate_succeeded backup
          compaction summary requests to backup-model: 4; history ends with a Compaction entry; every turn answered
```

(Repeated `candidate_failed` lines for the same auth refusal are coalesced by the existing decision-log rule, so fewer lines appear than on `main`.)

With no fallback configured, one message: `main` replies "Your request couldn't be completed."; this change replies "This saved login isn't available. Choose another login under Models in the OpenClaw app or run `openclaw configure`."

Proof artifice: both models are one scripted local Responses server, and the dead login is a profile declared in config with no stored credential.

What the substitute proves and what it does not: the reporter ran `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` with a Codex OAuth profile; this run uses a local provider on the OpenClaw runtime. Compaction hits the same refusal through the same `rejectionError` (the reporter's `[compaction-diag] end … attempt=1 maxAttempts=1` line comes only from the embedded compaction path this change covers), so the compaction fix applies to their route; the OpenAI/Codex route itself was not run. The Gateway, auth preparation, fallback runner, compaction and CLI are the shipped ones. Upgrade run: not applicable (no update, Doctor, config or state change).

### Tests

- `compact.auth-preparation.test.ts`: "compacts through the configured fallback" gains an explicit-order row next to the cooldown row. Fails on `main` (compaction stops on the primary), passes here.
- `model-fallback.sticky-rate-limit.test.ts` ("shared model saturation guards", where `main` moved the pre-check cases in #198916): the rate-limit pre-check keeps a primary refused by its explicit auth order in first place with no recorded skip, so the runner attempts and reports it. A guard for the pre-check exemption (it passes on `main`, where the refusal was a plain `Error`).
- On the proof machine, the touched files plus neighbours (`prepare-auth*`, `compact.summary-fallback`, `model-fallback.test`, `model-fallback.{probe,personal-cooldown,sticky-rate-limit,shared-rate-limit.integration,reply-entry.e2e}`, `model-fallback-observation`): all pass on this change (5 shards).
- `pnpm check:changed` on `89d82d887f1`: passes (typecheck core and tests, lint, format, docs, guards) except the dead-export scan, which already fails on `main` (`src/gateway/openclaw-id/member-role-change.ts`, from #197770), outside this change.
- `model-fallback.sticky-rate-limit.test.ts` › "rechecks a fallback refused for an unusable saved login on the next turn": with `OPENCLAW_FALLBACK_SKIP_TTL_MS` set, a fallback refused for this saved-login reason is attempted again on the next turn instead of being skipped until the window expires, so fixing the order takes effect at once. The skip cache now owns that rule (`cachesAuthFailureSkip`). Fails on `main` (the backup is tried once in two turns), passes here.
- After merging current `main` on 18 Nov (`52b87b23676`; `main` had deleted `model-fallback.shared-rate-limit.test.ts`, so the guard case moved with the rest of that file's cases), on the proof machine: both touched test files and the `prepare-auth`, `model-fallback` and `model-fallback.personal-cooldown` neighbours pass, and `pnpm check:changed` passes in full.
- Test lines are net +77 against `main`: one row in the existing compaction fallback table, one guard case beside the existing pre-check cases and one skip-cache case; no existing test drives this refusal.

prs.title: fix: make the notices above the chat composer look alike
prs.body:
Closes #202261

## What Problem This Solves

The notices that sit above the chat composer don't look like one set. A read-only viewer sees "You need permission to send messages in this session." as a box filled with blue and set in blue text, right above a "Goal blocked" pill that keeps the composer's gray surface and colors only its icon. The microphone error, the "Fallback active" model pill and the "Models unavailable" banner have the same problem.

## User Impact

Every notice above the composer has the composer's own surface and hairline border, and its tone shows only in its icon (or, for notices without an icon, its text). The stack reads as one family on phone and desktop widths, in dark and light themes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The chat styles already say that composer neighbors keep a quiet card and that "status color belongs to the item, never to the surface". The goal pill, goal card and cloud disk space card follow that. This change moves the four outliers onto the same rule in CSS only:

- the status band (permission and other send-blocked reasons, composer errors): neutral surface, tone on the icon
- the model fallback pill: neutral surface, tone on the icon
- the microphone alert and the voice "Connecting" status inside the notice lane: neutral surface; the alert keeps its tone in its text since it has no icon
- the "Models unavailable" style banner above the composer: neutral surface and normal text

The status band's three per-tone fill rules are replaced by three icon-color rules, so the change is net smaller (+26/-20 lines, 152 bytes less minified CSS). No markup, component or test changes. Floating toasts and inline alerts elsewhere in the app are a separate surface and are not changed.

## Evidence

Screenshots come from the mocked Control UI (`dev:ui:mock --fixture goal --operator-scopes operator.read`, with the goal set to blocked). The first pair is the real page. The second pair adds the other notice kinds into the same composer lane using their real markup and English copy, so every kind is visible at once. prs.title: fix(doctor): stop suggesting doctor --fix for missing-binary skills
prs.body:
Fixes #201989

## What Problem This Solves

For a skill that is allowed but unavailable only because a local binary is missing, `openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/skills-readiness` recommended running `openclaw doctor --fix` to disable it. But `doctor --fix` intentionally preserves missing-binary skills — the binary may exist on a paired node (#178665) — so following the hint changes nothing and the warning returns on every run.

## User Impact

A user who follows the printed remediation for a missing-binary skill gets a command that intentionally does nothing, then sees the same warning again. The hint no longer offers a repair that cannot work: it now points at installing the binary or disabling the skill through the general per-skill control. Skills with other missing requirements (env/config/os) keep the existing `--fix` guidance, which still works for them.

## Why This Change Was Made

`unavailableSkillToFinding` in `src/flows/doctor-core-checks.ts` built one unconditional hint that recommended `doctor --fix` for every unavailable skill. The repair path (`src/commands/doctor-skills.ts`) preserves any skill whose `missing.bins` or `missing.anyBins` is non-empty, so the hint was misleading exactly for the binary case. The finding now branches: when a missing binary is involved the hint tells the user to install/configure the binary or disable the skill by setting `skills.entries.<key>.enabled` to false (noting paired-node preservation); otherwise it keeps the `--fix` recommendation.

The disable control is `skills.entries.<skillKey>.enabled` — the same path the finding already targets and the path `doctor --fix` writes (see the repair test). It is general: it does not require an allowlist to exist, and it applies to workspace skills, so it works in configurations where an allowlist removal would not (a follow-up review finding — the initial hint suggested removing the skill "from the allowlist", which is unavailable when no allowlist is configured and does not affect workspace skills).

## Evidence

### Discriminating regression (mock skills-readiness runtime)

`src/flows/doctor-core-checks.test.ts` builds two unavailable skills — one with a missing `bins` entry, one with a missing `env` entry — and asserts the binary finding's `fixHint` points at the binary and at `skills.entries.bin-gap.enabled`, mentions neither `doctor --fix` nor an allowlist, while the env finding keeps the `--fix` hint.

- Red on base (fix absent): `expected 'Install/configure the missing requirement, or run …'` fails the new assertion — 1 failed / 14 passed.
- Green on head: `src/flows/doctor-core-checks.test.ts` 15/15; adjacent `src/commands/doctor-skills.test.ts` 18/18.

### Real workspace skill through the shipped detection path (e2e)

The existing e2e `detects and repairs a real unavailable workspace skill` (`src/flows/doctor-core-checks.e2e.test.ts`) builds a real workspace skill whose metadata requires a missing binary, and drives it through `CORE_HEALTH_CHECKS.detect()` (the shipped production detection path) and `repair()`. Passes on head (1/1). This is real skill detection, not mocked skill state.

Additionally, I exercised the same production `detect()` path in an isolated workspace with two real skills — a missing-binary skill and an env-gap control — and captured the emitted findings:

```text

path: skills.entries.env-gap.enabled
message: env-gap is allowed but unavailable: env: SOME_REQUIRED_ENV.

```

```json
[
  {

    "category": "recommended",
    "docsUrl": "https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/skills",

  },
  {
    "checkId": "core/doctor/skills-readiness",

```

Before the fix, the missing-binary skill produced the same unconditional hint as the env control: `Install/configure the missing requirement, or run \`openclaw doctor --fix\` to disable unused unavailable skills.` (and the initial fix revision pointed at an allowlist removal, which the follow-up finding correctly rejected as unavailable in allowlist-free configurations).

### Shipped CLI terminal output (isolated `openclaw doctor --lint` session)

I built the PR head into a real CLI (`OpenClaw 2026.11.5`) and ran an isolated `openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/skills-readiness` session in a fresh HOME against the bundled skill catalog, capturing the terminal output. It reports 31 findings. Representative lines (7 of 31; the other 24 are structurally identical):


Across the full 31 findings, 29 missing-binary (or mixed binary+env) skills point at installing the binary or `skills.entries.<key>.enabled`; the 2 env-only skills (`openai-whisper-api`, `sherpa-onnx-tts`) keep the `--fix` guidance.

**Base control — same session against the shipped release CLI (`OpenClaw 2026.11.1`, without the fix):** all 31 findings, including every missing-binary skill, recommend `doctor --fix`:

```text

  fix: Install/configure the missing requirement, or run `openclaw doctor --fix` to disable unused unavailable skills.
```

### Honest scope of the proof

The `CORE_HEALTH_CHECKS.detect()` path above exercises the shipped production detector with real skills on disk, and the terminal output above is a real isolated `openclaw doctor --lint` session on the built CLI. The head build used the repository's `runtime` build profile, which skips the unrelated `worker-deploy` bundle step (an external Cloudflare-hosted fetch that the build container cannot reach through its corporate proxy); that step does not affect the Doctor lint path. The change is confined to the `fixHint` string produced by `unavailableSkillToFinding`; the discrimination test, the e2e, and the shipped CLI session all cover the branch.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/flows/doctor-core-checks.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 15/15 (head), 1 failed / 14 passed (base).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/doctor-skills.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 18/18.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/flows/doctor-core-checks.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 1/1 (real workspace skill, shipped detect + repair).
- Shipped CLI session — `openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/skills-readiness` on a head build (`OpenClaw 2026.11.5`): 29/31 findings use the corrected missing-binary hint, 2/31 (env-only) keep `--fix`; same session on the release CLI (`OpenClaw 2026.11.1`) shows 31/31 recommending `--fix` (see Evidence above).
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Format/lint: `oxfmt` and `oxlint` could not run in my local worktree (its node_modules is a symlink into another checkout; the format/lint tooling cannot resolve there). The change is a two-line string edit plus two assertion lines; `git diff --check` is clean, and CI runs oxfmt/oxlint.

## Scope and risk

- Production: `src/flows/doctor-core-checks.ts` (+9/−2). No new config, option, schema, migration, or persistence policy.
- The change only narrows when `--fix` is recommended and changes what the missing-binary hint suggests; it does not alter which skills `--fix` disables. Paired-node behavior and non-binary repair guidance are unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

Single-user Gateways showed a Users destination even when there was nobody else to find. Simply removing it on current main would also remove the way into Activity and eligible Remote access.

## User Impact

Users is hidden on confirmed single-user Gateways. Activity and eligible Remote access are in Pages instead. On multi-user Gateways the Users rail stays, including when everyone else is offline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing Gateway policy rather than online presence. A restored Users selection falls back to Sessions; if its rail button held keyboard focus, Sessions receives focus. The original change was reapplied to main after the sidebar rail was rewritten.

Focused sidebar tests and a production-build Chromium flow passed. The flow opens Activity and Remote access from Pages with the Users button hidden. The screenshots use the actual Control UI, dark desktop at 1100 × 760, with a synthetic solo Gateway. Before: `352cf811a87b6`. After: the reworked rail immediately before commit `19fc6fee3ca6c` moved the focus handoff into the sidebar controller; the focused regression passed on that commit. prs.title: feat: let plugins handle failed runs and show reporting receipts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugins cannot react to definitively failed runs or replace the fixed issue-report action with their own reporting result.

## User Impact

Plugins can observe committed terminal failures and show a named, linked reporting receipt beside the failure notice without creating another agent turn. Without a plugin, the existing report link remains unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the accepted lifecycle, existing failure receipt, plugin hook runner, and Control UI action registry. `run_failed` fires only for a newly committed terminal failure receipt; retries, Stop, yield, admission rejection, and incognito do not leak into reporting callbacks. External plugins require conversation-access permission.

Virtual receipts use literal text, safe links, the registered plugin identity and admitted icon. Reporting policy, storage, deduplication and recovery stay in the plugin. Delivery is best-effort, not a new durable queue. No Team-specific behavior is added to core.

## Evidence

- Native UI action/fallback/runtime tests: 48 passed.
- Chromium failure notice and receipt tests: 6 passed, including inspected real component captures.
- Failure recorder tests: 9 passed.
- Regression failed against the original hardcoded report-link renderer and passed with the extension.
- Gateway regression suites: 93 passed before the explicit `appended` storage-field repair; affected appender and hook tests passed after that repair.
- Extracted hook/observer coverage: 25 passed (8 real SQLite/Gateway tests and 17 plugin tests).
- Final storage-owner regression suites: 29 passed. The new memory-owner public-entry regression failed before the fix and passed after it, including duplicate-append suppression.
- Final isolated transcript UI suite: 22 passed.
- Core and Control UI production typechecks: passed with task-owned frozen dependencies.
- Touched core type-aware lint, touched UI lint, and changed stylesheet lint: passed; UI lint reports non-failing advisory warnings.
- Full `pnpm build`: passed, including Control UI and plugin SDK declarations. Bundle-budget warnings were advisory; their baseline attribution has not been established.
- Targeted format, `git diff --check`, native pre-commit formatting and line-cap guard: passed.
- Local autoreview against base `a139d420834e6e04641303c79eb7c6e0e4444fa5`, P0–P2: the last review returned exit 1 for three stale-index defects while confirming their working-tree fixes. Those fixes are committed in `72e0ae9ad9e88568a993e606f522d44e43315bdd`. No additional P0–P2 findings were established in the combined candidate. This was static review, not an independent test run.

### Actual component captures

Dark-theme Chromium component proof with synthetic plugin state; not a full live Gateway/model run. Before/after images are embedded and visually verified here, and were also delivered in the originating chat.

**Before**

![Before: built-in failure report action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f98d53b-8b12-49d6-9bdb-a387c679fedd)

**After**

**Remaining qualification:** marked ready after local build and focused checks passed; required exact-head CI is not yet verified. Full live-model Gateway proof has not been run; component and production-boundary tests are the current behavior evidence. The separate Team-specific plugin implementation is not part of this PR. No live configuration or deployment was changed.

prs.title: feat: let /codex review target a branch, commit or custom instructions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/codex review` can only review uncommitted changes. Native Codex `/review` can also review changes against a base branch, review one commit, or run a review with custom instructions, and the bundled Codex app-server already accepts all four `review/start` targets. OpenClaw always sent `uncommittedChanges`, and any argument to `/codex review` returned usage.

## User Impact

`/codex review` gains the native review targets:

- `/codex review` reviews uncommitted changes, as before.
- `/codex review --base <branch>` reviews changes against a base branch.
- `/codex review --commit <sha>` reviews one commit (7–40 hexadecimal characters).
- `/codex review <instructions>` starts a review with free-text instructions. Only a leading `--base` or `--commit` selects a target, so instructions such as `check the --force handling` or Markdown `-` bullets reach Codex as written.

Codex resolves branches and commits in the attached thread's checkout, which can differ from the Gateway's workspace. The chat reply still confirms only that the review started; it does not include the findings (unchanged, and tracked separately).

## Why This Change Was Made

- Parse the target once at command entry into a discriminated union matching the four app-server `ReviewTarget` variants, and send it as `review/start`'s `target`.
- Custom instructions come from the normalized argument tail, so spacing inside the instructions is kept instead of rejoined from tokens. For `--base` and `--commit`, unterminated quotes, missing or extra values, both selectors together and malformed SHAs return usage without an RPC or binding read, so a mistyped ref such as `--base rachel's-fix` cannot silently become `rachels-fix`. The shared argument tokenizer used by other `/codex` commands returns the same tokens as before; it only reports whether a quote was left open.
- Argument-bearing reviews previously returned usage before the native authorization and sandbox checks. Valid targets now pass through the same owner/`operator.admin` and sandbox checks as other native Codex commands; invalid ones still return usage only.
- The acknowledgment names the target and does not echo custom instructions.

## Evidence

Failing before the implementation, at test commit `02025915` (`pnpm test extensions/codex/src/command-handler-args.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`):

```text
Tests  20 failed (20)
```

An independent review of that implementation found that prose containing `--` words was rejected and that malformed quoting could change the branch. Its regressions failed on `52a0131b` (`Tests  10 failed | 20 passed (30)`), for example sending `"branch": "rachels-fix"`, and pass on `9ae9df85`.

Each new target reported `Number of calls: 0`. The authorization case expected `Only an owner or operator.admin can control Codex native execution.` and the sandbox case expected `Codex-native /codex review is unavailable because OpenClaw sandboxing is active for this session.`; both received `Usage: /codex review`.

After the fix: the new file passes 30/30, including a non-owner `operator.admin` review and a native rejection that produces no success reply, and `commands.test.ts` passes 96/96, including the existing default uncommitted-changes review. Adjacent command suites pass (157 tests in total). Scoped `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json`, `oxfmt` and the line-cap ratchet pass.

A real pinned Codex 0.169.0 app-server, started in an isolated home without credentials, decoded `review/start` for all four target shapes, including `commit` without `title`; each returned `thread not found` for the probe thread ID. No model review was run.

Not established locally: the repository typecheck wrapper refuses this checkout because declarations resolve into the shared pnpm store; CI runs it and passes.

`0933989d` adds an exhaustive `never` default to `formatStartedCodexReview` after CI's type-aware oxlint flagged `consistent-return`. Type-aware oxlint reproduced that error locally on `085db92a` and reports 0 errors after the fix; the 126 Codex command tests still pass.

### Live proof: `/codex review` targets

**PASS** on `0933989d3200a747bd77e79dd2c0f3c34e20dc9f` (tree `a81e37c508ed8e4f9fe1f54808425d21d9df13a0`). The candidate ran from a clean sibling checkout with the identical full Git tree and installed lockfile dependencies. The native macOS arm64 executable from the plugin’s pinned `@openai/codex` platform package reported `codex-cli 0.169.0`. The isolated app-server reported `account/read → chatgpt`; `thread/start` reported `gpt-6.2-sol`. No API key, mock app-server, or live Gateway was used.

**Reproduction.** Create a throwaway Git repo on `main` containing `port.py` with `parse_port(value)` returning `int(value)`. On `feature`, commit a change that catches `ValueError` and incorrectly returns `0`. In scratch state, use the production app-server client to start a fresh ephemeral thread in that repo for each accepted case (read-only, approval policy `never`). Save each returned thread ID in the production Codex binding store, using the plugin’s conversation-binding data and an in-memory state adapter. Call the registered `createCodexCommand(...).handler` with each argument string and that binding. Forward stdio unchanged to the pinned native app-server and capture the outbound `review/start` frame, its matching response, and the notifications for the same thread and turn. For the negative baseline, use the same registered handler with the four runtime modules that differ replaced by their verified Git blobs from `0167852c1cfca5334fbc04ae29bbc13830b68495` (the only other diffs are docs and a test).

**Observed output** (thread IDs replaced with `<thread>`; the SHA is from the synthetic repo):

| Command | Actual chat reply | Actual `review/start` params |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/codex review --base main` | `Started Codex review of changes against main for thread <thread>.` | `{"threadId":"<thread>","target":{"type":"baseBranch","branch":"main"}}` |
| `/codex review --commit 8e0d7e0d5feb4ef8420bcd8e57853f243601a281` | `Started Codex review of commit 8e0d7e0d5feb4ef8420bcd8e57853f243601a281 for thread <thread>.` | `{"threadId":"<thread>","target":{"type":"commit","sha":"8e0d7e0d5feb4ef8420bcd8e57853f243601a281"}}` |
| `/codex review focus on error handling` | `Started Codex review with custom instructions for thread <thread>.` | `{"threadId":"<thread>","target":{"type":"custom","instructions":"focus on error handling"}}` |
| `/codex review --base "main` | `Usage: /codex review [--base <branch> \| --commit <sha> \| <instructions>]` | None |
| `/codex review --base main` on baseline `0167852c` | `Usage: /codex review` | None |

Exactly three `review/start` requests were captured. Each returned `turn.status: inProgress` and the same `reviewThreadId` sent in the request. For **each matching turn**, the app-server then emitted `item/completed → enteredReviewMode`, `item/completed → exitedReviewMode`, and `turn/completed → completed` with no error. The three exit items contained review text of 668, 618, and 716 characters respectively; each mentioned the synthetic `port.py` fixture.

Independent review: READY at `9ae9df85` (two rounds; dash-prefixed instructions and malformed ref quoting were fixed). Local ClawSweeper on `52a0131b`: patch C, proof F (no live attached-thread run); its finding is the dash-prefixed instructions issue fixed in `9ae9df85`.

The approach is rebased onto current `main` and additionally proves that the policy applies to isolated agent-run announcements through the shared delivery append path. ## Behavior - `always`: include Control UI `Inspect` links on successful completion announcements and failure alerts (backward-compatible default). - `errors`: include links only on failure alerts. - `never`: omit links from both successful completion announcements and failure alerts. - Applies to isolated/direct cron completion delivery, successful completion announcements, failure alerts, and isolated agent-run announcements that share `sendCronAnnouncePayloadStrict`. - Webhook delivery is unchanged; prs.title: feat: block guest invites until the role's sandbox can start
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw ID is on, the built-in `guest` role requires a sandbox for its sessions, even if the Gateway has no working sandbox (agent sandbox mode is off and the Docker image was never built). Owners could still invite people as guests or move members to that role. Every turn those guests started then failed with a generic "Your request couldn't be completed." The cause, `Sandbox image not found: openclaw-sandbox:trixie-slim`, appeared only in the Gateway logs. The fix that error suggested, `openclaw doctor --fix`, did not build the image either, because Doctor ignored sandboxing that only a role requires.

## User Impact

A role can still require a sandbox before sandboxing is set up, but the Gateway won't grant it until the sandbox can start. On the **Access** page, these roles are disabled in the invite and **Change role** pickers ("Sandbox required · not set up yet"). A notice says in plain words what is missing, such as "Docker isn't running on the computer that hosts this claw" or "Its sandbox isn't installed on this claw yet", and never shows commands. **Ask OpenClaw to set it up** starts a conversation with the owner's default agent, docked beside the page. That agent receives the facts the Gateway reported, says what it will change, and then sets up the sandbox. **Check again** re-reads readiness afterward. Inviting someone to the role or changing a member to it through the API fails with `sandbox_unavailable`. Existing members keep their role. `openclaw doctor` now reports a missing engine or image for them and offers to build the default image when only a role requires sandboxing.

## Why This Change Was Made

A configured role is not the problem; granting it before its sandbox can start is. So the check runs where access is granted: when an invite is registered and when a member's role changes. The Access page runs the same check when it loads. A role is ready when every agent it can use has a reachable Docker or Podman backend and that agent's sandbox image is present. This also covers per-agent image overrides, which `agents.defaults.sandbox.mode` alone never showed: role-required sandboxes apply even when mode is `off`. Backends the Gateway cannot check (SSH or plugin backends) do not block. The check runs once per grant on the authority's write queue, after the owner's signature is verified. That keeps grants in arrival order and keeps forged statements away from the engine. Each engine probe is limited to 10 seconds, so a hung Docker daemon delays a sandbox-role grant briefly instead of blocking membership writes indefinitely.

Setup goes to the owner's agent rather than to a new Gateway action or a docs link. The agent can already start a container engine, build images, and run Doctor on the claw, and it covers every case, including a stopped engine or a custom image, without putting CLI commands in the UI. This replaces the earlier non-blocking warning on the invite form, which pointed at a docs index. That warning checked only whether the default engine answered, so it stayed silent when Docker was running but the image was missing, which is the case that broke.

Accepted edge cases:
- Approving a request on an invite created before the sandbox broke is not re-checked.
- Readiness can change after a grant, so a later image removal still fails at session start.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway on the Mac Studio (Crabbox `local-container` lease, `node:24.22.1-trixie`).** Each run used an isolated Gateway with OpenClaw ID on and the stock `guest` preset (`sandbox: "required"`, agent sandbox mode off), plus a linked synthetic claw. A real Chromium browser held the owner device key, and the Studio's Docker engine was reached through the mounted socket. Before = `main` at `fc58825c81bd`; after = this PR at `45f45ab769be` (Gateway enforcement unchanged since; later commits change the notice copy and add the handoff).

Scenario: Docker is reachable but `openclaw-sandbox:trixie-slim` is missing, with the role picker open on the invite form. Wide captures are stacked, Before then After.

### Clean comparison

**Before (`main`):** guest can be selected.

![Before: on main, the guest role is selectable in the invite role picker although its sandbox image is missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0630f1c2-9642-485a-a721-abe7dad05ce3)

**After (this PR):** guest is disabled and marked "not set up on this claw".

![After: the guest role is disabled in the invite role picker and described as sandbox required, not set up on this claw](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e150e71b-00bd-4f90-8579-537c03fe7c8d)

### Annotated comparison

![Before, annotated: guest option outlined as selectable while the sandbox image is missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4082035e-768a-4b70-bf93-fd148cefdfe2)

![After, annotated: guest option outlined as disabled because the sandbox is not set up](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d69ddf32-e0f7-4297-be69-3d6320185942)

With the picker closed, the invite form explains what is missing and offers the handoff to OpenClaw. This frame is from the Access layout e2e with a mocked Gateway, after the setup handoff landed at `79df064f644d`:

![After: invite form notice says the guest role needs a sandbox, its sandbox isn't installed on this claw yet, with an Ask OpenClaw to set it up button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/91f5fd0c-feca-49f9-9087-8522a6d47dd8)


| Scenario (after) | Access page | Invite / role change through the Gateway API |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No Docker CLI | guest disabled, notice: Docker is not running | `sandbox_unavailable` |
| Docker reachable, `openclaw-sandbox:trixie-slim` missing | guest disabled, notice: sandbox not installed | invite and `set_role` refused, `sandbox_unavailable` |
| Custom image present (set via `openclaw config set`, no restart) | guest enabled; invite created through the UI | invite and `set_role` applied; member moved to guest |

Before (`main`), the same missing-image setup accepted the guest invite and the role change.

`openclaw doctor --non-interactive` with only the guest role requiring a sandbox now reports: `Sandbox base image missing: openclaw-sandbox:trixie-slim. Run openclaw doctor --fix to build it…`.

Focused tests:
- Authority: refuses guest invites and `set_role` when the image is missing, and accepts both once it exists; a forged `set_role` is refused on its signature without probing the engine. Fails on `main`.
- Readiness: per-agent images, Docker and Podman, mode off, unverifiable backends, and naming Doctor only for the image Doctor actually builds.
- Doctor: image repair when only a role requires a sandbox; Codex namespace checks still follow sandbox mode.
- Access UI: disabled roles, kept explicit selection, disabled submit, no commands in the notice, the Ask and Check again actions, and the real-browser Access layout e2e.
- Setup handoff: creates a docked conversation with the default agent and sends the reported problem, or opens the conversation when there is no dock.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

- `pnpm test src/gateway/openclaw-id/ src/commands/doctor-member-roles.test.ts src/commands/doctor-sandbox.warns-sandbox-enabled-without-docker.test.ts extensions/openclaw-id-access/browser/*.test.ts* ui/src/e2e/access-member-layout.e2e.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `oxlint` on changed files
- `pnpm ui:i18n:check` reports catalog drift on `main` as well; new English strings are translated by the regular i18n sync.

</details>

prs.title: fix(models): honor --yes when re-running GitHub Copilot login
prs.body:
## Problem

`openclaw models auth login-github-copilot --yes` is documented to overwrite
an existing profile without prompting (`docs/cli/models.md`), but the flag
never reaches the provider auth flow: `models-cli.ts` forwards `yes` to
`modelsAuthLoginCommand`, `runModelsAuthLoginFlow` carries it, and then
`runProviderAuthMethod` calls `runProviderPluginAuthMethodUnpersisted`
without `opts` — so the Copilot method always asks
"GitHub Copilot auth already exists. Re-run login?" with **No** as the
default, and pressing Enter keeps the old token.

Fixes #202003

## Solution

- Add an explicit `overwriteExisting?: boolean` to `ProviderAuthOptionBag`
  (`src/plugins/provider-auth-types.ts`), the documented channel for CLI
  flags into provider auth methods.
- `runProviderAuthMethod` (`src/commands/models/auth.ts`) now passes
  `opts: { overwriteExisting: true }` when the login was started with
  `--yes`. Without `--yes` no `opts` is passed, so the existing prompt
  behavior is unchanged.
- The Copilot device auth (`extensions/github-copilot/index.ts`) skips the
  re-run confirmation when `ctx.opts?.overwriteExisting` is set and starts
  the device flow directly. The domain-change path is untouched: a tenant
  switch still forces a fresh login.

## Test evidence

New regression tests (red on base, green with the fix):

- `extensions/github-copilot/index.test.ts` — "re-runs login without
  prompting when overwriteExisting is set": existing same-tenant profile +
  `opts: { overwriteExisting: true }` starts the device flow, `prompter.confirm`
  is never called, and the fresh token profile is returned. On base the test
  fails: the flow reuses the stored token and never opens the device flow.
- `src/commands/models/auth.test.ts` — "forwards --yes as overwriteExisting
  to the provider login method" and "leaves provider login opts unset
  without --yes".

Full suites: `extensions/github-copilot/index.test.ts` + 
`src/commands/models/auth.test.ts` — 80/80 passed.
`tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, oxlint, oxfmt — all green.
`auth.test.ts` gained the repo-standard trailing
`oxlint-disable max-lines` comment: the two new tests pushed it past the
1000-line limit (pre-existing size, not new logic).

## Test note addressed (1e1db000a)
The two option-bag assertions in `src/commands/models/auth.test.ts` are replaced by a command-to-Copilot behavioral regression: the fake provider models the Copilot reuse decision — with `--yes` the fresh credential is persisted, without it the stored credential is retained — so the tests assert the observable outcome instead of the mock call shape.
Verification on this head (local): red/green checked (with the `--yes` forwarding disabled the new `--yes` test fails); full `auth.test.ts` file passes (40 tests); `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean.
Still outstanding: the real-behavior proof (TTY run showing `--yes` skips the confirmation, completes device authentication, and persists the replacement credential) needs a real GitHub device flow.

prs.title: fix: let admins suspend OpenClaw ID members and use one role for everyone
prs.body:
Closes #201526 (parts A–C; part D is in a separate PR)

## What Problem This Solves

People who reach a claw through OpenClaw ID were governed by a second role system. Their membership role decided what they could do, separately from the Gateway profile role that every other sign-in route uses. Because of this, admins couldn't suspend a member, @mention invitations judged members by the wrong role, and the same person could have different permissions depending on how they connected.

## User Impact

User impact: an OpenClaw ID member's permissions now come from their Gateway profile role, the same as everyone else's.

- **Admins and the owner can change or clear a member's role** with **People** or `users.setRole`. The member's connections close, and their queued and steered input, subagents, automations and recovered work stop immediately. New requests are checked against the new role. A single request that was already admitted is allowed to finish, matching #201334.
- **@mention invitations** of members now work and use the member's real role.
- **No role means no access, for members.** A member whose resolved role is missing or deny-all is refused at connect instead of connecting with nothing. A role catalog (`gateway.roles.definitions`) is enforced for OpenClaw ID members even without `gateway.roles.default`.
- **Gateways without OpenClaw ID members are unchanged.** For everyone who is not a current, linked OpenClaw ID member — local owners, shared-token/password clients, trusted-proxy (Tailscale-style) and Cloudflare Access identities — named-role enforcement still starts only when `gateway.roles.default` is set, exactly as on `main`. A healthy profile whose connection grant is empty keeps the existing scope-upgrade path. The one-time member role import only runs while `gateway.openclawId.enabled` is on.
- **Upgrade:** each existing member's current membership role is copied to their profile once, only when the profile has no explicit assignment, so nobody's access changes on upgrade. Saved automations, queued and restart work recorded before the upgrade are updated to the imported role in the same step, but only when their recorded permissions match; mismatched saved work is still refused.
- **Unchanged:**
  - Owner devices keep full owner authority, including device-token reconnects. A profile role never limits an owner device, and removing its certificate still ends its work.
  - Owner sign-in keeps working on personal Gateways that define roles without a default: setup-code pairing, browser-code pairing, owner ingress and MCP owner consent.
  - Nodes keep no operator scopes.
  - Removing a member works as before.
  - The membership role remains as the label shown on Access and in the loader.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw ID is meant to provide connectivity, with the Gateway as the source of truth for authorization. Members now resolve through their linked profile on the same path as every other identified person. Invite approval and Access role changes write the profile role, and the Gateway publishes the effective role name to Discovery as a label. This removes the member-specific special cases that each profile-based check previously had to remember.

## Evidence

**Compatibility matrix (written first, red on the previous head, now green):** a real-Gateway matrix of 31 cells — local owner, shared token/password, trusted-proxy identity, Cloudflare Access identity, OpenClaw ID member, and a member who also connects through a trusted proxy — against no roles, definitions only, definitions plus a default, and an explicit `users.setRole` assignment. Every non-member cell matches `main` (connect result, effective scopes, visible sessions, sending a turn, HTTP owner attribution, owner Web Push); member cells with definitions only are enforced.

**Enforcement scope, per call site:** all 27 production callers of the enforcement switch were classified. Callers that know the person (session sharing, tool invocation, cron admission, channel authority, HTTP/WS profile preparation, device pairing, push targets, PR-read capture, companion RPC, cron wake) resolve a per-person decision: enforce when `roles.default` is set **or** the stored profile is a current linked OpenClaw ID member. Callers without a person (global Web Push broadcast, kernel prewarm, visitor-access eligibility, doctor/CLI notes, anonymous pairing preflight) keep the `roles.default`-only rule. Device-token issuance re-checks membership immediately before credentials are delivered.

Real-Gateway tests with members connecting through OpenClaw ID:

- **@mention invitations** of `sessions.others: "invited"` members succeed in all three enforcement modes (enforcement off, permissive default, denying default), and the invited member sees only the invited session.
- **Demotion or clearing** by an admin and by the owner closes tunnel connections and stops in-flight runs, queued and steered input, subagent, automation and recovered work. Owner devices stay connected.
- **Reconnecting with no role** is refused.
- **Upgrade:** the role is imported once, survives a restart, and isn't re-imported after a role is cleared. Concurrent assignments are never overwritten, and repeat invitations assign their role.
- **Discovery labels** stay current across an OpenClaw ID off/on toggle and same-second snapshots.

Independent reviews found these issues, all fixed with regression tests:
- a missing role catalog granting uncapped access
- repeat invitations not assigning a role
- the upgrade overwriting a concurrent role assignment
- local iOS devices losing approval pushes
- the role-label publisher lost when OpenClaw ID was turned off and on
- delayed label publication
- an HTTP profile check that let requests through when it should have refused them
- MCP consent treating a signed-in person as the owner
- saved member work recorded before the upgrade being refused after the role import
- role changes aborting already-admitted single requests (#201334)
- saved sandbox-stream automations not migrated with the imported role
- question producers and their waiting native callers outliving a role change
- catalog-only enforcement reaching Gateways without OpenClaw ID members (now member-scoped, see the matrix above)
- zero-scope connections refused even for healthy non-member profiles
- owner HTTP attribution and owner Web Push lost on definitions-only config
- the member role import running while OpenClaw ID was disabled
- a device token issued while the holder's membership was changing
- publication-requester, cron owner and OpenClaw ID inert-service test fixtures that had not been updated for the profile-catalog contract, and an unsorted worker registration entry
- Doctor no longer warning about inactive non-member role assignments without a default (restored, #197785)
- member automation test fixtures not following main's plan-first automation creation
- the PostgreSQL publication conformance fixture not preparing the profile catalog (verified against PostgreSQL 17 for all four engine combinations)

The latest review found no P0–P2 issues.

CI and ClawSweeper also caught tests still written for the old rule, where the membership role took precedence, plus a few real regressions. All of them are fixed:
- owner device-token reconnects were refused
- owner authority was missing from saved publication snapshots
- "role changed" revocations fired when the role had not changed
- browser-code pairing was refused on personal Gateways that only define roles, where it is meant to keep working
- MCP owner consent was refused on those same Gateways
- removing an owner device's certificate no longer cancelled that owner's recovered work
- a mid-request permission re-check broke the repo rule that authority is checked once when a request starts

To stop finding these one CI round at a time, every test file that references membership roles or the membership ceiling was run locally: 1,614 tests across 91 files pass. They ran in several batches, not one green run. After merging current main (including #201713's recovery-policy checks, now part of the profile-recovery suite), 232 tests across 20 files pass. The latest repair passes 274 tests across 27 files, with the suspension tests unchanged. The member-only scope correction was verified across all 317 test files that reference roles plus 5 regression files (4,734 passing cases); two failures there reproduce identically on the merge base (a cross-device Stop timeout and a restart-marker assertion) and 24 opt-in live-provider, PostgreSQL and Docker cases were skipped. Typecheck, lint, format, line limits and the lifetime-check limit all pass.

**Test-line allocation:** this PR adds 4,037 net test lines: the standard allowance of 400 plus 3,637 recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/201526-oid-role-unify.txt`. The extra lines cover:
- real-Gateway suspension and invitation flows
- the one-time role upgrade and its persistence
- recovered work, including owner-certificate and member cut-offs
- HTTP and WebSocket connection checks
- owner-device, owner-pairing and MCP owner/person isolation
- saved work surviving the upgrade: pre-upgrade sources read back, storage reopened, queued and restart work restored, a matching automation run and a mismatched one refused
- question producers, waiting callers and Goal runs being cut off on role loss while admitted single requests finish
- the 31-cell compatibility matrix proving non-member Gateways behave as on `main`, plus membership-fenced credential issuance

These are new security behaviors that had no existing tests to extend.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/gateway/server.openclaw-id-session-invite.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server.openclaw-id-member-suspension.test.ts \
  src/gateway/openclaw-id/member-profile-role-recovery.test.ts \
  src/gateway/openclaw-id/member-profiles.persistence.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server.auth.openclaw-id-tunnel.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

Also run: every test file referencing membership roles or the membership ceiling, the previously failing CI suites, and the openclaw-id service, publisher, role-presets, role-policy, users, doctor member-roles, browser pairing and Access plugin suites.

</details>
