prs.title: fix(ui): keep assistant answers out of the collapsed Worked fold
prs.body:
Related: #180490

## What Problem This Solves

On main, a completed Control UI turn collapses into one "Worked" line, and that line swallows **about a third of Claude's answers** (and those of other models that don't label commentary) along with the tools.

The fold hides every assistant text group that is not the run's last reply, unless the provider labels it as commentary. So an answer followed by any tool call (saving a note, updating a file) is hidden, and only the short closing line stays visible. A steered run that produces two replies shows only the last one.

This affects **every model that does not label its commentary**, not just Claude: as far as we know, everything except OpenAI models. Fresh GLM-5.3 Flash and DeepSeek v4.1 Flash runs on current code store their text with no phase label (examples below). Claude is where it shows most, because it routinely answers and then calls a tool to record the result.

## Why This Change Was Made

`isCollapsibleWorkGroup` treated every unphased assistant text group as completed work unless it owned the turn's final reply. That is a guess: an absent phase is unknown, not commentary, and `toolUse` is an execution stop reason, not a narration label (Claude often answers and then calls a tool to record the result).

The runtime prompt added in #159416 (refined in #178108) tells models that "Commentary is optional progress and may be hidden" and asks them to repeat every pending answer in the final response. That works for providers that tag commentary natively (OpenAI): their commentary really is throwaway progress, and the answer carries a final-answer label, so important messages stay visible.

It cannot help models that do not tag commentary, or streamed turns with no definitive final answer. The instruction does not create phase labels, so the UI still cannot tell an answer from progress, and generation ending or a later tool call does not establish that earlier text was commentary. Unlabeled text must not be folded on that assumption, hence this change.

The change adds one guard: an assistant text-only group is collapsible only when every message in it resolves to explicit `commentary` through the existing `resolveAssistantReplyPhase` (provider phase, text signatures, keyed stream-fallback commentary). Everything else is unchanged: one Worked line per turn, the same partition and ownership logic, tools and reasoning still fold, and providers that label commentary (OpenAI/Codex, Muse Spark) fold exactly as before. No CSS, renderer or layout change.

**Intentional change to existing behavior.** Main currently treats any assistant text without a phase label as narration and folds it. That assumption holds for providers that tag commentary natively, such as OpenAI, which is what the existing tests and runtime prompt (#159416, #178108) are built around. It does not hold for providers that never send a phase, where it hides real answers (34% in the replay below). This PR deliberately reverses that default. Maintainer sign-off on this behavior change is requested.

Key points for review:
- **An absent phase is unknown, not commentary.** Folding is now driven only by an explicit commentary label (provider phase, text signature, or keyed stream fallback), never by a missing one.
- **Natively tagged providers are unchanged.** OpenAI/Codex (and Muse Spark) commentary folds exactly as before.
- **OpenClaw's own rows still fold.** Host-generated assistant rows (provider `openclaw`, e.g. publication receipts) are identified with the existing `isTranscriptArtifactProvider` and fold as on main; only model-authored text is affected.
- **Layout is unchanged.** One Worked line per turn, the same rows in the same positions; every tool call still folds, and expanding Worked shows rows in transcript order.
- **Prompt guidance cannot substitute for labels.** Asking models to keep commentary throwaway does not give the UI a way to tell an untagged answer from progress.

## User Impact

**Hidden answers go from about 1 in 3 to zero.** The Worked line still collapses only the work: same count, same positions, every tool call still inside it. Expanding it shows tools between the answers they came between, as on main.

Trade-off: short unlabeled status lines (for example "Build passed; tests running now.") are now visible too, in their chronological place, for models that do not natively tag their commentary.

## Evidence

| Measure | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Answers hidden in the collapsed fold (1,474 sampled text blocks, two blind classifiers) | **34%** (25% if status lines count as narration) | **0%** |
| Turns that hide at least one answer | about **1 in 5** | **0** |
| Unlabeled assistant text blocks hidden (962 sessions, presentation replay) | 4,874 | **0** |
| Worked rows (same replay) | 3,483 | 3,483, **zero** differences in position, key, reply owner or duration |
| Tool cards inside Worked | 35,164 | 35,164 |
| Rows revealed, rendered A/B in the real Control UI (979 sessions) | | **4,051** across 432 sessions |
| Previously visible rows lost / sessions gone blank | | **0 / 0** |
| Expanded rows: same IDs and text, by session | | **979 / 979** |

**Method.** Every Claude Code session on one workstation (about 3 Oct to 11 Nov 2026) was replayed through main's real history import and presentation code (`840105308d2`, default View settings), then rendered on two otherwise identical scratch Gateways with and without this change. *Answer* means text that tells the user something (a result, explanation, decision, question or status), even if it also says what happens next.

**Screenshots** (synthetic conversation, same data and settings on both builds).

One streamed turn: three long answers between tool batches, ending with a notes-file write.

| | Main | This PR |

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Web-fetch contract fixtures duplicate the registry's credential projection and choose the public-artifact route outside the registry owner. That leaves two places responsible for loading the same contract providers.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible change. Bundled web-fetch contract tests keep their lazy loading, provider IDs, credential assertions, and runtime fallback behavior. No public SDK signature or production provider contract changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing artifact-first path into the contract registry and let the fixture helper delegate to it. A successful empty artifact result remains valid; a missing artifact still reaches the same scoped runtime fallback and propagates its errors.

This maintainer-requested cleanup removes 10 net lines from the helper/registry code. One focused registry regression adds 38 net test lines, so the total diff grows by 28 lines; shared contract assertions remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Independent full source/test review accepted signed head `71077c3d5109a2c0e3bc9575fe8a53088aa0ea09`, based on `58dbe4055043f7c090a03b3c8a610a9e521e3452`.
- Normal formatter, signed commit hook, and diff checks pass. Exactly three files changed.
- Original-head native isolated proof passed 67 cases across four files: web-fetch contracts, registry retry/fallback, public artifacts, and shared provider contracts. This includes the new fixed fixture's lazy loading, independent credential expectation, and propagated runtime refusal after an artifact miss.
- The complete native test command took 61.35s wall, 50.03s user and 36.68s system time, including dependency bootstrap; two Vitest shards took 35.58s. This is command cost, not a performance comparison.
- Original-head nine scoped static checks passed: core, SDK-test and plugin-platform-test types; changed production/test lint; format; SDK exports; web-fetch boundaries; test-line ratchet.
- Normal isolated bootstrap completed in 7.7s: 1,482 package archives reused and zero package-archive downloads; the Matrix 0.6.6 postinstall separately downloaded its public platform binary. No install occurred in an authored checkout or through shared dependencies.
- The original [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44679806971) failed its mock-exports ratchet: the new fetch mock omitted the real module's other exports. The correction uses typed async `importOriginal`, spreads the real exports, and overrides only the fetch resolver. No baseline exception or assertion change was made.
- Correction proof passed the previously failing mock-exports checker (8.561s), all 22 affected tests across registry retry and public artifacts (26.943s whole command), plugin-platform test types, test lint, format, and the line ratchet. The compiler cache miss (1.387s) is included in the observed command cost. All commands exited successfully and settled.

The correction retains the original production change and all lazy/artifact-first/runtime-fallback assertions. Native correction review and GitHub-mode preparation passed. The corrected head's [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44682268934) passed, including the formerly failing baseline-ratchets job; both required CI gate surfaces and selected security checks succeeded.

prs.title: fix(sessions): scope orphan lifecycle sweep to the cleanup's session-key prefix
prs.body:
Fixes #202134

## Problem

Plugin helper-session cleanup (`planSessionLifecycleArtifactCleanup`) rescans
every orphan transcript in the store on each call: `readOrphanWindowPage`
paged through all orphan windows and read each one's `transcript_events`
JSON to check its marker, ignoring the cleanup's own
`sessionKeySegmentPrefix`. With many unrelated orphans the sweep held the
session writer for 8–13 s, so finished Active Memory recalls timed out and
other sessions' writes queued behind it. Non-matching orphans were never
deleted, so every call rescanned them again.

## Fix

- `readOrphanWindowPage` now takes the cleanup's `sessionKeySegmentPrefix`
  and filters at the SQL layer (`sessionKeySegmentStartsWithSql`, mirroring
  the existing `sessionKeySegmentStartsWith` predicate: the segment is the
  key after its second colon, or the whole key when there is no second
  colon). SQLite uses `instr`, PostgreSQL uses `strpos`.
- `planSqliteOrphanLifecycleTranscriptStateDeletes` requires
  `sessionKeySegmentPrefix` and keeps the exact JavaScript predicate per row
  as a second check; `planSessionLifecycleArtifactCleanupPages` threads the
  prefix through to both the first orphan page and the sweep.
- Other callers (dreaming cleanup, same prefix) are unaffected: they pass
  their own segment prefix and the sweep now only scans their window.

## Tests

- New regression `scopes the orphan marker sweep to the cleanup's own
  session-key prefix`: 1 in-scope orphan + 129 out-of-scope orphans;
  only the in-scope orphan is marker-scanned
  (`diagnostics.markerWindows` 1, `diagnostics.windowRows` 1) and deleted
  with the victim entry. Fails on the base (sweep scans all 130 windows).
- Existing paging test updated so its seeded orphans belong to the
  cleanup's own prefix (`unrelated-history`); PostgreSQL lifecycle test
  seeds `pg-` windows and passes `pg-` as the prefix.
- `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-artifact-planning.test.ts`
  and `session-accessor.sqlite-lifecycle-artifacts.postgres.test.ts`:
  8 tests passed (PostgreSQL suite skipped without a mixed connection),
  re-run after the oxlint-driven `.sort()` → `.toSorted()` fix in the new
  test.
- `tsgo:core`, oxlint (3 files), oxfmt (3 files): clean.

## Fix for Codex review (b971f3cbb)
The P2 finding is addressed: the shared orphan inventory no longer filters by the cleanup's session-key segment prefix by default, restoring the marker-based reclamation contract from #165254 and #182245. Prefix scoping is now an explicit opt-in (`scopeOrphanSweepToSessionKeySegmentPrefix`), used only by the Active Memory recall cleanup — the foreground helper teardown from #202134. Dreaming cleanup and maintenance reclamation keep cross-prefix behavior, and the SQLite/PostgreSQL fixtures are back to their original cross-prefix seeds.
Verification on this head (local):
- `session-accessor.sqlite-artifact-planning.test.ts` + `extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts`: 96 passed (scoped-sweep planner test asserts both the opt-in, 1 marker-scanned window, and the default, all 130 reclaimed).
- `session-accessor.sqlite-cleanup-race.test.ts` (untouched cleanup-reclamation regression): 18 passed.
- `oxfmt --check` on all 11 touched files: clean.

prs.title: fix: keep automation timing separate from run status
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The automation editor puts live messages like “No next run scheduled” beside the date you configured. They look like part of the schedule, even when they describe a retry or an automation waiting to run.

## User Impact

The tray shows only the configured timing and, where supported, the model and reasoning. On phones the timing controls use their own block just below the composer. A saved one-shot’s distinct run status appears under the automation title; validation sits just below the tray. The configured schedule and save behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the settings people can edit separate from live execution. Reuse the same frequency picker for event and process-exit schedules without creating new process commands. Keep the configured time zone with the schedule, and omit a redundant status when the next activity merely repeats the date already shown.

## Evidence

211 automation UI tests and 3 focused Chromium tests passed, including saving an unrelated edit without changing a rearmed one-shot’s authored schedule. Targeted formatting and style checks passed. Full CI was not run locally.

Matched light-theme Chromium captures with synthetic Gateway data. Viewports: 1120 px desktop, 700 px narrow, and emulated 400 px phone. Base: `18c6b79f44789`; candidate: `e8e2b7b1eea38` (same source tree as published head `912ae81c3006`).

### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Before: Run status beside the configured time](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6628180e-c91a-4e88-bb63-8f09b42ef7db)

**After**

![After: Run status under the title, timing and model controls in the tray](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/543b4d17-1e3d-4cb0-8d66-cd22788e15a5)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![Before: Run status highlighted in the timing row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cf664bc5-4f59-4b0a-acd9-0e82e4d313af)

**After**

![After: Run status highlighted in the header](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89751e30-3227-4595-833c-1fba3ab57d3b)

All 29 matched annotated pairs: [one-shot runtime, recurrence and triggers](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202260#issuecomment-7031428567) · [payloads, drafts, permissions, viewports and menus](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202260#issuecomment-7031435351).

### State inventory

| Area | What can appear |
| --- | --- |
| Timing | **Once:** local date and time. **Every:** amount and unit (seconds, minutes, hours, days). **Hourly:** days and all-day or hourly window. **Daily/Weekly:** days and time. **Monthly:** day of the month and time. **Custom:** cron expression. A configured cron time zone stays with timing; fine-tuning such as stagger remains in Advanced. |
| Triggers | **Event:** trigger type; source, event name and arguments (or the plugin-owned explanation) are separate. **On exit:** existing process trigger; command help stays separate. **Stream:** source details use the stream-specific editor instead of the regular prompt tray. |
| Model and reasoning | Agent tasks show the inherited/default or selected model. Reasoning is shown only when supported; command, script and system-event payloads have no model or reasoning selection. Catalog and permission states (loading, unavailable, disconnected, saving, read-only) are handled by the existing pickers. |
| Runtime | Saved one-shot: no next run, moved/rearmed next activity, running, waiting, paused, or automatically stopped. These appear under the title, not in the tray. No status repeats the configured time or follows a new or changed schedule draft. |
| Draft and layout | The tray is shared by new/edit drafts; invalid fields keep their messages next to the controls but outside the tray. At narrow desktop widths controls can wrap; the phone layout uses labeled timing rows. Timing, model and reasoning controls retain their picker overlays. |

Reported and co-authored by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/875a01aa-1cce-45c3-808d-5c2c98ed3aa8)

prs.title: fix(access): label invite-only roles in the role picker
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the Access page, choosing a role for a member shows a short description of what that role can do. Roles configured with `sessions.others: "invited"` (a valid config value) showed the raw key `sessions.invited` instead of a readable description. This was seen on a live claw with a custom `collaborator` role.

## User Impact

Owners now see "Only sessions they're invited to" for invite-only roles in the role picker. The other session-access descriptions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway passes each role's `sessions.others` value through to the Access page unchanged, and the config schema allows `none | invited | view | suggest | write`. The Access page's English catalog and its `Role` type only covered four of those values. This change adds the missing English label and a shared `RoleSessionAccess` type that lists all five values. The English `sessions` catalog is now checked with `satisfies Record<RoleSessionAccess, string>`, so a missing label fails typecheck instead of showing a raw key. No other session-access consumer in the extension or the owner link projection branches on this value.

Foreign locales are not edited by hand. They follow the repository's i18n rules (generated after merge). Until then, `translateControlUiMessage` falls back to English for the new key.

## Evidence

- New `people-roles.test.ts` case renders every access level and checks the invite-only description. It fails on `main` (raw key) and passes with this change.
- Removing the `invited` label makes `pnpm tsgo:extensions` fail with `Property 'invited' is missing in type ... Record<RoleSessionAccess, string>`.
- Gap: no screenshot. The only visible change is one description string in the role picker.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openclaw-id-access/browser` — 6 files, 21 tests passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — pass
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/openclaw-id-access` — no problems
- `oxfmt --check extensions/openclaw-id-access/browser` — clean
- `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` (no diff), `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` — pass

</details>

prs.title: fix(mantis): keep hosted proof storage isolated
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Request-bound Mantis proofs fail on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu before candidate execution: Podman ignores the storage override, and the runner's temporary path exceeds its run-directory limit.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202237

## User Impact

Mantis can prepare, verify, and clean up its bounded rootless storage on hosted runners. This prepares the remaining runner cutover without changing request admission or enabling channel traffic.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use Podman's per-user storage configuration under the existing owner and a short private temporary path. Bind the final container configuration override, accept an omitted networking field from older Podman, and keep rejecting reported mismatches. Pin Crabbox recovery state separately so moving Podman's configuration does not move recovery records into disposable storage.

The 32-GiB reservation, mount identity, rootless execution, actual store-path checks, and guarded cleanup remain enforced.

## Evidence

- A hosted baseline probe reproduced incorrect graph/run roots on Podman 4.9.3; a separate diagnostic confirmed its 50-character run-directory limit.
- Independent source review found no blocking issue.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed `18c6b79f4478` → `e3651516c9f0` with no correctness or security findings.
- Hosted proof passed on Ubuntu 24.04 with Podman 4.9.3: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44682176715
- Two new regression cases fail on the base implementation. The fixed run passes all 83 cases across five focused storage/caller test files, plus targeted typecheck, lint, and formatting.
- Real Podman setup, cross-step configuration validation, and guarded cleanup passed: graph/run roots remained in the verified 32-GiB filesystem, which was unmounted and removed normally.
- The three changed source/test files are identical between the tested checkout and this PR head.
- Temporary probe workflow changes are absent from the final diff.
- Full candidate image, SSH, browser, and channel proof remain part of the separate runner cutover.

prs.title: fix(worktrees): end generated worktree names with the worktree ID
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw publishes a session's work to a branch named after its managed worktree, `openclaw/<name>`. Generated names come from a small readable pool (`keen-barnacle`) or the session title (`release-planning`), and name allocation checks only the local repository. GitHub keeps branches after their PRs close, so a new worktree can get a name whose branch already exists remotely with unrelated history. Publication then refuses the push with "GitHub publication cannot safely extend the published branch", which describes a different situation.

This happened on a real publication: a new task got `keen-barnacle`, and GitHub still held `openclaw/keen-barnacle` from a PR closed three weeks earlier. On `openclaw/openclaw` today, 104 of the 420 two-word generated names already exist as `openclaw/*` branches, so about one new generated name in four collides.

## User Impact

Generated and title-derived worktree names now end with six characters from the new worktree's random ID, for example `release-planning-ab38b4` or `brisk-lobster-3f9a1c`. That makes a clash with a branch left on GitHub by earlier work very unlikely, and allocation needs no network lookup. Names you supply (`worktreeName`, `--name`) are unchanged and used exactly as given.

## Why This Change Was Made

A guaranteed-unique part has to be new for every worktree. A commit hash isn't: the same commit can be published more than once. The worktree's own ID is a fresh random UUID, so its six-hex prefix gives 16.7 million possibilities per readable name, against a few hundred existing branches in total. The readable part stays first, so branches remain recognizable.

The existing local checks (registered worktrees, local branches, unmanaged paths, numeric suffix) still run as a final local guard. When one forces another candidate, the ordinal goes after the ID (`release-planning-ab38b4-2`), and a long name is shortened in its readable part so all six ID characters survive. The name-based "reuse the caller's own checkout" branch inside name allocation could no longer match a fresh ID, so it was removed; owner reuse already happens before naming. The managed-worktrees doc describes the new names and says the suffix makes collisions unlikely rather than impossible.

## Evidence

Real behavior, with `ManagedWorktreeService` run from each checkout against a scratch repository. The scratch remote already holds an old `openclaw/release-planning` branch from earlier work, and the local branch is gone. Each run creates a worktree with the title "release-planning", commits, and pushes its branch to that remote, as publication would.

Before (`origin/main` 1ade2b7a889):

```
generated name: release-planning  branch: openclaw/release-planning
push openclaw/release-planning: REJECTED !	refs/heads/openclaw/release-planning:refs/heads/openclaw/release-planning	[rejected] (non-fast-forward)
```

After (this branch):

```
generated name: release-planning-ab38b4  branch: openclaw/release-planning-ab38b4
push openclaw/release-planning-ab38b4: accepted
```

Tests:
- `name.test.ts`: the ID suffix, the ordinal after it, and truncation of a 64-character name that keeps the whole ID.
- `service.canonical-paths.test.ts`:
  - Fallback and title names end with the worktree ID's first six characters, and the branch is `openclaw/<name>`.
  - A generated name avoids an unmanaged branch and a path with the same bare title.
  - Concurrent generated names stay distinct.
- `service.pending-slots.test.ts`: two owners creating with the same title at once get distinct names, with no contention and no leftover pending slot. This replaces a test of a same-name race that can no longer happen for generated names.
- Existing tests that asserted `-2` and `-3` name suffixes after crashes, removals and retained checkouts now assert a fresh ID-suffixed name instead. They're in `service.acceleration`, `service.capacity`, `service.pending-slots` and `server.sessions.create-worktree-spawn`.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

- `pnpm test src/agents/worktrees/`: 441 passed, 2 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `service.apfs.test.ts` (executable mode 0700 vs 0755), which fails the same way on `origin/main` on this machine.
- 16 gateway, spawn and session worktree test files (`server.sessions.create*`, `server-methods/worktrees`, `sessions-spawn-tool`, `subagent-spawn`, `agent.worktree-race`, workboard cleanup recovery, state migrations, `github-publication-session-access`, `dashboard-session-title.transport`, `session-slug`): 257 passed. `server.sessions.create-worktree-spawn` rerun on the final head: 27 passed.
- `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm format:docs:check`, and `oxlint` on the changed files: clean.
- I didn't run the full suite and typecheck locally. This machine's shared dependency store isn't supported by the build's declaration step (`Declaration input escapes checkout`), so CI covers them.

</details>

prs.title: fix(publication): target the default branch for an abbreviated commit base
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A managed worktree can be created from an abbreviated commit ID, for example `worktreeBaseRef: "908c17fa6bd"` on a spawned session. The worktree records that text as its base. GitHub publication picks the PR base branch from the recorded base, and it treats only full 40- or 64-character IDs as commits. So it reads `908c17fa6bd` as a branch name, can't find that branch on GitHub, and fails with "The pull request base or its Git history could not be verified. Check repository read access, connectivity, and local Git objects…". That points at the wrong cause. It failed twice on a real publication before the same commit was retried with its full ID.

## User Impact

Publishing from a worktree whose recorded base is an abbreviated commit ID now targets the repository's default branch, as it already does for a full ID. Branch bases are unchanged, including hex-looking names that exist locally or on GitHub.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix is in publication's base-branch selection, so the worktree registry and its reuse checks are unchanged. Existing worktrees with an abbreviated base also publish correctly. A new helper, `resolveRecordedPublicationBaseBranch`, treats a hex-looking recorded base as a commit only when all of these hold:

- No local branch has that name. Git prefers a branch over an object ID, so a local branch is what creation used.
- It resolves to a commit whose ID starts with it.
- GitHub reports no branch with that name (404).

If GitHub has the branch, or the lookup fails for any other reason, the base stays a branch exactly as before. Anything that isn't hex goes through the existing parser unchanged. `prepare_pr` is unchanged.

## Evidence

Real behavior through publication's own target selection, `prepareGitHubPublicationTarget`, with live GitHub reads. `ManagedWorktreeService` creates a worktree from an 11-character commit ID in a scratch repository whose `origin` is `openclaw/openclaw`. Target selection then reads the repository from GitHub and picks the PR base. These calls are read-only; nothing is pushed.

Before (`origin/main` 1ade2b7a889):

```
worktree base recorded: 6c1547a4a82
publication target: openclaw/openclaw head openclaw/pinned -> base 6c1547a4a82
```

After (this branch; GitHub answered HTTP 404 for a branch named `e5e2ef5f660`):

```
worktree base recorded: e5e2ef5f660
publication target: openclaw/openclaw head openclaw/pinned -> base main
```

Before the fix, the next publication step asks GitHub for the branch `6c1547a4a82`, which doesn't exist, and that is the "base or its Git history could not be verified" failure.

Tests in `github-publication-recorded-base.test.ts` run against a real Git repository and a stand-in `gh`:
- An abbreviated commit ID (lowercase or uppercase) that GitHub reports missing targets the default branch.
- A full commit ID targets the default branch without a GitHub lookup.
- The same abbreviated name stays a branch when GitHub has it or can't confirm it's missing.
- `main`, `origin/main`, a local branch named `cafe1234`, and hex text that names no commit stay branches without a lookup.
- Only an HTTP 404 counts as missing. `Not Found (HTTP 503)` and connection errors stay unknown.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

- `pnpm test src/gateway/github-publication-*.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-github-read.target.test.ts`: 32 files, 675 passed, 23 skipped.
- `pnpm format:check`: clean.
- I didn't run the full suite and typecheck locally. This machine's shared dependency store isn't supported by the build's declaration step, so CI covers them.

</details>

prs.title: fix: bound reloadable chat history
prs.body:
## Current correction and gates

Hosted candidate: `97fb87fc939f8773a96f9bc9e6008611959d93e9` (tree `45340ab120fae2a7aabde4be1a1aa236e43eaf4b`). Native proof publication completed successfully. The PR remains open and **NEEDS WORK**; no merge or deployment is claimed.

A signed local correction, `a48b5cd804603dbeb94b3488b5e79e0655a49371`, removes the residency loop's forbidden non-null assertion while preserving reverse occurrence admission, and fixes the native-scroll fixture to represent exhausted newer history using the canonical absent fields. This two-file delta is 6+/7- production lines and 1+/1- test lines. Qualified formatting, whitespace and normal commit hooks pass. This correction is not yet published. One complete independent Codex P0–P2 review of the exact commit and its owning contracts found no actionable findings. Focused remote proof passed all 24 residency tests, all 9 native-scroll tests, and syntax lint with zero warnings/errors. The first type invocation was rejected before checking source because it used noncanonical graph names. The corrected type-only run passed both canonical UI Chat and packages graphs.

### Integrated candidate evidence

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44570690892) tested merge `1f38271e94c1df6ebb264ac4f3d179796529b646`, with ordered parents baseline `a38c7df01e968814be530663f931432e580e3be5` and the hosted candidate. The completed run has 77 successful, 9 failed and 21 skipped jobs. Eight failures are substantive; the ninth is the aggregate gate. Build and all three UI unit shards passed.

Failure disposition:

- Core type stripe 3 and core lint stripe 2 found the fixture type and residency assertion fixed in the local correction. The corrected fixture/runtime cases, offending lint rule, UI Chat type graph and packages type graph now pass in the local correction.
- The Node changed shard's two preparation-barrier failures reproduce on exact baseline `a38c7df`: 2 failures and 13 passes through the canonical CI shard runner. These are inherited; follow-up: FaultSequencePreparationBarrier.
- UI E2E shards 2, 3 and 4 use an explicit new-automation name field that the baseline intentionally hides outside edit/clone mode. The failing fixtures and relevant editor are identical between the actual tested merge and its baseline. Follow-up: CronAutomaticNamingFixtures.
- Real-Gateway shard 1's legacy Cron provider-count failure reproduces on that exact baseline, with the preceding naming scenario retained: three calls versus two expected. The provider-removal case passes in the baseline run; its CI failure is still under investigation. Real-Gateway shard 2 passed.
- The Chat asset cap is exceeded. The same-toolchain normalized measurements are shown below. Existing CSS/request violations also occur on the baseline and are not reported as passing caps.

Both baseline reproductions used the same isolated Testbox, frozen baseline dependencies and pinned Bun. Node proof: 2 failed/13 passed. Browser proof: 1 failed/2 passed across the two selected files. These are baseline attribution results, not successful candidate qualification.

### Assets and remaining acceptance

| Normalized gzip | Baseline a38c7df | Hosted candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS | 90,540 B | 90,407 B |
| Chat bootstrap | 1,332,622 B | 1,340,658 B |
| New Session bootstrap | 820,950 B | 804,794 B |

The approved Chat cap remains **1,339,362 B**; the candidate exceeds it by 1,296 B. A proposed fixed cap of **1,341,357 B** would preserve 699 B of headroom, but has not been approved and has not been applied. Compression rules, allowances and other caps are unchanged.

The bounded history/source-coverage/cursor ownership fixes and earlier native scroll/17-case geometry proof remain recorded below with their original scopes. The current screenshot's browser-wide memory exhaustion has not been reproduced end to end, and this PR does not claim to resolve the whole campaign.

Against pinned application baseline `307d9c45fb2548d300276c473ccb7c5cab4768bc`, the hosted candidate adds 4,541 net production lines and 15,519 net test lines. Production growth implements bounded history residency and canonical source/cursor ownership. The local correction removes one further production line. The canonical test-LF ratchet remains 15,485 = 15,085 credit + 400 allowance; test diff classification and that ratchet are different measures.

## What Problem This Solves

Long chat sessions retain more transcript bodies as readers page. This change bounds reloadable resident history, releases evicted bodies from presentation caches, and keeps older/newer navigation reversible.

## User Impact

Ordinary residency targets **400 entries / 3,145,728 serialized JSON code units / eight source segments**. Source atomicity, the current reader packet and live/pending/error custody have explicit exceptions; one bounded staged packet is separately charged. These are retained-body targets, not a whole-pane RAM ceiling.

Readers can move older/newer, return to Latest and restore semantic bookmarks. Search states its loaded-window scope; export loads complete history separately. Capacity/unavailable outcomes are visible. A local command after an authoritative empty-history read stays before the first later turn, including after resident-prefix retirement and older-page admission. Unloaded or unknown history never implies the beginning. Command replies retain transient custody and retire rather than entering persistent raw history.

**Tradeoff: bounded residency makes a full 900→1→900 traversal perform more pagination and rendering work. Historical matched comparisons remain rejected, with substantial wall-time and renderer-CPU regressions disclosed below. The owner accepts that product tradeoff after investigation; this is no numerical benchmark pass or speedup claim.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical source/packet/cursor ownership controls trimming, reopening, continuity and retirement. SQLite and actor-memory reads certify same-snapshot Stop continuation; UI admission revalidates a fresh selected packet. Numeric adaptive budgets cross awaits, prepared bodies do not. One synchronous owner performs final prefix fit and accepted-prefix receipt adoption. Visible fitting reads commit without an unnecessary fallback/staged read, while sparse/raw progress, smaller-envelope retries and cancellation retain their existing contracts.

Accepted raw source facts and one canonical publication owner govern local-output placement; empty views, stale reads, pending inputs and unavailable outbox storage do not confer authority. Local occurrence placement preserves consecutive command order without inventing durable sequence zero. Edge-only history traversal advances navigation while preserving the original held packet bodies, certificate and opaque endpoints; actual cuts or body changes still revoke that custody.

One native offset producer supplies paging/follow facts before callback-induced rendering, preserving input/link ownership and anchor ordering. Its accepted reader-policy baseline is independent of geometric synchronization: measuring the current position before scroll capture cannot consume upward paging intent. Presentation-owned partial retirement releases dormant bodies while preserving safe survivor seeds. One shared weak derivation owner preserves exact digest bytes for fresh immutable stream/snapshot envelopes and per-source reactions. Reply-preview revisions follow final lookup facts; releasing nonempty quote bodies still invalidates their previews.

Integration is fixed at **b59c593cb0b7ad88ba2118768840c010e3253d95**, through signed native successors of earlier 650/21cd/ed40/99 integrations. The latest join preserves 13 reviewed manual resolutions and 20 clean overlapping postimages; this is source-composition evidence, not a current runtime pass. Navigation-only admission lives in the existing lazy packet runtime; ordinary hydration preparation stays eager, and successful navigation commits synchronously through the already-resolved module. The cold owner now preserves incoming boot boundary probing followed by at most one default 80-entry / 256 KiB fill. Canonical input display places queued steerNow input in pending presentation once, preserving hidden-input omission and persisted-steer deduplication. The absolute task Chat cap remains **1,303,958 B** against incoming main policy 1,296,751 B: 7,207 B above incoming policy, a cap difference rather than measured current asset headroom; no new asset allowance. M3 adds no dependency, configuration, SQLite-schema or protocol-version bump. Inherited main is not a new whole-repository review.

## Evidence

**Historical H qualification, retained:** The prior signed source was **088247b8509d6f96a506ccf5a204ac61d6f9f855**, tree **5279d3bd19e03ee13f6311f5520e36c84d6c8694**, ordered parents G deb8a8ea and frozen incoming **6580679f718148c883b457da6a71f25e267e1bfc**. The **whole authored M3 delta against that actual incoming parent is280paths**; incoming changes are preserved rather than credited as authored work. Four conflict owners compose the current contracts: absolute Chat cap1,303,958; captured negative non-smooth end-command retirement including issued commands, while smooth settling remains owned; one host retirement before callback-capable settlement with lifecycle/new-command guards; and direction-matched reader/cancellation controls. The auto-merged task-based mount and history-intent ownership remain intact. Settlement work is published before refresh/invalidate so synchronous cancellation or a newer owner cannot be overwritten. Current cold admission/tail/in-flight owners and final synchronous publication remain canonical. Fresh native init completes0 with28 signature validations. One complete native source review covers all280paths and42complete current source contexts in16passes,800,000bytes/pass,largest796,096,no hidden paths/model/provider/context override. prs.title: fix(agents): requester tools lose authority after child resume
prs.body:
Related: #167022

## What Problem This Solves

An already-admitted requester can lose tool authority when continuing a paused child replaces the child's delivery cohort. This candidate separates the consumed requester's execution lifetime from that mutable delivery progress.

The one-use handoff must still be current at registration and consumption. After consumption, a supplied requester receipt retains requester/store identity for later caller checks and exact-model binding. Delivery keeps its cohort checks. Existing admitted-run liveness, cancellation, operator authority and delegated restrictions remain composed; handoffs without a requester receipt retain the strict predicate. No new grant, registry, configuration, schema or dependency is introduced.

Candidate: `9800ab830b4c08a7bc73d19c2a7056c3299cc528`.
Inspected base: `b81742c8bfb591847601678178ff824336fc73eb`.

## Previously recorded focused validation

- The consumed-handoff/model-binding regression fails on the original implementation; 11 existing cases pass.
- The sessions_send final-enqueue regression fails after **simulated** cohort replacement on the original implementation; 14 other cases pass, including requester/store replacement refusals.
- With the candidate, all **67 focused tests** pass across handoff, model binding, requester-policy and final-enqueue suites. Recorded wrapper wall time: **45.82 seconds**. The two changed test files report approximately 2 and 17 seconds including per-file setup; CI timing remains pending.
- Core production types, both changed-test type graphs, targeted type-aware lint, formatting and git diff --check passed.
- Separate shipped qaRuntime builds passed for exact candidate and base, in 44.7 and 43.2 seconds. Build/source stamps agree. These are runtime-build results, not full package/release validation.

Those focused regressions explicitly supply handoff-bearing caller options. Their simulated evidence is separate from the real-model experiments below. No tests or builds were rerun for this final body assembly.

## Live experiment — shipped Codex runner

One real-model trial per exact source used the shipped Gateway and Codex runner in isolated fixtures. Children remained OpenClaw-managed; native rollout metadata records multi-agent version disabled.

Both trials recorded the child's explicit message wait and registry successor/generation/cohort replacement. Their actual tool receipts differ:

| Tool receipt | Candidate | Exact base |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resume | accepted, mode=resume; isError=false | agent tool caller authority is no longer active; isError=true |
| Independent subsequent notify | queued; isError=false | same caller-authority error; isError=true |

**The base produced a successor even though its resume receipt reported an error.** Both independent sends were captured in the final outcome history. Within each trial they belong to the same requester-settle run, use distinct native outer calls, and place the first outer output before the second call. Committed successor replacement was observed before the second call. This is scenario-level live red/green evidence for the Codex-mediated caller flow.

### Authority-path inference and limits

Codex explicitly forwards trustedInternalHandoff into coding-tool options at `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.ts:223`; both built artifacts retain that field. `src/agents/agent-tools.caller.ts:57` reads the settle batch and line 78 selects its receipt predicate. `src/gateway/subagent-completion-tool-handoff.ts:135` constructs the candidate's consumed-execution predicate. Caller authority is captured/composed at `src/agents/tools/gateway-caller-context.ts:440` and line 670. Notify checks communication authority immediately before enqueue at `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.delivery.ts:93`.

This pinned source/build mapping, selected-runtime diagnostics and real receipt difference support the assembly-path explanation. Callback identities, Boolean predicate values, the precise handoff-consumption return and selected requesterPolicySource were not directly recorded. No source, model-I/O or callback instrumentation was added.

Notify success establishes **process-owned queue admission**, not receiver model execution, restart durability or external/channel delivery. The driver captured final history after a final-marker or authority-error observation plus a three-second grace. Later teardown restart/abort diagnostics are not the tested authority failures.

## Separate embedded experiment and remaining gap

The earlier embedded experiment completed the functional sequence on both sources, so it did not establish live base failure or patched-branch coverage. Inspection found that `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-tool-prepare.ts:246` passes handoff to profile resolution, but codingToolOptions starting at line 319 omits it; the shared context builder at `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-tool-run-context.ts:91` does not supply it either.

**That shared embedded omission remains unfixed in this candidate.** The separate Codex red/green result does not repair or retroactively upgrade the embedded experiment. Coverage across other runtimes, revocation cases and every report on the related issue is not claimed, and upstream acceptance is not presumed.

## Evidence and isolation

[Reviewed six-file evidence snapshot](https://gist.github.com/wzysmarthome-dot/dfbf75e8acb274a3d305071e808b16b8) — 27 projected redacted records, integrity hashes and the pre-publication body draft.

The linked six-file evidence snapshot includes projected redacted primary-record excerpts with stable synthetic labels, relative timestamps, source hashes and JSON pointers. They are not complete raw logs or raw terminal output. Actual receipts and source/build inference are labeled separately.

Both Codex fixtures staged only the same designated subscription profile, with no alternative profile or API-key billing fallback. No real conversations, memories or business data were copied. Task ports/processes and temporary credential state were cleaned; production configuration content was unchanged. Both source trees remain at the exact SHAs above and clean. The linked bundle preserves the reviewed pre-publication snapshot. Its local-only status notes describe the assembly stage, not the current publication state.

prs.title: fix(memory): exclude deleted cron-job archives from memory indexing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#200075: deleting a cron job leaves its session archive behind as an
artifact keyed by the cache-stable base key `agent:<id>:cron:<job>` (no
`:run:` segment). `isMemorySessionIndexable` only excluded archived keys
matching `isCronRunSessionKey`, whose pattern requires the
`:run:<runId>` scope, so those base-keyed archives were treated as
indexable conversations. The sessions-eligible count grew with every
cron cleanup and `memory status` stayed `dirty=true` indefinitely —
re-indexing never cleared the flag because the indexer correctly skips
what admission wrongly admits.

## The Change

- `isMemorySessionIndexable` now checks archived keys with
  `isCronSessionKey`, which covers both the base (`cron:<job>`) and the
  isolated run (`cron:<job>:run:<id>`) scopes — matching the
  live-session admission semantics already shipped for the
  system-only-cron-base case in #161834 (its fix handled the metadata
  catch-up path; this closes the archive-artifact path).
- `isCronSessionKey` is re-exported through the session-key plugin SDK
  surface so the extension can use the canonical predicate.
- The parameterized indexability suite moves inside a describe block:
  at the file top level it never executed under the shared extension
  runner (previously the file silently ran 5 cases; it now runs 17).

## Evidence

- **Runtime proof through the shipped `memory status`/`memory index`
  CLI** (built from this branch, isolated profile, synthetic cron-base
  session created via `chat.send` then deleted via `sessions delete`,
  which retains the transcript as a `.jsonl.deleted.*` archive;
  embeddings provider unreachable by design — no network calls needed):

  **Before (main, unfixed — built from `cf74e641eb9`):**

  ```text
  Indexed: 0/1 files · 0 chunks
  Dirty: yes
    sessions · 0/1 files · 0 chunks · 0.0 B text + embeddings
  # memory index --force:
  Memory index failed (main): openai embeddings failed ... (401)
  # → the deleted cron-job archive is admitted as an eligible session
  #   source and attempted-forever: dirty never clears.
  ```

  **After (this branch, same state):**

  ```text
  Indexed: 0/0 files · 0 chunks
    sessions · 0/0 files · 0 chunks · 0.0 B text + embeddings
    no eligible session transcripts found
  # memory index --force:
  No memory files found in ...; nothing indexed (main).
  Dirty: no
  # → the archive is no longer admitted; after one sync the agent is
  #   clean. A normal interactive session stays indexable in both runs.
  ```

- **Regression-first unit proof**: the new `cron-base-archive` case
  fails before the fix (`expected true to be false`) and passes after;
  the existing `cron-run-archive` case documents that the run scope
  stays excluded. Full file: **17/17**
  (`manager-session-sync-state.test.ts`).
- **Sibling suites stay green**: startup catch-up (includes the
  #161834 regression) + interval sync — **37/37**.

## Risk / compatibility

One-line semantic widening on the memory admission gate only: cron
family keys (base + run) were already excluded from indexing by other
gates (`generatedByCronRun`, `sessionKind`), so archived artifacts now
admit exactly what the indexer would have skipped. No indexing output
changes for live sessions; CLI `memory status` for agents with deleted
cron jobs goes clean after one sync.

prs.title: fix: make automation editing show one title and a named session
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The automation editor repeats the automation name, styles Automation scratch differently from Advanced, and shows an internal key for a named session in **Runs in**.

## User Impact

The editor keeps one editable name, gives the two disclosures the same appearance, and shows the destination session’s name rather than its key. Saving still preserves the same destination.

## Why This Change Was Made

prs.title: fix(update): replace settled cleanup warnings in reports
prs.body:
## What problem does this PR solve?

Late cleanup can resolve a warning in durable update history while the CLI or Gateway completion still reports the old warning. A failed cleanup receipt write can also disappear when the successful cleanup supplied an explicit empty warning list.

## Why is this the right fix?

The shared result projector now replaces an explicitly supplied warning list before merging the new rows. It uses the same bounded, truncated keys as the existing writer, preserves omitted lists and unrelated rows, and processes successive results in order. The cleanup result owner adds a new bookkeeping warning to any explicit list.

This keeps the terminal update outcome and existing persistence owners unchanged. Production delta: +26/-10 (net +16), for canonical key generation and the complete-warning-list contract. Test delta: +133/-46 (net +87).

## Evidence

- Reproduced the stale warning with the committed projector and converter: an explicit empty list retained the prior cleanup warning.
- Added actual CLI JSON/text report coverage and extended the real Gateway cleanup fixture through late verification and receipt-write failure.
- Independent P0–P2 source review: no findings; the review was rechecked against the final test-only fixture correction. Autoreview found no actionable issues in the production change.
- TypeScript syntax and `git diff --check` pass.
- [Linux/Node proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44677613732): both corrected Gateway regressions fail against the original production files and pass on head `bdce8c0ec83`; formatting and lint pass. Wrapper exit 0; Testbox stopped.
- [Earlier focused run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44676806353): all 72 unchanged CLI, step-key and cleanup tests passed. Its two new Gateway cases exposed a fixture write placed after terminal completion; the final test-only commit moves that write before completion, and the linked corrected run verifies both cases.
- [Direct-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44677646472) found 18 Markdown lint errors in the unchanged generated `docs/releases/2026.11.5.md`; the file and lint inputs are identical to the frozen base. This unrelated release-docs follow-up is outside the updater fix.
- [Latest-stable package acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44677000663) passed fresh installation and the published-upgrade-survivor/base lane from `openclaw@2026.11.6` in 620 seconds. This validates the identical production change at `b1c3912` before the final test-only correction.
- [Normal PR merge-checkout CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44678888721) passed on final head `bdce8c0ec83`, including all 42 selected jobs and the aggregate CI gate.
- [ClawSweeper reviewed the final head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202244#issuecomment-7031334846) with no actionable finding and no before-merge action. Its latest-stable proof request is fulfilled above. The targeted stale-warning and receipt-failure scenarios are proved through actual CLI/Gateway consumers and real cleanup fixtures, rather than replayed through an installed CLI entry point; that proof limit remains explicit.

prs.title: fix: nested HTML stalls outbound delivery
prs.body:
Closes #199439

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an outbound message with deeply nested non-convertible tags (about 450 KB) blocks the Gateway for 18 seconds.

## User Impact

User impact: long nested HTML in a reply no longer stalls delivery. Output is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Empty-element removal rescanned the whole tag run from every opener. It now pairs each opener with its last closer in one scan per run.

Accepted edge: a tag quoted inside another tag's attribute is no longer removed alone.

## Evidence

- New test fails on base, passes with the fix (22/22 in `sanitize-text.test.ts`).
- 64k nesting: 18 s before, 0.17 s after. 200k: 0.45 s.
- 300k random inputs: output identical to the old regex apart from the edge above.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes (dead export scan skipped).

## Real behavior proof

Shipped Gateway (loopback, token auth) with the IRC channel pointed at a local stub IRC server, Node v24.22.3, Linux. One `send` RPC through the Gateway with a 64000-deep `<span>` reply (832001 chars) wrapping `x`, while `/healthz` is polled. Base `a8a7ce9`, head `96fea79`:

```text
base: send 11856 ms, worst /healthz 11239 ms, gateway logs "main-thread stall elapsedMs=11372"
head: send  1011 ms, worst /healthz   207 ms, no stall logged
both: stub IRC server received 1 PRIVMSG, 1 byte, "x", sha 2d711642b726
```

<details>
<summary>Agent transcript (trimmed)</summary>

**User:** Find the open issue you are most confident fixing that has no PR. Open a PR. De-duplicate code. Keep comments, commits and PR text very short. Follow CONTRIBUTING.md and the PR template.

**Agent:** Searched open bugs with no linked PR. #197381 already has #197811. Chose #199439: source-confirmed, no PR, clear regression to write.

**Agent:** Confirmed the cost is `EMPTY_HTML_ELEMENT_RE` rescanning the tag run from each opener, which is quadratic in nesting depth.

**Agent:** Added a 32k-depth regression test. It failed on base.

**Agent:** Replaced the regex with a single scan per run of whitespace and inert tags, pairing each opener with the last matching closer.

**Agent:** Fuzzed 300k random inputs against the old regex. The only differences are tags quoted inside another tag's attribute, noted in the PR.

**Agent:** `tsgo` flagged unchecked indexed access. Restructured to typed tokens. `pnpm check:changed` passes.

</details>

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening the model picker across equivalent saved sessions or ordinary saved-row revisions retains duplicate catalog projections.

## User Impact

Equivalent selections share retained model-picker results while preserving per-session selection, runtime and role presentation and retaining the existing auth/currentness checks. No settings, schema, dependency or public API changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

One canonical selection key serves the existing inner and outer caches. Request authority ends with preparation, and retained auth/account observers keep owner facts rather than request closures. This removes duplicate request-derived keys and first/last-request retention without adding another cache. The existing best-effort cache-settlement behavior is preserved.

The no-twin picker path now builds fresh public choices without intermediate wrapper/singleton arrays. Invariant remote catalog envelope schemas are reused while per-call provider checks and dynamic date validation remain unchanged.

Production change: +19 net lines for selection and lifetime separation; tests/support +220; benchmark +142. The two allocation follow-ups remove five net production lines. The [ClawSweeper settlement concern](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200067#issuecomment-6914081385) is addressed: [PR #168690](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168690), commit `c3924e74859736dcf85c2b114226c375e30e7c50`, intentionally chose best-effort cache settlement. The separate restored guards/retry loops and five tests demanding a stronger guarantee were removed. Selection, authority lifetime and live auth/provider behavior stay in scope.

## Evidence

Candidate `356e1a488b85ce4660a563634594c01533ffd3ac`; baseline `d32ac41084fcaef1099ecdbfeb1cfa81da532642`.

**Draft; not ready to merge. The completed coverage is:

All four planned canonical type graphs passed using **tsrs**, the Linux default behind the repository's `run-tsgo` wrapper: core, gateway-methods, agents-other and scripts. The old-key mutation fails both neutral retention cases; the old account-observer mutation fails both shared-pin cases. Exact source is restored before the full build. Source, installed dependencies and build outputs are sealed; command exit 0, native settlement and the known run's terminal teardown are verified. This is targeted proof, not a green whole-CI claim.

The earlier native attempt ran zero producer cases, tests, type graphs or builds: the provider client hit its 15-minute readiness timeout while queued and the launcher exited 1. Its local wrapper is settled, but native/GitHub settlement remains **UNKNOWN** because no run association was returned. The adapter's reported `hasHost:false` is not independent teardown evidence. The exact claim remains retained for supported reconciliation; current CI does not relabel that failed attempt.
Independent static review completed on this exact candidate with zero actionable findings. The earlier allocation was incomplete because owner context was missing. The repaired review supplied those owners and completed all three assignments; the benchmark assignment repeated only because the native helper requires aggregate coverage. The preceding [native Node proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43861333100) on `ba2b65bc2dec1ce01adfc46f02bb5fc2dbb5701c` completed 189 positive cases, seven expected-failure controls, five canonical type graphs, formatting/lint and full build. No broad-CI pass or waiver is claimed. The current draft CI gate is skipped by repository policy, not passing proof.

The following ten failures were recorded in the earlier CI snapshot. Additional completed failures are listed below. Unchanged source is not matching baseline execution, and none is silently waived:

Propagation owners unchanged; mismatched field and intended successor identity UNKNOWN. Follow-up: Goal successor parameter mismatch. |

Relevant owners unchanged; surviving holder/timing UNKNOWN. Follow-up: interrupt replacement settlement attribution. |

Later completed CI jobs add these named follow-ups: message-buffer scenario authorization and real-Gateway device-picker visibility remain UNKNOWN; the same stale-account `models.authRefresh` assertion matches the separately replayed inherited failure. Plugin-reload continuation/revocation and manual compaction hit fixture deadlines, with no established branch causality. Scheduled-command reset is a source-confirmed stale test expectation against the intended current-parent behavior; Swift WebChat redundant-type lint is unchanged source. Missing Bun also recurs. These failures remain explicit landing evidence gaps or scoped source attributions; the whole manual CI run is not green.

The completed [13-case Node 24.22.1 diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43845149206) reproduced first/last input retention across all four real-owner fixtures. The outer lifetime repair released the last inputs; the combined outer/preparation repairs released all neutral inputs while both shared-account fixtures still retained their first inputs. The final account observer repair and lint-compatible authority lifetime passed all four retention cases again on the current candidate in the completed cache suite. Its Actions conclusion is cancelled because of native teardown; command exit 0 and the complete artifact establish the diagnostic result. The complete paired matrix preserves 616 named metrics / 3,080 paired cells, all five endpoint values, direction, signed deltas, undefined percentages, and observation counts. Its 202 ≥20% adverse cells include repeated distribution statistics and derived metrics, not 202 independent trials. Handler/admission/queue diagnostics sometimes cover only a subset (population 57–64 of 64; hits 538–571 of 576), while the RTT/process/main-CPU tail comparisons use complete request populations. Raw request records remain bound separately; requests are not pooled as independent trials.

The [controlled-feed scored attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43876823511) is **INVALID / HOLD**. Both builds passed and 17 of the 20 declared runs completed. Run 18, startup-interference pair 4 candidate, produced all 641 responses but failed the required observation that a metadata commit overlap the population RPC windows. Runs 19–20 were not executed; no arm was retried or replaced. The command exited 1, native settlement and the known workflow teardown are verified, and the failed result is retained. The cohort ended before final source/build/dependency seals or a completion receipt, so those are unavailable. No performance qualification is taken from the stable subset or partial interference pairs. Archive SHA-256: `0faa97de342c6d131e6c6168861ac25b416c5b9ab6dfec62299e24c12a83261e`.

The [compiled-Gateway RSS diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43880781396) completed one baseline/candidate pair on the same 4-CPU Linux allocation with Node 24.22.1. Both used pristine compiled entries, no TSX or diagnostic child preload, no metadata overlay, no IPC profiler and no forced GC. This is a descriptive single pair, not performance qualification.

| Exact Gateway PID RSS (MiB) | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Ready, before the first request | 1,285.020 | 1,331.266 |
| After response 1 | 1,427.824 | 1,351.141 |
| After response 65 | 1,244.078 | 1,227.145 |
| After response 641 | 1,267.941 | 1,252.000 |
| Maximum observed by the sampler | 1,431.816 | 1,354.980 |

The sampler recorded 309 observations over 15.466 seconds for baseline and 357 over 17.949 seconds for candidate, with a 50 ms target interval. These are exact-process observations, not a kernel-recorded peak, all-descendant memory or small-device qualification. The large compiled-process footprint already exists before the first request; TSX/profiling instrumentation and growth over 641 requests cannot alone explain it. Attribution to main-isolate, worker or native allocations remains open.

All 641 responses per arm passed ordered payload, revision, selection and count equality; both persisted the same canonical remote catalog revision. Controller-observed mean RTT was adverse: population **13.968 → 18.098 ms (+29.6%)** and hits **9.639 → 12.182 ms (+26.4%)**. This pair does not establish causality or a speed/RSS improvement. Both Gateways exited 0 after native SIGINT and their process groups were absent; source, dependencies and build outputs were sealed, and the native allocation settled. Archive SHA-256: `ad420464ab4c9f0b2dd36655fcb45e1093862563b31402310c324aa6cb89c5b9`.

The current head has no performance-acceptance claim. Compiled startup memory attribution is the next diagnostic boundary. The stopped-runtime retained-read defect remains a separate follow-up. **Overall performance INVALID / HOLD is unchanged.**

### Compiled startup attribution — diagnostic only

A [single baseline startup run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43888640990) on `d32ac41084fcaef1099ecdbfeb1cfa81da532642` completed all 641 responses with 1,000 configured models and 64 saved session keys. All 14 commands passed; source, dependency and build seals matched at completion. The compiled child used no TSX, benchmark preload, metadata overlay or active CPU profile. Existing product diagnostic RPCs and one final main-isolate heap snapshot were enabled for attribution, so this is not another scored or uninstrumented comparison.

The main snapshot retained 227.712 MiB and contained 6,102 script identities, with no repeated complete script identities detected. Code-associated retained size was 98.665 MiB; source-string association was 46.514 MiB. These overlapping measures must not be added. After roughly 60 seconds, immediately before capture, process RSS was 1,007.906 MiB and main heap used was 218.195 MiB. Cached startup telemetry reported 554.5 MiB across 12/16 heap samples at readiness and 644.4 MiB across 13/16 during maintenance. All three fresh stability queries returned zero memory events, leaving fresh per-worker attribution unavailable.

Native SIGINT shutdown, process-group exit and lease closure were verified. The 235,552,946-byte raw snapshot stayed remote/private; only bounded, sanitized summaries were retained. Archive SHA-256: `c55008d1d2cfa4403e7cb7f7c5a0994783f962c0bf64b7780d70124bc489d551`. This supports further startup/import-owner investigation; it does not establish a leak, an additive RSS breakdown, a candidate improvement or small-device qualification. **The existing INVALID/HOLD remains unchanged.**

### Controlled-feed qualification protocol — prospective

The admitted protocol now advances to **five fresh pairs per scenario: 20 fresh Gateways**, baseline `d32ac41084fcaef1099ecdbfeb1cfa81da532642` and candidate `356e1a488b85ce4660a563634594c01533ffd3ac`. It retains 1,000 synthetic models, 64 verified saved sessions and 641 checked responses. Default remote refresh stays enabled through the existing loopback fixture server. The completed current-head correctness proof is reused; no positive suites, type graphs, negative controls or separate pristine build are repeated.

**Fixed order before execution:** A = baseline, B = candidate. Run stable-catalog pairs 1–5 in order **AB, BA, AB, BA, AB**, then startup-interference pairs 1–5 in order **BA, AB, BA, AB, BA**. Every arm gets a fresh Gateway and fixture. No post-hoc reordering, selective retry or pooling of requests. Any failed admission condition remains a failed cohort with all collected evidence retained.

Both benchmark workspaces are created, installed and built afresh and symmetrically under the same owned allocation. Native readiness is bounded to two minutes; the fixed overall deadline is 40 minutes, including setup, with a 60-second cleanup reserve and a 180-second controller limit per Gateway. The archive cap is **64 MiB**, with the unchanged 4 MiB limit per saved receipt and 1 MiB terminal reserve. Admission reports were 1.55–1.56 MB each: 20 such reports plus 3.23 MB of original/derived feed and seals require about 35 MB, above the former 32 MiB cap. Whole reports are kept or the budget check fails; no truncation or dropped observations.

All arms receive the same captured real V3 catalog contents: 1,968,254 original bytes, SHA-256 `42c53b518f7c0a68b8fefdd09e161f958a75b4fb8448d059c2af3b7a093bc45e`, 57 providers, 1,390 models, 1,042 provider-pricing records and 5,489 upstream-pricing records. After both real builds, only `generatedAt` changes to one recorded current timestamp later than both build stamps; compact UTF-8 serialization yields one derived wire payload whose actual size/hash is recorded. Original contents and order remain unchanged. No product clock or build stamp is overridden.

- **Stable catalog:** complete enabled refresh, canonical adoption and naturally observed metadata settlement before the first request. Preserve the first request, then 64 population reads (one already-cached key plus 63 new keys), then 576 repeats. Natural metadata/cache epochs must remain unchanged through all three resource checkpoints and their GC brackets. The original retained-selection heap-growth primary applies to this scenario.
- **Startup interference:** use a fresh Gateway with one pending feed request; release it immediately after the first resource checkpoint and before population, without waiting for adoption. Require a completed successful refresh, matching stored/canonical revision, and an observed metadata commit overlapping a population RPC window (explicit 2 ms cross-process tolerance). Heap growth here is not labeled retained-selection growth.

Both scenarios require all 641 ordered payload/revision/count checks, exact input/source/dependency/build seals and graceful Gateway shutdown. The private observer records only natural primitive transitions; it does not capture extra facts or add per-request IPC. Epochs do not identify the generation served by retained fallbacks, and first/last timestamps do not reconstruct multiple intermediate transitions. Active CPU/allocation profiling is disabled. Existing TSX/preload and forced-GC instrumentation remain disclosed; these are not shipped-device RSS measurements.

The unchanged adverse-metric rule below applies separately to each scenario. Report all five paired values and run-level distributions/endpoints, without pooling. The original five-pair HOLD and complete matrix remain preserved; completing this cohort alone does not declare acceptance.

## Prospective performance acceptance

Before measurement: five serial baseline/candidate pairs on one qualified host, baseline d32ac41084fcaef1099ecdbfeb1cfa81da532642 versus this exact committed head. Use the committed real Gateway/WebSocket equivalent-session case: 1,000 synthetic models, 64 verified shared saved sessions, 641 responses per run (first 1, population 64, hits 576). Keep each run's phase distributions separate, including per-key revisions, full response hashes, returned model totals and all raw resource cells. Report all five paired values; each run's phase CPU/latency median, p95, p99 and spread; and RSS, heap, external-memory and array-buffer endpoints at responses 1, 65 and 641. The primary statistic is the median of the five individual values 1 - candidate growth / baseline growth, with positive improvement in at least four pairs; requests are not pooled as independent trials.

Primary target: at least 20% median paired reduction in post-GC main-isolate heap growth from response 1 to response 65, with improvement in at least 4 of 5 pairs and positive baseline growth. Zero/negative denominators remain byte deltas, without percentages. Record endpoints after responses 1, 65 and 641; these are forced-GC endpoints, not peak memory. RSS covers the whole Gateway process. CPU/latency are per-request observations, not endpoint CPU deltas that include GC.

Any adverse change of 20% or more is a HOLD. Smaller adverse metrics are also disclosed and are not automatically accepted; any user-facing regression needs owner acceptance. No RSS reduction or performance acceptance is claimed before the paired results are reviewed.

Separate follow-ups: canonical parameter insertion-order handling; investigate retained reads after runtime stop with a real active-flow witness; the unrelated CI surfaces named above. None is changed here.

prs.title: fix(channels): record a refused queued request for the owner without replying in the channel
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

When a queued channel request is refused at admission because the requester's channel access is gone (`ChannelRunAuthorizationError` kind `denied`), the runner meant to stay silent on the channel, but:

1. **Nothing told the session owner why the run stopped.** The lifecycle error terminal had no `errorNotice`, so the transcript and Control UI showed only a generic failure.
2. **The "silent" reply was not marked silent.** It returned a bare `NO_REPLY` text without `silentReply` metadata. `normalizeReplyPayload` suppresses only payloads with that metadata (`normalize-reply.ts:94-98`), and outbound normalization deliberately keeps literal `NO_REPLY` text (`infra/outbound/payloads.test.ts:106-116`). So the payload reached the reply dispatcher's `deliver`. On a channel that reaches this branch, the literal text could be sent to the conversation whose access had just been revoked.

**Reach:** this branch fires only when a channel supplies a public child-session publication renewal (`child-session-publication.ts:29-39`, bound in `host-context-builder.ts:94-126`). Today that is only the X plugin (`extensions/x/src/ingress.ts`). Discord, for example, never reaches it (see Evidence).

## Change

`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-error-handler.ts`, denied branch only:
- The existing lifecycle error terminal now carries a fixed, host-authored `errorNotice`: "This request was not started because the requester no longer has access to this channel." It contains no cause text, requester text, channel ids or policy details.
- The final payload is marked silent through the existing `setReplyPayloadMetadata(..., { silentReply: true })`.
- Unchanged: the token, reply-operation and model-patch failure, the log line, and the `unavailable` branch, which still replies "could not verify current channel access".

Docs: `docs/channels/groups.md` states that such a refusal is silent on the channel but recorded for the owner.

## Evidence

Proof tier: source (`ocx test`).

- New regression in `agent-runner-execution-terminal-failures.test.ts`, through the real runner and reply dispatcher:
  - exactly one visible `run-failed-before-reply` receipt with the run id and the notice;
  - the projected history shows it;
  - replaying the same terminal adds no second receipt;
  - a synthetic secret in the nested cause appears in neither the displayed nor the projected text;
  - **zero** `deliver`/`deliverPrepared` calls.
  On unchanged main, the notice assertion fails and `deliver` receives bare `NO_REPLY` once.
- 159 tests across 13 files; production and test typecheck, oxlint, format, four ratchets, docs MDX and format checks: pass.
- **Real Discord run** (isolated Gateway, leased Discord QA credentials, real channel; same scenario on main and on this head): message 1 held busy, message 2 queued, the requester removed from the channel's `users` with `config.patch`. On both revisions, a fresh message from the removed sender was ignored, confirming the revocation. Message 2 still ran and replied normally, and this branch was not reached, because Discord supplies no publication renewal. So there is no live proof of this branch; the X plugin has no live proof route here.
- That run found a separate, pre-existing Discord bug, not changed here: message 2 was **admitted after** the revocation (main: patch 05:15:42.400Z, admission 05:15:43.874Z; head: 05:13:44.596Z then 05:13:46.279Z), because Discord preflight reuses its earlier sender decision (`message-handler.preflight.ts:581-605`). It will be fixed in its own PR.

Production +9 −2 lines, test +76, docs +2.

prs.title: fix: stop counting saved prompt checkpoints as chat bytes
prs.body:
Closes #202172

## What Problem This Solves

The active-transcript byte count used by `compaction.maxActiveTranscriptBytes` includes every saved `openclaw.system-prompt` checkpoint: the full system prompt plus tool surface. That entry is not conversation, and compaction cannot shrink it. With a large tool surface the checkpoint alone can use most of the cap: byte-triggered compaction fires early, and the post-compaction measurement can stay above the cap, latching `transcriptByteCompactionLatch` and repeating the bounded-context notice.

## User Impact

User impact: compaction pressure now measures conversation bytes without saved prompt checkpoints. Chats with many tools stop compacting early and stop latching the bounded-context notice after a normal compaction. Stored checkpoints and context acquisition are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Added an explicit `excludeSystemPromptCheckpoints` accounting option, used only by `readCompactionTranscriptBytes`.
- The projection reader excludes rows whose facts navigation entry has `customType: "openclaw.system-prompt"`, under a separate cache key so normal accounting is unaffected.
- The in-memory actor accounting path applies the same filter.
- Resident replica accounting declines its cached shortcut when exclusion is requested, so warm sessions reach the exclusion-aware projection reader.
- Rows without optional fact records are classified through canonical transcript navigation instead of being assumed conversational.
- Context eligibility, checkpoint restoration, raw hydration limits, and usage/tail accounting are untouched.

## Evidence

- New tests in `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-projection-facts.test.ts`, `src/config/sessions/session-actor-memory-history.test.ts`, and `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-accounting-replica.test.ts` build a 150 KB checkpoint and verify default accounting still counts 3 events while compaction pressure counts 2 conversation events and drops the checkpoint bytes. Separate regressions cover a deleted fact row and the resident-replica shortcut.
- Red on base: removing the exclusion makes the projection test report 3 events; restoring the fact-row assumption and the replica shortcut makes the missing-facts and warm-path tests fail.
- Green with the fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/config/sessions/session-actor-memory-history.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-transcript-projection-facts.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-byte-size.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-transcript-accounting-replica.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 60 tests passed.
- Format, oxlint, and `git diff --check` pass.

Gap: no live Gateway with a large MCP tool surface was reproduced; the tests measure the accounting boundary directly.
