prs.title: fix: fail when gateway install options would be ignored
prs.body:
Closes #202002

## What Problem This Solves

When the Gateway service is already installed, `openclaw gateway install --port <new>` (or `--token <new>`) without `--force` returns `ok: true` / `already-installed` and exits 0, but the service keeps the old port and token. Automation that changes a port or rotates a token believes the change was applied; clients then connect to the old port.

## User Impact

User impact: the command now fails with an actionable error when an explicit `--port` or `--token` would be ignored, instead of reporting success. A matching explicit port/token still returns `already-installed`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before the already-installed success result, the installed command is inspected for its port and embedded token. A differing explicit `--port` fails with a `--force --port <n>` reinstall hint; a differing `--token` fails with a hint to set `gateway.auth.token`/`OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` and reinstall, because install does not persist `--token`. Other refresh reasons (`--runtime`, `--wrapper`, config/env token drift, CA bundles) keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- New tests in `src/cli/daemon-cli/install.test.ts` cover rejected port, rejected token, matching values, and a matching config-backed token with no supervisor metadata.
- Red on base: with the new check removed, the port and token tests fail with no recorded failure; the matching case still passes.
- Green with the fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/daemon-cli/install.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 41 tests passed.
- Format, oxlint, and `git diff --check` pass.

Gap: no live launchd/systemd/schtasks service was exercised; the tests use the shared install-plan and service mocks.

prs.title: fix(pr): retain equivalent reviewed workflows for baseline proof
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Initial baseline-proof preparation rejects a retained reviewed workflow whenever main advances, even when the complete workflow, dependency and policy inputs are unchanged. This change admits that equivalent case without relaxing later publication or merge gates.

## Change

- For initial `prepare-baseline-refresh --for-proof`, authenticate current main, require reviewed-workflow ancestry, and compare complete inventories, file types/modes, dependency/install inputs and runtime policy. Carry provenance through the native context and signed baseline binding. Equal commit IDs reuse their computed facts within each check; every admission boundary remains.
- Validate custody and preparation inputs before retiring active evidence. Preserve pending-proof acceptance retirement and qualified-baseline rejection rules.
- Keep the selected workflow's dependency revision independent of the bootstrap revision. Creator reentry retains the selected revision; unbound commands use the bootstrap revision. The consolidated materializer retains authenticated tree export and lifetime ownership.
- Batch read-only blob hashing in the existing native Git owner using at most five unlinked, read-only snapshot descriptors. Preserve native object-format, collision-detection and filter semantics; validate ordered output count and IDs. Attempt every acquired descriptor close once, preserve the primary error, and clean the snapshot directory. Object-writing hash calls, fresh authority reads, replay, signatures and FD7/8/9 custody remain unchanged.
- Remove discarded fixture setup and the first acquisition's immediate delete/restore roundtrip. Subsequent acquisitions still restore the complete private root. The generated fixture GitHub adapter resolves each response's required refs in one fresh ordered Git query, preserving overrides, errors and merge-live behavior. All native transitions, assertions and 120s test deadlines remain.

Against frozen main `1aced63107163f7b47deafb6a4a11e66dacd59b2`, the authored scope is **18 files**: production **+825/-358 (net +467)**, tests **+1155/-82 (net +1073)**, docs **+28/-5**, inventory **+17**, and one three-line allocation record. Production growth implements complete admission, sealed provenance, validation before evidence retirement and bounded immutable-snapshot ownership. The latest production delta is **+86/-30 (net +56)**; no cache, asynchronous hashing service or replacement crypto implementation was added.

The allocation grants exactly **673** lines beyond the normal 400-line allowance for **1073** net test lines, with no unused credit. Coverage includes real-Git workflow admission, frozen dependency selection, preflight preservation, captured-hash descriptor cleanup and fresh fixture-adapter refs. The native staged ratchet against the frozen base passed with both new test files tracked. The allocation does not waive runtime or review gates.

prs.title: feat: let agents participate selectively in group conversations
prs.body:
## Problem and motivation

When mention gating is disabled in a group, the primary reply model receives admitted messages and decides whether to participate as part of an agent turn. Many of those messages are exchanges between other people, questions that have already been answered, or chatter where another reply would add little value. Starting the primary agent for every such message creates unnecessary work and conversation noise.

Requiring an explicit mention avoids some of that work but misses indirect invitations and useful opportunities to contribute. A configured Decision Model should make the participation choice using the existing group etiquette, while the primary model keeps generating replies in its usual voice.

## Solution

With the existing default-off Decision assistance setting enabled and a Decision Model configured, assess eligible unmentioned text messages in always-on groups and channels before primary generation.

The assessment receives the current message, reply reference, bounded recent conversation, and bounded workspace identity text. Identity context uses the existing workspace loader and context formatter, preserving heading/prose `IDENTITY.md` files and configured identity precedence.

- **Reply:** continue through the ordinary agent generation and delivery path. The turn carries approval as the existing result-required completion policy, and turn context tells the primary model to generate its reply in its usual voice.
- **Silent:** record the incoming message through the existing transcript owner and finish the turn without primary generation.
- **Assessment unavailable:** use the ordinary reply path.

The existing admission, transcript, queue, cancellation, permissions, and delivery owners remain responsible for their normal work. A declined queued source is consumed after persistence, so the recorded input is not retried as an abandoned request. The completion owner uses confirmed current-source delivery evidence. `NO_REPLY` after message-tool delivery prevents duplicate output. An undelivered `NO_REPLY` remains an unfulfilled reply and follows existing bounded generation recovery and failure handling. Source-delivery retries retain that requirement; they do not make another participation choice. Exhausted or refused retries record failure through the existing runner, and system notices retain their existing permission.

## Scope and rollout

This uses the existing Decision assistance Labs flag and configured `decisionModel`; there is no separate participation setting. An already-saved enabled preference also enables this capability after upgrade.

Explicit mentions, commands, media inputs, ambient room events, internal events, and generic CLI backends keep their existing paths. When Decision assistance is disabled or unavailable, the primary model retains its ordinary participation behavior.

Assessments use the selected Decision provider and may incur its normal charges. The provider receives the identity and conversation evidence described above. Each assessment is bounded by the turn timeout and a maximum of 30 seconds.

## Validation

The existing approved-text case reproduced approval followed by primary `NO_REPLY` completing without an answer before the fix, then passed with normal generation recovery and delivery. The existing message-tool case still completes without a duplicate reply. A second revised existing case reproduced queued delivery retry being disabled by the stronger completion policy.

Focused validation covered 168 existing cases across five files. After the final source-receipt consolidation, all 73 affected immediate/queued consumer cases passed in 77.02 seconds. The unchanged terminal-resolution and stranded-recovery suites also passed. No test cases or fixture frameworks were added.

The final messaging type-check graph, formatting, syntax guards, whitespace checks, and source/test line ratchets pass. Independent source review is clean. It also traced private transcript receipts, exhausted retry settlement, and refused retry enqueue through the existing owners. The 129-line allocation covers the excess above the 400-line allowance: 529 net test lines retain native participation, persistence, source settlement, and delivery coverage.

Full package build, final-head CI, and a controlled live-provider replay remain unverified.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): count incomplete WAL checkpoints during fallback
prs.body:
Closes #202219

## What Problem This Solves

SQLite WAL reclamation underreports incomplete checkpoint attempts when a busy TRUNCATE falls back to PASSIVE. The reported count omits the first incomplete attempt even when both attempts are blocked.

## User Impact

Operators inspecting reclamation results get the number of incomplete attempts. Archive cleanup still uses effective checkpoint completion to decide whether it can proceed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record each callback result before the next attempt can replace it. The final result continues to express whether the checkpoint completed. Reported by [yunligou711-commits](https://github.com/yunligou711-commits).

## Evidence

- Real temporary SQLite databases with a pinned reader reproduced both undercounts on base d119c6b0035e. When PASSIVE completed the count was 0 instead of 1, and when PASSIVE remained blocked the count was 1 instead of 2. Both regressions pass with the fix.
- 47 focused tests across checkpointing, reclamation, archive pruning, and WAL budget recovery. 357.19 seconds elapsed on the ECS development host. Production and relevant test type checks, targeted typed lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Independent desktop review verified staged tree 3638586efd88 and found no blocking issues. GitHub CI will exercise the broader suite.

### Built-runtime replay

Built the runtime from PR head c9c4661fe6c4396418d3c976d6e785b3855e8485 with the repository tsdown unified runtime target. Node 24.22.1 and SQLite 3.53.4. The replay called the built session page-reclamation entry, which dispatched the normal session.archivePruning.reclaimPages operation to the database worker. Each case used a fresh temporary database and a real read-only SQLite transaction. In the second case a write after the reader's snapshot left a newer WAL frame.

Runtime results, printed from the worker replies:

```jsonl
{"scenario":"passive-completes","checkpointCalls":2,"checkpointIncomplete":1,"checkpointCompleted":true,"vacuumPasses":0}
{"scenario":"passive-blocked","checkpointCalls":2,"checkpointIncomplete":2,"checkpointCompleted":false,"vacuumPasses":0}
```

The replay ran offline with a temporary home, configuration, and state directory. These counters are from the worker response. The earlier native regressions provide the base comparison. The external-contributor CI run awaits maintainer approval.

prs.title: feat(plugins): composer tasks can send their result and resume in a returning chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two gaps in composer tasks (#201695), found while using the Better plugin:

- **No send.** An action whose result the user wants sent right away ("rewrite and send") had to insert it and leave the user to press Enter.
- **Work is dropped on a chat switch.** Leaving the chat retires the action, so its card disappears while the work it started (a Gateway run) keeps going. Coming back shows nothing, the work is unreachable, and the plugin cannot even stop it because its UI handle has ended. In Better this surfaced as "already running; Cancel stops it" with no card and no Cancel.

## User Impact

- `task.propose(text, { title, send: true })` inserts the text and then sends it through the composer's own send, as Enter would: same admission, follow-up queueing, connection, dictation, goal and pending-attachment checks. When the composer cannot send yet, the inserted draft stays unsent with its Undo receipt; a locked editor keeps the proposal for Use, as with `insert`.
- A composer action can declare `attach`. The host calls it, with the same context as `run`, each time a built-in composer shows the chat (mount, chat switch, return from another page), so the action can start a task again and follow its earlier work. `startTask({ startedAt })` keeps the original elapsed clock. Leaving still aborts the action's `signal` and retires the card; the action keeps its work going and stops it only when the task's signal aborts while `signal` has not (the user's Cancel).

Both are optional and additive.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Send goes through the existing owner.** The mounted composer publishes its send beside its Escape stop policy (`state.sendDraft`, cleared on unmount), and `submitDraft` now reports whether it submitted. The task owner calls it after inserting; no second send path.
- **Attach is a presentation event, not a retained handle.** Composer handles still retire on chat switch, so a retained handle never touches another chat's draft. `attach` gets a fresh handle bound to the chat being shown, once per presentation lifetime, after the render settles. The work's own owner (the plugin's Gateway run) decides whether there is anything to show.

## Evidence

- New e2e in `native-plugin-composer.e2e.test.ts`: `send: true` produces exactly one `chat.send` with the rewritten text and clears the composer (red without the send: 0 sends); a running task leaves with its chat and returns with the original clock (`1m 0Xs`) when the chat is shown again, then inserts its result there.
- All composer-task and native plugin UI e2e (19) and unit tests pass; `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:core`, oxlint, controller guard, line-cap and test-lines ratchets.
- Chat boot JS +73 B gzip vs the merge base, within the limit.

**SDK impact.** Additive: optional `send` on `ControlUiDraftProposal`, optional `attach` on `ControlUiAction`, optional `startedAt` on `startTask`. The only consumer is the Better plugin.

prs.title: fix(feishu): attach recent group images to @-mentions with no media
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in a Feishu group, the bot cannot read a screenshot the user sent before @-mentioning it in a separate message, so it sees only a placeholder and asks the user to resend the image.

## User Impact

Group @-mentions can now reference screenshots sent before the @, however much earlier, as long as the image is still among the last 20 group messages. No change for DMs or for @ messages that already carry media.

## Why This Change Was Made

The channel only resolved media for the @ message itself. `resolveFeishuMediaListWithLookback` (new, `extensions/feishu/src/bot-recent-images.ts`) resolves media for the current message as before, and when the @ message is in a group with no media of its own, it lists the 20 most recent group messages and attaches any image/post messages found (max 5). Lookback failures only log and never break the message. One extra `im.message.list` call per media-less group @-mention, capped at 5 downloaded images.

## Evidence

- New unit tests in `extensions/feishu/src/bot-recent-images.test.ts` (4 tests): current media short-circuits the lookback, lookback attaches a recent group image, DMs skip the lookback, lookback failure returns current media. All 4 pass.
- The lookback test fails when the lookback is disabled (verified by temporarily forcing an early return).
- Full `extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts` passes (60 tests); total 64 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` (typecheck), oxlint, oxfmt, and `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` all pass.

prs.title: fix(openrouter): non-Gemini image models ignore the requested aspect ratio
prs.body:
Related: #199883 (fixes the aspect-ratio part; resolution forwarding for non-Gemini models stays open there)
Related: #199902 (same bug; this PR differs in how it treats resolution, see below)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: images generated through OpenRouter with a non-Gemini model (for example Seedream 5.5) always come back in the model's default shape, because the requested aspect ratio is dropped before the request is sent.

## User Impact

User impact: `aspectRatio` now takes effect for every OpenRouter image model on the dedicated image endpoint.

One behavior change to be aware of: a ratio the selected model does not support now returns OpenRouter's error, which names the accepted values. Before, that ratio was silently ignored and an image in the default shape was returned. Resolution handling is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dedicated `/images` request took its geometry from the Gemini-only chat `image_config`. It now reads the aspect ratio from the validated request for all models.

Resolution stays Gemini-only on purpose. For edits, `image_generate` infers a resolution from the reference image (`4K` at 3000 px or more, `2K` at 1500 px or more), and other models accept different sets: Seedream 5.5 rejects `4K` and accepts `1K`, `1.5K`, `2K`. Forwarding the inferred value for every model would turn a Seedream edit of an ordinary phone photo, which works today, into an HTTP 400. Doing that safely needs per-model `resolutionsByModel` data, which fits better in a follow-up.

#199902 forwards both fields. That is the one functional difference between the two PRs, and the live results below are meant to help either one land.

## Evidence

**Live, shipped CLI entry point** (`openclaw infer image generate`, real OpenRouter key, paths shortened). The patched run is `node openclaw.mjs` from this branch after `pnpm build`, in an empty state directory with only `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` set. It reports `OpenClaw 2026.11.4 (ff91bc0)`; the current head `e409aa844` has the same tree and differs only in the commit message (`Related` instead of `Closes`). The "before" run is the released npm package, not a build of the base commit.

```
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20)
$ openclaw infer image generate --model openrouter/bytedance-seed/seedream-5-5 --aspect-ratio 16:9 \
    --prompt "A red paper boat on a calm pond, minimal." --output released-seedream-16x9.png --json
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "image.generate",
  "transport": "local",
  "provider": "openrouter",
  "model": "bytedance-seed/seedream-5-5",
  "attempts": [],
  "outputs": [
    { "path": "released-seedream-16x9.png", "mimeType": "image/png", "size": 5008357, "width": 2048, "height": 2048 }
  ],
  "ignoredOverrides": []
}

$ node openclaw.mjs infer image generate --model openrouter/bytedance-seed/seedream-5-5 --aspect-ratio 16:9 \
    --prompt "A red paper boat on a calm pond, minimal." --output patched-seedream-16x9.png --json
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "image.generate",
  "transport": "local",
  "provider": "openrouter",
  "model": "bytedance-seed/seedream-5-5",
  "attempts": [],
  "outputs": [
    { "path": "patched-seedream-16x9.png", "mimeType": "image/png", "size": 2550015, "width": 2048, "height": 1152 }
  ],
  "ignoredOverrides": []
}

$ node openclaw.mjs infer image generate --model openrouter/bytedance-seed/seedream-5-5 --aspect-ratio 3:4 \
    --prompt "A red paper boat on a calm pond, minimal." --output patched-seedream-3x4.png --json
  ... "width": 1536, "height": 2048 ...
```

The released CLI reports `"ignoredOverrides": []` while returning a square image, so the drop is silent today.

**Live, provider code called directly.** `buildOpenRouterImageGenerationProvider().generateImage(...)` was run from this checkout with a real key (in-process, not the CLI), prompt "A red paper boat on a calm pond, minimal.":

| Code | Model | `aspectRatio` | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| base `7f234bd91` | `bytedance-seed/seedream-5-5` | `16:9` | 2048x2048 (bug reproduced) |
| this PR | `bytedance-seed/seedream-5-5` | `16:9` | 2048x1152 |
| this PR | `bytedance-seed/seedream-5-5` | `3:4` | 1536x2048 |
| this PR | `google/gemini-3.1-flash-image` | `16:9` | 1376x768 (path unchanged) |
| this PR | `openai/gpt-image-2` | `4:5` | HTTP 400, "aspect_ratio: not supported. Accepted: 1:1, 3:2, 2:3, 4:3, 3:4, 16:9, 9:16, 21:9, auto" |

**Live, direct `POST /api/v1/images` calls** (to answer the open question about resolution on #199883):

| Model | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `bytedance-seed/seedream-5-5` | `aspect_ratio: 16:9`, `resolution: 2K` | 2048x1152 |
| `bytedance-seed/seedream-5-5` | `aspect_ratio: 3:4`, `resolution: 1K` | 832x1110 |
| `bytedance-seed/seedream-5-5` | `aspect_ratio: 1:1`, `resolution: 4K` | HTTP 400, "resolution: not supported. Accepted: 1K, 1.5K, 2K" |
| `bytedance-seed/seedream-5-5` | edit (`input_references`), `resolution: 4K` | HTTP 400, same message |
| `bytedance-seed/seedream-5-5` | edit (`input_references`), `aspect_ratio: 3:2` | 2048x1366 |
| `black-forest-labs/flux.2-pro` | `aspect_ratio: 16:9`, `resolution: 2K` | 2048x1152 |
| `openai/gpt-image-2` | `aspect_ratio: 3:2`, `resolution: 2K` | 1536x1024 |

**Tests and checks**, run locally on Linux, Node 24.22.2:

- New regression `forwards the requested aspect ratio for non-Gemini canonical requests`: fails on base (`aspect_ratio` missing from the request body), passes with the fix. It also asserts that a `4K` resolution is not forwarded for a non-Gemini edit.
- `pnpm test extensions/openrouter/image-generation-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 11 passed
- `pnpm test:extension openrouter`: 286 passed
- `pnpm test src/image-generation/runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 15 passed
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the two changed files, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `git diff --check`: passed
- `pnpm build`: passed (needed for the CLI runs above)

**Gaps**

- The custom-base-URL chat-completions path is not changed and still sends `image_config` for Gemini only. It was not tested live.
- Live coverage is limited to the models in the tables above. The CLI proof covers generation; the edit path was exercised through direct endpoint calls and the unit regression, not through the `image_generate` tool.
- PR CI has not run yet: the workflow is waiting for maintainer approval (`action_required`).

AI disclosure: written with an AI coding agent (Claude) on behalf of the issue reporter. The live calls and test runs above were executed, not simulated.

Updates `androidx.test.uiautomator:uiautomator` from 2.4.0 to 2.4.1 Updates `org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on` from 1.86 to 1.87
Changelog

Sourced from org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on's changelog.

Version 1.87

Release: 1.87
Date: 2026, 11th November.

Defects Fixed

  • PrivateKeyFactory, and so the ML-DSA and ML-KEM KeyFactory services, ignored the tag of the RFC 9881 / RFC 9935 private key CHOICE and applied no length checks, so mislabelled or inconsistent seed, expandedKey and both forms were accepted. Each form is now checked for its tag, exact lengths and consistency; the pre-RFC draft forms are still read.
  • X500Name.equals was quadratic in the number of RDNs for names that are equal but not byte-identical, and is reached from unverified CMS, TSP and S/MIME messages; the CMS signer and recipient stores could also be slowed with colliding ids. Name comparison is now n log n and the stores no longer hash their entries (CVE-2026-103611).
  • Tables keyed on ASN.1 object hash codes, which a sender can make collide - Extensions, X509Extensions, ExtendedKeyUsage, the CMS AttributeTable, the EST CSRAttributesResponse and the CMS digest algorithm sets - made parsing quadratic in the number of entries. They are now ordered maps and sets.
  • CMSSignedData digested the content once for every signer verified. Signers using the same digest algorithm now share one digest, and the new org.bouncycastle.cms.max_digest_algorithms property can bound the number of distinct digest algorithms computed over one message.
  • The verify side of the ML-DSA-CALCULATE-MU signature service, and MLDSASigner.verifyMu, did not absorb the message, so a correct mu was accepted only for an empty message, and the signer was left unusable afterwards. verifyMu now derives mu as generateMu does and compares in constant time.
  • KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("SM2", "BC") was built on the generic EC generator and could draw a private key of n - 1, which GB/T 32918.1 excludes. It now uses SM2KeyPairGenerator.
  • ESTResponse was quadratic in the number of repeated header lines, and a read limit only applied after the header block. Header values are now collected once and the header block counts against the read limit.
  • The C509 encoding of RFC 6955 proof-of-possession signature values and of the RFC 9883 privateKeyPossessionStatement attribute did not follow draft-ietf-cose-cbor-encoded-cert-21 and could not be reconstructed. Both now convert in each direction, and the draft-ietf-cose-c509-test-vectors-02 vectors drive the tests.
  • DANE SMIMEA support: JndiDANEFetcherFactory mangled the owner name of listed records so lookups failed, DANEEntryStore kept only one entry per owner name, and DANEEntrySelectorFactory mishandled addresses with a quoted local-part or no '@'. All three are corrected, and DANEEntry rejects a record that is not a full certificate entry.
  • TimeStampToken accepted a token whose signing-time attribute disagreed with the genTime in its TSTInfo. Such a token is now rejected (org.bouncycastle.tsp.allow_inconsistent_signing_time switches the check off), and TimeStampTokenGenerator sets signing-time from the genTime (CVE-2026-103615).
  • TimeStampToken.validate() accepted an MD5 message imprint and TSPAlgorithms.ALLOWED included MD5. MD5 is removed from ALLOWED, validate() rejects an imprint algorithm outside the allowed set, and TSPAlgorithms.LEGACY and org.bouncycastle.tsp.allowed_imprint_algorithms are provided for callers needing it (CVE-2026-103606).
  • CRL-based revocation checking mishandled a CRL entry reasonCode outside the RFC 5280 set: 11 left the certificate unrevoked and other values threw an unchecked exception. An undefined reasonCode is now processed as unspecified.
  • OERDefinition.enumItem(label, value) discarded the explicit enumerand value. The value is now kept and unnumbered items are numbered as X.680 sec. 20 specifies.
  • OERInputStream did not detect a stream ending inside an INTEGER or BIT STRING value, decoding the zero-padded buffer instead. Length-driven reads now fail with EOFException and do not allocate a declared length up front.
  • The OER codec encoded a signed INTEGER whose upper bound is exactly the maximum of a fixed-size word in the next word up; X.696 sec. 10.4 bounds are inclusive.
  • The ETSI TS 102 941 response code wrappers range-checked a truncated int value, so 2^32 was accepted as "ok". Out-of-range values are now rejected.
  • OERInputStream accepted an empty group of octets as zero in four places where X.696 requires at least one octet. Each now fails with an IOException.
  • OEROutputStream could not encode a CHOICE whose chosen alternative has a tag number of 63 or more.
  • OEROutputStream rejected a required SEQUENCE component as absent when it arrived wrapped in a defined OEROptional.
  • OERInputStream failed with a NullPointerException for an absent optional SEQUENCE component selected through a switch that has a default value.
  • OERInputStream truncated a SEQUENCE OF count to 32 bits. A count that does not fit in 31 bits is now rejected.
  • OERInputStream rejected a valid SEQUENCE OF on streams whose available() reported fewer bytes than the element count. The count is now bounded by the decoder's allocation ceiling instead.
  • OERInputStream could not decode a variable-size BIT STRING, and mis-sized a fixed one that is not a whole number of octets. Both forms of X.696 clause 13 are now decoded, and OERDefinition gains bitString() and bitString(lower, upper).
  • OEROutputStream wrote a negative INTEGER under a type with a non-negative lower bound as a different, positive value. It is now rejected.
  • OERInputStream.uint64() read its value as signed; it now reads unsigned.
  • The OER codec treated an INTEGER with a positive lower bound as signed, where X.696 sec. 10.2 gives it the unsigned encodings.
  • The OER codec encoded and decoded negative ENUMERATED values wrongly; both directions now follow X.696 sec. 11.4.
  • ASN1Enumerated rejected negative values, which X.680 allows. The checks are removed, isNegative() and longValueExact() are added, and valueOf() returns shared instances for 0 to 15.
  • A PBEKey stored in a BCFKS KeyStore was not reported as a key entry, so KeyStore.getEntry() returned null for it.
  • The CMS content-type decoders (SignedData, EnvelopedData, AuthenticatedData, AuthEnvelopedData, EncryptedData) and the streaming CMS parsers let unchecked exceptions escape for short or malformed content. Malformed content is now reported through the declared CMSException or IOException.
  • A KeyAgreement asked for its shared secret before doPhase returned data rather than throwing IllegalStateException - for Diffie-Hellman, the private value itself. Every key agreement in the provider now refuses the request.
  • Mac.getInstance and KeyGenerator.getInstance failed for the HMAC SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256 object identifiers; both are now aliased.
  • A KTSParameterSpec naming an HKDF with parameters was accepted at Cipher init and failed with an unchecked exception from wrap or unwrap. The KTS Ciphers now report it at init as InvalidAlgorithmParameterException.
  • A DTLS handshake deadlocked when a handshake message ahead of the peer's ChangeCipherSpec was lost while the ChangeCipherSpec and Finished arrived, as retransmissions were discarded as belonging to the old epoch. They are now accepted until the handshake completes.
  • The lightweight key info factories encoded a GOST R 34.10-2012 key on a legacy CryptoPro curve under id-GostR3410-2001. The digestParamSet now decides, and is OPTIONAL on read and write per RFC 9215 (bc-csharp github #707).
  • Name-constraint checking canonicalised a host with an extra empty label, such as "example.com..", into a name that matched no constraint, escaping an excluded subtree. A tested name whose host carries an empty label is now refused where a constraint of that type is in force (github PR #2436).
  • SSLContext.createSSLEngine() from BCJSSE in the 1.86 bctls jar failed with NoSuchMethodError on JDK 9 and later, from a return type mismatch between the base and jdk1.9 copies of SSLEngineUtil. The copies now agree, and a new multiReleaseCheck build task checks every multi-release jar for such mismatches (github #2448).
  • The BCFKS key store derived its scrypt keys with the block size r in place of the parallelization parameter p, so stores with p != r were not RFC 7914 readable. Derivation now follows RFC 7914, older stores are still read, and org.bouncycastle.bcfks.scrypt_p_eq_r (default true) keeps written stores readable by earlier releases.
  • Building an evidence record was cubic in the number of data objects. SortedHashList and SortedIndexedHashList now sort once, with the same resulting order and root hashes (github #2456).
  • ERSDataGroup recomputed its hash on every request rather than using the ERSCachingData cache.
  • ERSArchiveTimeStampGenerator rebuilt its reduced hash tree on every call; it is now built once.
  • Grain-128AEAD returned corrupted plaintext, with no error, from a decryption driven in chunks carrying more than the tag length. One-shot decryption and encryption were unaffected (github PR #2447).
  • The certificate path validators looked up an indirect CRL entry by serial number alone, so where two issuers had revoked the same serial number a revoked certificate could be reported as not revoked. Entries are now matched on issuer and serial number, including for CRLs parsed by the JDK's provider and in the jdk1.4 distribution.

v1.13.0

This release is based on Kotlin 2.4.10 and reverts a breaking change introduced in 1.12.0.

Besides that, it improves JsonElement.toString performance.

In 1.12.0, Json format started intercepting almost all exceptions thrown by serializers during serialization and deserialization, and wrapping them into a JsonException with additional information about JSON path and input.

The impact of the change was underestimated, and it was decided to revert the change.

Updates `org.robolectric:robolectric` from 4.17 to 4.18
Release notes

Sourced from org.robolectric:robolectric's releases.

Robolectric 4.18 adds Linux arm64 support to the native runtime, supports native resources on SDK 36 and above, and contains many performance improvements and bug fixes.

If you have any issues, please file them here.

Breaking Changes

  • Support for SDK 23 has been removed. The minimum supported SDK is now 24, matching AndroidX (#11604).
  • The shadows-httpclient module has been removed. It was deprecated in 4.17, and org.apache.http is no longer instrumented (#11373, #11544).
  • @TextLayoutMode has been removed. Realistic text layout, the default since 2019, is now always used (#11498).
  • ShadowRemoteCallbackList has been removed, as the real RemoteCallbackList works without it (#11368).
  • HttpResponseCache.install() now also sets ResponseCache.getDefault(), as it does on a device (#11493).

Linux arm64 support

Robolectric's native runtime now includes Linux arm64 (aarch64) native libraries, so tests that use native SQLite (the default) and native graphics (@GraphicsMode(NATIVE)) can run on Linux arm64 environments, such as GitHub's ubuntu-24.04-arm runners, AWS Graviton machines, and arm64 Docker containers on Apple silicon. No configuration is needed (#11625, #11633). As on Apple silicon, the legacy SQLite mode (SQLiteMode.Mode.LEGACY) isn't supported on Linux arm64.

Other Highlights

  • Native resources (ResourcesMode.NATIVE) now work on SDK 36 and above, not only SDK 36 (#11578).
  • Robolectric no longer prints the "restricted method in java.lang.System has been called" warnings on JDK 24+ (#11482).
  • The shadow annotation processor now supports KSP (#10996).
  • Lots of performance improvements:
    • Resource values are shared between bags and themes instead of copied (#11726, #11595)
    • Faster shadow method lookups (#11723, #11593)
    • Cached resource reference resolution (#11586)
    • Cached service and plugin lookups (#11451, #11594, #11631)
    • Native runtime assets are extracted once and shared (#11453, #11522)
    • Faster class loading checks in the sandbox (#11662)
    • Regexes compiled once instead of on every use (#11399, #11400, #11401)
  • Conscrypt is now enabled by default on Mac arm64 (#11352).

What's Changed

  • Sign all .module metadata files. by @​brettchabot in robolectric/robolectric#11327

prs.title: fix: MCP App cards report a missing session while session metadata changes
prs.body:
Closes #199765

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an MCP App card shows `MCP App unavailable: Session "…" was not found.` for a non-admin Control UI user when the session's metadata (label, activity time, token counts) is written while the App view or an App operation is in flight.

## User Impact

MCP App cards and their tool and resource operations keep working while a session's harmless metadata changes. Changes to access (visibility, session reset, lifecycle replacement, creator, incognito) still end the read.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both MCP App retained reads (`mcp.app.view` and the shared handler behind `mcp.app.callTool`, `listTools`, `listResources`, `listResourceTemplates` and `readResource`) used the strict row match, so any metadata write made the retained row non-current. They now pass the existing `allowMetadataChanges` option, which compares only access facts through `hasSessionReadAccessChanged`. #162681 made the same change for approval subscriptions. Write authority for `mcp.app.callTool` is unchanged: it is still checked by its own session mutation authorization.

## Evidence

New `src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-app.session-metadata.test.ts` sends `mcp.app.view` and `mcp.app.readResource` through `handleGatewayRequest` as a non-admin `view`-role reader, with a real committed session write landing while the read is held.

- Base: both fail on the metadata-only case with the reported error, `UNAVAILABLE: Session "agent:main:mcp-app-metadata" was not found.`
- Fix: both pass; visibility revoked and session replaced are still rejected.
- Neighbors: `mcp-app.test.ts`, `mcp-app.view-grant.test.ts`, `server-methods.session-scoped-reads.test.ts` pass (87 tests).
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the changed files pass. Typecheck was not run locally; left to CI.
- Cost: the new file's tests take about 3 s; `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall time is about 170 s here, almost all transform.

Live run (throwaway Playwright test, not committed): real Gateway, a non-admin `guest` profile through the trusted proxy (scopes `operator.read`/`operator.write`/`operator.sessions.*`, role `sessions.others: write`), the Control UI `mcp-app-view`, and the stdio MCP App fixture from the conformance suite. The session is shared and owned by another profile. A real `replaceSessionEntrySync` writes label, tokens and `updatedAt` every 5 ms while the App mounts, then once while an App `tools/call` is in flight.

- Base (`mcp-app.ts` from the parent commit): the card shows `This app couldn't load. Session "agent:main:mcp-app-metadata-proof" was not found.`
- Fix: the App mounts and renders `initial-result`, and the in-flight `tools/call` returns `companion-called` after the metadata write.

Not run on base: the in-flight operation step, because the view already fails there.

prs.title: fix(update): keep legacy Git services on their release launcher
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repairing a Gateway service while a legacy Git release is active can save its direct `dist/index.js` path instead of the existing release launcher. That bypasses release selection and launcher-owned trial recovery.

## User Impact

Services restored from the older `lib/node_modules/openclaw` layout keep using the prefix-level launcher. Current Git layouts retain the same behavior. No configuration or migration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The release-slot parser already validates both layouts and returns their install prefix. Use that prefix instead of reconstructing it from the package directory. Keep the OpenClaw package-name restriction and the caller's existing launcher-access check.

Production delta: +4/−5 lines. Test delta: +45/−13 lines.

## Evidence

- A filesystem probe using the actual owner modules reproduced the legacy lookup failure at `92d147da1552602f7636665e49dd75677b5e48d3`; the same probe passes current, legacy, and other-package rejection cases at `0c6828c45bc2edc79c987c4d0ea4bc6f2c5ae8e2`.
- Independent source review: no actionable finding. Autoreview (P0–P2) reviewed the complete committed range against that base: scoped-clean.
- Local ClawSweeper could not start because its installation is missing `typescript`; autoreview is the documented fallback.
- Blacksmith Testbox: **30/30 focused tests passed under Node 24.22.1** across `git-release.test.ts`, `package-release-slot.test.ts`, and `program-args.pnpm.test.ts`. [Run and logs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44673527204). The transferred source tree `b3a6e7b1a671973d47fc3a0df89f8ed6a2568b7f` equals the reviewed commit tree; the wrapper recorded exit 0 and stopped the lease after completion. [Package Acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44674019443) passed for this head: npm 12 fresh installation and the published-upgrade-survivor/base lane from openclaw@2026.11.6 (593 seconds). [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44674203488) also passed.
- A second [isolated Node run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44674127825) confirmed the legacy service regression fails with the original owner module, then both layout cases pass with the fix. Targeted formatting and lint also passed; the Testbox recorded exit 0 and was stopped.
- The new regression exercises real filesystem links and `resolveGatewayProgramArguments`. It proves selection of an existing launcher; it does not execute a historical launcher or claim a full historical-release upgrade.

ClawSweeper reviewed this unchanged head with no code findings and no before-merge tasks. The fresh-install and latest-stable proof requested in its testing notes is now linked above; the historical-launcher execution limitation remains explicit.

prs.title: fix: stop unavailable chat widgets from flooding history reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening an old chat with an unavailable Canvas widget can repeatedly request the same failed view whenever later chat events arrive or rows remount. Those requests also search the transcript before discovering that the widget file is gone, competing with other users' history and artifact reads.

## User Impact

Missing saved widgets keep their error visible until the page reloads or the agent creates a replacement. Temporary loading failures, including sandbox startup failures, retry at most five times with exponential backoff, then offer manual Retry. Successful widget responses are unchanged. No configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing request owner now retains terminal failures across row remounts, retires their event subscriptions, and preserves retry backoff. Its request bookkeeping moves into a focused sibling module to stay within the view owner's line limit. Successful HTML remains owned only by mounted views.

The server opens a document immediately after session admission, before searching for its transcript receipt. Missing files release the retained read without entering the shared history-worker pool. Existing files still require the same receipt authorization before any content is returned. Both view responses and dashboard imports consume the document already read by that owner, so successful imports perform one source read. Sandbox startup failures are marked retryable after a valid source read; missing sources retain their terminal classification. Source loading and host startup remain parallel. An admitted session reader now receives generic UNAVAILABLE for a nonexistent arbitrary ID before receipt lookup, while present unreferenced IDs remain FORBIDDEN; document IDs are random UUIDs, and this reveals no bytes or paths.

## Evidence

The synthetic production-bundle Control UI reproduction falls from 13 view requests after 12 later chat-final events to 1. The event/remount unit regression falls from 25 requests to 1. The transient-error regression falls from 45 requests to 6 total attempts. All three fail on the original behavior.

48 focused UI unit tests, 2 Chromium parking/lifecycle tests, 1 mock-Gateway browser E2E, and 48 Canvas server tests pass. Another 31 board tests pass; the dashboard-import work-count regression fails before the follow-up with two source reads and passes with one. The server regression creates a real saved receipt, removes its synthetic document, invokes the actual request route, and verifies UNAVAILABLE without transcript matching; it fails on base. Existing success, guest/branch/archive/revocation and sandbox behavior remain green.

Codex autoreview of the complete local candidate against 66fc4d8848c5ab6ff3d29c8c5d093cfc5a95de7d: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. Production and full-tree unused-file scans pass. All changed-file gates pass after targeted correction: the first full `pnpm check:changed` caught line-cap/format issues, fixed before the second run; the second full run passed every gate except an unknown event payload in the benchmark assertion. The corrected scripts typecheck and lint rerun passed. Core, all core test graphs, UI, scripts, SQLite guards, controller/i18n guards and dependency/import checks are covered. The final-head hosted Codex review was clean on the initial head. Hosted reviews found a sibling dashboard duplicate read and temporary host failures being classified as terminal. Both are fixed with base-red regressions, including actual WebSocket port-conflict recovery. Independent follow-up Codex autoreviews are clean through P3; ClawSweeper reviewed final head `95fb4283e352f972734d9a62c91b7e2378685407` with zero actionable findings and zero open items.

Runtime production LOC: +50. This implements terminal request state and finite retries in the existing owner and carries the already-read document through server authorization. Tests: +313. The rerunnable synthetic performance driver is separate from runtime production.

An additional real-Gateway WebSocket regression occupies the sandbox port, observes retryable UNAVAILABLE for an existing document and nonretryable UNAVAILABLE for a missing document, releases the port, and receives identical HTML. The identical test is red on c3d2601 and green with the classification fix. The UI recovery table proves no retry before 1,000 ms, then successful mounting.

The first CI run also exposed an inherited startup-test timing failure from #196482: cold chat preparation may yield before its row mounts. Controlled slow preparation reproduces the same missing-row assertion on the exact PR parent and CI main parent. The test now awaits the existing row with `waitForSolid`; all Retry/Discard assertions remain intact and the five-test file passes. No production startup behavior changed. The separate 18-error release-page markdownlint regression from #201913 is unchanged and documented in the CI attribution comment.

Related open work: #198629 changes widget loading presentation; #201028 adds widget-header inspection and extracts loading. This repair is limited to failed-read ownership and missing-source work.

### Performance

Acceptance recorded before measurement: remove all history-worker dispatches for missing documents; lower owner latency, CPU and allocation; retain successful behavior. The committed driver is `scripts/perf/canvas-missing-document-measure.ts`. Five interleaved before/after blocks, 20 warm reads per serial block; setup excluded. CPU includes worker threads; native allocation samples the actual synchronous scan in the measuring isolate in a separate run.

| Metric (median of five blocks) | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Missing document owner p50 / p95 | 27.668 / 28.870 ms | 0.140 / 0.235 ms |
| Process CPU per read | 31,214 µs | 369 µs |
| Native scan-owner allocation per read | 6,555,076 B | 52,306 B |
| History-worker requests per 20 missing reads | 20 | 0 |
| Other session history p50 behind 32 missing views | 523.824 ms | 1.867 ms |
| History-worker requests per mixed burst | 33 | 1 |

Serial A/A p50: 27.640 / 27.881 ms (+0.87%); allocation A/A: 6,540,568 / 6,559,968 B (+0.30%); mixed A/A: 559.975 / 548.683 ms (−2.02%). Mixed block medians range 517.209–542.336 ms before and 1.728–2.036 ms after (two bursts/block; not a fleet-tail estimate). A separate CPU profile attributes 4,046 ms to the transcript scan subtree, primarily SQLite row iteration and row matching. Initial mixed measurements were excluded because only one worker was warm; the committed workload warms both before its A/A controls.

The synthetic fixture has 10,000 SQLite sessions and a 10,001-message selected transcript (118 MB database), running on macOS/APFS. This measures real history/file owners after session admission, not transport, a production Linux deployment or complete Gateway latency. The relevant scan is bounded by the selected transcript rather than total workspace size. The shared queue explains history/artifact contention; separate session-describe/send delays are not conclusively attributed by this proof.

Rerun with an absolute new fixture path: `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/canvas-missing-document-measure.ts --fixture <path> --prepare`, then omit `--prepare` for timing; use `--mode allocation --native` for scan allocation or `--workload mixed --iterations 2` for queueing.

### Visual proof

Synthetic mock-Gateway content only; 1280 × 900, light theme. Before is 66fc4d8848c5a; after is 154f1c1cea68d991d6f488fe6ceb364331839f08. The runtime UI source is unchanged in subsequent server and test follow-ups. Clean before/after and annotated before/after follow.

![Before: unavailable widget offers Retry and later chat events repeat its read](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6b7eafe-7641-4eef-becb-1981fc16733b)

![After: terminal unavailable state remains visible without repeated reads](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d75f8bc-5a2a-4027-aae4-00cbd28355ec)

![Before annotated: Retry is offered for a missing widget](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fcf2610e-3414-456a-b0a0-28b5abeb3b46)

![After annotated: unavailable state stays visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be642288-8ed6-463d-8ade-29106636a33a)
## Final CI attribution

[CI run 44675298258](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44675298258), attempt 1, completed at final head `95fb4283e352f972734d9a62c91b7e2378685407`. All selected checks except the two independently attributed main regressions and their aggregate passed, including both real-Gateway E2E shards and security-fast. CI remains failed; the maintainer explicitly authorizes pinned admin landing for proven inherited-only failures.

The 18 release-page MD001/MD024 errors reproduce identically on actual tested main parent `69eb76e6347b37573f91b01240e6b1d6c12871d2`. Restoration `72702a3600f77` / #201913 introduced them versus a clean predecessor. Release page and lint inputs are unchanged by this PR.

Browser shard 3 failed `community-invite-showing.e2e.test.ts:141`: after dismissal it expected Sessions focus, but CI's retained route was `/activity`. Exact-parent reproduction preserves runtime source and the original assertion: delaying the Activity module 300 ms and allowing its pending navigation to settle reproduces the same result. The test clicks Sessions while it remains selected, so the existing handler returns and Activity later commits; dismissal correctly focuses People. #199825 (`7701d7e404c61`) changed the test from a menu click to asynchronous People/Activity navigation without awaiting the route. #201038 (`a6983ed7eeb7`) introduced the current presented-page synchronization; #201208 (`62f44bc09d97`) retained the Sessions no-op in its new location. All five involved owner/test files are identical between main parent and tested merge. Normal passing replays are not offered as a fix. Waiting for Activity and then Chat via the existing route helper makes the same controlled reproduction green; that separate repair is recommended to the lead, not silently folded into this Canvas patch. Both failures are actionable main regressions, not noise.

prs.title: fix(update): keep the temp workspace refusal in the update report
prs.body:
Fixes #201107

## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw update` swaps the live package, the candidate build refuses to start in a temp workspace whose ancestor is group- or world-writable without the sticky bit. That refusal is the actionable half of the failure: it names the directory and the exact `chmod` that clears it.

The update report drops it. The refusal line contains a quoted private path, so the update state inspector redacts the whole diagnostic to `[redacted-diagnostic]` and the user sees only:

```
State schema inspection failed (exit): [redacted-diagnostic]
```

`openclaw update` then rolls back with no way to learn what to fix. Running the candidate's `update-candidate-state.worker.js` by hand prints the real sentence, which is how the report in #201107 was diagnosed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refusal is a closed cause produced by our own code (`assertSafeTempAncestors` in `src/infra/tmp-openclaw-dir.ts`), so it can be published as a fixed public sentence instead of either the raw line or nothing. Two constraints shaped the fix:

- Publishing the raw line would leak a private ancestor path, and loosening `redactPublicSupportDiagnosticLine` to keep arbitrary text would weaken every other update diagnostic that goes through it.
- The temp-permission reason must survive, because "writable temp directory" is the whole explanation, and the `chmod +t` / `chmod go-w` guidance is the fix the user has to run.

So the refusal is promoted through the existing closed-cause table rather than through the redactor: `UPDATE_CANDIDATE_STARTUP_FAILURES` gains an entry for it, and the state inspector resolves the table before falling back to redaction. The public sentence keeps the cause and both recovery commands, and replaces every path with `[redacted-path]`-style omissions by simply not including them.

## User Impact

`openclaw update` now reports why the candidate could not start:

```
State schema inspection failed (exit): temp workspace ancestor is group/world writable without
sticky protection; have its owner run chmod +t for a shared temp directory or chmod go-w for a
private ancestor
```

Users with a permissive `umask` (the #201107 report used `umask 002`, where `~/.local`, `~/.local/lib`, and `~/.openclaw/tmp` are `775`) can act on the message instead of re-running the update blindly. Nothing else changes: the same condition still refuses startup, no path is published, no directory permission is altered, and other worker failures keep their existing redaction.

## Evidence

### Review follow-up: the public report now keeps the closed cause

The first revision promoted the refusal only for the state inspector's own summary. `prepareUpdateFailureReport` re-redacts every fact message through `redactPublicSupportDiagnosticLine`, and its fallback asks `readPublicSupportCauses` which closed sentences may be published — that table did not know the refusal, so the generated report still showed `[redacted-diagnostic]` and dropped the `chmod` guidance. The fix adds the refusal to that shared owner (`src/logging/diagnostic-support-causes.ts`), publishing the fixed sentence and never the ancestor path.

### Real `openclaw update` run (end to end, non-interactive)

Isolated clone of this branch (HEAD `4653ea168f6`, `node_modules` linked, `dist` built from this change), `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` under `/tmp/oc-201133-evidence`, `TMPDIR` pointed at a `0777` directory with no sticky bit (`/tmp` itself is `1777`, so the default root was safe and the fallback ancestor is what fails):

```
node repo/dist/index.js update --yes --no-restart --json
EXIT=1  failedStep: requested  failureFacts[0].code: Error
```

Base (upstream `main` `5ce057b893d` dist, same clone) generated report:

```
Failed: requested — Exit code: 1; No safe OpenClaw temp root is available. Default root: Error: Temp workspace ancestor [redacted-path]
Failing check requested (Error) at dist/tmp-openclaw-dir-BisosRri.mjs:3:2036
```

With this change, the same run's report:

```
Failed: requested — Exit code: 1; temp workspace ancestor is group/world writable without sticky protection; have its owner run chmod +t for a shared temp
Failing check requested (Error) at dist/tmp-openclaw-dir-BisosRri.mjs:3:2036: temp workspace ancestor is group/world writable without sticky protection; have its owner run chmod +t for a shared temp directory or chmod go-w for a private ancestor; No safe OpenClaw temp root is a
```

Reports: base `openclaw-update-report-MjctaY/91c67c78-…md`, fix `openclaw-update-report-N34EIh/8e0bd2ff-…md` (paths under the isolated `TMPDIR`). Both still print the raw ancestor path in the separate “Update terminal preparation failed” line; that line is the pre-existing terminal-preparation diagnostic, identical on base and with this change, and is not part of this fix.

### Regressions

- `src/infra/update-candidate-state.diagnostics.test.ts` — `keeps the temp workspace ancestor refusal when the worker fails`: base **1 failed | 22 passed**, with the fix **23 passed**.
- `src/logging/diagnostic-support-redaction.test.ts` — `publishes the temp workspace ancestor refusal without its private path`: **98 passed** with the fix; fails on base.
- `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-failure-report.test.ts` — `keeps the temp workspace refusal cause in a report read back from saved history` (drives `recordUpdateRunStep` → `getUpdateRun` → `prepareUpdateFailureReport`): **11 passed**; fails on base.
- Base run of all three files (production files reverted to upstream `main`): **3 failed | 129 passed**.
- `oxlint` clean on all changed files.

```
机制对位: 症状在 src/infra/update-candidate-state.diagnostics.ts:209（failure 把 detail 交给 redactPublicSupportDiagnosticLine）与 src/logging/diagnostic-support-causes.ts 的封闭原因白名单（缺该拒绝），我改这两处与 src/infra/update-preflight-details.ts:27，因为该拒绝是我方代码产生的封闭原因，可以按固定公开句发布而不是整条抹掉
复现: node repo/dist/index.js update --yes --no-restart --json（隔离 clone、0777 非 sticky TMPDIR）在 base 上报告为 "Temp workspace ancestor [redacted-path]" 且无原因行，修复后报告首行与失败检查行均含 "temp workspace ancestor is group/world writable… chmod +t … chmod go-w"；单测层 base 3 failed | 129 passed → 132 passed

契约核对: 公开原因白名单由 readPublicSupportCauses（src/logging/diagnostic-support-causes.ts）拥有，UPDATE_CANDIDATE_STARTUP_FAILURES（src/infra/update-preflight-details.ts:8）拥有 inspector 侧闭因，redactPublicSupportDiagnosticLine 的放行仍由其 line === cause 规则（src/logging/diagnostic-support-redaction.ts:564）决定

```

## AI Assistance

This change was prepared by an AI agent (HeMiaolin's assistant) working from the report in #201107 and the review finding on this PR: it reproduced the redacted report at the inspector boundary, traced the refusal to `assertSafeTempAncestors`, extended the shared closed-cause table, and ran a real end-to-end `openclaw update` in an isolated clone to prove the generated report now names the cause and the `chmod` fix.

prs.title: fix: stop Mac app updates from getting stuck when your Gateway wrapper is stored in ~/.openclaw
prs.body:
Related: #202215 (this fixes new occurrences; Macs that already hit it keep an incomplete-update record, see User Impact)
Related: #169919

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway install --wrapper <path>` lets you start the Gateway through your own script, such as a secrets shim or a Node version picker. If that script is stored inside the OpenClaw state directory (for example `~/.openclaw/service-env/` or `~/.openclaw/scripts/`), the Mac app ends its update flow in "Gateway update needs help: The installed Gateway service command could not be inspected." Retry cannot clear it, because the app has nothing it can repair.

## User Impact

User impact: the Mac app now treats a Gateway that starts through your own wrapper in the state directory as externally managed. A fresh app update finishes without the recovery window, and you keep updating the Gateway with the CLI, the same as when the wrapper is in `~/.local/bin`. Services the app installed itself are still detected as app-managed.

If you already saw this window, the app has stored an unfinished-update record, and this change does not clear it. You may then see "The Gateway could not be checked" until that record is cleared with `defaults delete ai.openclaw.mac openclaw.postAppUpdateReceipt` (see #169919).

## Why This Change Was Made

The app decided that it managed the Gateway whenever the service's executable was anywhere under the state directory. It then could not parse the wrapper command into a CLI it could run, so it stopped in the managed-runtime-unavailable state.

Now only two locations prove ownership by themselves: the managed launcher path (`bin/openclaw`) and the seeded runtime subtree (`runtime/`). Other executables under the state directory go through the existing `node`/`bun` entrypoint check. So `tools/node` is detected as before, and versioned installs such as `tools/node-v24.x/bin/node` now follow the same rule: managed when the entrypoint is in the state directory, external otherwise. A wrapper placed inside `runtime/`, or registered at the launcher path itself, is still treated as app-managed, as it was before.

## Evidence

**Real app update and relaunch, in a disposable macOS 26.6.2 VM (tart):** an onboarded install of the official 2026.11.4 release, Gateway CLI 2026.11.6 from npm, and a LaunchAgent started through `~/.openclaw/service-env/my-wrapper.sh` (the same `/bin/sh <env-wrapper> <env> <wrapper> gateway --port 18789` shape as the report). Both runs start from the same saved app settings: last launched version 2026.11.4 and no pending receipt. Each then installs a 2026.11.5 app build over the release and launches it, so the app records the 2026.11.4 → 2026.11.5 update itself.

- **Before, `main` at `9745e409c50`:** "Gateway update needs help / The installed Gateway service command could not be inspected". The receipt is left with `gatewayUpdateIncomplete: true`.
- **After, this PR at `38ef5159778`:** no window. The update finishes quietly and the receipt is cleared. The app connects to the Gateway (`client=openclaw-macos … version=2026.11.5`), and the Gateway keeps the same PID with `Connectivity check: ok`. The LaunchAgent is unchanged, and the app settings are unchanged apart from the two last-launched markers.

### Clean comparison

![Before: main shows "Gateway update needs help" for a healthy Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d48100f-c149-4459-a12b-e2edf71dc3af)

![After: this PR, no recovery window, app running](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6431430b-19c4-4092-a089-fee39fc45709)

### Annotated comparison

![Before, annotated: recovery window for a healthy Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3bbabcc-8ac6-4f17-b0cf-5513bd36aec0)

![After, annotated: app running with no recovery window](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/556f8f2c-21f8-4478-92c8-42f8118114f8)

Both builds come from `scripts/package-mac-app.sh` with `BUILD_CONFIG=debug BUNDLE_ID=ai.openclaw.mac ALLOW_ADHOC_SIGNING=1 OPENCLAW_SKIP_MLX_TTS=1 BUILD_ARCHS=arm64`, so they share the release app's settings domain. The Sparkle download and install step itself was not exercised; the relaunch into the newer build was. The unpatched 2026.11.4 release showed the same window on its own launch in this setup.

### Upgrade from the latest stable release (2026.11.5)

Same VM and wrapper. The official 2026.11.5 release (Developer ID, team `FWJYW4S8P8`) shows the same window after its own update from 2026.11.4. With its pending receipt cleared (last launched 2026.11.5, Gateway still running), I replaced it with this PR's build and relaunched. Result: no window and no receipt left behind. The app connects as `version=2026.11.6`, the Gateway keeps the same PID with `Connectivity check: ok`, the LaunchAgent still runs `my-wrapper.sh`, and the app settings are unchanged apart from the two last-launched markers.

This build is `38ef5159778` with only the root `package.json` version set to 2026.11.6 for the packaging run (not committed), because packaging requires the app version to match the JavaScript build and the app records an update only when the version changes.

![Before: official 2026.11.5 release shows the recovery window](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/110d3c06-2dd2-43f2-b7bd-da152e808dd6)

![After: upgrade from 2026.11.5 to this PR, no recovery window](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ff58c12-65d8-45e6-8f9f-bfc7a68898e0)

![Before, annotated: official 2026.11.5 release](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1289b141-00f4-4091-abf9-a404ce54fa3e)

![After, annotated: upgraded from 2026.11.5 with no window](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a197218a-4da5-4647-b897-6d930a3d864a)

- **New test, fails without the fix and passes with it:**
  - Operator wrappers in `service-env/` and `scripts/`, given bare, behind the env wrapper, and behind `/bin/sh` plus the env wrapper, are not app-managed.
  - For such a service, `resolveGatewayAction` returns no action on a fresh receipt instead of `managedRuntimeUnavailable`. An incomplete receipt keeps the existing ownership-check failure.
  - A versioned `tools/node-v24.x` Node with an outside entrypoint is external; with a state-directory entrypoint it is managed.
  - The stable service Bun (`runtime/service/bun`), the per-build Bun, and the managed launcher behind the env wrapper are still managed.
  - With the source change reverted, the test fails with 15 failed expectations.
- **Existing tests still pass:** the 6 other runtime-ownership and repair-gate tests in `UpdateOrchestrationTests`. All 7 are pure path and decision checks with no file, defaults or service access. I ran each one on its own on a development Mac.
- **Formatting and lint:** `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` and `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` pass with the pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 and SwiftLint 0.65.1.
- **Local review:** autoreview (openclaw/agent-skills `0a5ba4b`, helper `source-sha256:2ea67c44…`, Codex engine), `--mode branch` against base `9745e409c50`, head `38ef5159778`, max priority P2: scoped-clean, with no actionable findings.
- **Original report:** on the reporter's Mac (app 2026.11.5, Gateway 2026.11.6 on npm under nvm), a wrapper in `~/.openclaw/service-env/` brought the recovery window back on every relaunch, while `openclaw gateway status --deep` showed a healthy Gateway. Moving the wrapper out of the state directory and clearing the pending record worked around it.
- **Gap:** I did not run the full macOS suite. `docs/platforms/mac/dev-setup.md` asks for a disposable VM for that, so I'm relying on the `macos-swift` PR CI for it.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests
scripts/format-swift.sh macos
scripts/lint-swift.sh macos
python3 <agent-skills>/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base 9745e409c50 --engine codex --max-priority P2
```

The single tests were run with one exact `--filter` each, for example
``--filter 'UpdateOrchestrationTests/`[^`]*operator wrappers stored'``. Other native tests in this package need the isolated setup in `docs/platforms/mac/dev-setup.md`.

</details>

prs.title: fix: match the web first-run setup to the Mac welcome
prs.body:
Closes #202132

## What Problem This Solves

On a new install, the dashboard's first-run card on main picks an AI by itself and tests it ("Connecting your AI... Checking a real conversation") without showing what it is doing or letting the user choose. Its only choice is **Sign in with ChatGPT**, plus buttons for whatever else the Gateway happened to find. When setup fails, the card lists the Gateway's error text. The Mac app's welcome window walks through clear steps and waits for the user to pick an AI.

## User Impact

The web first-run setup follows the Mac welcome: **Welcome to OpenClaw**, **Where should your assistant run?**, **Connect your AI**, then **You're all set!**.

**Connect your AI** is a short list with one row per provider. Picking a row replaces the list with that provider's own card, with **All choices** to go back:

- **ChatGPT** (first, as on main): when the Gateway already has a Codex login, opening the card tests it, as main does. Otherwise, or when that test fails, the card shows one **Sign in with ChatGPT** button, the same sign-in main uses.
- **Claude**: one **Use my Claude Code login** button when the Gateway found one; otherwise a Claude API key field.
- **Run a model locally**: local models the Gateway found, LM Studio (Connect server) and the Ollama download.
- **Another provider**: every other API key and sign-in (OpenRouter, Copilot and so on) in one menu, plus any other AI the Gateway found.

A refresh link (**Check again**) sits above the list, and as an icon on the local models card. Nothing is tested or saved until the user picks a provider. Errors are one short sentence with the Gateway's text under **Show details**.

## Why This Change Was Made

The card on main calls `openclaw.setup.auto`, which chooses for the user. This PR switches the card to `openclaw.setup.detect` (read only) and runs the user's pick through the same Gateway wizards the web Model Setup page uses (`openclaw.setup.activate.start`, `openclaw.setup.auth.start`, `openclaw.setup.prepare.start`). That way plugin approvals, sign-in codes and the live test question show up as steps the user can answer on the provider's card.

Other details:

- Utility-only choices (a setup helper model) are left to Model Setup, because they cannot finish first-run setup on their own.
- OpenClaw has no browser sign-in for Claude, so the Claude card uses the easiest existing route: a Claude Code login, otherwise an API key.
- The card no longer uses the shell hook that opened a native AI setup window, so I removed it from `nativeSetupCapability`.
- `openclaw.setup.auto` stays on the Gateway: the Mac app checks for it before opening the dashboard on first run.
- The docs for first-run setup describe the provider list.

## Evidence

Screenshots come from the Control UI browser test (`ui/src/e2e/custodian-auto-setup.e2e.test.ts`) against a mocked Gateway with made-up data. Main is its own version of that test; the PR is head 65dda328274.

- Custodian unit tests (`ui/src/pages/custodian`): 145 of 145 pass, including the ChatGPT login test then sign-in, the Claude Code login, local model setup, an API key, cancellation and error display.

prs.title: fix(cron): a session cron's reply reaches the model once
prs.body:
## Problem

A session-target cron (`sessionTarget: "session:<key>"`) or a main-session cron runs its turn in the target conversation. That turn's own assistant reply stays in model context (it is hidden from the chat view because cron execution prose is audit-only).

When the turn settles, `settleSessionEventTurn` publishes the settled reply into the same conversation through `commitCronConversationResult`, so the chat view can show it. The cron turn still holds the session at that moment, so `commitBackgroundResultToSession` writes the row as a pending background result (`excludeFromContext` + `openclawModelPlacement: "pending"`). The next request boundary then places it into model context as a normal assistant message.

Result: the model sees the cron reply twice. In a real run the model apologised for "answering twice". Isolated crons are not affected (0 copies in the chat).

## Solution

The settle step's commit is always into the conversation that the cron turn ran in, so the row is for display only. `settleSessionEventTurn` now passes `displayOnly: true`. The writer then stores `excludeFromContext: true` with no pending placement, so the row is shown in the chat and never placed into model context.

### Why a parameter (and not derivation or removal)

The brief asked for subtraction first. I checked both options:

1. **Derive at the write site.** `commitBackgroundResultToSession` only knows "this session has active work". It cannot tell whether that work is the producer (this cron turn) or a foreign turn (a user typing while an isolated cron result arrives from another session, a subagent completion). Both callers also pass the same `{ kind: "cron", jobId, runId }` provenance. The run registry entry that names the job (`cronRunsByJobId`) is consumed before the commit. Exact derivation needs new state; a heuristic (active cron turn in this session) would drop a foreign result from model context when two crons overlap.
2. **Drop the commit.** The cron turn's own reply is `display: false`, so this commit is the only persistent display path. Removing it removes the reply from the chat after a reload. Making the raw reply visible instead changes what the chat shows (no_change, silent replies, directive text, media).

So the only callers that know the fact ("my own turn already holds this text") state it. The flag is threaded through `commitCronConversationResult` → `commitBackgroundPayloadsToSession` → `commitBackgroundResultToSession`. Two callers set it:

- `settleSessionEventTurn` (`src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-automation.ts`): session-target and main-session cron turns.
- `commitExecutionResult` (`src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.ts:112-136`, callers `:196` and `:421`): a persistent execution committing into its own conversation.

### Is the isolated runner reachable with a `session:` or `main` job?

- **From the cron timer: no.**
  - `script` payloads return early (`src/cron/service/timer-execution.ts:362`).
  - `runsCronMainSessionRoute` (`src/cron/service/timer-session-route.ts:20-30`) sends every non-plugin-command job with `sessionTarget: "main"`, or with `session:` and `agentTurn`, to `executeMainSessionCronJob` (`timer-execution.ts:379`).
  - Validation (`src/cron/service/jobs-validation.ts:106-127`) allows only `agentTurn` or `command` on `session:` targets, and only `systemEvent`, `agentTurn` or `script` on `main`.
  - In `executeDetachedCronJob`, `command` payloads go to the command runner (`timer-execution.ts:479`), and anything else that is not `agentTurn` is rejected (`:526`).
  - What remains for `runIsolatedAgentJob` (`:541`) with a `session:` target is a plugin-command job. `runPluginCommandScheduledTurn` claims those, because `readPluginCommandScheduledJob` either returns the schedule or throws (`src/gateway/plugin-command-scheduled-run.ts:70-92`). So they never reach `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn` (`src/gateway/server-cron-agent-run.ts:39-60`).
- **From persistent webhooks: yes.** `src/gateway/server/hooks.ts:315` builds `sessionTarget: "session:<key>"` for `sessionMode: "persistent"` and calls `runCronIsolatedAgentTurn` directly (`:548`). That path's `commitExecutionResult` committed into the execution's own conversation, so it had the same double copy. It now passes `displayOnly: true` too, and the persistent-session delivery tests assert the flag. This part is proven by reading the code and by those unit tests; no real-Gateway run covers webhooks.

### Behavior notes

- **Host-authored payloads in the same commit become display-only too.** For example, the `isError` payloads kept on `no_change`. They no longer reach the model through the placed row. This is intended: the model already saw its own turn, and the host text is for the reader.
- **Retries that straddle the deploy.** A retry over an old pending row with the same idempotency key stays pending, because the retry spreads `priorMessage` (`src/sessions/background-session-result.ts:164-169`). Only runs that straddle the deploy are affected.
- **Reset between turn end and commit.** The row lands display-only in the new transcript. This is defensible: the reset already dropped the turn that produced it.
- **CLI runtime.** By reading the code, CLI runtime sessions take the same settle path, and their history reader also skips `excludeFromContext` rows, so the fix holds. This is not tested end to end.

### Unchanged

- Isolated crons, source-conversation commits (an isolated cron created from a chat), run-outcome notices and subagent completions keep their placement.
- Readers: placement readers match only `openclawModelPlacement: "pending"`; the Control UI automation boundary reads `openclawAutomation`, which is kept. Existing pending rows from older versions are still placed once (accepted, transient).

## Evidence

### Tests (red on merge base `dbc1aa04e88f`, green on head)

`src/cron/session-cron-result-single-copy.gateway.integration.test.ts`: a real Gateway, cron service and session store; only the provider endpoint is synthetic. For each transport (OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages): user turn, cron run, two follow-ups, then count copies of the cron reply in the last request and display rows in `chat.history`.

| Test | Responses base | Responses head | Anthropic base | Anthropic head |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| session-target cron: 1 model copy, 1 display row | red (2 copies) | green | red (2 copies) | green |
| main systemEvent cron: 1 model copy, 1 display row | red (2 copies) | green | red (2 copies) | green |
| isolated cron: unrelated chat has 0 copies, 0 rows | green | green | green | green |
| isolated cron from a chat: keeps placement (1 copy, 1 row) | green | green | green | green |

The last two are guards for unchanged behavior, so they pass on both sides.

Unit cases in `src/sessions/background-session-result.test.ts`: while a turn holds the session, `displayOnly` writes `excludeFromContext` with no placement, and a commit without the flag stays pending.
 Consumer suites (background result, destination/current-session completion, double announce, cron notifications, session event handoff and automation result, CLI history boundary): 248 tests pass. `tsgo:core` passes. `check:test-types` reports only existing errors in `test/scripts/release-*` (unrelated).

### Real Gateway, main vs head

Isolated scratch Gateways from source (`--profile` scratch state, `env -i`), real providers, an unrelated chat running 12 turns concurrently. Scenarios: session-target cron + 2 user turns, main systemEvent cron + 2 turns, isolated cron, isolated cron created from the chat. "copies" = assistant copies of the cron reply in the last request of the conversation. Cache = cached input / input tokens per request after the cron run (Anthropic: cache read / cache write).

| Route | Scenario | Copies main | Copies head | Cache per request after cron, main → head (last 2 requests) | Display rows main / head |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAI Responses | session-target cron + 2 turns | 2 | **1** | 33665/35391, 35388/35961 → 33391/35109, 35106/35679 | 1 / 1 |
| OpenAI Responses | main systemEvent cron + 2 turns | 2 | **1** | 31610/32256, 32245/32900 → 31338/31976, 31973/32611 | 1 / 1 |
| OpenAI Responses | isolated cron (other chat) | 0 | 0 | 30651/31225 → 30378/30952 | 0 / 0 |
| OpenAI Responses | isolated cron from this chat | 1 | 1 | 30659/31233 → 30386/30960 | 1 / 1 |
| Claude (Anthropic Messages) | session-target cron + 2 turns | 2 | **1** | 62675/2754, 65429/883 → 62542/2746, 65288/883 | 1 / 1 |
