prs.title: fix(agents): freeze a prompt series' tool set at its first request
prs.body:
> **Size:** production code vs `main` (base `3da2118`, excluding tests and docs) is +290 / -205 (net +85). Not net negative: the growth is the execution-gate conversion itself (build the session's full list, then gate by turn policy in assembly and the message policy), keeping refused tools out of delegation, capture, guidance and the preparer path, the run-policy mark that keeps the empty-allowlist error identical to `main`, and the opt-out admission path `toolSearch: false` still needs. 27 added lines are a move (`session-prompt-delta.ts`) forced by the line-cap ratchet.
>
> **Isolated crons keep main's narrowed list.** A session whose key is an isolated cron run (`agent:<id>:cron:<job>:run:<runId>`, one run per session, `isCronRunSessionKey`) has no series to share, so it keeps the listing narrowed to its allowlist, as on `main`. Every other session, including a cron that runs in a shared session, keeps the fixed listing. Call gates apply everywhere. First request of an isolated cron with `toolsAllow: ["read"]` (tools / input tokens; Claude input = uncached + cache read + cache write):
>
> | | main `3da2118` | `a5d2e08` (fixed listing everywhere) | this head |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | OpenAI | 4 / 6,128 | 14 / 12,368 | 4 / 6,114 |
> | Claude | 4 / 9,206 | 14 / 20,121 | 4 / 9,258 |
>
> A cron that runs in a named shared session (journey J2) still sends the fixed list (14 tools), which is what keeps that session's later turns on one cached prefix.
>
> **Scope:** this PR covers core and plugin tools. MCP and LSP keep `main`'s behavior exactly: their runtimes start only when the run's allowlist permits it, and sender/group denies still apply at MCP discovery. Because MCP tools sit in the deferred catalog, an MCP-only-allowlist cron after `/compact` (J12) no longer narrows the pinned tool list on this head; what remains (the deferred directory following the allowlist, sender denies dropping an MCP server, and starting MCP/LSP from the pin) is the follow-up: pin-owned MCP/LSP listing with a lazy runtime start.

## Problem

The session prompt owner pins the tool definitions of a prompt series. A turn that built a tool the pin lacked extended the pin, so the provider tool list changed. Tools sit at the front of the request, so the whole cached prefix missed.

The list changed with turn authority:

- A chat whose series starts on a cron turn has no `message` tool under the `coding` profile. The next user turn in `message_tool_only` delivery builds `message`, the pin grows, and that request reads 0 cached tokens.
- A run's `toolsAllow` (cron, queued follow-ups, cross-session events) narrows the list. A subagent child's spawn turn (`disableMessageTool`) lists no `message` while its follow-up turns do.
- Group `tools` / `toolsBySender` policy narrows the list per sender, so a guest and an owner in one group chat send different lists.
- The deferred MCP directory sat in the `tool_search` definition, so an MCP server that connected later changed a tool definition.

Freezing the pin alone made the first turn's omissions permanent (an owner turn after a narrowed turn silently lost tools). This PR makes the list independent of turn authority and gates calls at execution instead.

## Solution

1. **Freeze** (`session-prompt-state.ts`, `prepareSessionToolSurface`): on a fixed listing the series' first request pins the tool set and every definition. A pinned tool a turn did not build stays listed and refuses its call. The tool policy digest's inputs changed (it now includes `config.mcp`), so every session starts one new pin after upgrade.
2. **MCP directory out of `tool_search`**: `buildToolSchemaDirectoryPrompt` appends the bounded, sanitized MCP directory to the system prompt's `### Deferred Tool Schemas` section. An MCP server that connects, disconnects or changes its tools reaches the model as an appended prompt-update note, never as a definition change.
3. **`message` always listed, gated at execution**: on a fixed listing the assembly builds `message` regardless of reply mode; `resolveTurnToolSurface` refuses it on a turn that cannot send ("message cannot send on this turn: ... Do not retry message.").
4. **Every run allowlist and group/sender policy is an execution gate** (core and plugin tools): on a fixed listing, `toolsAllow` on any trigger and the group `tools` / `toolsBySender` policy no longer narrow construction. `resolveTurnToolSurface` refuses the tools the turn's policy omits ("`<tool>` is outside the tools this run allows. Do not retry `<tool>`."), marks them unavailable and as run-policy refusals, and never hands them the source's execution preparer, so direct calls, the agent loop's preparer path and a `dispatch_action` rewrap all refuse. Turn authority, child inheritance, cron-creator capture and the catalog restriction read the same policy, so the callable set is unchanged (table below). An allowlist that leaves nothing callable still fails with "No callable tools remain", as on `main`.
5. **Guidance follows callable tools** (m6): `applyPromptBuildToolsAllow` drops listed-but-refused tools from `callableToolNames`, so a turn that cannot send is not told to "use the message tool".
6. **Docs**: `docs/reference/prompt-caching.md`, `docs/tools/tool-search.md`, `docs/concepts/experimental-features.md`.

### Authority recheck at `390da1c` (fixed in this head)

- **A1** (allowlists narrowing the list): for core and plugin tools, the allowlist no longer narrows construction on a fixed listing. The attempt-level filter is skipped (the assembly's turn policy already refuses what the allowlist omits, so the old attempt-level gate was redundant and is deleted). The MCP part (J12) is out of scope; see Scope.
- **A2** (refused copies carried the source's execution preparer): `copyAgentToolMetadata` no longer copies the preparer onto a target that refuses execution (the turn-policy refusal in `resolveTurnToolSurface`, including the scoped-reads split). Ring-zero tools: a ring-zero harness run has no Tool Search controls, so it is never a fixed listing and the allowlist still removes them, as on `main` (test).
- **m-a**: a tool built after the session pin is logged (`tools built after the session pin wait for the next prompt series`).
- **m-b / 1b** (fixed for plugins): on a fixed listing, plugin construction keeps every grant plus the default plugin tools and uses a denylist without sender, group and run denies; those refuse at execution. Children still inherit the full denylist. The MCP part (a sender deny dropping a whole MCP server at discovery) is out of scope.
- **1a** (fixed): `progress_card` is built whatever the run allowlist names and refused by the turn policy. `show_widget` keeps its admission rule (a scheduled run gets it only when its allowlist names it); that rule grants a capability rather than narrowing one, and changing it would remove widget authoring from such runs. Documented, not changed.
- **1c**: the bundle pass (MCP/LSP) is back to `main`, except that tools the turn refuses are not delegated or captured.
- **1d** (fixed): the scoped-reads split is marked before its metadata copy, so it never inherits the source's preparer (test red before the fix).
- **1e** (fixed): the built-after-pin log fires once per series and tool set.
- **m4a** (accepted): a completion handoff on a fixed listing does not mark run-allowlist refusals, so they can hide an allowlist that matched nothing (`main` removed them).
- **m3** (accepted): a grant that only a guest's `allow` names builds that optional plugin tool on the guest's turn only. Plugin tools are catalog entries, so the pin holds; the cost is one prompt-update note per sender flip. Same class as the `show_widget` rule.
- **m6** (accepted): a refused call still runs plugin `before_tool_call` hooks; the refusal happens after them and authority is unaffected.
- **m5c**: the fixed listing has no unit test of the MCP call lifecycle; the real-route journeys (J5, J12) cover it. A cataloged client tool in the restored empty-allowlist error is also not unit-tested here.
- **`fixedToolListing` kept**: Copilot (`tool-bridge.ts`), Codex (`dynamic-tool-build.ts`) and agentsapi pass a run allowlist into OpenClaw tool construction; I did not verify that each of them removes `progress_card` later, so the registration flag stays.
- **structured_output** (documented): swarm collectors re-add `structured_output` after policy, so it stays callable under a `toolsAllow` that omits it. `main` removed it. Benign: it only records the collector's own result.
- **Restored error** (fixed): "No callable tools remain" now matches `main` exactly except for tools a run allowlist or sender/group policy refuses (these were absent on `main`). Owner-only tools and cataloged client tools count as before (test: an allowlist naming an owner-only tool on a non-owner turn does not error, on `main` and head).
- **MCP/LSP startup**: unchanged from `main` (out of scope). Auth prompts: starting the MCP runtime only reads credential status; sign-in starts only when a connect tool is called from an untainted owner direct chat, so a cron start raises no prompt.
- **m-c**: the empty-allowlist error counts only callable tools, so a sender `allow` typo or a `toolsAllow` that names only refused tools fails with "No callable tools remain", as on `main` (same test green on both).
- **m-d**: guidance drops cataloged tools the turn refuses, not only direct ones.

### Exceptions (behavior unchanged)

Items 3-5 apply only when Tool Search lists a fixed set (`listsFixedToolSet`: controls enabled, `mode: "tools"`, no `include`/`exclude`). Otherwise (`tools.toolSearch` off, `disableToolSearch` runs, memory flush, Code Mode, selectors, `mode: "directory"`) filtering and pin admission stay as on `main` (gate A J8 below: per-turn lists equal between arms). Out of scope (follow-up): other trigger-dependent definition text, e.g. the `message` description's action list (see Risks).

### Fable D findings at `53145b8`

- **M1** (owner turns lose tools after a narrowed turn): fixed by item 4.
- **m2** (rewrap could bypass the gate): fixed; the production-path test "keeps a run allowlist refusal through a catalog rewrap" calls through a `dispatch_action` rewrap and gets the refusal.
- **M3** (fork mismatch): gone with item 4; a fork sends the source's list unchanged (test below).
- **m4** (history growth): after the split the MCP directory flips again on allowlisted turns, as on `main`: an allowlist naming no MCP server starts no MCP runtime, so a prompt-update note goes out on the cron turn and another on the next user turn. The cache is kept (notes append); the follow-up removes the flip.
- **m5** (fork before the first post-upgrade turn): accepted edge case. `readSessionForkPin` ignores the policy digest, so such a fork sends the old pin plus `message` once (one miss); the source re-pins on its own next turn. Test: "lets a fork that runs before the first post-upgrade turn add message once".
- **m6**: fixed by item 5.

## E2E on this head (`45ef8f8c583f`, base = merge base `3da2118f243c`)

Isolated scratch Gateways (own state dir, random port, `env -i`) from source copies of each commit, real provider routes (OpenAI Responses and Claude via an Anthropic-messages proxy), a logging proxy recording provider usage per request. Both arms ran the same journeys with the same config (`visibleReplies: "message_tool"`, Tool Search on), with an unrelated chat running turns and `sessions.compact` throughout. OpenAI: `read` = `cached_tokens`, uncached = input − cached. Claude: `read` = `cache_read_input_tokens`, uncached = `input_tokens`, plus `write` = `cache_creation_input_tokens`.

**J1: cron starts a chat, then the user** (cron request, then user turns)

| route | arm | tool lists in the chat | cron→user request | session total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude | base | 2 (cron A, user B) | read 9,668 / write 16,952 | write 42,138 |
| Claude | head | 1 | read 23,965 / write 3,168 | write 28,339 |
| OpenAI | base | 2 | read 0 / uncached 17,007 | both user turns stopped by the model's `message` loop (below) |
| OpenAI | head | 1 for the turns (see note) | read 15,667 / uncached 1,972 | `hello-j1` and `second-j1` delivered |

**J2: shared-session cron with `toolsAllow: ["read"]`, then the owner asks for `exec`**

| OpenAI | head | 14 tools (fixed) | same list, read 13,582 / uncached 4,968 | 18,934 |
| Claude | base | 4 tools | 14 tools, read 9,554 / write 21,734 | 32,060 |

Cron result on head (both routes): `exec` refused visibly ("exec is outside the tools this run allows. Do not retry exec."), `read` returned `gate-file-contents-7731`, `exec` did not run. Base: the model reports exec unavailable (not listed). The owner's later `exec` ran on both arms.

**J2i: isolated cron with `toolsAllow: ["read"]`** keeps the narrowed listing, matching base: 4 tools on both arms; first request input OpenAI 6,110 (base) vs 6,145 (head), Claude 9,206 vs 9,260 total.

**J11: one group, guest denied `exec` (sender policy), then owner**

Guest `exec` on head: refused with "exec is outside the tools this run allows. Do not retry exec." (base: not listed, the model says it is unavailable). Guest `read` worked and both owner `exec` calls ran on both arms.

**Side effects.** Every journey's replies arrived on head (J1 user replies, J2 cron + owner, J11 five group replies, J2i cron `ok`); refused tools stayed refused and never executed. The OpenAI model on this route sometimes fills every optional `message` field (a `gatewayUrl`, a made-up target) and loops; this happened on **both** arms (base: both J1 user turns and one unrelated-chat turn stopped by the 20-repeat guard; head: three unrelated-chat turns stopped the same way, and J1's first reply was kept private, then delivered by the stranded-reply retry). The stranded-reply retry runs with `toolsAllow: ["message"]` (`stranded-reply-recovery.ts`, unchanged by this PR), so it sends a message-only list and misses the cache once (OpenAI uncached 9,207) on both arms; not changed here, noted as a follow-up.

**UI** (Control UI of the head and base scratch Gateways, after the journeys; chat area cropped): the J2 chat shows the cron's visible refusal, the J11 group shows the guest's refusal, J1 renders both delivered replies.

|---|---|---|

The live operator Gateway was untouched during the runs (its pid and config unchanged).

## Evidence

### Tests (red on merge base `3da2118f243c`, green on this head)

- `src/agents/session-tool-listing.test.ts`: one tool list across user, cron, exec-wake, subagent, steer and allowlisted turns, checked on each turn's own built list and on the sent list; one list for every sender of a group chat; a fork sends the source's list unchanged; a cron turn after `/compact` re-pins the owner turn's list (green on main too: this fixture does not reproduce the #201655 4-vs-3 case); a later user turn sends with `message` in a cron-started series.
- `attempt-tool-prepare.scheduled-tools-allow.test.ts` (real `prepareEmbeddedAttemptToolBase`): refusal-equivalence table "allows exactly the calls main allowed" for cron/user/event `toolsAllow`, group guest sender and group owner sender; one tool set for every group sender with the guest refused through `dispatch_action`; refusal kept through a catalog rewrap; an allowlist matching nothing still fails (green on main and head).
- `agent-tools.turn-authority.test.ts`: a turn-policy refusal and the scoped-reads split never carry the source's preparer (red on `390da1c` / before the fix).
- `attempt-prompt-tool-policy.test.ts`: "leaves a listed tool the turn refuses out of the callable guidance" (main: `['message','read']`, head: `['read']`).
- `attempt-session-runtime-prepare.test.ts`: production `admitNewTools` wiring (inverting it fails 2 tests). `session-prompt-state.test.ts`: one new pin after an upgrade changes the policy digest.

### Execution-based refusal equivalence

`attempt.configured-mcp-lifecycle.test.ts` now runs its cataloged case with an `include` selector: the fixed listing builds every core tool, which that harness does not mock. The fixed-listing MCP path is covered by the real-route journeys (J5, J12, J13).


`attempt-tool-prepare.scheduled-tools-allow.test.ts` builds tools through the production tool base, bundle pass (a mocked bundle MCP server) and catalog, then executes every listed tool through the direct path, the preparer the agent loop prefers, and a `dispatch_action` rewrap. The callable tables (cron/user/event `toolsAllow`, group guest, group owner) pass unchanged on `main` and on this head; the three paths agree for every tool. New: an MCP-only allowlist lists the full set (red on `390da1c`), sender `allow`/`deny` policies including an MCP tool, a refused tool is never delegated or captured, and only-refused-tools fails loudly (green on `main` and head, red on `390da1c`). A tool counts as callable only when a call with schema-valid placeholder arguments passes every gate, starts the tool's implementation and does not come back refused; exceptions and timeouts before the implementation starts count as not callable.

### Callable set, base vs head (`toolsAllow: ["read", "group:web", "sessions_*", "message"]`; group deny `exec, process, write, edit, apply_patch` for the guest)

| group guest | guest set (identical on base and head) | full session list (40), denied tools refused |

| head | last reply | 14 | 46,915 / 1,153 (hit) |

One miss on the first head turn, then cache hits on the cron and owner turns.

### Gate C (append-only journeys from #201723)

Stability journeys: head 5/5 pass, main 5/5 pass (they do not separate the arms). Randomized seeds 1-10 on head: 60/60 pass (anthropic-messages, openai-responses, openai-completions, google, bedrock, and the Tool Search opt-out surface).

### Gates

- `pnpm tsgo:core`: pass. oxlint, oxfmt on changed files, `git diff --check`: clean.
- Production code vs `main` (excluding tests and docs): +290 / -205 (net +85); see the size note at the top.

### Test lines

Net test lines +994 against the 400 allowance. Duplicate tests were removed first (the scheduled-run table duplicate, the separate catalog-rewrap test, the sender-deny MCP case, the bundle MCP fixture, and the duplicate group-sender listing test). The remaining 594 lines are recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/201710-session-tool-listing.txt`: refusal equivalence against `main` executed through the production tool base, bundle pass and catalog for five policy shapes across the direct, preparer and `dispatch_action` paths, plus series listing, fork and upgrade pin cases.

### Local ClawSweeper (gpt-6.1-sol, normal)

Head `45ef8f8c583f`: patch is correct, no findings (exit 0). The local review reads only the committed range and its tests; the real-route journeys above are outside its inputs. An earlier P2 at `9543fde3` (sender change dropping a direct-only tool such as `computer` from a frozen group listing) is fixed by item 4: every sender builds the same list.

## Risks

- `message` and allowlist-refused tools are listed (and refused visibly) on turns that cannot use them. Each costs one definition.
- The `message` definition's action list still depends on the turn that starts the series (a cron-started WebChat series pins "Supports actions: send" without `react`). The pin keeps it stable; `react` is not advertised in that series until a rebuild point. Main would extend the pin (a miss) instead. Follow-up.
- Upgrade: every existing session re-pins once on its first turn after the upgrade (the toolPolicy digest changes), costing one cache miss per session. This is the same accepted one-time cost as #201843.
- MCP names and sanitized descriptions now enter the system prompt's deferred-tool section instead of the `tool_search` description.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep projected prompt updates out of later user turns
prs.body:
## Problem

Some routes cannot send a system prompt update as a system message (`inHistorySystemUpdates` is false). Examples: custom OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions providers, and Claude through a non-native Responses proxy. On these routes, the boundary projects the update as a plain `{ role: "user" }` message. The update is the last message of its turn.

When that turn ends silent (a `NO_REPLY` turn after an `AGENTS.md` edit, or a silent exec wake that carries a `## Tooling` update), no assistant message follows the update. On the next turn, the stream boundary merges the new user message into the update (`mergeConsecutiveUserMessages`). `canMergeUser` refuses carriers, operator messages and synthetic messages, but not this projected update. The result: a message that the provider already received is rewritten, and the prompt cache misses from that point.

## Fix

- When `inHistorySystemUpdates` is false, the projection puts a symbol-keyed marker (`PROJECTED_PROMPT_UPDATE`) on the projected update message.
- `canMergeUser` refuses to merge across that marker.
- A symbol key is not in `JSON.stringify` or structured clone output, so the marker never reaches a provider request, the worker protocol or the transcript. Only `canMergeUser` reads it.
- Why not `synthetic`: at least one route has `inHistorySystemUpdates` false and also reads `synthetic` on user messages. The ChatGPT Codex backend (`provider: "openai"`, `api: "openai-chatgpt-responses"`, `chatgpt.com`) is not a native Responses endpoint (`packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-endpoint.ts:21-25` needs `api: "openai-responses"` on `api.openai.com`), so its prompt updates are projected as plain user messages. The same backend is the only one eligible for ChatGPT V2 compaction (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/chatgpt-v2-compaction.ts:35-55`, `usesNativeOpenAICodexResponsesBackend`). During V2 compaction it sets `retainUserProvenance` (`packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts:221-223` → `openai-chatgpt-responses-request.ts:118-124`). Then `openai-responses-replay-messages-internal.ts:441-448` tags non-synthetic user input as retained, and `chatgpt-v2-compaction.ts:180-185` checks non-synthetic user input before persistence. A `synthetic` update would drop out of the V2 retained input on that route, which changes behavior. The symbol changes nothing there.
- Routes with `inHistorySystemUpdates` (native OpenAI Responses, direct Anthropic) are unchanged: they keep `operatorMessage` and never get the marker.

Production diff: 8 added, 2 removed lines in 2 files.

## Scope and limits

- Accepted gap: Bedrock Converse. It requires strict role alternation, so the stream boundary calls `mergeConsecutiveUserMessages` with `preserveContextBoundaries: false` for `bedrock-converse-stream` (`attempt-tool-call-replay-sanitization.ts:382`) and never consults `canMergeUser`. A silent turn rewrites the prefix there with or without an update. This PR does not change Bedrock.
- One-time cache miss on upgrade: the marker also stops an update from merging backward into a user message directly before it in the same turn. Where history was sent as `[user + update]`, the first request after the upgrade sends `[user, update]`. After that request, history is append-only again.
- Longer runs of consecutive user-role messages: after a silent turn a request can now contain, for example, user, carrier, update, user, carrier in a row (main merged the update with the next user). Carriers already produce consecutive user-role messages on every turn on these routes, so this is not a new failure class.
- Google Gemini routes do not merge user turns (`validateAnthropicTurns` is false), so this bug does not occur there.
- The OpenAI provider plugin's own Chat Completions policy does not merge user turns either. The bug occurs on custom and plugin-owned OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions routes that use the strict OpenAI-compatible replay policy.
- This supersedes the closed #201654 (silent replies in replay) for the routes above.

## Evidence

### Tests (`attempt.silent-prompt-update.test.ts`)

The test runs the real boundary projection, the real stream sanitization wrapper with the resolved transcript policy, and the real transport for each route (`streamOpenAICompletions` / `streamOpenAIResponses`). It captures the live payload object in `onPayload`, before serialization, so the key check sees symbol keys too.

| Test | Merge base `1579eb4` | Head |
|---|---|---|
| custom Chat Completions, silent `NO_REPLY` after `AGENTS.md` edit | red | green |
| custom Chat Completions, silent exec wake with tooling update | red | green |
| Claude through custom Responses proxy, silent `NO_REPLY` after `AGENTS.md` edit | red | green |
| Claude through custom Responses proxy, silent exec wake with tooling update | red | green |
| both routes: update before a visible reply (request unchanged) | green | green |
| both routes: unmarked consecutive user text still merges (marker absent = main) | green | green |

### Which route merges

The original capture and the gate below use the same config: provider id `oaic` (a custom provider, no owning plugin, plugins disabled), `api: "openai-completions"`, model `gpt-5.6-sol`, base URL pointing to a local logging proxy in front of the OpenAI API.

- No plugin owns `oaic`, so `resolveTranscriptPolicy` uses `buildUnownedProviderTransportReplayFallback` (`src/agents/transcript-policy.ts:161`). That fallback sets `validateAnthropicTurns: true` for `openai-completions` (`transcript-policy.ts:79,105`).
- With that flag, the stream wrapper merges consecutive user messages (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-tool-call-replay-sanitization.ts:378-383`, the same line 381 on `8a23d7c`). `canMergeUser` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/turns.ts:433`) decides which messages may merge.
- The OpenAI plugin's own policy sets `validateAnthropicTurns: false` for every API (`extensions/openai/replay-policy.ts:18`, same on `8a23d7c`), so `provider: "openai"` with Chat Completions never reaches this merge.

### Real Gateway, custom Chat Completions provider `oaic` (`gpt-5.6-sol`)

Isolated scratch Gateways (main = merge base, head = this branch), a logging proxy that captures each request body, provider cache numbers from the response `usage`. An unrelated chat ran 6 turns concurrently on each Gateway (6/6 ok).

Journey 1: turn 1, then a `NO_REPLY` turn after an `AGENTS.md` edit, then two user turns.

| Request | Main | Head |
|---|---|---|
| silent turn | append-only | append-only |
| next user turn | **REWRITE at message 6** (update merged with the new user text); cached 29457, uncached 1205 | append-only; cached 29850, uncached 568 |
| following turn | append-only | append-only |

Journey 2: background exec, then a silent exec-completion wake that carries a `## Tooling` update, then a user turn.

| Request | Main | Head |
|---|---|---|
| wake turn | append-only | append-only |
| next user turn | **REWRITE at message 13**; cached 30860, uncached 5129 | append-only; cached 33013, uncached 2731 |

### No-regression routes (same two journeys, main vs head, concurrent chat active)

Native OpenAI Responses (`gpt-6.2-astra`, `inHistorySystemUpdates` on) and Claude (`claude-opus-5-5`) through an Anthropic-compatible proxy (`anthropic-messages`, no stream merge). Request layouts come from the cache trace (`stream:context` fingerprints); cache numbers from `cache:result`. The proxy captured the Claude request bodies; no body contains the marker.

| Route / journey | Main | Head |
|---|---|---|
| Responses, `NO_REPLY` after `AGENTS.md` edit | 4 requests, all append-only, layouts `uu → uuauuu → uuauuuuu → uuauuuuuauu` | same layouts, all append-only |
| Responses, silent exec wake | 6 requests, all append-only | same layouts, all append-only |
| Claude proxy, `NO_REPLY` after `AGENTS.md` edit | 4 requests, all append-only; last turn cacheRead 72882, cacheWrite 925 | same layouts, all append-only; cacheRead 72771, cacheWrite 925 |
| Claude proxy, silent exec wake | 6 requests, all append-only; last turn cacheWrite 8052 | same layouts, all append-only; cacheWrite 8080 |

Responses cache numbers differ by at most 3 tokens per request (timestamp text). Concurrent chat: 6/6 turns ok in every run.

### Gates (head `53c326c`)

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `ocx test` on the new test file | 8/8 pass on head; on the merge base the 4 silent-turn cases fail and the 4 controls pass |
| `ocx test` sanitization, LLM boundary, cache stability, transcript policy, prefix stability suites | pass |
| oxfmt (changed files) | pass |
| oxlint (changed files) | pass |
| `pnpm tsgo:core` | pass |
| `pnpm check:test-types` | 7 errors, all in `test/scripts/release-*` files that this PR does not touch; none in changed files |
| Local ClawSweeper (`gpt-6.1-sol`, normal speed) | complete, "patch is correct", 0 findings |



## E2E (exact head `53c326c`, rerun 2026-11-20)

Two isolated scratch Gateways from source: merge base `1579eb4` and head `53c326c`. Real custom Chat Completions route `oaic` (`openai-completions`, `gpt-5.6-sol`) through a logging proxy that saves each request body and the provider `usage`. Both Gateways ran the same script. An ordinary chat ran concurrently with the journeys.

### Silent `NO_REPLY` turn after an `AGENTS.md` edit, then user turns, `/compact`, and one more user turn

| Request | Base: layout vs previous | Base cached / uncached | Head: layout vs previous | Head cached / uncached |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| silent turn (update is last) | append-only | 29495 / 646 | append-only | 29222 / 646 |
| next user turn | **REWRITE at msg 6** | 29495 / **1207** | append-only | 29865 / **568** |
| following user turn | append-only | 30699 / 576 | append-only | 30430 / 576 |
| first turn after `/compact` | rewrite (compaction, expected) | 0 / 31085 | rewrite (compaction, expected) | 0 / 30812 |

### Silent exec-completion wake that carries a `## Tooling` update, then a user turn

| Request | Base: layout vs previous | Base cached / uncached | Head: layout vs previous | Head cached / uncached |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wake turn (update is last) | append-only | 30897 / 2408 | append-only | 30621 / 2409 |
| next user turn | **REWRITE at msg 13** | 30897 / **5130** | append-only | 33027 / **2731** |

On base the next user message merges into the projected update, so the provider cache stops at that message. On head, history stays append-only and the cache continues to the end of the earlier request.

### Side effects

- Ordinary chat, 3 turns: every reply arrives on base and head; every request is append-only (head cached / uncached: 29226 / 583, 29806 / 583).
- `/compact`: works the same on base and head ("Compacted (31k → 1.4k)"). The next turn replies normally. The post-compaction request is the one rewrite that compaction is allowed to make, on both sides.
- Every turn of every journey returned `status: ok` on both Gateways.

### UI (Control UI of each scratch Gateway, chat history after the journeys)

Head and base render the same history. No "System prompt update" bubble or other prompt-update text appears in any session on head (checked in the rendered chat log text as well). The silent `NO_REPLY` turn shows only the user message, as on base.

Head, `NO_REPLY` journey with `/compact`:

![Head: NO_REPLY journey with compact](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2313c741-a82a-41e6-900c-4762e0516bb8)

Base, same journey:

![Base: NO_REPLY journey with compact](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c15a26c-d4b9-48c0-9836-4dbbe924aca2)

Head, silent exec wake journey:

![Head: silent exec wake journey](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/77426d6e-8d20-439a-bfbe-2f8bec1118e5)

Base, same journey:

![Base: silent exec wake journey](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/792c5ff5-64de-404d-881e-527ec24abf9b)

### Review and CI on this head

- Local ClawSweeper on `53c326c`: `review_status: complete`, "patch is correct", 0 findings.
- PR CI on `53c326c`: all required checks pass.

prs.title: fix(gateway): share the directory watch helper with catalog workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway and its prepared model catalog workers can each spawn a directory-watch helper. Each helper adds a resident runtime while the worker keeps its watches open.

## User Impact

The catalog worker shares the Gateway's helper. Native watch admission and recursive file traversal still run in the helper, preserving the protections for Linux stalls and macOS shutdown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route catalog-worker subscriptions through a private message port owned by the worker pool. The pool closes subscriptions on retirement, including on Bun where worker termination can leave the other port open. Bundled copies of the watch client share the same helper state within an isolate. Shared-transport and lifetime ownership account for the 104 net production lines.

## Evidence

- macOS arm64 synthetic watcher fixture, with one main and one worker subscription, five interleaved repeats per arm and runtime. The acceptance rule was one helper, actual worker file-change delivery, and helper retirement on owner release. Node 26.7.0 helper count 2 → 1, median helper RSS 123.5 → 61.9 MiB, median one-event delivery 11.35 → 11.32 ms. Bun 1.3.14 helper count 2 → 1, median helper RSS 104.2 → 52.5 MiB, median one-event delivery 11.34 → 11.60 ms. The fixture measures helpers before teardown. Gateway memory, launch latency, and cold-turn TTFT still need an integrated baseline and candidate run.
- The new regression in `src/infra/directory-watch-host.test.ts` covers registration through the shared helper, notification with only a worker subscribed, and final helper retirement.
- Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Autoreview of the complete patch against `5dd7ef8adbf3` reported no P0–P2 findings. The review was static.
- The corrected watcher test shard and production types passed on `01dfce88218`. The current head also passed the focused watcher shard, core lint and production types. Release-tooling test types and an unused export elsewhere failed the overall run.
- A packaged Linux Node 24.22.1 Kova run of the production patch measured **1,377.6 MiB across four processes at +120.108 s** in the many-bundled-plugins Gateway scenario. The scenario exceeded its existing peak RSS thresholds, and all four smoke scenarios recorded budget violations. The run uses the same production files as the current draft. The pinned base measured **1,455.6 MiB across five processes at +120.038 s**. All four scenarios recorded budget violations on both heads. The scenario-wide peak and the separate agent scenario peak were 32.9 MiB and 46.2 MiB higher on the candidate. One observation per arm on separate hosted runners leaves those differences unresolved. [Base run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44533527478) · [Candidate run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44529507669)

## Same-host acceptance rule

Run five serial, interleaved baseline and candidate pairs against packaged runtimes on the same Linux host. Use the same Node 24 patch on both arms, OCM v0.2.48 and Kova `7c162a3276a31fbbb60c362d94124b6cad5187ca` (the revision that adds the settled sample), with Kova smoke scenarios `gateway-performance` and `gateway-session-send-turn`, mock provider, and no concurrent scenario work. Compare cold/warm readiness and turn latency separately. Require successful Gateway startup and cold/warm turns, one fewer Gateway descendant and lower settled Gateway-tree RSS at ready +120 s in every pair. Report per-arm median, p95 and range, and the five paired differences for those metrics plus scenario peak, cold-turn Gateway-tree peak, pre-provider latency, first visible assistant text, and turn completion. A repeatable adverse movement in a user-facing metric blocks landing. First visible assistant text is measured by polling Gateway history. Use the `mock-openai-provider` fixture for the five paired repetitions. First verify that this fixture starts the Gateway-owned and catalog-owned watcher helpers on the baseline. The earlier 80-plugin fixture is a separate pressure sample and takes over six minutes per arm to provision.

## Controlled Linux results

Measured the pinned base and current PR head in packaged Node 24.22.1 runtimes. Five interleaved pairs completed on one 4-vCPU Testbox using Kova’s `mock-openai-provider` state for both scenarios. All ten runs reached readiness and completed cold and warm `sessions.send` turns. Kova measured settled process-tree RSS against the verified readiness PID and start ticks.

| Metric | Pairs | Baseline median / p95 (range) | Candidate median / p95 (range) | Paired changes (candidate − baseline) |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| Settled Gateway-tree RSS (MiB) | 5 | 1436.7 / 1457.6 (1430–1457.6) | 1357 / 1361.6 (1342.8–1361.6) | -76, -80.7, -73, -85, -114.8 |
| Settled process count | 5 | 5 / 5 (5–5) | 4 / 4 (4–4) | -1, -1, -1, -1, -1 |
| Gateway cold readiness (ms) | 5 | 6756 / 8390 (6229–8390) | 6275 / 7804 (5713–7804) | -2677, -554, 1575, 1035, -464 |
| Gateway warm restart readiness (ms) | 4 | 12000 / 12688 (11180–12688) | 11559 / 14291 (9905–14291) | -2021, -372, 1603, 236 |
| Gateway scenario peak root RSS (MiB) | 5 | 1796.3 / 1866 (1751.9–1866) | 1731.8 / 1887.6 (1681–1887.6) | -134.2, 135.7, -115.3, -45.7, -66.2 |
| Turn scenario cold readiness (ms) | 5 | 6761 / 8301 (6257–8301) | 7309 / 8856 (5695–8856) | -1066, -1027, 555, 2047, 1042 |
| Turn scenario peak root RSS (MiB) | 5 | 2399.4 / 2483.6 (2313.7–2483.6) | 2387.5 / 2441.4 (2309.4–2441.4) | -69.5, 10.3, -42.2, -90, 84.5 |
| Cold turn pre-provider (ms) | 5 | 3234 / 4136 (2977–4136) | 3995 / 4020 (2823–4020) | -411, -155, -136, 539, 1018 |
| Cold turn first visible text (ms) | 5 | 3430 / 4667 (3164–4667) | 4375 / 4490 (3037–4490) | -314, -127, -292, 549, 1211 |
| Cold turn completion (ms) | 5 | 3554 / 4667 (3309–4667) | 4375 / 4490 (3073–4490) | -437, -252, -292, 549, 1179 |
| Warm turn completion (ms) | 5 | 603 / 626 (580–626) | 612 / 614 (573–614) | 2, -34, -12, 19, 9 |

The main Testbox command exited successfully after all five pairs and stopped its lease. The backing Actions job was cancelled during that normal cleanup. Kova’s continuous startup and cold-turn process-tree sampler did not establish identity coverage. The scenario peak values are snapshots of the Gateway root; the settled values are verified process-tree samples. Earlier helper-level Node/Bun tests separately identify the process removed. [Same-host Kova run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44584314271)

Two pairs on a second 4-vCPU Testbox used the 80-plugin pressure fixture for Gateway startup and the same mock-provider fixture for turns. Both removed one Gateway process and reduced settled Gateway-tree RSS by 82.3 and 87.7 MiB. Sampled Gateway root RSS after the warm restart varied between pairs (changes of +112.4 and −25.8 MiB). Cold turns completed in 5,586 → 3,662 ms and 3,159 → 3,645 ms. The slower candidate spent an extra 255 ms before the provider; its trace has the same counts of `agent.prepare` (26) and `plugins.metadata.scan` (3) and zero catalog spans in that window. [Pressure Kova run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44582191486)

The five-pair host measured cold completion median 3,554 → 4,375 ms (+23%), with improvement in three pairs and two slower pairs. This result needs a focused rerun before merge. Rerun the same packaged `gateway-session-send-turn` workload alone, five serial interleaved pairs on one Testbox with the same Node, Kova and exact revisions. Compare paired pre-provider time, first visible text, cold completion and warm completion, per-arm median and p95, and the recorded agent-preparation span counts and durations. Keep the merge hold if the cold-turn slowdown repeats.

## Cold-turn confirmation

A third 4-vCPU Linux Testbox completed five serial interleaved pairs with the exact same packages, Node, Kova pin and `gateway-session-send-turn` alone. The native command exited successfully and the lease was stopped. Each cold turn had 26 `agent.prepare` spans, three plugin metadata scans, zero model catalog spans, and a successful assistant response. All warm turns completed.

prs.title: improve(ci): speed up compiler receipt recording
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Recording compiler receipts for all plugins repeatedly checks filesystem admission for inputs whose bytes are already captured in the same snapshot. This adds work to the package-boundary CI job.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. In five paired measurements across all 147 plugins, median receipt-recording time fell 25.0% (35.424 → 26.574 seconds). This is a recording-phase result; total CI spend and whole-job savings are not established.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing phase-scoped byte cache before filesystem admission. Cache misses and fresh snapshots still validate the physical input boundary. A captured input remains usable if its filesystem path changes later in that phase; no new external bytes are read. The benchmark can load both snapshot owners from the baseline revision while keeping its physical corpus fixed.

Simplification: five production lines reuse existing state; no new cache or policy. The regression protects captured bytes and fresh-snapshot rejection. Total delta: 42 additions and 7 deletions, including benchmark support and regression proof.

## Evidence

Baseline: `58dbe4055043f7c090a03b3c8a610a9e521e3452`. Candidate: `73a9586c3277cc800c160a9832db5ca3ba81326c`.

- Baseline full boundary check passed all 147 plugins plus the canary.
- Baseline reproduction confirmed that a cached read re-enters filesystem admission after a path replacement.
- Diagnostic CPU profile: about 10.1 seconds of a 37.5-second recording pass traversed snapshot input admission; this is profiling evidence, not a measured speedup.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed the full committed range at the base/head above: no actionable correctness or security findings. Runtime measurements were outside that read-only review.
- All 59 focused tests passed, including the new captured-byte/fresh-snapshot regression and existing boundary invalidation tests.
- Tooling and scripts test typechecks, scoped lint, and formatting passed.
- Full package-boundary check passed: 147 compiled plugins and one negative canary; 216.177 seconds total. This total is not a matched baseline comparison.

Predeclared acceptance: five paired fresh-process baseline/candidate runs on the same isolated host and full 147-plugin receipt corpus; identical receipt digest, fewer counted filesystem operations, at least 10% lower median receipt-recording time, no slower p95, and no CPU or peak-RSS regression of 20% or more. This measures recording only, not compilation or total CI spend. Reject the candidate if the threshold fails.


Qualification passed on one isolated Linux x64 host (8 CPUs, 16 GiB RAM; Node 24.22.1). Five sequential baseline/candidate pairs used fresh processes and the same physical receipt corpus, with only the two implementation modules substituted for baseline runs.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median recording seconds | 35.424 | 26.574 |
| Sample p95 recording seconds | 35.875 | 27.044 |
| Median CPU seconds | 38.74 | 29.91 |
| Median peak RSS, KiB | 1,189,452 | 1,193,852 |
| Counted filesystem calls | 2,177,619 | 436,831 |

Nearest-rank p95 is the maximum of five samples. Counts and digest were stable within each implementation; all ten runs produced digest `eca55b704eb6ea76669c12c5a5129e5de33a2eb36b613ad378b27842cc1784e0`. Filesystem calls fell 79.9%; median CPU fell 22.8%; median RSS rose 0.4%. No acceptance limit failed.

prs.title: fix: keep large chat history reads bounded
prs.body:
Related: #201972, #201910

## What Problem This Solves

Opening a large chat can read old transcript payloads even though the returned history page is small. The extra reads compete with other sessions for the database page cache.

## User Impact

History pages and cursors remain identical. Looking up the input behind a displayed run now reads the selected input instead of walking unrelated history. No migration or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

With analyzed SQLite statistics, the run-input visibility query can visit active events and their payloads before applying its unique idempotency key. Select the input sequence through the existing unique identity index first, then apply the same active-window, role, steering and visibility predicates. The normal message-page query already selects its indexed range before payloads; this fixes the separate input lookup.

Production delta is +2 lines: one scalar subquery replaces the join. No schema, index, cache or permission changes.

## Evidence

The regression fails before the fix with 2,001 JSON field evaluations for a present input and an absent input; the fixed reader stays within four. Existing hidden-input, steering, compaction and legacy cases pass.

Writer-built, analyzed 33.6 GiB SQLite fixture with 4,096 background sessions; real history RPC worker owner; fresh read handles and a 2 MiB SQLite page cache. These are logical VFS read bytes/page spans, not physical disk I/O or a production latency claim:

| Events | Page | Before bytes / spans | After bytes / spans |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 14,402 | Tail | 28,989,972 / 7,080 | 1,468,948 / 361 |
| 144,002 | Tail | 264,772,256 / 64,644 | 1,460,896 / 359 |
| 144,002 | Offset | 264,436,384 / 64,562 | 1,489,568 / 366 |
| 144,002 | Older cursor | 265,398,463 / 64,798 | 2,410,687 / 592 |

Interleaved baseline, duplicate-baseline and candidate reads preserve the entire serialized worker page, including encoded message bytes and cursors. All five counterbalanced A1/B/A2 rounds are complete: 270 calls, plus 360 allocation confirmation calls, all preserving the exact page and cursor bytes. Acceptance is byte-identical pages, history-independent input lookup work, and no material CPU/allocation regression. The committed workload is `scripts/perf/session-history-page-reads-measure.ts`; compile its documented VFS probe and run baseline with `--owner-file`, then candidate against the same `--fixture`.

Warm worker CPU medians (ms/call), A1 / A2 / candidate:

| Events | Tail | Offset | Older cursor |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 14,402 | 18.233 / 19.397 / 4.886 | 20.872 / 21.002 / 6.031 | 22.048 / 22.851 / 8.402 |
| 144,002 | 151.043 / 150.037 / 3.471 | 143.978 / 152.624 / 4.821 | 145.706 / 153.724 / 6.833 |

A/A read counts are identical. Allocation is broadly unchanged: 20-sample confirmation for the largest older-cursor page is 8,711,604 / 8,693,912 / 8,706,888 sampled bytes (A1/A2/candidate). The initial five-sample +2.7% candidate median did not persist. Sampling uses 8 KiB intervals and excludes native SQLite memory. Separate worker CPU profiles show native row-iteration self-samples dropping from 10,937 ms to 82.6 ms over 120 calls per arm. No physical I/O or whole-Gateway latency claim; Node v26.12.1 on macOS/APFS, observed host load 3.44–6.69.

Focused validation: 3 input-visibility tests, 12 history-worker/query-plan tests, 2 browser history-settlement tests, and 3 UI history E2E tests pass. The new regression's file takes about 3 seconds of test work (29.6 seconds including compilation); browser and E2E runs took 3.7 and 21.9 seconds. `pnpm check:changed` completed with only benchmark lint errors; those were fixed and its exact script lint and script typecheck reruns pass. All other changed-code checks pass. Both production and full-tree unused-file scans pass.

Codex autoreview of the complete local candidate against `d119c6b0035e141d47b68f59f283cc2ee91f10f7`, through P2, is scoped-clean with zero actionable findings. ClawSweeper and exact-head CI remain landing gates.

prs.body:
Fixes #201963

## What Problem This Solves

When a chat RPC fails in the main-session subscription test, the assertion hides its error details and leaves the event waiter unobserved. Fixture cleanup can then add an unrelated unhandled WebSocket rejection to the failure.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Developers get the failed RPC's details without a second unhandled rejection from this test.

## Why This Change Was Made

Observe the event waiter and RPC assertion together, while registering the listener before sending. All existing authorization and visibility assertions remain intact.

This repairs test failure handling. The separate production admission fix, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201790, has merged and is included in the refreshed baseline.

## Evidence

- Forced an invalid `chat.send` message through the real Gateway fixture on Linux with the repository's pinned Bun runtime. The original code failed its assertion and produced one unhandled WebSocket-close rejection. The patched code failed only its assertion, with the `INVALID_REQUEST` details visible.
- Targeted formatting parity, type-checking and lint passed with zero warnings or errors.
- **Original-head integration failure, before baseline refresh:** the original baseline passed 2/2 tests; the patched ordinary run passed 1/2 and failed with `UNAVAILABLE: Session actor turn was refused by its current owner`. One diagnostic replay preserving the original wait order passed 2/2. Those passes do not establish that the intermittent refusal is fixed or that timing is irrelevant. The refusal originates in production session-actor admission; the exact rejected guard remains unproven.
- Local autoreview covered the complete range `cd2ae19272a3ee7be456385fa7efc56d6e2109a6..2f23b19caddf73e5f76384ad871bbefdb25dbdfb`, priorities P0–P3: complete, scoped-clean, no findings. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; the maintainer fallback route is used.
- Conflict resolution at `8a1c43e37a99bf7b5308c918a747cbe80b5c256b` preserves the merged production fix and changes only the same test waiter block. The candidate file is byte-identical to the previously reviewed and tested patch; independent exact-candidate source review passed. The full target test passed 2/2 in [the Gateway CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44675264741/job/136086045701), and [CI run 44675264741](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44675264741) succeeded for this head. The tested merge checkout was `c9aef378aff4fc052e03787f59ce145c60d93eee`. These results qualify this patch; they do not establish that every intermittent production refusal is fixed.

prs.title: feat(ui): embed iOS Simulator in Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI needs a readable, controllable iOS Simulator inside the Mac app, without a separate Portal dashboard or VNC service.

## User Impact

This draft adds a portrait Simulator panel in Systems with live device pixels, tap, drag, Home, keyboard input, and pasted Unicode text. The Mac node captures the Simulator framebuffer and sends HID input through pinned, attributed SimulatorKit helpers. The Gateway binds one capture and control lease to the authenticated viewer and the Mac desktop authority lifecycle.

The earlier VNC/noVNC Focus implementation was removed. There is no Python or VNC service in this design.

## Evidence So Far

- A signed isolated debug app built from `0e768769103` showed the booted iPhone in Control UI. The panel stayed Live for 36.7 seconds across two Systems polls at an observed 7.9–8.4 fps without reconnecting.
- An embedded tap changed iOS Settings from General to About; independent Simulator accessibility state confirmed About. An embedded drag scrolled About. The text composer entered `General` and `café 漢字` into the iOS Settings search field, confirmed by independent Simulator accessibility state.
- Disabling app-level Computer Control made an embedded Home action fail visibly with `PERMISSION_MISSING`; the iOS search state remained unchanged. The in-app confirmation is no longer visible, but the task app currently shows Allow computer control off.
- Focused Gateway tests passed 17/17 and UI tests passed 32/32 at `6e517f34757`. At `8685133c9ae`, the lease test passed 4/4 and the macOS package lock fixture passed 6/6. At `011cf141cce`, the Systems refresh test passed 3/3, scoped lint passed, and the test-line ratchet passed exactly at 6,590,659 lines. At `93008f974c1`, pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 reports 0/4 changed source files, syntax parsing passes, and `OpenClawIPCTests` compiles in a task-owned validation checkout. At prior head `a3f367890f4`, the repo macOS SwiftLint wrapper reports 0/426 and 0/22 violations, the SwiftFormat wrapper reports 0/423 and 0/33 files, and `OpenClawIPCTests` compiles in the same isolated validation checkout. Native macOS test targets also compiled at `8ba0de355ea`; native test execution belongs on CI/VM under the Mac development guide.
- An isolated app bundle at `8ba0de355ea` passed deep signature verification, exact revision stamping, executable/signature checks for both Simulator helpers, and bundled MIT/Apache/NOTICE checks. A task-local booted-Simulator probe of the updated touch helper received two cancel acknowledgments followed by the EOF release fence (`1,1,2`), then exited successfully.
- A Control UI browser probe at 375px and 1280px showed the portrait framebuffer at 221×481px and 245×534px respectively, with no horizontal overflow and Home/text controls visible. The 375px probe passed on the same CSS as current head `011cf141cce`.
- The CSS budget was increased by the smallest measured amount after removing redundant declarations: 325,109 to 325,224 gzip bytes. The prior exact-SHA CI comparison measured chat/new boot JS changes at +0 bytes against its base. A local Node 26 comparison could not build the historical base with the candidate toolchain and fell back to absolute budgets; it is not a passing differential result.
- A read-only security recheck found no remaining blocking lifecycle issue in the corrected source. Automatic cleanup failures produce a fixed sanitized macOS log message; explicit capture stop and execution close return the error, with the execution kept revoked.

## Still Open Before Review

- A distinct isolated debug bundle at prior head `a3f367890f4` passed exact revision stamping, strict deep ad-hoc signature verification, both Simulator helper executable/signature checks, and byte-identical MIT/Apache/NOTICE/UPSTREAM resources. Ad-hoc signing does not establish durable macOS permission continuity. Live tap, drag, Home, text, and revoke verification remain pending because the task app shows Allow computer control off; no permission prompt was accepted by this task.
- [Manual CI at `8ba0de355ea`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42594998626) found branch-caused package fixture, lint, test-line, dead-export, cursor policy, typecheck, and CSS budget failures addressed in `8685133c9ae`. [Manual CI at `8685133c9ae`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42598115166) confirmed package, typecheck, UI, dependency, and CSS-budget repairs; two further lint errors are addressed at `011cf141cce`. The terminal [macOS Swift job at `8685133c9ae`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42598115166/job/129108418497) found four source formatting violations, one legacy FileHandle read guard failure, and a Simulator close test whose fake service accepted input after stop. `93008f974c1` addresses those exact failures. [Exact-SHA CI at `93008f974c1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42614244837) confirms macOS native tests and packages passed; its release phase found PR-owned SwiftLint violations now addressed at `a3f367890f4`. [Exact-prior-head manual CI at `a3f367890f4`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42634516698) is terminal failure. All three macOS Swift jobs (packages, release, tests) passed. The failed jobs include control-ui-i18n, additional extension package boundary, one UI E2E shard, iOS build tests, check-lint, several Node shards, and ci-gate; The failed-job logs now identify two direct branch gates: `check-lint` rejects two new `createEffect` calls in `ui/src/pages/systems/simulator-preview.tsx` (ratchet `2 > 0`), and `control-ui-i18n` reports catalog fallback baseline drift. The other failures occur in Discord declaration generation, a chat E2E locator timeout, iOS lifecycle/Watch tests, and Node test shards outside the changed files; same-base equivalence remains UNKNOWN. `ci-gate` aggregates these failures. Manual `workflow_dispatch` enforces strict i18n; normal source PR policy defers translations. Final live proof and maintainer review are pending. This PR stays draft and must not be merged yet.
- Current source head `33d701ebebf` replaces the two new Simulator `createEffect` calls with a keyed capture lifetime. A focused regression covers control revocation, stop-before-restart ordering, and text-draft retention. The scoped commit hook formatted both changed files and `git diff --check` passed. Focused Testbox source preparation completed but the runner queued, so no remote test/static result was obtained; its task lease was stopped with GitHub settlement still unresolved. [Exact-head hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44676423269) was dispatched for the new head and is pending. The source PR intentionally contains no generated foreign locale/fallback metadata under `ui/AGENTS.md`; the strict manual i18n gate remains separately reported.
- Unclassified manual-CI errors: [Discord package boundary TS2883](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42594998626/job/129085968493), [chat waiting E2E pane timeout](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42594998626/job/129085969109), [runtime process graph assertion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42594998626/job/129085970796), and [cold-load CLI spawnSync error](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42594998626/job/129085971210). Their cause is unknown without same-base proof.
- With more than one booted iOS Simulator, the panel asks the operator to shut down extras and retry. Device selection is a follow-up, not part of this singular-device draft.
