prs.body:
## Integration update (2026-11-19)

Current candidate: `96dc22a3080d0538556e4c934233dbde6648955b`. This signed, two-parent merge preserves prior pin head `bf665f2db8cbfed047cd084d9ee4ed333653549b` and integrates main `59bc2068530eda00138a202bac129a7335d8de57`, including all nine landed qualification repairs (PRs #201713, #201717, #201720, #201724, #201725, #201730, #201736, #201744 and #201749). The earlier callback-lifetime repair in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201685 remains included. Relative to the integrated main, the PR still changes only the canonical Bun pin and two documentation references (+19/-19); all three files match the previous candidate byte-for-byte. Independent integration review verified staged tree `ddaf8844940dbfa5469a19c53a0acc958739bde8`, exact repair ancestry, no conflicts and no extra worktree changes. Normal commit hooks and whitespace checks pass. This PR remains draft and unqualified.

[Full Node/Bun validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830) completed against prior candidate `bf665f2db8cbfed047cd084d9ee4ed333653549b` with `validation_tier=main`, `test_runtime_policy=dual-all`, no release gate and no PR-selection input. Its 21 test-job failures plus the failed aggregate gate are recorded below; 130 jobs passed and 13 skipped. [Fresh full Node/Bun validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44498303546) is running at new candidate `96dc22a3080d0538556e4c934233dbde6648955b`, with `validation_tier=main`, `test_runtime_policy=dual-all`, no PR-selection input and no release gate. It tests the nine integrated qualification repairs together with main's Gateway shutdown cleanup and SQLite initialization changes. Earlier failures remain unresolved until that exact-head evidence completes. Diagnostic probes below intentionally retain their frozen prior source.

### Current full-run findings

Latest inspection of [run 44498303546](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44498303546) has eight failed Bun shards and the two previously recorded Node/Chromium UI failures, with three jobs still running. The Bun failures cover Doctor continuation/readonly-worker timeouts, reclaimed worker placement, pending-result admission, transcript commit recovery, cancelled-tree signal diagnostics, resident Gateway restart handling, placement-reclaim cancellation, and update custody after timeout. These are observed failures on the existing pin, not resolved cases or proof of a common cause. The job names contain `node-compact`, but their failing inner invocations explicitly identify the Bun runtime. The first Doctor job is [135471789665](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44498303546/job/135471789665).

The upstream integration is now in draft [Bun #222](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/pull/222) and [WebKit #56](https://github.com/openclaw/WebKit/pull/56), with both commit histories preserved. [Matched source-pair qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44509743849) is running; none of these OpenClaw failures is claimed fixed by that unqualified pair.

The [completed snapshot-phase probe](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44498115292), controller `33bd941ef28e29d4cdbaf3e5f72b509c09f973fd`, reproduces both continuation cases on frozen source `bf665f2db8cbfed047cd084d9ee4ed333653549b`. Cached-true completes its first maintenance snapshot, then stalls in cycle 1 at `snapshot-prepare`, route `awaited-worker`, phase `staging-create`; teardown and restoration complete. Cached-false stalls in cycle 0 before snapshot entry, with teardown at `close-async` and restoration not started at capture. The group also times out in the readonly-worker IPC-observation case: 2 files failed, 53 passed, 1 skipped; 3 tests failed, 545 passed, 5 skipped. The `staging-create` marker brackets a worker request whose budget preflight can await filesystem stats before IPC and before its request timeout is armed; it does not isolate directory creation, copying, or Promise starvation. The next discriminating boundary is budget wait versus request dispatch versus reply settlement. Artifact `14516114510` ZIP SHA-256 `d10ed25c4c751097efc6476366e01df2f414e730d26a9b7248130a6a11d74b29`; report SHA-256 `679562bb4966b7459f374024ca8d3483804df3729b34934ca4efcbaefd568df2`. This diagnostic does not qualify the pin.

The [completed Doctor acquisition probe](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44493072169), controller `0e8dc90f619c93756a6fd13e990e2cc9adfaec2e`, failed only the cached-writer case at 120 seconds; cached-false passed. Its failure snapshot is `gateway-released`, cycle 0: both recorded direct lease queries and their cleanup completed, while the test had not reached its mutation callback. Teardown and mock/environment restoration completed. The exact 56-file group reports 54 files passed, one failed, one skipped; 547 tests passed, one failed, five skipped. Native invocation and settlement completed; source and pin restored cleanly. This occurrence does not establish a lease deadlock or engine cause. Text artifact `14514212325` (38885 bytes), SHA-256 `9660aa76f6b6b330adb474b0d72f55f041e20837b82df9d1d7fdd52c50c35acb`; native log SHA-256 `e0546fb46ce258912a693bf70a793b7715b435f4d34a3fe18002df7448780e12`.

The [next repair-admission probe](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44494843369), controller `42fedc9afff66d6948d8454072e04c908562cccb`, retains the same frozen source, pin and 56-file group. It distinguishes legacy-lock inspection, maintenance reacquisition, agent-lease reads and exceptional schema preflight using per-case synchronous phase markers. No added waits, retries or success-path logs; 42 controller checks and independent review pass. It completed: both continuation cases passed and emitted no failure frame. The warm readonly-worker IPC-listener case separately timed out at 120012 ms; the 56-file group finished with 547 passes, one failure and five skips. All native work settled, with clean source/pin restoration. This did not reproduce or resolve the original continuation failure. Artifact `14514558457`, SHA-256 `6857cc898d909b4b9948f9512977ef728f626b2a16a56c4ffb04af4b44aeb00b`; native log SHA-256 `aae646c615ccd1cafb5f13620b2bd9d8a92a351f59f52c69dc010638d5a695bc`.

The [warm-worker phase probe](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44496487700), controller `023355a26c84519e1e75defa354f955b3611c820`, retains the same 56-file Doctor invocation and all prior continuation diagnostics. It adds one test-only, failure-only record for the separately timed-out readonly-worker case. Primary operation, reader close, child cleanup and fixture teardown are recorded independently; the test keeps its assertions, awaits, listeners and timeouts. All six source projections are hash-verified; 52 controller tests and independent review pass. It completed with the cached-writer continuation timing out at 120021 ms, cached-false passing at 5286 ms, and the warm-worker case passing at 745 ms. The last observed continuation phase is `maintenance-resources-acquire`, cycle 0: the non-schema lease check completed, while the schema-maintenance lease check was at `snapshot-prepare` with cleanup not started. Fixture teardown and environment/mock restoration completed; native work settled and the source/pin restored cleanly. This narrows the awaited boundary without identifying the blocked inner operation. The group reports 547 passes, one failure and five skips. Text artifact `14515717643`, SHA-256 `d9cdc820780815c4572871f8e30695117e912218649b0a9248dd0bd5cde4ffab`; native log (281335 bytes), SHA-256 `c1500fdfd6f19843de9840a0101e157754be2193913b7d5d48a045a1f0e673c4`.

The [snapshot-boundary probe](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44498115292), controller `33bd941ef28e29d4cdbaf3e5f72b509c09f973fd`, extends that same Doctor invocation with bounded route, preparation and internal-cleanup phases. This distinguishes reusable-lease selection, waiting for a single-flight result, staging allocation, raw copy, and cleanup. It changes no waits, Promise handlers, authority checks or timeouts; 54 controller tests and independent review pass. All seven projected source hashes are verified. A `flight-wait` observation alone cannot distinguish an already-joined flight from a producer not yet entered. The probe is pending and is not qualification evidence.

The [Beam failure-location probe](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44496175089), controller `6c3f44695d4349200000a928110e67759217758d`, is pending. It retains the original 80-file group, outer/group worker limits and both Node and Bun. Only the generic failed continuation path emits bounded error classes and repository-relative stack locations; no messages or private paths. The original RPC response is unchanged. Forty-eight controller tests and two independent reviews pass. This is diagnostic evidence, not pin qualification.

The full run completed with 130 successful jobs, 21 failing test jobs plus the failed aggregate gate, and 13 skipped jobs. The last running shard (`checks-node-compact-large-3`) passed. These are recorded failures, not a qualification waiver:

- [Worker build recovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412653861): the Node reconnect/claim-settlement case fails with a prepared-model-runtime publication timeout; its Bun execution passes. This reaches the same publication owner and broad workspace-plugins phase as the earlier worker-turn-context failure, but a shared root cause is not established. The current phase includes metadata resolution, registry preparation and subsequent input preparation. Log SHA-256: `a0583f02129b68bdee300b808f12724a294412232f3e7f55c1db2e5b1922b488`.
- [Config RPC, invited receipts and Beam](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412661468): Node times out in two config-RPC cases, including one teardown restoration. The invited-receipt assertion fails under both runtimes because it expects an already-admitted read to be revoked; the documented admission contract lets it finish and denies the next request. [A test-only correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201749) preserves artifact-byte denial and fresh-request refusal; [hosted Node/Bun proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44494366881/job/135458563885) passes the real product case under both runtimes. PR #201749 merged as `703cd16725348658db97188cba3f03b5acf13baa`; the new candidate integrates this merge. Two Bun Beam adoption cases report the generic load failure; its underlying cause is not yet established. Log SHA-256: `7ff6f70a828de819976abe095ab0eec37b405f16fe93c4e50975e19d4ac0da7a`.

- [Early final, retained send and profile-role preparation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412653702): Node alone times out in early-final reconciliation while Bun passes. Retained-send product proof times out under both outer runtimes, each waiting on an owned Node child; no inner allowed/revoked verdict is established. Both runtimes also reject a profile-role test assertion because admitted profile preparation resolves after a role-config change, consistent with captured-request policy; [The focused test repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201744) requires admitted profile work to finish and a fresh call to be rejected; [dual-runtime proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44493029890/job/135454012366) now passes: cross-device Stop and all four profile-preparation cases pass under Node and Bun. The repair merged as `fd933a39c52813ae77bd3bec9be10b597f5f613f`. All eight native invocations completed. No shared cause is established. Log SHA-256: `4547bd1697da375bdf4e908e0016a093195ba7b846cbf08ebbfd755db3b38353`.
- [Recovery authority tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412653874): the same four stale expectations fail under Node and Bun. [The focused test-only repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201713) preserves admitted work while verifying fresh starts are rejected; its first CI attempt exposed an introduced same-session claim deadlock. Head `37d9dabead4ab` repairs that setup through the existing preparing-source path; fresh review passed, and [exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44486741626/job/135432807175) passes all 18 cancellation and two member-role cases under Bun. It merged as `f165544e2ce40e46682bd67b6a98777f506dafec`; repaired-head Node coverage remains pending.
- WebKit dependency setup timed out in jobs [2/10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412649148) and [9/10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412649308), before tests. The same setup boundary failed on [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44479739339/job/135409354284).
- [Plugins UI roster loading](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412649346): the exact test and initial-roster timeout also fail on [an earlier main run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44473223458/job/135388112252).
- [Transcript reader stability](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412649236): a transient 22 px anchor shift fails the two-history-refresh case. [The exact case passes on scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44479739339/job/135409354406), so no inherited-failure attribution is established. The later distance-from-end change reflects added content, not another reader scroll.
- [Hosted Doctor process cancellation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412653803): Node expects an abort but receives an unconfirmed-process-cleanup error; the same Bun group passes. This is separate from the earlier cached-writer continuation timeout; attribution is pending.

- [Cron history cleanup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412653904): Node and Bun both finish the admitted deletion, contradicting the old mid-request revocation expectation. [A separate test-only repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201717) requires completed archival and verifies a downgraded operator cannot remove a different live job through a fresh request; it merged as `89e63e0cdf96313f2b08af67bf85c1ac29647851` after [exact-head Bun CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44486069714/job/135430578392) passed both cases. Repaired-head Node coverage remains pending.
- [Gateway startup projection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412661511): Node times out connecting in the configured-UI case; the corresponding Bun group passes. Attribution is unresolved.

- [Resident update restart](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412653833): Node passes the corresponding group; Bun fails both before/after-resident-answer cases at the receipt guard after the simulated service-stop acknowledgement. The returned ledger record does not satisfy that guard; actual process-stop failure is not established. [The failure-only returned-step replay](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44489972288), controller `b7829ca27723f0f847490cc07fe733af1250cc77`, passed all 850 tests with seven skips across the exact 64-file Bun group (63 files passed, one skipped). Both resident cases passed, so no failed-outcome step record was emitted. The old parser rejected bar-delimited project names and left the original report INCONCLUSIVE; parser repair `3bfeddfea1c048d4322cd5239efcbeda065f1649` recovered both passing case records from the unchanged [artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44489972288/artifacts/14513181635), SHA-256 `0c0b2f4ba637790a17dec200cbb3a84ad3015a31a1b874da72d9fea9502c6d2d`; native log SHA-256 `e0898b6f4d64d81955f570d61ea5ff78c02c3d5b2e2e4a9694720efba1c481f8`. Native execution settled and source/pin restored cleanly. The projection adds no database read or await, but earlier groups and passing Node runs were omitted and caches were cold. The original failure remains unresolved; this pass cannot qualify the pin or establish a process-leak/engine cause.
- [Doctor continuation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412653712): both cached-writer cases pass Node and time out under Bun; the false case also times out in teardown. Both begin with an open writer, and the false case closes it only after Gateway release. The timeout alone does not identify the stalled phase or establish the same earlier cached-only failure. [The failure-only replay](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44488270412), controller `2b15fc2fe88f29d9894941043a721667f495dcb0`, completed the exact 56-file Bun group: 53 files passed, two failed and one skipped; 545 tests passed, three failed and five skipped. The cached-true case timed out at its second maintenance acquisition (cycle 1), with teardown waiting in async database close; cached-false then failed while creating its fixture with read admission closed. The warm readonly-worker case separately timed out. This is phase evidence, not proof of an engine or writer cause. The original report is INCONCLUSIVE because its parser mistook a Vitest source excerpt for telemetry and did not accept bar-delimited project names. Parser-only repair `3bfeddfea1c048d4322cd5239efcbeda065f1649` passed 39 checks and recovered both failure records from the unchanged [artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44488270412/artifacts/14512498311), SHA-256 `c263391cee64838564c75993f1215956dd2708030a135c14c21050c63c77a17b`; native log SHA-256 `8ac164e7ca86815b1059bfbf340b97e5d1a1f4b612ef7bacd6a902df11ae58d5`. Native execution settled and restored source/pin cleanly. Earlier groups and passing Node executions were omitted; this diagnostic does not qualify the pin.
- [Session inventory enrichment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412653712): Node and Bun resolve the admitted read where the test expects role-change rejection. [The test-only repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201720) preserves the existing fresh-read privacy assertions. [Exact-head Bun CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44487307963/job/135434860147) passes all 14 privacy cases. The repair merged as `ebbd85cb6e7fbf04b72378577977fbf5de84e98a`; repaired-head Node coverage remains pending.
- [Stall observer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412653956): Node's delayed-capture test receives an unexpected sample. This case is intentionally skipped under Bun. [The focused test repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201725) counts stack packets separately from kernel samples while retaining delay rejection and budget checks. [Exact-head Node/Bun CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44489069327/job/135440544491) passes all four Node cases (the repaired delayed-capture case in 42 ms), plus three Bun cases with the expected delayed-capture skip. The repair merged as `6e55f5c4d918f2b01e4dd72ff358404fdf554d28`.

- [Cron command device removal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412653769): Node and Bun both reach the 60-second command timeout where the test expects device removal to stop already-admitted work. Source audit points to another stale expectation after the captured-admission policy change; [The focused real-child repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201724) is ready after [exact-head Bun CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44488958586/job/135440172986) passed in 2,115 ms. It requires admitted command completion and fresh-run refusal. The repair merged as `b8a2e78b82bdbbf4c20d6f1bbfd93d267007cac0`; repaired-head Node coverage remains pending for pin qualification.

- [Worker-turn initial setup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412653746): one Node case times out while holding input until syncing is authoritative and active; the exact Bun case passes. The timeout does not identify setup, admission, activation, settlement, or disposal as the stalled boundary. No shared retention cause is established.

- [Worker-turn attachments](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412653958): the Node worker-turn case times out; its Bun counterpart and both remote-exec counterparts pass. This test checks media bytes and workspace manifests, not heap retention. The timeout identifies neither execution nor session-end settlement as the stalled boundary; no shared cause is established.


- [Git release service ownership](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412654330): two Node cases supply synthetic service states without the now-required observed systemd manager UID, so inspection returns unavailable before the intended ownership assertions. Bun deliberately skips this suite. [The two-field fixture repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201730) has [exact-head Node proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44490808007/job/135446374289): all 12 cases pass, including both repaired ownership cases. Bun intentionally skips the suite. The repair merged as `fd4807ae11361d77fc25a702abf835a6b55ad71b`; production inspection is unchanged.

- [Followup startup and Visitor Access](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412653735): Node times out waiting for queued startup settlement after a prepared-model-runtime lifetime error; Bun passes that group. Separately, Node and Bun both fail two Visitor Access assertions that expect retained execution ownership to disappear synchronously during source revocation, before validation resumes. The later commit assertions are not reached. [The Visitor test-only repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201736) requires both admitted renewals to succeed and persist, then verifies execution-owner cleanup. [Exact-head hosted proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44491285948/job/135448205770) passes all five Visitor Access scenarios under both Node and Bun, including both revocation rows and final owner cleanup. The Visitor repair merged as `03115b5ed660e18fb46a7abcb70f7838595fc514`. The startup timeout is a separate boundary; no shared engine cause or unauthorized commit is established.

- [Chat stop and plugin-metadata retirement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412653725): Node and Bun both time out at the cross-device Stop product case. Later Gateway suites fail startup while plugin metadata is still retiring; secondary undefined-handle cleanup errors follow failed setup. Node also rejects the enabled cold harness fixture in the agent model catalog. The Stop wait, retirement cause, and fixture eligibility remain unproven; these failures are not waived.

- [Worker runtime publication and usage overview](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44480739830/job/135412661477): Node times out during prepared-model publication for direct worker ownership and fails to settle the committed usage overview inside its one-second test wait. Corresponding Bun invocations pass. No specific plugin, suspended operation, or shared cause is established.

## Integration update (2026-11-18)

Previous candidate: `b3db8b351ac3910858693a4f0a444d226177e81d`. [Previous-head Node/Bun validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44043551104) completed with 127 successful, 22 failed, 13 skipped and 2 cancelled jobs. Workflow and checkout both used this SHA, with base `42b907f`, `validation_tier=main`, `test_runtime_policy=dual-all`, no release gate and no PR-selection input. This exercised the previously omitted cases. The PR remains draft; the pin is not qualified.

- [Doctor continuation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44043551104/job/133904495388): Node 24.22.1 passed both cached-writer cases. Bun timed out in the cached-writer case, including teardown; the following uncached case failed while seeding its fixture with closed read admission, before Doctor started. Both runtimes passed the warm IPC regression and activation siblings. The original stall remains unlocated; the subsequent setup failure does not independently establish a second Doctor bug.
- [Invitation retention](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44043551104/job/133904501591): Node passed commit and rollback. Bun retained the commit callback sentinel while its control collected. The test and relevant callback owners match the original diagnostic candidate, but matching symptoms do not establish an identical root cause.
- [Control UI shard 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44043551104/job/133904491089): Bun failed `preserves newer model controls when accepting an older draft (identity=false)` while waiting for the model-picker option to appear, before selecting the newer controls or accepting the older submission. The cause of the missing option is unresolved. UI performance passed. This failure is separate from callback retention.
- [Spawn proxy retention](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44043551104/job/133904495351) failed in the default Node shard with one retained proxy; the corresponding Bun group passed. It is not evidence of a common Bun retainer.
- [Dependency analysis](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44043551104/job/133904492764) reported unused production exports `resolveSessionTranscriptPath` and `resolveSessionTranscriptPathInDir`. Their source, analysis inputs and dependency lock match main at `42b907f`. Other failed jobs remain unresolved; this summary does not waive them.

This signed merge preserves the original pin commit and both signed fixture integrations, and incorporates main at `42b907fdd6764ad34177c7fbec56a4f052881f6f`. Relative to that main revision, only the canonical Bun pin and two documentation references differ (+19/-19). All three landed fixture files match main byte-for-byte. Independent source review, signature verification, formatting and diff checks passed. The Bun pin is unchanged from the original candidate.

- [PR #200074](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200074) prevents the anchor preload from consuming startup IPC.
- [PR #200310](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200310) limits Doctor fixture request observation to its canonical readonly child while preserving every child's database guard.
- The [superseded scoped PR gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44040670671) ended with 48 successful, 1 failed, 20 skipped and 7 cancelled jobs. It omitted the Doctor continuation, invitation retention and warm regression cases; it does not qualify this pin. Older pre-merge runs are likewise not current-head proof.

The [closed-admission root-cut comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44041176672) used original candidate `4ea5bab`, with the original timer, collection and assertions. Old Bun passed all 8 cases; new Bun passed 7 and failed commit callback retention. Both pins collected all 4 closed admissions and the control in each case. This rules out the removed closed-admission roots in that projection, without identifying the surviving reference. Both cells settled and restored cleanly.

The [callback-identity comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44227751894) used the same original candidate and eight case identities. Old Bun passed all eight; new Bun passed seven and reproduced commit retention. Immediately after the original timer and GC, the new-pin commit case retained both `prepareMentionInvitation` and its returned `assertCurrent` guard, while the outer persistence Promise and control had collected. Rollback and both old-pin cases collected all observed objects. Both cells settled and restored the test and pin cleanly. This narrows the surviving identities without identifying their strong retainer; weak-reference instrumentation changes allocation/layout and does not qualify the current pin. The [signed diagnostic controller](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/commit/fbba4f90be4d9486e68565826ae2e0258a830a43) received independent source review, parser tests, syntax checks and source-projection validation before execution.

A [follow-on operation-spy probe](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44229002630) invalidated its old-pin control: old Bun changed from eight passes to seven passes and commit retention. Its observed operation parameters and run callback collected, while acknowledgement/completion callbacks survived, but the added observer changed the previously passing behavior. No runtime attribution or production repair is justified from this probe. Inspection of the pinned `@vitest/spy` 5.0.5 implementation found that spying adds `.then()` handlers to returned Promises; restoring the mock clears its histories but does not detach those handlers. The earlier review assumption that this probe added no Promise reactions is withdrawn. The old cell settled and restored cleanly; the new cell was cancelled before a verdict, and the run is fully stopped. The uninstrumented current-head failures remain the qualification blockers.

The [corrected direct-operation comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44266127995), controller [`1f2539fd`](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/commit/1f2539fd39084eb9446963c6b09386dbbca231bc), removes that spy and observes the original operation entry without wrapping its call or attaching Promise reactions. Old Bun passed all eight cases; new Bun again failed only commit retention. The operation parameter object and its run, acknowledgement and completion callbacks collected in both cases on both pins. Only the invitation preparation callback, returned guard and sentinel survived the new-pin commit case; the persistence Promise and control collected. This excludes those observed operation identities as the surviving roots in this projection, not every internal continuation. Both cells settled and restored both projected files and the pin cleanly. The same case identities and effective group hash were verified; instrumentation still changes allocation/layout and does not qualify the pin or establish an engine cause.

A subsequent [two-case async/disposal reduction](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44267580631), controller [`bebc5ef9`](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/commit/bebc5ef99f128414546af59c9f861bd2c2a8df47), passed commit and rollback with both pins. It retained the same Vitest configuration, outer guard-array ownership and single timer/collection boundary, but removed the database and publication owners. Both cells restored cleanly. The reduced fixture therefore lost a necessary condition; it is not a reproducer, does not exonerate either runtime or application ownership, and does not qualify the original failure. Further diagnosis needs a verified retaining path rather than another assumed lifetime cut.

The [transformed-code capture](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44039352845), also on the original candidate, recorded 7 passes and the commit retention failure. Its sole variant uses lowered disposal with both disposal calls present; helper identity remains unresolved. It establishes neither cause nor qualification.

The [bounded profile-symbol inventory](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44268679677) completed against the admitted published profile (ELF SHA-256 `522fdc6d7f2a627d891195dadd2ee8a8e416efecde6be249cda965d8f5d752fb`, build ID `c785eaeb8d8f2537f3c40779bb203167a0481d00`). It found defined JSC function, Promise, lexical-environment and marking-visitor symbols. All six tool operations settled successfully; the profile was not executed and no debugger attached. Symbol presence does not establish C++ object layouts, debugger callability or a retaining edge.

The [first post-GC stack attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44269708655), controller [`f19aac16`](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/commit/f19aac161e0ae8e83d5513ee6672ce4cd7233db9), used that exact profile executable and reproduced seven passes plus the original commit-retention failure. All six preparation steps passed and the native shard completed with exit 1. The debugger child exited 1 without its receipt; the parent continued, but attachment and detachment were not verified. The overall capture is INCONCLUSIVE and source was retained for runner teardown. It supplies no stack, root or scanner evidence. A [follow-on run](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44270470941) was cancelled before native execution after source review found that LLDB rejects hyphens in Python module names. The collector was renamed and import preflight passed in [the corrected run](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44270679872), but attachment timed out at 60 seconds without a receipt. A [phase-marker run](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44271629950) then reached debugger startup but never entered the collector before the same deadline. Both repeated seven passes and the original commit-retention failure; neither verified debugger detachment, and neither establishes stack ownership or a scanner cause. Their sanitized snapshots again recorded a 20-node, 27-edge reverse graph with no reported root path, while the overall snapshot status remained incomplete. The [same-profile attach/detach preflight with lazy symbol loading](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44272629368) passed exact PID/start-time/revision/executable-hash binding, attachment, detachment, debugger exit 0 and parent continuation. The full eight-case projection then reproduced seven passes and the commit-retention failure, but attachment to the loaded Vitest worker again timed out before collector entry. All seven preparation steps passed. Minimal-process attachment therefore works; loaded-worker attachment remains the unqualified boundary. No stack capture or frame ownership is established, and the overall result remains INCONCLUSIVE. Raw debugger output remains private to the hosted runner.

The [bounded packet-class trace](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44274550136) confirms that the loaded worker answered memory and thread queries while LLDB remained before collector entry; the minimal-process preflight attached and detached successfully. Disabling LLDB JIT-module loading in [the next comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44275554682) left the same timeout and seven-pass/one-commit-retention-failure outcome. That debugger candidate is unsupported. Neither run reached stack capture or verified loaded-worker detachment. Raw protocol payloads remained private; reported packet classes do not establish a matched request/reply identity or server deadlock. The [GDB attachment-only preflight](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44277542375) passed on the exact published profile executable: identity, attach, detach, debugger exit zero and parent continuation verified. No OpenClaw test was run in that preflight.

The [full GDB diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44277962649) then completed capture and clean detachment in the real Vitest worker. It collected 13 native frames and 19,856 bytes of main-thread stack, omitting 23 other threads. One word at stack offset 3,544 matched a zero-incoming Function cell in the recorded reverse graph; no general-purpose register matched. The graph still contained 20 nodes and 27 edges, with no reported root path. This is a post-GC occurrence, not proof of a GC-scanned root, frame ownership or the retention cause. The original eight cases remained seven passes and the commit-retention failure. The snapshot retains `complete: false`; a separate complete-recorded-graph admission enabled this diagnostic without claiming a root path. Test source and the candidate pin were restored, and tracked source was clean.

The anonymous fulfillment handler in `session-turn.ts` remains a source-backed candidate for that Function. The [identity-preserving WeakRef calibration](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44470952342) passed its admission rule: old Bun passed all eight original cases and collected the callback in both outcomes; new Bun passed seven cases, failed the original commit-retention assertion, and retained the callback and sentinel only after commit. Both controls collected, and exactly one callback was observed in each case. The observer returns the original function and adds no Promise reaction. This preserves the original old-pass/new-fail distinction; it does not identify the captured stack Function or prove a GC root. The [full identity run](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44472006339) identified that callback as the captured Function: callback index 0 matched collector cell `n1`, present once at main-stack offset 3,608. Capture, clean detachment, debugger exit zero and parent continuation all verified. The eight cases remained seven passes and the original commit-retention failure; rollback callback and sentinel collected. This identifies the Function, not a GC-scanned root or engine cause. Source, test and pin were restored, with tracked source clean. Artifact `14504439609`, report SHA-256 `cac2f530c666bdd8c232c885970cf6ca9bf13c97db1b3d6ad9499b985b34a8dd`.

A source-only candidate moves only the identified fulfillment handler to a private module-level function, preserving its result shape and leaving the inline rejection handler and `.then` ordering intact. The native line-cap gate passed without increasing counted lines. The [validation run](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44473306447) uses controller `a5200973f6d638aeeee140e592dfd654ffa79bd3` and source projection SHA-256 `bf4abb5852f07d92b4ad3a697fc09513815ec2aebbd776bc2445562ad7765657`. Acceptance: the original uninstrumented eight-case test must pass with the new published Bun, including commit collection, rollback error identity and admission cleanup; source and pin must restore cleanly. Only then may the unchanged 309-file native group run and pass. No observers, debugger, extra GC or changed assertions are included. This is a bounded lifetime-fix experiment; no RAM or latency improvement, engine-cause or fresh pin-qualification claim is made.

GDB evidence: attachment artifact `14414847759`, report SHA-256 `1aaa3b9b549f54a40250d0636a76a4c25fd721327e4f82687222cf44185be5da`; full-capture artifact `14414489763`, report SHA-256 `b7a0bffe4b8fe190025fd1ee5913ed55bf666c58f8fb1b38780c47b98edc4324`. Raw snapshots and debugger output stayed private to the hosted runner; published evidence contains bounded classifications and identifiers only.

Historical evidence below belongs to its stated source or projection. It does not supersede the current-head failures above.

## What Problem This Solves

CI and app-managed runtimes still select the October OpenClaw Bun build.

## User Impact

Updates the shared Bun pin to [the signed November prerelease](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/releases/tag/openclaw-v1.4.4-20261115-9debcc4b9d-webkit-3357f9d63e) across all six supported targets.

## Why This Change Was Made

Regenerates the shared pin from the published manifest, including archive and executable checksums, and updates the two current documentation references.

## Evidence

**Validation remains blocked by Doctor, invitation retention and other unresolved findings. The separate POSIX fixture repair has landed with passing projected proof and its own successful CI; this unchanged pin candidate is not ready to land.**

- Candidate: `4ea5babab09c338812ae50dbcdaed990f48cd0fc`.
- [Bun publication run](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43794773536) passed six-target build/signing/smoke and its frozen OpenClaw/Birdclaw consumer gates; published checksums and cryptographic provenance were verified. Those consumer gates tested their frozen sources, not this PR head.
- Static checks passed: canonical manifest projection, signed Windows flags, JSON parsing, exact scope, and diff hygiene. Independent source/diff review found no P0–P2 issues. Full local ClawSweeper review covered the complete three-file, one-commit range with no actionable findings. After the shared repository history repair, the retained native review-artifact validator passed with the candidate and workflow unchanged. This is structural validation only: the review remains NEEDS WORK with failing tests and behavioral gaps.
- [Exact-candidate Linux Bun-only qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43808664006) passed all ten canonical package and smoke stages.
- [Exact-candidate macOS compatibility comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43809623573) passed 30 cells and 792 test cases with no new regression reported. Old-pin execution covered Darwin ARM64; the new pin also passed the Darwin x64 Rosetta probe. Linux asset checks in that run were format/hash checks, not Linux runtime qualification.
- [Actual-head dual-runtime CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43805983669) finished with failure: all 270 jobs completed, with 218 passed, 38 failed, six cancelled, and eight skipped. The macOS test job was cancelled and skipped bundled app recovery. The dual-runtime UI2 failure still needs runtime attribution.
- Focused ARM packaged-recovery proof is now accepted from the [corrected app-host run](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43825007091): seven preparation steps and all three expected native phases passed; six ARM receipts covered both native-first settings and sharing omitted/true/false at the exact candidate, new pin and build. Cleanup exited zero and source remained clean. The outer workflow failed only after native proof, when its parser selected a different-schema fs-safe receipt and raised `KeyError: 'revision'`. This closes the focused ARM recovery gap, not full Swift, x64 or overall repin qualification. The [initial broader-build run](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43818225493) timed out before cases.
- Doctor remains a qualification blocker. The [matched Linux old/new comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43813941006) had identical 1,052 case identities and five skips: 1,047 old-pin passes versus 1,045 new-pin passes and two failures, including SQLite snapshot allocation/cleanup errors and timeout with uncertain settlement. The [two unchanged cached-writer cases in isolation](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43840085160) passed with both pins and restored cleanly; that does not explain or qualify the failing original 116-file group.
- The Doctor readonly-child observer candidate still fails in the original 116-file group. The [uninstrumented helper-only run](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43942906159) timed out cached-writer=true at 120,025 ms while false passed in 6,006 ms. The [same candidate with case/cycle phase writes](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43948269897), controller `59bc44ff`, reversed those outcomes: true passed in 5,432 ms; false failed in 300,006 ms across the 120-second test and 180-second hook budgets. Both runs recorded 114 files passed, one failed and one skipped; 1,046 tests passed, one failed and five skipped. Each completed with native exit 1, no controller failure or settlement uncertainty, five passing preparation steps, and restored source/pin with tracked source clean. Native arguments, environment, full preset, reporters and budgets stayed unchanged. The phase run recorded 62 contiguous case-attributed frames: true had no unmatched entry; false entered maintenance acquisition and finally-isolation without returned markers, with afterEach preceding the finally frames. Framing completeness means only untruncated attributed records; a missing returned marker may reflect a throw, not a stall. Marker writes can affect timing and scheduling. Neither failure is waived, and no internal cause, timeout fix or unchanged-C qualification is established. The [earlier cause diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43869768145) remains distinct: snapshot-staging readiness-deadline and channel-closed cleanup errors, native 143, uncertain settlement and no restoration.
- The same controlled comparison found a candidate-only invitation failure in `session-mention-invitation.test.ts:285`: identical 3,308 case identities and 34 skips, with 3,274 old-pin passes versus 3,273 new-pin passes and one failure. The callback sentinel remained retained while its control collected; both runs settled and restored cleanly. See the [old evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43813941006/artifacts/14204168676) and [new evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43813941006/artifacts/14203779105). The [isolated eight-case replay](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43823276474) also passed with the old pin and failed with the new pin. A [native-callback contrast](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43825930364) passed all eight cases with one collection request per retention case and restored cleanly, but changed the collection call site, Promise rooting and ordering. It neither qualifies unchanged C nor establishes a cause or waives the original failure. The [latest labeled reverse-graph diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43844491409) again recorded seven passes and the same commit-retention failure across eight cases. Its graph is complete as recorded: 20 nodes, 27 edges and no reported root path. The sole Function with zero recorded incoming edges has an unrepresented label; lexical, invitation-guard and message-preparation links remain source clues. Native retention still fails. Extra GC, layout perturbation, possible address reuse and unverified weak-edge semantics prevent a retention-strength, scanner or cause conclusion; the original failure is not waived. The [post-settlement transformed-code capture](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43851272064) again finished with seven passes and the same retention failure. It found one exact cached-code variant, but matched zero disposal anchors, so the capture remains incomplete and establishes no engine cause.
- The [static profile-symbol prerequisite inspection](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43860210092) finished INCONCLUSIVE without executing Bun or a debugger. Four complete type queries found no definitions; the SourceCode query hit the fixed 8 MiB output cap and terminated with uncertain settlement, leaving two types unqueried. This establishes neither broad type absence nor debugger readiness; it does not waive repin failures.
- In the same Linux comparison, the storage owner recorded 1,043 new-pin passes and three skips versus 1,042 old-pin passes, one failure and three skips. Both results remain separate from the unresolved failures.
- The original process comparison recorded 1,655 old-pin passes and 47 skips versus 1,650 new-pin passes, five failures and 47 skips; both runs settled and restored cleanly. The earlier claim of identical 1,702 case identities is withdrawn: 1,701 match, while one egress-redacted parameterized logging title differs in length (21 versus 22 characters). All 47 skip identities match exactly; no normalization or waiver is applied. The five new-pin 120-second timeouts were in `service-child-group-anchor.preparation.test.ts`: worker-close; control EOF with cancellation false/true; IPC disconnect without cancellation; and parent loss without cancellation.
- The [full-context POSIX diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43848482243) recorded early startup IPC delivery to the fixture listener before owner-handler installation, with one preparation timeout and the other nine cases passing. The resulting [fixture-only repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200074) now has [passing original-group proof](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/43852974587): exact C plus only that signed helper change, new Bun, 1,655 passes, zero failures and 47 skips across 1,702 cases; all ten anchor cases passed. The original 168-file group, configuration, environment, arguments, timers, GC and assertions remained unchanged, with no diagnostic observer or reporter. All five preparation steps and the native command exited zero, settlement completed without uncertainty, and source and pin were restored cleanly. Case identities match the original old-pin and pre-fix full-context records, preserving the original new-pin logging-title caveat above. This remains scoped projected proof. The fixture repair has now merged as [`3baa3645653f47caeeef6bf034232d9116149b7f`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3baa3645653f47caeeef6bf034232d9116149b7f), with the landed helper matching the reviewed fix. Its separate [exact-head CI attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43854391297/attempts/2) succeeded with 25 passed, 30 skipped and zero failed after one supported failed-only infrastructure recovery. This pin candidate remains unchanged; neither that fixture-head CI nor the projected proof qualifies a fresh Bun-pin head or resolves its remaining failures.

## Separate Follow-ups

The pin change remains scoped to three files. Recorded failures also exposed three unchanged owners for separate fixes: pairing fixtures advertise no `operator.pairing` scope; CI omits required Bun setup for two Node interoperability tests; prepared MCP catalog data is parsed as JSON after a serializer emits bare `undefined`. Their failures remain recorded; source attribution does not make the full CI run green.

Calibration evidence: controller `9e1cb7808ffab3072b7fc2a6f3463a1aa19427e3`; old artifact `14504218985`, report SHA-256 `c21996276063a5e5c7cda446500670cbaf3679d0f4884b2497d83184a32654c9`; new artifact `14504820759`, report SHA-256 `b49737deae16cf571976377f0e7e330031ca1c08f34c24de54157c57dfe9c4a3`. Source, test and pin were restored in both jobs, with tracked source clean.

## Callback lifetime repair landed

The fulfillment-only repair in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201685 landed as `8db39f34886f082ead5a84183d359d9535eb15b7` and is now included in this integration head. Its source-only projection passed all eight original invitation cases on the new published Bun in https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44473306447. The unchanged original 309-file group also passed: 305 files passed, four skipped; 3,274 tests passed, 34 skipped, zero failures. Both native commands exited zero with complete settlement, unchanged test bytes and clean source/pin restoration.

The repair's exact-head CI passed all six selected Node test jobs, build, baseline ratchets and PostgreSQL shards. Its merge-context run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44477106190 completed with 35 successful jobs, 27 skipped and two failures plus the aggregate gate: a plugins asset-request assertion matching scheduled main, and a Node environment-setup timeout contacting Ubuntu package mirrors before tests. All five PostgreSQL checks, including PostgreSQL 16 smoke, passed. Native landing retained those unrelated failure attributions through the supported exception. These results prove the scoped repair, not this fresh full pin candidate; the remaining Doctor and full-runtime qualification work is not waived.
## Beam owned-view diagnostic: reproduced

The failure-only location capture completed in https://github.com/openclaw/bun/actions/runs/44496175089 at controller `6c3f44695d4349200000a928110e67759217758d`, using frozen source `bf665f2db8cbfed047cd084d9ee4ed333653549b` and the existing candidate pin. Both target cases passed on Node and failed on Bun:

- HTTP Visitor publications are privately readable by their initial publisher through admitted RPC.
- Preserves model admission and rolls back revoked owned Beam adoption.

The two captured cause chains include `src/state/openclaw-state-db-cache.ts:667`, where the frozen source rejects a retired state database lifecycle, followed by the state worker owner/store and plugin resource host. These are handler observations, not frames individually bound to a test case, and do not yet establish why the lifecycle differs. The group also reports other failures on both runtimes. This is diagnostic evidence, not qualification of the pin.

Artifact `14518610253`: archive SHA-256 `26c304370f0cef3224f61b33718b744d7e206e2439857ba4b867263c6db8b41d`; `report.json` SHA-256 `9d10a5267f0b85c6b879bbde32cc766a05524d14050c14485649f5b043c9c2e2` (32,448 bytes).

The full run at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44498303546 is still in progress at integration head `96dc22a3080d0538556e4c934233dbde6648955b`. Observed failures include Chromium UI cases in shards 6/10 (cached transcript row positioning) and 7/10 (plugin inventory setup). Those jobs run Node/Chromium without installing the Bun pin. prs.title: fix: inline preview of larger workspace images in chat Files panel
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large images in the chat workspace Files panel showed "This file not previewable inline" even though they are perfectly viewable in a browser. The previous 256 KiB cap was too restrictive for common screenshot and photo sizes.

## Changes

- `src/gateway/workspace-file-limits.ts`: add `WORKSPACE_IMAGE_PREVIEW_MAX_BYTES` (5 MiB)
- `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.ts`: use the image cap for image files whose content has been verified locally as a browser-supported image
- `src/gateway/server-methods/workspace-files.preview-cap.test.ts`: new test file (8 tests, incl. 3 remote-parity tests)

## P2 content-verification (review remediation)

The 5 MiB cap previously trusted the file extension alone. `toSessionFileEntry` now sniffs the first 4100 bytes of image-extension files and applies the image cap only when the sniffed MIME type is a browser-supported image (avif/gif/jpeg/png/webp); anything else falls back to the 256 KiB text-preview path.

Follow-up commit (P2 remote-bypass fix): remote-bridge roots report prefix sniffing as `unsupported`. Extension alone is never trusted there: when content verification is unavailable, the generic 256 KiB cap is kept for all files, and the 5 MiB image cap applies only after local content has been verified as a browser-supported image. This matches main's behavior for remote workspaces and the remote-preview contract of #159895.

## Evidence

- `workspace-files.preview-cap.test.ts`: 8/8 tests pass, including 3 remote-parity tests asserting that `unsupported` prefix reads keep the 256 KiB cap for image- and non-image-extension files alike
- 3-run regression capture (BASE -> pre-P2 -> post-P2) at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pnwave/moltbot/proof-assets/pr-199935/a-regression-proof.txt
- Shipped-entry-point proof (Gateway via `dist/index.js`, real session + `sessions.files.get` RPC, no device identity) at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pnwave/moltbot/proof-assets/pr-199935/a-gateway-proof.txt

Related: #144881
