prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.



## Round 3 (ClawSweeper re-review findings + live-Gateway proof)

Head `1e502cd5e72` (synced with upstream/main, 0 behind). All review findings addressed:

- **[P1] Historical catalog hashes preserved** — the companion table leaked into predecessor schema generation, replacing historical hashes. New generation-owned transform `withLegacySkillSelectionCompanionAbsent` strips the unreleased table + indexes from every predecessor layout (`getOpenClawStatePredecessorSchema`, `state-before-provision-source`, `state-before-bootstrap-deferred` inputs). Historical inputs are byte-identical to upstream; the historical hash assertions are restored untouched; generated SQLite catalogs regenerated (228/235 inputs byte-identical, only current-layout inputs changed, as intended).
- **[P2] Input truncation marked before digest suffix** — names cut at the 64-char input budget are now marked truncated up front, so `aaa…(64)+alpha` vs `aaa…(64)+beta` keep distinct audit identities (regression test added).
- **[P2] Canonical decoder reused** — the writer owned a copied run/tool/message decoder; it now imports `parseAgentRunRow`/`rowToAuditEvent` from `audit-event-row.ts`, with companion decoding confined to `rowToStoredAuditEvent` + the distinct companion row shape.
- **[P2] Bootstrap privacy extraction removed** — the unrelated `workspace-bootstrap-privacy.ts` extraction is reverted; `src/agents/workspace.ts` is byte-identical to upstream again.
- **[P3] Stale sequence cache invalidated** — companion allocation consumes shared sequences outside the retention fast path (including duplicate-source attempts); the writer now drops the cached high-water mark on the skill path (regression test: ledger row after a skill write reports its true stored sequence).
- **Stale generated gateway validators** — the PR updated the protocol schemas but not the compiled predicates, so `kind=skill_selection` / `status=observed` failed gateway validation (2 gateway tests red). Regenerated via `scripts/generate-gateway-validators.mts`; 21/21 gateway tests green.
- **Test hygiene** — the `PRIVATE_PROMPT_CONTENT` absence assertion now supplies the sentinel as input (prompt/toolInput/skillFileContents); the unrelated expired-identity rendering case is removed from this PR.
- **Data-model compatibility proof** — new regression test builds a v39 pre-companion database with a stored legacy row, opens it with the current build (migrates 39→40, row intact), records a skill_selection (shared sequence continues at 2), and reads both rows back.

### Live-Gateway behavior proof (new, real Gateway + shipped CLI)

Production chain on a temp state dir — real tool-boundary read of a real `SKILL.md` through `wrapToolWithBeforeToolCallHook` → observer → recorder → store → **running Gateway** (fresh build, `--auth none`, loopback) → shipped CLI:

```
$ openclaw audit --kind skill_selection
TIME                          KIND             STATUS    AGENT  RUN           ACTION                     SELECTED
2026-11-14T23:42:01.167Z      skill_selection  -         -       observed  main   proof-run-1   skill.selection.observed  skill:proof--demo

$ openclaw audit --kind skill_selection --json
{"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":2,"eventId":"2c71cbfc-…","sourceSequence":1,
"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main",
"sessionKey":"agent:main:proof","sessionId":"proof-session-1","runId":"proof-run-1",
"action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection",
"actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"proof--demo"}]}
```

Stored rows: ledger `agent.run.started` (seq 1) → companion `skill.selection.observed` (shared seq 2, `main`/`agent:main:proof`/`proof-session-1`/`proof-run-1`/`proof--demo`) → ledger `agent.run.finished` (seq 3). Metadata-only, no prompt/tool content persisted. (An LLM-driven variant was attempted with local ollama `qwen2.5:7b`/`gemma4:12b`; the agent loop stalled at the reply watchdog, so the trigger is the repo-blessed scripted tool call — every stage after it is production code on a live Gateway.)

### Verification on this head

- `test/scripts/sqlite-schema-catalog-equivalence.test.ts` 203/203
- `runtime-skill-selection` + `audit-events.skill-selection*` incl. new upgrade/sequence tests green
- `audit-events` (37), `commands/audit` (36), `gateway/server-methods/audit` (21/21) green
- `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files, line-cap ratchet clean vs upstream merge-base


## Round 4 (re-review findings, head `883b4d8d003`)

Both P2 findings fixed, plus the requested proof/test adjustments:

- **[P2] Buffered run starts retained until acceptance** (`src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts`) — the skill path now keeps the buffered start for the existing paired-settlement contract when `writer.record(start)` returns false, while skill observations still record independently. Regression test: with a rejecting writer, the terminal settles as one paired `recordRun(start, finish)` instead of a lone finish.
- **[P2] Companion counts bound to transaction outcomes** (`audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts`) — tentative counts stage `rollback`/`invalidate` hooks through `stageSqliteTransactionState`, as the canonical ledger does. Negative control verified: without the fix a rolled-back overflow batch leaves the cap violated at 100,001 rows; with it the next insert trims honestly to 98,976. Covered by `drops tentative companion counts when their batch rolls back`.
- **Upgrade proof targets v2026.11.3** — confirmed the 2026.11.3 release is schema v39 (no companion table), so the regression test builds exactly that layout, opens it with the current build (migrates 39→40, `schema_meta` intact), and shows the stored audit row plus continued shared sequencing.
- **Flagged low-value tests removed** — unrelated date/empty-limit CLI variants and the full marker-construction equality case are out; encoding, truncation, and production-boundary coverage retained.
- Real-agent/model invocation remains best-effort: local ollama models (`qwen2.5:7b`, `gemma4:12b`) stall at the agent reply watchdog in this environment, so the trigger stays the repo-blessed scripted tool-boundary call; every stage after it (observer → recorder → store → running Gateway → shipped CLI) is production code, demonstrated in Round 3.

Verification on this head: skill-selection storage 7/7 (incl. rollback + v2026.11.3 upgrade), audit-events + commands/audit 45/45, gateway 21/21, runtime-skill-selection green, `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.


## Round 5 (re-review: settlement intent + true v2026.11.3 fixture, head `4fd73e177bc`)

- **Buffered run-start settlement intent documented** (`src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts`) — the skill path flushes the buffered start as a best effort so the ledger holds the run before its independent skill rows arrive (readers join by run; legacy run/tool views stay coherent), while rejection retains the start for the existing paired settlement boundary. This keeps the PR #178220 paired-start/finish contract: the terminal still settles as one paired run.
- **Upgrade fixture is the true v2026.11.3 layout** — verified the 2026.11.3 release is schema v39 without the companion table (release commit `50330aa9cf5`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 39`, no `audit_skill_selection_events`). The regression test now builds the fixture from the current schema minus only the unreleased companion table at version 40 (matching the release lineage), opens it with the current build, and asserts: `user_version`/`schema_meta` intact, a stored workspace setting row byte-identical, the stored audit row readable, lazy companion creation on first skill write, and continued shared sequencing with correct readback.
- Real-agent/model invocation remains environment-blocked (local ollama models stall at the agent reply watchdog; xAI cloud models need the `xai` extension whose dist build is broken by a pre-existing missing-`@solidjs/compiler` resolution from root, unrelated to this PR). The live-Gateway proof in Round 3 (production tool boundary → recorder → store → running Gateway → shipped CLI) stands as the in-environment maximum.

Verification on this head: skill-selection storage 7/7, audit-events + commands/audit 45/45, gateway 21/21, runtime-skill-selection green, `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.


## Round 6 (head `a71b0be6d94`)

- **True v2026.11.3 upgrade fixture** — the reviewer correctly noted the published v2026.11.3 is schema v22 (verified: release tag → commit `847611dcaa3`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 22`, no companion table), not v39. The compat regression test now builds the fixture from `getOpenClawStatePredecessorSchema(22)` (verified to reproduce the release's `audit_events`/`schema_meta`/`workspace_setup_state`/`config_machine_state` tables byte-identically; only later-dropped device/gateway tables differ, which audit admission does not touch). The fixture migrates 22→40 (backup custody via the standard test-support helper, as a real install would back up first) with `schema_meta`, a stored workspace setting, and the legacy audit row byte-identical, then records a skill_selection via lazy companion DDL with continued shared sequencing and correct readback.
- **Removed the remaining flagged whitespace-only decision-limit variant** in `src/commands/audit.test.ts` (restored the upstream single-case form).

Verification on this head: skill-selection 8/8, audit-events + commands/audit green, gateway 21/21, runtime-skill-selection green, `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.


## Round 7 — product upgrade run from published v2026.11.3 (head `a71b0be6d94`, no new commits; proof only)

- **Genuine release write**: ran the published v2026.11.3 source (release tag → `847611dcaa3`, schema v22) to create a state dir and record a legacy agent run through its production audit writer (`sequences 1–2, run release-run-1, user_version 22`).
- **New-build upgrade**: fresh `dist` rebuilt from PR source; the new Gateway booted the release DB with no schema refusal and migrated 22→40, release rows intact.
- **New skill write + shipped CLI readback through the running new Gateway**: production tool-boundary read of a real `SKILL.md` → observer → recorder → store (`skill.selection.observed`, shared sequence 4, `upgraded-run-1`), then `openclaw audit --run release-run-1 --json` returns the release rows and `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection --json` returns the new skill row with full attribution. Full redacted transcript kept with the run notes.
- Real-agent/model trigger remains environment-blocked (local models stall at the reply watchdog; xAI needs the `xai` extension whose dist build fails on the pre-existing missing-`@solidjs/compiler` root resolution). The trigger is the repo-blessed scripted tool-boundary call; every stage after it is production code on live Gateways, now demonstrated across a genuine published-release upgrade boundary.



## Round 8 — P2 rollback fix + missing proof piece (head `d541860e07a`)

- **[P2] Clear schema readiness when lazy creation rolls back** (`src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts`) — `ensureSkillSelectionAuditSchemaOnce` now binds the `skillSelectionSchemaEstablished` flag to the owning SQLite transaction via `stageSqliteTransactionState` (rollback/invalidate drop both the readiness flag and the warm row-count). A rolled-back lazy DDL no longer leaves a stale flag that skips recreation; the next write on the same handle recreates `audit_skill_selection_events` instead of failing with `no such table`. Postgres path binds the same way (no-op outside a transaction).
- **Regression test** — `recreates companion schema after lazy creation rolls back`: drops the companion table on a live handle, clears caches, runs a doomed `runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction` (lazy DDL + throw), asserts the table is gone, then asserts a follow-up `recordAuditEventInDatabase(skill_selection)` succeeds with the table present. Negative control: without the bind the follow-up throws `no such table`.
- **Missing real-behavior piece since Round 7 (22→40 boot already proven)** — production writer rollback/recovery exercised end-to-end on the same handle (drop → doomed lazy-DDL batch → recovered skill write → `audit.activity.list` readback path covered by `audit-events.skill-selection` + `gateway/server-methods/audit` suites). Real-agent/model trigger remains environment-blocked as documented in Rounds 3–7 (local ollama stalls at reply watchdog; xAI needs the broken `xai` dist); every stage after the repo-blessed scripted tool-boundary call is production code.
- **Owner decision still open** — default collection (`logging.audit.enabled`, 30-day retention, 100k row cap) awaits maintainer approval under the audit doctrine; contributor-side approval only.

Verification on this head:
- `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection.test.ts` 8/8 (incl. new rollback-schema + existing rollback-count + v22 upgrade)
- `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts` + `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts` 17/17
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts` 21/21
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files



## Round 9 — re-verification on sync head + genuine release-upgrade proof (head `8de7c834dba`, no new PR commits since Round 8)

Since Round 8 (`d541860e07a`) the branch only absorbed upstream sync merges — `git log d541860e07a..HEAD` shows sync commits plus upstream fixes, zero PR-owned changes. Full re-verification on the merged head plus a fresh end-to-end proof against a genuine published-release state dir.

- **Contract re-verified**: async worker `listAuditEventsInDatabase` (`src/audit/audit-event-read.kernel.ts`, delegated from `audit-event-writer.worker.ts`), companion table `audit_skill_selection_events` (storage + schema + migration), 4-field run-usage receipt (`name`/`source`/`activation`/`skillFile`, session attribution via audit side-effect only). (`workspace-bootstrap-privacy` no longer exists on either side — absorbed by upstream bootstrap refactors; zero references repo-wide.)
- **Suites green**: `audit-events.skill-selection` + `skill-selection-hidden` + `runtime-skill-selection` + `agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e` (via include-override, excluded from default projects by the `*.e2e` glob) — 26/26; `audit-events` + `commands/audit` + `gateway/server-methods/audit` + `sqlite-schema-catalog-equivalence` — 292/292; `tsgo:core` clean; `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files.

### Live-Gateway proof (new, genuine v2026.11.3 → PR-head upgrade)

State dir created by the **published release itself** (worktree of tag `v2026.11.3` @ `847611dcaa3`, deps installed, `gatewayWatch` dist built): release Gateway booted fresh (user_version 22, device identity issued, local credential custody created), one legacy `agent.run.started` recorded through the release production writer (`release-run-1`, seq 1). Release Gateway stopped; **PR-head Gateway booted the same dir** (fresh `gatewayWatch` dist): migration **22→40** with the release row byte-identical, companion table present, audit CLI serving.

Production tool-boundary read of a real `SKILL.md` through `wrapToolWithBeforeToolCallHook` → observer → `recordRunSkillUsage` (4-field receipt) → bus `skill_selection` event → the exact production recorder the Gateway subscribes (`createAgentEventAuditRecorder` + real async writer) → store with lazy companion path → shipped CLI against the running Gateway (`OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL=ws://127.0.0.1:18796`, `--auth none`, loopback):

```
$ openclaw audit --kind skill_selection
TIME                          KIND             STATUS    AGENT  RUN           ACTION                     SELECTED
2026-11-15T22:52:33.227Z      skill_selection  -         -      observed  main   proof-run-r9  skill.selection.observed  skill:r9--demo

$ openclaw audit --kind skill_selection --json
{"events":[{..., "sequence":3, "kind":"skill_selection", "agentId":"main",
"sessionKey":"agent:main:proof-r9", "sessionId":"proof-session-r9", "runId":"proof-run-r9",
"action":"skill.selection.observed", "status":"observed", "redaction":"metadata_only",
"selectedSkill":"r9--demo"}]}
```

Stored rows: ledger `agent.run.started` (seq 1, `release-run-1`, preserved) → ledger `agent.run.started` (seq 2, `proof-run-r9`) → companion `skill.selection.observed` (shared seq 3, full attribution) → ledger `agent.run.finished` (seq 4). Metadata-only, no prompt/tool content persisted. Real-agent/model trigger remains environment-blocked as documented in Rounds 3–8; every stage after the repo-blessed scripted tool-boundary call is production code on a live Gateway, this time across a genuine published-release upgrade boundary with release-created credential custody (the synthetic-fixture shortcut fails at the client-credential migration without it — verified).

Note: `openclaw audit` without an explicit `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL` resolved to an unrelated Gateway on this host's default port; the proof pins the URL explicitly.



## Round 10 — P1 validator regen + real-model trigger (head 82915d6ae6d, no upstream drift)

- **[P1] Regenerated Gateway validators** — `pnpm gateway:validators:gen` on this head; only `packages/gateway-protocol/src/compiled/protocol.generated/predicates.js` changes (+4246/-4235 from renumbered checks). `check_1259` now accepts `skill_selection` (`check_1262`), `check_1264` now accepts `observed` (`check_1267`). Verified through the **real request validator** (not mock):
  ```
  VALIDATOR {"kind":"skill_selection"} => true
  VALIDATOR {"status":"observed"} => true
  ```

prs.title: fix(diagnostics-otel): reject non-finite OTel duration env values
prs.body:
Closes #201797

## What Problem This Solves

`OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL=1e309` parses to `Infinity`, which passes the existing positive-value guard (`Infinity > 0`) and reaches `PeriodicExportingMetricReader`. Node's `setInterval` then overflows the 32-bit signed range down to a 1 ms timer: the reporter observed 206 OTLP export requests in a 300 ms window with a `TimeoutOverflowWarning`, instead of the documented default-interval fallback. The same shared numeric reader covers `OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_TIMEOUT`, `OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY`, and `OTEL_BSP_EXPORT_TIMEOUT`, so every duration setting inherited the hole.

## Fix

`readPositiveOtelNumber` now rejects non-finite values with the same warning-and-fallback path it already uses for non-positive ones (`!Number.isFinite(value) || value <= 0`). `Number.isFinite` also covers `NaN`, which `getNumberFromEnv` cannot produce (it already warns and returns `undefined` for NaN input) but keeps the helper's contract total for future callers. All six OTel numeric settings keep their documented defaults on invalid input; no configuration precedence, defaults, or dependency versions change.

## Evidence

- New `service.nonfinite-real-sdk.test.ts` runs the real SDK against a loopback OTLP receiver:
  - pre-fix (base `1579eb4dea`): `1e309` produces no invalid-value warning (`invalid: 0`), a live `TimeoutOverflowWarning: Infinity does not fit into a 32-bit signed integer`, and an export burst; the pre-existing `0` control already warned and stayed quiet.
  - post-fix: the `1e309` case warns once and issues zero requests with zero overflow; the control is unchanged. Red and green were both observed locally on this branch.
- `service.test.ts` / `service.otlp-export.test.ts`: 93 passed on this tree.

## Shipped Gateway real-behavior capture

After-fix (this branch, head `3bc6aa03db`) and before-fix (unmodified local `main`, `4442518e37`) were both driven through the shipped Gateway/plugin entry point: an isolated Gateway process (`openclaw gateway run`, source-tree launch of the same commit) with the diagnostics-otel plugin enabled through `plugins.entries`, metrics-only OTLP export to a loopback collector on `127.0.0.1:4319`, and `OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL=1e309` in the process environment.

After-fix observations:

- `startup trace: plugins.gateway-load.plugin.diagnostics-otel ... loadFailedCount=0.0` followed by `http server listening (2 plugins: diagnostics-otel, memory-core; 100.3s)` — the plugin loads and its service starts under this branch with the invalid value in the environment.
- OTLP metrics exports arrive at the loopback collector 4 times over ~4 minutes, 59942 ms and 59998 ms apart: the invalid `1e309` was rejected and the documented 60000 ms default interval is in effect. No rapid export loop, and zero `TimeoutOverflowWarning` lines in the Gateway output for the whole run.

Before-fix contrast (same command, same environment, same collector):

- One `TimeoutOverflowWarning: Infinity does not fit into a 32-bit signed integer. Timeout duration was set to 1.` line, and the loopback collector recorded 5631 `/v1/metrics` POSTs over roughly two minutes of millisecond-cadence exporting before the run was stopped.

Both captures ran with `gateway.mode=local` and loopback-only endpoints; no credentials, external hosts, or non-public endpoints are involved.

## Notes for reviewers

- `service.nonfinite-real-sdk.test.ts` intentionally uses the real SDK plus a loopback receiver (per the issue's real-SDK reproduction requirement); it observes a 300 ms window and asserts zero requests under the 60 s default interval, so it stays deterministic.
- The review asked for a failing real-SDK metric-interval regression before opening the repair PR; the red run on the unmodified tree was captured first, then the fix landed in a second commit-free state on this branch.

prs.title: fix(auth): remove provider credentials through shared owner
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related to #127543. Provider-wide model logout could return a removal list derived from a pre-removal snapshot instead of the credentials committed by the shared removal owner. For an operator using inherited credentials, the response could claim one set was removed while the persisted owner store contained a different set.

## Fix

Keep the existing shared credential-removal owner as the mutation boundary and return its committed removal inventory. The infer CLI and Gateway logout now publish that inventory. Targeted profile and API-key cleanup retain their existing warning, generation, rollback, and session cleanup behavior.

## Evidence

The shipped CLI was run from this head with isolated temporary state and synthetic credentials. A shared `openai:shared` token was seeded, then the child agent ran:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs infer model auth logout --provider openai --agent child --json
```

It returned:

```json
{"provider":"openai","removedProfiles":["openai:shared"]}
```

A separate Node process read the child-visible persisted store after the command and returned:

```json
{"profileIds":[]}
```

This demonstrates the user-visible receipt and the persisted removal independently of the command's own output. The test suite also covers the Gateway response projection and existing auth-key cleanup paths.

## Validation

- `src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-status.test.ts` passed with 50 tests.
- The focused CLI receipt test passed with 1 test and 121 name-filtered skips.
- The focused auth-key removal tests passed with 3 tests and 44 name-filtered skips.
- `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.

The full build reached the declaration-generation phase but was stopped after more than five minutes to avoid another prolonged resource spike. No provider revocation or live external API call was performed. The proof covers persisted saved-credential removal and the user-visible CLI receipt. This PR changes security-sensitive Gateway auth code, so it still requires the repository's current maintainer security approval before merge.

prs.title: fix(ui): Codex update failure offers a vague "Start a new session"
prs.body:
Related: #201130

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a Codex-harness turn fails because Codex is too old for the model, Control UI titles the failure "Couldn’t finish this reply" and offers **Start a new session**, which does not say what it does. The session it opens gets a one-line request to "do the update it asks for", so the agent has to work out which Codex to update and how.

## User Impact

User impact: the failure now reads **Codex needs an update** and offers **Update Codex**. One click opens a session on the OpenClaw harness with step-by-step instructions. The agent finds the Codex this Gateway runs, updates it with the package manager that installed it, checks the new version, restarts the Gateway and tells you to try your message again. **Try again** in the original session then works on the updated Codex. OpenClaw itself still never installs or updates Codex. Channels are unchanged and still show the text instructions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The notice already knows the failure is a harness update (`harness_update_required`), so it now uses that for its title and button. The Codex harness is the only one that returns this code today. The update prompt tells the agent to:

- find the Codex the error names: global CLI, desktop app, configured path or remote app-server;
- update that copy with the same package manager (`npm i -g @openai/codex@latest`, `brew upgrade codex`, …) and never install a second copy;
- confirm with `codex --version`;
- start a safe Gateway restart without waiting for it. The restart runs only after the reply ends, so waiting for it never finishes; the first live run spent 2 minutes trying to confirm the restart.

For a desktop app or a remote app-server, the agent says what to update and changes nothing.

## Evidence

**Before / after** (same Gateway, ChatGPT login, Codex 0.164.0 configured, `openai/gpt-6.2-sol` on the Codex harness):

| Before (`main` 8aa2808c7f44) | After |
|---|---|
| ![Before: Couldn’t finish this reply, Start a new session](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ebf0d84f-80fd-4adf-98f4-90769b1fe973) | ![After: Codex needs an update, Update Codex](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7dee9f5d-7c84-416a-8a9d-caeed27d09da) |

**End to end, real Control UI** (isolated source Gateway, a real ChatGPT subscription login and real model turns). The video is sped up during model waits:

1. Send a message on the Codex harness. The turn fails: `gpt-6.2-sol needs a newer Codex than 0.164.0. Update the Codex at …/npm-global/bin/codex (set by plugins.entries.codex.config.appServer.command), then restart the Gateway.`
2. Click **Update Codex**. A new OpenClaw-harness session opens with the instructions.
3. The agent ran `command -v codex`, `codex --version` and `npm ls -g --prefix …`, then `npm i -g --prefix … @openai/codex@latest`. It reported **0.164.0 → 0.171.0** and asked for a safe restart. The Gateway restarted after the reply.
4. In the original session, **Try again** succeeded. The Gateway log shows the Codex harness on `detectedVersion=0.171.0`.

![Update session reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/878a901b-6132-4259-8849-c294bea246ca)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d1ad7da-00a8-4127-96d2-0e96f1e5940a

Three live runs, each starting from Codex 0.164.0 (the first used an earlier draft of the prompt). Every update succeeded; the two runs on this head also retried the original message successfully.

- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-run-failure-notice.test.ts`: the update notice shows the new title and an **Update Codex** button, and the button creates the OpenClaw-harness session.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm check:test-types`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, oxlint and oxfmt pass.
- Control UI chat boot: 244 B gzip smaller than `main`. The existing CSS and request-count overruns are unchanged from `main`.

**Merge danger:** two-way door. The change is copy, one icon and prompt text; a revert fully undoes it, and it writes no state or config. The blast radius is Control UI users whose Codex-harness turn needs a newer Codex.

prs.title: feat: count realtime voice tokens in session usage and cost reports
prs.body:
Closes #202165

## What Problem This Solves

Voice conversations with an OpenAI realtime model (Discord voice, Talk, Voice Call) never record the realtime model's token usage. Session usage, `/usage cost` and Control UI Usage show the agent turns behind a voice session but nothing for the realtime model, which is the part billed to the OpenAI API key. One Discord voice setup ran about 93 minutes of assistant speech and over 100 consults with zero realtime usage recorded.

## User Impact

Session usage and cost reports now include a row per realtime model (for example `openai / gpt-realtime-2.1`) next to the consult model, with input, output and cached tokens from every billed response, including responses cancelled by barge-in. These rows show as unpriced unless the realtime model has a configured price: the model price table has no audio rates, and a configured text price does not cover audio tokens.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Realtime bridges get a provider-neutral `onUsage` callback that reports, once per provider response, the billing provider and model, the response id, the outcome status, and the token split (text/audio/image input, cached input, text/audio output).
- The OpenAI bridge reads `response.usage` on every `response.done`. That includes cancelled responses and responses that finish on a connection already replaced by a max-duration rotation, because those are billed too.
- Usage is reported from the terminal handler's `finally`, before response state is released, so a throwing terminal consumer or diagnostic observer (the case #121177 supports) no longer skips a billed response. A throwing `onUsage` is caught and logged, and does not block cleanup or the next queued response.
- Core records each report in the voice session as a hidden, empty assistant row under the provider and realtime model. This is the same usage-only row shape CLI runs already use: hidden in chat, and dropped from model replay. The response id is the transcript idempotency key, so a replayed report adds nothing.
- These rows are billing-only: `isBillingOnlyUsageRecord` (an `api: "realtime"` row that carries usage; voice transcript rows never carry usage) keeps them out of agent context accounting. The transcript accounting tail behind the memory-flush preflight skips them as both usage anchor and trailing context, the parent-fork context estimate skips them, and the status usage accumulator adds their counters to the session totals without letting them replace the context size (`totalTokens`/`contextUsage`) or the session's model identity.
- Wired into Discord voice (channel session), the Talk gateway relay, Control UI Talk with Gateway control, and Voice Call (when the call has a session key).

Not included, left as follow-ups:
- Audio pricing in the shared cost model.
- Azure OpenAI realtime: it bills outside the OpenAI catalog, so its usage is not labelled `openai`.
- GPT-Live: its wire protocol carries no usage.
- The meeting bot: its only session is a consult subagent session that may not exist yet.

Accepted tradeoffs:
- Each recorded response counts as one assistant message in usage message counts, as CLI usage-only rows already do.
- A response that finishes before the voice session's transcript exists (a brand-new channel with no consult yet) is logged as "not recorded" instead of creating the session.

Related: open PR #164531 touches OpenAI realtime transcript events; this change does not overlap it.

## Evidence

**Real-model e2e (real agent model, real OpenAI `gpt-realtime-2.1`, Talk gateway-relay).** An isolated test Gateway (own home, loopback port, no production state) ran the PR build with an OpenAI Platform key. The agent model was `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`; the realtime model was `gpt-realtime-2.1` with no mocks. A driver sent one agent turn with `chat.send`, opened a Talk realtime session on the same session key, and streamed two spoken requests as 24 kHz PCM16 (generated with OpenAI TTS) through `talk.session.appendAudio`. Turn 1 completed normally; turn 2 was cut off with `talk.session.cancelOutput` right after the model started speaking, so OpenAI finished it as `cancelled`.

| provider / model | count | input (uncached) | output | cacheRead | total | cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| openai / gpt-5.4-mini (agent turn) | 1 | 1135 | 529 | 23680 | 25344 | $0.0050 |
| openai / gpt-realtime-2.1 | 2 | 2598 | 118 | 1536 | 4252 | unpriced (`missingCostEntries: 2`) |

Both realtime responses are counted, the cancelled one included: completed = input 1966 (768 cached), output 92; cancelled = input 2168 (768 cached), output 26. Uncached input (1966-768)+(2168-768) = 2598, output 92+26 = 118, cacheRead 768+768 = 1536, which matches the report exactly. `chat.history` is unchanged by the usage rows: the agent turn, then the two voice transcripts and the realtime assistant line, with no usage rows.

prs.title: improve(ui): show subagent avatars beside transcript names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Subagents have colored avatars in the chat sidebar, but their names in the transcript lack those visual cues. This makes it harder to match a launched agent to the sidebar while several agents are working.

The latest correction removes both the redundant leading bot icon and its empty space. The previous revision hid the icon but left a 22px indentation.

## User Impact

Subagent names in launch and stop summaries show the same avatar and color as the sidebar. The summary still shows two names and the remaining count; expansion and name links work as before.

Rows with inline agent avatars omit the entire leading icon element. Their text starts at the transcript's left edge, with no empty icon gutter. Expanded launch rows follow the same rule. Rows without a visible agent identity keep their existing fallback icon. No setup changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript and sidebar share the existing avatar rendering and session-key color calculation. The latest correction moves the visibility condition outside the icon's wrapper in the two transcript renderers, removing the wrapper's width, margin and adjacent gap. No CSS, lifecycle outcomes or activity grouping changed. No reactive owners, effects or handlers were added.

## Evidence

Earlier gutter correction: `8193a8b719dc`.

- 41 existing tests passed across the disclosure, sidebar and lifecycle suites using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Changed-file lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- The production UI was exercised with a fixture-backed Gateway containing 12 running subagents, in light and dark themes. The summary and all 12 expanded launch rows have no leading icon gutter. Expansion and opening an agent through its name passed in both themes.
- Before/after browser measurements confirmed that the summary text moved from a 22px indentation to alignment with the preceding commentary. This is browser-renderer proof, not a live model run.
- Local autoreview against `b894fe5e3729` returned scoped-clean for P0–P2. This was static review, supported separately by browser checks.
- No permanent styling tests were added.

Validation limitations: local UI typechecking remains unverified because the compiler wrapper rejects the shared dependency installation used by this worktree. This earlier revision did not address the raw CSS failure. See the final alignment correction below.

### Latest correction: clean comparison

Same fixture, viewport, theme and crop. Before is `ec2c5958ac50`, with the empty gutter; after is `8193a8b719dc`, without it. The composer is excluded.

![Before: empty icon gutter](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e825853-3861-4577-bd69-207bba57cfde)

![After: no icon or empty gutter](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3997275c-504c-4513-8522-52dffe3703a2)

### Latest correction: annotated comparison

![Before: unwanted indentation highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0a2e0a1c-c6bd-4c40-955c-44c5e36b958d)

![After: text starts at the transcript edge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a9313fbd-0b18-4671-b20a-86ce96fc1926)

### Original avatar introduction

Historical proof for base `b894fe5e3729` versus the earlier avatar revision: [base without inline avatars](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/29628584-fc4c-449c-a57b-f816e2ea0917), [earlier revision with avatars](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/511face3-7b6f-4038-805c-e2b076582d7b). The current result is shown above.

### Final alignment verification

The avatars sat half a CSS pixel lower than the text on Chromium. The final change aligns them with the text without reintroducing the leading gutter. The 18 px avatars and 4 px spacing are unchanged.

Before (desktop):

![Before: inline avatar sits half a CSS pixel lower than the text](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a970ff5-edfc-473c-873a-1c0a6b3c5bd2)

After (desktop):

![After: inline avatars and text share the same vertical position](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/baafc0eb-f279-4119-bfeb-3cb4922e9043)

Expanded (dark):

![Six expanded launch rows share the transcript left edge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1163f22d-ff02-4786-ba7a-19d680c7372d)

Phone (390 px):

![Phone: aligned avatars; the existing one-line clipping still applies](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12aefaf6-7365-41dc-81f1-982c3bf0ff6d)

Verified at 1440 px and 390 px in light and dark with synthetic Gateway history. At phone width, long summaries retain their existing clipping behavior; tapping the row expands all six entries. Opening an agent from its name opens the intended Subagents panel.

The paired production build against `92d147da1552` adds 44 B raw CSS (64 B allowed) and 19 B gzip, with no budget change. The 32 focused tests and scoped lint/format/style checks passed.

prs.title: fix(gateway): work started by a cron run dies when the parent run ends
prs.body:
Closes #185961

## Decision for maintainers: cron reassignment

**Behavior change:** with this PR, children spawned by a cron-root run keep running after the parent run returns, **including when that cron job is later reassigned or deleted**. Today they die when the parent returns, whether or not anything was reassigned. That is the reported bug, and the reason the issue asks where the child's lifetime should start.

- Children still stop on `/stop`, on aborting the parent with its descendants, and on a reset of the requesting session (the existing requester-wide subagent cleanup), the same as children of a main session.
- The cron root's own session stays fenced, which is what #161085 protects: a child writes only to its own session, and its completion report runs as a new run in the cron key with its own fresh fence.
- If children should also stop when the cron job is reassigned, each child would need to hold a cron-root lease for its whole life. This PR does not add that; I'm happy to follow up if you prefer that design.

Jobs a cron-root run starts with the cron tool (`action: "run"`, second fix below) need no decision: the started job is admitted as its own cron run in the cron run queue, and an isolated job runs in its own `:run:` session, which takes no cron-root lease or request fence. Dropping the caller's fence only stops the job inheriting a fence that ends with the caller's run; it changes no lifetime policy.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: work started by a run in a cron job's base session (`agent:<id>:cron:<job>`) fails with "Guarded request authority is no longer active" once that run ends:

- sub-agents it spawns die, and their completion reports never reach the cron session;
- a job it starts with the cron tool (`action: "run"`) that outlives the tool's wait (60 s by default) fails on its first provider request after the parent returns.

## User Impact

User impact: children spawned from a cron-root run keep working after the parent run returns, and their results are delivered back to the cron session, the same as children of a main-session run. Jobs a cron-root run starts with the cron tool finish normally even when the parent run ends first.

## Why This Change Was Made

A stable cron root fences its own provider requests for the life of its run (#161085): the run's prompt executes inside `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority`, which marks the fence inactive when the run returns. `sessions_spawn` runs inside that prompt and launches the child through the in-process `agent` dispatch. The child's queued work captures the async context, so the child, and later its completion-report turn, inherit the parent's fence and fail on their first provider request after the parent returns.

The in-process `agent` handoff (`withInProcessGatewayDispatch`) already starts accepted autonomous runs outside two caller-owned scopes, the caller's transcript writer and its operator tool authority, because they "must not retain the caller's … authority after that invocation closes". This change adds the caller's request fence to that list, through `runOutsideGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` in `fetch-request-authority.ts`. The child then establishes its own fences when it runs, like any other run.

The cron job launch (`launchCronRunQueueResult` in `src/cron/service/run-queue.ts`) has the same gap: it already drops the caller's operator tool authority because "the launch owns its lifetime beyond the request acknowledgement", but a `cron.run` from a cron-root run's tool call launches the job inside that run's fence. The launch now also starts outside the caller's request fence, through the same helper; the job then sets up its own fence when its agent turn runs.

The request store can also carry a per-request egress check (`beforeRequest`). A run installs it only around its own provider stream call (`attempt-stream-settle.ts`), not while tools execute, so none is active when `sessions_spawn` hands off and none is dropped.

## Evidence

On unchanged `main`, both the mock-model Gateway runs and the live runs with a real Anthropic model show the reporter's exact error chain: the child's next provider request fails with "Guarded request authority is no longer active", the completion-report turn into the cron session fails with the same error, and the Gateway logs `Subagent announce give up (permanent_failure)`. With this change, the child finishes and its report reaches the cron session in both.

### Gateway regression (built Gateway process, local mock model)

`test/gateway-cron-root-subagent-spawn.e2e.test.ts` (new, one case) starts the built Gateway with a local OpenAI Responses mock. An `agent` request on `agent:main:cron:child-lifetime` spawns one child with `sessions_spawn`; the child's provider replies are held until the parent's `agent` request has returned. The case requires the child's second provider request and the report turn into the cron session to both arrive. Tool search is off so `sessions_spawn` is a direct tool, as in the existing `cron-isolated-spawn-only-child-delivery` QA scenario. Unchanged `main`, Gateway log (ids shortened):

```
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=subagent:agent:main:cron:proof-job error="Guarded request authority is no longer active." taskKind=spawn sessionKey=agent:main:subagent:3966…
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main error="Guarded request authority is no longer active." taskKind=turn sessionKey=agent:main:cron:proof-job runId=announce:v1:…
[agents/subagent-announce] Subagent completion direct announce failed for run e0da64e0… err={"name":"GatewayClientRequestError","message":"Guarded request authority is no longer active.",…}
[warn] Subagent announce give up (permanent_failure) run=e0da64e0… requester=agent:main:cron:proof-job
```

Mock-model Gateway runs of this scenario: unchanged `main` failed 4 of 4 with the chain above (the child never reaches the model); with this change 9 of 9 passed. Those counts come from a longer local version of the test; the committed case is that scenario trimmed to its core assertions (the committed case waits on the child's own run with `agent.wait`: on unchanged `main` it fails as soon as that run ends with `status: "error"`, 1 of 1; with this change it passes 2 of 2 in about 20 s).

### Live run (real Anthropic model)

Same built Gateway with `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`, reached through a local recording proxy that holds the child's first reply until the parent's `agent` request has returned. The parent was asked to spawn one child and reply `SPAWNED`. The child was asked to read a file and reply `LIVE-CHILD-OK`. Three runs on each side, cron key `agent:main:cron:live-child-lifetime`: `main` failed 3 of 3 as below; with this change 3 of 3 completed and delivered the report (in two of them the child answered with a sentence instead of the exact marker word, but its run finished and the report arrived). Excerpts from the first pair:

Unchanged `main`: the model's reply to the child's first request (a `read` call) arrives, then the child's second request fails inside the Gateway before it leaves, and the report turn fails on the fence:

```
response role=parent tools=[sessions_spawn] … response role=parent text="SPAWNED"
parent run returned status=ok
response role=child status=200 tools=[read]
[model-fetch] error provider=liveproxy api=anthropic-messages model=claude-sonnet-5-5 elapsedMs=0 sessionKey="agent:main:subagent:4f9c…" requestNumber=2
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main error="Guarded request authority is no longer active." taskKind=turn sessionKey=agent:main:cron:live-child-lifetime runId=announce:v1:…
[warn] Subagent announce give up (permanent_failure) … requester=agent:main:cron:live-child-lifetime
```

With this change:

```
parent run returned status=ok
response role=child status=200 tools=[read]
response role=child status=200 text="LIVE-CHILD-OK"
response role=report status=200 text="The live-child task finished successfully and returned exactly LIVE-CHILD-OK. …"
[agent] run announce:v1:agent:main:subagent:1978…:b355… ended with stopReason=stop
```

No "Guarded request authority" line in that Gateway log.

### Job started with the cron tool (one-off Gateway run, not committed)

Same built Gateway and mock model. A cron-root `agent` run creates a job with the cron tool and starts it with `action: "run"` and a 1 s wait; the mock holds the job's provider replies until the parent's `agent` request has returned. Unchanged `main`, the job's `cron` `finished` event, 62 ms after the parent returned:

```
{"action":"finished","status":"error","completionStatus":"failed","error":"Guarded request authority is no longer active.",…}
```

With this change the job finishes with `status: "ok"` after two provider requests, 5 of 5 runs (about 17 to 20 s each, mostly Gateway startup). This stays out of the committed tests: the unit case below covers the same contract without a second Gateway boot.

**Unit (cron launch):** `src/cron/service.run-queue.test.ts` › `starts a manual run outside its caller's request fence` runs `cron.run(id, "force")` inside a request fence and requires the job runner to see none. It fails on `main` (the runner sees the caller's fence) and passes here.

**Agent handoff:** this was an extra assertion in the existing launch case of `server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.authorization.test.ts`. `main` removed that whole suite in #198943 (consolidating redundant coverage), so the case left with it. The handoff stays covered end to end by the Gateway case below, whose spawned child crosses that dispatch boundary and fails on `main` without this change.

**Consumers:** 17 related test files (every `server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.*` suite, `server-plugin-subagent-runtime*`, `subagent-spawn.in-process-gateway`, `subagent-announce-completion-delivery`, `fetch-guard.authority`, `attempt-execution-phase`): 164 of 164 pass. One fork-transport timeout under a loaded host passed 3 of 3 on rerun; that test reads through `sessions.get`, not the changed `agent` path. For the cron launch: `src/cron/service` and `service.run-queue.test.ts`, 536 of 537 pass on current `main` plus this PR; the one failure (`ops.gateway-mutations.test.ts` › `leaves durable state unchanged when its caller is revoked during validation`, a 10 s `cron.add` timeout) fails the same way on unchanged `main`, 3 of 3.

Test lines are net +139 against `main`, within the per-PR allowance (the earlier allocation record is removed): one root-cause unit test that reuses `service.run-queue.test.ts`'s service and command-job helpers (+26, fails on `main`) plus one Gateway case (113 lines, which also waits for the report's committed chat event and checks it in the cron session's `chat.history`, reusing the shared Gateway test-instance and mock-model helpers) for the report turn into the cron session, which no unit layer reaches; ClawSweeper's review of the issue asked for exactly this regression. The Gateway case takes about 22 s, mostly Gateway startup; the cron-tool path is shown by a one-off Gateway run in the body instead of a second committed Gateway case.

After merging current `main` on 18 Nov (`16c28ff6acc`): #177296 wrapped the autonomous `agent` dispatch in `withoutGatewayToolCallerIdentity`; the merge nests it inside this change's `runOutsideGuardedFetchRequestAuthority`. On an isolated Linux test machine `service.run-queue.test.ts` and the Gateway case pass, and `pnpm check:changed` passes in full.

**Stopping a detached child** (existing coverage, rerun on this change): `subagent-control.accepted-stop.test.ts`, `subagent-control.commands.test.ts` and `subagent-announce.requester-settle-cancel.test.ts` pass (92 tests with the launch test). Locally, aborting the child (`sessions.abort`) or resetting the cron root (`sessions.reset`) after the parent returns stopped the child before its next provider request (2 of 2 each; the child sent no further request).

**Operator revocation** (one-off proof run, not committed): the cron-root parent was started by an operator connected with its own device. After the parent returned, an admin revoked that device's operator token (`device.token.revoke`), then the held child was released. 2 of 2 runs on this change; the child never reached the provider:

```
02:42:55.560 [gateway] device token revoked device=8483… role=operator
02:42:55.582 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=subagent:agent:main:cron:child-lifetime error="Session turn no longer owns controller admission" taskKind=spawn runId=100e39c3…
agent.wait → {"status":"error","stopReason":"rpc","providerStarted":false}; provider requests from the child: 0
```

**Checks:** `pnpm check:changed` on the change: typecheck, format, lint, line-cap, test-line, assertion and mock ratchets pass. Its remaining failures do not involve this change: Knip reports unused exports in untouched files (`extensions/knowledge/src/conversation-access-view.ts`, `src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-manifest-comparison.ts`, `src/state/openclaw-agent-execution-cleanup.ts`), and the SQLite worker ratchet could not run on the test host (`rg` missing).

Proof artifice: the Gateway runs use a local mock OpenAI Responses server (or, for the live run, a recording proxy in front of the real model) that holds the child's or job's replies until the parent's `agent` request has returned; operator revocation was triggered by an admin call; unit tests run inside a hand-made request fence.

Not tested: a cron job woken by `sessions_send`, and the CLI-runtime (`claude-cli`) parent path. Both reach the child through the same `agent` handoff. For the cron-tool path: a started job whose target is the main session (it queues behind the caller's turn, so on `main` it always starts after the fence has closed; the change covers it the same way, but no run shows it), `runMode: "due"`, and a real model.

Follow-up, not in this PR: `runOutsideOperatorToolGatewayAuthority` has other callers. Chat dispatch, channel startup and plugin services start with no request fence. Session maintenance can run inside a cron-root turn; whether its work can outlive that turn is not traced here.

Three standalone test suites lose track of fixture directories when a teardown removal fails.

- Temporary instrumentation was restored byte for byte.
- Scoped scripts-test typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, line-cap and max-lines checks pass.
- Independent classification and preservation reviews found no gaps. Local ClawSweeper review found no actionable defects.
- Test code is +6/-9 lines. Production and shared helpers are unchanged.

Maintainer-directed test audit. No release-note entry is required.

[CI attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44673355979) reports 18 Markdown heading errors in `docs/releases/2026.11.5.md`. Closes #201953

## What Problem This Solves

The two sandbox preparation benchmarks duplicate filesystem counter setup and restoration that already have a shared helper.

## User Impact

Reuse `countSyncFsCalls` from #201832 in both callers. This removes 42 lines without changing the helper or production sandbox code.

- Real-filesystem parity passed for both original and replacement blocks: two rounds, counters, return values, ENOENT errors, native realpath calls, named ESM exports, and restoration.

Matching baseline failures have not been established; these results are not claimed green. [Normal PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44582042631) passed at the exact reviewed head `f918208a096cf9e491e2ffa4ec64b44a0812f3a4`.

prs.title: feat(gateway): admit sessions_send wake starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_send` can fan out wake-starting work through the gateway `agent` RPC. Before this change, concurrent senders could bypass sender-local batching and rate limits. This adds an optional gateway-owned admission boundary for typed `sessions_send` wake traffic. It intentionally does not affect `mode:notify`, which does not create recipient work.

## Summary

- add a disabled-by-default `gateway.sessionsSendWakeAdmission` policy (six starts per 15 minutes by default)
- enforce it at the common gateway `agent` admission boundary only for typed `inputProvenance.kind=inter_session` / `sourceTool=sessions_send`
- persist one idempotent per-recipient decision in a separate SQLite database, atomically, and fail closed if state is unavailable

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/sessions-send-wake-admission.test.ts`: 4/4 passed (default-disabled, seven-recipient load, restart/idempotency, fail-closed state error)
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm format:check`, and `git diff --check` passed locally
- implementation is based on released OpenClaw `v2026.10.9` / `8b18b557`, matching the runtime that exposed the issue

## Rollout

Feature remains off by default. This PR contains no config enablement, runtime rollout, or gateway restart. Rollback is retaining the disabled flag or reverting this commit; the receipt database remains as audit evidence.

Tracking: cbire880/the-roost#2473, OP#1548
