prs.title: perf(skills): index discovery watch roots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discovery checks each skill's physical path against every initial watch root. With many plugin skills this repeats the same containment work thousands of times per scan, creating avoidable CPU work and temporary path values.

## User Impact

Use an index of the already-resolved initial roots to find the relevant containment root. Keep the existing containment guard, fresh realpath observations, watch-directory order and nested external watch targets. The proposed benefit is less discovery CPU and peak component memory, with small-workspace overhead measured explicitly. No setting, dependency, cache lifetime or worker limit changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing runtime path lookup as `src/infra/path-root-index.ts`; move its implementation unchanged and update all five existing production callers. Discovery constructs one index for each workspace scan from only the original physical roots. Newly discovered external targets never enter this index, so a parent external watch cannot suppress its nested external target.

For the declared fixture, source-derived containment-guard work falls from 80,800 to 1,200 calls per stress scan across four workspaces, and from 240 to 64 in the small fixture. These are code-path counts, not measured allocation or timing results. Index construction and ancestor lookups still have a cost; the comparison below must establish the net result. Generated-skill admission remains unchanged.

## Evidence

- Runtime net +1 line. The existing lookup moves without behavior changes; no compatibility forwarding owner remains. All five importers and the wrapper source inventory move together.
- One worker-handler regression using the real filesystem and captured transport checks ordered watch directories with overlapping initial roots, generated aliases and nested external targets. Existing lookup, relocation, plugin asset/tree, retained-runtime safety, discovery import/integration and containment tests provide sibling coverage.
- Initial frozen source proof: `e34e7748c6fc8f2d4725937c73d157bcc6395087`. Each runtime passed 128 owner tests and 143 wrapper tests, with one failed fixture expectation. Three filesystem-dependent cases were skipped (case-insensitive paths and two metadata-name aliases), as were three wrapper recovery cases requiring native `mv --exchange --no-copy` support. The fixture expected two alias-mediated external records that the existing filesystem boundary intentionally rejects; its expectation is corrected without changing runtime code. All 14 other stages passed, including lint/types and the unused-file audit; the full build was explicitly skipped after the test failure. This first proof excludes the subsequently added measurement script and lint-inventory row. The follow-up below closes these missing surfaces without repeating the passing suites.
- Reused measurement tooling: `scripts/perf/discovery-worker-idle-measure.mjs`, with explicit small/stress fixture selection. The current net deltas are +1 runtime line, +71 test lines and +470 verification-tooling lines, with no net inventory growth. Formatting and relevant static checks passed. This is a repeatable compiled-component workload, not a shipped runtime framework.
- Final source proof: all 18 stages passed on `1137a4883610b458e7cd22811f93bf66f4baa2a7` (tree `a3ddaeef4f52552d5bd0485b3a6e2dd6f1631608`), including the corrected eight discovery tests plus 14 lint-inventory tests on each of Node and Bun, affected lint/types, formatting, script syntax, the full build with `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=0`, and both unused-file scans with zero entries. The full build completed in 330.3 seconds, including declarations, and emitted seven UI budget advisories whose attribution remains pending the paired builds. Full proof SHA-256: `ecafe436cd6a3f206f707b7641ae503013083f5ace1eba5a9590a29dff23b3f4`. The final adapter-only correction keeps every runtime byte unchanged; its functional/static receipt is SHA-256 `f0e33cc01db0012230dec83868451783e0787f4ca015f68d52b3169b2a16d3ae`: the old adapter failed the expected alias/canonical path assertion, while the corrected adapter completed all 203 scans with five memory messages and joined worker termination. Formatting, syntax, lint and script types passed; original source was restored, the fixture removed and full dependency/generated-build seals matched before and after. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its shared checkout was dirty and was left untouched. Local autoreview covered `0b4d5d08b689296514e61d5f5d9a18ec3c511529` through `1137a4883610b458e7cd22811f93bf66f4baa2a7` at P0–P3 and found that fixture-path defect. A complete P0–P3 follow-up on commit `f62db8be50fc08f0110cb61b6aac7ccc226ba5df` found no actionable issues. Hosted review and CI remain separate. No paired acceptance trial has run for this candidate. The separate old-red/new-green symlink-ancestor fixture check qualified the benchmark path repair; its timing and memory values were omitted from the report and do not inform the fixed acceptance criteria or count among the 24 acceptance children.

Release-note context: discovery reuses a bounded per-scan root index to avoid repeated watch-root containment searches. Runtime performance remains unproven until the declared comparison passes. `CHANGELOG.md` is release-owned.

### Performance acceptance declared before measurement

This remains a draft until required correctness, review, CI and performance gates pass. Prior held experiments are not acceptance evidence for this change. No regression waiver is implied.

#### Frozen inputs and workload

- A: `0b4d5d08b689296514e61d5f5d9a18ec3c511529`, tree `a3a70d445009447ed170012ad267d9a220838841`.
- B: `f62db8be50fc08f0110cb61b6aac7ccc226ba5df`; tree `19067c021bfe53c4603070a52bda0919484f54e5`; reviewed full binary diff SHA-256 `d905d7e8668b1872dd74e5132ae9160ae207cd264cc697ebe085179b8b36414a`.
- Committed workload SHA-256 `ad48bbf869c425b215d3c25e894a642a63bb55a7d622f815c20d531a015874c1`. Private collection controller SHA-256 `fabfe4fbd4c1f908ebd51fa2048a0bcd9f85c95bf6f49e9d78b8be3866c4adc5` and evaluator SHA-256 `e5adfae5f89695177f4e839b27fdbed7198f81fd81d1bde52269275d3f94ab54` are frozen before dispatch and recorded in the results. Collection requires at least 3,600 seconds remaining after native source preparation and 1,800 seconds before the fixed 24-child loop. Each child has a 180-second cap; failures stop collection and remain evidence. The exact absolute cutoff and authoritative lease expiry are recorded at launch, with time reserved for source/dependency/build seals and cleanup.
- Exact Node 24.22.1 on Linux x64, pnpm 12.15.0, unchanged default worker heap limits. Every measured child uses the same committed adapter (`--size small` or `--size stress`) and has empty `NODE_OPTIONS`, the compiled worker uses `execArgv: []`, and each child receives a fresh empty compile-cache directory. Build-time inherited heap flags are recorded separately.
- Both exact revisions are installed and fully built before any child runs. Complete tracked-source, installed-dependency and generated-build seals are checked per arm before and after collection. Installed package content and arm-local links must match after the declared path normalization; the two installer metadata files remain bound by each arm's full seal. No shared writable dependency hardlinks.
- Two fixed sizes in order **small, then stress**. Each has six independent pairs in serial order **AB, BA, AB, BA, AB, BA**: 24 fresh child processes total. No replacement or adaptive additional samples.
- Two fixed synthetic workloads, each with four workspaces: small has eight local skills and the same four plugin contributions per workspace; stress has 100 local skills and the same 100 plugin contributions per workspace. Both use the production-default 256,000-byte skill-read limit. Each child performs **101 scans, five seconds idle, 101 scans, five seconds idle, then one next scan**: 203 exact-oracle passes. The raw results preserve 16 provenance records and 12 effective names per small workspace, or 300 provenance records and 200 effective names per stress workspace; path, content hash, description, source, publication directory and key order are verified.
- Five worker memory messages: the initial unsolicited sample plus four requested burst/idle boundary samples. The production memory port reads heap counters and heap-space statistics. No GCProfiler, task GC metrics, heap snapshots, observer-forced GC or source loader runs in the worker. Production idle GC remains active.
- Process RSS sampling every 20 ms plus endpoints. The complete child and joined worker exit are required. Every exclusive fixture/cache is removed and absence is recorded. Failed, timed-out or incomplete children invalidate the campaign.

#### Fixed metrics and estimator

Each item below is a separate acceptance metric; lower is better. The estimator is fixed before results: arm median and nearest-rank p95 across the six independent child summaries for each size separately. With six children this p95 is the observed maximum, not a reliable tail estimate. Report every child's raw value, all six matched-pair absolute/percentage deltas, their median and range. Undefined percentages from zero baselines are identified separately. Never pool the 101 scans as independent children or pool the two sizes. There are 184 acceptance cells and 552 matched-pair acceptance deltas across both sizes.

| Family | Separate metrics | Count |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Startup | elapsed, process CPU, main-thread CPU | 3 |
| Two complete bursts | elapsed, process CPU, main-thread CPU for each burst, including verification | 6 |
| First requests | first scan and first scan after idle: elapsed, process CPU, main-thread CPU | 6 |
| Warm scan latency | median and nearest-rank p95 of the remaining 100 scan latencies in each burst, computed within each child first | 4 |
| Two idle intervals | elapsed, process CPU, main-thread CPU for each interval, including after-burst sampling | 6 |
| Two inclusive resumptions | elapsed, process CPU, main-thread CPU from the idle timer wake, through after-idle sampling, to the next first reply before verification | 6 |
| Final next scan | elapsed, process CPU, main-thread CPU from dispatch to reply | 3 |
| End to end | elapsed, process CPU, main-thread CPU from worker creation through the final verified scan | 3 |
| Process RSS | ready, after each burst, after each idle, after final next scan, sampled peak | 7 |
| Worker allocated heap capacity | `heapTotal` after each idle | 2 |
| **Total** | **46 metrics per size, median and observed maximum: 184 acceptance cells across both sizes** | **46** |

Three primary medians must be strictly lower in B for the stress workload: **first-burst process CPU**, **second-burst process CPU**, and **sampled peak process RSS**. These test reduced discovery work and whole-component peak memory; RSS is not an allocated-byte counter. The small workload tests index-construction overhead under the same complete acceptance surface. This is a separate path-index candidate: the previous GC experiment's unused-capacity premise does not apply because this change neither alters GC eligibility nor requires large idle heap capacity. No GC threshold or large-capacity premise is used here. The prior GC experiment remains STOP.

Any adverse acceptance cell is **HOLD**, including small changes that may be noise. Any adverse cell at or above **20%** is **STOP**; use exact decimal comparisons on the recorded numbers. A zero baseline with a positive candidate is STOP; both zero is unchanged. All three primary improvements, no adverse cells and all execution/provenance gates are required for performance acceptance. Report every movement; do not drop outliers, change the estimator or run replacement children after observing results. Investigate failures separately rather than rerun until green.

Additional diagnostics are disclosed separately: per-scan values and within-child summaries; worker live heap, external/ArrayBuffer bytes, heap spaces and limits; initial/pre-worker state; sample send/receive gaps, idle timer overrun, RSS sampling gaps, host resources/load and all build advisories. These do not silently replace the named gates. Raw timer intervals must be at least 4,990 ms; the requested delay is 5,000 ms.

#### Interpretation limits

This measures an isolated discovery component process, not a deployed Gateway, concurrent foreground traffic or device-wide memory. RSS includes the parent, its verification/report data and worker. V8 `heapTotal` is allocated heap capacity, not a measurement of resident worker bytes; never subtract or add it to RSS. Sampling may miss peaks. Boundary sampling and verification can extend idle time; inclusive resumption timing owns the sampling delay before the next request. Five seconds of idle does not prove GC settlement, and this workload does not observe major-GC completion.

Filesystem and shared build caches are not flushed; fresh process and compile-cache state does not mean a cold OS cache. Both arms use the same observer and fixture. A lower component RSS does not establish lower deployed Gateway memory or behavior under concurrent load. Production GC remains unchanged in both arms; all observed idle and resumption costs remain acceptance gates.


## Measured outcome: STOP — not approved to land

The original fixed trial completed all **24 children / 4,872 verified scans**, with no replacements or exclusions. Both independent full builds passed with `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=0`. Final source, dependency and build seals matched their pre-measurement values; all sample fixtures and both arm worktrees were removed. The native run exited 0 and released its workspace owner. Collection succeeded, but the declared performance acceptance did not.

The frozen evaluator reports **78 adverse acceptance aggregates out of 184, including 17 STOP aggregates**. Small-workload results account for 71 adverse aggregates and all 17 STOPs; stress has seven adverse aggregates. This PR must remain unmerged. No threshold, metric, sample count or order was changed after measurement.

All three stress primary medians improved:

| Primary metric | A | B | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| First burst process CPU | 29,911.036 ms | 14,765.504 ms | −50.635264% |
| Second burst process CPU | 28,928.893 ms | 12,454.3955 ms | −56.948247% |
| Peak component RSS | 305.595703 MiB | 298.890625 MiB | −2.194101% |

Those gains do not override the small-workload regressions. Its median end-to-end process CPU increased from 2,436.2745 to 2,593.615 ms (+6.458242%); median peak RSS increased from 185,159,680 to 187,410,432 bytes (+1.215573%). Its first-scan observed maximum increased from 27.752351 to 47.697622 ms (+71.868762%). With six children per arm, the declared p95 is the observed maximum, not a robust tail estimate. These are failed acceptance observations, not proof that every adverse difference is a persistent product regression.

Complete aggregates, all A/B child summaries, all paired absolute/percentage changes, paired medians/ranges, and adverse diagnostics:

- [Small workload evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202189#issuecomment-7029392917)
- [Stress workload evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202189#issuecomment-7029393495)

Exact-head [CI completed successfully](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44663665734): 58 jobs succeeded, 26 were skipped, none failed. The local CI watcher timed out without attaching; that is a watcher limitation, not the CI verdict. The [exact-head hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202189#issuecomment-7029034611) has no findings or remaining before-merge items, and required this declared result before merging. Performance STOP remains decisive.

Both full builds emitted the same seven UI budget advisories and identical measured values: largest ordinary JavaScript 564.3 KiB; largest CSS 57.2 KiB; total CSS 331.2 KiB compressed / 1,707.4 KiB raw; chat boot 21 requests / 1,303.1 KiB compressed; new boot 803.4 KiB compressed. They were already present in A and were not introduced by this index change.

Evidence bindings:

- Archive SHA-256: `3f250794d80297d05bef72141e36e54ca8f1ce10037bc9f5cdb0b4f746f7611c`
- Complete report SHA-256: `20e169f69743f11a785591590f009440ea72ced8f09eb5ce52854078e6b000ab`
- Frozen evaluator SHA-256: `e5adfae5f89695177f4e839b27fdbed7198f81fd81d1bde52269275d3f94ab54`
- Evaluated output SHA-256: `5cedafa8e0b60312dc43219c716e27470ee7784c03697fa14a3085b5b69d55b7`

Interpretation remains limited to this compiled discovery component and fixed fixtures. RSS is whole component-process RSS, not a per-worker or deployed Gateway measurement. Boundary memory samples do not establish GC completion or physical residency of allocated heap capacity. Filesystem caches were not flushed. No additional trial is scheduled for this candidate.

Named follow-up only: investigate the small-root setup/lookup cost and justify any future linear-versus-index crossover design with a separately declared experiment. No heuristic or threshold is added to this stopped candidate.

prs.title: improve: avoid repeated history scans before replies in long chats
prs.body:
Related: #185111

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: repeated history scans before replies in long SQLite chats. Demonstrated with Codex: recording the accepted prompt invalidates the history index, forcing another full scan before the next reply even though the conversation's structure has not changed.

## User Impact

User impact: later replies can reuse the history index instead of scanning the entire saved conversation again. In the 200,003-event Gateway proof, the second and third reads examined 325 and 327 navigation rows instead of about 200,000.

**The first uncached read is still slow.** Restarting the Gateway or genuinely changing the history can require another full scan. This addresses repeated scans between replies, not all of #185111. No settings, database format, or upgrade action changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing navigation index when a canonical user-message rewrite changes only private `__openclaw` metadata. Continue rotating the normal transcript generation, refreshing changed page sizes, and reading selected message payloads afresh. Real edits, replacements and copied histories still invalidate navigation; a read from an older SQLite snapshot cannot certify the next read's index. PostgreSQL retains its existing generation-based reuse.

When account usage and chat history share the agent database, updating usage also invalidates the history index. This PR prevents that unrelated invalidation while the existing auth receipt still refreshes account usage/health. Credential and shared-state writes retain their existing behavior.

Most of the diff in `session-accessor.sqlite-model-context.ts` is re-indentation; view it with whitespace hidden.

This complements #190615, which removes unnecessary additional history reads within a reply. It neither includes nor depends on that PR.

## Evidence

### Full-product repro on main

A built Gateway, native Codex app-server and QA channel processed three incoming messages against a seeded 200,003-event conversation. On main `b03fd2fed06`, the Gateway returned all three expected answers but scanned the entire archive before every turn:

```text
navigation rows: 200003 / 200005 / 200007
history read ms: 8452 / 7791 / 7694
```

### Live Gateway run: isolating the two causes

The same workload on `059db8a7c5a` shows why both corrections belong together:

| Change applied | First navigation read | Second | Third |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| History correction alone | 200,003 | 200,005 | 200,007 |
| Auth correction alone | 200,003 | 200,005 | 200,007 |
| Both corrections | 200,003 | 325 | 327 |

Captured combined-candidate summary:

```json
{
  "scannedRows": [200003, 325, 327],
  "historyMs": [5226, 528, 421],
  "messages": [3208, 3214, 3216]
}
```

With both, whole-history reads took 5,226 / 528 / 421 ms. All three answers were correct; selected message counts remained 3,208 / 3,214 / 3,216. Actual auth usage writes ran on every turn without clearing the history index. These are single-run timing observations, not a statistical speedup claim; work counts are the acceptance measure.

Proof artifice: synthetic saved history, temporary count/timing instrumentation, and a local scripted model with a declared 1,048,576-token capacity to avoid fixture-induced fallback. Built-in context handling was used; this is not a real-provider or Lossless Claw qualification.

### Regression and compatibility checks

The permanent tests cover bounded navigation work after prompt recording, fresh content after edits/replacement, an older read snapshot followed by a committed write, and auth-state freshness without unrelated history invalidation. Test lines are net +314 against `main`: reuses the existing model-context fixture (one case now also wraps the write-receipt reader to commit a rewrite mid-rebuild) and agent/shared-state table to protect distinct navigation-work, read-snapshot and auth-publication contracts; no permanent Gateway harness is added. The navigation-work and auth-scope assertions fail on unpatched code; the snapshot test also rejects the unsafe candidate that omitted the read-lifetime guard.

Earlier validation on `059db8a7c5a` passed 8 real PostgreSQL tests and exact returned-history/error comparisons across byte/event limits. The existing PostgreSQL inline-auth startup probe also fails on main with a missing `openclaw_engine_anchor`; the separate admitted-owner PostgreSQL tests passed. No schema or stored transcript bytes are changed by this optimization.

After merging current `main` on 18 Nov (`16c28ff6acc`): #200793 rewrote page tracking in `session-model-context-pages.ts` (pages discovered from rows, no per-page `through`). The merge keeps `main`'s page discovery and this change's read-currency checks; because `main` now captures a cold rebuild's page receipts after reading its rows, the currency check moved after that capture, right before the snapshot is published (a write between the two must keep the rebuild out of the cache). A missing anchor no longer evicts another session's warm snapshot. Only reads with an event-count limit can reuse the history index. Other reads (full-fidelity context, native history seeds) now skip capturing a write token they never use; `takes the navigation receipt only for event-limited reads` covers it.

New test: `keeps a cold rebuild out of the cache when a rewrite lands before its page receipt` commits a native prompt annotation (a rewrite that keeps navigation warm) at the moment the rebuild reads its first page receipt, then requires the next read to scan again. On an isolated Linux test machine it passes here and fails with the check in its pre-move position (`expected 0 to be greater than 0`: the stale rebuild was trusted).

The three-message Gateway run, repeated on `main` `16c28ff6acc` plus this change (same 200,003-event seed, native Codex app-server, QA channel and scripted model; logging limited to navigation rows, history time and selected messages, since the earlier observation patches predate #200793):

```json
{
  "scannedRows": [200003, 325, 327],
  "modes": ["canonical", "warm", "warm"],
  "historyMs": [6997, 656, 552],
  "messages": [3208, 3214, 3216]
}
```

All three answers were correct; the work counts and selected messages match the 16 Nov combined candidate. The owner, consumer and #200793 sparse-sequence tests pass, test lines are +314/400, and `pnpm check:changed` passes in full.

Earlier branch base: `1fa849cee30`. The candidate passed 113 targeted tests. The test-line check passed at +204/400; production and test type checks, changed-file lint and formatting passed. The broader check's unused-export failure also reproduces on unmodified main. Hosted CI has not run. Earlier runtime results above retain their original source versions.

prs.title: fix(meetings): one slow browser audio pull ends a talk-back call
prs.body:
Fixes #177633

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: one slow browser audio pull ends a meeting talk-back call. The browser audio transport closes the realtime bridge on the first failed pull, so a single browser request that misses its 5 s deadline drops the call, even though the page capture is still alive.

## User Impact

User impact: a talk-back (`bidi`) meeting call now survives one stalled audio pull. The participant loses at most a few seconds of audio: the batch the stalled pull was carrying, if the page had already handed it over, and what the page dropped while the pull was stuck. Two failed pulls in a row still end the call, and a capture the page reports as closed still ends it at once. No config or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createBrowserMeetingRealtimeAudioTransport` pulls captured audio from the page about three times a second. Any pull error called `fail()`, which stops capture and closes the bridge.

A failed pull does not mean the capture is gone. The node audio transport (`realtime-node-audio-transport.ts`) already tolerates transient input errors, counting `consecutiveInputErrors` up to 5. The browser transport now uses the same counter and warning, with a limit of 2. Two is a cautious limit, not one the page forces. The page keeps only the newest audio (47 chunks) and closes a capture after 10 s without a pull reaching it. A pull that reaches the page resets that clock even if it then stalls, as in the clearest run below, so the page could survive more than two such failures in a row. Ending the call on the second keeps a capture that is truly gone from leaving the participant talking to silence for long. The count resets after the pull and any audio processing complete without an error, so unusable audio or a failed hand-off to the realtime engine still counts as a failure. Every browser safety and authority check still runs on every pull; nothing is skipped or cached.

## Evidence

### Live run

Live Slack huddle in a lab container: Linux, Chrome 155, OpenClaw built from #177357 (`83d04fa`) with #173898 applied, OpenAI realtime voice. Lab-only stage timing was added inside the browser plugin's `/act` route. IDs are placeholders.

Four talk-back runs failed 5–15 s after the join with `Meeting browser audio capture failed: Error: browser request timed out`. In each run, successful pulls finished their page work in about 3 ms. The failing pull in the clearest run finished its page work, then waited in the response's URL check until the request was cancelled:

```text
02:07:12.426 guard assert-done
02:07:12.426 fffvt evaluate-start
02:07:12.428 fffvt evaluate-end
02:07:12.681 fffvt guard-exit
02:07:12.682 post json-ok-start      <- resolveTabUrl -> navigation URL check (hostname lookup)
02:07:17.411 post released           <- request cancelled; 4.7 s with no further stage
02:07:17.413 Meeting browser audio capture failed: Error: browser request timed out
```

With the SSRF policy active, that check resolves the page hostname on every call. In the same container, 2 of 200 lookups of the Slack hostname took about 5006 ms, exceeding the audio pull's 5 s budget. In another run, the failing pull stalled before its page work started, at a step that run did not split further.

With the hostname pinned in the container's hosts file, a two-way conversation ran for 2 minutes: 371 audio pulls, no failures, and the participant heard the agent answer.

With this change (and #173898) and normal DNS, the same lab ran a two-way conversation for over 12 minutes. Four pulls stalled in the first 30 s; each was retried, participant audio resumed, and the agent kept answering the participant coherently for the rest of the call:

```text
03:07:16.375 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
03:07:24.193 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
03:07:33.775 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
03:07:41.694 Meeting browser audio input failed (1/2): Error: browser request timed out
```

Twelve minutes after the join, `slackhuddles status` still reported `inCall: true`, `audioInputRouted: true`, `providerConnected: true`, `bridgeClosed: false`, and the log had no `capture failed` or session-close entry. Before this change, every normal-DNS run ended at the first such stall. The live run used `8cc7ccc`; later commits only move the counter reset after audio processing and reword its comment; a stalled pull never reaches that point. The participant heard some agent replies cut short. The log shows four `audio output backpressured` warnings, which may explain them; that output path is not touched here and the cut-offs were not matched to log times.

prs.title: fix: uninstall also removes the node host service
prs.body:
Closes #202025

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw uninstall --all` removes only the Gateway service. If `openclaw node install` registered a node host service, it stays behind after the state and CLI are gone and keeps relaunching. The uninstall docs do not mention it, so users have no hint that a service remains.

## User Impact

User impact: a complete uninstall now stops and removes the node host service as well. If node teardown fails, state and workspace deletion are preserved, the same gate the Gateway service already uses.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `--service` scope now runs the existing `resolveNodeService()` adapter after Gateway teardown: absent services are skipped, loaded services are stopped, and the registration is uninstalled even when stopping fails. Failures point to the manual `openclaw node uninstall` fallback. The interactive service choice, `--service` help, CLI reference, and uninstall guide now disclose that both the Gateway and node host services are removed, and the docs list the node-specific launchd/systemd/Task Scheduler labels.

## Evidence

- New focused tests in `src/commands/uninstall.test.ts` cover installed, absent, and failing node services.
- Red on base: with the uninstall call reverted, "stops and removes an installed node service" fails with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times`, and "preserves user data when node service teardown fails" resolves instead of rejecting.
- Green with the fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/uninstall.test.ts src/commands/cleanup-utils.test.ts src/commands/reset.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 3 shards passed (27 + 14 tests).
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check ...` and `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <changed files>` pass; `git diff --check` is clean.

Gap: native launchd/systemd/Task Scheduler teardown was not exercised against a live service; the tests use the shared service adapter contract.

prs.title: fix: stop reporting removed paths that never existed
prs.body:
Closes #202026

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw uninstall` and `openclaw reset` print `Removed <path>` even when the path never existed. On a Mac without `/Applications/OpenClaw.app`, `openclaw uninstall --app` claims it removed the app. Users cannot tell what was actually deleted and what still needs removing.

## User Impact

User impact: cleanup output now says `Not found: <path>` for targets that did not exist, so an uninstall report matches what was actually removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`removePathPreserving` checks the target with the existing `pathExists` helper before `fs.rm` and chooses `Removed` or `Not found` accordingly. Successful removal and dry-run output keep their current wording. This covers uninstall, reset, and the other callers that share this helper.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(browser): avoid background screenshot stalls after Playwright connects
prs.body:
Related: #165312 (P1), specifically the [headless background-tab reproduction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165312#issuecomment-6014153598).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a missing activation step that can stall background-tab screenshots after a headless browser switches from raw CDP capture to Playwright.

## User Impact

User impact: headless background tabs receive the same pre-capture activation in both screenshot backends, including element and labeled captures. Known headed browsers keep their existing focus behavior. This draft does not establish a fix for the original intermittent headed/Xvfb hang or recover a capture that is already stuck.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared Playwright capture path now follows the existing raw-CDP rule using the running browser's observed launch mode. Screenshot media helpers move intact into a sibling module to keep the route within its line budget. Existing capture deadlines, emulation restoration, and queue ownership remain in place.

The focus-sensitive risk is activating a headed browser by mistake; added mode coverage checks that an observed headed launch overrides a conflicting profile configuration for both backends.

## Evidence

### Local Gateway and Chromium

Built main `02078202f31` and the same base with this PR's full patch applied. Both runs used the real Gateway, Browser CLI, and managed Chrome for Testing 154.0.8037.92 on Linux with Node 24.22.1. The Browser plugin files in the candidate match those in GitHub's merge ref `29675fb80a6a`.

1. Open two local HTML pages with distinct background colors. Take a normal screenshot of A, open B, run `openclaw browser snapshot --target-id "$a"` to establish the Playwright connection, then run `openclaw browser focus "$b"`.
2. On main, `openclaw browser screenshot "$a"` exited 1 with `Screenshot via Playwright timed out after 20000ms`. Repeating it reported that the cancelled capture was still running.
3. With the patch, the same screenshot and retry each exited 0 in about three seconds and saved 780×437 PNGs. With B brought forward before each request, element capture, `screenshot --labels`, and `snapshot --labels` also saved PNGs. FFmpeg pixel readback confirmed A's background color, and both labeled outputs reported two annotations.
4. With the patch and a visible Chrome window under Xvfb, taking a background screenshot kept B selected, as shown by the X11 window title. The headed capture still timed out and its retry reported a pending capture. The PR remains a draft while that behavior is open.

The standalone Chromium route fixture also passed against the unmodified production source. The real Gateway sequence above supplied the failing/passing headless reproduction. Local Codex autoreview of the current-main patch returned `scoped-clean` at P0.

### Earlier validation

Source inspection against `bfcaa1b2cd1cf2f0e7d617b773e4743218eb219c` found activation in `captureScreenshot` but none in the shared Playwright screenshot owner. Both screenshot routes and snapshot-label capture now carry the same launch-mode fact. The pinned [Playwright Chromium implementation](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/v1.64.1/packages/playwright-core/src/server/chromium/crPage.ts) implements `bringToFront` with `Page.bringToFront`; its screenshot path does not perform that activation.

Added regression coverage for true/false/unknown launch modes, launch-mode propagation to both backends, and a real Chromium route sequence that backgrounds an already captured tab and requests ordinary, labeled, and snapshot-label images. Existing interruption tests continue to target capture/restoration ownership.

Validation actually completed: `git diff --cached --check` passed; an independent read-only source review found and corrected the new regression's `path` versus `imagePath` handling. No additional concrete P0–P2 finding remained in that review. Production delta is +18 lines after accounting for the helper move; tests/test support are +51 lines.

[Remote Chromium regression](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/actions/runs/40626440967) passed the background-tab route test on a temporary child of head `160ab685fbad35d3e60612d469d85a98c65f4619` (1 passed, 15 skipped; test body 1.085 s). This uses real headless Chromium and production route handlers with a test route context.

[Remote base comparison](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/actions/runs/40627216743) ran the same candidate test with the two production screenshot paths restored to the PR parent. The test passed both before and after, so it did not reproduce the reported stall or establish a behavioral before/after fix.

Hosted CI for the ready-for-review PR remains pending.

prs.title: docs: create Docker state folders before onboarding
prs.body:
Closes #202041

## What Problem This Solves

The Docker guide's Manual and Headless flows run onboarding before creating the host bind-mount sources. On a fresh Linux host with rootful Docker Engine, Docker creates `~/.openclaw`, `~/.openclaw/workspace`, and `~/.openclaw-auth-profile-secrets` as `root`. The image runs as `node` (uid 1000), so onboarding fails with `EACCES`.

## User Impact

User impact: following either flow on a fresh Linux server now creates the state directories as the current user first, so the documented onboarding command succeeds.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both flows now show `mkdir -p ~/.openclaw/workspace ~/.openclaw-auth-profile-secrets` and explain why rootful Docker needs it. Each recipe also states that the image runs as UID 1000, so a host user with a different UID must make the directories writable by UID 1000, with a link to the existing permissions and EACCES guidance. This matches what `scripts/docker/setup.sh` already does.

## Evidence

- Docs-only change; no runtime behavior changed.
- `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/install/docker.md docs/install/uninstall.md` passes.
- markdownlint reports no findings for the changed files.
- Format check and `git diff --check` are clean.

prs.title: fix: preserve foreground exec output
prs.body:
Root cause: src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts:722 builds the exec outcome from `session.aggregated.trim()`, and that one trimmed string becomes both the model-facing text and the structured `aggregated` value that Code Mode hands to the program, so leading and trailing whitespace in command output is lost.

Fixes #202173

Thanks @sasan1200 for the report and the fix.

## What Problem This Solves

When a Code Mode program runs a command with `exec` and reuses its output, leading and trailing whitespace is gone. A unified diff that ends in a blank context line comes back 3 bytes short, and Git rejects it as a corrupt patch.

## User Impact

Programs get the exact output of a successful foreground command, so diffs and other whitespace-sensitive output can be passed on to the next command. The text the model reads for a direct `exec` call is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

For a successful command (exit 0), the structured result now uses the process output the session already keeps. Failures and nonzero exits keep their current text with the diagnostics. Nothing new is shown to the model.

Consumers of the structured value: the Code Mode value (now exact), the `/bash` chat reply, command-exec replies and cron diagnostics (they all trim before showing it, so no change), live command-output events (may now end in a newline), and stored transcripts (keep the exact bytes, still under the same caps).

The other test updates show the same change: those tests assert the real output of commands like `pwd` and `cat`, which ends in a newline. None of them tested trimming on purpose.

## Evidence

Proof comment: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202177#issuecomment-7028677391 (CI follow-up: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202177#issuecomment-7029040640)

- Isolated Gateway, Code Mode, scripted local model, same 84-byte patch. Base 0eb1fa3f7471 returns 81 bytes, and `git apply --check` on the returned patch exits 128 (`corrupt patch at <stdin>:6`). This head returns 84 bytes and the check exits 0.
- Control: with Code Mode off, the tool text the model receives for ordinary `exec` output is byte-identical on base and head.
- The strengthened Code Mode agent-loop test fails on base and passes here. Focused suites: 6 files, 100 tests passed, plus a sweep of 19 exec and Code Mode files (259 passed). The group-cleanup test also expected the trimmed heredoc output and now expects its newline.

Merge danger: a two-way door. A revert fully undoes it, and it writes no state or config. Blast radius: Code Mode programs and anything that reads the structured `aggregated` value of a successful foreground exec, which now keeps leading and trailing whitespace. Production +3 lines, tests +1 line (9 files).

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

prs.title: fix: return a busy child's steering receipt at once
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a parent agent sends a message to its own child while the child is busy in a long tool call, `sessions_send` waits about 30 s and then reports an error. The message does reach the child, but the parent thinks the send failed and often retries or gives up.

## User Impact

User impact: a parent's message to a busy child now returns at once as `accepted` / `steered`, and the child still sees the message at its next steering boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Steering returns at acceptance. Once the receiving run accepts a steered message, it owns that message until it commits it or the run ends. `sessions_send` no longer waits for the transcript commit. The durable-fallback and commit-wait path for `sessions_send` steering is removed.
- Admission-only contract: after acceptance, the receiving run owns the steered input until it commits or the run ends; a refused commit is never seen by the model, and custody is released exactly once when the run ends.
- The tool deadline result now uses the schema's `error` status instead of a `timeout` shape the schema did not allow. Models see this change.
- The `steerTargetRunId` stamp is written on the committed transcript row as part of the admission write, and confirmation no longer waits for runtime persistence. This also stamps plugin steering, which previously had no stamp.
- Commit-wait (`waitForTranscriptCommit: true`) and its `timeout` status remain for the other callers (announce, `chat.send`, steer adoption).

Known window: if the receiving run is cancelled or fails, or the Gateway restarts, between acceptance and the next steering boundary, the steered message is withdrawn although the sender holds `accepted`. Plugin steering on main already has this window. On main's restart model, a restart stops the child and wakes the parent, so the parent learns the child was interrupted and can resend. Making accepted steers survive a restart needs a replay-authority decision and is not part of this PR.

Split from #202111. The restart half of that PR is parked as reference, because main's own restart model now owns that class.

## Evidence

Real Gateway journey on a built Gateway (isolated state, real model), current main vs this branch. The parent spawns a child doing a 75 s exec, sends it a MARKER with `sessions_send`, then waits:

| | main (`416b357c`) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions_send` call → result | 30,066 ms, `error` | 74 ms, `accepted` / `steered` |
| Steered MARKER row in the child, and the MARKER in the child's final reply | 1 row, stamped; in the final reply | 1 row, stamped; in the final reply |

Tests:
- Steering receipt at acceptance (red on main: the steering-provenance test hangs 120 s, and the admission test returns `status: "timeout"`).
- The commit stamp is written for uncommitted messages.
- Steering custody is released exactly once when the receiving run ends, including the source-revoked case (the refused commit never reaches the transcript).
- The plugin steering contract now expects the stamp.
- Suites: sessions_send 11/13/132, user-turn transcript 89, steering custody 5, all green. tsgo and lint are clean.

Production code: +29 / −47 (net −18).

**Merge danger:**
- Two-way door: no schema, config or stored-state change.
- Blast radius: agents that steer a busy session with `sessions_send`, and plugin steering stamps.

prs.title: fix(auth): preserve refresh token on provably undispatched OAuth refresh failures
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #201933

OpenAI `chatgpt-token-sharing` and xAI `device-code` refresh transports wrapped
every transport failure as an unknown-outcome error, even when the failure
proved the refresh grant was never dispatched (closed local proxy,
`ECONNREFUSED`, DNS failure, pre-TLS disconnect, local SSRF block). The OAuth
manager then wrote a terminal failed refresh fence, invalidating a still-valid
rotating refresh token and forcing manual re-login after a brief local outage.

This change classifies provably undispatched refresh failures as
`phase: "before-dispatch" / outcome: "not-attempted"` so the manager rolls the
claim back instead of fencing the credential:

- New shared helper `createNotAttemptedOAuthRefreshError` in
  `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-oauth-runtime` (used by both adapters, so the
  policy lives in one place). It qualifies only two kinds of evidence, read
  from the nested cause chain so undici's `fetch failed` wrapper does not hide
  the code:
  - a pre-connect transport code from the shared retry classifier
    (`EAI_AGAIN`, `ECONNREFUSED`, `ENETUNREACH`, `ENOTFOUND`,
    `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`);
  - an `SsrFBlockedError`, which the guarded fetch raises before opening a
    socket.
- Both adapters track `responseSeen` via `onResponse` and classify only when
  no response was received. Any response — including a redirect — means the
  provider may have consumed the rotating grant, so the failure stays unknown.
  The OpenAI classification applies only to `grant_type=refresh_token`;
  login/JWKS transport failures are untouched.
- Ambiguous failures (`ECONNRESET`, timeouts after dispatch, aborts, unknown
  errors) keep their existing behavior: the OpenAI adapter rethrows them
  unchanged, the xAI adapter keeps its `token-response / unknown` error, and
  the manager still fences them.

No manager change was needed: `oauth-manager` already rolls back the claim
when `isTransientOAuthRefreshFailure` is true, and the new outcome satisfies
that check. The issue's suggested manager retry was omitted deliberately —
rollback already preserves the credential for the next attempt.

## Test report

New regression tests, red on the base and green with the fix:

- `src/plugin-sdk/provider-oauth-runtime.test.ts` — the classifier returns a
  `before-dispatch / not-attempted` error (recoverable per
  `isRecoverableOAuthRefreshFailure`) for `ECONNREFUSED` (direct and nested
  under undici's `fetch failed`), `ENOTFOUND`, `EAI_AGAIN`, and
  `SsrFBlockedError`; returns `undefined` for `ECONNRESET`,
  `UND_ERR_SOCKET`, unknown errors, and aborts.
- `extensions/xai/xai-oauth.test.ts` — `refreshXaiOAuthCredential` against a
  stubbed fetch throwing `ECONNREFUSED`/`ENOTFOUND`/`EAI_AGAIN` rejects with
  the `not-attempted` outcome; a 302 response followed by `ECONNREFUSED`
  stays `token-response / unknown` (response seen).
- `extensions/openai/token-sharing-oauth.runtime.test.ts` — same
  `not-attempted` classification for refresh attempts; ambiguous failures
  (`ECONNRESET`, unknown) keep their existing shape and stay unrecoverable.

Suites run (`--maxWorkers=2`):

- `pnpm vitest run src/plugin-sdk/provider-oauth-runtime.test.ts` — 14 passed.
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/openai/token-sharing-oauth.runtime.test.ts` — 40 passed.
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/xai/xai-oauth.test.ts extensions/xai/xai-oauth-refresh-bytes.test.ts` — 54 passed, 2 failed.
- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-manager.test.ts` — 19 passed.
- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-refresh-failure.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-refresh-fence.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.unknown-outcome.test.ts` — 3 files, 52 passed.

The 2 xAI failures are pre-existing device-code polling flakes in this
environment, not regressions: `stops authorization with stalled=false
cancel=false` and `preserves authorization_pending and slow_down pacing
before valid tokens` fail identically on the unmodified base (verified with
`git stash`).

`oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on all touched files; `tsgo:core`
exits 0.

prs.title: fix: Mattermost and Feishu render agent callback buttons, Mattermost taps arrive once
prs.body:
## Problem

Follow-up to #201764 (core marks agent-authored controls) for two channels:

- **Mattermost and Feishu drop typed callback buttons.** A `message` action button with `action: { type: "callback", value }` is never rendered (Mattermost leaves it out; Feishu shows only the label), so the agent's choice can't be tapped. Only legacy `{ label, value }` buttons render.
- **Mattermost delivers every button click twice.** The interaction handler enqueues a `Mattermost button click: action="…"` system event into the session and then also dispatches the click as an inbound message, so the agent sees the same tap twice.

## Root cause

- `extensions/mattermost/src/normalize.ts` (`resolveMattermostPresentation`): any button with an `action` that is not an `ask_user` question returns `[]`.
- `extensions/feishu/src/presentation-card.ts` (`resolveFeishuCommandButtonValue`): any `action` other than `command` returns `undefined`, so the button degrades to a markdown label.
- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/interactions.ts`: after the post update, the handler both calls `core.system.enqueueSystemEvent(…)` (resolving the session through a separate `resolveSessionKey` callback) and `dispatchButtonClick(…)`, which runs the normal inbound path.

## Solution

- Mattermost and Feishu render a typed callback button when a message action marked it for the agent (`agentControlText(value)` is defined). The existing tap paths already decode the mark (#201764): Mattermost through the signed `callback_data` context, Feishu through the quick envelope. Unmarked typed callbacks (plugin-owned, no handler on these channels) stay label-only, as before.
- Mattermost delivers a click once, through `dispatchButtonClick` (the inbound path with the sender's identity and session plan). The system-event block and the `resolveSessionKey` callback that only served it are deleted.

## What was deleted

- Mattermost's duplicate system-event delivery and its `resolveSessionKey` option (−44 lines).

## Accepted edges

- The agent no longer gets the `Mattermost button click: action="…" by … in channel …` system-event line; it gets the click once as an inbound message (`callback_data: <value>` for agent buttons, `[Button click: user @… selected "…"]` for legacy ones).
- Mattermost and Feishu value sizes stay as they are (Feishu 1024 bytes; Mattermost has no cap, a separate decision).

## Tests (red on base, green on head)

| Test | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| `mattermost/normalize.question.test.ts`: marked typed callback renders with `callback_data: ::pick:a`; unmarked typed callback does not | ✗ (no button) | ✓ |
| `mattermost/interactions.test.ts`: a click calls `dispatchButtonClick` exactly once and enqueues no system event | ✗ (system event enqueued) | ✓ |
| `feishu/presentation-card.test.ts`: marked typed callback renders a callback button with `q: ::pick:a`; unmarked stays `- Plugin` | ✗ (label only) | ✓ |

The tap side (mark → `callback_data: <value>`) is covered by the #201764 handler tests for both channels.

Gates: Mattermost and Feishu extension suites (`slash-http.boundary.test.ts` excluded: it fails identically on main), `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm check:test-types`, assertion-safety, mock-export, max-lines, line-cap and test-line ratchets, oxlint and oxfmt.

## E2E

Not run. There is no Mattermost or Feishu live harness (no E2E skill and no QA Lab live transport for either).

## Size

- Production: +8 / −45 (net **−37**).
- Tests: +38.

prs.title: perf(templates): show the full category on View all without a second read
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Clicking **View all** used to replace a four-card Template shelf with placeholders while the Gateway fetched the category again. Now the Control UI expands the full ordered list immediately if ClawHub certified the shelf as complete and its overview read started less than 30 seconds ago. The overview still shows four cards per shelf and preloads only their artwork; category results do not wait for another batch of icon decodes.

The Gateway opts in to `include=categoryEntries`, filters public listings, and uses the same duplicate handling and ranking as the full category read. Optional `additionalEntries` carries the remaining cards: `[]` certifies that the visible shelf is complete; an absent field means the client must fetch the category. Expired, superseded, or uncertified shelves fall back to that read. Category chips, text search, retry, permissions and installation are unchanged. No shared cache or speculative reads.

## Evidence

Matched cold-browser Chromium runs on two isolated Gateways against the same live catalog after [the registry change](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4844). Three interleaved loads each for Travel, Productivity, Research, Engineering, and Operations: 15 observations per arm. Every list matched an independent category-chip read in identity and order.

| Measurement | Control | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Click → full ordered cards painted, mean | 881.56 ms | **14.50 ms (−98.36%)** |
| Click → full ordered cards painted, median | 875.70 ms | 11.40 ms |
| Category RPCs caused by 15 clicks | 15 | **0** |
| Initial overview paint, mean | 1,196.13 ms | 1,102.61 ms |
| Initial overview paint, median | 1,031.90 ms | 1,055.10 ms |

**Research, ~108 ms after click:** [Before (107.9 ms)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b15c1ade-4f7d-424d-861c-3e324fc4bf2b): 24 placeholders, no cards. [After (107.5 ms)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ba8efb20-a3cf-4a41-a8a1-1c6c2a6fb9f7): all 16 cards, no placeholders. Raw and annotated screenshots appear below. The four-card starting shelf and final category identities/order matched.

Measured candidate `81716edcaa2` and initial published head `988a9edf60e` have identical source trees. Control `8926913e8a2` includes a measurement-only change selecting the canonical category router; that adjustment is not in this PR. Integrated head `0c1da2c50f3` regenerates the validator against `main`; its 13-file feature patch matches the measured patch (stable patch ID `e4c49c431e03`, zero context). The benchmark numbers above are from the measured candidate, not a new integration-head benchmark.

### Validation

- The four-card fixture previously flashed placeholders. Afterward its six ordered public cards appeared in one UI update, with no new requests or artwork decodes. Expiry and reconnect regressions failed before their guards and passed afterward.
- 115 focused tests passed on both the measured and integrated trees: 33 UI, 58 catalog source, 16 Gateway, 8 protocol. Scoped lint, formatting and affected typechecks passed on the measured tree.
- `pnpm gateway:validators:check` and `pnpm protocol:check` passed on both trees, including Swift/Kotlin contract checks. No protocol-version bump.
- Reproduce: `BENCH_CONTROL_URL=<isolated-control> BENCH_URL=<isolated-candidate> node scripts/perf/template-category-view-all.mjs`.

Review only; no merge or deployment requested.

prs.title: fix(exec): preserve empty quoted values during shell preflight
prs.body:
Related: #154513

## What Problem This Solves

Shell preflight drops intentionally empty quoted option values. `env --argv0 "" python3 bad.py` then loses its interpreter position and bypasses the Python source check; Node target extraction similarly misses a preload following empty inline code. This repair also addresses the reported POSIX backslash-newline discrepancy in the same permissive shell tokenizer.

## User Impact

Shell analysis keeps empty words and their comment boundaries. Outside single quotes, permissive shell parsing removes backslash-LF without creating an argument or starting a word. The public process-command parser retains its existing empty-entry/backslash behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict is reconciled using main's existing word-start state rather than adding a second tracker. Strict raw-syntax rejection remains intact: both strict tokenization and the actual `planShellAuthorization` entry point continue refusing line continuations. Permissive preflight normalization does not establish execution approval.

## Evidence

- On unchanged main, the empty-word/continuation regressions and both original script-target cases failed. Through the actual ExecTool preflight flow, the empty `env` value caused the malformed Python command to start and return a completed exit-1 result on this host, instead of rejecting with a `not_started` receipt. The repair rejects before launch with the expected Python shell-injection error.
- The Node `--eval "" --require ./preload.js` case executes its real preload and returns `preload`; this is a compatibility control, not a claimed baseline failure.
- Four owning files pass: 67 tests and 3 Windows-only skips, 99.74s total wrapper wall, including utility behavior, script metadata, full ExecTool preflight, and actual approval-plan refusal. Cold transformation dominates the preflight file's 93.27s duration; test execution accounts for 3%.
- Targeted owning-file TypeScript graph, production and test type-aware lint, formatting, diff checks, and the documented test-line budget passed. The unique 68-line allocation accounts for the distinct tokenizer, execution-boundary, metadata, and approval regressions against current main.
- Existing control-command and approval-binding consumer files: 43 tests passed, 4.46s total wrapper wall. CI timing is pending.
- This is a real ExecTool/preflight/subprocess component chain with the fixture's existing approval stub. No live Gateway/model/user-approval transport or native Windows execution proof is claimed; the full repository suite was not run.

prs.title: fix: show how to set up secure access when Connect a device can't make a code
prs.body:
Fixes #202045

## What Problem This Solves

On a new install the Gateway listens only on its own computer, which is the intended default. The first time the owner opens **Connect a device** and chooses **Create setup code**, the dialog shows "Couldn't create a setup code. Try again." with a list of config keys and a **Reload** button that gives the same result every time. Someone pairing their first phone has no way forward.

## User Impact

User impact: instead of the error, the owner sees **Set up secure access** with Tailscale Serve first, a trusted home network option that says what it opens and how to undo it, and **Retry**. Loopback stays the default and the dashboard changes no settings. Every other setup-code failure looks the same as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The Gateway's `device.pair.setupCode` refusal for a loopback-only Gateway carries a new error detail, `DEVICE_PAIR_GATEWAY_LOOPBACK_ONLY`, so the dashboard can tell this case apart without matching message text. The message itself is unchanged, so `openclaw qr` and older clients keep working.
- The dialog shows the new state with:
  - **Use Tailscale (recommended):** encrypted from anywhere while the Gateway stays on loopback, with the copyable `openclaw config set gateway.tailscale.mode serve` command and a link to the Tailscale guide.
  - **Use your home Wi‑Fi instead** (collapsed): only on a trusted network; the connection isn't encrypted, the Gateway stays reachable on any network the computer joins, and phones get Limited access, which still includes chat history and approvals. Copyable `openclaw config set gateway.bind lan`, plus the undo: bind back to loopback, restart, and remove devices you no longer want.
  - **Use a public HTTPS address** (collapsed): the existing `gateway.publicOrigin` and device-pair `publicUrl` settings.
  - The access choice stays editable, and **Retry** replaces Reload.
- The detail code, its reader and the new copy load only with the pairing dialog, so the Control UI boot bundles are byte-identical to main.
- The connect-and-pair docs describe the new state.

## Evidence

Isolated Gateway in a clean macOS VM, default install (`openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --auth-choice skip --no-install-daemon`, then `openclaw gateway run`, so `gateway.bind` is loopback and Tailscale is off), dashboard opened from its one-time pairing link, **Connect a device** then **Create setup code**. Before: origin/main cd2ae19272a3 (the dialog and setup-code code are identical on this branch's base). After: this branch. In the after run, **Retry** keeps showing the setup panel while the Gateway is still loopback-only, and `openclaw qr` prints the same message as before.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Couldn't create a setup code, config keys, Reload](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/6a8a441cda419769519c675503efa21ebcb9a4b1/images/2026/11/52d871e9-346b-4898-b613-8ad7a6268b2d.png) | ![After: Set up secure access with Tailscale first, home Wi-Fi and public HTTPS options, Retry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/ad13e66104b79801d9df436c76b4c47af23dd7d4/images/2026/11/8aa6e12f-433d-41ca-ac99-9012f911b2a2.png) |

Tests:

- `src/gateway/server-methods/device-pair-setup.test.ts`: a loopback-only refusal carries the detail, and the generic failure carries none. 28 passed; the new case fails on main.
- `ui/src/pages/devices/view-pairing.test.tsx`: the detail shows **Set up secure access** with **Retry** and no raw error, while another failure still shows its message. 13 passed.
- `ui/src/lib/device-pair-setup.test.ts`: create failures keep the selected access and the failure for the dialog. 27 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, core `tsgo`, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, `pnpm protocol:check` (no generated model changes), `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, formatter.
- `pnpm ui:build` budgets against main: boot JS gzip identical (new boot 822232 B, chat boot 1334008 B); total CSS +6 B gzip, +14 B raw.
- Not run: Tailscale Serve end to end (no tailnet in the VM), and the full UI and Gateway suites (left to CI).

prs.title: feat: start your first conversation with your own agent
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Connecting an AI can leave first-agent provisioning unfinished and send people into a separate setup conversation. The handoff should start the conversation with the regular agent they will keep using.

## User Impact

On a fresh install, connecting the first primary model also creates the regular first agent and opens its persistent Home conversation with an editable “Wake up, my friend!” draft. No user message is sent automatically. Existing installs and agents are left as they are, utility-only connections stay in Model Setup, and if the agent handoff target isn't available the dashboard opens the ordinary chat instead of reporting a failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Automatic detection, sign-in, alternatives, retry and native recovery controls now live in Model Setup, and native onboarding opens that same surface (`/settings/model-setup?firstRun=auto`).

The Gateway decides when to create the first agent; clients do not ask for it. Gateway setup (`surface: "gateway"`) creates the canonical first agent only when the activation selects the **first** primary model on an install with **no authored agent roster**. That is the fresh-install signal. Installs that already have a primary model (including those using an implicit `main` with no `agents.entries`), CLI activation, access-only sign-in and utility-only setup keep their existing shape. Canonical creation publishes the verified model and accepted native consent in one config write; failed application restores the previous authored config, including the absence of a first agent, and does not schedule the proactive job.

The handoff target is fail-open by design:

- Already-configured automatic setup (`openclaw.setup.auto`) is read-only again: it never activates, writes config or throws because a first agent is missing.
- After a successful primary activation, the Gateway reads the agent's Home target (`agentId`, `sessionKey`, `bootstrapPending`) on a best-effort basis. An unreadable config, unknown agent or workspace error omits the target and logs a warning; it never fails a connection that already succeeded.
- The UI opens the regular agent's Home with the starter draft when a target is present and the ordinary chat when it is not, including after a lost activation reply or a Gateway restart.

The Linux/Windows desktop app's automatic first run now opens `/settings/model-setup?firstRun=auto` like the macOS app (stale `/custodian?onboarding=1` links still show the manual setup prompt). The saved Ask dock preference is kept across reloads; the retired Ask "minimize after onboarding" plumbing is removed. A failure to schedule the optional default check-in job after the agent and model are applied is reported as a warning instead of failing setup.

**Protocol surface:** one optional `firstAgent` reply field on `openclaw.setup.activate`, `openclaw.setup.auto` and the wizard's `modelActivation`. There is no new request flag, no new server capability and no new activation kind, so older Gateways and clients are unaffected and the generated request validators are byte-identical to `main`. The `openclaw.json` config schema is unchanged.

## Evidence

Candidate: `87fb5434c06c5ffee4b719b85a424693b936e65c` (merged with `main` at `0eb1fa3f747`). The Codex auto-detect and existing-install scenarios were rerun on `8600ad8` after rebuilding (later commits only add failure handling after first-agent publication and a test allocation); the device-code scenario ran on the previous head `709eae4`.

**Real local Gateway runs.** Built candidate (`pnpm build`), disposable loopback Gateways with private `OPENCLAW_HOME`/state/config, the real Control UI driven by Playwright Chromium, the real Codex CLI 0.170.0 with its existing ChatGPT login, and live model verification. All test state was deleted afterwards.

| Scenario | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh install, `?firstRun=auto`, Codex auto-detect | Detected the shared Codex login, ran a live verification turn, card showed “Using Codex (openai/gpt-6-astra)”. Config gained canonical `agents.entries.main` (name, workspace, agentDir) and the workspace was seeded with `BOOTSTRAP.md`. “Start talking to your agent” opened `/chat/main` with “Wake up, my friend!” focused and unsent (“No messages yet”). Only `openclaw.setup.auto` and `openclaw.setup.detect` were requested: no `sessions.create`, no `chat.send`. |
| Same install, reopened `?firstRun=auto` | Status `configured`; `openclaw.json` SHA-1 identical before and after (read-only). |
| Existing install: primary model in `agents.defaults`, no `agents.entries` | Status `configured`, no error, no config write (byte-identical), no workspace or `BOOTSTRAP.md` created. Handoff opened `/chat/main` with an empty composer. Before this change, the same shape triggered a live activation, config write and agent creation, and threw if the live check failed. |
| Fresh install, OpenAI device-code sign-in from Model Setup | Reached the provider step: the wizard showed the device code and approval link, and `openclaw.setup.auth.start` carried no first-agent flag. Approving the code needs the account owner and was not completed in this run, so the post-sign-in handoff is covered by the provider sign-in lifecycle tests below rather than a live sign-in. |

**Automated suites** (all on the candidate):

- Backend: `setup-inference-activate.test.ts` (44, including new first-Gateway / CLI / already-configured provisioning scenarios), `setup-inference-activate.native.test.ts` (6, host-only Codex activation: success, existing agent, consent rejection, probe failure, cancellation, application failure with rollback), `setup-inference-credentials.lifecycle.test.ts`, `system-agent-first-agent.test.ts` (6 read-only/fail-open handoff cases: implicit main, pending bootstrap, authored agent, utility, unknown agent, unreadable config), `system-agent-setup-auto.test.ts`, `system-agent.test.ts` (40) and the other `system-agent*`/`models-auth-login*` suites. `models-auth-login.catalog.integration.test.ts` times out identically on unmodified `main` on this host and is unrelated.
- UI: 742 files / 8,617 tests under `src/app`, `src/components`, `model-setup`, `custodian` and `model-providers`, including the ordinary-chat fallback for a ready connection without a handoff target and a saved-Ask-dock reload regression (red with the previous `setOpen(false)` on refresh, green now). Browser e2e `model-setup-automatic.e2e.test.ts`: 11/11.
- Post-publication failures: `setup-inference-activate.native.test.ts` includes `job-failure` (the default check-in job rejects) and `bookkeeping-failure` (agent provenance rejects after the config is published). Setup still succeeds with the agent created and bootstrap pending; the bookkeeping case fails without the fix.
- Linux/Windows desktop: Rust navigation tests updated for the Model Setup route; the native onboarding fixture builds with `vite.onboarding.config.ts`. `linux-app.yml` (Rust tests, native onboarding proof, Windows and macOS companion jobs) was dispatched on `8600ad8`: [run 44662821719](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44662821719), result pending at the time of writing.

prs.title: fix(exec): preserve explicit symlink-parent traversal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an explicitly configured POSIX executable can be missed or resolve to another file when its path follows a directory symlink and then `..`.

## User Impact

CLI backends and command resolution identify the executable the operating system will run for absolute, relative, home-expanded, and working-directory-relative paths with these components.

## Why This Change Was Made

Lexically collapsing `alias/..` before filesystem lookup changes its meaning when `alias` is a symlink. Preserve parent components at the shared path owner through executable lookup, ordinary script snapshots, approval preparation, rendering, and revalidation. Canonical OS identity stays separate from invocation spelling, so the command launched is the command whose identity was approved. Windows normalization and executable admission remain unchanged.

## Evidence

The original filesystem resolver regressions failed on the old implementation. A new real-file approval-to-launch regression also reproduced the review's reported defect: with both targets present, approval revalidation succeeded while the rendered shell command executed the lexical decoy; with only the physical target present, preparation or launch failed.

On merge commit `c7264a847`:
- Four owning/consumer files pass: 144 tests, 2 Windows skips; 15.13 seconds wrapper wall time. These cover executable lookup, command identity, ordinary script/approval binding, and reviewed shell rendering.
- The new cases prepare real approval bindings, render and execute the actual command through `/bin/sh`, observe the physical program's marker with and without a lexical decoy, then retarget the symlink and require revalidation to refuse it. Both cases also pass under explicit Node (2 selected tests, 9.26 seconds wrapper wall time); the owning run uses the current pinned Bun runtime.
- The existing real-Node cwd subprocess case now also reads an operand in a whitespace-only relative directory and separately checks the executable owner's unchanged blank-cwd fallback.
- Source-backed type-aware lint, changed-file formatting, whitespace, and the documented test-line budget pass. A unique allocation accounts for the 111 net regression lines; shared budget and CI rules are unchanged.
- Fresh independent review found no actionable findings. Main `3115c80e8` was integrated without rewriting the PR's existing commits.

Validation gaps: this real-file component chain does not establish a live Gateway/user-approval transport result. Native Windows execution, full production types, full build/test, and broader checks were not run on this merged head. Exact-head CI is pending.
