prs.title: fix(compaction): announce compaction before the pre-compaction memory flush
prs.body:
Closes #200270

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `agents.defaults.compaction.notifyUser: true`, the "🧹 Compacting context..." notice reaches the chat only after the pre-compaction memory flush. The flush is a full model turn; on a large local context it can take minutes (the reporter saw 5.5 minutes on a 244k-token transcript), and during it the chat shows nothing, so the session looks hung.

## User Impact

User impact: OpenClaw now sends the start notice before the memory flush begins, so `notifyUser` covers the whole maintenance window. As on `main`, each notice is awaited and a failed delivery is logged without stopping maintenance. If the flush refreshes the session's usage below the threshold, the existing "🧹 Compaction not needed" notice follows, except in the two accepted cases below (a latched byte limit, where the bounded-context warning is the closing notice; a cancelled turn, where nothing follows). Turns whose token compaction is handed to the native ChatGPT route's own boundary send no notice, as on `main` (that hand-over depends on the route, not the chat's size, so a notice there would repeat every turn). Without `notifyUser`, nothing changes.

The start notice goes out only after maintenance admission. Accepted edge cases: with a latched byte limit, the bounded-context warning is the closing notice after “Compacting context…”, as on `main`; no “Compaction not needed” follows; refused maintenance sends no compaction-start notice, though unrelated context warnings may still appear; queued web-chat turns keep `main`'s deferred compaction notices, so a memory-maintenance warning can appear there before “Compacting…”; the flush starts once the start notice is delivered, so a channel that hangs on delivery delays the flush, as it delays compaction on `main`; if the turn is cancelled during the flush, no closing notice follows the start notice, as on `main` for a cancelled compaction. The start notice is attempted once, before note-saving. Delivery failure is logged; maintenance continues without retrying the notice.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runSessionCompactionIfNeeded` awaited `beforeCompaction` (the memory checkpoint) and then replanned, and only the replan reached the start notice, just before the compactor. Now:

- `beforeCompaction` now receives an `announceStart` callback; its owner calls it after its own admission and before the flush (the reply path, right after `admitReplyMaintenance`; the agent command delivers no notices and does not call it). If the checkpoint or the replan after it fails once the start notice is out, the notice is settled as "Compaction incomplete" (not when the turn was cancelled: judged by the same combined signal the memory flush stops on, the run's abort signal plus the operator's authority, via `resolveFollowupAbortSignal`; the existing failed-compaction path uses the same check, which on `main` read the run's signal alone); the shared notifier never sends a terminal notice twice. The announce step is best effort: notice lookup or delivery failures do not prevent the memory checkpoint; slow delivery can delay it. The checkpoint still runs before the replan exactly as on `main`: without `notifyUser` the notice-only lookup is skipped (the reply path keeps its notice callback for mandatory warnings, so the setting itself is checked), and if that lookup throws (a provider parameter hook), the start notice is skipped and logged while the checkpoint runs. If compaction is still needed after the checkpoint, its existing provider check runs as on `main`. Unit cases cover both a checkpoint failure and a replan failure after a successful checkpoint (exactly one start and one incomplete notice). `announceStart` sends the start notice unless token compaction is handed to the ChatGPT boundary (`defersTokenCompactionToChatGPTBoundary`, which reads route metadata only), and the notice state carries into the replan, which does not send it again. The flush itself runs exactly as before. The callback type and the announce step live in `compaction-notice.ts`, so `agent-runner-memory.ts`, which is over its line cap, grows by one line (+32/−31); the line-cap check passes.
- A replan that ends without compacting reports "skipped" when a start notice was sent, unless the bounded-context warning already closed the run (latched byte limit).
- The notice bookkeeping (start sent, terminal sent, best-effort delivery) moves from a closure in `agent-runner-memory.ts` to `createCompactionNotifier` in `compaction-notice.ts`, the module that already owns these notices. As before, a start notice clears the terminal flag, so a failure after a bounded-context warning still reports "Compaction incomplete".

`docs/concepts/compaction.md` (Compaction notices) says "Compacting context..." is sent once maintenance is allowed and before the memory flush, that "Compaction not needed" follows when nothing is left to compact unless the chat has reached its transcript size limit (then the bounded-context warning is the last message), and where no notice is sent.

Not changed: notices still go through the existing queued notice path (`sendDirectCompactionNotice`, queued follow-up handling); only when the start notice is sent moved. Also not changed: when compaction or the memory flush run, notice texts, and the `context_bounded`, degraded and incomplete notices.

## Evidence

### Live run: full-product repro on `main` and the same run on this change

Built Gateway (`openclaw.mjs gateway run`, `main` `52b87b23676` and this change (`8a4626bbc93`), run 19 Nov) with the bundled `memory-core` plugin and `compaction.notifyUser: true`. The chat is a direct message on OpenClaw's `qa-channel` test channel (built with the private QA runtime, staged as QA Lab does); each outbound message carries the time it reached the channel. The session model is a local Responses server with a 64k window that reports request size as usage. Ten short messages build history; an eleventh long one pushes the session past the compaction threshold, so the memory flush runs as compaction's checkpoint. The server holds the flush turn (its prompt starts "Pre-compaction memory flush") for 20 seconds. Times are seconds from the reply to the tenth message; the eleventh message goes out right after it (the two runs reach that point at different times because Gateway startup differs).

`main`:

```
memory flush:                 0.5 → 20.5
"🧹 Compacting context..."   20.6   (after the flush)
compaction summary requests  21.0, then the reply at 21.4
```

This change:

```
"🧹 Compacting context..."    0.2   (before the flush)
memory flush:                 0.3 → 20.3
compaction summary requests  20.6, then the reply at 21.0
```

Proof artifice: the model is a scripted local server and the 20-second hold stands in for a slow flush on a large local model. The reporter's transcript was 244k tokens; this run uses a 64k window. The completion notice in both runs is the degraded-summary warning, because the scripted summary is short; that path is unchanged. Upgrade run: not applicable (no update, Doctor, config or state change).

### Tests

- `agent-runner-memory.compaction-notice.test.ts` (new, beside the other split-out preflight suites): the real `runSessionCompactionIfNeeded` with a memory checkpoint records the order of notices and checkpoint. When the checkpoint leaves compaction due: start, checkpoint, compaction, end. When it leaves nothing to compact: start, checkpoint, skipped. When token compaction is handed to the ChatGPT boundary: the checkpoint only, no notice. When the checkpoint fails after the notice: start, then incomplete. On the proof machine the first two cases fail on `main` (the checkpoint comes before the start notice; with nothing to compact `main` sends no notice) and all four pass here. Those `main` runs used the suite before the `announceStart` callback existed (17 Nov); the current table calls the callback, which `main` does not pass. Three existing tests that call the checkpoint by hand now pass a no-op `announceStart`.
- `reply-agent-turn-preparation.test.ts` › "announces compaction only after a scheduled turn's maintenance admission": the real preparation code, the real `admitReplyMaintenance` and the real `runSessionCompactionIfNeeded` (only the memory flush and model calls stubbed). Refused (a scheduled turn outside its active window): the admission check runs and nothing follows (no notice, no flush). Admitted: admission → start notice → flush → "skipped". (Without `notifyUser` the hand-over probe is never called; the preflight suite covers that with the notice callback installed.) Both cases fail on this PR's merge version, which announced before admission (`['notice start', 'admission']`).
- `agent-runner-memory.compaction-notice.test.ts` › "settles the start notice once when the replan after the memory checkpoint fails": checkpoint succeeds, the replan fails, and exactly one start and one incomplete notice appear. It fails on the previous revision, which settled only checkpoint failures (`['notice start', 'checkpoint']`).
- `agent-runner-memory.compaction-notice.test.ts` › "runs the memory checkpoint when notifyUser is off / the ChatGPT hand-over probe fails": with the notice callback still installed, the checkpoint runs in both cases, and with `notifyUser` off the notice-only lookup is never called. Both fail on the previous revision (the probe ran unconditionally and its error stopped the checkpoint).
- `agent-runner-memory.compaction-notice.test.ts` › "sends no incomplete notice when operator authority is withdrawn during the memory checkpoint / compactor": the start notice is sent, the operator's authority is withdrawn and the checkpoint (or, without a checkpoint, the compactor) stops; no "incomplete" follows. The compactor case reaches the existing failed-compaction path.
- Merged with `main` on 18 Nov (`52b87b23676`): #200714 turned the failed-compaction throw into `settleFailedPreflightCompaction`, which conflicted with this change's notice rename; the merge keeps both (the "incomplete" notice, then `main`'s settle step; a throw from it still finds the run ended, so no second notice).
- On the proof machine, on this change's code and tests: the new suite, `agent-runner-memory.test.ts`, `agent-runner-memory.{accounting,byte-preflight,byte-pressure,preflight-stale-tokens}.test.ts`, `reply-agent-turn-preparation.test.ts`, `src/agents/command/maintenance.test.ts`, `memory-flush.test.ts`, `queue.pending-inputs.test.ts` and `agent-runner-direct-runtime-config.test.ts` pass (11 files, 173 tests). `pnpm check:changed` passes on this head.
- Test lines are net +296 against `main`: one new suite of nine cases (sharing one setup helper) plus the admission case in the existing preparation suite, reusing the existing preflight fixtures (`createFlushSessionEntry`, `createModifiedMemoryFlushPlan`, `createTestFollowupRun`, `withTestModelContextTokens`) and the module mocks of the split-out preflight suites. The existing `agent-runner-memory.test.ts` already holds the checkpoint test but is over its line cap, so the case could not go there.

prs.title: fix: keep state intact when a live Gateway blocks reset
prs.body:
Closes #202023

## What Problem This Solves

When a foreground or externally supervised Gateway is still running, `openclaw reset --scope config+creds+sessions` can report that it cannot reset sessions but still delete the local config and credentials.

## User Impact

If the Gateway or another maintenance command owns the state, the combined reset now keeps config, credentials, and session history intact and asks the operator to stop the owner before retrying. Dry-run still previews the selected removals.

## Why This Change Was Made

The combined reset takes the existing exclusive lock before any removal and holds it through all three cleanup steps. Once admitted, a failure in one target does not block unrelated cleanup. File removal refuses a custom path that would delete the active lock.

## Evidence

- With an isolated foreground Gateway and a session created via RPC, the base command exited 1 but removed config and credentials. A fresh build of the candidate exited 1 and preserved both files byte-for-byte, retained the same session ID, and left the Gateway healthy. After the fixture Gateway exited, retry exited 0 and removed session history, config, and credentials while keeping the workspace. Dry-run previewed without removing anything. Only disposable fixture data was used.
- The patch applies cleanly to `main` at `a14344254e30`. The reset and lock-owner source is unchanged from the reproduced base. A build of the combined main-plus-patch tree was not run.
- The registered CLI regression failed on the base; the final eight reset, cleanup, onboarding, and uninstall suites passed (109 tests), including dry-run, independent failure, and custom OAuth lock-overlap coverage.
- Independent native review against `d5f3e4d7b75a` found two P2 custody issues. Both were corrected and re-reviewed on patch `ad82f7b8b814`; no material findings remained. The follow-up reviewed mid-operation custody loss statically but did not inject it at runtime.
- Focused typecheck, formatting, lint, and the mock-export ratchet passed. The one retired mock allowance was removed; the local aggregate check did not finish. The [exact-head CI aggregate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44627712431/job/135933025066) passed; the specialized [published-driver update job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44627712431/job/135926865009) was skipped.

**Sanitized terminal evidence (disposable foreground Gateway).** `verify:` lines are harness read-backs, not CLI text.

```text
$ openclaw reset --scope config+creds+sessions --yes --non-interactive
Before, Gateway running: exit 1
verify: config and credentials deleted; session and workspace retained; Gateway HTTP 200

After, Gateway running: exit 1 — Stop the Gateway and retry.
verify: config, credentials, and workspace byte-identical; same session ID; Gateway HTTP 200

After, with --dry-run: exit 0
verify: preview only; config, credentials, and session retained

After the fixture Gateway stopped, same reset: exit 0
verify: config, credentials, and session removed; workspace unchanged
```

**Latest-stable existing-data compatibility (official tag source → exact PR tree).** The official `v2026.11.6` tag (`06afb10d3272`) was built from its unchanged lockfile using the standard frozen install; supply-chain policy passed. That runtime used the real CLI and Gateway to set `gateway.reload.mode=off`, create a labeled session and persist a transcript note without model inference. We stopped it, then started the exact code tree published at `09546c85766a` on the same disposable profile. This was a runtime switch with standalone Doctor, not an npm-artifact install-over, `openclaw update`, or managed service test. The candidate source runner reports its base version `2026.11.5`; its source tree matches the PR exactly. No production state or real credentials were used.

```text
stable: config set gateway.reload.mode off                  exit 0
stable: sessions.create / chat.inject / chat.history        exit 0
stable: foreground Gateway stopped; listener closed
candidate: doctor --fix --non-interactive                   exit 0 (agent SQLite v38 -> v43)
candidate: config get gateway.reload.mode                    exit 0 (off)
candidate: offline sessions listing / live chat.history     exit 0
verify: original authored settings, session ID/label and full returned transcript preserved;
        synthetic credential and workspace files byte-identical
candidate: reset --scope config+creds+sessions --yes --non-interactive --dry-run   exit 0
verify: config/credentials/workspace bytes, session and transcript unchanged
candidate: reset --scope config+creds+sessions --yes --non-interactive while owned  exit 1
verify: same files, session and transcript unchanged; Gateway HTTP 200
candidate: same reset after stopping the fixture Gateway    exit 0
verify: config, credentials and session removed; workspace unchanged
```

Doctor did rewrite config: it added `agents.entries`, `skills`, `wizard`, and `meta.migrations.skillLibraryToolSplit`, and refreshed `meta.lastTouchedVersion`. No pre-existing authored setting changed. The byte-for-byte config assertions for dry-run and refusal compare against the post-Doctor snapshot. A direct offline read before Doctor refused the older schema as expected; nothing was reseeded during the successful source-to-source transition.

Contributor: Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm)  
Reported by Anmol (@anmol0b)

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2edc3159-c613-4611-ac1c-48d712e40c67)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/9ac47b47-a901-4432-9bce-8c67b4178b07)

## Worked on by

prs.title: fix: schedule Template automations in the adding device’s time zone
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Previously, a 9 AM Template automation could run at a different hour on the device that added it: the job used the Template’s declared time zone. Now, adding it from Los Angeles schedules it for **9 AM Los Angeles time**, even if the Gateway is in London. The cron expression stays unchanged; the job uses the adding client’s validated IANA time zone, falling back to the Template’s declared zone if the client supplies no valid zone. Interval schedules are unchanged.

The catalog and inline chat previews reflect the device-local schedule. In the automation dialog, the schedule subtitle now lines up beneath the automation name. Reviewed and direct adds, chat setup, and retries retain the selected zone; resuming from another device does not move an existing job.

[Compare the before-and-after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202175#issuecomment-7028141806).

## Evidence

Published head `2c7529bcf02c` and tested commit `4eb44d3037b6` have the same Git tree (`49f0ddbc2bd3`). 192 backend tests and 31 Chromium tests passed, as did `pnpm check:changed`. The repaired dialog crop had no changed pixels against the inspected candidate.

- **Before:** On base `d66f296eae1e`, both new regression cases expected `America/New_York` but got `UTC` (with `enabled: false` and with `enabled` omitted). Both pass on the repaired revision.
- **After, real Gateway Add:** A paired Los Angeles Chromium client added a Template declaring `Europe/Paris`. The reviewed plan selected Los Angeles. After apply, a separate Gateway query returned one paused job: `0 9 * * 1` in `America/Los_Angeles`. The fixture scripted the greeting, not the schedule.
- **Stable stored jobs:** OpenClaw 2026.11.6 created an enabled Paris job (`0 9 * * 1`) and a paused Tokyo job (`30 17 * * 5`). The candidate’s production scheduler loaded a read-only backup with both IDs, declaration keys, names, enabled flags, expressions, and zones unchanged.
- **Pending setups:** 2026.11.6 did not have these receipt fields. Pre-feature `main` wrote one `templateInitialization` and one `templateSetup` receipt, neither with a device zone. The candidate read the full contents unchanged (before/after SHA-256 prefixes `26462d217c96` and `6b8173f92c6b`). In a separate Gateway integration test, a Tokyo retry after a failed first turn retained the original New York setup instructions, including the instruction to preserve user-enabled jobs.

**Limits:** The stored-data checks were not a full in-place upgrade. The candidate identifies as 2026.11.5, so the in-place switch refused a downgrade; the disposable simulation stopped at migration because its clone lacked matching local client credentials. Neither safeguard was bypassed. The cross-device chat retry was tested at the Gateway boundary, not with a live model executing the setup.

prs.title: fix: give OpenClaw ID members their new access when their role is raised
prs.body:
Stacked on #201610 (base `openclaw/grand-lobster`).

## What Problem This Solves

When an owner raises an OpenClaw ID member's role (for example viewer → operator), a browser that member had already paired kept its old, narrower access. It reconnected right away but stayed at the old role. A hard refresh didn't help. Lowering a role worked; raising one didn't.

## User Impact

User impact: a member whose role is raised gets the new role's access the next time their browser reconnects, with no new device approval. This works whether the role was changed on **Access** (which revokes the browser's token) or with `users.setRole` (which doesn't). Lowering a role still takes effect on reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI reconnects asking for the scopes it saved under the earlier role. For an OpenClaw ID member, the Gateway granted only what was asked for, capped by the role. So a browser that saved viewer scopes could never ask for more, and the paired grant never grew.

With #201610, a member's access comes from their linked profile role, and connect-session applies that role as the ceiling. This PR makes the Gateway ignore a member browser's saved request. An OpenClaw ID member's Control UI/webchat connect now asks for every operator scope, still capped by any `x-openclaw-scopes` connection header. The existing member pairing lane widens a narrow paired grant (scope-upgrade or token reissue), and connect-session caps the connection to the member's **current** role. As a result, a member always connects with exactly its role's scopes.

The rewrite happens after the device signature is verified, and only when the connection is authenticated as an OpenClaw ID member through `trusted-proxy`. Owner devices, nodes, native apps, and other trusted-proxy, Tailscale and Cloudflare browsers are unchanged. When they ask for more than they hold, they still need approval.

Notes for reviewers:
- **Persisted grant.** A member browser's paired grant can now hold `operator.admin`. This matches what a fresh member pairing already stores on #201610, where the Control UI asks for its default set, which includes admin. The grant isn't authority for members: approval mints a new token that members never receive (member hellos carry no device token), tokens are bound to the tunnel peer, and every member connection, HTTP request and plugin route is capped by the current profile role.
- **Token revocation.** A role change on **Access** already revokes the member's bound tokens: `roleChangeDisconnects` emits a `disconnect` event, and `applyEvents` revokes `tokensBoundTo` those peers. `users.setRole` only disconnects. This PR handles both cases through the same-key lanes, so it doesn't add revocation.
- **No Control UI change.** `docs/gateway/protocol.md` says to keep a stored token's scopes when the hello returns the same token. Member hellos carry no device token, so persisting `hello.auth.scopes` wouldn't reach members anyway.
- **Hello scopes.** For a tunnel member, `hello.auth.scopes` is now the role's scopes, not whatever the client asked for. The scope matrix member row now expects `read`+`write` instead of an echoed `talk`. That's the same authority, because `operator.write` implies `operator.talk`.

## Evidence

Real Gateway tests in `src/gateway/server.auth.openclaw-id-tunnel.test.ts`. A member browser starts with a paired grant that matches its earlier role, as an older build approved it. Its role changes, and it reconnects twice the way the Control UI does, with its saved token and saved scopes:
- viewer → operator, token revoked (Access page): operator scopes, no pending approval. **Fails on the base** (got `operator.sessions.read`).
- viewer → operator, token kept (`users.setRole`): operator scopes, no pending approval. **Fails on the base.**
- operator → viewer, token revoked: only `operator.sessions.read`. Passes on both.

The non-member guards still pass unchanged:
- "a signed-out browser asking for more than it was approved still needs approval" (OpenClaw ID owner)
- "keeps a revoked token's same-access reconnect on the owner approval path" (ordinary trusted proxy)

<details><summary>Commands and results</summary>

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server.auth.openclaw-id-tunnel.test.ts src/gateway/server.openclaw-id-role-reload.test.ts src/gateway/server.operator-role-scope-matrix.test.ts src/gateway/server.auth.trusted-proxy-device-autoapprove.test.ts`: 4 files, 75 tests passed on the rebased head.
- Also passed: `server.openclaw-id-member-suspension`, `server.openclaw-id-session-invite`, `openclaw-id/remote-signout`, `ws-connection/connect-device-tokens`. `server.openclaw-id-rebind` is gated on id-e2e and was skipped.
- Base proof: with the `connect-device-pairing.ts` change reverted, the two raise rows fail and the lowering row passes.
- New tunnel test rows: about 0.1 s each. The tunnel file runs in about 33 s locally, most of it transform.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --staged`: all green except the dead-export scan. That scan flags `issueGatewayConnectDeviceTokens` in `connect-device-tokens.ts`, which this PR doesn't touch; the export comes from #201610.
- Autoreview (isolated subagent, read-only): no P0–P2 findings. Its one coverage note was that the first test version started from a broad grant. The test now seeds the narrow grant an earlier build approved.

</details>

prs.title: fix(gateway): recover-lock can clear the Linux legacy config lock that blocks Doctor maintenance
prs.body:
Related: #201472

Linux companion to #201912. #201912 lets macOS (like Windows since #182031) admit a stopped namespace-less legacy owner by itself and keeps Linux refusing on purpose, because a Gateway in another PID namespace can share the lock directory; its refusal on Linux tells the operator to remove the system-temp file by hand, because `recover-lock` does not inspect it. This PR makes `recover-lock` inspect that file on Linux, so the documented explicit recovery covers it. Rebased onto #201912 and narrowed to Linux; macOS and Windows behavior is #201912's and unchanged here.

This fixes the recovery route on a build that contains it. The issue's other ask, a route for an install already rolled back to 2026.11.4 (whose CLI has no `recover-lock`), stays open under the same issue for the maintainers.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on Linux, `openclaw doctor --fix` (and so every update, which runs Doctor) refuses maintenance when an older Gateway left a per-config lock file in a separate system temporary directory (`$TMPDIR/openclaw-<uid>/gateway.<hash>.lock`) with no process namespace, even though its process exited long ago; and `openclaw gateway recover-lock`, the documented way to clear a lock whose owner cannot be verified, never inspected that directory, so it reported "No Gateway lock or owner lease is present." Since #201912 the refusal for that file says to remove it by hand after checking the process has stopped on the host and in every container sharing the directory.

Scope: this fixes recovery wherever the fixed `recover-lock` command is available. An install already rolled back to 2026.11.4 has no `recover-lock` command, so how such an install obtains the fixed command (for example the updater running recovery from the candidate) remains unresolved and is left to the maintainers under #201472. When the service's temporary directory sits inside the state directory, the historical lock path is the same as the state-local config lock that `recover-lock` already inspects, and #201912's refusal already names `recover-lock` there; this change does nothing for that layout.

## User Impact

User impact: on Linux, an operator blocked by "Legacy Gateway lock ... still has a live or unverified owner" can run `openclaw gateway recover-lock` (as the Gateway service account, with the same `TMPDIR`), see that record listed, and clear it with the printed `--confirm <fingerprint>` command; Doctor and the update then complete. For that file, the Doctor refusal now names that command before #201912's manual delete, which stays as the fallback when `recover-lock` skips the file or is not installed; the instruction to check the host and every container sharing the directory first applies to both. Nothing is reclaimed automatically: a record without a namespace is still "unverified", and the confirmation is the operator's statement that its process has stopped. A verified live holder is still refused.

If the file cannot be inspected safely (not owned by the operator, writable by others, under a parent directory another user could replace, not a regular single-link file, or larger than 16 KiB), `recover-lock` names the file and the reason instead of reporting an empty inspection, a confirmation that had to skip it says so, and a confirmation with nothing eligible says that nothing was recovered.

macOS and Windows are unchanged: they admit a stopped namespace-less record once its heartbeat is older than 90 seconds (#182031, #201912), so `recover-lock` does not inspect a separate system-temp copy there and #201912's Doctor message stays as it is. Other platforms (FreeBSD and the like) are also left out; the inspection runs only on Linux.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor's maintenance admission checks the historical per-config lock under the system temporary directory, but lock recovery only observed the three state-local lock paths. Inspection now also observes that file on Linux, deduplicated when it is the same file as the state-local config lock; confirmation takes it first, so a failure to take custody of it leaves the state-local records untouched; and the Linux Doctor refusal for that file names the recovery command, as it already does for the state-local file. The ownership policy from #178076 is unchanged.

Because the file lives in a shared directory and confirmation deletes it, the checks are sized against what a wrong deletion could reach: the file and its directory must be owned by the current user and writable by nobody else (so the bytes shown are the operator's own record); the configured path's own components are checked first, and a symbolic link in it that another user controls is refused (it could redirect the lookup to a directory that passes every later check); the path is then resolved to its canonical form and every parent must be owned by the current user or root, and a parent writable by others must carry the sticky bit (otherwise another local user could rename a parent and redirect the confirmed path between inspection and confirmation); a symbolic link or directory that another account substitutes in the configured path is owned by that account, and the checks run again at confirmation, so it fails the owner test or the parent walk; that account cannot create components owned by the current user or root; the file is opened without following symlinks and without blocking (a FIFO cannot hang the command), must be a regular single-link file, and is read only up to the existing 16 KiB sidecar bound. Confirmation then re-verifies identity (device, inode, timestamps, size) and bytes before removal, as for the other lock files. POSIX ACL entries are not inspected; this is a known limit.

## Evidence

Full-product check through the shipped CLI (`openclaw.mjs` of a built tree, Linux container, root): the reporter's lock record (no `processNamespace`, exited PID, mtime 30 Sep 2026) at `/tmp/openclaw-0/gateway.<hash>.lock`, then `doctor --fix --non-interactive`, `gateway recover-lock`, `--json`, `--confirm`, Doctor again.

### Full-product repro on main

main `d9e2d8a89dd` (includes #201912), 19 Nov 2026 (the next main, `d5f3e4d7b75`, changes no file this PR touches):

```text
== 1 doctor --fix --non-interactive (with the legacy lock)
doctor rc=1
  Doctor could not enter maintenance. Legacy Gateway lock /tmp/openclaw-0/gateway.3518e90d.lock still has a live or unverified owner (PID 28). If that process has stopped on this host and in every container sharing this directory, remove that file as the Gateway service account. Stop the Gateway service and other OpenClaw processes using this state, then run openclaw doctor --fix from an independent shell.
== 2 gateway recover-lock (inspect)
recover-lock rc=0
  No Gateway lock or owner lease is present.
== 3 gateway recover-lock --json
  { "present": false, "holders": [], ... }
== 4 skipped: inspection listed no record to confirm
RESULT lock_after_recovery=present
== 5 doctor --fix --non-interactive again
doctor rc=1
```

### Live run with this PR

Same container recipe, same record, the patched build of this head on that main:

```text
== 1 doctor --fix --non-interactive (with the legacy lock)
doctor rc=1
  Doctor could not enter maintenance. Legacy Gateway lock /tmp/openclaw-0/gateway.3518e90d.lock still has a live or unverified owner (PID 28). If that process has stopped on this host and in every container sharing this directory, run `openclaw gateway recover-lock` as the Gateway service account with the same TMPDIR to inspect and explicitly recover it, or remove that file as the Gateway service account. Stop the Gateway service and other OpenClaw processes using this state, then run openclaw doctor --fix from an independent shell.
== 2 gateway recover-lock (inspect)
recover-lock rc=0
  /tmp/openclaw-0/gateway.3518e90d.lock: holder 28 at unknown host, last renewed 4327232 s ago. Stop the holder before retrying; if it has already stopped, run `openclaw gateway recover-lock` to inspect and explicitly recover the unchanged owner.
  Stop the recorded holder through its service manager or container first. If you have confirmed it stopped, recover exactly these unchanged records with:
  openclaw gateway recover-lock --confirm <fingerprint>
== 3 gateway recover-lock --json
  { "present": true, "holders": ["/tmp/openclaw-0/gateway.3518e90d.lock: holder 28 ..."], ... }
RESULT recover_lists_legacy=yes
== 4 gateway recover-lock --confirm <fingerprint>
rc=0
  Gateway lock recovery completed. Start the Gateway again.
RESULT lock_after_recovery=removed
== 5 doctor --fix --non-interactive again
doctor rc=0
```

Doctor still refuses before recovery (the owner stays unverifiable); the difference is that recovery now reaches the file and Doctor passes once it is gone.

Focused tests (`src/infra/gateway-lock-legacy.test.ts`, `src/infra/gateway-lock-recovery.test.ts`): the new cases fail on unpatched main (the "red" lane copies them there) and pass with the change under the node runtime. The direct consumers of the two changed modules (`gateway-lock-recovery.postgres.test.ts`, `doctor-health.legacy-update.test.ts`, `doctor-maintenance.interruption.process.test.ts`, `update-command-service-drain.test.ts`) pass. Typecheck, lint and format run through CI's own `check:changed` on the bench.

### Upgrade run from a real 2026.11.4 install (Linux container, user `node`)

`npm i -g openclaw@2026.11.4`, state initialized by `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`, a config marker set (`gateway.port 18799`), then the lock record above planted at `/tmp/openclaw-1000/gateway.5b681173.lock` (exited PID 273). The 2026.11.4 Doctor admits it (control). The candidate is this branch packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs`.

Phase A, the real updater with the lock present (`openclaw update --yes --tag <candidate.tgz>`): the candidate's Doctor refuses with the new message and the update rolls back to 2026.11.4, as on 2026.11.5 today; the install is back on 2026.11.4 and the config marker is intact. This is the unresolved part: a rolled-back install cannot run recovery by itself.

```text
✗ openclaw doctor (2.6s)
  Failing check doctor (doctor-failed): Doctor could not enter maintenance. Legacy Gateway lock [redacted-path]
  ... Legacy Gateway lock /tmp/openclaw-1000/gateway.5b681173.lock still has a live or unverified owner (PID 273). If that process has stopped on this host and in every container sharing this directory, run `openclaw gateway recover-lock` as the Gateway service account ... or remove that file as the Gateway service account.
⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: doctor-failed.
RESULT A version_after=OpenClaw 2026.11.4 (d843d6a) lock_present=yes
marker gateway.port = 18799
```

Phase B, the manual route (installing the candidate by hand, not through the updater): `npm i -g <candidate.tgz>`, then Doctor refuses with the hint, `recover-lock` lists the record and prints the confirm command, the confirm removes the file, Doctor exits 0, and the config marker and state database are intact.

```text
installed: OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (ead12fa)
doctor (lock present) rc=1
recover-lock: /tmp/openclaw-1000/gateway.5b681173.lock: holder 273 at unknown host, last renewed 4329492 s ago. ...
  openclaw gateway recover-lock --confirm <fingerprint>
confirm rc=0  Gateway lock recovery completed. Start the Gateway again.
RESULT B lock_after=removed
RESULT B doctor_after rc=0
marker gateway.port = 18799
```

Phase C, the real updater from the untouched 2026.11.4 state (restored from a copy taken before the lock was planted) once the file is gone: the update completes and the config marker is intact.

```text
installed: OpenClaw 2026.11.4 (d843d6a)
state restored to the 2026.11.4 copy; lock present: no
update rc=0
✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.11.5 (from 2026.11.4); 23 warnings need attention.
RESULT C version_after=OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (ead12fa)
marker gateway.port = 18799
```

The candidate labeled `ead12fa` is the bench's own commit of this head's patch on top of main `d5f3e4d7b75` (the same content as this head, which passed the CI-style `check:changed` run there; the full-product runs above use the same tree). A first attempt at phase C reinstalled 2026.11.4 on a state that phase B's candidate Doctor had already migrated, which 2026.11.4 refuses to open ("uses newer schema version 40; this build supports 22"); that was the test's mistake, so phase C restores the pre-B state.

Proof artifice: the lock record was written by a script (the reporter's own recipe) with an already-exited child process as the recorded owner; no Gateway was running in any run; the candidate was packed from this branch rather than published to npm.

Proof gap: the bun test runtime is not installed in the bench containers, so the bun run of the focused tests is left to PR CI. This improves the guidance shown by the new build only; Doctor's message in an install already rolled back to 2026.11.4 is unchanged.

Data model: no stored data or record format changes. The lock record is read as before; the only new stored effect is the removal of the inspected file after confirmation, which the recovery test suite covers for both the state-local and the historical layout.

Test lines are net +54 against `main`: the recovery layouts (system temp dir, state tmp dir, non-regular path, world-writable parent) are four rows of one new `it.each` in the existing recovery suite, and #201912's platform table additionally expects the recovery command on Linux; no existing test covers the historical path in recovery.

prs.title: test(prompt-cache): extend the prefix journey with cron, steer, overflow and a concurrent chat on five transports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The prefix-stability journey is the CI check for "every provider request in a chat extends the previous request byte for byte, except at declared rebuild points". It did not cover four triggers that run in production chats: a scheduled job that comes due in the chat, a user message steered into a running tool call, tool results that fill the window, and an unrelated chat that compacts while the target runs. It also ran on three transports only.

## Solution

- `test/prompt-cache-prefix-stability.test-support.ts` adds these steps:
  - **steer**: `chat.send` while the target run is in a foreground `exec` held for 3 s; the steered input must join the same run right after the tool result. The Gateway exposes no signal for the moment the run takes a queued steer, so this hold is timed (accepted edge: a very slow worker can turn the steer into a follow-up turn and fail the step). Checked and ruled out as signals: the steered message reaches `chat.history` only after the tool is released (never within 10 s of holding, and a 10 s hold turns the steer into a follow-up turn); its `pendingInputs` entry stays `queued` until consumed; the `message.queued` diagnostic from `embedded-agent-runner` does not fire for this path; the `followup-queue-steer` one fires about 40 ms after the send but before `injection.admit()` (`src/auto-reply/reply/queue/enqueue.ts`), so it marks acceptance, not the handoff to the run.
  - **cron**: `cron.add` with an `at` schedule 3 s ahead and `sessionTarget: session:<target>` (not `cron.run`, which skips the trigger). The step waits until `cron.runs` shows the settled run.
  - **tool-result overflow**: a second agent (`other`, exec only, 64k window) reads 24 x 8k tool results in one run, so the pre-request pressure check acts. The only allowed rebuild there is a compaction.
  - **concurrent chat**: `sessions.compact` on the other chat while the target is mid tool call; the target tool stays open until compaction returns, then the test releases it.
- The fake usage now follows the request size, so pressure checks see real occupancy.
- Fake transports move to `test/helpers/fake-model-transports.ts` and add Gemini and Bedrock (ported from an unreviewed local branch). New wrappers: `prompt-cache-prefix-stability.{google,bedrock}.e2e.test.ts`.
- The seeded randomized suite (`prompt-cache-prefix-randomized.*`, 15 turn kinds, seeds 1 and 2 in CI; seeds 1 and 4 for Chat Completions and 1 and 6 for Anthropic, so each file's default seeds hit its known breaks) is ported with two harness fixes:
  - **Second seed in a file could not start a run.** The subagent registry keeps runs in memory by session key after the Gateway closes. The second seed reused the session key, loaded the first seed's retained child from a deleted state dir and failed every turn with `Retained subagent payload is unavailable` (`subagent-registry-read-snapshot.ts:206`). Each seed now has its own session keys.
  - **A turn after a silent reply ran the wrong step.** Main drops a silent reply from replay, so the next request also carries the earlier `STEP-SILENT` marker. The fake now acts on the newest marker only (seeds 9 and 10 timed out waiting for a child that was never spawned).
- Breaks that main still has are listed per chat and transport (`KNOWN_BREAKS`, `KNOWN_TOOL_ADDITIONS`), each with its owner. **Entries expire:** every stability entry for the transport must match in the run, and every randomized entry must match in at least one seed of its file, so a landed fix fails the journey until its entry is removed. A known entry checks the **whole request**, not only its first difference: the tool addition must be the only change once the two tools are taken out; the cron merge and the sent tool-result trim must leave every other message unchanged (the trim keeps the original head and tail around its notice, which may itself be cut short); the silent-reply merge was already checked structurally. On the opt-out surface a tool-policy config change (`toolsChanged`, applied with `config.patch`) may replace the tools and system prompt, but its history must still only grow; on the default surface it must stay append-only. The new `web_fetch` membership must reach the provider. `test/prompt-cache-prefix-known-breaks.test.ts` holds negative controls (a known change plus a rewritten earlier message fails).
- **Every request is classified by its `session=` runtime line** (`requestSession`: the system prompt, or the first message where Chat Completions carries it). Only a request without one counts as a compaction summary; a request from an unexpected session fails the journey.
- **Default surface.** Both journeys run on the default tool surface (Tool Search on), where the invariant is defined. The fake provider calls a tool the request does not list through `dispatch_action`, as a model does, so subagent and inter-session steps work there. `prompt-cache-prefix-randomized.no-tool-search.e2e.test.ts` keeps an opt-out run (`tools.toolSearch: false`, Anthropic).
- **Cron-first chat (default surface).** A scheduled job runs as the first turn of a new chat, then the owner sends a turn there; both requests must carry identical tool declarations in order. Main adds `message` on the owner turn (13 -> 14 tools), so this is a known break owned by #201710. The check requires the growth: the cron request must not list `message`, the owner request must, and once `message` is taken out of the owner request only, the chat has no prefix break. The entry therefore fails on #201710 until it is removed.
- Each tool and image step of the randomized suite must deliver its result to the provider (read output, both parallel results, an image block), so a degraded step fails even when the prefix stays append-only. On Anthropic the signed thinking of the `thinkingTool` step (thinking text and `sig_N` signature) must reach the tool continuation request, which also proves that the request enabled thinking.

## Findings on main (product code not changed here)

| # | Where | First differing request / field | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | cron `session:<key>` job, every route | The cron reply reaches the model twice. The scheduled turn stores its own reply (context-eligible). Settlement then commits the same text as an `automation-result` row (`src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-automation.ts:231` -> `src/sessions/background-session-result.ts:135`), stored pending with `context_eligible=0` because the cron run is still active. The next request appends an `openclaw.background-result-placement` marker (`src/agents/sessions/background-result-placement.ts:85`) that places the pending row into model context after the next user turn. Anthropic and Responses: appended copy (`ok 14` at messages 41 and 44), invisible to an append-only check. Chat Completions and Gemini: the copy merges with the next tool-call message, so message 44 changes. | #201838 |
| 2 | Bedrock cron | `cron.add` refuses a provider that authenticates through the AWS SDK ("requires a stored inference account"). Intended behavior: the journey expects the refusal. | not a break |
| 3 | tool-result overflow, Gemini | other chat: `functionResponse.response.output` of results already sent is replaced by `[... N more characters truncated …]` (`truncate_tool_results_only`) | #199530 |
| 4 | randomized, opt-out surface only (`tools.toolSearch: false`) | after a switch to a second provider, a turn started by a subagent completion or an inter-session message adds `skills_read`, `skills_search` to the tool list. On the default surface (Tool Search on) the tool list stays identical, on main and on #201710. | designed exception of the opt-out surface (`docs/reference/prompt-caching.md`); no entry on the default surface |
| 6 | cron-first chat, stability journey | the owner turn after a scheduled first turn lists `message`, which the cron turn did not | #201710 (red on main without the entry; on 390da1c green without it and red with it) |
| 5 | randomized, Bedrock and Chat Completions | silent reply dropped from replay; the user turns around it merge. Chat Completions merges only user turns without a runtime-context carrier (system-prompt update notes, exec-wake and other host system turns, inter-session and subagent-completion inputs); Bedrock merges every adjacent user pair | Chat Completions: #201843. Bedrock: accepted gap (closed #201654, no production impact on our hosts) |
| 7 | randomized, Anthropic, default surface (Tool Search on) | after a `config.patch` reload (`toolsChanged`), a later ordinary turn rebuilds the prompt: skills added mid-session move into the system prompt's skill list, and the "System prompt update" messages (Tooling, Skills) that carried them as appended deltas drop out of the history. Seed 6: skills added at steps 9 and 12, the model switch at step 14 rebuilt without them (allowed: they arrive as deltas), the user turn at step 21 rebuilds. Lead: `refreshConfigReloadSkills` -> `refreshSkillsDiscovery` (reason `config-change`, `src/skills/runtime/refresh.ts:533`) -> `bumpSkillsSnapshotVersion`. The same seed passes when the step writes the config file instead of calling `config.patch`. The entry accepts only this: every added skill is named in a dropped Skills update, only prompt-update messages drop, nothing else changes, and at most one such rebuild per earlier reload. | #202150 |

Steer: no break on any transport.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **Advisor fork check dropped.** The randomized suite claimed to check that an Advisor fork shares the parent's prefix, but `forks=0` in every earlier run (including 14bdf8e and ad1cd95): the fake model answered the post-tool turn at once, the run ended, and the Advisor cancels its review at run end. Holding that reply up to 5 s made forks arrive (6-10 per seed), and the fork request then differed from the parent's next request on all five transports: tools (`skills_read`/`skills_search`, `web_fetch`), system prompt (AGENTS.md lines added by a workspace-edit step, the alternate model's identity line) and Bedrock image blocks. These may be real fork cache breaks; the check is removed here and the findings need their own investigation.
- **MCP-only cron allowlist** (#201710 journey J12): fixed by #201710 at d827cce (MCP tools sit in the deferred catalog, so an MCP-only cron keeps the pinned tool list). No journey here configures an MCP server, so there is no entry.
- Extra request params fields beyond system, tools and messages are not compared (review minor 4).
- The string vs single-text-block equivalence stays for every message: Anthropic documents string content as shorthand for one text block, and its cache markers sit on several of the newest user messages, so restricting the equivalence to the last message produced false breaks. Concurrent compaction of another chat: no break in the target on any transport.

## Evidence

All `ocx test` (vitest from source, real Gateway, fake provider endpoints).

- **Head bf13587:** stability 5/5 on five transports; randomized default seeds on every file (Anthropic 1,6; Chat Completions 1,4; the rest 1,2; opt-out 1,2): 12/12, each file's known breaks matched; unit negative controls (`prompt-cache-prefix-known-breaks.test.ts`) 6/6.
- **Anthropic seeds 1-10** (8bb4168, same matchers): 10/10; the skills-refresh entry matches from seed 6 on.
- **Full run on 5174647** (before the skills-refresh entry): randomized seeds 1-10 on five transports plus the opt-out variant and stability: 64/65, the one failure being finding 7. It reproduces, passes with the ad1cd95 test code, and passes when `toolsChanged` writes the config file instead of calling `config.patch`.
- **Known-break expiry:** the stability journey requires every entry for its transport to match; the randomized files require each entry to match in one of the file's default seeds (skipped when seeds or a journey are overridden, or when a seed did not finish).
- **Cron-first step** on bf13587 test code (stability journey; Bedrock refuses `cron.add` by design, so the step runs on four transports):

| Code | Entry | Result |
|---|---|---|
| main (this branch) | without | fails 4/4: the owner turn adds `message` |
| main (this branch) | with | passes 5/5 |
| #201710 390da1c | with | fails 4/4: the cron turn already lists `message`, so the entry has expired |
| #201710 390da1c | without | passes 5/5 |

- **Local ClawSweeper** (gpt-6.1-sol, normal speed) on bf13587: "patch is correct", 0 findings.
- **Gates:** `pnpm tsgo:test:root` pass, oxfmt/oxlint pass on changed files, `git diff --check`, test-lines ratchet pass (+1138 net, record of 738 in `config/test-lines-allocations/prompt-cache-invariant-journey.txt`: the owner asked for the randomized suite and the two new transports; reviews asked for whole-request known-break checks with negative controls, expiring entries and the narrowed skills-refresh entry).
- Wall time per file (local, 5 files in parallel): stability 50-90 s, randomized 60-95 s per seed. These are release-tier compositions; no cheaper layer proves cross-feature request bytes.

Known breaks (#1, #3-#7) are accepted structurally, each checking the whole request; nothing else is filtered.

prs.title: fix(doctor): quote literal-like agent ids in the restore command
prs.body:
Closes #202034

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor's restore hint prints `openclaw config set agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId <id>` with the ID unquoted. `config set` parses a bare value as JSON5, so valid IDs like `123`, `true`, or `null` become a number, boolean, or null and the schema rejects the write.

## User Impact

The printed restore command always writes a string. Literal-like agent IDs work without the user having to discover `--strict-json` or manual quoting, matching the WhatsApp doctor contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

- JSON-quote the agent ID and add `--strict-json`, so `config set` parses it as a string.
- Update the existing `ops` expectation and add a numeric-ID regression that runs the same non-interactive Doctor path.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-config-flow.session-store-owner.test.ts --maxWorkers=4` — 18/18 passed.
- Red-on-base: reverting only `doctor-session-store-owner.ts` makes the numeric-ID case fail (the note has no quoted `'"123"'` + `--strict-json`).
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; oxlint clean on both files.

### Shipped CLI trace (isolated profile)

```text
$ openclaw doctor
Doctor warnings:
  agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId is missing; ...
  "openclaw config set agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId '"123"' --strict-json".

# bare value is the bug path
$ openclaw config set agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId 123
rc=1  Config validation failed: agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId: Invalid input: expected string, received number

# the printed command works
$ openclaw config set agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId '"123"' --strict-json
rc=0  Updated agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId.
$ openclaw config get agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId --json
"123"

$ ... agentId true    -> rc=1 expected string, received boolean
$ ... agentId '"true"' --strict-json -> rc=0; get -> "true"
$ ... agentId null    -> rc=1 expected string, received null
$ ... agentId '"null"' --strict-json -> rc=0; get -> "null"
$ ... agentId ops     -> rc=0; get -> "ops"
```

### Latest-stable upgrade trace (config created by openclaw@2026.11.6)

```text
$ openclaw@2026.11.6 onboard ...          # isolated profile, config version 2026.11.6
$ (this head) openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive
Doctor complete.                           # agent schema 38 -> 43
$ (this head) openclaw doctor
Doctor warnings:
  agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId is missing; ...
  "openclaw config set agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId '"123"' --strict-json".

$ openclaw config get gateway.mode --json      -> "local"
$ openclaw config get agents.entries --json    -> {"123":{},"true":{},"null":{},"ops":{}}
$ openclaw config set agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId '"123"' --strict-json
rc=0  Updated agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId.
$ openclaw config get agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId --json -> "123"
$ openclaw config get gateway.mode --json      -> "local"
$ openclaw config get agents.entries --json    -> {"123":{},"true":{},"null":{},"ops":{}}
```

prs.title: feat: use Discord realtime voice on GA OpenAI models with a ChatGPT sign-in
prs.body:
Closes #202179

## What Problem This Solves

Someone signed in to OpenClaw with ChatGPT (no OpenAI Platform API key) cannot use Discord realtime voice on the GA models (`gpt-realtime-2.1`, `-2.1-mini`, `-2`). OpenAI is reported as "not configured", even though browser Talk already runs the same models on the same sign-in. Discord's default agent-proxy mode picks a GA model, so this blocks Discord voice for every OAuth-only install. Voice Call and Gateway relay hit the same limit.

## User Impact

OAuth-only installs can run Discord voice (and GA Voice Call / Gateway relay) on GA realtime models. Consult routing, wake names, barge-in, `silenceDurationMs` and `reasoningEffort` behave as they do with a Platform key. Installs with a Platform key are unchanged: the key still wins, and a configured but unavailable key still fails with the existing error instead of switching accounts.

## Why This Change Was Made

#115211 removed an earlier OAuth fallback because the realtime WebSocket then answered "realtime conversation requires API key auth". A live check on 2026-11-20 shows the socket now accepts a ChatGPT access token when the request carries `chatgpt-account-id` (evidence below).

The direct GA socket now resolves auth in one place: Platform auth first, then the ChatGPT OAuth profile only when no Platform source is configured. For OAuth it adds `chatgpt-account-id`, the same header the GPT-Live and browser-broker routes already send. Provider readiness (`isConfigured`) counts the OAuth profile for GA models on `api.openai.com` only. Custom `baseUrl` endpoints never receive the OAuth token, and GPT-Live keeps its own routes. If OpenAI rejects the OAuth token, the error says so instead of blaming an API key.

## Evidence

**1. Live OpenAI API with a ChatGPT sign-in (no Platform key), 2026-11-20.** Standalone probe; the token was never logged:

- `wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime?model=gpt-realtime-2.1`, no `call_id`, `Authorization: Bearer <ChatGPT access token>` + `chatgpt-account-id` + `originator: openclaw` → `101`, `session.created`, `session.updated`; a text turn returned audio and the transcript "The probe works."
- Discord-style session on the same socket. Server VAD (`create_response: false`, `interrupt_response: false`, `silence_duration_ms: 700`), `reasoning.effort: "low"`, the `openclaw_agent_consult` tool. The session echoed the settings as sent. Real speech ("What's on my calendar today?") was transcribed exactly. A forced `tool_choice` produced `openclaw_agent_consult({"question":"What's on my calendar today?"})`. After the tool result, the model said "You've got one thing today: a dentist appointment at 3 pm in Chatswood."
- `gpt-realtime-2.1-mini`: same results.

**2. Isolated e2e through the branch's real code.** Fresh `OPENCLAW_HOME`, a fixture ChatGPT OAuth profile in the auth store, Discord's agent-proxy provider resolution (`surface: "gateway-relay"`, `autoRespondToAudio: false`) and the real OpenAI bridge. Network went through `OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PROXY_URL` to a local mock of the realtime socket (TLS for `api.openai.com` from a throwaway CA). Mock log on the branch:

```
handshake  path=/v1/realtime?model=gpt-realtime-2.1  authorization="Bearer eyJhbG…"  chatgpt-account-id=acct-e2e-fixture  originator=openclaw
session.update  model=gpt-realtime-2.1 reasoning={effort:low} turn_detection={server_vad, silence_duration_ms:650, create_response:false, interrupt_response:true} tools=[openclaw_agent_consult]
input audio → transcript "What's on my calendar today?"
response.create tool_choice={type:function,name:openclaw_agent_consult} → tool call → function_call_output → spoken answer
driver: {"step":"result","toolCall":{"name":"openclaw_agent_consult",...},"assistantTranscript":"You have one event today: a dentist appointment at 3 pm.","audioBytes":9600,"ok":true}
```

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Branch, OAuth profile only | provider resolves to `openai`/`gpt-realtime-2.1`; OAuth bearer + `chatgpt-account-id`; full consult turn ✅ |
| Branch, Platform key + OAuth profile | Platform key sent, no `chatgpt-account-id`; full consult turn ✅ |
| `main`, OAuth profile only | `Error: Realtime voice provider "openai" is not configured` (the reported failure) ❌ |

**3. Tests**

- New `realtime-voice-bridge-oauth.test.ts` (8 cases): OAuth connect with account header and full session policy; Platform first; configured-but-unavailable key keeps the existing error; neither credential names both; no OAuth for a custom endpoint or GPT-Live (readiness and connect); rejected sign-in message.
- On `main` with the new tests: 3 of 8 fail (OAuth connect, combined error, rejected sign-in message). The other 5 pass on `main` by design: they guard existing behavior. `realtime-voice-provider-routing.test.ts` expected GA readiness to refuse OAuth and now expects it to count; it fails on `main`.
- Branch: `realtime-voice-bridge-oauth`, `realtime-voice-browser-auth`, `realtime-voice-bridge-connection` 63/63 ✅; `realtime-voice-provider-routing` 19/19 ✅.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` ✅, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` ✅, oxlint `extensions/openai` ✅ (212 files), `run-format --check` ✅, `git diff --check` ✅, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` ✅ (+213, allowance 400).

**Gaps:** No live run against a real Discord voice channel; the e2e drives Discord's provider resolution and bridge parameters, not the Discord voice manager. The full `pnpm test:extension openai` suite was not run locally. Live coverage is `gpt-realtime-2.1` and `-mini`, not `gpt-realtime-2`.

Simplify pass: one auth resolver for the direct socket (`requireOpenAIRealtimeSocketAuth`), reusing the existing ChatGPT subscription resolver and Platform resolver; no new transport. Production +96/−24 lines in 3 files, tests +214/−1, docs +26/−14.

AI-assisted: yes. The author reviewed the code, tests, docs and evidence.

## What Problem This Solves

After onboarding with a named profile, the skipped-service and skipped-AI next steps print bare commands. Copying those commands into a shell without an exported profile can select the default installation instead of the one just configured.

Bare commands already work when the shell exports OPENCLAW_PROFILE. This change preserves that behavior and makes the printed commands self-contained.

Onboarding includes the selected profile in its foreground Gateway command and the skipped-AI commands for onboarding, channels, and dashboard. Default-profile output stays unchanged. Use the existing formatCliCommand owner rather than constructing profile flags manually. Both skipped-AI branches pass formatted commands into the existing English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese translations. The explicit skipped-service message uses the same formatter.

The patch is limited to these next steps, not a CLI-wide wording sweep. The separate skipped-AI closing-headline change is not included and is not a dependency.

No source change or test rerun was needed for this review outcome. prs.title: fix: stop automations posting a bare "Tool Call failed" after repeating their result
prs.body:
Closes #202140

## What Problem This Solves

Sometimes an automation records its result through Tool Search, then records the same result again. When that happens, the run posts a standalone `⚠️ Tool Call failed` bubble to the chat. Nothing actually failed, because the first result was saved. But the bubble doesn't name a tool or give a reason, so people can't tell whether something broke.

## User Impact

User impact:

- If an automation records the same result twice, the run stays quiet as intended.
- Tool failures called through Tool Search now name the real tool, for example `⚠️ Automations failed`, not the generic `Tool Call`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Repeating the result is now accepted.** Calling `record_result` again with the same outcome and summary returns the result that was already accepted. Recording a *different* second result is still rejected.
- **Warnings name the real tool.** The failure summary now keeps the name of the tool the dispatcher called. The no-reply warning uses that name, the same way Tool Search chat rows already do (#163829, #165095).
- **What stays the same:** the identity used for running tools and for recovery is unchanged. Interactive turns still show genuine failure notices.

How this was introduced:

- #137775 made the no-reply `⚠️ <tool> failed` warning unconditional.
- #163829 and #165095 changed chat rows to show the called tool instead of the dispatcher. They left the warning using the dispatcher label, which dates back to the original Tool Search work (#79823) and was kept in the rename to `dispatch_action` (#169552).
- #186652 deliberately keeps the warning for `no_change` runs. That is why the duplicate reached an unattended run.

prs.title: feat(macos): one provider list and in-page sign-in on Connect your AI
prs.body:
Fixes #201267

## What Problem This Solves

On main, the "Connect your AI" page of Mac onboarding lists recommended installs, local model servers, sign-ins and API keys as separate technical sections, and the ChatGPT sign-in ("Codex login (browser)") sits under "More sign-in options". Picking it opens a sheet with an "OpenAI Codex OAuth" note about redirect URLs and localhost:1455, then asks to "Paste the authorization code (or full redirect URL)". A failed sign-in names "Codex login (browser)".

## User Impact

Only the "Connect your AI" page and the ChatGPT sign-in wording change. Welcome, "Where should your assistant run?", "Getting things ready", "Reach it from anywhere" and the final page are the same as on main.

- **One list:** ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, API key and "A model on your own computer", plus More providers for every other option. Logins the Gateway finds are tagged "On this Mac" (or "On your Gateway" when the Gateway runs elsewhere) and are only tested when picked.
- **The picked provider's card replaces the list:** its sign-in steps, key form or live check show on their own, in the page instead of a sheet. "Choose another AI" goes back to the list, and so does canceling a sign-in.
- **ChatGPT sign-in:** picking ChatGPT opens the browser sign-in straight away, with no OAuth note. If the browser can't hand the sign-in back, the card asks in plain words for the address from the browser's address bar: right away when OpenClaw can't receive the sign-in, otherwise after 60 seconds instead of 15. The terminal sign-in (`openclaw models auth login`) gets the same text.
- **Failures name the provider picked:** a failed ChatGPT sign-in says "ChatGPT couldn't complete the test" and marks the card "Not connected".
- The setup mascot shows plain dark eyes; the teal highlights glare at that size.

Existing installs don't see onboarding again. The Gateway has no Google account sign-in for setup, so the Gemini entry asks for a Gemini API key.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page flow stays as on main and only the presentation of "Connect your AI" changes, in line with #200272. The picker groups the Gateway's existing detection, sign-in options and verification into rows; the Gateway still decides what is available and tests every connection. The ChatGPT wording lives in the OpenAI plugin's sign-in flow, which the terminal and the app's setup screens share.

## Evidence

Two app builds on a fresh macOS VM, the same steps in each: Welcome, Next, "On this Mac", Next, then "Connect your AI".

- **After:** this PR's head (`603cee2b93a`).

prs.title: fix: skip memory advice for missing workspaces
prs.body:
Closes #201991

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor tells an agent to install a memory system even when that agent's workspace directory does not exist. This makes a missing workspace look like an existing workspace that merely lacks memory guidance.

## User Impact

Doctor skips memory advice for a missing workspace, while retaining it for an existing empty workspace. No workspace is created by this check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared memory-advice predicate now checks for workspace existence through the existing filesystem helper before inspecting its contents. The helper preserves non-ENOENT errors and follows directory symlinks; the same predicate serves terminal and structured workspace suggestions. No existing machinery was removed: the change adds 3 production lines and 29 test lines.

## Evidence

An isolated `openclaw doctor --non-interactive --no-color` run with synthetic multi-agent state reproduced the misleading advice before the fix and no longer showed it afterward. Both runs exited 0, kept the existing-empty-workspace control, and left the missing directory absent. Selected terminal output, with unrelated lines omitted:

```text
BEFORE
Agent "main": Memory system not found in workspace.
Agent "missing": Memory system not found in workspace.
Doctor complete.

AFTER
Agent "main": Memory system not found in workspace.
Doctor complete.
missing_created=false
```

The last line is a separate filesystem check, not Doctor output. Runs used Node 26.12.1, an isolated HOME, config and state, and an available local port. The tested tree `085eea13a065f56358dc18db4f604ba041283a17` matches the PR head tree.

- The new collector regression failed on the unpatched base and passed after the fix. It checks missing, existing empty, symlinked and existing-memory workspaces.
- Four focused test files passed 117 tests. After a test-only collection change for TypeScript compatibility, the changed test file was rerun: 17/17 passed.
- Core typecheck, the `commands-doctor` test typecheck, targeted lint and formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. `build:runtime` passed on the base, and the post-fix CLI run rebuilt the runtime.
- The full test-typecheck was not rerun after fixing a test-only TypeScript lib incompatibility; the targeted test typecheck passed.

<details>
<summary>Validation commands</summary>

```sh
pnpm openclaw doctor --non-interactive --no-color
pnpm test src/commands/doctor-workspace.test.ts src/flows/doctor-workspace-suggestions.test.ts src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts src/flows/doctor-health.update-scope.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test src/commands/doctor-workspace.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm tsgo:core
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.commands-doctor.json
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts src/commands/doctor-workspace.test.ts
node scripts/run-format.mts --check src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts src/commands/doctor-workspace.test.ts
git diff --check
```

</details>

### Live proof: installed stable to installed PR build, same state

In an isolated HOME, npm prefix, config and state directory, installed the official latest stable package `2026.11.6 (06afb10)`, started its local Gateway, and ran Doctor. After stopping that Gateway, installed a self-contained package built from the PR tree into the **same npm prefix**, restarted the Gateway against the **same state**, and ran Doctor again. Both Gateways were healthy and both Doctor commands exited 0.

Selected, redacted output (unrelated lines omitted):

```text
BEFORE: official stable 2026.11.6 (06afb10)
Gateway health: ok=true
Agent "main": Memory system not found in workspace.
Agent "missing": Memory system not found in workspace.
Doctor complete. (exit 0)

AFTER: installed PR build 2026.11.5 (5b6431a)
Gateway health: ok=true
Agent "main": Memory system not found in workspace.
Doctor complete. (exit 0)
missing workspace created: false
```

The health and missing-directory lines summarize separate checks, not Doctor output. The two synthetic agent IDs and selected system-agent setting were unchanged. SHA-256 hashes of two synthetic workspace/state files matched, and the SQLite `quick_check` result was `ok` both before and after. This verifies those specific fields and files, not every config field or database row. Both isolated Gateways were stopped after testing.

The package was produced with `node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --allow-unreleased-changelog --output-dir <isolated-output>`; its repository tarball integrity validation passed. Both installs used `npm install --prefix <isolated-prefix> --no-audit --no-fund`, first with `openclaw@2026.11.6` and then with the generated PR tarball. Gateway and Doctor ran from that prefix. The tested PR source tree `085eea13a065f56358dc18db4f604ba041283a17` matches the current PR head `e7035d3d490a8abd289a495f0fe12133becb0eed` tree.

**Upgrade-proof limitation:** This is a real package installation replacement with retained state, not a normal semantic-version upgrade: the PR build identifies as `2026.11.5`, lower than latest stable `2026.11.6`, and their histories diverge. OpenClaw's automatic updater was not exercised. The test used synthetic local data and a local Gateway, not a real user session or external model. Whether this installation transition satisfies the requested latest-stable upgrade gate remains for review.

## What Problem This Solves

Settings has no written rule for where a control belongs, so each page grows its own mix of preferences, forms and status.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Contributors get one rule set for placing Settings controls.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reorganization only moves, groups, renames, removes duplicates and states scope. It adds no new controls or data and changes no config keys.

Scope of this PR:

- Add the organization rules to `ui/docs/design-system/settings-design.md`: user task first, one owner per setting, scope stated on each page, sidebar as the scarce resource.
- Closed scope vocabulary: This browser only, This device only, You on all devices, This agent, Whole Gateway.
- Forms keep today's titles (internal section names never appear), stay complete and never split across pages; when a form mixes subjects it stays where it is.
- Hubs: an entry whose tabs are existing pages, with their URLs kept.

## Evidence

None yet. Before/after screenshots, Control UI e2e and checks come before this leaves draft.

<details><summary>Series</summary>

1. **this PR** docs(ui): document how Settings pages are organized
2. #199797 improve(ui): send old Settings links to the new home of each moved block
3. #199798 ~~improve(ui): Settings forms stop repeating fields that have their own control~~ (cancelled)
4. #199799 improve(ui): remove the repeated Small model selector and stale meeting readouts
5. #199800 improve(ui): Agents links to other pages instead of repeating them as tabs
6. #199801 feat(ui): add a General Settings page and open Settings there
7. #199802 improve(macos): open Settings on General
8. #199803 ~~improve(ui): move Customize UI from Plugins to Appearance~~ (cancelled)
9. #199805 improve(ui): gather command rules, device binding and approval forwarding in Approvals
10. #199806 improve(ui): move agent GitHub accounts to All agents
11. #199807 improve(ui): group installed agents and session sources as External agents in Models
12. #199808 improve(ui): rename Search to Web and add the agent browser settings
13. #199809 feat(ui): add a Webhooks Settings page
14. #199810 improve(ui): move ACP and Node Host forms to Advanced
15. #199811 improve(ui): show Infrastructure as one page with storage, Gateway and Discovery
16. #199812 improve(ui): turn Talk into Voice with spoken replies and meetings
17. #199813 feat(ui): Settings hubs, starting with Privacy & security and Secrets
18. #199814 improve(ui): Advanced hub with config file, Logs, Debug and Labs
19. #199815 improve(ui): Plugins hub with Plugins, Skills and MCP
20. #199816 improve(ui): Devices hub with Paired and Cloud
21. #199817 improve(ui): Gateway hub with Overview and Server
22. #199818 improve(ui): Channels hub with channels, routing, messages, sessions and commands
23. #199819 improve(ui): list Agents & Tools before Connections in Settings
24. #199820 improve(ui): state the scope on every Settings page

</details>
