prs.body:
## Summary

Recovered the missing focused Goal 24 execution evidence without running contributor code on a credentialed operator host, modifying the product branches, or touching main.

Temporary proof-only workflow on `proof/goal24-secretless-20261115`, explicitly authorized by @RomneyDa on November 15, 2026, including billed macOS execution. No merge, backport, release, or main-branch mutation is requested. This draft is an evidence carrier, not intended to merge.

## Verified product proof

### History — PASS

PR #198091, source `eb919fb0d0b19dfa86c3e7055145b5a83ae27ef9`; tooling `c95caafe0fc52d86bdae05ebba9515085a300b3d`.

[Hosted run 43768728614](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43768728614/job/132979610910): 6 transcript recent-text tests and 5 inbound-context tests passed. Includes all physical-row boundaries, oversized-user barriers, shared 64 MiB budget, and the replay-suppression-after-restart regression. JSON reports prove selected test execution.

### Prefix stability — PASS

The earlier 11 history tests do **not** cover `src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`. The focused correction at tooling `9838c5239d071ab5845c061da812f2aa76f1db5c` runs that entire suite against the same immutable PR #198091 source `eb919fb0d0b19dfa86c3e7055145b5a83ae27ef9`, requiring all 14 cases and the completion-handoff authority regression. Zero or partial execution is rejected.

[Hosted run 43771398337, history job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43771398337/job/132987885912) passed: all **14 prefix-stability assertions**, 6 recent-text tests, and 5 inbound-context tests (25 total). The downloaded JSON reports and summary agree on the exact source/tooling SHAs above, with every assertion passed. Prefix cases cover browser/CLI/ACP wakes and recovery, GitHub catalog stability, completion/scheduled/message definitions, wake-screen gating, and completion-handoff authority. Ubuntu 24.04 x64, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0. This is focused suite evidence, not a real-model end-to-end claim.

Correction validation: 10 synthetic driver/preflight cases pass, including prefix-zero and partial-suite rejection. Against the prior driver, the new selection/zero/partial checks fail as expected (7 pass, 3 fail); this is harness regression proof, not product base-red evidence. Targeted lint/format, workflow validation, and 1,416 workflow/native-launcher regression tests pass. Initial workflow validation hit an empty-token environment error; rerunning with those empty variables removed passed.

Fresh native independent review of the exact correction from `a493a0599f16ed151dc8c773f280d9f8c349e7c0` to `9838c5239d071ab5845c061da812f2aa76f1db5c` found no P0–P2 findings. Reviewed diff SHA-256: `28b466d8d024083d844ab23859180ab6441370b42f54ac4c34edf06d5d818cf3`. This is the explicit native fallback, not an autoreview/ClawSweeper result; the configured autoreview service credit failure remains unresolved, and no model or service route was switched.

### Audio — converter regression PASS; shipped delivery remains unproven

PR #198525, source `a9a084486e3df10193dfa9ac5ab9faa9f53a4619`; initial tooling `c95caafe0fc52d86bdae05ebba9515085a300b3d`.

[Hosted run 43768728614](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43768728614/job/132979610823): both focused budget cases passed. The exact timeout-removal mutation failed both cases, including the expected `[5000, 5000, 5000]` versus `[5000, 2000, 1000]` assertion. This is mutation evidence, not a base-red claim.

Real unmocked FFmpeg 9.0.2 → afconvert → afinfo control proof passed on macOS 27.0.1 arm64: a two-second synthetic MP3 converted to mono 24 kHz CAF, exactly 48,000 valid frames versus 48,000 independently decoded PCM frames; tiny exhausted-budget rejection and scratch cleanup verified. This control did not reproduce the original segmented-MP3 truncation. Tiny-budget proof does not claim subprocess termination. The production temp resolver selected its standard root outside isolated TMPDIR; both roots were checked for leftovers.

#### Original ten-segment regression — independently reproduced and repaired

[Hosted run 43772299539, audio job 132990706530](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43772299539/job/132990706530) passed on November 15, 2026, using tooling `d43289d7095dadf3c3adc9c41792281cb1e67a12`, the same pinned product head, macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, and FFmpeg 9.0.2. The job took 5m58s.

The exact committed synthetic fixture is 166,176 bytes, SHA-256 `7b2d8a3b1244383a4cfc3beaa57ba756c0d76c7d485fa80f927a458bdb60c0f0`. It contains ten independently encoded mathematical-tone segments; no private/user audio or provider call was used.

| Measurement | Independently decoded mono 24 kHz PCM | afinfo valid frames |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source MP3 | 1,153,775 frames / 48.073958 s | n/a |
| Original converter | 79,440 frames / 3.310000 s | 79,200 |
| Fixed converter | 1,154,088 frames / 48.087000 s | 1,153,775 |

The baseline is the unchanged production converter module from pre-fix commit `e80a6dd9fdb4c7ce724472dd5d1b216afb4e70a7`, SHA-256 `867e5fd7ad1b477b1f4ab1023e15d440873c6f9d3d98253bfa6ac4240f6b370d`, loaded alongside the fixed checkout's unchanged runtime dependencies. Only the converter, two tests, and fixture differ between that pre-fix commit and the product head. This is causal original-module red/fixed-module green proof, not a full baseline package build: original conversion succeeded, then the preservation assertion failed specifically on decoded frame loss; the fixed module passed. No helper or codec was mocked.

Fixed output differs by 313 decoded frames (13.042 ms), within the 480-frame Opus-padding allowance. Independent frequency checks at all ten segment centers matched 440, 477, 514, 551, 588, 625, 662, 699, 736, and 773 Hz, with non-silent energy. These samples establish segment presence/identity, not whole-waveform or speech-semantic equivalence. Fixed conversion took 731 ms inside the existing five-second budget. Both variants left no conversion workspaces in the product temp root or isolated TMPDIR.

Downloaded summary and separate native logs agree on the source/tooling/fixture identities and exit statuses (baseline 1, fixed 0). The receipt gate rejects missing/duplicate cases, setup failures mistaken for baseline red, incomplete segment proof, and missing cleanup. Earlier budget/mutation/control proof was retained, not rerun.

**Distinct unfulfilled gates:** no installed-package TTS delivery, Messages transport, receiving-device playback, or shipped missing-FFmpeg/original-attachment fallback was exercised. No paired external device is available to this session (`nodes.list()` returned none). The converter result does not satisfy these gates and makes no overall readiness/merge claim.

### macOS permissions — candidate PASS; causal callback failure reproduced

PR #198869, source `77ee3e8424d789b7bad5804a9dc5a1693f34c91e`; tooling `a493a0599f16ed151dc8c773f280d9f8c349e7c0`.

[Hosted run 43769449537](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43769449537/job/132981863979): app/tests compiled; all 10 PermissionManagerTests passed. Retained Swift Testing events prove discovery, start, and completion of `speech authorization completion can enter from a background queue`. Xcode 27.1 / Swift 6.4 / macOS 27.0.1. This is candidate-only regression coverage, not by itself causal base-red/fix-green evidence or interactive signed-app TCC behavior.

The initial permissions job stopped at an overly exact Swift 6.3 preflight on the supported newer Swift 6.4 image, before building or executing tests. The repair enforces the Package.swift minimum (6.3+) and accurately classifies setup failures. Only the missing permissions job was run again; the passing history/audio results were retained. The next history-only matrix collected the missing prefix-stability proof. At that stage, the matrix ran only the newly added segmented-audio comparison; completed history, permissions, and audio-budget proof were not repeated.

#### Off-main callback causal proof — collected November 16, 2026

Final proof head: `9325008d1f891d8539c6ec0155e6388cacf3c95f`. Product code was not changed by this proof: candidate `77ee3e8424d789b7bad5804a9dc5a1693f34c91e` and full baseline `2f4ae4d3284bf17ad4930cf6770dac14c025bfc1` differ only in PermissionManager.swift and its original tests.

The same added Swift test, `Goal24SpeechFrameworkBoundaryTests.offMainFrameworkCompletion`, is explicitly **transplanted into both immutable checkouts**. It calls the real `PermissionManager.ensure([.speechRecognition], interactive: true)`. An Objective-C fixture intercepts only Speech authorization status/request selectors, dispatches the framework's actual received completion on a global queue, and records exactly one off-main invocation. No Swift production method, package setting, or actor-checking flag is patched. The candidate must return an authorized result, resume on MainActor, and report one request.

| Native execution | Product / tooling | Observed result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Candidate, run 43783553823 / job 133026037240](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43783553823/job/133026037240) | candidate above / `924b7db5b02bcd42305bcbe3e7f34ed9dc2bdd4d` | Build passed; exactly one selected function started/completed; off-main marker once; test passed in 0.012 s; native launcher exit 0. |
| [Initial baseline, same run / job 133026037588](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43783553823/job/133026037588) | baseline above / same tooling | Build passed; same test started; marker once; Signal 5; no completion; launcher exit 1. The job remained red because Swift's crash helper could not produce the required stack. |
| [Baseline stack diagnostic, run 43786255830 / job 133034441205](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43786255830/job/133034441205) | baseline above / final tooling above | Build passed; one start, zero completions, marker once; actual SIGTRAP captured; launcher exit 1; strict expected-failure gate passed with executor and original production callback frames. |

The collected crashing-thread stack is: `_dispatch_assert_queue_fail` → `dispatch_assert_queue` → `_swift_task_checkIsolatedSwift` → `swift_task_isCurrentExecutorWithFlagsImpl` → the original `PermissionManager.ensureSpeechRecognition` authorization callback → Speech block bridge → fixture's background dispatch block. This is the required callback-entry actor-isolation failure, not a compilation, setup, or zero-selection failure. The fixture's diagnostic SIGTRAP handler records an actual signal and exits 133; it never raises one. SwiftPM/launcher reports exit 1. Candidate execution was retained, not repeated for this diagnostic.

**Environment qualification:** the paired candidate/initial-baseline jobs both used macOS 27.0.1 arm64. The later hosted baseline diagnostic image had advanced to macOS 27.2 arm64; Xcode 27.1 (27A9275), Swift 6.4 (swiftlang-6.4.0.34.1), Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0 were unchanged. The final stack is therefore a cross-image corroboration of the earlier same-image differential, not a claim of same-image stack capture. Both variants' Swift test SHA-256 is `07670b386db7e63744294bfe64193bc2f8a496fc2c78f01c0e73bddcb0159352`. The Objective-C fixture changed only to add diagnostic signal capture; its hashes are `5e2d8fd2ca8a7f26ac5af7376a6bd050c8fdc5a70ba6b2dbdedb47156ef4eec7` before and `6dc25ce0a5952fa911d0f1303f76baf865b7365c9e5738a27fa28cf6fcc37746` after.

Earlier [Swift-seam control run 43780908432](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43780908432) did **not reproduce**: both variants executed one function and passed. Its initial event gate counted suite and function events together. Corrected local replay identified candidate success and control nonreproduction; no macOS rerun was spent on that parser correction. [Compiler-only run 43782722861 / job 133023349215](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43782722861/job/133023349215) then showed why: the extracted original imported callback has an executor-entry check, unlike the mutated Swift seam. That compiler probe is supporting diagnosis, not exact candidate SIL or runtime proof.

Fresh independent native reviews found no P0–P2 findings: boundary delta SHA-256 `1b697abfba74f7df7ac3d29bd911b8f2a9e6d61e6a983b5521d58092f371e48a`; diagnostic delta `014b0c31ffc0f59fb35c12cef7fc38ec1f511b7e84571b0bf2964f04b2b1cb5f`. Final synthetic gate checks: 26/26 pass, including Signal 5 and rejection of missing/wrong stacks. Targeted lint/format, workflow validation, and 8 files / 1,416 native-workflow guard tests passed (217.82 s wrapper). Retained artifacts were replayed through the final strict gate: candidate pass and expected baseline failure both accepted.

**Limitations:** this is causal native production-callback proof with synthetic OS responses. It does not exercise a signed app's interactive first grant, denial/regrant, Settings navigation, TCC persistence, or a real user's device. Those external gates remain unfulfilled. No merge, backport, release, main write, or rerun of history/audio/billing was performed.

## Safety and validation

- Fresh disposable hosted VMs; read-only repository permission; no secrets/OIDC/environments/shared caches; checkout credentials not persisted. Contributor subprocesses receive an allowlisted environment and isolated HOME/state. These checks are not a process sandbox; the disposable VM is the isolation boundary.
- Immutable source SHAs, fixed commands, 30/45-minute job bounds, bounded subprocesses, seven-day synthetic-only artifacts. No user audio or HOME/state upload. Audio-only Homebrew provisioning was bounded to eight minutes with auto-update/analytics disabled.
- Independent native source/security review and final-delta review found no P0–P2 blockers. Local ClawSweeper/autoreview executors were unavailable; this is explicitly a native fallback, not a claimed ClawSweeper/Codex result.
- The segmented-proof final diff against `9838c5239d071ab5845c061da812f2aa76f1db5c` received fresh independent native review, with no P0–P2 findings: SHA-256 `591f83cb056a99c0550f90032e8e576d49af37564d69c2cf7d4f68049415bb82`.
- Required workflow/macOS-launcher tooling regressions: 8 files, 1,416 tests passed again for the segmented-proof change (241.06 s wrapper wall time). Sixteen synthetic driver/preflight cases pass (about 0.63 s), including zero/partial proof rejection and Swift-version checks.
- Workflow validation (pinned actionlint/zizmor plus repository guards), targeted lint, formatting, native-harness typecheck with repository ambient declarations, and whitespace checks pass.

## Scope

One bounded driver reuses the repository's test wrapper and macOS isolation owner; the native fixture imports the real audio implementation. No product change, generic runner manager, free-form command input, compatibility path, main write, merge, backport, or release. The initial three-lane workflow remains in the first commit and its artifacts remain attached to the first run.

## Billing — paired runtime observations collected

PR #197369: baseline `489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b` versus candidate `8cb8b3e98da2980e1312480decf3079e0ddd0a0c`. Final proof tooling `16f421ebb28694e48f388ce745e6df848af8fad1` (initial harness `935834f61761725baa063fdfc46d6c31a0ae9cc5`); original runtime tooling/Bun pin `b27440329b4c450ec4c572e40ed338ed98f3d9c7`.

Five fixed Linux groups cover the unresolved jobs 132481409032, 132481406074, 132481409054, 132481409138, and 132481420753. Fourteen selected files include all 18 originally failing cases. Each baseline/candidate group receives its own fresh Ubuntu 24.04 VM, Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0; original pinned Bun is staged without shared caches. Node precedes Bun. Original runtime/private-QA preparation is retained where the original job built it. Per-case/per-runtime failure signatures, nonzero execution, required-case admission, and actual file start-time order are checked. Missing cases/reports and setup timeouts remain failures, not successful observations. Any observed test failure keeps the hosted job red.

**Important limitation:** this is a bounded focused replay with a common fixed serial order, not the original full parallel shard load. It omits sibling files and separates Node/Bun invocations to preserve distinct reports. A passing replay means “not reproduced,” never “fixed” or “inherited.” Candidate-only failures likewise require causal investigation. The upstream runtime-preparation change `7cd145595bf99f4caec9148b85db37bbb9147fab` is not applied or claimed as a fix. No new billing-path causal attribution is claimed.

Validation: 11 synthetic evidence-admission tests pass, targeted lint and formatting pass, `git diff --check` passes, and the unchanged final workflow passes repository workflow validation (actionlint/zizmor and repository guards). Initial lint findings were corrected and the final lint command passed with failure propagation. Fresh independent native source/security review of the complete final four-file delta found no remaining P0–P2 findings after correcting order enforcement, all required state cases, and exact wrapped timeout signatures. The final review hashes match the published files. This is the existing explicitly labeled native fallback, not a ClawSweeper/autoreview service result.

No completed history, prefix, audio, or permission proof is rerun. No main/product-branch write, merge, backport, or release.



### Billing harness boundary correction — November 15, 2026

Run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43775844906 completed with all ten jobs failing the nonzero gate: the pinned Vitest 5 accepts a sequencer constructor in configuration, not a CLI module path. The Node reports contained zero executed tests (`TypeError: Sequencer is not a constructor`); Bun was not reached. This is harness/setup failure, not billing regression evidence. All artifacts were collected and retained.

Commit `16f421ebb28694e48f388ce745e6df848af8fad1` narrowly attaches the constructor to the original config export, preserving original config paths, setup, source pins and selection. Synthetic constructor/policy test added (12/12 pass); syntax, targeted lint and diff checks pass. Independent native final-delta review found no P0–P2 findings (delta SHA-256 `c4b7ebefe370ce48ebe244ceb77739b92a7f1afc9dc364ed2bb56ac10b4971bf`).

Changed-harness recovery run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43777174095 — completed November 16, 2026, 00:20 UTC; all ten artifacts collected. Eight jobs passed and both state jobs retained actual test failures. No unchanged-job rerun or repeated completed history/audio/permission proof.


### Collected paired results

Run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43777174095 executed all selected cases on **both exact source pins**, Node then Bun, with identical fixed preparation and admitted file order. Case identities, statuses, and complete failure messages compare identically between baseline/candidate for each runtime/group. **364 executed assertions: 356 passed, 8 failed.** No zero-test or missing-required-case admissions; no incomplete runtime observations.

| Original job / group | Baseline Node / Bun | Candidate Node / Bun | Observation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 132481409032 / state | 14 pass + 2 fail / 14 pass + 2 fail | 14 pass + 2 fail / 14 pass + 2 fail | Same two Beam UNAVAILABLE failures on both pins and runtimes; all other selected state cases pass. |
| 132481406074 / chat | 62 pass / 62 pass | 62 pass / 62 pass | Pending chat.startup metadata assertion did not reproduce. |
| 132481409054 / reload | 1 pass / 1 pass | 1 pass / 1 pass | Original Bun 120-second timeout did not reproduce. |
| 132481409138 / startup | 6 pass / 6 pass | 6 pass / 6 pass | sessions.list and sessions.github.options timeouts did not reproduce. |
| 132481420753 / compaction | 6 pass / 6 pass | 6 pass / 6 pass | backend-not-entered signature did not reproduce. |

The two state failures are in `server.beam-owned-view.test.ts`:
- `HTTP Visitor publications are privately readable by their initial publisher through admitted RPC` (assertion at line 287).
- `preserves model admission and rolls back revoked owned Beam adoption` (assertion at line 559).

All eight failing assertions report `UNAVAILABLE` / `Could not load this Beam. Refresh and try again.` The four **Bun** failures match the original required case/runtime signatures. Node reports the same symptom on both pins, but is deliberately **not** labeled an original runtime-signature match because the original signature was Bun. This establishes that these Beam symptoms also occur before the billing diff under this focused preparation; it is not blanket attribution of the original failing shard.

The ACP-native timeout/catalog-retiring cascade, config.set reread timeout, and sessions.create timeouts were not reproduced. Passing replays do not establish fixes, absence of flakiness, or baseline attribution for those original failures. The runtime-preparation hypothesis remains unproven. No product repair is included, and the state jobs remain red rather than masking expected failures. No further reruns were submitted after collection.

## Matrix — causal original-module qualification

PR #197000 candidate `bf8ee2c6152a18386a175ad329013bc20a4a8051`; original module source `937f77cb20ded2e041f5ea876200d01b449d0329`. Product code is unchanged by this proof. Execution tooling `08e028a6bba5f6e1dcdc09739cdb26730ea55dd8`; final admission-only tooling `f00d850619271dbd39cf713dc43322d2fd622925`.

- Run 43790032640 (tooling `a95800834f9353eb801eebff4a8b274ecb9f1d99`): all **97 SDK cases passed**, isolated wrapper wall time **71.404 s**. Its job was red only because the old evidence gate incorrectly rejected a legitimate repeated parameterized title; the retained report was re-admitted, not rerun.
- Run 43790694571 (tooling `a4dec2e6e0c3f006aeaf24a195bfc514da4de2eb`): candidate **transport 16/16** (**51.330 s**), **authority integration 14/14** (**3.005 s**), and selected message-owner cases **2/2** (**65.565 s**) passed. These are isolated, serial wrapper wall times including setup, not per-case sums or full-file timing for the filtered owner suite.
- The same run replaced only `sdk/client-core.ts`, `sdk/message-wire-dispatch.ts`, and `src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.ts` with original bytes, keeping candidate dependencies and tests. In the real SDK → guarded loopback HTTP pair, the **direct 403 failed** the intended permanent-rejection assertion at `transport.test.ts:154:35`, while **307 → 403 passed** its uncertainty assertion. Original-wire wrapper wall time **50.774 s**, launcher exit 1.
- The driver initially rejected that genuine causal failure because Vitest abbreviated `Cannot send to room` to `Cannot se…`. The repair admits only the exact observed M_FORBIDDEN/403 prefix, expected `retryable: false` object, pinned assertion path/line/column, required two case identities/statuses, and launcher exit 1; it still rejects missing/extra/duplicate cases, setup/timeout/connection failures, wrong error, wrong assertion, wrong expectation, and unrelated truncation. The original structured JSON is preserved and replayed; no product rerun was spent on the admission repair.

This is an **original-module differential in the candidate environment**, not a full historical-baseline checkout/build, live homeserver test, or proof of encrypted recipient delivery. The tests and all three changed-module hash pairs are checked against the retained report before the continuation executes.

Validation: 26/26 synthetic admission checks pass; the exact retained report is rejected by the old gate and admitted by the repaired gate. Targeted lint, format, Node syntax, whitespace checks and repository workflow validation pass. Workflow validation initially encountered empty token variables; rerunning with only those empty variables removed passed. Fresh independent native review found no P0–P2 findings in the continuation three-file delta (SHA-256 `3df2a28366a1d16d76015b792192b26d20235b4b64c8a2223c929b574fd3a70f`). This is the established explicitly labeled native fallback, not an autoreview/ClawSweeper result; the configured service's 402 credit failure was not retried or bypassed.

[Continuation run 43791792505 / job 133051654842](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43791792505/job/133051654842) downloaded only the two fixed retained artifacts using read-only Actions access and executed only the previously missing **original-owner** pair. Original `sentBeforeError=false` passed; original `sentBeforeError=true` failed with `OutboundDeliveryError: message failed: MatrixError: [403] M_FORBIDDEN`, created at the pinned test's line 457, rather than returning `delivery_unconfirmed`. Candidate versions of both cases passed in the prior run. Original-owner isolated wrapper wall time: **66.949 s**, launcher exit 1; per-case times 30.257 ms / 12.829 ms.

The continuation job remains **red**: its evidence gate mistook Vitest's ordinary `runWithTimeout` stack-frame name for a timeout diagnostic. The final admission-only correction filters stack frames out of infrastructure diagnostics, preserves real timeout/setup/connection rejection, and requires the exact original-owner error prefix and source location. All six retained JSON reports replay successfully through that corrected gate, with no further product execution. The final workflow disables the completed Matrix job; no completed SDK, candidate, wire, history, audio, permission, or billing stage was rerun.

[Retained artifact 14193046368](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43791792505/artifacts/14193046368), `goal24-matrix-43791792505`, contains the six source reports, original-owner log, and the original red summary. prs.title: feat: localize model failure notices in English and German
prs.body:
Closes #199735
Related: #113105 (localization tracking), #193641, #167341

## What Problem This Solves

German-speaking conversations still receive fixed English recovery notices when a model request fails, including on WhatsApp.

## User Impact

Operators can select English or German for supported model-failure notices through `messages.locale`, with a WhatsApp channel/account override via `messageLocale`. A verified person's `messages.locale` preference, set through the existing `users.prefs.set` RPC, takes precedence in direct messages. Groups use channel/account and global defaults. English remains the default and the fallback for unsupported client locales.

This is a bounded localization slice for model-failure notices, not complete localization of every command or status message. It does not add a language picker or translate ordinary model answers. The feature adds no database schema migration.

## Implementation

The reply owner captures language once per request and carries it through execution, followups, and transcript metadata. Queued messages with different languages are not collected into one turn. Personal choice reuses the authenticated profile preference store; WhatsApp supplies its resolved account setting through the existing inbound context.

Failure producers render from classified facts. The captured language also reaches combined tool/provider failures, subscription lifecycle events, shared harness lifecycle events, and failures without an assistant message. Error categories are recorded before translation and survive deferred delivery; replacement failures clear obsolete categories. Raw diagnostic classification, provider codes, cancellation, and provider-refusal handling retain their semantics. The existing Gateway text fallback remains for older lifecycle producers.

A narrow subscription parameter projection keeps forwarding explicit and the preparation module within the existing size limit. No lint threshold or test assertion was weakened.

## Validation

- Initial feature validation: 376 tests in 18 files covered English compatibility, returned/thrown failures, personal preference persistence, Gateway client locale, queue separation, transcript metadata/write hooks, WhatsApp configuration/inbound propagation, and prompt-prefix stability. Subsequent original-feature review regressions also passed; those runs overlap.
- Follow-up repair validation: 271 tests in 14 affected runner/lifecycle/dispatch/prompt suites passed. After the parameter projection was extracted, all 45 subscription-owner tests passed again.
- Final category/recovery checks: 16 Gateway tests passed, including German immediate and deferred failures with preserved error categories and provider codes; 59 observation/lifecycle/recovery tests passed. These totals overlap earlier runs.
- The combined tool/provider regressions, personal-language Gateway regression, incomplete-turn regression, and shared-harness language regression failed before their respective fixes.
- Core typecheck, type-aware lint over every changed TypeScript file, formatting, and the test-line budget check passed. A fresh independent static review returned no actionable P0–P2 findings in the selected repair scope; runtime validation was run separately.

- Transport-copy follow-up (`e3c9ca299f49`): 107 focused presentation/formatter tests and all 10 native Gateway error-event tests passed. New regressions reproduced the incorrect German timeout copy for connection/DNS failures and generic internal errors before the fix; genuine timeouts retain timeout copy. The Gateway regression also preserves the existing structured timeout retry category. Core typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, and test-line budget passed again; a fresh independent static review of this small delta returned no actionable P0–P2 findings. The built-Gateway/restart/upgrade evidence below is retained from the preceding revision and was not rerun for this renderer-only correction.

### Built Gateway and latest-stable upgrade

The committed `test/gateway-localized-failures.e2e.test.ts` drives a built Gateway over real RPC/WebSocket and HTTP model transport, with a local deterministic Responses fixture and an actual failed read tool. It verifies German defaults, personal English overriding German, durable preferences, and English fallback after restart.

The optional upgrade lane was run from the official `openclaw@2026.11.3` package (commit `847611dcaa3bf0e2783335f961dd1fd0580e4d9f`). The existing Doctor migration completed; a previously saved preference and conversation remained readable, and the existing conversation was replayed into the subsequent model request.

Observed terminal messages:

```text
legacy: "Modellanfrage abgewiesen: synthetic request rejected"
personal-en: "LLM request rejected: synthetic request rejected"
english-fallback-after-restart: "LLM request rejected: synthetic request rejected"
```

Run the current-version lane with:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts \
  test/gateway-localized-failures.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

For the upgrade lane, additionally set `OPENCLAW_TEST_LOCALIZATION_BASELINE` to the published package's `openclaw.mjs`. All state and processes are temporary and isolated.

Measured Vitest wall duration was 39.42 seconds for the ordinary Gateway lane (28.263 seconds in the test body), and 87.12 seconds for the optional upgrade lane (73.937 seconds in the test body), excluding runtime build preparation. The upgrade lane intentionally includes two installed versions, Doctor migration, and real process restarts; helper-only tests cannot establish that compatibility. CI seconds are not available because upstream execution awaits approval.

The test-line allocation records the excess over the normal 400-line allowance. The additional proof protects distinct ingress, queue, terminal, persistence, and real Gateway/restart/upgrade boundaries; helper-only tests had missed the personal-language lifecycle bug. Against the original PR merge base, the complete feature has +623 net source lines and +804 net test lines. The allocation covers 404 lines above the allowance.

## Limits and maintainer actions

No live WhatsApp message or external model API was used, and no production server was changed. WhatsApp evidence remains local production-path testing with synthetic inputs.

The runtime build completed with UI bundle-budget warnings; their attribution was not established and no budget was changed. Upstream CI execution and the enforced security-sensitive review require maintainer approval of the current revision. Maintainer acceptance of the new locale settings and precedence remains a product decision.

prs.title: fix(snapshot): disable trusted_schema while restoring a git backup
prs.body:
Fixes #160732.

## What Problem This Solves

A Git backup restore runs the backup’s schema.sql. With SQLite trusted_schema enabled, a trigger from that file could invoke a function that should be unavailable to the restore.

## Summary

The restore connection sets trusted_schema=OFF before loading the schema, matching snapshot verification.

## Evidence

The diff adds a regression in `src/snapshot/git-backup-codec.test.ts` that adds a load_extension call to a backup trigger and checks that SQLite rejects the subsequent insert. The test suite has not been verified locally for this PR.

prs.title: fix(plugins): read JSON5 plugin manifests in doctor and recovery paths
prs.body:
> **Proof refreshed 2026-11-20 against the latest release `v2026.11.6`.** The upgrade proof now starts from `v2026.11.6` (`06afb10d327`, published 2026-11-19) instead of `v2026.11.3`, which is what the previous review asked for. Both the `v2026.11.6` base and this PR's head `cc6dac4b097` were built to their own `dist` (shipped `scripts/tsdown-build.mts` + `copy-bundled-plugin-metadata.mts`, Node 24.22.1) and driven as real CLIs on a real SQLite state database. The head change itself is unchanged: the four commits are byte-identical to the previously reviewed head (`23deadb73807`), replayed onto current `main` (`aa2dc6433e1`). Suites re-run on the shipped trees: `doctor-plugin-registry.test.ts` 33/33 and the three records/json-files suites 37/37, both green.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor` (and the install-record recovery path) silently skips any managed npm plugin whose `openclaw.plugin.json` uses JSON5 — comments, trailing commas, or unquoted keys — because the stale-managed-npm-shadow check (`doctor-plugin-registry.ts`) and the recovery reader (`installed-plugin-index-record-reader.ts`) parse the manifest with a strict JSON reader that returns `null` on such syntax. The plugin is documented as JSON5-capable (`docs/plugins/manifest.md`: "Native manifests are parsed with JSON5"), the main loader accepts it (`manifest.ts:218` `parsePluginCacheJson(file, { json5: true })`), and `openclaw plugins install` installs it. But Doctor's shadow check reads the same file strictly, so a stale managed npm package shadowing a bundled plugin is never reported and never repaired — the user's plugin silently keeps the old version with no hint from `openclaw doctor`.

Fixes #201715

Precedent: #198808 (same shape: a JSON5-capable manifest reread with strict `JSON.parse`; the CLI browser builder was switched to the JSON5-capable reader). This PR applies the shape to the two remaining strict readers of installed-plugin manifests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two remaining strict readers are the only places that parse a user-installed `openclaw.plugin.json` with plain strict JSON. `package.json` reads stay strict (npm `package.json` is never JSON5). The fix adds one shared reader, `tryReadJson5ObjectSync` in `src/infra/json-files.ts`, that keeps the strict-JSON fast path, falls back to JSON5, and preserves the `null`-on-failure contract of the existing `tryReadJsonObjectSync` — so a malformed manifest degrades exactly as before. Both call sites route their `openclaw.plugin.json` read through it.

Production LOC is `+72/-10` (net +62), two call sites change, one shared helper added in the JSON-reader owner, plus a recovery rekey. No new validator / option / config / persistence.

Classification: `behavior-completing` (a stale shadow that was silently skipped is now reported and repaired, matching the loader's documented JSON5 acceptance).

## User Impact

A user who installed an npm plugin with a JSON5 manifest (comments, trailing commas, unquoted keys) now gets the stale-managed-npm shadow warning and `--fix` repair from `openclaw doctor`, instead of the shadow being silently skipped and the bundled plugin staying shadowed by an old managed copy. Strict JSON manifests and all other doctor behaviors are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Discriminating test (producer-chain, real repair path)

The regression adds a JSON5 variant of the existing `warns about stale managed npm packages that shadow bundled plugins` case in `src/commands/doctor-plugin-registry.test.ts`: it builds the same bundled-vs-managed fixture but writes the managed package's `openclaw.plugin.json` as JSON5 (`{ id: 'bundled-demo', ..., }` with a leading comment), then runs `maybeRepairPluginRegistryState` and asserts the shadow warning and the `@openclaw/bundled-demo@2026.5.2` note are emitted.

- RED on base (`v2026.11.6`, `06afb10d327`): the JSON5 case fails at `expect(notes).toContain("Managed npm plugin packages shadow bundled plugins")` — the strict reader returns `null`, `pluginId` is undefined, and the stale package is skipped.
- GREEN on head (`cc6dac4b097`): the same case passes; the full file stays green (33/33).

Remote proof run (sandboxed runner, docker Node 24.22.1, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/doctor-plugin-registry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`), tree-local md5-pinned base vs head:

```text
RED  (base, strict read):   1 failed | 32 passed  ->  expected '' to contain "Managed npm plugin packages shadow bundled plugins"
GREEN (head, JSON5 read):   Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 33 passed (33)
```

### Fixup: retain the atomic-writer import

A first revision of the shared reader accidentally replaced the `@openclaw/fs-safe/atomic` import in `json-files.ts`, leaving `writeTextAtomic` with an undefined `writeFsSafeTextAtomic` (ClawSweeper P1). The current head restores the atomic import alongside the new read import; the atomic-writer tests stay green (`src/infra/json-files.test.ts`: 22/22 on head).

### Fixup: rekey persisted package-name recovery records

A released strict reader could already have persisted an install record keyed by the npm package name for a package whose JSON5 manifest declares a different `id`. Reading the JSON5 id then yields the same install path under the manifest id (ClawSweeper P1). `mergeRecoveredManagedNpmInstallRecords` now rekeys the persisted record to the recovered manifest id **before** building recovery candidates — deleting the old key first would discard persisted metadata (`integrity`, `installedAt`, …) and lose the active-path authority. A regression in `src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-records.test.ts` covers the previously persisted package-name case and asserts the persisted metadata is retained:

```text
RED  (JSON5 id read, no rekey):   expected { source: 'npm', …(6) } to match object { source: 'npm', …(8) }  (metadata lost / duplicate key)
GREEN (JSON5 id read + rekey):    Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 11 passed (11)
```

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/doctor-plugin-registry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 33/33 on head (RED on base for the discriminating assertion).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/json-files.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 22/22 on head (atomic writer tests intact).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-records.test.ts src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-records.managed-npm.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 15/15 on head (reconcile regression included).
- `git diff --check` — clean.

### Shipped proof: real `openclaw doctor` on a JSON5 manifest

Built both trees to a real `dist` and drove the actual CLI binary (`node dist/entry.js doctor --lint --all --only core/doctor/plugin-registry --json`), not the test harness. The fixture is a genuine managed npm plugin install under an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`: `npm/projects/openclaw-a2a-d83b9340a9/` with a `package.json` declaring `@openclaw/a2a`, the installed package's strict `package.json`, and an `openclaw.plugin.json` written as JSON5 (leading comment, unquoted keys, single quotes, trailing comma):

```json5
// Native manifests are parsed with JSON5 (docs/plugins/manifest.md).
{
  id: 'a2a',
  name: 'A2A',
  configSchema: { type: 'object' },
}
```

`@openclaw/a2a` is a real bundled plugin, so the managed copy is a genuine shadow. Four-cell matrix, same fixture, two real builds:

Re-run on the two shipped builds for this refresh — base `v2026.11.6` (`06afb10d327`) and head `cc6dac4b097`, each built to its own `dist` and driven as a CLI:

```text
===== BASE (/w/v2026116) =====
  manifest is JSON5 (leading // comment, single quotes, trailing comma)
  "ok":true
  SHADOW_FINDING=ABSENT
  package exists before --fix: yes
  package exists after --fix: yes
  AFTER_FIX=clean
  CONTROL(strict JSON): SHADOW_FINDING=PRESENT

===== HEAD (/w/head) =====
  manifest is JSON5 (leading // comment, single quotes, trailing comma)
  "ok":false
  SHADOW_FINDING=PRESENT
  finding: Managed npm package @openclaw/a2a@2026.5.2 shadows bundled plugin a2a.
  package exists before --fix: yes
  package exists after --fix: no
  AFTER_FIX=clean
  after-fix ok: "ok":true
  CONTROL(strict JSON): SHADOW_FINDING=PRESENT
```

Four-cell matrix:

| `openclaw.plugin.json` | base `v2026.11.6` (strict reader) | head `cc6dac4b097` (JSON5 reader) |
|---|---|---|
| strict JSON | `Managed npm package @openclaw/a2a@2026.5.2 shadows bundled plugin a2a.` | same — no regression |
| JSON5 | **no finding** (`ok: true`) | **`Managed npm package @openclaw/a2a@2026.5.2 shadows bundled plugin a2a.`** |

The strict-JSON row proves the diagnosis path itself is unchanged; only the JSON5 row changes. On head the repair is real: `doctor --fix` deletes the stale package (`exists after --fix: no`) and the follow-up lint is clean. Raw head output:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/w/s-head2/state node dist/entry.js \
    doctor --lint --all --only core/doctor/plugin-registry --json
{"schemaVersion":1,"ok":false,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":77,"findings":[
  {"checkId":"core/doctor/plugin-registry","severity":"warning",
   "message":"Managed npm package @openclaw/a2a@2026.5.2 shadows bundled plugin a2a.",
   "path":"/w/s-head2/state/npm/projects/openclaw-a2a-d83b9340a9/node_modules/@openclaw/a2a",
   "target":"a2a",
   "fixHint":"Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to remove stale managed npm packages and rebuild the plugin registry."}], ...}
```

Repair path, end to end on the same state:

```text
$ node dist/entry.js doctor --fix --non-interactive
before --fix: package exists = yes
after  --fix: package exists = no
$ node dist/entry.js doctor --lint --all --only core/doctor/plugin-registry --json
ok: true   findings: <none>
```

### Shipped proof: v2026.11.6 → head upgrade keeps legacy keys and metadata

The compatibility question is whether an install record persisted by the **released** strict reader (keyed by the npm package name) survives the upgrade. Both sides here are the real thing: the latest release `v2026.11.6` resolves to `06afb10d327` and that commit was built to its own `dist` and run against the real state database; the head side is this PR's `cc6dac4b097`, built the same way. Both runs used the shipped `scripts/tsdown-build.mts` + `copy-bundled-plugin-metadata.mts` build, Node 24.22.1.

The fixture is a non-shadow managed npm plugin — `@vendor/demo@1.2.3`, not in the bundled set — so the upgrade path exercises the record rekey rather than the shadow repair:

```json5
// JSON5 manifest
{
  id: 'demo',
  name: 'Demo',
  configSchema: { type: 'object' },
}
```

Each phase is a separate process, all against the real SQLite state (`state/openclaw.sqlite`, `config_machine_state.value_json` under `plugins.installedIndex.index.installRecords`). Phase A runs the `v2026.11.6` tree, Phase B and B2 run the head tree in fresh processes.

```text
[A] package dir: /w/state-up/npm/projects/vendor-demo-4e2ce35bbb/node_modules/@vendor/demo
[A] manifest is JSON5 (comment + single quotes + trailing comma)
[A] v2026.11.6 strict reader -> keys: ["@vendor/demo"]
[A] seeding metadata onto key "@vendor/demo": integrity + installedAt
[A] on disk after persist -> keys: ["@vendor/demo"]
[A] on disk record: {"source":"npm","spec":"@vendor/demo@1.2.3","installPath":"/w/state-up/npm/projects/vendor-demo-4e2ce35bbb/node_modules/@vendor/demo","version":"1.2.3","resolvedName":"@vendor/demo","resolvedVersion":"1.2.3","resolvedSpec":"@vendor/demo@1.2.3","integrity":"sha512-legacy-v2026.11.6","installedAt":"2026-05-02T00:00:00.000Z"}

[B] on disk before head read -> keys: ["@vendor/demo"]
[B] head JSON5 reader -> keys: ["demo"]
[B] metadata retained: {"integrity":"sha512-legacy-v2026.11.6","installedAt":"2026-05-02T00:00:00.000Z","installPath":"/w/state-up/npm/projects/vendor-demo-4e2ce35bbb/node_modules/@vendor/demo"}
[B] on disk after persist -> keys: ["demo"]
[B] persisted: {"integrity":"sha512-legacy-v2026.11.6","installedAt":"2026-05-02T00:00:00.000Z","installPath":"/w/state-up/npm/projects/vendor-demo-4e2ce35bbb/node_modules/@vendor/demo"}

[B2] fresh-process reload -> keys: ["demo"]
[B2] reloaded: {"integrity":"sha512-legacy-v2026.11.6","installedAt":"2026-05-02T00:00:00.000Z","installPath":"/w/state-up/npm/projects/vendor-demo-4e2ce35bbb/node_modules/@vendor/demo"}
[B2] VERDICT=PASS
```

The released strict reader keys the record by the npm package name (`@vendor/demo`); head reads the JSON5 `id` and rekeys to `demo`, keeping `integrity`, `installedAt` and `installPath`; the rekeyed state survives persistence and a cold reload.

Note on where the write comes from: `loadInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecords` itself only reads and caches, as the review observed. The rekeyed map reaches disk when a caller that owns registry persistence writes it — the plugin-install commit path, or `openclaw doctor --fix` when its preflight selects `migrate`/`initialize` (with a readable index already present, preflight selects `skip-existing` and doctor intentionally writes nothing). Phase B uses that same production write pair (`withPluginLifecycleLease` + `writePersistedInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecordsWithLease`) rather than inventing a new one.

Result: the identity migrates, the persisted metadata and install path survive, and the state is stable across persistence and a fresh-process reload.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+72/-10` net +62 (one shared helper in `json-files.ts`; two call sites; atomic import retained; recovery rekey)
- Test LOC: `+61`

prs.title: fix(agents): continuation-skip turns tell the model its workspace instructions were removed
prs.body:
Related: #196122

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `contextInjection: "continuation-skip"`, every continuation turn on routes that pin the system prompt (direct Anthropic, official OpenAI Responses) tells the model that AGENTS.md, USER.md, MEMORY.md and every heading inside them were "(removed)".

## User Impact

On those routes, skipped turns keep the workspace instructions the model already has, without a system update revoking them. Skipped turns still send no workspace files, and an explicit `contextInjection: "never"` still announces the removal. Sessions that already received a false removal from an earlier skipped turn get their files redelivered once on the next skipped turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

A skipped continuation withholds files that the pinned prompt prefix still carries, but the prompt series diffed the file-less prompt against that prefix and reported each Project Context section as removed. The bootstrap stage now reports that it withheld already-delivered context, and the pinned series reuses its own Project Context block for that comparison, placed inside the framed stable region (before `<!-- /openclaw:attempt:STABLE -->`, or the cache boundary when unframed). If the saved comparison state already lost the block, the block comes from the admitted prefix, which still has it.

Scope: this does not change what unpinned routes (OpenRouter, most OpenAI-compatible providers) receive on skipped turns. Whether those routes should keep workspace files under `continuation-skip` is the separate product question in #196122; this PR leaves the #154923 behavior as is.

## Evidence

- Regression in `session-prompt-state.test.ts` built from real `buildAttemptSystemPrompt` output (with STABLE/DYNAMIC framing): on a pinned series, a withheld turn emits no update; redelivering unchanged files emits nothing; a removal without the withheld flag reports `(removed)` for the file and its inner headings; a comparison state that already lost the files redelivers them (`Be brief.`) once.
- Mutation checks: ignoring the STABLE terminator makes the "no update" assertion fail; dropping the admitted-prefix fallback makes the redelivery assertion fail.
- `session-prompt-state.test.ts`: 36 passed. `tsc` for `tsconfig.core.json`, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json`, `tsconfig.scripts.json`: no errors in changed files or for `workspaceContextWithheld`. `check:test-lines-ratchet` passes with the allocation. `oxfmt --check` / `oxlint` clean.
- Evidence gap: I have not captured a live provider request on a pinned route. Pinned routes require a direct Anthropic or official OpenAI endpoint with a real key, so the existing loopback Gateway fixture (`gateway.continuation-skip-bootstrap.integration.test.ts`) resolves as unpinned and cannot show this path. `attempt-bootstrap-prepare.test.ts` hits `EMFILE` on Windows for 14 cases, identically on unmodified `main`.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

The composer browser test can report that a dropped file disappeared when its attachment preview is still loading. On a cold, busy test runner, compiling the lazily loaded preview takes longer than the filename assertion allows.

prs.title: fix(tui): run built-in login in-process so a same-session auth resumes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A local TUI `/auth` login saves the credential and reports `auth flow finished for <provider>`, then the very next turn in that same session fails with `Secret owner account:[...,github-copilot:github] is configured but unavailable (secret reference was not materialized by the active runtime)`. A fresh `openclaw` process using the same saved credential chats fine. The TUI only works again after a restart.

Fixes #201751

## Why This Change Was Made

Two compounding defects:

1. **The login ran as a child process.** `tui.ts` spawned a separate `openclaw models auth login` process. That child could not acquire the gateway state ownership the TUI already holds, so it failed with `OpenClaw state database is busy... holder <tui-pid>`, and the login could not publish its credential into the running session at all. A same-session auth could therefore never resume — only a restart worked.

2. **Even when the credential was persisted, nothing republished it.** `oauth.ts` `published` requires the stored profile to be present in `getRuntimeAuthProfileStoreSnapshotCore(agentDir)`. For a profile saved after the session's snapshot was prepared, that snapshot is the pre-login generation, so `published` is false and the resolver throws `SecretSurfaceUnavailableError` with reason `secret reference was not materialized by the active runtime` — the reported message. The old code cleared the published generation and hoped a retained runtime would rebuild it, but nothing triggered the rebuild when the write happened in the same process tree rather than through an observed file event.

The fix runs the built-in login **in-process** (sharing the TUI's state owner and embedded runtime) and rebuilds the published auth generation at the login boundary:

- `runLocalProviderLogin()` in `src/tui/tui-auth-invocation.ts` calls `modelsAuthLoginCommand` with `createNonExitingRuntime()` — in-process, no child process, so no state-ownership conflict.
- `refreshAfterLogin` calls `refreshRuntimeAuthProfileStoreAfterLogin()` (in `src/agents/auth-profiles.ts`): it re-observes the persisted auth store (`refreshAuthProfileFileState`) and republishes through the secrets runtime's `refreshActiveProviderAuthRuntimeSnapshot` hook.
- `src/secrets/runtime.ts` binds `refreshActiveProviderAuthRuntimeSnapshot` as the post-login republish hook at **module scope** (where it already registers the auth-store external-refresh hook). Binding at load time — not inside the external-file callback — is what lets a fresh process that has never fired a file event republish a same-session login.
- `tui.ts` `runAuthFlow` keeps the Codex child branch; for the built-in local path it suspends the TUI (`withTuiSuspended`), runs the login in-process on the TUI's own abort signal, and records the completion so the next turn waits for it. `tui.ts` is grandfathered over its line cap, so the new sequence lives in `tui-auth-invocation.ts` and `auth-login.types.ts` (types moved out of the oversized `auth.ts`); `tui.ts` itself does not grow.
- `modelsAuthLoginCommand` gains `refreshAfterLogin`; when it is set and the login did not refresh, it raises `ProviderCredentialsSavedError` ("Sign-in was saved, but this session could not refresh... Restart the local TUI and retry") instead of silently claiming success.
- SIGTERM hygiene copied from #200605: `PREPARED_MODEL_RUNTIME_LIFETIMES_KEY` is hoisted to a shared constant (`prepared-model-runtime.{lifecycle,types}.ts`), and `runtime-cleanup-scope.ts` releases the native-worker-backed model generation on CLI cleanup, so a SIGTERM with an auth prompt open still exits.

Behavior is unchanged for Codex-backed logins (Codex owns its own store and keeps its child branch) and for profiles already present in the published generation.

## User Impact

Signing in from the local TUI now lets the same session send its next message, instead of requiring a restart. Users who already restart lose nothing; the stale-generation window that produced the misleading error is closed.

## Evidence

### Discriminating unit regression (fresh-process binding, no file event)

`src/secrets/runtime-file-observation.test.ts` gains `republishes the persisted store through the production-bound refresh hook without a file event`. It activates a real secrets snapshot, then calls `refreshRuntimeAuthProfileStoreAfterLogin()` with **no external-file event having fired**, and asserts the post-login refresh republishes through the hook the secrets runtime bound at module scope. This is the exact fresh-process shape: with the binding inside the external-file callback (base) a process that never fired a file event has no hook and reports no republish; with the binding at module scope (head) it republishes.

```text
# BASE (binding inside the external-file callback) with the same test
FAIL  runtime-file-observation.test.ts > republishes the persisted store through the production-bound refresh hook without a file event
AssertionError: expected false to be true
      Tests  1 failed | 5 passed (6)

# HEAD (binding at module scope)
PASS  runtime-file-observation.test.ts > republishes the persisted store through the production-bound refresh hook without a file event
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/secrets/runtime-file-observation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

`src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.test.ts` keeps a fresh-process contract — `does not fabricate a published generation when no secrets runtime bound the republish hook` asserts an unbound process reports no republish (rather than inventing a generation). 15/15 on head. Neighbouring owners stay green on head: `tui.test.ts`, `runtime-file-invalidation.test.ts`, `file-state.test.ts` — 50 + 23 tests passed.

### End-to-end: real built CLI + PTY, both credential shapes

`src/tui/tui-pty-local.e2e.test.ts`'s existing local-auth case is now a **parameterized, in-process, real-PTY run against a built CLI and a mock Gateway** (`itWithBuiltCli.for(["inline API key", "store-backed token"])`), reusing the new helpers `prepareLocalAuthProviderFixture`, `signInToLocalPtyProvider` and `readLocalPtyAuthProfile` in `tui-pty-local-test-support.ts`. Both variants pass on head.

Each variant drives `/auth tui-pty-mock` through the real TTY, completes the provider's prompt with a sentinel value, and asserts that a **message in the same session** reaches the mock Gateway with the new credential:

- **inline API key**: one prompt (`Enter T05 local auth API key`), one follow-up request; `authorization === "Bearer <sentinel>"`, `body.model === "gpt-5.5"`, persisted profile is `type: api_key` with the sentinel key.
- **store-backed token** (`kind: device_code`, warm session already active): `requests` length is 2 — the warm-session request plus the post-login request with the **new** `Bearer <sentinel>` — and the persisted profile is `type: token` with `tokenRef.source === "store"` and no inlined token, proving the login refreshed the active session rather than just writing storage.

Both variants also prove the lifecycle regression fix: after re-opening the auth prompt, the TUI is SIGTERMed and **exits with code 0 and no signal** (the TUI shutdown handlers run and release the native-worker-backed model generation), then the persisted profile is asserted on disk.

```text
# HEAD (in-process login), both cases, real PTY against built CLI
PASS  tui-pty-local.e2e.test.ts > TUI PTY real backends > authenticates a manifest-discovered provider and resumes the unchanged local model (inline API key)
PASS  tui-pty-local.e2e.test.ts > TUI PTY real backends > authenticates a manifest-discovered provider and resumes the unchanged local model (store-backed token)
```

The prior child-process version of this test passed the message-turn assertion only because it reloaded the store from outside the TUI process; the in-process run exercises the actual same-session path, which is the reported scenario.

### Honest scope of the proof

The e2e runs a real TTY and a built CLI, but the provider is a **local mock provider**, not the reported GitHub Copilot device flow (a network device-auth flow this environment cannot drive). The decision boundary that produced the reported error — the post-login republish in a process that never fired a file event — is covered directly by the unit regression above; the e2e covers the full same-session resume path with a real credential of both shapes.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/secrets/runtime-file-observation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 6/6 on head; the added case fails `expected false to be true` on base.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 15/15.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/tui/tui.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/runtime-file-invalidation.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/file-state.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 50 + 23 tests passed.
- `tui-pty-local.e2e.test.ts` — both credential cases pass against a built CLI on a real PTY (mock Gateway).
- `node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mts --base origin/main --no-merge-base` — OK (changed source files; `tui.ts` does not grow).
- `node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main --no-merge-base` — OK.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` on the changed files — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

## Scope and risk

- Production files (18 changed): `oauth.ts` +24, `runtime-file-observation.ts` +13, `secrets/runtime.ts` +5, `tui-auth-invocation.ts` +20, `auth.ts` −33 (types moved to `auth-login.types.ts` +49), `prepared-model-runtime.lifecycle.ts` +5/−4, `prepared-model-runtime.types.ts` +4, `runtime-cleanup-scope.ts` +3, `tui.ts` +26/−34 (net −8), plus `tui-command-context.ts`, `tui-command-handlers.ts` and barrel export. No new config, option, schema, migration, or persistence policy.
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses `refreshAuthProfileFileState` (persisted-store observer), `refreshActiveProviderAuthRuntimeSnapshot` (secrets-owned refresh, already registered for auth-store refresh) and the `PREPARED_MODEL_RUNTIME_LIFETIMES_KEY` constant; no new resolution primitive.
- Files touched are not part of any open PR's file set (checked against the ~200 open PRs' file lists: `runtime-snapshots`/`auth-profiles`/`oauth`/`runtime-degraded-state` all clear).

prs.title: improve: preview a Template without expanding its files in chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A prepared Template fills the conversation with a file inspector even when the publisher only wants the summary. Publication can take minutes, and a lost response must not lead to a second upload.

## User Impact

The draft stays in a compact chat card. **Preview** opens the file inspector used for Import; **Publish** works from the card or the dialog. Pending shows a blue badge and **View submission**. There is no email alert or automatic redirect. On publication the card offers **Copy link**. An uncertain submission offers **Check status**, not a second upload; a confirmed failure offers **Retry**.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preview and Publish use the same reviewed archive. Revising the draft closes an outdated preview. While the card is active, it checks a pending submission 30 seconds after each response and stops on a final receipt. Opening the submission on ClawHub is the publisher’s choice. Email delivery is not part of the Control UI contract. The link uses the Gateway-provided Template URL; viewing an unpublished release there depends on the signed-in pending listing on ClawHub.

## Evidence

- [Current Pending and delayed-status screenshots: desktop/mobile comparisons and both walkthroughs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202060#issuecomment-7024084670). These supersede those states and the videos in the [original 11-state gallery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202060#issuecomment-7022133859). Running bundled UI with scripted Gateway responses, 1440 × 844 and 390 × 844; only idle video playback is accelerated.
- On the alert-free candidate, a real disposable Gateway sent one reviewed archive to a loopback registry and checked the same attempt at +30.312 s and +60.481 s. No duplicate upload, navigation or new tab. Neither the hosted link nor production email delivery was exercised by this test.
- 20 focused creator tests and four responsive Chromium scenarios passed on the alert-free candidate. The pristine base rendered Publish but no Preview; the new Preview opens the exact file, goes Back and closes without uploading.
- The preceding CSS repair passed [hosted CI, including the performance and lint gates](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44621399599) without changing budgets. Against `f9553398b8e` its local paired CSS delta was −990 B raw and +58 B gzip (allowance +64 B). This follow-up removes the email notice, its copy and its dedicated CSS rules.

prs.title: fix: show the right agent and live activity when adding a template
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
After clicking Add on a template, the new chat could show the previous agent in the switcher and a generic recipient in the composer until setup finished. While the model prepared a tool call, the chat showed only a timer. Its first greeting could also appear twice: once as a message and once as a Message tool row.

## User Impact
The first chat frame names the template agent. Chat shows “Preparing a tool call” before execution begins. A successful greeting in the same chat appears once; failed sends and sends to other chats remain visible.

## Why This Change Was Made
The new chat already knows the template name, so it can show it without waiting for the saved agent record. Template Add overlaps the registry fetch with agent creation and starts dependency setup alongside the opening model request. The installer still verifies the package, and the model still performs conversational setup.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw ID on macOS only works when the app is built with its native transport (`OPENCLAW_IROH_NATIVE=1`). Release builds don't include it. Today those builds still show OpenClaw ID in several places: a "Reach it from anywhere?" onboarding page whose only button is disabled, "Sign in with OpenClaw ID" and "Use a node invitation" choices during setup, a Settings section and a menu bar item. Users see a feature they can't use.

## User Impact

User impact: In macOS builds without the native transport, OpenClaw ID no longer appears. Onboarding on this Mac goes straight from AI setup to the final page. Builds with `OPENCLAW_IROH_NATIVE=1` behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw ID should stay completely hidden until we're ready to ship it. This change adds one gate, `MacOpenClawIDFeature.isEnabled`, which checks whether the native transport is in the build. It applies the gate to every OpenClaw ID entry point:
- the onboarding page order and the step after AI setup
- the onboarding connection choices
- the final onboarding page, which now says "Running on this Mac" instead of pointing to OpenClaw ID
- the Settings › Connection section
- the menu bar sign-in item and removal subtitle
- the dashboard's removal-recovery page

<details><summary>Entry points reviewed</summary>

An independent review checked the remaining OpenClaw ID strings, the sign-in presenter's callers and the deep-link handlers. The only extra path it found was removal recovery. That path is reachable only from state left behind by an earlier native-enabled build. It is gated in the second commit.
</details>

## Evidence

- Focused macOS tests ran on a Mac Studio host through Crabbox at `92a61e01ce00`: 71 tests in 6 suites. They cover the new skip-reachability page order, the existing enabled-build orders, status menu descriptors, first-run handling and OpenClaw ID removal. All new and changed expectations passed. `scripts/lint-swift.sh` passed.
- 5 cases of `onboarding installs only for an app-managed local Gateway` failed at `OnboardingViewSmokeTests.swift:188`. That assertion checks that no managed CLI exists at `~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw`, but the shared Studio has one installed for its live Gateway. This PR doesn't touch that assertion. CI on a clean runner should be authoritative.
- Gap: there are no screenshots of the shortened onboarding flow yet.

prs.title: feat: show planned automations and their controls in chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A text confirmation doesn't show which requested automations were saved or let you change their settings. Installing a template with multiple automations leaves a separate notice for every job.

## User Impact

Chat shows one compact card for one automation, or one grouped card for the request. Each planned row starts with a switch-shaped placeholder. Once saved, the row opens that job's settings and its switch is usable. A failed row stays in place with a red alert triangle and **Not created**, without controls.

## Why This Change Was Made

The agent or template installer declares the ordered plan before saving jobs. Results fill those rows by identity, not by timing or by matching chat text. Controls use the persisted job ID and viewer permissions. Reopening chat reconciles the card with current scheduler state. Ordinary chat doesn't wait for the optional card renderer before showing history.

## Evidence

**Two creation paths.** The matched captures below compare baseline `200bd90934ef` with the first verified candidate `1fed82508666`, using a real isolated Gateway, scheduler, agent and Chromium. No automations executed or notifications were sent.

- [One ordinary prompt, two different automations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66ba5ea2-2721-40ed-8284-feb0556c8fb7): one two-row card replaced plain text. The first switch worked while the second job was unsaved. In the natural run the first frame with both placeholders was 2.9 ms after the first observed save. A [separate controlled-timing replay](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/34273be4-086b-4fa5-aaf0-39f3e54b2461) made both placeholders visible while storage was still empty, without changing production timing.
- [Install the three-job Weekly Planner template](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b0d0394-531e-4c09-8b86-cc40dc9b23ad): one card replaced three notices. The installing window opens chat after Apply finishes. A [second paired window during that same install](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9278067d-38b4-4dd1-b564-ecab331d3857) captured one, two, then three switches without moving the rows. One-job requests stayed standalone; a native refusal and template collision produced inert failed rows.

**Upgrade and hard reload.** The published `v2026.11.6` package created a real conversation and a paused Friday archive. Replacing it on the same disposable state preserved IDs, message text and timestamps, Friday's 16:15 America/New_York schedule, and its paused state. One new prompt created Morning brief. Its own settings and switch worked without changing Friday archive. This was an exact-build replacement, not an update-channel selection test.

On an intermediate build, a hard refresh could leave the entire transcript loading despite the Gateway returning the saved jobs. Using the same upgraded conversation and Gateway, the repaired UI `822d08893059` restored all five message groups and the checked switch in 379 and 405 ms on two cache-bypassed reloads. Returning from settings worked too. Blocking only the optional card module still rendered the ordinary conversation, without inventing controls. **Published head `44767fb952ac` has the same source tree as `822d08893059`.**

**Review repairs and validation.** A proven no-effect validation failure releases its planned slot for retry; an uncertain dispatch does not. Scheduled creators retain their existing permissions and do not acquire a chat-only precondition. Wrapper dependency inventory and generated prompts were refreshed. All 54 scheduled-authority tests passed on the repair branch. The final reload repair passed 18 targeted tests, UI typechecks, lint and architecture guards. Paired builds with unchanged limits measured chat boot JS **−63 B gzip**, the same **21 requests**, and total CSS **−103 B gzip / −1,241 B raw**.

**Test-line allocation:** 995 additional lines beyond the default allocation cover scheduler receipt provenance, template rollback and collisions, durable chat replay, and the independent authority of each saved job's controls across layers.

prs.title: fix(windows): distinguish invalid Scheduled Task inspection responses
prs.body:
Related: #199617

## What Problem This Solves

Windows update failures report the same “invalid response” for malformed PowerShell JSON, invalid access facts, and an invalid task snapshot, hiding which inspection step failed.

## User Impact

Operators receive a specific, privacy-safe failure category in service errors and bounded update reports. Service-stop verification and existing refusal behavior remain unchanged.

**This is a diagnostic improvement, not a verified fix for the terminal-origin beta.2 → beta.3 update failure. The original failure category and root cause remain unknown. Native Windows proof of the patched diagnostic through the installed updater remains outstanding.** The inspecting runtime must contain the change; a newer candidate cannot change probes executed by an older installed updater.

Peter’s related mitigation [#199918](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199918) merged on November 16 as `ae678bf4c6b808b3ffc69b67e62d3a54c5e0d67f`. It refuses Gateway-started Windows Scheduled Task updates before mutation; it does not repair the terminal-origin invalid-response failure reported in #199617.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep classification in the existing Task Scheduler probe and formatting in the existing service-error owner. Attach a closed stage at each of the three existing invalid-response branches, then carry it through the existing service and report paths. The labels identify the failed inspection step, not its underlying cause. Emit no raw PowerShell output, task definitions, account values, or parser exception text; retain the generic message when no stage is available. Parsing acceptance, access checks, retries, state, and service mutations are unchanged.

## Evidence

The source remains `7b970278f1b469973fc59ce62c4e7bbabf391b28`. The November 20 follow-up changes this evidence description only; it does not claim a new implementation, new test execution, or a repaired Windows update.

### Original implementation evidence

Retained from the implementation report, not independently rerun during this evidence-only follow-up:

- Three synthetic native-response regressions fail on the unchanged implementation and pass with this patch. They distinguish JSON, access-fact, and snapshot failures while keeping a synthetic secret out of the error and cause.
- 99 focused tests passed across `schtasks-state-probe.test.ts`, `service-command-read.test.ts`, `update-command-service-report.test.ts`, and `update-command-service-unavailable.test.ts`, using `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1`. The report cases preserve the category within the 200-character failure-fact bound and assert that service stop/install/restart remain uncalled.
- Core production typecheck, services and config/CLI test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Auto Review (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2) assessed the complete local diff against `7d7d86bb79ca24bfaf9343290cb22f80d705ab20`: scoped-clean, no findings; it did not independently execute tests. The existing [hosted source review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199651#issuecomment-6897019692) also reports no findings on the unchanged published head. Neither review substitutes for native Windows proof.

### Incident and CI follow-up

- The [November 19 reporter update](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/199617#issuecomment-7023968687) confirms terminal-origin updates from installed 2026.11.5-beta.2 (`c0f42f6`) to beta.3. The retained failure report lacks the underlying native output, exit code, HRESULT, and elapsed time. Later successful probes in other contexts cannot identify which branch failed originally. No access, locale, execution-policy, CLIXML, or Windows Job cause is established.
- The exact-head [baseline-ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44079742929/job/134028115017) records GitHub’s hosted-runner communication-loss annotation; its log remains unavailable. The [ci-gate log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44079742929/job/134053671804) fails on that job and labels its main comparison as **job-name-only**, not matching failure signatures. **The required PR ci-gate remains red.** Successful lint/typecheck/changed-test checks do not make the overall gate green.
- The later [scheduled-main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44092629110/job/134072440272), at `f1d40db4d99bca224aac35d4f71a7d5dc925c216`, shows all ten ratchets passing in the available log tail. This follow-up independently compared its `checks-baseline-ratchets` job definition with this PR’s: identical definitions, but different events and source trees. That result neither proves this PR’s ratchets pass nor identifies the cause of its runner disconnect.
- The reporter separately summarizes November 19 R2 run `5df0df8e-88b7-48b0-a710-9ef95b671cc6`: installed 2026.11.5 (`e13cf15`) → 2026.11.10-beta.1, with npm/package-swap failures. Those artifacts were not retrieved in this follow-up; the comment supplies no artifact download links. This separate run is not evidence for the inspection error or this diagnostic patch.

**Remaining proof:** redacted output from a native Windows updater containing this patch must show the category reaching a bounded CLI/update report while inspection uncertainty still prevents mutation. The original beta.2 → beta.3 failure and a successful repair of that incident remain separate investigation work. No live Gateway/service changes or additional reporter update run were performed or requested here.

<details>
<summary>Simplification and follow-up validation</summary>

The requested `pr-simplify` pass reviewed the full diff against `7d7d86bb79ca24bfaf9343290cb22f80d705ab20`, direct callers, and the earlier inspection-diagnostic and Windows-access changes. No further source reduction was justified: the patch uses the existing probe, formatter, and report owners without adding a helper, logging pipeline, retries, or state. The generic no-stage diagnostic preserves the existing error contract.

Each test group protects a different failure: the probe tests catch lost classification and raw-output disclosure; service-command tests catch loss during strict command inspection/sanitization; report tests catch truncation or propagation loss and unintended service mutation. The native proof-helper schema change prevents its existing parser from stripping the optional stage; it is not proof that a native run occurred.

Whole-change delta remains production +15/-6, tests/support +73/-42, documentation +6/-0 across seven files. Follow-up source delta is zero. The imported tree exactly matches the published head, and `git diff --cached --check 7d7d86bb79ca24bfaf9343290cb22f80d705ab20` passes. Unchanged focused/type/lint/format evidence is reused rather than represented as freshly executed. Native Windows proof is still absent.

</details>

Reported and requested by Donniefi.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1956c2fd-32f7-43ce-bdd7-546240eba2b4)
- [Follow-up discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/235176eb-04cb-46e9-b356-c63ff16f0f5f)
- [Follow-up evidence rework and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/3f291ee2-7535-44a8-804a-43833e327c66)
