prs.title: fix(cli): avoid slow help with empty plugin config
prs.body:
Closes #114067

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw --help` loads the full config/runtime graph for a standalone `{"plugins":{}}` config even though it prints the same cached help as an absent config.

## User Impact

Root and `nodes` help can use the existing fast path with that empty plugin configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launcher admits only the strict-JSON standalone empty block. Meaningful plugin settings, dynamic config and dotenv side effects continue through the config owner. This removes unnecessary entry/config loading without adding a cache or another plugin policy. The existing startup benchmark now includes the reported workload and an explicitly selected disabled-plugins control.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: identical help output and zero runtime imports for the inert config, at least 20% lower median startup time, and no control median/p95/RSS regression above 20%. Five serial interleaved base/candidate rounds used the same official `cliStartup` build on Linux x64 with Node 24.22.1; one-minute host load ranged 8.09–8.76. Each sample used a fresh process and isolated state; source-launcher compile caching stays disabled by repository policy.

Workload: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-cli-startup.ts --case help --case helpInertPlugins --case helpDisabledPlugins --runs 1 --warmup 0 --timeout-ms 30000 --json`, repeated in A/B order.

| Config | Exit median, base → fix | Exit p95, base → fix | Range, base → fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Absent | 97.4 → 96.5 ms | 103.3 → 99.7 ms | 96.2–103.3 → 95.5–99.7 ms |
| Empty plugins | 2101.4 → 95.0 ms | 2271.6 → 124.0 ms | 2084.5–2271.6 → 89.0–124.0 ms |
| Plugins disabled | 2919.1 → 3052.6 ms | 3095.2 → 3127.3 ms | 2857.1–3095.2 → 2860.6–3127.3 ms |

Empty-config first-output median/p95 fell from 2037.1/2176.2 to 88.3/116.8 ms; median peak RSS fell from 193.2 to 53.8 MiB. The disabled-plugin control's median duration increased 4.6%; both controls satisfy the acceptance rule.

Official `pnpm --silent openclaw --help` checks (pinned Bun fork) separately confirmed 870 → 0 runtime dist modules and 1 → 0 entry loads for the inert config. Its 8,007-byte stdout matches absent-config help exactly. Disabled plugins retains 944 runtime modules and its distinct, unchanged 7,802-byte output. All six base/candidate invocations exit 0. CPU profiles also show runtime module work disappearing.

- Both launcher regressions fail on the base. Candidate launcher suite: 107 pass, one platform skip; startup harness: 15 pass.
- Official startup build, targeted strict types, lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Final response contracts and budget comparison against the same-machine base report pass.
- The checked-in x64 fixture gate reports no-config help latency above its historical baseline on both versions: base 96.2 ms and fix 103.7 ms versus fixture 53.1 ms. The gate remains unchanged; the five-round base/fix comparison above records the actual change.
- Independent P0–P3 review of the complete three-file change against `89ee0bd382d16` (local diff `5317025c00bf`): no findings.

### Latest-stable retained-config upgrade check

On Linux x64 with Node 24.22.1 and npm 11.19.1, installed `openclaw@2026.11.3` (the current npm/GitHub stable release) in an isolated npm prefix with `--allow-scripts=openclaw`. Ran installed root and `nodes` help, then replaced that temporary installation with the reviewed source checkout at `11072ba75bd7` using npm's local-source install. The candidate executes the reviewed launcher with the existing official `cliStartup` runtime (build metadata `89ee0bd`).

The same default `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`, containing `{"plugins":{}}` plus a newline, stayed byte-identical through installation replacement and every invocation: 13 checks, 15 bytes, SHA-256 `512bc81cb9f83d93d1e3a6668087087468e3c199ed5122a9c7c035b3fef4f65d`. All 10 help/version invocations exited 0 with empty stderr.

| Installed CLI | Root help | `nodes` help | Empty config vs. absent config |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Published stable `2026.11.3` | 7,897 bytes | 1,542 bytes | Both byte-identical |
| Candidate launcher `11072ba75bd7` | 8,007 bytes | 1,542 bytes | Both byte-identical |

Between the two installations, `nodes` help differs only in its build header; root help also differs in command inventory, wording and the support link. Each installation preserves its own help output with the retained empty-plugin config. The same-build base/fix comparison above separately verifies byte-identical output for this patch.

prs.title: fix(telegram): callback handling fails when button markup is unchanged
prs.body:
Related: #21898, #82347, #133166

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Telegram callback handling fails when editing or clearing buttons leaves the message's reply markup unchanged.

## User Impact

User impact: Repeated button updates can complete as a no-op instead of failing with Telegram's `400: message is not modified` error, allowing subsequent callback feedback to continue. Other Telegram errors still propagate.

## Why This Change Was Made

`editCallbackButtons` now uses the existing unchanged-message error predicate to treat an already-applied reply-markup edit as success. `clearCallbackButtons` shares this path. The change is limited to that idempotency guard and regression coverage for edit/clear operations; it does not change general callback ingress retry or lane recovery.

PR #21898 addresses related unchanged-message handling in a separate send/edit path. Issues #82347 and #133166 describe related callback retry/lane-blocking failures, but have different triggers; this PR does not claim to close them.

AI disclosure: The patch, regression tests and PR description were prepared by Pinchy, an AI agent running OpenClaw. Pinchy’s current main model is OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`); other models may have been used during the preparation process. This names the current main model, not a verified model for every historical run. Independent validation and testing were performed by Claude Code, identified by the host verifier as Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`), including the red/green tests, formatting, lint, extension typecheck and Telegram suite listed below. prs.title: improve: let ordinary agents run typed setup actions directly
prs.body:
Stacked on #202148. **Partial backend migration only:** full retirement of the legacy setup conversation remains pending a separate compatibility decision. This PR stays draft.

## What Problem This Solves

A regular agent's setup and configuration requests can currently go to another assistant for interpretation, even when the requesting agent already knows the exact action. This creates a separate conversation instead of returning the controlled operation's outcome to the agent doing the work.

## User Impact

Ordinary agents can use typed setup actions in their current workflow, with existing permissions, human approvals and consent controls. Creating another agent does not force a conversation handoff; missing-model readiness notices remain visible.

Legacy tool `message`/`sessionId`, public fuzzy `openclaw.chat`, and CLI `setup --message`/`--yes` behavior remain supported. Non-config actions retain live inference-owner checks. Typed calls require the admitted in-process Gateway tool context; no fallback grants broader execution. No public RPC, persisted schema, retention or permission change is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing typed action mapping, normal Gateway admission, exact proposal/approval manager, consent checks and operation executor instead of asking another assistant to choose the action. The tool schema is an object, omits `approved`, and rejects mixing typed actions with legacy conversation fields. Its private exact-request data carrier supplies operation data, not caller authority.

The existing approval owner applies standing grants or waits for the exact human decision. Denial, expiry and cancellation settle without a write; late approval cannot revive a cancelled request. Temporary state is disposed after settlement. Applied-operation audit and historic setup transcripts remain available; ordinary conversation input is not copied into the old machine-wide logbook. Protected sign-in, fixed-command recovery and first-agent provisioning retain their existing owners.

## Evidence

- The real tool → Gateway router → approval manager → configuration writer path covers automatic application, allow-once, deny, expiry, cancellation/late-approval rejection, unprivileged refusal, invalid config without helper inference, and refusal to self-broaden approval policy. Audit and old-history preservation are asserted. The new typed config case failed on the base with `message required`, then passed.
- **203 selected cases:** 202 passed in the full 10-file run; after the final readiness-notice adjustment, the three affected unit files passed 84 cases, including one new utility-only case. These are overlapping runs, not 286 independent tests. Unchanged Gateway/tool/prefix results were reused.
- Production typecheck, targeted production/test lint, formatting and whitespace checks passed. Full `GOMAXPROCS=2 pnpm build` passed, including declarations and public SDK checks.
- **Attributed inherited failure:** the Gateway-test typecheck exits 2 with exactly the same sole `ui/src/app/navigation-surface.ts(38,35)` / `HTMLElement.dismissPanel` diagnostic on clean predecessor `2d91c9d8ce7b0742eb992e6c640f92ec12e67f99` and this candidate, using the matching runner/config and installed dependencies. This file is left to PR2's owner; the failure is not waived.
- **Inherited UI budget findings:** the preceding fresh build reported CSS gzip 58,442 versus 58,315 bytes and chat boot JS requests 21 versus 20. Exact UI input comparison against the predecessor covered 9,827 files, including 4,058 consumed inputs, with no missing/different bytes. Both signatures match the actual build receipt `4f8279a9fb3bb9de72a29dae91a8650b0ce9d4153a8ef6234d2d778462ff4730`. Unchanged bundled-plugin UI outputs were reused; this is paired input proof, not a second browser/build run. No budget relaxation was made.
- **Supplemental independent source review completed:** the reviewer assessed all 15 changed files and relevant admission, operation, approval, execution, inference and transcript owners at `057c96418d73864aca74c14a19cd2a484a9ca42a` against `2d91c9d8ce7b0742eb992e6c640f92ec12e67f99`. No new likely P0/P1/P2 findings were identified. The assessment confirmed that typed input does not grant authority, approvals/cancellation retain their existing owners, legacy behavior is preserved, and typed calls avoid a second assistant turn or copying input into the old logbook. Independent checks covered all 39 declared action mappings, source/tree identity and `git diff --check`. The reviewer inspected the boundary-test assertions but did not rerun the author-reported executable suites. This is a narrative source assessment, not successful configured autoreview/ClawSweeper execution or landing approval. Bound Auto Review still fails before assessment on the diagnosed baseline `compat.cachesInstructions` configuration mismatch. Applicable security checks remain required; no hard-security CODEOWNERS path is changed by this incremental diff.
- **Unverified:** real regular-agent/model and worker execution, full stacked first-run/upgrade and native proof. No visual source changes or new screenshots are claimed. No ready, merge or deployment is authorized. Draft CI has not been claimed as passed.

prs.title: feat(gateway): connect approved trusted-proxy CLI and TUI devices within their grant
prs.body:
Related: #199692

Depends on #199698. This branch is stacked on it, so until #199698 merges the diff also shows its commits.

## What Problem This Solves

A device approved for fewer scopes than its client requests, such as a team guest approved for only `operator.sessions.write`, can't know its grant before it connects. Its first connection after approval therefore always files a scope-upgrade request, for scopes the admin already decided not to give.

## User Impact

User impact: with the new opt-in `gateway.auth.trustedProxy.narrowToDeviceGrant`, an approved CLI or TUI device behind the trusted proxy connects within its grant from the first connection. No upgrade request is filed and no audit entry is written. The TUI also keeps a device token, as the CLI already does. When named operator roles are enforced, a human operator identified by the proxy still receives no device token, as before; their CLI and TUI connect within the grant on every connection without storing it.

The option defaults to `false`, so existing Gateways behave exactly as before.

With the option on, `openclaw security audit` reports a new warn-level finding, because the TUI's token, like the CLI's, authenticates a direct Gateway connection without the proxy identity until the device is revoked.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Existing mechanism:** the Gateway already narrows a same-key scope upgrade to the paired grant, with no pairing request or audit entry, for browser and native UI clients when `trustedProxy.deviceAutoApprove` is enabled. This change gives that lane to CLI and TUI devices under its own option.

**Which connections it applies to:** same-key operator devices that authenticate through the trusted proxy and send no browser `Origin`. For those:
- A request that exceeds the grant connects with the intersection, and the hello reply reports the resulting scopes. That is how a newly approved device learns its grant.
- A connection never receives more than the grant. A request that includes `operator.admin` overlaps every grant, because admin implies every operator scope, so it connects within the grant.
- Only a request that shares no scope with the grant, such as `operator.pairing` alone against a session-only grant, still files the upgrade.
- Browser clients and new device enrollment are unchanged.

**TUI device token:** trusted-proxy auth treats the TUI like the Control UI and issued it no device token. Under the option it gets one, so it keeps the grant between runs. With the option off, its default, nothing changes. Named-role human operators stay tokenless either way.

**New audit finding:** `gateway.trusted_proxy_narrow_to_device_grant` (warn). `deviceAutoApprove` already reports a warn finding; this option reported nothing. The finding and `docs/gateway/trusted-proxy-auth.md` tell the admin to keep the proxy as the only Gateway ingress, and to remove a device with `openclaw devices remove <deviceId>` when its user's access ends.

**Config-surface budget, 2654 to 2655:** the option adds one boolean key, so the core count in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` grows by exactly one. It has to be an option rather than a default because it changes which connections file upgrade requests and which clients hold device tokens; existing admins rely on both. No existing key fits: `deviceAutoApprove` also auto-approves new device enrollment, which an admin who only wants guests to stay within their grant should not have to accept. No other config is added.

**Docs:** `docs/gateway/trusted-proxy-auth.md` gains a section for the option, its config reference entry and the audit checklist line. The section says that the option is off by default and that named-role human operators get no device token. `docs/start/multiplayer.md` points guests' admins to it. `docs/cli/tui.md` marks the TUI's trusted-proxy behavior without a device token as the default and links the option.

## Evidence

- **Server tests:** in `src/gateway/server.auth.trusted-proxy-device-autoapprove.test.ts` 20/20:
  - An approved session-only TUI connects within its grant and receives a device token, with no pending request and no upgrade audit line.
  - The same holds for a CLI requesting `operator.read`, which connects with `operator.sessions.read`.
  - With the option off, the TUI still files the upgrade.
  - Without the Gateway change, the TUI and CLI cases fail; the option-off case passes on both.
- **Audit test:** `src/security/audit-gateway-exposure.test.ts` 27/27, with the finding present only when the option is on. Without the finding, the new case fails. `audit-gateway.test.ts` 8/8.
- **Config tests:** `zod-schema.gateway-auth.test.ts` 57/57, `doc-baseline.integration.test.ts` 10/10, `configure.gateway.test.ts` 16/16. Typecheck, lint and format are clean.
- **Rebased on current `main` with #199693's pairing hint:** this branch is now on `main` at `3a3eed8695e` and includes `5ce6d65f695` and `49d8da05cf6`, #199693's `openclaw gateway call` hint for an unpaired edgeAuth device, which keeps an explicit `--url`. `git range-diff 987c04a0086..465d5ab0c3c origin/main..1c9cb58e474` shows all ten commits unchanged except the regenerated config baseline hashes in the gateway commit (the core count is still 2654 to 2655). The live run below was made at `4cce58081cc`, before the restacks. On `1c9cb58e474`, after a clean install: `server.auth.trusted-proxy-device-autoapprove.test.ts` 20/20, `audit-gateway-exposure.test.ts` 27/27, `audit-gateway.test.ts` 8/8, `zod-schema.gateway-auth.test.ts` 57/57, `doc-baseline.integration.test.ts` 10/10, `configure.gateway.test.ts` 16/16, `call.edge-auth.test.ts` 6/6, `call.stored-grant-scopes.test.ts` 5/5, `call.test.ts` 91/91, `gateway-chat.connection.test.ts` 16/16, `client.approved-grant.test.ts` 3/3, typecheck clean, config baseline check and line-cap ratchet OK.
- **Live run** at `4cce58081cc` (built with `pnpm build:runtime`): a loopback Gateway with `gateway.auth.mode: "trusted-proxy"`, behind a small TLS proxy standing in for Cloudflare Access (it answers 302 unless the request carries `Cf-Access-Token`, then injects the identity headers). The guest config has only `gateway.remote.url` and `gateway.remote.edgeAuth`: no token, no password, no stored device token. `--tls-fingerprint` is there only because the test proxy uses a self-signed certificate. The output is trimmed, and IDs and ports are from throwaway test state. The admin approves only `operator.sessions.write`, and the Gateway has `narrowToDeviceGrant: true`. The branch includes #199693 and #199698, rebased on current `main`.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep the transport identity on an oversized history placeholder
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`chat.history` replaces any message over `CHAT_HISTORY_MAX_SINGLE_MESSAGE_BYTES` (128 KiB) with a bounded placeholder. That placeholder rebuilds `__openclaw` from an allowlist — `toolOutput`, `id`, `runId`, `seq`, `idempotencyKey`, `turnBoundary`, `transcriptPosition` — and `transport` was not on it.

For a client that locates the turn it started by the channel message id (`__openclaw.transport.messageId`), a large inbound message therefore lost its anchor: the entry was still there, but every identifier it could match on was gone except the derived `idempotencyKey`. Clients had to reverse the derivation instead of reading the field.

The fix keeps the transport identity, projected to the three identifiers a client actually matches on — `channel`, `accountId`, `messageId` — so the placeholder stays bounded instead of copying whatever else a channel may attach to `transport` (the test pins that an unknown extra field is dropped). Nothing else about the placeholder changes: same sentinel text, same cap check by the caller, same `truncated`/`reason` markers, and metadata-free remains the fallback when even the reduced envelope is over budget. `Closes #201645`.

## Evidence

Red first — the new case in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-budget.test.ts` on the base commit fails with the placeholder's `__openclaw` missing `transport` (`Tests 2 failed | 5 passed`; the same file runs in two lanes).

After the change, on `9e3936872`:

- `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-budget.test.ts` → **7 passed**
- the surrounding history suites (`chat-history-response-page`, `chat-display-projection`, `server.chat.gateway-server-chat-history`, `chat-abort.history-budget`, `server.chat-history-cursor`) → **5 files / 112 passed**
- `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --openclaw-focused-config <2 files>` → 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-methods.json` → no diagnostic in the touched files
- `scripts/run-format.mts --check` → clean

The pinned case is the reported scenario: a 4 KB `user` message (budget 1 KB) carrying `transport: { channel, accountId, messageId, extra }` — the placeholder keeps the three identifiers, drops `extra`, and still reports `truncated` / `reason: "oversized"`.

Net test-line growth: 25 lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/201645-chat-history-oversized-transport-identity.txt`.

prs.title: improve(ios): rebuild the chat transcript around the web reading model
prs.body:
## Problem

On long, tool-heavy sessions the iOS chat fell well short of the web Control UI:

- Scrolling back stopped after the first history page. `olderCursor` was never decoded, so older pages were never requested.
- Every tool call between messages was its own card. Completed turns had no "Worked for <duration>".
- Subagent spawns showed only the wrapper card: no "Launched <name>" row and no way to open the child.
- `sessions_yield` acknowledgments were hidden under "Tool details". Failed commands showed no exit code.
- Raw paths and plain `#123` appeared instead of file and PR chips.
- The header had no session title. The composer read "Message main…" (the agent id) and cut the model name.
- Assistant replies sat in cards capped at 560 pt, and iPad width depended on size classes.

## Solution

One transcript model, with the web UI as the guide:

- **Layout:** assistant replies span one reading column, and user messages keep a tinted bubble. One width rule uses the measured pane width `w`:
  - margin 16 pt, or 24 pt from 700 pt;
  - column `min(768, w − 2·margin)`;
  - user bubble 82% of the column, or 68% above 600 pt.

  This deletes `openClawAssistantBubblesInCleanChrome`, `openClawAssistantUsesReadingColumn`, the assistant card style with its seam drawing, and `readingColumnWidth` / `usesExpandedLayout` / `expandedHorizontalMargin`.
- **Container:** iOS keeps `List` (#192232).
  - Older pages load after an upward scroll within ~1200 pt of the top, and the reading position is restored after the prepend.
  - Rows are deduped by `__openclaw.id`, then `seq`.
  - "Show earlier" appears only after a failed load.
- **Tool activity:**
  - A completed turn folds into one "Worked for <d>" row (web `chat-turn-presentation.ts`).
  - Adjacent tool rows in unfolded turns become one "Ran commands, read files" disclosure.
  - Subagent launches always stay visible as "Launched <name>" rows that open the child.
  - A confirmed `sessions_yield` shows its acknowledgment.
  - Commands read "Ran <cmd>", with "Exit code N" on failure.
  - Continuation rows keep a multi-run turn together.
- **Chips:** file references and GitHub items in message bodies get chips, following the web markdown rules. PR merge state is not fetched; chips use the web's unknown-state look.
- **Chrome:**
  - the session title shows in the navigation bar;
  - the composer placeholder uses the agent identity name from `agent.identity.get`;
  - the model label is readable.
- **Reply footer:** relative time. Exact time, duration, tokens, cost, context and model sit behind a tap, like the web tooltip.

Newly decoded fields, all already sent by the Gateway, so there is no schema change: `olderCursor`, `hasMore`, `__openclaw.seq`, `recordTimestampMs`, `customType`, `continuation`, tool `exitCode`.

**References and what we didn't adopt:**
- T3 Code mobile: per-turn fold.
- opencode-mobile/opencode-mobile: prepend restore.
- Ice Cubes: `List` with re-anchoring by id.
- Not adopted: a UIKit collection-view host, a manual-only "Load earlier" button, lazy tool loading (needs a new Gateway API), and multiple timeline styles.

## Evidence (draft: more to come)

- **Real session, iPad 13" simulator:** 35 history pages, 4,414 messages, 2,199 tool calls.
  - Scrolling back reaches the first turn in about 30 swipes.
  - All 161 user messages render; the web DOM also has 161.
  - Every subagent launch is visible: 55 rows for 57 spawns.
  - The other row kinds are within a few rows of the web.
- **Replay:** feeding all 35 pages through the view model keeps every one of the 4,414 messages.
- **Scroll workload** (iPad simulator, behavior probe, 120 slow swipes each way):

  | | main (1 page) | this PR (35 pages) |
  |---|---|---|
  | Bubble body evaluations | 10.1/s | 1.6/s |
  | Long frame gaps per 1,000 frames | 58.2 | 48.8 |
  | Viewport jumps | 0 | 1 |

  These numbers predate the scroll-owner change below; prepend behavior is now measured by `prepend-no-jump`.
- **OpenClawKit (macOS `swift test`):** 2,700 of 2,705 pass. The 5 failures are timing tests under full-suite load: 2 audio-player tests that also fail on `main`, plus TLS cancellation and canonical-history tests that pass when run alone.
- **iOS unit tests (iPhone 17 simulator):** 1,117 pass. The one failure, the audio case of `managed assistant media starts its artifact load with the playback route`, also fails on `main`: since #196787 audio loads only after Play is tapped, and the test still expects an automatic load.
- **macOS:** the package and test targets build.

Still pending:
- before/after screenshots from synthetic fixtures (iPhone and iPad);
- the AdaptiveLayoutUITests matrix, including accessibility text sizes;
- device Animation Hitches and before/after phone traces (`ChatScrollPerformanceUITests`, dedicated iPhone);
- a macOS test run.

## Scroll, gesture and redraw ownership

On a phone the transcript bounced on expand/collapse, could scroll while the sidebar opened, and redrew every row on unrelated state changes. Five writers set the scroll offset independently (reader run anchor, synchronous follow, paging restore, bottom-pin `follow`, scroll commands), and two gestures (the shell's SwiftUI drag and the transcript's pan) ran at once.

- **One scroll owner:** `ChatReadingPosition` (pure policy `ChatReadingPolicy` + a UIKit adapter on the transcript's collection view) is the only code that writes the transcript offset on iOS. `ChatReaderRunAnchor.swift`, `ChatSynchronousFollow.swift`, the paging restore and the bottom-pin writer are deleted. Rules:
  - following: stay at the bottom as rows stream in;
  - reading: hold the top visible row, no write unless rows above it changed;
  - expand/collapse: the tapped header keeps its screen position;
  - older-page prepend: hold the distance from the end of the content, so `List`'s own compensation is never counted twice;
  - the transcript scroller has a directional lock, so a sideways swipe never scrolls it.
- **One drawer gesture owner:** `SidebarDrawerPanRecognizer` opens the sidebar only from a 44 pt leading-edge zone below the nav-bar row; the transcript's pan waits for it to fail. The shell's SwiftUI `DragGesture` is gone.
- **Rows redraw only on their own content:** Gateway health, link previews, the agent name and the drawer flag no longer reach every row's inputs.

**Accepted edge:** when an older page lands mid-fling, the reader's scroll in the ~2 frames where `List` changes the content is not kept (8.4–8.8 pt measured). There `List`'s compensation cannot be told apart from the reader's scroll (it can land before the content height changes); an attempt to observe the offset during that window adopted `List`'s write and jumped ~1,500 pt, so it was reverted. `prepend-no-jump` stays a `bad` case for this.

**Measurement tooling** (DEBUG, only with `--openclaw-behavior-probe`): offset-writer attribution and signposts (`ChatScrollInstrumentation`), drawer-pan marks, and four `pnpm ios:behavior` cases with gates; plus `ChatScrollPerformanceUITests` (XCTHitchMetric) for device hitch runs.

**Behavior cases** (iPhone 17 simulator, 3 samples each, same seeded 40-turn chat):

| Case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `sidebar-open-still` (edge swipe and button) | passes | passes 3/3 |
| `swipe-right-still` (40 pt drift down and up) | passes | passes 3/3 |
| `disclosure-header-still` | header and drawn rows move up to 71 pt (bottom-pin writer) | header 0 pt, rows 0.2 pt, no offset writes; now a `guard` |
| `prepend-no-jump` | no restore owner | one `ReadingPosition.prepend` write per landing; −8.4 to −8.8 pt on the first prepend, 0 on the second (gate ≤ 4 pt, stays `bad`) |
| `stream-turn` (8 samples) | passes | passes 8/8, 0 pt drawn movement |

The simulator's synthetic drags never start the transcript's own pan, so the sidebar and swipe cases pass on `main` too: they guard the fix but don't reproduce the device bug. Device hitch numbers are pending on a dedicated iPhone.

Offset writers during the prepend case, all samples: `user` (reader), `system:…UpdateCoalescingCollectionView…` (`List`), and `ReadingPosition.prepend`. No other writer.

**Streamed list items stopped re-fading.** `ChatStreamingAssistantTextBody` swapped a plain render for a `TimelineView` whenever a word reveal started or caught up between chunks. That rebuilt the subtree, and every list item in the streaming reply (each holds its own reveal state) faded in again from zero. On this branch the finished bullets blinked in 2 of 8 `stream-turn` runs (read by the screen check as a 55 pt move); `main` has the same code but didn't trigger it in 5 runs. One `TimelineView`, paused while idle, keeps the identity; 8/8 runs clean after. `stream-turn`'s early drawn window now spans three 40 pt strips, so the setup gate stops failing when the reply draws sooner.

## Impact

macOS shares `OpenClawChatUI`:
- the reply footer becomes a tap popover, matching the web;
- the QuickChat user bubble uses the tinted surface;
- the desktop column is 768.

prs.title: fix(infra): collect idle worker heap capacity growth
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a busy task burst, an idle worker can keep a large allocated V8 heap even though most of its objects are gone. This can leave OpenClaw using more memory between tasks on small devices.

## User Impact

Workers also become eligible for idle collection when their allocated heap capacity has grown. The intended benefit is lower memory between bursts; collection can consume CPU and slow the next request, so both costs are explicit acceptance gates below. No operator setting or migration is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing idle-GC owner compares only `heapUsed` and `external` with the last successful collection. Include `heapTotal` in the same 32 MiB growth check, keeping the one-second delay, cancellation, in-progress guard and post-success baseline. The baseline updates after every successful collection even if V8 keeps its capacity, so an unchanged large heap does not schedule repeated collections.

## Evidence

- Runtime: `src/infra/worker-idle-gc.ts`, net +2 lines. No configuration, dependency, schema or worker-limit changes.
- Tests: extend the existing sequential threshold test for capacity-only growth, exact threshold, cancellation, timer recheck, nonshrinking collection and deferred collection. Existing native held/released payload and task cleanup tests remain in the focused proof. Net +56 test lines; the buffered-admission cancellation case is included separately.
- Measurement tooling: new committed `scripts/perf/discovery-worker-idle-measure.mjs`, reusing the existing discovery fixture and exact raw-record oracle. It supplies repeatable compiled-worker evidence; it is not a shipped runtime abstraction. It adds 465 verification-tool lines, counted separately from runtime and tests.
- Behavioral proof: the new capacity assertion fails against A on Node and Bun. Candidate coverage totals 17 unique passing tests per runtime: the original 16 tests, the corrected threshold test replay, and the buffered-admission cancellation case. No candidate tests were skipped. Formatting, runtime/test/script lint, core/infra-test/script types, syntax, line limits and both unused-file scans pass.
- The initial proof found a test-only promise type mismatch and a Node MessagePort lint false positive. Both were corrected and the affected checks passed; the original partial proof remains identified by SHA-256 `f12e2655fceeaa62552af374c7955e0daed5a9f197d5244a592d87cf2faac691`.
- Full build passed in 279.026 seconds with `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=0`; declaration generation, UI build and export/bootstrap checks ran. The final 53-row proof has SHA-256 `66b63f1916ad05945baa8b6d3458a50d3c745c1bf3c2b82f3de1e1fea5573b42`, all 15 stages exited zero, all 39 source pins match the signed candidate, and native cleanup completed. No performance samples have run.
- The build reports seven Control UI budget advisories: largest JS and CSS gzip, total CSS gzip and raw, chat boot JS requests and gzip, and new boot JS gzip. These are disclosed, not attributed to this patch; the declared A/B build comparison will retain both sets of measurements.
- Exact committed-source review: one complete independent pass, zero actionable findings. This is source review, not performance evidence. Hosted review and required CI remain pending.

Release-note context: idle worker collection also notices growth in allocated V8 heap capacity. A reduction in post-idle memory is the proposed benefit; the comparison below must establish it and bound CPU and next-request costs before landing. The release owner maintains `CHANGELOG.md`.

### Performance acceptance declared before measurement

This remains a draft until required correctness, review, CI and performance gates pass. Prior held experiments are not acceptance evidence for this change. No regression waiver is implied.

#### Frozen inputs and workload

- A: `0b4d5d08b689296514e61d5f5d9a18ec3c511529`, tree `a3a70d445009447ed170012ad267d9a220838841`.
- B: `bad303c69d8f9f6512e254bfad73c780c0147100`; tree `a8015aca47b6bee4d02d0e50f2fa1376ad7081a1`; reviewed full binary diff SHA-256 `2a14f8a065a1a59f662821745b16f43c09daa8c06991e2047f86130f8edce3ad`.
- Committed workload SHA-256 `ec463f72303a407f7f96427622b7fb366a31a0a977cd035b514f855ba75b6597`. Private collection controller and evaluator are frozen before dispatch, with their hashes recorded in the results.
- Exact Node 24.22.1 on Linux x64, pnpm 12.15.0, unchanged default worker heap limits. Every measured child has empty `NODE_OPTIONS`, the compiled worker uses `execArgv: []`, and each child receives a fresh empty compile-cache directory. Build-time inherited heap flags are recorded separately.
- Both exact revisions are installed and fully built before any child runs. Complete tracked-source, installed-dependency and generated-build seals are checked per arm before and after collection. Installed package content and arm-local links must match after the declared path normalization; the two installer metadata files remain bound by each arm's full seal. No shared writable dependency hardlinks.
- Six independent pairs, twelve fresh child processes, serial order **AB, BA, AB, BA, AB, BA**. No replacement or adaptive additional samples.
- One fixed synthetic workload: four workspaces, each with 100 local skills and the same 100 plugin contributions; production-default 256,000-byte skill-read limit. Each child performs **101 scans, five seconds idle, 101 scans, five seconds idle, then one next scan**: 203 exact-oracle passes. The raw results preserve 300 provenance records and 200 effective names per workspace; path, content hash, description, source, publication directory and key order are verified.
- Five worker memory messages: the initial unsolicited sample plus four requested burst/idle boundary samples. The production memory port reads heap counters and heap-space statistics. No GCProfiler, task GC metrics, heap snapshots, observer-forced GC or source loader runs in the worker. Production idle GC remains active.
- Process RSS sampling every 20 ms plus endpoints. The complete child and joined worker exit are required. Every exclusive fixture/cache is removed and absence is recorded. Failed, timed-out or incomplete children invalidate the campaign.

#### Fixed metrics and estimator

Each item below is a separate acceptance metric; lower is better. The estimator is fixed before results: arm median and nearest-rank p95 across the six independent child summaries. With six children this p95 is the observed maximum, not a reliable tail estimate. Report every child's raw value, all six matched-pair absolute/percentage deltas, their median and range. Undefined percentages from zero baselines are identified separately. Never pool the 101 scans as independent children.

| Family | Separate metrics | Count |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Startup | elapsed, process CPU, main-thread CPU | 3 |
| Two complete bursts | elapsed, process CPU, main-thread CPU for each burst, including verification | 6 |
| First requests | first scan and first scan after idle: elapsed, process CPU, main-thread CPU | 6 |
| Warm scan latency | median and nearest-rank p95 of the remaining 100 scan latencies in each burst, computed within each child first | 4 |
| Two idle intervals | elapsed, process CPU, main-thread CPU for each interval, including after-burst sampling | 6 |
| Two inclusive resumptions | elapsed, process CPU, main-thread CPU from the idle timer wake, through after-idle sampling, to the next first reply before verification | 6 |
| Final next scan | elapsed, process CPU, main-thread CPU from dispatch to reply | 3 |
| End to end | elapsed, process CPU, main-thread CPU from worker creation through the final verified scan | 3 |
| Process RSS | ready, after each burst, after each idle, after final next scan, sampled peak | 7 |
| Worker allocated heap capacity | `heapTotal` after each idle | 2 |
| **Total** | **46 metrics, median and observed maximum: 92 acceptance cells** | **46** |

The primary benefit requires both **second-idle process RSS median** and **second-idle worker `heapTotal` median** to be strictly lower in B. Fresh A must reproduce unused allocated capacity: the median of each child's second-idle `heapTotal - heapUsed` must exceed 32 MiB. This is not resident memory or proof of an unobserved GC baseline. First-to-second idle capacity changes are reported diagnostically; A need not shrink after its first burst. A failure to reproduce is inconclusive, not evidence of a benefit.

Any adverse acceptance cell is **HOLD**, including small changes that may be noise. Any adverse cell at or above **20%** is **STOP**; use exact decimal comparisons on the recorded numbers. A zero baseline with a positive candidate is STOP; both zero is unchanged. Both primary improvements, no adverse cells and all execution/provenance gates are required for performance acceptance. Report every movement; do not drop outliers, change the estimator or run replacement children after observing results. Investigate failures separately rather than rerun until green.

Additional diagnostics are disclosed separately: per-scan values and within-child summaries; worker live heap, external/ArrayBuffer bytes, heap spaces and limits; initial/pre-worker state; sample send/receive gaps, idle timer overrun, RSS sampling gaps, host resources/load and all build advisories. These do not silently replace the named gates. Raw timer intervals must be at least 4,990 ms; the requested delay is 5,000 ms.

#### Interpretation limits

This measures an isolated discovery component process, not a deployed Gateway, concurrent foreground traffic or device-wide memory. RSS includes the parent, its verification/report data and worker. V8 `heapTotal` is allocated heap capacity, not a measurement of resident worker bytes; never subtract or add it to RSS. Sampling may miss peaks. Boundary sampling and verification can extend idle time; inclusive resumption timing owns the sampling delay before the next request. Five seconds of idle does not prove GC settlement, and this workload does not observe major-GC completion.

Filesystem and shared build caches are not flushed; fresh process and compile-cache state does not mean a cold OS cache. Both arms use the same observer and fixture. A lower post-idle RSS does not establish lower peak memory under load, and more aggressive low-memory GC may increase idle CPU or clear optimization caches. Those costs remain acceptance gates.

---

## Completed comparison: STOP — not eligible to land

The predeclared comparison completed on November 20, 2026 against the exact candidate above. The original 10,488-byte declaration remains the unchanged prefix of this body (SHA-256 `b4f7d25a446de9ab391763046215da0fe1018e4f158723911cc2853b063f6834`). No samples were replaced or excluded.

**Numeric verdict: STOP.** All 12 children completed all 203 verified scans (2,436 total), with 50 adverse acceptance cells out of 92; two crossed the frozen 20% stop threshold. Burst-1 idle process CPU observed maximum increased from 113.284 to 153.021 ms (+35.077328%); burst-2 idle main-thread CPU observed maximum increased from 41.356 to 53.834 ms (+30.172164%). These small-sample estimates trigger the declared rule; they do not establish a persistent population regression.

The fresh-baseline premise also failed: median second-idle unused allocated worker heap was 3,339,632 bytes (3.184921 MiB), below the required >32 MiB. Second-idle component RSS median decreased from 128.507812 to 126.789062 MiB (−1.337467%), but worker heapTotal medians were equal at 22.394531 MiB, so the two required strict median wins were not achieved. Two baseline children retained high second-idle capacity; none of the six candidate children did. The observed maximum second-idle RSS fell 57.242293%, but six samples do not establish a robust tail benefit and do not override STOP.

All 22 preparation/build/measurement stages ended with exit 0, no signal, timeout, or reported error. The final controller report is complete, `cleanupUnknown=false`; both fixture worktrees were removed with exit 0 and verified absent, all 12 child fixture cleanups passed, and both arms' source/dependency/build final seals equal their premeasurement seals. The local agent daemon restarted during collection after nine displayed results; the original remote run continued unchanged. Its SSH/native/wrapper process chain and source capsule subsequently disappeared naturally, and the existing native copy route retrieved the final archive with exit 0. The original local tool-session exit code was lost in that restart and is not represented as recovered.

### Evidence identities and build qualification

- Archive: 969,887 bytes, 37 unique regular members, SHA-256 `1187976811fbfe4b1235dba245087a3370011ab6430efe9b468596c4e0976bd1`.
- Controller report: 300,123 bytes, SHA-256 `ba43b588f338388f18746870f37621e969f1605466355977a44db36faa8d7653`.
- Frozen analyzer output: 293,894 bytes, SHA-256 `dd97b92008ca6069be99c679a5143737a21af96445a03a9ecf701d923a43d2cf`.
- Frozen analyzer: SHA-256 `fa8a542fb5c549f03a4c2820033c415874887861a3b753bf9eaa66c83c011c86`.
- A/B full builds passed in 382.141709/325.147254 seconds with `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=0` (declaration generation retained). Their log hashes are `329b622cce3f5d8594a341bcb00ff223e8683ed14a14a519badbb012414e211d` / `28ff481abe844c159c389cc388f71077b75cd02dd331fcf6b04595a970bfb8ae`.
- Independently installed dependency contents match after the declared arm-path normalization and exclusion of `.modules.yaml` / `.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json`: 111,327 files, 5,165 links, 2,804,487,654 bytes; SHA-256 `780b2ceb977e27548f6c7bd4a212b9169bee7572087e9f46803feb5c50be59f6`. Each excluded metadata file and each full physical install remain bound separately in the report.

|Arm|Source seal|Full dependency seal|Build seal|
|---|---|---|---|
|A|`15c106cc6bed626a675c3d3761337241d00668d19ce1ef46c5ac875c6acc6ab1`|`08dcd9a002eaa7b895c322476763277ff3425b91dd2badf7e9267fdc4a56d038`|`15c2b14eb4d15ce8290c9b098f126b8e1650798d40edb9aa6de3cfcd01d37863`|
|B|`ea0effe729af4bbef0c9598df6d7256de05402ff723bd314437a26838885baa8`|`d843138b845c9d3cb8ac960175172328af45509304cbca6e1f651fc3a63f90d6`|`fe82ced01ead8f27d8d71cd07336a7fdef5cf355ce3be0dcae93dd03b459ed32`|

All seven UI budget advisories and their underlying asset values are identical between A and B: largest ordinary JS 564.3 KiB (limit 563.7); largest CSS 58,604 bytes (58,315); total CSS gzip 339,102 bytes (337,312), raw 1,748,419 bytes (1,740,234); chat boot 21 requests (20), gzip 1,334,415 bytes (1,332,637); new boot gzip 822,653 bytes (822,243). They are inherited baseline advisories in this comparison.

### Complete numerical disclosure

All rows below preserve the frozen metric roles. Memory values are MiB; durations/CPU are ms; host loads are dimensionless. Values are rounded to six decimal places only for display; decisions used the frozen Decimal evaluator before rounding. `max` is the declared nearest-rank p95 of six child summaries. Warm-latency median/p95 are first calculated within each child from its 100 warm scans; those child summaries are then aggregated. A positive delta is adverse for acceptance rows. `HOLD` marks any adverse aggregate and `STOP` marks an aggregate at least 20% higher. Diagnostic movements are disclosed without becoming acceptance gates.

In child tables each vector is pair 1 through 6, irrespective of execution order (AB, BA, AB, BA, AB, BA). Absolute deltas and percentages are paired B−A. Raw vectors retain all children; ranges and medians describe these six paired differences, not pooled scans.

<details><summary>Acceptance: all aggregate cells</summary>

|startup.elapsedMs (ms)|237.102869 → 249.856446; 12.753576 (5.378921%)|276.829485 → 297.927571; 21.098086 (7.621329%)|median HOLD, max HOLD|
|startup.processCpuMs (ms)|335.9575 → 340.387; 4.4295 (1.31847%)|384.664 → 407.59; 22.926 (5.960007%)|median HOLD, max HOLD|
|startup.mainCpuMs (ms)|4.34 → 4.4755; 0.1355 (3.12212%)|4.858 → 5.757; 0.899 (18.505558%)|median HOLD, max HOLD|
|nextScan.elapsedMs (ms)|252.30402 → 266.081666; 13.777645 (5.460732%)|274.441203 → 295.857177; 21.415974 (7.803484%)|median HOLD, max HOLD|
|nextScan.processCpuMs (ms)|268.2295 → 292.296; 24.0665 (8.972354%)|308.913 → 326.802; 17.889 (5.790951%)|median HOLD, max HOLD|

### Disposition and remaining limitations

PR remains draft and blocked by the predeclared performance STOP. The tested head remains `bad303c69d8f9f6512e254bfad73c780c0147100`; no threshold, sample count, policy, runtime limit, or source was changed after measurement. There is no automatic retry or landing request.

Hosted review on that exact head reported no actionable finding; it did not waive the performance requirement. CI completed with 34 successful jobs, 29 skipped jobs and two failed jobs: the concrete failure is the intentional-lint-suppression inventory missing the new Node MessagePort annotation, plus the aggregate gate reporting that failure. Both UI E2E jobs passed. The inventory-only housekeeping correction is deferred because the candidate is rejected by performance; skipped jobs are not counted as passed validation.

This is a compiled discovery component process under the declared synthetic corpus, not deployed Gateway or small-device RSS. `heapTotal` is allocated V8 capacity, not measured physical residency. Boundary memory sampling reads heap-space counters; no GC completion or post-major-GC state is inferred. Inclusive idle/resumption CPU and wall clocks include sampling waits, so those costs were not hidden from acceptance.

Named follow-up, separate from this rejected candidate: test the owner-level sequence where a successful idle collection establishes a baseline while a large payload remains live, then a later task releases that payload without growing heapTotal/external beyond that baseline. Current evidence does not establish a failure in that sequence; repeated-GC avoidance remains intentional. The independent discovery path-index candidate proceeds separately, without importing this GC change.

## What Problem This Solves

Skills showed one flat grid. Opening a result could show a setup dialog, a file editor, or release notes depending on where it came from. There was no consistent page to read or link to.

Browse Trending, Installed, and Skill library shelves or search across them. Open any card to read its rendered `SKILL.md` on a dedicated page. Reload keeps the page open; Back restores the previous query or shelf. Management and editing stay in Settings.

Reuse the Plugins catalog controls and detail layout. The reader gets the document from the installed skill, library entry, or selected ClawHub publisher and release. Search updates the current history entry without replacing the focused input.

prs.title: fix(cron): keep an execution-only failure out of the delivery diagnostics
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An isolated cron turn that fails with a fatal structured payload skips normal outbound delivery on purpose (`src/cron/isolated-agent/run-finalize.ts`: the structured-error branch returns `delivered: false` without a delivery error). Both places that author a run's delivery state still did:

```ts
error: result.deliveryError ?? result.error
```

so the *execution* error was handed to `resolveDeliveryState` as the *delivery* error. The resolver's `runStatus === "error" && delivered !== undefined` branch keeps whatever error it was given, and the run's execution error ended up in `lastDeliveryError` / `deliveryError` on the finished event — two diagnostic categories carrying one failure, with a delivery status the run never reached. The same resolver already says a run error is not delivery's error when no delivery has been reported; this is the branch that slipped past it.

The fix is one predicate, `resolveDeliveryDiagnosticError`, used by both authoring paths (`applyCronRunOutcome` and `authorCronRunCompletion`):

- a recorded `deliveryError` always wins;
- an execution error only stands in for a delivery error when the run did not report that it skipped dispatching (`deliveryAttempted === false` means the run has no delivery error of its own);
- everything else keeps today's behaviour, including the verified-send control and the failed-run evidence that carries `delivered: true` with unverified delivery.

Nothing else changes: run status, `lastError`, failure alerts, suppression reasons and the "do not announce structured provider errors" guard are untouched. `Closes #201999`.

## Evidence

Red first — the new `src/cron/service/timer-outcome-delivery-error.test.ts` on the base commit: `2 failed | 1 passed`, both failures `expected 'SYNTHETIC_PROVIDER_RATE_LIMIT' to be undefined` (one through `applyJobResult`, one through `authorCronRunCompletion`).

After the change, on `28e5a1653`:

- `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/cron/service/timer-outcome-delivery-error.test.ts` → **3 passed**
- the surrounding cron suites (`timer.regression`, `service.failure-alert`, `service.manual-delivery`, `service.persists-delivered-status`, `service.restart-delivery`, `service.trigger-eval`, `timer-outcome-finalization.receipts`, `run-recovery`, `timer.batch-finalization`, `timer.pacing`) → **11 files / 136 passed**, including `persists failed-run delivery evidence (verified=false)`, which keeps reporting the run error when the run did report a delivery.
- `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --openclaw-focused-config <4 files>` → 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json` → no diagnostic in the touched files (the `@openclaw/fs-safe` and `config/io.audit.ts` diagnostics are pre-existing on this checkout)
- `scripts/run-format.mts --check` → clean

Three cases are pinned in the test: a dispatch that never ran keeps `lastDeliveryError` empty while `lastError` stays, the completion author agrees, and a dispatcher-recorded delivery error is still reported verbatim.

Net test-line growth: 87 lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/201999-cron-delivery-diagnostic-error.txt`.

prs.title: fix: keep proxy-signed-in automations running after proxy settings change
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a Gateway sits behind a trusted proxy, an automation created from an authenticated chat records the Gateway's shared-auth "generation". For trusted-proxy Gateways this value is only a hash of the proxy admission settings (`userHeader`, `requiredHeaders`, `allowUsers`, `allowLoopback`, `trustedProxies`). Every later run had to match that hash exactly. Any change to those settings therefore refused each of these automations permanently, even one that only tightens access, like adding a required header. The jobs were then auto-disabled with "The operator authority that created this automation was refused … Cause: Restart recovery authentication owner changed".

This also happens on upgrade when the deployment layer changes the rendered proxy settings. For example, a newer OpenClaw Enterprise controller adds `gateway.auth.trustedProxy.requiredHeaders: [x-openclaw-scopes]` to Gateways that enable HTTP chat. The saved configuration doesn't change, but the proxy settings the Gateway runs with do, and so does their hash. Every proxy-created automation saved before the upgrade is then refused and disabled at its next run.

## User Impact

User impact: automations created through trusted-proxy authentication keep running after proxy transport settings change. This covers both upgrades that change rendered proxy settings and operator edits. They are still refused when the proxy user's access actually changes: removal from `allowUsers`, changed identity scopes, or the Gateway leaving trusted-proxy mode. Rotating a shared token or password still refuses jobs created with that credential. Jobs that were already auto-disabled with this error keep their saved authority, so the owner can re-enable them with `openclaw automations edit <id> --enable` once this ships; they don't need to be recreated. Re-enabling does not change the job's execution revision, so the saved source is kept.

## Why This Change Was Made

Saved operator sources already carry the grant fingerprint for the proxy user (`authPolicy`). That fingerprint records whether trusted-proxy mode is on, whether the user is still in `allowUsers`, the user's identity scopes and the browser-origin decision. It is rechecked on every restore. Live proxy clients already follow this rule: a proxy policy change only revokes them when `allowUsers` or the password fallback changes (`resolveSharedAuthInvalidation`). Restoring a saved automation was the one path that still compared the raw handshake hash. Restore now skips that comparison for sources authenticated by the proxy itself (`authMethod: "trusted-proxy"`, with no OpenClaw ID principal) and relies on the saved grant check. Token and password sources, password fallback behind a proxy (`authMethod: "password"`) and OpenClaw ID tunnel sources keep the exact generation check.

Tradeoff: a saved proxy automation now survives `trustedProxies`, `userHeader`, `requiredHeaders` and `allowLoopback` changes. These settings control which requests the proxy hop admits, not who the saved user is. New connections still face the new rules. Adding a required header only tightens admission for new requests, so it should not retire work an allowed user already authorized. An operator who wants to retire proxy automations should remove the user from `allowUsers` or change identity scopes, which still refuses the jobs.

## Evidence

- New `src/gateway/operator-run-recovery.trusted-proxy.test.ts`. It captures a proxy-authenticated source, persists and decodes it as cron storage does, publishes a new generation through the config-write owner, then restores it through `restoreGatewayQueuedOperatorRecovery`.
  - Adding `requiredHeaders`: **red on base** (`GatewayOperatorRecoveryAuthorizationError`), green with the fix.
  - Removing the user from `allowUsers`: refused (base and fix).
  - Switching to token mode: refused (base and fix).
- The existing shared-credential rotation tests still refuse after rotation. These suites pass: `operator-run-recovery`, `cron-stream-source-authority`, `run.operator-continuation`, `server-shared-auth-generation` and `provider-create-recovery`.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes, including format, lint and core plus core-test typecheck.
- Upgrade-path reproduction with a synthetic Gateway: trusted-proxy auth with an env SecretRef password fallback, a private `trustedProxies` CIDR, and a saved proxy-created automation. Startup and config hot reload alone kept the generation unchanged and the job passed; only adding a `requiredHeaders` entry changed the generation and, before the fix, refused the job.

Update contract: this changes no stored format, Doctor step, config or update path. Older saved sources keep their shape and are read as before, so no migration or upgrade-from-stable run is needed.

prs.title: fix(cli): request scopes a session-only device grant covers
prs.body:
Related: #199692

Depends on #199693. This branch is stacked on it, so until #199693 merges the diff also shows its commits.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a device paired with only `operator.sessions.write`, as the multiplayer guide recommends for guests, can't use `openclaw gateway call` or `openclaw tui`. The CLI asks for `operator.read` and the TUI for admin, read, write and approvals, so every connect becomes a scope-upgrade request for the admin.

## User Impact

User impact: a session-only guest can list, read and create its sessions from the CLI and use the TUI within its grant. Once the TUI has stored the grant with a device token, its connections and `gateway call` file no upgrade request. Behind trusted-proxy auth the Gateway issues the TUI no device token and `gateway call` stores none, so there each connection is refused once with a scope-upgrade request and then works within the grant. #199699 removes that refusal as a Gateway opt-in.

Devices whose grant holds the general scope are unchanged, and a device that needs a real upgrade (for example `operator.read` to `operator.admin`) still files one.

In the TUI, a session-only device gets no command list or pending approvals, because those need `operator.read` and `operator.approvals`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Where the client learns its grant:**
- `gateway call` projects its least-privilege scopes through the stored device grant with the existing `projectOperatorScopesForMethod`. It narrows only when the method's session-scoped alternative still authorizes the call.
- The TUI connects within a stored grant that holds `operator.sessions.*` and none of its default scopes, unless `--token` or `--password` is given.

**A device approved before it ever connected:** it has no stored grant, so its first request can exceed it. The Gateway's scope-upgrade refusal already reports `approvedScopes`, and the client uses that:
- The gateway client gains an opt-in `fitScopesToApprovedGrant` hook that reconnects once within the reported grant, which the TUI uses.
- `gateway call` retries once with the session grant.
- The TUI stores the device token it receives with the grant, so its later connections, and `gateway call` reading that stored grant, fit it. `gateway call` keeps its read-only storage mode on the retry and stores nothing.

Until a grant is stored, each connection still files that request first, because nothing tells the client its grant before it asks. Behind trusted-proxy auth nothing is stored, so that holds for every connection. The opt-in Gateway change in #199699 removes it.

**Moves:** two moves keep the touched files within the line-cap ratchet without changing behaviour:
- CLI scope selection, including the existing `sessions.create` cwd escalation retry, moves to `src/gateway/call-scopes.ts`.
- The gateway client's host-dependency defaults move to `packages/gateway-client/src/client-host-deps.ts`. `client.ts` re-exports their types, so the package API is unchanged.

**Docs:** `docs/start/multiplayer.md` and `docs/cli/tui.md` describe the guest behaviour and when the first-connect request remains.

## Evidence

- **New tests:**
  - `src/gateway/call.stored-grant-scopes.test.ts` 5/5. A session-only grant reads with `operator.sessions.read`; a read grant and a method without a session scope keep their request; a refused request retries with the reported grant and keeps read-only storage on both attempts (this case fails without the read-only fix); a grant that can't serve the method does not retry.
  - `packages/gateway-client/src/client.approved-grant.test.ts` 3/3, against a real WebSocket server that refuses with a scope upgrade: reconnects once within the reported grant; pauses without the hook, or when the hook keeps the request.
  - `src/tui/gateway-chat.connection.test.ts` 16/16, adding session-only, read, `operator.pairing` and `--token` grants.
  - Without this change, the session-only, retry, `operator.pairing` and `--token` cases fail; the keep-behaviour cases pass on both.
- **Existing tests:** `call.test.ts` 91/91, `client.test.ts` 95/95, `client.handshake.test.ts` 22/22, `client.device-auth.test.ts` 25/25, `reconnect-policy.test.ts` 19/19, `tui.test.ts` 51/51.
- **Static checks:** typecheck, lint and format are clean.
- **Restack onto #199693's pairing hint:** this branch now sits on `a675d1b23b7`, which adds the `openclaw gateway call` hint for an unpaired edgeAuth device and keeps an explicit `--url` in it. `git range-diff 3411a94ae50..48d8e528f08 a675d1b23b7..74994fa1a99` shows this branch's two commits unchanged, and the runs below were made at `48d8e528f08`, before the restack. On `74994fa1a99`: `call.edge-auth.test.ts` 6/6, `call.stored-grant-scopes.test.ts` 5/5, `call.test.ts` 91/91, `gateway-chat.connection.test.ts` 16/16, `client.approved-grant.test.ts` 3/3, typecheck clean, line-cap ratchet OK. On `71857425b24`, the same two commits on #199693's first hint commit: `client-bootstrap.auth.test.ts` 6/6, `client.test.ts` 95/95, `tui.test.ts` 51/51.
- **Live run** at `48d8e528f08` (built with `pnpm build:runtime`): a loopback Gateway with `gateway.auth.mode: "trusted-proxy"`, behind a small TLS proxy standing in for Cloudflare Access (it answers 302 unless the request carries `Cf-Access-Token`, then injects the identity headers). The guest config has only `gateway.remote.url` and `gateway.remote.edgeAuth`: no token, no password, no stored device token. `--tls-fingerprint` is there only because the test proxy uses a self-signed certificate. The output is trimmed, and IDs and ports are from throwaway test state. The admin approves only `operator.sessions.write`. The Gateway has `narrowToDeviceGrant` off, as it is by default and as it is without #199699.

- **Upgrade from 2026.11.3, stored credentials kept:** the same loopback trusted-proxy setup, starting on the published `openclaw@2026.11.3` package for both the Gateway and the guest. prs.title: fix(cli): connect through gateway.remote.edgeAuth without a Gateway token
prs.body:
Closes #199691

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw tui`, `openclaw tui --url` and `openclaw gateway call` refuse to dial a Gateway behind Cloudflare Access (or another identity-aware proxy) when the client has `gateway.remote.edgeAuth` but no Gateway token or password. A guest's device therefore never files its first pairing request.

## User Impact

User impact: a CLI configured with `gateway.remote.edgeAuth` connects to a trusted-proxy Gateway without a shared Gateway secret. On first contact `openclaw tui` gets `device pairing required` and leaves a request for the admin, as the [Cloudflare Access guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/cloudflare-access#verify) already describes. Configurations without edgeAuth, and targets on other origins, still require credentials as before. A Gateway on token or password auth still needs its credential: edgeAuth only gets the connection through the proxy, and the Gateway then refuses the missing token. A device that has never connected pairs through `openclaw tui`; its `openclaw gateway call` now says so instead of answering with a bare `missing scope: operator.read`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three local prechecks reject a connection that has no token, password or stored device token: one in `callGatewayWithScopes`, `ensureExplicitGatewayAuth` for `--url` targets, and the TUI's connection resolver. None of them knew that the proxy authenticates the upgrade. Each now skips the shared-credential requirement when edge-auth headers are configured for the target's origin, using the existing `gatewayEdgeAuthValueForTarget` origin match. The Gateway's device pairing then decides access, so nothing new is trusted on the client.

First pairing stays in `openclaw tui`. `openclaw gateway call` is read-only, so on a device that has never connected it has no device identity to pair; the Gateway accepts the connection and refuses the method with `MISSING_SCOPE`. When edge-auth headers are set, the call has no device identity and the Gateway answers `MISSING_SCOPE`, the error now adds `Fix: this device is not paired with this Gateway yet. Run \`openclaw tui\` once to pair this device, ...` (`withEdgeAuthPairingHint` in `src/gateway/call-device-auth.ts`). When the call was given `--url`, the command in the hint keeps it (`openclaw tui --url <url>`), as the existing stored-device-auth recovery message does, because a bare `openclaw tui` can select another Gateway, such as a local one. `call.ts` is over its line cap, so its edge-auth header lookup is inlined, as the TUI's already is, to keep the file from growing.

`docs/cli/tui.md` and `docs/gateway/remote.md` say that, when the Gateway uses trusted-proxy auth, the first connection through edgeAuth needs no token and sends a pairing request, and that a Gateway on token or password auth still needs its credential.

## Security

Based on a source comparison against `main`, the CLI connects through Cloudflare Access as another interface to the same Gateway, using Access headers instead of the web UI's browser cookie. Both paths use the same server authentication, scope caps and role limits. This change grants no new scopes. Access headers do not replace Gateway token or password authentication.

New TUI devices still need pairing approval under the Gateway's existing policy. A fresh `openclaw gateway call` can connect without a device identity, but the server clears its claimed scopes. That device-less session receives scoped access only through explicitly configured identity grants, capped by role limits, as with the existing device-less web UI path. Without those grants, pair through `openclaw tui` before making scoped calls.

## Evidence

- **Tests:**
  - New `src/gateway/call.edge-auth.test.ts` (6 cases) and one new case in `src/tui/gateway-chat.connection.test.ts`.
  - Pairing hint: an edgeAuth device with no identity that gets `MISSING_SCOPE` now sees the `openclaw tui` hint; without this change that case fails with the bare `missing scope: operator.read`. With `gateway.mode: "local"` and an explicit `--url`, the hint names `openclaw tui --url <url>`; that case fails on `d2fade98ea1` with the bare `openclaw tui` hint. A device with an identity keeps the bare message on both. `call.test.ts` 91/91.
  - On `main`, the edgeAuth cases fail with the same errors users see: `requires credentials before opening a websocket`, `gateway url override requires explicit credentials` and `Missing gateway auth credentials.`. With this change they pass.
  - The case for a remote without edgeAuth passes on both, showing that it still requires credentials.
  - Neighbouring suites pass: `client-bootstrap.auth.test.ts` 6/6, `gateway-chat.connection.test.ts` 12/12, `tui.test.ts` 51/51.
  - Typecheck and format are clean. Lint reports nothing in the touched files.
- **Live run** at this head (`3411a94ae50`, built with `pnpm build:runtime`): a loopback Gateway with `gateway.auth.mode: "trusted-proxy"`, behind a small TLS proxy standing in for Cloudflare Access (it answers 302 unless the request carries `Cf-Access-Token`, then injects the identity headers). The guest config has only `gateway.remote.url` and `gateway.remote.edgeAuth`: no token, no password, no stored device token. `--tls-fingerprint` is there only because the test proxy uses a self-signed certificate. The output is trimmed, and IDs and ports are from throwaway test state. The admin approves the TUI's request as it was requested.

  <details><summary>Guest and admin terminal output, proxy connect frames, Gateway audit count</summary>

```text
$ openclaw tui            # configured target: edgeAuth only, no token or password
gateway connect failed: GatewayClientRequestError: device pairing required (requestId: 51f8be07-4e56-416f-9730-90e2f5fe7893)   (x3, the TUI keeps retrying)
$ openclaw devices list   # admin
pending [('51f8be07-4e56-416f-9730-90e2f5fe7893', 'openclaw-tui', ['operator.admin', 'operator.read', 'operator.write', 'operator.approvals'])]
(admin rejects it, to see the explicit-URL path file its own request)
$ openclaw tui --url wss://127.0.0.1:19742 --tls-fingerprint <test cert>   # explicit URL, no token or password
gateway connect failed: GatewayClientRequestError: device pairing required (requestId: 7066e138-a59c-45d1-9cb2-9486248f6b9f)   (x5, the TUI keeps retrying)
pending [('7066e138-a59c-45d1-9cb2-9486248f6b9f', 'openclaw-tui', ['operator.admin', 'operator.read', 'operator.write', 'operator.approvals'])]
$ openclaw devices approve <that request>   # admin approves it as requested
Approved a9d73fadc5f1... (7066e138-a59c-45d1-9cb2-9486248f6b9f)
$ openclaw devices list   # admin

$ openclaw tui            # first start after approval
gateway connected
$ openclaw tui            # second start
gateway connected
$ openclaw gateway call sessions.list --json   # call 1
```

prs.title: feat(gateway): echo resolved session key on chat completion responses
prs.body:
Related: openclaw/openclaw#183497

## What Problem This Solves

Callers of `/v1/chat/completions` cannot discover the generated session key for a request, so they cannot use that key to continue the conversation later.

## User Impact

- Authorized JSON and streaming responses return the resolved session key in `x-openclaw-session-key` when it is representable as an HTTP header value.
- If a key contains characters HTTP headers cannot represent (for example a Unicode `user` value such as `张三`), the header is omitted and the request continues normally. Existing session identity and routing are unchanged; callers can continue using their stable `user` value.
- The OpenAI response body is unchanged; its `id` remains the run ID (`chatcmpl_...`). Callers that need explicit continuation can send a returned header value as `x-openclaw-session-key` on the next request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The endpoint already supports explicit `x-openclaw-session-key` routing and stable `user`-derived sessions, but its default per-request key is random and was not disclosed in the response. Echoing the resolved, header-safe key closes that discovery gap without changing the OpenAI response body or existing routing behavior.

## Evidence

### Real-model continuation trace (isolated Gateway, real configured model)

Sanitized transcript from an isolated Gateway started from contributor head `1de212d1` (separate state directory and config path, loopback port, bearer-token auth; real agent execution with the environment's configured provider and model — provider and model identities intentionally omitted; no mocks):

```
JSON-initial:   status=200 x-openclaw-session-key=PRESENT
JSON-initial:   id=chatcmpl_64330bf6-4a32-4252-9ac9-5d3f8332aa3c reply="OK"
JSON-initial:   echoed-key=agent:main:openai:d7499482-fea8-4c8e-ba4a-0847863ffc72
JSON-followup:  status=200 x-openclaw-session-key=PRESENT
JSON-followup:  same-key-echoed=true reply="SKE-NONCE-JSON-240A5BFF96D1"
JSON-CONTINUITY: nonce_recalled=true
SSE-initial:    status=200 x-openclaw-session-key=PRESENT
SSE-initial:    stream-received=true reply="OK"
SSE-initial:    echoed-key=agent:main:openai:c114df69-79fc-4dd1-a964-8003026cf56e
SSE-followup:   same-key-echoed=true reply="SKE-NONCE-SSE-D569953C1612"
SSE-CONTINUITY: nonce_recalled=true
```

Per mode: the initial request embeds a fresh synthetic nonce and returns `200` with the echoed `x-openclaw-session-key` response header; the follow-up request sends **only** that echoed key as the `x-openclaw-session-key` request header, and the same conversation recalls the exact nonce. Covered for JSON and `stream: true` (SSE); all four responses echoed the header. The gateway log for these runs shows real provider execution (transient provider rate-limit retries followed by success), not a mock. This trace is evidence for head `1de212d1`; the base integration below keeps the introduced feature diff byte-identical (verified against the new base: exactly the same 137 added lines in the same four files), and the focused HTTP suite below re-proves the echo boundary on the merged head. No user data, credentials, private endpoints, or provider/model identities are included.

### Validation commands and results (current head `708c7803`)

- `corepack pnpm test src/gateway/openai-http.session-key-echo.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 1 passed (1)` (107s). Covers generated, `user`-derived, and explicit keys; streaming; rejected session targets; and a Unicode `user` request that still succeeds without the unrepresentable response header.
- `corepack pnpm exec oxlint src/gateway/openai-http.ts src/gateway/openai-http.session-key-echo.test.ts test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server-paths.mjs` — passed, no findings.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` on the four changed files — all files correctly formatted.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/gateway/openai-http.ts","src/gateway/openai-http.session-key-echo.test.ts"]' --concurrency 2` — all shards passed.
- `node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base d902b29bce5` — `Test lines OK. Net test lines: +128; allowance: 400; allocation credit: 0.`

### Current upstream CI state

At head `708c7803`, the upstream CI and PR tooling Darwin runs are `action_required` and have no executed jobs yet. The fork workflows require repository-maintainer approval to run; this contributor account has read-only upstream access and cannot approve them. Therefore `openclaw/ci-gate` currently reports failure because successful CI evidence is not yet available, not because the new head has produced a failing test result. Local validation above is not presented as a substitute for upstream CI.

- [CI run awaiting approval](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44536033931)
- [PR tooling Darwin run awaiting approval](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44536033184)

The exact-head ClawSweeper re-review has completed: the live JSON/SSE continuation evidence was judged sufficient, and no actionable code findings remain. The review still requires maintainer approval of the standalone response-header contract and fork CI execution; no duplicate re-review is requested. Maintainer follow-up is needed for workflow approval and for the standalone response-header contract decision below.

### Base integration (named gate)

Merged current `main` (`d902b29bce5`) as an ordinary merge commit (`708c7803`, no rebase, no force, contributor history preserved). Reason: the `darwin` check on the previous head runs `test/scripts/pr-dependency-cache.test.ts`, which does not exist in this branch's pre-October base (`explicit test/source file(s) not found`) — a base-drift tooling gate failure, not a code defect. After the merge that test file exists and the introduced contributor diff is unchanged.

### Review boundary

An independent introduced-diff review (Codex agent, separate from the authoring session; not a canonical autoreview run, which is unavailable in this environment) covered the complete four-file introduced diff at head `708c7803` and found no actionable findings. It is not a full-repository autoreview execution.

## Maintainer decision still needed

The standalone-contract question from the ClawSweeper review remains open: should chat completions expose the authorized, header-safe session key as a public response contract independently of ephemeral mode and TTL? The review recommended accepting it; this PR does not self-approve that decision and keeps it visible as a merge gate.

## Scope

This PR implements session-key echo only. Ephemeral storage and per-request TTL remain out of scope until their lifecycle semantics are agreed in #183497.
