prs.title: fix: show native notification settings in the iOS app
prs.body:
Closes #164557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Notifications shows Safari Home Screen installation instructions when opened inside the native iOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone and iPad app users can see their native notification delivery and permission settings and open the existing device settings pages. Browser/PWA and macOS notification flows remain separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already observes the native device-settings capability but did not pass its snapshot into the notification view. This repair uses that existing owner, shows a loading state while its snapshot is pending, and keeps missing status values unknown. Device links use application navigation so the native Back history is retained; modified clicks keep normal link behavior.

Upstream migrated the settings UI from Lit to Solid. This update keeps the current Solid renderer and ports the native-notification regression with it. Native notification presentation and capability-to-view props live in focused siblings to respect the existing file-size guards. No notification transport, native permission operation, configuration key, dependency, or generated translation memory changes.

## Evidence

Current tested head: `c326ed5fc8fc63d243f337ff928a9cca42304f5b` (tree `f7d308969f6204e5309accb9137dfac74b82069c`). This is a normal two-parent merge preserving the original PR head `d7bdb5a3c123b1db96eeb9322a42efeb0075df71` and upstream `5584b16af9109db5235f776cb1302093f6bf2f59`.

- The real Notifications route, ConfigPage, capability adapters, and rendered DOM are exercised together. The migrated test fails eight native cases against untouched upstream production; the Safari/PWA/Mac controls pass.
- Final focused run: **140 tests passed in six files, 8.12 seconds wall time**, covering iPhone/iPad, base paths, delayed and changed native snapshots, missing fields, ordinary/modified clicks, absent callbacks, and browser/Mac controls.
- Production Control UI build completed successfully in **18.94 seconds**.
- i18n verification, focused style checks, documentation MDX/link checks, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety guards, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review identified missing route-loader result narrowing in the migrated test fixture. Explicit route and result guards address it; the final focused rerun and fresh canonical P0–P2 autoreview passed without remaining actionable findings.

**Outstanding verification:** Physical iPhone QA and inspected before/after screenshots remain unavailable. The DOM tests provide synthetic bridge-contract evidence and do not establish native-device or visual behavior. Production UI typechecking, a reduced focused typecheck, and typed lint were terminated with exit 137/SIGKILL without source diagnostics; those gates are not claimed green. Full repository tests have not run, and current-head hosted CI is not yet verified. This remains a draft pending those checks and the required native/visual evidence.

Checks ran on Node 24.19.0 through the repository wrappers. Dependencies were installed with the frozen lockfile using the environment's pnpm 11.25.0. The pinned pnpm 12.9.0 install was attempted but could not open its store operation lock on this host's read-only filesystem; this tooling limitation remains explicit.

prs.title: fix: preserve reset data when state ownership is refused
prs.body:
Closes #202023

## What Problem This Solves

openclaw reset --scope config+creds+sessions could remove openclaw.json and the credentials directory after an unmanaged Gateway refused state ownership. The session cleanup correctly rejected the operation, but the command caught that refusal and continued with unguarded file deletion.

## User Impact

When the state owner is active, the reset now refuses before deleting configuration, credentials, or session history. After exclusive ownership is acquired, the existing best-effort behavior remains: an individual session store or independent removal failure is reported while the other selected cleanup targets are still attempted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-removing reset scope now uses one existing state-cleanup owner for session history, configuration, and OAuth cleanup. Ownership admission happens outside the ordinary session-store failure catch, and the owner assertion remains active through both file-removal effects and the existing resource-draining release. The standalone session helper and onboarding fail-fast behavior remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Base regression: the registered reset flow reproduced the issue with a real cross-process owner; the command returned nonzero but the config-preservation oracle failed with ENOENT.
- Focused regression green: 16 live ownership tests plus 84 compatibility tests passed, for 100 focused tests with no skips or failures. Coverage includes active-owner data preservation, owner-free cleanup, real config/OAuth deletion barriers, archive-collision best effort, independent removal failures, dry-run, onboarding, full reset, and uninstall.
- Lifetime negative control: a temporary preflight-then-release implementation was rejected by both real file-effect barriers because a competing process acquired ownership before deletion.
- Static checks passed: production and test lint, pnpm tsgo:core, commands test typecheck, format, diff check, and the mock-export guard.
- Official runtime build passed through pnpm openclaw --version and the repository's qaRuntime build path.
- Real CLI/Gateway proof passed: an isolated foreground Gateway remained healthy while the registered reset refused with exact ownership error and all data hashes unchanged; after normal Gateway shutdown, the same CLI removed sessions/config/credentials while preserving workspace and auth profiles.

Focused commands included:

~~~text
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.core.json src/commands/reset.ts src/commands/cleanup-utils.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.commands.json src/commands/cleanup-live-state.test.ts src/commands/reset.sessions.test.ts src/commands/reset.test.ts src/commands/cleanup-command.test-support.ts
pnpm tsgo:core
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.commands.json --incremental
~~~

prs.title: fix(daemon): Linux updates run out of space on a RAM-backed /tmp when TMPDIR was never set
prs.body:
Refs #199559 (one of its causes; the rest stays open there)
Related: #199030

Scope: this PR fixes one defect, the Linux service installer writing a `TMPDIR` the operator never set. It does not change how an explicit `TMPDIR` ranks against the state volume (the open decision on #199030), and it does not repair units installed before it, Doctor recovery, hidepid hosts or update cleanup, which stay on #199559.

## What Problem This Solves

On Linux, `openclaw gateway install` freezes the host default `/tmp` into the gateway's systemd unit as `Environment=TMPDIR=/tmp` when the operator never set `TMPDIR`. Update staging treats that as an explicit operator choice and stages on `/tmp` first, so on a host where `/tmp` is a small tmpfs, `openclaw update` runs out of space even when the state disk has plenty free.

## User Impact

User impact: on Linux, a gateway service installed or refreshed without `TMPDIR` in the installer's environment no longer gets `TMPDIR` written into its unit, so update staging ranks the state volume first instead of a RAM-backed `/tmp`. Operators who set `TMPDIR` keep it exactly as before. macOS (state-dir `tmp`) and Windows are unchanged. Existing units lose the frozen `TMPDIR=/tmp` on the next `openclaw gateway install --force`; reinstall already drops the old unit's `TMPDIR` rather than replaying it (shown below).

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveServiceTmpDir` returned `env.TMPDIR || os.tmpdir()` on Linux, so the host default was frozen into the unit as if it were an operator choice. Update staging (`update-candidate-snapshot.ts`, `update-retained-runtime.ts`) treats any `TMPDIR` as explicit and ranks it ahead of the state volume. On Linux the function now returns `undefined` when `TMPDIR` is unset or blank, so the unit omits it (`renderEnvLines` skips non-strings) and the process still resolves `os.tmpdir()` at run time. The darwin-only callers in `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-*` keep a `string` return through an overload.

## Evidence

Real systemd run on a throwaway Debian trixie host (systemd user services with linger, `/tmp` a 160 MiB tmpfs, state on the root disk), Node 24.22.3. "Stable" is npm `openclaw@2026.11.5` (`OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15)`, the current `latest`). "Fix" is this PR's two commits applied to the `v2026.11.5` tag, same patch-id as the PR head, packaged with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` (`OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (23254fc)`). Installer shells had no `TMPDIR`. Full redacted transcript below.

- **Before (stable 2026.11.5, fresh `openclaw onboard --install-daemon`):** unit has `Environment=TMPDIR=/tmp`; the running service process has `TMPDIR=/tmp`; `Connectivity check: ok`.
- **Upgrade from 2026.11.5 through the fixed installer:** with the stable gateway running and a cron job stored, `openclaw gateway install --force` from the fix (no other step). The unit diff against the backed-up 2026.11.5 unit changes only `ExecStart`/`PATH` to the new build and drops `Environment=TMPDIR=/tmp`. Service `active`, `Runtime: running`, `Connectivity check: ok`, `openclaw health` ok, service process has no `TMPDIR`.
- **Existing settings and data after the upgrade:** `openclaw.json` byte-identical (same SHA-256), gateway auth token unchanged (hash compared), `state/openclaw.sqlite` (`user_version` 36, 103 tables), the agent database (`user_version` 38, 58 tables) and `control/services.sqlite` unchanged in schema version and table set, and the stored cron job is still listed with the same id and schedule. The change writes no stored data and no schema; it only changes which `Environment=` lines the installer renders.
- **Explicit TMPDIR kept:** `TMPDIR=/var/tmp openclaw gateway install --force` (fix) → `Environment=TMPDIR=/var/tmp` in the unit and in the running process; `Connectivity check: ok`.
- **Update snapshot selection:** the shipped `assessInitialUpdateSnapshotCapacity` (from the fix's `dist/update-candidate-snapshot-*.mjs`), run with each unit's environment:
  - stable 2026.11.5 unit: `explicit-tmpdir /tmp: 71 MiB needed; 107 MiB free.` ranked first, then `state-volume`.
  - fix unit: `state-volume /home/oc2/.openclaw.update-captures: 71 MiB needed; 15 GiB free.` ranked first, then `system-tmpdir /tmp`.
  `allocateSnapshotRoot` takes the first candidate that fits, so the stable unit stages on the tmpfs while the fix stages on the state volume. A full `openclaw update` is not exercised here: the updater skips this host as `container-image-install` before staging.
- **Earlier run, 2026.11.3:** the same checks from a 2026.11.3 unit (including `openclaw gateway stop --force` + `openclaw doctor --fix` before the reinstall) gave the same result; that transcript is in this PR's history.
- **Tests:** five cases in `src/daemon/service-env.test.ts` (Linux unset, Linux blank, Linux explicit, macOS state dir, Windows host default); three fail without the fix. `pnpm test src/daemon/service-env.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 35 passed on the PR head, on `v2026.11.5` + this PR, and on current `main` (5fb231527f4) + this PR; the commits cherry-pick onto both without conflict.
- **Wider tests and checks (PR head):** `pnpm test src/daemon src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts src/commands/daemon-install-path.test.ts src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-lease-path.test.ts src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-cleanup-repair.test.ts` pass except two cases in `src/daemon/service.test.ts` that fail identically on `main`. `pnpm check:changed`: format, lint, all typecheck graphs and every other guard pass; the dead export scan fails with 36 entries, none in touched files.
- **Local review:** autoreview (Claude engine, since Codex is not used), complete committed range of the first commit, P0 threshold: clean, 0 findings (comment above).

<details>
<summary>Redacted transcript (2026.11.5)</summary>

```text

OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15)
$ (stable) openclaw onboard --non-interactive ... --install-daemon     # installer TMPDIR: <unset>
```

prs.title: improve(ui): highlight skill references in the composer
prs.body:
Related: #152599 (inline `$skill` references; standalone slash commands are unchanged). Builds on #192242.

## What Problem This Solves

Selected skills remain raw `$command_name` text in the composer, making them harder to distinguish from surrounding prose and person mentions.

## User Impact

Chat and New Session show known skill references as highlighted, atomic names with the existing skill icon and no visible `$`. Copying and sending preserve the canonical reference. No configuration or migration is required.

**Still draft; not performance-qualified for shipping.** The repeated scanning and premature editor-loading defects are repaired, and both hosted correctness findings are fixed. The startup asset gate still fails by **448 bytes**. First skill use and skill-only rich editing still cost substantially more than native text; several New Session p95 cells remain higher. These limits are not waived by this repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the generic native-first editor and extension contract from the final merged #192242, rather than introduce another editor, overlay or dependency. Skills use the existing command catalog and share atomic boundary editing with people. Display labels no longer grant reference identity: only canonical commands and normalized command identifiers are recognized. Unknown references, shell variables, escaped dollars and code remain literal.

Ordinary edits map existing skill decorations instead of rescanning the draft. Token/Markdown-sensitive edits still use the canonical parser; image-bearing drafts deliberately retain full parsing. Atomic editing checks only affected chip boundaries and does not serialize large pastes for single-character separator checks. Literal dollars may load the small parser, but cannot fetch CodeMirror until a reference is admitted. Catalog replacement explicitly refreshes labels/removals and admits unchanged restored drafts; subscriptions end with their native/editor owners. Native undo snapshots, asynchronous handoff, IME boundaries and retired-frame guards are preserved. Skill integration still composes through the mention adapter, not a new feature framework.

## Evidence

### Current repair and review — November 16

Published head `0283e5b68266ebb706dab8a9d74623406693488e` has exactly the tested product tree of implementation `ec4b449ebd8e2e0e468f10da9fec32b8ec9b789b` (`37b3739503d08c1fbe431ff51ae1ba6af24bcb99`); the publisher's final commit is attribution-only.

- **218 browser tests passed in 13 files**, including person/skill editor consumers, native handoff, undo, paste/drop, composition simulation, ref disposal, catalog/command consumers, overflow, height and mobile fixtures. UI and script typechecks, scoped lint/format, controller guard and whitespace checks passed.
- **Both source-server real-UI Chat/New Session flows passed** with a synthetic Gateway. The new network assertion first failed on both routes: `$HOME`/`$unknown` fetched the rich editor. It now passes while actual skill selection and canonical submission still work.
- Both hosted P2 findings on `6d45233` were reproduced red and repaired: display-name aliases could look selected without resolving on submission; unchanged drafts did not react to catalog arrival/rename/removal. The catalog regression verifies stable editor identity, raw text and selection.
- Independent local **autoreview through P2 was scoped-clean** for the final staged repair against `6d45233`, subsequently committed as `ec4b449`. It included the generic editor, mention adapter, import lifecycle, catalog owner, Gateway reference-resolution contract and Markdown parser as context. Static review is not runtime proof. Earlier reviewer findings for indentation, adjacent backticks, native history and literal-dollar loading were repaired; the staged-only loading finding disappeared when the reviewed working-tree fix was committed.
- **900 valid repair timing observations** were collected across explicit source stages: 390 at `08ec3b39`, 270 at `452d63a5`, then **240 on the final product tree**. Completed interrupted work was retained rather than replayed; one restart interruption in the first stage is excluded from valid observations. Earlier-stage measurements are not relabeled as final-head proof.
- Final separate diagnostics found **zero full-draft skill scans for twelve unrelated keys** in both Chat and New Session, down from twelve on the original feature. Ten people/eight skill chips and exact raw text survived; one editor remained mounted and stylesheet rules did not grow during typing. A final bounded 21-round-trip session lifecycle replay also passed on baseline and candidate; this is not a universal no-leak claim.

### Acceptance rule — unchanged

Baseline `491c2944f56ad7d6d9a561a17dfffcd42cab49e3` already contains the final merged mention foundation. Compare same-toolchain production builds with at least ten serial rotating baseline/candidate/identical-baseline rounds. Report median, p95, ranges and host load; keep traced diagnostics separate. Require no correctness loss, unexpected RPCs, per-key remounts/owner-echo transactions or unbounded resource growth. Median regression must be at most 5% with no worse p95; unresolved tails need confirmation. A confirmed move above 20% blocks blanket performance acceptance. Existing asset limits remain unchanged. Mock-renderer, live-Gateway and native-device evidence remain separate.

### Final production-build timings

Chromium `156.0.8078.4`, Linux x64, real production UI with a synthetic Gateway. These are **renderer main-thread CPU milliseconds per action**, not per-key latency, INP, total process CPU or live-provider latency. Long typing is twelve trusted characters in a 64 KiB draft; mixed drafts contain ten people/eight skills. Paste is 256 KiB synthetic clipboard input. Catalog size is 200. Each row has ten observations per variant; each cell is **median / p95**. A/A is an identical baseline.

| Flow | Baseline | Final candidate | A/A control |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chat person-only long | 55.567 / 60.265 | 55.551 / 60.269 | 56.480 / 59.302 |
| Chat mixed long | 52.028 / 58.309 | 54.160 / 57.572 | 54.125 / 56.980 |
| Chat literal dollars | 38.862 / 43.498 | 39.343 / 42.133 | 38.111 / 45.286 |
| New Session person-only long | 52.058 / 54.542 | 53.371 / 58.238 | 53.519 / 57.152 |
| New Session mixed long | 45.783 / 50.206 | 46.555 / 55.102 | 46.154 / 49.780 |
| New Session mixed paste | 23.195 / 25.057 | 23.746 / 26.502 | 22.933 / 25.102 |
| Chat first skill, including first dollar | 47.118 / 52.273 | 87.230 / 91.677 | 48.570 / 52.067 |
| New Session first skill, including first dollar | 45.679 / 49.449 | 74.020 / 81.182 | 44.615 / 48.706 |

The original mixed-typing median regressions were +8.39% Chat and +8.97% New Session. Final mixed medians are +4.10% and +1.69% versus baseline, and +0.06% and +0.87% versus A/A. This supports removal of the measured hot-path waste, not universal parity: New Session person/mixed/paste p95 are still +6.78%, +9.75% and +5.77% versus baseline. The complete acceptance rule therefore remains unmet.

**First-use work is not hidden in preparation.** New `first-skill` workloads start from an untouched native draft and include the first dollar, catalog readiness, typing the query, selecting the skill and settling imports. Older `activate-skill` rows measured selection after typing the query; they are selection-only evidence, not cold first-use parity. Native-to-rich first-use cost remains approximately +40.1 ms in Chat and +28.3 ms in New Session. At the earlier `08ec3b39` stage, short skill-only typing was 20.170 → 36.529 ms and 200 occurrences were 64.712 → 127.286 ms. Those are native-versus-rich feature costs, not all attributable to parsing, and are not waived or claimed as final-head measurements.

Final CPU ranges: Chat mixed baseline 49.655–58.309 / candidate 51.451–57.572 ms; New Session mixed baseline 45.098–50.206 / candidate 44.695–55.102 ms; Chat first-skill baseline 46.277–52.273 / candidate 85.950–91.677 ms; New Session first-skill baseline 43.821–49.449 / candidate 70.785–81.182 ms. Final host load ranged 1.95–6.04 on 128 logical CPUs. Complete distributions and per-run manifests remain in the linked task under `catalog-final-summary.txt`, `catalog-final.log.summary.json`, and raw observations. No outliers were removed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, prior evidence and scope</summary>

The committed workload extends `scripts/lib/control-ui-chat-composer-scenarios.ts`, using the existing engine runner. With matched baseline and candidate builds:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts \
  --bundle-dir .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui \
  --compare-bundle-dir dist/control-ui \
  --control-bundle-dir .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui \
  --source-root .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base \
  --compare-source-root . \
  --control-source-root .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base \
  --engines chromium --viewport desktop --pairs 10 \
  --steps composer-qualification-chat-first-skill,composer-qualification-new-first-skill,composer-qualification-chat-literal-dollar,composer-qualification-chat-person-long,composer-qualification-chat-mixed-long,composer-qualification-new-person-long,composer-qualification-new-mixed-long,composer-qualification-new-mixed-paste \
  --output .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/rerun
```

Earlier qualification of `6d45233` retained 510 editing/activation and 62 startup observations, 157 browser cases, eight emulated narrow/dark observations, four scan diagnostics, profiles and bounded retention. Its boot CPU and heap results are historical evidence, not a fresh final-head certification. Earlier repairs retained their own exact-source summaries; only the final table above qualifies the current product tree.

The simplify pass preserves the existing foreign-DOM owner and CodeMirror extension contract. No dependency, editor, overlay, global cache, custom Markdown parser or permission change was added. Necessary growth covers the skill feature, selective invalidation, native history and catalog notification/disposal. Versus `491c2944`, production UI is +714/−263 lines, tests +488/−19, and benchmark code +359/−1. Net test growth is 469 lines; the documented per-change allocation is 69 beyond the standard 400 for reproduced handoff, Markdown, lazy-loading and catalog/identity failures. Startup/performance limits were not raised.

</details>

### Startup asset gate — still failed

Final normalized largest-JS gzip is **569,985 → 570,497 bytes (+512)**. The inherited-over-cap differential permits only 64 bytes: **448 bytes remain over the allowed increase**. Original feature growth was +676 bytes; this repair does not claim the remaining failure is harmless. Chat/New boot gzip grows 539/486 bytes; request counts remain 21/17. CSS bytes and request counts are unchanged. The boot manifest was regenerated without a source diff. No unrelated byte-offset changes or budget increases were used.

Reproduction: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts --dist dist/control-ui --base-dist .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui --json`. The strict comparison exits 1. Inherited absolute CSS/request overages are distinguished from this new differential failure.

### Remaining limits

This is a verified repair update to a draft, not a shipping or zero-regression claim. Startup size, native-to-rich feature cost and remaining p95 regressions are unresolved. WebKit/Firefox could not load the app under the environment's proxy policy on either build; no bypass was attempted. Native OS IME, mobile Safari, real-device/network and live Gateway/provider performance remain unqualified. Composition browser tests simulate events, not a physical input method. No merge or deployment occurred.

The existing inspected visual evidence is retained; this repair changes computation and correctness, not the chip design. Captures use the real UI with a synthetic Gateway; mobile is an emulated 390px viewport.

![Before: raw skill references](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02c4e4c3-1f4d-46fa-8017-bcb02d634e13)

After — highlighted skill names and icons:

![After: highlighted skill references](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4de3ea02-abd4-4fb9-b1c0-4f0f5c6b3fb8)

<summary>New Session at an emulated mobile width</summary>

![New Session skill references at 390px](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/209f61df-ec7c-476b-bdce-3dd520544a58)

</details>

Requested and designed with @vyctorbrzezowski.

prs.title: fix(ios): keep session pins personal to the signed-in profile
prs.body: Related: #198377 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: pinning a session on iOS changes shared session metadata instead of the signed-in user's personal navigation. ## User Impact iOS pins follow the signed-in profile's personal shortcuts, the same as web. Existing shared pins stay stored but are no longer shown as personal pins; users can pin those sessions personally. Connections without personal preferences get a profile/sign-in explanation and never fall back to shared writes. Personal-only pins (hiding legacy shared pins, refusing profileless pins) is the requested product behaviour. ## Why This Change Was Made - Align iOS with the personal-navigation contract in the [user-model documentation](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/user-model) and with web, which already maps `session:` entries in `ui.railShortcuts` to the Sessions Pinned section. - Re-read before writes and compare the exact snapshot, preserving unrelated shortcuts and reporting conflicts. - Keep session eligibility, child-session filtering, grouping and layout unchanged. - Preserve stored shared pin metadata without importing it into personal pins. ## Evidence Lint-enabled Xcode 27.2 run of the final apps patch: ```text LINT_BYPASS=0 KIT_TESTS=13 tests in 1 suite passed SIM_TESTS=xctest=0 swift-testing=19 rc=0 STATUS=PASS ``` **Profile isolation and cross-client refresh** (iOS simulator against an isolated Gateway with a second, trusted-proxy-authenticated profile B). Another Owner client pinned X and iOS showed it as pinned. A pin that belonged only to B was not shown as pinned in the Owner app. An unpin made on iOS was read back as unpinned by a separate Owner client. Storage readbacks show each profile's write left the other profile's shortcuts unchanged. [XCTest output](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/native-rpc-xctest.txt) · [storage readbacks](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/profile-isolation.jsonl) **Seeded upgrade.** A v2026.11.5 Gateway and app were seeded with an existing personal shortcut and an existing shared pin, then upgraded in place to this PR (same simulator, data kept). Before: the shared pin is in Pinned and the personal shortcut is not. After: the personal shortcut is in Pinned and the shared pin is shown unpinned but still stored. Gateway readbacks before and after the upgrade match byte for byte, including the legacy pin timestamp. [stable seed](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/stable-store.json) · [after upgrade](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/head-store-after-ui.json) · [stable XCTest](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/upgrade-stable-xctest.txt) · [head XCTest](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/upgrade-head-xctest.txt) | | Before (v2026.11.5) | After (this PR) | | --- | --- | --- | | Existing shared pin | | | | Existing personal shortcut | | | **Matched base/head.** The same iOS XCUITest ran against separate disposable Gateways on the merge base and on this PR, with the same signed-in profile confirmed at each checkpoint. Merge base: Pin set the shared `pinned` field and timestamp, and personal shortcuts never changed. This PR: Pin added the session to the profile's personal shortcuts only, and shared pin metadata stayed identical at every checkpoint. Unpin reversed each. [Result](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/MATCHED.md) · [base readbacks](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/matched-base-checkpoints.txt) · [head readbacks](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/matched-head-checkpoints.txt) **Missing profile.** iOS is an ordinary client of the same auth and profile model as web, and handles a missing profile the same way. Web refuses to persist a pin or shortcut when the profile is missing or the preference read is not `ok` ([`server-prefs-profile-runtime.ts:97-109`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/669ae72f7a9bbd48daf36b66ee2e044d32ea7353/ui/src/app/server-prefs-profile-runtime.ts#L97-L109)), and its test verifies `no_durable_identity` sends no write ([`server-prefs.navigation.test.ts:316-325`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/669ae72f7a9bbd48daf36b66ee2e044d32ea7353/ui/src/app/server-prefs.navigation.test.ts#L316-L325)). iOS matches this: the native method test verifies `no_durable_identity` shows the profile-required explanation after one read and attempts no write, with no fallback to shared pins. Normal sign-in always provides a profile on both clients; a connection without a durable identity is refused before the preferences handler, and the store stays unchanged. Preference tests also cover mixed arrays with compare-and-set snapshots, absent versus empty preferences, idempotent repinning, empty keys and unrelated shortcuts. [Full evidence](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/6b86c63a3208d3149fc17033bf0b97b9214c7da2/EVIDENCE.md) AI-assisted.

prs.title: fix: retain channel requester when child completion resumes parent
prs.body:
Related: #182043, #168823. Adjacent cohort work: #164366 (completion-wave selection is unchanged).

## What Problem This Solves

A parent resumed by child completion loses the original channel requester's identity and can reject already-authorized owner tools.

## User Impact

In-process child completion resumes as its original requester, subject to current owner checks and the existing completion tool-policy ceiling. Guests are not promoted to owners. No configuration or state migration is required.

Successful-child live proof is now established. Human security/domain review and current-head CI/review remain outstanding; this authorization-boundary change stays draft pending those gates. Crash recovery and automation-management grants are outside this fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

Registration and refreshed followup custody already retain the operator source, but did not opt into the existing retained-requester capability. Single-child and batch delivery now re-enter that capability only for dispatch, passing its selected origin and matching live assertion into normal agent admission. Synchronous cleanup checks do not reacquire requester identity.

Operator source/scopes govern batch delivery independently of requester identity. Homogeneous batches retain the canonical requester principal, ignoring display-name changes. Mixed-human batches retain existing operator-owned delivery without selecting a member's personal identity. Cancellation-only fallback is unchanged. No owner bit is directly set or denylist relaxed. One shared source-comparison owner serves both consumers; no new schema or persisted authority manager.

## Evidence

### Successful-child live proof — November 15

Published head: `72e1afde461c17d25eea1c55efd7e6428eff7ed5`; tree: `c8b1bd8c868d1465f281d54ae08a90148d2cc351`. The published tree is identical to successful-child live-tested source `95d3c159e330ec66c204f82b8dbf36166a0c3408`. Managed publication and Git tree equality were read back; publication is complete. This does not establish exact-head hosted CI or review approval.

The observed harness failure was diagnosed, not waived: completion execution retained a released plugin invocation scope and failed with `agent harness host capability is no longer active` / `Plugin invocation scope is closed`. The maintained upstream repair [#199618](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199618), merged commit `7789e95139dc42390c506d8bc835816dc5e3ec43`, was integrated for this evidenced base risk. Four requester-retention patches remained range-diff equivalent. No authority guard was disabled; diagnostic instrumentation was removed before the final build.

Isolated Hetzner cx33, managed Crabbox 0.83.0, actual Discord dedicated canary and OAuth-backed Codex. Runtime build run `run_ef7f98426c65a22759ed382c265373e8` passed. Live run `run_6cbacb2b5d039ae9bc64d29924127505` exited 0. Direct provider has no hosted run URL.

Acceptance was verified from stored parent/child histories, actual tool results, terminal RPC observations and runtime logs—not merely a success marker:

1. One real bot-authored owner stimulus reached Discord; parent `config.get gateway.mode` returned `ok/local`.
2. Exactly one isolated child produced its requested final; exact child run `a1e93a32-609e-435a-a051-488aa7a00ff9` settled with `agent.wait status=ok`.
3. Actual `announce:v1` completion resumed the waiting parent.
4. Resumed parent's second owner-only `config.get gateway.mode` returned `ok/local`; its exact completion run also settled `status=ok`.
5. Runtime logs contained zero prior host-capability, closed-plugin-scope, lane-error or cleanup-failure signatures.

The harness now rejects absent/failed child finals, checks both terminal statuses and both actual owner reads, and captures diagnostics on failure. Guest retention uses `--stop-after never` independently of runner success; TTL/safety limits remain active. Failed V5/V6 captures were preserved. V7's 13 evidence files were downloaded, read back, hashed and checked against both injected credential values (zero matches) BEFORE provider deletion. Exact lease absence and Gateway shutdown were verified. Raw captures remain private. Existing dedicated bot secret and a static OAuth access token were used only in isolated state; no refresh-token transfer, production-state copy, API-key fallback or production deployment.

### Deterministic checks and review

- Rebased-source focused suites: 29 requester-policy + 69 registry + 24 direct-delivery tests = **122 passed**, wrapper 89.41s.
- Targeted TypeScript, oxlint and `git diff --check` passed; publication reconciliation has an empty source diff against the validated source/tree.
- Original regression failed on base `c99807a541c86cc49ffcc4d9dbabd1219f65bc53`.
- P1 mixed-human rejection and P2 display-name-sensitive comparison were repaired and independently reviewed before the base integration. That review is prior-head evidence, not current-head approval.
- Guest denial, source revocation, mixed-human cohorts and cancellation non-borrowing remain deterministic proof, not live Discord claims. No crash/restart, upgrade or full-package-build proof is claimed.
- Earlier error-completion run `run_864c67a5c1af1389d068c700b2b46fea` remains valid only for child-error recovery; it has been superseded for successful-child acceptance by V7 above.
- Exact-head broad CI/hosted review and human security/domain approval remain unverified. No merge or production deployment is claimed.

Rollback is a revert of the requester-retention change. Earlier setup failures and the failed required scenarios were retained, not relabeled as success. Driver-authored test prompts remain where cross-conversation cleanup was denied; no permission bypass was attempted.

prs.title: fix(memory): bound heading-only chunk merges to the chunker maximum
prs.body:
Closes #198958

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `prepareMemoryIndexChunks` merges a heading-only chunk into the next chunk without any size bound, producing one oversized embedding input that non-native OpenAI-compatible endpoints reject, aborting the rebuild.

## User Impact

Heading-only runs stay within the chunker's ceiling while a heading still attaches to its following body. Existing indexes rebuild because the chunking version changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add `resolveMarkdownChunkMaxChars` as the single owner of the chunker ceiling and reuse it in `createMarkdownChunker`.
- Bound heading-only merges to that ceiling when the following chunk is also heading-only.
- Measure with the chunker's weighted CJK estimator, not raw UTF-16 length.
- Bump `MEMORY_CHUNKING_VERSION` so existing indexes rebuild across the boundary change.

## Evidence

- Unit: `pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-index-preparation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 11/11 passed, including the 200-heading bound and a CJK case that distinguishes weighted from raw length. Red-on-base produces a 3689-character merged chunk against a 32-character ceiling.
- Real rebuild on the same 400-heading CJK corpus (`openclaw memory index --force --agent main`):
  - before (origin/main): 11 chunks, max chunk **8291 chars** (above the 8000-byte embedding cap);
  - this head: 25 chunks, max chunk **735 chars**, max span 73 lines.
- Real embedding endpoint (local OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings`, 8 dims):
  - `memory status --deep`: `Vector store: ready`, `Semantic vectors: ready`, `Vector dims: 8`, 25 chunks.
  - `memory search "第399章 中文标题"` -> top hit `memory/cjk-headings.md:734-800` (score 0.613).
  - `memory search "sapphire lighthouse"` -> top hit `memory/note.md:1-2` (score 0.898).
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; oxlint clean on all changed files.

### Latest-stable (v2026.11.6) index upgrade

```text
# index built by openclaw@2026.11.6 (chunking v6)
max chunk: 4496 chars, 13 chunks
$ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive   # agent schema 38 -> 43
Doctor complete.
$ (this head) openclaw memory index --agent main
Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed.
memory_index_meta_v1 ... "chunkingVersion":7 ... "vectorDims":8
max chunk: 735 chars
$ memory search "第399章 中文标题"
0.651 memory/cjk-headings.md:734-800
$ memory search "sapphire lighthouse"
0.884 memory/note.md:1-2
```

prs.title: improve: keep setup and help in your agent's Home conversation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Settings help and agent setup can send people into a separate “Ask OpenClaw” conversation instead of the agent they use for real work. This retires that frontend while keeping recovery controls and earlier setup history available.

## User Impact

Plugin and setting questions open an editable, unsent draft in the selected agent’s regular Home conversation, preserving the existing draft. Settings creates agents through the normal creation flow and offers a separate role/team planning entry. Android Settings opens ordinary Home rather than another assistant.

Models and Updates remain directly usable when inference is broken. Administrators can read configuration changes and earlier setup conversations in **System history**; stored transcripts are not deleted or imported into ordinary chat. The shared Home/plugin dock and saved placement/size preferences remain. Old /custodian URLs redirect by readiness and never create an agent on load.

**Draft limitations:** actual Android build/device and Apple-platform acceptance, live-provider lifecycle proof, and complete independent source review are still pending. This is not ready to merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is **PR2 of the stacked series**, based on #202108 at 340fad47aeb444cc7fa4d19626267380d523e374, not main. Caller migration and removal land together so no navigation, palette, store, event or restore path can reopen the retired conversation. Backend system-agent operations, CLI/rescue paths and their authorization remain outside this PR.

Contextual help uses ordinary chat permissions and is bound to the viewer, Gateway, agent and session. Embedded Settings uses its visible ordinary chat route instead of a disabled dock. The bootstrap closing line now points back to this agent; recognition of untouched v2026.11.5 bootstrap files is preserved.

## Evidence

- 202 affected UI unit tests passed, including draft/context ownership, direct credential recovery, dock retention and admin-only history recovery.
- 68 workspace/bootstrap tests and 16 prompt-prefix stability tests passed. The v2026.11.5 template fingerprint was independently checked against the released source.
- Targeted Chromium tests passed for desktop/phone plugin help, retained unsent drafts and redacted credential values, embedded iOS/Android routing, legacy-link readiness without creation, first-agent handoff/reconnect/cancellation, inference-independent Updates recovery, and affected settings navigation/layout.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint, stylelint, controller guards, UI/native source-catalog verification, documentation links and diff checks passed. The production UI build completed. Paired predecessor/change builds retain inherited CSS-size and chat-request advisories; no budget or exception was raised.
- Simplification removes the interactive custodian frontend and its obsolete tests rather than adding another assistant. Existing history APIs and the normal chat/draft owners remain authoritative.

The browser evidence renders the actual UI with synthetic Gateway fixtures; native-embed browser tests are **not native-app or live-provider acceptance**. The configured Auto Review helper is unavailable in this environment. Independent source review remains blocked in this environment and is required before this draft can be marked ready; no clean review is claimed.

The latest predecessor refresh was rechecked with UI typecheck, 14 wizard-owner tests and 9 automatic-setup browser cases. The paired build-budget comparison used PR1 at 4ea6d2e; the remaining CSS/request advisories were already present there and were not relaxed.

### Clean comparison

**After**

prs.title: docs: explain the Proactive check's cost on shared local model servers
prs.body:
Related: #202146, #134994, #201282

## What Problem This Solves

People who run OpenClaw on a local model server don't learn from the docs that the default Proactive check sends
the main conversation's whole prompt to their model every 30 minutes, even when it has no way to reach them. On a
server with one or two parallel slots it also pushes the conversation they are using out of the prompt cache.

## User Impact

The local models page now says what the job costs on a local server, how to find it, and how to turn it off, run
it less often, or move it to a smaller model. Docs only; no behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cost shows up only in server logs. On one install with a local llama.cpp server (two 65,536-token slots), the
default job made 344 requests in 6 days with a median prompt of 51,212 tokens: 62% of all prompt tokens the server
processed. No channel was configured, so every run ended with `Owner delivery unavailable (no-route)` (details in
#202146). The section points to the existing commands. If #201282 lands and removes `skipIfScratchEmpty`, the
second bullet should go.

## Evidence

- Docs checks on this branch: formatting clean (`format:docs:check`), MDX check passed, link audit 0 broken links,
  markdown lint 0 issues, pre-commit hook passed. `docs:spellcheck` fails on main already, in other files; nothing
  in `local-models.md`.
- Every flag used exists on main (`src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-options.ts`: `--every`, `--model`, `--session`,
  `--light-context`); `automations disable` is documented in `docs/gateway/heartbeat.md`.
- The measurement comes from the llama.cpp server log and the Gateway's automation run history over
  2026-11-13 to 2026-11-19 (2026.11.3 source build; the job definition is unchanged on main).

prs.title: improve: show progress when creating a Template and keep the agent’s portrait
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you asked an agent to make a Template, you could wait minutes without seeing which skills or routines it was choosing. Its Publish card could also show generic artwork instead of the agent’s portrait.

## User Impact

The agent acknowledges the request, tells you which skills and plugins go with it, then explains which routines it is keeping. The private Publish card uses the agent’s portrait when available. Nothing is published without your action.

## Why This Change Was Made

One inventory command gathers the agent’s skills, installed plugin releases, and active routines. It reuses the existing private draft creator for ordinary chat requests. The agent writes the instructions a new owner needs without a word quota. A paused routine does not become a new owner’s running job. The Gateway re-encodes the portrait for the card and archive rather than copying the original image metadata.

## Evidence

- On an earlier revision, two real-model browser runs reached an enabled Publish button in 59.1s and 64.9s, compared with 67s previously on the same model. The first messages appeared at 7.4s and 7.9s, followed by separate skills and routine updates. These were fresh conversations with a configured agent, not fresh installs or timings of the final inventory implementation. The recordings contain private workspace details and are not attached publicly.
- In both runs, the portrait in chat matched the artwork on the card. Previously the card showed generic artwork. A fixture with one active and one paused routine previously offered both; after the follow-up fix, only the active routine was offered. The 85 focused draft, Gateway, and review-card tests passed (41 + 32 + 12).
- With only `- **Avatar:** avatars/demo.png` in a synthetic agent’s `IDENTITY.md`, the previous inventory omitted the portrait. With the same workspace and the real agent roster projection, the repaired inventory staged all 68 PNG bytes unchanged for review. The inventory, identity parser, and agent listing tests passed, as did `pnpm check:changed --staged` for the portrait repair. This checks discovery and staging, not fresh-install behavior.
- Before the packaging repair, the worker build rejected an unstaged native SVG binary. Afterwards all 12 portable worker builds completed without that binary, and the Gateway’s SVG portrait packaging test still passed.
- With synthetic installed-release records, the old inventory missed a managed skill and reported a plugin alias at `latest`; the repaired inventory returned `@demo/managed-brief@1.2.3` and `@demo/adapter@2.3.4`. The committed CLI-boundary regression also covers an unversioned installation request, agent filtering, and reusing a supplied draft without creating a second one. `pnpm check:changed --staged` passed on the inventory repair.

**Fresh-install limitation:** The clean-install rehearsal retained the imported agent and its portrait, but stopped before the first model reply. It is not an install-to-Publish demonstration or an exact-head latency measurement. The maintainer approved landing without that recording; review and required CI still apply.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep Model Setup probes out of chat history
prs.body:
Root cause: packages/session-url-contract/src/session-key.ts:8 the incognito key pattern lists only `dashboard`, `subagent` and `internal-session-effects`, so the Model Setup check key `agent:<id>:setup-inference:incognito-…` (src/system-agent/setup-inference-turn.ts:90) is treated as a normal session and the Codex harness leaves `ephemeral` off its `thread/start` (extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-requests.ts:252).

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw shares its Codex home with Codex Desktop or the CLI, a tool-free Model Setup probe can appear in chat history. If a user reopens that thread and asks it to run a command, the probe's saved instructions can still cause a tool refusal.

## User Impact

New Model Setup probes use temporary Codex threads and stay out of saved chat history. Normal chats still save their Codex threads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Model Setup creates keys in the `setup-inference:incognito-…` namespace. Add that namespace to the shared incognito key classifier so the existing Codex `thread/start` logic sends `ephemeral: true`. The setup turn still runs with `disableTools: true`. Ordinary keys in the same namespace stay non-incognito; Model Setup is the only producer of `setup-inference` keys.

Doctor side effect: each check's audit rows (`agent.run.started`/`finished`) carry its session key. With this change, `openclaw doctor` reports those rows as keys in the reserved incognito namespace, and `openclaw doctor --fix` rewrites their `session_key` to a `legacy-incognito-` key. That applies to rows from earlier checks and from new ones. Control UI incognito chats already get the same Doctor finding today. This PR is on hold until Doctor's reserved-key repair skips `audit_events`.

The regression test covers a probe-shaped key and an ordinary key in the same namespace.

## Evidence

Isolated Gateway run with the real bundled Codex app-server and a local ChatGPT backend: on `main` the Model Setup check starts a saved Codex thread (`ephemeral` unset, one rollout, listed by Codex `thread/list`). On this head it sends `ephemeral: true`, writes no rollout, Codex lists no thread, and the check still succeeds. A normal chat afterwards still saves one thread. Output and Codex source references: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199452#issuecomment-7026472339

Focused test `src/shared/incognito-session-key.test.ts`: the setup-check key case fails on the merge base and all 10 cases pass on this head.

Thanks @pimalaispaphuket-debug for the fix.

Merge danger: two-way door for the Codex thread behavior; reverting restores saved probe threads, and no config or schema changes. Not fully reversible for audit history: after this change, `openclaw doctor --fix` rewrites the session key on Model Setup check audit rows, and a revert does not restore those rows. Blast radius: Model Setup checks on the Codex runtime, Doctor runs on installs that have run a check, and the other incognito-key consumers, which now treat these probe-only keys as incognito.

prs.title: fix(tools): report a send that may have landed as unconfirmed
prs.body:
## Outstanding tool-result proof — November 19, 2026

The current-head code findings are resolved and `openclaw/ci-gate` is successful, but the real accepted-without-receipt **message-tool/model** proof remains outstanding. The November 17 Synapse test is valid SDK recovery evidence, not that missing proof: its proxy replaces only the first success with 429, then exposes a successful receipt on retry; the fixture asserts one delivery callback. It therefore cannot establish `status: "delivery_unconfirmed"`, `delivered: false`, and no model resend. The earlier readiness qualification below must not be read as clearing this remaining runtime gate.

A bounded execution preflight on November 19 found no usable secretless runner in this repair scope: local Docker has no daemon socket; direct AWS credential resolution failed before allocation. The retained Goal 24 hosted workflow is push-only on its separate proof branch and its Matrix job is disabled; changing that branch is outside this four-PR repair scope. Native `review-init` was also attempted; after transient cache contention cleared, the retained-anchor dependency cache failed validation because `kysely` could not resolve. No cache locks or shared installs were altered, no product code was executed locally, and no new runtime success is claimed.

Remaining acceptance: an isolated Gateway agent/model invokes the real message tool; the homeserver accepts a send while all transport recovery ends without a receipt; the tool returns `delivery_unconfirmed` with `delivered: false`; independent recipient history contains exactly one event and the model does not resend. A qualified secretless execution route is still required. Existing causal, SDK, encryption, and current-head CI evidence below is retained without rerunning it.

## Current correction and proof status

**READY FOR REVIEW — M3/M4 evidence resolved; native preparation completed.** Current signed head: `bf8ee2c6152a18386a175ad329013bc20a4a8051` (tree `c8a203d47cc697a578ec478d79bdfcf2b80d340d`). Native publication verified; independent exact-candidate source review found no actionable P0–P3 issue. This is readiness qualification, not merge approval.

- Earlier owner-recorded `sentBeforeError` stays `delivery_unconfirmed`, even with later nested rejection. A typed Matrix HTTP 403 proves permanent rejection only for a fresh SDK event with exactly one matching wire request; repeats, redirects and existing events remain uncertain. Queue-reconciliation wording requires held custody.
- **M4 resolved in source and current CI:** unique per-client mock transaction IDs preserve the production duplicate-dispatch guard; all 97 SDK tests, including concurrent room ordering, passed.
- Added real Matrix SDK → guarded loopback HTTP regressions for first-403 versus 307→403, with wire count/path and client cleanup. These do not exercise SDK-event reconstruction/resend.
- Native baseline refresh incorporates canonical `976a4fb8784a326579108e03d0df4356dad501a3`, including scripts typecheck fix `5e302bddf1cbf56acc94bc84061bff1eede74031`; no duplicate repair.
- Signature, ancestry, product-diff identity, `git diff --check`, and trusted formatting passed. Product diff SHA256: `a21a1ad7197749e6513cfb8a3bb99c5e5cb3d8fc2aa86bcdf9e6ffc5d2095971`.
- **M3 causal/timing portion collected:** the independent original-module-red/candidate-green pairs and isolated Matrix test-file wrapper wall times are now available below. The original-module differential is not a full historical-baseline checkout; the separate authenticated live proof is recorded below.
### Current-head CI — passed

CI [43618778733](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43618778733), attempt 2, completed successfully on November 14, 2026 at 17:13:43 UTC: 47 jobs passed, 28 skipped, no failures; `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. Workflow Sanity, OpenGrep, CodeQL and Critical Quality also passed. Periphery reporting passed with platform scans skipped.

This run binds head `bf8ee2c6152a18386a175ad329013bc20a4a8051`; tests checked out GitHub merge commit `15e89eb3ced433a73cb7c6c8bdfb3ac40cbb3ed8` against canonical main `89c5b179fc3d82eb37dba517b789475d4314e0e3`, not a literal head-only checkout.

- Matrix SDK: 97 tests; transport: 16; transport authority integration: 14. Actual SDK→HTTP direct-403 and redirect→403 regressions passed (56ms and 37ms). Matrix times are per-case sums (26.850s / 0.658s / 0.048s), **not isolated file wall times**.
- Message-tool execution: 74 tests / 22.71s Vitest duration; scheduled lifetime: 18 / 18.28s; accepted results: 35 / 13.37s. Total across these six requested files: 254 passing tests.
- Production types, extension/scripts test types, all five core test-type stripes, general lint and all five core-lint stripes passed. Neither the prior duplicate transaction-ID error nor scripts TS18048 recurred.
- This establishes candidate-green, not independently replayed baseline-red/fix-green. No live homeserver delivery or encrypted recipient event was tested.

## Matrix — causal original-module qualification

PR #197000 candidate `bf8ee2c6152a18386a175ad329013bc20a4a8051`; original module source `937f77cb20ded2e041f5ea876200d01b449d0329`. Product code is unchanged by this proof. Execution tooling `08e028a6bba5f6e1dcdc09739cdb26730ea55dd8`; final admission-only tooling `f00d850619271dbd39cf713dc43322d2fd622925`.

- Run 43790032640 (tooling `a95800834f9353eb801eebff4a8b274ecb9f1d99`): all **97 SDK cases passed**, isolated wrapper wall time **71.404 s**. Its job was red only because the old evidence gate incorrectly rejected a legitimate repeated parameterized title; the retained report was re-admitted, not rerun.
- Run 43790694571 (tooling `a4dec2e6e0c3f006aeaf24a195bfc514da4de2eb`): candidate **transport 16/16** (**51.330 s**), **authority integration 14/14** (**3.005 s**), and selected message-owner cases **2/2** (**65.565 s**) passed. These are isolated, serial wrapper wall times including setup, not per-case sums or full-file timing for the filtered owner suite.
- The same run replaced only `sdk/client-core.ts`, `sdk/message-wire-dispatch.ts`, and `src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.ts` with original bytes, keeping candidate dependencies and tests. In the real SDK → guarded loopback HTTP pair, the **direct 403 failed** the intended permanent-rejection assertion at `transport.test.ts:154:35`, while **307 → 403 passed** its uncertainty assertion. Original-wire wrapper wall time **50.774 s**, launcher exit 1.
- The driver initially rejected that genuine causal failure because Vitest abbreviated `Cannot send to room` to `Cannot se…`. The repair admits only the exact observed M_FORBIDDEN/403 prefix, expected `retryable: false` object, pinned assertion path/line/column, required two case identities/statuses, and launcher exit 1; it still rejects missing/extra/duplicate cases, setup/timeout/connection failures, wrong error, wrong assertion, wrong expectation, and unrelated truncation. The original structured JSON is preserved and replayed; no product rerun was spent on the admission repair.

This is an **original-module differential in the candidate environment**, not a full historical-baseline checkout/build, live homeserver test, or proof of encrypted recipient delivery. The tests and all three changed-module hash pairs are checked against the retained report before the continuation executes.

Validation: 26/26 synthetic admission checks pass; the exact retained report is rejected by the old gate and admitted by the repaired gate. Targeted lint, format, Node syntax, whitespace checks and repository workflow validation pass. Workflow validation initially encountered empty token variables; rerunning with only those empty variables removed passed. Fresh independent native review found no P0–P2 findings in the continuation three-file delta (SHA-256 `3df2a28366a1d16d76015b792192b26d20235b4b64c8a2223c929b574fd3a70f`). This is the established explicitly labeled native fallback, not an autoreview/ClawSweeper result; the configured service's 402 credit failure was not retried or bypassed.

[Continuation run 43791792505 / job 133051654842](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43791792505/job/133051654842) downloaded only the two fixed retained artifacts using read-only Actions access and executed only the previously missing **original-owner** pair. Original `sentBeforeError=false` passed; original `sentBeforeError=true` failed with `OutboundDeliveryError: message failed: MatrixError: [403] M_FORBIDDEN`, created at the pinned test's line 457, rather than returning `delivery_unconfirmed`. Candidate versions of both cases passed in the prior run. Original-owner isolated wrapper wall time: **66.949 s**, launcher exit 1; per-case times 30.257 ms / 12.829 ms.

The continuation job remains **red**: its evidence gate mistook Vitest's ordinary `runWithTimeout` stack-frame name for a timeout diagnostic. The final admission-only correction filters stack frames out of infrastructure diagnostics, preserves real timeout/setup/connection rejection, and requires the exact original-owner error prefix and source location. All six retained JSON reports replay successfully through that corrected gate, with no further product execution. The final workflow disables the completed Matrix job; no completed SDK, candidate, wire, history, audio, permission, or billing stage was rerun.

[Retained artifact 14193046368](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43791792505/artifacts/14193046368), `goal24-matrix-43791792505`, contains the six source reports, original-owner log, and the original red summary. The corrected admission result is a local replay, **not a new green hosted run**. Fresh independent native review of the final admission/disable delta also found no P0–P2 findings (SHA-256 `f2eeb134d198b733cdd40f441837d580cc4f7c0ddfd4321dc2606e188889a13e`). Final 26/26 admission tests, exact six-report replay, targeted lint/format/syntax, workflow validation, and whitespace checks passed.

### Real Matrix homeserver proof — November 17, 2026

[Hosted run 43990720491 / job 133730280334](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43990720491/job/133730280334) **passed all three required live contracts** against unchanged candidate bf8ee2c6152a18386a175ad329013bc20a4a8051, using execution tooling b25f1009d0b0dfafc2e1ffe624751f28fa94ee0f. The earlier causal/timing jobs were not rerun.

Disposable Ubuntu 24.04 / Node 24.22.1 ran real Synapse 1.165.0, pinned to ghcr.io/element-hq/synapse@sha256:b7f105b3c5f6d8bdb0a1aaff51ec4264dd109d8ed5532009d176bcb28a57ca0a. Temporary local Alice/Bob accounts exercised the production SDK, transport, SQLite-backed durable plan, and crypto.

- Authenticated send: Bob independently read exactly one event matching the returned event ID and sender (0.969 s).
- Accepted-then-429: the proxy received upstream HTTP 200 before returning 429; retry reused the identical transaction path and event ID, with one delivery callback and one recipient event (2.700 s).
- E2EE: an independent recipient SDK decrypted the plaintext; server history independently showed one m.room.encrypted / m.megolm.v1.aes-sha2 event containing ciphertext and no plaintext body (1.810 s).

[Artifact 14286724744](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43990720491/artifacts/14286724744), goal24-matrix-live-43990720491, is 3,677 bytes; archive SHA-256 0c2c15a77af0ac2cd7d06e32681af4ea4a496d686ad7acc9caaf367191193b48. Downloaded report/observations passed exact identity and three-case admission. Fixture SHA-256 d5337fc5ce60f4741ed87bab770c1dd40e35ae9ef3c3366b01aee277c30d23dc. Inspection found no token/password fields or bearer credentials; raw SDK/server-state/install logs were not uploaded. Container cleanup exited 0.

Initial run 43990033248 at c408675efbcce1a96ca983a4478aa7d8df66664e passed authenticated delivery but could not open SQLite for the remaining cases. The driver correction selected the canonical isolated database-worker configuration, narrowing only its include list; the unchanged fixture then passed. This is a harness correction, not a product-code fix. Six admission tests plus targeted lint, format, syntax, and whitespace checks passed. Prior independent findings were addressed; @RomneyDa explicitly waived further independent/formal review for this proof-only patch on November 17, 2026. No new formal review is claimed.

**Limits:** retry is within one sendMessageMatrix invocation, not Gateway queue restart/replay or persisted-plan reload. Cross-signing/device trust is not verified. No real-user device, real-model flow, merge, main write, deployment, backport, or release is claimed. Final retention head 4f4d4c3baa37a1c41ed9e60f222e4b499ea44b9f disables the live job; all five prior jobs remain disabled.


### Native readiness qualification — November 17, 2026

Reused the unchanged exact-head independent source review; no new review or signature is claimed. Native `review-init`, `review-checkout-pr`, and `review-validate-artifacts` completed with `READY FOR /prepare-pr`, zero findings. Native `prepare-run` completed at the same head and verified that the remote already matched; no product commit or push was needed. The native gate receipt is `github_pending` (not a fabricated successful-test stamp); separately observed exact-head CI run 43618778733 attempt 2 and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. PR remains open, non-draft and mergeable; no merge was requested.

### Historical failures and environmental limits

- Historical head `4aa0faa30907ba9ce07cfaccdaa7dd21c4bbf1b9`: CI run 43606138401 attempt 2 failed on M4 fixture collision and inherited scripts TS18048. It passed message-tool execution (74 tests), scheduled lifetime (18), accepted results (35), production types and lint. None of this is current-head runtime proof.
- Secretless AWS allocation failed before any lease because credentials were unavailable. No AWS tests or credentialed fallback ran; no contributor runtime executed on the trusted local host.
- The earlier absence of live Matrix credentials was resolved by the disposable, secretless Synapse fixture above; no production credentials were used.

The results below belong to the contributor's earlier head and are retained for attribution/history, not current-head proof.

<details>
<summary>Historical contributor description and earlier-head evidence (superseded where noted above)</summary>

## What Problem This Solves

A `message` tool send can pass the point where the channel may already have accepted it and still come back as a failure — #196802 has Matrix answering `/send/m.room.encrypted/<txn>` with `429 Server is unavailable` after it accepted the event. The tool then reported a plain failure (`message failed: MatrixError: [429] ...`), the model did what "failed" implies, and the room got the same text twice. The delivery queue already knew better: it recorded `unknown_after_send` and reconciled the entry as already sent minutes later, but that knowledge never reached the tool result.

The queue's terminal failure already carries it. `OutboundDeliveryError.sentBeforeError` is set when an earlier attempt of the same intent started or its outcome is unknown, which is exactly the "may have landed" state. This projects that one case as a `delivery_unconfirmed` tool result so the model waits instead of minting a second send.

Two facts decide what the model may be told, and both already exist on the error:

- **Who owns reconciliation.** `owner.project(...)` stamps `queueCustody = "held"` while the durable queue still owns the attempt and `"released"` once it is retired; a `skipQueue` send (`message-tool-execution.ts:575`, scheduled direct sends) has no owner at all. Only `"held"` keeps the Gateway-reconciliation wording. Undefined or `"released"` reports `No queued retry owns it, so the send may already have reached the recipient; check it before resending.` — because there is no row to reconcile and promising one would be false.
- **What the provider already proved.** A permanent pre-dispatch rejection can carry `sentBeforeError` evidence from another payload in the same batch. When the error graph holds a `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError{retryable:false}`, the projection returns nothing and the rejection keeps its actionable error and cause.

Everything else keeps its current behavior: a failure that provably never left still throws, and a failure with confirmed platform sends keeps its existing partial-delivery path (`projectScheduledMessageActionPartialResult`), because the projection requires an empty `results` list.

Open question for the Matrix owner: `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/transport.ts:269-283` wraps `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError` only when the fetch never started, so a post-dispatch 403 is still reported as `sentBeforeError` and is indistinguishable here from an accepted-then-429 send. Classifying those as `retryable: false` in the adapter would route them through `isProvenDeliveryNotSentError` and out of this projection; that policy is not decided inside a tool-result projection.

Closes #196802

## Evidence

Red — both new behaviours fail against the previous projection, test kept (`node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/tools/message-tool-execution.test.ts`):

```
×  message tool unconfirmed delivery > does not promise a queued retry when custody is undefined
×  message tool unconfirmed delivery > does not promise a queued retry when custody is released
×  message tool unconfirmed delivery > keeps a provider-proven rejection actionable
   Tests  3 failed | 70 passed (73)
```

Green — same command on `937f77cb2`:

```
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  73 passed (73)
```

Other checks, on `origin/main` at `584084d77`:

- `src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.accepted-results.test.ts` — passed.
- `src/agents/tools/message-tool.scheduled-lifetime.test.ts` — 17 passed, 1 failed (`settles provider revocation during send via direct as accepted`). That failure reproduces identically with this change reverted, so it is a pre-existing Windows baseline, not a regression.
- `oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json` on the touched files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-root.json` — no diagnostics for the touched files (the repo's pre-existing `@openclaw/fs-safe` drift in unrelated files is unchanged).
- `run-format.mts --check` — all files formatted.
- Test-line ratchet: `config/test-lines-allocations/196802-message-tool-unconfirmed-delivery.txt` = 67, matching the +67 test lines.

Diff against `584084d77` is +96/-3 across `message-tool-execution.ts` (rename), `message-action-execution.ts` (projection), the test file, and the ratchet allocation.

Why the proof is not here: this machine cannot build the dist (`@openclaw/fs-safe` in `node_modules` predates `preserve`, so `build-all.mts runtime` dies in `plugins:assets:build`), and the remaining item needs a live homeserver that accepts a message and then answers 429 without an event id. A maintainer proof run only has to assert `status: "delivery_unconfirmed"` with `delivered: false` on the tool result plus one recipient event.

</details>

prs.title: fix: let setup use account models with a fresh catalog
prs.body:
Fixes #202016

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw setup` can reject an account-available model as unknown when its local catalog is cold, including when the model is pinned to the built-in `openclaw` runtime. Users currently have to complete a separate model-catalog refresh before setup can verify inference.

## User Impact

Users can run setup with a fresh catalog without manually refreshing it first. Setup still requires a successful inference response; unavailable models remain rejected. No configuration migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

When setup cannot resolve its configured model locally, its read-only runtime now waits for provider-scoped discovery and captures the resulting model facts before inference. This reuses the existing catalog owner, preserves cancellation and cleanup, and does not save discovered rows or alter the configured model. Ordinary turns and explicitly selected native runtimes retain their existing paths.

## Evidence

The real setup command handler failed with `Unknown model` against a synthetic HTTP provider on baseline `99e2b6eb1f9bf8867ce647e11d9279da943443fa`, then passed with the fix. All five regression cases and 34 focused sibling tests pass: 39 tests across five files.

The four additional baseline cases also fail: implicit runtime rejects the available model; empty/failed listings never reach catalog discovery; cancellation cannot reach an in-flight listing. Patched tests cover matching request credentials, no inference after empty/failed discovery, cancellation closing discovery, unchanged config bytes, and no persisted catalog rows.

Core and services-test type checks, focused lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. `pr-simplify` consolidated duplicate request/body assertions without reducing coverage. Regression test time: 13.01 s; complete focused run: 127.20 s wall. CI timing is not yet available.

Validation gaps: no live OpenAI/model-account or macOS run and no full build/CI run. Local automated review could not start because the reviewer configuration rejected the `cachesInstructions` compatibility field; no clean-review verdict is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Focused test command</summary>

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/system-agent/setup-inference.cold-catalog.integration.test.ts \
  src/system-agent/setup-inference-turn.test.ts \
  src/commands/system-agent-with-inference.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/prepared-runtime-context.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.prepared-harness-source-delivery.integration.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

Local implementation commit: `16cce2c2706177121943e139115b0b2c119f8f7b`.

</details>

Co-authored with @daniel-lxs.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-t_49bs8y)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs

prs.title: fix(test): retain Doctor failure details in upgrade receipts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Upgrade-survivor CI now identifies a rejected post-activation Doctor step, but its bounded failure receipt omits the process state and finding severities that explain why that step was rejected. The full update output can be truncated before those details.

## User Impact

CI maintainers can distinguish process failures from Doctor findings using the retained receipt. This is diagnostic-only; update behavior and acceptance rules are unchanged, and the underlying observed update failure is not resolved by this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Append bounded termination, signal, killed/output-limit flags, failure-fact and finding counts, and up to eight Doctor check IDs/severities to the existing rejected-step context. Finding messages and raw failure details are excluded. The existing acceptance predicate and independent receipt/redaction owner are retained.

## Evidence

- Natural failure: [scheduled CI artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44637548930/artifacts/14586886837) identifies step 23 of 27, post-activation Doctor inspections, exit 1, with recoverable-maintenance advisory; the discriminating step details were unavailable in the bounded update payload.
- Native receipt proof: the new metadata assertion fails on the base (1 failed, 41 skipped, 1.02s); the candidate passes both complete assertion and migration-diagnostic files (134 tests, 35.41s). This exercises the real assertion CLI, independent receipt, redaction, and bounded publication.
- Targeted root-tooling typecheck, changed-file typed lint, and format all passed.
- Fresh full-range local ClawSweeper review of `f03cea11e222` → `aa49c85a8a47`: no correctness/security findings (0.93 confidence); the review was read-only, and the native runtime proof above completed afterward.

The existing receipt regression retains oversized-output truncation, secret redaction, and step coordinates, and additionally checks finding bounds and exclusion of private finding/failure messages. No Docker replay is part of this change.

prs.title: fix(codex): avoid promising repairs for unresolved assignment warnings
prs.body:
Related: #199607.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor promises to repair duplicate or obsolete Codex assignments even when it found only unresolved ownership warnings and cannot safely change them.

## User Impact

Warning-only detection now asks operators to inspect unresolved warnings and explains that uncertain assignments are preserved. Uncertain state remains pending, diagnostics remain visible, and actual duplicate/obsolete repairs still run. No schema or readiness-contract change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial replacements-only proposal was withdrawn after review showed it could bypass warning delivery and incorrectly certify plugin readiness. This narrower correction preserves the established recovery contract instead of treating missing ownership evidence as completion. Detection continues beyond warning-only pages to find available repairs.

## Evidence

- Baseline host regression failed on the generic repair promise; the discarded candidate also failed by returning no plan.
- Focused Codex suite: 20/20; host Doctor suite: 16/16. The host regression uses isolated real SQLite to exercise inspection, repair and replay, asserting visible recoverable diagnostics, withheld completion and unchanged serialized rows.
- Pagination regression proves later-page repairs still run without discarding warning-only rows.
- Formatting, targeted lint and diff checks pass. Source-owner typecheck includes changed production and test files; package-boundary typecheck requires SDK declarations absent in this checkout.
- Independent read-only Codex review of the full candidate found no P0-P2 findings. Structured autoreview CLI unavailable.
- Real shipped Doctor CLI proof: built and executed the supported `pnpm openclaw doctor` entry point on macOS; eight preview, advisory, repair, and replay invocations exited 0. Warning-only and mixed-page fixtures showed unresolved guidance, byte-preserved uncertain assignments, later-page repairs, and idempotent replay; no uncertain ownership assignment was removed.
- Latest-stable state migration replay: installed registry stable `2026.11.3` in a disposable Linux guest, completed configuration validation and Doctor, and obtained healthy Gateway status with Discord configured. Copies of the stopped stable profile were seeded through the shipped stable SDK, then inspected, repaired and replayed through the exact PR source CLI. All six completed Doctor invocations passed. The warning-only serialized row was unchanged; the 513-row mixed fixture retained all 512 warning/inert rows, changed only the valid current-session binding from two duplicate assignments to one, and was identical on replay. Channel/provider settings and the selected model were preserved.

prs.title: fix(sessions): preserve the initial followup policy denial reason
prs.body:
Closes #200072

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `sessions_send(mode: "followup")` replaces every policy denial with `Followup session access was revoked.`, even when the denial happens on the initial admission and nothing was revoked. Operators cannot tell a real authorization restriction from a defect, and the endpoint and reason are discarded.

## User Impact

The initial refusal now names the endpoint (requester or target), the policy code, and the real message. Only a denial detected after admission keeps the "revoked" wording, so a restriction is no longer misreported as a lost grant.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Track whether the initial admission already succeeded. A first denial reports "denied"; a later one reports "revoked".
- Surface the endpoint role plus the denial `code` and `message` from the policy owner instead of a fixed string.
- Keep the access watcher, revocation latch, and custody behavior unchanged.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/sessions-send-followup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 6/6 passed, including the new initial-denial case and the existing revocation latch cases.
- Red-on-base: reverting only the custody source produces `Followup session access was revoked.` instead of the denial details.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; oxlint clean on both changed files.
