prs.title: fix: show a plugin page that opens directly or after a reload
prs.body:
Root cause: `ui/src/plugins/control-ui-view.solid.tsx:283` (merge base 999e873a9165) tries a plugin view's mount once, when it settles, and `mount()` returns at `:231` while the host is detached. On a direct link or reload, the plugin activation selects the workspace replacement and registers the page together. The shell's workspace nodes leave the document, and the routed page (`ui/src/pages/plugin/plugin-page.tsx:165`) is built inside them before the replacement re-inserts them with `mountDefault`. That skipped mount was never retried.

Fixes #201511

Thanks @namhnguyen for the report and the precise analysis, and @deepujain for the fix.

## What Problem This Solves

When a plugin page is opened by direct link or reload (`/plugin?plugin=<id>&id=<page>`) and the plugin has selected a workspace replacement that calls `mountDefault(...)`, the page area stays empty. There is no error and no "Retry view" card. Opening the same page from the menu works.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin pages opened directly or after a reload show their content instead of a blank page. Opening a page from the menu, and moving a page after it has mounted, work as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin view now keeps a mount it skipped while its host was detached and runs it when the host connects. It uses the per-view handle the element already keeps. The pending mount runs at most once, and it is dropped when the view unmounts or is replaced. A page that has already mounted is not mounted again when it moves. There is still one mount path: the connect hook calls the same mount function as before.

## Evidence

Browser proof on a real Gateway with the built Control UI, before/after screenshots and observed lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201542#issuecomment-7026364016

- Before (merge base): on direct link and on reload, the page view is connected but the plugin's page `mount` never ran, so the area is blank. After: the page renders, with `mount` called once.
- Controls: opening from the menu renders on both builds. Moving the mounted page does not mount it again on either build.
- Regression test in `ui/src/plugins/control-ui-surface.test.tsx` follows the real order: the shell reuses its workspace nodes, and a delegating replacement builds the page while they are detached. It fails on the merge base (page never rendered) and passes here. It also moves the page and checks that it is not mounted again or disposed.
- Bundle size: chat boot JS +20 B gzip, startup JS +0 B (`scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts` against the merge base; the rule allows up to 600 B).

Merge danger: two-way door. This is a Control UI-only change with no stored state or contract change, so a revert fully undoes it. If it were wrong, the blast radius is plugin views (pages, panels, widgets, replacements) that mount while their host is detached.

prs.title: fix: long outbound replies stall the gateway while being split
prs.body:
Closes #199440

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the gateway stalls and spikes memory when it splits a long outbound reply that has spaces or non-ASCII text.

## User Impact

User impact: a multi-MiB message no longer blocks other sessions for seconds or allocates GBs of native memory.

## Why This Change Was Made

The grapheme helpers segmented the whole remaining text for every chunk. They now segment a bounded window, so the work is linear.

## Evidence

- New work-volume test fails on `main`, passes here.
- `chunkText` on 4 MiB of spaced text: 2478 ms before, 15 ms after.
- chunk, text-chunking and markdown-core tests pass (286). tsc, oxfmt, oxlint clean.
- Not run: Windows, a live channel send.

## Real behavior proof

Real `chunkText` (`src/auto-reply/chunk.ts`), 4 MiB spaced input, limit 4000, fresh process, Node v24.22.3, Linux x86_64. Run in a checkout of base `918847e` and head `3c0c157`:

Only 2 cases differ, where the limit is smaller than one cluster (cut inside it, no text lost). This check also found a CRLF/prepend whitespace bug, fixed in the second commit.

prs.title: fix(install): honor --beta for git installs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Installing with `install.sh --install-method git --beta` still installs the latest stable release. The flag is accepted, nothing warns, and the ref that gets checked out is `latest` instead of `beta`.

## User Impact

User impact: `--beta` now installs the beta channel for git installs, the same way it already does for npm and Bun installs. Explicit versions and branches are unchanged, and a flag-selected `--beta` whose beta dist-tag is unavailable (e.g. no npm on a fresh host) falls back through latest resolution instead of failing to check out a nonexistent `beta` ref.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolve_git_openclaw_ref` (`scripts/install-policy.sh`) builds its request from `OPENCLAW_VERSION` alone. `--beta` only sets `USE_BETA=1` (`scripts/install.sh`), and that flag is read by the npm and Bun engine paths — after the git ref was already resolved. The resolver now prefers the beta channel when `USE_BETA` is set and the request is a channel (`latest`/`next`/unset), keeping an explicit pin or branch authoritative. Because the git ref resolution precedes `ensure_node`, a fresh host without npm made the beta dist-tag lookup fail and returned the literal `beta`; flag-selected beta now falls back through latest resolution, while an explicit `--version beta` keeps its literal meaning.

Scope note: this PR covers the `--beta` half of #201335.

## Evidence

**Real registry + real checkout (base vs this head).** Channel selection is exercised without any stubbed npm: the installer read the public registry and checked out real upstream tags.

```
$ npm view openclaw dist-tags --json
{ "latest": "2026.11.6", "beta": "2026.11.10-beta.1", "extended-stable": "2026.10.33", "alpha": "1.10.0-alpha" }
```

The checkout target was a blobless clone of `github.com/openclaw/openclaw` (`--filter=blob:none`, the same form the installer uses), driven through `--git-dir`; `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` were isolated and a settings file plus a workspace marker existed before the runs and survived them.

Base (upstream main `416b357`), `--beta` on a git install — the flag is accepted but latest is installed:

```
$ bash scripts/install.sh --install-method git --beta --no-onboard --git-dir <repo>
Beta channel: enabled
· Using git ref: v2026.11.6
$ git -C <repo> describe --tags --exact-match HEAD
v2026.11.6
```

This PR's head, same command, same registry, same checkout (an upgrade from latest-stable to beta):

```
$ bash scripts/install.sh --install-method git --beta --no-onboard --git-dir <repo>
Beta channel: enabled
· Using git ref: v2026.11.10-beta.1
· Fetching requested version
· Checking out v2026.11.10-beta.1
$ git -C <repo> describe --tags --exact-match HEAD
v2026.11.10-beta.1
$ git -C <repo> status --porcelain | wc -l
0
$ cat "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH"
{ "gateway": { "mode": "local" }, "agents": { "defaults": { "workspace": "<isolated>/ws" } } }
```

Latest-stable baseline on the same checkout without `--beta` (this head): `Using git ref: v2026.11.6` → `Checking out v2026.11.6`, HEAD `v2026.11.6`.

**Missing-beta fallback (stubbed npm).** The public registry always publishes a `beta` dist-tag, so the fallback cannot be produced against it. That case keeps the stubbed-`npm` environment (controlled `dist-tags`, local git checkout with `v2026.11.5` and `v2026.11.6-beta.2`): base (policy before the fallback) prints the literal `beta` and the checkout fails, this head falls back to latest.

```
# base commit (policy before the fallback)
Beta channel: enabled
· Using git ref: beta
# this PR's head
Beta channel: enabled
· Using git ref: v2026.11.5
```

**Unit/regression coverage.** The `resolves the git install ref` cases in `test/scripts/standalone-installers.test.ts` source the real `scripts/install-policy.sh` in bash with a stubbed `installer_npm`, including the flag-selected beta fallback and the explicit-beta literal cases.

Base (policy change stashed, test present) — `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/test-projects.mts test/scripts/standalone-installers.test.ts`:

```
× resolves the git install ref: --beta selects the beta tag
× resolves the git install ref: --beta without a requested version
AssertionError: expected 'v2026.11.5' to be 'v2026.11.6-beta.2'
Tests  2 failed | 9 passed (11)
```

With the fix:

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  14 passed (14)
```

```
机制对位: 症状在 scripts/install-policy.sh:317 resolve_git_openclaw_ref（只读 OPENCLAW_VERSION，--beta 只设置 install.sh 的 USE_BETA），我改同函数加上 USE_BETA 分支与 beta 缺失回退
复现: base(416b357) --beta → Using git ref: v2026.11.6；head → v2026.11.10-beta.1 且 HEAD 切到该 tag
证据类别: 真实 npm registry + 真实 GitHub 仓库 checkout，本机可得: 是（上述 transcript）
契约核对: git 安装的 ref 由 scripts/install-policy.sh 的 resolve_git_openclaw_ref 独占决定，调用点 scripts/install.sh:2997
风险: 1 生产脚本 + 1 测试；不跨层、不触碰状态机
```

## AI Assistance

Implemented with an AI coding agent (OpenClaw contributor workflow). All quoted output above is from runs on this machine; the settings file and workspace marker were created before the runs to show they survive the checkout.

prs.title: perf(skills): isolate discovery metadata memo lifetime
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skill discovery loads the Gateway's source-capture machinery just to register a metadata memo. That gives a read-only worker initialization work and retained dependencies it does not need.

## User Impact

Skill discovery keeps the same results and refresh behavior. The change removes its dependency on Gateway capture ownership; memory and latency improvements are being evaluated before this draft can be considered for landing. No configuration, schema, worker limits, or operator action changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Memo registration now belongs to a small module that owns the existing callback map. Gateway lifecycle cleanup still clears operation-owned callbacks before checking live Gateway ownership, then clears process-owned callbacks after the published snapshot is reset. All eight production registrants use the new owner.

The existing lifecycle and management tests protect refresh/close behavior. The discovery import guard starts from a cold module graph, runs real scan, plan, and library operations while refusing Gateway capture initialization, and restores its guards before shared cleanup.

Runtime changes are currently +30/-27 lines; tests are +134/-112. The three added runtime lines establish the separate memo owner. The committed measurement command adds 355 tooling lines, reported separately from runtime and tests. Release-note context: avoid initializing Gateway source-capture custody in read-only skill discovery.

## Evidence

The cold-import negative control reproduced the specific Gateway capture-owner failure on Node and Bun. The candidate passed all 17 tests across three focused files on each runtime. Core, plugin-test, services-test, and script types, the line-count guard, and production/full-tree unused-file scans passed. The full build, including declaration generation, passed on the same runtime/build inputs. The final adapter passed formatting, lint, syntax, script types, and a real Worker early-exit regression: exit code 7 preserves the original failure and writes an incomplete result instead of throwing from cleanup. Both regression arms exited nonzero as expected; neither collected performance samples.

The full build ran at tree `41e78bf28e12522b02911d0d5d64775ea4b208de`. The first trial source differed only in the standalone measurement adapter's reviewed cleanup fix; its complete 40-input proof matched tree `3e9d9ff0324d73ad75825b56271178d7a689a1f7`. The corrected trial changes only that adapter's fixture and result oracle; runtime/build/test inputs remain unchanged. Its affected formatting, lint, syntax and script-type checks passed with all 40 source pins matching the signed correction. The focused independent correction review reported no findings. Retained proof SHA-256 values are `cefd8b53122eefc63663623d243fb7e052ed4ec76dd7c451415d385d50cda35e` (runtime tests and static checks), `dd016156a246e6048caf072118dc18f16e470ea5a9a77e33552da7f11ece547b` (full build and compiled closure), and `e83a99e282db17667e3c02edeec7b6ff499e0cd7e56c102e688845bb322753a1` (original adapter), and `9ea06075b00f467894f9f6287ebc2a0c97c82f47b3ad19708828adbaece8cad3` (corrected adapter script checks). The preceding oracle-check attempt failed only its lexical-sort lint rule; that mechanical correction passed the final checks. Neither check attempt collected performance samples. No performance result is claimed yet.

The compiled discovery closure contains 233 files and 1,000,619 bytes under the parser's relative static-import/export traversal. The emitted plugin-skills chunk imports the new 428-byte memo owner, which contains only the callback map and registration/clearing functions. Gateway capture-custody initialization is outside that path; the separate pure capture-path helper remains legitimately reachable. External imports, dynamic imports, `require`, and skipped dependency bodies are explicit traversal boundaries. This is structural evidence, not allocated memory or measured savings.

The build reports seven Control UI budget advisories: largest JavaScript and CSS gzip size, total CSS gzip and raw size, chat-boot request count and gzip size, and new-boot gzip size. These are disclosed build advisories, not a UI budget pass. The first trial built both exact arms and all seven advisory lists and underlying served-asset values were identical. These are inherited baseline advisories for the unchanged runtime patch, not regressions attributed to the memo-owner split.

The earlier compiled diagnostic identified a static path from discovery through plugin skill loading and metadata lifecycle into source-capture initialization. That diagnostic motivates this repair; it is not a measurement of this branch.

### First trial: invalid result oracle, zero accepted samples

The first declared trial used candidate `65eacef5920e87909e7831fc2a8ea01df5133327` and published declaration SHA-256 `3af85c46937948cbff1dd2f038017e0b335cd9a7a7a74896b377a5fcf354aa65`. Both isolated installs and full builds passed. Its first small baseline child failed the benchmark's unique-raw-name assertion: production intentionally returns both a plugin's direct source and its generated link for collision diagnostics. The small fixture returned 16 raw rows representing 12 effective names. No verified first scan or performance sample was accepted; partial startup values are not acceptance evidence.

The failed archive is preserved with SHA-256 `735644b0b0647b945d126eb3f9d876cc5e7b1c14be7329ab7ffc22b4cefbde67`. Subsequent read-only seals matched both arms' full source, dependency, and build bytes. No matching fixture process was observed, but inaccessible same-user process metadata limits that observation. The native run owner released and the task's lease was then released. The initial conservative cleanup-unknown result is retained, not rewritten as a successful campaign.

The exact first-trial compiled comparison found 258 relative-static files / 1,337,346 bytes in A and 233 / 1,000,619 bytes in B: 25 files and 336,727 bytes removed from that traversal. Actual emitted capture-custody initialization is present in A and absent in B. This establishes the intended compiled boundary, not an RSS or latency win.

The corrected fixture verifies the exact raw record multiset, paths, source/provenance, descriptions and content hashes, plus the unique effective names, workspace order, fingerprint shape and empty execution-only entries. It removes a redundant planned-request source plan and uses the normal isolated default plugin-publication directory. The former explicit directory override bypassed the unchanged-publication cache and re-inspected links. **This corrects warm fixture behavior; the two trials are not an identical workload.** Skill quantities, scan counts, clocks, metric definitions and acceptance thresholds remain unchanged. The next trial starts with fresh processes, fixtures and output.

### Corrected performance rule — publish before the new trial

Baseline A is `4a8cfdede80241cd222eb5945ad11a6e039f5611` (tree `82a3e0fa1fdf04073bb0b2912741cf1ce79538cb`). Candidate B is `b69bccf995b0ea3c4b4a44b4c6c8af8170680236` (tree `153c321598883dbd47cae2d4230f4b3d617c9c19`); the full binary A-to-B diff SHA-256 is `1adde0977c0d9e145dff787e66ae0abf48f75db2e4ff38d73c26a364b3d4b12f`. The same committed workload bytes run against both complete compiled builds. Both builds and frozen dependency/runtime inputs must qualify before any samples.

Each arm uses its own exact source checkout, canonical frozen install, and full declaration build. Complete source, dependency, workspace-link, and build seals must match before and after the series; normalized dependency payloads must match across arms. The controller admits work only with at least 3,600 seconds left after native source preparation and 1,920 seconds before four preflight children and 1,200 seconds before the acceptance collection. Each child has a 180-second timeout followed by a bounded cleanup join; a timeout or unknown cleanup stops further samples. The absolute run deadline and native owner release are recorded with the result. Controller completion means sample collection completed, not that the acceptance rules passed.

Run the committed `scripts/perf/discovery-worker-measure.mjs` (verified SHA-256 `a80d6efa552ec579897e8ea2db47ab87fc02ecfb42ac6c0688e4d83fc6f37534`) with Node 24.22.1 on the same Linux host. Each sample is a fresh component process with one actual compiled discovery worker, `execArgv: []`, the same resolved resource limits, and no injected worker loader, profiler, or forced GC. Production idle-GC behavior remains unchanged. Fixture creation and build preparation are outside the measured interval.

Two workloads, reported separately:

- Small: four workspaces, eight workspace skills each, four shared plugin skill contributions.
- Stress: four workspaces, 100 workspace skills each, 100 shared plugin skill contributions.

Each child measures worker construction through the ready handshake, the first planned scan, and 100 subsequent scans with no artificial idle interval. Every scan must return all four expected workspace keys, an empty execution-only list, the isolated default publication directory, the exact raw multiset (small: 16 rows / 12 unique names; stress: 300 / 200), and matching source paths, provenance and content hashes. A child must complete all 101 scans and join its explicitly requested, post-measurement worker termination. Unexpected exit, timeout, missing result, source/dependency/build drift, or incomplete cleanup fails the run.

Before collection, four separate preflight children run A and B for each workload, all 101 scans each. A private copy of the committed adapter checks that cloned first-scan replies with missing or duplicated records, a wrong generated path, wrong content hash, wrong publication directory, reordered workspace keys, or unexpected execution entries are rejected. Preflight results and timings are retained separately and excluded from all acceptance aggregates. Any preflight failure stops collection. The 20 acceptance children execute the untouched committed adapter. Preflights can warm filesystem caches for both arms; fresh processes and empty per-child compile caches do not mean cold operating-system caches.

Each workload has five serial, counterbalanced A/B pairs in fixed order: `AB, BA, AB, BA, AB`. There are five independent children per arm and workload; individual warm scans are not independent samples. Use a new empty compile-cache namespace and new fixture for every child; do not flush operating-system caches. Record host load before and after each child.

Acceptance fields:

| Phase | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| Startup | Construction-to-ready elapsed time and total process CPU; RSS at ready |
| First scan | Elapsed time and total process CPU; RSS after the verified first scan |
| Warm work | Per-child scan latency median and nearest-rank p95; total elapsed time and process CPU for all 100 scans, including verification; RSS after warm work |
| Entire measured interval | Sampled process RSS peak; one physical worker start and 101 completed scans |

All RSS values describe the whole component process, including its controller and worker. A 20 ms sampler plus endpoints can miss short peaks. They are not per-worker RSS, deployed Gateway RSS, or a leak measurement. Main-thread CPU, pre-worker RSS, sampling gaps, resolved heap limits, and host load are diagnostic fields; report them and every adverse change without treating them as independent worker-memory evidence.

For the 12 continuous acceptance fields, compare arm medians and nearest-rank p95 values across five child summaries: 48 cells across both workloads. Worker and scan counts are exact per-child invariants. At five children, nearest-rank p95 is the observed maximum and is a noisy tail estimate. Pair differences describe spread; individual pairs are not separate pass/fail cells. Also report all five matched-pair absolute and percentage differences, their range, and the raw child values. Warm latency median/p95 is computed inside each child first; do not pool 500 scans into a larger sample size. Preserve decimal arithmetic through aggregation and threshold decisions; round only for presentation.

A pass requires lower small-workload median ready RSS and median RSS after the first scan, plus no worse acceptance cell in either workload. An adverse aggregate point estimate is an uncertain result, not proof of a persistent regression. Every adverse acceptance cell keeps the change on HOLD pending investigation and explicit maintainer acceptance; a regression of at least 20% in any acceptance cell is a stop. Zero denominators use absolute units and are not silently dropped. Report adverse diagnostic fields too. Do not choose estimators, drop samples, rerun away adverse values, or revise thresholds after observing the data.

This comparison establishes the discovery component's startup and repeated-scan behavior. It does not establish Gateway-wide memory savings, concurrent request latency, or a different worker heap policy.

---

## Corrected trial result: HOLD — no landing

The premeasurement declaration above remains unchanged (13,144 bytes; SHA-256 `d409d378d1c9079ce50f5179de07465e8f27b8614e22c15ec597a672d8aedbcf`). The corrected trial completed all 20 acceptance children / 2,020 scans and four separate qualification children / 404 scans. All seven reply-mutation checks rejected their invalid inputs. The invalid earlier trial remains separate and contributed zero samples.

**The numeric verdict is HOLD: 13 adverse acceptance cells out of 48; zero cells reached the 20% stop threshold.** Both required small-workload RSS medians were lower: ready RSS by 999,424 bytes (0.697462%) and post-first-scan RSS by 995,328 bytes (0.686926%). That does not satisfy the no-adverse-cell rule. Stress post-warm median RSS increased by 7,278,592 bytes (2.329178%); stress median sampled peak increased by 10,072,064 bytes (3.218334%). These are uncertain adverse estimates in this batch, not a demonstrated persistent regression or an accepted tradeoff. No samples were discarded or replaced; no threshold or estimator changed.

The native envelope exited 0, reported success and released its workspace owner. Both temporary arm worktrees were removed with exit 0 and verified absent. Each arm’s complete source, dependency and generated-build seals matched before and after the trial. Collection completion and clean custody do not override the numeric HOLD.

### Exact trial identity and scope

- A: `4a8cfdede80241cd222eb5945ad11a6e039f5611`; tree `82a3e0fa1fdf04073bb0b2912741cf1ce79538cb`.
- Measured B: `b69bccf995b0ea3c4b4a44b4c6c8af8170680236`; tree `153c321598883dbd47cae2d4230f4b3d617c9c19`.

- Raw archive: 880,614 bytes / 62 regular files, SHA-256 `c3137abfe7d7ec325032419c99c77bd46c683bad605ca4cdd02df90a65734034`. Report: 300,109 bytes, `de2401212ffcd165189f38ee813cca6361271ea4cab9592a25a9ebb06043ee3b`. Evaluated result: 159,933 bytes, `2cdfe1e7050a14b6c5d713e0b7ce9c31fc0f3e0247983d034d7801905143821a`.
- Node 24.22.1 / pnpm 12.15.0, Linux, eight CPUs; parent `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096`. Reported worker limits were `maxYoungGenerationSizeMb=-1`, `maxOldGenerationSizeMb=-1`, `codeRangeSizeMb=-1`, `stackSizeMb=4`; limits are not allocated memory.

The two predeclared arm-local metadata exclusions (`node_modules/.modules.yaml` and `.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json`) had separately retained, differing arm hashes; each was stable within its own arm.

### Structural result and inherited build advisories

Both full builds completed. The exact compiled discovery static closure changed from 258 files / 1,337,346 bytes in A to 233 files / 1,000,619 bytes in B (25 fewer files, 336,727 fewer bytes). The old lifecycle/capture-custody initialization is absent from B’s inspected closure; the new memo owner is an import-free 428-byte chunk. This is emitted-code evidence, not allocated-memory attribution. Traversal covers parser-recognized relative static imports/exports; dynamic imports, require boundaries, external packages and skipped `node_modules` bodies are not claimed as an exhaustive runtime graph.

All seven UI advisory values were identical in the A and B build logs: largest JavaScript gzip 564.3 KiB (limit 563.7), largest CSS gzip 57.2 KiB (56.9), total CSS gzip 331.1 KiB (329.4), total CSS raw 1,707.5 KiB (1,699.4), chat boot JavaScript requests 21 (20), chat boot JavaScript gzip 1,303.1 KiB (1,301.4), and new-tab boot JavaScript gzip 803.4 KiB (803.0). They are inherited in this comparison, not new regressions from the memo split.

### CI inventory repair and remaining gates

The measured head exposed a wrapper-inventory omission in CI: the new memo owner was missing from `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`. The extracted-wrapper provisioning tests could not load it, and the eager-import-closure checks correctly rejected the missing dependency. The canonical repair adds that owner beside the existing lifecycle entry. Runtime and measured adapter bytes are unchanged by this one-line repair.

CI run `44639300675` completed on measured B with 54 successful jobs, 27 skipped jobs and four failed jobs (three test jobs plus the aggregate gate). Besides the two inventory-related jobs, `checks-node-changed` failed four of five Bun cases in `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/gateway-plugin-turn-handover.e2e.test.ts` (declared, undeclared, declared context engine, bundled Knowledge), with a JSON parse error reported from the catch at line 251 and two unhandled `gateway client stopped` rejections. That additional failure remains unresolved and its relationship to this change is unknown; it is not classified as a flake or covered by the inventory repair. No E2E rerun or unrelated code repair has been performed.

Inventory correction completed on signed commit `566e7a2b7e37583ce420ae27b2e0fcaa2084e5ae` (tree `65e824d85defda91bc6f70f9936e21b707525ae7`): one added wrapper inventory entry for the memo owner, with no runtime or measurement-adapter edits. The original three wrapper suites passed on both pinned Node and Bun: **41 passed and 2 Darwin-only skips per runtime**. The Linux unsupported-filesystem case passed; the two skips are not macOS/APFS proof. All four command stages exited 0 with no signal/error; all 52 pinned inputs and the complete 66,074-file physical source seal matched before/after. Raw proof: 77,319 bytes, SHA-256 `00596de6ed958ad19bc57025a29dc7759faafca97d883dd0dbc58ad7e0e491c5`; the native envelope exited 0 and released its workspace owner. No full build or performance samples ran for this correction. The measured head remains `b69bccf995b0ea3c4b4a44b4c6c8af8170680236`; the inventory changes the build input fingerprint, so final-head full build/CI/review and measurement applicability remain pending. Numeric HOLD and the unresolved Bun E2E failure remain in force.

Next investigation is separate allocation/residency attribution under the same compiled owner contract. Shared transient allocation, worker heap capacity and RSS are not interchangeable; no new causal explanation or optimization is claimed here. Existing held PRs and their evidence remain separate.

Named follow-up: repair the repeated-tool JSON fixture and join its reload promise. Source inspection found that the default repeat guard can append a plain-text note to the third identical tool call while this fixture parses tool output as JSON. That mechanism predates the frozen baseline, but the offending payload was not captured in these four CI failures; their execution attribution remains UNKNOWN. No E2E retry or fixture change is included in this PR.

### Separate residency diagnostic — no acceptance replacement

A separate, instrumented B-only diagnostic ran on signed `566e7a2b7e37583ce420ae27b2e0fcaa2084e5ae` with pinned Node 24.22.1. One fresh process used the original 16,384-byte skill-file limit; a second used the production default of 256,000 bytes. Each used the same four-workspace, 100-skill/100-plugin corpus and exact result oracle, with two 101-scan bursts and five seconds of idle after each burst. Both completed all 202 scans and 12 checkpoints; all four command stages and the native envelope exited 0. The owner explicitly terminated and joined each worker after measurement. Source, dependency and generated-output seals matched before/after; both task fixtures were removed, and the native lease was released.

This used a freshly qualified **runtime-only build** (`OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1`), not the pending final-head full-build gate. The host had eight CPUs and approximately 16 GiB RAM with inherited `--max-old-space-size=4096`; this is a compiled component-process observation, not a deployed Gateway or constrained-device measurement. Compiled worker entry SHA-256: `ddb97f84ac7ac6de56cff980914ede14e4e308ace61ba2a5766d5061bb89ac12`.

The four post-idle observations are below. RSS covers the entire parent-plus-worker process. Worker `heapTotal` is allocated V8 heap capacity, **not measured physical/resident bytes**. New major events are those drained between the preceding scan checkpoint and the idle flush barrier; their timestamps are drain timestamps, not collection timestamps.

| File limit (bytes) | Burst | Process RSS (MiB) | Worker heapUsed (MiB) | Worker heapTotal (MiB) | New major GC events | Last new major epilogue heap (MiB) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16,384 | 1 | 148.395 | 18.411 | 21.730 | 2 | 18.354 |
| 16,384 | 2 | 319.391 | 22.325 | 158.480 | 0 | UNKNOWN (no new major) |
| 256,000 | 1 | 137.441 | 18.388 | 21.980 | 2 | 18.331 |
| 256,000 | 2 | 316.887 | 19.112 | 166.480 | 1 | 19.050 |

Sampled process RSS peaks were 321.852 MiB at 16,384 bytes and 317.137 MiB at 256,000 bytes. At the production default, burst 1 moved from 310.059 MiB RSS and 52.018/163.793 MiB worker heapUsed/heapTotal before idle to the first default-limit row above. After burst 2, a newly observed major collection left only 19.050 MiB in its heap epilogue while sampled heapTotal remained 166.480 MiB and process RSS remained 316.887 MiB. The 16,384-byte second idle had no newly observed major: its post-major state is explicitly UNKNOWN.

These observations show low live worker heap alongside much larger allocated capacity after the second burst. They do not show a 300 MiB retained catalog, identify all resident bytes, prove a permanent leak, or explain the original A/B adverse cells. The production file-size default also retained high final RSS in this single observation. No RSS-minus-heaps attribution is made.

A separate source-level follow-up is warranted in `src/infra/worker-idle-gc.ts`: its existing 32 MiB growth check considers heapUsed and external memory but not heapTotal. Allocated capacity can therefore remain high without satisfying either trigger. Any capacity-sensitive repair must preserve idle cancellation and successful-collection baselines, and measure next-request CPU/latency as well as post-idle RSS; no such repair is part of this PR.

Instrumentation limits: one child per file limit, fixed order, no filesystem-cache flush, and no claim of historical dependency equivalence. Memory/GC checkpoints can change idle opportunities. Parent heap includes retained telemetry/report rows (102 worker memory messages, approximately 255 kB of serialized memory records per child); verification caused approximately 0.95 MiB temporary parent heap growth at sampled checkpoints. Parent profiler stop/restart gaps were not observed. No observer forced collection; the worker's existing production idle-GC policy remained enabled.

There is also a conditional Node 24.22.1 observer-lifetime caveat: `GCProfiler::Stop` can leave native callbacks/writer storage until the weak object's collection. Those native costs are not isolated by heapUsed/external counters. A named follow-up is to qualify eager callback/writer cleanup with a native lifetime test. This concerns enabled GC diagnostics/telemetry and CodeMode; it is not evidence that ordinary discovery enables that profiler, nor a demonstrated permanent leak or A/B regression cause.

Raw diagnostic archive: 153,145 bytes, SHA-256 `b921e5a09f2027a3dea7d24efe6ac0dd4223c7f8f7a673b6e301545892c30ed1`; report: 14,466 bytes, SHA-256 `79434e87faf524f6557ea81d0d686f49815aeb2ff5472b73afbbacc44e082990`; private adapter: SHA-256 `520c7914b2473b273c1efa523580c8f9c41178372814a884cf3249e842aa3754`. All eight archive members and their recorded hashes were verified. **The 20-child acceptance HOLD, unresolved Bun E2E failure, and pending final-head gates remain unchanged.**

prs.title: fix: reduce sidebar refresh work during session updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Streaming session facts repeatedly scan every retained session-list view, even when most views do not contain the changed row. This adds main-thread work to list refreshes and session-event processing.

## User Impact

Session-list refreshes do less unrelated invalidation work. Row contents, viewer authorization, model visibility, full responses and deltas retain their existing contracts. There are no configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retained-view owner now indexes the views containing each row key. Keyed changes retire only those views; reset keeps the full path. Replacement, retirement, eviction and clear release the reverse memberships together with row ownership. The existing byte budget accounts for the additional bookkeeping. Event-audience `factsRevision` remains unchanged because event consumers need it independently of retained lists.

This completes the per-view membership work in #200899. Runtime code grows by 23 lines for the index and shared cleanup lifecycle; no separate cache or invalidation owner is added.

## Evidence

The owner regression fails on the original scan with 200 unrelated membership probes and passes with zero probes. It compares the retired-view set with the original scan across replacement, duplicate keys, repeat invalidation, LRU eviction, reset, clear and stale handles. All 33 focused tests pass, including delta behavior, recipient/model isolation, encoding accounting and collection after eviction.

Synthetic persisted workload: 500 rows, 20 in-process recipients, 100 mixed queries retaining 200 selection/presentation views, 50 entry fact changes/s for 60 seconds, and 20 real list-owner calls/s. Five alternating A1/A2/B triples ran serially. Each run produced 10,500 keyed notifications, retired the same 1,284 views, and matched normalized wire bytes.

| Median of five runs | Baseline A1 | Baseline A2 | Index |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Invalidation µs/notification | 4.596 | 4.804 | 2.140 |
| Main-thread CPU µs/input change | 2,347 | 2,539 | 1,865 |
| V8 allocated bytes/input change | 1,376,021 | 1,368,899 | 1,375,355 |
| List p99 ms | 4.653 | 5.012 | 2.565 |

Acceptance required identical invalidation membership/wire bytes, removal of unrelated membership probes, lower invalidation time, and no material CPU/allocation/list-tail regression. Indexed invalidation is 53–55% cheaper in these measurements. Whole-call timing has substantial A/A drift, including adverse individual candidate comparisons, so the total CPU and tail differences are **not** claimed as product speedups. Allocation differs by −0.05%/+0.47%. No production stall resolution, live WebSocket/model-turn, large-database I/O or filesystem throughput claim is made.

The workload is rerunnable with `scripts/perf/session-list-invalidation-measure.ts`; `--source-file` loads a saved baseline owner through the identical loader. Revision tokens, generated fixture profile IDs and timestamps are normalized for cross-process wire comparison. Separate profiles do not count as timing samples.

Full-context Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P1. The patch was rebased unchanged onto `416b357cb2b1f` after #202117 landed; all 33 focused tests passed again (44.06 s test runner / 48.46 s wrapper wall time). The table above is pre-rebase evidence; both baseline and candidate cache-owner source hashes remain identical after rebase.

The complete post-rebase `pnpm check:changed` passed. Its first attempt had only an unused benchmark lint directive; that directive was removed before the final pass. Exact-head [CI run 44642871747](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44642871747) is green; the watcher excludes superseded draft-run checks. Hosted Codex also has no findings. [ClawSweeper's final-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202135#issuecomment-7026206004) has zero findings and zero open checklist items; its real-transport proof limitation is disclosed above.

Post-rebase integration controls retained the identical digest, 10,500 notifications and 1,284 retirements in every run. The first A1/A2/B triple was adverse overall: CPU 1,998/1,721/2,883 µs/change, p99 4.605/4.444/5.167 ms, invalidation 4.044/3.133/3.711 µs/notification. This triggered a bounded reversed B/A2/A1 investigation; both unchanged baselines then reproduced the slow overall regime:

| Reversed control | Baseline A1 (last) | Baseline A2 | Index (first) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Invalidation µs/notification | 6.254 | 6.420 | 3.783 |
| Main-thread CPU µs/change | 3,384 | 3,278 | 3,225 |
| V8 allocated bytes/change | 1,374,252 | 1,357,432 | 1,377,334 |
| List p99 ms | 5.273 | 5.188 | 5.136 |

The reversal does not reproduce a candidate-specific whole-call regression. Indexed invalidation remains 39.5–41.1% lower in that control; allocation is +0.22%/+1.47%. Whole-call speedup remains unproven, and the adverse first triple is retained above rather than discarded.

Separate CPU profiles show invalidation self samples 29→3, with 9 new reverse-membership cleanup samples. Replacement inclusive samples rise 32→39, the index-maintenance tradeoff. Packed-facts preparation remains visible. A scratch-only direct key/value JSON encoding experiment passed parity but measured 63.106 µs/list against 58.557/60.868 µs A/A controls (100 rows, five changed, 1,000 warmups, 4,000 measured lists). It supplies no demonstrated benefit and is not included.

prs.title: improve(sessions): reduce stalls when reloading long chats
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reloading long chats unnecessarily copies unchanged tool-result messages on the Gateway main thread. The string-sharing path thaws immutable hydration payloads, so model-context publication must copy and freeze them again.

## User Impact

Less CPU, allocation, and synchronous blocking while reloading large histories. Stored transcripts, model context, history bytes, and writable Plugin SDK views retain their existing behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing codec now reuses an equal resident message when both payloads carry the transcript owner's immutable admission. Equality includes property order to preserve serialized bytes. Entry envelopes remain private, and the existing per-entry ownership path detaches nested payloads before SDK exposure. Changed messages and mutable resident views retain the existing string-sharing path.

Production delta is +31 lines: the ordered comparison and ownership checks avoid the redundant copies without giving up physical string sharing. No new cache, state owner, or API is introduced. Rewrite/rollback and mutable SDK copies remain because their callers hold independent writable references.

## Evidence

The regression fails on base `abd4b4fc6a828` and passes with the fix. Equal, changed, reordered, and mutable resident payloads preserve serialized bytes and mutation isolation after publication. The real asynchronous SQLite reload test also verifies physical string sharing, rewrite correctness, and nested SDK mutation isolation. 105 distinct focused tests passed, including model-context snapshots and prompt-prefix stability.

Receiver-owner benchmark: 5,000 entries, 16 KiB tool results plus nested metadata; fresh structured-cloned reply each operation; two warmups and ten measured operations per process; five counterbalanced A/A and A/B pairs. Allocation was sampled separately, including collected objects. All 400 measured operations had identical history/model-context hashes.

| Median across five processes | Base | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU / operation | 78.79 ms | 48.90 ms | −37.94% |
| p50 synchronous task | 77.72 ms | 45.20 ms | −41.84% |
| p95 / max synchronous task per process | 82.55 ms | 60.31 ms | −26.94% |
| Sampled allocation / operation | 62.71 MiB | 31.53 MiB | −49.72% |

A/A CPU: 77.41 / 78.57 ms; allocation: 62.99 / 62.82 MiB. Baseline CPU range 74.19–79.45 ms; candidate 47.90–50.94 ms. Maximum-task ranges 80.12–84.90 ms versus 58.35–63.67 ms. Host load is recorded per sample. This measures freeze, reload adoption, and initial-context publication; it excludes SQL, worker transport, and workspace discovery and makes no whole-Gateway stall claim.

Reproduce with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/transcript-hydration-clone-measure.ts --output /isolated/result.json`; use `--owner-file /isolated/base-codec.ts` for the base and `--allocation` in separate processes.

Independent Codex autoreview: complete local diff against the base above, P0/P1, scoped-clean, no findings. Codec suite: 34 tests, 12.12 s wall; hydration suite: 21 tests, 40.51 s wall; remaining 50 focused tests cover snapshots and prompt stability. Existing subprocess/SQLite fixtures account for most runtime; the change adds no new boot fixture. No browser-runtime module or visual behavior changed.

`pnpm check:changed` completed all selected checks. It initially reported two proof-only type errors (test-message narrowing and a benchmark unique-symbol import); both were corrected and their affected typechecks now pass. Production types, scoped lint/format, zero unused exports, database/schema boundaries, and import-cycle guards passed. The final four-case regression and benchmark smoke also pass. Final Codex P1 review of the corrected diff is scoped-clean.

prs.title: fix(gateway): show Claude CLI progress notes as progress, not replies
prs.body:
Closes #202118

## What Problem This Solves

In a Control UI chat on the Claude CLI runtime, the short notes the agent writes before calling a tool show up as normal replies instead of progress. When a turn writes such a note and then ends without a final answer, the note is the newest message and reads as the agent's answer.

## User Impact

User impact: Claude CLI chats in the Control UI show pre-tool notes as progress, the same way other runtimes already do, so a progress note no longer looks like the agent's reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude CLI history is imported with Anthropic's raw stop reason, `tool_use`. OpenClaw history and the Control UI use the provider-neutral `toolUse`, and the Control UI only treats `toolUse` as commentary. The import already converts Claude's `tool_use` content blocks to the provider-neutral form; this applies the same mapping to the stop reason. Other stop reasons, including `end_turn`, are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Regression test: importing an assistant entry with `stop_reason: "tool_use"` now yields `stopReason: "toolUse"`, and `end_turn` passes through unchanged. The `tool_use` case fails on `main` (8a6d3a04ee7) and passes with this change.
- Stock Control UI classification, checked on `main`: `assistantMessageKind` returns `reply` for a text message with `stopReason: "tool_use"` and `commentary` for `"toolUse"`.
- Earlier live check: on a 2026.11.2 install with the same one-line mapping, all 137 imported pre-tool notes in one Claude CLI session read `toolUse` after a gateway restart; final answers kept `end_turn`/`stop`.
- Focused tests: `src/gateway/cli-session-history.claude-input.test.ts`, `cli-session-history.test.ts`, `cli-session-history.merge.test.ts` (73 passed). `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass; oxlint and format check clean on the touched files.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high), branch mode, base `origin/main` 8a6d3a04ee7, head 839c9320a1c: clean, no actionable findings.

## Real behavior proof (isolated Gateway, real Claude CLI turns)

Setup: this branch, built from source and run as an isolated dev Gateway with throwaway state, not a production install. The agent ran on the Claude CLI runtime (Claude Code 2.1.321, `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`). Two real turns were sent from the Control UI. Each wrote a pre-tool note, called an OpenClaw tool (`read`, then `write`), and ended with a final answer. Claude's native JSONL for that session records `stop_reason: "tool_use"` on both notes.

The same chat was then reloaded on two builds of the same tree. The only difference between the builds was `src/gateway/cli-session-history.claude.ts`: **before** = `main` 8a6d3a04ee7, **after** = this PR at 839c9320a1c. Each build ran after a Gateway restart, with a fresh browser profile, so neither the history index nor the browser cache carried over.

`chat.history` for the reloaded chat (assistant entries):

| Imported entry | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| "Checking the workspace before I read the file." | `"tool_use"` | `"toolUse"` |
| `read` tool call | `"tool_use"` | `"toolUse"` |
| "The file says alpha." (final answer) | `"stop"` | `"stop"` |
| "Saving the note to notes2.txt now." | `"tool_use"` | `"toolUse"` |
| `write` tool call | `"tool_use"` | `"toolUse"` |
| "I wrote `beta` to notes2.txt in the workspace…" (final answer) | `"stop"` | `"stop"` |

Control UI message actions after the reload, read from the rendered DOM:

| Message | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| "Checking the workspace before I read the file." | Reply, Copy, React | Copy, React |
| "The file says alpha." | Reply, Copy, React | Reply, Copy, React |
| "Saving the note to notes2.txt now." | Reply, Copy, React | Copy, React |
| "I wrote `beta` to notes2.txt…" | Reply, Copy, React | Reply, Copy, React |

With the fix, the pre-tool notes are classified as commentary (progress): they lose the reply action, which `assistantMessageCanOwnTurnActions` withholds from `toolUse` narration. Final answers are unchanged and still own the reply action.

Hovering the pre-tool note after reload. Before: reply, copy, and react icons. After: copy and react only.

| before (`main`) | after (this PR) |
|---|---|
| ![before: pre-tool note offers Reply](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alfredjbclaw/openclaw/68a93f373f30e0ccf19baccdeefe50fb0d361268/pr-202119/before-hover-note.png) | ![after: pre-tool note has no Reply](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alfredjbclaw/openclaw/68a93f373f30e0ccf19baccdeefe50fb0d361268/pr-202119/after-hover-note.png) |

Hovering the final answer after reload. It keeps the reply action on both builds.

| before (`main`) | after (this PR) |
|---|---|
| ![before: final answer offers Reply](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alfredjbclaw/openclaw/68a93f373f30e0ccf19baccdeefe50fb0d361268/pr-202119/before-hover-answer.png) | ![after: final answer still offers Reply](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alfredjbclaw/openclaw/68a93f373f30e0ccf19baccdeefe50fb0d361268/pr-202119/after-hover-answer.png) |

Scope note: in these two turns the note bubble looks the same on both builds; what changes is its classification (`commentary` vs `reply`) and the actions it offers. Both turns ended with a final answer even though the second prompt asked Claude to stop after the tool call, so the case where a note is the last message of a turn was not captured live. That case is covered by the classification shown above.

prs.title: improve: browse Templates under Household and Entertainment instead of Personal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Templates page groups Templates under category chips, and several of those chips did not match what people publish. "Personal" was a catch-all for meal planners, game companions and tutors alike, while "Governance", "People" and "Finance" contain no community-published Templates at all. Someone browsing for a kitchen helper or a game companion had to scan one long mixed row.

## User Impact

The Templates page now shows All, Engineering, Operations, Household, Entertainment, Travel, Productivity, Research, Health, Sales, Product and Other, in that order. The overview uses the same order and omits empty rows. Household (home, family, meals) and Entertainment (games, music, learning for fun) replace Personal. Governance, Finance and People are removed.

- The matching [ClawHub change](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4841) is deployed and backfilled. Both filters were verified against production.
- First-party Templates still stored under Personal, Governance, Finance or People no longer have a chip or an overview row. They remain available through search. Their records were not rewritten.

## How It Works

The Templates page and matching Plugin category chips read one category list and use the same renderer. Household reuses the home icon. Entertainment's popcorn artwork loads with the catalog pages, not the shared startup icon registry. Nonmatching Plugin slugs keep their existing icon fallback. The Template manifest schema is unchanged: it validates the shape of `categories`, not which categories exist.

## Evidence

The chip row on a real Control UI against live ClawHub data, before and after.

Desktop, 1440px:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Chip row before: All, Personal, Health, Travel, Productivity, Research, Engineering, Governance, Operations, Finance, Sales, Product, People, Other](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d2fb8b9f-af99-4bc7-8ac1-786de105a5b5) | ![Chip row after: All, Engineering, Operations, Household, Entertainment, Travel, Productivity, Research, Health, Sales, Product, Other](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/533b4e47-8502-444e-8efd-596a085d2346) |

Narrow, 400px (the chip row scrolls sideways; each strip is the row paged end to end):

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Narrow chip row before, scrolled through all 14 chips](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26827d67-c1c7-4513-bf74-e37be6675027) | ![Narrow chip row after, scrolled through all 12 chips](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/30ed23ca-d32b-4dac-9d4c-3f68a06f1899) |

What was checked on `133ba582a09`:

- All 31 Templates browser tests passed. Coverage includes the twelve distinct category glyphs; focused tests also check chip order and the Household filter request.
- The matching-Plugin regression failed on the previous category list: Household rendered a box. It passes with the home and popcorn glyphs; matching uses slugs, not similar labels.
- The full changed-file gate and the clean, base-relative Control UI performance check passed against `577dd004115`. No performance budgets were changed.

### Populated rows after the production backfill

After the [ClawHub backend deployment](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/actions/runs/44583073216), the backfill changed the 26 community listings still needing updates. All 32 mapped listings are now correct.

The screenshots below were captured on `61dce2607c7`. The same check was repeated on `133ba582a09` in an isolated Control UI against live ClawHub, without mocked catalog requests. Each overview showed four cards; each selected filter showed five. All five names matched the corresponding public API response, including Cooking Companion and Gaming Companion, the fifth results not shown in the overview.

prs.title: feat: use GPT-Live-1.1 with an OpenAI API key
prs.body:
Closes #202123

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI released `gpt-live-1.1` to the API on 2026-11-19. Choosing it for Talk with an OpenAI API key does not work: OpenClaw knows the public API model only by the exact name `gpt-live-1`, so `gpt-live-1.1` is handled as an unlisted GPT-Live model. It gets two voices instead of the public API list, and the Gateway relay is not offered for it.

## User Impact

User impact: people who use GPT-Live with an OpenAI API key can select `gpt-live-1.1` for Talk, Discord voice, Voice Call and meetings, with the same voices and Gateway relay as `gpt-live-1`. `gpt-live-1` stays the default, and nothing changes on the Codex route.

## Why This Change Was Made

`gpt-live-1.1` runs on the same `v1/live/sessions` endpoint as `gpt-live-1`, and OpenAI's docs say it uses the same events ([model page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-live-1.1), [changelog](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)). The public API check now accepts both names, and `gpt-live-1.1` is listed for the picker with the public API voice list. No default changes.

## Evidence

- The new test cases fail without the source change and pass with it. With the pre-PR `realtime-quicksilver.ts`, three fail: `publishes gpt-live-1.1 with its own catalog voice profile` (the provider's models do not include `gpt-live-1.1`), `distinguishes released routes from unlisted family members`, and `speaks the public Live API protocol to gpt-live-1.1` (it gets `input_audio.append` where the Live API takes `session.input_audio.append`). With this PR all of them pass.
- The whole OpenAI extension lane passed before the protocol case was added: 91 files, 1120 tests passed, 1 skipped. The file with that case passes on its own (7 tests).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` and `pnpm format:check` pass.
- `pnpm lint:extensions` reports nothing in the files this PR touches. It exits 1 on two `max-lines` errors in `extensions/crabbox` and `extensions/tlon` test files, which this PR does not touch.

Gaps:

- Not live-tested. I have not run a `gpt-live-1.1` session through OpenClaw, so that OpenAI serves it with the same events as `gpt-live-1` rests on OpenAI's docs.
- The local review tools (autoreview, ClawSweeper) were not run.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```
pnpm test extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver.test.ts extensions/openai/realtime-voice-browser-auth.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test:extension openai
pnpm tsgo:extensions
pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
pnpm format:check
pnpm lint:extensions
```

Base commit: 8a6d3a04e.

</details>

prs.title: fix(cron): a job targeting another agent's session never runs
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #190123

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where a user on a multi-agent gateway who scheduled work into another agent's
  conversation with `openclaw cron add --session session:agent:<other>:…` and no `--agent` got a job
  that could never run. The create was admitted for one agent while the job's own session belonged
  to another, so the due run failed in milliseconds (`cron job agent is unavailable: worker`, or on
  the reporter's install `SQLite session store path belongs to agent main; requested agent worker.`)
  and the one-shot (`at`) job was then auto-disabled as a permanent error: the payload never ran and
  nothing told the creator why. On today's `main` the same command in a two-agent roster does not
  even reach that point — it is refused with `invalid cron.add params: Multiple agents are
  configured, but this operation has no explicit owner.` Either way the scheduled work is silently
  lost.
- The CLI made this worse by naming the wrong owner: it printed `No --agent specified; the job will
  run with the configured default agent.` for a job whose session already named one.
- **Related:** #190123 (reporter's source trace names the create default and the owner resolver);
  #190156 (earlier attempt at this report, withdrawn by its author before merge — it changed the
  global owner-resolution precedence and left the due-run leg on `job.agentId` untouched). This PR
  takes the narrower route: name the execution agent once at `cron.add` admission, and leave global
  attribution precedence alone. Fix signal labels: `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`,
  `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:source-repro`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** one execution agent is named before any `cron.add` admission step reads it,
  so caller-scope matching, creator-session and inference capture, declaration matching, and the
  persisted row all agree on the same owner. `bindCronCreateExecutionAgent`
  (`src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.ts`) resolves it — an explicit `agentId` wins,
  otherwise the job's own session reference decides (`sessionTarget` `session:<key>` first, the same
  precedence the run uses through `resolveCronSessionTargetSessionKey`, then the legacy scoped
  `sessionKey`) — and `cronAddHandler` applies it to the request *before* it builds anything else.
  That one resolved `jobCreate` then flows unchanged into `cronCreateMatchesCallerScope`,
  `captureCronCreatorSession`, the `matchesExisting` declaration matcher, and `context.cron.add`.
- This re-points the earlier revision of this PR, which bound the agent inside `CronService.add`.
  That happened *after* two gateway consumers had already read the unresolved input, leaving two
  real inconsistencies (both raised in review):
  - `cronAddHandler` handed `matchesExisting` the unresolved `jobCreate`, so
    `cronJobMatchesDeclarationScope` compared the configured default (`main`) against the stored
    owner (`worker`) and excluded the row it should have converged onto — repeating a declaration
    would have created a second job instead of preserving the first one's id and history;
  - `captureCronCreatorSession` ran before that binding, so it loaded the execution session and
    captured inference for the configured default agent while the job was stored for another.
  `src/cron/service/ops-mutations.ts` is therefore back to `main`: the service no longer re-resolves
  ownership, and there is exactly one binding point.
- Also removed: the previous revision's `manageAll` exception in `cronCreateMatchesCallerScope`. It
  was unreachable — `CRON_MANAGEMENT_METHODS` (`src/gateway/cron-creator-authority-grant.ts`) lists
  `cron.list/get/update/run/remove/bind` and excludes `cron.add`, `mintCronCreatorAuthorityGrant`
  throws for a management method outside that list, `getCronManagementAuthority` only returns inside
  a redeemed method-bound management context, and the one other caller (`cron.update`) passes a
  `creatorScope` built with `manageAll: undefined`. Its test fabricated the capability with
  `vi.fn()` instead of reaching it through admission. Creation authority is unchanged from `main`:
  an agent turn still cannot create a job that another agent would execute, and a scoped caller
  targeting a foreign session is refused exactly as before (`cronPatchSessionRefsMatchCaller` already
  refused it on `main`).
- Deliberately **not** changed: `tryResolveCronJobEffectiveAgentId`'s precedence (explicit id →
  scoped `sessionKey` → configured default), so visibility, scheduling, run receipts, and the Doctor
  heartbeat cutover keep their existing attribution semantics; already-stored jobs are never
  reinterpreted or migrated. Detached targets (`isolated` / `current` / `main`) name no agent and
  still fall back to the caller scope or configured default, and a malformed `session:` target names
  no owner instead of throwing out of a pure resolver.
- **Out of scope:** no change to run-time session resolution, delivery, the one-shot disable policy,
  the SQLite scope check, or existing stored jobs; no config surface added; no other create path
  (plugin `service-cron`, `templates-add`) is re-pointed; no refactor of the caller-scope module.
- **Highest-risk area:** `cron.add` admission — a job that used to be stored without an `agentId` now
  stores the session's agent, which is visible to declaration convergence, agent-filtered listings,
  and inference capture.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The value is written only when the input carries no `agentId` and
  its own session reference names one, and every consumer downstream reads that same value.
  Regression tests run through the real admission boundary (`handleGatewayRequest` +
  `cronHandlers["cron.add"]` + a real `CronService` on an on-disk store) and cover the persisted
  owner, repeated-declaration convergence, agent-filtered listing, both caller-scope outcomes, an
  ownerless row stored by an older build, the declaration matcher's input contract, and the CLI
  warning.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** on a gateway with per-agent session stores, `openclaw cron add --name probe
  --at <t> --session session:agent:worker:dashboard:<uuid> --message ping` (no `--agent`) warns
  `No --agent specified; the job will run with agent worker, named by its session.`, stores the job
  with `agentId: "worker"`, reports `worker` in `cron list`, and the due run really executes a turn
  in `agent:worker:dashboard:<uuid>` under `agentId=worker` instead of dying against `main`. An
  identical repeated `--declaration-key` converges onto the same job id. An agent turn still cannot
  create a job for another agent, and a job stored by an older build still loads and lists unchanged.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.ts`
  (`bindCronCreateExecutionAgent`, plus the reverted `cronCreateMatchesCallerScope` /
  `applyCronCreateCallerScopeDefault`), `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-add.ts` (the single binding
  point), `src/cron/agent-id.ts` (`resolveCronJobSessionRefAgentId`),
  `src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.ts` (warning text), and the regressions in
  `src/gateway/server-methods/cron.gateway-policy.integration.test.ts` (`Gateway automation
  execution agent`), `src/gateway/server-cron.session-target.test.ts`,
  `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-caller-scope.test.ts` (`create-time execution agent`), and
  `src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts`. Also `docs/cli/cron.md`: the create-time precedence this introduces
  (explicit `--agent` → the job's own agent-qualified session reference → configured default) is now
  documented separately from stored-job ownership, which is unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** yes — a real `openclaw gateway` process and the real `openclaw` CLI,
  both run from this branch's source (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts …`, self-reported
  `OpenClaw 2026.10.9`), against an isolated state dir with per-agent SQLite session stores
  (`session.store: "<state>/sessions/{agentId}.sqlite"`), token auth, and a local
  OpenAI-compatible endpoint on `127.0.0.1` standing in for the model provider so a due turn can
  complete offline. Worktree `aispace/worktrees/issue-190123`, head `c9b5ca8e25d`, base
  `origin/main` `36ddf502c84`, Node v26.12.1. The before legs restore `origin/main` copies of the
  four touched source files and re-run the identical commands against an identically configured
  gateway.
- **Distinct accounts, final effect (added in this revision):** the run above was repeated against a
  second isolated state dir whose two agents own **separate provider credentials** — `main` resolves
  `localmain/proof-model-main` (key tail `1111`), `worker` resolves `localworker/proof-model-worker`
  (key tail `2222`), both served by one local endpoint that logs the `Authorization` header it
  receives. This is the leg that shows target-derived agent selection picking the *account*, at the
  last observable effect (the provider HTTP call), rather than only in the stored row.
- **Agent-turn authority chain, allowed and nearest-forbidden, at the provider HTTP boundary
  (head `acd435275ff`):** the same two-account gateway was reconfigured with
  `tools.gatewayPolicy.automations.scope: "caller"` so a **model turn** — not the operator CLI — is
  the automation caller, and the drives below replay the authority chain end to end through a real
  `openclaw agent` turn (real gateway process, real signed agent-runtime identity, production
  `cron.add` admission), with the synthetic endpoint logging which account served every request.
  Three cases, one gateway run, head `acd435275ff` (this head; the touched source files are
  unchanged since the traces above):
  ```text
  # CASE A (allowed): a real chat turn for main creates a job for MAIN's own session
  $ openclaw agent --agent main --session-key agent:main:proof-chat-allowed \
      --message "R5_ALLOWED_MAIN: create the automation now" --json
  { "runId": "2c8a73c1-…", "status": "ok", "summary": "completed",
    "agentMeta": { "sessionFile": "agent:main:proof-chat-allowed",
                   "provider": "localmain", "model": "proof-model-main" } }

  [gateway] cron: job added                            # admission accepted the bound create
  $ openclaw cron list --all --json
  { "id": "a8f948ad-df46-4a2f-8691-dc5eede99c61", "name": "r5-allowed-main",
    "agentId": "main", "enabled": true,
    "sessionTarget": "session:agent:main:proof:due",
    "schedule": { "kind": "at", … } }

  # the due run, after the creating turn had long completed — served by main's account
  [fake-openai] chat/completions #3 model=proof-model-main keyTail=1111 route=text tools=[]
  $ openclaw cron runs a8f948ad-… --json
  { "action": "finished", "status": "ok", "completionStatus": "succeeded",
    "runAtMs": 1794199443284, "durationMs": 6218,
    "model": "proof-model-main", "provider": "localmain", "summary": "r5 done" }

  # CASE B (nearest-forbidden): the same turn shape targets WORKER's session
  $ openclaw agent --agent main --session-key agent:main:proof-chat-forbidden \
      --message "R5_FORBIDDEN_WORKER: create the automation now" --json
  [gateway] [tools] dispatch_action failed: GatewayClientRequestError:
    invalid cron.add params: job agentId outside caller scope | INVALID_REQUEST
  { "runId": "e8d70282-…", "status": "ok", "summary": "completed" }   # turn completed with the rejection
  $ openclaw cron list --all --json          → { "jobs": [], "total": 0 }
  $ grep -c "keyTail=2222" <endpoint log>   → 0        # worker's account NEVER used
  $ ls <state>/sessions/                        → main.sqlite … (no worker.sqlite, ever)

  # CASE C (revoked mid-create): the same allowed create, turn aborted while the create is in flight
  # driver: sessions.abort fired 10ms after the scripted tool-call stream was served
  transcript: seq 4 user message; seq 7 assistant toolCall dispatch_action (automations add)
  12:56:32.781  endpoint served the tool-call stream (main's account, keyTail=1111)
  12:56:32.791  tool call dispatched (transcript seq 7)
  12:56:32.797  sessions.abort fired
  12:56:32.985  [gateway] sessions.abort requested … session=agent:main:proof-chat-revoked-1
  12:56:33.162  lane task error: agent run aborted, sessionKey=agent:main:proof-chat-revoked-1
  → no tool result event recorded; no continuation model request reached the endpoint
  $ openclaw cron list --all --json          → { "jobs": [], "total": 0 }
  $ grep -c "due-revoked\|keyTail=2222" <endpoint log> → 0
  ```
  What the three cases establish together, all observed at the provider HTTP endpoint:
  **A** — an agent-turn create for the turn's own session persists with `agentId: main` and its due
  run (after the creating turn completed normally) is served by `main`'s credentials — a normally
  completed creator turn keeps its captured persistent authority, and that authority reaches the
  provider. **B** — the same agent-turn caller naming another agent's session is rejected at the
  production `cron.add` admission (`job agentId outside caller scope`), nothing persists, and
  `worker`'s provider account is never touched (zero `keyTail=2222` requests for the whole run; the
  only session store ever opened is `main.sqlite`). **C** — the identical allowed create with the
  creator authority revoked mid-flight (turn aborted while the create was in progress: the tool
  call is recorded at :32.791, the abort lands at :32.985, no tool result is ever recorded)
  persists nothing and issues no provider request for the job.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # 1. local OpenAI-compatible endpoint (canned streaming chat completion) on 127.0.0.1:18099
  node <proof-dir>/fake-openai.mjs

  # 2. real gateway from this branch's source: two agents (main, worker), per-agent SQLite stores

    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway --port 18790

  # 3. real CLI create in the reporter's shape: no --agent, session belongs to another agent
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<proof>/state node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts cron add \
    --name probe --at 45s --session session:agent:worker:dashboard:2b6f1c9a --message ping \
    --no-deliver --url ws://127.0.0.1:18790 --token <redacted>

  # 4. repeated identical declaration (convergence), listing, then wait out the due time

      --no-deliver --disabled            # run twice, identical payload

  sleep 75 && … cron list --all --json && ls <state>/sessions/

  #   git checkout origin/main -- src/cron/agent-id.ts src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-add.ts \
  ```

  redacted):

- **Before evidence (distinct accounts):** the identical two creates against a gateway on

- **Review state:** Awaiting the maintainer decision on the owner question ClawSweeper raised (infer
  the execution agent from a qualified session target vs. reject the combination). CI green on

  agent-turn authority-chain leg above was added after the last review: no runtime files changed

prs.title: fix(ios): keep chat state when the Gateway reconnects after background
prs.body:
## Problem

After the background grace ends (about 25 s), the iOS app drops its Gateway sockets. When the user comes back, it reconnects, and two things happen that throw away state the screen already has:

1. `IOSChatViewModelOwner` calls `viewModel.load()`: a full bootstrap. It raises `isLoading`, repaints from cache and re-reads history and every catalog. macOS handles the same event with the in-place `.reconnected` recovery. iOS uses `composerChrome: .clean`, which draws no spinner for `isLoading`, so this is wasted work rather than a visible glitch. The before/after recordings below look the same.
2. Media resolver health drops while the new socket is probed. `ChatMediaImageAttachment` keys its load task on that health, so a loaded image falls to "Image unavailable", then shows "Loading image…" and downloads again.

## Solution

- `OpenClawChatViewModel.recoverAfterReconnect()` (new, shared) runs the same in-place recovery as a transport `.reconnected` event. It marks health unknown, re-subscribes the active session on the new socket (before, only bootstrap did this), then runs one history read, catalog refreshes and a health probe. Run, history, outbox and progress-card state from the old socket is reset as before.
- The owner only takes this path when owner, agent and Gateway authority are unchanged; a Gateway change still detaches and rebuilds. So this recovery keeps the model, agent, source and composer catalogs on screen while they reload in the background, and the reloads replace them. Transport events can't know this, so they still clear catalogs as before. Without this, the in-place recovery made the model chip read "Default" and hid the permission shield for about half a second on every resume. Base iOS had neither.
- `IOSChatViewModelOwner` calls it instead of `load()` on operator reconnect.
- `ChatMediaImageAttachment`: a decoded image is complete without the resolver, so a health change no longer drops it.

## Evidence

`pnpm ios:behavior` gets a `resume` case. It streams a reply that ends with an image, leaves to Settings for 40 s and comes back. Setup gates confirm the image loaded first and the app logged `Background reconnect suppressed` while away. The probe now also records the loading flag, resolver health and image load states. The QA mock's `UXSTREAM` prompt takes `IMAGE`, which ends the reply with a `MEDIA:` line.

`resume`, 3 samples each, same Mac, simulator, isolated Gateway and QA mock. "Base" is this branch with the reconnect change and the image guard removed, so the probe is the same in both columns:

| Gate / metric | Base | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| connection dropped while away (setup) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| image loaded before leaving (setup) | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| no transcript reload on return | **0/3** | 3/3 |
| image stays loaded | **0/3** | 3/3 |
| no remounts | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| reading position holds (≤1 pt) | **0/3** (2.7 pt) | 3/3 (0 pt) |
| image state changes on return (median) | 2 | 0 |
| health drops (median) | 1 | 1 |

Health still drops once by design: the new socket's health is unknown until its probe answers.

Recording frame about 1 s after returning: base (left) shows the image dropped to "Image unavailable" and the reply collapsed; this PR (right) keeps it.

![Resume after background: base drops the image (left), this PR keeps it (right)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b68b0c0c-3c00-4b94-947d-299c3e8b912c)

Full harness before the rebase (`stream-turn`, `stream-follow`, `scrolled-up`, `keyboard`, `relaunch`, `resume` with the image): every gate 3/3, exit 0.

Rebased onto `main` after #192232 (head `7faab7dfab8`; one conflict, the probe modifier in `ChatView.swift`). `resume` with the image: every gate 3/3. The other cases can't run on current `main`: #192232 moved the iOS transcript to a `List`, `scrolled-up` can no longer find `chat-transcript` to scroll, and `stream-turn` drifted 68 pt. Not caused by this branch, whose only `ChatView.swift` change is the probe modifier's arguments; the harness needs updating for the `List` transcript separately.

Unit: `ChatViewModelReconnectBurstTests` gets `owner reconnect reconciles in place without a reload`. It checks that the loading flag stays off, health isn't reused from the replaced socket, history is read once, and the model label and session controls stay through the recovery. It also checks that a capability change made on the Gateway while the app was away (skills enabled) reaches the kept catalog. It fails if the owner recovery clears catalogs like a transport event, and also if it keeps the catalog without reloading it. Local suites pass: `ChatViewModelReconnectBurstTests`, `ChatComposerParityTests`, `ChatStreamReplayTests`, `ChatViewModelOutboxTests`, `ChatViewModelUnreadTests`, `ChatViewModelReactionsTests`, `ChatSessionSidebarMenuTests`, `ChatGatewayEventSubscriptionTests`.

Local gaps, not caused here:

- `ChatViewModelTests` doesn't finish locally, on base or on this branch. In both, about 373 tests pass, none fail, and the same ~20 tests never finish. Run alone, the test where serial runs stall passes. PR CI skips the macOS Swift jobs that run OpenClawKit tests, so CI doesn't cover this suite.
- `ChatStreamReplayTests` `canonical history adopts a final with different content framing` fails about 1 run in 4, on base and branch; it doesn't use reconnect, health or `load()`.
- The composer briefly shows "Connect to a gateway" during the reconnect, on base too. It comes from the app model's routing identity, which this change doesn't touch.

Review: local ClawSweeper couldn't run because Codex isn't logged in on the review host (401). The automatic hosted ClawSweeper review found one P2: kept composer capabilities were never reloaded after reconnect. Fixed in `7faab7dfab8` (was `3830f102e60` before the rebase); the re-review found no findings.

prs.title: fix(android): keep model names during temporary catalog gaps
prs.body:
Closes #195456

Related: #192252 (delayed-picker behavior is not addressed).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android's composer replaces a known model name such as `Beta` with the raw ID `beta` when the catalog temporarily clears, even though the selected model has not changed.

## User Impact

The unchanged selection keeps its familiar name during disconnects and catalog gaps. Fresh catalog metadata replaces that name; changing Gateway, agent, session, or model clears it. Model selection, availability, eligibility, and request ordering remain unchanged.

**Validation limitation — native visual proof remains incomplete.** Local compilation, lint, focused tests, and red/green regression results have now been reported passing; real Android/Gateway before-and-after evidence is still outstanding.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep a display-only name in the existing composer, keyed by its existing Gateway/agent/session owner and the selected model reference. The current catalog still owns model choices and capabilities. An authoritative blank name clears the remembered name rather than reviving an old alias.

## Evidence

- **Evidence reconciliation (2026-11-20):** the [November 19 issue update](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/195456#issuecomment-7023970455) confirms that the older emulator observation is **pre-fix evidence**, not current-head visual proof. Its available-local-evidence and direct R2-prefix search found no exact-head Android/Gateway before/after capture. The [updated issue review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/195456#issuecomment-6728528623) identifies the same remaining native proof gap, not a new code defect. - Focused `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest`: **82 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** — 10 catalog tests, 58 model-selection tests, 12 picker tests, and both added Compose regressions.
- **Red/green:** the base plus only the added tests compiled and failed the continuity assertion as intended: expected `Beta`, observed `beta`; the scope-reset test passed. Both new tests pass on the PR head.

## What Problem This Solves

PowerShell offers no value completion when the current option and its value are quoted together, such as `openclaw completion '--shell=f'` or `openclaw completion '-sf'`.

## Why This Change Was Made
