prs.title: fix: reclaim stale scratch clones and Git repack leftovers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A local clone created in a managed worktree's scratch directory can make automatic cleanup preserve the whole checkout forever as a nested repository. Those clones keep base Git packs hardlinked, and abandoned repack temporary files are also missed by maintenance.

## User Impact

Idle managed worktrees can clean themselves up again, including previously stopped scratch-only checkouts, so their pack hardlinks stop pinning storage. Real user nested repositories and live or queued work remain protected. Completed sessions no longer stay active solely because their activity timestamp is recent. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared snapshot/nested-repository inventory excludes disposable `.openclaw/tmp/` content. Existing stopped receipts are re-evaluated through the existing fingerprint owner, then eligible removals use the normal serial pacing and leases. Session idleness comes from session completion and live custody instead of the worktree activity stamp.

On Linux, temporary-pack cleanup also recognizes repack `.tmp-<pid>-pack-*` files and sidecars. It requires age over 24 hours, a definitely dead PID, and the existing exclusive file lease and inode checks. Any live or unknown PID is retained, including closed sidecars awaiting publication. Logs report removed file count and apparent bytes; hardlinks elsewhere can still retain physical storage.

## Evidence

145 focused tests plus the corrected retention case pass across the affected maintenance, GC, snapshot, session-facts, scratch, and Gateway owners. Regressions fail on the exact base for scratch nested-repository detection, automatic re-arming, terminal-session facts, and stale repack selection. A separate Linux production-path test passes with the fix, and a real Git subprocess protects its closed sidecar until exit. Real local clones prove pack nlink drops after cleanup; the unchanged consolidation owner then folds the formerly shared packs.

The overdue snapshot retry fixture succeeds on both base and candidate at attempt five with retryAt six weeks overdue. No retry cap was reproduced, so this change does not invent a scheduler repair.

Worktrees UI boundary checks pass: 28 component tests and five Chromium E2E tests. `pnpm check:changed` passes for the full change and the one-line CI correction. Initial CI caught a retained-checkout fixture that still supplied an idle owner; it now supplies an active owner, preserving every snapshot-retention and lookup-count assertion. The exact failing case reproduces before that correction and passes afterward. Production code is unchanged by this correction. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean with no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings. Production code grows by 58 lines for PID safety, scratch exclusion, receipt re-evaluation, byte accounting, and terminal owner facts; no new cache or schema.

Serial synthetic btrfs A/A controls and A/B measurements use a 62,000-file, 1.14 GB checkout and a separate 35 GiB/5,000-row background SQLite storage fixture. This is a reclamation-cost comparison: the base preserves the clone while the candidate snapshots and removes it. Across five interleaved pairs, first-GC wall median is 110.5 ms before (checkout retained) and 9.31 s after (snapshot saved, checkout removed, pack nlink 2 -> 1). Process CPU medians are 102 ms / 6.17 s; main-isolate allocation medians are 9.68 MB / 961.11 MB. A/A wall controls are 117.3 / 124.1 ms. These numbers measure newly enabled removal work, not a speedup. CPU excludes Git children; allocation excludes worker/native memory. The background DB is not a copied production DB or a claim to exercise the complete agent schema.

prs.title: fix(macos): treat failed port inspection as unknown, not free
prs.body:
Closes #190152

## What Problem This Solves

macOS `PortGuardian` asks `lsof` which process is listening on a port. `lsof` can fail in ways that say nothing about the port: missing from `PATH`, exceeding the 5 second probe deadline (for example on a wedged SMB/NFS mount), or exiting non-zero for an unrelated reason. The old code folded all of those into "no listener", and every caller treated the port as free. Three symptoms:

* `gateway install --force` / launchd repair overwrote a Gateway that was started by hand, because the "is the owner ours?" guard was skipped when the probe returned nothing.
* `ManagedNodeGatewayMigration` decided the existing service was absent and took the port over.
* The child-start path skipped the attach step and spawned a second Gateway on a busy port, producing the repeated start failures and the Onboarding screen that claims nothing is listening.

Reproduced by pointing `PATH` at an `lsof` stub that sleeps past the deadline, or by removing `lsof` entirely: the port reports idle while a real listener is bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

A missing answer is not a negative answer, so the probe now has three outcomes. `PortGuardian.inspect(port:)` returns `PortInspection`:

* `.free` — `lsof` ran, exited 1, and printed nothing at all. This is the only case that may be read as "the port is idle". `lsof` also exits 1 on its own errors (for example when `proc_listpids` fails) after printing a diagnostic, so a silent exit is required: stderr is checked, not just the code.
* `.owned(Descriptor)` — the listener was parsed successfully.
* `.unknown` — timeout, pre-flight failure, unexpected exit code, or unparseable output.

`lsof` runs with `-b` so a stuck mount cannot block the probe, and the shell call goes through `ShellExecutor.runDetailed` because the old `run` threw the exit code away, which is how "exit 1, nothing matched" got confused with "exit 2, lsof is unhappy".

`lsof -b` writes its own account of the filesystems it skipped (`avoiding readlink(...)`, `avoiding stat(...)`, `WARNING: can't stat() <fs> ... Output information may be incomplete.`) to stderr even on a clean exit 1 with no match, so "stderr is empty" cannot identify a clean probe. Any other `lsof:` diagnostic is treated as a failed probe.

Every consumer handles `.unknown` explicitly and conservatively: persistence ensure returns `.skipped` instead of reinstalling, repair collects no evidence from an undecided probe, migration raises "the existing owner was preserved", and the attach path never spawns a child on a port it could not inspect. Two cases in that last path are kept apart on purpose: if attaching rejects the Gateway with a named reason (token mismatch, protocol mismatch, non-gateway data) that reason is published as-is, because a retry cannot fix it and the old code already showed it; only when there is no such evidence does startup stop with "Could not determine whether port X is free". Symmetrically, if the attach path re-inspects the port and finds it genuinely free, the start continues instead of leaving the Gateway stuck in `.starting` with no child process. Onboarding follows the same rule and states that the port could not be checked rather than promising an automatic install. The diff is +535/−99 over nine files, the bulk of it regression tests; it cannot shrink much further because the tri-state has to reach every place that read `nil` as "free".

One deliberate deviation: for `.unknown` the readiness publisher keeps the existing `isCurrentGatewayReadiness` check rather than `canPublishGatewayReadiness(instance: nil)`. The latter is always false for `.child` starts and would pin a failed child start in `.starting`; the old predicate keeps today's behaviour without claiming anything about port ownership.

## User Impact

* Failing probes no longer cause a Gateway to be replaced, migrated, or started twice; the app waits for the next probe instead of acting on a guess.
* Healthy machines are unchanged: a successful `lsof` with no match is still `.free`, so install, repair and start paths behave exactly as before.
* Debug diagnostics and Onboarding stop claiming "nothing is listening" when the probe failed; they report the port could not be inspected.
* Trade-off, accepted on purpose: an inconclusive probe during migration records one failed attempt and retries next launch, instead of stealing a running service.
* Everything touched lives under `apps/macos/`: no shared package, CLI or protocol surface changed.
* Stored state is unchanged: `PortInspection` is a runtime result, not a persisted model, and no `Codable` type in this diff gained or lost a case. Older builds still read every file this version writes, and an upgrade starts from the same on-disk shape it wrote before, so the retained resume command, hosting preference and profile selection are read exactly as today.

## Evidence

Proof branch `proof/macos-portguardian-inconclusive-190152` @ `8ba01475601` (rebased on `main` `999e873a916`), run through a throwaway `proof/190152` workflow on a hosted `macos-26` runner (Xcode 26.6, Swift 6.3.3, Node 24, pnpm 12.15.0, repo-pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 / SwiftLint 0.65.1 via `lint-swift.sh` + `format-swift.sh`). That job patches one unrelated, pre-existing build break at job time (`OpenClawChatUI/ChatMediaVideoAttachment.swift` uses `VideoPlayer` without an availability guard and does not compile on hosted runners); the patch is never committed and is not in this diff.

```
Build complete! (692.57s)                   # swift build --build-tests
✔ Test run with 8 tests in 1 suite passed after 5.751 seconds.     PortGuardianDiagnosticsTests
✔ Test run with 92 tests in 1 suite passed after 27.279 seconds.   GatewayProcessManagerTests
0/440 files require formatting, 6 files skipped                    swiftformat (0 errors)
0/35 files require formatting                                      format-swift.sh macos
```

`swiftlint` reports one `type_body_length` warning on `GatewayProcessManager` (834 lines against an 800 line advisory limit); upstream's wrapper treats size limits as advisory under Actions, so the job stays green.

### macOS-hosted end-to-end probe run

The same proof workflow also runs three throwaway suites that live only on the proof branch (never in this diff). They drive the shipped probe on real sockets and on real failing `lsof` implementations placed in `PATH`, they reproduce the pre-change probe side by side so the red row and the green row come from one run, and they drive the app-level owners (probe, onboarding presentation, stored settings). Run [44639619325](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/openclaw/actions/runs/44639619325), job `macos-portguardian`:

Before (pre-change probe, `lsof` without `-b` through `ShellExecutor.run`, non-zero exit collapsed to an empty list):

```
[proof-base] failing probe   -> 0 listeners, isListening=false   # a broken probe reports the port idle
[proof-base] timed out probe -> 0 listeners                      # a hung probe reports the port idle
[proof-base] real free port  -> 0, broken probe -> 0             # the two are indistinguishable
✔ Test run with 3 tests in 1 suite passed after 5.605 seconds.
```

After (this branch):

```
[proof] control: real lsof, idle port 49388: exit=1 success=false timedOut=false preflight=nil
[proof] control: real lsof, idle port 49388: stdout=<>
[proof] control: real lsof, idle port 49388: stderr has 11891 chars, 175 lines
[proof] inspect attempt 1/6: free
[proof] control: PortGuardian.inspect: free
[proof] failure stub: isListening (must be true = possibly occupied): true
[proof] failure stub: PortGuardian.inspect: unknown
[proof] timeout stub: PortGuardian.inspect: unknown
[proof] timeout stub: elapsed: 5.215990667000001 seconds
✔ Test run with 7 tests in 2 suites passed after 10.798 seconds.
```

App-level owners on the same host (`App-level entry proof` step):

```
[proof] app 1 inspect with broken lsof: unknown
[proof-app] app 1 child gateways on port 49393: 0
[proof-app] app 2 inspect took 5.330697666 seconds, unreadable=true
[proof-app] onboarding subtitle: Could not check whether port 49394 is free. Startup waits until it can.
[proof-app] app 2 onboarding would promise an automatic install: false
[proof-app] app 3 upgraded read: seen=true version=3 mode=local resume=/opt/homebrew/bin/openclaw gateway --port 18789 paused=Optional(false)
[proof] app 4 faulted: unknown
[proof] inspect attempt 1/6: free
[proof] app 4 recovered: free
[proof] stub was invoked 1 time(s)          # only the faulted row; recovery used the real lsof
✔ Test run with 4 tests in 1 suite passed after 5.586 seconds.
```

Two things in that output are worth stating plainly. First, the control row: a real, successful "no match" from `lsof -b` writes **11.9 kB across 175 stderr lines** on that machine and the probe still reports `.free`, which is the concrete reason this PR cannot use "stderr is empty" as the signal — the noise is the tool describing the mounts it skipped, not a failure. (`lsof` is addressed by absolute path inside the throwaway suite because other rows rewrite `PATH`; production resolves it through `PATH` exactly as before.) Second, this runner's real `lsof` fails `proc_listpids` intermittently even on an idle port, which the probe correctly reports as `.unknown`, so the `.free` rows poll until the tool answers cleanly and print every attempt; the recovery row's `attempt 1: unknown → attempt 2: free` is that intermittency, not a retry loop hiding a defect.

Input variant → observed output (executed, not asserted by inspection):

| Probe input | Result | Test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lsof` absent from `PATH` | `.unknown`, `isListening == true` | `a missing lsof is unknown instead of a free port` |
| `lsof` stub sleeping 8 s, real listener bound | `.unknown` after 5.5 s (killed at the deadline) | `an lsof timeout stays unknown within the probe deadline` |
| `lsof` exit 2 | `.unknown`, never "idle" | `a failing lsof never reports the port as idle` |
| `lsof` exit 1, stdout empty, no diagnostic | `.free` | `listener classification keeps failed probes undecided` |
| `lsof` exit 1 with `lsof: proc_listpids failed` on stderr | `.unknown`, not "idle" | `listener classification keeps failed probes undecided` |
| `lsof` exit 1 with only its own `-b` notes (`avoiding readlink`, `avoiding stat`, `WARNING: can't stat`) | `.free` | `listener classification keeps failed probes undecided` |
| real `lsof`, loopback listener | `.owned`, pid == test process | `real lsof reports a loopback listener as owned` |
| real `lsof`, unbound port (emits `-b` notes on stderr) | `.free` | `real lsof reports an idle port as free` |
| real `lsof`, idle port (emits 11.9 kB / 175 lines of `-b` notes on stderr) | `.free` | `proof 1 real lsof on an idle port is free` |
| `lsof` stub exiting 1 with `proc_listpids failed`, through the shipped probe | `.unknown`; `isListening == true` | `proof 2 real summed lsof failure is unknown` |
| same stub through the pre-change probe | 0 listeners, `isListening == false` | `base 1 a failing probe reads as free and not listening` |
| `lsof` stub hanging 30 s, through the shipped probe | `.unknown` after 5.6 s | `proof 3 real summed lsof timeout is unknown` |
| same stub through the pre-change probe | 0 listeners | `base 2 a timed out probe reads as free` |
| real idle port vs. failing probe, pre-change probe | both 0 listeners, indistinguishable | `base 3 a real unlistened port and a broken probe are indistinguishable` |
| undecided probe during persistence ensure | only `status` runs, no `install` | `defers persistence when port inspection is inconclusive` |
| undecided port, attach probe fails | `.failed` with "Could not inspect port N", child supervisor stays inactive | `unreadable port attach failure stops an app hosted start` |
| undecided port, attach cannot reach health but re-inspection finds it free | child start continues instead of a stuck `.starting` | covered by inspected code path; no dedicated fixture |
| app owner, `lsof` broken in `PATH` | `.unknown`, zero child gateway processes spawned | `app 1 broken lsof keeps the app hosted start from spawning` |

## What Problem This Solves

The Android sidebar’s New session action visually blends in with Search and Close instead of standing out as the primary action.

## User Impact

New session gets a highlighted, rounded container while retaining the existing 48dp touch target, accessible label, click behavior, and disabled/loading state. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

prs.title: feat(voice-call): elevate one realtime call's consult tools with a keypad PIN
prs.body:
Related: #193571

## What Problem This Solves

Realtime phone calls run every consult at one fixed `realtime.toolPolicy`. Operators who keep it at `safe-read-only` (the safe default) cannot do owner-level work from a phone call, and raising the policy globally gives every admitted caller owner tools on every call.

## User Impact

User impact: an operator can turn on `realtime.elevation`, and on a call with a trusted number (an inbound caller, or the callee of an outbound call, in `allowFrom`), the person on the line can press `*`, a PIN, and `#` to give that one call the elevated consult policy (default `owner`) until hangup. Everything else keeps the configured `toolPolicy`. Elevation is off by default, so nothing changes for existing configs.

Risks and limits, kept visible:

- Twilio only. Digits come from Twilio Media Streams `dtmf` messages. Config validation rejects other providers while elevation is on.
- Only calls whose other party is in `allowFrom` can elevate: the caller of an inbound call, or the callee of an outbound call. Whoever answers an outbound call still has to enter the PIN; elevation is never automatic. Elevation requires `inboundPolicy: "allowlist"` or `"pairing"`. Caller ID can be spoofed (see #193571 for STIR/SHAKEN attestation), so the PIN is the credential; the allowlist only narrows who may try.
- Wrong PINs count per hashed number across calls (inbound and outbound share one budget) within `lockoutMs`, so hanging up and redialing does not reset the budget. After `maxAttempts` the caller is locked out for `lockoutMs`. Failure counts and lockouts are in memory; a Gateway restart clears them.
- Elevation ends when the call's media stream ends. A stream reconnect within the same call drops the tool policy back to `toolPolicy` (the caller re-enters the PIN), but the call's later consults stay in its isolated elevated session, because the call's transcript still carries answers from owner tools.
- A consult that is already running keeps the policy it started with.

## Why This Change Was Made

The realtime handler already owns each call's telephony binding, so it now also owns that call's keypad state and passes the call's current consult policy to the consult tool handler, which uses it for `toolsAllow`. A new `DtmfElevationGate` collects digits after the prefix, submits on `#`, after 3 seconds without a key, or at 12 digits (not at the configured PIN length, so the length stays private), and compares with `safeEqualSecret`. On success the realtime model gets a short notice so it can tell the caller; on a wrong PIN it gets a "not accepted" notice; failures are counted per hashed caller number across calls (a window of `lockoutMs`), so redialing cannot reset the attempt budget. After `maxAttempts` the call is hung up and the caller is locked out for `lockoutMs`. During a lockout any entry hangs up the call without checking the PIN, so retries reveal nothing. A correct PIN clears that caller's failure count.

Digits never reach the realtime model, the transcript, or logs. Logs record only the outcome, attempt count, and the hashed caller number on lockout. Caller audio is withheld from the model between the prefix key and submission, in case the carrier leaves tones in the media.

The PIN is a secret input (`realtime.elevation.pin`, registered in `configContracts.secretInputs` and marked sensitive), resolved the same way as `twilio.authToken`. It must resolve to 4 to 12 digits; the startup error never echoes the value.

Config surface: this raises the plugin config budget in `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` from 5080 to 5087 (the `realtime.elevation` object and its six fields). The feature is opt-in and needs an operator-set PIN, so it cannot ride on an existing field.

To stay within the line-cap ratchet for `realtime-handler.ts`, the existing caller-transcript buffer helpers and `withFallbackConsultQuestion` moved unchanged into `realtime-transcript-text.ts`.

<details>
<summary>Config</summary>

```json5
realtime: {
  enabled: true,
  toolPolicy: "safe-read-only",
  elevation: {
    enabled: true,
    pin: { source: "env", provider: "default", id: "VOICE_CALL_ELEVATION_PIN" },
    prefix: "*",               // one key: 0-9 or *
    elevatedToolPolicy: "owner", // or "safe-read-only"
    maxAttempts: 3,              // 1-10
    lockoutMs: 3600000,
  },
}
```

</details>

## Evidence

Focused tests, all passing locally:

- `realtime-dtmf-elevation.test.ts`: eligibility (inbound + allowlisted only), prefix gating, `#` submit, `*` restart, inter-digit timeout, 12-digit submit, wrong PIN, failures counted across calls (redial does not reset), failure window expiry, success clears failures, lockout across calls and expiry, close drops pending entry.
- `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation.test.ts` (real WebSocket path): consult before the PIN gets `safe-read-only`, after the PIN gets `owner`; caller audio is withheld while entering the PIN; the PIN never appears in manager events, model notices, or console output; a stream close drops elevation; `maxAttempts` wrong PINs hang up the call, and during the lockout the correct PIN on the next call hangs up without a notice.
- `runtime.test.ts`: a consult with call policy `safe-read-only` runs with the read-only `toolsAllow` list, and with `owner` runs with `toolsAllow` undefined (normal agent tool policy).
- `config.test.ts`: defaults, runtime and manifest schema agreement, validation errors, PIN resolution.
- `stream-frame-adapter.test.ts`: Twilio `dtmf` frame parsing; Telnyx frames stay ignored.

Also updated: two `realtime-handler.test.ts` assertions now expect the consult context to carry `toolPolicy: "safe-read-only"`.

Results:

- `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: 52 files, 633 tests passed; database-workers lane 15 files, 182 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `pnpm lint:extensions`: clean.
- `pnpm check:changed`: every lane green except the dead-export scan, which reports only pre-existing entries outside this change (for example `extensions/google/provider-catalog-runtime.ts`, `src/config/sessions/session-history-types.ts`).
- `pnpm config:docs:check`: OK after `pnpm config:docs:gen`.

- `runtime.test.ts` (added in 6f93e38): an elevated consult runs in the session `<caller session key>:elevated:<callId>`; consults before the PIN and on later calls keep the caller's normal session.
- **Reconnect isolation (8a6d57d, the P1 from the last review).** The gate remembers which call ids were elevated (pruned after a day), so `wasElevated` survives a new binding for the same call. `realtime-dtmf-elevation.test.ts`: "keeps a call marked elevated across rebinding while its tool policy resets". `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation.test.ts` (real WebSocket path): elevate, end the stream, reconnect the same call; the next consult gets `toolPolicy: "safe-read-only"` **and** `elevated: true`. Together with the `runtime.test.ts` case above, the reconnected call's consults run in `…:elevated:<callId>`, so its retained transcript never enters the shared per-phone session, and a later call without the PIN can't read it.
- **Outbound (4277a5a).** `realtime-dtmf-elevation.test.ts`: "opens only when the other party is allowlisted, in either direction", and "shares failures and lockout between inbound and outbound calls with one number".

Rebased onto `main` at ae0d37b3c4 (2026-11-17). The only conflict was the generated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`, regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen` (`config:docs:check` OK). On the rebased head:

- The PR's test files (`config`, `runtime`, `realtime-dtmf-elevation`, `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation`, `realtime-handler`, `stream-frame-adapter`): 6/6 files pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.
- `pnpm lint:extensions`: the only errors are `max-lines` in `extensions/crabbox/…/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.test.ts` and `extensions/tlon/…/monitor/index.test.ts`, both on `main` and outside this change.

What the calls show:

- **Read-only before the PIN.** `bf202c8f` and `7992d6c1`: the first consult asked for current alerts; the agent had only the read-only tool list, couldn't reach Grafana, and said so.
- **Elevation.** After `*<PIN>#`: `Realtime keypad elevation granted … toolPolicy=owner`. The next consult in each call used Grafana MCP tools and reported the firing alerts.
- **Reset on hangup.** `52e9a519` (call-back after `bf202c8f`): the consult ran with the read-only tool list again, and the owner tools (Grafana MCP) were not in its catalog.
- **Wrong PIN.** `f10831ae`: `Realtime keypad elevation rejected … attempt=1/3`, and the model received the "not accepted" notice. I stopped after one attempt to avoid locking out the test number; the 3-attempt hang-up and lockout are covered by `realtime-handler.dtmf-elevation.test.ts`.

**Found live and fixed in 6f93e38.** With the default `sessionScope: "per-phone"`, the call-back in `52e9a519` couldn't run owner tools, but its consult answered from results the elevated call had left in the caller's shared session. Elevated consults now run in a session scoped to the call (`…:elevated:<callId>`), so owner-tool results never land in the shared session. Re-checked live: `7992d6c1` elevated and fetched alerts into `…:elevated:7992d6c1…`; on the call-back `4fd2dbc6`, the agent had no record of them. The docs now cover this, plus `sessionScope: "per-call"` for no carry-over at all.

### Live outbound proof (2026-11-16, same host and build)

After `*<PIN>#`, the consult ran in `agent:main:voice:call:49796487-…:elevated:49796487-…`, had the owner tool catalog (133 tools, including Grafana MCP), and reported the firing alerts. Those matched Prometheus `ALERTS` at the same moment.

### Upgrade and compatibility

- Upgrading this host from 2026.10.7 to 2026.11.4 kept the existing voice-call config (Twilio store SecretRef auth token, realtime provider settings, allowlist, tool policy). `realtime.elevation` defaults to `enabled: false`, so existing configs load and behave as before.
- Operator note: when a newly installed plugin version adds a secret input path (here `realtime.elevation.pin`), the Gateway reads the secret-input registry only at startup. Until a Gateway restart, voice-call fails to start with `unresolved SecretRef`; `secrets reload` and a plugin reload are not enough. This is core behavior, not something this PR introduces.





### Live reconnect + callback proof, and upgrade from v2026.11.5 (2026-11-18)

Elevate → forced stream reconnect → consult → unauthenticated callback on a real Twilio call: after the reconnect the tool policy resets, but the call's consults stay in its isolated session, and the callback's shared session never sees the elevated answer. Also covers the upgrade and data-model proof from the current stable release (v2026.11.5) in a sandbox. Details and redacted logs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200198#issuecomment-6979119355

prs.title: fix: stop retrying Anthropic requests that require credits
prs.body:
Related: #201855

## What Problem This Solves

Anthropic can return HTTP 429 with `error.details.error_code: "credits_required"`. OpenClaw treats that funding refusal as a temporary rate limit and retries the same request, delaying the error that tells the user to check their account.

## User Impact

This response now follows the existing billing-error policy instead of the transient retry budget. Ordinary throttling still retries. This does not change Claude CLI account pinning or address the separate five-hour quota notice in the issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Anthropic classifier previously recognized only its generic rate-limit and server-error descriptors. It now gives the exact funding code precedence, including the JSON `error_code` field retained in SDK error text. The change stays in the provider's existing classification hook.

## Evidence

- The regression failed on the base with `rate_limit` instead of `billing`. It also covers an exposed code and rejects a mere textual mention or longer code name.
- Built the QA runtime and invoked `node openclaw.mjs agent exec` with isolated state, a synthetic key, and a loopback Anthropic HTTP fixture. The first response was the reported funding refusal; a second request, if made, received a successful stream. The base sent **2 model requests** and retried. The fix sent **1 model request**, exited with an error, and reported `anthropic ... returned a billing error`.
- An ordinary HTTP 429 control on the fix sent **2 model requests** and completed successfully after the retry. The classifier, SDK transport, and runner were not mocked. This is local HTTP-fixture proof, not a live Anthropic account test.

- `pnpm test:extension anthropic --maxWorkers=1`: 526 tests passed across 45 files (95.89 s). The changed `index.test.ts` also passed alone: 29 tests, 65.22 s wall time including cold compilation; CI duration is not available yet.
- The classification corpus, HTTP 429 precedence, and retry-controller suites passed: 109 tests across 3 files. Targeted production/test typechecks, lint, formatting, the test-line budget (+17), and `git diff --check` passed. The QA runtime build passed.
- Simplification retained the existing owner and test. Independent scoped review found no actionable issues. Tests used Node 24.22.1/Linux; formatting and lint used the repository fallback because the pinned Bun download was unavailable.


Cloud status: CI is waiting for maintainer approval ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44591844490)); no jobs have executed. The hosted Codex review could not complete because the account's code-review quota is exhausted. The independent local scoped review above completed successfully. These are pending remote checks, not passing CI results.

## Recorded CLI evidence

These are excerpts from the saved CLI runs described above, not a new mock of the classifier. The baseline is `021000b8de9743b1eefdff56c5b722ee5fdb25c2`; the fixed build contains the two-file patch published as `00dddda770ba4420ae8d74a5988fd2ea421b53cb`. Temporary paths and generated session/run IDs are redacted. Unrelated startup warnings are omitted. No live account or credentials were used.

Command used in each isolated state directory:


The local HTTP server records every request. Its first response is HTTP 429 with `Content-Type: application/json` and `x-should-retry: false` (SDK-level retry is disabled; the observed second request is OpenClaw's retry). The funding-case response body, as configured in the fixture, is:
```json
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"rate_limit_error","message":"Request rejected","details":{"disabled_reason":"org_level_disabled","error_code":"credits_required","exhausted_included_allowance":false}}}
```
The ordinary-throttle control uses the same response without `details`. In every run, a second model request, if received, gets an HTTP 200 SSE response containing `fixture response` and `stop_reason: end_turn`.

prs.title: fix(android): capitalize sentence starts in chat
prs.body:
Related: #139408, #152748 (closed broader Android proposals; this PR isolates sentence capitalization only).

## What Problem This Solves

The Android chat composer does not request automatic sentence capitalization from supporting keyboards. This proposal changes that input default; it is not a claim that the current default violates an established product contract.

## User Impact

Users can start messages and subsequent sentences with automatic capitalization, subject to their keyboard settings. No settings, migration, or changes to existing drafts are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The composer does not request sentence capitalization from Android's input method. This three-line change supplies `KeyboardCapitalization.Sentences` through `KeyboardOptions`, leaving autocorrection and all other keyboard defaults unchanged. It does not rewrite typed text or include the unrelated changes from the closed proposals above.

## Evidence

### Current review and CI — October 31

Published head: `40c67c2df5f03430376ae9098b945e8746b9708c`. GitHub reports the branch mergeable. The [current-head CI gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38503473608/job/115659038371). The [completed ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171601#issuecomment-6159892013) identifies no actionable code findings and accepts the recorded typing evidence.

**Area-owner decision requested:** should the Android chat composer request sentence capitalization by default, subject to the keyboard's settings? The review recommends acceptance without rewriting drafts or adding an app setting. Owner acceptance remains outstanding; passing checks and the advisory review do not supply it. No new implementation or device testing is claimed by this refresh.

- Real Android/Gboard reproduction using identical on-screen key positions, with no Shift taps or injected text: the GitHub v2026.10.3 baseline produced `h. h`; the repaired composer produced `H. H`. Android input flags changed from `0x228001` to `0x22c001`, adding only `TYPE_TEXT_FLAG_CAP_SENTENCES` (`0x4000`). Autocorrection was already enabled in both.
- The isolated candidate built from base `4a538d5fb3665c6af278e32026ae8fe4e722de69`, with the exact three-line patch submitted here, also produced `H. H` with actual Gboard taps. Only its test package identity differed. The test was offline; no message was sent, and the synthetic draft was cleared afterward.
- Passed `:app:compileThirdPartyDebugKotlin`, `:app:ktlintCheck`, and `:app:assembleThirdPartyDebug`, including Mermaid asset generation and package identity verification.
- Fresh independent review of the scoped patch reported no P2-or-higher findings. Repository commit hooks passed. No full cross-platform suite or alternate-keyboard coverage is claimed.

AI-assisted implementation and validation; the change is limited to the existing Android chat composer.

prs.title: fix: stop worktree pack consolidation inflating delta storage
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Worktree Git cleanup can consume disk while consolidating single-link packs: many small deltas become larger even though their objects and compressed payloads are unchanged. A real maintenance-owner regression reproduces 1.454× output/input growth in both ordinary and promisor packs.

## User Impact

Worktree maintenance preserves compact delta references, eliminating this avoidable encoding growth. The synthetic history fixture now writes slightly less pack data than it retires. No migration, configuration, or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

`pack-objects --stdout` defaults to full object-ID delta references. The local `index-pack` consumer supports compact offset references, so pass `--delta-base-offset`, as Git's own repack does. The existing geometric selection, hardlink exclusion, class separation, verification, thread/window limits, and retirement ordering stay intact. Production LOC is unchanged (+2/-2, including the explanatory comment).

This fixes the reproduced encoding overhead; it is not a general output-size preflight for arbitrary Git transformations. Excluded-pack lists are unnecessary for this repair and would introduce dependencies on retained packs outside the verified batch. Git can also create auxiliary packs when promisor packs reference ordinary objects; the benchmark preserves promisor ancestry closure so it measures consolidation rather than that separate promotion behavior.

## Evidence

The real-owner regression fails on parent `8a6d3a04ee74654ce03828eb91be4364bf734334` at 1.454014× and passes after the fix. It checks the complete reachable/unreachable object census, full fsck, source retirement, class markers, and the kept shared inode. All **60 focused tests pass**, with one Linux-only cleanup test skipped locally (137.15 s Vitest / 141.11 s wrapper; the new cases take 1.05 s and 0.32 s).

The committed workload extends `scripts/perf/managed-git-maintenance-measure.ts`: 32,768 deterministic 4-KiB revisions, 16 history packs, two packs hardlinked into three clones, and a kept 62,000-file / 1.14-GB checkout pack. Acceptance was output/retired bytes ≤1.01 after versus ≥1.3 before, with object equivalence and no new steady-state writes. Five interleaved pairs use identical restored fixtures, fresh owner processes, and warm filesystem caches. A/A controls have identical bytes and 9.84% wall spread. Initial samples overlapping a declaration build were excluded before the replacement controls were run.

| Two maintenance passes | Parent median / observed p95 | Fix median / observed p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Pack bytes written | 1,913,810 / same | 1,413,814 / same |
| Single-link pack bytes retired | 1,414,198 / same | 1,414,198 / same |
| Output/input ratio | 1.353283× | 0.999728× |

prs.title: fix: preserve the real reason a worker failed
prs.body:
Fixes #202022

## What Problem This Solves

When a worker fails, its active task can report only “Native worker task channel closed.” That hides the exception or exit reason needed to diagnose the failure.

## User Impact

User impact: failed active worker tasks preserve their original exception, error code, nested cause, or observed exit status.

This improves the diagnosis; it does not prevent the underlying crash. Queued requests refused during failed startup retain their existing generic wording. No configuration changes, retries, sleeps, or increased memory limits are introduced.

Owned tasks still preparing input reject promptly with the worker failure already observed. Their cleanup continues to hold input and admission until preparation settles; later supervisor evidence cannot replace that already-delivered result.

## Why This Change Was Made

The task channel can close before the supervisor delivers the actual worker failure. The existing completion owner now waits for the existing retirement result before choosing that task's failure, while retaining failed-cleanup ownership and synchronous settlement behavior.

Native error encoding also preserves inherited data-valued codes, including Bun's out-of-memory code, without invoking getters.

## Evidence

- Owned-preparation follow-up: real-channel regressions for both `runTask` and `startTask` fail on `0e4af48` (results remain pending) and pass on `dcc3954`. All 99 acceptance tests across retained, owned, preparation, bootstrap, and native-error suites pass after pr-simplify; targeted typecheck, lint, format, and `git diff --check` pass. Acceptance wall time: 11.09s; retained-suite test time: 1.24s; CI time not yet measured.
- Simplify pass for this follow-up: reuse existing failure selection and cleanup, with no new lifecycle state or retries; share the real-worker fixture between ordinary and owned regressions. Delta against the previous head: production +3/-2 lines, tests +81/-2, documentation +4/-1.
- Four regression tests failed on main `99e2b6eb1f9bf8867ce647e11d9279da943443fa` with only the test changes, and passed with the fix. @daniel-lxs confirmed the same red/green comparison.
- The real production worker transport was exercised with exceptions, nested causes, explicit exit, memory exhaustion, and channel-only closure on Node 24.20.0 and the pinned Bun 1.4.4 fork. Replacement tasks completed after cleanup.
- Rebased original local commit `64fd4a73749c` onto `6b3c804312d7e3b3e4d45ce226c0feac590cf581`. The patch identity is unchanged. All 91 focused tests passed again on rebased candidate `300292dc9df3d965a47a1f5a6fdca75f7c06b9fa`.
- Typecheck, lint, formatting, and pr-simplify passed for the unchanged patch before rebase; `git diff --check` passes after rebase.
- Independent static review of the production snapshot found no concrete lifecycle regression. Native Auto Review could not start because of a runner configuration incompatibility and is not counted as a clean Auto Review.
- Validation is isolated worker-transport testing, not a production deployment.

prs.title: fix(android): nest child sessions under their parent in the sidebar
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In the Android app, child sessions (subagent runs, spawned workers, forks) show up as ordinary top-level rows in the sidebar's Recent, Pinned and folder sections, and in Overview's recent threads, mixed in with real conversations. On a busy Gateway, the parent conversation gets buried among its own workers.

## User Impact

In the sidebar, child sessions now sit under their parent behind a disclosure that shows how many there are. Parents start collapsed. While collapsed, a parent still shows:

- a working spinner, queued icon or unread dot when a hidden child has one;
- its hidden children's pending questions and approvals.

A parent ranks by its newest child's activity, so a child that starts working keeps the thread on the first Recent page. A parent opens automatically when the session you have open is one of its children, and so does a collapsed Pinned section when that parent is pinned (until you toggle Pinned yourself). A collapsed sidebar section (Pinned, a folder, Groups, Recent) shows and announces a spinner, queued icon or unread dot when one of its sessions has a hidden child with that state, since those children no longer appear in Recent. Hidden failures stay on the child row. Sidebar search still lists each matching session once, without nesting, and each result reports only its own requests. Children of Home stay top-level conversations, since Home is a page rather than a row (as on the web). Overview's recent threads and its Threads count list top-level sessions only, ranked by each thread's newest activity. Opening a child works as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Threads page already nested children, but the sidebar and Overview never read parent links. The Threads parent-link rules now live in one shared function, `sessionParentLinks`, used by all three:

- A child links to its parent through `parentSessionKey`, or else `spawnedBy`.
- A child stays at the top level when it's pinned, filed in a folder, or an ordinary New chat (existing Threads rules), or when the Gateway marks it `sidebarRoot` (as on the web; Android now reads that field).
- A child whose parent isn't listed, or whose links form a loop, stays at the top level.

The sidebar and Overview also keep children of Home at the top level. In the sidebar, rows that belong to a catalog section neither become nor get children in Recent, so nothing appears twice.

Unlike the web sidebar, subagent run rows stay visible as nested children instead of being folded away. That keeps them reachable from the phone, which is how they're used today.

## Evidence

Real app on an Android 16 emulator (API 36, 1080×1920, 420 dpi), launched in screenshot-fixture mode (scene `home`). For this capture only, I added two child rows (`parentSessionKey = discord:release-planning`, one running) to the fixture's default session list; that local change is not part of this PR. Before: `origin/main` 1fbcec108f4 built with the same fixture rows. After: this branch.

### Sidebar, Recent expanded

| Before | After: collapsed | After: expanded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Before: Check release blockers and Draft release notes are top-level Recent rows above Android release planning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d7ffd068-1db2-40d3-9529-e8defcb5fc83) | ![After: Android release planning shows a working spinner, a count of 2 and a chevron; its children are hidden](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee6d4d7b-457b-4a5f-8a68-50b79b2a6b8b) | ![After: Check release blockers and Draft release notes are indented under Android release planning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02c04348-eae6-4dbf-82bc-105b9271feac) |

### Overview, recent threads

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Recent threads lists Check release blockers and Draft release notes; Threads count is 6](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d906a1d9-427d-441a-82c8-e7d602002d55) | ![After: Recent threads lists New chat, Android release planning and Product notes; Threads count is 4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cfa37954-fab1-4fe5-9ea3-8b628c128ab1) |

On the same emulator build, sidebar search for "release" listed "Draft release notes", "Check release blockers" and "Android release planning" once each, with no child toggle.

Tests:
- `SidebarNavigationAccessibilityTest` (production `OpenClawSidebar`):
  - The child is hidden until you tap the toggle.
  - The collapsed toggle reports the child as Working, and the collapsed Recent header reads "Collapsed, Working".
  - Expanding shows the child indented below its parent and above the next session, and tapping the child opens it.
  - Collapsing hides it again.
  - When the open session is a child, its parent starts expanded and still collapses on tap.
- `SidebarShellLogicTest`:
  - Grandchildren nest.
  - Pinned, filed, `sidebarRoot`, ordinary New chat, unlisted-parent and catalog-parent rows stay top-level.
  - Children of Home (canonical, legacy `main`, and `isMain`) stay top-level.
  - A parent ranks by its newest child, including across the Recent page limit.
  - A collapsed parent reports its hidden children's questions and approvals.
  - Parents start collapsed, the open child keeps its parent expanded, and the user's choice wins.
  - A collapsed Pinned section opens for an open child of a pinned parent.
  - A collapsed section reports work in its sessions' hidden children.
  - A collapsed parent reports a running, queued-only or unread child, but not a failed one.
- `ShellScreenLogicTest`: Overview leaves out children but keeps Home's children and children whose parent isn't loaded, and it ranks a parent by its newest child.
- `ChatControllerTranscriptCacheTest`: `sidebarRoot` is parsed and kept through partial session updates.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

- `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.ui.*' --tests ai.openclaw.app.chat.ChatControllerTranscriptCacheTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.chat.ChatControllerSessionSearchTest`: 1373 tests, 0 failures (includes the existing Threads tree tests in `SessionsScreenGroupingTest`)
- `./gradlew :app:ktlintCheck :app:assemblePlayDebug`: passes
- `pnpm native:i18n:check`: passes. The toggle reuses the existing translated "Expand child sessions" / "Collapse child sessions" strings.
- The new sidebar and Overview tests fail on `origin/main`: the child still shows as a separate row, there's no toggle, and Overview lists the child.

</details>

Local ClawSweeper (GPT-6.2 Sol) review history: four range reviews, each raising follow-up edge cases (pinning of Home children, hidden requests, Recent ranking, search nesting, pinned reveal, queued state, section activity, accessibility, Overview ranking, failed-child rollup). Each was fixed with tests. The last local review was gold (C) on the head before the final fix commit; that commit was not re-reviewed locally.

prs.title: fix: prevent workspace Azure resource redirects
prs.body:
## Summary

An untrusted workspace `.env` could supply an Azure OpenAI resource name that changed the host of a credentialed model request. Reserve that variable from workspace dotenv and require resource names used for host construction to be one DNS label. This closes a sibling gap in the existing workspace endpoint filter; prior Homebrew filtering and the AI package extraction remain intact.

## What Problem This Solves

1. `src/infra/dotenv.ts` filtered direct endpoint overrides but accepted `AZURE_OPENAI_RESOURCE_NAME` from a workspace `.env`. The CLI loaded that file before an Azure model request, so repository content could influence provider routing when the operator had not set the variable in a trusted source.
2. `packages/ai/src/providers/azure-openai-responses.ts` interpolated the value into `https://${resourceName}.openai.azure.com/openai/v1`. A value such as `evil.example/x` parsed with `evil.example` as the request host, while the Azure client held the operator's API key.

The fix prevents workspace content and malformed resource names from selecting an arbitrary host for the credentialed request. Legitimate resource names and explicitly configured custom base URLs remain available.

## Why this design

- Reserve the precise Azure routing key at the existing workspace dotenv boundary, including both synchronous and asynchronous loaders.
- Reject a malformed resource name before constructing the provider URL; accept a single DNS label and leave explicit base URL precedence intact.
- Keep the existing trusted process/global dotenv and custom endpoint paths. Add no configuration option or dependency.

## Why this does not conflict with related PRs

| PR | Governed layer | Relation |
|---|---|---|
| [#54631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/54631) | Workspace dotenv admission | Established the filtered loader and endpoint blocking; this adds one missed Azure routing key to that owner. |
| [#150912](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150912) | Homebrew workspace controls | Blocks a different group of environment controls; its changes are already in the base. |
| [#99059](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99059) | Reusable AI runtime package | Preserved Azure transport behavior in `@openclaw/ai`; this validates its resource input within that package. |

All three changes are included in the base. The shared dotenv file gains one entry; no prior path is replaced.

## Evidence of Fix

| Path and mode | Before on `v2026.11.6` or base | After on `c96424124cf` | Observed command/result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Workspace `evil.example/x`, Azure request with synthetic key | Release-tag CLI loader admitted the value; captured final fetch targeted `evil.example` with the synthetic `api-key`. | CLI loader left the workspace key unset; with a configured Azure model base URL, captured final fetch targeted `configured-resource.openai.azure.com` with the synthetic key. | `PROBE_RESOURCE_NAME='evil.example/x' PROBE_EXPECTED_HOST='evil.example' pnpm exec tsx /tmp/azure-release-probe.mts` and `pnpm exec tsx /tmp/azure-fix-probe.mts`: both assertions passed in isolated source checkouts. |
| Upgrade with workspace-only valid `legacy-resource` and no other base URL | Release-tag CLI/provider composition sent one captured request to `legacy-resource.openai.azure.com`. | The same workspace-only setting produced a visible “Azure OpenAI base URL is required” result and zero requests. Moving the setting to isolated global runtime dotenv restored one captured request to `legacy-resource.openai.azure.com`. | `PROBE_RESOURCE_NAME='legacy-resource' PROBE_EXPECTED_HOST='legacy-resource.openai.azure.com' pnpm exec tsx /tmp/azure-release-probe.mts`; `pnpm exec tsx /tmp/azure-upgrade-probe.mts`; `PROBE_TRUSTED_GLOBAL=1 pnpm exec tsx /tmp/azure-upgrade-probe.mts`: all assertions passed. |
| Workspace filter and provider regressions | New tests failed on the base: workspace key reached `process.env`; malformed resource caused one captured request. | Workspace filter and provider tests passed; malformed resource produced zero requests. Valid resource and custom `azureBaseUrl` routes passed. | `pnpm test src/infra/dotenv-workspace-blocklist.test.ts packages/ai/src/providers/azure-openai-responses.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 27/27 passed after the fix. Provider suite after the custom-base-URL case: 18/18 passed. |

The CLI-to-provider probes used real production entry points and an intercepted final fetch, so no external network request or real credential was used. They are local proof artifacts; the committed regressions provide repeatable owner-level checks. A live Azure model and full Gateway run were not performed.

## SDK / caller upgrade contract

Callers using valid trusted resource names retain Azure routing. Existing workspace-only `AZURE_OPENAI_RESOURCE_NAME` settings stop supplying a route; move that value to the process environment, global runtime dotenv, or explicit configuration. Resource strings containing URL syntax now fail before a request; operators using a custom host can keep the existing `AZURE_OPENAI_BASE_URL` or `azureBaseUrl` path. The provider tests cover valid names, rejection, and explicit custom URL precedence.

## Testing

- Red on base and green with fix for the workspace and Azure provider regressions; final targeted provider suite 18/18.
- `pnpm test src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 16/16 passed.
- Targeted oxlint and oxfmt, `pnpm docs:check-mdx`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:packages`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm build`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed base `c25f49d92f4` through head `c96424124cf`; it found no definite code defect and requested the entry-point and upgrade evidence recorded above. Its pre-PR proof rating did not include these later probes.

prs.title: fix: conversation deletion leaves dependent automations enabled
prs.body:
Related: #199300

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes conversation deletion leaving execution-dependent automations enabled, without disabling independent work merely created in or reporting to that conversation.

## User Impact

- An independent command created in conversation A and reporting to B keeps running after A is deleted.
- A reporting-only link does not disable an automation. Missing internal delivery is recorded as a delivery error, without recreating the deleted conversation or silently routing the report elsewhere.
- Automations that actually use the deleted conversation's inherited context, workspace, session-scoped authority, or execution target are disabled before deletion. Reporting elsewhere does not detach those real dependencies.
- Definitions and activity history remain. If a required disable fails, the conversation remains and the error explains that some jobs may already be disabled. Existing human and model management restrictions still apply; already-running commands may finish.

A plain command uses its saved process definition and requester authority. Agent/script jobs that inherit creator resources, and commands with parent-dependent triggers or session-scoped grants, remain dependent. Explicit external chats remain external destinations; deleting a local transcript does not delete the external chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first version treated all links as lifecycle ownership. This revision separates association from execution dependency and reuses the scheduled execution-context owner for the decision. Requester authority is retained independently rather than promoted to legacy operator access when the creator is gone. Doctor and the replay reader consume the same parent decision.

The reviewed embedded-cleanup regression is also fixed: local deletion uses the existing paused offline cron owner while general embedded cron RPCs remain unavailable. Hosted disable failures still prevent deletion. No schema, new persistence layer, scheduler, or client-side mutation sequence is added.

## Evidence

- The registered deletion handler, real SQLite session/job stores and production occurrence admission reproduce the creator/reporting regressions before the repair. Nine current handler scenarios pass, including independent commands reporting elsewhere, reporting-only deletion, explicit execution targets, partial disable failure, and human/model authority. Only command/model execution edges are synthetic.
- Real completion tests verify explicit destination delivery after source deletion, missing internal reporting without recreation or fallback, visible delivery errors in retained history, and loading/delivery of v2026.9.9-shaped jobs without rewriting receipts or schema.
- Execution-context/admission/binding, stored-shape fixtures, Doctor/replay, owner-authority and binding checks pass. The final core/UI types, scoped lint, formatting, i18n and diff checks pass.
- The previous CI failures in embedded ACP/spawn cleanup and incomplete hosted test fixtures are repaired. Seven affected files completed with 86 passing cases. An overbroad eight-file run reached its external 600-second command limit during unrelated production-boundary cases; it was not restarted or given a higher limit. Completed results were retained, and the 11 unfinished named collector/deletion-boundary cases passed a bounded replay. The entire broad production-boundary suite is not claimed green locally; new-head CI remains the broad gate.
- 64 organizer cases and two production-built browser flows pass. Sidebar and Sessions Cancel/Confirm behavior stays unchanged: one exact-session delete and no client-side automation writes. Browser Gateway responses are synthetic. Final browser proof took 19.93s including build. No live user session or automation was mutated; no full live upgrade rehearsal was run.
- Canonical autoreview with Codex GPT-6.1 Sol reviewed the complete revised candidate against `89ee0bd382d16ec16183a10e81a8930a92ed1909` at P0–P2 and returned scoped-clean. The reviewer did not execute tests independently. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable. The forward-only published tree is byte-identical to that reviewed candidate; it retains the original PR ancestry rather than force-pushing the rebased draft.

### Before

Current-main production-built Control UI, light theme, synthetic Backup maintenance conversation. This warning treats linked automations as a separate cleanup task.

![Before: linked automations may keep running](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06b4e704-947f-4b56-b042-344ef4257bfc)

### After

The same dialog now distinguishes execution dependencies from independent work and reporting.

![After: only execution-dependent automations are disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4fc2962b-7247-41d3-9b98-24a2bc2ab9e7)

## Contributor credit

Requested and co-authored by @vyctorbrzezowski.

The delegated-administration product test still expects a config write to be cancelled when its standing grant changes after approval. The current approval contract lets that approved write finish, so scheduled CI fails on the old expectation.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the real writer paused, revoke the grant, verify the live policy and unchanged file before resuming, then require the exact config change and preservation of every other setting. Retain the successful control's response assertion. The revoked case does not assert the known misleading outer-caller response noted by the owning change; correcting that response is separate work.

## Evidence

- [The approval-contract change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/59ca885df5945ec14d3ad5afb085c629365181f1) explicitly retains an approved apply after later source-grant revocation.

An initial whole-config check on the control also exposed expected migration stamping; the final whole-config preservation assertion applies after the control has normalized the config.

prs.title: fix(voice): ground progress claims in client-owned GPT-Live calls
prs.body:
Closes #199428

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: client-owned GPT-Live voice calls do not receive the rule against invented acknowledgments and progress claims.

## User Impact

User impact: client-owned WebRTC calls receive the same grounding rule as Gateway-controlled calls. This is an instruction-delivery fix, not a guarantee of model compliance.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Move the existing grounding rule into a small always-on session instruction block.
- Keep the provisional launch acknowledgment exception unchanged.
- Keep host-control result and freshness instructions gated to Gateway-controlled calls.
- Do not change delegation, call ownership, or transport behavior.

## Evidence

- Real client-owned GPT-Live WebRTC call through candidate Gateway `talk.client.create` with the real consult runtime: provider HTTP 201, broker HTTP 200, Chromium connected, and provider `session.started`. A transparent test-only fetch observer captured the actual outgoing instruction payload: grounding rule present, host-only freshness policy absent. Voice closure and temporary-session deletion confirmed; isolated test Gateway restored. [Redacted live proof and harness](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/0dc4baf0cd068dd8fe73cb69c381cf0c81e4b09d/voice/LIVE-PROOF-199431.json).
- Exact-head runtime build passed with checkout-owned frozen dependencies. Live proof establishes instruction delivery and transport acceptance, not model compliance or iOS UI acceptance. No production changes or deployment.
- Paired CI attribution: `client-native-control.test.ts` reproduces the same four after-cancel failures on this head and with both changed production files restored to parent `3c6bb67f82ae`. Each run: 10 passed, 4 failed, exit 1; the after-cancel result is the verification fallback instead of completion. Tests and runner configuration were unchanged; production bytes were restored after replay. This observed failure signature predates the grounding patch.
- Stock source with regression tests: 4 failed, 49 passed across three test files.
- Patched source: 55 passed across four test files, including session shaping boundaries.
- Broker test inspects client-owned WebRTC session instructions; relay test inspects the outgoing call configuration.
- Wire tests check rule delivery with host control omitted, false, and true, and assert host-only instructions stay gated.
- Scoped oxfmt and git diff --check passed.

Two independent static reviews (Codex and Muse): no actionable correctness or security findings.

[Stock regression output](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/5aed80388a76ec53daefeca742a277b56bddfbfb/voice/red.log) · [Patched test output](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/5aed80388a76ec53daefeca742a277b56bddfbfb/voice/green.log)

AI-assisted. [Sanitized work log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/5aed80388a76ec53daefeca742a277b56bddfbfb/AI-WORK-LOG.md).

prs.title: feat: start local sessions from public GitLab projects
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

GitLab users cannot choose a public project in New session and start working in a managed checkout through a supported plugin integration. Repository plugins also lack a public contract for joining that workflow.

## User Impact

- Enable the bundled, off-by-default GitLab plugin to search public GitLab projects and start Gateway-local sessions and worktrees. Self-managed HTTPS GitLab origins are configurable.
- Plugin authors can register repository sources through a narrow public SDK entrypoint. Existing GitHub behavior and configuration remain unchanged.
- Private GitLab repositories, merge-request publication, and plugin-backed cloud workspaces are not included. Cloud repository requests with a plugin source fail with an actionable local-placement message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plugins supply repository discovery, URL admission, and Git transport; the host retains checkout storage, leases, project registration, worktree preparation, and source selection. The selected source remains attached to deferred session preparation and local forks.

Plugin clones now prepare in attempt-private staging. A settled failure or caller cancellation can clean that attempt without needing a cancellation-sensitive canonical-checkout lease assertion. An uncertain Git-process cleanup preserves its staging directory; another attempt cannot overwrite it. Only a successful clone with current checkout authority moves into the managed target.

This candidate is integrated with upstream main at `8a6d3a04ee74654ce03828eb91be4364bf734334`. The unconsumed worker SDK is absent rather than preserving a broken undispatched-parent inheritance path. UI conflict resolution retains upstream's native private fields, and protocol/config outputs were regenerated.

## Evidence

- **Canceled-clone regression:** the canceled case failed before the repair because the populated directory remained. After repair, all five repository-source tests pass, including settled failure, cancellation, uncertain-process preservation, and retry through real Git and the project registry.
- **Focused validation:** 120 tests pass across eight plugin, Git transport, clone-runtime, and New Session UI test files. The public sessions.create test rejecting plugin-backed cloud workspaces also passes.
- **Build and static checks:** pnpm build completes successfully; core, UI, and extensions typechecks pass; scoped lint passes with one unchanged upstream Solid test warning. Gateway/UI validators, config metadata, touched-file formatting, and diff checks pass.
- **Validation gap:** ten Gateway worktree cases could not complete because this sandbox's system temporary filesystem is 1 GiB while the production allocator requires a 4 GiB safety reserve. Capacity checks were not weakened. These cases need exact-head CI on a qualified filesystem.
- **Review gap:** independent Auto Review could not start because its managed runner rejected an unsupported provider configuration field (compat.cachesInstructions). No clean independent review is claimed. This PR remains draft pending that review and the remaining runtime proof.
- **Owner decisions retained:** the public SDK stage and startup-bundle budget still need maintainer judgment. Earlier startup measurements were not rerun on this refreshed base.

### Visual evidence retained from prior author validation

These inspected, sanitized screenshots demonstrate the unchanged picker appearance on the author's earlier revision f959e0164b4c74feb7de1d316aac54daca211a71. They are not fresh current-head end-to-end captures.

| Before: GitHub results only | After: GitLab results also available |
| --- | --- |
| ![Repository picker before enabling GitLab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raw-labs/openclaw/f959e0164b4c74feb7de1d316aac54daca211a71/before-picker-github-only.png) | ![Repository picker with a GitLab results group](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raw-labs/openclaw/f959e0164b4c74feb7de1d316aac54daca211a71/after-picker-gitlab-group.png) |

Contributor credit: @miguelbranco80.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/a77c882f-a25e-4ef4-8c15-0f327a3d729b)

## Worked on by

- @miguelbranco80

prs.title: fix(gateway): let admins stage role assignments before roles are enabled
prs.body:
## Problem

With `gateway.roles.definitions` configured but no `gateway.roles.default`, named roles are an inert catalog: explicit profile assignments are ignored until a default enables enforcement. `users.setRole` nevertheless refused every named assignment in that state:

```
Named-role assignment requires gateway.roles.default to enable named-role enforcement.
```

So an administrator could not assign anyone a role before turning roles on. Setting the default first gives every non-owner, including other administrators, the default role at once, which can lock them out of administration until the shared-secret owner repairs it.

## Solution

`users.setRole` now accepts a role defined in `gateway.roles.definitions` even when no default is set. The assignment is stored and stays inert until a default enables enforcement, then it applies. Nothing else changes:

- Unknown roles are still refused, and the shared owner profile is still refused.
- The existing commit, policy invalidation, connection retirement and change-history record run unchanged for staged assignments.
- `users.list` already reports the staged state accurately (stored `role`, no `effectiveRole`, `roleSource: "default"`), so it is unchanged.

Docs (`docs/gateway/operator-scopes.md`, `docs/gateway/config-gateway.md`) now describe staging and the safe order to enable roles: define roles, stage administrators, confirm that each administrator's verified identity sign-in still has `operator.admin` (an admin-only call succeeds), set the default, then recheck under the enforced role. They also say to keep shared-secret owner sign-in available as the repair path, since named roles never limit it.

No new RPC, config key or schema change.

## Proof: isolated local Gateway

A local Gateway built from this branch (`node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run`), using a temporary state directory and config. Auth is `trusted-proxy` on loopback with TLS and a local owner password, using synthetic people `ada@example.test` (identity grant `operator.admin`), `sam@example.test` and `pat@example.test`. Roles start as `{ admin: [operator.admin], member: [operator.read] }` with no default. A small client drives real WebSocket connects and RPCs.

**Before (base `0167852c1cf`):**

```
[ada] connected profile=32f00d47-… scopes=["operator.admin"] sessionCap=(none)
[ada] users.setRole {"profileId":"32f00d47-…","role":"admin"} -> REFUSED: Named-role assignment requires gateway.roles.default to enable named-role enforcement.
```

**After (this branch):**

```
[ada] connected profile=00dd1dd5-… scopes=["operator.admin"] sessionCap=(none) roleAllowsAdmin=true
[sam] connected profile=5448eb1c-… scopes=["operator.read","operator.write"] sessionCap=(none)
[pat] connected profile=ec77b990-… scopes=["operator.read","operator.write"] sessionCap=(none)
[ada] users.setRole {sam, "member"} -> ok {"role":"member"}
[ada] users.setRole {pat, "ghost"} -> REFUSED: unknown operator role "ghost"; define it under gateway.roles.definitions before assigning it
[ada] users.setRole {"gateway-owner", "admin"} -> REFUSED: the shared owner profile is not governed by operator roles
[ada] users.setRole {ada, "admin"} -> ok {"role":"admin"}
--- staged, gateway.roles.default still unset ---
[owner] connected profile=gateway-owner scopes=["operator.admin"] sessionCap=(none)
[owner] users.list ada: role=admin effectiveRole=(none) roleSource=default
[owner] users.list sam: role=member effectiveRole=(none) roleSource=default
[owner] users.list pat: role=(none) effectiveRole=(none) roleSource=default
[sam] connected profile=5448eb1c-… scopes=["operator.read","operator.write"] sessionCap=(none)   <- staged role is inert
--- owner sets gateway.roles.default=member via config.patch (live reload, changedPaths ["gateway.roles.default"]) ---
[ada] connected profile=00dd1dd5-… scopes=["operator.admin"] sessionCap=write roleAllowsAdmin=true   <- staged admin keeps admin
[ada] users.list ada: role=admin effectiveRole=admin roleSource=assigned
[ada] users.list sam: role=member effectiveRole=member roleSource=assigned
[ada] users.list pat: role=(none) effectiveRole=member roleSource=default
[sam] connected profile=5448eb1c-… scopes=["operator.read"] sessionCap=none roleAllowsAdmin=false
[pat] connected profile=ec77b990-… scopes=["operator.read"] sessionCap=none roleAllowsAdmin=false   <- unassigned gets the default
[owner] connected profile=gateway-owner scopes=["operator.admin"] sessionCap=(none)   <- password owner sign-in unaffected
[owner] change history: Settings updated configuration: gateway.roles.default
[owner] change history: Role for profile 00dd1dd5-… changed from no role to "admin" by profile 00dd1dd5-…
[owner] change history: Role for profile 5448eb1c-… changed from no role to "member" by profile 00dd1dd5-…
```

## Tests

- New `src/gateway/server.auth.role-staging.test.ts` runs the same flow through a real Gateway with WebSocket connects and RPCs (Tailscale-identified people plus shared-token owner ingress). It covers staging with a catalog and no default; the staged person staying uncapped; unknown-role and owner refusals; the staged admin's own connection being retired; change-history entries naming each target, role and acting admin; then, after the default is set, the staged admin keeping `operator.admin`, the staged member and an unassigned person capped to the default, and the owner keeping full access.
  - Red on base: `users.setRole` returns `ok: false` with the refusal above (assertion at the first staging call). Green with the fix.
  - Cost: one test, about 6.7 s of test time with `--maxWorkers=1` (two Gateway boots, one before and one after the default is set). Net test lines are about +165, under the 400-line budget.
- `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-role-catalog.test.ts` (definitions-only admission): it used to seed a stored role directly and then expect `users.setRole` to be refused. It now stages `guest` through `users.setRole` and asserts that `users.list` shows `role: "guest"`, `roleSource: "default"` and no `effectiveRole`. Clearing with `role: null` still succeeds, and the device-token admission assertions are unchanged. I audited the whole file (one test); there is no dead code.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/users.test.ts`: removed `requires gateway.roles.default to assign a named role from definitions alone`, which asserted the removed refusal. The tests above replace it. I audited the rest of the file in full: the remaining tests cover distinct behavior (schema and unknown-role validation, owner refusal mapping, publication ordering, profile-acquisition races, member-profile refusal). I found no tautologies, dead helpers or duplicates.
- Ran: `users.test.ts`, `users-role.worker.test.ts`, `connect-role-catalog.test.ts` and the new test (4 files, 52 tests passed); oxlint and oxfmt on the touched files; docs format, lint, MDX and link checks; `git diff --check`.

## Scope and related work

This keeps main's documented activation rule, where `gateway.roles.default` is the switch that enables named-role enforcement. It only lets administrators prepare assignments before flipping that switch. OpenClaw ID member profiles remain refused here and are managed on **Access**.

#201610 also edits this validation, the same `users.test.ts` case, `connect-role-catalog.test.ts` and the same `operator-scopes.md` paragraph, as part of a broader change to role activation. The two PRs overlap textually in those places, so whichever lands second resolves them. If #201610's activation rule lands, a staged assignment simply applies immediately, and this PR's docs and test follow that rule.

prs.title: fix(windows): consult netstat after an empty PowerShell listener census
prs.body:
Closes #195492

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on Windows, `readWindowsListeningPidsResultSync` treats a successful but empty PowerShell `Get-NetTCPConnection` census as an authoritative "no listener" result and never consults its netstat fallback. A live listener that CIM omits is then reported as a free port, and consumers can clean up a healthy Gateway.

## User Impact

When PowerShell returns no listener, the reader now asks netstat before reporting an empty census. A listener that only netstat sees is returned. A port is reported empty only when both native collectors see nothing, and a non-empty PowerShell result is still trusted without a second query.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Only short-circuit on a non-empty PowerShell census.
- On an empty census, run the existing netstat fallback and union both observations.
- Preserve the previous result if netstat itself fails after PowerShell succeeded, so the fallback cannot make the reader less available.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/infra/windows-port-pids.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 4/4 passed: empty-PowerShell/netstat-listener, non-empty PowerShell, both empty, and PowerShell failure.
- Red-on-base: reverting only `windows-port-pids.ts` makes the empty-census case return `{ ok: true, pids: [] }` instead of the netstat listener.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; oxlint clean on both files.
