prs.title: fix(database-port): prepare runtime config before the offline memory rebuild
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

A successful database port can leave memory indexes dirty because local embedding acquisition reads an unprepared runtime configuration. Publish the freshly loaded destination configuration before opening the memory plugin. This also replaces a pre-port snapshot when the process already has one.

Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/201575.

## What Problem This Solves

An otherwise successful database port can leave memory indexes dirty when local embedding acquisition reaches an unprepared configuration reader.

## Root Cause

The rebuild loads destination configuration with `observe: false`, which does not prepare the strict runtime reader used by local-service acquisition. On trusted main `3587df70a233dc639b733b9169797d3abd138301`, both cold-reader and pre-port-snapshot regressions return `failed` instead of `rebuilt` (2 failed, 6 passed).

The earlier capture-only approach can reuse an existing snapshot. Use `setAppliedRuntimeConfigSnapshot(config, config)` on the configuration already loaded under fresh offline custody. No second configuration load, new settings, schema changes, or changes to per-agent credential isolation are needed.

## Real behavior proof

RAN on trusted main with this repair. Both modified files are byte-identical to the PR head. Contributor-checkout execution was left to exact-head PR CI.

Used a disposable PostgreSQL 18 server with required search extensions, a private Unix socket, synthetic memory, and `memory.search.provider: local`. The real bundled local embedding adapter and process supervisor used a loopback llama-compatible fixture returning deterministic vectors. This is transport/indexing proof, not real model inference.

1. `openclaw memory index --agent main --force` seeded a nonempty SQLite index: `Memory index (main): 1 file indexed.`
2. Changed `MEMORY.md` so the next rebuild required an uncached embedding.
3. `openclaw database port --family agent --to postgres --json` completed. The local service started, became ready, and exited cleanly. Selected result:

```json
{
  "phase": "complete",
  "engine": "postgres",
  "memoryRebuilds": [{
    "agentId": "main",
    "status": "rebuilt",
    "elapsedMs": 2993,
    "files": 1,
    "chunks": 1,
    "plannerStatistics": {"status": "analyzed", "tables": 52}
  }]
}
```

4. `openclaw memory search otter --agent main --json` returned the updated `MEMORY.md`, with both vector and text scores. The fixture recorded three embedding requests: initial indexing, post-port rebuilding, and searching.

## What was not tested

- Real llama-server/GGUF inference, paid providers, channels, Gateway turns, or a stable-release upgrade campaign.
- Local PostgreSQL 16/17; broad compatibility belongs to PR CI.
- Before/after latency benchmarking. The baseline cannot complete the rebuild, so these results make no performance claim.
- Local independent review: ClawSweeper was unavailable. Autoreview's isolation preflight could not launch the configured CLI, so it produced no review verdict. The [exact-head hosted fallback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201594#issuecomment-6998927977) completed with no actionable findings and accepted the CLI proof.

Fixture setup initially rejected an unsupported `sync` key and writable temporary ancestors; only the disposable fixture was corrected. Initial logging also needed its own file. These setup failures did not reach the rebuilt memory path.

## Evidence

The regression fails on unpatched main and passes with this repair. The shipped-command port and search proof above reaches the production local adapter and a deterministic transport fixture. [The exact-head hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201594#issuecomment-6998927977) found no introduced defects and accepted the runtime proof; the required problem/evidence headings were then restored and their [context check passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44537765895). The follow-up review has no remaining findings or before-merge requests.

## Verification

- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44535941029): success, 46 passed jobs and 30 skipped jobs; all five PostgreSQL conformance jobs passed.
- `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-database-port-memory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: red on main (2 failed, 6 passed); green with repair (8 passed). Green shard wall time: 68.09 seconds; reported duration: 65.17 seconds, 95% transformation. New cases: 15 ms and 32 ms. CI file-level timing was not extracted separately.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- Focused `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.json` on both modified files: passed.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` on both modified files: passed.
- `pnpm build:runtime`: passed. UI budget warnings were reported; this PR changes no UI files.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Simplification/readiness pass: reuse the existing runtime publication owner and already loaded configuration. Keep one parameterized regression for cold and stale snapshots. Whole PR: production +4/-1, tests +25/-0, two files. Memory-disabled reporting is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(doctor): only suggest --fix for foreign launchd jobs this invocation can repair
prs.body:
Closes #201390

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on macOS, `openclaw doctor` always advises `openclaw doctor --fix` for stray `ai.openclaw.*` launchd jobs, even when `--fix` is designed to refuse that repair (non-default install identity, external service policy, active update, or another supervisor). Users follow advice that cannot help, see it on every run, and never learn the real reason.

## User Impact

Doctor now checks the same identity, policy, and supervisor gates before printing any removal hint. When it cannot repair, the per-job line and the summary name the specific reason and give a next step that works: run Doctor from the owning install/profile, remove the job through the supervisor, retry after the update, or remove the launchd job manually.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Resolve repair eligibility once, before building the report, and reuse it for both the advice and the actual repair.
- Reject the `--fix` hint when the invocation cannot repair, replacing it with a reason-specific explanation.
- Add an opt-in `repairAvailable` control to `formatForeignLaunchdJobs` so the per-job `Removable with openclaw doctor --fix.` line is accurate too. The default keeps `gateway status` output unchanged.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-foreign-launchd-jobs.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 13/13 passed, including the default-identity advice case and the four refusal cases.
- Red-on-base: reverting both source files makes all four refusal cases fail.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; oxlint clean on all three changed files.

prs.title: improve: reduce work when refreshing changed session rows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refreshing a changed session row repeatedly builds a full merged agent configuration to read individual fields and strips undefined fields twice. This adds CPU and allocation work to session-list updates even when the configuration has not changed.

## User Impact

Session-list rows retain identical serialized contents, immutability and config-reload behavior. The changed-row owner allocates less while updating resident sessions; there are no new options or migration steps.

## Why This Change Was Made

Borrow the agent entry already prepared by the config roster owner for reasoning, fast-mode, workspace and sandbox inputs. Its existing snapshot/publication lifecycle handles reloads. Public clone-on-read and merged-config APIs keep their mutation contracts. Session-specific fast-mode and workspace decisions remain session-specific. Remove the redundant undefined cleanup; the row freezer already handles it while publishing the row.

The freezer already shares unchanged fields and recognizes deeply frozen descendants, so its aliasing behavior is preserved. This starts after #202061 and #202063 and does not repeat their lookup or sandbox work. Production delta: +13 lines for the shared read-only accessor and implicit-agent/default preservation, with no new cache or retained state. The rejected initial approach added a merged-config cache; simplification removed it.

## Evidence

All 24 formal synthetic samples produced byte-identical final rows and identical materialization counts. The fixture has 500 resident rows across three agents in 5,000 sessions, using real metadata writes, transcript appends, reconciliation and archive/re-promotion. Each arm uses the same source-loader path. Two baseline A/A controls and five alternating pairs were run separately for timing and allocation.

| Metric (median of five) | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Owner CPU, 10,000 changed-row reads | 446.766 ms | 418.781 ms (−6.26%) |
| Owner sampled allocation | 687.798 MB | 660.996 MB (−3.90%) |
| 1,000-event stream CPU | 1532.247 ms | 1297.953 ms (−15.29%) |
| Event-stream sampled allocation | 685.123 MB | 683.458 MB (−0.24%) |

The owner CPU A/A drift was −5.93%, so the timing gain is modest relative to noise; owner allocation A/A drift was +0.27%, and all five candidate allocation samples were below every baseline sample. Stream CPU ranges overlapped widely (before 1283–1781 ms; after 1259–1608 ms), so its median is not a stable whole-Gateway estimate. This is a resident-owner benchmark, not a claim about large database scans or filesystem performance. No production data or systems were accessed.

Separate instrumented runs reduce full merged-agent-config constructions from 4,500 to 2,400 (−46.7%); all other work counts and row digests match. CPU profiles confirm the duplicate cleanup disappears; they are excluded from timing medians.

75 focused tests passed across nine suites, including real config reload followed by changed rows, public mutable-shell isolation, fast-mode semantics, sandbox/workspace siblings, row aliasing and prompt-prefix stability. The new fast-mode regression observes zero unrelated default-field reads; restoring the original resolver call produces 20 and fails. `pnpm check:changed` and `git diff --check` pass. Complete-context Codex autoreview is clean through P2.

prs.title: fix: send infer audio/video --model files only to the requested model
prs.body:
Root cause: src/cli/capability-cli/media-understanding-command.ts:49 passes `--model` only as `activeModel` (a conversation-model hint), and the media selector never treats it as a choice: `src/media-understanding/runner.ts:727` takes configured `tools.media.models` entries without looking at it, and with no entries, audio swaps the requested model for the provider default (`runner.ts:439`).

Related: #176246 (reported by @yetval; the earlier strict-pin proposal #172409 was closed in favor of that issue).

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw infer audio transcribe --model provider/model` and `openclaw infer video describe --model provider/model` ignore the flag when `tools.media.models` has an entry, and upload the file to that configured entry, which is often a different provider. With no configured entry, `--model openai/whisper-1` is sent as `gpt-4o-transcribe`. The docs say `--model provider/model` pins a specific backend (`docs/cli/infer.md`).

## User Impact

With `--model`, the file goes only to the requested provider and model. If that model fails, its existing error is returned and no configured entry, CLI backend or provider default receives the file. Runs without `--model` keep today's configured selection and fallback chain.

## Why This Change Was Made

The maintainers chose strict pinning, as the docs already promise. The requested model becomes the only media attempt. It reuses a configured descriptor (credential owner, base URL, headers) only when that entry is the same provider and model. The CLI reaches this through an internal runtime entry, so the plugin runtime API is unchanged. The earlier revision's optional public `modelOverride` field and its SDK doc are removed. `docs/cli/infer.md` keeps the pin wording and adds one line for audio and video.

Thanks @alkor2000 for the original change (kept as the first four commits) and @yetval for the report and repro.

## Evidence

Observed proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190287#issuecomment-7023768213. The CLI was built from source with isolated state and local fixture providers that record every upload. A is the configured chain (a failing entry, then a working one) for audio and video, B is requested with `--model`, and W is a transcription endpoint for the whisper-1 case.

| Run | Base 5fb231527f4f | This PR f3d3739a89 |
|---|---|---|
| audio `--model openai/gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` | A ×3 (voxtral-a-broken ×2, voxtral-a), B 0 | B ×1 (gpt-4o-mini-transcribe), A 0 |
| video `--model moonshot/kimi-b` | A ×3 (qwen-a-broken ×2, qwen-a), B 0 | B ×1 (kimi-b), A 0 |
| audio `--model openai/b-fail` (B returns 500) | A ×3, exit 0 with A's text | B ×2 (500, transport retry), A 0, exit 1 with "Audio transcription failed (HTTP 500)" |
| video `--model moonshot/b-fail` (B returns 500) | A ×3, exit 0 with A's text | B ×2 (500), A 0, exit 1 with "Moonshot video description failed (HTTP 500)" |
| audio, no `--model` (control) | A ×3, result voxtral-a | A ×3, result voxtral-a (same) |
| video, no `--model` (control) | A ×3, result qwen-a | A ×3, result qwen-a (same) |
| audio `--model openai/whisper-1`, no `tools.media.models` | W model=gpt-4o-transcribe | W model=whisper-1 |

- `src/media-understanding/resolve.test.ts`: the new pin case (audio and video) fails on the merge base and passes here. `src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts` (121 tests) and the media runner/runtime suites pass.
- Full build (`--dts`) passes, including the plugin SDK export check. Head 2057fd7882 adds only a `// mock-isolation:` comment on the media runtime mock in `capability-cli.test.ts` (the mock-exports ratchet asks for one when a mock factory changes; the mocked runtime would otherwise reach provider uploads and credential lookup), and drops that factory's stale grandfathered hash from `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt`, on top of the proven f3d3739a89; production code is identical.
- Deltas against the merge base: production +60/−25, tests +54/−23 (the new regression, plus one CLI case moved to the media CLI test module to stay under its line cap), docs +1.

Merge danger: two-way door. A revert restores the old selection; nothing is written or migrated, and the public plugin runtime types are unchanged. Blast radius: only `openclaw infer audio transcribe` and `openclaw infer video describe` runs that pass `--model`. Channel media understanding and runs without `--model` take the same path as before.

prs.title: fix(release): notify Windows after core readback
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Windows publication notifications racing npm propagation during releases, as reported by @RomneyDa during the 2026.11.6 publishing job. The npm child could notify Windows before the shared parent completed core registry readback.

## User Impact

Windows notification runs only after successful core visibility, release verification, and evidence binding. It remains optional: notification failure does not invalidate npm publication or block other release jobs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing notification job from the npm child into the shared release parent, depending on successful `publish`. Reuse the existing payload/notification helper with the exact preflight tarballs, including the protocol package’s own version and SHA512 integrity. Remove the unused child outputs and recording wrapper rather than introduce a cross-workflow waiting handshake.

Successful parent recovery follows the same notification path. Standalone npm-only dispatches no longer notify immediately; parent completion or existing nightly reconciliation owns notification. No package is republished by this change.

## Evidence

- Ordering regression fails on the base: the parent has no post-readback notification job.
- Notification suite: **15 tests passed**, including executing the actual moved shell step against synthetic tarballs and checking both exact payloads (131 ms test time, 1.23 s wrapper wall time).
- Parent publication suite: **57 tests passed** alongside the earlier notification suite (9.78 s combined wrapper wall time); parent code is unchanged.
- Workflow checks passed: actionlint, zizmor, generated CI ownership, composite-action interpolation, and conflict-marker checks.
- Focused oxlint, oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent native review of the complete change against `d16e92a0db0d`: no P0–P2 findings; reviewed ordering, payloads, artifact selection, recovery, and optional failure behavior. Local Codex CLI/ClawSweeper were unavailable; this is not a helper-validated autoreview.
- Local tooling typecheck could not run: the declaration generator rejects the borrowed dependency installation outside this isolated checkout. The original-head hosted production/test typechecks passed; the new head still requires CI verification.
- No live release, npm publication, or Windows dispatch was performed.

Simplification: one parent owns notification timing; no new helper/state/coordination mechanism. Workflow delta: +65/-60 lines; tests replace obsolete child-recording cases with the moved-step integration and ordering guard.


### CI repair

- Fixed the stale npm-child receipt assertion: successful publication now asserts that the child emits no Windows notification records. The parent notification integration remains the payload owner.
- Updated four existing workflow assertions to match authenticated manifest acquisition (exact repository/run/attempt and trusted verifier), and the current full-checkout contracts. These acquisition/checkout changes already exist in base d16e92a0db0d; this repair changes tests only.
- All four failing workflow cases pass (1.31 s wrapper), plus all 8 publication-authority and 15 notification tests (21.45 s combined wrapper). Formatting and git diff --check pass. The redundant whole-file workflow run was stopped; the remaining 583 cases are delegated to PR CI.
- Follow-up CI run 44568684917 passed both formerly failing test shards and all production/test typechecks. It exposed the same restrict-plus-operands error as local lint in the previously untouched empty candidate-file fixture mapping. Removed the unnecessary map over the fixture's always-empty list, preserving its empty API response without casts, suppressions, or dependency changes.


- Final lint repair proof: focused oxlint passed for all three changed test files (2.44 s), formatting/diff checks passed, and all 8 publication-authority tests passed (20.40 s wrapper).


### Final CI verification

- Exact head `ed5c2d8d3d196a7dd9d71d02e88f3e61d7f9570c`: [CI run 44571103009](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44571103009) completed successfully, including both formerly failing test shards, lint, and production/test typechecks.
- Commit status `openclaw/ci-gate` is success: CI and applicable security review requirements passed. [Gate review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44573101044).
- Prior local lint failure is resolved. Local declaration-generation limitation remains local-only; hosted typechecks passed.

prs.title: fix(ios): embedded Dashboard pages ignore device appearance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: opening Automations or another embedded Dashboard page in the iOS app abruptly switches to the saved web theme instead of following the app’s device appearance.

## User Impact

Embedded iPhone and iPad pages use native-aligned surfaces, red accents, and sans-serif typography in the device’s light or dark mode. Saved web theme, accent, and font choices remain unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing theme owner separates rendered iOS appearance from saved web preferences. A private palette uses the existing document-start and runtime stylesheet lifecycle; only iOS embeds fetch it. The redundant first-paint theme-name table is replaced by the equivalent naming formula. Appearance explains that its theme controls customize the web Dashboard.

iOS embeds load one versioned 1,686-byte palette stylesheet, like the selected built-in web palettes; ordinary browsers do not fetch it. The existing first-paint and load/error behavior is retained.

This does not add native theme synchronization, replace native controls, or change Android/macOS appearance or navigation.

## Evidence

Addresses [ClawSweeper’s P2 byte-budget finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199394#issuecomment-6888222427) on `0e05c2920f79a7edaf17201de7d0477a9a3db3ad`. Repair head: `5ce5df3a571f247ce2043da26961b38249e56309`.

**Acceptance:** unchanged deterministic byte/request limits against base `65cf8cdc3780439cb599853f443c45fed28a98e4`; no budget or baseline increases.

| Same-toolchain measurement | Reviewed candidate | Repair | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Document gzip | 14,103 B | 13,966 B | Below the unchanged 14,026 B ceiling |
| Shared total CSS raw growth over base | +1,287 B | 0 B | Pass |
| Shared total CSS gzip growth over base | +195 B | 0 B | Pass |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 | Unchanged |
| Largest JavaScript differential gate | Within allowance | Within allowance | Pass |

- The unchanged differential performance checker passes on the repair. Existing base CSS/largest-asset debt remains visible as warnings; the PR adds no new failing budget. Startup JS grows 70 B and complete route boot JS grows 114 B over the paired base, within existing limits.
- Both strengthened production-browser scenarios pass: phone dark and iPad light, first-paint names **and background colors**, one native palette load per document, live mode changes, unchanged web preferences, and no native-palette fetch in the ordinary-browser control. Fresh production build plus E2E: 16.74 seconds; scenario execution approximately 4.4 seconds.
- 84 related tests pass across six files (4.30 seconds), including every built-in document-start theme name and palette URL in both modes. UI and selected UI app/E2E test-graph typechecks, scoped lint, stylesheet lint, formatting, i18n verification, and diff checks pass.
- Final independent Auto Review of the complete local candidate against the base found no actionable **P0–P2** issues. The reviewer did not independently execute the tests.
- Phone Automations, phone Appearance, and iPad Automations captures were regenerated on the repair and are byte-identical to the three published after images below; their existing uploaded assets are reused.
- Simplification: the global entry CSS no longer carries an iOS-only palette, and the duplicate HTML theme-name table is removed. No new preference store, configuration option, bridge, or compatibility layer. Production/docs delta: +143/−47 lines; regression coverage: +206 lines.

<details>
<summary>Reproducing the size comparison</summary>

The stock `pnpm ui:check-performance:base 65cf8cdc3780439cb599853f443c45fed28a98e4` runner exceeded this sandbox’s 1 GiB `/tmp` capacity while expanding the base archive. The exact base production inputs and frozen candidate were instead built serially in the task-owned checkout with the same installed toolchain and fixed build identity; source backups and a finally block restored the candidate before its build. The repaired build used Vite’s native config loader through the repository TypeScript loader.

The existing supported comparator was then run without changes:

```text
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts --base-dist <paired-base-dist>
```

It reproduces the reviewed candidate’s document/CSS failures and exits successfully on the repair. Precompressed-asset verification also passes. These are deterministic size measurements, not latency benchmarks.

</details>

**Proof boundary:** screenshots use synthetic data and the real production web bundle with the iOS document-start embed capability. They are not simulator captures; Xcode/iOS simulator verification is unavailable in this Linux sandbox. Hosted CI on `5ce5df3a571f247ce2043da26961b38249e56309` confirms that the [performance gate passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43672048654/job/132684408743). UI E2E shards [1/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43672048654/job/132684409028) and [3/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43672048654/job/132684408975) fail; partial attribution is summarized below, and the aggregate gate is red. This PR is not ready to merge. Hosted timing details are not yet summarized.

**CI attribution follow-up:** the WebKit 390 px older-history failure (`190` messages expected, `30` received) matches the complete terminal failure signature in [scheduled-main job 132671550925](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43667891698/job/132671550925), main commit `41f2b981d240cab9e55b07cba991282a795317b5`. This is stronger than the report’s job-name-only classification. That main job also exhibits the same two subpixel footer geometries, with expected/received reversed. The PR’s zero-geometry footer result and Logs auto-follow-resumption failure remain **new/unknown**, not waived or called inherited. A focused replay of the cached-header connection case passes on the candidate (1 passed, 1 dashboard case not selected; 16.06 seconds including build). That is a non-reproduction, not a fix or evidence that the CI failure is unrelated. The additional local WebKit replay is blocked at browser dependency qualification in this sandbox; no test assertions were bypassed, and no CI rerun was requested. No specific introduced defect is established by this bounded investigation. The aggregate gate remains red. The retained main-log window includes the terminal summaries, not the full execution chronology.

### Before and after

Same synthetic Automations page, saved Manuscript Light appearance, and dark device mode. Browser captures of the iOS embed, not simulator screenshots.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: saved web theme overrides dark device appearance](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f1b3caf-d9ec-41ad-a59b-7e3844f215cd) | ![After: native-aligned dark appearance](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/061ca087-f104-4973-b9ea-cee8a1f0bea8) |

<details>
<summary>Additional embedded contexts</summary>

Appearance settings explain the web/device distinction after a live switch to light mode:

![Appearance guidance in light mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0fb6d0c-8ab4-4889-9082-a9dd9188b5c0)

iPad-width Automations in light mode:

![iPad embedded Automations in light mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e2a5f16c-9b34-431c-82fc-0eb750056086)

</details>

## Contributor credit

Reported and scoped by Jacqueline Henriksen.

## Work sessions

An upgrade-survivor failure can report only “successful update contained a failed core step.” Large updater output may be truncated, and the log diagnostic skips advisory-labelled steps even when the owning assertion rejects them.

prs.title: fix(talk): voice consults fail when the chat runs on Claude CLI or a locked native harness
prs.body:
Closes #199378

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Talk voice consults fail with `No API key found for provider anthropic` when the chat's model runs on Claude CLI, or `Model selection is locked` when the chat uses a locked native harness, although typed messages work.

## User Impact

User impact: Gateway voice consults use the same chat runtime, owner, sender, and tool permissions as typed messages, including Claude CLI and locked Codex. Plugin and channel voice bridges are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Key tenets for review:

- Route through `agentCommandFromGatewayIngress`, not the embedded provider runner. Keep exact-source acquisition, controller-input custody, operator authority, operational-instance binding, and terminal-write draining. The command inherits the Talk claim; no second input is reserved.
- Forward owner, sender, tool caps/bindings, client capabilities, approval reviewer, elevated defaults, and source assertion. Reject provider/model overrides. Abort closes delegated authority immediately.
- Borrow the published Gateway reply runtime, with command-owned loading when no owner is published. Preserve locked native runtime selection only for this Gateway path; plugin bridges retain their refusal.
- Treat configured consult thinking as a supported preference, matching #194184. Use per-run thinking without changing persisted chat preferences; explicit unsupported user thinking still fails.
- Prepare the agent workspace with typed-turn bootstrap policy so a first voice turn does not falsely report a vanished workspace. Forward session workspace/cwd pins.
- Consume the settled command owner's visible terminal result, including CLI completions without embedded receipts. Reject recorded errors, error stop reasons, aborts, replaced voice ownership, and stale lifecycle results.
- Retain private ReplyPayload metadata during projection without changing wire shape or speaking preceding queued answers twice.

Deliberate behavior changes: revoked callers receive the typed-turn delivery-fence rejection rather than model text. Gateway voice consults receive ordinary command-owned model and usage bookkeeping.

Existing test fixtures now mock the command-owner seam, clear workspace attestations when deleting test workspaces, inspect the exec-session pin, and wait for actual backend/finalization boundaries. The test-line allocation covers real-Gateway regressions.

## Evidence

### Latest head (November 19): routing fix only; thinking unchanged from main

- **Exact head 17db728ab8f:** Build exited 0 in 3m20.7s. Both candidate-only saved-auth Talk probes exited 0 and verified real workspace tool results of five. Claude CLI finalized “There are five: AGENTS, BOOTSTRAP, IDENTITY, SOUL, and USER.” Locked native Codex finalized “There are five Markdown files at the top level.” Both saved nonempty PCM (1,560,946 and 1,635,826 bytes). In-memory diagnostic tracing showed one command-completion callback and successful completion claim per probe (current and completed), each followed by a speakable provider append. CLI deletion/archive and native lock-preserving archival were verified; supervisors self-unloaded. This is standard relay/API and saved-audio evidence, not a new yield, rendered UI, phone, or live-compaction proof.

- **Yielded CLI consultations (review P1):** a yielded command settlement now completes through the existing command-owned claim, so a Claude CLI consult that calls `sessions_yield` can settle its acknowledgment and retain late-result ownership. Exact spoken acknowledgment delivery remains unverified in the live yield probe below. Abort, error, terminal-receipt and current-owner fences are unchanged. RED reproduced on 000cbff with the real Gateway command controller, then GREEN. A real-command embedded-yield regression checks one acknowledgment, one claim and one late append, so there is no double delivery.
- **Thinking: unchanged from main.** Voice consults use `talk.consultThinkingLevel`, else `high`, for every runtime, exactly as on main. The command owner only normalizes that level to what the selected runtime supports. Earlier revisions of this PR changed this default; that is reverted (no owner decision is needed).
- Focused suite **111/111** passed on 8a0563d63c0 (the mock-only matrix was replaced by one bridge regression); scoped type-aware lint exit 0. Exact-head build passed, exit 0 in **3m51.5s**.
- **Fresh 8a0563d saved-auth diagnostic live probes:** Claude CLI executed a real workspace count/list returning **5** (AGENTS.md, BOOTSTRAP.md, IDENTITY.md, SOUL.md, USER.md); finalized provider speech: “There are five Markdown files at the top level: AGENTS, BOOTSTRAP, IDENTITY, SOUL, and USER.” Locked native Codex / gpt-6.1-sol executed a real count returning **5**; finalized speech: “There are five Markdown files at the top level of my workspace.” Both exit 0; PCM **1,671,346 / 1,731,826 bytes**. CLI deletion/archive receipt and native supported archival/history were verified; native runtime/model locks remained set and no active run remained.
- These two probes used **in-memory diagnostic harness instrumentation**, not an uninstrumented binary: each recorded command completion, `claimAppend` with `current=true, completed=true`, and a speakable provider append. No tracked source or built files were edited. Saved Settings auth was used in place; no login, credential import, downgrade, production change, or deployment. Supervisors self-unloaded. The earlier b34992b standard CLI attempt remains inconclusive, not an established dropped-result regression.
- **Separate historical b34992b yielded-CLI probe:** real `sessions_spawn` and `sessions_yield` returned yielded status with stored acknowledgment “CLI yield ack”; requester-final later reported five. Exact spoken acknowledgment delivery is **not proven**: “I hear you” preceded the yield. Speech initially said four before requester-final arrived, then corrected: “Correction: the child agent finished with five Markdown files.” The deleted child’s underlying tool output remains unverified. This is not exact-head yielded acceptance or proof of faithful initial speech. Raw transcripts, detailed traces, and audio remain private.

- **Historical yielded CLI consult (8a0563d, diagnostic tracing):** the acknowledgment reached the provider append exactly once (`providerAppend {"channel":"speakable","text":"yield ack"}`, preceded by `claimAppend {"current":true,"completed":true}`), and the late result reached it exactly once: "clean yield late result: the child counted 5 top-level markdown files … The exact child tool output, from `ls -1 *.md; echo "---"; ls -1 *.md | wc -l`, was: AGENTS.md, BOOTSTRAP.md, IDENTITY.md, SOUL.md, USER.md, then a line of three dashes, then 5." There was no duplicate append. Limits: the realtime model spoke a guessed count before the late result arrived, then spoke the delivered result; the child ran with cleanup=delete, so its tool output is shown as relayed in the late result, not read from the deleted child's history.
- **Data-model compatibility from latest stable 2026.11.5 (auth-free):** a clean 2026.11.5 install was seeded, with no model calls, with a model-locked native Codex session (`modelSelectionLocked`/`runtimeSelectionLocked` true), a chat with `thinkingLevel: low`, and Talk settings (`consultThinkingLevel: medium`, `silenceTimeoutMs: 1789`). It was then stopped, and candidate 8a0563d started on the same state. Every seeded field (session keys, ids, lifecycle revisions, model/provider, both lock flags, thinking level, Talk settings) read back identical (`equal: true`). The only difference is the runtime capability descriptor the candidate reports (cloud/device placement support), which is expected and is not persisted session data. No login, credential, or production change.

- **Retained-child yield follow-up (8a0563d):** actual spawn used `cleanup=keep`; supported child `chat.history` directly retained the real `exec` call (`ls -1 *.md`) and its five-file output (AGENTS.md, BOOTSTRAP.md, IDENTITY.md, SOUL.md, USER.md). Diagnostic tracing recorded exactly one `CLI YIELD ACK` provider append after `claimAppend current=true, completed=true`, and exactly one late-result provider append reporting five. Probe exited 0; supervisors self-unloaded. This closes the deleted-child evidence gap, not faithful initial speech: realtime speech still guessed before correcting to five. prs.title: fix: greet new agent users in their selected language
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Switching the Control UI from English to Brazilian Portuguese translated the interface, but creating an agent still opened a conversation in English. Both its saved introduction and the role choices ignored the selection.

## User Impact

A new agent greets you and asks about its role in the language selected when you create it, without requiring a reconnect. Existing conversations are not translated or rewritten.

## Why This Change Was Made

The creation request now carries the current interface language. The Gateway uses the same supported locale for the introduction it saves and the role question it asks the model to write. Clients that omit the field use their connection language, falling back to English. Template setup is unchanged.

## Evidence

[Before and after: browser screenshots and annotated comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202112#issuecomment-7024552992)

On two isolated production builds, connect in English, select **Português brasileiro** in Appearance, create Luma on the same connection, then reload. On the baseline, Luma said “Hi, I’m Luma. Happy to help.” and asked about roles in English. On the candidate it said “Olá, sou Luma. Estou aqui para ajudar.” and asked “Qual papel você gostaria que eu desempenhasse?”, offering all four roles in Portuguese. Both rendered messages matched the saved transcript. The role question came from a real model; no responses were mocked.

Baseline: a14344254e. Tested commit: 71e94c4831. The published head 9a3590443f has the identical Git tree. Local validation: 33 UI tests, 13 Gateway onboarding tests, the public WebSocket creation integration, protocol checks, and `pnpm check:changed` passed. The WebSocket test passed under its original timeout on an isolated rerun. All 23 supported locales were checked for named and unnamed saved greetings; only Brazilian Portuguese received the full browser/model comparison.

## What Problem This Solves

The same category could have different icons on Plugins and Templates when the registry supplied a different icon. The public registry currently matches for both shared categories, Productivity and Research, but the UI did not guarantee that.

Productivity keeps its task list and Research keeps its magnifying glass in both catalogs. Other plugin categories retain their registry icons and existing fallback. Skills has no category filters and is unchanged.

In Chromium, a fixture supplied a box for Productivity and a globe for Research. Plugins showed the conflicting icons before the change and matched the rendered Templates page afterward. The normal registry case and Skills page were unchanged.

prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

[OpenClaw 2026.11.5](https://www.npmjs.com/package/openclaw/v/2026.11.5) ships PostgreSQL shared state and agent stores. Published-driver CI now installs that npm release with both stores on PostgreSQL and checks that users can open the same session and transcript after the installed updater activates the candidate.

## Root Cause

Published-driver CI seeded SQLite only. PostgreSQL migration fixtures checked individual schema changes without exercising the released npm updater and candidate activation on populated PostgreSQL stores. The operator guide still described stable PostgreSQL upgrades as inapplicable.

## Real behavior proof

Ran the new fixture against disposable PostgreSQL 17 with the published 2026.11.5 npm package and a candidate built and packed with the CI artifact commands. The fixture wrote a session and transcript through the released Gateway, verified its backup, ran the installed `openclaw update --yes --json --no-restart --tag <candidate.tgz>`, and started the candidate Gateway. The updater recorded `succeeded` at `finished` and replaced the installed build.

```sh
node scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/published-driver-postgres.mjs candidate.tgz artifacts
```

```text
Published 2026.11.5 PostgreSQL state 36 → 40, agent 38 → 43; Gateway history preserved
```

The fixture requires a disposable PostgreSQL DSN in `OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN`. It checks the original store identities before opening the candidate Gateway.

## Verification

- The base workflow resolver emitted no PostgreSQL selection. The patched resolver emitted `postgres=true` for the 2026.11.5 candidate. Older and frozen candidates stay out of this case.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/ci-published-driver-update-plan.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 31 tests.
- Candidate build and tarball integrity, workflow sanity, targeted formatting and lint, and `git diff --check` passed. The final local upgrade fixture took 4m18s.
- The first CI run flagged the fixture's promise rejection typing. The follow-up passed the type-aware script lint and repeated the full upgrade and planner suite. [Updated-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44633456653)

## Evidence

Local autoreview covered the initial patch at P0 through P2 and found no actionable defects. The follow-up changes error handling types and preserves the same upgrade path. The production and full-tree unused-file scans both passed.

## What was not tested

This case uses foreground Linux Gateways and synthetic RPCs. Managed service restart, PostgreSQL rollback restore, Windows package update, and paid model calls are outside this case.

prs.title: fix(sessions): speed up watched session updates on PostgreSQL
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

A session event with several watchers makes PostgreSQL write each watcher's progress in a separate request. On a remote database, those requests add up while the shared-state writer lock is held. This change writes independent cursor updates in batches, so eight watchers take one cursor write.

## Root Cause

The shared-state worker already reads independent watcher cursors together, then upserts each row individually before committing the event. The synchronous PostgreSQL bridge waits for each upsert. Server logs on the baseline recorded eight cursor upserts for every event in a warm eight-watcher run.

## Real behavior proof

Recorded a goal event through `recordSessionStateEventAsync` on disposable PostgreSQL 18.7 and checked durable history through `listSessionStateEventsSince`. Two alternating baseline/candidate pairs yielded 16 warm samples per revision per delay. The same Unix-socket proxy applied either zero delay or 10 ms per direction. The client awaited the production shared-state worker.

| Added round-trip delay | Main median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 | Cursor upserts per event |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 ms | 10.96 / 48.35 ms | 11.45 / 16.40 ms | 8 → 1 |
| 20 ms | 312.26 / 446.57 ms | 157.57 / 166.89 ms | 8 → 1 |

Ranges were 7.80–48.35 / 7.97–16.40 ms without added delay and 304.58–446.57 / 155.64–166.89 ms with added delay, baseline / candidate. Both candidate runs read back all 17 goal events, including warm-up.

The existing fanout regression now checks cursor writes as well as stored progress and excluded watchers. On main it failed with `expected 1003 to be less than or equal to 11`. Independent rows share batches of 100. Keys that can bind to the same value keep sequential reads and writes, and each event's writes finish before the next event starts.

Started an isolated foreground Gateway with PostgreSQL shared state and a loopback mock model. Created a session, seeded eight watchers, and edited its goal over the WebSocket RPC. The reply returned the edited objective, the event appeared in durable history, and the server recorded one cursor upsert.

```json
{"rpc":"sessions.goal.update","status":"updated","durableGoalEvent":true,"watcherCount":8,"cursorWrites":1,"modelCalls":0}
```

## What was not tested

Managed PostgreSQL, real WAN or TLS behavior, full model turns, or mixed reader/writer load. The Gateway smoke used a loopback mock model. It made zero model calls.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/sessions/session-state-events.test.ts src/sessions/session-state-events.worker-boundary.test.ts src/sessions/session-state-events.worker-control.test.ts src/sessions/session-state-events.ownership.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `git diff --check`
- Focused tests passed 48/48 across four files. The fanout test passed in 1.53 seconds locally.
- Type-aware lint, targeted type checking and formatting passed for the two changed files.
- Local review preflight stopped before loading a reviewer. Hosted review follows the repository fallback.
- The first CI run caught a stale operation name in the database worker inventory. The repair replaces that exact entry with `writeMaterialCursors` under the existing worker-only classification. The targeted inventory classified the real writer as `W` and found zero main-thread SQL calls in the kernel. The worker registry and ratchet contract suites passed.
- The whole-repository local ratchet terminated inside its resource scope. The hosted ratchet checks the repaired head.
- On the repaired head, the hosted baseline ratchet and aggregate CI passed. [Baseline ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44631802256/job/135940995604) · [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44631802256) · [Aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44633697967)

prs.title: fix(exec): autoAllowSkills ignored for gateway-host exec
prs.body:
Closes #158165

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with exec approvals in `allowlist` mode and `autoAllowSkills: true`, an agent whose commands run on the Gateway host is still denied (`exec denied: allowlist miss`) the binaries its own workspace skills declare in `requires.bins`. `autoAllowSkills` only took effect on node hosts.

## User Impact

User impact: Gateway-hosted agents (containers, servers, most self-hosted setups) can use `allowlist` mode with `autoAllowSkills` and have the binaries of their eligible skills allowed, without a hand-kept allowlist that duplicates skill metadata. Binaries of disabled or otherwise ineligible skills, and binaries no skill declares, stay denied. With `autoAllowSkills` off (the default), nothing changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway exec host evaluated the allowlist without skill bins, while the node host passes them (`skills.bins`). When the agent's effective approvals enable `autoAllowSkills`, the gateway host now trusts only the bins declared by **the executing agent's eligible skills**: the set its prompt sees (`resolveWorkspaceSkillPromptEntries`: enabled, allowed by the bundled-skills allowlist and the agent's skill filter, requirements met). It never trusts every installed skill, so a disabled bundled skill cannot grant execution trust. Those bins go to the same allowlist evaluation the node host uses. This is the agent-scoped option recommended in the issue review. Bins are resolved on the same `PATH` the command resolves on: the Gateway's `PATH` plus operator `tools.exec.pathPrepend`. Host exec already rejects a requested `PATH` (`Custom 'PATH' variable is forbidden during host execution`), so a tool call cannot point a skill bin name at another binary; a test pins that invariant. The evaluation moves into a sibling module, so the already-over-cap gateway host file shrinks.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway, allowlist mode, before and after.** Same script for both: a fresh state dir; approvals `agents.main = { autoAllowSkills: true, allowlist: [] }`; two workspace skills, `skill-tool` (requires `skill-tool`) and `disabled-skill` (requires `disabled-tool`, with `skills.entries.disabled-skill.enabled: false`); the three executables on the Gateway's `PATH`; `openclaw gateway run`; then one `openclaw agent` turn per command. The model is a scripted local OpenAI-compatible stub (deterministic, no keys) that asks the `exec` tool to run one command and replies with the result.

```
===== BEFORE (published 2026.9.5 image)
[before] OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (ec9c1a1)
[before] approvals main: {"autoAllowSkills":true,"allowlist":[]}
[before] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: skill-tool
[before]   reply:   "error": "exec denied: allowlist miss"
[before] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: disabled-tool
[before]   reply:   "error": "exec denied: allowlist miss"
[before] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: other-tool
[before]   reply:   "error": "exec denied: allowlist miss"

===== AFTER (this PR, built from 659b5e30dc)
[after] OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (659b5e3)
[after] approvals main: {"autoAllowSkills":true,"allowlist":[]}
[after] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: skill-tool
[after]   reply: exec returned: skill-tool ran
[after] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: disabled-tool
[after]   reply:   "error": "exec denied: allowlist miss"
[after] agent turn: the model asks exec to run: other-tool
[after]   reply:   "error": "exec denied: allowlist miss"
```

Eligibility is OpenClaw's own: when the executables sit only in a `tools.exec.pathPrepend` directory, `openclaw skills check` lists `skill-tool (bins: skill-tool)` under missing requirements, so the skill is not in the agent's prompt and its bin is not trusted either. The trusted set always matches what the model is shown.

**Tests and checks**

- New `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.auto-allow-skills.test.ts` (real exec tool, gateway host, allowlist mode): an eligible skill's bin runs with `autoAllowSkills` on; denied with it off; **a bin only a disabled skill declares stays denied**; a bin no skill declares stays denied; a requested `PATH` reaching a planted skill-named binary is refused. The eligible-skill test fails with the source change removed (1 failed / 4 passed). ### Final-initiation recheck (revision 7)

**What was wrong.** The skill-authority recheck ran once, before launch preparation. The launch could then still await four things before the native spawn: standing-grant consumption (cron), secret-egress registration, the supervisor scope fence, and adapter preparation. The synchronous guards at the end of `runExecProcess` checked only source, operator and committed-policy/grant authority. So a skill uninstalled, or a bin repointed, during one of those waits still let the pinned command launch.

**What changed.**

- Each async re-resolution (`verifyGatewaySkillBinAuthority` in `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway-allowlist.ts`) now returns the authority it verified, and the recheck holds it. That held authority is the skill source revision (`getSkillsSourceVersion`, read before discovery), the bins that authorized the command, and the PATH they resolve on.
- A new synchronous check, `findStaleHeldGatewaySkillBinSegment`, rechecks that held authority. It denies in three cases: nothing was verified, the skill source revision moved (a skill was installed, removed or reconfigured), or an authorizing bin now resolves to a different executable. It uses the same `isSegmentAuthorizedBySkillBins` comparison as allowlist evaluation, so the single shared implementation is kept.
- `createGatewaySkillBinAuthorityRecheck` (in `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway-revalidation.ts`) exposes that check as `assertSkillBinAuthorityCurrent`. The gateway composes it into the `assertCurrent` it hands to the runtime: the committed-authorization assertion for the inline paths and detached approval, and the grant's assertion for cron standing grants.

**Where it runs.** `runExecProcess` passes that `assertCurrent` to the supervisor as `beforeSpawn`. It also wraps it into `initiateSpawn` (`createExecLaunchLifecycle().wrap`), which calls it synchronously right before `launch()`. No await sits between the check and the native spawn. All six launch paths go through it: inline ask, ask-fallback, auto-review allow-once, detached approval, direct allowlist, and cron standing grant. A refusal at initiation throws `GatewaySkillBinAuthorityWithdrawnError`, an `ExecProcessPreflightError`. The exec tool unwraps it into the usual denial result, and a detached launch reports it in its follow-up. On the cron path the grant has already been consumed when this final check refuses. That matches how the other final-initiation refusals already behave there.

**Regression tests.**

- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.skill-initiation.test.ts`, new. It runs the real gateway authorization, `runExecProcess`, supervisor, child adapter and native launch. The skill bin is a copy of `touch` that writes a marker file. Trust is withdrawn inside the secret-egress registration await, after the spawn preflight has passed. That is the only seam: the registry is wrapped through `importOriginal`.
  - `launches the skill bin while skill trust holds through initiation` is the allowed control. The marker is written.
  - `denies at native initiation when the authorizing skill is uninstalled after preflight`
  - `denies at native initiation when the trusted bin name is repointed after preflight`
- `detached approval launch denies at native initiation when trust is withdrawn after preflight`, in `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.auto-allow-skills.test.ts`. The supervisor stand-in uninstalls the skill and then calls the real `initiateSpawn` hook. The launch callback is never invoked, and the follow-up carries the skill denial.

With the fix (3 + 12 tests across the two files, all pass):

```
✓ launches the skill bin while skill trust holds through initiation
✓ denies at native initiation when the authorizing skill is uninstalled after preflight
✓ denies at native initiation when the trusted bin name is repointed after preflight
✓ detached approval launch denies at native initiation when trust is withdrawn after preflight
```

Without the fix (the three source files reverted, tests kept), the withdrawn command launches and runs:

```
× denies at native initiation when the authorizing skill is uninstalled after preflight
  → expected { status: 'completed', …(7) } to be undefined   (exitCode 0, exitReason "exit")
× denies at native initiation when the trusted bin name is repointed after preflight
  → expected { status: 'completed', …(7) } to be undefined   (exitCode 0, exitReason "exit")
× detached approval launch denies at native initiation when trust is withdrawn after preflight
  → Received: "Exec denied (gateway id=…, spawn-failed): skill-tool"   (initiation was not refused)
```

### Executing-agent skill ownership and real Gateway traces (revision 8)

Head: `0a4297accba` (one commit on top of `e0e151ea91b`; no rebase, the branch merges cleanly with main).

**What was wrong.** Tool assembly can borrow another agent's tool policy. `agent-tools.ts` then has two ids: `agentId`, the policy owner from the capability profile (`options.policyAgentId`, or the profile a caller passes in), and `executionAgentId`, the agent that actually runs (`options.agentId`, or the agent of `runSessionKey`). Exec defaults received only `agentId`, and `resolveGatewaySkillBins` used it. So under a borrowed policy, `autoAllowSkills` loaded the **policy** agent's workspace, while the run's skill snapshot (`skillScope`) came from the executing agent. A bin declared only by the policy agent's skill was trusted, and a bin declared by the executing agent's own skill was not.

**What changed.**

- `ExecSkillScope` gains `ownerAgentId`. `agent-tools.ts` now always sets `skillScope.ownerAgentId = executionAgentId`, next to the session filter and overrides from the same run's snapshot. Before, the scope was only set when a snapshot existed.
- `resolveGatewaySkillBins` (`bash-tools.exec-host-gateway-allowlist.ts`) resolves the workspace and the eligible skills from `skillScope.ownerAgentId`. It falls back to `agentId` only for callers that don't separate the two. That one resolver feeds all three skill checks: allowlist evaluation, the async re-resolution in `verifyGatewaySkillBinAuthority`, and the authority it holds. The held authority records that agent's `workspaceDir` and skill source revision, so the synchronous `findStaleHeldGatewaySkillBinSegment` check at native initiation watches the executing agent's skills. No await was added before the spawn.
- Approval policy is unchanged and stays with `agentId`. That covers the approvals-file entry, the `autoAllowSkills` flag, ask/security, and the cron standing-grant source match.
- Node host, for comparison: `skills.bins` returns the union of bins across **every** configured agent (`agentSkillFilter: "ignore"`), so the node has no per-agent owner to disagree with. The gateway stays narrower: only the executing agent's skills that its run admitted.
- The skill owner is carried inside the existing `skillScope` instead of as a new top-level exec option. This keeps `bash-tools.exec-run.ts` at the line cap: a top-level field would have taken it from 700 to 701 counted lines.

**Regression tests.**

- New: `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.skill-owner.test.ts`. It has no mocks. It assembles exec through `createOpenClawCodingTools` with `agentId: "execution"`, `policyAgentId: "main"` and `runSessionKey: "agent:execution:main"`, the same borrow shape as the gateway-tool assembly test. Then it calls the real exec tool, which runs the gateway authorization, supervisor and native launch. The approvals entry exists only for `main`. Each agent's workspace has one skill: `main` declares `policy-tool`, `execution` declares `exec-tool`. Both bins are copies of `touch`.
  - `runs a bin declared by the executing agent's own skill`: the marker is written.
  - `denies a bin declared only by the policy agent's skill, with no I/O`: `exec denied: allowlist miss`, and there is no marker.
- `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.skill-initiation.test.ts` (real native path) adds a borrowed-policy variant. The allowed control runs as `execution` under `main`'s policy. `denies at native initiation when the executing agent's skill is uninstalled under a borrowed policy after preflight` uninstalls the skill during the post-preflight await. The denial comes from the synchronous initiation check against the executing agent's held authority.

With the fix:

```
✓ skill-owner      > runs a bin declared by the executing agent's own skill
✓ skill-owner      > denies a bin declared only by the policy agent's skill, with no I/O
✓ skill-initiation > launches the skill bin while skill trust holds through initiation (borrowed policy: true)
✓ skill-initiation > denies at native initiation when the executing agent's skill is uninstalled under a borrowed policy after preflight
```

Without the fix (`agent-tools.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway-allowlist.ts` and `bash-tools.exec-types.ts` reverted, tests kept), the policy agent's bin runs and the executing agent's own bin is refused:

```
× denies a bin declared only by the policy agent's skill, with no I/O
  - "denied": "Error: exec denied: allowlist miss",  "ran": false
  + "details": { "status": "completed", "exitCode": 0, "exitReason": "exit", … },  "ran": true
× runs a bin declared by the executing agent's own skill
  - "details": { "status": "completed", "exitCode": 0 },  "ran": true
  + "ran": false
× launches the skill bin while skill trust holds through initiation (borrowed policy: true)
  → exec denied: allowlist miss
× denies at native initiation when the executing agent's skill is uninstalled under a borrowed policy after preflight
  → exec denied: allowlist miss
```

**Correction to the cron standing-grant wording (revision 6).** Revision 6 said the cron recheck means "a withdrawn skill denies the launch without spending the grant". That is too broad. The skill recheck applies only to segments the occurrence's own preflight admitted on **skill trust**. A command the operator explicitly allow-always granted runs on that grant, whether or not a skill still declares its bins. The grant was minted for the exact operation (command, cwd, env), so it authorizes the command independently of skill trust. Grant consumption in detail:

- **Not consumed:** the occurrence's preflight admitted a segment on skill trust, and the async recheck before consumption finds that trust withdrawn. The launch is denied and `useCount` is unchanged.
- **Consumed, then denied:** trust is withdrawn after consumption but before native initiation. The synchronous initiation check refuses the launch, and the use is already spent (as revision 7 noted).
- **Consumed, launched:** the skill is withdrawn before the occurrence starts. Its preflight then admits nothing on skill trust, the grant covers the whole command, and the occurrence runs on the grant. This is `occ3` below.
- **Grant not used at all:** every segment is admitted on skill or allowlist trust, so nothing asks. The command runs directly and the grant is neither checked nor consumed.

### CLI grant carries the admitted skill narrowing; merged with main (revision 10)

Head: see the latest commit (main merged in at `b110c2259f0`, plus four commits). The branch was about 21,900 commits behind, so main is merged in, not rebased; the merge commit holds only the conflict resolution.

**The remaining P1.** Revision 9 fixed whose skills a CLI-backend run trusts, but not *which* of them. `buildCliMcpGrantContext` copied no skill state into the loopback grant, so `resolveGatewayScopedTools` built mediated exec without the session's `skillFilter`/`skillOverrides`, and the gateway resolved the executing agent's full eligible set. A session with `skillOverrides: { "exec-tool": false }` (or a filter that left `exec-tool` out) could still launch `exec-tool` without approval, and the final rechecks repeated the same widened scope.

**Fix (`e4f477f2022`).**
- `buildCliMcpGrantContext` captures the run's `skillFilter` and `skillOverrides` from its skill snapshot as `admittedSkillScope` on `McpLoopbackRequestContext` (host-captured, never read from MCP headers).
- `tool-resolution.ts` passes `execSkillScope: { ownerAgentId: sessionAgentId, ...admittedSkillScope }` to mediated tool assembly. Evaluation and every spawn-boundary recheck read that same scope.
- SDK surface: `skillOwnerAgentId` is removed from the public `OpenClawCodingToolsOptions`; `execSkillScope` is on `InternalCodingToolsOptions` only, and the public `PluginCodingToolsOptions.exec` type omits `skillScope`. Plugin callers cannot supply either, and assembly always derives the scope itself.

**Regression, CLI grant path (`src/gateway/tool-resolution.skill-owner.test.ts`).** Still no mocks. The context now comes from the real `buildCliMcpGrantContext` and is spread into `resolveGatewayScopedTools` the way `mcp-http.runtime.ts` spreads it; the resolved exec tool runs through real gateway authorization, the supervisor and a native launch of a `touch` copy.

```
✓ runs a bin declared by the executing agent's own skill
✓ denies a bin declared only by the policy agent's skill, with no I/O
✓ runs a bin whose skill the session's snapshot admits
✓ denies a bin whose skill the session's snapshot left filter-excluded, with no I/O
✓ denies a bin whose skill the session's snapshot left override-disabled, with no I/O
```

With only the `admittedSkillScope` line in `buildCliMcpGrantContext` reverted, both exclusion cases launch the binary:

```
× denies a bin whose skill the session's snapshot left filter-excluded, with no I/O
  - "ran": false
  + "ran": true
× denies a bin whose skill the session's snapshot left override-disabled, with no I/O
  - "ran": false
  + "ran": true
```

**Adapting to main.**
- Main localized `collectSkillBins` into the `skills.bins` handler (#179567). This PR is a second consumer, so `src/skills/discovery/bins.ts` is restored and `skills.bins` uses it again; no duplicate collection logic.
- The revalidation module no longer carries copies of `resolveGatewayExecApprovalDrift`, `revalidateGatewayExecApprovalBinding` and `buildGatewayExecApprovalDeniedToolResult`; main moved them to `bash-tools.exec-approval-binding.ts` and `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.output.ts`, and the gateway host imports them from there.
- `exec-approvals-skill-bins.ts` uses `isPathScopedExecutableToken` from `exec-authorization-plan.ts` instead of a local copy.
- Exec defaults moved to `agent-tools.assembly.ts` on main; `skillScope` is set there now.
- `bumpSkillsSnapshotVersion` no longer takes `changedPath`; the gateway skill suites drop it.
- Line cap (`0e17db36d6c`): main shrank `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts` to 1171 counted lines, so the skill wiring would have grown it to 1198. The per-session consecutive auto-review denial streak moves to `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.auto-review-denials.ts`, and allowlist evaluation plus its skill-bin authority recheck become one entry point in the revalidation module (`evaluateGatewayShellAllowlistWithSkillAuthority`, with `holdWith` for the standing-grant initiation check). The ratchet passes with no over-cap growth.

**Tests run (local, 2 workers), on the final head:** `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway` (including the auto-review denial cases), `.auto-allow-skills`, `.skill-initiation`, `.skill-owner`, `tool-resolution.skill-owner` and `bash-tools.exec-cron-grant` (including the standing-grant skill recheck): 74 passed. Before the line-cap refactor, `exec-approvals`, `server-methods/skills.remote` (`skills.bins`) and `cli-runner/mcp-grant-context` also passed.

| `tool-resolution.skill-owner.test.ts` (3 cases added) | 5 passed | 28.9 s (Vitest 16.3 s) |

The dead-export scan's findings are all in files this PR does not touch (already present on main). oxlint could not run locally because this worktree lacks `eslint-plugin-solid`; CI runs it.

**Test-line budget.** Main now ratchets total test lines. This PR's net test growth is 848 lines across the five gateway skill-trust suites, recorded as an exact allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/158244-gateway-auto-allow-skills.txt`. **Live CLI-backend run (head 555a55b).** A real `openclaw gateway run` with the bundled `claude-cli` backend (`claude-cli/claude-opus-5`). prs.title: fix: speed up compaction for PostgreSQL-backed chats
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Compacting a PostgreSQL-backed chat can spend one database round trip per short message assembling the summary input. Compaction now batches selected reads. It keeps the same summary text and retained message order.

## Root Cause

The prepared compaction renderer introduced in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/777fc99a8993b55fab66e3cb17faf4ef520cd40f did a sequence lookup each time its per-entry callback needed text. The finalizer repeated that lookup for each retained row and each new suffix row. With 160 short messages, the render worker issued 160 payload SELECTs.

The renderer can defer exact-size entries until selection finishes. The read worker groups small inline payloads into batches of up to 128 rows and 2 MiB, using the same source snapshot and transcript fence. Elision that needs actual text during selection and payloads above 16 KiB still use individual reads. Finalization uses the same batch reader for retained rows and the appended suffix.

## Real behavior proof

PostgreSQL 18 over a disposable local Unix socket, Node 26, 160 short messages, one warmup per revision and five interleaved measured runs per revision. The acceptance rule was identical ordered summary text and at most eight payload SELECTs.

| Prepared render | Payload SELECTs | Median | p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Base | 160 | 8.18 ms | 11.54 ms |
| Patch | 2 | 2.37 ms | 2.66 ms |

The regression also compacts a transcript with a 20,000-character message and a new user message appended before finalization. Full render, sampled render, and finalization used 3, 2, and 4 payload SELECTs respectively. The sampled text matched the existing serializer. Finalization kept the pending message.

To run the database regression, use PostgreSQL with the standard OpenClaw test extensions and run:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs \
  --engine postgres --connection "$TEST_POSTGRES_DSN" -- \
  src/config/sessions/session-compaction-render.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

An isolated foreground Gateway with a PostgreSQL agent store completed the real `sessions.compact` RPC on 8 MiB and 40 MiB transcript fixtures. Each run made one loopback mock-model request, persisted the summary, and preserved the same retained user request after the Gateway stopped. The prepared worker returned `preflight`, `prepared`, `rendered`, and `finalized` in both runs.

## What was not tested

No remote database, external provider, or paid model calls. The timings cover the prepared render operation and use a local socket. The 1/2 MiB setup smoke produced an unstable heap slope. The Gateway proof at the default fixture sizes passed the residency limit and observed zero removed transcript bytes hydrated on the main thread.

## Verification

- Baseline reproducer failed on the payload-read budget, with 160 SELECTs.
- PostgreSQL conformance regression passed on the patch. The test case took 0.43 s on the CI repair rerun, plus setup and worker compilation.
- The focused compaction serializer, preparation, and SQLite bounded-context suites passed 66 tests.
- Scoped formatting, type-aware lint, production types, agent/session test types, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The first CI run caught the worker's use of the global `Iterator` value outside the project's TypeScript library target. The suffix read now uses a generator to keep SQLite iteration lazy. Both affected typecheck lanes passed locally.
- Local autoreview covered the complete patch through P2 against `1fbcec108f4e4` and returned no actionable findings.
- Exact-head CI for the repaired branch. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44633967355

prs.title: fix(database): show PostgreSQL shared-state ownership
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

`openclaw database ownership status` now shows the recorded external supervisor for PostgreSQL shared state. It reads the configured store and keeps the existing JSON and text output.

## Root Cause

The status handler sent the shared-state SQLite path straight to the SQLite ownership reader. On PostgreSQL that path holds the store identity, while the ownership record lives in PostgreSQL. A fresh command printed `{"status":"unowned"}` for a prepared store with a committed supervisor record.

Status now resolves the configured engine and uses the existing read-only shared-state ownership operation for PostgreSQL. PostgreSQL follows the configured state directory. SQLite keeps the same path as the claim command. During config recovery, an identifiable SQLite store can still report its ownership. Engine resolution errors for a PostgreSQL target fail status even when another SQLite file exists.

## Real behavior proof

On PostgreSQL 18.7, the CLI process regression prepared a shared-state namespace, committed a synthetic supervisor record, and ran `database ownership status --json` in a fresh process. Main returned `"status": "unowned"`. The patch returned `"status": "external"` and the stored supervisor record. The regression checks both an inherited and a config-supplied state directory, and compares the local anchor bytes before and after status.

Ran with the repository PostgreSQL conformance preload pointed at a disposable Unix-socket server.

```sh
pnpm test src/cli/database-ownership.postgres.test.ts src/cli/database-ownership.process.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The candidate build also passed through the normal launcher after `pnpm build:ci-artifacts`. With the state directory inherited from the environment and with it supplied by config, `node ./openclaw.mjs database ownership status --json` returned `{"status":"external","ownership":{"version":1,"mode":"external","managerId":"supervisor","claimedAt":1}}` (path omitted). The two outputs matched, including the database path. The anchor bytes matched.

For a published-package control, v2026.11.6 claimed a disposable SQLite store and successfully ported shared state to PostgreSQL. Its status returned `{"status":"unowned"}`. Running the candidate CLI against that installation returned `{"status":"external"}` and the original ownership record. The config, anchor, and PostgreSQL schema version 36 matched before and after. The candidate checkout was labeled 2026.11.5 and printed the newer-config warning while completing the read.

## What was not tested

The version swap exercised the CLI against retained data. It did not run a managed update, start a Gateway, or measure startup latency. The proof used isolated state and made no model calls.

## Verification

- Six focused tests passed. They cover PostgreSQL ownership and state-directory routing, SQLite claim behavior, and the distinction between recovery from malformed config and unresolved PostgreSQL credentials.
- Focused formatter, type-aware lint, and diff checks.
- Production changes are limited to the status handler (+49 net lines). Tests use the production CLI role and real store preparation (+96 net lines). The PostgreSQL regression took 2.02 seconds locally and 4.62 seconds in hosted CI.
- Exact-head CI passed, including all four PostgreSQL conformance shards and the PostgreSQL 16 Gateway smoke. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44632015764

prs.title: fix: clarify PostgreSQL schema upgrades for Git installs
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

The Git update guide and schema inspection warning tell operators that the new release migrates state at startup. PostgreSQL shared-state and agent schema migrations require Doctor with writers stopped. The guide now gives that step for direct starts, and the warning reports that the update continues without promising a migration.

## What Problem This Solves

An operator preparing a Git release update can read the startup promise and skip Doctor before starting a Gateway on an older PostgreSQL schema.

## User Impact

Git users can follow the PostgreSQL migration procedure from the update guide. An inconclusive schema inspection no longer promises an automatic migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The PostgreSQL guide already owns the migration procedure. The update guide identifies the affected stores and links to the procedure. The warning reports the outcome known to the updater.

## Root Cause

The Git release path skips the updater's pre-restart Doctor and allows schema inspection to be inconclusive before a new-version process opens the stores. The warning treated that decision to continue as proof that the next startup would migrate state. The PostgreSQL guide requires stopped-writer Doctor for a direct start, and PostgreSQL agent schema migration checks maintenance authority before executing the migration. [PostgreSQL migration guide](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/postgresql#updates-and-schema-migrations)

## Real behavior proof

An existing integration test makes a retained SQLite agent store unreadable, then runs the updater's real post-activation schema inspection against a candidate runtime. A failed read before the candidate opens state yields a warning and leaves the update eligible to continue. The fixture uses SQLite to drive the common inspection error path. On main, the Git release case failed because the warning ended with `The update continues; the new release migrates state when it starts.` With the patch, it ends with `The update continues.` and still classifies the read as a warning.

## What was not tested

A full managed Git release switch, service restart, and live PostgreSQL upgrade were outside this run. The runtime test made no model calls.

## Verification

- `pnpm test src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrated-schema.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'an unreadable store'` on main produced one expected failure and three passes.
- `pnpm test src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrated-schema.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` after the fix produced `27 passed (27)`. The command took 302 seconds including the runtime build. The later docs wording edit left both TypeScript files byte-identical.
- `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/install/updating.md docs/gateway/postgresql.md`
- The docs publishing parser resolved the new link to the PostgreSQL migration heading.
- Targeted formatting, type-aware lint, the CLI update TypeScript shard, and `git diff --check` passed.

- Final-head CI passed 38 jobs, including `check-docs` and the required `openclaw/ci-gate`. [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44630247895)

## Evidence

AutoReview found that the initial wording covered too many PostgreSQL stores. After narrowing it to shared state and agent stores, the final patch reviewed against `1fbcec108f4e4ed21c698d82e31e7ce23498b342` through P3 had no actionable findings. The patch removes the Git-specific warning branch and adds no test cases.
