prs.title: fix(state): name the state directory when it cannot be made private
prs.body:
Refs #137242

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw onboard` and `openclaw gateway install` stop with "State ownership directory must be a user-owned real directory" or "State ownership directory permissions are not private" when `~/.openclaw` is on a mount that shows files as root-owned or ignores chmod (Apple VirtioFS shares, SMB, NFS). The message does not say which directory failed or what the user should change.

## User Impact

The error now names the directory, the uid that owns it, and that the state directory has to be on a local filesystem that supports file ownership and permissions. Nothing changes about what is accepted: these mounts are still rejected.

This does not close #137242. Making install work on these mounts would mean relaxing the state-ownership lock, the `@openclaw/fs-safe` sidecar lock and the 0600 systemd environment file, which is the open security decision on the issue. This PR covers the "name the state directory and a safe local-filesystem recovery path" option from the issue review.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ensureOwnerDirectory` (`src/infra/gateway-state-owner-directory.ts`) owns the check that the state-ownership lock directory (`<stateDir>/tmp/openclaw-<uid>`) is user-owned and mode 0700. It is the first check these mounts fail on current main, before the systemd environment file named in the issue is reached. The ownership and permission checks are unchanged; only the two error messages change. The non-directory error keeps its existing text.

<details>
<summary>Where current main stops on a chmod-less state dir</summary>

- Files shown as root-owned: `gateway install` fails in `ensureOwnerDirectory` on the uid check. `onboard` fails earlier with a bare `EPERM: operation not permitted, fchmod` from the `@openclaw/fs-safe` sidecar lock (`createNativeExclusiveFile` → `fchmodSync`, reached through `withSetupMigrationTargetLock`).
- Files owned by the user but chmod silently ignored: both commands fail in `ensureOwnerDirectory` on the 0700 check.
- The lock directory moved under the state dir on purpose (`resolveGatewayLockDirForCanonicalStateDir`, "clean break" from process temp), so a state dir on such a mount always reaches this check.

</details>

## Evidence

Linux container (`node:24.22.1-trixie-slim`), non-root `testuser`, account home as `HOME`. Main (`e5f1a21`) and the candidate were each packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` and installed with `npm install -g`. `systemctl`, `loginctl` and `busctl` are the shims from `scripts/e2e/lib/doctor-install-switch/shims`, not a real systemd user manager. `~/.openclaw` is a vfat loop mount: with `umask=000` files show as uid 0, writes work and `chmod 600` returns EPERM, the behavior the issue describes for VirtioFS. With `uid=<testuser>`, chmod returns 0 but has no effect. Commands: `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --mode local --auth-choice skip --skip-daemon`, then `openclaw gateway install --port 18789`.

Root-owned mount, `gateway install`:

```
main: ... failed to acquire gateway state ownership at /home/testuser/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-1001/state.<hash>.lock | State ownership directory must be a user-owned real directory. Stop the Gateway and other state owners for this profile, run `openclaw doctor --fix` against the same state/config, then restart the Gateway.
fix:  ... | State ownership directory /home/testuser/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-1001 is owned by uid 0, not this user (uid 1001). Run OpenClaw as the user that owns its state directory, and keep that directory on a local filesystem that supports file ownership and permissions. Stop the Gateway ...
```

User-owned mount that ignores chmod, `onboard`:

```
main: State ownership directory permissions are not private
fix:  State ownership directory /home/testuser/.openclaw/tmp/openclaw-1001 permissions could not be set to 0700. Run OpenClaw as the user that owns its state directory, and keep that directory on a local filesystem that supports file ownership and permissions
```

Control, `~/.openclaw` on the container's own disk, same on main and fix: `onboard exit=0`, `Installed systemd service: /home/testuser/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service`, `install exit=0`.

Not changed by this PR:
- On the root-owned mount, `onboard` still prints the bare `EPERM: operation not permitted, fchmod` from `@openclaw/fs-safe`.
- The migration retry text that follows the error still suggests `openclaw doctor --fix`; it is shared by all legacy-migration lock failures.

Tests: `src/infra/gateway-state-owner-directory.test.ts` (1 test) fails on main's `ensureOwnerDirectory` and passes on the fix. `pnpm test src/infra/gateway-state-owner-directory.test.ts src/infra/gateway-state-owner.test.ts src/infra/gateway-lock.test.ts src/infra/state-migrations.lock.test.ts`: 63 passed. `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass; oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the touched files; `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base upstream/main` passes (+26).

Production delta +14/-2; test delta +26/-0.

Merge risk: two-way door; only error text changes, with no config, state or behavior change. Blast radius is the two `ensureOwnerDirectory` errors, which are surfaced wherever state ownership is acquired.

prs.title: fix: stop worktree maintenance duplicating shared Git packs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Worktree housekeeping can consume disk when local Git clones share hardlinked packs. It writes a private replacement, but deleting the shared inputs releases no pack data.

## User Impact

Maintenance preserves hardlinked packs and consolidates only private packs. Its existing progress log now includes replacement bytes written and single-link pack bytes removed, making a pass's storage effect visible. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Filter shared packs before backlog admission and geometric selection, so only reclaimable bytes determine the progression. Private packs still converge without pulling shared history into later rewrites. Promisor separation, kept/cruft exclusions, verification, bounded retirement, and lease/ref-queue ordering remain intact. Temporary-pack cleanup moves unchanged into a sibling module to satisfy the existing 700-line cap. Production grows by 20 lines for the exclusion and accounting.

## Evidence

A real-Git regression fails on the parent and passes with the fix: three local clones retain the base's shared inodes, two private peers fold once, and subsequent simulated hourly passes write no new packs. All objects remain readable. Focused proof: 58 tests passed, one Linux-only skip. Codex autoreview is clean through P2.

The existing committed benchmark now supports three local hardlinked clones and per-pass `statvfs` measurements. Shared-only A/A controls each wrote 68,262,108 bytes and freed zero; the fix wrote zero across six passes. Mixed synthetic fixtures use 23 shared/42 private packs plus a kept 62,000-file (1.14 GB) checkout pack. Their before/after logical totals are 68,262,108 / 44,107,867 bytes written, with 44,109,179 single-link bytes retired in both. Five interleaved pairs measured 39.80 MB → 1.01 MB median filesystem consumption and 10.71 s → 10.62 s owner wall time. Total process-tree CPU was 20.39 s → 20.45 s; peak RSS 798.9 → 800.3 MB. JavaScript CPU median was 5.21 s → 5.70 s; these loaded-host timings do not establish a latency or CPU win. Separate allocation samples were 142.1 → 112.0 MB. Shared-only proof with diagnostic files outside the measured volume consumed 84.15 MB on the parent, versus one 4 KiB metadata allocation and zero free-space loss on passes 2–6 with the fix. `pnpm check:changed` passes. The changed owner test file took 23 seconds of test time in its standalone run; the final three-file focused run took 233 seconds under host load. Exact-head [CI run 44625480785](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44625480785) passed. [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202082#issuecomment-7023682609) reviewed `602b88e249ae16bca80c56f28678079fca49dd55` with zero findings and zero open items; hosted Codex review also completed without findings. No CI rerun or inherited-failure exception was needed.

Measurements use an isolated APFS filesystem; btrfs extent behavior was not measured. Log byte counts cover pack data, exclude sidecars, and do not claim extent-level reclamation for reflinks or snapshots. An external clone started during an admitted pass can change link counts; existing admission and retirement semantics are preserved.

Commands: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/worktrees/git-maintenance.test.ts src/agents/worktrees/service.gc-performance.test.ts src/agents/worktrees/service.removal-budget.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`; `pnpm check:changed`; `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/managed-git-maintenance-measure.ts --mode prepare --packs 65 --hardlinked-packs 23 --blobs-per-pack 32 --state-dir <fixture>`, then `--mode measure --passes 6 --state-dir <fixture>`.

prs.title: fix(codex): isolate catalog and client imports
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200486

## What Problem This Solves

Cold Codex model discovery can block configuration updates long enough to exceed their existing deadline. The reproduced configuration cohort exposed roughly 17.9 seconds of synchronous catalog import work; a subsequent repair exposed another expensive import during client request preparation.

## User Impact

Codex model discovery avoids loading unrelated tool-construction and execution-policy code on its catalog path. The original 14-file, 26-case configuration regression cohort now passes with its original order, two workers and unchanged deadlines in a separately ported integration checkout.

This is a draft: full review and broader qualification remain unfinished. The SDK surface gate is still failed and unwaived.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog now uses the existing host model-auth contract, with its supported direct-registration path preserved. Shared timeout, OAuth predicate and error definitions move to their existing lightweight owners, removing the eager imports that pulled unrelated runtime code into catalog and client loading.

The existing request owner also gains an internal, enforced control-plane scope used by the catalog. It shares one method classification with the sandbox guard, captures scope and method before asynchronous work, and rejects disallowed methods before sending. The callback receives bound lifecycle operations rather than a raw client. Control-plane methods can include mutations; MCP reload still requires execution policy. The default guarded request path remains intact.

Catalog discovery drains the initial account read before capturing account lifetime, and cancellation can retire the exact captured client while preserving sibling leases. Authentication selection, refresh fences, credential reads and request authority remain in their existing owners. No timeout increase or new public SDK, configuration, schema or protocol surface is introduced.

## Evidence

- **Focused behavior:** 285 Node and 285 Bun cases passed across 15 whole files at `f3ee16738326134d4ea70b472a209f9bad65aaa5`, with zero skips. This covers request authority, forbidden zero-send behavior, cancellation, release, catalog ordering and physical-client retirement. The subsequent `f3ee1673` to `ddfbab55` delta changes only a test assertion from `.sort()` to `.toSorted()` plus formatting.
- **Final-source checks:** at `ddfbab552ecbbfd09714b97875c3c98fe0d79989`, scoped format and type-aware lint passed with zero warnings/errors; both extension type stages passed. Full `pnpm build` completed all 17 phases. The isolated Codex import profile completed its baseline and Codex children with verified cleanup.
- **Original regression:** the separately ported integration checkout passed all 26 cases in the original 14 files, with zero skips. Earlier failing runs remain failures; instrumented runs are not substituted for this ordinary regression result.
- **Still open:** the current full source review is running. Broader qualification is incomplete, and the remote provider's missing run association currently prevents safe continuation. There is no whole-PR, hosted-CI or measured latency-improvement claim.
- **SDK gate remains failed:** 3,905 exported symbols exceed the 3,894 cap; 2,247 callables exceed the 2,243 cap. Source comparison attributes the excess to changes already present in the base and attributes no added public exports or callables to this repair. That is source-derived evidence, not an executed base-versus-head symbol inventory. No cap increase or landing exception is approved.

<details>
<summary>Scope, dependency checks and proof limits</summary>

`git diff --numstat 86441105b165150c743886aa4eb8a1deeca8d525 ddfbab552ecbbfd09714b97875c3c98fe0d79989` gives 91 changed paths and 1,947 changed lines: production +700/-602 (net +98), tests +580/-61, documentation +2/-2. Production growth supplies the enforced internal capability and lifetime boundary; the connected import removals and their callers remain one repair.

The upstream Codex contract was inspected directly at `414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6`, including `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/catalog_processor.rs:248`, `codex-rs/app-server/src/models.rs:12` and `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/model.rs:43`.

Physical-process tests use a synthetic peer and controlled clock; they do not prove an authenticated upstream binary or the complete public harness path. The import profile is a cold-import snapshot, not a complete dependency-closure or performance comparison.

Related: #167410 (not a claim to fix every timeout reported there).

## What Problem This Solves

A Codex parent waiting for a native child can lose its original tool declarations when that child finishes but its result is still being delivered. Separately, ending the parent turn too early can replace a successful yield acknowledgement with cancellation before Codex records it.

## User Impact

The parent can resume with its original native thread and saved tool declarations after child completion, and its successful yield acknowledgement is recorded before interruption. Saved declarations do not revive old tool executors. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

This refresh keeps only two production repairs still absent from the pinned main:

- Retain saved declarations while the existing completion owner holds current delivery custody, independently of execution retention. Recheck that owner after loading metadata.
- Wait for matching native output receipts before terminal interruption, including the outer Code Mode output for nested yields.

Upstream already owns child-result context propagation, end-of-turn user context, detached announcement dispatch, and sibling-completion retention (#190999). This PR does not duplicate those repairs. Regression tests also check compatibility with closed foreground scope and bounded-history finalization rejection; those tests are not claims that this PR newly fixes either mechanism.

## Evidence

Refreshed head: `205d6d97ed2664ac714b827e35bbd824de015d8b`, based on main `da8fd166f5bca52a464470cf9172bdd7a58106cf`.

- **162 distinct tests across 14 focused suites passed.** This includes real native Codex 0.169.0 recording the yield output before interruption; direct/nested receipt ordering; pending-result catalog continuity without stale executor revival; revoked custody; final-effect Gateway authority; bounded-history finalization rejection; upstream sibling retention; and original-child follow-up.
- **Fail-before proof against pinned main:** substituting only main's lifecycle controller makes both direct/nested yield regressions fail at the premature `turn/interrupt` assertion. Restoring this PR's controller passes them. No assertions or ownership guards were weakened.
- Core/plugin production types, scoped core/plugin test types, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap and test-line-budget checks passed.
- Fresh local **Codex autoreview**, full committed range with 13 complete owner-context files, P0–P2: **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. This is source review, not runtime qualification.
- All six prior commits rebase without conflicts. Range-diff preserves their changes, apart from test-inventory context. Main subsequently advanced to `1fae66036cc0dbcaae0696975030375ba4d278bc`; inspected drift and merge-tree are clean. Checks/review above remain bound to the pinned base/head, not an untested later rebase.

Tests ran separately in secretless, network-disabled containers using synthetic fixtures. Summed test-command wall time: **948.39 seconds** (including cold worker compilation). Native boundary test command: **53.84 seconds**. Repeated inner/outer tooling summaries counted once. Hosted CI for this rewritten head is pending; CI timing is not yet available.

The retained test allocation covers native-boundary, custody, authority and receipt-ordering regressions; shared baselines remain unchanged.

Earlier PR heads had focused source checks and local reviews. </details>

A worktree publication that reused an existing pull request told the user “Published,” even though that request did not push a commit or trigger CI.

## User Impact

When the Gateway confirms reuse, the conversation links to the existing PR and says this request made no push and started no CI run. Other successful results still link to the PR. The public publication receipt and client protocol retain their existing shape.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conversation notice uses the recorded source head, published head, and GitHub effect evidence from the worktree receipt. A recovered publication that pushed a commit still receives the ordinary PR notice. Publication execution and storage are unchanged.

## Evidence

- All three real-Git transcript regressions fail on the pinned base at the old “Published” notice and pass with the fix. The reuse case keeps the existing commit and write count. Both lost-response cases show the ordinary PR link.
- 156 tests passed across worktree, repository, personal publication, transcript reporting, readiness, and source/compiled protocol validation. The three regression cases passed again after the final test helper cleanup.
- Core typecheck, typed lint, format, and whitespace passed. Test-line budget is +48 against the +400 allowance, with no allocation change. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issue.
- The verified revision incorporates upstream `eedb353df007419105cd4d2b11fd73b84bc1a509`. The generated protocol matches that base exactly.
- Earlier Team observations on [#192980](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192980) recorded two native publication requests with the same head and no second push or new CI run. Those observations cover the deployed behavior before this copy change.

## Worked on by

- @MertBasar0

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep chat startup responsive and cached history at latest
prs.body:
Related: #160271. Targets that PR's branch.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes empty chats freezing navigation and cached conversations opening above their latest message.

## User Impact

New conversation remains usable after an empty chat. Cached history reaches its latest message while preserving explicit reader and Scroll to latest intent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Settle authoritative empty history without waiting for virtual rows, retire obsolete row projections, and retain initial positioning until history is ready. Admit the first response's input identities before rendering so historical messages cannot masquerade as new remote input. Live input keeps its existing takeover behavior.

Existing history and gallery test fixtures now follow the pane/virtualization lifecycle; their assertions are preserved.

## Evidence

**Live Gateway and model:** the Gateway and bundled UI were built from `473662ad7d48`. Four real conversations were created through the in-app Chromium browser (477 × 842 px), with five requested model turns and no mocked Gateway responses.

- New-session creation remained responsive across all four chats.
- After closing the tab and extending A through the real Gateway, a cold reopen showed the final response at **0 px** from the end.
- A→B→A and A→B→C→D→A preserved the same paragraph at **0 px shift**; A's pane eviction was observed.
- Scroll to latest settled at **0 px** and retained that position after another eviction cycle. B/C/D finished within **0.5 px** of latest.

| Reading A before switching | A after B/C/D and pane eviction |
| --- | --- |
| ![Real-model chat A before switching](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/719a9277-34fb-40f4-9008-de82498724ef) | ![Same paragraph and position after four-chat return](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a0f976f-cf16-466d-bb76-7530542cfdb5) |

<summary>Cold reopen after the real server conversation grew</summary>

![Final real-model response visible after cold reopen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/491d55e9-a811-46c7-97ba-c17304026329)

The browser previously displayed a fitting, one-sentence response. While its tab was closed, the normal Gateway agent command extended that same conversation with a 24-section response. The reopened UI reached its final paragraph. The transient cached-preview frames were not captured. Live proof consists of inspected screenshots and timestamped DOM measurements, not continuous video.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Controlled parent-versus-candidate regression proof</summary>

Actual production UI in Chromium 153 with deterministic Gateway responses. Before: `8716dcb603f0`; after: `473662ad7d48`. Each pair uses the same fixture and viewport.

| Flow | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Empty chat → New conversation | ![Before: navigation stalls after the first empty chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3868ae4e-2770-46be-959b-9f4e62c45aee) | ![After: New conversation is interactive](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a7b37a30-7e94-4350-a9a6-31374b71d7e6) |

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a3b90666-867a-46e4-90aa-38c5e62c0049

Locally, 400 focused unit tests, 46 browser checks, and the complete changed-file gate passed. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The cached-history browser regression fails before the repair and passes afterward.

**CI audit:** [22 inherited dependency advisories](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41192204541/job/124511327072); the lockfile and audit inputs are identical to the parent. This PR changes no dependencies. Native Safari and the disappearing-text symptom remain unverified.

prs.title: fix: ACP prompts that also deliver to a channel no longer hang without a reply
prs.body:
Root cause: src/gateway/server-chat.ts:802 `sendLivePayload` broadcasts only Control UI visible runs; a `deliver: true` run routed to a session's external channel goes only to `sessions.messages.subscribe` subscribers (server-chat.ts:809-820), and the ACP bridge forwarded `deliver: true` (src/acp/translator.prompt-stream.ts) without ever subscribing, so it never saw the reply or the final frame.

Fixes #202047

Thanks @ElanHasson for the report and the fix.

## What Problem This Solves

An ACP client (through `openclaw acp`) can ask for a reply to also go to the session's channel with `_meta: { deliver: true }`. When the session has an external reply route, for example a main session that last talked on a messaging channel, that prompt streams no text to the ACP client and never finishes.

## User Impact

ACP clients get the streamed reply and a normal `end_turn` for `deliver: true` prompts, and the channel still gets the reply once. Prompts without `deliver: true`, and `deliver: true` prompts on sessions without an external route, behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bridge now calls `sessions.messages.subscribe` (`operator.read`) for the session before its first `deliver: true` prompt on the current Gateway connection, with `subscriptionId: "acp:<sessionId>"`. The bridge already holds `operator.write` for `chat.send`, which satisfies `operator.read`, so no new authority is used and no change is made to which connections may see which session.

Lifecycle:

- Subscribes once per ACP session per Gateway connection. Later `deliver: true` prompts send no extra request.
- On Gateway disconnect the bridge forgets its subscriptions (the Gateway drops a closed connection's subscriptions), so the next `deliver: true` prompt subscribes again on the new connection.
- `session/close` releases the subscription with `sessions.messages.unsubscribe`. Bridge shutdown closes the connection, which releases the rest.
- No duplicate chunks: visible runs go through the broadcast only and are not sent again to subscribers (server-chat.ts:802-807), and the bridge does not declare session-scoped events, so subscribing does not change its broadcast fanout.

Accepted edge cases, with no extra code:

- An idle session evicted without `session/close` keeps its subscription until the connection closes; the bridge ignores frames no pending prompt claims.
- If `session/load` rebinds the same ACP session id to another key, the old key's subscription stays until the connection closes.
- A `deliver: true` run in flight across a Gateway reconnect still settles through disconnect recovery, but its live text after the drop is lost.
- If the subscribe request fails, the prompt fails with that error before `chat.send`.

## Evidence

Real Gateway, real `openclaw acp` process over stdio, scripted local model, `qa-channel` fixture channel with a recording bus; the main session got its external route from one channel turn. Observed lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202048#issuecomment-7021699353

| Case | Base 99e2b6eb1f9b | This PR 81d0123652 |
|---|---|---|
| Route + `deliver: true` | no chunks, no result in 30 s; channel send 1 | reply streamed once, `end_turn`; channel send 1 |
| Route, no `deliver` (after the deliver prompt) | reply once, `end_turn`, channel 0 | reply once, `end_turn`, channel 0 |
| No route + `deliver: true` | reply once, `end_turn`, channel 0 | reply once, `end_turn`, channel 0 |

Regression: `src/acp/translator.prompt-prefix.test.ts` "subscribes once per connection before deliver prompts and releases on close" fails on the base and passes here (subscribe before the first deliver prompt, none for the second, again after reconnect, unsubscribe on close). The earlier spawned-Gateway e2e file is folded into that case.

Production +39/-1, tests +28/-2 against the merge base.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert removes the subscribe call and restores the hang; no state, config or contract changes. Blast radius: `openclaw acp` users sending `deliver: true` prompts.

prs.title: fix(cli): stop openclaw logs from printing raw JSON for blank lines
prs.body:
Closes #201820

## What Problem This Solves

After `openclaw gateway status`, or any other command that prints a blank line, `openclaw logs` shows each blank line as the whole raw JSON log record instead of a log line. That record carries internal metadata, including the machine hostname and absolute paths under the home directory, so the noise also ends up in log excerpts people paste into bug reports or chats.

## User Impact

User impact: in `openclaw logs` text output (TTY and `--plain`), a record whose positional log arguments are all empty, such as a blank line printed by a CLI command, now shows as `<time> <level>`. This is how `openclaw channels logs` and the Control UI Logs view already show these records. Records without positional log arguments, for example single-object logger records, still print their raw line as before, preserving content stored only in non-message fields. `openclaw logs --json` and the log file are unchanged. No config, flag, or default changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`formatLogLine` in `src/cli/logs-cli.ts` used `parsed.message || parsed.raw`, so an empty message fell back to the raw record. Blank console lines are captured as `{"0":""}` records, and `parseLogLine` correctly returns `message: ""` for them; the CLI text view is the one consumer that turned that into the raw line. The fallback dates from `efa5f0b` (2026-01-09), with no comment or test describing it.

The fallback is kept but narrowed. When every positional log argument is empty, the message is shown as empty; records without positional arguments keep the raw fallback. In practice, only when the parsed message is empty, the formatter looks at the record's numeric argument keys: if there is at least one and all of them are empty strings or `null`, it shows an empty message; otherwise it keeps the raw line, so records whose content lives only in other fields stay visible. Logs are still written raw; the writer and `parseLogLine` are unchanged.

Unchanged on purpose: blank lines from the JSON console style (`{"time":…,"level":…,"message":""}`, seen only when `--follow` falls back to the systemd journal) have no positional arguments, so they keep printing as before. Those lines carry no `_meta` metadata.

<details>
<summary>Why the formatter parses the raw line again</summary>

`ParsedLogLine` does not record whether positional arguments existed or were all empty, and `--json` spreads it as-is, so adding a field there would change the JSON output. The extra `JSON.parse` runs only for lines whose parsed message is empty; other lines take the same path as before. The numeric-key test matches the one `parseLogLine` already uses, and an empty joined message from `parseLogLine` implies every positional argument was an empty string or `null`.

</details>

## Evidence

"Before" results were taken on main `ebbd85c`. "After" results were taken on `ebbd85c` with this PR's change applied: the real entry-point runs used the same `src/cli/logs-cli.ts` as commit `020edf6344cb`, and the focused tests ran on that commit's full diff.

Real entry point, before and after. Setup: the CLI ran from a source checkout through `scripts/run-node.mjs`, the script behind `pnpm openclaw`, and reported `OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (ebbd85c)`. It used an isolated HOME on a Linux x64 dev host with a minimal local config (`gateway.mode: local`, token auth). The Gateway port was pinned to an unused privileged port and the Gateway was stopped, so `openclaw logs` used the local file fallback.

- Before (`ebbd85c`): one `openclaw gateway status` run wrote 23 log records, 4 of them blank lines. `openclaw logs --plain --utc` printed all 4 blank-line records as raw JSON containing `"hostname"`.
- After (`ebbd85c` plus this change), with a copy of that same 23-record log:
  - The 4 blank-line records render as `<time> info`. The other 19 lines are byte-identical to the "before" output.
  - `openclaw logs --json` output for those 23 records matches the "before" output record for record (deep equality).
  - A fresh `openclaw gateway status` run on the patched build appended 23 more records, 4 of them blank lines, which also render as `<time> info`.
  - None of the 46 text lines contains `{"0":""`, `"hostname"`, or `"_meta"`.

<details>
<summary>Redacted terminal output (before and after)</summary>

Lines are copied from the captured output, with timestamps as captured (UTC). The hostname, the source-checkout path, and the isolated HOME path are replaced with `<host>`, `<source-checkout>`, and `<isolated-home>`; each run used its own isolated HOME. The long JSON line is truncated where marked, `…` marks omitted unrelated lines, and `stderr:` labels the line written to stderr.

Before (`ebbd85c`), `openclaw logs --plain --utc --limit 200`:

```text
stderr: Local Gateway RPC unavailable; reading configured file log instead.
Log file: <isolated-home>/.openclaw/logs/openclaw-2026-11-19.log
…
2026-11-19T10:16:30.193Z info Host desktop: disabled
2026-11-19T10:16:30.193Z info {"0":"","_meta":{"runtime":"node","runtimeVersion":"24.22.1","hostname":"<host>","date":"2026-11-19T10:16:30.193Z","logLevelId":3,"logLevelName":"INFO","name":"openclaw","path":{"fullFilePath":"file://<source-checkout>/dist/console-BPV4arGE.mjs:3:4644", … (truncated here)
2026-11-19T10:16:30.193Z info Config (cli): ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
…
```

After (`ebbd85c` plus this change), the same frozen log, then one fresh `openclaw gateway status` run:

```text
stderr: Local Gateway RPC unavailable; reading configured file log instead.
Log file: <isolated-home>/.openclaw/logs/openclaw-2026-11-19.log
…
2026-11-19T10:16:30.193Z info Host desktop: disabled
2026-11-19T10:16:30.193Z info
2026-11-19T10:16:30.193Z info Config (cli): ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
…
2026-11-19T11:14:01.649Z info Host desktop: disabled
2026-11-19T11:14:01.649Z info
2026-11-19T11:14:01.649Z info Config (cli): ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
…
```

</details>

Focused tests:

- New case in `src/cli/logs-cli.test.ts`: "renders blank positional messages in $mode output without the raw record and keeps other records raw", run in plain and pretty mode. It covers a blank-line record, plus four records that must keep their raw line: an unrecognized JSON line, a single-object record, an `Error` record with an empty message whose `stack` must stay visible, and a record with an empty `message` field but a non-empty positional argument.
- On `ebbd85c` with only the test change, 2 of the file's 19 tests fail: exactly the two new cases, at the first assertion; the only differing line is the blank-line record printed as raw JSON; with this change, all 19 pass. `pnpm test src/cli/logs-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 7.5 s wall time, 4.89 s Vitest duration. Consumers: all seven `src/cli/logs-cli*.test.ts` files plus `src/logging/parse-log-line.test.ts`, 8 files and 54 tests, pass.
- Targeted checks:
  - `oxfmt --check` passes on both files;
  - oxlint with the core config reports 0 warnings and 0 errors (the lint command printed by `pnpm check:changed --dry-run`);
  - `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass.
  - `pnpm build` passes with this change.
  - `pnpm check:changed --base ebbd85c` passes locally, including the repository ratchets (line cap, max-lines, assertion safety, mock exports).
- CI: pending at the time of opening

Not covered:

- The Gateway-running path (`logs.tail`) was not run end to end. All three sources (RPC, local file, journal) go through the same formatter, and the focused test feeds a `logs.tail` payload through the registered command. On 2026.11.5 the bug showed on both the running and stopped paths.
- The focused test does not exercise the real write-then-read path; the before/after run above covers that.

prs.title: fix(channels): configure and onboarding save channel tokens as plaintext
prs.body:
Closes #175333

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a channel token entered in `openclaw configure`, `openclaw onboard --classic` (also the Gateway's `wizard.start` setup flow), `openclaw agents add` or the chat's channel setup is saved as plaintext in `openclaw.json`, while the same token entered through `openclaw channels add` goes to the protected secret store since #169732. Doctor then warns about plaintext secret-bearing fields, and the prompt option itself says "Stores the credential directly in OpenClaw config".

## User Impact

A new or changed channel credential entered through any of these setup paths is saved in the shared secret store, and `openclaw.json` keeps a `store` SecretRef, as with `openclaw channels add`. Config saved by earlier releases is not rewritten: only credentials that differ from the config the channel step started from are moved, so existing plaintext values, env references and SecretRefs stay as they are.

## Why This Change Was Made

#169732 put the protected-store step inside `persistChannelPluginConfig`, which only `channels add` and the Gateway's channels wizard use. The other setup paths run the same `setupChannels` prompts but commit through `writeWizardConfigFile`, `commitSetupConfigFile` or `commitConfigWithPendingPluginInstalls`, so they never reached it.

- The store loop moves unchanged into `storeChannelSetupCredentials` in `src/commands/channels/plugin-config-persistence.ts`. `persistChannelPluginConfig` calls it as before, so `channels add` keeps its authority checks and its retained-entry notice.
- `configure`, onboarding, `agents add` and `runHostedChannelSetup` call it right before their config commit. The hosted chat setup passes its existing `beforePersistentApply` and `assertPersistentEffectCurrent`, so it uses the same checks it already applies to the config write.
- The plaintext option's hint becomes "Saves the credential in the protected secret store". `docs/cli/channels.md` and `docs/start/wizard-cli-reference.md` say where the credential goes.

No new authority checks: writing the credential to the store needs no more authority than the plaintext config write these paths already did. Each flow's authority is still checked where it already is, when the flow starts and at its commit, per the "check authority one time, when work starts" rule in `AGENTS.md`. This is the main difference from the closed #175334, which added mid-flight revocation checks and grew to +611/-91.

Accepted limit: if the config commit fails after the store write, `configure`, onboarding, `agents add` and the hosted chat leave an unreferenced store entry without the "retained" notice `channels add` prints. The config keeps its previous value, and a retry stores the credential under a new name.

## Evidence

Built `dist` and drove the real interactive CLI in a pseudo-terminal (same step file on both builds), Node 24.22.1 on macOS, with isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_PROFILE` and a synthetic Telegram token.

`openclaw configure --section channels` → Add or update channels → Telegram → Enter Telegram bot token:

| Check | Main `0aafe6691b8` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Entry option hint | "Stores the credential directly in OpenClaw config" | "Saves the credential in the protected secret store" |
| `channels.telegram.botToken` | `"123456789:AAsynthetic…"` | `{ "source": "store", "provider": "default", "id": "CHANNEL_SETUP_7618…" }` |
| Token text in `openclaw.json` | present | absent (0 matches) |
| `doctor --lint --json` | "openclaw.json contains plaintext secret-bearing config fields." | no plaintext warning |
| `secrets audit --check` | not run | "clean. plaintext=0, unresolved=0", exit 0 |

- `openclaw onboard --classic --flow quickstart` (other steps skipped by flags) → Select channel → Telegram → token: this branch saves `{ "source": "store", "provider": "default", "id": "CHANNEL_SETUP_7505…" }`, with no token text in `openclaw.json`. I didn't build main again for this path; the main-side output is the reporter's capture in #175333 (`"botToken": "123456789:AAsyntheticOnboardToken…"`).
- Control: `openclaw channels add --channel telegram --token …` on main still saves a `store` SecretRef. That path runs the same moved loop.
- Regression `registered configure saves a new channel token in the protected store` (`src/cli/program/register.configure.persistence.test.ts`) drives the registered `configure` command. It fails on main (`expected null to match object { source: 'store', … }`) and passes here.
- `hosted-setup.runtime.test.ts` asserted that the plaintext token reached the config writer. It now expects the store ref.
- Consumer suites (22 files across setup, configure, onboarding, `agents add`, hosted chat, Gateway wizard and cold-import tests): 297 passed. Targeted oxlint, format check, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, the test-lines ratchet and `git diff --check` pass.

Hosted Gateway chat setup (this branch): isolated `openclaw gateway run` with a local OpenAI-compatible mock model as the verified inference route. Typed `connect telegram` through the `openclaw.chat` RPC (`openclaw gateway call openclaw.chat`), then answered each wizard step the same way (token source 1, synthetic token, allowFrom, skip admin):

- The token-source step shows "Saves the credential in the protected secret store".
- The run finished with "Done — telegram is configured.", and `channels.telegram.botToken` is `{ "source": "store", "provider": "default", "id": "CHANNEL_SETUP_687B…" }`. The token text is absent from `openclaw.json` and from every file in the state directory (0 matches).
- `secrets audit`: `unresolved=0, storeResidue=0`. Its only two `plaintext` findings are `gateway.auth.token` and the mock provider `apiKey` that the harness config seeds.

Upgrade from latest stable v2026.11.6 (`npm install openclaw@2026.11.6`, `06afb10`), same isolated state for both versions. An earlier run from v2026.11.5 gave the same results.

1. On 2026.11.6: config with a plaintext `channels.slack.botToken`, an env SecretRef `channels.slack.appToken` (`SLACK_APP_TOKEN`) and unrelated settings (`gateway.port`, `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`), then `openclaw channels add --channel discord --token …`. That release stores the Discord token itself: `channels.discord.token` → `CHANNEL_SETUP_0576…`.
2. On this branch: `openclaw configure --section channels` adds Telegram.

| Path | After this branch's `configure` |
|---|---|
| `channels.slack.botToken` (plaintext from 2026.11.6) | unchanged |
| `channels.slack.appToken` (env ref) | unchanged |
| `channels.discord.token` (store ref written by 2026.11.6) | unchanged |
| `gateway.port`, `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` | unchanged |
| `channels.telegram.botToken` | new `store` ref `CHANNEL_SETUP_6308…`; token text absent from `openclaw.json` |

- Other config changes: only `channels.telegram.*`, `plugins.entries.telegram`, `wizard.lastRun*`, two `meta.migrations` flags from current main, and `meta.lastTouchedVersion`, which shows the checkout's package version.

prs.body:
Related: [original PR #192940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192940). This is the bot-published replacement of that message-only change; the original PR remains open separately.

## What Problem This Solves

A worktree publication that reused an existing pull request told the user “Published,” even though that request did not push a commit or trigger CI.

## User Impact

When the Gateway confirms reuse, the conversation links to the existing PR and explicitly says this request pushed no new commit and triggered no CI run. Other successful results still link to the PR. There are no public receipt or protocol changes, migrations, or required user actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conversation notice uses the recorded source head, published head, and GitHub effect evidence from the worktree receipt. A recovered publication that pushed a commit still receives the ordinary PR notice. Publication execution and storage are unchanged.

## Evidence

This replacement reuses the patch-identical operator proof recorded in [#192940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192940); the tests and independent review below were not rerun in this publication session.

- Three real-Git transcript regressions fail on the pinned base at the old “Published” notice and pass with the fix. Reuse keeps the existing commit and write count; both lost-response cases show the ordinary PR link.
- 156 focused tests passed across worktree, repository, personal publication, transcript reporting, readiness, and source/compiled protocol validation. The three regressions passed again after the final test-helper cleanup.
- Core typecheck, typed lint, and format passed. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issue. The test-line ratchet is +48 against the +400 allowance, with no allocation change.
- This publication session verified the exact transferred patch hash, full tree, eight-file scope (90 insertions, 24 deletions), whitespace, and index/worktree consistency. Protocol packages, protocol documentation, and workflows are identical to the pinned base.
- Hosted CI for this replacement has not yet been observed. No workflow approval, rerun, or dispatch is part of this publication.

prs.title: feat(ui): render explicit TeX equations in Control UI Markdown
prs.body:
Replaces #95995, preserving its author and commit history.

Related: #42840

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI chat displays explicit TeX equations as raw text, and Markdown can consume their backslashes or alignment syntax.

## User Impact

Inline `\(...\)` and display `\[...\]` / `$$...$$` equations render in chat and other Markdown views. Prices such as `$5` and `$10`, inline code, and fenced code stay literal. Single-dollar math is deliberately unsupported.

## Why This Change Was Made

Updated for OpenClaw **2026.11.5**, targeting its `release/2026.11.5` maintenance branch. Markdown recognizes complete explicit delimiters before escaping and preserves display equations across streamed blank lines. The existing Solid bridge renders sanitized source with lazily loaded **KaTeX 0.19.1 (MIT)**, pinned in the package manifest and lockfile. Vite builds the renderer and fonts into Gateway-local assets; no CDN or checked-in vendor bundle is needed.

KaTeX uses `trust: false` and bounded explicit dimensions. The sanitizer adds one custom tag without broadening style, SVG, MathML, or attribute permissions. Font declarations are registered once in the document; equation styles stay in shadow roots.

## Evidence

- **77 Chromium tests passed** across the new math suite and existing streaming-security suite. On the original source, the math suite fails four regressions and passes two literal-input cases.
- **Native production chat E2E passed**: inline/aligned/display equations, loaded fonts, literal code/currency, and source/display changes on a retained host. The before capture uses the official unpatched 2026.11.5 UI with the same synthetic message.
- `pnpm ui:build`, targeted lint, parser/runtime/state typecheck, formatting, and diff checks passed. The production report has an advisory total-CSS warning of **308535 B gzip versus 308526 B**; no budget baseline was raised. Full UI typechecking remains for CI; the local sparse checkout does not contain its complete transitive type graph.
- Fresh independent review found no actionable issues. Simplification uses the existing parser, sanitizer, streaming cursor, and Solid bridge; the opaque MathJax bundle is removed. Relative to v2026.11.5: 258 net lines in source/dependencies/docs/allocation and 215 regression-test lines. The separate test allocation covers exactly those parser, streaming, shared-consumer, and real-chat regressions.

**Before — OpenClaw 2026.11.5**

![Before: raw TeX in Control UI chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/72d0611e-fc4f-4e39-b5ee-ed0b7dddc168)

**After — explicit equations, with prices and code preserved**

![After: rendered equations in Control UI chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0adcb6a5-23e7-4cc4-b480-1e2413bab47c)

prs.title: fix: point doctor to the config file when validation fails
prs.body:
Closes #202032

## What Problem This Solves

When Doctor encounters an invalid setting it cannot migrate, its recovery hint sends users to `config unset`. That command also requires a valid config, so users get stuck when they follow the hint.

## User Impact

Doctor now shows how to locate the active config and tells users to correct the reported setting there. The command includes the selected profile when one is active.

## Why This Change Was Made

`config file` can resolve the path while the config still fails validation. The fallback uses that read-only command and preserves any more specific repair hint supplied by the check.

Thanks to @anmol0b for reporting the recovery loop and to the ClawSweeper review for the invalid `gateway.port` test case.

## Evidence

On Windows I ran the built CLI with an isolated profile and set `gateway.port` to a string. On the base, Doctor recommended `config unset`, which exited 1 and left the invalid value in place. On this branch, Doctor gives the active-profile lookup command. I used the returned path to correct the port, and the same final-validation check then passed.

Terminal excerpts show the actual output. I redacted the fixture directory and kept only the relevant fields in the final JSON.

```text
> node openclaw.mjs doctor --fix --non-interactive
Location: gateway.port
Next step: Run `openclaw --profile proof-pr202032-fixed-followup-built doctor --fix` to migrate or remove retired keys. If no migration applies, find the active config with `openclaw --profile proof-pr202032-fixed-followup-built config file`, correct or remove the reported setting manually, and rerun Doctor.

> node openclaw.mjs config file
<isolated-profile>\openclaw.json

# After correcting gateway.port in that file
> node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --only core/doctor/final-config-validation --json
{"ok":true,"checksRun":1,"findings":[]}
```

I updated the existing final-validation regression to check the new hint and removed the separate converter test. The existing case failed on the prior PR head and passed after the test update.

- `pnpm test src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 94 tests in 496s locally.
- `pnpm test src/flows/doctor-lint-flow.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 5 tests in 34s locally.

prs.title: fix(doctor): heartbeat migration stuck after a full-disk archive write
prs.body:
Closes #200083

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor --fix` can never migrate `HEARTBEAT.md` again when its archive write once failed partway, for example on a full disk. The warning says "Rerun doctor to retry safely", but every rerun reports `heartbeat migration archive collision` until the user finds and deletes the stranded file under `state/backups/heartbeat-migration/` by hand.

## User Impact

After freeing space, the next `doctor --fix` migrates the heartbeat file as the warning promises. That includes users already stuck on an earlier release: an empty or partial archive of the same `HEARTBEAT.md` is replaced on the next run. Any other mismatching archive is still kept and reported as a collision.

## Why This Change Was Made

`archiveSource` in `src/commands/doctor-heartbeat-scratch-migration.ts` creates the archive with an exclusive `writeFile(..., { flag: "wx" })`. A failure other than `EEXIST` means either this call created the file or no file exists, so the change removes that path before rethrowing. Same shape as the merged #199426 (plugins pack) and #199447 (templates create).

Earlier releases already left such files behind, so upgrading alone would not unstick those users. The `EEXIST` branch now compares bytes. An archive equal to the source is accepted as before. One whose bytes are a strict prefix of the source (empty or cut short) can only be a failed write of this same file, because the archive name is the source's SHA-256; it is removed and the exclusive write retried. Anything else still throws `heartbeat migration archive collision` and is kept.

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

The archive code dates from #112967. When the content write fails after the exclusive create, the empty or partial file stays behind. On the next run the exclusive create fails with `EEXIST`, the partial bytes fail `hashCronScratchSource`, and migration throws `heartbeat migration archive collision`. Nothing ever removes the file.
</details>

## Evidence

Built `dist` for main `0aafe6691b8` and for this branch, then ran `node dist/entry.js doctor --fix --non-interactive` (Node 24.22.1, macOS) with isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_PROFILE`. `state/backups/heartbeat-migration` was a 2 MiB HFS+ disk image filled to 16 KiB free, so the 63 KiB `HEARTBEAT.md` archive could be created but not written: a real ENOSPC, not an injected one. Script: `hdiutil create` + `dd` + `truncate`, then three Doctor runs, freeing the space before the second.

- Main: run 1 `ENOSPC ... write. Rerun doctor to retry safely.` and a 0-byte `main-<sha>.md` stays behind. Runs 2 and 3, after freeing space, both fail with `heartbeat migration archive collision ... EEXIST`, exit 1, and `HEARTBEAT.md` is still present.
- This branch: run 1 shows the same ENOSPC warning and leaves no archive file. Run 2 prints `Migrated <tmp>/workspace/HEARTBEAT.md into cron`, exits 0, and writes a 63013-byte archive with mode 0600. Run 3 has no heartbeat warnings, exits 0.
- Control on main: with the disk completely full, the exclusive create itself fails (`ENOSPC ... open`), nothing is stranded, and the retry migrates. This branch keeps that behavior and the ordinary migration: mode 0600, archive name `main-<sha256>.md`.
- Regression `retries the migration after a failed archive write` in `doctor-heartbeat-source-archive.test.ts` writes 8 bytes and then throws ENOSPC. It fails on main (`expected [ 'Checklis' ] to deeply equal []`) and passes here.
- Regressions `repairs a partial archive left by an earlier release` and `keeps a different existing archive` seed the archive path with a prefix or with different bytes. The repair case fails without the `EEXIST` change (collision warning) and passes here. The different-bytes case keeps the file and reports the collision on both. `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-heartbeat-source-archive.test.ts src/commands/doctor-heartbeat-scratch-migration.test.ts`: 37 passed.
- Targeted oxlint (including the 700-line `max-lines` limit), format check, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test` and `git diff --check` pass. The ENOSPC reproduction above was rerun on head `74d0229b021` with the same result.

<details>
<summary>Main vs branch output (paths shortened)</summary>

```text
== [main-0aafe66] free space on archive volume: 16 KiB
run 1: <tmp>/workspace/HEARTBEAT.md was not migrated: ENOSPC: no space left on device, write. Rerun doctor to retry safely.  exit=1
       -rw------- 0 main-ebb31a2a…34e1.md
run 2 (after freeing space): HEARTBEAT.md was not migrated: heartbeat migration archive collision at <tmp>/state/backups/heartbeat-migration/main-ebb31a2a…34e1.md | EEXIST: file already exists … Rerun doctor to retry safely.  exit=1
run 3: same collision, exit=1, HEARTBEAT.md present: yes

== [fix-final] free space on archive volume: 16 KiB
run 1: <tmp>/workspace/HEARTBEAT.md was not migrated: ENOSPC: no space left on device, write. Rerun doctor to retry safely.  exit=1
       archive dir: (empty)
run 2 (after freeing space): Migrated <tmp>/workspace/HEARTBEAT.md into cron  exit=0
       -rw------- 63013 main-ebb31a2a…34e1.md   HEARTBEAT.md present: no
run 3: no heartbeat warnings, exit=0
```
</details>

Upgrade from latest stable v2026.11.6 (`npm install openclaw@2026.11.6`, `06afb10`) to this branch (head `74d0229b021`), same isolated state, two agents (`main`, `ops`) with their own workspaces, legacy `agents.defaults.heartbeat` plus unrelated settings (`gateway.port`, `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`). Script `upgrade.sh <clean|pending|stranded>`. Scratch is read from `cron_job_scratch` in `state/openclaw.sqlite` with `sqlite3 -readonly`.

1. **Data migrated by 2026.11.6 stays intact.** 2026.11.6 `doctor --fix` migrated `main`. Across three Doctor runs from this branch, two of them with the archive volume refilled:
   - the `main-071c…` archive (52 bytes, hash matches its name) is unchanged;
   - the `cron_job_scratch` row is unchanged (same row hash);
   - `gateway.port`, `thinkingDefault` and the agent list are unchanged;
   - no heartbeat warnings appear. A `HEARTBEAT.md` added after the migration is left alone, because 2026.11.6 already retired the legacy heartbeat config.
2. **A migration left pending on 2026.11.6 completes after a full disk.** 2026.11.6 `doctor` without `--fix` left both files pending. The first run from this branch, with 16 KiB free:
   - migrates `main`;
   - reports `ENOSPC ... write` for `ops` and leaves no `ops` archive.

   After freeing space, the next run migrates `ops`, writing a 63017-byte archive whose hash matches its name and a second scratch row. The `main` archive, the `main` scratch row and the settings are unchanged, and a rerun changes nothing.
3. **An archive already stranded by 2026.11.6 is repaired.** 2026.11.6 itself hit the full disk and left a 0-byte `ops-146e….md`.
   - On head `88043b82529`, before the repair commit, every run from this branch still reported `heartbeat migration archive collision` for `ops`.
   - On head `74d0229b021`, the first run after freeing space migrates `ops`: the archive becomes 63017 bytes and its hash matches its name, `ops` gets a scratch row, and the legacy heartbeat config is retired. The `main` archive, the `main` scratch row, `gateway.port`, `thinkingDefault` and the agent list are unchanged, and a rerun changes nothing.

Credit: @wangmiao0668000666 reported this and published a similar cleanup in the closed #200091. This PR is a smaller variant against current main, with a real full-disk reproduction.

Production delta +10/-2; test delta +39/-0.

Merge risk: two-way door. Reverting restores the stranded-file behavior with no state or config migration. Blast radius is the HEARTBEAT.md archive step of `doctor --fix` when its exclusive write fails or finds an existing archive that is a prefix of the source.

prs.title: fix(agents): terminate background CLI tasks on cron timeout
prs.body:
Closes #138499

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where cron jobs running automated agent turns that launch background CLI tasks via the `exec` tool leave orphaned processes running on the host when the cron job times out, causing the Gateway restart drain loop to block and eventually force-shutdown.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a cron job hits its execution deadline, `cleanupTimedOutAgentRun` triggers an abort with reason `"cron_timeout"`. We ensure this timeout reason propagates through `abortEmbeddedAgentRun` and `EmbeddedAgentQueueHandle.abort` to `prepareEmbeddedAttemptStream`, where the abort is classified as a timeout with `TimeoutError`.

Key design decisions:
1. **Timeout reason ordering & re-entrancy**: In `prepareEmbeddedAttemptStream`, `input.abortRun(true, createTimeoutAbortReason())` and `attempt.onDeferredLifecycleAbort?.(reason)` are invoked before `attempt.onAttemptAbort?.()`, preventing re-entrant generic cancellation callbacks from the lane controller from latching first and discarding the `TimeoutError`.
2. **Selective background process termination**: In `bash-tools.exec-run.ts`, backgrounded execution retains its abort signal listener until process settlement (`settlement.onSettled = detachAbortListener;`), allowing `isSignalTimeoutReason(signal?.reason)` to terminate background processes on `TimeoutError` while preserving them across ordinary turn cancellations and restarts.
3. **Task settlement & restart unblocking**: Process settlement triggers `finalizeBackgroundExecTask`, recording the task's terminal state and clearing the `background-exec` active work restart blocker in `gateway-active-work.ts`.

## User Impact

Scheduled cron jobs that launch background CLI commands will no longer leak orphaned processes when the cron job reaches its execution deadline, preventing host resource exhaustion and enabling graceful Gateway restarts.

## Evidence

### 1. Real Behavior Runtime Verification
Executed an end-to-end integration test against the real process supervisor, real exec tool, real process registry, and real gateway active work monitor (`verify-cron-timeout-real.ts`):

prs.title: fix(recovery): yield between store recovery iterations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #149935: On systems with many agent session stores (especially on slower storage volumes, SD cards, or external drives), `recoverRestartAbortedMainSessions` iterates sequentially over all store targets without yielding to the Node.js event loop. Each store recovery executes synchronous SQLite queries, filesystem operations, and transcript reads. While individual store checks are fast, across dozens or hundreds of agent stores (reported 63.6s with 237 agents), this synchronous I/O accumulates into a multi-second or multi-minute continuous event-loop block. During this time, the Gateway is completely unresponsive—HTTP requests hang, WebSocket pings fail, and health checks timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup session recovery consists of two distinct synchronous phases:

1. **Store Discovery Phase (`discoverRestartRecoveryStoreTargets`)**:
   As noted in [issue #149935 comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/149935#issuecomment-5696431792), discovery is a separate synchronous phase: it resolves session directories, validates agent database admission, and queries each store via `hasSessionEntriesByStatusReadOnly` (`main-session-restart-recovery-shared.ts:107`) to filter candidate store targets. In our production-path measurement across 20 stores, discovery executed in ~29.87 ms (~1.49 ms/store).
2. **Store Recovery Loop Phase (`recoverRestartAbortedMainSessions`)**:
   The recovery loop iterates through all discovered store targets and calls `recoverStore`, performing deep transcript inspection, state transitions, and session resumption. The accumulated synchronous I/O across stores in this loop represents the primary multi-second stall reported in #149935.

### The Fix: Yielding Strictly Between Store Recoveries
- **Strictly Between Stores**: The recovery loop now yields only when transitioning between stores (`if (i < targets.length - 1)`). This ensures no unnecessary trailing timer is scheduled after the final store, eliminating fake-timer deadlocks in single-store startup tests (`vi.useFakeTimers()`).
- **`setTimeout(resolve, 0)`**: Yielding via `setTimeout(..., 0)` turns the Node.js event loop through the timer phase, interleaving concurrent Gateway requests, WebSocket heartbeats, and health checks between store recoveries without altering recovery semantics, execution order, or store ownership checks.

`src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-yield.test.ts`:
- Spies on `recoverStore` across multiple stores.
- Enqueues an independent event-loop callback (`gateway-callback`) immediately when store A completes.
- Asserts that the callback executes strictly *between* `end:A` and `start:B` (`["start:A", "end:A", "gateway-callback", "start:B", "end:B"]`).
- **Negative Verification**: Temporarily commenting out the yield causes this test to fail with `AssertionError: expected -1 to be greater than 1` because `start:B` runs in the same tick as `end:A`, starving the callback until after `end:B`.
- **Backoff Test Verification**: Verified that single-store recovery under `vi.useFakeTimers()` in `main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts:4247` (`retains canonical retry backoff when startup recovery begins immediately`) passes without hanging because no yield is scheduled when `targets.length === 1`.

- **Zero Semantic Changes**: Recovery logic, error handling, session mutation, and ownership admission rules in `recoverStore` remain identical.
- **Zero Trailing Delay**: When only one store exists or after the last store is recovered, no extra timer is scheduled.
- **Lockfile & Changelog Integrity**: `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `CHANGELOG.md` are completely untouched.

prs.title: fix(config): reject unconfigured secret providers during strict validation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #147435.

When a configuration references a `SecretRef` targeting an unconfigured provider alias (for instance, `store:store:OPENAI_API_KEY` or an undeclared custom exec/file provider when `secrets.providers` is omitted or lacks that alias), `openclaw config validate` previously passed green. 

When the Gateway daemon subsequently started up, runtime resolution in `src/secrets/resolve.ts` threw `SECRET_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED` during required secret activation. Under service supervisors (`launchd` / `systemd`), this triggered an unbounded crash loop (in the reported incident, 18 failed boots in ~6 minutes) with zero pre-restart warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two gaps in `src/config/validation.ts` allowed unconfigured secret providers to slip past validation:
1. **Empty-Providers Guard**: Line 740 guarded provider checks with `Object.keys(mutatedConfig.secrets?.providers ?? {}).length > 0`. If `secrets.providers` was absent or empty (the common case for operators using shorthand refs without having declared a provider map), validation skipped provider inspection entirely.
2. **Missing Existence Check**: `collectSecretRefProviderSourceIssues` previously only called `resolveSecretRefProviderSourceMismatch(config, ref)`. By design, `resolveSecretRefProviderSourceMismatch` returns `null` when `!configuredSource` (i.e. when the provider does not exist), checking only whether an *already declared* provider's source matches the reference source.

This change:
- **Existence Check in Strict Validation**: Checks `const providerConfig = params.config.secrets?.providers?.[ref.provider];` and `if (!providerConfig && !isBuiltInDefaultSecretProviderRef(params.config, ref))` emits:
  `Secret provider "${ref.provider}" is not configured.`
- **Removes Empty-Providers Guard**: Runs `collectSecretRefProviderIssues` whenever `opts.semanticValidation === "strict"`, ensuring empty or omitted `secrets.providers` maps are strictly checked.
- **Preserves Built-in Default Providers**: Respects `isBuiltInDefaultSecretProviderRef(params.config, ref)` so that built-in `env:default:*` and `store:default:*` references (as well as aliases configured via `secrets.defaults`) remain valid without requiring redundant provider definitions.
- **Preserves Non-Strict Runtime Validation**: Keeps `semanticValidation === "runtime"` lenient so that inactive plugin surfaces remain unblocked during non-strict passes.
- **Strict Credential Opacity**: Strictly avoids interpolating `ref.id` into the validation message, preserving the secret token sanitization invariant.
- **Clean Export Boundary**: Internal validation issue collector resides in `src/config/validation-issues.ts` without creating unused exports on the public `validation.ts` surface, satisfying Knip deadcode checks.

## User Impact & Compatibility Semantics

- **Early Rejection Before Boot Crash Loops**: Operators running `openclaw config validate` or saving configuration mutations via the CLI/API will immediately see a clear, actionable diagnostic (`Secret provider "store" is not configured.`) before service restart.
- **Whole-Config Persistence Contract on Inactive Surfaces**: Because `writeConfigFile` enforces `semanticValidation: "strict"` to protect the Gateway from boot failure, candidate configurations containing undeclared secret provider references across any section (including disabled channels) are caught prior to persistence. This guarantees that saving a configuration never leaves the Gateway in an unbootable crash-loop state.
- **Remediation & Recovery Paths**:
  - `openclaw doctor` does not synthesize missing external secret provider credentials or undeclared provider aliases automatically.
  - Instead, operators remediate undeclared provider references through normal configuration tools:
    1. Declare the provider in `secrets.providers` via `openclaw config set secrets.providers.<alias> '{"source":"<source>"}' --strict-json` (or editing `openclaw.json`).
    2. Switch the reference to a built-in default provider alias (`store:default:*` or `env:default:*`).
    3. Remove the stale/unused reference.

## Evidence

- **Unit Tests**: Added comprehensive test cases in `src/config/validation.policy.test.ts`:
  - Strictly rejects unconfigured secret providers when `secrets.providers` is omitted.
  - Strictly rejects unconfigured secret providers when other providers are declared.
  - Allows built-in default provider refs for `env` and `store` without explicit provider declarations.
  - Verifies that secret ref IDs are strictly redacted and never leaked in validation issues.
- **Integration Tests**: Added real CLI integration test in `src/cli/config-cli.secrets.integration.test.ts`:
  - `rejects unconfigured provider refs during real config validate` verifying real `openclaw config validate` exits with code 1, prints the diagnostic, and redacts the secret ID.
- **Architecture & Linter Hygiene**: `collectSecretRefProviderIssues` is placed in `src/config/validation-issues.ts` with path deduplication via `seenPaths`, preserving `src/config/validation.ts` line-count limits and passing oxlint and knip deadcode scans with 0 errors / 0 warnings.
- **Test Suite Results**:
  - `src/config/validation.policy.test.ts`: 22/22 passed.
  - `src/cli/config-cli.secrets.integration.test.ts`: 22/22 passed.
  - Knip production and full-tree unused-export scans passed with 0 entries.

<details>
<summary>Real-World Verification Proof Run (14 Scenarios)</summary>

```
=== Starting Real-World Proof for Issue #147435 ===

--- Scenario 1: Exact Incident Repro ---
  [PASS] Strictly rejected unconfigured store provider: Secret provider "store" is not configured.
  [PASS] Verified secret ref ID was not leaked in issue output

--- Scenario 3: Arbitrary Sources (exec, file) ---

--- Scenario 4: Built-in Defaults Preservation ---

--- Scenario 5: Declared Providers vs Source Mismatches ---
  [PASS] Correctly configured provider store:{source: 'store'} passed strict validation
  [PASS] Source mismatch correctly detected: Secret provider "store" has source "file" but ref requests "store".

--- Scenario 6: End-to-End Real CLI Execution ---
```

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the browser troubleshooting page says locks naming another hostname stay unverified, but never explains how to recover when the lock is stale. Operators of headless Macs lose the managed browser or reset the profile and lose cookies.

The page now gives a safe recovery path: inspect the `SingletonLock` symlink, confirm the recorded PID is dead and no browser uses the profile, remove only `SingletonLock`/`SingletonSocket`/`SingletonCookie`, and restart. It also names the macOS hostname fix that prevents recurrence.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add a step-by-step section grounded in `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.ts`: the lock is a `<hostname>-<pid>` symlink, the error fires when that hostname differs from `os.hostname()`, and cleanup removes the three singleton files.
- State the safety boundary: do not remove a lock that names a live browser on another host sharing the profile.
- Point out that profile data is preserved.

prs.title: fix(approvals): record an approval route notice that could not be delivered
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

After native approval delivery, the route coordinator may send a notice to the chat the request came from. That notice is also the **manual fallback** when native delivery reached no one: "Approval required. I could not deliver the native approval request. Reply with: /approve …". If that send failed, the `catch` swallowed the error without a trace. Its comment assumed the approval delivery had already succeeded, which is not true for the fallback. The requester saw nothing, and operators had no record of why.

## Change

`src/infra/approval-native-route-coordinator.ts`: the notice stays best effort, but a failed send now logs a warning with the approval id, the channel and the error. The notice text is not logged. The comment is corrected.

## User impact

No change to what users receive. When the only `/approve` instructions cannot be delivered, operators now see why in the Gateway log, instead of a silent stall.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(gateway): recover completed waits after restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A caller can disconnect after a successful chat turn and miss the reply. Replacing the Gateway used to make `agent.wait` time out for the original run ID even when an identical retry did not execute the tool again.

## User Impact

An authorized caller can recover the successful result and its original timestamps after a restart when the Gateway opens a single saved session with one identifiable initiating input. Steering inputs do not own that result. Multiple saved sessions, incomplete or oversized history, and ambiguous input ownership fall back to the ordinary wait timeout. Live observations take precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway keeps at most one candidate from its startup session projection. After a live-cache miss, it checks the stored run ID and the initiating input's byte-exact idempotency key in a single bounded read. A later change of run ownership invalidates the candidate. The wait checks for a current reservation again when the read completes. A recovered result must pass the target session’s read policy. An unreadable draft follows the same wait path as a missing run. A positive wait deadline includes the recovery read, and a late read cannot replace a timeout. If a zero-timeout poll cannot read the saved result, it checks for a newly published live completion and otherwise returns timeout. The fix uses existing session data.

## Evidence

- The public wait handler and SQLite regression tests exercise a steering key that differs only in whitespace, a concurrent reservation in another session, and a reused ID hidden by a later run across restarts. The public RPC test checks an owner and a nonmember with the view role against the same draft. A separate timing test delays a successful recovery read beyond the caller’s deadline. The plugin test also covers a nonmember caller.
- In an isolated upgrade test, the caller disconnected after the turn started. The original run ID returned `ok` before retry and on six subsequent waits. An identical retry preserved the tool call ID and random output, with exactly one execution. A fresh request produced a second execution and a different output.
- The session list displays the fallback model when the client run ID has surrounding spaces. After reopening, only the initiating transcript’s exact ID recovers the terminal result. Adding or removing spaces returns timeout.
- The session identity ratchet passed with its existing baseline.
