prs.title: fix: let PostgreSQL Gateways start with plugin-backed secrets
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

A cold Gateway using PostgreSQL for shared state can fail while preparing valid plugin-backed secrets. Secrets preparation now reads plugin metadata through the worker. Web-provider discovery passes the installed-plugin records and migration readiness it read to the scoped loader. External channel contracts reuse the prepared manifest registry.

Related to #201058.

### Scope

Three small adjustments keep every secrets-preparation path on the worker-read facts:

- Plugin metadata is now also loaded when the only plugin-backed surface is a web tool (`tools.web` search or fetch config, via `hasRuntimeWebToolConfigSurface`), so web-tool-only configs get the prepared manifest registry instead of a later synchronous read.
- Plugin metadata is also loaded when only the `assignmentConfig` needs it, so a projected assignment config does not fall back to a synchronous read.
- The channel secret collector skips the `channels.defaults` key. It is shared channel defaults, not a channel id; without the skip, a config whose only channel key is `defaults` would look up a channel contract for it and fall into the synchronous config-wide manifest resolver.

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway that keeps shared state in PostgreSQL could fail to start from cold when its config uses plugin-backed secrets, for example a web search provider plugin with a SecretRef API key. Secrets preparation runs on the Gateway main thread, and plugin metadata, installed-plugin records and migration readiness were read synchronously there. PostgreSQL connections are only allowed from the database worker, so startup stopped with `PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker` before any credential was resolved. SQLite Gateways were not affected.

## Root Cause

The synchronous manifest resolver on the Gateway thread opened PostgreSQL while loading plugin metadata. The regression fixture reproduced the actual admission error, `PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker`, with both a fresh ledger and a committed migration receipt.

Switching only the metadata read leaves a second path through web-provider discovery and the synchronous loader. The loader checks migration readiness. Its asynchronous reader publishes a reusable readiness result only when the process has a committed migration receipt. A fresh ledger can therefore return an empty result from the worker and still cause a synchronous PostgreSQL read afterward. The loader now consumes that empty result explicitly. No cache policy or admission guard changes.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

The fixture opens a disposable PostgreSQL shared-state store, installs the Gateway process role, and verifies that the real guard refuses synchronous PostgreSQL connections on the test thread. It calls `prepareSecretsRuntimeSnapshot` and uses a local plugin that registers a web search provider. Success means the named provider was selected and the synthetic SecretRef was materialized.

```sh
# Set POSTGRES_TEST_PRELOAD to the file URL for
# scripts/test-database-conformance-preload.mjs with connection=<encoded test DSN>.
NODE_OPTIONS="--import=$POSTGRES_TEST_PRELOAD" pnpm test src/secrets/runtime-web-provider.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

- Before, PostgreSQL stopped at the admission guard in both cases. SQLite passed.
- After, PostgreSQL with no receipt, PostgreSQL with a receipt, and SQLite all passed (`Tests 3 passed (3)`). Local PostgreSQL was 16.16 with a dedicated database and non-superuser role. The test file ran in 8.89 seconds including test setup and transform on the final run.
- The new test is a `.postgres.test.ts` suite, so the hosted PostgreSQL conformance job runs it on this head.

### Verification

- Final local run passed 39 tests across the PostgreSQL regression, web tools, and core secrets snapshots. Channel-contract, plugin-origin, and plugin-loader sibling tests passed before the final web-tools simplification.
- Targeted formatting, type-aware lint and type checking, and `git diff --check` passed.
- [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201063/checks) provides the broad and fork-head checks. On the previous head, the hosted PostgreSQL conformance job ran `src/secrets/runtime-web-provider.postgres.test.ts` and all three cases passed.
- A follow-up test-only commit marks the three updated install-record and manifest mocks as intentionally isolated (`// mock-isolation:`) and drops their superseded entries from `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt`. This fixes the baseline-ratchets mock-exports check; no runtime code changed.
- Remaining CI red is inherited from `main`: `checks-node-changed-compact-large-3` fails only `src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts` "uses fresh revisions after agent create, update, and delete before reload applies" (`gateway request timeout for agents.delete`). Scheduled `main` [run 44401396829](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44401396829/job/135146008105) fails the same test with the same error in the same shard. Its fixture config has no SecretRefs, plugin entries, channels, or web tools, so secrets preparation takes the fast path and never reaches the code this PR changes.

## What was not tested

Full Gateway socket startup, live provider calls, and production startup latency were outside this focused run. The PostgreSQL baseline stopped before credential materialization, so there is no successful before/after latency comparison for the repaired path. The fixture disables bundled plugins, so the bundled web-provider path and the web-tool-only metadata trigger are covered by the existing unit suites, not by the PostgreSQL regression.

prs.title: improve: avoid scanning unrelated chats when refreshing session facts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refreshing chat rows and reading their transcript receipts can scan unrelated resident sessions before finding the requested chat. This creates avoidable work as the resident session set grows.

## User Impact

User impact: session facts are read with bounded work for the requested chat. Row contents, immutable shared fields, database isolation, and invalidation behavior are preserved; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The replica owner already maintains a session-key index for publications, including aliases, eviction and LRU order. Use that index for exact row reads and explicitly keyed transcript receipts, then apply the existing physical database and exact-key checks. Unkeyed receipt reads retain their existing behavior. This adds no cache or freshness owner.

The broader row investigation found that #201591 and #201758 already remove duplicate acquisition comparison and repeated deep freezing. A blanket revision-only refresh skip would miss independent runtime/plugin inputs, so this change stays at the evidenced replica lookup boundary.

## Evidence

Five alternating baseline/candidate pairs use 500 resident rows in 5,000 synthetic sessions, 128 warmup events, and 1,000 measured events: no-op refreshes, real metadata writes and transcript appends, reconciliation, and archive demotion/re-promotion. Timing and allocation run in separate processes. Allocation sampling includes objects collected by both minor and major GC.

| Median | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Replica lookup CPU, 10,000 reads | 101.93 ms | 37.87 ms | -62.8% |
| Replica lookup wall time | 102.22 ms | 38.28 ms | -62.5% |
| Replica lookup sampled allocation | 214.19 MB | 69.23 MB | -67.7% |
| Mixed-event main-thread CPU | 1,016.10 ms | 1,028.26 ms | +1.2% |
| Mixed-event sampled allocation | 409.38 MB | 409.86 MB | +0.1% |

A/A replica timing/allocation vary by less than 1%. Mixed-event CPU varies by 19.6%, wall time by 17.3%, and event p95 by 32%; the mixed-workload differences are within those controls. This establishes an isolated lookup improvement, not a whole-Gateway speedup.

All final 500-row digests match. Both arms return 2,540 hits in the lookup probe; visited candidates fall from 958,705 to 2,560. Reconciliation visits fall from 5,453 to 2. The event stream has 550 skipped materializations, 200 rebuilds and 50 creations; 200 transcript events avoid full materialization. All 500 injected no-op refreshes still read inputs but perform zero model-revision calls, freezes, plugin captures or replica scans. This synthetic mix is not a claim about a production event distribution.

The work-count regression fails with the original pool scan and passes with indexed lookup, including identical keys in two physical stores. Focused replica/transcript tests (44), projection/fingerprint tests (7), and affected browser/UI E2E tests (4) pass. Existing aliasing tests verify isolated mutable reader shells and frozen shared descendants. `pnpm check:changed` passed without skipped guards. Codex autoreview has no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Baseline: `f685aad5977d707e47ba402b3d072e482a6b091b`; candidate: `2f8a11998f635e87fc11a07f56c86fc3c070f2fd`. The benchmark overlays only the original replica module for baseline runs. This in-process owner fixture does not reproduce large-database filesystem costs or full Gateway throughput. Production delta is +7 lines for selecting the existing index at two call sites; no new retained state.

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): before_agent_finalize never runs for Claude CLI agents
prs.body:
Closes #198667

## What Problem This Solves

We hit this in daily use: our main agent runs on `claude-cli/*` and kept ending turns on promises like "I'll pick that up next" with nothing scheduled, so the work silently stopped until the user asked. On one day it happened twice in a single chat, and a transcript scan found the same pattern in 9 sessions. OpenClaw's answer for this is a `before_agent_finalize` plugin, but the Claude CLI runtime never runs that hook (it starts Claude Code with all hooks disabled), so such plugins are silently skipped for Claude CLI agents.

## User Impact

Finalize plugins now run when a Claude CLI turn is about to end, as on the embedded runner and Codex: `revise` gets one more model pass with the plugin's reason, while `continue`, `finalize`, or no registered hook let the turn end as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime registered only `UserPromptSubmit` and `PreToolUse` with Claude Code. It now also registers Claude Code's native `Stop` hook and relays it to `runAgentHarnessBeforeAgentFinalizeHook` (the path Codex's `Stop` relay uses), answering `revise` with `{ decision: "block", reason }`. Revisions are capped at three per turn, like the embedded runner, so a hook can't loop a turn. The relay is bound to the admitted turn's async scope (`AsyncLocalStorage.bind`, as #159000 does for native tool permission), so a warm transport reused across a plugin refresh runs the current turn's handlers. The relay lives in new `cli-runtime-hooks.ts` and `before-agent-finalize.ts` modules (with `carriesTurnContext` and `privateInputHolds` moved alongside it) to keep `cli.runtime.ts` and `execute-plugin.ts` under their line caps.

## Evidence

**Real use:** our production Gateway (2026.11.5 with this PR's change applied, Claude Code 2.1.322, a real chat channel) with a small local plugin that revises a draft ending on an unbacked promise of more work. Counts come from Claude Code's own session transcripts.

| Period | Real turns where Claude Code ran the `Stop` relay | Plugin asked to revise | Extra passes per revise |
|---|---|---|---|
| Day before, stock runtime | 0 (hooks disabled) | 0 (plugin can't run) | none |
| First ~2 h with the plugin on | 36, across 10 sessions | 3 | exactly 1, then the turn ended |

All three revisions were on replies whose follow-up was already scheduled; in the extra pass the agent rechecked its scheduled job and sent its reply again, as the plugin's reason asks. Condensed, redacted record of one (field names as Claude Code logs them):

```text
attachment hook_blocking_error  hookEvent=Stop hookName=Stop:Callback
  "promise-guard: your reply ends on a promise of more work ("I'll switch the build") …"
system stop_hook_summary  hookCount=1 hookErrors=[promise-guard: …]
assistant (stopHookActive pass)  tool: check scheduled follow-up → final reply sent
```

**Live, before and after:** throwaway Gateways on 2026.11.1 and on this branch, `claude-cli/claude-haiku-5-5`, with a probe plugin that revises a draft of exactly `FIRST` once to `SECOND`.

| Gateway | Prompt | Hook calls seen | Final answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026.11.1 | FIRST | `agent_end` only | `FIRST` |
| this PR | FIRST | finalize (draft `FIRST`, revised), finalize (draft `SECOND`, `stopHookActive: true`), `agent_end` | `SECOND` |
| this PR | OK (control) | finalize (draft `OK`, left alone), `agent_end` | `OK` |

Tested on `c519342c4c` (rebased on main `f96a979a0f3`; live rows for this PR rerun on it).

- Tests: new cases in `extensions/anthropic/cli-runtime.test.ts` (revise, continue, finalize, the cap, no hook) fail on main and pass here; `execute-plugin.finalize.test.ts` covers the host relay, including a warm transport holding an earlier plugin scope (fails without the bind).
- Checks: `pnpm check:changed` passes; focused tests and core + anthropic typechecks pass.
- Gap: real use covers one Claude Code version (2.1.322) and the 2026.11.5 port of this change; the callback reads only the documented `Stop` fields.

prs.title: fix: restore PostgreSQL model billing route warnings
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Model config edits on PostgreSQL Gateways now use the auth-profile worker to check whether an edit changes how a model is billed.

## What Problem This Solves

A successful model config edit could omit the warning about moving between subscription and metered credentials. PostgreSQL rejected the Gateway's attempt to read the auth profiles used to compare the routes.

## User Impact

Model config writes return the existing billing-route advisory when the selected billing route changes and the relevant credentials can be read.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing async read-only auth-profile loader in the shared comparator. The Gateway and Doctor await the same comparison. The comparison still shares one credential snapshot for each owner across the before and after values.

## Root Cause

`config.patch` calls the billing comparator after persistence. The comparator used `loadAuthProfileStoreForSecretsRuntime`. That call reached `readSelectedAgentAuthDatabase` synchronously, outside database admission on the Gateway thread. The write-flow catch logged `billing route comparison skipped` and returned an empty advisory list.

## Real behavior proof

Run an isolated Gateway with PostgreSQL for state, agents and Workboard, and a loopback mock model. Prime the agent with one turn. Run this pair eight times with an unused model reference:

```sh
openclaw config set agents.defaults.models '{"openai/fixture-unused":{}}' --strict-json --merge
openclaw config unset 'agents.defaults.models["openai/fixture-unused"]'
```

| Observation | Baseline | Fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Successful CLI writes | 16 | 16 |
| PostgreSQL worker-guard stacks | 16 | 0 |
| Logged skipped billing comparisons | 16 | 0 |
| Median RPC time after two warm-up writes | 1,432 ms | 1,472 ms |

The timing samples include normal reload work and varying host load. The PostgreSQL regression seeds synthetic metered and subscription credentials and asserts the warning. On main, it fails with `AUTH_PROFILE_STORE_UNREADABLE` at the sync read. With the fix, it returns the expected warning.

### Warning returned by the Gateway

In the isolated sweep build, seed two synthetic profiles using the auth-profile writer. Start with `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6@anthropic:metered` as the primary model. Read the current hash with `openclaw gateway call config.get --json`. Call `config.patch` with that `baseHash` and the following `raw` patch:

```json
{"agents":{"defaults":{"model":{"primary":"anthropic/claude-opus-4-6@anthropic:subscription"}}}}
```

The Gateway returned `ok: true` and two entries in `billingRouteWarnings`. The primary-model warning was:

> Billing route changed for agents.entries.main.model.primary (agent main): anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 via metered API-key profile anthropic:metered -> anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 via subscription/OAuth profile anthropic:subscription. Review its model and authentication settings.

The sweep included the local equivalent of the readiness cache fix. With that line removed, the same request hit the separate guard through `readPluginStateMigrationReadiness` during model runtime reload. With the line present, the request applied and returned the warnings with zero guard hits. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201976

## What was not tested

Production credentials, live providers, and actual billing charges. The billing warning was exercised on PostgreSQL 17.

## Verification

- Focused Vitest run passed 33 tests across the Gateway writer, Doctor migration, shared comparator, and PostgreSQL auth suite.
- The new PostgreSQL regression took 2.35 seconds locally. The full three-case PostgreSQL file took 8.91 seconds in its Vitest lane.
- Format, lint, core types, affected test type graphs, and `git diff --check` passed.
- A maintainer code review of the complete seven-file diff replaced the automated review.
- Exact-head CI passed all four PostgreSQL 17 shards and the PostgreSQL 16 Gateway cron smoke. The billing regression passed in 5.10 seconds on PostgreSQL 17. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44607458939/job/135856008949
- The required CI, dependency, and security status checks passed. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44611944843

## Evidence

The two sweeps exercised the same 16 config writes. The regression establishes the user-visible warning with persisted credentials. The fix reuses the existing worker-backed read and the before/after credential snapshot. It adds no new runtime owner or cache.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Logs, usage, Dashboards, settings, file, skills, project, people and Gateway directory searches miss results when the query is `Σ`/`σ` and the text has a word ending in capital `Σ` (or the query is `ς`). Sessions and Files search were fixed in #189131 and #189113.

Each matcher now passes the query and the candidate through the existing `foldSearchCase` helper, on top of its existing lowercasing and NFC normalization. No new helper, and sites that used `toLocaleLowerCase` keep it.

| Filter | main @ e08aa74ea | This PR |

| `Σ` | "No log entries yet" | line shown |

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two embedded-runner admission tests fail before exercising their lifecycle checks because #201333 removed the redundant workspace directory creation they used as a barrier.

The second reported main failure, an inactive-run diagnostic expectation left by #201790, is already repaired by #202049. Its unchanged steering-custody suite passes all 28 cases on this base.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The tests again verify that closing or replacing admission during preparation prevents both routing audit work and backend dispatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Hold the real transcript-target preparation result before dispatch checks admission. Workspace creation now belongs inside the backend path, after routing, so waiting there would lose the no-routing contract. All existing rejection, routing, backend, cleanup, and deadline assertions remain intact. No production hook, timeout increase, retry, or duplicate coverage is added.

Production delta: 0 lines. Test delta: +11 / -7 lines.

## Evidence

On base `f9553398b8e5de2d24d46ea53a899eda5dd1db17`, both preparation cases fail twice with `embedded run settled before attempt preparation`; the other 13 cases pass. The repaired full suite passes 15/15 twice through the repository E2E runner. Initial E2E build preparation also passed. Vitest duration was 93.51/37.48 seconds before (cold/warm) and 26.06/47.83 seconds after; these are correctness controls under shared-host load, not a performance claim. Exact-head CI ran all 15 cases under pinned Bun in 47.76 seconds (49.04 seconds for the test shard); both admission cases passed.

Codex autoreview of the local change against that base, including dispatch and transcript-preparation owner context, is scoped-clean through P2 with no actionable findings. `git diff --check` and focused formatting pass. `pnpm check:changed` passed, including the affected test typecheck, lint, boundary guards, and all dead-export scans. Exact-head [CI run 44617085124](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44617085124) passed: 17 successful jobs, 32 intentional skips, zero failures. prs.title: fix(plugins): Talk and plugin-loading requests fail with "must run in a worker" on PostgreSQL Gateways
prs.body:
Closes #201969
Related: #201063, #201876, #196174

## What Problem This Solves

When a Gateway keeps its shared state in PostgreSQL, Talk in the Control UI never gets past "Talk catalog is warming", and other requests that load plugins on demand fail with `Cannot open PostgreSQL connection: PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker`. Examples are `talk.config` and provider-auth preparation for automations at startup. This started with 2026.11.5. 2026.11.3 does not do it.

## User Impact

On PostgreSQL Gateways, Talk loads again, and requests that load plugins on demand reuse the plugin readiness that the Gateway's worker already read instead of failing. SQLite Gateways stop rereading that ledger on every synchronous plugin load. This change adds no config, schema, or permission changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plugin loading checks a small ledger of unfinished plugin data migrations. Gateway startup reads it in a worker, and synchronous loads later reuse that result. The reuse key was the migration receipt, which only a migration write creates. Since #197510 the receipt is looked up without creating one, so a normal Gateway run has none. The startup result was never kept, and every synchronous load read the ledger again on the main thread, which PostgreSQL refuses.

Until a migration write publishes a receipt, readiness is now keyed by the state database's current read admission. A migration write still publishes a new receipt and forces a fresh read. Closing or replacing the database retires the admission. The receipt lookup still does no filesystem work.

#201063 (secrets preparation) and #201876 (agent plugin tools) move their own callers to the async loader. This change fixes the shared cache that every synchronous caller depends on, including Talk's speech and realtime provider lookups and cron's provider-auth preparation. It does not address the separate synchronous installed-plugin index read on config hot reload (#196174).

## Evidence

**Real Gateway, disposable PostgreSQL 17.11 (Unix socket), macOS, isolated state, state/agent/workboard all on PostgreSQL.** For diagnosis only, the built guard printed a stack whenever it fired. That print is not part of this PR.

| Build | `talk.catalog` (2nd call) | `talk.config` | Main-thread guard hits |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026.11.3 `636454ee16a` | catalog returned | ok | 0 |
| main `b23642c2330` | `UNAVAILABLE: Talk catalog is warming` on every call, `talk.catalog refresh failed` logged | ok in this fixture | 4 (startup cron provider auth ×2, `listSpeechProviders` ×2) |
| this PR `73e2117` | catalog returned (`modes: realtime, stt-tts, transcription`) | ok | 0, still 0 after 4 more minutes of uptime |

All guard stacks on `main` go through `readPluginStateMigrationReadiness` → `loadOpenClawPluginsSteps` → `resolveRuntimePluginRegistry`. A diagnostic print in `selectReadiness` showed `receipt=true hit=true` on 2026.11.3 and `receipt=false hit=false` on `main`.

**Regression tests (red on `main`, green here):**
- `src/plugins/plugin-state-migration-readiness.postgres.test.ts` (new, runs in the forked database lane): Gateway process role on thread 0 with PostgreSQL state. An async readiness read is followed by a synchronous one. On `main` the synchronous read throws `Cannot open PostgreSQL connection: … must run in a worker`; with this change it returns the settled result. `node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection <disposable DSN> -- src/plugins/plugin-state-migration-readiness.postgres.test.ts`: 1 passed.
- `src/plugins/plugin-state-migration-readiness.test.ts`: the two "unpublished readiness" cases now expect one ledger read instead of one per load, with zero filesystem calls during receipt lookup as before. The close case still rereads after `closeOpenClawStateDatabaseByPathAsync`, and an ordinary state write no longer forces another read. On `main` these fail with 2 and 3 reads; 3 passed here.

**Checks:** `pnpm tsgo:prod` passed. `oxfmt --check` on the touched files and `git diff --check` are clean. `pnpm lint` reports no findings in the touched files. Its only errors are existing `max-lines` failures in 22 untouched files that are also on `main`.

**Gaps:**
- Production shows the same error for `sessions.create`, `chat.metadata` ("prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published"), cron script automations, and the reload restart preflight. They were not reproduced in the disposable fixture, so this PR does not claim them.
- `talk.config` failed in production but not in the fixture, whose plugin config is simpler. `talk.catalog` fails in both, in the same realtime/speech provider phases.
- Accepted edge case: an unpublished readiness result lives as long as the state database's read admission. Replacing the database file under a running Gateway without closing it is outside the Gateway database ownership contract.
- Production delta: +4 / −1 lines, 3 of them a comment. Test delta: one new 59-line PostgreSQL test, one lane registration line, and expectation updates in the existing suite.

prs.title: perf(state): isolate runtime schema inspection from migrations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Starting a state reader eagerly loads database migration and worker-environment schema code even when the database already has the current schema. This adds avoidable startup work to ordinary reads and Gateway startup.

## User Impact

User impact: ordinary state reads can validate the current database without loading the maintenance graph. The performance benefit is not yet qualified; this PR remains a draft until the comparison below passes. Database validation, repair refusals, and Doctor behavior are preserved. No schema version, configuration, pool limit, or migration policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing schema-inspection owner now contains the six runtime assertions and their read-only audit/approval predicates. Maintenance and runtime callers use that owner directly. The compatibility module no longer re-exports the runtime schema builder. The distinct audit and admitted-facts approval queries retain their original behavior.

This removes an eager ownership dependency without adding a cache, a module, or a second validation path. The formatted change is +6 production lines (456 added, 450 removed) and +4 test lines (30 added, 26 removed). Most changed files only move imports. The existing eager-import guard covers the migration, runtime-schema, and worker-environment schema owners.

## Evidence

Independent source review is complete; final local autoreview completed on the exact formatted candidate (base `d5f3e4d7b75a94fb9e78da1925bc3e88233f9bd8`, diff SHA-256 `9894f39e07d8852735a1854920736b95ad04a8c21236a2eee4a64618c704600c`, P0–P3, three complete passes, no findings). Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because the shared runner was not clean; the selected fallback is local autoreview followed by one hosted review when ready. Native focused proof completed with all 20 stages passing and no errors or signals. Node 24.22.1 and pinned Bun 1.4.4-canary.1 (`191755ec1`) each passed 56 focused tests across seven files, five selected audit/refusal tests, and the selected architecture-boundary case. Other cases in the filtered files were intentionally not run. Formatting, scoped core/test and script lint, the Kysely guard, the file-line cap, five relevant type lanes, and the full build passed. The build actually executed declaration emission, UI build, and export checks. All 67 final source pins match the tested candidate.

The baseline source-graph check showed all nine forbidden owners reachable, then restored the candidate before its proof. This is a forbidden-boundary reproduction, not a failing product test. The resulting state-reader entry is 466,712 bytes; marker absence alone does not establish the complete compiled boundary. The separately declared compiled A/B comparison is pending. Prior compiled Gateway observations motivated this work but do not establish this patch's benefit.

The full build emitted advisory UI budget violations: largest JS gzip 564.3 > 563.7 KiB; largest CSS gzip 57.2 > 56.9 KiB; total CSS gzip 331.2 > 329.4 KiB; total CSS raw 1707.5 > 1699.4 KiB; chat boot JS requests 21 > 20; chat boot JS gzip 1303.1 > 1301.4 KiB; new boot JS gzip 803.4 > 803.0 KiB. They are not reported as budget passes or attributed to this change without a baseline comparison.

Proof JSONL SHA-256: `23768054272d3ad378e0108b088a2d1a43507a176e2676932ae6c531cdf6b2d5`. Compiled performance, exact-head hosted review, and GitHub CI remain pending.

### Performance rule declared before measurement

A is the frozen baseline `d5f3e4d7b75a94fb9e78da1925bc3e88233f9bd8`; B is signed candidate `6e70c2e1afaf1880c5ff519b52aa87a8716ebb28` (tree `0193842c559521fea65254ee97b036cb2fcf393d`). Both complete source trees are built in separate temporary fixture worktrees in one owned native invocation. Each arm uses the canonical frozen installer, independent arm-local workspace links, the same dependency inputs, Node 24.22.1, package-manager version, environment policy, and build command. Source, dependencies, runtime, and generated outputs are sealed before and after measurements. Exact commits, trees, build identities, commands, hashes, host capacity/load, and the declaration body hash accompany the results.

Use the two existing committed workloads, with no product-source loader, allocation profiler, or CPU profiler enabled:

- State-reader owner: `node --expose-gc scripts/perf/state-read-boot-bench.ts --build-root ARM --iterations 1000`. Six cold/handoff reads and 1,000 warm reads are separate phases. The fixture contains 10,000 unrelated machine-state rows and 40 plugin descriptors. Fixture creation and imports precede the measured phases; existing main-isolate GC before each phase remains unchanged. This is a synthetic owner workload, not a Gateway or concurrent-load result.
- Gateway: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-gateway-startup.ts --case pluginMetadataMaintenance --entry ARM/dist/entry.js --runs 1 --warmup 0 --timeout-ms 120000 --json`. The controller uses TSX; the product child and workers use the selected compiled build. This existing fixture enables plugins and disables the UI. It exercises real health/readiness/session RPCs and the plugin-metadata maintenance phase, without model turns or an injected concurrency workload.

For each workload, run five serial matched pairs in order **AB, BA, AB, BA, AB**: five fresh children per arm, ten children per workload, twenty total. The two workloads are analyzed separately. The existing compile-cache policy is preserved: ambient cache overrides are cleared, each Gateway child receives a fresh native temporary parent, and the owner benchmark retains its existing fresh scratch directory. Filesystem page cache is uncontrolled and the interleaving is disclosed. Do not pool the 1,000 warm operations or the six cold operations as independent samples.

For every scalar below, report all five child values per arm, midpoint median, nearest-rank p95 across the five children (the maximum), min/max spread, and all five matched absolute/percentage deltas. Acceptance cells are the arm median and p95, not a post-hoc selection among individual pairs. Zero denominators remain explicit rather than becoming fabricated percentages.

- Owner acceptance metrics, separately for cold and warm: elapsed time, process CPU, main-thread CPU, and end RSS. Also gate the four ordered cold-command times, whole-child maximum RSS, and physical worker starts by script and total. The whole-child maximum includes setup; it is not the measured-phase maximum.
- Gateway acceptance metrics: trace elapsed time at maintenance-phase completion (not the phase body duration), first output, HTTP listen, ready-log, health, readiness, first session RPC and shutdown times; reported process-tree CPU; sampled leader peak RSS; and ready/post-ready RSS when those trace points exist. Missing optional trace points remain missing.
- Diagnostics, reported with every adverse movement but not reclassified as acceptance gates after results: owner pre-phase RSS; before/after main-isolate heap-used, heap-total, external and array-buffer bytes; Gateway ready/post-ready main heap-used and external memory; all other emitted startup timing/count fields and host load. CPU/core ratio is descriptive, not a lower-is-always-better metric. Current-isolate heap counters do not establish whole-process memory ownership.

**Pass rule:** the nine forbidden owners must be absent from the candidate state-reader source closure, and the compiled relative-import closure and retained top-level imports/initializers must confirm the intended boundary; absence of source labels or marker strings alone is insufficient. Physical worker starts must not increase. Both primary memory outcomes—cold-owner end RSS and Gateway sampled peak RSS—must improve in median and p95. Every named acceptance timing, CPU, process-memory, and worker-count cell must hold or improve. Any adverse acceptance cell is disclosed and leaves the PR on HOLD unless the owner explicitly accepts it in the PR; any increase of 20% or more in a named acceptance cell is a stop. All adverse diagnostics and raw pair deltas are also disclosed. A missing required sample, timeout, source/dependency drift, failed correctness oracle, or uncertain child cleanup is incomplete proof, never a passing sample.

The owner workload must reach its result oracles and exit 0 after cleanup. The Gateway must report successful health/readiness/session RPCs, raw `startup.maintenance.plugin-registry` outcome `success`, and clean teardown (`shutdownForced=false`, `exitCode=0`, `signal=null`, `exitedBeforeTeardown=false`). A registry-refresh claim additionally requires `registrySource=derived`. Native child ownership must be released. Gateway RSS is sampled leader RSS through teardown; process-tree CPU has the existing `ps` resolution and exited-descendant limitations. Neither is a unique-memory sum. No load, leak, or universal small-device claim follows from these two fixtures.

Results, unfavorable cells, and remaining limits will be added here before readiness or landing. This comparison does not accept or supersede the separate HOLD on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201959.

## Measured status: HOLD — incomplete comparison

The declared run stopped after all ten owner children and the first Gateway A child. All eleven workload commands exited 0 with no signal; the controller exited 1 because the Gateway success oracle could not be satisfied. The frozen startup-trace producer emits `outcome` only for plugin-service spans, not `startup.maintenance.plugin-registry`. Its ordinary maintenance completion line is emitted from `finally`, so neither that line nor the absence of a warning proves success. The required success evidence is missing. No Gateway A/B result or overall performance pass is claimed.

The owner batch independently contains adverse acceptance cells, including increases above the declared 20% stop. This PR remains a draft on HOLD. The trace-contract defect does not waive those observations, and no fresh acceptance run is being substituted for this batch. These are observed failures of the declared acceptance rule, not yet an attribution of a persistent product regression.

Original premeasurement declaration: body SHA-256 `3dbee25aec3860ae10ead12dccd826285b4fead40fd115483cab6bf45c55f8d4`. Complete failed-run archive: 1,516,093 bytes, 36 regular members, SHA-256 `252afbcd822e273f088eb961772c7c6e4d9bc4bbd062b089bcd7643fddcfb0c5`; report SHA-256 `40b577922933619a5eea79ba804fe0afb5353837c27f3cd1ae12f151a737e535`. It contains both full builds, source/compiled closure reports and captured compiled files, all ten owner JSON results, and the first Gateway raw result/log. Source A/B and declaration are unchanged. The original report has `complete=false`, `cleanupUnknown=true`, and no final seals because the oracle stopped the controller. A separate read-only postseal completed with exit 0: both arms’ complete physical source, dependency, and generated-build seals match their premeasurement values. The original failed report is preserved. The native execution owner released its claim; all eleven workload children exited cleanly, including the Gateway managed-group teardown. The later scoped process scan found no fixture matches; same-user process metadata permission denials limit that scan, so it is not a global no-holder claim.

Each row below uses five independent children per arm, in declared pair order AB, BA, AB, BA, AB. Both arms completed full builds with declaration emission. The state-reader entry shrank from 749,197 to 466,712 bytes. ### Follow-up compiled candidate census: diagnostic, with plugin failure

**This census is not a healthy-Gateway footprint or an acceptance comparison.** The existing startup timeline records `memory-core` with `loadFailedCount=1` and no plugin preparation worker. The earlier single-A Gateway startup had `loadFailedCount=0`. That difference invalidates interpreting the census's lower worker count as a saving. The detailed cause was absent from the bounded ordinary output; the benchmark's normal cleanup removed its default file log. A separate one-child diagnostic reproduced the failure with the existing file logger enabled: `SpawnBrokerError: Spawn broker failed before readiness: exited with code=0 signal=none`. Gateway startup also reported this broker failure and an in-process-spawn fallback, but `memory-core` still failed to load. No uninstrumented broker regression was established; the diagnostic IPC-reference mechanism was then reproduced separately below.

The instrumented census used the same compiled B source and prepared fixture. It completed the real readiness/first-RPC path, observed a matching successful plugin-registry maintenance timeline span, and exited with code 0, no signal or forced shutdown. Native execution and cleanup completed, and complete source/dependency/build seals matched before and after. The timeline's successful maintenance task does not establish a healthy plugin load or prove the derived-registry branch ran.

|---|---:|---:|

The final pool census identified two separate transcript pools, two shared-state readers, and single credential, logger, discovery and cron-reader pools. No catalog or plugin-preparation worker was present in this failed-plugin run. Heap limits are capacity, not allocation; worker heaps are not summed into process RSS. The measurements motivate inspecting actual emitted dependencies and the plugin failure, not changing heap caps speculatively.

Census archive SHA-256: `8812d187feccff3b1fba44e3b6191ef72490cc3d8923cae29bac9ad1323e72cc`; report SHA-256: `0f273e11c36766660621207ab03bcb6243048c029fa3052ca6a3399371d1e571`. Source remains `6e70c2e1afaf1880c5ff519b52aa87a8716ebb28`. The declared comparison remains **HOLD**; this diagnostic changes no acceptance gate.

The failure-only diagnostic completed with exit 0, no signal or forced shutdown, matching source/dependency/build seals, no retained adapter files, and native ownership released. Its completion means the diagnostic and cleanup succeeded; the plugin failure remained. No further Gateway retry was used. Failure archive SHA-256: `097d6dc487934f0789f36f11a42ca2f5899bafaf741a0823a3adccc9e5c34dd6`; report SHA-256: `75f9bcaa6d45a6ef4910bcd165fa9a17d27bcb3ac8a8bbc2ab4b8985ee9a1986`.

**Instrumentation contamination:** the private census preload was injected through inherited `NODE_OPTIONS`. Its `isMainThread && process.send` guard also admitted IPC child processes, including the spawn broker, and it called `process.channel.unref()`. In the pinned Node 24.22.1 implementation, this explicit unref overrides subsequent listener-driven reference counting until an explicit ref. The real broker inherits its parent's environment.

A bounded Node-only probe used three sequential IPC children, with no OpenClaw imports. Each installed its listener and sent an installation marker; the parent waited 100 ms before sending a request if the child was still alive:

| IPC child | Installed marker | Request sent / reply received | Exit | Forced cleanup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ordinary message listener | yes | yes / yes | 0, no signal | no |
| Census-style listener plus explicit unref, then real listener | yes | no / no | 0, no signal | no |
| Same shape followed by explicit ref (dependency control only) | yes | yes / yes | 0, no signal | no |

This establishes that the diagnostic can cause an IPC child to exit before its request. The broker failure and missing plugin-preparation worker therefore cannot be attributed to this schema patch from these instrumented runs. No repaired census, new Gateway run, or replacement acceptance batch was used. The original census and failed comparison remain recorded, with their limitations and **HOLD** unchanged. Synthetic probe recipe SHA-256: `24f201e1a86d2d096172437f0e421f468b10b7837fa99335ed35d57699bdd146`; native terminal exit 0, three children, all joined without forced cleanup.

prs.title: improve(ios): align app icon composition with Apple's design guidelines
prs.body:
Closes #187629
Related: #101411, #138002.

## What Problem This Solves

The iOS app icon’s mascot nearly fills the canvas, leaving little surrounding space instead of following Apple’s guidance to emphasize centered primary content with a simple background.

## User Impact

The iOS icon gains a more balanced composition while preserving its existing mascot, colors, and backgrounds. macOS, Debug icons, separate Watch app assets, and app behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apple’s [Human Interface Guidelines for app icons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/app-icons) recommend keeping primary content centered and using the production-template grids to guide placement. Apple also states:

> “you don’t need to fill the entire icon canvas with content.”

This reduces the iOS foreground to a centered 0.86 scale while retaining full-bleed backgrounds and leaving masking to the system. The chosen proportion is a design interpretation of Apple’s guidance, not an Apple-mandated percentage or a universal circular clipping boundary.

The unchanged macOS Original icon provides a supporting source-level sizing reference. A representative comparison with other iOS icons provides additional visual context; it is not the primary justification for this change.

The existing generator now produces release PNGs from a static, app-specific SVG rather than the animated browser favicon. Default remains opaque white, Dark retains transparency, and Tinted remains system-generated.

## Evidence

### iOS before and after

Actual baseline and regenerated PNG assets, shown with a presentation-only rounded mask. All annotations are in English. These are asset previews, **not native Home Screen screenshots**.

![iOS app icon before and after, with light and dark small-size previews](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/569b65bb-d646-4eab-8ae5-a307d1fe2316?raw=1)

### Supporting comparison with other iOS icons

Equal-size tiles using artwork returned by Apple’s US App Store lookup API for Shortcuts (915249334), WhatsApp (310633997), Signal (874139669), Telegram (686449807), Slack (618783545), and GitHub (1477376905). This representative asset comparison does not establish every app’s native appearance or system effects.

![Before and after alongside six other iOS app icons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23dccfd1-4ea8-4e31-ab9e-89ef0c0385b6?raw=1)

prs.body:
Related: none found. I searched open and merged PRs and issues for "forwarded" and "senderIdentity" transcript metadata.

## What Problem This Solves

When a channel user turn is stored, OpenClaw records who sent it: `__openclaw.senderId` plus an observation `senderIdentity` (`pluginId` and the platform's user id). When the message is a forward, for example a Telegram message carrying `forward_origin`, the text is someone else's words. The transcript gave no sign of that, so anything reading transcripts or `chat.history`, such as a memory importer, would attribute the forwarded text to the person who forwarded it. The prompt already tells the model about forwards (the "Forwarded message context" block). The stored turn did not.

## User Impact

A reader of `chat.history` or session archives can now tell "Alice wrote this" apart from "Alice forwarded this". For example, a memory system that files first-person claims ("I moved to Austin") under the sender can skip forwarded text instead of assigning someone else's claim to the forwarder. Nothing changes for users who don't read transcripts.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `buildChannelUserTurnSender` sets `forwarded: true` on the turn's sender input when the inbound context has `ForwardedFrom`, the same signal `inbound-meta.ts` uses for the prompt's forwarded block. Telegram fills it from `forward_origin`.
- `buildPersistedUserTurnMetadata` writes `__openclaw.forwarded: true` under the same condition that already gates `senderIdentity`: a displayed turn with no provenance or `external_user` provenance. Inter-session, relayed and hidden turns never carry it.
- The sender fields are unchanged. They still name the person who posted the message in this chat, which is the only identity the platform verifies.
- The change is additive. It adds no new store or schema, and existing readers ignore the key.

## Evidence

### Real gateway: a Telegram forward, stored and read back through `chat.history`, across an upgrade from the latest stable

Setup: `openclaw gateway run --bind loopback` with the Telegram channel's `apiRoot` pointed at a local fake Bot API (a small HTTP server that answers `getMe`, `getUpdates`, `sendMessage` and the other startup calls, and hands out Telegram-shaped updates I queue), plus a local mock model provider. No real Telegram and no paid model. The forward goes through the real Telegram plugin, so `forward_origin` → `ForwardedFrom` is the shipped mapping. Ids below are placeholders.

1. **Latest stable first.** `openclaw@2026.11.6` from npm (`06afb10`) on an empty state dir. Two group updates arrived through `getUpdates`: a plain message from `<sender>`, and a message from `<sender>` with `forward_origin: { type: "user", sender_user: { id: <origin> } }`. Both were stored with `senderId: "<sender>"` and an observation `senderIdentity`; neither has a forward marker (the baseline).
2. **Upgrade in place.** Stopped it and started this PR's head (`57c11c2`) on the same state dir and config. It logged:
   ```
   [state/upgrade] Upgrading state to 2026.11.5: state/openclaw.sqlite v36, agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite v38
   [state/upgrade] State upgraded to 2026.11.5 by migration chain; previous files kept as *.pre-2026.11.5-57c11c2d5c5f-<timestamp>.
   ```
   `/readyz` returned 200 and Telegram polling resumed. (main's version string is still 2026.11.5 while npm `latest` is 2026.11.6, so this moved state written by 2026.11.6 onto a build labelled 2026.11.5; the migration chain accepted it.)
3. **New turns on the PR build.** One forwarded update from `<sender>` and one plain update from `<other>`.
4. **Read back.** `openclaw gateway call chat.history --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:telegram:group:<group>","limit":30}'` returned all 8 messages (4 user turns, 4 mock replies). The user turns:

   | Turn | Stored by | `senderId` | `senderIdentity` | `forwarded` |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | plain message before upgrade | 2026.11.6 | `<sender>` | observation, telegram | absent |
   | forwarded before upgrade | 2026.11.6 | `<sender>` | observation, telegram | absent |
   | forwarded after upgrade | PR head | `<sender>` | observation, telegram | `true` |
   | plain message after upgrade | PR head | `<other>` | observation, telegram | absent |

   The forwarded turn, trimmed:
   ```json
   {
     "role": "user",
     "content": "forwarded after upgrade",
     "__openclaw": {
       "senderIsOwner": false,
       "senderId": "<sender>",
       "senderName": "Sender",
       "senderIdentity": { "type": "observation", "id": "<sender>", "pluginId": "telegram", "accountId": "default", "senderKind": "human" },
       "forwarded": true,
       "transport": { "channel": "telegram", "conversationRef": "<conv>", "messageId": "<msg>", "accountId": "default" }
     }
   }
   ```

Turns stored before the upgrade load unchanged and are not backfilled. The only error line in the gateway log is the sandbox's systemd exec-isolation notice ("requires Delegate=yes …"), which is unrelated.

### Tests and guards

- New tests in `src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.persistence.test.ts`, run on a real SQLite transcript target:
  - "marks a platform-forwarded channel message without changing who sent it": **fails on main** (`d5f3e4d7b75`) and passes with this change.
  - "leaves the forward marker off ordinary and non-external channel messages" covers a plain message and an `inter_session` turn that carries `ForwardedFrom`.
- Nearby files: `user-turn-transcript.persistence.test.ts` and `user-turn-transcript.test.ts`, 63/63 passing.
- Guards on the final head: every `lint:tmp:*` script, `check:test-lines-ratchet`, `check:database-worker-ratchet`, `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `check:assertion-safety`, `check:test-timeout-race-ratchet`, `lint:kysely`, `check:temp-path-guardrails`, `check:database-first-legacy-stores`, `tsgo:core`, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files, and `git diff --check`. All exit 0.

### Gaps

- The Bot API was a local fake, so no message crossed Telegram's network. Everything from `getUpdates` onward was the real gateway and plugin.
- A forward with a hidden origin (`forward_origin.type: "hidden_user"`) wasn't sent through the gateway; it's covered by the existing `inbound-context.ts` mapping only.

### Accepted edge cases

- Channels that don't report forwards never get the marker. Its absence means "not reported as a forward", not "verified original".
- A forward whose `forward_origin` is hidden still counts as a forward, because `ForwardedFrom` is set from the hidden sender name.
- Before-message hooks can add the key. That can only make a reader more cautious, so unlike `senderIdentity` it isn't protected against hook edits.

prs.title: fix(agent): block direct openclaw cli state mutation in exec and prioritize messaging tools in code mode
prs.body:
Related: #187354

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Embedded agent runs in Code Mode (`tools.codeMode: 'auto'`) inside the Gateway container spawn the full `openclaw` CLI inside shell `exec` to manage cron and automations, triggering child process bootstrapping (~500MB+ RAM), SQLite database lease lock contention, container OOM kill (exit code 137), and an unverified completion message sent to end users upon restart recovery.

## User Impact

User impact: Prevents container OOM crashes and false-positive completion confirmations when users ask agents to schedule reminders or manage automations via chat/messaging channels. Models are steered immediately to use fast in-process async tool globals rather than launching the CLI binary as a subprocess, while remote node and sandbox CLI workflows remain preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

In response to ClawSweeper architectural review feedback:
1. **Preserves CLI execution outside Gateway context:** Scopes the CLI footgun guard to Gateway execution (`host === "gateway"` or default). Legitimate CLI execution against external nodes (`host: 'node'`) or sandboxes (`host: 'sandbox'`) continues without restriction.
2. **Root-option-aware command parsing:** Reuses OpenClaw's `getRootOptionAwareCommandPath` to parse subcommands after global flags (e.g. `openclaw --no-color cron --help` and `openclaw --profile dev automations create`).
3. **Accurate tool remediation arguments:** Fixed remediation text to reference the actual `message: ...` parameter expected by `message({ action: 'send', target: ..., message: ... })`.
4. **Prioritizes messaging-critical tools in Code Mode:** Ensures `automations`, `cron`, and `message` are retained at priority 0 in `formatCodeModeCatalogIndex`.

## Evidence

- Unit tests in `src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.test.ts` verifying:
  - Gateway rejection of `openclaw cron --help` and root-option variants (`--no-color`, `--profile`).
  - Correct remediation message formatting with `message: ...`.
  - Preserved execution on `host: 'node'` and `host: 'sandbox'`.
- Unit tests in `src/agents/code-mode.test.ts` verifying catalog prioritization for `automations`, `cron`, and `message`.
- Grounded in production reproduction in OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (`openclaw-gateway` Docker image) documented in #187354:
  `Killed\n\n(Command exited with code 137)` following `await exec({ command: "openclaw cron --help" })`.

prs.title: feat: let plugins finalize streamed speech without provider-specific code
prs.body:
Closes #187368

## What Problem This Solves

Voice-integration plugins need to upload audio during capture, then end input and obtain a complete transcript without implementing each speech provider's WebSocket protocol.

## User Impact

Plugins can use optional `api.runtime.mediaUnderstanding.transcribeAudioStream` through the existing typed plugin runtime, with ElevenLabs Scribe v2 Realtime as the first adapter. Existing continuous sessions keep synchronous `sendAudio` and their close/VAD behavior. Older hosts without the optional runtime method retain batch behavior.

Streaming requires an explicitly selected supported model and format. Omitted models, CLI selections, and unsupported batch-only profile/request/header/prompt/provider options return unsupported **before input is consumed**. Once admitted, failure throws instead of automatically replaying audio or changing provider. This does not make every existing batch provider realtime-capable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing session exposes callbacks and close, but no end-of-input acknowledgment covering every accepted sample. Add awaited finite writes/finalization, and let the runtime reuse media selection, policy, credentials, secret admission, and configured limits. The finite helper owns bounded completion/cancellation; ElevenLabs owns framing and acknowledged manual commits.

The consumer no longer imports a private-local SDK facade: the new operation is declared on the already-published `OpenClawPluginApi.runtime.mediaUnderstanding` type and lazily bound by the host. The private-local transcription/provider helpers remain private and official-provider-only. No new public subpath, package export, or blanket promotion of private SDK internals is introduced. Registered-plugin projection preserves optional absence and applies the existing selected plugin scope/revocation guard.

**SDK-owner decision requested before merge:** accept this optional extension of the existing typed runtime capability. This PR proposes that direction; neither the linked issue nor source review is represented as upstream owner approval.

## Evidence

### Branch refresh — 2026-11-16

Current head: `e1f81d130eaa93d960a237ffc0d1d1a4dbeb0f6f`, incorporating upstream main `ec025eba2df15ab949239fa17dfd99ac4286b50c` to resolve merge conflicts. The finite-input contract and no-replay-after-admission behavior remain unchanged.

The refresh follows upstream's split provider-context types and `PluginCapabilityCatalogHostContext`, preserves lazy saved-key lookup on both continuous and finite connections, and carries the upstream caller-authority callback through finite completion. Existing tests now cover direct/saved credentials and revoked caller authority before final commit. Upstream proxy, reconnect, backpressure and continuous-session behavior remain intact. No new retry loop, dependency or public SDK subpath was added.

Source review found no actionable defect; exact-file formatting and diff whitespace checks passed. The current test-line budget passed: +1468 test LF, 400-line allowance, 1068 allocation credit (reduced from the old record). The added growth protects progressive input, acknowledged completion, cancellation and live ownership at separate boundaries; no unrelated test allowance changed.

Fresh executable validation is **pending**, not passing. The local lint attempt could not initialize because this checkout lacks `eslint-plugin-solid`; this is an incomplete-tooling result, not a code verdict. No local full dependency installation, test/typecheck run, paid provider call, deployment or restart occurred. [Current-head GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43930692011) is `action_required`, waiting for upstream approval to run. Please approve the run; no test pass is claimed. Current test wall time and CI seconds are not yet available.

SDK-owner acceptance of the optional runtime contract remains required before merge. All proof below belongs to the explicitly named earlier revisions; it does not establish a pass for this refreshed head.

<details>
<summary>Historical evidence and review context — prior heads only</summary>

### Branch refresh — 2026-11-03

Refreshed PR head: `9cb1098365adeeff8f21e97bbc75d73f9e77430c`, integrating upstream main `a4727b5506f371ae656fbee82fa93a3f29d91157`.

The only textual conflict was adjacent import additions in `src/realtime-transcription/websocket-session.ts`. The resolution retains both `createNodeProxyAgent` from merged proxy fix #187369 and the finite-runtime `getPluginRuntimeGatewayRequestScope` import. Main's environment-proxy routing and provider-shutdown queued-audio cleanup (#191761), and this PR's finite lifecycle and final-effect ownership checks, are preserved. The feature diff remains 28 files, +2347/-38 against the incorporated main.

Executable validation for this refreshed head is owned by [GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41663533787). The run completed **failure**: all 108 scheduled jobs finished, with **76 passed, 28 skipped and 4 failed**. The failures are the three component jobs described below plus their dependent aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`; there were no additional component failures. Production and test types, architecture/source contracts and documentation checks have passed. No local dependency installation, build or test execution was used for this refresh. SDK-owner acceptance of the optional runtime contract remains requested before merge. Nothing has been merged upstream, installed or restarted.

### Current-head built-Gateway proof — passed on GitHub

[Job 126014134718](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41663533787/job/126014134718) passed the existing `finite-transcription.e2e.test.ts` through a built Gateway process, loaded consumer plugin, injected typed runtime, bundled ElevenLabs adapter and synthetic WebSocket origin. The emitted `FINITE_STT_GATEWAY_PROOF` records complete input of 288000 bytes, acknowledged commits at 256000/288000, the complete combined transcript, and cancellation after 32000 bytes with zero commits. There were two connections and zero unexpected HTTP requests. This is current-head process-boundary evidence, not a live ElevenLabs account, published-package or microphone claim.

### Current-head CI outcome and remaining blockers

- [Control UI E2E](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41663533787/job/126014131210): the Brave/Firecrawl settings-edit mock-request timeouts match [scheduled-main job 125978618719](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41653621604/job/125978618719), including the same test/stack locations and empty request log. The affected UI test, controls, suite support and mock Gateway helper are byte-identical across that baseline, incorporated main and this PR.
- [Core lint stripe 4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41663533787/job/126015859338): `ui/src/pages/about/view.test.tsx:143:32`, `typescript(no-misused-spread)` on the navigator spread. This file is byte-identical to incorporated main (blob `affa75cf344c6dc3989243a7934fb6411fbc68f4`); the older scheduled baseline has a different lint failure, so a matching baseline execution is **not** claimed.
- [Test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41663533787/job/126014132071): global total 6437667 exceeds effective ceiling 6437534 by 133. The exact CI merge/base comparison adds this PR's 1442 test lines and exactly 1442 allocation credit, leaving the same 133-line base-tree deficit. The [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41663533787/job/126026091513) failed because those three dependency groups failed. These findings do not represent passing CI or permission to waive its gate. No unrelated UI repair or CI rerun was performed. The older proof below remains explicitly prior-head evidence.

### Prior-head process and lifecycle evidence

The proof sections below were executed on `79b395a14b0a03bf31c66a88e950a7c13af83232` or the explicitly named earlier heads.

### Stronger process-boundary proof — executed on this head

The new `test/e2e/qa-lab/media/finite-transcription.e2e.test.ts` replaces the duplicate mocked happy-path test with a real Gateway process. [Exact-head build and execution job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40886048121/job/123490837973) **passed**:

2. The Gateway loads a temporary consumer plugin and the bundled ElevenLabs adapter. 3. Producer gates hold source input after the first 32000-byte upload reaches the actual WebSocket origin. The test then releases the remaining input and requires 288000 bytes, commits at 256000/288000 bytes and the complete combined transcript.
4. A second RPC request is canceled through the loaded plugin while input is stalled. It must close the actual socket with only 32000 bytes, zero commits and no batch replay.

This extends executed proof beyond in-process registration/provider composition to CLI bootstrap, plugin discovery/loading, authenticated Gateway RPC and the built runtime. The job ran `pnpm build qaRuntime` with `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1` successfully (13:56:06–13:59:03 UTC), then executed the E2E with `OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1`. The test passed in 48.581 seconds (85.06 seconds for the file), with shard exit 0. Those durations include test/Gateway work and are **not transcription-latency benchmarks**.

Actual `FINITE_STT_GATEWAY_PROOF` emitted by that execution:

```json
{"entry":"Gateway RPC -> loaded consumer -> typed host runtime -> bundled ElevenLabs -> WebSocket","complete":{"bytes":288000,"commits":[256000,288000],"result":{"result":{"supported":true,"text":"First segment. Final starlight.","no_speech":false,"mode":"realtime","provider":"elevenlabs","model":"scribe_v2_realtime"},"inputEnded":true,"gatewayPid":5508}},"cancellation":{"bytes":32000,"commits":[]},"connections":2,"unexpectedHttp":0}
```

The Gateway PID in the result was asserted different from the test process. This still uses a **synthetic protocol origin**, not live ElevenLabs recognition, a published npm artifact or physical satellite. No such broader claim is made.

Fresh independent source review of the proof found no actionable P0/P1/P2 after fixing the shared audio-selection config and using the existing prepared media-Gateway owner, claimed listener and joined cleanup. Formatting, commit hooks, line caps, strict extension import boundaries and whitespace checks passed locally. No new workflow, QA-lab source changes, public SDK exports, dependency installation or full local build/test rerun were added.

### Executed lifecycle and transport proof on `351cad743` (unchanged production code)

- The existing private request scope binds the real registered consumer's authority assertion and instance disposal signal before awaits. Final socket construction/send, finite frame/commit, resumed acknowledgment and completion recheck that owner. No new public authority parameter, lifecycle manager or polling loop. Bare record revocation fences the next continuation/effect; actual disposal also cancels stalled runtime waits.
- **Red baseline:** tests/helper-only `9da755ec7b9c64d7edcb38b61b3fa389082d034b`, unchanged production `60b79011`, failed all six real-owner revocation cases with "promise resolved instead of rejecting"—not setup failures. [Core final connect/send](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40869483776/job/123433196562), [registered consumer/runtime/ElevenLabs/socket](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40869483776/job/123433196535).

prs.title: improve: use less CPU when classifying session workspaces
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Building session-list workspace permissions repeatedly expanded sandbox tool groups and compiled policy globs for every row, even though the row only needed to know whether its workspace was sandboxed.

## User Impact

Session workspace classification does substantially less CPU and allocation work. Workspace permissions and tool enforcement remain unchanged; no configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sandbox owner now exposes a boolean-only owned-row classification. One shared predicate keeps it identical to full status, whose result construction and policy resolution stay unchanged. This removes the unused work instead of retaining another policy cache. Production code grows by 12 lines for the shared predicate signature; there is no cache or lifecycle machinery.

## Evidence

The regression fails on the parent with 20 policy reads for 20 rows and passes with zero. A deterministic differential test checks 400 classifications across randomized groups, globs, allow/deny/alsoAllow lists, agent overrides, session requirements, and config replacement mid-stream. All 35 focused tests pass, including physical legacy ownership and sandbox enforcement. Final focused rerun: 35 tests, 129.45 s wrapper wall including cold compilation; the new regression and differential cases take 18 ms and 13 ms respectively.

The existing committed owner benchmark now supports `--workspace` and measured-region CPU profiles. It uses 10,000 synthetic sessions across four agents, 40 plugin entries, and 160 tool patterns, with 25,000 measured calls per sample. Five counterbalanced pairs per metric, plus A/A controls; all output digests match.

| Owner workload | CPU µs/call, median (p95 sample) | Sampled bytes/call, median (p95 sample) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Minimal container config | 18.986 (20.084) → 1.513 (1.678) | 53,821 (53,862) → 1,909 (1,956) |
| Configured container | 18.929 (19.199) → 0.791 (1.011) | 53,405 (53,408) → 1,735 (1,798) |

Acceptance: unchanged classification digests, zero unused policy preparations, lower owner CPU/allocation. A/A CPU drift was 0.58–1.68%; allocation drift 0.02–0.13%. Profiles confirm the policy-expansion stack disappears. p95 is across sample means, not per-call latency. No database or workspace tree is read by this owner, and no whole-Gateway latency claim is made.

Reproduce with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/sandbox-status-measure.ts --workspace --iterations 25000 --output <file>`; use `--owner-dir` for captured parent owners and separate `--allocations` / `--cpu` passes. Baseline: `f685aad5977d7`.

`pnpm check:changed` passed; the final extraction also has focused type/lint verification. Independent Codex autoreview: complete local diff against `f685aad5977d7`, committed unchanged as `d0efe08582bf7`, P0–P2, scoped-clean with no accepted/actionable findings. No Control UI import of the changed owner.

Full-status sibling control (five counterbalanced pairs, 25,000 calls/sample): median CPU 19.676→19.287 µs and 19.202→18.754 µs; sampled allocation 55,062→55,026 B and 54,616→54,633 B (differences below 0.1%). Full output digests match. No extra status object remains.

prs.title: fix: play workspace audio links in the chat side panel
prs.body:
Related: #162552

## What Problem This Solves

Clicking a workspace MP3 link in a chat opens a side panel that offers only Download, even though the same recording can play when sent as an audio attachment.

## User Impact

Play supported audio directly in the side panel. Download remains available, and unrecognized binary files keep their existing fallback. No plug-in or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route files identified as audio by the Gateway to the existing player, rather than treating every non-PDF binary as download-only. Request the media URL through the same authorized session-file callback used by Download; do not construct a URL from the workspace path.

## Evidence

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Workspace MP3 offers Download only](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f23fb4b4-513c-4167-9240-1b7244293cb7) | ![Workspace MP3 with playback controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6fcee66f-3d85-443c-a206-3dfe4da6329f) |
| ![Download-only state highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/556d220f-affa-4449-a668-a00291043d94) | ![Play and seek controls highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b9d190d-9d01-49d4-8a7a-168a6e8e28b3) |

Desktop Chromium reproduced the download-only panel on the original base. The existing browser scenarios cover workspace MP3 playback and the neighboring PDF preview and download.

### Playback grant renewal

The sidebar requests a fresh grant through `sessions.files.download` before the five-minute grant expires. Buffered playback continues on the existing stream. A seek outside the buffer switches to the fresh URL and restores the requested position and playback state. A transient renewal error leaves the player mounted while it retries. Each renewal asks for the current file at the selected workspace path.

The new panel regression failed against the previous PR implementation: the grant callback had been called once when the second call was due. It passes with renewal enabled, including a retryable failure and a terminal response. The media-owner regression also failed before the fix: an unbuffered seek retained the old ticket. Both regressions pass in the updated branch.

**Isolated gateway evidence.** Using an 11-minute synthetic MP3 and desktop Chromium, clicking the workspace link opened the player and Play advanced the native audio clock. After five minutes of wall-clock time, the original grant returned HTTP 404 and a fresh grant returned HTTP 206. The browser had buffered through 382.089 s. Seeking to 606.34 s used a fresh grant and the native playhead continued advancing. Download produced the original filename and all 5,280,748 bytes matched the input.

```text
duration: 660 s
original grant after expiry: 404
renewed grant, range bytes=1024-1031: 206
buffer before seek: 0-382.089 s
seeked: 606.34 s, readyState 4
range request: bytes=4816896-
response: 206, bytes 4816896-5280747/5280748
download: sample.mp3, 5280748 bytes, byte-for-byte match
```

Validation covered 61 focused UI tests, 18 gateway download tests, both MP3/PDF browser scenarios, UI and chat-test type checks, formatting, and focused lint. Browser coverage was Chromium on macOS.
