prs.title: fix(ios): nest child sessions and fold subagent runs in the sidebar
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The iPhone sidebar listed far more chats than the Control UI sidebar. Every child session was flattened into a peer row, and subagent runs — which have no transcript of their own — got a row each. One conversation with two runs and a follow-up chat took five rows in the drawer.

Runs spawned from Home were the worst case: Home is not a session row in the drawer, so those runs had no parent to nest under and appeared as extra top-level chats.

Archived chats were already hidden (the Gateway list is queried with `archived: false`, and the shared model filters archives), so they are not part of this fix.

## User Impact

- The drawer lists the same top-level chats as the Control UI. Child chats sit under their parent behind a chevron with a child count, collapsed until opened, and open automatically when one of them is the current chat.
- Subagent runs no longer appear as chats. The row that replaces them still says what they were doing: a spinner while one runs, a clock and "Waiting for a concurrency slot" while one is queued, a warning triangle and the error line when one failed, and an unread dot. Any conversation a run started appears in its place. This holds whether the parent lists the run as a child or only the run names its parent.
- Runs started from Home show on the Home row whether they are running, failed (with the error line), or unread.
- Pinning and groups still own placement: a chat you pinned or moved into a group stays in that section rather than following its parent into another one.
- The 20-row recent cap now counts top-level chats, so one busy parent cannot push the rest of the list away.

No configuration, migration, or data change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two owners disagreed with the drawer. `RootSidebar.sessionNodes(for:)` flattened each section's session tree into peer rows, and the iOS path never folded subagent runs. The shared `sections()` owner also builds one tree per placement bucket (pinned, each group, recent), so a run whose parent sits in another bucket — a pinned parent, a grouped parent — had no parent row in its own section and became a root.

The shared model now folds runs after placement instead of assuming parent and child share a section:

```diff
 ChatSessionSidebarModel.foldingSubagentRuns(sections)
-  runs become rows when their parent is in another section
+  run nested in a conversation's tree -> folds there (its badges are already counted)
+  run at the top of its section       -> owningConversationKey, badges added once
+  run's own conversations -> rows in its place
 ChatSessionSidebarModel.foldedRuns(in:under:)   # Home
+  same owningConversationKey walk, so backref-only runs reach Home too
 RootSidebar
-  flattened(section.nodes).prefix(20)      # every descendant as a peer row
+  sessionTreeRows(roots.prefix(20), childExpansion)
+  childToggle                              # chevron + child count
+  sessionSubtitle: failed child > own status > queued child > work line
+  Home row: failed-run triangle and error line
```

`owningConversationKey` prefers the roster's own child link (`childSessions`), falls back to the run's `spawnedBy`/`parentSessionKey`, and walks through intermediate runs that have no row, stopping at the first ordinary conversation. Section folding and Home both use it, so a run lands on one surviving row. A run whose ancestor has no row at all (an archived parent, a filtered search) hands its conversations over as rows instead of vanishing with it.

The rules come from the Control UI session tree (`ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-tree.ts`), not new ones: runs are never rows, their persistent children take their place, and the owner keeps their badges and attention. `Node.previewSessions` and the run classifier moved to the shared model so the macOS sidebar and iOS use one copy; macOS behaviour is unchanged.

### Review follow-up (revision 3)

ClawSweeper's revision-2 review found four places where folding dropped a run's status along with its row. All four are fixed in `34d59f2`:

- **Badges counted by section membership.** A run linked to its parent only by `spawnedBy` stays a separate root in the section tree, so the parent never counted it, yet folding skipped its badges whenever the parent sat in the same section. Folding now treats a run as counted only when it is nested in the owner's tree; top-level runs add their badges once.
- **Home ignored backrefs.** Home collected runs through forward `childSessions` links only, which the Gateway freshness-filters. Home now uses the same ownership walk as folding, still stopping at an ordinary child conversation.
- **Home hid failed runs.** The Home row now shows the warning triangle and "Child session … failed: …" line for an unread failed run.
- **Queued runs looked idle.** A queued run's parent now shows a clock and "Waiting for a concurrency slot" in place of the work line.

The two overlapping fold tests ClawSweeper flagged are merged into one, keeping the all-run empty-section assertion.

## Evidence

Synthetic demo data only: the app's screenshot/demo transport with a temporary fork-only fixture flag (not part of this PR). GitHub-hosted macOS runners.

**Review follow-up** ([fork screenshot run](https://github.com/jorge-monalee/openclaw/actions/runs/40895184173)). The fixture adds three runs that name their owner only through `spawnedBy`: "Morning digest" (failed, unread, started from Home), "Hotel booking" (queued, under the idle "Trip planning"), and "Itinerary summary" (finished, unread, under "Trip planning").

| Prior PR head (`ad293c2`) | This head (`34d59f2`) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Prior head: Home shows only a spinner with no sign of the failed Morning digest run; Trip planning looks idle with no subtitle, no queued icon and no unread dot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d758f887-dd94-4e07-9aab-d6ba595411ab) | ![This head: Home shows a warning triangle and "Child session Morning digest failed: Digest timed out"; Trip planning shows a clock, "Waiting for a concurrency slot" and an unread dot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d5d48d0-2d1a-4934-80d0-e5ec27c12a6a) |

Before, Home keeps only its running run's spinner and "Trip planning" looks idle. After, Home names the failed run and its error, and "Trip planning" shows its queued run and its unread finished run. "Release plan" is unchanged. Captured on the `xcode-27` image (iPhone simulator, iOS 27) because `macos-26` arm64 runners were unavailable; both columns come from the same run.

**Original change** (revision 1, iPhone 17 Pro simulator on `macos-26` / Xcode 26.6, earlier fixture: "Release plan" with a running run, a failed unread run and one child chat; "Trip planning"; an archived "Q3 plan" with an orphaned run; a run started from Home):

| Before (`main` at `dadf912`) | After, default | After, expanded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Before: Inbox triage, Release plan, Collect release notes, Competitor research and Changelog draft are separate rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d72dd15-cc54-4ed6-9e55-eea949bdf352) | ![After: Release plan carries the spinner, failed warning, unread dot and a collapsed child count; Home shows its run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f19c80eb-6330-48cd-9c70-2d8c46f3580d) | ![After expanding: Changelog draft nested under Release plan](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9a7b50e1-c367-4831-8b93-b423ce28bd01) |

Tests:

- **Red on the prior head, green on this head** (shared package): the new tests run against `ad293c2`'s sources fail exactly where the review said: with only a `spawnedBy` link, the parent's badges are `failedCount 0, hasUnread false` instead of `1, true`; and Home's runs are `[home-run, nested-run]` without `backref-run`. The forward-linked case passes on both heads, so the fix does not double count. With the fix, `swift test --filter 'ChatSessionSidebar|ChatCommandPalette'` passes 310 tests in 24 suites ([run](https://github.com/jorge-monalee/openclaw/actions/runs/40885246537); that run's head differs from `34d59f2` only by `///` → `//` on one nested-function comment).
- **iOS**: `RootTabsPresentationTests`, `RootSidebarTypographyTests`, `OpenClawTypographyTests` pass on this head (85 tests, including the new `drawer row says its folded run is waiting for a slot`), plus the sidebar UI test that produces the screenshots ([run](https://github.com/jorge-monalee/openclaw/actions/runs/40895184173)).
- **Original change** ([run](https://github.com/jorge-monalee/openclaw/actions/runs/40807125391)): `drawer folds subagent runs into their parent session` fails on `main` and passes on the PR.
- SwiftFormat and SwiftLint (iOS and macOS scopes) clean and `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passes on this head ([run](https://github.com/jorge-monalee/openclaw/actions/runs/40885839927)); `git diff --check` passes.

Not covered: a physical iPhone.

Prepared by Jorge's AI assistant on his behalf.

prs.title: fix: keep channel replies authorized through long-running attempts
prs.body:
Related: #145506

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes channel replies losing delivery authority while a fallback candidate is still running beyond its original attempt timeout.

## User Impact

Long-running replies can still prepare delivery until their candidate finishes or is cancelled. Cancellation revokes authority immediately, even while the model promise is still settling. Scheduled automation keeps its existing admission owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Channel capabilities used a timeout-derived expiry although retries and approval waits can outlive one attempt. Use the existing run-owned lifetime and revoke it on the candidate's abort signal and in its existing finally block.

```diff
- expire authority at the attempt-derived deadline
+ retain authority while the candidate is active
+ revoke on cancellation, and always on settlement
```

This addresses one reproducible route to “plugin delivery capability is no longer active”; it does not claim to resolve every session-key or registry-replacement cause in the related reports. No timeout increase, new owner, or migration.

## Current real-model evidence — 7 November

[The exact-head compiled Gateway/channel flow now passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6713019903): 1/1, exit 0, on a7b13235d820. The existing dist/entry.js image ran the actual native model and registered qa-channel HTTP ingress/outbound path; one nonce reply reached the correct account/room. The exact inbound transport completion receipt confirmed deferred delivery/preview settlement before the 250 ms no-extra-message check and clean exit. Setup took 12.173 s and the real-model settled flow 8.077 s. No credential copy, build, install, source patch or extended deadline.

This closes the previously missing real-agent/model isolated compiled-Gateway registered-channel integration boundary. It does not turn the archived Telegram public:fallback or its CI result green, add a 41-minute real wait, or claim published-package installation/live Telegram proof. Existing simulated-clock/cancellation regressions keep their stated scope. The remaining inherited queue-context/CI disposition is separate; no empty push, manual CI retry or unqualified merge approval is inferred. Earlier dated statements that real-model proof was absent describe their then-current evidence, not this latest result.

## Evidence

### QA2 reproduced on the candidate and its exact CI main base — 7 November

The retained QA2 artifact 13046107768 from [run 41210635478/job124564973204](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41210635478/job/124564973204) was downloaded and inspected, not inferred from its job name. The historical synthetic merge 7c97777d is no longer served; no replacement is claimed to be that exact object.

Two separate private qaRuntime builds completed through the repository owner: candidate a7b13235d820b7a3b738543df5af180003077bd4 in 93.3s; actual historical CI main base 2d7376d2e6e111ae28bdf7d9e888cbb077139204 in 116s. Each build-info commit matched its checkout. Dependency declarations/lock/workspace files matched; dependencies were copied COW into an isolated baseline, not installed or reconciled. The first baseline setup missed workspace-local dependency links and stopped before runtime proof; those existing links were copied from the same declared dependency snapshot, then the qualified build succeeded. No source/config/timeout was changed to clear setup.

Both ran ONLY the original subagent-completion-direct-fallback scenario with mock-openai, crabline Telegram loopback, concurrency 1, fastMode:false and the unchanged 60s assertion. Both failed at public:fallback with the same event sequence and outcome: visible/silent controls delivered their exact markers; fallback child execution terminal/ok; fallback delivery suspended/permanent_failure; no expected fallback marker; loopback sendMessage aborted. The scenario and mock-provider source hashes match across both trees.

This establishes that the failed behavior already occurs on the CI main base without this PR delta. It is not evidence that the branch introduced the QA2 failure, and is not a passing QA verdict or proof that no other branch-specific defect can coexist. The A/B comparison alone did not identify the abort owner. [The subsequent first-abort observation and upstream source check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6711153646) narrowed it to the current consuming async-work scope in the shared Telegram queue, not the prepared reader’s captured requestSignal. Merged PR #189457 already restores the submitted caller context before admission and dispatch; duplicate #194701 is superseded. That separate fix is not present merely because this candidate’s original QA2 artifacts exist, and this PR’s acceptance remains incomplete. No timeout, assertion, revocation check or retry protection was weakened.

The log wording about potentially sent chunks is classification, not proof of an identified delivered chunk. Existing ambiguous/post-dispatch retry protection is retained. The isolated observation and producer source work are now recorded in the linked follow-up. Reuse the merged queue-boundary correction; do not weaken the ended-scope guard, extend deadlines, or claim that these source findings pass the original scenario.

Private qaRuntime is not a public package/release build, a live Telegram test, real-model acceptance or full PR qualification. Both isolated Gateway probes completed and exited; no operator Gateway, installed package, updater attempt or workflow retry was touched. No new source commit/empty push is justified by these A/B results alone. Candidate/CI-base reports, diagnostics, raw local Gateway logs and a hashed comparison are preserved for the remaining cause investigation.


- On base `32f9477bf46d`, the two regression cases fail: authority expires after 41 simulated minutes with a 30-minute attempt timeout, and cancellation leaves authority valid until model settlement.
- With this change, all 6 execution-authority cases and 10 adjacent runner-utils cases pass: `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-message-authority.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Focused typecheck, lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Independent read-only review found no blocking issue.
- A separate isolated backport probe against the published 2026.10.8 package uses its actual channel minting and plugin delivery preparation: the baseline refuses after 41 minutes; the candidate succeeds. Wrong session/run, explicit revocation and registry replacement still reject. Zero external deliveries.
- Scope of proof: source tests use the real execute/mint/resolve path with the model and fallback selection mocked; elapsed time is simulated. No live provider retry, real approval wait or external channel delivery was exercised. Broad integration remains for CI.

Reversible code-only change; affected scope is channel reply delivery authority.

## Current source-boundary proof — 29 October

[Qualified local final-transport evidence and repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6493700861) on head `d2c24b2642cd941ce3b4cb4c99141b64e40856c0`: three cases pass through production authority/delivery owners and actual loopback HTTP, including independent cancellation, normal settlement and candidate replacement while a started send is held before physical I/O. The existing final adapter-handoff hook now rechecks reply authority. Production core types, focused fixture types, canonical core/extension lint, formatting and native ratchet pass. The new fixture/source contains synthetic data only; raw private diagnostics remain withheld. No actual unresolved user decision prevented these local tests. This is explicit **source integration with model/fallback selection controlled by the fixture and a simulated clock jump**, not a shipped-package CLI, real-model/approval wait or live Telegram/Test Server claim. The original stronger shipped-flow request remains for fresh review to assess; no automated approval or merge acceptance is inferred.

## CI fixture repair — 29 October

Previous fixture-repair head: `8eb48f11b00270abf5635155f2a02c8b81071a4e` (fixture repair `be7378539e81` plus inventory-position-only conflict avoidance; all tested source/test blobs and lane membership unchanged). [CI diagnosis, repair and passing local checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6494309715): move the host authority integration test out of Telegram extension-private ownership; consume the existing public test facade and route through the existing host-SQLite fork inventory. All three original observable-behavior cases and assertions are preserved. The normal wrapper now passes 3/3 without a pool override; the unchanged extension boundary suite passes 11/11, with core-import guard, focused types/lint/format and native budget checks passing. No production behavior or boundary guard changes. The previous entry and proof remain pinned to `d2c24b2642cd`; the fixture path at that revision was `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-reply-authority.telegram-http.test.ts`. New-head hosted CI is separate and not claimed green. The accepted loopback final-effect coverage remains source integration with a controlled model and simulated clock: **the required real-agent/model isolated-Gateway channel proof remains missing**. No new review request or live proof is claimed.

## Sparse type-graph repair — 29 October

Previously published head: `992fc2ee9ee6d57ec33234cdaa98cfae7fe9f178`. [Fresh CI diagnosis and proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6494615934): the root integration owner is now `test/reply-authority.telegram-http.integration.test.ts`, still on the existing SQLite fork lane. The sparse core messaging graph drops from 264 Telegram source files to zero and the complete core tsgo boundary guard passes without any guard/config exception. The relocated three-case integration, focused root types/lint/format and native budget pass. Test bodies/assertions and production source are unchanged. Prior evidence retains its source identities. New-head hosted CI remains separate. The previous macOS job additionally invoked a tooling test absent from its PR checkout; that workflow/source-version mismatch is documented, not claimed repaired or attributed to queue capacity. **Real-agent/model isolated-Gateway proof remains outstanding**; this fresh result is still controlled-model/loopback/simulated-clock evidence.

## Current Darwin workflow/source integration — 31 October

Current published head: `a7b13235d820b7a3b738543df5af180003077bd4`, normal merge of pinned main `ef60dd054202b29fc88da7b460f0594266faf2ff`. [Qualification and limitations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186851#issuecomment-6544754752): the required `test/scripts/pr-git-invocation.test.ts` is now present; the entire seven-file PR patch has the same stable patch-ID before and after integration. Checkout-local frozen/prefer-offline dependencies were reconciled with lifecycle scripts disabled. **13 distinct targeted tests passed**, with 12 Windows-only tooling skips on macOS. Core and focused integration types/lint, seven-file format, whitespace and the core tsgo boundary guard pass. Native ratchet against prepared main: **6,342,969 / 6,368,719**; no author budget increase. The initial default comparison against the old parent rejected inherited main allocation credit; that failure and the supported prepared-base qualification are disclosed in the evidence. GitHub confirms MERGEABLE; exact-new-head CI remains separate. **Real-agent/model Gateway proof remains outstanding**: the HTTP regression still uses controlled model/fallback selection and a simulated clock. No production installation, restart, broad core build, new grant or live-model/channel run.

## Exact-head QA failure — 31 October

At `a7b13235d820b7a3b738543df5af180003077bd4`, [QA Smoke CI profile 2/6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41210635478/job/124564973204) fails `subagent-completion-direct-fallback` at `[public:fallback]` after 60 seconds. The artifact records child execution `ok`, but delivery `suspended/permanent_failure`. Gateway logs show Telegram `sendMessage` aborting at 14:36:41.843Z, followed by an `OutboundDeliveryError` and the incomplete-send duplicate-prevention guard. Visible and silent control cases delivered.

This is the same observed failure sequence as the independently captured PR173026 run, not proof of a common root cause or an inherited-main classification. The announcement delivery owners, Telegram production sources and scenario are byte-identical to pinned main `ef60dd054202b29fc88da7b460f0594266faf2ff`; attribution still requires production-boundary reproduction. The CI gate also reports failure. No rerun or green-only push was requested.

The existing isolated reproduction attempt for this failure sequence stopped before Gateway startup at the runtime-artifact-publication guard; its checkout has no prepared `dist/entry.js`. That setup failure is not product proof, and no guard was bypassed. The source-pinned QA runtime must be qualified before identifying the abort owner and selecting a regression/fix. Previously passing focused tests are unchanged evidence, not a fix for this QA failure. **Exact-head CI and real-agent/model acceptance remain incomplete.**

## What Problem This Solves

A failed upgrade-survivor run can lose the failed update step when the updater reports `status: ok` and its output exceeds the diagnostic limit. Both recent Docker failures retained only the beginning of that report and a generic acceptance error.

## User Impact

CI diagnostics can retain the failed step and its redacted error context. This does not change update behavior or acceptance, and does not fix the underlying update failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing failed-step prelude for both recognized update statuses before applying the unchanged 16 KiB output limit. Keep the existing redactor, advisory filtering, and original output order.

## Evidence

- Observed failure: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44608567145/job/135859616413 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44608567145/artifacts/14574031886.
- Adds one `status: ok` case to the existing diagnostic-publication matrix; existing error, timeout, output-limit, redaction, ordering, and size assertions remain.
- Native Node 24.22.1 proof: the new status-ok case failed on the original reporter at the missing failed-step assertion (1 failed, 40 skipped); the candidate passed all 41 migration-diagnostics cases.
- Scoped root-scripts typecheck, typed lint, and formatting passed.
- Fresh local ClawSweeper review of `366814443535..9d881ff8a6f2` found no actionable correctness or security issues; its read-only runtime gap is covered by the native proof above.
- No Docker rerun was performed. The underlying updater failure remains unresolved.

prs.title: feat: let clients load agent rosters without portraits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large inline portraits can dominate `agents.list` responses and delay mobile clients that need the agent roster before opening a conversation.

## User Impact

Clients can request a fresh authorized roster without downloading portraits by sending `includeAvatars: false`. Existing clients keep the same response when they omit the option or pass `true`.

This is opt-in: clients must request the lightweight roster. It does not change portrait caching policy, authorization, or the default avatar representation, and it has not been deployed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing roster projection now skips avatar resolution and omits `identity.avatar` and `identity.avatarUrl` on explicit opt-out. Names, emoji, theme, routing and model metadata remain intact. This removes image work from roster bootstrap without introducing a server cache or a second roster endpoint.

The schema, generated validator, and protocol documentation are updated. Older gateways can reject the new parameter; clients may retry the legacy request only for that parameter-validation error.

## Evidence

- Five new regression cases exercise the real RPC handler, validator, authorization, and roster projection for local, inline-data and remote portraits, plus Control UI HTTP avatar representations. They fail against the base with `INVALID_REQUEST` and pass with this change.
- Lightweight requests make zero avatar-resolver calls, omit both image fields, and preserve the rest of the authorized roster. Legacy and explicit-true responses match. A synthetic 32 KiB local image loses its image payload from the serialized response.
- 14 focused tests pass: five new roster cases, five existing roster authorization cases, and four existing avatar cases.
- Targeted TypeScript checking, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Protocol schema generation, Swift/Kotlin native protocol generation, and generated validator freshness checks pass.
- Local canonical autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) completed on the full working-tree change against `6bd45e1ba9820b30300db404037bc5aa76648c02`, with the affected production owners supplied as source context: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Review was static; it did not execute project code.

Not verified: end-to-end mobile latency or live gateway deployment. The tests establish work and payload removal, not a measured network speedup.

### Running-Gateway transport and latest-stable compatibility proof

Verified on reviewed head `0329434db09ac58286eca3ddf400f39addcf563e` using isolated synthetic state and real authenticated loopback WebSocket connections. Started the official latest-stable `openclaw@2026.10.8` package (`dc2523e5a5c7a309517fd7fa834add938231d526`), captured legacy requests, stopped it, ran the reviewed runtime's ordinary backed-up `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive` migration, and started the reviewed Gateway against the same state.

- Configured valid local PNG, inline data-URI, and public-placeholder remote portraits.
- Stable `{}` response: 200,220-byte payload. Stable rejects the new option with `INVALID_REQUEST: unexpected property 'includeAvatars'`.
- After upgrade, `{}` is deep-equal to the entire stable legacy payload. `{includeAvatars:true}` is also deep-equal to `{}`.
- `{includeAvatars:false}` returns 2,517 bytes, deep-equal to the legacy payload with only `identity.avatar` and `identity.avatarUrl` removed from each agent. All non-portrait fields are preserved.
- Both fixture Gateways shut down cleanly. No production service/configuration was changed. This proves payload/transport behavior, not mobile/Tailscale latency or the package-updater installer. No model credentials/calls were needed; unrelated plugin/browser/model Doctor health gaps in the disabled-integration fixture are not claimed as passing.

[Full redacted request/response excerpts and commands](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186812#issuecomment-6474332805). No code change was needed for this feedback. Upstream maintainer acceptance of the optional public RPC projection remains outstanding; this evidence is not owner approval.

prs.title: feat(memory): opt topic files into per-entry chunking with a marker
prs.body:
Closes #179954

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: curated memory kept in topic files under `memory/` is indexed with the size-based chunker, so unrelated one-fact bullets are merged into ~400-token chunks. A query pulls in neighboring facts and the mixed embedding ranks specific facts lower than the same bullets in `MEMORY.md`.

## User Impact

User impact: a topic file under `memory/` can opt into per-entry chunking by carrying one marker line. Files without the marker are indexed exactly as before; there is no new config key.

```markdown
<!-- chunking: entries -->
```

## Why This Change Was Made

Shape agreed with @steipete in the issue (option 1, chunking only):

- The marker uses the existing HTML-comment carrier style and is stripped before indexing like the other annotations. It must sit on its own line, so prose or code samples that mention it do not opt a file in. Only `memory/` files honor it.
- `prepareMemoryIndexChunks` gets one more input to the existing `perEntry` predicate; the chunker itself is unchanged.
- Recall metadata eligibility and path provenance are untouched (`memory-path-provenance.ts`, `curated-annotations.ts` extraction). The marker does not make a file a curated root, so trigger and importance annotations stay ignored in topic files. Project scope was already read for topic files and now applies per entry in marked files, which follows from the chunk boundaries.
- Adding or removing the marker changes the file content hash, so the normal per-file reindex handles it. `MEMORY_CHUNKING_VERSION` is not bumped because unmarked files chunk as before.
- Docs updated in `memory-builtin`, `memory`, and `memory-architecture`.

## Evidence

Tests (all pass; the three behavior tests fail on the base without the change):

- `manager-index-preparation.test.ts`: marked file chunks per entry with the marker stripped; unmarked file stays one size-based chunk; marker in prose, unknown mode, and non-`memory/` paths are ignored; trigger/importance stay null and project scope still applies as for an unmarked topic file.
- `manager-per-entry-marker.test.ts` (real manager, SQLite index): file indexed size-based, marker added then a normal sync gives per-entry chunks, marker removed then a normal sync returns the original size-based chunks.
- `curated-annotations.test.ts`: marker detection, stripping keeps line numbers, marker never reaches recall metadata.
- Full `extensions/memory-core`, `packages/memory-host-sdk`, `src/plugin-sdk` vitest run: 463 files pass, 9 skipped, 2 fail (see below). `pnpm check:changed` typecheck/format/guards and `pnpm lint:docs` pass.

Paired corpus: the same 24 synthetic one-line bullets (team facts), once in a topic file with the marker and once without. Chunks were produced by the real `prepareMemoryIndexChunks` (400 tokens, 80 overlap) and embedded with a local embedding model (Qwen3-Embedding-4B 4-bit served by a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint, plain queries, cosine similarity, vector ranking only). The unmarked file becomes 2 chunks (20 and 8 bullets); the marked file becomes 24 chunks.

| Query | marked: top score | marked: bullets returned | marked: target rank | unmarked: top score | unmarked: bullets returned | unmarked: target rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Which food should we avoid when booking a team dinner? | 0.602 | 1 | 1 | 0.395 | 20 | 1 |
| How many API calls per minute are allowed? | 0.892 | 1 | 1 | 0.529 | 8 | 1 |
| Who do I ask to change the analytics warehouse schema? | 0.779 | 1 | 1 | 0.501 | 20 | 1 |
| When is the database backup restore-tested? | 0.710 | 1 | 1 | 0.533 | 20 | 1 |
| What is the Friday deploy rule? | 0.731 | 1 | 1 | 0.584 | 20 | 1 |
| How long do we keep logs? | 0.823 | 1 | 1 | 0.492 | 20 | 1 |

With such a small corpus the right chunk is found either way. The difference is what comes back: one bullet at a clearly higher similarity versus 8-20 unrelated bullets in one chunk at a lower score. The gap grows with file size, since a larger unmarked file has more diluted chunks competing with each other.

Shipped-CLI proof (head `f81c3b246`; built `openclaw.mjs`, local oMLX embeddings `Qwen3-Embedding-4B-4bit-DWQ` through `memory.search.provider: "omlx"`, throwaway `HOME` and state dir, real index untouched). Corpus: `MEMORY.md` (3 bullets), `USER.md` (2), `memory/people-marked.md` (6 bullets + marker), `memory/people-unmarked.md` (6 bullets). `openclaw memory index --agent main`, then `openclaw memory search --json`:

| File | base `bec3ad81d` chunks | PR chunks |
|---|---|---|
| `MEMORY.md` | 3 | 3 |
| `USER.md` | 2 | 2 |
| `memory/people-marked.md` | 1 (lines 1-11) | 6 (1-5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10-11) |
| `memory/people-unmarked.md` | 1 (lines 1-9) | 1 (lines 1-9) |

| Query | base top hit | PR top hit |
|---|---|---|
| who is allergic to peanuts | 0.490 `marked:1-11` | 0.633 `marked:6` |
| who manages the Cluj warehouse | 0.577 `marked:1-11` | 0.794 `marked:7` |
| who is allergic to shellfish | 0.443 `unmarked:1-9` | 0.518 `marked:6` (then 0.445 `unmarked:1-9`) |
| vendor contract with the catering company | 0.503 `marked:1-11` | 0.730 `marked:9` |

Upgrade compatibility (same state dir: index with base `bec3ad81d`, switch to the PR build, run `openclaw memory index` again without `--force`): `MEMORY.md`, `USER.md` and the unmarked file keep identical chunk counts and chunk hashes (sha256 digests `6f2efb3f`, `f8bc8e7a`, `f9c76450`) through every step. The marked file is rewritten to 6 per-entry chunks when it is next touched or edited (7 after appending a bullet); adding the marker to the unmarked file gives 6 chunks and removing it restores the original single chunk with the original hash, with all other files untouched. A file that already carries the marker keeps its old chunks until it changes (or `--force`); the marker is new, so no existing corpus is affected. No index-identity warning and no rebuild were needed. Full tables are in the PR comment.

CI: type, lint and package-boundary checks pass on the earlier head. `test-lines` now passes locally (`slack: 237`, baseline untouched) after consolidating duplicated detector test rows; the add/remove-marker reindex test is unchanged.

Fence detection requires only spaces/tabs after a closing delimiter (as `packages/markdown-core/src/fences.ts` does). Upgrade from the latest stable (`v2026.10.8`) to this branch, with existing settings, files and index data preserved, is documented in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186649#issuecomment-6468411633).

Known gaps, none caused by this change (each reproduces with the three source files reverted to `main`): `manager-search-knn-subprocess.test.ts` ("KNN child loaded unrelated runtime: kysely") and two `qa-runtime.test.ts` waitForHealth tests fail locally. `pnpm check:changed` reports two further failures. The Plugin SDK surface budget fails identically on a clean `main` (public entrypoints 160 > 158), and the SQLite worker ratchet could not run locally because `rg` is not installed. No Ollama was used; the embedding model above is the local provider.

prs.title: fix(android): let Back close the keyboard before leaving the screen
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Android, pressing Back while the keyboard is open can leave the current screen instead of closing the keyboard. In chat, Back jumps to Overview and the keyboard stays up over it, so a draft-in-progress conversation disappears from view.

## User Impact

Back closes an open keyboard first. The next Back navigates as before. No setting or migration is involved.

## Why This Change Was Made

With Android's newer Back dispatch, Back goes to whichever Back callback the window registered most recently. The keyboard's callback is only on top if it registered after the app's. When the app's navigation callback becomes active while the keyboard is already open, or the keyboard doesn't register a callback, the app's callback runs and navigates.

The shell now adds a Back handler that hides the keyboard while the keyboard is visible. Because it's added when the keyboard opens, it's the newest app callback, so whichever side receives Back, the first press closes the keyboard. When the keyboard's own callback is on top (the usual case), nothing changes.

## Evidence

Reproduced on the real app in an Android 16 emulator (API 36, Gboard, 1848×2448 at 420 dpi to match a Galaxy Z Fold inner screen, 3-button navigation, screenshot-fixture data). Flow: open the sidebar, tap Search, tap the search field (keyboard opens), close the sidebar (keyboard stays open), tap **Chat** on Overview, then press Back.

- **Before** (`origin/main` 4eb3541d255): Back navigates from Chat to Overview and leaves the keyboard open (`mInputShown=true`).
- **After** (this branch): the first Back closes the keyboard and Chat stays open (`mInputShown=false`). The second Back goes to Overview. The usual flow (open Chat, tap the composer, Back) still closes the keyboard first and then navigates.

### Clean comparison

| Before: keyboard open in Chat | Before: after one Back |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Chat with the keyboard open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8c18867-31ea-424a-ab0e-0e03b243ed79) | ![Before: Back went to Overview and the keyboard is still open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4fc213b1-4bce-4a9e-b5b8-bf2d25ff4848) |

| After: keyboard open in Chat | After: after one Back |
| --- | --- |
| ![After: Chat with the keyboard open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ff6fcc6-9e04-4d3b-83a4-19a82ce69fcb) | ![After: Back closed the keyboard and Chat is still shown](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b1c1d30-d959-477c-996b-3fa6af1080c7) |

The reported device was a Samsung Galaxy Z Fold. I didn't test on Samsung hardware or with Samsung Keyboard. The emulator reproduces the same callback-order failure, and the fix doesn't depend on which keyboard is installed.

Regression test: `RootScreenFoldTest.backClosesAnOpenKeyboardBeforeLeavingChat` opens Chat, types a draft, reports the keyboard as visible, and sends Back through the activity's dispatcher (the case where the app's callback outranks the keyboard's). It checks that the keyboard closes, Chat and its draft stay on screen, and a second Back leaves Chat. It fails on `origin/main` because the first Back leaves Chat.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

- `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.RootScreenFoldTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.SidebarNavigationAccessibilityTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.ShellScreenLogicTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.CommandPaletteLogicTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.SidebarGatewayPickerTest`: 113 tests, 0 failures
- New test with the `ShellScreen.kt` change reverted: fails (`chat-composer-surface ... is not displayed`)
- `./gradlew :app:ktlintCheck :app:assemblePlayDebug`: passes
- Emulator checks used `adb shell input keyevent 4` and taps on the navigation bar's keyboard-dismiss Back button. Keyboard state came from `dumpsys input_method`.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

When continuing a child task, OpenClaw can report that access was revoked even when the first continuation attempt was denied. It also loses which side rejected the continuation, making the operator's access check harder.

## User Impact

Callers can distinguish an initial rejection from later loss of access, identify the parent or child endpoint, and receive a safe next step: ask an authorized operator to check continuation access for both conversations.

Permissions do not change, and hidden-session details remain private. This diagnostic fix does not repair early session-resolution failures, explicit message source-admission failures, automation management scope, or unrelated Goal/completion-delivery failures. No configuration or migration is required.

prs.title: fix(matrix): password accounts stay offline forever after the homeserver revokes the cached token
prs.body:
Closes #186011

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Matrix account with password auth stays offline permanently (every request `401 M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN`, E2EE never initializes) after its device is deleted or logged out on the homeserver, because the plugin keeps reusing the revoked cached token and never logs in again.

## User Impact

User impact: password-configured Matrix accounts now recover on the next start by logging in again with a fresh device, instead of requiring operators to hand-edit `state/openclaw.sqlite`. Accounts without a configured password, and transient homeserver/network failures, behave exactly as before.

Note for operators: recovery creates a new Matrix device, so the account needs the usual E2EE verification/bootstrap for that device afterwards (same as any new device).

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveMatrixAuth` returned matching cached credentials before ever reaching the password login, and nothing cleared them when the homeserver rejected the token (`clearMatrixCredentials` had no runtime caller). Now, when a cached token is about to be used and a password is configured, the token is checked once with `whoami`. Only a definitive revocation (`isMatrixAccessTokenInvalidatedError`) clears the cached credential and falls through to the existing password login; any other failure keeps the cached token. A successful check is remembered per process, so repeated auth resolves (probe, directory, shared client) do not add round-trips.

Tradeoff: one extra `GET /account/whoami` per cached token per process, only for accounts that have a password configured.

## Evidence

- New tests in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client.test.ts`:
  - revoked cached token → credential cleared, password login, fresh token/device saved (fails on `main` without this change, passes with it)
  - non-revocation whoami failure (HTTP 500) → cached token kept, nothing cleared or saved
  - live cached token → verified once, second resolve skips whoami
- `pnpm test extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client.test.ts`: 24/24 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all lanes ok (typecheck extensions + extension tests, lint changed files, format, plugin boundaries, import cycles, …) except the dead-export scan, which reports `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-archive-types.ts: SessionColdOversized` — an unrelated file this PR does not touch.
- Live reproduction against a throwaway Synapse 1.163.0 in Docker (bot with password auth + `encryption: true`), steps from #186011:
  - before (OpenClaw 2026.10.7): after deleting the bot's devices via the admin API and restarting, 0 login attempts, 8× `401 M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN`, cached credential unchanged, no device on the server.
  - after (this branch, built with `pnpm build`, gateway via `node openclaw.mjs gateway run`): starting from the same state (cached credential for device `IGBSDYPYCO`, no devices on the server), the gateway logged in again on startup — the server now lists a new device `VTHIDYRSLN`, the cached credential was replaced with it, and the log shows 0 `M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN` errors.
  - Not covered here: the new device then hits the existing secret-storage/cross-signing state of the account (`Initial cross-signing bootstrap failed and automatic reset is disabled`) and needs `openclaw matrix verify bootstrap` like any new device. That is pre-existing behavior and out of scope for this PR.

- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (and so `openclaw/ci-gate`) is red because `main` is already over the test-line ceiling on its own; this PR adds +61 test lines in `client.test.ts` and leaves `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` untouched (details in the PR conversation).
- Secret scanning: synthetic token fixtures in the new tests carry `// pragma: allowlist secret`, and the pre-existing embedded-credentials URL fixture in the homeserver URL rejection test now carries `// trufflehog:ignore`; TruffleHog 3.99.4 flagged that line as a URI credential and blocked the automated review. A local TruffleHog 3.99.4 scan of the changed files, diff and PR text is clean.

prs.title: improve(compaction): skip unused snapshot byte accounting
prs.body:
Related: #196550

## What Problem This Solves

Compaction repeats conversation classification and computes transcript byte sizes that its full-fidelity planning does not consume.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Short planning/rendering worker tasks, bounded Gateway payloads, and overlapping summary calls are preserved. **The new `a03b` repair reduced CPU and RPC time on the bounded workload below, but overall performance and landing are NOT accepted. Burst lifecycle process RSS median increased 2.74%, and worker-local observed heap p95 increased 34.37%. Keep this draft pending explicit owner judgment on memory and all other adverse moves, plus normal CI, mergeability, and authority gates.** The original `12ad` negative comparison remains immutable. No universal CPU benefit is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing meaningful-content result when preparing conversation-anchor facts. In the planner’s existence-only check, stop classifying after the first real conversation message while still visiting every message and checking cancellation. The shared classifier’s full lookback behavior remains unchanged for other consumers.

For unbounded SQLite snapshots only, the shared snapshot producer now skips two eager model-size projections per navigation row (2N evaluations). An explicit size request still uses the original size SQL and existing bounded batches. Bounded snapshots and their navigation cache, PostgreSQL’s fused projection, omission handling, snapshot/fence/identity checks, cancellation, and native-writer durability remain unchanged. No work is moved outside the measurement boundary.

No cache, retained transcript payload, new configuration, changed summary selection, or persistence/authority change is introduced.

## Evidence

- **Original classification scope:** independent static owner/caller review and local autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings on `12ad15841a49778e9d9c0b6b9af1511fe5e20d0a`. The completed original 30-observation result below applies only to that head.
- **New repair source:** reviewed repair commit `7ac21e5d1b14d49e97170bd03a68738165b04c55` is published through empty metadata commit `a03b3d25606cd3c8664a6fc069c66e081f829b81`. Both have tree `94e6b6dd8350b4f1b82d9ceb08dc4e6de8dcd951`; source is identical. The exact two-file repair patch SHA-256 is `7c60e0afad0cd31cba985dab630099ff3380b71bf0b66e7116cc920cc47af437`.
- **New SQLite work-count proof:** the actual snapshot operation on original `12ad` fails the intended zero-eager-sizing assertion with six executed `octet_length` calls for a header and two inline messages. The repair performs zero eager calls, then exactly two calls when those messages’ sizes are explicitly requested, with exact byte values preserved. This proves removed SQL sizing work, not overall CPU savings.
- **New repair validation:** 53 focused tests passed across snapshot, seed, actual compaction-source integration, model-context, and selected lifetime/authority/refusal cases before a fixture type correction. The corrected selected work-count test then passed (one selected, four intentionally skipped), without double-counting it as additional coverage. The correction uses the existing `isIndexedSessionEntry` predicate; the original TS18046 failure is retained. Final independent, local autoreview, and parent hands-on reviews found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Targeted production/test type graphs, lint, line-cap, format, and diff checks exited 0.
- **New repair normal build:** normal `pnpm build` exited 0 in 181.1 seconds with Node 26.12.1 / pnpm 12.15.0, before commit at `12ad` plus the exact reviewed `7c60…` patch. Source/dependency hashes remained unchanged. This is not an `a03b`-bound native performance build. The secretless build used network-disabled private isolation, eight CPUs / 16 GiB, default heaps, absent NODE_OPTIONS, enforced zero task swap, and the existing physical exact-lockfile dependency closure. No shared dependency reconciliation or guard override occurred. Its TypeScript experimental-API warning remains retained; Control UI content-cache reuse is not a new UI-budget pass. All original warnings and failed setup/gate receipts remain retained.
- **New commit-bound native build:** canonical `a03b` sourcePerformance build exited 0 on Node 24.22.1, eight CPUs / 16 GiB, default heaps, absent NODE_OPTIONS, zero task swap, network-disabled build/runtime, and private frozen-lock dependencies. Dependency preparation was separate: secretless normal public-registry frozen-lock installation with lifecycle scripts disabled. Separate v1/v2 offline preparation failures remain preserved; they were not relabeled successful builds.
- **New workload qualification:** committed workload `007777bbf9917bdc62a488b9e348990fc06c6a04` passed 12 head contracts. The same reviewed new assertions on the base produced four expected failures across three methods. Normal commit hooks exited 0 and all three human coauthor trailers were preserved.
- **New native series completed:** six separate diagnostic qualifiers passed, then all 30 planned original light, unprofiled observations completed with controller exit 0. No observation was rerun, discarded, corrected, or pooled. Parent hands-on source/native/aggregate auditing and an independent result audit rederived all 15 metrics across all 30 observations with no actionable P0–P2 numerical or integrity discrepancies. This is NOT overall acceptance or a memory waiver.
- **Remaining gates:** exact-`a03b` broad CI is unproven. Dirty mergeability was observed; the current pre-edit metadata read returned unknown. No base integration or conflict repair has been performed. Overall performance and landing remain pending explicit owner judgment on memory and every other adverse tradeoff. A scoped request to resolve this is not acceptance of regressions or merge authority.
- **Original classification red/green regression:** the exact new classifier test on base `8857554b178506f962068509227e5c10ebe6cc8a` fails only its two intended work-count assertions (`expected 2 to be 1`), while all 11 existing cases pass. The candidate passes all 13 cases. This proves eligible-content reads fall from two to one, not overall CPU savings. The native observer does not separately count these helper calls.
- **Original `12ad`: 94 candidate tests passed** across the classifier, safeguard-source, safeguard, actual worker compaction-source integration, context-report, and prompt-prefix stability suites. Tests ran serially through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1` on Node 26.12.1. No separate Bun-runtime proof is claimed.
- For original `12ad`, formatting, the three-file line-cap ratchet, targeted lint, production and changed-test type graphs, and the normal `pnpm build` all exited 0. Task-private physical frozen-lockfile installations supplied the required `oxlint` 1.89.0; the shared installation was not reconciled, and no hook or content guard was overridden. Validation receipts, all 15 retained log hashes, source/dependency integrity, and exact build identity were independently audited. The earlier local hook/tool-version failure remains retained.
- **Build caveat:** the successful normal build printed eight Control UI asset-budget violations and dynamic-import warnings. This is not a passing UI-performance check. No baseline attribution was established, so these warnings are not labeled inherited or caused by this patch.
- **Original `12ad` native proof completed:** six separately tagged qualifications and all **30 original comparison observations** completed, controller exit 0. All imports/physical identities, native compactions, exact 8,192-byte seed/post-RPC follow-ups, warm-target invariance, source/build/workload/fixture bindings, default-heap/no-swap checks, independently observed main-thread CPU brackets, and graceful cleanup passed. No observation was rerun, discarded, corrected, or pooled with earlier evidence.
- **Original `12ad` broad CI remained unproven:** the complete observed exact-head inventory had six successful dispatch/metadata/scope/actionlint checks and 102 skipped checks. Skips are not broad-suite proof. The original #196550 110-observation comparison is separate and does not validate this patch.

### NEW a03 repair protocol — predeclared method, now completed

Compare architecture-matched baseline `8857554b178506f962068509227e5c10ebe6cc8a` against new candidate `a03b3d25606cd3c8664a6fc069c66e081f829b81` (the same reviewed source tree as `7ac21e5d1b14d49e97170bd03a68738165b04c55`). The count goal is to remove 2N unused eager model-size evaluations from unbounded SQLite planning without moving work outside measurement or changing selected inputs, bounds, overlap, cancellation, authority, or durability.

- Use the existing committed canonical real-Gateway rig and model-mock workload, not a new benchmark framework. Native sourcePerformance builds and runtime use Node 24.22.1, eight CPUs, 16 GiB, default heaps, absent NODE_OPTIONS, enforced zero task swap, network-disabled runtime, cleared credential environment, and private exact-lock dependencies. Fixed model delays remain 250 ms for `long01` and 2,000 ms for burst. Native seed/post-RPC continuity must remain exactly 8,192 bytes.
- Run six separately tagged diagnostic qualification observations first. Their timings are excluded from acceptance. Observe actual model-request counts during qualification and bind those facts later; no new counts are assumed here.
- Acceptance contains 30 new observations: five serial interleaved main→PR pairs for whole-generation `long01` cold, five pairs for `long01` warm using a separate sacrificial warm-up session, and five pairs for cold correlated `s01` burst across ten physical sessions. Keep cold and warm populations separate.
- Use the new `repair199040-` tag namespace. Freeze the exact order, source/commit/tree/dist/lock/image/environment, committed workload, fixture, native-build bindings, and observed qualification/model-work facts before the first acceptance observation. Every required input must be bound before timing. The new native-build/workload/qualification bindings were frozen before acceptance, and the six qualifiers and 30-observation series are now complete.
- Measure whole-process CPU including all workers, separately observed main-thread CPU, complete compaction RPC wall time, process RSS, worker-local/lifecycle memory with scopes named, parse/hydration/work counts, and summary overlap. Do not sum thread RSS or noncoincident heap maxima. Main-thread CPU, memory, continuity, selected inputs, and burst concurrency must hold.
- Require a measurable process-CPU reduction, not merely avoidance of a large regression. A 20% or greater process-CPU or RPC median or p95 regression in ANY required population stops performance acceptance. Keep every smaller adverse move visible; landing with such tradeoffs requires explicit owner acceptance. This protocol grants no merge authority.
- Report n, median, nearest-rank p95, minimum/maximum and spread for each arm/population. With five observations per arm, p95 is the maximum. No pooling, outlier removal, fsync subtraction, relabeling, or retries/replacement of failed tags; retain every failure and adverse result.
- Keep prior original-199040 30 observations and six qualifiers, #196550’s 110 observations, frozen15e80 and old35 immutable and excluded. The original15e +58.2387% cold-long01 RPC-p95 landing gate is NOT waived.
- Coverage remains one whole observed generation plus one correlated source replay, not a broad corpus. Fixed mock summaries establish runtime/continuity, not provider summary quality; post-compaction unrelated RPC probes do not establish during-compaction responsiveness.

**Completion status:** all six diagnostic qualifiers and all 30 planned original acceptance observations completed with exit 0. The predeclared method and acceptance rules above are unchanged. CPU/RPC improvement was measured; overall performance acceptance remains pending owner judgment on the adverse memory and other tradeoffs below.

### NEW a03 completed results — CPU/RPC improved; memory judgment pending

**Visible adverse memory tradeoff:** burst lifecycle-process RSS rose from 2,465.82 to 2,533.35 MiB at the median (+2.74%; p95 +2.50%). Worker-local observed heap rose from 100.77 to 108.67 MiB at the median (+7.84%), and from 102.24 to 137.38 MiB at p95 (+34.37%). Worker-local observed heap is not process RSS or summed concurrent heap. This does not prove a retained leak, but it is not safe to dismiss. prs.title: fix(openai): let fast voice answers skip acknowledgments
prs.body:
Related: #175603.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway-controlled OpenAI Talk acknowledges every delegated request immediately, even when the answer is ready fast enough to speak directly. Repeated acknowledgments make short conversations feel repetitive and add unnecessary speech before the result.

## User Impact

Work starts immediately. An answer or failure arriving within 1.5 seconds skips filler. Slower requests receive at most one short acknowledgment using the existing caller-language, naturally varied wording from #175603. Wording variation remains model-directed, not guaranteed.

Spoken updates, follow-ups, controls, and call shutdown cancel an unsent acknowledgment. Status, cancellation, final results, and failure delivery retain their existing ownership. No new configuration or client changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Race the existing consult against a short acknowledgment timer in its existing controller. This avoids a separate predictive model call or delaying the actual work. The timer is canceled when the consult settles or its presentation becomes obsolete, and uses the original socket's delivery checks.

The 1.5-second window is an initial UX choice, not a measured latency improvement. An answer arriving just after that window can still follow an acknowledgment already submitted to the provider.

## Evidence

- Baseline regression: 12 failures / 20 passes against the unmodified controller, including the new fast-answer, slow-answer, and cancellation cases failing on its immediate append.
- All 89 focused tests pass across delegation (32), public delegation (8), Gateway bridge and browser session (36 combined), and agent-tool prompt stability (13). Two old consumer expectations of immediate filler were updated and their 40-test subset rerun successfully.
- Changed delegation/public-delegation suites: 25.43 seconds including compilation; 28.19 seconds including runner cleanup. Earlier four-suite voice run: 6.52 seconds with cached compilation. Hosted CI timing pending.
- OpenAI package typecheck, type-aware lint of all four touched TypeScript files, formatting, and whitespace checks pass.
- Independent autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings in the diff. Review was limited to supplied changes; focused execution provides the runtime proof above.
- Graphify AST-only refresh completed for the OpenAI package. Generated graph files are not part of this PR.

No live provider/audio or physical-device acceptance test was run. The running Gateway and native app were not changed.

The simplification pass retains one timer in the existing controller and no new policy owner, queue, config surface, or predictive classifier. Production delta: +30/-2 lines; tests: +113/-17; docs: +5/-2.

prs.title: fix: bound Codex catalog startup and client cleanup
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/152886

## What Problem This Solves

Codex catalog startup can load the agent runtime prematurely and retain client work after its owner closes, while competing health refreshes can consume catalog admission during Gateway startup.

## User Impact

Catalog and client work keeps its existing owner, cancellation and cleanup boundaries. A canonically bundled Codex plugin can use the host's state APIs without mislabeling a locally patched archive as an official npm installation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the catalog factory available when the harness loads while deferring heavyweight authentication code and actual client/catalog requests. Close owned transport work, fence native catalog walks, and align the bundled harness with native Codex 0.159.3.

This branch also includes its inherited Gateway health ownership, catalog admission, fleet metadata and serialized build fixes. It contains six commits and 39 changed files relative to the release branch's common ancestor; the final Codex commit changes 24 files. It preserves installed-plugin provenance and the existing local-archive trust refusal. Host bundling uses the canonical package composer.

## Evidence

- 45 focused tests passed on the final source in 27.37 seconds; native version and npm lock checks also passed.
- The canonical Core build completed successfully, with source/dependency and process-closure checks preserved.

prs.title: fix(gateway): let delegated OpenClaw changes work from CLI-backend agents
prs.body:
Related: #136036, #137017

## What Problem This Solves

Delegated `openclaw.chat` calls from CLI/subprocess and worker harnesses failed with `delegated OpenClaw approval requires an active run authority`. Fully in-process agents retained the ambient caller identity, but harness tool calls crossed the Gateway WebSocket boundary, where that process-local identity is intentionally unavailable.

## User Impact

CLI and worker-harness delegated calls retain their signed source ownership and approval guard, including when optional wire delegation metadata is absent. Existing run, tool-abort and worker-lifetime fencing remains fail-closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root cause

The approval gate only consulted the process-local Gateway tool caller identity. OpenClaw already has a host-minted, HMAC-signed `agentRuntimeIdentityToken` for trusted cross-process calls, including the exact admitted run authority and worker turn claim, but `openclaw.chat` was not included in that transport.

The first revision attempted to mint replacement authority from the delegated session id. Review identified that as unsafe. The signed-identity revision then exposed two narrower defects:

- Distinct calls in one source run receive distinct tool-bound lease claim ids. Approval reconciliation compared those claim ids, so a later call retired the original pending decision even though its exact lease was still live.
- The wire fallback retained the generic 30-second request timeout although delegated human interaction is budgeted for 900 seconds and the approval owner can wait 600 seconds before staging/application completes.

## Design

This revision carries the existing source-run authority instead of synthesizing or transferring it:

- `openclaw.chat` is eligible for the signed agent-runtime identity token.
- The host binds the exact tool abort signal into the delegated run authority before signing it.
- Explicit host-prepared Full Access is transported only for `openclaw.chat`; model-authored parameters cannot create it.
- On Gateway arrival, signed agent/runtime/session/routing facts establish delegation even when the optional wire field is omitted; model-supplied metadata cannot override or opt out of that binding.
- Ambient in-process identity remains authoritative when present. Wire calls use the verified signed runtime identity.
- Pending-approval reconciliation first validates the original exact application lease, then compares both callers' active canonical source owner plus local/worker kind and exact worker turn claim. It never replaces the authority stored on the pending record.
- The delegated wire call uses the existing 900-second human-interaction budget. The generic Gateway default remains 30 seconds, and the Codex owner retains its separate 30-second completion grace.
- Run release/replacement, original tool abort, Gateway replacement, worker-claim loss, and delegated-session replacement still fail closed.

No new configuration keys, SQLite surfaces, dependencies or retries are introduced. The existing transient signed-identity token carries an optional host-prepared Full Access fact. Existing canonical owner and human-wait helpers were sufficient.

## Security properties

- No authority is derived from a session id or model-authored delegation fields.
- The signed identity can only be minted by the host holding the local runtime-token secret.
- Full Access is a host-prepared restrict-only fact; omission never bypasses approval.
- Reuse grants observation of an existing pending decision only after its original exact application lease is revalidated.
- The original record retains its exact lease, signals, and application predicate. Closing a later sibling lease cannot transfer or cancel that authority; closing the original lease still blocks application.
- Worker authority remains bound to the canonical placement/turn claim.

## Evidence

- Published head `cea0acc7028934a9609bb656a14cb21a3496db94` integrates GitHub-confirmed current-main conflicts against pinned upstream `3260d7b41a8c2404b8b3dc800240573dfb1cc7e1`. Preserves upstream compact delegate-test layout and PR timeout/permission/session-continuation contracts. Production authority changes merged without manual conflict; removed a now-unused moved import and compacted a local parameter name to satisfy changed-file lint. Validation passed: 91 focused authority/identity/delegate tests across five suites (55.731s wrapper), production core types and all three affected test-type shards, changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, pinned-main diff check, line-cap and assertion-safety ratchets. The newly integrated cron fixture needed a true-or-undefined permission normalization in its test transport only; its affected integration suite and Gateway-method types pass after that correction. Fresh independent scoped review of the frozen production tree found no actionable P0/P1; retained for the final one-line test-adapter correction. No fresh real delayed-human transport proof, replacement-head hosted verdict, or maintainer signed-carrier acceptance is claimed.

- Prior published head `fad89b4b638381fbb5e964c5d0cade97d01b0afc` reconciles a GitHub-confirmed approval-test conflict onto pinned upstream `d1618ccd0b276f985711ff297b1b87a77bdad35d`. Upstream removed a redundant ambient-only parameter case; the later maintained cross-lease wire/ambient approval coverage remains intact. Seventeen patches replay identically; the first differs only in its upstream conflict context. Prior independent review is retained for this mechanical delta, not claimed as fresh review. All 10 local gates passed: 99 tests across five focused suites (56.058s wrapper), production core types, all three affected test-type shards (agents-root, agents-other and Gateway-methods), changed-source type-aware lint, formatting, diff, line-cap and assertion-safety checks. The initial lint attempt could not load the newly required eslint-plugin-solid; refreshing the isolated installation from the unchanged frozen lockfile resolved it without source or lockfile workarounds. No replacement-head hosted verdict or fresh live-runtime result is claimed. Real delayed-human-decision proof and area-owner signed-carrier acceptance remain outstanding.

- Prior published head `db8ec1bb286e5b9bd9a77a7fcaea911869673b9a` addresses revision 24’s test-quality feedback: removed the synthetic delayed-decision mock test and unused fake-timer cleanup. The retained relay test verifies the requested 900-second budget and returned approval outcome. All 15 delegate-tool tests passed (`pnpm test src/agents/tools/openclaw-delegate-tool.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 8.655s wrapper / 6.67s Vitest); affected agents-other test types, type-aware changed-file lint, formatting, diff check, line-cap and assertion-safety gates passed. Production sources are byte-unchanged from the prior validated head, whose exact-head hosted CI was observed SUCCESS at 07:13 UTC and durable revision 24 found no production defect. Those prior-head results are historical. That prior head’s hosted CI was observed SUCCESS at 2026-10-08 17:53 UTC; durable ClawSweeper revision 25 reviewed that head and reports no actionable findings, with area-owner acceptance still outstanding. No fresh independent production review or live run is claimed for this test-only deletion.
- A real human decision after 30 seconds remains unverified by the historical CLI evidence. The removed synthetic timeout test did not establish that transport behavior; the historical timeout RED/GREEN results below are synthetic test evidence only.

- Prior published `4cde0ad5c4cd3cbe31b96320f8a7e01954e2d74b` reconciled a confirmed import conflict onto pinned upstream `2f1f73ccb2224bbe7d961b4c0d3b29cfdd51e7f8`. The maintained hosted-routing suite retains the delegated signed-identity case and drops an obsolete Workshop approval import removed upstream. All other patches replay unchanged; delegated authority, method-scoped Full Access and exact approval-lease intent remain unchanged. Fresh validation of the source committed as `4cde0ad5c4cd3cbe31b96320f8a7e01954e2d74b`: 103 authority tests across five focused suites passed (50.477s wrapper); production core types and all three affected test-type shards (agents-root, agents-other and Gateway-methods) passed. Changed-source type-aware lint, formatting, diff, line-cap and assertion-safety gates passed. Prior independent scoped review is retained for the mechanically reconciled delta, not claimed as a fresh review. Prior 27-test URL-boundary proof is retained for the unchanged canonicalizer. No fresh live-runtime proof or replacement-head hosted CI result is claimed. Assigned-reviewer acceptance of the signed Full Access carrier remains outstanding.

Tested head: `cea0acc7028934a9609bb656a14cb21a3496db94` (base `3260d7b41a8c2404b8b3dc800240573dfb1cc7e1`).

- Resolved current-main conflicts without changing delegated authority intent. Migrated the one PR-specific signed Full Access wire/lifetime case into the maintained hosted-routing suite; the retired baseline suite remains deleted. Preserved current-main admitted identity reconstruction and inherited permission schema.
- Omitted-delegation RED/GREEN regression: the real `openclaw.chat` handler test failed before the repair, choosing connection ownership instead of signed source ownership. The parameterized regression checks both omitted and spoofed wire metadata, signed session ownership, and delegated-only operator approval. Both regression variants pass after the repair.
- Prior published `c6ab9511e93f586626135c67633e5240db04ea32` validation: 107 tests across five focused suites passed (36.14s wrapper); production core types, type-aware changed-file lint, formatting, diff check, line-cap ratchet and assertion safety passed. Fresh independent review: the sole P1 concerned the old index version; the reviewer explicitly recognized this working-tree repair as addressing it and reported no other concrete P0/P1 defect. The corrected index was verified and committed. Affected Gateway-method test types: passed (exit 0).
- Prior published head `bd1287586199249975f6a268ccbf2553686ad3f0` had successful exact-head hosted CI; those are not current-candidate CI results. The earlier 27 core-test compiler shards passed with the documented aggregate-wrapper exit-124 limitation. Current validation reruns affected proof rather than claiming those prior results as fresh full coverage.
- Historical RED/GREEN timeout evidence: test-only `06648dac970` failed at the generic 30-second timeout ([red runtime job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33936113189/job/101224617458)); `537130294ac2e1360700ab2f094df4b8e9a8b05d` passed 241 files / 5,013 tests ([green runtime job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33936776749/job/101226276241)). These are not current-head CI results.
- The earlier real CLI proof below is historical transport evidence, not a fresh live run of this rebased candidate. No serving runtime was changed for this reconciliation. Hosted CI for prior head `db8ec1bb286e5b9bd9a77a7fcaea911869673b9a` was observed SUCCESS at 2026-10-08 17:53 UTC; security-owner/maintainer acceptance remains an external gate.

### Earlier real CLI harness proof

Verified against a locally built Gateway through the real `openclaw agent` Codex app-server path:

1. **Active Full Access succeeds:** an admitted `finance-worker` Codex turn invoked the `openclaw` tool over the Gateway WebSocket and changed `update.checkOnStart` from `true` to `false`. The terminal receipt recorded exactly one successful `openclaw` tool call. An independent CLI read observed `false`; the test then restored and schema-validated `true`.
2. **Source abort fails closed after dispatch:** a second admitted CLI turn emitted the `openclaw` tool call, then received `SIGINT` through the CLI's same-connection abort path. The persisted tool result was `OpenClaw dynamic tool call aborted.` and an independent CLI read remained `true`.

## Observer-cancellation ownership

Proposal-failure retirement belongs to the caller that installed the pending approval. A later same-source observer whose distinct lease closes fails its own live-authority check without clearing or force-denying the original owner's still-live approval. Original-owner cancellation remains fail-closed. The current focused approval-authority suite includes this order-sensitive regression.

Agents can ask structured `ask_user` questions, but a multi-question or multi-select prompt could become a text list in Telegram, and the Control UI did not keep each answer visible in the conversation.

prs.title: docs(gateway): describe restart wakes for background processes accurately
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

`docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md` still describes the pre-#199499 behavior for background processes:
- "a session counts as running when … it owns a running background process";
- "Background process: … its root session receives the resume input";
- "a shutdown marker still resumes … when a completed reply had background commands".

#199499 deleted the `hadBackgroundExec` marker and moved lost background commands to their own exit notices, but left these sentences behind. Shutdown selection (`src/gateway/session-restart-resume-selection.ts:91-150`) selects active session operations, live agent runs, sub-agent roots and yield waits. It does not select background-process owners, and a finished turn clears `lifecycleRunId` (`src/config/sessions/session-run-lifecycle-projection.ts:293-295`), so crash discovery skips it too.

## Change

Docs only:
- an interrupted root gets the ordinary resume input;
- a finished root with a notifying background command gets the lost-process exit notice instead;
- named accepted edge case: an interrupted root that also had a notifying background command gets both inputs and may reply twice. This is rare, visible and recoverable, and it is kept so that restart recovery stays independent of process reporting.

## Evidence

- A real-Gateway restart (isolated Gateway, real model, SIGKILL) on unchanged `main`: an interrupted root with a notifying background command received the resume input and the lost-process notice, and replied twice.
- `pnpm docs:list`, `pnpm docs:check-mdx`, `pnpm docs:check-links`, `pnpm format:docs:check` and `git diff --check` pass. `pnpm lint:docs` reports one existing, unrelated `MD012` in `docs/internal/conversation-history-redesign.md:340`.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Hovering over Workspace files in the Publish Template card can turn the row pale in a custom dark theme. The file names become hard to read just as the user is about to open them.

## User Impact
The row still highlights on hover, but its title and file names stay readable. Clicking it still opens the files; it does not publish the draft.

## Why This Change Was Made
The row used a hover color derived mostly from the custom theme’s muted text. It now uses the existing translucent surface highlight so the card background shows through. No layout or publication logic changed.

## Evidence
In Chromium with the same synthetic draft and dark theme, the hovered title improved from 2.68:1 to 12.38:1 contrast; the file summary improved from 1.90:1 to 8.77:1. Both failed the 4.5:1 regression threshold before the change and passed afterward. The five-test source review suite and `pnpm check:changed` passed locally.
