prs.title: refactor(gateway): return a started in-process Gateway request's real outcome
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

An agent tool that calls a Gateway method in-process (`openclaw`, `gateway`, `sessions`, `portal`, `progressCard`, `screen` and others) re-checked the caller's authority **after the method had finished**. The binding check also ran again after dispatch. If the run ended or the Gateway reloaded while the method ran, the tool discarded the method's real result (or its real error) and reported `agent tool caller authority is no longer active`.

After #201998 this became visible: a system-agent config change that a human approved while the run was live is applied, but the agent is told it was refused. `system-agent.chat` also re-checked request authority at six points after its queue start, including just before sending the completed result.

The repo rule (AGENTS.md, "Choose good compromises") is to check authority one time, when work starts. Revocation and reload apply to the next request, and a started request may finish.

## Change

- `in-process-gateway.ts`: caller authority and the Gateway binding are checked once, before dispatch. The post-dispatch checks on success and on error are deleted, so the method's real outcome is returned. The positional completion-revalidation flag is gone. The remaining boolean, renamed `forwardAbortSignal`, controls only whether the request's abort signal reaches the dispatch wait. Every caller keeps its previous cancellation behavior.
- Cron: the completion receipt and `isCommitted` stay, now only for cancellation settlement (committed work survives a Stop; uncommitted work is cancelled) and `cron.run`'s async-work ownership.
- `system-agent.ts`: after the queue-start check, the six repeated request-authority checks are replaced by session-ownership checks (transcript and greeting cache). During initialization there is also an explicit cancellation check on the request and approval signals, so a user Stop still stops it.
- Kept: admission and queue-start authority, Gateway routing, session ownership, and the dispatcher and commit guards. Those guards are the next S1 chain, in their own PR.

## User impact

A tool call that started returns what actually happened. An approved system-agent change that applied is reported as applied, not refused. A user Stop still cancels work that has not committed.

## Evidence

Proof tier: source (`ocx test`).

- New end-to-end regression: a real human-approved `openclaw` call through `in-process-gateway` into `system-agent.chat`, with the caller's run ending before the result is delivered (pending-approval branch). On unchanged `main` it fails with `agent tool caller authority is no longer active`. With the fix it returns the applied result.
- `system-agent-owner-write.integration.test.ts`: with a live and with a revoked source grant, the change persists AND the outer tool returns `done: config.set`.
- Tests that pinned only the deleted re-checks were removed or migrated (the hosted pending-run row, the revoked-history row, revoked during an unrelated eviction, completion masking, post-dispatch binding retirement). The bounded-eviction test and the cancellation tests are kept.
- 80 test files (1,143 tests) after the rebase onto #201998, plus 60 tests in 3 files after the binding change. `pnpm tsgo`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxlint, format, and the lifetime-check, line-cap, session-identity, mock-export and max-lines ratchets: pass.

Production +71 −66 lines (the Cron cancellation settlement moved into the two dispatch closures). Tests +452 −834 lines.

**HOLD — open draft; no valid 5–10k deletion replacement survived the named-keeper checks.** Original head: `71f70f9d3016669d37ff3c194b71a13588261d05`; reviewed source base: `b90c5739fa5cbff09f35de8985e1579b4442d5cd`. All four proposed areas retain their candidates: native/provider lifecycle (10 suites), agent execution and delivery (12 suites plus one helper), storage/update/cron (9 suites plus two helpers), and UI/plugin controls (10 suites). Across the 41 suites, the named keepers miss concrete boundaries including native turn settlement, prepared payload custody, physical SQLite admission and rollback, UI focus/lifecycle, and real plugin SDK composition. Dependent helpers remain with their retained consumers.

Preserve the six prior exact-main retentions: `templates-catalog.e2e.test.ts`, `ChatSessionSidebarQueryTests.swift`, `agent-lifecycle-registry.test.ts`, `prepared-model-runtime.catalog-owner.test.ts`, `session-manager-hydration.test.ts`, and `reply-agent-turn-preparation.test.ts`, with their selectors. No source changes or replacement PR are proposed.

This is bounded static source/keeper evidence, not executed runtime proof. The historical WebKit picker failure's cause remains **UNKNOWN**. No exact-main replay or inherited-failure claim is added; the historical zero-finding review does not override the newly identified keeper gaps.

---

## Current validation status

**Skipped from landing; draft, not merged.** Exact head: `71f70f9d3016669d37ff3c194b71a13588261d05`. [Exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198966#issuecomment-6880070552) has zero findings, but CI is not green.

## What Problem This Solves

Consolidates redundant test coverage under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198737 while preserving named existing coverage and distinct failure detection.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. This tranche removes **33,431 net lines** (+59/-33,490; 33,549 changed lines) across 59 paths. It removes 41 whole suites and three unused test support modules. No new runtime or support implementation is added.

## Keeper Decisions

The [manifest](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/71f70f9d3016669d37ff3c194b71a13588261d05/test/scripts/coverage-consolidation/recut-198798-198799-d.tsv) names a surviving keeper for every removed file. Previously retained `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-agent-turn-preparation.test.ts` and `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatSessionSidebarQueryTests.swift` also remain exact selected-main keepers.

Removed the orphaned compaction-runtime, SQLite prepared-admission and update-command lease-service support modules. Each retired suite was its helper's only importer; no surviving importer remains. prs.title: fix(codex): preserve worker GitHub execution credentials
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes worker-hosted Codex commands losing the session's admitted GitHub identity and automatic Goal continuations losing repository dispatch authority after the originating turn ends.

## User Impact

A dedicated Full Codex worker can use the selected GitHub App without falling back to an ambient account. Installation and renewal require exact-generation acknowledgements; cleanup joins refresh and revocation. Ordinary paired nodes and other managed identities do not receive this launch binding. The App's repository permissions and the model's authentication are unchanged.

First in a two-PR stack, extracted from `5eea78634ab` with Goal changes from `23dcc5f19b1`. Base remains `galiniliev/main7-worker-prerequisites` at `1f67db94064`; land those prerequisites before retargeting to `main`. Recovery is in #201032.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the Gateway grant owner, private worker profile, native command carrier and Goal queue. Automatic turns retain a dispatch factory, not a settled request's authority.

The Azure run exposed a conflict: the host-owned managed-identity safeguard disabled the native surface required by worker placement. The fix pins the selected App, requires the exact dedicated placement and original operator before issuance, and refuses to launch without the grant. It does not lift the native-tool guard for local or shared execution or for restricted turns. No new schema, store or authority source is added.

## Evidence

### Managed App worker admission repair

- The new admission regression was red on the previous production code and is green with the repair. Separate negative cases cover restricted turns, missing grant, missing exact worker execution scope and shared-placement refusal. The final replayed stack passed **31** focused local environment, admission and transport cases. The Gateway grant and worker launcher suites passed **81** cases; the new fail-closed admission case passed separately.
- The isolated Gateway/paired-node test passed on the integrated repair, including exact worker selection, resume, cancellation and cleanup using synthetic loopback inference. It does not exercise live GitHub App issuance. Affected typechecks, typed lint, formatting, plugin import/export checks and test/line budgets passed. Scoped independent P0–P2 review reported no actionable finding in the supplied source. The full SDK API diff did not finish rendering within the local bound; declaration generation and export checks passed. Parent net test growth is **860** lines with **460** allocated above the standard allowance for credential, Goal, dispatch, migration and publication boundaries.

### Compatibility replay and isolated Azure evidence at `456819cbddd4`

- [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44287142431) passed on `456819cbddd4`, including all 11 previously failing native identity cases. This is not a CI claim for the refreshed head.
- Galin replayed published OpenClaw 2026.11.5 state through Doctor and two fresh Gateway starts. Shared SQLite migrated **36→41** and agent SQLite **38→42**. The native binding and three transcript events remained byte-identical. The synthetic placement retained its environment identity and owner epoch; released and candidate builds reclaimed it the same way. PostgreSQL 17.11 passed 14 selected migration/shared-state cases; nine transport and five schema-engine cases also passed.
- An isolated Azure Sandbox ran pinned Codex 0.164.0 with real worker-owned command authentication. A local marker command completed and the real model returned the expected reply. GitHub API and Git HTTPS reads passed separately on the controller. In the live follow-up, a version-pinned App binding with one repository and only `contents: read` and `metadata: read` resolved, and the worker enrolled. The turn stopped before command launch at the [native surface gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/456819cbddd463e2796ecd45509efeb20a194ad7/extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.ts#L525). The session was reclaimed and Crabbox reported zero leases. **Still needed:** repeat with `0a970b700b2c` to verify live worker GitHub commands before and after renewal, authenticated Goal continuation and revocation.
- Deployed `456819cbddd4` as a private runtime package in fresh Azure Container Apps. The installed commit matched; health/readiness were 200, and model listing returned 401 unauthenticated and 200 authenticated with the default agent. This smoke did not establish external worker enrollment.

<details>
<summary>Earlier validation and review history</summary>

- **9/9** worker transport fixture cases and **5/5** real Gateway worker Goal RPC cases. The continuation regression was red on prerequisite `1f67db94064`.
- Synthetic sibling batch **59/59**, representative publication/admission **114/114**, mixed native/synthetic **16/16**, and two complete native/boundary files **59/59** after restoring native identity coverage.
- **43/43** real PostgreSQL, **30/30** frozen-chain SQLite migration, **37/37** dispatch, and **29/29** synthetic current-DDL cases. The older artifact build at `4eabcf3b2463` passed with UI budget warnings; its build and release-state replay are not current-head proof.

</details>

Original implementation: @galiniliev. Review and repairs preserve the original contributor's authorship.

prs.title: fix(cron): owner-targeted automation failure alerts go to the last chat, not the owner
prs.body:
Root cause: `src/cron/service/failure-alerts.ts:241` builds the inherited failure-alert route from the job's primary delivery but drops `target` and `directPolicy`, so `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.ts:488` resolves an owner-targeted job's alert as a plain `channel: "last"` delivery instead of reaching the owner resolver the job's own delivery uses (`src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-target.ts:232`).

Fixes #189947

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: failure alerts for automations with `delivery.target: "owner"` (for example heartbeats migrated by Doctor) go to the job session's last conversation (another DM sender or a group) or the channel's `defaultTo`, or fail with `Delivering to Telegram requires target <chatId>`, while the job's own delivery goes to the owner DM or reports the owner unavailable.

## User Impact

User impact: for owner-targeted automations without an alert-specific route, failure alerts now go where the automation's own delivery goes, the positively identified owner DM.

- No identifiable owner, or `delivery.directPolicy: "block"`: the alert is recorded as Not delivered and the existing in-app fallback is queued, the same outcome as the job's own delivery. That fallback turn stays in the session (`deliver: false`, no external conversation), so it cannot reach the last conversation either.
- Explicit alert routes are unchanged: a `channel`, `to` or `accountId` in the job's `failureAlert`, `delivery.failureDestination` or global `cron.failureAlert` keeps its configured routing.
- Jobs that are not owner-targeted but set `directPolicy: "block"` now honor it for inherited alerts too.
- No config or schema change. A job whose alert newly inherits the owner target counts as a changed destination, so an open incident may alert once more after the cooldown.

## Why This Change Was Made

The alert route now carries `target` and `directPolicy` when it inherits the primary route without an alert-specific selector. The dispatcher and the Gateway alert sender pass both to the existing `resolveDeliveryTarget`; owner resolution itself is unchanged and there is no second resolver.

Thanks @Satoshi-Kusumoto for the report and the fix. The maintainer pass merged current `main`, dropped the test-lines allocation and the shared test-support module, and folded the new test files into one owner-target row in the existing rejected-alert suite plus target/`directPolicy` assertions in the existing Gateway routing case.

Deltas against the merge base: production +29/-3 across `failure-alerts.ts`, `notification-intents.ts`, `notification-dispatch.ts`, `state.ts`, `wake.ts`, `server-cron-notifications.ts`; tests +26/-6; docs +4.

## Evidence

- `src/cron/service.failure-alert-notifications.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.test.ts` (`ocx test`): red on the merge base `f96a979a0f3b` (owner-target row: `expected undefined to be 'owner'`; Gateway routing case: `resolveDeliveryTarget` called without `target`/`directPolicy`), green on this head.
- Telegram Test Server proof (base vs candidate, explicit-route and no-owner controls): base: the alert lands in the group; candidate: it lands in the owner DM, and the job's own delivery goes to the same DM; an explicit `failureAlert.to` still reaches the group; with no identifiable owner the alert is Not delivered with `Owner delivery unavailable (no-route)` and the in-app event is queued in the session, the same result as the job's own delivery. Observed lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189953#issuecomment-7020414143
- Upgrade from v2026.11.6 with an open incident: the released alert is the only one; both candidate starts inside the cooldown stay suppressed and the persisted incident loads unchanged, matching the cooldown note above. Observed lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189953#issuecomment-7021933179

Merge danger: two-way door. A revert restores the old routing; nothing is written or migrated beyond the existing incident signature. Blast radius: failure alerts for cron jobs with `delivery.target: "owner"` or `directPolicy: "block"` and no alert-specific route, on every channel.

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve native sessions during worker recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes retained Codex conversations losing native continuity on worker reconnect or confirmed replacement, with useful exit diagnostics that do not export native stderr.

## User Impact

Retained reconnects require recorded native state. Exact provider-confirmed loss permits a fresh thread seeded from bounded retained history; failed recovery preserves the original binding. A preexisting home from interrupted startup does not prevent the first thread from starting. Refusals explain how to restore retained state or continue separately without deleting the binding. Diagnostics contain bounded enum/numeric facts, not prompts, credentials or raw stderr.

Depends on #201026 at `0a970b700b2c`, targeting `galiniliev/main7-codex-worker-credentials`. Both depend on prerequisite `1f67db94064`. Land prerequisites and parent before retargeting to `main`. Recovery uses existing v41 columns without a new migration. Unknown/dormant state, inspection errors and requested teardown do not authorize fresh-thread recovery. If a replacement is lost before its binding commits, an older binding may require operator recovery; exact predecessor checks do not invent transitive lineage.

## Why This Change Was Made

Verified placement facts supply the current owner and retention policy. Unexpected provider-confirmed destruction records the exact attached predecessor before retirement in the existing transaction. Receipts preserve it through reopen and eligible redispatch. The native binding remains the existing-state authority; replacement commits only after history seeding succeeds.

Startup stderr is drained and classified immediately, but diagnostics wait until input-listener registration queues framed readiness. Aborting startup releases the wait without sending premature data or hanging cleanup. The bounded queue, privacy rules, framing and retained-state admission remain unchanged. The private contracts facade avoids loading heavyweight session runtime during registration.

## Evidence

### Compatibility replay and isolated Azure evidence at `32b0916d5b3f`

- Galin replayed published OpenClaw 2026.11.5 state through Doctor and two fresh Gateway starts. Shared SQLite migrated 36→41 and agent SQLite 38→42. The native binding and all three transcript events remained byte-identical; the synthetic placement retained its environment identity and owner epoch. Released and candidate builds reclaimed the synthetic offline placement the same way.
- Galin enrolled an Azure Sandbox in an isolated Gateway. Two real model turns succeeded, and the second resumed the original native thread. After stopping and restarting Azure, the runner appeared offline. A replacement enrolled for the same session and refused to start a new thread because the retained home was missing. A read-only check after shutdown verified the original binding. No provider-confirmed loss was recorded.
- A follow-up used the published npm **2026.11.6** updater to activate an explicit tarball of `32b0916d5b3f` in a fresh network-isolated fixture. The normal candidate Gateway readiness check passed and the receipt recorded `finished / succeeded`. Shared SQLite migrated **36→41**, `quick_check` passed, and all compared fields of the synthetic placement and worker rows were preserved without creating recovery lineage. This is shipped CLI updater activation on fixture state, not a managed-service restart or preservation of a live Azure placement.
- **193 focused tests** passed across SQLite lineage, Codex binding, migrations and the Crabbox adapter. A separate pinned Codex **0.164.0** probe with synthetic loopback inference showed the original user message and reply present exactly once in a distinct history-seeded thread, including after restart. This is protocol proof, not live provider recovery.
- Deployed `32b0916d5b3f` as a private runtime package in fresh Azure Container Apps. Installed commit matched; health and readiness returned 200. Model listing returned 401 unauthenticated and 200 authenticated with the default agent. This smoke did not establish external worker enrollment.
- [CI at `32b0916d5b3f`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44287145206) passed the previously failing Codex framing E2E and was red on pnpm portability and the memory descriptor probe; both signatures also appear in [an earlier run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44280126105). The refreshed stack passed targeted environment, App admission and transport tests, extension typecheck and both test budgets. Previous-head deployment and updater results are not current-head hosted CI claims.

**Remaining live proof:** Crabbox’s Azure retained-resource inspection does not establish exact unexpected destruction. Missing or offline observations must not be promoted to confirmed loss. Proving automatic history-seeded replacement on Azure needs an authoritative provider signal for the exact retained resource. Live placement preservation across update remains separate from the offline updater replay.

<details>
<summary>Earlier validation and review history</summary>

- **8/8 broker-backed provider-loss cases** passed: reopen, failed-spare retry, redispatch and ambiguous-loss refusal. Removing the producer's loss argument caused the intended failure. **22/22** placement projection cases and **141/141** guidance/docs/provider cases passed.
- [Earlier hosted startup failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44280126105/job/134721795749) was reproduced in two native startup cases. Fixed native and diagnostics suites passed **6/6**. The isolated Gateway/paired-node test passed with a pinned binary and synthetic inference, covering exact worker selection, resume, cancellation and cleanup. Gateway Goal RPC cases passed **5/5**.
- Parent proof includes **43/43** real PostgreSQL, **30/30** frozen-chain SQLite migration and **37/37** dispatch cases. Earlier API/build evidence is pinned to `a7a7984462ea` and `4eabcf3b2463` (the latter with UI budget warnings). Child test growth is **856** lines with **456** allocated above the standard allowance. Earlier hosted review at `69253f04630a` confirmed the private-doc and refusal-guidance findings addressed.

</details>

Original implementation: @galiniliev. The replay preserves the original contributor's authorship.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: test: consolidate redundant coverage (198796, part 1)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preserves distinct current-main regression coverage while retaining the existing test-consolidation scope for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198737. This is a fix-only update of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198950; it is not merged.

## User Impact

No production behavior change. Five suites are restored exactly from current main, their test selection is retained, and one unused Telegram test helper is removed with its deleted consumer.

## Current Head and Scope

Published head: `08d5c11ea9ad922a45ea5fce18d0efa81088ecf0`. Frozen main/base: `2435c1faa791de766688ba27ca7a14a92e30b7e4`. Prior published head: `ba2a3c02b3e60ff69e5660cc576373848365ca1c`.

**35 suites and one 44-line orphan helper deleted; +79/-33106; 33027 net lines removed; 33185 changed lines across 58 paths. Production source delta: 0.**

The final test delta is rebased onto the frozen main. Nine modify/delete conflicts and the package/selector conflicts were resolved only within the owned test scope. Windows script resolution preserves every current-main token except the deleted state-ownership test. Existing fixture corrections and historical test measurements remain intact.

## Current-main Retentions

| Suite | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| `src/sessions/session-controller.watchdog.test.ts` | Retains current late-assessment cancellation and watchdog ownership assertions. |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-permissions.test.ts` | Retains same-session background effects, restricted sender, cross-session and revoked-before-write cases plus unrelated maintenance. |
| `src/gateway/session-utils-store-lookup.test.ts` | Retains first-database discovery and physical-store read ownership assertions. |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-cards.test.tsx` | Retains prepared failures, original execution receipt navigation and current display assertions. |
| `ui/src/e2e/chat-run-lifecycle.e2e.test.ts` | Current CI inventory explicitly names it as the non-recording behavior keeper for the dedicated Mantis workflow. |

All twelve self-keepers in the manifest, including the seven earlier retentions, match frozen main byte-for-byte. Other changed deletion candidates contain fixture or wording updates: GC tests capture the existing worker context and freeze timing; Control UI text uses the web-app name; attributed identity selects the activity summary; warm boot updates its expected module count. Those changes add no distinct coverage requiring another retention in this repair.

## Evidence and Limits

- Native source admission and exact-main checkout completed. The normal commit hook passed formatting and both staged-content scans, then failed because the AGENTS-size command preloads absent local dependencies. Used the documented `CONTRIBUTING.md` iterative-commit `--no-verify` exception for this signed commit after equivalent checks passed: canonical private-literal scan, cached markdownlint-cli2 0.24.0 on the changed doc, AGENTS size (27 files), line-cap ratchet (15 changed source files), scoped formatting, syntax, JSON and whitespace. No hook settings or dependencies changed.
- Whitespace, scoped oxfmt, JSON and syntax checks passed. Manifest covers all 36 deleted paths; all named keepers exist. No resolved relative import/mock points to a deleted path. Cross-tranche manifest obligations were checked.
- The only retained deleted-path literal is historical measurement in `test/scripts/fixtures/ci-measured-compact-jobs.json`; its recorded source revision is unchanged.
- `extensions/telegram/src/draft-stream.api.test-helpers.ts` has exactly one importing suite on frozen main: deleted `draft-stream.test.ts`. No surviving importer remains. Its current blob is 44 lines.
- Local dependencies are absent in the native checkout. No install, runtime test, typecheck or build was run; fresh exact-head CI is pending. Prior-head results below are historical evidence only, not proof for this head.
- The previous UI failure was attributed by matching executed-main evidence; no assertion, timeout or production fix is claimed here.

## File-to-Keeper Manifest

Tracked manifest: `test/scripts/coverage-consolidation/recut-198796-a.tsv`. It has 48 rows: 12 self-keepers, 35 suite deletions and one orphan helper deletion. Original rank provenance is retained; removed-line counts reflect the frozen main.

<details>
<summary>Historical previous-head validation</summary>

## Current validation status

**VALIDATED against observed main failures; raw CI and aggregate gate remain FAILURE.** Signed head: `ba2a3c02b3e60ff69e5660cc576373848365ca1c`. [CI attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43651984728/attempts/2) is complete, with no queued or running jobs. Its only failed test surface is [UI shard 2/4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43651984728/job/132631748628); the [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43651984728/job/132634874930) fails solely on that UI group. This is main-equivalent validation, not a claim of a green GitHub gate.

- UI: `chat-cli-history-redaction.e2e.test.ts:119:47` times out after 30 seconds waiting for `.activity-empty`. That exact failing locator is present in [executed-main evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43648056043/job/132610402188) at main `18a62d6ff93428f15b0801ba5efe4ef0452a8f15`. Twenty-one relevant test, owner, style and harness inputs match this head, tested main `3987f958`, and that baseline. The other 22 files in the UI shard passed. No UI assertion, timeout or production source was changed.
- The gate records success for the selected Node test group, core/lint/test-type shards, baseline ratchets, QA smoke, build, docs, Android and PostgreSQL groups. The earlier recovered-artifact, session-event and native-hook failures did not recur in attempt 2. No claim is made that their original causes were established.
- The separate [Darwin tooling attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43651984438/attempts/2) succeeded after the original retained operation-lock failure. Its test and 18 copied inputs match main; a single focused local run also passed. The original kernel/probe cause remains unproven.
- The existing-keeper selection sentinel and Git-family trigger repairs remain in this head. The worker-artifacts helper matches frozen main exactly. No speculative suite restore, production patch, timeout increase or assertion relaxation was made.

No further rerun is requested for this unchanged head. Skipped/cancelled checks are not counted as passing. Ready for Vincent's review; not merged.

</details>

prs.title: fix: stop a failed Git checkout update from claiming data at risk without evidence
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw update` updates a Git checkout in place (the legacy runner, used when the Git release layout is unavailable) and anything fails after its Doctor starts, the run records "data at risk (state-migrated-no-rollback)". The runner sets that mark before Doctor runs and never compares state. So a Doctor that failed before writing anything, missing Control UI assets, or a HEAD check failure all tell the user to keep the Gateway stopped, and `openclaw update repair` then refuses to start it.

## User Impact

A Git checkout update whose Doctor fails without changing state no longer reports data at risk. If the previous checkout can be restored, the updater restores it and starts the previous Gateway, as before. If it cannot be restored (for example a tracked file was edited during the update), the Gateway stays stopped with a true message, and `openclaw update repair` is no longer blocked. A real state change, or a Doctor that reports its own data-risk verdict, still records the mark.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rule: an update records "data at risk" only on positive evidence that state changed and was not verified. An inconclusive read, a timeout or an unknown failure becomes a warning or a true restart-unsafe outcome.

- **Git runner** (`src/infra/update-runner-git.ts`): starting Doctor now records only "restart unsafe: state-migration-started". The CLI already compares pre- and post-activation state schemas after every post-activation failure (`inspectActivatedUpdateState`, and `rollbackFailedUpdate` before any restore). That comparison is the owner of the "state migrated" evidence; the runner's default duplicated it without evidence.
- **Doctor verdict carried** (`runPackageUpdateDoctor`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-package.ts`): the Doctor child writes its own typed `maintenanceRefusal` verdict. The package/Git Doctor runner never read it, and the runner's blanket mark covered it by accident. It now raises `DoctorMaintenanceRefusalError` when a settled Doctor step carries a `data-at-risk` verdict, as the fresh-Doctor path already does. The Git runner records `recovery.dataAtRisk` from it and still reports `doctor-failed`. Lost requester authority or a recording failure keeps its own error and reason.
- **Other consumers of that throw:**
  - The package swap gets a failed verification step and restores the previous package, through the existing `runPackagePostInstallVerification`.
  - Fresh-profile initialization keeps a Doctor refusal a pre-activation `target-state-initialization` refusal, so nothing is marked before activation.
- **Final recovery** (`src/cli/update-cli/update-command-failure-recovery.ts`): the automatic restart was refused only when a data risk was recorded. Without the runner's mark it would have started a candidate whose Doctor failed. It now also refuses `state-migration-started`. Other unsafe reasons (for example `runtime-verification-failed`) still restart, as before; audit entry 14 lists cases where restarting is right.

No new config key, stored field, schema value, JSON field, exit code or permission.

| Situation (in-place Git update, Doctor fails) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| State unchanged, checkout restorable | rolled back; previous Gateway started (the CLI's rollback overwrote the mark) | same |
| State unchanged, checkout rollback refused (tracked file edited) | `dataAtRisk: state-migrated-no-rollback`; "Keep the Gateway stopped: data at risk"; `update repair` refuses forever | no data mark; restart unsafe (`state-migration-started`); Gateway kept stopped; guidance names `openclaw update repair` and `openclaw triage`; repair is not blocked |
| Doctor migrated state, then failed | mark `state-migrated-no-rollback` (blanket) | mark from evidence: the CLI's schema comparison and database restore (unchanged code paths) |
| Doctor child reports `data-at-risk` (e.g. `incomplete-migration`) | blanket `state-migrated-no-rollback` | the child's own reason (`incomplete-migration`), reason `doctor-failed` |
| Unsafe recovery not involving a started Doctor | final recovery restarts | same |

## Evidence

Behavior checked through the real entry point: a Git checkout (dev channel) installed and built in a Docker container with real systemd, a managed Gateway service, and a busy agent-database writer. A real `openclaw update` runs on the legacy runner (the release slot holds a non-link path, so the updater warns and updates in place). The fault is external: the activation Doctor exits 1 at startup while the Gateway is stopped. It writes nothing; a NODE_OPTIONS preload in the update's environment does this, with no product hook. At the same moment a tracked file in the checkout is edited, as an editor or formatter would. Afterwards the cell reverts the edit and runs a plain `openclaw update`.

- **RED on base:** pending (cell queued; this body is updated when it finishes).
- **GREEN on head:** pending.
- **Base, simple case (Doctor fails, checkout clean):** the run is already rolled back on base, with the previous Gateway serving and no mark. This is why the red case needs the refused rollback.
- **Unit and CLI regressions:** red on base production code, green on head. Recordings: [unit red (base)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/47932d9d-6b79-4e14-97c2-446eb1de3acb), [unit green (head 8e7b5d8; later commits only merge main)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6568bf6b-e76a-49ad-8ad3-d2b8ecb7aaaf).
  - `update-runner-git.test.ts` "retains the candidate after migration starts": 5 rows red on base (`dataAtRisk: state-migrated-no-rollback`), all green. The `doctor-data-at-risk` row keeps the child's mark (negative control).
  - `update-command-post-update-recovery.test.ts` "records no data risk when a Git checkout's Doctor fails": a real Git checkout and real `finishUpdate`.
    - `operator-edited`: red on base (`expected 'state-migrated-no-rollback' to be undefined`), green.
    - `restorable`: guard; rolls back on both.
    - `unsafe-without-doctor`: negative control; final recovery still restarts.
  - `update-command-package-doctor.test.ts` "carries a failed Doctor child's own data-risk verdict":
    - `runner` row red on base.
    - `revoked-runner` row red on the first head (which wrapped the authority error).
    - The package-verification, none and deferred rows are guards.
  - `update-command-initialization.test.ts` "pre-activation route": the refusal row is red on base; the uncertain-child row is a guard.
  - `update-command-database-rollback.test.ts` `git` scenario: a candidate Doctor really migrates two databases, then fails with a `data-at-risk` verdict. It still reports `doctor-failed`, and the pre-migration databases are restored.



<details><summary>Mutation table (each guard removed; the named test fails)</summary>

| Mutation | Killed by |
|---|---|
| Runner keeps the blanket pre-Doctor mark (base) | runner "retains the candidate…" (5 rows), CLI `operator-edited` |
| Runner drops the child's typed verdict (`recovery.dataAtRisk = refusal.reason` removed) | runner `doctor-data-at-risk` |
| Runner reports a refusal with a failed step as `unexpected-error` | database-rollback `git` scenario |
| Doctor runner does not carry the verdict | package-doctor `data-at-risk, runner` |
| Doctor runner carries any verdict kind | package-doctor `deferred, runner` |
| Doctor runner wraps an error raised after the child settled | package-doctor `data-at-risk, revoked-runner` |
| Final recovery ignores `state-migration-started` | CLI `operator-edited` (restart attempted) |
| Initialization passes the refusal through | initialization refusal row |
| Initialization swallows other errors | initialization uncertain-child row |

</details>

Checks run on the head:
- Pass: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxfmt and oxlint on touched files, `git diff --check`, `node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs`, `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets`.
- Pass: `test/scripts/update-restart-module-outcome.test.ts`, `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts`.
- Affected update suites through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`: 16 files, 420 tests. The run first flagged five database-rollback fixtures that call `runPackageUpdateDoctor` directly; they now use `try/finally` so their post-Doctor writes still happen, as the real swap does.
- `autoreview` does not run on this machine. An independent reviewer read the diff against the behavior contract:
  - Fixed: a test assertion that failed at the first head, wrapping of authority errors, and a stale rollback reason.
  - Left (below): the inspection catch.

Full raw logs are not attached because the Crabbox artifact store rejected the upload (`http 401`); the decisive excerpts are above.

Base proof was taken at `138482e6517`. `origin/main` then moved to `36681444353`, but the range touches only the Git release runner and a package space test, not these paths, so the reproduction was not rerun.

## Test files audited

All of each touched file was read:
- `update-runner-git.test.ts`: one table's expectations changed.
- `update-command-package-doctor.test.ts`: one table added.
- `update-command-initialization.test.ts`: one table added.
- `update-command-doctor-rollback.test-support.ts`: the Doctor exit code is now a fixture parameter; one table added.
- `update-command-database-rollback.test.ts`: two Doctor fixtures moved into `try/finally`.

No test was removed or skipped.

## Steps still left to a person

None added. When a checkout's rollback is refused, the Gateway stays stopped (as before), and the message names `openclaw update repair`, which re-runs the candidate's Doctor and starts the Gateway, and `openclaw triage` for the agent-assisted route. Before, repair refused forever in that state.

## Not proven / left

- **Inspection catch (audit P0-0):** `inspectActivatedUpdateState` still turns a failed state read into `rollback-state-unverified` for in-place Git updates, because `candidateOpenedState` is always true for that runner. Before this PR the blanket mark hid it. It is now the remaining evidence-free mark on this path, and it is not changed here.
- **Doctor classifier:** `src/commands/doctor-maintenance-inspection.ts` maps `GatewayLockError` to `gateway-state-unverified` and the preflight catch-all to `incomplete-migration`. Those need typed errors at their producers; another PR handles them.
- **Package flow:** it still decides from its own state comparison and does not record the Doctor child's verdict (unchanged).
- **Handoff path:** the handoff helper exits 79 on any unsafe recovery (audit entry 14). This PR does not change that.
- **Killed Doctor (separate defect):** an exploratory cell that SIGKILLed the activation Doctor left the Gateway down. Doctor custody was reported as `active-mutation`, and both repair and the next update failed on a stale artifact lock. Reported separately.

prs.title: fix: let source builds and Git updates finish on 8 GiB machines
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A source build of current `main` does not fit in 8 GiB of memory. In an 8 GiB container with nothing else running, a cold `pnpm build` is OOM-killed in its declaration step, in 3 of 3 runs. That build runs during a Git install, a manual `pnpm build`, and `openclaw update` on a Git checkout when the installed updater is 2026.11.4 or 2026.11.5. The memory goes to the native TypeScript compiler, which #198661 made parallel. The build's memory guard cannot see that memory, because `--max-old-space-size` does not bound a Go child process.

## User Impact

On a host where the build owner caps the build heap (below about 13 GiB of usable memory), the declaration step now runs single-threaded, and a cold build completes in an 8 GiB container. Hosts with more memory keep the parallel pass. Declaration output is the same in both modes.

The margin at 8 GiB is small. With a Gateway and a busy writer in the same 8 GiB container, the update passed, but the container peaked at 7848 MiB (7.66 GiB) of anonymous memory, 344 MiB under its limit, during the build. This PR does not claim that every 8 GiB host can build. When memory is too low, the existing guard refuses before touching anything, and the old build keeps serving; see the negative control below.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **What the parallel pass costs.** At 12 GiB it peaked at 8386 MiB (8.19 GiB) in its cgroup. The single-threaded pass peaked at 6101 MiB (5.96 GiB), and at 8 GiB it was not slower: 1m45s against the parallel pass's 2m15s at 12 GiB.
- **Who already decides memory.** `tsdown-build` sizes the build heap. It grants its uncapped default (12288 MB) only when memory is ample, and it uses the same fact to allow two parallel runtime builds.
- **How the decision reaches the emitter.** `tsdown-build` now hands its frozen budget to every build child in `OPENCLAW_TSDOWN_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB`. `build-all` used to add it, and that duplicate is gone. A small shared module holds the threshold, so both use one rule. The emitter runs the compiler in parallel only when that budget is 12288 MB or more and stable type ordering is on. It never reads Node heap flags or V8's total heap limit.
- **What stays single-threaded.** The Windows default (8192 MB) stays single-threaded. On a large Windows host that costs some speed; the output is identical. A run without the budget (a bare `tsdown`) also stays single-threaded, as before #198661. An explicit `OPENCLAW_TSDOWN_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB` of 12288 or more counts as a statement that memory is ample.

**Which side runs this code.** The build runs the scripts of the tree being built, so the candidate's code decides, under any installed updater.

- **Installed updaters that run the declaration pass:** 2026.11.4 and 2026.11.5. Once a target contains this fix, these published updaters get it.
- **Updaters that skip it:** `v2026.11.6`, `release/2026.11.10` and `main`. Since #189463 they set `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1` for update builds, in both the in-place and the release layout.
- **Where the change also applies:** Git installs and manual `pnpm build`.
- **Release branches:** none needs it. `release/2026.11.10` reverts #198661, and `release/2026.11.6` and `v2026.11.5` predate it.

**What this PR does not change: the build memory guard** (`MEASURED_MIN_TSDOWN_HEAP_MB = 4352`, from #123979). Measured on this base, its floor is too low, not too high:

- A cold build alone is OOM-killed at 5 GiB with the guard's own 4352 MB heap.
- It is also killed at 6 GiB, with the guard's heap or with 4352 MB or 3584 MB.
- It passes at 7 GiB.
- Neither a smaller heap nor four rolldown threads moved the 6 GiB result. The pressure is native memory plus the build's own parent processes, not the heap.

A per-process sample at the moment of the kill at 6 GiB:

| Process | RSS |
|---|---|
| tsdown child | 4.9 GB |
| `build-all` | 869 MB |
| tsdown-build wrapper | 343 MB |
| pnpm | 123 MB |

The guard also counts pnpm's own memory as competing: at 5 GiB alone it computed a 4310 MB heap and refused. Raising the floor would refuse more hosts, and I have no data for hosts with fewer than 16 CPUs. So this is recorded as a follow-up, not changed here.

## Evidence

**Recordings** (cold `pnpm build`, container `memory.max` 8 GiB, no swap, 16 CPUs, nothing else running). Full raw logs are not attached because the artifact store rejected uploads from this machine.

RED, base `eb381dceef2`: `write-unified-entry-dts` fails after 1m4.6s, `oom_kill 1`, `memory.peak` 8192 MiB, 155 s.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0b5e4e9a-2bfb-47d1-af1c-7e93b2ed924d

GREEN, final head `75ddce3266b`: every phase done, `write-unified-entry-dts` 1m46.3s, `oom_kill 0`, `memory.peak` 6993 MiB, 273 s.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40f63ef0-a88f-4b4c-9136-4acafc880377

GREEN, earlier head `5697d27a366` (same reproduction): `oom_kill 0`, `memory.peak` 7327 MiB, 254 s.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb9bf86f-6e5d-422a-9d84-cc14956a6a91

**Isolated build floor** (cold `pnpm build` of the base, alone, 16 CPUs, no swap):

| Limit | Heap | Declaration pass | Result | Wall | Peak anon |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 GiB | guard (7347) | parallel (base) | OOM kill in declarations, 2 of 2 runs | 155-176 s | 8093-8097 MiB (7.9 GiB) |
| 12 GiB | guard (11520) | parallel (base) | ok | 302 s | 8386 MiB (8.19 GiB) |
| 8 GiB | guard (7424) | single-threaded (this PR) | ok | 273 s | 6473 MiB (6.32 GiB) |
| 7 GiB | guard (6400) | single-threaded | ok | 259 s | 6641 MiB (6.49 GiB) |
| 6 GiB | guard, 4352, 3584 | single-threaded | OOM kill in tsdown runtime phase | 70-75 s | 5888-5985 MiB (5.75-5.84 GiB) |
| 5 GiB | forced 4352 | single-threaded | OOM kill in tsdown runtime phase | 58 s | 4915 MiB (4.80 GiB) |
| 4.5 GiB | forced 3840 | single-threaded | OOM kill in tsdown runtime phase | 53 s | 4596 MiB (4.49 GiB) |

Measured floor alone: between 6 and 7 GiB.

**`openclaw update` cells** (Docker update matrix, managed Gateway serving, writer at 8 MiB/s on a 512 MiB agent database, Git tag on the beta channel):

| Cell | Installed, target | Memory | Result | Update wall | Build | Outage | Peak anon |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| In-place, head | 2026.11.5 to `5697d27` | 8 GiB | ok, serves `5697d27` | 1125 s | 497 s (declarations 4m26s, single-threaded) | 272 s | 7848 MiB (7.66 GiB), no OOM kill |
| Release layout, head | `main` `ea74900` to `5697d27` | 8 GiB | ok (conversion plus target) | 414 s | 144 s + 133 s (no declaration pass) | 6.8 s + 13.3 s | 7878 MiB (7.69 GiB), no OOM kill |
| In-place, head (repeat) | 2026.11.5 to `8040c3c` | 8 GiB | ok | 1058 s | 510 s | 249 s | 7617 MiB (7.44 GiB), no OOM kill |
| Negative control | 2026.11.5 to `5697d27` | 6 GiB | guard refused before removing anything; still serving 2026.11.5, `readyz` true | 96 s | refused at 9 s | 0 | 5865 MiB (5.73 GiB) |
| In-place, base | 2026.11.4 to `eb381dc` | 8 GiB | build passed (423 s, parallel, peak 7953 MiB (7.77 GiB)); the update then failed in the 2026.11.4 updater's own SQLite validation (known, unrelated) | 631 s | 423 s | 0 | 7953 MiB (7.77 GiB) |

Notes on the cells:
- **Outage timing.** The 272 s outage happens during activation (Git import 126 s, Doctor 63 s), after the build has finished. Earlier 12 GiB and 8 GiB cells from 2026.11.4/2026.11.5 to `release/2026.11.10` had 203 s and 179 s outages.
- **Negative control output.** The refusal message the update printed: "The resolved OpenClaw build heap is 2796MB, and a full build needs 4352MB ... Stopping before any build output is removed." The run record ends `preflight-no-good-commit` with the next action `openclaw triage`.
- **Base-target cell.** It shows the parallel pass can also squeeze through at 8 GiB under a Gateway. Isolated, it failed every time.

**Tests**
- `test/scripts/native-declaration-boundary.test.ts`: one test now compiles a 16-module fixture in fresh Node processes, setting the planner budget (`OPENCLAW_TSDOWN_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB`) per case:
  - without stable ordering at a 12288 MB budget;
  - with stable ordering at a capped 7424 MB budget;
  - with stable ordering at a 12287 MB budget, at a 7424 MB budget with an inherited `--max_old_space_size=12288`, and with no budget but `--max-old-space-size=12288`;
  - with stable ordering at a 12288 MB budget.
- It asserts that each mode is deterministic and that the capped and uncapped stable passes emit identical declarations and maps. Off Windows, a recording wrapper around the fixture's real compiler shows which config the compiler received: single-threaded for the first three, parallel for the last.
- Red on the base emitter: the 7424 MB case receives a parallel config. Red on two earlier versions of this PR: the total-heap check admitted the 12287 MB case, and the flag-reading check admitted the underscored-alias case. Green on the head.
- `test/scripts/tsdown-build.test.ts` (adjacent owner guard): the tsdown child's env now carries the budget. It is `4352` for a capped plan, `12288` on an unconstrained host and `8192` for the Windows default. These assertions fail on the base.
- `test/scripts/build-all.test.ts`: unchanged; its existing child-env assertions still pass with the duplicate removed.
- Run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/tsdown-build.test.ts test/scripts/build-all.test.ts test/scripts/native-declaration-boundary.test.ts`: 163 passed, 3 skipped.
- Also run: `pnpm tsgo:scripts`; the root tooling typecheck; `pnpm lint:scripts`; oxfmt; `git diff --check`; the baseline ratchets, all ok. The test-lines ratchet is +68.
- `pnpm tsgo:test:root` failed on 4 unrelated `release-*` test files inherited from main at the time; that has not been rechecked on the current head.

**Audit and review**
- The touched test file was audited in full. The two-case determinism `it.each` was replaced by the single test above. Its parallel case ran in-process under the test runtime (Bun), where the heap fact does not exist, so it could no longer select parallel mode.
- The new test keeps the compiles and equality checks on Windows and adds a cross-mode equality check. No other case changed.
- An independent read-only review found nothing blocking. Its should-fix items:
  - cross-mode equality: added;
  - Windows coverage: kept;
  - Windows stays single-threaded, and the threshold is coupled to the owner's default: both documented in the code comment.
- `autoreview` does not run on this machine.
- Second independent review (final design): nothing blocking. It asked that `tsdown-build` export the budget itself and share the threshold; both are done. It also asked to note that Windows stays single-threaded and that the threading check does not run on Windows (the compiles and equality checks do).
- ClawSweeper round 1 (on `8040c3c`): overall C, proof B, patch C. Its four findings, all fixed:
  - the total-heap check admitted a capped 12287 MB budget: fixed (the final head reads the planner's budget), with a test case;
  - temporary paths inside shell quotes in the test wrapper: the wrapper now derives its paths from `$0`;
  - wrong arithmetic in the comment: corrected;
  - `release/2026.11.6` listed as running declarations: corrected; `v2026.11.6` skips them.

- ClawSweeper round 3 (on the final head `75ddce3`): overall B, proof B, patch B, "patch is correct". Its one finding asked this description to name the planner budget as the threading input, and it now does.
- ClawSweeper round 2 (on `27dc770`): overall D, proof D, patch C. Its finding was that an inherited `--max_old_space_size=12288` alias survives the planner's rewrite and admitted the parallel pass. Fixed by reading the planner's budget, with a test case. It also said the full-build proof predated the final logic; the final-head recording above answers that.

**Head.** The update cells ran on `5697d27` and `8040c3c`. The final head differs only in how the emitter learns the admitted budget. At the guard-computed budget in these cells (below 12288 MB) every version chooses the same single-threaded mode. Main merges since then touch no build code; the release-layout runner change (#201917) belongs to the installed updater, not the target build.

## Not proven

- **Repeatability at 8 GiB.** Two in-place runs passed, peaking at 7848 MiB (7.66 GiB) and 7617 MiB (7.44 GiB). Runs with an extra 1 GiB resident and at 12 GiB were done after merge; see the headroom comment on this PR. 8 GiB works in these cells but is marginal.
- **Fewer CPUs.** Only checked after merge at 5 GiB on 4 CPUs, where the build is still OOM-killed.
- **Windows and real systemd.** Not run on Windows, on bare-metal systemd hosts, or as a Gateway-initiated update.
- **The guard's floor.** It is stale (it admits builds that are then killed between about 5 and 6.5 GiB of memory limit). That is not changed here.

Steps left to a person: none for builds that fit. When memory truly is too low, the update ends with the old build serving and a recorded failure. The run record names `openclaw triage` as the agent route. Adding memory cannot be automated.



_Correction: peak-memory figures in this description are exact MiB from cgroup `memory.stat` (`anon`, whole container). An earlier version divided MiB by 1000 and labeled the result GiB._

prs.title: fix: avoid rereading compacted history before replies
prs.body:
Related: #184750

## What Problem This Solves

Preparing a reply in a long compacted conversation can still decode all of its old tool results before choosing the model's context. That work delays model dispatch even when compaction has already removed those results from the model's view.

## User Impact

Eligible current, bounded conversation reads skip payloads before the retained compaction window. Context bytes, ordering, tool-result omissions and checkpoints remain unchanged. No migration, configuration change or new cache is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model-context reader now borrows the existing active-position, identity and dependency-facts owners to establish a safe retained window before running its unchanged native navigation SQL. It retains the full reader for fences, historical anchors, native seeds/full-message reads, resets, missing or stale facts, prefix background sources/placements, prompt restarts, and inherited model state it cannot safely skip. The certified window initializes the existing navigation snapshot with write receipts for all active prefix pages; repeated reads retain warm reuse, and semantic rewrites retain canonical invalidation.

This supersedes #184750 with credit to Wesley (@ensignwesley), whose proposal identified the compacted-history opportunity. The replacement preserves the existing absolute byte-cut policy; uncompacted histories still need exact prefix byte costs. It does not pursue a backfill or stored-facts change.

## Evidence

The real SQLite writer/worker differential suite compares complete serialized context against the unchanged full reader across compactions, resets, branches, pending/placed results, prompt restarts, missing/stale facts, fences, anchors, omissions, checkpoints and synthetic tool-result provenance. The bounded-work regression fails on the base (245 projected navigation rows versus fewer than 20) and passes with this change. The equal-stored-facts byte-cut counterexample also retains its original results.

Writer-built synthetic measurements with real host admission, two rotating sessions, six calls per run, separate timing/read/allocation runs and A/B/B/A controls:

| Compacted prefix | CPU/call before → after | SQLite logical bytes/call before → after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 turns | 68.0 → 12.6 ms | 15.71 → 1.98 MB |
| 4,000 turns | 588.6 → 40.9 ms | 143.43 → 5.12 MB |

At 4,000 turns this is 14.4× less CPU, 28× fewer read bytes and 61% less sampled allocation. A/A CPU differs by 2.2%; repeated byte counters match exactly. The output is identical (86 events / 731,248 bytes). Statement count rises from 6 to 10. EXPLAIN uses existing keyed session/sequence paths; no table-wide scan. These are worker-owner measurements on macOS/APFS, not production physical-I/O or whole-Gateway claims.

Warm reuse is preserved: 2,000-call A/B/B/A controls average 1.56 → 1.54 ms CPU, with identical five statements and 889,442 logical read bytes per call. The admitted regression asserts zero navigation projection on repeat and re-certification after a prefix rewrite.

The 15-case admitted differential/regression suite and all selected consumer suites pass (113 tests total), including zero navigation projections on repeat reads and full fallback after a prefix rewrite. Local Chromium history-settlement browser tests (2), history-recovery E2E tests (3), and production/full-tree unused-file scans pass. Final Codex review of the admitted snapshot implementation is clean. The complete changed-code check passed its production/type/format/dead-export/boundary gates. Its one benchmark-only Promise-executor lint issue was corrected; targeted lint and the final `pnpm check:changed --base 044b7b5` follow-up gate pass.

Production grows by 205 lines to certify the compacted window while retaining the exact full-reader fallback; the helper is a focused sibling because the accessor was already at its line cap. No new state or duplicate projection implementation is introduced.

ClawSweeper identified a missing trusted-wrapper runtime closure. Its existing inventory test reproduced four missing modules; adding those four paths makes the test pass. The correction is separately Codex-reviewed and changes no trust or runtime policy.

The final worker-probe suppression inventory entry records its verified `Reflect.apply` receiver binding; all 14 guard tests pass, and the two-line inventory correction has an independent clean Codex review.

Earlier CI exposed two independently reproduced main regressions: #201333 (`f5d35bc826f39361035322567d4c70adefd14cc5`) removed the preparation `mkdir` awaited by two fault tests; #201790 (`f7235a87b27fa205703785f6e83b690b392291e3`) removed the actor-command wrapper whose diagnostic spans the inactive-input test still required. The former reproduces on the original exact parent, the latter on CI's newer exact main parent. They are recorded as main regressions, not ignored failures.

An interrupted baseline runner was recovered with a single-job retry. That retry exposed this PR's test-line budget excess. The fixtures now share message/header setup and oracle calls, preserving all 15 scenarios and assertions within the existing 400-line allowance, with no allocation record or configuration change. The final bounded-work test still fails on the exact parent with 245 projected rows versus fewer than 20. The test-only consolidation leaves production and benchmark measurements unchanged. The complete changed-code run passed every check except one cursor-probe TypeScript overload; restoring the typed native invocation resolves that error, and its targeted typecheck and formatting pass.

prs.title: fix(workboard): write tools return the whole card with all its comments and history on every call
prs.body:
Closes #162498

## What Problem This Solves

Every Workboard write tool (`workboard_comment`, `workboard_move`, `workboard_heartbeat`, `workboard_release`, `workboard_claim`, `workboard_proof`, ...) answers with the whole card: notes, every past comment, events and proof. An agent that keeps a card current pays for that history again on each call, and the result grows with every comment. #162498 measured 21 KB on average per `workboard_comment` call, and #180394 measured ~28 KB per heartbeat.

## User Impact

Write tools now answer with the same compact card summary `workboard_list` uses (id, title, status, claim state, links, diagnostics), plus the id of what they added: `commentId`, `attachmentId` or `proofId`. `workboard_claim` still returns its token. `workboard_read` still returns the full card. Agents that read history from a write result need `workboard_read` instead. Nothing in the repo did that: the dispatcher, worker prompts and Control UI use the store or the read path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Most write tools share one result helper, which returned the full redacted card. This PR changes that helper's contract once, keeping the card nested under `card` so its status is never mistaken for the tool result's. The writes outside the helper (create, link, claim, proof, decompose) get the same summary. `summarizeCard` moves next to the helper unchanged, so list and write results share one shape.

## Evidence

**Live, before and after:** throwaway Gateways, tools called through `POST /tools/invoke`. A card gets 30 comments of 700 characters, then each tool runs once on it. The numbers are `details` JSON characters.

| Tool, on a card with 30 comments | 2026.11.5 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `workboard_comment` | 27,145 | 222 (`card`, `commentId`) |
| `workboard_move` | 27,277 | 171 |
| `workboard_claim` | 27,719 | 341 (token still returned) |
| `workboard_heartbeat` | 27,760 | 292 |
| `workboard_proof` | 28,029 | 343 (`proofId` still returned) |
| `workboard_release` | 27,967 | 171 |
| `workboard_read` (control) | 32,706 | 32,706, all 31 comments |

Tested on `3b0d6fc24e8`.

- Tests: new `tools.compact-results.test.ts` checks that comment, move, heartbeat and release results stay small and leave out metadata and notes while read keeps them (fails on main, passes here). `tools.test.ts` assertions that read history from write results now read it from the store. 8 workboard test files pass, and lint and typecheck pass.
- Review: autoreview (claude), `origin/main..3b0d6fc24e8`, no P0–P2 findings, clean.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

Credit: @-mentions are left out on purpose. #162498 (21 KB on average per comment call) and #180394 (heartbeat/release, ~28 KB per heartbeat) both measured this. A third measurement on a real deployment over 3 days, 184 agent sessions: `workboard_comment` results over 12 KB totalled 2.32M characters in 92 calls; the largest single result was 35,302 characters, 24.7K of them past comments and 5K events.

Alternatives considered: a per-tool `compact` flag or a comment-only patch would leave move, heartbeat, release and the rest echoing the card. Trimming comments inside the full card would still send notes, events, proof and attempts. The list summary already exists and is what agents use to choose work, so writes reuse it.

Repro script: creates a card through `/tools/invoke`, adds the comments, then prints each write tool's result size, with `workboard_read` as the control.

</details>

prs.title: fix(codex): keep a remote turn running across a gateway restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a Gateway is stopped or restarted gracefully while a Codex agent is running a command in an app-server the Gateway only connects to (over a WebSocket or Unix socket), the Gateway interrupts that turn on the way down. The command is killed, and the restarted Gateway's recovery input then runs it again. After a crash the same turn keeps running and the restarted Gateway waits for it, so a clean shutdown currently does more damage than a crash.

## User Impact

A Codex turn in a remote app-server now survives a graceful Gateway stop or restart when its session will be resumed, as it already survives a crash: the command finishes once, and after the restart the agent continues from its result instead of running it a second time. Everything else is interrupted exactly as before: turns in sessions that restart recovery does not resume, turns in an app-server the Gateway started itself, turns in a worker-hosted app-server, turns in a [sandboxed session](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/config-agents/sandbox) (an OpenClaw agent sandbox, `agents.*.sandbox.mode`, whose commands the Gateway admits; Codex's own `appServer.sandbox` policy does not count), turns waiting on the stopping Gateway (an approval, a question, or an OpenClaw tool call), user Stop, and session resets.

## Why This Change Was Made

A graceful stop aborts every active run with the restart abort reason, and the Codex harness answered every abort with `turn/interrupt` plus background-terminal cleanup. The same reason is also used by session resets, lifecycle-generation eviction and cron cancellation while the Gateway keeps running, so the reason alone cannot say "the next Gateway will pick this turn up".

The shutdown already decides, per session, whether to write a restart marker, and it does so before it aborts anything. This change carries that decision on the abort itself:

- restart-marker persistence reports each committed marker as agent plus session key (under `session.scope: "global"` every agent's main session has the key `global`);
- `stopSession` accepts a per-session reason, asked with the agent and key of each operation or input;
- the shutdown gives a marked session a resumable restart abort (the same restart abort code, plus a `resumesAfterRestart` flag) and every other session, including one whose agent is unknown at the stop, the plain restart abort.

The agent harness runtime surface exports `isAgentRunResumableRestartAbortReason`. The Codex abort listener skips the interrupt only when all of these hold:

- the reason is resumable;
- the app-server transport is not `stdio` (the Gateway did not spawn it);
- the attempt is not worker-hosted (that worker owns a disposable app-server);
- the turn's commands are not admitted by the Gateway (a sandboxed session: the Gateway would end those commands anyway);
- the turn has no open server request to this Gateway (nobody else could answer it).

The attempt still ends as a restart abort. Its cleanup releases the thread as for any other ended attempt, which sends one `thread/unsubscribe` and nothing else to the app-server. For a loaded thread the app-server handles that request the same way as the disconnect after a crash: `unsubscribe_connection_from_thread` and `remove_connection` (`codex-rs/app-server/src/thread_state.rs`) both only drop the connection from the thread's subscribers, and a thread unloads only once it has no subscribers and no active turn (`UnloadingState::unloading_target`, `request_processors/thread_lifecycle.rs`). Upstream pins this in `thread_unsubscribe_during_turn_keeps_turn_running` (`tests/suite/v2/thread_unsubscribe.rs`), in both 0.164.0 and 0.169.0, the version this repo pins.

The next Gateway's existing recovery path adopts the thread: a restart input for an adopted thread whose turn is still active waits for it (1 s polls, up to 120 s), then continues from the thread's result; past 120 s the reply says the work is still running. No config or protocol field is added.

Docs: one paragraph in `docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md` and a short note in `docs/concepts/session.md`.

## Evidence

Focused tests on a non-hosted runner, on this branch merged with main `64416d16a2c`.

Red on main `0eb6488cd3c` (with the new tests) and green with this change:

- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.activation.test.ts`, `Gateway shutdown` block: a resumable restart abort of a turn in a WebSocket app-server ends the attempt aborted, and the only request it sends after the turn is accepted is `thread/unsubscribe` (no `turn/interrupt`, no background-terminal request). On main the same case sends the interrupt and the terminal cleanup.
- `src/gateway/session-restart-resume.test.ts`: marker persistence reports exactly the resumable conversations, with their agent. Cron, scheduled automation, ACP/external-owner and locked-harness sessions are not reported. Two agents on the literal `global` key with one marked: only that agent's session gets the resumable reason, and a lookup without an agent gets the plain one.
- `src/sessions/session-controller.stop.test.ts`: a restart Stop of an operation, and of a claimed input, gives the per-session reason only to its own session. Two operations on `global` under two agents: only the agent the reason was asked for gets it.
- `src/gateway/server.agent-execution-shutdown.test.ts`: through a real Gateway `stop` and `restart`, the running root session's run is aborted with the resumable restart reason.
- `src/agents/run-termination.test.ts`: the resumable abort is still a restart abort (stop reason `restart`). Plain restart aborts, direct aborts and drain refusals are not resumable.

Green on main and with this change (the cases that stay as before): an interrupt is still sent for an app-server the Gateway started (`stdio`), a user Stop of a remote turn, a plain restart abort of a remote turn (a session reset, or the shutdown of a session that gets no marker), and a remote turn with an OpenClaw tool call open. The decision itself is the pure function `keepsCodexTurnAtGatewayStop`; a table test keeps a resumable remote turn and flips each of its five conditions (plain restart reason, `stdio`, worker-hosted, process admission, an open request), and each flip gives the interrupt; turning any one condition off in the function fails exactly its own row. Unchanged and green: `thread-lifecycle.adoption.test.ts` ("waits without interrupting a remote turn that survived the Gateway restart"), which covers the next Gateway's side.

Also clean on the same runner: `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files, and `pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test` and `tsgo:core:test`.

The first CI run on this branch failed one case, `test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts` "restart markers survive graceful shutdown (suspend/reopen and blocked store: false)": the shared store's clean-close receipt was `checkpoint-incomplete` (WAL checkpoint `blocked`). The same failure happens without this change. Run 20 times each the way `checks-node-changed` runs the file (its shard script, Bun runtime policy, two Vitest workers, four CPUs), the case failed 2 of 20 on this branch and 2 of 20 on its CI base `f96a979a0f3` alone, with the same receipt; the sibling case (`blocked store: true`) failed 1 of 20 on each, the same way. The idle close of an agent database during shutdown runs one `TRUNCATE` checkpoint with `busy_timeout` 0 on a worker thread, and it can meet another connection on the same file that still holds the write lock or a read snapshot. This change does not alter the order or the set of writes on that path: a marked session's run gets a different abort reason object with the same restart code, and only the Codex harness reads the new flag. A fix for the flaky close is a separate change.

The problem was seen on a production-shaped test install with the Codex app-server in its own workload. A graceful Gateway stop during a long command interrupted the turn, and the resume ran the command again. After a hard kill at the same point the turn kept running, and the resume answered from its result.

There is no live trace of this change yet. It will come from the same kind of install once it takes this change: a graceful Gateway restart during a long command, then a check that the command ran once and that the resume answered from its result.

## Risks

- **A remote turn now outlives a graceful stop, as it already outlives a crash.** A supervisor replacement and a final stop look the same to the Gateway: both arrive as SIGTERM and both write restart markers. So after a final `openclaw gateway stop`, a marked session's remote turn also keeps running until it ends by itself, which is what a hard kill does today; its result is used only if a Gateway starts again and resumes the session. To end that work, stop the agent turn first (user Stop still interrupts), or stop the app-server.
- Sessions the shutdown does not mark are interrupted as today: cron runs, sub-agents, externally owned, archived or incognito sessions, a session changed during shutdown, and a completed reply. A marker write still in flight when the persistence deadline passes also gets the plain reason and is interrupted as today.
- Some refusals happen only when the next Gateway starts: a changed restart scope, a recovery admission failure (principal, target, workspace or session event), and a parked or unreachable yield. The old Gateway cannot know about these, so those turns behave as after a crash. The remote turn finishes on its own and nobody reads its result. Before this change it was interrupted.
- Requests to this Gateway. A turn with an open request to the stopping Gateway is still interrupted, and on that path the Gateway answers its pending requests as an abort does today. A request the turn sends after the stopping Gateway has let it go is not left unanswered: until the connection closes, it is declined (approvals, questions, elicitations) or failed (OpenClaw tool calls), through the aborted handler or `defaultServerRequestResponse` (`server-requests.ts`). After a crash nothing answers it. Requests through the native hook relay, and approvals or questions without this turn's id, are not counted as open requests, so they do not keep the interrupt.
- Unlike a crash, the kept path sends one `thread/unsubscribe` before the connection closes. For a loaded thread with a running turn the app-server treats it like a disconnect (see above); this rests on reading the app-server source and its own test, not on a live trace.
- Turns placed on a worker environment get their abort over a channel that only carries the string `restart`, which is rebuilt into a plain restart abort, so they are interrupted as today.
- `isAgentRunResumableRestartAbortReason` is a new export on `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`. The SDK surface baseline is acknowledged at release.

prs.title: fix: show when status skips plugin compatibility checks
prs.body:
Closes #202007

## What Problem This Solves

When I run `openclaw status` or `openclaw status --deep` while troubleshooting a plugin, the overview shows “Plugin compatibility: none” even though the command skipped that check. The output makes a skipped check look like a clean result.

## User Impact

Both commands now display `not checked (use --all)`. Running `openclaw status --all` collects the compatibility diagnostics and reports the result.

## Why This Change Was Made

I kept a skipped check distinct from a completed check with zero notices. This preserves the existing lightweight status path and gives users the command that actually runs the check.

Thanks to @anmol0b for reporting the behavior and to the ClawSweeper review for suggesting the `--all` hint.

## Evidence

- On Windows, I exercised the built CLI against a separate loopback Gateway before and after the patch. Both regular and deep status changed from `none` to `not checked (use --all)`. The full status still reported a clean result for the same empty-plugin configuration.
- The new renderer regression failed on the base and passed with this fix. The five status suites passed all 56 tests locally in 202 seconds. The changed test file passed all 17 tests in the commands-light lane, which took 119 seconds on this Windows checkout, mostly in setup and transforms. CI timing is pending.
- The scoped runtime build, changed-file formatting and lint checks, and core type check passed. The wider runtime-and-UI build hit the Control UI asset budgets on the base. Hosted CI will provide broader coverage.
- I reviewed the changed scan and rendering paths locally. The shared autoreview tool was unavailable in this checkout.

## Hosted review and CI

ClawSweeper stopped at the input scan. I matched the reported base blob to an existing database-rendering test fixture and verified that the affected lines are unchanged in this patch. Could a maintainer confirm whether the fixture can be qualified for review? [Scanner run](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/44608391367)

The exact-head CI run still requires approval before it can execute. [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44606602960)
