prs.body:
Refs #197515

## What Problem This Solves

After updating, the Codex plugin can stay in `pending-state-migration`, so Codex agents and native child workers fail with `owner-plugin-degraded`. Running `openclaw doctor --fix` or `openclaw update repair` again never clears it. This happens when a long-lived session was reset after it had native Codex child work recorded: the reset keeps the session ID but gives the session a new lifecycle revision, while the old assignments have none.

## User Impact

User impact: Doctor now retires those leftover Codex child assignments from the earlier session lifecycle, the Codex data upgrade completes, and the Codex plugin becomes available again after the update (or after one `openclaw doctor --fix` on an affected install). No data or settings other than the stale assignment rows change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor's Codex native assignment repair kept any assignment whose lifecycle revision appeared on only one side and reported a recoverable warning. Any plugin migration warning keeps that plugin's deferred migration pending, which keeps the plugin unavailable, so the warning never cleared.

Native recovery itself only restores assignments whose owner revision equals the current session's: `restore` in `native-subagent-assignment-inventory.ts` and `readCurrentNativePendingAssignments` in `session-binding-record.ts` both require strict equality, and the runtime owner takes the revision from the current session entry. A reset or message cut keeps the session ID and mints a fresh random revision, and revisions are never reissued. A one-sided assignment can therefore never be delivered again, exactly like an assignment with a different revision, which Doctor already retires. Doctor now uses the same rule: keep only equal revisions (including both absent on legacy owners, the #186506 case) and retire the rest together with their matching submission receipts. Unknown requesters, malformed rows and conflicting facts are still preserved with warnings.

Adopting the new revision instead was rejected: that would let native recovery deliver pre-reset child results into the reset conversation, which resets are meant to stop. Native Codex delivers the child completion to its own parent thread in-process (`maybe_start_completion_watcher` in `codex-rs/core/src/agent/control.rs`), so retiring the OpenClaw-side assignment only drops OpenClaw's re-delivery bookkeeping.

Production LOC: −14 (`native-assignment-repair.ts` +11/−25). No schema, persisted-shape or SDK change.

## Evidence

- Regression tests `retires assignments whose assignment lacks the lifecycle revision` and `... session lacks the lifecycle revision`: fail on base with `Preserved Codex assignments with unknown lifecycle evidence in session:...`, pass with the fix (19/19 in `native-assignment-repair.test.ts`).
- Live upgrade lanes on a Crabbox AWS Linux box (npm global installs, systemd Gateway, official `@openclaw/codex` served from a local registry for the candidate builds). Each lane creates `agent:main:main` through a real `sessions.reset` RPC (the session gets a lifecycle revision) and seeds one Codex binding whose native assignment owner has none, the shape reported in #197515:

| Lane | Update | Codex after update |
|---|---|---|
| 2026.11.4 → published 2026.11.5 | succeeded, readyz 200 | `configured-unavailable: pending-state-migration`, 1 Codex migration warning, assignment kept |
| 2026.11.5 → current main (1680f545048) | succeeded, readyz 200 | same: pending, warning, assignment kept |
| 2026.11.5 → this fix | succeeded, readyz 200 | activated, no Codex migration warning, assignment retired |
| stuck 2026.11.5 install: `doctor --fix` retry, then → this fix | Doctor retry: still pending; update succeeded, readyz 200 | activated, no warning, assignment retired |

Not covered: a real Codex model turn, which needs OpenAI credentials the box does not have. The activation state shown is the gate behind the reported `owner-plugin-degraded` worker failures.
- Reviews: autoreview scoped-clean (P0–P2); independent read-only Codex review found no P0–P2 defects.

prs.title: fix(gateway): settle a lost yielded child after restart so its parent wakes
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

After a Gateway restart, a parent session can be parked waiting on a child (`sessions_yield`). If that wait cannot survive the restart, startup fails the child: `recordRestartYieldFailure` writes the visible error "The Gateway restarted, but the child completion this run was waiting for can no longer arrive…". That only failed the child's SESSION, though. Its registry run stayed held as yielded (`subagent-registry-run-pause.ts`), so the parent's owed completion was never delivered. The parent stayed parked on a wake that could never come.

Seen on a live Gateway: a parent stayed asleep for over two hours after one restart, and again after the next, until a human wrote to it.

## Change

- After the existing lifecycle failure, settle that exact yielded run through the existing completion owner (`completeSubagentRunWithRecovery`, exported from the registry). It runs with `settleYielded: true`, the unchanged terminal error, and normal cleanup and delivery.
- `suppressSessionEffects: true` only prevents a duplicate visible failure on the child session, since the lifecycle write above already owns it. It does not suppress the parent's notification.
- The completion owner already selects the exact `runId`, refuses rows that are resumed or not yielded, and does nothing when there is no registry entry. So a root session's own run is unaffected.

Follows #201970 (restart root discovery through visible spawned children).

## User impact

A parent whose child's wait could not survive a restart now gets that child's failure result and wakes up, so it can re-instruct the child. Before, it stayed silent until someone wrote to it.

## Evidence

Proof tier: source (`ocx test`).

- New regression in `subagent-registry.requester-wake-settlement.test-support.ts`, which runs the real `resumeMarkedSessions` startup path.
  - On unchanged `main`: the child session is `failed`, but the registry outcome stays `undefined`.
  - With the fix: the registry records the terminal error, the parent receives exactly one agent request with `subagent_settle` provenance, and the delivered-cleanup acknowledgment completes.
- 12 restart-resume and registry pause/yield/settle files pass. An earlier 36-file scope also passed.
- `pnpm tsgo`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxlint, format, and the lifetime-check, line-cap and session-identity ratchets: pass.

Production +17 lines, test +55 lines.

prs.title: fix(gateway): resume the true root after restart through visible spawned children
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

After a Gateway restart, OpenClaw stops running subagents and resumes only their ordinary root session, which then re-instructs its children (#185730, `docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md`). Root discovery (`resolveRootSubagentRequester`) walked up the ancestry only while the session key looked like a hidden subagent (`agent:…:subagent:…`). A VISIBLE spawned child (a dashboard session created by `sessions_spawn` with `visible: true`) stopped the walk. Its restart marker was then rejected because it is a spawned child, and the real root was never marked.

Seen on a live Gateway: a root chat → visible coordinator → hidden workers tree stalled after a restart and needed a human message 25 minutes later.

## Change

- Follow RECORDED native spawn ownership up to the ordinary root: the session's `spawnedBy`, or `createdVia: "spawn"` with parent, controller or requester fallback. The walk now covers visible and hidden native children alike, and keeps the cycle guard, the recorded child-authority (owner) check and the session-incarnation match.
- `sessions_send` also registers requester edges, but it creates no child and carries no spawn metadata. Those sessions stay independent roots, which keeps the case #188402 narrowed the walk for: an ordinary conversation must not inherit an excluded cron requester. Run records cannot tell the two edges apart, so the walk reads the session's creation metadata in a worker, once per ancestry step. A session without a registry entry stops before any read.
- Selection snapshots live owners before those reads, keeps the live-root-before-parked precedence, and still runs inside the existing shutdown persistence budget.
- `docs/tools/subagents/operations.md` notes that visible spawned children resolve to their root.

## Evidence

Proof tier: source (`ocx test`).

- New `session-restart-resume.ancestry.test.ts`, with two cases: a hidden worker under a visible spawned coordinator, and a visible worker directly under the root. Both fail on unchanged `main` (`resumeAfterRestart` undefined on the root) and pass with the fix, through a real shutdown marker into the startup enqueue.
- Frozen head: 11 files, 110 tests pass, including the existing cron-ownership protection.
- `session-restart-resume.workspace.test.ts` timed out under heavy host load (load above 70). An instrumented run on the fix then passed in 27 s with no root-resolver calls or ancestry reads, and its close took 244 ms. It does not touch the changed path.
- `pnpm tsgo`, `pnpm check:test-types`, type-aware oxlint, format and the line-cap ratchet: pass.

Production +50 lines, test +99 lines, docs +4 lines.

prs.title: fix: recover longer session history text within response bounds
prs.body:
Related: #64970

## What Problem This Solves

Agents reviewing long conversations cannot request visible message text beyond the fixed 4,000-character `sessions_history` preview, even when the complete message fits within the existing response budget.

## User Impact

Callers can opt into `maxChars: 1..64000` for bounded visible-text recovery. Omitting it preserves the 4,000-character default. The 80 KiB response cap, access checks, physical-session checks, and existing reasoning/tool-preview limits remain in place.

This is not an unbounded export: oversized source rows remain explicitly incomplete, and historical/pre-reset discovery is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool requests a bounded read through its existing authorized `chat.history` owner and applies the requested limit to visible text locally. Reads retain at least the existing upstream preview size so smaller text requests do not shorten reasoning/tool previews. It preserves upstream truncation facts and marks a source-row group incomplete when the local byte cap splits its display siblings, rather than silently treating the surviving sibling as complete.

The existing Control UI full-message/export path serves interactive readers; it does not supply this model-facing reader option. Unlike the closed environment-override proposal in #65029, this is a bounded per-call option, not a new global setting or a higher default. It builds on the pagination owner in #97101 and structured truncation in #126342.

## Evidence

Current published head: `3faaa5a937f1b1eb298911f04a5e4a67640edb6a`, integrated with upstream `6b3c804312d7e3b3e4d45ce226c0feac590cf581`. The published tree `ee244f4afdfa9293cff092ec7cbc40ada0c643e1` matches the validated workspace exactly. Earlier conflicts were limited to generated prompt artifacts and resolved by the canonical generator.

- **95 affected tests passed** across five files: history, anchor budgeting, embedded adapter, real-storage composed history, and prompt-prefix stability. Three-shard wall time: 50.52 seconds.
- Both canonical production and agents-tools test typechecks passed. Scoped repository lint and formatting passed, as did whitespace checks against the integrated base. Prompt snapshots (6 files) and assertion-safety checks passed before the adapter-only repair; their inputs are unchanged. Net test growth is +354 lines, within the 400-line allowance.
- The original recovery regressions fail against the unmodified implementation. Preview-bound regressions for tool-result aliases/envelopes, nested results, and small text limits were reproduced and fixed.
- **Hosted review finding addressed:** the embedded adapter discarded `maxChars`, clipping at 8,000 before the tool could recover 16,000 characters. The existing adapter now forwards the parsed option to the shared text-limit owner. The new `sessions-history-tool.embedded.test.ts` writes through `SessionManager.appendMessageAsync` into isolated real storage, then invokes the real tool, embedded adapter, and history reader without replacing the adapter/reader/storage with mocks. It fails at exact 16,000-character recovery before the fix and passes afterward, then verifies two byte-capped pages recover the original 16,000-character message plus three 40,000-character messages in order, without omission or duplication. Each response remains at or below 80 KiB. Its normal runner uses the established host-owned database lane; the composed case completes in about three seconds of test time.
- Prior full-feature and CI-repair Auto Review passes were P0–P2 `scoped-clean`. The fresh three-file embedded repair received an independent narrative P0–P2 source review with no findings, including its test-lane registration. That reviewer inspected supplied sources but did not execute tests or independently verify the checkout SHA; this is not an Auto Review machine receipt or maintainer approval. The native Auto Review service currently rejects its own runtime configuration before execution.
- **Current-head CI gates passed:** [CI finalizer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44606766159/job/135862438343) and [consolidated gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44609653987), both on `3faaa5a937f1b1eb298911f04a5e4a67640edb6a`. Production/test types, prompt snapshots, security-sensitive/dependency review, and applicable security lanes passed. The bounded checks reader does not expose the entire 141-check inventory, so this is a verified gate result, not a claim that every job ran or passed.
- **Current-head hosted re-review completed:** the [durable review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197807#issuecomment-6828977121) confirms the embedded-adapter repair, reports no findings and no Before-merge items, and marks the PR ready for maintainer review. Overall readiness/proof remain **1/6**, patch quality **4/6**—not Diamond.

The [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197807#issuecomment-6828977121) also asks for an isolated live-Gateway/real-agent demonstration. The new test supplies real-storage/tool/adapter integration evidence, **not live Gateway or model proof**. That requirement remains incomplete because this sandbox has no admitted isolated live-agent runner; the operator-input CLI route cannot preserve an agent-exec caller’s attribution and was not used as a workaround. Native `scripts/pr` preparation is also unavailable here because `gh` is absent. **No Diamond or merge-ready claim is made.**

The change reuses existing preview and history owners. It does not change live Gateway state or configuration, deploy anything, provide arbitrary oversized-message export, or provide exhaustive pre-reset ingestion.

RoboClaw independently reviewed the supplied contribution and added the scoped preview-bound fixes and regressions. The author-preserving local commit is `c923e10ebcbfd7e37f1629f3cf6e5c2dd75dea48`; the managed publisher created `b71a064d6faee5f6fbc66affadeb30266f515fc1` with an identical tree and the original contributor as co-author. Preservation of the original primary Git author remains unresolved.

prs.title: feat: add llmman to the Models page Add provider list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI -> Models only lists hosted providers in the "Add an account" picker. Someone running llmman, a local OpenAI-compatible model server, has no way to add it from the UI and has to hand-edit `models.providers.llmman` in config.

## User Impact

User impact: llmman now appears in Models -> Add an account, with its own logo, next to the hosted providers. Saving a key (any non-empty value works for a local server; `llmman-local` is the documented marker) sets up the provider and discovers the models your llmman server reports, so you can pick one as a default and chat with it. Models are listed by a short name: `docker.io/ai/gemma4:latest` shows as `gemma4` and `docker.io/ai/qwen3.8:27b` as `qwen3.8:27b`. A model from another namespace, host, or tag keeps it (`docker.io/alternate-ai-place/gemma4` shows as `alternate-ai-place/gemma4`). Existing manual `models.providers.llmman` configs keep working unchanged, and an explicit `baseUrl` still wins.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker only shows providers whose plugin manifest declares an API key auth choice for guided setup. llmman had no bundled plugin, so it could never appear. This adds a small bundled `llmman` plugin modeled on the existing local-server providers: default base URL `http://127.0.0.1:17434/v1`, models discovered from `/v1/models`, and the `llmman-local` non-secret marker. It also ships llmman's own manatee mark, shown in full color instead of the flat mask used by monochrome marks (source, checksum, and Apache-2.0 license are recorded in the attribution files). llmman reports models by their full reference and no display name, so the plugin shortens the display name by dropping the default `docker.io/` host, `ai/` namespace, and `:latest` tag. Only the display name changes: the model id, which is what the server is sent and what config stores, is untouched (llmman rejects a bare `ai/gemma4` as an unknown Hugging Face repo, so ids cannot be shortened safely). A display name the server supplies itself is kept. No core auth, catalog, or capability code changes, and no other provider's behavior changes.

## Evidence

Clean before/after pair (Models -> Add an account, searching "llm"). Before, only LiteLLM matches; after, the llmman row, with the llmman manatee logo, is listed too:

| Before (origin/main) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: searching "llm" in the Add an account picker lists only LiteLLM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c20dd403-81ac-4500-b079-7559d07706c4) | ![After: searching "llm" lists LiteLLM and a separate llmman row with the llmman manatee logo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eecb0fc9-4e00-4c7e-bf86-3374daaf47a3) |

The rest of the flow on this branch, run end to end on an NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, aarch64) against a live llmman 0.1.652 server:

| Choose llmman, enter a key | Provider card after saving | Model dropdown |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![The llmman API key dialog](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68eb3409-5b90-420b-9884-8a665aa4dffb) | ![Models page: llmman card with 5 models](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/655767ca-84a0-4d81-b9c6-16ca5d514538) | ![Model dropdown listing the five models discovered from the llmman server](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ebf0e39-7fff-46d6-bc80-d56a1b2fc0ed) |

| Chat with the discovered model | Test access on the llmman card |
| --- | --- |
| ![Control UI chat: two turns answered by gemma4 via llmman](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09d7cde4-1de4-449e-9bfc-aa558879f9da) | ![Models page: gemma4 selected as default; llmman card shows Access verified, request round-trip 3331 ms](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e5c4120-fc21-441b-9dd1-43e96d2e0f2c) |

What was checked:
- **Real chat round trip, on the Spark:** the Control UI chat got replies from `gemma4` (llmman id `docker.io/ai/gemma4:latest`) through llmman (two turns). `qwen3.8:27b` also answered through the Gateway (`openclaw infer model run --gateway`, about 20 s). `openclaw models list --provider llmman --all` shows all five discovered models as Local with Auth yes.
- **Same-build comparison:** the "before" is the exact upstream parent commit (`4ea2deb`) built and run on the same machine as this branch, with the same search and dialog framing.
- **Tests and checks:** plugin tests (manifest shape, discovery against a stub `/v1/models` server, marker and key handling, explicit-config precedence, no-server case, short display names), gateway capability test, Models page data test, provider icon tests, API key flow test, plugin inventory check, and docs format check pass. Type checks and the dead-export scan from `pnpm check:changed` pass on the rebased tree, and oxlint and oxfmt are clean on every file this PR changes. The repo-wide lint step of `check:changed` still reports three `max-lines` errors in files this PR does not touch (`src/cli/daemon-cli/lifecycle.ts`, `extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.test.ts`, `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/index.test.ts`); they are present on the upstream parent commit.

Notes for reviewers:
- **Where the full reference still shows:** the model dropdown, the default Model row, and the chat composer use the short name. The line under **Test access** ("Profile llmman:manual · llmman/docker.io/ai/gemma4:latest" in the last screenshot) still prints the exact provider/model reference the check used. That line is built by the gateway's shared probe code for every provider, so I left it alone here rather than add docker-specific logic to core. It would be a small follow-up if you want it shortened too.
- **Notice right after saving:** the card can show "API key saved, but the check didn't finish. No model is available for this provider." until you pick an llmman model. The post-save check tests with a model you have configured and has nothing to try on a fresh setup. Once a model is selected, **Test access** on the card passes (screenshot above). I left that shared check alone to keep this PR small.
- **Reasoning models:** discovered models are registered with `reasoning: false`, so for a model like gemma4 the Gateway logs that it emitted reasoning that was hidden. Replies still work. Reading reasoning support from the server would be a reasonable follow-up.
- **Bundle budget notices:** the Control UI build prints the same six size-budget notices on this branch and on the parent commit; this change adds about 0.1 KiB of raw CSS.

<details>
<summary>Agent transcript (condensed excerpt; the user request is paraphrased)</summary>

**User:** The Control UI Models page only offers hosted providers and no local one. Add llmman so it appears in that list, test it thoroughly through the UI, open a PR with screenshots and the agent transcript, then add the llmman logo, and run the end-to-end test on a DGX Spark with gemma4 and qwen3.8. Address the gaps listed in the first PR description and leave the PR in a mergeable state.

**Agent (investigation):** The "Add an account" picker is built from provider capabilities, and a provider only gets one when a bundled plugin manifest declares an `api-key` auth choice with `appGuidedSecret: true`. llmman was documented as "Plugin: none", so it could never be listed.

**Agent (implementation):** Delegated the code change to opencode (claude-sonnet-5-5, high thinking) with a scoped prompt: a new bundled `extensions/llmman` plugin modeled on the litellm and lmstudio plugins, manual configs unchanged, no changes to other providers, plus tests, docs, and registry updates. Reviewed the whole diff myself.

**Agent (logo):** llmman's brand mark is its manatee image, which llmman publishes in its docs-assets release and pins by SHA-256. Downloaded it, checked the hash, wrapped it in a square SVG for the Control UI, added a CSS rule so it keeps its colors instead of being masked to one color, used it for the plugin package icon, and recorded source, checksum, and license. A first attempt pasted extra text into the attribution file through a shell quoting mistake; a scan of the diff caught it and the commit was rewritten.

**Agent (testing on the DGX Spark):** Built the branch on the Spark (aarch64) and ran a throwaway Gateway there, with headless Chrome driving the real Control UI against the Spark's llmman server (gemma4, qwen3.5, qwen3.8). Picker, key dialog, save, provider card, and model dropdown all work and list the four discovered models. gemma4 answered in the chat UI, and qwen3.8:27b answered through the Gateway CLI. Tried marking the key choice `credentialOnly` to avoid the post-save notice; that made setup two steps and still showed a notice, so it was reverted. Found that the notice clears once a model is selected (Test access then reports Access verified).

**Agent (cleanup):** Squashed the branch to one commit, rebased it onto current main, rebuilt the exact upstream parent for a like-for-like "before" screenshot, and re-ran the checks on the rebased tree.

**Agent (model names):** Feedback was that docker.io is the default host, ai the default namespace, and latest the default tag, so docker.io/ai/gemma4:latest should read as gemma4 everywhere, while other namespaces, hosts, and tags stay visible. Since llmman only reports the full reference and rejects a bare ai/ prefix, I kept the ids as they are and set the display name in the plugin, with tests for the default host, namespace, and tag, another namespace, another host, another tag, and a server-supplied name. Amended into the same commit, rebuilt on the Spark, and retook the screenshots that show model names.

</details>

prs.title: fix(gateway): resume a root whose yield source was lost instead of failing it
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

At Gateway startup, a session parked in `sessions_yield` whose wake source could not survive the restart was always closed with a visible failure (`recordRestartYieldFailure`). For a sub-agent that is correct: since #202000, the registry also settles it and its requester wakes. For an ordinary **root** session, nothing settles: `completeSubagentRunWithRecovery` returns at once when there is no registry row. So the root's work just failed and stayed failed until a human wrote to it. The restart contract says an interrupted root gets one ordinary input to inspect current state and continue.

Seen live: a root failed at startup and was only rescued by an unrelated child-settlement turn nine seconds later.

## Change

- `resolveSessionYieldWait` (the registry read owner, `subagent-registry-read.ts`): at the root branch, when no waiting child resolves but a child still owes this requester a completion, it returns `waiting`. "Owes" means a pending settle wake, or an owed completion that is not yet terminal, is still yielded, or has a delivery pending or in progress. That registry completion is then the root's only wake.
- `session-restart-resume.ts`: a root that is still `unreachable` (nothing will ever wake it) is admitted through the ordinary restart-resume input instead of being failed. Sub-agents keep the lost-source failure plus registry settlement (#202000).
- No ordering, fence or handshake. The registry is one shared map across physical agents, so a child in another agent's store counts. Startup awaits registry hydration before restart resume (`server-startup-observers.ts:63`, then `:74`).
- A failed delivery does not count as owed: it is terminal (`subagent-registry-lifecycle-finalize-cleanup.ts:234-244`), so counting it would park the root forever.
- `docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md`: corrected the lost-source row and paragraph.

Follows #201970 and #202000.

## User impact

After a restart, a root session waiting on work that cannot continue resumes on its own to inspect and reconcile, or wakes on its child's settlement. It is not left failed until someone writes to it.

## Evidence

Proof tier: source (`ocx test`).

- New regressions through the real `resumeMarkedSessions` startup path. On unchanged `main`, both roots are marked `failed`. With the fix:
  - a root with no owed child gets exactly one restart input, across two boots, and is not failed;
  - a root whose lost-source child is settled is woken once by `subagent_settle`, with no restart input and no failed status.
- 19 files, 230 tests: restart-resume, registry read/yield and requester-wake settlement. Four orphan-matrix expectations that required yielded roots to fail were updated to one normal resume.
- `pnpm tsgo`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxlint, format, and the lifetime-check, line-cap and session-identity ratchets: pass.
- Unrelated: `subagent-registry-worker.test.ts` "releases serialized payloads while their immutable registry rows remain resident" also fails on clean `main` (d9e2d8a89dd0).

Production +24 −5 lines, tests +47 −17, docs +4 −2.

prs.title: fix: an update with nothing to do no longer copies your databases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every direct `openclaw update` copied the whole state (config and every database) into `<state-dir>.update-captures/<run-id>` before it knew whether it would change anything. An update that turned out to be already current, or that was refused, still copied. On a 20 GiB instance that is minutes of disk I/O and 20 GiB of temporary space for an update that does nothing, and on shipped versions the copy stayed behind.

## User Impact

An already-current `openclaw update`, and an update refused before it changes anything, no longer copy the databases. A real update still keeps exactly one original-state capture, taken just before it starts changing state. Nothing new to configure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Owner rule: "if snapshots aren't needed, don't do them"; a version check never copies.

- **Root cause.** The capture was taken by the initialization owner (`update-command-initialization-run.ts`) before admission, for every direct CLI run. Whether the run is already current is decided later: for package installs at target selection (known, but not consulted), for Git installs inside the runner after fetch (in-place) or after the build (release layout). Nothing reads the capture before those decisions; it is manual-recovery evidence and is handed to Doctor and finalization later.
- **Fix: the same owner, taken lazily.** The initialization owner keeps the only capture code and exposes it on the in-process run context as `captureOriginal()` (runs at most once; never serialized; no new stored field, store, or config). The run calls it at its first state change:
  - activation (`beforeActivate` in `update-command-execution.ts`), after its last pre-stop refusal check and before the service stop, so the Gateway still serves while the copy runs: package activation, Git in-place mutation, and Git release activation. In release mode this is after the built-equals-running check and immediately before activation; a build alone changes no state;
  - a handoff of the update to the running Gateway (`handoffUpdateFromGateway`, once it has decided to hand off), because the handed-off update changes state in another process that cannot capture. One place covers both callers, candidate admission and execution;
  - on an already-current core: the legacy config repair, writing a changed update channel, publishing changed plugin records, a hand-off of post-core work to a fresh process (which always runs Doctor repair), or the fresh Doctor that runs after a plugin changed (`update-command-noop.ts`, `update-command-convergence.ts`). Those are the points where the run knows beforehand that state-changing work follows. The plugin cohort's per-step checkpoints are not used, since they fire even when nothing changes.
- **Kept eager on purpose.** A profile with no state database yet still copies at initialization. The copy is cheap and records that the database was absent before this run's history created one (the #161044 contract for fresh profiles). Fresh-state initialization that writes state before execution also copies first, as before.
- **Refusals.** #161044 took the capture before a refused update was written to history so the capture would hold only earlier history. A refused update changes nothing but its own history row, which is not data anyone recovers from, so it now copies nothing. Downgrade confirmation still happens at the same point; it used to be folded into the capture.
- **Plugin operations on an already-current core.** Plugin package files are installed first; they are not part of the capture. Install-index rows (in the state database) and plugin config entries are published only when plugins changed, and the run copies just before that publication. Plugin data is migrated only by the fresh Doctor, which runs after the copy and keeps its own migration backups.
- **Gateway-started updates** take no capture, before and after this change: the CLI they start carries a run id, which disables the capture, and their Doctor only reads an existing one.

## Update behavior for published updaters

On an already-current run there is no candidate: the installed CLI does everything. Shipped drivers up to and including 2026.11.6 (published to `latest` today without this change) keep copying on no-op runs. The copying stops from the first release that contains this change. The leftovers those drivers leave are removed by the cleanup from #201711, which is already on main: a run recorded as already current has its capture retired at the next cleanup point. A real update driven by a published updater keeps that updater's capture behavior; the candidate does not take a second one.

## Evidence

**Checklist for landing:**

- **(a) A real update still copies before its first state change, on every shape.**
  - Package: one sealed capture, recorded on the run.
  - Git in-place: one capture via the runner's mutation hook.
  - Git release: the release runner calls that hook exactly once before activating a rebuilt release, and never for a release that equals the running one.
  - Handoff to a running Gateway: package on Linux and macOS, and Git, each leave exactly one capture.
  - Gateway-started updates: no capture before or after this change (see "Gateway-started updates" above).
- **(b) No path changes state before the capture exists.** Every state-change point checks for the capture first: activation, handoff, legacy config repair, a changed channel, plugin record publication, fresh post-core process, post-plugin Doctor, and fresh-state initialization. Each has a test that fails with its hook removed. Plugin publication on an already-current core copies first too (round 2). Plugin package files installed before publication are not part of the capture.
- **(c) A no-op or a refusal before any state change writes nothing to captures.** Covered for package and Git no-ops, the Git release no-op, the metadata refusal, and the before-stop publication refusal. The disk sampler in the cells measures the same thing.
- **(d) Real updates record the same `original-state-capture` step and warnings.** The real-update cases assert the step. The failed-capture warning keeps its full text, run step, JSON and stderr. The capacity-warning cases are unchanged and pass.
- **(e) Messages stay true.** Docs now say when the capture is taken (`docs/cli/update/repair-and-recovery.md`, `docs/cli/update.md`). No user-facing message text changed.

**Owner tests through the real `openclaw update` command path** (`src/cli/update-cli.capture-space.test.ts`, process-isolated lane, real capture code):

- Already-current package update: copies nothing, records no `original-state-capture` step. RED on base: one capture directory.
- Already-current Git update: the same. RED on base: one capture directory.
- Update refused before it changes state (registry metadata refusal): copies nothing. RED on base: one capture directory.
- Real package update: still exactly one sealed capture named by its run, recorded on the run (passes on base and head; guards against skipping a needed copy).
- Gateway-started update (run id inherited): no capture on base or head.
- Real update whose capture fails: continues with the full `NO ORIGINAL-STATE SNAPSHOT ... unavailable` warning on the run, in JSON and on stderr. This case moved here from `update-command-fresh-preview.test.ts`, where it used an already-current run that no longer copies.

**The other state-change points, each proven to need its hook** (each test fails with only that fix reverted):

- Handoff to a running Gateway (`update-cli.service-authority.test.ts`, package on Linux and macOS, and Git): the handed-off update leaves exactly one sealed capture. Without the fix, the package and Git cases leave none.
- Already-current legacy config repair (`update-cli.config-convergence.test.ts`): the capture exists when the repair runs. Without the fix: none.
- Already-current core whose post-core work continues in a fresh process (`update-command-convergence-authority.test.ts`): capture, then hand-off. Without the fix: hand-off only.
- Already-current core with a changed plugin (`update-cli.fresh-doctor.test.ts`): exactly one sealed capture exists when the post-plugin Doctor starts. Without the convergence hook: none.
- Already-current core writing a changed channel (`update-command-convergence-authority.test.ts`): capture, then convergence. The same run without a channel change copies nothing. Without the fix: convergence only.
- Pre-stop publication refusal of an in-place Git update (`update-command-execution.test.ts`): refused runs copy nothing; permitted runs copy once. Without the fix, both refused cases copied.
- Git release runner (`update-runner-git-release.test.ts`, real Git repositories): a rebuilt release reaches the mutation hook exactly once before activation; a release that equals the running one never reaches it.
- Real Git in-place update (`update-cli.capture-space.test.ts`): one sealed capture, recorded on the run.

**#161044 contract, rewritten** (`update-command-fresh-preview.test-support.ts`): a fresh profile still records the database's absence before history (unchanged, passes on base and head); an existing profile copies only at its first state change, after its own history row (RED on base: copied before execution); a refused update now copies nothing (RED on base: a recovery set existed). "Doctor sees an already-current update's completed history" keeps its Doctor and history checks and now asserts that no capture step exists (RED on base).

**`update-command-run-service-ownership.test.ts`:** its refused `--tag main` update asserted that the refusal copied the service profile's state with the selected service env. A refused update now copies nothing. The case now asserts no capture and no capture reference, and keeps its admission, env-selection, ledger and output checks. The fixture rows that only fed the old copy-content check were removed; the earlier run stays because it gives the service profile its state database.

**Changed expectations, and why removal is safe:** the foreground-failure case (`update-cli-failure-recovery.test-support.ts`) still expects the cleanup step, because its fresh post-core process runs Doctor repair and so the run copies first. The already-current plugin-exception case (`update-cli.plugin-convergence.test.ts`) no longer expects a cleanup step: that run copied nothing, so nothing is cleaned. That is the behavior this PR adds.

Recordings of the owner tests (the same `update-cli.capture-space.test.ts` cases). RED, with the six product files at base `c25f49d92f4` and tests from this head, shows 3 failed (package no-op, Git no-op and refusal each copy) and 3 passed (the controls). GREEN on this head shows 6 passed.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/039d06d5-e0c8-41da-b185-f040d9a502b1

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0bc4f4c-e9d8-4d1e-9818-c50736c0d424

**Checks on this head:** the touched and affected suites (capture, already-current, fresh Doctor, plugin and config convergence, service authority, convergence authority, fresh preview and terminal, status recovery, capture cleanup, automatic cleanup and its policy, upgrade-survivor no-op, update-restart module outcome, eager-import closure) pass under umask 022; three cases that timed out at 120 s while a package build ran in parallel pass when run alone. `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass; oxlint clean on touched files; `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base cd2ae19272a --no-merge-base` passes, with test lines at +178 of 400; `pnpm check:docs` passes; `git diff --check` clean. `autoreview` does not run on this machine.

**Independent review** (fresh read-only reviewer with the diff and the contract, not my conclusions) found one P0 and two P1 gaps, all real and all fixed above with failing-first tests:

- **P0:** a handoff during candidate admission took no capture.
- **P1:** an already-current legacy config repair wrote config without one.
- **P1:** an already-current core that hands post-core work to a fresh process (Doctor repair) took none.

Its P2 notes are addressed as follows:

- The weak fresh-Doctor assertion now checks the count of sealed copies at the moment Doctor starts.
- The copy taken after admission includes the run's own history row; see Not proven.

**Rating round 1 (ClawSweeper, head `bf0d7312785`): overall F, proof F, patch D.** Each finding was checked against the code first.

- **Channel write before the copy on an already-current core: real, fixed.** `openclaw update --channel beta` on an already-current core with no plugin change wrote `update.channel` before any copy. The copy now happens first whenever a changed channel will be written (`update-command-convergence.ts`). Test: fails with only that fix reverted, and the same run without a channel change copies nothing.
- **Plugin publication before the Doctor copy:** at first answered with the approved "tell beforehand" rule and listed as a gap; fixed in round 2, below, at the one point where the plugin owner does know.
- **First Git release conversion publishes the release link before the copy: not a capture gap, rejected.** The capture holds config, includes, databases, and declared plugin resources (`src/infra/update-recovery-baseline-capture.ts`). It has never held the install layout. The first release is built from the commit that serves now (`update-runner-git-release.ts`, the conversion step), so publishing it changes no captured state. Activation of the target release still goes through the mutation hook, where the copy is taken.
- **A pre-stop refusal still copied: real, fixed.** An in-place Git update with `--no-restart` and a running owned Gateway is refused by the before-stop publication check, which ran after the copy. The copy now comes after that check and still before the service stop (`update-command-execution.ts`). Test: the refused cases copy nothing and the allowed ones copy once; both refused cases fail with only that fix reverted.
- **Docs blurred repairs on an unchanged core with unchanged runs: fixed.** The recovery guide now lists each repair that copies on an already-current core.
- **Proof rated mock-only:** the installed-package cells and the recordings were not finished at that head. Their results are below.

**Rating round 2 (head `4983faf2f3b`): overall F, proof F, patch D.**

- **Plugin publication before the copy on an unchanged core: real, fixed.** The plugin owner knows that a write is coming only when plugins actually changed. At that point it publishes install records and config through one `beforeCommit`, used by both its records-only path and its config path. The run now copies there first (`beforeRecordPublication`, passed by post-core convergence). This also covers already-current Git release installs, where no Doctor hook runs. The plugin cohort's `beforePersistentEffect` checkpoint was tried and rejected: the test showed it fires many times even when nothing changes, so it would have copied on every no-op run with plugins. Test (`update-command-plugins.persistence.test.ts`): a plugin change gives exactly copy, then commit, with the new records published; no change never copies.
- **The copy spent the activation deadline: real, fixed.** The before-stop check and the copy now run before the activation clock starts. The run's `--timeout` deadline gets one owner method, `exclude(operation)`: it stops the deadline during the copy and moves it by the copy's duration. The copy keeps its own step bound, as on main, where it ran before the deadline existed. An expired budget stays expired. Test (`restart-health-deadline.test.ts`): five seconds of excluded work leave a 1 s budget at 600 ms remaining, the budget then expires on time, and excluding after expiry is refused without running the work.
- **A handoff copied before resolving the installed updater: real, fixed.** The copy now follows the entry-point check and still precedes releasing the executor. Test (`update-command-report-handoff.test.ts`): the missing-updater refusal copies nothing.
- **Docs promised too much for failures before activation: fixed** (`docs/cli/update.md`).
- **Proof:** recordings are linked above, and the installed-package cells follow.

**End to end (installed-package Docker cells, local OrbStack, update-matrix harness with the per-directory disk sampler).** Each cell installs the packed build relabeled as 2026.11.5, with a managed Gateway service, about 2 GiB of agent database and a busy writer (1 MiB/s). It then runs a real `openclaw update --yes --json` to the same build stamped 2026.11.6, a plain repeat (already current), and `openclaw update --tag 9999.0.0 --yes --json`, which the registry cannot resolve. Bytes are allocated bytes of `~/.openclaw.update-captures`, sampled every 5 s, relative to the start of each step.

| Step | RED: base `cd2ae19272a` | GREEN: this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Real update (2026.11.5 → 2026.11.6) | `ok`, capture step recorded, captures peak +2,119 MiB, 283.9 s | _pending_ |
| Repeat, already current | `skipped/already-current`, capture step recorded, captures peak **+2,119 MiB**, 37.1 s | _pending_ |
| Refused update (`target-metadata-preflight`) | capture step recorded, captures peak **+2,119 MiB**, 59.9 s, and the 2,119 MiB copy stays behind | _pending_ |

The disk figures come from the per-directory sampler; the VM-wide free-space delta is not used.

## Not proven

- Git in-place and Git release-layout no-ops are proven at the owner (the runner reports already-current before calling the mutation hook; release mode reports it after the built-equals-running check and calls the hook only before activation). They were not run as installed Docker cells; the dev cells build OpenClaw from source inside the container twice per cell.
- A manual restore from a capture taken after admission brings back this run's own "running" history row; the next update reconciles it as abandoned. Captures taken before this change held only earlier runs.
- Windows: the handoff to a running Gateway is Linux and macOS only, unchanged.

## Steps left to a person

None. An already-current or refused update does nothing that needs a person. Copies left by drivers up to 2026.11.6 are removed by the existing automatic cleanup on the next update.

## Follow-ups (recorded, not built)

- **Same-schema real updates still take the full capture.** A real update whose target does not change any schema migrates no database, so under the approved policy (at most one copy-on-write clone per migrating database) it needs no database copy at all; only its config and plugin resources could change. This PR keeps today's full capture for every real update. Today's capture is a byte copy on both macOS and Linux, not a clone: the original-state backup acquires each SQLite source with `preserveSourceArtifacts: true` (`src/infra/update-recovery-baseline-capture.ts:360`), which takes `prepareSqliteReadOnlyCopyInProcess` (`src/infra/sqlite-snapshot.ts:557`). That copies the live family with `clone: "never"` (`src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.ts:452`), on purpose; the synchronous variant at `:188-190` states why: reflinks would lock the source inode and add shared extents to live databases. Only publishing the private staged image into the capture directory (`src/infra/sqlite-snapshot.ts:285`, via `copySqliteFile` with `clone = "auto"` at `src/infra/sqlite-file-copy.ts:17`) can use `clonefile`/`FICLONE`, and only when staging and capture share a volume. So a capture costs at least one full byte copy of every database, plus one clone or second copy.
- **Plugin-only changes on an already-current core** copy the whole state before the fresh Doctor. A narrower capture of only the plugin's declared resources would need a capture scope the owner does not have today.

prs.title: fix(imessage): deliver persistent background-task announcements
prs.body:
Related: #196962.

## What Problem This Solves

Persistent background tasks can finish successfully yet fail to deliver their iMessage announcements with “iMessage message reference does not belong to the selected conversation.” An internal session-event ID can be inherited as a reply target despite not identifying a native message.

## User Impact

Tasks can retain their own history and deliver separate, top-level announcements when the account’s exclusive local Messages database proves the automatically inherited reply target does not exist. Native replies and explicit reply validation remain intact.

Remote or unavailable lookup evidence retains existing validation; this is not a blanket fallback on lookup failure. No core contract, configuration, or database schema change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This follows the channel-owned approach in these related adapter PRs:
- Discord: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196963
- Feishu: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177297
- Telegram: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200877

Unlike Discord snowflakes or Feishu message prefixes, native iMessage GUIDs can look exactly like synthetic UUIDs. Format rejection would break legitimate threading. Instead, the adapter carries existing implicit/explicit metadata through automatic-final and message-tool sends and uses its existing worker-backed lookup to distinguish absent messages from wrong-chat or unbound messages. Cross-account/chat references and explicit invalid anchors still reject.

No new cache or core policy is introduced. LEFT JOIN preserves existing messages without valid chat associations as mismatches, not missing messages. The existing send-result parser moves to the sibling message-ID module without behavior changes to respect the send-module growth ratchet.

Simplification pass: retained one authorization owner and existing lookup/cache machinery; no further reduction identified. Original adapter-change delta: 147 additions / 28 deletions across ten files, including 85 regression-test lines. The later routed-reply follow-up adds 9/removes 1 test lines in one additional file.

## Evidence

- Before: on 2026.11.5, a persistent scheduled execution succeeded but iMessage delivery failed with the conversation-binding error. The exact original failed reference was not recovered.
- Offline execution of extracted installed functions reproduced synthetic event-ID propagation with zero history. This is mechanism evidence, not a complete live baseline trace.
- A native-send regression failed before the fix at the observed rejection. Candidate tests exercise both registered adapter send paths with worker-backed SQLite and a mocked native send boundary, including native UUIDs, explicit invalid anchors, wrong-account/chat references, orphan/dangling bindings, unavailable lookup, and receipts.
- Release-based candidate: 65 focused tests passed; after parser extraction, all 38 send tests re-passed. Focused typecheck/lint/format, standalone plugin build and installed imports passed.
- Live release-based candidate after installation and restart: two successive runs in one task-private persistent session delivered through separate DM delivery—automatic final and message-tool send. Native Messages readback found exactly one labeled outgoing message each, both sent/delivered, error 0, and null thread-originator fields. Temporary automation was removed after successful delivery.
- Exact main-based head `dcbf14b14eb08649d726f4d7f8b875a89639acbb`: 64 focused tests across four files passed; formatting and diff checks passed. No 1Password changes.
- Prior independent agent review found a dangling-chat association edge; selecting the joined chat ROWID and a negative control addressed it. This was not ClawSweeper/autoreview, and is not claimed as a fresh review of this main-based range.

**Main-based qualification completed (2026-11-19):** an isolated detached checkout of exact head `dcbf14b14eb08649d726f4d7f8b875a89639acbb` received its own frozen-lockfile dependency install (`@openclaw/fs-safe@0.27.1`). Fresh SDK and package-boundary declarations, targeted iMessage production typecheck, targeted lint of all seven changed production TypeScript files, and standalone iMessage npm-runtime build passed. All 64 focused tests across four files re-passed in two shards (89.46s). Existing exact-head format/diff proof retained. The original checkout and installed runtime were not modified. This resolves the prior dependency/SDK qualification gap; broad PR CI and maintainer review remain outstanding.

**Earlier release-based live-proof limits (superseded for exact-head transition coverage by the capture below):** the live candidate was release-based, not this main-based head; tests used a DM rather than the original group/weather fixture, and recipient UI was not independently inspected. Native `reply_to_guid` values were populated and are not claimed null. There was no same-fixture live baseline/candidate A/B or wire-anchor trace. Ordinary human replies and explicit valid anchors have local coverage, not additional live sends. Raw household logs and private destinations are not published.


## Exact-head Gateway/native runtime transition capture — 2026-11-19

Captured on reviewed head `dcbf14b14eb08649d726f4d7f8b875a89639acbb`, built locally in an isolated checkout. Both runs used the same task-private persistent session and explicit, separate iMessage DM delivery.

**Real boundaries:** Gateway scheduler and session-event dispatch, registered automatic-final/message-tool paths, adapter authorization, worker-backed local Messages database lookup, native imsg RPC, and native database delivery readback. **Stand-in:** a deterministic loopback OpenAI-compatible model selected a final response or one message tool call. It did not provide a reply ID; the runtime inherited it. This is transport/runtime proof, not model-quality evidence.

The observation-only Node loader adds metadata logging to compiled modules in memory; files on disk and production source remain unchanged. No authorization result, arguments, return values, or native send are mocked/changed. Original and instrumented module hashes are below. Internal IDs and native GUIDs are SHA-256 hashes so the chain can be correlated without disclosing identifiers or destinations.

For each lane, the SAME event-ID hash appears at session-event creation, implicit adapter input, and `missing-implicit-anchor-dropped`. Native RPC then has no `reply_to`; its receipt GUID hash matches the exactly-one native message row marked sent/delivered with error=0. Both scheduler runs are delivered, without fallback; the tool lane records matching message-tool delivery. Native thread-originator fields are null.

Setup attempts are excluded from the successful trace: the initial run-scoped session was expired and generated one diagnostic failure-alert DM; a subsequent model fixture mismatch produced intentional silence. These were inspected before the corrected runs. No uncertain send was retried. The temporary automation was removed after delivery evidence; the isolated Gateway exited cleanly and the local model server stopped. Production Gateway remained running unchanged.

**Remaining limits:** recipient UI was not inspected; this uses a DM, not the original group/weather fixture. No identical-fixture baseline run is claimed. Prior release-based live observations remain separate historical evidence. The routed-reply consumer-test finding was subsequently addressed in `c2d22e2ac68` (test-only; production code is unchanged from this live capture).

<summary>Captured transition, scheduler outcomes, and correlated native readback</summary>

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The real-Gateway automation ownership test counts an Activity recap request as an automation execution call. A completed legacy run can therefore fail its exact two-call assertion even though the execution witness was written.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. The fixture keeps its strict execution, credential, model-selection, ownership-transfer, and persistence checks while serving Activity recaps separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing mock inference classifier to recognize the source-owned Activity recap system prompt before naming or execution bookkeeping. Other tool-less requests continue through the existing checks.

## Evidence

- [Original CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44566158760/job/135709305299): exact two-call assertion received three calls.
- Two isolated Linux baseline runs at `0eb6488cd3ce5918c4d1fe48d0a4bb4cd2d290a2` reproduced the failure. The extra request was tool-less, contained the completed synthetic answer, and did not activate the settled-turn finalizer.
- Local ClawSweeper review of `0eb6488c…11ecb4a6` found no actionable findings (correctness confidence 0.93); the review was read-only.
- The full real-Gateway file passes both original cases on macOS arm64 with Node 24.22.1 (title 2.819s; ownership 9.335s). A temporary counter observed five exact Activity recap matches; it was removed afterward. All original two-model, execution witness, credential, transfer, and persistence assertions passed unchanged.
- Targeted formatting, type-aware lint, and the UI E2E typecheck leaf pass.
- Candidate Linux coverage remains for ordinary PR CI; the two Linux runs above are baseline evidence, not candidate passes.

prs.title: fix(doctor): warn about Docker and image problems for per-agent sandbox configs
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #201988

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who enable sandboxing per agent (`agents.entries.<id>.sandbox`) would get a clean `openclaw doctor` report while that agent's sandboxed turns fail. Doctor only inspected `agents.defaults.sandbox`, so with per-agent-only sandboxing it never reported Docker being unavailable and never warned about (or offered to repair) a missing sandbox image — including a per-agent `docker.image`. The first visible symptom was a failed sandboxed turn. The Linux Codex bwrap namespace note was skipped the same way.

- **Related:** #201988 (issue body already pinpoints `resolveEnabledSandboxBackend` vs the runtime's agent-first mode resolution); no competing open PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor now enumerates every sandbox source it must treat as enabled — `agents.defaults.sandbox` plus each agent entry whose resolved mode is not `off` — using the same fallback chain as the runtime (`agentSandbox ?? globalSandbox ?? default`, including the `shared` scope's exclusion of agent docker/browser overrides). For each source it reports engine unavailability and missing images with the config path and per-agent disable hint, and dedupes identical (engine, kind, image) checks so defaults+agent overlap never double-prompts. Defaults-only messages are byte-identical to before.

- **Intended outcome:** per-agent-only sandboxing produces the same Docker-unavailable warning and missing-image repair prompt that `agents.defaults.sandbox` already gets, naming the offending agent entry.
- **Out of scope:** no changes to runtime sandbox resolution, no new config surface, no UI changes.
- **Highest-risk area:** message/behavior drift for the existing defaults-only paths.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** all 23 existing `doctor-sandbox` unit tests pass unchanged; new tests pin per-agent behavior (entries + legacy list rosters, mode inheritance, per-agent image, bwrap note).

## User Impact

Users enabling sandboxing per agent now learn about broken sandbox prerequisites from `openclaw doctor` before a turn fails, and can repair them with `openclaw doctor --fix` — including per-agent images. Reviewers should focus on `src/commands/doctor-sandbox.ts` (`resolveEnabledSandboxSources`) and the regression tests in `src/commands/doctor-sandbox.per-agent-sandbox-mode.test.ts`.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** built CLI (`pnpm build:runtime`) in a worktree, isolated state dir with `agents.entries.work.sandbox = { mode: "all", docker: { image: "evidence-sandbox:missing" } }` and `agents.defaults.sandbox` unset; real Docker client 20.10.0; Linux host.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  pnpm build:runtime
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/issue-201988-state node openclaw.mjs doctor --non-interactive
  DOCKER_HOST=unix:///tmp/nonexistent-docker.sock OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/issue-201988-state \
    node openclaw.mjs doctor --non-interactive
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/doctor-sandbox.per-agent-sandbox-mode.test.ts \
    src/commands/doctor-sandbox.warns-sandbox-enabled-without-docker.test.ts
  bash skills/fix-pr/scripts/validate.sh src/commands/doctor-sandbox.ts \
    src/commands/doctor-sandbox.per-agent-sandbox-mode.test.ts
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.commands-doctor.json --builders 1
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  Doctor: Sandbox
  ◇  Sandbox ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
  │  Sandbox mode is enabled for agent "work" (agents.entries.work.sandbox,  │
  │  mode: "all") but Docker is not available.                               │
  │  Docker is required for sandbox mode to function.                        │
  │  Isolated sessions (automations, sub-agents) will fail without Docker.   │
  │  Options:                                                                │
  │  - Install Docker and restart the gateway                                 │
  │  - Disable sandbox mode: openclaw config set                              │
  │    agents.entries.work.sandbox.mode off                                   │
  ╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

  (Docker reachable, per-agent image absent)
  ◇  Sandbox ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
  │  Sandbox base image missing: evidence-sandbox:missing. Build or pull it  │
  │  first. Sandboxed turns will fail until the image is available.          │
  ╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** `openclaw doctor` reports Docker unavailability for the agent-only sandbox config and checks the per-agent `docker.image` (offers `doctor --fix` repair for default images); both doctor sandbox health paths now cover per-agent sources.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** same commands on `origin/main` (`4c444a51b9e`): the "Doctor: Sandbox" section prints no warning at all — neither for the Docker-unavailable case nor for the missing per-agent image (`grep -c "Sandbox mode is enabled" before-doctor-docker-down.log` → 0). First symptom was the failed sandboxed turn, exactly as reported.
- **What was not tested:** no podman backend run against a real podman daemon (covered by unit tests with synthetic engine descriptors); `doctor --fix` image build itself was not executed against the real Docker daemon (prompt path is covered by existing tests).
- **Proof tier:** L2
- **Proof limitations:** none
- **Review state:** Awaiting CI + maintainer review

prs.title: fix(update): finish the Gateway restart a shipped pnpm updater refused
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A pnpm install updated by published 2026.11.5 to a release with the same database schema (2026.11.5 → 2026.11.6) keeps a working `openclaw` command. Since #201735 the Gateway stays down: `openclaw update` exits 1 with `service-revalidation-failed`, and the restart and the recovery restart are refused with `managed-service-ownership (service-ownership-changed)`. In a real cell the Gateway stayed down for 402 s, until the user ran another command.

Root cause, in the installed updater, which this change cannot patch:
- After the package swap, 2026.11.5 checks the service's loaded command against the new root (`update-command-service-revalidation.ts:333-398` at v2026.11.5).
- Its fallback compares against the pnpm global entry, which pnpm has just repointed into a new versioned store directory. The unit still names the 2026.11.5 store entry, so the service looks foreign.
- `main` fixed this check (#201735), but only a fixed updater runs it. 2026.11.5 hands the remaining steps to the new package only when the schema migrated (`update-command-migrated.ts:141-146` at v2026.11.5).
- So schema-migrating hops already work (2026.11.4 → 2026.11.6, 2026.11.5 → 2026.11.10, both shown in real cells), and same-schema hops do not.

## User Impact

On a same-schema pnpm hop driven by 2026.11.5, the Gateway now comes back on the new version without another command. The new package's Doctor, which that updater does run after the swap, prints one line saying OpenClaw will try to restart the Gateway after the updater exits. After the updater exits, a background process refreshes the service definition and starts the Gateway through the ordinary `openclaw gateway install --force` and `openclaw gateway start` owners. The installed updater still prints its own failure and exits 1, because it decides that before this code can act.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is compatibility code for shipped updaters that cannot be patched. It applies to 2026.11.5 and earlier, and to 2026.11.6 and 2026.11.10 builds without the #201735 fix. The module comment names those versions, and the module is removed once no supported upgrade path starts from such an updater.

Two other routes were rejected:
- **Forcing the handoff by reporting a schema migration that did not happen.** That would publish false `dataAtRisk`/no-rollback records and turn off the updater's own recovery.
- **Editing the unit from the Doctor during the update so the shipped check passes.** On systemd the shipped check reads the manager's loaded `ExecStart` over D-Bus (`systemd-service-files.ts:204-222` at v2026.11.5), so passing it would need `daemon-reload`. The updater also spawns its Doctor with service repair and activation disabled.

How it works:
- **Gate.** The Doctor step "Gateway restart handoff" in `src/flows/doctor-health-startup.ts` acts only when all of these hold:
  - an update is in progress, and the parent's no-repair and no-activation flags are set;
  - exactly one running update run, whose recorded driver is alive and is this Doctor's parent;
  - the running package is the active pnpm global entry's store directory;
  - the service names this same pnpm home's store entry for an earlier version, is owned by this installation, and has a writable definition.
- **Spawn.** The finisher is spawned detached and confirms that it took the single-instance lock before the Doctor prints its line.
- **Wait and re-check.** It waits up to 60 minutes for the run to finish and the updater to exit. It acts only on `service-revalidation-failed`, and re-checks every gate under the Gateway service operation lock. It yields if a newer update started, if the service is running, or if the Gateway answers.
- **Fixed drivers.** The driver's version cannot tell a fixed build from an unfixed one, so the gate does not use it. Under a fixed driver the finisher only waits for the run to end with another outcome and exits.
- **Recording.** On success it records the verification on the run (existing fields) and a warning row. If it gives up, the warning names the reason and the verified recovery: `openclaw gateway install --force`, then `openclaw gateway restart`, or `openclaw triage`. A real cell showed that `openclaw gateway restart` alone exits 78 in this state.

**Where the finisher runs.** On Linux it is launched through `systemd-run --user --scope --collect --unit=openclaw-update-restart-<runId>.scope`, using the managed-service handoff launcher's existing `systemd-run` resolution (`update-managed-service-handoff-launcher.ts`). Without its own scope it would share the updater's cgroup and die with it. For a Gateway-started update, that cgroup is the transient `openclaw-update-<id>.service` (`KillMode=control-group`, v2026.11.5 `update-managed-service-handoff-launcher.ts:49-76`), which stops when its helper exits. The scope has no `PartOf=` on the Gateway, so the finisher's own `gateway install --force` cannot stop it. If `systemd-run` is missing, it falls back to a plain detached spawn. On macOS it is a detached process.

**Single instance.** A per-run file lock. The existing owners were checked and none fits:
- the update executor fence and the managed-handoff lease are exclusive per installation, so holding either through the wait would block the `openclaw update` the finisher must yield to, and the lease has no row kind for this;
- the Gateway service operation lock serializes every Gateway command, so it is taken only around the final re-check;
- `sqlite-live-owner` authorizes only the Gateway's own database reads.

**What readers show after a successful finish.** The stored run keeps `status: failed`, `reason: service-revalidation-failed`, plus the verification and the warning row; no new field or status value was added. `isRefusedRestartFinishedLater` (`src/infra/update-run-restart-finished.ts`) recognizes that combination. With it:
- `openclaw update status` leads with "✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.11.6 (from 2026.11.5); 1 warning needs attention.";
- it states that the recorded outcome is unchanged, and drops the failure lines and the triage advice;
- the Control UI update card shows no failure banner, and the chat `/update` summary reads as updated;
- `update status --json` prints the stored record unchanged;
- a run that gave up still reads as failed.

**Gateway-started updates.** The shipped 2026.11.5 Gateway refuses `update.run` for a pnpm global-virtual-store install before changing anything (`update.ts:427-432`, install surface `package-root`). So that path never reaches the finisher. That refusal also exists on `main` and is handled in a separate PR.

The docs correct the earlier claim that 2026.11.4 and 2026.11.5 always hand the later steps to the new package: they do so only when the schema migrates.

## Evidence

Draft. Unit tests: `update-shipped-restart-finisher.test.ts`, 14 tests, using a real update run ledger and a real pnpm store layout on disk. Each gate was removed in turn, and every case that guards it failed. Real Docker cells on the 2026.11.6 line (#201739 plus this commit) are running and will be added here:
- green: 2026.11.5 → this build;
- the user running a plain `openclaw update` 5 s after the failure;
- npm control;
- fixed-driver control;
- forced post-swap failure;
- 2026.11.4 start;
- the CLI-started and Gateway-started hops on real systemd.

The red cell is published 2026.11.5 → #201739 head `848912c`: exit 1, the Gateway down for 402 s, and back only after a second update.

**Start layout covered.** Every cell starts from a registry install made by `pnpm add -g`, which puts the package in `store/v11/links/@/openclaw/<version>/…`. That is also where a user who recovered by hand with `pnpm add -g` ends up, so a later update from such an install starts from the layout the cells already use. The target layout is the project-store layout the updater itself produces (`global/v11/<group>/node_modules/.pnpm/openclaw@<version>…`), which a real public-registry cell confirmed.

## Steps left to a person

None on the covered hop. If the finisher gives up, its warning names the verified recovery and `openclaw triage`.

## Not proven yet

- **Target layout from a registry: now covered.** A real cell ran published 2026.11.5 → a plain `openclaw update` → published 2026.11.6 from the public registry only. The updater installs a registry target in the project-store layout (`global/v11/<group>/node_modules/.pnpm/openclaw@<version>…`), the same layout class the earlier tarball-target cells used. See https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201739#issuecomment-7018135106.
- **Still unproven:** a fixed target installed from a registry. It cannot be exercised before a fixed version is published; the fixed builds were proven as tarball targets.
- **Still unproven:** pnpm 11, which ignores the `virtualStoreType=project` setting the updater passes, so its target layout may differ. A pnpm 11 cell is being prepared.
- Real systemd and launchd, the Gateway-initiated update path, and `KillUserProcesses=yes` at logout. In the last case the next `openclaw update` or the verified recovery heals the install.
