prs.title: feat: notify users when they arrive or leave, using device location updates
prs.body: Resolves #163480 ## What Problem This Solves iOS nodes emit `location.update` events on significant location changes, but the gateway drops them as `unsupported_event` — verified by two independent users on current builds (#163480). This PR makes the event consumable and closes the full chain: **fix → significance detection → event-driven APNs notification**, with no heartbeat, no session turn, and no coordinates in logs. - **Gateway:** `location.update` is validated, dispatched to the node-event consumer registry, and instrumented at the dispatch boundary. The response ack path no longer crashes (`logGateway.info` → `warn` — every event ack previously failed with `UNAVAILABLE` after dispatch). - **Plugin surface:** `registerNodeEventConsumer` — a plugin-API subscription hook for gateway-validated node events (currently allowlisted to `location.update`). This is the "plugin hook" requested in #163480. - **memory-core consumer:** armed location intents evaluate each fix against fence geometry. Enter fences fire on the first inside fix when armed from afar (previously required a 0→1 crossing that never happened when the intent was armed while already outside); stale-facts-cache reads no longer mask fires. - **Direction-gated crossings (bug fix):** an exit fence no longer fires on an arrival fix, and an enter fence no longer fires on a departure fix — see below. This was found during live verification, not by the test suite. - **Delivery:** fires push an APNs alert at fire time (new plugin-SDK surface `sendNodeIntentAlert`, category `openclaw.location-intent`) — delivery no longer waits for the target session's next turn. The routed system-event enqueue is retained as an in-session record; push failures are logged and never re-arm the one-shot. ## Direction-gating bug (found and fixed during live verification) `decideLocationFire` gated only *one* side of each transition on direction. The inside branch fired for `previous === 0` regardless of direction, and the outside branch fired for `previous === 1` regardless of direction. Consequences observed on real drives: - **2026-11-13 06:33** — a Göteborg *arrival* fence fired on the user's morning *departure* from inside the fence. - **2026-11-16 15:29** — a home *exit* fence fired while the user was *arriving* home (the fix that also correctly fired the Göteborg arrival fence in the same second). Both branches are now direction-gated: `enter` fires only on 0→1 (including the first inside fix when armed from afar), `exit` fires only on 1→0. Each branch carries the live-fire evidence in a comment, and two regression tests cover both directions — the existing test's comment promised this behavior but never asserted it, which is how the bug survived review. ## Evidence - **2026-11-14, live drive:** Skene fence (1.5 km, enter) fired on a real outside→inside crossing from an unsolicited background fix; the APNs alert appeared on the owner's phone (screenshot-timestamped, matching the log fire and the intent description text). Exactly one fire, no duplicates. - **2026-11-16:** home-exit fence (200 m) fired on a real departure; the ack-crash fix verified live (three fixes traced, zero `UNAVAILABLE`). - **2026-11-17, full drive test (3/3 fences, 0 evaluation errors):** | Time | Fence | Fix distance | Accuracy | Outcome | |---|---|---|---|---| | 10:58:46 | home exit (200 m) | 7 m *inside* | 16 m | baselined, **no fire** ✓ | | 11:21:49 | home exit (200 m) | 512 m outside | 46 m | **fired** — correct direction | | 11:37:28 | store (1000 m) | 427 m from store | 11 m | **fired** | | 11:42:51 | destination (1000 m) | 52 m from center | 34 m | **fired** | All three notifications owner-confirmed on the phone (screenshots matching the log timestamps). The exit fence baseline-then-fire sequence is the live proof of the direction-gate fix; the destination fire (52 m from a decoded Plus code) validates arrival geometry end to end. - Consumer tests assert: single push per fire, fire-on-first-inside-fix, no re-arm on push failure, and both direction gates. - **2026-11-18, latest-stable upgrade proof:** the review asked for upgrade evidence covering the changed `standing_intents` fields. The v2026.11.5 release's shipped agent schema (schema version 38, pre-location `standing_intents`) is frozen as a fixture; a database built from it migrates to the current schema, the four additive location columns and `idx_standing_intents_location` arrive, an existing keyword-intent row survives untouched with absent-feature defaults, and a location intent in the stored kernel format is accepted by the migrated table's constraints. Covered by `openclaw-agent-latest-stable-upgrade.test.ts`; fence evaluation and delivery on the identical post-migration shape are covered by memory-core's suites. The added test lines carry a justified allocation record (`config/test-lines-allocations/200867-location-update-consumer.txt`). - **2026-11-18, PostgreSQL store upgrade (review P1):** opening an existing PostgreSQL agent database previously failed schema admission after this change — the location columns changed the canonical DDL with no version bump or migration, so `verifyPostgresSchemaDefinition` threw a schema-drift error, and the migration derivator made every historical version inherit the new fields. The agent schema now advances 43 → 44 on both engines through the existing versioned-migration owners: a new PostgreSQL migration adds the columns, NOT VALID checks (all-new columns cannot be violated by existing rows), and the index in one transaction; the v43 migration entry now targets the pre-location historical shape so old versions keep their real catalog; SQLite converges through its existing additive machinery on every migration branch. Schema 43 remains a supported witness version. Verified by the same suites as above — 55/55 across migration, latest-stable, and location kernel tests. - **2026-11-19, shipped PostgreSQL live-server upgrade (v2026.11.5, schema 38 -> current, the complete migration chain):** the prior entry showed only the final v43 -> v44 hop. The test now builds the predecessor from the v39 migration step's `fromSchema` — the schema-38 shape the v2026.11.5 release actually ships — so reopening at the current schema runs the full shipped 38 -> 44 chain through the engine's own reopen-driven migration on a live PostgreSQL 16 server. Terminal output (redacted; connection string and namespace elided): ``` opened v38 (v2026.11.5) store, namespace: evidence_v44_agent_... pre-upgrade standing_intents columns (16): channel_scope, cooldown_seconds, created_at, creator_sender, description, expires_at, fire_count, id, intent_key, last_fired_at, max_fires, sender_scope, source_session_id, status, trigger_embedding, trigger_keywords confirmed: NO location columns in the pre-upgrade store --- reopening at schema v44 (destination admission) --- destination admission: SUCCESS (verifyAndRecordPostgresSchema passed, version 44) post-upgrade standing_intents columns (20): ... delivery_target ... last_inside, location_trigger ... trigger_kind idx_standing_intents_location: CREATE INDEX idx_standing_intents_location ON ... standing_intents USING btree (status, trigger_kind NULLS FIRST, location_trigger NULLS FIRST) existing keyword intent preserved: status='armed', location columns default NULL location intent accepted by the migrated constraints existing keyword intent still queryable on the upgraded store evidence namespace dropped; server clean EVIDENCE COMPLETE: shipped v2026.11.5 (schema 38) -> v44 PostgreSQL upgrade succeeds; existing data preserved and usable ``` A keyword reminder armed on a real schema-38 v2026.11.5 store survives the complete shipped upgrade chain usable, destination admission validates the migrated schema against the canonical DDL, and a location intent is accepted by the migrated constraints — the shipped-upgrade evidence and the data-model compatibility proof for both remaining before-merge items. Reproducible as `src/state/openclaw-agent-v44-postgres-upgrade.evidence.test.ts` (infra project) against any PostgreSQL 16 server; the connection arrives only via the OPENCLAW_PG_EVIDENCE_CONNECTION environment variable (never committed) and the test skips without it. ## Known limitation: fence radius cannot buy lead time at driving speed Reported by the owner on the 2026-11-17 drive: the store fence fired **after** he had passed the store. Measured along-track against the store→destination leg, the firing fix was **+404 m past** the store (137 m cross-track, 427 m straight-line — i.e. comfortably *inside* the 1 km circle, 573 m from the edge). The cause is fix cadence, not fence logic: - 4.28 km travelled between consecutive fixes → 49 km/h on a ~5-minute significant-change cadence - a 1 km circle is a 2 km-wide band; at 4.28 km spacing the chance any given fix lands inside is only ~47%, i.e. whether it fires before or after the POI is close to a coin flip **Enlarging the radius does not fix this.** To gain one fix-interval of lead you would need R > 4.2 km at 50 km/h and > 6.7 km at 80 km/h. At that size the notification fires while the user is kilometres away, so "you're passing the store" becomes false. Radius trades precision for reliability; there is no setting that delivers both at driving speed. This is a property of the fix-delivery platform, not of the fence evaluator. The mechanism that actually fixes approach timing is **device-side region monitoring** (`CLCircularRegion`, 20-region limit): the OS surfaces a callback *at the boundary crossing*, independent of the significant-change cadence. That is the planned device-fence direction, and this drive is its concrete justification. Until then, a fence that fires shortly *after* a high-speed POI is behaving as designed given the fixes it receives. ## Consent and privacy (answers the labels on #163480) - **Consumption is consent-scoped:** fixes are evaluated only against location intents the user explicitly armed ("notify me when I arrive at X"). No armed intents → no consumption into anything user-visible; fixes are evaluated and discarded. - **No precise-location persistence:** coordinates are never written to gateway logs, prompts, or system events. The dispatch-boundary log line records the event name and node id only. (The prior closed PR #50936 was flagged for passive precise-location delivery; this design evaluates and discards.) - **No autonomous turns:** a location fire pushes a notification and enqueues a passive in-session record. It never starts an agent turn — consistent with the passive device-event direction (#196989). Any follow-up ("lets stop by X") is a user-initiated turn. - **Existing consent basis:** the event only exists when the user has granted iOS Always location to the app; this PR consumes that signal purpose-scoped, per #163480's discussion. ## Scope boundaries - One consumer per event by design (registrar rejects a second subscriber for `location.update`; dispatch uses first-match). Fan-out to multiple consumers is a deliberate follow-up, not included here — it widens the location access surface and deserves its own security review. - No fix history is stored; fixes are evaluated against armed intents and dropped. A bounded presence/fix store is a separate proposal. - The event-driven push is the interim surfacing policy ("fired ⇒ notify"). Whether and how to notify is a policy layer question; the follow-up direction (below) explores a tunable local judge for it. - Device-side region monitoring (the fix for the lead-time limitation above) is out of scope for this PR. - **File structure is ratchet-driven, not stylistic.** `location.update` handling lives in `server-node-events-location.ts` alongside the existing `server-node-events-*.ts` handlers. The chat `subscribe`/`unsubscribe` arm moved to `server-node-events-chat-subscription.ts` for one reason: the dispatcher is grandfathered in `config/max-lines-baseline.txt`, and that ratchet rejects *any* growth, so a two-line case arm plus its import had to be offset. That extraction is behaviour-preserving and covered by the existing chat subscribe/unsubscribe tests, but it is unrelated to this feature — call it out if you would rather it land separately. ## Follow-up direction (not in this PR) Significance is currently declared geometry. The next layer separates geometry (deterministic, in code) from interruption policy (a local decision model, evaluated only on events, with the fence verdict as the fail-open baseline). An 11-case eval (incl. negative controls and a conjunction scenario: "passing a store × open shopping-list need") found local decision models (`clef-flash`, `d3:2b` via Ollama's `/v1/systemone`) that discriminate correctly with ~160-token calls. Full methodology and results: https://gist.github.com/zigit/8c765c33d1edea1435f9b26d6d22c896 This PR intentionally ships only the deterministic layer. ## Why this shape (the box, not the cloud) > "It ain't gonna be some cloud… then I don't know who has my shit. It will be > like a box that knows what I need, and when I pass by Ralph's on my way home > I get a message: 'You know we ain't got no milk.' That's what I expect we > have in the future." > > — will.i.am, on stage at CES 2013, as recalled by this PR's author That quote is the reason this PR is shaped the way it is, and the reason the example notification in the drive-test screenshot reads *"We ain't even got no milk."* Thirteen years later the box is an OpenClaw gateway on a Mac, the milk is a reminder in a local database, and the message arrives within a few hundred metres of the store — verified on a real drive, with the notification landing on the phone as the car passed. Two parts of the quote turned out to be design constraints rather than rhetoric: - **"not some cloud… I don't know who has my shit"** — fixes are evaluated against armed intents and discarded; coordinates never reach a log, a prompt, a system event, or a third-party API. The follow-up judge layer runs on a local decision model precisely so that the one component that reasons about *where you are* does not require sending *where you are* anywhere. - **"knows what I need"** — the trigger is a conjunction the user declared (an armed intent, an open shopping need), not an inference over harvested behaviour. Consent is the mechanism, and it is per-intent and revocable. This PR ships the deterministic half: geometry in code, significance declared by the user. The contextual half — a small local model deciding whether a crossing is worth interrupting you — is the follow-up below. ## Change type - [x] Bug fix (ack-path crash; enter-fence miss when armed from afar; direction-ungated crossings) - [x] Feature (node-event plugin hook; event-driven location-intent push) - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Docs - [ ] Tests (covered by existing consumer tests; new asserts added for both direction gates)

prs.title: improve: avoid an extra worker during transcript archival
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cold transcript maintenance qualifies its database readers on the session-store lane, then starts a foreground-history worker just to enumerate the same targets. A cold process can pay for a second transcript worker before archival begins.

## User Impact

Reuse the already-qualified store lane for cold target inventory. This is intended to avoid an unnecessary worker startup when history is cold. A process whose history reader is already active may see no memory reduction. The completed serial owner-workload comparison reduced cold-history median end RSS by 117.563 MiB (7.028%) and removed one transcript-worker startup in every cold pair. This is not Gateway RSS or concurrent-load proof. This PR remains on performance HOLD.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the existing session-store lane to the cold-inventory read owner, matching ordinary store inventory. Registry checks, qualification before FIFO admission, replacement detection, final validation, and reader cleanup stay in place. No pool merge, new cache, configuration, dependency, or schema change. Store-lane contention remains an unresolved merge gate. Foreground-history latency during active cold inventory must be qualified before lifting HOLD; the prewarmed control does not test concurrent load.

Existing inventory tests cover replacement and rejection for status and maintenance on this route. They are safety coverage, not a claimed failing baseline for the startup count. The committed archive-worker workload now reports worker starts and separates cold-history from a real prewarmed-history reader.

## Evidence

Source review and final committed-range local review found no actionable findings. Linux Node 24.22.1 and pinned Bun each passed the corrected nine-case inventory suite; the unchanged four sibling files contribute 44 previously passed cases per runtime, qualified by a complete physical-source comparison. Scoped format, lint, types, and the full candidate-tree build passed. The required isolated Gateway cold-storage flow subsequently PASSED: automatic archival, hot reload, missing-payload/backup refusals, restart/recovery, and archive/restore byte checks; all three task-owned Gateway process groups were absent afterward. Earlier budget/preflight attempts did not execute this proof. Exact-head required CI/native acceptance remains incomplete.

The build succeeded with five advisory UI budget violations: largest CSS gzip 57.2 > 56.9 KiB; total CSS gzip 331.1 > 329.4 KiB; total CSS raw 1707.5 > 1699.4 KiB; chat boot JS requests 21 > 20; chat boot JS gzip 1302.6 > 1301.4 KiB. Their attribution is unproven; this PR does not claim those budgets passed.

### Acceptance rule declared before measurement

- Workload: committed `scripts/perf/archive-worker-churn-measure.ts`, 64 finished sessions across two stores, 40 sweeps per fresh process, no built-entry override. Its real archive/restore byte oracle must pass in every process. This is a representative small-device fixture, not proof for the benchmark default of 10,000 sessions or large installations.
- Two separately reported modes: cold-empty-history and `--warm-history` (two real reads through one retained reader, with a foreground-worker assertion). Prewarming is not concurrent user load.
- Five serial counterbalanced baseline/candidate pairs per mode: 20 fresh processes, independent n=5 per arm per mode. Identical committed workload, Node 24.22.1, dependencies, full source graph and fixture; only the reviewed cold-target owner differs between arms. The baseline is a counterfactual using the frozen pre-change cold-target module on the same candidate graph, not a separate historical build.
- Counts first: every cold pair must remove exactly one history worker startup, with no added worker in another lane. The prewarmed mode must add no worker startup. Report all-worker and per-lane counts, not just archive workers.
- Report iteration 0 separately. For iterations 1–39, summarize each child's median and p95 before comparing arms; 195 sweeps are not 195 independent samples. Include spread, paired deltas, process CPU, main-thread CPU, event-loop p99/max over each whole 40-sweep child, and host load.
- Report process-wide RSS before/end and the 25 ms sampled peak separately from worker counts. Never add isolate heaps or call this Gateway RSS. Both arms use the same source loader and owner-overlay mechanism; this is an owner workload, not a pristine no-preload process. No RSS saving is assumed.
- Acceptance cells are fixed before the run: for each mode and each declared latency, CPU, RSS, or event-loop metric, compare the baseline and candidate arm median and p95 across the five independent child summaries. Use the usual midpoint median and nearest-rank p95 (`ceil(0.95 × n)`, so the maximum for n=5); adverse percentage is `100 × (candidate / baseline − 1)`. Cold iteration 0, each child’s warm median, and each child’s warm p95 stay separate. Report every matched-pair delta and range as well; do not select a different estimator after seeing results. A zero baseline gets an absolute delta, not an invented percentage, and any increase remains a regression under the rule below.
- Win requires the count reduction and no regression in the declared latency/CPU/memory/tail metrics. Disclose every adverse cell; a >=20% adverse cell stops acceptance. Any worse metric needs explicit owner acceptance recorded here, not an appeal to noise. Otherwise remove the change if no measurable gain.

The rule above was published before measurement in body SHA-256 `49c5ceb46724af1bf87e465aac43363a48b76cb4972309570f3c0771abc19cb3`. The historical instrumented diagnostic motivated this experiment and does not qualify this candidate or waive another PR's HOLD.


## Completed measurement — acceptance HOLD

All 20 fresh serial children completed with exit 0, no signal/error, 40 observations each (800 total), matching archive/restore byte oracles, and zero active/pending lane tasks. Full source and installed-dependency seals matched before/after. Execution is valid; acceptance is still HOLD: **14 of 56 aggregate cells worsened; none reached 20%**. No adverse cell has been waived. There are also 46 adverse matched-pair deltas, including 16 at least 20%; correlated metrics/checkpoints are not separate independent experiments.

Cold-history first-operation median wall time fell 22,098.191 → 14,531.898 ms (−34.239%). Median end RSS fell 1,672.773 → 1,555.211 MiB; sampled peak fell 1,672.648 → 1,555.086 MiB. All five paired cold end-RSS deltas improved (−70.719 to −148.395 MiB). Prewarmed-history median end/peak RSS fell 1,727.367 → 1,709.641 MiB (−1.026%), but first-operation median wall/process CPU/main-thread CPU increased 3.551% / 5.390% / 11.774%. Their causes remain unproven; instrumented diagnosis is separate from acceptance.

The 40 measured sweeps have no eligible archive work; each process then exercises one eligible archive and verifies restored event bytes. These numbers describe the committed owner workload, not 40 real archival jobs, total OS threads, a pristine no-loader process, or Gateway memory. The 25 ms RSS sampler stops before the separate endpoint read: three sampled peaks are 128 KiB below end RSS. The two measurements remain separate.

### Work counts

All five pairs in each mode had the same counts below. Counts are starts in the measurement window; cumulative lane counts include the prewarming worker.

| Worker type | Cold A | Cold B | Prewarmed A | Prewarmed B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Transcript | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Logger | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| Native lifecycle | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| State reader | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Archive | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Gateway state heartbeat | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **All tracked starts** | **6** | **5** | **4** | **4** |
| Cumulative history-lane workers | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| Cumulative store-lane workers | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| Cumulative search-lane workers | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

### All adverse aggregate cells

| cold history | warm child median / wall ms | median | +0.877% |
| cold history | warm child median / process CPU ms | median | +4.490% |
| cold history | warm child median / main-thread CPU ms | median | +0.280% |
| cold history | RSS before MiB | median | +0.553% |
| cold history | RSS before MiB | p95 | +1.545% |
| prewarmed history | first operation / wall ms | median | +3.551% |

| prewarmed history | RSS before MiB | p95 | +0.770% |
| prewarmed history | whole-child loop p99 ms | median | +4.741% |
| prewarmed history | whole-child loop max ms | median | +7.539% |

### Remaining contention gate

The exact-head hosted review requires resolving simultaneous cold inventory versus ordinary store reads before merge. A source-backed bounded risk remains: with two SQLite history workers busy, cold inventory occupying one store worker can overlap another status request’s pre-FIFO qualification and create a second store worker (four retained workers versus three in the baseline scenario). Existing pool caps and retirement remain; this is not evidence of an unbounded leak. Serial/prewarmed measurements do not resolve that overlap or prove load savings. No readiness, auto-merge, or threshold change is implied by this update.

### Complete measurement tables

A = the frozen pre-change cold-target owner on the same candidate graph; B = this PR. Values are rounded to three decimals; percentages/deltas were computed from unrounded values. RSS units are MiB, other row units are shown. Arm p95 over five children is the maximum, distinct from a child’s warm p95 over 39 sweeps.

prs.title: fix(macos): launch alert shows the CLI's schema refusal instead of generic credential steps
prs.body:
Closes #201468

## What Problem This Solves

When the macOS app's bundled CLI refuses a forward schema migration because an older Gateway service still uses the same state, the launch alert hides the refusal. Instead it tells the user to run `openclaw doctor --fix` and restore backup credentials. Doctor meets the same refusal, so that advice cannot work, and the refusal's own remedy appears only in the unified log.

## User Impact

User impact: with an older, separately installed Gateway service (for example a global npm install), the alert now shows the CLI's refusal. The refusal names both versions, the service's install root, and `openclaw update`.

Every other credential startup failure still shows the existing Doctor/backup recovery, unchanged. That includes native credential admission errors, other CLI failures such as an invalid config, timeouts, and the background-only stderr path.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ClientCredentialStartup.prepare` now throws a `PreparationError`. When the CLI exited with the refusal from `assertGatewayServiceSchemaMigrationAllowed` (`src/state/openclaw-state-service-installation.ts`), the error also carries that sentence. The launch handler shows that sentence only for that refusal.

Two cases deliberately keep the generic recovery:

- **Native admission failures**, such as `Local client credential schema does not match version 1`. They carry no next step. This addresses the earlier review finding.
- **The previous build's app-managed service**, the `StaleGatewayServiceReplacement` path. There the refusal names `openclaw update`, which reports `host-managed` on an app-owned install, so it would replace one wrong instruction with another. That variant has a different root cause: replacement stops the service, but the guard reads the installed service definition. It is described in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/201468#issuecomment-7020325845 and belongs in its own fix.

The alert title and the generic text are the existing strings, so the localization inventory does not change. The branch is rebased on main after #201505, so the handler uses `requestTermination()`.

## Evidence

- **Regression test** (`ClientCredentialStartupTests`): drives the real `prepare` boundary with a child CLI that exits 1 and prints the refusal on stderr. It asserts:
  - the recovery is exactly the refusal sentence;
  - it is `nil` (generic recovery) on the app-managed replacement path;
  - it is `nil` for a native admission error;
  - it is `nil` for an unrelated CLI failure (the existing failed-preparation test).
- **Composition test:** the `ClientCredentialStartupCompositionTests` malformed-config launch keeps its expected `OpenClaw client credentials need recovery.` stderr. The earlier revision of this PR would have changed it.
- **Local checks:** `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passes (`changed=false`) and `git diff --check` is clean. All changed Swift lines are within the 120-column limit.
- **Gaps:**
  - I worked from Windows without a Swift toolchain, so the Swift build and native tests run only in `macos-swift` CI.
  - I have no Mac, so there is no after-fix screenshot of the real launch alert against an older service. If a maintainer or one of the reporters can run the packaged app in that state, that is the remaining proof.

prs.title: fix(linux): let dashboard users grant microphone access
prs.body:
Closes #202024

## What Problem This Solves

Microphone input in the Linux companion's embedded Gateway dashboard fails with “Microphone access is blocked. Allow it in browser site settings to list inputs.” The embedded app has no browser site-settings permission control, leaving the user unable to grant access.

## User Impact

The registered Gateway dashboard can request microphone access through a native Allow/Deny dialog that identifies the Gateway origin. Deny is the default. Camera and screen capture are not granted, and ordinary embedded browsing tabs and widgets do not receive this handler.

**Limitation:** this fixes microphone permission, not complete Realtime Talk support. On the tested Ubuntu 22.04 / WebKitGTK 2.50.4 installation, `RTCPeerConnection` remains unavailable, independently of microphone consent. Realtime Talk still needs a WebRTC-capable browser runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Linux shell did not handle WebKit's media permission requests. The change installs an audio-only consent handler before a registered dashboard starts navigation and uses the existing Gateway document owner to admit requests. A pending dialog is cancelled on navigation or closure; accepting a stale dialog cannot grant access to another dashboard.

The change adds no dependencies, stored permissions, Gateway configuration, or browser-engine packaging. WebRTC experiments have been excluded from this patch.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the failure through the actual Linux desktop binary on base `cd2ae19272a3ee7be456385fa7efc56d6e2109a6`, using an isolated local HTTP dashboard fixture: `getUserMedia({audio:true})` returned `NotAllowedError` without a prompt. The patched desktop binary displays the native consent dialog. The reporter also confirmed the prompt in their actual Gateway dashboard.
- The native GTK/WebKit regression passes with synthetic capture devices: Allow returns an audio track; Deny, combined audio/video, and an unadmitted origin all reject. It never records a physical microphone. The test is explicitly display-dependent and must be invoked with `--ignored --test-threads=1`.
- All 53 existing `gateway_windows::` tests pass.
- Locked Linux debug build, Rust formatting, targeted documentation formatting, and patch whitespace checks pass.
- Author simplification/code review completed. Local autoreview and ClawSweeper are not installed; no independent review is claimed. Hosted review and CI remain pending.

The screenshots below show the real desktop app displaying a synthetic dashboard fixture, not a full authenticated Talk session. The “after” image is the native dialog; the “before” image is the dashboard's rejected capture result. Images contain only fixture content.

### Before

![Before: microphone capture fails without a consent prompt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/861b9824-6deb-4027-9ade-13e97b8f9128)

### After

![After: the Linux app offers Deny and Allow for microphone access](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08b2274d-8618-4337-a214-684ad1b5d1eb)

<details>
<summary>Focused verification commands</summary>

```sh
cd apps/linux/src-tauri
cargo +1.97.1 fmt --check
WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1 WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1 \
  cargo +1.97.1 test --locked --bin openclaw-desktop \
  microphone_linux::tests::webkit_microphone_consent -- --ignored --test-threads=1
cargo +1.97.1 test --locked --bin openclaw-desktop gateway_windows::
cargo +1.97.1 build --locked
```

The renderer environment settings work around this test host's graphics issue. EGL warnings also occurred during the passing capture tests.

</details>

**Do not merge this proposal.** Corrective head `f8eec7035cdbcf8d7d664e2cf37ccc29e5e62423` restores the unsafe deletions from prior head `a46afa9e1284d6a03f92c7a91ca492b872cdb046`. [Periphery job 132524038529](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43618219498/job/132524038529) flags `OpenClawIDDiscoveryAccountError` as unused. A source audit found no Swift changes in this PR: the shared-kit, iOS, macOS and intersection-script sources match the actual CI base `aedf`. The type is still thrown at `OpenClawIDDiscoveryAccount.swift:208` and declared at line 227; no deleted test references to it were found.

This establishes **no identified deletion path**, not an executed green-main result or a baseline waiver. The shared OpenClawKit intersection failure **also reproduced on main** at `989f4a6d1e4096461fc6c4fbae993f56f3b02a6e`: [main job 132532509861](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43620917710/job/132532509861) reports the identical `OpenClawIDDiscoveryAccountError` declaration and exits 1. The branch is based directly on frozen main. Inventory cleanup stays coupled to this part's deleted files. The existing Windows test command drops only the deleted `test/scripts/worker-deploy-build-plugin.test.ts` argument.

## User Impact

No production behavior change. Production LOC: **+0/-0**. Tests remove **30,560 lines**; 13 inventory/selection owners remove **62 net lines**; the manifest adds **33 lines**. The Windows test-command edit is **+1/-1**.

The follow-up owner-builder audit removed the three stale `docker-release-artifacts` shorthand outputs while preserving other owners and the input-routing selectors.

prs.title: fix(agents): node tools with an unverified plugin owner can pass plugin-ID tool policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a node tool that claims a plugin owner it is not registered under can pass a tool policy that allows tools by plugin ID, when the tool was first admitted through a broad plugin grant.

## User Impact

User impact: a plugin-ID entry in a tool allowlist now admits only tools whose ownership was verified when the node tool was materialized. The same holds for the tools a cron job captures from its creator, and for descriptors that use a case or whitespace variant of the reserved owner name without being genuine node-MCP descriptors. Exact tool-name grants, broad plugin grants, registered owners and genuine node-MCP descriptors behave as before. Deny rules still match on the claimed owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node-tool materialization already distinguishes verified from claimed ownership, but that distinction was lost in policy metadata, in caller snapshots and in cron creator-tool capture. The reserved-owner exception also normalized the ID without checking that the descriptor really has the node-MCP shape. The ownership decision is now made once, during materialization: the reserved exception requires the core MCP command and non-empty server and tool metadata, and unverified ownership is carried through the policy and cron projections. Plugin-ID allows and intersections expand using verified owners only.

## Evidence

Run with Node 24.22.2 and pnpm 12.15.0. Transport is mocked; no remote tool is invoked.

- The regression in `src/agents/node-plugin-tools.test.ts` uses real node publication, materialization, policy filtering and cron creator selection. Replayed unchanged against `main` it fails 7 of 25 cases; on this branch all 25 pass.
- A second, separately written test set covering the policy pipeline, caller snapshot, cron creator selection and reserved-owner variants: 19 failed / 6 passed on `main`, 25 passed on this branch.
- Changed-scope suites (policy, cron, caller and delegated authority, node snapshots, effective-tool reporting, embedded construction, prompt-prefix stability): 20 suites, 359 tests passed.
- Full build and all test typechecks passed. Scoped lint reported no warnings or errors across the ten changed TypeScript files; formatting, policy guards, import cycles and the test-line budget check passed. The per-change test allocation is 140 lines.

Gap: the broad `pnpm check` passed production, UI, extension, script and root-test types and script lint, then extension lint reported two line-limit errors in unchanged Tlon and Crabbox tests that also occur on an untouched `main`; the remaining core lint scan was stopped there, so the full check is not claimed green locally.

### Running Gateway with a connected node

A real built Gateway and a real built node host were started from each revision, with device and node pairing approved through Gateway RPC. Synthetic external plugins supplied harmless marker tools. A loopback MCP HTTP server stood in for the node-MCP far end, and a loopback Responses endpoint stood in for the model, recording the tool names it was offered. Neither is a hosted service or a real model. No product source was changed and the same driver ran on both builds.

- Base: `b382a29a688a`. Head: `3d064663c293`. Node 24.22.2, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, private-QA build.
- Policy: `tools.allow = ["policy-owner", "node-mcp", "policy_exact", "automations"]`, full profile, Code Mode and Tool Search off. `node.list` confirmed the published descriptors. Offered tools were read from `tools.effective` and from the requests of a completed turn, which agreed.
- In that turn the model stand-in created a cron job through the product's `automations` tool; `cron.get` returned the persisted tool cap. The policy was then replaced through `config.patch` with `["policy_exact", "automations"]` and the job was run with `cron.run`.

| Synthetic tool | Base: offered | Base: in cron cap | Head: offered | Head: in cron cap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `policy_verified` (registered, verified owner) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| `control_probe` (genuine node MCP) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| `policy_claimed` (claims `policy-owner`, not registered under it) | **yes** | **yes** | no | no |
| `policy_exact` (exact-name grant) | yes | yes | yes | yes |

After the plugin-ID entries were withdrawn, the cron run was offered only `policy_exact` on both builds.

Not observed: a non-MCP descriptor using a case variant of the reserved owner could not be published through the normal node-plugin loader on either build (the manifest loader rejects the reserved ID case-insensitively), so that case is covered by the unit regression only.

Limits: local stand-ins for the MCP far end and the model; offerings and the cron cap were observed, not execution of an excluded tool; restart and crash recovery were not exercised.

prs.title: fix: reconnect shared provider credentials outside the agent roster
prs.body:
Closes #195867

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: operators cannot reconnect shared provider credentials through native sign-in after the legacy `main` owner leaves the runnable agent roster.

## User Impact

An authorized operator can sign in once to the canonical shared credential owner. Inheriting agents continue to read through the common store while keeping their individual models, model policies, and private credential overrides. Shared sign-in rejects `--set-default`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve this explicit login target only when inheritance names `main`, that agent is absent, and the existing canonical ownership rules admit the target. Use the current credential writer, profile-order owner, and runtime refresh path. Discovery uses the configured ambient agent; `main` remains a credential owner without becoming a runnable agent.

The normal unknown-agent guard stays intact. Shared login cannot cross the admitted state owner, and administrator admission, current authority, revocation, and ownership-change checks remain active. There are no new flags, configuration keys, protocol fields, schemas, dependencies, or token-copy operations.

The auth context is extracted into a sibling module to keep the existing file within its growth cap. The separate test allocation covers only the measured regression growth.

## Evidence

Reviewed head: `f4265dbc55fd5c1283312d78ad0fc238e746cb30`, based on `7ebc4f3e67137c34b0850dfa8cab2b8d68e6576d`. Current main was checked again before publication; none of the touched paths changed through `bbf0d7380315f660bf79561223da1d34eadd4ac3`.

- Baseline: the actual shared-login RPC wizard rejects the absent canonical owner with `Unknown agent id "main"`.
- Fixed: 11/11 owner regressions and 113/113 related native-owner tests pass.
- Core types, targeted typed lint, runtime build, formatting, file-growth caps, and the native test-line budget pass. The allocation matches 272 net added test lines.
- An independent source review found no remaining actionable findings. Final fixture identifiers were anonymized bijectively; the 11 owner tests and formatting/budget checks were rerun afterward. Unchanged production hashes bind the preceding types, lint, sibling tests, and build; these were not described as rerun.
- The successful runtime build emits nonfatal UI size diagnostics: largest JS gzip 564575 versus 564484 bytes, chat boot 1267.2 versus 1266.4 KiB, and new boot 784.7 versus 784.4 KiB. Attribution to this change is unproven; no budget guard or override was changed.

The native owner fixture uses synthetic OAuth, real task-owned SQLite stores, and Gateway RPC. It checks shared persistence and profile order, refreshed inherited views, preserved private overrides and model policies, and rejection of unknown/mismatched owners, a changed owner, revoked authority, and a different state root. A successful shared login does not prove that every private override should be removed.

No real credentials, private configurations, personal sessions, or runtime logs are included in this PR. The public-head proof uses synthetic provider I/O. A separate integration was used to smoke-test native provider sign-in and ordinary inference; that is not presented as an exact-public-head live-provider test.

prs.title: fix(webchat): show denied slash command feedback
prs.body:
## Problem

Related: #198259. When commands.allowFrom legitimately rejects a password-authenticated Control UI caller without a matching verified sender identity, plain-text /status previously vanished without a reply.

## Change

Internal WebChat command denials now return a visible refusal with an actionable next step: “Ask your Gateway administrator for command access.” The native-command branch remains first and preserves its existing wording. External /status text and native wrappers retain their existing silence. This changes feedback only: operator.admin does not bypass commands.allowFrom, and verified identity, authorization checks, owner attribution, and scopes are unchanged.

The correction also updates the /learn undo and /loop regressions to expect the visible refusal while retaining no-effect assertions.

## Current corrected candidate

Signed candidate: 683d6c24b54059a95ecfac1354050ea480142ec1. It adds a one-line persisted Workshop /learn undo consumer correction to bddd6464b82dfbefff03179a40470bddf89447f1; earlier corrections fixed the /loop expectation and denial-table type inference. Production remains identical to 66dbaeef42542e6f22616cb20d621c39a0bebdab; baseline remains d43de8d733674c942c8eb7bfb7333a30de4f910f.

- Exact current Workshop correction: all 34 integration tests passed under Node 24 in secretless, network-disabled Podman. Messaging typecheck, targeted type-aware lint (zero warnings/errors), formatting and whitespace passed. Independent review of blob 4fd157b30afd3bdc445c0652fa44bfd8e7e6e5e0 is READY with no findings. The persisted feed and both skill-file no-effect assertions remain unchanged. Initial dependency/cache setup failures occurred before meaningful testing; the corrected isolated setup passed.
- Previous exact loop correction: 9 tests passed; messaging typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting and whitespace passed. The no-rewrite assertion and owner-only denial remain intact. Independent exact-blob review READY, no findings.
- Previous 3817b584: 26 commands-info tests and messaging typecheck passed. These repeat prior coverage, not additional distinct tests.
- Previous 66dbaeef: four focused suites / 70 tests and full build passed (2m 19.6s). Budget warnings are not performance qualification.
- Full-delta and subsequent test-only correction reviews retained. Neither old-head results nor pending/skipped checks establish current-head broad green CI.

## Current guidance browser proof

One real-Gateway Chromium scenario passed in a secretless, network-disabled Podman container. It uses real browser pairing, a synthetic session, a nonmatching commands.allowFrom identity, and /status entered through the composer. The screenshot below visibly includes the administrator-guidance sentence. No cloud model was contacted. The image was inspected and contains synthetic content only.

Provenance: archived source and compiled Gateway/UI from 66dbaeef; all subsequent published corrections through 683d6c24 change tests only, so production source is identical. Supplemental browser harness and package build artifacts were staged separately. Earlier attempts failed during dependency setup before Gateway readiness; they are not browser proof and did not replace historical captures.

![Current production guidance: unauthorized command with administrator next step](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d25a984-4ac9-4c49-9f31-dacf2139ca0c)

## Historical real-Gateway visual proof

The original two-file denial patch was tested on canonical main d43de8d733674c942c8eb7bfb7333a30de4f910f in an isolated, network-disabled Playwright container with a task-owned real Gateway and real browser pairing. This is **historical main-plus-original-patch proof, not exact-candidate proof of the corrected administrator-guidance wording**.

The scenario creates a synthetic session, sets an allowlist identity that does not match the authenticated WebChat operator, and sends /status through the visible composer. Before: the command finishes silently and the refusal assertion times out. After: the original bare refusal is visible. No cloud model is contacted. Both screenshots were inspected and contain synthetic content only.

| Before (main) | After (main plus original denial patch) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: slash command has no refusal](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/521273ab-3196-4759-b508-c131354291e7) | ![After: visible authorization refusal](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66a96235-52f9-4535-8c5c-353b9586fcba) |

## Current-head CI and remaining qualification

**Technical review-ready; broad CI remains red, not merge-ready.** On November 16, 2026, native exact-head commit validation and correction-review gate admission completed successfully for 683d6c24b54059a95ecfac1354050ea480142ec1; the latter records `github_pending`, not successful CI proof. Feature-specific proof is satisfied by the retained focused checks and real-Gateway browser scenario on identical production bytes. No further PR-caused defect was demonstrated. The PR remains draft because the shared publisher's original publication receipt names an older head and refuses promotion of the current head; that publication-state blocker is separate from technical review readiness. Full run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43632645107 completed on November 14, 2026, at 21:48 UTC: **269 jobs, 232 successful, 23 failed, 3 canceled, 11 skipped, zero pending**. The 23 failures include the aggregate ci-gate, leaving 22 substantive failed jobs. Actual checkout logs confirm candidate **683d6c24b54059a95ecfac1354050ea480142ec1**, trusted harness **c31bb2a16d8c766b7ae191cb9c266dfdbb12a543**, and baseline **d43de8d733674c942c8eb7bfb7333a30de4f910f**; workflow metadata alone was not treated as checkout proof. Validation used full tier with no release gate. This is completed observation and attribution, not broad-green or merge readiness.

The corrected Workshop QA4 job 132563023849 passed under both Node and Bun: 63 passed files / 1 skipped in each invocation, including the previously failing persisted unauthorized /learn undo case. The current messaging typecheck passed. All five Windows shards passed. QA10 passed 64 files / 1,150 tests under each runtime. These successes do not erase other failures or incomplete suites.

All substantive failed jobs and all three canceled jobs were examined. Attribution distinguishes demonstrated source defects, exact recurring signatures, and independent boundaries with unresolved dynamic causes:

prs.title: perf(agents): prepare skill read attribution per snapshot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every read-tool attribution walks the selected skills and re-derives their host and path aliases. Large skill catalogs therefore spend CPU and allocate temporary path strings even when a read is unrelated to a skill.

## User Impact

Skill attribution performs a prepared lookup. Skill precedence, workspace-host exclusion, node identities, command activation and emitted telemetry remain unchanged. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Snapshot publication, hydration, resource remapping and harness handoff prepare one read-path index. An owner-managed WeakMap keys it by the immutable snapshot: the harness clones and deeply freezes its plain-data snapshot, so an attached Map would violate that boundary. The index cannot cross cloning, serialization or object spreads; remapped snapshots cannot inherit old host aliases. Later skills overwrite earlier aliases to retain `findLast` precedence. Typed external snapshots initialize the same index on first use.

The repeated field-type checks were redundant with the resolved Skill contract. Existing whitespace semantics remain. Canonical telemetry still resolves the matched file through the existing filesystem-aware owner; that result is not an immutable snapshot fact.

The production diff is +28 lines: snapshot index lifecycle and six owner preparation boundaries replace the per-call scan. No global string-keyed cache is added.

## Evidence

Acceptance written before measurement: 200 synthetic skills × 10,000 calls to the real attribution owner; preserve complete match output; remove per-skill work from warm calls; CPU/allocation improvement must exceed A/A spread. Five interleaved pairs per measurement; timing and allocation collected separately. The fixture includes workspace/Gateway hosts, node paths, 6,700 matches and 3,300 misses. This owner does not access session databases or discover workspace files.

| Metric per 10,000 calls | Baseline median [min–p95] | Candidate median [min–p95] |
|---|---:|---:|
| CPU, ms | 387.888 [384.916–407.002] | 24.491 [24.310–25.012] |
| Wall, ms | 387.929 [384.906–407.041] | 24.468 [24.290–24.992] |
| Sampled allocation, MB | 785.860 [780.258–786.624] | 19.595 [19.308–20.045] |

A/A CPU medians: 402.803 / 393.490 ms (2.31% spread). A/A allocation medians: 784.680 / 785.121 MB (0.06%). Cold preparation median 1.790 ms (0.214–2.011 ms; CPU median 1.660 ms), outside warm timings. Node v26.12.1; 1-minute host load 5.65–6.95. V8 allocation sampling includes collected objects. With five samples, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum; these are owner measurements, not whole-Gateway latency claims.

The baseline visits 1,338,350 skill entries; the candidate prepares 200 entries once, then performs 10,000 lookups. Full-match digests agree in every run. Separate CPU profiles confirm the per-skill path-resolution frames disappear.

Reproduce with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/skill-usage-match-measure.ts [timing|allocation|cpu] [owner.ts] [profile-output]`. Preserve the base diagnostics module beside its source as `agent-tools.before-tool-call.diagnostics.baseline.ts` for baseline runs.

Validation: 230 distinct focused tests passed across nine files, covering publication, hydration, remapping, resource transfer and the actual before-tool-call wrapper/telemetry flow. The new differential test covers 80 randomized snapshots; the work-count regression fails on the base and passes with the index. The changed test file took 9.53 seconds including compilation/import (31 ms differential test, 2 ms work-count test). The complete focused run took 316 seconds including a successful fresh build.

Independent Codex autoreview, including the frozen harness handoff, of the complete staged change against `32d629f3ef0bbb10440716d4475e731a5f6ec717`: scoped-clean through P2, no actionable findings. `pnpm check:changed --staged --base 32d629f3ef0bbb10440716d4475e731a5f6ec717` passed on the final source; both production and full-tree `pnpm deadcode:unused-files` scans passed. An initial brace-only lint failure in the test/benchmark was corrected before the final clean run. Landing requires exact-head green CI and a completed ClawSweeper review with no open items.

prs.title: test(update): add a Git release upgrade-survivor scenario
prs.body:
## Problem

#201874 shipped because no upgrade lane ran a Git install. All 35 upgrade-survivor scenarios start from an npm package, so the Git release layout from #199706 never booted in CI before users hit it.

## Change

- Adds an opt-in `git-release` upgrade-survivor scenario. Starting from `7db69bedeab6` (the #201874 reporter's build), it:
  1. builds the checkout and installs the Gateway service (systemctl shim);
  2. lets that build convert the install onto the old release layout;
  3. reproduces the type-stripping failure through the Gateway;
  4. updates to the candidate twice, the first run by the old build and the second by the candidate;
  5. asserts the release left `node_modules`, the old link is gone, and `tools.invoke web_search` succeeds with no stripping error in the Gateway log.
- The scenario stays out of the aggregate lanes and the published-baseline matrix; run it with `OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_SCENARIO=git-release`. Three full builds take about 24 minutes, so it gets a 3600 s container timeout.
- Corrects the update guidance in `docs/install/updating.md`. The run showed two things:
  - The old release cannot run its own updater, so users must update from a terminal with the checkout's `openclaw`.
  - With a web search provider configured, the Gateway on the old layout fails at startup.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_SCENARIO=git-release bash scripts/e2e/upgrade-survivor-docker.sh` against #201917's head `6b5d14b1`: exit 0, `summary.json` `passed`, 23m35s. Step results are in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201917#issuecomment-7016805807
- The same scenario against tag `v2026.11.5` shows the published release never takes the release layout: its updater returns `root: …/git-checkout` with no release link.
- `ocx test` on the survivor catalog, baseline, plan and qualification tests; `bash -n`; `git diff --check`.

prs.title: fix: observer fallback models get time after a primary timeout
prs.body:
Related: #191600, #191653, #196345

## What Problem This Solves

Session assessments can stop even when a configured recovery model is usable. The observer's shared timer includes preparation, every fallback candidate, and the JSON validation retry. Increasing that timer by the configured candidate count does not fix a slow invalid first reply followed by a valid retry: 25 seconds plus 10 seconds still exceeds the default 30-second deadline.

## User Impact

Each completion keeps its existing bounded execution budget, including configured fallback candidates and the second JSON-output attempt. Caller cancellation and physical settlement retain their existing ownership. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing bounded preparation phase, then clear its timer when preparation finishes. Isolated completion already owns candidate deadlines, cancellation, and cleanup. #191199 owns the richer utility-fallback diagnostics; this PR does not duplicate them.

The integrated base's regression still expected the retired shared signal to abort after 60 seconds. It is now reconciled with the actual utility fallback owner: parameterized recovery and exhaustion cases verify both candidates receive 30 seconds, the request does not finish before the fallback's turn, and the observer releases its active controller. The existing JSON retry and physical-settlement regressions remain covered.

#191653 gives one pass through the configured fallback chain more time, but leaves both JSON attempts under the same observer timer. #196345 makes invalid output advance to utility fallbacks and retains the second JSON attempt. The remaining problem here is the timer shared by both attempts.

## Evidence

- Current upstream `fbacc803` versus this exact PR head, with the actual observer module, simulated time, and stubbed model completion: an invalid response at 25 seconds followed by a valid retry at 35 seconds hits the outer 30-second timeout on main and succeeds on the PR. Both attempts receive the unchanged 30-second budget. The preparation watchdog and caller cancellation still work in both versions. This is a focused timer test, not a new transport or production Gateway run.
- Current head: `b06239dbe55c7bd98967341364e25861569f1302`; integrated base: `84a72ed32320a44ac161e1e0be4f858d44861b3c`.
- The original merged consumer was reproduced locally with its `expected true, received false` failure before updating it. Removing the production repair from the current integrated tree also makes the candidate-exhaustion and JSON-retry regressions fail: **2 failed, 1 passed, 11 skipped**. Restoring the repair returns the two complete gateway files to **22 passed**. The utility completion runtime file separately produces **17 passed**.
- The gateway run took **29.31 seconds wall time**, mostly compiler preparation and imports; the prior run took 35.58 seconds. Individual completion cases took at most 214 ms with fake timers. No wall-clock sleeps were added.
- Focused oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Full-index test-line accounting reports `6653545` lines against a `6653549` ceiling, with **4 lines of slack**. The separate `session-observer-candidate-deadlines.txt` allocation is exactly **91** lines, matching net regression growth across the two files. The shared scalar baseline is unchanged.
- The current narrow typecheck did **not** run to completion: the repository's declaration-input guard rejects the existing dependency installation outside this checkout. No guard was bypassed and no dependencies were reinstalled. The repaired head's hosted production and test typechecks now pass; earlier-head local typecheck results are not claimed for this head.
- Local self-review covered the complete four-file change against the integrated base, timer ownership, both fallback outcomes, JSON retry, cancellation, settlement, and the allocation. This is not a claim that local autoreview or local ClawSweeper ran.

The current fallback regressions execute the real utility fallback runner with controlled candidate I/O. They are not live-provider or production-Gateway validation. Earlier loopback HTTP evidence at `621fc9b34240818185a75e692f3204e3c7572c07` exercised default preparation/completion, utility fallback, isolated completion, and real local HTTP transport: the primary timed out after 29,771 ms, the fallback returned a valid digest, and the active controller was cleared. That is prior-head transport evidence, not a fresh transport run on this head. The current production change still clears the same preparation timer; no provider adapter or isolated-completion implementation is changed by this PR.

Fresh hosted checks are green: 51 passed, none failed or pending, and run `42974000216` completed successfully at this exact head. This includes the repaired changed-test lane, baseline ratchet, and production/test typechecks. Maintainer review remains pending. The full local suite, live model service, production Gateway, and native addon execution are not claimed as passing.

prs.title: fix(update): recognize pnpm 11 group-local virtual stores as global installs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On pnpm 11, OpenClaw's own updater installs the new package into the group's local virtual store, with `.pnpm` directly under the group:

`<PNPM_HOME>/global/v11/<group>/.pnpm/openclaw@<version>_…/node_modules/openclaw`

A real pnpm 11.28.13 cell (published 2026.11.5 → plain `openclaw update` → public 2026.11.6) produced exactly that layout. pnpm 12 uses `<group>/node_modules/.pnpm/…`.

pnpm layout inference in `src/infra/update-global.ts` only recognized the pnpm 12 form. A pnpm 11 install addressed by its real path was therefore classified as an unmanaged `package-root`, with three effects:
- An update or Gateway `update.run` started with that root is refused (`unmanaged-package-install`).
- Doctor and Control UI detection report the install as unmanaged.
- The refreshed Gateway service definition pins the per-version `<group>/.pnpm/openclaw@…/dist/…` path (`src/daemon/program-args.ts:81-99`) instead of the stable `<hash>/node_modules/openclaw` entry. pnpm removes that directory on the next update.

## Root Cause

`inferPnpmProjectRoot` (`src/infra/update-global.ts`) accepted only `node_modules/.pnpm`. For the pnpm 11 form it took the project to be `<group>/.pnpm/openclaw@…`, so it never reached the `v11` global root.

## Fix

The same matcher now accepts both `<project>/node_modules/.pnpm/<pkg>/node_modules/openclaw` and `<project>/.pnpm/<pkg>/node_modules/openclaw`. No second matcher was added. The `.pnpm` branch of `inferPnpmGlobalRootFromPackageRoot` already runs the isolated-root check first, so it needed no change.

`resolvePnpmGlobalInstallOwner`, which the program-args refresh uses, now finds the active entry, and the saved service definition names the stable `<hash>/node_modules/openclaw` path.

`rewritePnpmVersionedOpenClawEntryPath` (`src/infra/openclaw-root.ts:10-19`) is unchanged. For grouped layouts it can only yield the per-group `<group>/node_modules/openclaw`, which is not stable on pnpm 12 either. The stable entry comes from the argv launcher root and the owner lookup.

The shared-store guard is kept. A real path inside the shared content store, `store/v11/links/@/openclaw/<v>/<hash>/node_modules/openclaw`, still does not count as the install owner, and a test now asserts this with that realistic path.

## User Impact

- pnpm 11 global installs are recognized as pnpm installs when addressed by their real path.
- After an update, the Gateway service definition names the stable entry, so the next update does not leave the service pointing at a removed directory.

**Update behavior:** this is a fix in the new package's own detection. It applies when this code is the running updater, Gateway or Doctor. Shipped updaters keep their behavior.

## Evidence

Each unit case was red on the base where marked, then green:
- `src/infra/update-global.bun-owner.test.ts`, "detects a pnpm v11 install by its real path in the `node_modules/.pnpm` / `.pnpm` virtual store". The `.pnpm` case failed on the base (`{kind: "package-root", mode: "unknown"}`) and passes now. It covers detection, `resolveUpdateInstallSurface` and `resolveTarget`.
- Negative controls in the same file, green:
  - an application image's `app/.pnpm`;
  - `app/node_modules/.pnpm`;
  - a stale `v11` group with no active link and no lockfile, which stays unmanaged (removing the lockfile requirement turns it red);
  - the shared-store real path, which stays `package-root`;
  - npm and Bun globals, unchanged.
- `src/daemon/program-args.pnpm.test.ts`, systemd case over both virtual-store forms. The `.pnpm` case failed on the base with ENOENT, because the saved entry pointed at the removed per-version directory. Now it saves `<hash>/node_modules/openclaw` and runs the replacement version.
- `src/infra/update-native-package-stage.test.ts`, a new `pnpm11-grouped` launcher-stage case covering relocation of a `<group>/.pnpm` candidate and its NODE_PATH. It passes on the base too, because the stage does not use this inference; it guards the layout.
- `src/infra/update-launcher-repair.test.ts`, a pnpm 11.28.13 shim captured from the real cell, with no `PNPM_HOME` and the root set to the `.pnpm` real path. It passes on the base too, and fails if the `/global/v\d+/` home marker is broken.

Checks:
- touched and adjacent tests pass (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`, 20 files, 284 tests);
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass;
- oxfmt and oxlint are clean, and both import-cycle checks report 0;
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` passes and `git diff --check` is clean.

Real-cell evidence of the pnpm 11 layout and the shipped failure:
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201739#issuecomment-7019905738
- Real pnpm 11 cells on a fixed build with this commit are queued.

### Cherry-pick for the release line

This is one self-contained commit. It applies cleanly onto `release/2026.11.6` (stacked on #201739) and `release/2026.11.10` (#201740 merged with the current release tip). On each, the touched tests pass (45) and `pnpm tsgo:core` passes. It will be added to those backports as a separate commit after this PR has its final head.

## Not proven

- Real pnpm 11 cells on a fixed build with this commit are queued.
- The Control UI half is not in this PR: a Gateway whose root is the pnpm 12 store-link real path is still classified `package-root`. That is a separate PR at the Gateway's root owner, because it has to handle several global groups linking the same store directory.

## Steps left to a person

None for this change.

prs.title: fix(cron): report undelivered native-only WebChat results
prs.body:
Related: #197884

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a route-less automation can report successful delivery even when its channel-native-only result was deliberately not added to the creating WebChat conversation.

## User Impact

Such a result now records Not delivered with an explicit missing-visible-content error. Normal text/media results still use the supported creating-conversation fallback; confirmed external native-only sends still count as delivered. No configuration, protocol, retry, or retention changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conversation writer already returns an explicit skipped outcome when channel-native content has no honest transcript projection. The cron dispatcher consumed ok but ignored skipped. The routeless branch now preserves the writer diagnostic and uses its existing delivery-target failure path, rather than asserting that something visible was committed.

## Evidence

- Baseline: 7bccde609cbb0eaa054ac07a6d5ccd91ec712a92. Two new real-dispatch/real-conversation-writer regression cases (current and isolated execution with a WebChat creator) fail on the baseline: delivered:true / status:delivered even though the writer reports native-only payload not added to conversation. Tests use isolated SQLite state and synthetic Discord embed content; no mocked commit receipt.
- Red command: node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/isolated-agent/current-session-completion.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "does not report a native-only". 2 failed, 15 skipped; 97.49s including cold worker compilation, 3.72s test execution.
- Green: both complete current-session and destination-completion suites passed (33/33, 152.25s), including both new regressions, visible text/media commits, native-only external Discord delivery, lifecycle fencing, and no duplicate writes. prs.title: fix: keep Auto Review timeouts from hiding reviewer results
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/201834

Companion: [openclaw/agent-skills#398](https://github.com/openclaw/agent-skills/pull/398). Both PRs need to merge together.

CI: [openclaw/agent-skills#398](https://github.com/openclaw/agent-skills/pull/398/checks) passed every check that ran on [`9f3d03a`](https://github.com/openclaw/agent-skills/commit/9f3d03a14944e40186c54ffff312c3d620391e75): 15 passed, with 6 dispatch checks skipped.

## What Problem This Solves

Auto Review can stop a reviewer before its process budget has elapsed, or discard a completed result while it is being delivered. A late delivery failure can then hide the original timeout behind a missing-file error.

## User Impact

Updated helpers use one reviewer-process timeout, and failed result delivery preserves the original helper or reviewer failure. **Older helpers keep working with finite limits and retain their existing timeout behavior. They still need the helper update to fix the original timer race; this OpenClaw PR alone does not remove their early handoff timer.** An omitted limit retains the native 600-second default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The companion helper delegates timeout ownership to the host. OpenClaw keeps its existing process watchdog and disables the duplicate native attempt timer only when the helper advertises that capability. No limit is increased. Result delivery uses the parent lifetime, and cancellation, output limits, process cleanup, and helper validation remain intact.

## Evidence

Published OpenClaw head: [`c935e018d248d5d3c110cc8aa56b0e70b7c67716`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c935e018d248d5d3c110cc8aa56b0e70b7c67716).

Real Auto Review tool, process runner, and Python helper with a controlled reviewer process (not a live model). The same four-second budget and success assertions were used throughout. Baselines: OpenClaw 08b4ac92c1978f1f68dd78b53e7879ba24363c1b and agent-skills 3cc834ceec0410c4ff37c09e5b81c91e65fc9fc9.

| OpenClaw | Helper | Observed result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main baseline | Main baseline | **RED: 2 failed, 7 passed** — delayed launch times out early; delayed delivery returns FileNotFoundError |
| This PR's final production code | [Published companion #398](https://github.com/openclaw/agent-skills/pull/398) | **GREEN: 9 passed** |
| This PR's final production code | Old helper | 2 known race failures, 7 passed; ordinary finite/default-timeout reviews remain usable, with no capability refusal |
| Main baseline | [Published companion #398](https://github.com/openclaw/agent-skills/pull/398) | 1 failed, 8 passed — combined reviewer timeout and submission failure still hides the timeout |

The nine checks cover delayed launch, delayed delivery after successful exit, genuine process timeout, successful JSON emitted before an over-budget exit, cancellation, submission failure, timeout plus submission failure, finite-limit smoke, and omitted-limit smoke. Both fixed delayed-completion cases return complete validated reports; over-budget cases never report success.

The matrix predates test-only simplification; production bytes are identical to the final candidate (OpenClaw tool Git blob 16ed8be900589022c2c1b2a463a88b031fcd0d45; helper script blob 955877badb9f2ac2087a011fc67fb247fc030fe4). Focused tests were rerun after simplification:

- OpenClaw: 23 passed, 39.57 s including cold compilation (41.95 s wrapper wall time).
- Canonical helper: 31 passed in 13.086 s; validation passed for 9 skills.
- Focused production typecheck, lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. CI timing is not available yet.
- Independent Auto Review was interrupted without producing a report; this is **not** a clean independent-review claim. No live-model review, full-repository suite/build, or deployment is claimed.

### Simplification

Re-derived both changes around the existing process owner. Removed the unused helper-test delay parameter/sleep branch and the redundant two-pass setting in the OpenClaw submission-failure test; corrected its lifecycle comment. No assertion or production fix was removed. Whole OpenClaw delta: production +40/-11 lines, tests +57/-5, docs +11/-3. The companion removes the independent handoff timer rather than adding timeout padding.

Contributor credit: @daniel-lxs.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-t_ozxrey)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes #197806: the first macOS Speech Recognition permission callback can arrive on a TCC background queue. The callback inherited MainActor isolation, so it could trap before reaching the existing dispatch to the main queue.

## User Impact
Starting Talk Mode can complete the permission request instead of crashing at callback entry. Permission policy and existing cancellation/current-request checks are unchanged.

## Change
Use an explicitly `@Sendable` authorization callback and resume its continuation directly, which is safe from the framework callback queue. The existing PermissionManager remains the owner. The callback is now inline at the Speech framework call; the regression uses a test-only Objective-C framework-boundary fixture to deliver the callback off-main without showing a permission dialog.

## Historical evidence through November 14 (superseded below)
- Compared the reported native crash stack with the existing macOS callback and the already-fixed iOS sibling.
- Added a native regression that invokes the production authorization completion from a background queue and verifies return to MainActor. The test deliberately preserves the legacy non-Sendable framework callback type so Sendable inference cannot hide the original defect.
- Published candidate: `77ee3e8424d789b7bad5804a9dc5a1693f34c91e`, refreshed through native preparation onto baseline `2f4ae4d3284bf17ad4930cf6770dac14c025bfc1`. The permission source and regression are unchanged from original head `2b88cdfb1ce5d37f217b6e0c27145188374b72d6`; the baseline-relative product delta remains two files (+23/-5). The baseline includes the landed worker-build fix `d43de8d733674c942c8eb7bfb7333a30de4f910f`.
- Native proof-publication receipt: `PUSH_PURPOSE=proof`, `PUSH_REVIEW_OID=d0d61ba2bd17d9a6c8587053236d6a6e07840274`, `PUSH_PENDING_FINDINGS=S1`. Publication is for validation, not approval to merge. Independent correction review remains **NEEDS WORK** and S1 remains unresolved. `git diff --check` passed; source review alone is not runtime proof.
- Original-head CI run 43600769918: macOS packages and MLX jobs passed, but neither executes PermissionManagerTests. The app test job was skipped after build-artifacts failed at `identity-file.worker.js: 240 evaluated modules exceeds budget 220`.
- Automatic exact-head CI run 43620767745 completed successfully on November 14, 2026, at 17:25 UTC, but **did not execute macOS compilation or tests**. Build-artifacts job 132526082452 and both macOS Swift jobs were skipped/unselected. Preflight correctly detected the two permission files and `OPENCLAW_CI_RUN_MACOS=true`; `scripts/ci-build-manifest.mjs` explicitly suppresses native lanes for ordinary pull_request events through `!ordinaryPullRequest`. That green gate is not permission proof; actual PermissionManagerTests executed in that run: **0**.
- After the automatic run completed, launched the existing exact-SHA CI proof route once: run 43621092538, title `CI release gate 77ee3e8424d789b7bad5804a9dc5a1693f34c91e`, workflow_dispatch on the PR branch with `target_ref` pinned to that SHA, `release_gate=true`, and `pull_request_number=198869`. This is validation only, not release publication. Preflight job 132526732000 passed; its log binds both checkout and workflow revision to the exact candidate and detects the two permission files. Build-artifacts job 132527245151 succeeded, including the native runtime artifact; the former worker-build blocker did not recur. Package and MLX jobs also succeeded, but are not PermissionManagerTests evidence.
- **Actual app compilation succeeded:** macos-swift (tests), job 132529359671, compiled PermissionManager.swift and PermissionManagerTests.swift with `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --enable-code-coverage --disable-index-store -Xswiftc -gline-tables-only --build-tests`. `Build complete! (493.21s)` was logged at 17:49:25 UTC on November 14, 2026.
- **App regression execution remains incomplete:** the default native profile began at 17:49:35 UTC, but job 132529359671 hit its 30-minute limit and was cancelled at approximately 18:07 UTC. GitHub's annotation states `The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 30m0s`. Run 43621092538 therefore concluded **cancelled**, not passing. Artifact `macos-native-test-logs` (ID 14125323672) contains a 549,578-byte default-profile log. It records PermissionManagerTests suite start, one parameterized test start, and **2 argument-case starts; 0 completed PermissionManager test reports, 0 suite completions, and 0 starts of the off-main callback regression**. No passing count is inferred from starts. The log also records 600-second failures in PairingGatewayOwnershipTests and TalkModeRuntimeSpeechTests; their cause and relationship to this change are not established. No unchanged-CI rerun or unrelated timeout repair was performed.
- Base-red/fix-green callback-entry execution remains unverified. Compilation alone, incomplete suite execution, and package/MLX success do not establish that causal proof.
- This Linux host has no Swift/macOS SDK or pinned SwiftLint. No paired Mac is available; earlier macOS allocation preflights did not supply a usable worker. Next proof needs bounded execution of the actual PermissionManagerTests/off-main callback on a qualified isolated macOS worker, plus a causal negative control, rather than another unchanged broad run.
- Interactive TCC proof remains outstanding: use an isolated, stably signed macOS app at a fixed path and bundle ID, fully quit/relaunch after resetting only that test app's permissions, then exercise first-time grant and denial plus Settings recovery. No operator permissions or live services were changed. Signed Git source is not signed-app TCC proof.

## Scope
Only the macOS permission owner and its native regression. No merge, backport, or release is authorized by this proof publication.

## November 16: completed native callback qualification

The execution gaps described in the historical November 14 evidence above are now resolved for exact candidate `77ee3e8424d789b7bad5804a9dc5a1693f34c91e`. No product source changed.

- [Run 43769449537](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43769449537), tooling `a493a0599f16ed151dc8c773f280d9f8c349e7c0`: full native app/test compilation passed in 442.792 seconds.
