This is execution, not a skip or discovery-only result.
- Equivalent causal proof reaches the real Speech Objective-C boundary with synthetic OS responses. [Baseline run 43786255830](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43786255830), source `2f4ae4d3284bf17ad4930cf6770dac14c025bfc1`, compiled successfully and then trapped with **Signal 5** at the production PermissionManager callback entry, with Swift executor and dispatch-queue assertions. Its test process exited 1; the overall job passed because it verified that expected negative control.
- [Candidate run 43783553823](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43783553823), source `77ee3e8424d789b7bad5804a9dc5a1693f34c91e`, compiled and completed the same Swift boundary test with an off-main callback, exit 0. The Swift test hash matches across both runs. Objective-C fixture hashes and macOS versions differ (27.0.1 versus 27.2), so this is **equivalent causal boundary evidence**, not a byte-identical same-environment A/B experiment.
- Fresh independent read-only qualification confirms mandatory S1 callback evidence is complete. The recorded S1 acceptance requires unavailable signed-app TCC interaction to be disclosed, not silently treated as executed or added as a new gate. Native readiness is now qualified: the clean authenticated current-main wrapper (`f947bdc94981e299fe26b5a71af8bfdd4e7ac125`) already contains the bootstrap closure repair from `8743f1bfafa41aebdb3a33a7137eaa6d70bd0eb7`. It successfully ran `prepare-validate-commit`, `prepare-gates` in `github_pending` mode, and `prepare-push` for this exact candidate, preserving retained workflow `976a4fb8784a326579108e03d0df4356dad501a3`. The remote branch already matched, so publication skipped a redundant push. This is ready for review, not merge readiness or a claim that every CI check passed.

**Still unverified:** real stable-signed-app first grant, denial, relaunch, and Settings recovery. No TCC permission reset, operator app changes, credential substitution, or real user/device interaction was performed. No previously completed proof was rerun.


## November 19: remove production test seam

Published signed correction `06fcdb61e9f629b9d13b9ee85bff2cc39e4c4930` to this existing branch through native proof publication. It removes the request-injection helper, keeps the explicit `@Sendable` callback inline, and tests `PermissionManager.ensure` through the real Objective-C Speech boundary. The four-file patch does not change permission policy.

- Fresh independent source/ABI review found no P0–P2 defect. `git diff --check` passed; this is not native execution.
- The historical November 16 evidence remains valid for its named head, **not the new committed fixture**. Exact-head macOS build/link now passes; execution of the off-main regression and completion of the broad native suite remain unverified (R1). This is proof publication, not merge readiness.
- Ordinary current-head CI: run 44537484356. Current-head Periphery: run 44537484030.
- Exact-head native qualification: [run 44538193166](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44538193166), workflow source and `target_ref` both `06fcdb61e9f629b9d13b9ee85bff2cc39e4c4930`, `validation_tier=main`; completed with the results below. This runs existing CI without release/deployment. Prior request 44537528020 failed admission before native execution because main-tier validation requires the workflow and tested source to have the same revision; only the dispatch workflow-ref input was corrected.

prs.title: fix(auth): sessions stay on a backup account after the preferred account recovers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a chat keeps trying a backup account first on every turn after the preferred account has recovered. This happens when the backup cannot serve the session model.

## User Impact

User impact: with an explicit `auth.order` (preferred account first, backup second), a session returns to the preferred account once it has succeeded again. Before, every turn sent a request to the backup first and paid for a failed attempt and an in-turn rotation.

## Why This Change Was Made

An automatic session pin on a later explicit-order profile yields back only when the preferred profile still has `lastRateLimitAt` (#136784). A success on the preferred profile clears that record. Any session's success counts, including the same-turn rotation that served the request after the pinned backup failed. From then on the pin stays on the backup. It only moves when the backup's short model-scoped cooldown (30 s, reset after each expiry) happens to be active at the next turn.

The session resolver now also yields to an earlier explicit-order profile in one case. The pinned backup's latest recorded outcome must be a failure, and the preferred profile must have succeeded after it. The latest success is the later of `lastUsed` and `lastProbeAt`. Profiles inherited from the shared auth store record only `lastProbeAt` on success; the first revision of this PR read only `lastUsed` and missed them. A backup whose latest outcome succeeded stays pinned. So a preferred profile that cannot serve the session model does not cause a pin to bounce every turn. User pins, implicit order and the existing rate-limit path are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Gateway runs with a fake two-account provider

To prove the behavior, I ran a real Gateway against a local OpenAI-compatible server that plays two accounts. `mockai:primary` serves `sol` and `luna`, and can return 429 on `sol` (`retry-after: 120`). `mockai:backup` rejects `sol` with 404 `model_not_found` and serves `luna`. Config: `auth.order.mockai = [primary, backup]`, model `mockai/sol`, fallback `mockai/luna`. Profiles live in the shared state-db store, as on the affected install. Turns go through `chat.send` (the WebChat path), and each `turn` line below lists the requests that turn sent.

A full build needs about 4.7 GB of heap, which this host could not spare. So "patched" is published `openclaw@2026.11.3` with this PR's resolver change applied to its compiled `session-override` chunk. The diff is the same 7 added lines and 1 changed line as `src/`. Both runs use the same scenario and state:

1. The primary hits its limit on `sol`. A `seed` session puts it into a 120 s cooldown.
2. The first `chat` turn starts during that cooldown. The resolver auto-pins `mockai:backup`.
3. The quota resets. After the cooldown expires, an `other` session succeeds on the primary, which clears `lastRateLimitAt`.
4. Three `chat` turns follow, about 45 s apart, which is longer than the backup's 30 s cooldown.

Unpatched 2026.11.3. Every turn tries the backup first, and the pin never moves:

```text
== 22:34:14 turn session=chat: chat turn 1 after the reset
   provider: POST account=backup model=sol -> 404 model_not_found
   provider: POST account=primary model=sol -> 200
== 22:35:01 turn session=chat: chat turn 2 after the reset
   provider: POST account=backup model=sol -> 404 model_not_found
   provider: POST account=primary model=sol -> 200
== 22:35:49 turn session=chat: chat turn 3 after the reset
   provider: POST account=backup model=sol -> 404 model_not_found
   provider: POST account=primary model=sol -> 200
usage mockai:primary {'errorCount': 0, 'lastProbeAt': '-4s'}          # no lastUsed
session agent:main:chat model: sol pin: mockai:backup auto
```

```text
22:34:18 [agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: runId=proof-14eb6954d0b5 decision=rotate_profile reason=model_not_found from=mockai/sol profile=sha256:05787e2380fe
22:35:05 [agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: runId=proof-c5959e43ecc5 decision=rotate_profile reason=model_not_found from=mockai/sol profile=sha256:05787e2380fe
22:35:53 [agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: runId=proof-47c523530309 decision=rotate_profile reason=model_not_found from=mockai/sol profile=sha256:05787e2380fe
```

Patched, same scenario. After the reset, turn 1 still starts on the backup, because the backup's latest outcome was its `luna` success during the seed. That failure makes the backup's latest outcome a failure, so from turn 2 on the session returns to the primary:

```text
== 22:57:42 turn session=chat: chat turn 1 after the reset
   provider: POST account=backup model=sol -> 404 model_not_found
   provider: POST account=primary model=sol -> 200
== 22:58:46 turn session=chat: chat turn 2 after the reset
   provider: POST account=primary model=sol -> 200
== 22:59:36 turn session=chat: chat turn 3 after the reset
   provider: POST account=primary model=sol -> 200
session agent:main:chat model: sol pin: mockai:primary auto
```

### Upgrade from 2026.11.3 with saved order and a user pin

I started from the unpatched end state above. Then I added a user pin on another session (`/model mockai/luna@mockai:backup` → "Auth profile set to mockai:backup") and stopped 2026.11.3. Next I started the patched build on the same state directory:

```text
state after upgrade, before any turn:
   auth.order: {'mockai': ['mockai:primary', 'mockai:backup']}
   session agent:main:chat model: sol pin: mockai:backup auto
   session agent:main:pinned model: luna pin: mockai:backup user
== 22:49:06 turn session=chat: chat turn 1 after upgrading
   provider: POST account=backup model=sol -> 404 model_not_found
   provider: POST account=primary model=sol -> 200
== 22:50:17 turn session=chat: chat turn 2 after upgrading
   provider: POST account=primary model=sol -> 200
== 22:51:11 turn session=chat: chat turn 3 after upgrading
   provider: POST account=primary model=sol -> 200
== 22:51:32 turn session=pinned: turn on the user-pinned session (patched)
   provider: POST account=backup model=luna -> 200
== 22:51:42 turn session=fresh-after-upgrade: brand new session
   provider: POST account=primary model=sol -> 200
final:
   auth.order: {'mockai': ['mockai:primary', 'mockai:backup']}
   session agent:main:chat model: sol pin: mockai:primary auto
   session agent:main:pinned model: luna pin: mockai:backup user
   session agent:main:fresh-after-upgrade model: sol pin: mockai:primary auto
```

The saved order and the user pin survive the upgrade. A fresh session starts on the preferred profile. Turn 1 after the upgrade still tried the backup, because the user-pinned session's `luna` success had been the backup's latest outcome.

### Live install (pre-fix, stable 2026.11.3)

Order: `openai:<plus-account>`, then `openai:<free-account>`. The free account rejects 6.1 Sol with `model_not_found`. Both profiles are in the shared state-db store, and neither has `lastUsed`. Eight consecutive Telegram turns each logged `decision=rotate_profile reason=model_not_found profile=sha256:<free-account>` before succeeding on the plus account. The pin moved only when a reply came within the backup's 30 s cooldown; every earlier gap was 36–120 s.

### Tests

- In `src/agents/auth-profiles/session-override.test.ts`, the table test covers agent-local profiles (`lastUsed`) and shared-store profiles (`lastProbeAt`). For each, one case returns to the preferred profile, and one keeps a backup whose latest outcome succeeded. Both return cases fail on `main` (`expected 'openai:api-backup' to be 'openai:api-primary'`).
- `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-support.config.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/session-override.test.ts`: 26/26 pass. Without the fix, the two return cases fail. In that run, one unrelated test (`rotates to an available profile without restoring concurrent session metadata`) also failed after 111 s on the loaded host; it passes with the fix.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on both files: clean.

prs.title: improve: show plugin names and icons in Template contents without source labels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Template's page lists the skills and plugins it adds. Plugin rows showed the raw package reference (for example `@openclaw/workflow-tools`) with a generic plug icon, and every skill and plugin row carried a "ClawHub · Version 1.2.0" or "Bundled with template" label. The rows were hard to scan and looked unlike the same plugins on the Plugins page. On a phone, the "Installed" status also stacked above the row's chevron instead of sitting beside it.

## User Impact

User impact: Template contents now show each plugin by its display name and its own icon, the skill and plugin rows no longer carry source or version labels, and "Installed" stays on the chevron's line at phone widths. No migration or user action is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Plugin rows take their name and artwork from the installed inventory when the plugin is present, otherwise from the plugin catalog detail for the Template's exact pinned version. Artwork loads through the existing authenticated plugin icon transport, and the plug icon remains the fallback when artwork is missing or fails to load.
- The "Installed" check still compares the exact package and version, so a different installed version is not reported as installed.
- The stacked control layout on narrow screens now applies only to action rows (status over a button). Navigation rows keep the status beside the chevron.
- The Plugins page skill rows already had no source label; a regression assertion now protects that.
- The version remains available inside a plugin row's expanded details, and the sidebar preview's selected-item pane is unchanged.

## Evidence

Before/after screenshots (clean and annotated): [proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201652#issuecomment-7001322141). Before is the merge base `a32fc09b4ce`; after is this PR's tree. Both use the real Control UI with the same synthetic mocked-Gateway fixture.

- Red on the base, green on the head: the browser regressions failed on the old labels (`ClawHub · Version`, two `Bundled with template` labels) and on the phone alignment (status centre 22.8px above the chevron centre).
- `ui/src/pages/agents-home/templates-catalog.e2e.test.ts` and `ui/src/pages/plugins/plugin-overview.e2e.test.ts`: 37 passed on the rebased head. The cases cover installed-inventory branding, catalog branding with the exact-version request, unavailable artwork falling back to the plug icon, a different installed version not showing "Installed", and phone/desktop layout.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, scoped oxlint, stylelint, `oxfmt --check`, and `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers` pass.
- Size: production +154/-38 across five files (one new 65-line icon component), tests +104/-33.
- Review: no local automated review was run; hosted ClawSweeper review is requested through this PR.
- Not covered: a live ClawHub registry and real plugin artwork (fixture-only), and WebKit.

prs.title: fix(codex): doctor --fix removes an appServer.command that points into a missing plugin generation
prs.body:
Related: #181037
Complementary prevention (merged): #191693

## What Problem This Solves

Recovery only: older cleanup versions may already have deleted the managed Codex generation referenced by `plugins.entries.codex.config.appServer.command`. The merged prevention fix #191693 keeps configured generations on disk, but cannot restore files already deleted.

## User Impact

Run `openclaw doctor --fix`, then restart the Gateway. Doctor removes only the stale command override so normal managed binary selection resumes (or `OPENCLAW_CODEX_APP_SERVER_BIN` applies). This may select a newer Codex binary. Other app-server settings, including arguments, remain unchanged. Plain Doctor previews the repair through its existing normalization flow.

Existing generation pins, unrelated custom executables, and non-missing filesystem errors remain untouched. No runtime fallback or cleanup changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the repair with the Codex plugin's existing Doctor normalizer. Recognize only the historical `openclaw-codex-8902d781d4__openclaw-generation__g-<16 lowercase hex>` directory layout beneath the state directory's `npm/projects`, and remove the override only when the generation stat returns `ENOENT` or `ENOTDIR`.

The historical name is deliberately frozen recovery data, not a second implementation of future install naming. This removes the hash-helper dependency, duplicate containment check, and nested exception scaffolding without adding SDK surface or state. Tests use an independent historical fixture and consolidate repeated setup and assertions.

Limits: no recovery of arbitrary custom paths, pinned non-default npm roots, relative command paths, external state-directory symlink aliases, or missing binaries inside an otherwise existing generation. No claim that updating alone applies this unpublished plugin repair; direct Doctor recovery is the supported scope.

## Evidence

- Simplified head: `090cc4fea9b5`; original contributor head: `5e9100d477b2`.
- Credential-free Linux ARM64 container, Node 24.22.1, frozen dependency install; no host state or credentials mounted. Tests ran with networking disconnected.
- Focused recovery and sibling Doctor suites: **60/60 passed**, two Vitest shards in 129.43s. After cleaning leftover source files from the reused image, the recovery suite was rerun: **21/21 passed**, 66.96s wrapper / 61.51s Vitest, dominated by compilation. The subsequent final change only adds required braces to a test conditional and adjusts its line allocation.
- Both primary recovery cases fail on pre-fix `c147613091ca` because the command remains configured; they pass with the repair.
- Targeted production/test TypeScript check passed using the repository test config with the two touched files as roots. Targeted source-backed lint: zero warnings/errors (23.4s). Pinned formatting, pre-commit checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent source review: no P0–P2 findings. Local ClawSweeper completed the full `c147613091ca..be697c268f72` range: no correctness/security findings. Final delta since that review is only the test braces and 122→124 line allocation; no production changes.
- Initial package-boundary validation encountered stale source files in the reused image; these were removed before the final focused checks. No successful full repository build is claimed.
- No new live Doctor/Gateway/model/channel or latest-stable updater run was performed. The contributor's earlier live evidence below is prior-head evidence, not a claim of current-head execution. Hosted CI is pending the push.

Compared with the original revision: production additions 62 → 44; regression test lines 394 → 124. The 124-line test allocation covers missing-generation recovery, managed selection, idempotency, preservation of settings and working pins, custom-path boundaries, symlinks, and filesystem-error distinctions.

**Live run on the current head: stable 2026.11.3 writes the state, `4087062` repairs it** (2026-11-14; Linux x64, Node 24.22.1). Added after the hosted review of `4087062da5d5`; the bullet above saying that no new live run was performed and that hosted CI was pending predates this run, and hosted CI on `4087062` has since passed (`ci-gate`). `4087062` merges main at `928c118f64db` into `090cc4fea9b5`; the four files of this PR are byte-identical in both. `openclaw@2026.11.3` was npm's latest stable release at each recorded checkpoint (`npm view openclaw dist-tags` reported latest 2026.11.3 when the sign-in window opened and at the end of the run). This head also identifies as 2026.11.3 (`OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (4087062)`), so the two builds differ by commit, not by version string. The candidate was a fresh clone of `4087062` (fetched by commit id), installed with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and built with `pnpm build` in an isolated directory. Test-host adaptation: the host also runs an unrelated, older OpenClaw Gateway as a system service under another account, and because of it this head's installed-service check refused to migrate the isolated state; every command of this head in this run, including its Gateway, therefore set `OPENCLAW_SYSTEMD_UNIT=openclaw-gateway-r5p-absent.service`, a unit that does not exist, so that check did not consider that service. That service was not changed, and the setting is unrelated to the Doctor repair under test. One isolated `HOME`, so the state directory is `<home>/.openclaw`; the Gateway listened on loopback with token auth; one real OpenAI OAuth sign-in (device code); the Telegram turns came from a self-created test bot in a private chat, with plain-text messages sent by hand; the CLI turns used `openclaw agent` through the Gateway, not `--local`. Redacted output is in the collapsed block below.

- **Stable writes the state.** `npm install -g --prefix <prefix> openclaw@2026.11.3 --allow-scripts=openclaw` (`OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d)`), then `openclaw plugins install npm:@openclaw/codex@2026.11.3 --accept-capabilities`, which installed a flat managed project. The stable CLI wrote the Gateway, Telegram, tool-policy, and agent-runtime settings and the `appServer` keys `transport: "stdio"`, `homeScope: "agent"`, `mode: "guardian"`, `sandbox: "read-only"`, `approvalPolicy: "on-request"`, `requestTimeoutMs`, and `args`. At this point neither the stable CLI nor the plugin install had written `appServer.command` or `plugins.load.paths`.
- **Stable works before the stale override.** After sign-in, with the stable Gateway running, `openclaw agent --session-id r5p-cli` asked the model to remember the code word `cw-9235c2ad` and returned `CLI-PRE-OK`. After Telegram pairing, a message asking the bot to remember `tg-ab3117bc` was answered with `TG-PRE-OK`.
- **The stale override.** The Gateway was stopped, and the stable CLI set `appServer.command` to `<home>/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-codex-8902d781d4__openclaw-generation__g-a727c792f2e53a82/node_modules/@openai/codex-linux-x64/vendor/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex`. The path was written by hand, not left behind by an update or a cleanup, and no directory existed at it while the stable build ran.
- **Before (stable 2026.11.3).** `openclaw doctor` and `openclaw doctor --fix --yes` keep the command: the preview listed no removal and left the config file byte-identical, and both runs printed core Doctor's existing custom-command warning (`Custom Codex app-server command bypasses OpenClaw's managed exact-version binary.`); `--fix` applied stable Doctor's own repairs (its output reports the agent roster, the `openai/gpt-6-astra` model entry, two session titles, a plugin-registry refresh, the OAuth directory, and three disabled skills, with two `Updated config` writes) and left `appServer.command` and the other `appServer` keys unchanged. With the stable Gateway running again, `openclaw agent --session-id r5p-cli-stable` exits 1 with `Codex catalog updater cannot run: <home>/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-codex-8902d781d4__openclaw-generation__g-a727c792f2e53a82/node_modules/@openai/codex-linux-x64/vendor/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex or its working directory was not found`. A Telegram message asking for `STABLE-OK` got no reply within 3 minutes, and the Gateway logged `[telegram] dispatch failed: CodexAppServerSpawnError: Codex catalog updater cannot run: <home>/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-codex-8902d781d4__openclaw-generation__g-a727c792f2e53a82/…`, then `spooled update <id> failed; keeping for retry`.
- **Which Codex plugin this head ran.** Two Codex plugins with the same version were present: the npm-installed `@openclaw/codex@2026.11.3` in the state, which does not contain the removal message, and the copy bundled with this head's build at `<src>/dist/extensions/codex`. In a source checkout, a compiled bundled plugin under `dist/extensions` ranks ahead of a same-id npm install regardless of version; only a `plugins.load.paths` selection ranks higher (`resolveDuplicatePrecedenceRank`, `src/plugins/manifest-registry-build.ts:151-183`, compared at `:455-470`). Observed in this run: after the hand-off, this head's `openclaw plugins inspect codex --json` reported `plugin.origin` `bundled` and `plugin.rootDir` `<src>/dist/extensions/codex`, with the npm copy listed only under `diagnostics`; Doctor printed `Kept bundled plugin "codex" from the OpenClaw source build; …`, and the CLI warned `duplicate plugin id detected; global plugin will be overridden by bundled plugin (<src>/dist/extensions/codex/index.js)`; the Gateway on this build logged `duplicate plugin id detected; global plugin will be overridden by bundled plugin (<src>/dist/extensions/codex/index.js)`; and the removal message appears in this build's copy but in no file of the npm copy.
- **After (this head, same state).** The stable Gateway was stopped, an empty directory was created at the seeded generation path, and the same `HOME` was handed to this head's build.
  - First repair, generation present: `openclaw doctor --fix --yes` ran this build's pending database migrations (state database v23–v40, listed under "Doctor changes"; agent database schema v27 -> v42; pre-migration SQLite backups saved under `<home>/.openclaw/state/` and `<home>/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/`) and kept `appServer.command`, since the generation directory existed; the `appServer` subtree was byte-identical. Config changes in this run: none (the config diff was empty).
  - The empty generation directory was then removed by hand, standing in for an older cleanup that deleted it.
  - Preview: `openclaw doctor` lists `Removed plugins.entries.codex.config.appServer.command; it pointed into an OpenClaw-managed Codex plugin generation that no longer exists. …` as a pending change and leaves the config file byte-identical.
  - Repair: `openclaw doctor --fix --yes` writes it. The only `appServer` change is the removed `command`; all config changes in this run: `plugins.entries.codex.config.appServer.command` removed, `meta.migrations.skillLibraryToolSplit` and `meta.migrations.skillWorkshopPlugin` added, and `wizard.lastRunAt` updated by Doctor's run metadata.
  - Restart: the Gateway started on this build; the Codex app-server line was `Codex app-server: using bundled 0.164.0 (no codex on PATH)`.
  - Turns: in the same CLI session, `openclaw agent --session-id r5p-cli` asked for the code word and returned `cw-9235c2ad`. In the same Telegram chat, the stable-phase message that the stable Gateway had kept for retry was answered with `STABLE-OK` after the hand-off (22:09 +09:00 in the Telegram client), before the follow-up was sent and with no other message sent to the bot in between; the follow-up was then answered with `tg-ab3117bc` (about 9 s after the Gateway received the message); no spawn error was logged after either reply.
- **Preview before migration.** On a separate state written by 2026.11.3 with the same kind of command and no directory, this build's `openclaw doctor` and `doctor --lint` exited 1 because the state-database migration had not run yet (`OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; …`, `… Client credentials require backed-up migration custody; stop the app and run openclaw doctor --fix.`), `doctor --json` reported `ok: false` with the pending migrations, and none of them listed the removal; `doctor --fix --yes` ran the migrations and removed the command in the same run. So the first Doctor command after the hand-off above was `doctor --fix --yes`, and the preview ran after it. The migration step is not part of this change.
- **Existing data still loads and works (data-model compatibility).** This head first upgraded the stored data (state database v23–v40; the agent database, which holds the sessions and the auth profile, schema v27 -> v42) and then used the state written by 2026.11.3 without a new sign-in, pairing code, or token: the CLI connected with the stored Gateway token. The CLI session and the Telegram chat that 2026.11.3 wrote before the hand-off were continued after the repair, and the code words given there were answered (above); the Telegram update that the stable Gateway had spooled for retry was processed and answered by this head after the hand-off. After the Gateway stopped, this head's `openclaw models auth list --provider openai --json` showed the one OpenAI profile from the stable-phase sign-in (OAuth, not expired), `openclaw pairing list telegram` showed no pending request, and `openclaw sessions --json` listed the two CLI sessions (`r5p-cli`, `r5p-cli-stable`) and the Telegram session. The npm-installed `@openclaw/codex@2026.11.3` was left in place: the `npm/projects` listing was identical before and after this head's Doctor runs, and Doctor did not remove the install record.
- **Other commands are kept.** Two more states written by 2026.11.3, Doctor only and without credentials, each with one command outside the managed root: an existing executable (`<iso>/custom-bin/codex`) and a missing path (`<iso>/missing/codex`). On each, this head's first `doctor --fix --yes` left the command and the other `appServer` keys unchanged and printed no removal, and a following `doctor` listed no removal and left the config file byte-identical. A command inside a generation directory that still exists is covered by the first repair above.
- **Not covered by this run.** No `openclaw update` was run: the stable install from npm wrote the state and a source build of this head took it over, which is the direct Doctor recovery scope described above. The npm-packed form of this head's `@openclaw/codex` was not exercised. The generation directory was created and removed by hand; the reported beta.1 → beta.3 sequence was not reproduced.

Your existing data and settings have been kept. …`); the update's plugin step then replaced this head's 2026.10.7 with the published 2026.10.9 (`Repaired plugin "codex".`), which does not contain this change; and the `post-plugin doctor` step that followed exited 0 with the command still in place. So this adapted run did not exercise the repair from an unpublished Codex plugin during an update. The upgrade evidence above is the same-state sequence instead: the stable CLI installed from npm wrote the state, and a source build of this head took it over, not `openclaw update`. Only the Codex plugin bundled with this head's source build was exercised (`plugins inspect codex`: origin bundled, `<worktree>/dist/extensions/codex`; Doctor printed `Kept bundled plugin "codex" from the OpenClaw source build` and the Gateway skipped the npm-installed 2026.10.8 copy (`plugin requires plugin API >=2026.10.8`), which does not contain the removal message); the npm-packed form of the candidate `@openclaw/codex` was not exercised in that sequence. The generation lifecycle was simulated by hand: the missing generation path was written into config by hand; no directory existed at it during the stable phase; an empty directory was created there before the hand-off, standing in for an old generation still on disk after an update, and it was removed after the first repair, standing in for the retained-generation cleanup. None of this came from an update rotation, and the reported beta.1 → beta.3 sequence was not reproduced. The Telegram turns used a self-created test bot in a private chat (BotFather Threaded Mode on), with plain-text messages sent by hand rather than through the `telegram-e2e-userbot` skill, which drives a leased Telegram Test Server user; the CLI turns used `openclaw agent` through the Gateway, not `--local`. The current-head run under **Evidence** does not depend on `openclaw update` or on the adapted run above: it is the same-state hand-off from an npm-installed 2026.11.3 to a source build of `4087062`.
- **Preview before migration.** On the state written by 2026.10.8, this build's `openclaw doctor`, `doctor --json` and `doctor --lint` reported the pending state-database migration (`state database schema migration pending`) and did not list the `appServer.command` removal; `doctor --fix --yes` ran the migration. So the first Doctor command after the hand-off was `doctor --fix --yes`, and the preview above ran after it. The migration step is not part of this change.

**Open question:** should the update that retires a generation also prevent this first failure? That would mean treating a generation that is retired but still on disk as stale. Possible owners are core's retained-generation cleanup or the update-time Doctor; this PR does not choose between them.

Maintainer edits are enabled ("Allow edits and access to secrets by maintainers"); this fork has no Actions secrets or environments configured.


</details>

PostgreSQL cron coverage did not prove that a scheduled one-shot automatically retries after a Gateway restart in the same process.

The new case enables the scheduler before launch and uses only `cron.add`. Recovery requires distinct interrupted/successful receipts, matching public history and task IDs, exactly two provider requests, a disabled retained one-shot with cleared durable markers, and clean final database teardown.

The existing manual restart and both process-exit cases remain. Only the new case uses a 210-second budget, allowing the native 120-second startup deferral. prs.title: fix: let large memory forget operations complete
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a memory forget selection contains more chunk IDs than SQLite can bind in one query, preview or purge can fail with `too many SQL variables` instead of reporting or completing the requested operation.

## User Impact

Large forget operations can count and remove the selected chunks and vectors while retaining unrelated indexed rows.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `sqliteStringSet` helper represents an ID set with one bound value. The FTS count, vector count, and SQLite purge deletes now use that existing owner; PostgreSQL keeps its existing bounded-set query behavior.

## Evidence

At head `64883380d39`, shipped-entry CLI runs against an isolated synthetic state containing 34,000 selected chunks plus an unrelated keeper row:

```text
$ pnpm openclaw memory forget --agent main --session target --dry-run --json
{"dryRun":true,"artifacts":{"indexChunks":34000,"ftsRows":34000,"vectorRows":34000},"refusals":[]}

$ pnpm openclaw memory forget --agent main --session target --json
{"dryRun":false,"artifacts":{"indexChunks":34000,"ftsRows":34000,"vectorRows":34000},"refusals":[]}

After apply, read-only database verification:
{"remainingChunks":["keeper"],"remainingVectors":["keeper"]}
```

Both CLI commands exited 0. The focused owner regressions also pass: `pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/memory-forget.sources.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "counts fts and vector rows past the sqlite bind-variable limit|applies a forget past the sqlite bind-variable limit"` reports 2 passed and 13 other tests filtered out. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, targeted oxlint, targeted oxfmt, and `git diff --check` passed.

The full `memory-forget.sources.test.ts` run passed both new regressions, then made no further progress in existing tests and was interrupted after three minutes; it is not claimed as a complete pass. The new regressions were not run against the base, so no base-failing test result is claimed. Exact-head CI is awaiting maintainer authorization (`action_required`, zero jobs).

prs.title: fix(update): keep the openclaw command and Gateway working after a pnpm update
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Backport of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201735 (proposal for the release owner; do not merge without the release owner's decision).

On pnpm-managed installs (`pnpm add -g openclaw`), `openclaw update` can leave no working `openclaw` command, because the launcher points into the removed update stage, and on pnpm 11.28/12.21 a Gateway that is refused restart and stays down. This was measured with published 2026.11.4 updating to public 2026.11.5.

## User Impact

User impact: pnpm installs update to a working CLI and a Gateway that serves the new version. Launchers already broken by an earlier updater are repaired by this release's Doctor and Gateway startup, without a user command.

## Why This Change Was Made

This carries the same commits as the main PR, cherry-picked cleanly onto this branch. It relocates and verifies pnpm's quoted shim form (`"$basedir_abs"/'target'`). It refuses to finalize a launcher that still names the stage, and fails an update whose published launcher cannot start instead of reporting success. Service revalidation now matches the unchanged definition against its own installation root after pnpm repoints the global entry into its versioned store. The fingerprint, name, profile and manager-UID protection is unchanged.

This branch now also includes the apostrophe and quoting fix. Launcher relocation parses each shell word, rewrites its value and quotes it again, so a pnpm home or global directory containing `'`, `"`, `$`, a space or a backslash relocates correctly, including pnpm's `'\''` spelling of the stage in `NODE_PATH`. A repair reports success only when nothing in the launcher still names the stage. It also includes the later review fixes from the main PR:
- the pre-stop guard checks only the launchers the swap publishes;
- a shim resolves physically only when it assigns `basedir_abs`;
- repair checks ownership on the same bytes it rewrites, skips FIFOs and other special files, and handles pnpm's home-level shim;
- the recovery command is `pnpm add -g --allow-build=openclaw openclaw@<installed-version>`;
- the launcher-name helper is a leaf module (`package-update-launcher-names.ts`), so the native stage adds no import cycle;
- a `$'` in a live path stays literal during relocation;
- the pre-stop refusal names the direct pnpm reinstall, the Gateway reinstall and restart, and `openclaw triage`.

The main PR lists the remaining follow-ups; they are not part of this backport.

## Evidence

- On `release/2026.11.10`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on the launcher repair, runtime relocation, native stage, all `package-update-swap*`, package filesystem, service install root, Gateway startup plugin, update-restart module outcome and eager import closure tests passes (232 tests). `pnpm check:import-cycles` and `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` report 0 cycles, and `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass.
- End-to-end proof is on the main PR, from real pnpm 12.21.0 cells: published 2026.11.4 and 2026.11.5 updating to the fixed build (the first hop), and fixed build to fixed build. Both end with a working CLI and the Gateway serving the new version.



## CI on `c89a3ee`

- `check-test-types` fails in its `extension-test-types` lane (`pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json`) with `extensions/openai/openai-api-key-catalog.test.ts(65,27): error TS2339: Property 'cachesInstructions' does not exist on type 'ModelCompatConfig'`. The failure comes from the release branch, not this backport. The release tip `7750bb3` (#201094) adds that test assertion, but this branch's `ModelCompatConfig` has no `cachesInstructions` field. No CI has run on `7750bb3` itself, so I ran the same lane locally on that bare tip and got the identical error. This backport changes no file under `extensions/`, `packages/` or `src/config/` relative to that tip.
- `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` failed before any test ran. The WebKit system packages could not be downloaded from `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` (connection timed out) or the fallback mirrors (`WebKit system packages did not download from the fallback archive mirrors (exit 124)`). This is a runner network failure. On the single rerun, `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` and `(2/2)` pass. `openclaw/ci-gate` stays red only because of `check-test-types` above.

## Not proven

- **Target layout from a registry: now covered.** A real cell ran published 2026.11.5 → a plain `openclaw update` → published 2026.11.6 from the public registry only. The updater installs a registry target in the project-store layout (`global/v11/<group>/node_modules/.pnpm/openclaw@<version>…`), the same layout class the earlier tarball-target cells used. See https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201739#issuecomment-7018135106.
- **Still unproven:** a fixed target installed from a registry. It cannot be exercised before a fixed version is published; the fixed builds were proven as tarball targets.
- **Still unproven:** pnpm 11, which ignores the `virtualStoreType=project` setting the updater passes, so its target layout may differ. A pnpm 11 cell is being prepared.

prs.title: fix(ui): retry dictation recordings when transcription returns no text
prs.body:
Related: #195982

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Control UI dictation recording disappears when transcription finishes without usable text, leaving no way to retry the same audio.

## User Impact

User impact: Retry recording resends the captured audio without reopening the microphone, and recovered text returns to the draft for an explicit Send. Discard recording and Escape release the recording.

Recovery is memory-only in the current tab and draft: reload, draft replacement, or another recording discards it. Existing usable-preview text recovery is unchanged; this does not claim to recover audio after preview text was already committed or close every part of #195982.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing capture session retains its encoded audio until text is recovered or the recording is discarded. The existing dictation owner retains an empty result for explicit retry, while the lazy status component presents retry/discard controls. Each retry creates a new Gateway transcription session through the normal authorization path and never sends a chat message automatically.

The final-transcript grace period starts after an admitted replay finishes uploading and the provider closes, so a slow upload cannot discard the eventual transcript. No persistent storage, configuration, credential, Gateway API, or microphone-selection changes.

This preserves the merged listening feedback and lazy loading from #198424 / #198643. It does not import the separate initial-drain status work in #196063.

## Evidence

### Current result: 90165f97

Head **90165f9792e5236f68571ef0c6c10c6e258503cb** passes the [required CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43613965487/job/132507889100), [Control UI performance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43613965487/job/132505379431), and the [security-sensitive/dependency review gates](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43614972941). No budget, baseline, or required check was weakened. [Substantive ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198845#issuecomment-6877437378) completed for exact head 90165f9792e5236f68571ef0c6c10c6e258503cb: Findings None; Before merge None. The preceding f2bfb015 review identified the notice defect repaired below.

### Successful recovery clears only its obsolete notice

The real Gateway reproduction on f2bfb015 recovered the transcript but failed the assertion that the red failure notice had disappeared (expected zero danger notices, observed one). The current capture session retains the notice-specific dismissal returned through the existing error callback. A successful replay resolves that notice; another failed attempt replaces only the prior recording notice. Main-composer conditional clearing, New Session's existing clearError(expected), and the rail's existing abortable-toast lifecycle preserve unrelated errors.

The existing disconnect stop/report order is retained, including errors before capture-session construction. Tests also cover recovery after a capture disconnect, repeated failures, failure/cancellation, same-tick replacement errors, and obsolete-draft callbacks. Regression assertions failed before their repairs and pass afterward.

- Six focused suites: **101/101 passed**, maxWorkers=1 (3.75 s invocation).
- UI typecheck, formatting, targeted lint, git diff --check, and production UI/runtime build pass. The rail's existing unchanged liveValue line retains its pre-existing solid/reactivity warning; no lint errors.
- Fresh independent Auto Review (openai/gpt-6.1-sol, complete nine-file repair delta against f2bfb015, P0–P3): **scoped-clean** after fixing its verified notice-boundary findings. This is not a substitute for hosted current-head review.
- Same-machine normalized build versus the preceding passing f2bfb015: startup JS gzip unchanged (90922 B); largest boot JS +14 B (574871→574885); chat boot +45 B (1314729→1314774); New Session +32 B (818349→818381). CSS unchanged. Current-head CI independently passes the unchanged base-relative performance gate linked above.

### Real Gateway + local Whisper: current recovery proof

The built runtime and UI both identify **2026.11.3-90165f9792e5-2026-11-14T16-08-37.335Z**. The isolated createOpenClawTestInstance Gateway uses real browser pairing and the real Talk file-transcription relay with whisper.cpp v1.7.6 (a8d002cfd879315632a579e73f0148d06959de36), CPU, and ggml-base.en. Model SHA-256: a03779c86df3323075f5e796cb2ce5029f00ec8869eee3fdfb897afe36c6d002.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): custom providers on api.anthropic.com get 400s for thinking from another conversation
prs.body:
Closes #198838

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a custom provider pointed at `https://api.anthropic.com` gets a 400 ("thinking block … bound to a different conversation") on every request that replays thinking from another conversation, for example after a fallback to it from another runtime, and each turn recovers only by stripping all its thinking.

## User Impact

Custom `anthropic-messages` providers on api.anthropic.com now send the same thinking-binding controls as the bundled `anthropic` provider, so Anthropic drops only the mismatched blocks and the request succeeds the first time. Proxies, gateways, OAuth and the bundled provider are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both Anthropic request paths decided whether a request may carry `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior: "drop_block"` and the `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` beta with `isDirectAnthropicModel`, which also requires the provider id `anthropic`. That gate now uses the endpoint check alone (new `isDirectAnthropicEndpoint`, split out of `isDirectAnthropicModel`); every other caller of `isDirectAnthropicModel` keeps the provider-id rule.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5: change details</summary>

- `packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-payload-policy.ts`: `isDirectAnthropicEndpoint(model, env)` holds the existing endpoint logic (`anthropic-public` endpoint class, or a default-class base URL on api.anthropic.com, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` honored); `isDirectAnthropicModel` is now `provider === "anthropic" && isDirectAnthropicEndpoint(...)`, so its behavior is the same.
- `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` and `transports/anthropic-transport-stream.ts`: the API-key branch sets `directApiKeyBetaHeader` from `isDirectAnthropicEndpoint`. Proxies and gateways (Cloudflare, Kimi, Foundry) have their own base URLs; Copilot, Foundry bearer auth and OAuth take other branches.
- Left as is on purpose: the other features keyed on `isDirectAnthropicModel` for custom rows (server compaction default, server-side fallback, the direct-path beta defaults). Whether those should follow the endpoint too is a separate question.
- Test: `anthropic-binding-transport-parity.test.ts` gains a custom-provider-id row (fails on main, passes here). The Cloudflare, Foundry and Kimi rows now use their real base URLs; they had used the api.anthropic.com default and relied on the provider id to stay excluded.

</details>

## Evidence

**Live, before and after:** real Anthropic API key, throwaway Gateways on 2026.11.3 and on this branch, custom provider `anthropic-api` on `https://api.anthropic.com`, `claude-opus-5-5`, `--thinking high`. Turn 1 leaves a signed thinking block in the session. With the Gateway stopped, a one-off script rewrites turn 1's user message in the stored transcript, so that block is now bound to a different conversation prefix, as after a fallback. Turn 2 then runs in the same session.

2026.11.3, turn 2 (redacted):

```
[model-fetch] response provider=anthropic-api model=claude-opus-5-5 status=400 requestNumber=1
[provider-error] … status=400 body={"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"messages.2.content.0: Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block. The block is bound to a different conversation. …"}}
[session-recovery] Anthropic thinking stream error; retrying once without thinking blocks
[session-recovery] unable to repair rejected thinking replay: error=Error: Session transcript changed before rewrite publication
[model-fetch] response provider=anthropic-api model=claude-opus-5-5 status=400 requestNumber=2
[session-recovery] Anthropic thinking stream error; retrying once without thinking blocks
[session-recovery] stripped thinking blocks after provider rejected replay: repaired=2
```

This PR, turn 2 (two requests because the model ran one tool):

```
[anthropic] replayed thinking dropped: 1 block(s) (prefix_binding_mismatch at messages.2.content.0) requestNumber=1
[anthropic] replayed thinking dropped: 1 block(s) (prefix_binding_mismatch at messages.2.content.0) requestNumber=2
[agent] run … ended with stopReason=stop
```

No 400 and no `[session-recovery]`; both builds answered correctly. The "unable to repair" line is probably from the hand edit.

Control, through a local TLS stub posing as api.anthropic.com (`request.proxy` explicit-proxy): the bundled `anthropic` provider sends `block_binding: drop_block` and the `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` beta on both builds; the custom row sends neither on 2026.11.3 and both here.

Tested on 896f05edc79.

- The 400 itself, from a real 2026.11.1 Gateway on 2026-11-12 (custom provider on api.anthropic.com, after a claude-cli to API fallback): Anthropic answered "…bound to a different conversation. Remove the block, or set `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior` to "drop_block"…" 74 times in about two hours, each recovered by stripping thinking.
- Checks: focused Anthropic transport and transcript-policy tests pass (204), `pnpm tsgo:core` passes, format and oxlint clean on the changed files; autoreview: no findings.

Fixes missing custom models for a secondary agent when its local `models.json` is absent and the system agent owns the catalog.

## User Impact

Proposes read-only fallback to sanitized system-agent model inventory, while preserving local-catalog precedence and current request credentials. This remains a draft pending integration/security review and end-to-end proof; do not treat the focused checks as production validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ports the previous proposal to the newer model runtime without restoring the removed synchronous catalog reads. It uses the existing serialized capture owner and its pricing publication, places request-header composition in the current core registry, strips inherited API keys and sensitive headers, and only carries safe headers across matching routes. No agent catalog file is copied or created by the fallback.

The intended behavior still needs maintainer design review: sanitized system-agent inventory fallback versus an early actionable setup error. Help reviewing this boundary or routing it to the appropriate catalog/security owner would be appreciated.

Related: #188475

## What Problem This Solves

Reviewing several chat images still requires stepping through each image because the viewer has no visual overview or direct jump control.

## User Impact

Users can select a thumbnail to jump between images in the loaded conversation while keeping zoom, download, swipe, keyboard navigation, and return focus. The strip does not load earlier history or change video viewing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing gallery remains the selection owner. Visible thumbnails request small previews with each image's message scope; viewer renditions and original downloads keep their existing on-demand paths. The strip scrolls the current selection into view. Existing zoom chrome moves into the view module to keep its owning content module within the repository's size limit.

## Evidence

**Current publication status:** The reviewed repair candidate is now published at `f997ed20632085bceccb6ffcf5093fb947903fc7`. It addresses the three findings from the [review of the previous head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198825#issuecomment-6876627798): selected-image consumer locators, failure feedback overlapping thumbnails, and thumbnail-only original-file downloads. Original-only local files and third-party URLs use numbered direct-jump placeholders because the current media owners produce no bounded preview for those sources. This does not provide visual thumbnails for every source, so this PR remains related to, rather than closing, the feature request. Current-head CI and hosted repair review are still outstanding. GitHub currently reports a merge conflict; this publication is not a ready-to-merge claim. Initial implementation evidence follows; the repair evidence is identified separately below.

- Owning browser regression fails on main 93fdc3d9 and passes with the implementation: missing strip (0 thumbnails instead of 8), then direct jump, current marker, keyboard activation, zoom reset, mobile scrolling and focus return.

- Simplification: no new selection owner or original-image cache. The gallery dock reserves actual space for wrapping failure feedback; unsupported preview sources retain their explicit selection/download path. Existing effect/listener/query ratchets are unchanged.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tool preparation passes an auth-store-source Boolean through several private callers even though the credential helper never reads it. Four callers still perform asynchronous source probes just to populate that unused hint. Web-search also expresses its live lazy-preparation notification as a Boolean-returning callback whose return value is ignored.

## User Impact

No intended change to tool availability, credential selection, or public SDK inputs. Prepared, published, and authoritative empty auth stores remain the credential owners. Config credentials still short-circuit before provider-auth lookup, followed by environment and fallback credentials.

## Why This Approach

Remove the unused private hint and its four producer probes. Keep web-search's live notification explicit as a void callback at the same provider-auth lookup point, only when no auth store is supplied. Preserve the lazy preparation/retry path, error order, abort and authority checks, genuine source-check APIs, and real false-source auth test. The complete caller cutover removes 79 lines across 12 production files and two existing test inputs; no dependency, export, or public signature change.

prs.title: fix: keep Gateway available during optional plugin hook conflicts and invalid restarts
prs.body:
Related: #85695

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a running Gateway draining into an invalid config restart and an optional plugin's conflicting old/current hook permissions preventing an otherwise valid core Gateway from starting.

## User Impact

Operators retain authenticated control access while the affected plugin stays inactive, without restoring stale permissions or discarding newer settings. Ordinary SIGUSR2 restarts reject invalid disk config before draining or canceling pending channel reloads.

The cold-start exception is deliberately narrow: opposite boolean values for a plugin's retired `allowPromptInjection` and current `allowPromptModification` keys. Resolve the permission values explicitly, then run Doctor or save the corrected config. Other invalid core authentication/access settings and arbitrary malformed configs still need their existing repair paths; this does not close every case in #85695.

## Why This Change Was Made

Runtime readers share a plugin-local quarantine projection with activation policy. The source config, includes and last-known-good remain unchanged; strict validation and writers still reject the conflict. The degraded projection is never promoted as healthy. Existing signal settlement owns preflight and cleanup, including SIGINT/SIGTERM arriving during a slow preflight. Update-owned handoffs retain their own admission checks.

No generic unknown-key removal, whole-file rollback, auth bypass, new config option or persisted recovery manager is added. This is distinct from #198376's older-writer migration projection.

## Evidence

- Initial scoped owner proof: **424 passed, 1 skipped**. Follow-up: wrapper import/extraction closure **23 passed**; update target-schema **24 passed**; config snapshot, activation, Doctor permission and fresh-Doctor suites **44 passed**. All ran with `--maxWorkers=1`.
- Both hosted findings are repaired: the new runtime module is in the existing PR wrapper inventory; quarantine no longer overwrites malformed authored enablement. The added IO regression failed before that guard and passes afterward.
- Two dry-run tests independently failed on the pinned base and PR because their installation roots did not exist. They now use existing physical package/Git fixture helpers; preview/version/no-mutation assertions and production ownership admission are unchanged.
- Rebuilt current compiled CLI: both opposite permission conflicts, authenticated control, wrong-token refusal, unrelated plugin, inactive affected hooks, exact source/include/LKG retention, explicit repair and hot quarantine all pass. Malformed `enabled` remains a schema error. Invalid reload/SIGUSR2 retention, repaired retry, cold-valid startup and SIGINT/SIGTERM stops also pass.
- Published latest stable **2026.11.3** produced isolated state/LKG; candidate Doctor and all restart scenarios pass with port/auth/token/tool policy retained. This is a maintained source-built runtime upgrade fixture, **not full package-manager/service activation**. No live model/channel proof is claimed.
- Scoped types, lint, format and diff checks pass. Fresh independent native autoreview **P0–P2: scoped-clean, no findings**, against `c232d50420bd229ecf1943339881c7c6cda7d63c`, repaired snapshot SHA256 `eb029b393a78f59b28da3922fac90c6e283785be9a16ac433338a48a376d8d74`.
- Local native provisioning replay stopped before its provisioner: the wrapper could not acquire its operation lock for the synthetic PR. No lock/assertion guard was bypassed; this is **not passing provisioning evidence**. Exact-head hosted CI must verify those cases.

<details>
<summary>Redacted real CLI output and terminal receipts</summary>

The task-only fixture ran `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/gateway-invalid-config-recovery.proof.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **4 passed, exit 0**. It launched the built product CLI, not mocked Gateway handlers. Fixture paths, process IDs and timestamps are omitted below; plugin IDs are synthetic.

Pinned-base cold-start failure receipt, recorded before implementation:

```json
{"base":"c232d50420bd229ecf1943339881c7c6cda7d63c","coldExit":78,"hotReady":true,"lkgPreserved":true}
```

Original SIGUSR2 failure output (fixture paths/timestamps removed):

```text
[admission] closed: restart (SIGUSR2)
[gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
[gateway] restart mode: in-process restart (OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN)
[gateway] startup failed: Invalid config at [isolated config path]
```

Quarantine regressions with the original configuration/activation production code also failed in both boolean directions: the owning IO reader returned valid=false where the regression requires true (2 failed), and source activation re-enabled the quarantined entry (2 failed). Those are boundary-test red results, not additional Gateway transcripts. Current CLI and green regression results are recorded below.

### Paired real-CLI base/candidate controls

The original quarantine CLI attempt also contained an unrelated retired `debounceMs` key, so it is **not** used as isolated failure proof. prs.title: fix: planned restarts no longer log the expected subagent sweep skip as a warning
prs.body:
Refs #200440

## What Problem This Solves

Every planned Gateway restart can log `WARN subagent run sweep skipped: gateway is draining for restart`. The skip is the designed behavior: restart drain refuses new background work, and the next Gateway resumes the sweep. Logging it as a warning makes routine restarts look like faults. The reporter counted 155 of these lines in 31 days of nightly restarts.

## User Impact

The expected drain skip is still recorded, at info, so it no longer shows up as a warning on every restart. A genuine sweep failure still logs `subagent run sweep failed: ...` at warn.

## Why This Change Was Made

#147904 changed this refusal from a "sweep failed" message to "sweep skipped" and kept it as a record of skipped work. It went through `warn` only because that was the sweeper's only logger. The sweeper now also receives `info` from the registry's existing subsystem logger, and the drain skip uses it. Scheduling is unchanged: the refused tick still returns without rearming, as before.

Scope follows the review's suggested first repair: only the drain-skip severity. The health-refresh capacity errors and lease-wait volume in the issue need separate evidence, so this PR refers to the issue instead of closing it.

## Evidence

- New regression test in `subagent-registry-sweeper-recovery.test.ts`: with restart drain marked through the real Gateway work-admission module, a sweeper tick records the skip at `info`, makes no `warn` call, does no cleanup and keeps the run. It fails on current `main` (the skip goes to `warn`) and passes with this change.
- Sweeper and registry suites pass: sweeper recovery, lifecycle, owed batches, kill and restart settle, registry pressure, plus every suite using the sweeper test helpers and the lifecycle timer retention fixture (191 tests).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean.
- Live Gateway capture, before and after. Isolated state dir and port, model served by the repo's local QA mock provider (`startQaMockOpenAiServer`), channels skipped. Steps: `pnpm openclaw gateway run --port <port>`, then `pnpm openclaw agent --message 'Call sessions_spawn with task="..." mode=run'` so a real subagent launch arms the sweeper, then SIGTERM to that foreground Gateway timed to land just before the sweeper's next 60-second tick. The tick then starts inside the stop drain. Same steps on both builds; only the two runtime files differ.

  Before (`main`), structured Gateway log:
  ```
  00:34:22.986 [gateway] received SIGTERM; shutting down
  00:34:23.151 [agents/subagent-registry] subagent run sweep skipped: gateway is draining for restart
               "logLevelName":"WARN"
  00:34:23.219 [shutdown] completed cleanly in 230ms
  ```
  After (this branch):
  ```
  00:31:34.319 [gateway] received SIGTERM; shutting down
  00:31:34.503 [agents/subagent-registry] subagent run sweep skipped: gateway is draining for restart
               "logLevelName":"INFO"
  00:31:34.604 [shutdown] completed cleanly in 279ms
  ```
  Shutdown completed cleanly in both runs; only the recorded level changed.

prs.title: fix: let slow auto-compaction run to its configured timeout instead of stopping at 6 minutes
prs.body:
Root cause: `src/sessions/session-controller.watchdog.ts:103` (base `0eb6488cd3`) builds the reply watchdog's semantic deadline from the last progress plus 6 minutes and the open model requests only, so a nested compaction attempt's own deadline (`compaction.timeoutSeconds`, set in `compaction-session-agent.ts:221`) never counts and the turn is stopped as stalled once a long compaction summary has run past 6 minutes.

Fixes #201576

Thanks @kazuyuki-eguchi for the detailed report and timeline, and @chessing234 for the first fix in this PR (its two checks are kept as one regression in the watchdog suite).

## What Problem This Solves

With `agents.defaults.compaction.timeoutSeconds: 600`, auto-compaction on a slow local model was cut off after about 6 minutes with `Reply operation stalled`, so the 600 s budget could never be used. The turn failed, the next turn hit the same overflow, and the cycle repeated.

## User Impact

User impact: a quiet auto-compaction can now run until its own `compaction.timeoutSeconds`, and the turn continues once the summary arrives. Stop still cancels compaction at once, compaction still ends at its own timeout, and an ordinary stalled model call is still stopped at the usual window.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compaction already registers with the reply watchdog as a nested maintenance attempt with its own deadline (refreshed while it makes progress). The watchdog honoured that deadline only as a hard stop, not as a reason the turn was not stalled. It covered the summary request only while it was open, measured from the last progress before compaction began. Now a live nested attempt's deadline counts toward the stall window, and when compaction finishes the stall window restarts from that point. Native runtime-owned waits already work this way. No new setting, timeout or wording.

The earlier version of this PR added a separate `compaction-watchdog-allowance` module around recovery compaction. It is removed: the watchdog owner already has the hook, and this covers every compaction that runs through the compaction session, not only recovery.

## Evidence

Isolated Gateway (`ocx src`, pinned Bun, task-owned state), reporter's compaction config (`safeguard`, `qualityGuard`, `midTurnPrecheck`, `timeoutSeconds: 600`), and a scripted local OpenAI-compatible model. A turn reads large files, mid-turn context pressure triggers auto-compaction, and the compaction summary request stays quiet. Only the Gateway process's clock is stepped. Observed lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201928#issuecomment-7017676022

| Case | Base `0eb6488cd3` (main) | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quiet summary, answered after 420 s | `lane task error: lane=main durationMs=427663 error="Reply operation stalled"`, `caller_signal_aborted`; user sees "Your request couldn't be completed." | `auto-compaction succeeded ...; retrying prompt`, turn answers |
| Quiet past 600 s | n/a | compaction ends at its own timeout (`[compaction-diag] fallback ... reason=timeout`), turn continues |
| User Stop during compaction | n/a | `chat.abort` -> compaction ends 190 ms later, `agent run aborted` |
| Ordinary model call quiet 370 s, no compaction | request closed at the window, then retried | same |

Regression: `session-controller.watchdog.test.ts` "lets quiet compaction outlast the stall window while Stop still cancels it" fails on base (stopped as stalled at 7 min) and passes here.

Change size against the merge base: production +16/-2 (one file), tests +19. The contributor's new module and its test (+89) and the `compaction-runtime.ts` wrapper are gone.

Merge danger: two-way door, no stored state or config change; revert restores the old window. Blast radius: replies whose turn runs compaction (embedded runtime), and only while compaction runs; ordinary model and tool stalls are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ui): avoid duplicate history reads with inline commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reloading a chat with Inline commands enabled starts a history read that the foreground chat cannot safely reuse. It then upgrades live-output delivery and reads the history again.

## User Impact

User impact: removes the redundant startup history read while retaining the early connection. This remains a draft pending paired performance proof. The targeted regression cases passed in CI, but this does not yet establish the cause of the reported intermittent UI lag.

## Why This Change Was Made

The foreground pane already waits for its inline renderer and admits live output before taking its initial history snapshot. Leave that combined request with its existing owner when the saved setting is enabled. The early connection and local snapshot prewarm remain available; ordinary startup with inline commands disabled keeps its existing history overlap.

Production delta: +4 lines for one startup eligibility fact and its two consumers. Tests: +70 lines covering cold startup and cached history arriving before or after connection, followed by one foreground subscription with live output and initial history.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` and the native tooling-owner formatter passed for both changed files.
- Independent source review found no blocking issue in snapshot ordering, setting changes, route ownership, or teardown.
- Local autoreview completed on `cd2ae19272a3ee7be456385fa7efc56d6e2109a6..0230c840938d9c4cca77bd9d3970449d8b10c1dd`, P0–P3 coverage: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. Paired runtime performance proof remains pending.
- Exact-head draft CI finished with 30 successful, three failed, and 26 skipped jobs on `0230c840938d9c4cca77bd9d3970449d8b10c1dd`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44583086091. All three UI unit shards, both browser E2E shards, ratchets, and real-Gateway shard 2 passed. Actual execution is confirmed in UI shard 2: `early-gateway.test.ts` passed 20/20 cases, including all three new cold/before-cache/after-cache inline-history cases (16 ms, 70 ms, 11 ms). Native invocation `51f61695-e4e2-4433-95a2-52439ea573c7` completed with 800 files, zero unhandled errors, and exit 0. The `chat-early-gateway.test.ts` sibling passed too. Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44583086091/job/135770135576.
- The bundle-performance job failed on raw CSS: 1,748,509 candidate bytes versus 1,748,441 baseline bytes (+68, allowance +64). Both gzip totals are 339,096 bytes. The job compares against newer `6502a5769c0ea37a96384111b84ab406e9e82f89`, whereas the candidate and its merge base `cd2ae19272a3ee7be456385fa7efc56d6e2109a6` share identical CSS. Baseline commit `fce78dba585` shortened seven sidebar selectors (14 bytes) and removed a 27-byte background rule emitted twice by the existing hover guard (54 bytes). That accounts for the 68-byte difference; emitted sidebar asset names/sizes also differ in the expected direction. This PR changes no CSS, and neither the budget nor comparison baseline has been altered. The run is not green; bundle size is not latency proof.
- Real-Gateway shard 1 failed in the automation ownership fixture at `cron-human-owner.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts:466`: three `edited` requests were counted where two were expected. The fixture and Activity recap owner are unchanged by this PR; the automation route does not enter the changed inline-chat startup branch. The fixture counts background utility-model requests, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201962 already repaired the matching failure by classifying Activity recap requests before the ownership counter (merged as `d23fd767e6063f96c2c9e3569dc40cfd93054cce`). This is strong source-backed baseline attribution; this run did not record the exact third request's purpose. Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44583086091/job/135770136331.
- The third failed job is the aggregate CI gate reflecting those two lane failures. The optional failure-report job was not selected, so CI itself supplied no inherited-failure classification.
- The separate paired regression/performance run has not executed. The task checkout has no qualified dependency installation, and the selected remote provider refused before allocation because its API key was unavailable.
- The prepared proof payload uses native managed child ownership, compares identical emitted UI build metadata, balances six cold/first-warm pairs, and keeps bounded per-session RPC observation out of timing runs. Its syntax and a dependency-free synthetic interruption check passed. The harness cleanup dependency is now fixed and merged by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201981 as `f0f3db9e4aeb13be13e1e9d1e729a3572f0dc234`, with all nine lifecycle regressions and exact-head CI passing. Its four production files are unchanged from the hashes already pinned by this payload. At payload entry, those hashes are verified before measurement. A separately managed integration checkout and native source capsule can combine those files with this unchanged UI candidate. The remaining execution gate is the selected remote provider credential; no paired run has started.

Performance acceptance rule, recorded before measurement: use the committed `scripts/perf/warm-reload-proof.ts` workload with the same isolated built Gateway and separate baseline/candidate production UI bundles, a literal chat route, saved Inline commands enabled, 2,000 synthetic sessions, 80 ms network shaping, and at least five interleaved samples per arm. Report cold and first-warm startup separately, selected-session history/subscription counts, median, p95, spread, and host load. Accept fewer redundant history operations only if user-facing timing and resource metrics hold or improve; a 20% regression stops landing. Collect RPC counts in a separate instrumented run so census overhead does not contaminate timing.

Planned regression proof keeps the new tests while temporarily restoring only the baseline owner module, requires the three expected unwanted-subscription failures, then restores and verifies the candidate before running startup, subscription-admission, renderer-readiness, and shared-coordinator sibling coverage. Candidate regression execution is now proven by CI. The negative baseline replay and paired latency result remain pending.

prs.title: fix(perf): finish warm reload cleanup before releasing inputs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Interrupting the warm reload benchmark can leave its detached Gateway running after the outer command exits. Cleanup errors can also be discarded while comparison build inputs are removed, making later timing runs unreliable.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201971

## User Impact

Interrupted benchmarks retain ownership until children and output settle. Uncertain cleanup fails visibly and preserves build inputs. This is developer tooling; it does not change production Gateway or application behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing native cancellation and cleanup contracts for detached Gateway, CLI and build lifetimes. Browser acquisition propagates cleanup failure. Success follows teardown, the first interrupt stays authoritative, and Gateway cleanup starts before waiting for browser teardown.

This removes the benchmark's separate signal/stop paths. Production delta: +228 lines for the lifecycle owner, bounded CLI capture and cleanup-failure propagation. Tests: +384 lines. Most displayed churn in the main script is indentation under its cancellation owner.

## Evidence

- Exact head `ff8af2f6c049755a2a304c955ea94097aa651954`: CI completed successfully, 28 successful jobs and 31 skipped, with both required gates passing: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44592072954.
- All four new test files executed in the Linux Bun tooling shard: build cleanup 2/2, uncertain lifecycle cleanup 1/1, browser acquisition cleanup 2/2, lifecycle/CLI 4/4. All eight planned compact groups completed without failure: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44592072954/job/135801750692.
- Changed lint, production/test types, source contracts, guards, the npm lock check, changed Node checks and baseline ratchets passed. The final test-only lint correction leaves production code identical to the previously green revision.
- Real-process Node probes also passed failed spawn, CLI output/nonzero diagnostics, cancellation followed by terminal write/exit, and 6.2-second detached Gateway cleanup across the outer runner's five-second boundary. Repeated interruption preserved the first signal's exit status.
- Independent P0–P3 autoreviews were scoped-clean for the implementation and each follow-up. Targeted formatting, Node syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- Windows and the complete built-browser benchmark remain unrun. No measured UI speedup is claimed by this lifecycle repair.
