prs.title: improve: reduce work when restricted operators read chat history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reading chat history with a model-restricted operator role decoded and re-encoded the entire page, even when the role's model projection changed no messages. This creates unnecessary CPU and allocation work when opening or refreshing conversations.

## User Impact

History, cursor deltas, and subscription initial history keep the same wire JSON and the same shipped disclosure behavior. Model restrictions still use the committed policy after history preparation. Tool results, transcript content, and nested bookkeeping retain their existing semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

The history encoder now records a bounded list of byte ranges for policy-sensitive assistant rows in its existing encoding loop. The worker still transfers message bytes without copying them. The Gateway validates the internal index and projects only those rows, borrowing unchanged byte ranges. Missing or malformed indexes use the original full-materialization path. When every row is indexed, a single parse/encode avoids per-row encoding overhead. Unchanged delta envelopes retain their identity.

There is no client protocol, configuration, database, or cache change. Production delta is +112 lines (133 added, 21 removed), plus 299 test lines and a 163-line rerunnable benchmark. Growth is needed for the internal index, its validation/fallback, and immutable segment assembly; the implementation reuses the existing serializer and model-policy owner.

## Evidence

The regression fails on the base because a zero-metadata page loses its serialized identity. Focused proof covers exact wire JSON for restricted/unrestricted history, deltas, and nested initial history at 0/5/100% model-bearing rows; current adversarial disclosure semantics; malformed index fallback; policy changes across held readiness boundaries; worker sharing; and WebSocket delivery. P1 Codex autoreview found no accepted/actionable findings. The affected guest-question browser E2E passed. The final focused run passed 25 tests; the broader focused run passed 67 with one pre-existing skip. `pnpm check:changed --base 138482e6517d2271b5701372b12b00eff8f86217` passed in full on committed head `6550661ca07d2e57e1c84bcdf72fe1e7b63d755f`. Exact-head [CI attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44586578935) passed after one diagnosed infrastructure retry: Bun installation consumed 13 minutes of attempt 1’s 20-minute artifact-job budget. [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201983#issuecomment-7018422703) reviewed the same head with zero findings and zero open checklist items.

Synthetic 200-message pages, approximately 278–285 KiB; five alternating A/B pairs with A/A controls. CPU measurement is outside allocation sampling. The retained full-projection path is A; indexed projection is B. Separately compare the encoder against source pinned at `138482e6517d2271b5701372b12b00eff8f86217`.

| Model-bearing rows | Projection CPU µs/read, A → B | Sampled heap bytes/read, A → B | Encoder CPU µs/page, A → B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0% | 634.2 → 38.3 | 1,676,322 → 27,894 | 404.5 → 412.2 |
| 5% | 916.8 → 97.9 | 1,696,942 → 128,549 | 406.1 → 410.7 |
| 100% | 981.7 → 988.3 | 1,907,532 → 1,918,357 | 415.3 → 421.0 |

Final exact-commit run on `6550661ca07d2e57e1c84bcdf72fe1e7b63d755f`. A/A projection CPU medians differ by +0.24%, +0.34%, and +0.16%; sampled allocation differs by at most 0.35%. Dense projection CPU is +0.67% with overlapping observed ranges; encoder plus projection is about +0.88% CPU and +0.53% sampled heap. The bounded index adds about 3 KB of sampled encoder allocation at 100%. This is a sparse-page optimization, with the measured dense overhead disclosed. No whole-Gateway latency claim is made. Sampling excludes external buffer storage and socket compression.

Projection CPU ranges (µs/read, A / B): 0% 621.0–647.9 / 34.0–41.9; 5% 861.7–932.4 / 92.8–106.3; 100% 959.9–999.7 / 984.7–999.9. Nearest-rank p95 across five batch means is the upper bound, not a per-request latency percentile. Acceptance was exact bytes, removal of whole-page work for sparse pages, and no ≥20% regression.

Reproduce projection measurements:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/restricted-history-projection-measure.mjs
```

For the producer comparison, materialize the pinned `src/gateway/chat-history-response-page.ts` beside its relative imports under a temporary name, then pass that module path as the benchmark's first argument. Remove the temporary copy after measurement.

prs.title: fix(test): keep compiled Gateway workers on their host build identity
prs.body:
Closes #201964

## What Problem This Solves

Long-running compiled Gateway tests can shut down as though their installation was replaced even when the checkout did not change. Their generated worker build ID differs from the existing parent installation that maintenance checks.

## User Impact

No user-facing runtime change. Compiled test processes will use their host installation's identity, so unrelated metadata does not interrupt long-running qualification. Real installation replacement detection remains active.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared compiler finalizer now inherits valid parent build metadata on both cold compilation and cache restoration. Source-only checkouts retain existing identity synthesis; malformed present metadata produces a clear preparation error. The generated package remains type-only, preserving parent asset and plugin discovery.

This is the prerequisite for automatic scheduled-cron restart qualification in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201831. It changes test tooling only: no SQLite schema/version, migration, persisted format, runtime config or public API change.

## Evidence

- Native owner smoke passed: host identity wins over environment hints; absent metadata preserves synthesis; malformed metadata fails clearly.
- Native Node 26.7 loader probe passed: the real compiler dependency is captured without populating the intercepted request's cache, and the scoped wrapper is selected once.
- Formatting, syntax and line-cap checks passed. Independent owner/fixture source reviews and the completed compiler-change autoreview are clear. The final export-audit entry review is also clear.
- [Real cold compilation and retained-cache restoration passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44582018195/job/135766275929) on exact head `30380564d9cffa924edfd6a4883a5e0b1fd7cff0`: one integration case, 8.568 seconds, changed host identity and manifest hashes with unchanged executable outputs and no compilation on restoration.
- [All 11 metadata cases passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44582018195/job/135766275829): host precedence, absent-host synthesis, and malformed-host rejection. Exact-head CI completed successfully (35 passed jobs, 31 skipped); the original PostgreSQL recovery remains separate proof.
- [Exact-head ClawSweeper source review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201966#issuecomment-7017581418) found no defects. Its only rank-up move, completed cold/cache execution, is satisfied by the integration result above.
- The original scheduled-cron process exited with code 1 and planned-restart boot records. The exact historical reason was not captured; the original long-running PostgreSQL case remains a separate verification gate after this prerequisite.

Tooling delta: +52/-5 lines; tests: +274 lines. The positive tooling delta owns validation of the shared installation identity. Release-note context: repair compiled-test build provenance; no shipped runtime change.

prs.title: fix(browser): report crashed tabs as tab-scoped failures
prs.body:
Closes #194667

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the browser tool reports a crashed tab as a generic 20 s timeout and tells the agent the whole browser is unavailable, even though the browser and its other tabs keep working. `navigate` on a crashed target waits the full request budget, and the tab list gives no hint that the target is dead.

## User Impact

User impact: a crashed tab now fails fast with tab-scoped guidance to open the page in a new tab (or retry once a busy page settles), instead of steering the agent into browser-wide troubleshooting. `snapshot`, `screenshot`, and `navigate` all take that path; `tabs` marks targets observed as crashed in both the JSON payload and the CLI text output, and implicit tab selection prefers a healthy tab. Existing-session and extension-relay drivers keep their current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

A crashed renderer leaves its Chrome target listed while every page-level CDP command stalls. Snapshots waited out the full action budget and then attached the browser-wide unavailability hint, and `navigate` timed out the same way. The fix adds one bounded `Page.getFrameTree` liveness probe before snapshot and navigate work, maps Playwright `Target crashed` errors to a 409 with tab-scoped recovery text, and keeps the observed crash on the tab record for listing, the CLI handle list, and implicit selection. A dead renderer and a long-blocked main thread look the same to that probe, so the wording names both and suggests a retry once the page settles. Snapshot media helpers moved to a sibling module to stay under the file line cap.

## Evidence

- Targeted suite: `pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp-liveness.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/target-crash.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.snapshot.local-managed.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/client-fetch.loopback-auth.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.selection.crash.test.ts` — 6 files, 93 tests passed.
- Real renderer crash (gated Chromium test, system Chrome): `OPENCLAW_BROWSER_CRASH_E2E=1 PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH=... pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp-liveness.chromium.test.ts` — `Page.crash` then probe rejects with `BrowserTargetCrashedError` inside the bounded probe window.
- Real crash-frame shape on `79e875aabfa`: the same gated test crashes a renderer and asserts the message Playwright itself produces for a screenshot on the dead tab. Measured locally, the first line is `page.screenshot: Target crashed ` (trailing space) followed by a `Call log:` block; the matcher accepts the headline, the typed error is returned, and reverting only `target-crash.ts` makes 2/7 `target-crash.test.ts` cases and 1/23 `client-fetch.loopback-auth.test.ts` cases fail.
- Shipped Gateway + CLI proof on `4b9f8291e0d` (isolated state dir, local loopback only, no real credentials; headless system Chrome 157; local HTTP fixture; the target was crashed with CDP `Page.crash`, then observed through the normal CLI entry point):
  - `openclaw browser navigate http://127.0.0.1:18080/crashme.html --target-id crashme` — fails fast (~2 s) with `The tab crashed or stopped responding. The browser and other tabs are still available: open the page again in a new tab, or retry this target once the page settles.` instead of waiting out the request budget.
  - `openclaw browser tabs` — `2. crashme [crashed use: crashme tab: t1 label:crashme]`; the healthy tab stays listed unchanged (`1. healthy [use: healthy tab: t2 label:healthy]`).
  - `openclaw browser screenshot crashme` — same tab-scoped crash error before Playwright reports its own `Target crashed` frame; `openclaw browser screenshot healthy` still writes `$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/state/media/browser/<uuid>.png`.
  - Recovery: `openclaw browser open http://127.0.0.1:18080/crashme.html --label recovered` then `openclaw browser snapshot --target-id recovered` returns the page's AX tree (`RootWebArea "crashme"` / `heading "crash target"`).
- Independent live check by @wr-web (`Page.crash` + CLI on Windows) confirmed snapshot/screenshot on `906d205`; their navigate and tab-list findings are wired in `76b7e18520f` and `905b07cae7b`.
- Base behavior reproduced locally: after `Page.crash`, the listed page's WebSocket accepts connections but `Page.getFrameTree`, `Runtime.evaluate`, and `Accessibility.getFullAXTree` never answer; a healthy page answers in milliseconds.
- Ratchet and suite on the merged tree (`52c81a6a2b1`, merges `origin/main` `bd9166435e9`): the only conflict was the import block in `agent.snapshot.ts`, where upstream added `resolveProfileHeadless` while this branch moved the media helpers to `agent.snapshot-media.ts`; the resolution keeps upstream's `headless` wiring and this branch's helper extraction. `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` reports `Test lines OK. Net test lines: +395; allowance: 400; allocation credit: 350`. Full browser project suite (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-browser.config.ts`) passes 257 files / 3091 tests with 127 skipped; `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass, oxlint reports 0 problems on the 21 changed files, and `pnpm format:check` is clean.
- Gap: the live check drives the shipped CLI routes but not a full agent model turn; request-boundary behavior stays covered by the route tests.

prs.title: fix: finish a half-switched Git update instead of reporting it current
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a Git checkout install that runs from releases, an update can fail after it switched the release link but before any Gateway started the new release. The next `openclaw update` then treated that never-started release as the one serving. If the target was that same release it reported "already current" and the Gateway stayed on the old build. If the target was newer, it recorded the never-started release as the new trial's fallback, so a candidate that failed to start fell back to a build that had never run. Each attempt also left another full build on disk.

## User Impact

User impact: the next plain `openclaw update` repairs a half-switched Git install. If the target is the release already placed, the update finishes its activation without rebuilding. If the target is newer, the fallback stays the release that last served and the superseded release is deselected; release collection removes it once it has been deselected for 24 hours. Nothing manual is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause: `updateGitRelease` (`src/infra/update-runner-git-release.ts`) used the release link as the running release (`running = slot`), and `publishGitRelease` recorded whatever the link named as the trial's `previous`. The link records what the next start should load, not what serves. After an update fails between the switch and the restart, the link names a release whose trial is still armed with `attempts: 0`. The trial record's `previous` is the release that served.

Competing hypothesis: the false `already-current` came from the tree comparison or from `beforeRuntimeVerified`. Falsifier: with the same leftover and the same tree comparison, reading the serving release from the trial record turns the RED case green, and no change to the comparison is needed. The new runner tests fail on base for exactly this reason (`expected 'skipped' to be 'ok'`, trial `previous` = the never-served release).

Why the link was used: #199706 uses it so the serving release is found even when the CLI runs from the preserved checkout. That still holds. The link's release is still used whenever there is no trial, the trial has passed, the launcher counted a start, or a process holds a lease on it. A started trial stays under the launcher, which owns its state rollback, exactly as before.

The fix has one owner: `readGitReleasePlacement` in `src/infra/git-release.ts` reads the trial record and the leases and returns:
- `serving`: what serves;
- `fallback`: the release that last passed a trial;
- `unserved`: the placed release, only when it never started (`attempts: 0` and no live lease).

It uses only the existing trial fields and lease files. The runner then:
- **Builds on the serving release.** `before`, the already-current check and failure recovery use `serving`, not the link.
- **Target is the placed release:** the target is admitted through the caller's normal inspection hook, which is also where the CLI observes the service it will restart. The placed release is reused only if three things hold: its build verifies, the candidate worktree is checked out at the revision after local-commit replay, and that tree is the placed tree. The check runs before any install or build. The reused release then runs the ordinary candidate validator, and its armed trial is kept. The normal restart, verification and trial settlement follow.
- **Target is newer:** at the normal switch point, `supersedeUnservedGitRelease` rereads the trial. If the placed release is still never-started and on its trial, it puts the link back on the fallback and clears the stale trial. It does not delete the placed release: an `openclaw` started through the link may be running from it. The shared collector removes it later, under its rules (not selected, no live lease, not named by an open run, not the running updater's own release, deselected more than 24 h ago). If the release started, or its trial ended while the target built, nothing is touched and the new trial records what the link names. The new release then goes on trial.
- **Serving release is the target:** the link goes back to it, the placed release is deselected (left to collection), and the result is `already-current`. If the placed release started or ended its trial meanwhile, nothing changes and the result is `git-release-selection-changed`.
- **Collection keeps the fallback,** even when the link left it more than 24 h ago. Before this, a fallback older than 24 h could be collected while it was still the trial's `previous`.
- **Result note:** a `git-release-placement` note names both releases and says what the update did.

- **Link writes resolve.** `publishGitRelease`, the only writer of the link, computes the link text between real paths and checks that it resolves to the chosen release before it replaces the old link. Re-arming a trial for the release the link already names keeps that release's trial, so a trial never falls back to its own target.

### State table

Notation:
- A: the release that served last (the fallback).
- B: the release the link or a deferred trial names.
- C: the target.
- `src/infra/update-runner-git-release.test.ts` holds every owner test named here.

Every link write goes through `publishGitRelease`. It computes the link text between real paths and checks that it resolves to the chosen release before replacing the old link. The linked-state-directory cases cover each kind of write.

| # | What serves | Link names | Trial (target / fallback / attempts) | Lease on B | Target | Action | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A | A | none | – | C | Build C, switch, arm trial C → A. | "rebuilds a same-commit release…" and the existing launcher cases in `git-release.test.ts` |
| 2 | A | A | none | – | A (verifies) | `already-current`, nothing changes. | "reports a current release as prepared…" |
| 3 | the checkout at A's commit, or A | B | B / A / 0, no lease directory exists under `releases/.leases/`, and A's commit is the checkout's built commit (the only served evidence on disk) | no | C = B, and B verifies | Admit C, check the match after replay, validate B, reuse it. The trial is kept. | "finishes activating a placed release…" |
| 3a | as 3 | B | B / A / 0 | no | C = B, but replay changes the tree | Build normally. | "builds instead of reusing when local replay changes the target" |
| 3b | as 3 | B | B / A / 0 | no | C = B, but B does not verify | Build normally. | "builds instead of reusing when the placed build does not verify" |
| 3d | as 3 | B | B / A / 0 | no | C = B, but B has tracked edits, or Git cannot read its index | Build normally. | "builds instead of reusing when the placed worktree has tracked edits / Git cannot read the placed worktree's index" |
| 3e | unknown | B | B / A / 0, but A's commit is not the checkout's built commit, or a Gateway has run from a release (any lease directory, even from a boot that died) | no | any, with a restart | Change nothing; `git-release-fallback-unavailable`, not safe to restart, `openclaw triage`. No rebuild. | "changes nothing and refuses when the fallback has no evidence that it serves / is incomplete and a Gateway took a release lease" |
| 3c | as 3, and the launcher starts B during validation | B | B / A / ≥1 | – | C = B | Keep the trial with fallback A. A trial never falls back to its own target. | "finishes activating a placed release that never served, also when the launcher starts it during validation" |
| 4 | A | B | B / A / 0 | no | C newer | At the switch: reread; link → A, B deselected and left to collection; arm C → A. | "falls back to the serving release and deselects…" (includes the launcher back-out) |
| 4a | A, and B ends its trial during the build | B | none | – | C newer | Leave link and trial; arm C → B (what the link names). | "keeps the link on a release that ended its trial while the target built" |
| 5 | A | B | B / A / 0 | no | C = A | Run candidate checks on A, then the caller's mutation check, then link → A, B deselected; `already-current`. | "puts the link back on the serving release when that release is the target" (includes the refused mutation check) |
| 5a | B, which ended its trial while A was checked | B | none | – | C = A | Leave link and trial; `git-release-selection-changed`, not `already-current`. | "does not report the serving target current once the placed release ends its trial" |
| 6 | A or B | B | B / A / ≥1 | – | any | Launcher-owned, unchanged from main. | "leaves a trial whose release was started by the launcher to the launcher" |
| 6a | B | B | B / A / any | yes | any | Launcher-owned, unchanged from main. | "…leased by a running process to the launcher" |
| 7 | A | A | pending B / A | no | C newer | Link → A, pending trial cleared, B left to collection; arm C → A. | "a release a --no-restart update left: deselects it once superseded" |
| 7a | A | A | pending B / A | no | C = B | Reuse B; arm B → A. | "a release a --no-restart update left: reuses it when it is the target" |
| 7b | A (or the checkout) | B | B / A / 0 | no | any, with `--no-restart` | No repair: the link's release counts as running, exactly as before this change. A same-tree retry keeps the armed trial untouched. The result says this update does not repair it; it does not promise a later repair (see Follow-ups). | "leaves the half-switched link and trial alone under --no-restart for a newer / the placed target" |
| 8 | the checkout at A's commit | B | B / A (incomplete) / 0, no lease directory, and A's commit is the checkout's built commit | no | any, with a restart | Rebuild A's commit as R, or reuse an earlier rebuild. Nothing switches before C passes its checks; at the switch R is the fallback. | "rebuilds the serving commit as the fallback when it does not verify", "keeps the link and trial, and one rebuild, while the target keeps failing" |
| 9 | unknown | B | B / A missing, or A without Git metadata / 0 | no | any | Change nothing; `git-release-fallback-unavailable`, not safe to restart, `openclaw triage`. | "changes nothing and refuses when the fallback is gone / lost its Git metadata" |
| 10 | any | any | any | any | any write under a linked state directory | Real-path link text, verified before replacing. | "writes a link that resolves under a linked state directory for a newer / the placed / the serving target", "rebuilds the serving commit as the fallback when it does not verify under a linked state directory" |

There is no new config key, stored field, schema or protocol. Releases are removed only by the shared collector; the one retention change is that the Git collector also keeps the release the running updater executes from (compared by real path).

Update behavior: this runs in the installed updater, which for a Git checkout is the checkout's own build. An updater built before this change keeps the old behavior until the checkout runs a build with it.

**A safe fallback.** A back-out must always land on a working Gateway. The fallback must therefore be a build of the commit that serves right now, present and intact: its `build-info`, build and runtime stamps, entry and Control UI must verify against the commit its worktree has checked out.
- **Normal case:** the trial's `previous` is that build. In a conversion leftover, the Gateway still runs the plain checkout through the old service definition, and `previous` is the first release built from the commit the checkout's `dist` serves.
- **Evidence that `previous` serves:** the only reliable evidence on disk is the state a conversion leaves before its first restart: no Gateway has run from any release (no directory under `releases/.leases/`; every Gateway that runs from a release takes a lease there first, and the directory stays until the release is collected), so the service still runs the checkout, and the checkout's own `dist/build-info.json` reports `previous`'s commit. Nothing on disk records that a trial passed (settling deletes the record), a Gateway takes its release lease before it is ready, and the runner cannot ask the serving Gateway for its build. Without that evidence the update changes nothing and refuses (row 3e). So this PR repairs leftovers whose fallback is the checkout's built commit; other leftovers get the triage handoff.
- **`previous` present but incomplete, with that evidence:** the update rebuilds that commit as a new release, as the conversion does for its first release, and verifies it. The link moves to it only at the normal switch point, after the target passed its checks and the caller's mutation hook. A rejected target leaves the link and trial as they were.
- **`previous` gone, or no longer readable as a Git release:** the runner has no record of the serving commit. The checkout's `dist` is not proof that the service runs it. So the update switches nothing and ends as a retryable failure, `git-release-fallback-unavailable`, with `serviceRestartSafe: false`. The message says the Gateway keeps serving, not to restart it into the release link, and to run `openclaw triage` so an agent can rebuild a fallback from the serving commit.
- **Why the gone case can still happen:** with this change, collection keeps the fallback, so a fixed updater never removes it. It can still be gone if an older updater's 24 h collection removed it.
- **Never a fallback:** a never-started release is never recorded as a fallback by this path.

This fix is also what lets an install leave the state that shipped `8f80fe08` updaters create after #201327. They fail in their own process with a false "Agent database migration did not finish" and leave this same half-switched leftover. The next update from an updater with this change finishes or supersedes it.

## Follow-ups

- When the requested target is the commit of an incomplete fallback, the rebuilt fallback is not reused as the target; the update builds that commit a second time.
- A superseded release deselected by an update that publishes nothing (the serving-target path) waits for the next update that publishes a release before collection can remove it.
- The shared collector's open-update-run check names package releases only. Git release runs record no `packageRelease`, so a Git release is protected by selection, leases, this update's keep list and the 24 h grace, not by the open-run check.
- An interrupted first conversion whose checkout is then rebuilt at the placed commit makes the placed release look served by the checkout-commit evidence. Matching the running Gateway's build ID (the serving-evidence follow-up) removes this.
- A half-switched leftover still on the earlier `lib/node_modules` link (main builds before #201917) goes through #201917's migration, which rebuilds the serving commit at the new path from the link's release; the placement repair here reads only the new link.
- `openclaw update` started through the release link during a conversion leftover stops in validation with `source-artifact-ownership` and a type-stripping error. Nothing changes, but the message does not say what to do. Running it from the checkout works.
- On a converted install, an update interrupted during activation (observed in the e2e harness) recovered the Gateway before exiting, so the launcher starts the placed release (`attempts: 1`) and owns the trial. A leftover with `attempts: 0` there needs the Gateway to stay down, which the serving-evidence follow-up handles.
- `--no-restart` with a leftover keeps the old trial (C → B). It no longer promises that a later update repairs it; whether a later update can repair that state is not decided here.
- Reading the serving commit from the running Gateway would let the update repair leftovers whose fallback is not the checkout's built commit.

## Not proven

- A fallback that is gone, or has no served evidence, is handed to an agent (`openclaw triage`) and is not repaired automatically.

- A trial the launcher started is left as on main, where an update that supersedes it clears its trial. That is existing launcher-owned behavior, not changed here.
- When the target carries local commits, the placed-release match runs after replay, so the replay itself is repeated (no install or build).
- Platforms: macOS launchd only.
- A Gateway whose release lease could not be written (the lease is best effort) leaves no lease directory, so the checkout's build would still count as evidence while that Gateway serves a release.

The GREEN end-to-end cells ran at head `153c8aa733df`.

prs.title: fix: check a recorded data-at-risk mark before repair or the next update acts on it
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an update step fails after it may have touched state, the updater records a "data at risk" mark on that run, for example `rollback-state-unverified`. Most of these marks come from a failed read or a timeout, not from real damage. The published 2026.10.33 and 2026.11.5 updaters keep writing them, and nothing ever checked a mark:

- The update report said "Keep the Gateway stopped" even when the Gateway was running.
- `openclaw update repair` then refused to start the Gateway for that run every time, naming only `openclaw gateway status --deep`.
- The next `openclaw update` ignored the mark completely. When the installation was already current, it exited 0 without a word.

## User Impact

User impact: a recorded data-at-risk mark is now checked against the state on disk, without the user having to run anything first.

- **State consistent:** the next plain `openclaw update` prints one line, resolves the mark and continues. That includes automatic updates and updates that find the installation already current. `openclaw update repair` does the same and also starts a Gateway the marked update stopped.
- **Real inconsistency:** the update or repair still refuses and changes nothing. It says what is wrong and whether the Gateway is running, records the finding on the run, and names `openclaw triage` first and the manual command last.
- **Killed-update refusals from #201361** now also name `openclaw triage` before the manual command.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One verification owner** (`src/infra/update-data-at-risk.ts`) answers "is the state on disk consistent with the installed version?".
  - It reuses the runtime schema preflight: a child process reads the database in one native read transaction, with no copy, so it is safe beside a live writer. It also uses the existing recovery-admission readers.
  - Findings: a database newer than the installed build, a database behind it (unfinished migration), unfinished update recovery, an interrupted restore directory, retained `.migrated-<run>` files from the marked run's database rollback (state may be only partly restored), or unreadable state (unverifiable).
  - An `active-mutation` mark (Doctor writers that may still be alive) is not resolved from schemas alone. Before Doctor it is deferred to Doctor. After the run's own Doctor maintenance has held exclusive state and agent ownership, no earlier writer can still hold the state, and the schema check decides.
- **History is not rewritten.** A consistent verification records the step `finalize:data-at-risk-verified:<marked run>` on the run that checked. Readers in `src/infra/update-run-data-at-risk.ts` treat "marked, later verified" as resolved. No new field, schema or protocol. Published updaters store the mark as the `finalize:data-at-risk` step, which the current reader already decodes, so their marks are handled the same way.
- **Repair.** Before it touches the Gateway, repair verifies every unverified mark in recent history, not only the run that stopped the Gateway. Git release updates and refusals before mutation never stop it. Any inconsistent finding keeps every Gateway as it is, whichever run stopped it. The managed-handoff interrupted-update path reads the same receipt before it restarts.
- **Next update.** Admission runs the same check after foreground admission and before it creates its run, so already-current updates are covered too.
  - Consistent: one line, plus receipts on the new run.
  - Newer state or unreadable: a warning, and the update continues, because its own schema checks still guard activation and updating is the fix for newer state.
  - Anything else: refusal. The refusal happens after the run exists, so the finding is recorded for the agent `openclaw triage` opens.
- **Messages.**
  - Update failure guidance states whether the Gateway was observed running or stopped, which version is installed and whether the update was rolled back, and says the mark is unverified.
  - With the Gateway running, it says nothing is needed now. With it stopped, it names repair to bring it back.
  - Refusals put the next steps before the finding, so the recorded warning's 500-character limit cannot cut them off.
  - Update-path guidance that asks you to stop the managed Gateway names `openclaw gateway stop --force`, because a non-interactive shell refuses the bare command. That covers the repair, status and maintenance-error messages and their docs; #201331 changed one more line in `update-recovery-guidance.ts`.

<details><summary>Genuine refusals kept, and their negative controls</summary>

- **Database newer than the installed version.** Repair refuses and leaves the Gateway as it was (owner test with real SQLite; Docker cell `inconsistent-repair`). The next update warns and continues, and its target schema check still refuses a target that cannot open that state.
- **Unfinished migration** (database behind the installed version): owner test with real SQLite. The next update refuses, and the finding is recorded on the refused run.
- **Unfinished update recovery or an interrupted restore directory:** owner tests with real fixtures. Repair and update admission already refuse these first.
- **Partial database rollback** (the marked run left `.migrated-<run>` files): owner test. Another run's leftover does not count.
- **`active-mutation`:** never resolved by a schema check alone. It is checked only after the run's own Doctor maintenance has held exclusive state ownership.
- **Unreadable state or an unlistable state directory:** reported as unverifiable, never as consistent or as an interrupted restore.
</details>

## Update behavior for published updaters

The installed updater runs first and cannot be patched:

- Marks written by 2026.10.33, 2026.11.5 and main are read through the same `finalize:data-at-risk` step.
- A published updater still writes false marks; P0-0 and the catch-alls in the audit belong to other changes.
- When the state is consistent, the first update or repair run by a CLI containing this change resolves the mark without user action.
- A published Gateway's managed-update helper still logs its old text on exit 79. The helper this change ships logs "gateway left stopped: data at risk (...) recorded and not yet verified; run openclaw update repair to verify the state and restart the gateway".

## Steps still left to a person

- **A Gateway left stopped by a marked update when no further update or repair runs.** The Gateway is down, so no Gateway-driven path can run. The next `openclaw update` (or an automatic one, if the user re-enables it) resolves the mark; starting the Gateway takes repair. Agent route: `openclaw triage`. Follow-up: verify the mark inside the failing update's own recovery before it decides the restart.
- **Managed handoff exit 79 (P1-4).** Not changed; see the design below.
- **A real inconsistency.** By definition it needs a decision: finish a migration, restore a backup, or install a newer build. The message leads with `openclaw triage`, and the finding is recorded on the run.
- **An interrupted restore directory or partial rollback leftovers.** No command finishes these safely. The existing docs procedure applies, and the agent gets the file paths.
- **`active-mutation` while the earlier Doctor writers are still alive.** Doctor's maintenance admission waits for them and refuses while they hold the state. Once they exit, one repair or update resolves the mark.
- **An unreadable agent database registry.** Rollback leftovers beside agent databases cannot be looked for, so update and repair refuse and name `openclaw triage`. Retrying once the registry is readable resolves it.
- **`openclaw update repair` in Git release mode.** It refuses as on `main` and leaves the service untouched; the message names `openclaw triage`. A plain `openclaw update` still resolves the mark, as the `green-repeat` cell shows.

## Follow-ups

- **Verdict inside Doctor restoration admission.** After a mark was deferred to Doctor, Doctor restores a Gateway it parked before the post-Doctor recheck runs. Moving the check into Doctor's restoration admission closes that gap. Owner: Doctor maintenance restoration.
- **Unresolved-mark lookup independent of the 100-row history window.**
- **Git release-mode repair ownership** belongs with #201538 (`fix/update-git-release-running-build-from-evidence`). Two pieces are needed:
  - The ownership change this PR reverted, which accepts `openclaw-launcher.mjs` services whose release is a linked worktree of this checkout.
  - The Doctor stale-Gateway check, which must compare the running Gateway with the active release's build, not the checkout's.

  The landing review's two findings that #201538 must address are recorded with the diff in the release-mode worker's notes: the stale-build stop, and sibling `git worktree` checkouts that share a common Git directory.

## P1-4 design (managed handoff exit 79)

- **Why it diverges:** the direct CLI restarts a stopped Gateway after a failure with no data risk (`update-command-failure-recovery.ts`). Under the handoff, the helper stopped the service, not the updater, so `preManagedServiceStop.stopped` is false in the child. The updater then reports `serviceRestartSafe:false`, and the helper exits 79 and leaves the Gateway down.
- **Fix that keeps the exit-79 contract:** a candidate updater running under `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_RUN_HANDOFF=1` could take the helper's recorded `service-stop` as its own stop evidence. It would then run the same restart and verification and report `service: "healthy"` with `serviceRestartSafe: true`. The helper already restores nothing in that case and exits non-79.
- **Why it is left out:** it only helps once the installed updater contains it, and it needs its own red and green handoff proof. It is left for a follow-up.

## Evidence

Behavior checked, on the exact head unless noted. Base for red is `origin/main` `f4b42cc9ae7`, or `f5b717d232f` where stated.

- **Owner (real SQLite)**, `src/infra/update-data-at-risk.test.ts`:
  - Current state is consistent beside an open `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` writer, and the in-process copy path (`prepareSqliteReadOnlyLocation`) is never called.
  - Newer schema, behind schema, unfinished recovery, interrupted restore and partial-rollback leftovers are inconsistent.
  - Unreadable state and an unlistable directory are unverifiable; `active-mutation` is never resolved.
  - Red first: the no-copy and unlistable-directory cases failed on the first implementation, which used the maintenance copy path and labeled listing errors as an interrupted restore, then passed.
- **Repair** (`update-repair-service.test.ts`, real ledger and finalization):
  - A false mark with the Gateway stopped is verified, the receipt recorded, and the Gateway started.
  - The same with the Gateway running is verified, not restarted.
  - A mark on a run that never stopped the Gateway is verified once; a second repair does not check it again.
  - Inconsistent and unverifiable verdicts keep the Gateway as it was and print the exact refusal. One case uses a realistic UUID and path to prove the next steps survive the 500-character limit; another reports a running Gateway's version.
  - Reviewer-found regression: a Gateway another run stopped stays down when a later mark is inconsistent.
- **Next update** (`update-command-run.test.ts`):
  - A consistent mark prints one line and records the receipt on the new run, and a later update does not check it again.
  - An unfinished migration refuses and records the finding on the refused run.
  - Newer state warns and continues.
- **Guidance** (`update-recovery-guidance.test.ts`): exact text for running, stopped, rolled-back, failed-rollback and unobserved Gateways. Red on base `f5b717d232f` (11 cases fail), green on head.
- **Killed-update refusals** (`update-command-killed-run-refusals.process.test.ts`): every refusal names the agent route before the manual command.
- **Timeout attribution.** Two `update-command-database-rollback` cases and one `update-repair-cancellation` case timed out at 120 s in a 15-file local batch at load ~30. Run alone on the same machine:
  - The `git`/`git-edited` cases took 69 s/54 s on head against 71 s/59 s on base, and printed no data-at-risk verification.
  - `update-repair-cancellation` passed 7/7 on head.
  - Base failed a different case in that file in its own loaded batch. The timeouts were machine load, not added cost.
- **End to end:** the Docker cells below. The package and Git release-mode green cells ran on `787cf1befff`. The commits after it are merges of `main` (release tooling, UI, and the pnpm and Git-checkout update fixes #201735 and #201701) and touch no mark, verification or repair path.

## End-to-end: package install (installed tarball, real managed Gateway under a systemd shim)

`scripts/e2e/upgrade-survivor-docker.sh` with `OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_INSTALLED_RECOVERY_CUT=data-at-risk`. It installs the packed tarball, starts a managed Gateway, kills real `openclaw update` runs at fixed points, and writes the mark a failed rollback read leaves onto the killed run, in the row shape published updaters persist. Everything after that point goes through the installed CLI.

| Step | Red: base `f4b42cc9ae7` | Green: head `787cf1befff` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `after-mark-update`: next plain update after a false mark (Gateway stopped by the killed run) | exit 1. The update refuses: "the Gateway that update stopped is still not running" | exit 0 in 262 s. Prints `... verification found the state schemas match installed OpenClaw ... so that mark is resolved.`, records the receipt, installs the next version, and the Gateway serves it |
| `marked-repair`: repair after another false mark with the Gateway stopped | not reached | exit 0 in 53 s. Repair verifies the mark, records `finalize:data-at-risk-verified:<run>` on its own run, then starts the Gateway and verifies it (new PID, `marked-repair-probe` 0) |
| `inconsistent-repair`: the marked run's rollback left `openclaw.sqlite.migrated-<run>` | not reached | exit 1 in 18 s. `... The Gateway is stopped. Repair left the Gateway as it was. Run \`openclaw triage\` for an agent with the recorded facts, or by hand: keep that file and the update's backup; ... Found: the database rollback of update <run> left .../openclaw.sqlite.migrated-<run> ...`. The Gateway stays stopped and no receipt is written |
| `restored-repair`: the leftover removed | not reached | exit 0 in 50 s. Receipt recorded; the Gateway starts and serves |

The green cell took 736 s under host load 18 to 22. Gateway outage in each repair case is the repair's own time (53 s and 50 s), which ends with a verified serving Gateway.

`autoreview` does not run on this machine. Two independent read-only reviewers reviewed the diff and the tests; their findings and what changed are listed below.

## Tests changed or removed

- `update-repair-service.test.ts`: the "named data risk" case of "does not start a Gateway after %s" is replaced by the verified, inconsistent, unverifiable and later-mark cases. The old behavior (refuse forever) is what this change fixes.
- `update-recovery-guidance.test.ts`: assertions on "Keep the Gateway stopped" are replaced by exact rendered text.
- `update-command-post-update-repair.test.ts`, `cleanup.test.ts`, `status.test.ts`, `update-repair-command.test.ts`, the killed-run tests and `update-managed-service-handoff-lifecycle.test.ts`: expectations follow the new text.
- `update-data-at-risk.test.ts`: "never resolves a mark that records live Doctor writers" is replaced by a case that proves both halves: unverifiable (deferred to Doctor) before Doctor holds the state, consistent after. The old expectation was the repair loop that round 2 finding 4 reported.
- `doctor-health.legacy-update.test.ts`: "reports stale stop failure" gains an `identity-uninspectable` case. When service identity cannot be inspected, the stop is skipped, and the error must say so rather than "did not stop".
- `service-layout.test.ts`: the Git release-mode ownership cases are removed along with the reverted change; they move to the follow-up.
- Net test growth is +923 lines; `config/test-lines-allocations/update-data-at-risk-verification.txt` records 523 beyond the 400 allowance, with the reason.

## Reviewer findings

**First review (before the next-update and release-mode work):**
- The owner copied the database (the default preflight purpose was maintenance): fixed red then green.
- A listing failure was labeled an interrupted restore: fixed red then green.
- Some bare `gateway stop` instances remained: fixed in the update path.
- Repair only verified the stopping run's mark: fixed.
- The handoff reader ignored the receipt: fixed.

**Second review:**
- Repair could start a Gateway after reporting an inconsistent later mark (blocker): fixed, with a regression test.
- The 500-character limit cut off the next steps: the next steps now come first, multiple databases collapse to "(and N more)", and a realistic-length test covers it.
- `active-mutation` and partial-rollback marks could be falsely resolved: both now refuse resolution, with tests.
- A dangling "By hand:" in `refuse()`: fixed.
- Verification ran before foreground admission: moved after it.
- Only the newest mark got a receipt: all unverified marks are now resolved at once.
- `Keep the Gateway stopped` in `update-command-database-backup.ts` rollback-start messages: left as is. It belongs to the restore/rollback catch-all fixes (audit P2-1), not this change.
- No unit test for the handoff receipt reader: not added; that path is covered only by its existing refusal test.

## Not proven

- A mark written by the published `openclaw@2026.11.5` binary itself. The Docker cells use a copied record in the exact row shape that `v2026.11.5:src/infra/update-run-write.ts` and its codec persist.
- Windows.
- The managed handoff (`update.run`) trigger end to end; the Git cell uses the CLI trigger.
- An `active-mutation` mark end to end. It is covered by the owner test and the repair test (red on the previous head, green now), not by a Docker cell.
- Inherited failure, not caused here: `update-command-rollback.test.ts` "excludes a competing config writer..." fails on base `4c11507` as well.

## Rating round 1 findings and what changed

The round 1 rating was F/F/F; the reviewer saw no end-to-end evidence yet. Each finding was checked against the code:

1. **Rollback leftovers of agent databases were missed.** Real: the scan only listed the shared directory. Verification now walks the state directory, bounded in depth and entry count, for the marked run's `.migrated-<run>` files. A walk that cannot finish is unverifiable. Tested with both a shared and an agent leftover.
2. **The staged handoff helper's history read could reject an advanced schema.** Real: it ran for every run. It now reads history only when the run carries a mark. If that read fails, the mark stands, as before this change, so an unmarked recovery restarts as it did.
3. **A refusal did not reach the helper that restarts the Gateway.** Real: repair returned `coreUpdate: completed`. A mark refusal now makes repair report `coreUpdate: "pending"`, which the helper already treats as "post-core repair did not complete", so it leaves the Gateway stopped. Covered in the repair tests.
4. **A newer shared database cannot reach the verifier in the Docker cell.** Real: repair's own admission refuses newer shared state first. The Docker negative control now uses a rollback leftover, which reaches the verifier. A newer shared database is still refused by that existing admission, with its existing message.
5. **A newer database masked an unfinished migration.** Real: the warn-and-continue exception now applies only when no database is behind.
6. **"Repair changed nothing" overstated what repair did.** Real: Doctor and plugin maintenance had already run. It now says "Repair left the Gateway as it was".

## Rating round 2 findings and what changed

Round 2 rated proof D, patch F. Each finding was checked against the code:

1. **Rollback files beside an external agent store were missed.** Real. Leftover detection now reads the agent database registry (`readRegisteredAgentDatabases`) and checks the exact `<db>.migrated-<run>{,-wal,-shm,-journal}` family beside the shared database and every registered agent database. A registry read failure is unverifiable. Tested with a shared leftover and one beside an agent store outside the state directory.
2. **Doctor could cycle the Gateway before the check.** Real. Repair now checks unverified marks before Doctor maintenance starts and refuses there, so Doctor never parks or restarts the Gateway on an inconsistent mark (`expectRefusedBeforeDoctor`). An unfinished migration, and now a live-writer mark, are deferred to Doctor and checked again after it.
3. **The original-runtime handoff fallback could restart past a refusal.** Real. `assertRestartSafe` in the interrupted-handoff helper now checks every unverified mark in history, not only the interrupted run's, and falls back to the run's own mark when history cannot be read.
4. **`active-mutation` marks could never be resolved.** Real: repair told you to run repair again, and the next repair said the same thing. Before Doctor, the mark is now deferred to Doctor. After the run's own Doctor maintenance has held exclusive state and agent ownership, no writer the marked run left can still hold the state, so the schema check decides. One repair resolves it (red on the previous head, green now).
5. **The state-tree walk could exhaust its entry limit on large release-mode installs.** Real. The walk is gone; finding 1's registry check replaces it, so `git-install/releases` is never read.
6. **History was read with a cold synchronous snapshot before admission.** Real. The next-update check uses the async worker history read (`listUpdateRunsAsync`).
7. **Ahead and behind together named only the ahead database.** Real. The refusal names both, and its next step is to restore the pre-update backup, since neither `openclaw update` nor `doctor --fix` settles both.
8. **An unknown runtime was reported as stopped.** Real. The Gateway is reported stopped only when the runtime says `stopped`; otherwise its state is reported as unknown.

The low-value-test note on `update-recovery-guidance.test.ts` was not taken: the exact rendered text is what the brief asks to prove, and each case covers a distinct Gateway state.

## Rating round 3 findings and what changed

Round 3 rated proof D, patch F. Each finding was checked against the code:

1. **A live-writer mark hid a rollback leftover.** Real. The `active-mutation` deferral is now the verifier's last check, so a leftover, an interrupted restore, or a schema finding reports first. Owner test: an `active-mutation` mark beside a leftover now returns the leftover (red on the previous head).
2. **The interrupted-handoff helper checks history-wide marks.** Rejected in round 3; the landing review showed it was real (see below) and it is now fixed. `assertRestartSafe` runs after `finalize()`, and finalize verifies every unverified mark first and records receipts. A false earlier mark is resolved in the same finalize and does not hold the Gateway. Only a mark that finalize could not resolve keeps it down, which is the intended outcome.
3. **Restoration ignored receipts from earlier repairs.** Real for consistency. `restoreRepairGateway` now reads receipts across recent history, as admission does. No dedicated test: in the repair harness, a repair whose start failed does not leave a stop intent for the next repair to restore. So the path the reviewer describes is not reachable through repair today.
4. **A refusal after Doctor finished finalization with exit 0.** Real. A mark still refused after Doctor now fails finalization: abandoned runs are not acknowledged, the handoff is not completed, text mode prints `Update finalization failed.`, and the command exits 1 with the refusal. The next repair retries it. Repair test: red (repair `succeeded`), green (`failed`, and a later repair resolves the mark and starts the Gateway).
5. **Files a completed rollback keeps on purpose were treated as a partial restore.** Real. `restoreUpdateDatabaseBackup` keeps the displaced `<db>.migrated-<run>` files after a successful restore and records a completed `database rollback` step. A mark whose run has that step no longer counts those files. Owner test covers it.
6. **A registry read failure replaced a schema verdict.** Real. The round-3 fix let an unfinished migration hide unchecked agent leftovers; the landing review caught that and the fix below replaces it. Shared-database leftovers are checked without the registry. Agent leftovers are checked after the schema verdict, and when the registry cannot be read, the schema finding is reported instead of a generic registry error. An unfinished migration or newer state still cannot hide an agent leftover. No separate test, because the registry read failure cannot be produced from a fixture without mocking the reader.
7. **The skipped-stop message inferred liveness from the stop flag.** Real. The message now comes from the existing liveness check, so an already-offline service passes. When the stop was skipped, the error says `Stale Gateway PID <pid> was not stopped: <reason> Observed: service=..., PID=..., port ...=...`. Doctor test: red on the previous code (`did not stop`), green now.

## Landing review findings and what changed

The landing review on `231fdd86e36` rated proof C, patch F. Each finding was checked against the code:

1. **Release-mode ownership stopped a healthy Gateway** (P1, `service-layout.ts`). Real, and reproduced under real systemd. Reverted; see "Git release-mode repair: moved to a follow-up".
2. **Sibling `git worktree` checkouts could claim each other's service** (P2, `service-layout.ts`). Real. Reverted with finding 1.
3. **Unchecked agent leftovers were deferred or continued past** (P1, `update-data-at-risk.ts`, the coordinator's fix-6 blocker and its sibling). Real.
   - An unreadable agent registry with an unfinished migration returned the deferrable migration verdict, so Doctor maintenance could park and restart the Gateway without anyone having looked for agent leftovers.
   - An unreadable agent database returned `unverifiable` before the leftover scan, and a plain update continued past a leftover it never saw.

   The verifier now looks for leftovers first, beside the shared database and every registered agent database, before any other check. When the registry cannot be read, the result is `unverifiable` with `leftoversUnchecked`. It keeps any schema finding beside that fact ("the agent database registry could not be read, so database rollback leftovers beside agent databases are unchecked; and <schema finding>"), and is never `finishable` or `newerState`. Every consumer of the verdict refuses on it:
   - **Repair before maintenance:** it is not deferrable, so repair refuses before Doctor and leaves the Gateway as it was.
   - **The next plain update:** it refuses on `leftoversUnchecked` instead of warning and continuing.
   - **Finalize after Doctor:** any result other than `consistent` refuses and fails finalization.
   - **Managed handoff:** it restarts only on a receipt, and receipts are written only after a `consistent` verdict.

   Tests, red on `231fdd86e36` and green now:
   - unreadable registry with an unfinished migration, with and without an agent leftover, at the owner and through repair before Doctor;
   - an unreadable agent database beside its leftover;
   - a readable registry, unchanged;
   - the plain-update refusal.
4. **The interrupted-handoff entry guard blocked on older marks** (P1, `update-managed-service-handoff-interrupted.ts`). Real. The entry guard now judges only the interrupted run's own mark, as on `main`. The history-wide check stays after `finalize()`, which verifies older marks and records their receipts. Handoff lifecycle test: an interrupted managed update with only an earlier false mark recovers and restarts. Red on `231fdd86e36` (`gateway left stopped: data at risk (rollback-state-unverified)`), green now.
5. **The rollback-completed exception read a step compaction evicts** (P2, `update-run-data-at-risk.ts`). Real. It now also reads `diagnostic:database rollback`, which only a completed restore writes ("Restored pre-migration databases from ..."). The ledger's compaction keeps that step and its text. Owner test with a ledger compacted past the ordinary step: the retained `.migrated-<run>` file no longer counts. No new stored field.

## Rating round after the landing review

On `33e6184dbc6`: proof C, patch F. Each finding was checked against the code:

1. **Doctor can restore a parked Gateway before the post-Doctor check** (P1, `update-command-finalize.ts`). Real but narrow. A mark deferred to Doctor (an unfinished migration, or live Doctor writers) lets Doctor maintenance park a running Gateway, and Doctor restores it before the post-Doctor recheck runs. `main` has no recheck at all, so this is no worse than `main`.
   - Changed here: the refusal after Doctor no longer claims the Gateway was left as it was. It now says `Repair did not start or restart the Gateway after this check.` Tested in the after-Doctor refusal case.
   - Not changed: making the verdict part of Doctor's restoration admission changes Doctor's restoration owner. It is listed as a follow-up.
2. **The original-runtime branch of the interrupted handoff restores without the history-wide check** (P1, `update-managed-service-handoff-interrupted.ts`). Rejected for this PR. With no plugin cohort, no finalize runs there, so no receipt can be written. A history-wide check would bring back the stuck state the landing review reported, where a false older mark keeps the Gateway down. The branch behaves exactly as on `main`.
3. **An inaccessible rollback path was read as absent** (P2). Real. Leftover probes now separate "not there" (`ENOENT`, `ENOTDIR`) from "could not look". The latter goes down the same `leftoversUnchecked` refusal path. Owner test with an unreadable directory: red, then green.
4. **An unfinished migration was deferred while another database could not be read** (P2). Real. An unreadable database next to a behind or newer one is now `unverifiable` and never deferrable, with both findings in the detail. Owner test with real SQLite: red, then green.
5. **The repair's own row can push the oldest of 100 marked runs out of the window** (P2). Not changed. Only a mark at row 101 is affected, and that is the same history window `main` reads everywhere. The stopping run's mark is read by run ID, so it is never skipped. Listed as a follow-up.

## CI on `787cf1befff`

Three jobs in run [44525460079](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44525460079) failed, and none of them came from this change:
- `check-test-types-core-2` and `check-test-types-core-3` failed with eight TS2739 errors in `test/scripts/release-*` fixtures. `main`'s own CI run [44524514068](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44524514068) at `dbc1aa04e88` (the `main` merged here) shows the same errors in the same jobs. #201811 fixed them.
- `checks-node-compact-small-3` failed in `test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts` ("Expected workflow step Download full release validation manifest"). This change touches no workflow or release tooling.

Merging current `main` cleared them. The root test-type stripes pass locally on the merged head.

The later `package-acceptance-workflow` failure came from #201802 removing a workflow step without updating its test. It was inherited from `main`, and #201805 fixed it by restoring the step. This head merges `main` after #201805.

## End-to-end: Git release mode (installed checkout, real managed service, busy database)

These cells drive the update-matrix harness in Docker. Each one installs a real Git checkout, converts it to release mode through a real `openclaw update`, and runs a second real update under database write load. It then writes the mark that a failed post-activation schema read leaves, in the published row shape, onto that update's run while the Gateway keeps serving. Everything after that point goes through the shipped CLI.

| Cell | Code | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `red-repeat` (inside the `red-repair` cell) | base `cf9a9839e03` | The plain repeat update reports `already-current`, exits 0 and says nothing about the mark. |
| `green-repeat` | head `787cf1befff` (earlier also `b7f71419149`) | The plain repeat update, already current, prints `Update <run> recorded data at risk (rollback-state-unverified); verification found the state schemas match installed OpenClaw 2026.11.5 and no migration or restore is unfinished, so that mark is resolved.` It records `finalize:data-at-risk-verified:<run>` on its run (read back through `openclaw update status`) and exits 0 in 145 s. Busy load held throughout: 1278 write commits at 8 MiB/s on a 512 MiB database and 1278 readiness probes, with 0 failed and 0 outages. The Gateway served the same build before and after. |

`green-repeat` does not depend on the reverted release-mode ownership change. A plain update's mark check runs at update admission and never asks whether the service belongs to this checkout. The same cell's repeat step on base passed that path silently, with no ownership refusal.

### Git release-mode repair: moved to a follow-up

This PR no longer changes release-mode repair ownership. An earlier head accepted a Git release-mode service as the checkout's own (`src/daemon/service-layout.ts`). The landing review found two problems with that change, both of which make release-mode repair worse than on `main`:
- Once the service is accepted, Doctor's stale-Gateway inspection reads the expected build from the source checkout, not from the active release. It then stops a healthy Gateway that serves the release, and repair exits 1. A real-systemd cell reproduced this on `1e39a2c5828` ([raw output](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201668#issuecomment-7014449579)).
- Two independent `git worktree` checkouts share a common Git directory, so one could claim the other's release-mode service.

The change is reverted here. Release-mode repair behaves as on `main`: it refuses and changes nothing. The refusal is now true for this case. It names the Git release launcher, says this checkout cannot yet confirm that the release is its own, says the service was left untouched, and leads with `openclaw triage` (rendered-text test in `update-command-service-maintenance.test.ts`). The ownership change and both findings move to the release-mode follow-up (#201538), which also carries the Doctor stale-build fix.

Two related message fixes stay in this PR. Doctor's stale-Gateway stop now reports a stop that was skipped (`was not stopped: <reason>`) and one it could not confirm (`could not be confirmed stopped`) instead of always `did not stop`. Both have red/green tests in `doctor-health.legacy-update.test.ts`.

Raw terminal lines from every cell are in [this PR comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201668#issuecomment-7010468460). The full outputs (`fix.stderr`, `repeat.stderr`, update status JSON, asciinema casts) are kept locally, because the artifact store rejects uploads from this machine.

prs.title: refactor: reduce allocation while saving subagent progress
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Saving subagent progress repeatedly serializes the previous registry row even though that row is immutable and its canonical binding was already prepared. This adds allocation on the Gateway's mutation path.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Subagent registry mutations allocate less while preserving exact persisted bytes, no-op write decisions, runtime ownership, eviction, receipts, notices, and caller isolation. No schema, configuration, migration, or operator action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing immutable-row facts retain a weak reference to the canonical binding. A later commit can reuse it by exact object identity; when GC collects the binding, the unchanged codec rebuilds it. The reference does not keep a second serialized payload alive after the current JavaScript job ends. Strong retention was rejected: a 5,000-row sweep increased retained heap by 100 MB. Weak retention measured 328.1 MB versus baseline controls of 327.8/327.7 MB.

The selective copies from #201212 remain necessary: callers can mutate new nested containers while an ACK is pending. Sibling completion writers already bind their rows once. No separate cache owner or run-ID cache is introduced. Production delta is +14 lines for the binding's lifetime and fallback; test delta +126. The author simplification pass kept the existing clone, equality, and persistence paths intact.

## Evidence

All 75 focused tests passed in four files (46.99 s wrapper wall). A 160-step deterministic randomized differential sequence compares the old two-bind algorithm with actual real-worker writes, including exact JSON bytes, no-ops, nested completion changes, property order, eviction, parent-completion rows, deletion/recreation, and restore. Existing held-ACK aliasing, notices, receipts, and runtime-owner tests pass. A new collection test proves serialized payloads can disappear while rows remain resident, and no-op behavior survives rebinding. The metadata bind-count assertion fails on the original persistence implementation: two binds instead of one when the prepared binding is retained.

The committed benchmark uses 5,000 synthetic runs, 500 running children, 1,000 requester sessions and a 64-row repeated working set with 2 KiB tasks / 16 KiB results. Five serial A/A pairs and five serial A/B pairs were run separately for timing and sampled allocation (40 runs, 2,048 mutations each). All durable/resident digests matched. Node 26.12.1 on macOS; host load 3.77–7.58. This measures the actual registry/worker owner, not end-to-end Gateway throughput; unrelated workspace trees and agent-database scans are absent from this path.

Acceptance: lower commit allocation beyond A/A variation, exact output parity, no consistent CPU/read regression; investigate any metric regression of 20% or more. Per-mutation figures below are medians across the five runs. CPU improvement is not claimed.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Whole mutation CPU | 224.16 µs | 221.45 µs |
| Whole mutation median latency | 0.560 ms | 0.551 ms |
| Whole mutation p95 latency | 0.858 ms | 0.880 ms |
| Total sampled allocation | 191,284 B | 174,303 B (-8.9%) |
| Allocation under commitRows | 63,438 B | 48,060 B (-24.2%) |
| Allocation under binding | 38,781 B | 21,076 B (-45.7%) |
| Allocation under structuredClone | 12,386 B | 12,372 B |

A/A medians: CPU 226.88/225.02 µs, p95 latency 0.879/0.855 ms, allocation 191,933/191,596 B. Candidate p95 latency variation is comparable to the controls. Read-control CPU was 27.98→28.58 µs and median latency 27.13→27.92 µs; that path is unchanged. Synchronous preparation timings include freezing work moved from publication, so they are not interpreted as whole-operation speedups.

Commands:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-worker.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-memory.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.store.codec.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.store.sqlite.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm check:changed --staged
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/subagent-registry-commit-measure.ts --output <result.json> --mixed --working-set 64 --iterations 2048
# Baseline: add --source-file <persistence.ts from 6ef632bfb498e>.
# Separate allocation pass: add --allocation. CPU attribution: --cpu-profile.
# Full residency check: --working-set 5000 --iterations 5000.
```

Independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean at P0–P2 on the local change against `6ef632bfb498e`, with no actionable findings. `pnpm check:changed --staged` passed after correcting test type narrowing and mechanical lint findings; the two affected tests also passed again (10.71 s wrapper wall). Production sources are unchanged. Hosted ClawSweeper and exact-head CI will be checked before landing. No changed module is imported by ui/src, and no Node-only import was added to production.

Conflict integration: #201960 landed while final gates were completing. The merge preserves its deletion-only cleanup path and removal of an older clone assertion; the new bind-count assertion remains. The production optimization is unchanged. All 75 focused tests passed on the combined source (101.98 s including worker-cache rebuild), and a fresh independent Codex review is scoped-clean at P0–P2. `pnpm check:changed --staged --base origin/main` passed completely on the integrated source. The original head passed all 69 applicable CI checks and ClawSweeper with zero findings; these are prior-head evidence, and the integrated head is being gated separately.

prs.title: fix: let memory indexing finish for large PostgreSQL chat histories
prs.body:
Closes #201571

## What Problem This Solves

On an agent store moved to PostgreSQL, `openclaw memory index --agent <id>` fails with `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` when the agent has a long session history. The same agent indexes fine on SQLite. Memory search for that agent can't be rebuilt.

## User Impact

User impact: memory indexing on PostgreSQL agent stores now completes for large session histories instead of exhausting the 512 MB transcript worker heap. SQLite behavior is unchanged apart from slice queries also carrying the row bound.

## Why This Change Was Made

Large transcripts are read in short slices after the batch transaction. PostgreSQL was excluded from that path because `iterateSqliteQuerySync` buffers a full PostgreSQL result, and the slice query had no SQL bound, so the byte budget could only stop iteration after the whole remainder was already transferred. The PostgreSQL export therefore loaded every row at once.

This change:
- adds a SQL row bound (`TRANSCRIPT_PAYLOAD_SLICE_ROWS = 256`) to each slice query, resuming after a full page; the existing 2 MiB decoded-byte budget still ends a slice early;
- removes the PostgreSQL exceptions in the export reader and the memory worker's batch sizing, so PostgreSQL defers large transcripts exactly as SQLite does.

The heap cap itself is left alone: per the issue review, raising it only postpones the failure while the read stays unbounded.

Risk: PostgreSQL exports above the 4 MiB retained-snapshot limit now use several short read-only transactions instead of one. Transcript changes between slices are detected by the existing context-version check and retried, same as SQLite.

## Evidence

**End-to-end: shipped `openclaw memory index` on a large PostgreSQL history, unchanged 512 MB worker limit.**

Setup: PostgreSQL 17.12 with `unaccent` and `pg_trgm`. Fresh isolated state with `database.engine: "postgres"` and keyword-only memory (`memory.search.provider: "none"`), because native Windows can't run `database port` yet. One agent `main` with one long DM session: 30,000 messages of 8 KiB each, 30,001 `transcript_events` rows, about 240 MB in PostgreSQL. CLI built from this branch via `pnpm openclaw`. The same store was indexed three times with `openclaw memory index --agent main --force`:

| Build | Result |
| --- | --- |
| This branch | `Memory index updated (main): 1 file indexed.` exit 0 |
| `main` (`d902b29bc`): the 3 production files swapped back, rebuilt | `Memory index failed (main): Error [ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY]: Worker terminated due to reaching memory limit: JS heap out of memory [task=sessionTranscript.session-entries admittedInputBytes=932 exchanges=0 stage=running]` exit 1 (the reported failure) |
| This branch again, rebuilt, same store after the failed run | `Memory index updated (main): 1 file indexed.` exit 0 |

After the successful runs, `memory_index_sources` holds `sessions/main/large-dm-session.jsonl` (251,257,868 bytes) and `memory_index_chunks` holds 90,000 rows.

**Focused tests:**
- `session-accessor.sqlite-read-hold.postgres.test.ts` against a live PostgreSQL 17.12 server, through `pnpm test` with the conformance preload: **3/3 pass**. With the 3 production files reverted to base, all 3 fail (one transaction and one unbounded head payload query instead of row-bounded slices). Running it live also corrected my original version of this test (second commit): two regexes and a slice count that couldn't have been checked without a server.
- `session-accessor.sqlite-read-hold.test.ts`, `session-memory-entry.worker.test.ts`, `session-accessor.sqlite-export-budget.test.ts` through `pnpm test`: **20/20 pass**. The new SQLite regression `pages slices by row count when rows stay under the byte budget` fails on base (1 transaction) and passes with the fix (3).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: clean. oxfmt and oxlint are clean on changed files.

<details>
<summary>Local environment notes</summary>

Run on native Windows with Node 26.13. Two Windows-only tooling problems unrelated to this change came up and were worked around, not fixed: TypeScript 7's native compiler mishandles Windows extended-length paths when a checkout path is 248+ characters (so the run used a short-path worktree), and `scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs` passes a `C:` path to `--import` (so the same preload was supplied through `NODE_OPTIONS`). The `vector` extension wasn't available, so the e2e used keyword-only memory, which the docs support on PostgreSQL. The export path changed here is the same in both search modes.
</details>

prs.title: fix(codex): let setup verify the standalone installer runtime
prs.body:
Related: #161720

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: verified setup and repair inference stops before Codex startup when the official standalone install contains its `codex -> bin/codex` link, even though ordinary agent turns can use the same runtime.

## User Impact

Users of the reported standalone layout can pass the runtime-artifact capture step without deleting a link that the installer recreates on every update. No configuration change or migration is required.

This is a **draft implementation**, not a merge-ready security approval. Codex/runtime-boundary review and the remaining validation below are still needed. Only the exact installer link is admitted; other package symlinks remain unsupported.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing verifier owns package attestation but rejected every symlink. It now recognizes only the package-root `codex` link with literal target `bin/codex`, requires its canonical target to be that regular file inside the package, and fingerprints the link alongside the already-hashed target bytes. Before/after link metadata checks reject replacement during hashing; existing startup revalidation, cancellation, no-follow file reads, and resource bounds remain in place.

This deliberately does not introduce generic symlink traversal, directory-link support, or a second verifier. It retains the existing before/after filesystem-check model rather than claiming an atomic snapshot against concurrent writers.

## Evidence

- **Base-red / fix-green:** the shared-client capture regression failed on base `0633f256350b5580a5bdbcd8a6a5782750de03d4` with the reported `unsupported entry: .../codex` error before app-server startup. The same caller path passes with this fix using a real temporary package tree and a synthetic transport. This is boundary integration proof, not a real model or desktop setup run.
- **Focused checks:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/runtime-artifact.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/shared-client.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-startup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **232 tests passed**. Coverage includes target-byte changes, link removal/replacement, rejected non-installer links, npm/Windows neighbors, and expected-artifact startup checks.
- **Targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.** Lint and formatting were rechecked after the interrupted review/restart; the retained source diff is unchanged.
- Personally inspected the [pinned upstream installer](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/064c6b8c737f5b41d171fdda80bd9ef10ad06eb3/scripts/install/install.sh#L946-L971), which creates this exact relative link. The sibling Codex checkout was not mounted, so the source inspection used that pinned upstream file directly. The macOS report, Linux duplicate #177663, and newer Linux report in #161720 were reviewed; no new user-machine reproduction is claimed. #134727 is a distinct, closed npm-launcher issue.
- **Review gap:** local Auto Review was launched against the complete local delta from the base above, then stalled and was interrupted by the Gateway restart without a report. No clean independent-review verdict or PATCH QUALITY score is claimed. Continuing the authorized draft under the current maintainer workflow’s review-timeout policy.
- **Typecheck gap:** direct `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/codex/tsconfig.json --noEmit` failed on workspace package/declaration resolution and package-boundary `rootDir` errors (including `@openclaw/normalization-core`); it is not a passing typecheck. Canonical extension production/test typechecks and broader CI remain outstanding. No full build, real-model setup/update-repair flow, or native macOS/Windows run was performed.
- **Simplification pass:** kept the existing verifier as the sole owner, with no generic traversal/helper framework. Production delta is +32/-5 lines; test delta is +93/-35 lines (+58 net, including formatting of the existing parameterized client test).

Reported and requested by Donniefi.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.
