prs.body:
## Current repair and validation status

Published head `1be335c060b0815f9d5bce4a3dc8c216830aa300` on repaired prerequisite `8c67ab5e26fc741768e84a1dfcaea0f94053d8d1`. **Selected-check CI completed at the root-reported 19:25:07Z snapshot: 30 successful checks, zero failures, 55 skipped, one cancelled, and no active checks; the aggregate CI gate succeeded.** This records the selected checks, not execution of every lane. Independent source and mapping review approved publication. This is fix-only work; no merge is authorized.

This PR remains stacked on [PR #198739](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198739), whose repaired head is not merged. Its GitHub base remains `test/reduce-million-lines-20261114`. This packet's own delta from old shared ancestor `10e4db504e396a36e1d61a4a0152a55e0eb159c0` is reapplied onto that repaired prerequisite. Its CLI and Workshop suites, catalog fixture, retired post-compaction owner and current-main changes remain intact.

## What Problem This Solves

Script tests repeat setup, equivalent input permutations and assertions covered by retained suites. This packet consolidates them while preserving explicit failure contracts and removing unused committed review metadata.

## User Impact

No production change. Relative to the repaired prerequisite: **32 test paths, +1,382/-2,268: 886 net lines removed**. Relative to the prerequisite's frozen main `aa4d490a848b4d96801fd7afcdea6cc01cc80d6e`, the cumulative stack is **74 paths, +4,137/-6,362: 2,225 net removed**. The stack count includes PR #198739, not an independent saving for this packet.

The README and twelve JSON manifests are no longer committed: **734 review-only lines removed from the old published packet**. Useful mappings appear below instead of in a new repository artifact. Restoring the direct parser cases costs 27 net test lines against the old packet without those manifests.

## Repairs and keepers

- `test/scripts/check-no-random-messaging-tmp.test.ts`: the selected-main `finds tmpdir named import calls from node:os` and `finds tmpdir calls imported from os` cases are restored, each checking actual parser output `[3]`, with the original parser creation and `afterAll` closure. Source: native main `869734209368313e7bcbc325ee72752fd2b57a71`; both complete case blocks match it exactly. The retained integration still checks all selected runtime roots, local functions, allowed plugin support, exact `:2` diagnostics and nonzero exit.
- `test/scripts/check-deadcode-exports.test.ts`: the only content conflict retains main's `models the workflow planner without retaining removed consumers` case, current async runtime-process export assertions and the neighboring consolidated Solid/Vite table. No new main assertion is discarded.
- `test/scripts/ios-release-prepare.test.ts` and `test/scripts/ios-release-signing.test.ts`: kept retired into `test/scripts/ios-release-wrapper-args.test.ts`, which retains preparation metadata, signing-team rejection and wrapper argument coverage.
- Both prerequisite CLI suites remain exact-main; its retired post-compaction suite stays absent with its removed owner.

## Evidence

Signed head `1be335c060b0815f9d5bce4a3dc8c216830aa300` has sole parent `8c67ab5e26fc741768e84a1dfcaea0f94053d8d1`. Normal hooks, targeted formatting, all 30 changed-file TypeScript syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed. Main-added nonblank lines in every overlap are retained. Removed manifest files have no executable consumers in the selected prerequisite; named keeper files survive. The only absent source references in those mappings are the two explicitly retired iOS suites and synthetic tmpdir fixture paths.

No dependency install, runtime test or typecheck ran locally; the native checkout has no dependency install. Root observed exact-head selected-check CI completion at 19:25:07Z: 30 successful checks, zero failures, 55 skipped, one cancelled and no active checks. The [aggregate CI gate succeeded](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43935503352/job/133549105636). Skipped and cancelled checks are not passing executions; this is not an all-lanes proof. This update uses the root-reported snapshot and performs no new CI poll. The unmerged PR #198739 prerequisite remains a separate gate; this PR remains open, ready and fix-only, with no merge authorized.

## Preserved coverage mappings

The following data moved from the twelve unused JSON files. Historical schema/validation/baseline fields are omitted. The two restored tmpdir cases are removed from retired-case records: each now keeps itself. Remaining mappings describe retained contracts, not fresh runtime proof.

<details>

prs.title: fix(models): models status and Doctor stay silent when provider catalog discovery fails
prs.body:
Related: #166875

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw models status` and Doctor say nothing when the Gateway has published a rejected or unavailable provider catalog discovery, so only `models list` explains why a provider's models are missing.

This is the status/Doctor part that #167128 left open. It is a partial fix for #166875: it does not change xAI catalog discovery or establish why the reported account was rejected.

## User Impact

User impact: `models status` and Doctor now name the provider (and profile, when known) whose catalog discovery was rejected or unavailable, with a retry step. Doctor shows rejected discovery by default and unavailable discovery with `--severity-min info`.

- `models status` prints one stderr line per rejected or unavailable provider/profile outcome. JSON stdout and the `--check` exit status are unchanged.
- Doctor's `core/doctor/model-references` check reports rejected discovery as a **warning** and unavailable discovery as **info** (shown with `--severity-min info`).
- Behavior change: at the default threshold, explicit `openclaw doctor --lint` exits 1 instead of 0 when a catalog rejection is published. Bare `openclaw doctor --json` still exits 0 but includes the new finding, and its `ok` field follows the same warning threshold (from `doctor-lint-runner.ts`; the live run already had other findings, so it does not show that transition). Update runs use `--severity-min error` and are not affected.
- `models list`: its two existing discovery hints now name the full command (`openclaw models list --refresh`) instead of `--refresh`, because the same text is now shown by status and Doctor. The generic "could not refresh all providers" line now prints after these hints. stdout is unchanged.
- With the Gateway stopped, status and Doctor have no prepared catalog to read, so the new diagnostics do not appear (existing documented behavior).
- The hint names the global refresh command; it does not carry `--agent` or `--provider`.
- No configuration, schema, protocol, discovery, credential, or model-availability change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already classifies each provider's catalog discovery as `ready`, `auth-rejected`, or `unavailable` and publishes the outcome. `models list` printed the non-ready outcomes with its own code (#167128), while `models status` and Doctor share `getModelCatalogWarnings` (#169708), which only handled `ready`. This change moves the two non-ready diagnostics into that shared helper and removes the list-only copy, so all three commands use one owner and one set of strings. The helper has no other callers.

Doctor maps unavailable discovery to info because offline local servers (Ollama, LM Studio) report `unavailable`, and the models docs already state that offline servers produce no missing-ID warning; a warning would turn the default lint red whenever a local server is off. Rejected discovery needs user action, so it is a warning, like the existing missing-model advisory.

Production **+17 / -13**, tests **+57 / -9** (net +48), docs **+6 / -1**. `docs/cli/models.md` and `docs/gateway/doctor/running.md` describe the new behavior. No changelog change.

<details>
<summary>Intentionally unchanged</summary>

- xAI catalog requests and account eligibility (the remaining part of #166875).
- Gateway logging for catalog failures.
- Producer-side publication of catalog outcomes; this PR only consumes published outcomes.
- `refreshFailed` semantics: rejection stays separate from the generic refresh warning.
- `models status --json` output, Control UI, and Android.
- No static catalog fallback.

</details>

## Evidence

- **Focused tests** (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`), re-run on the current head (this branch with main `176f2ff9652e` merged in): `src/flows/doctor-model-reference-check.test.ts` 5/5, `src/commands/models/list.status.test.ts` 25/25, `src/commands/models/list.prepared-catalog.test.ts` 15/15. Wall time on the dev host, including Vitest startup: 57 s, 23 s, and 28 s; Vitest reports 51.8 s, 18.4 s, and 24.0 s. For the Doctor file, 92% of that is cold transform and its tests take about 1 s; the case stays at the check boundary because a helper-only test cannot show that Doctor consumes the prepared Gateway catalog. In CI on the earlier head `eedbbae4` (run 42437743994) the same three files passed in 4.25 s, 8.45 s and 6.64 s of Vitest time (5.73 s, 9.89 s and 8.04 s for their Vitest shards).
- **Negative control** (on `12026082dc86`): with production files restored to base and the final tests kept, the extended Doctor case and the new status case fail (no rejected or unavailable finding; no stderr line). The list case also fails on base, but only because its expected wording changed; it is a guard that each diagnostic prints exactly once, not a reproduction of the original defect.
- **Targeted checks** (re-run on the current head): `oxfmt --check` passed on the eight changed code and docs files; `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` on the six changed TypeScript files reported 0 warnings and 0 errors; `pnpm lint:docs` (markdownlint) reported 0 issues; `git diff --check` produced no output. Typecheck passed: `pnpm tsgo:core` (15 s) and `pnpm tsgo:core:test --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-commands","core-test-other"]'` (both graphs, about 11 s each). `pnpm check:changed --base 176f2ff9652e` passed.
- **Test-line budget**: this PR adds 48 net test lines (the new status and Doctor coverage and the list exactly-once guard), within the 400-line allowance of the current `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` (#197602). On the current head against main `176f2ff9652e`: `Test lines OK. Net test lines: +48; allowance: 400; allocation credit: 0.` The allocation record this PR first added (`config/test-lines-allocations/catalog-discovery-status-doctor-166875.txt`, allocating 48 test lines) is not needed under that rule and has been removed.
- **Real CLI and Gateway proof**: the built CLI entry (`openclaw.mjs`) and a real Gateway ran with an isolated `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (the config file lives in that state directory), channels disabled, on loopback, against a synthetic local LM Studio catalog server that returned 401, 403, 500, or 200 on demand. No credentials were configured, the setup used no external service, and per-command socket samples showed no non-loopback connections. LM Studio's catalog discovery goes through the same outcome owner as xAI's; this change only consumes published outcomes, so it does not depend on the provider.
  - Before the fix (base build): for 401, 403, and 500, `models status` printed no discovery diagnostic, and `doctor --lint --only core/doctor/model-references` reported no finding and exited 0. In the 200 mode, a configured model absent from the listing produced the existing missing-model warning in both `models status` and Doctor, confirming that both read the prepared catalog. The Gateway retried rejected discovery on its own about 30 and 90 seconds later; a separate probe confirmed these requests came from the Gateway, not from status or Doctor reads.
  - After the fix (same isolated setup, rebuilt from this patch): for 401 and 403, `models status` printed exactly one `Model discovery authentication was rejected for lmstudio. …` line, and `doctor --lint --only core/doctor/model-references` reported one warning with target `lmstudio` and exited 1. For 500, status printed the matching `Model discovery is unavailable for lmstudio. …` line; Doctor reported it as info, so the default lint exited 0 and the finding appeared with `--severity-min info`. In the 200 modes the existing missing-model warning was unchanged, `models status --json` stdout kept the same keys, and `models list` printed each hint once with the new wording. With `--agent work`, status read that agent's own prepared catalog, which still held its last successful listing (the refreshes ran for the default agent), so it showed the missing-model warning rather than the rejection.
  - Catalog request counts: each mode's `--refresh` made one catalog request. The status, Doctor, and RPC reads that followed made none, except one Doctor read in the rejected mode whose window caught the Gateway's second self-initiated retry (30 s and then 60 s after the rejected refresh, the same schedule as before the fix).
  - Revision: base `12026082dc86` with this PR's patch applied; commit `eedbbae4da93` on this branch has the same file contents. The current head merges main into that commit and removes the allocation record; the focused tests and targeted checks above were re-run on it.
  - An upgrade from the installed latest-stable npm package to this build, on the same state directory, is covered under **Latest-stable upgrade proof**; it does not exercise the stable package's own updater, a package-to-package replacement, or a stable-package Gateway, and neither run uses an xAI account or real credentials.
- **Latest-stable upgrade proof**: the exact npm release `openclaw@2026.11.2` (`OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (b556fdf)`; npm `latest` in the registry queries at 2026-11-09T09:47:24Z before install and 09:47:59Z after install) wrote settings and a second agent into an isolated state directory; the patched build's existing `doctor --fix --non-interactive` migrated that state; then the patched Gateway served it against the same synthetic LM Studio catalog server. The 401, 500 and 200 modes gave the same status and Doctor results as above, and the provider URL, default model, system agent, catalog-refresh and memory-search settings and the agent list read back unchanged across the upgrade and the Gateway run.
  - Stable side: the stable package was installed into an isolated prefix. A minimal loopback Gateway section (mode, bind, port, token auth, log file) was written first into an isolated `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; the stable CLI, run with that same isolated environment, then wrote the remaining settings (LM Studio provider URL, default model, system agent, catalog refresh and memory search turned off) and added the `work` agent with its workspace, which also recorded `main` as the default agent. The stable package ran only non-Gateway commands; its `models status` and focused Doctor ran with the Gateway stopped, and neither changed discovery diagnostic appeared in their output.
  - Migration: the stable CLI had written `agents.defaults.heartbeat`, which current main has retired; this PR does not touch it. In an earlier attempt, on state written by 2026.11.1, the patched Gateway refused to start on it; in this run the patched `openclaw config validate --json` reported the configuration invalid for that key. With the Gateway stopped we ran the patched build's `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` (an existing migration, unrelated to this PR) with `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external`, the setting the updater uses for its own doctor run (`src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrate.ts`), and with the service-manager commands on `PATH` replaced by stubs that log each call, do nothing and exit non-zero; one read-only `busctl` name lookup was logged, and doctor exited 0. It removed the retired key; added migration markers, run stamps and `enabled` keys for the `lmstudio` plugin and for three skills (`openai-whisper-api`, `sherpa-onnx-tts`, `trello`); changed the state database and the `work` agent database, keeping its own backups next to them; created the local client database; and wrote a pre-repair capture. The full list is in the details below. No configuration key that existed before the migration was changed, apart from the retired `agents.defaults.heartbeat` and the writer-managed stamp `meta.lastTouchedVersion`, which the config writer sets to the running build's version (`src/config/io.meta.ts`), so here main's 2026.11.1. Afterwards `openclaw config validate --json` reported the configuration valid, the workspace files were unchanged, and the patched CLI read back the same provider URL, system agent, default model, catalog-refresh and memory-search values and the same agent ids, workspaces and models (`agents list --json`) as the stable CLI had.
  - Patched Gateway: the Gateway was then started for the first time, from the patched build (base `12026082dc86` plus this PR's changes, same file contents as commit `eedbbae4da93`), which reports `OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (1202608)`: 2026.11.1 and 2026.11.2 were cut from a release branch forked from main, and main at this commit still carries the 2026.11.1 version string, so the version string does not indicate a downgrade. The loaded `dist/` tree and entry file were identical at the start of the run, before and after the migration, and before the Gateway started. A 200 refresh kept the existing missing-model warning for `lmstudio/fixture-absent`. A 401 refresh produced `auth-rejected`: `models status` printed the rejected-discovery line exactly once, and `doctor --lint --only core/doctor/model-references` reported one warning for `lmstudio` and exited 1. A 500 refresh produced `unavailable`: status printed the unavailable line exactly once, the default Doctor threshold did not report it, and `--severity-min info` reported one info finding for `lmstudio`. Each refresh made one catalog request. Before each mode's status and Doctor reads we waited at least 95 s after the applicable reference (Gateway start for 200, completion of the failed refresh for 401 and 500) and observed 35 s without a catalog request; those waits saw 1, 2 and 0 catalog requests (200, 401 and 500 modes) while no CLI command was running, and the status and Doctor reads themselves made none.
  - Settings and data across the Gateway run: the configuration file was byte-identical right after the migration and after the patched Gateway stopped, and 80 files and directories present before the Gateway first started, including the `work` workspace files, were unchanged. 4 SQLite database files (the state database and the `work` agent database with its WAL and shared-memory files) changed during the patched phase and were not byte-compared; instead, after the Gateway stopped the patched CLI read back the same agent ids, workspaces and models from `agents list --json`, and the same agent entries, provider URL, system agent, default model, catalog-refresh and memory-search values as right after the migration. No provider credentials were configured, CLI output contained no synthetic response body, and connection samples of the test processes showed no non-loopback peer.
  - Not covered: the stable package's own updater (`openclaw update`) was not used (the migration ran the patched build's `doctor --fix`), and the stable package never started a Gateway. SQLite files were not byte-compared; only the listed semantic readbacks were gated, and the automation list after migration (`cron list`) was recorded but not checked. The values of the keys doctor added or changed and the contents of the databases and the capture it wrote were not inspected.
- **Local review**: autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2, one pass) of this patch against `12026082dc86` reported `scoped-clean` with no actionable findings.
- **CI**: CI on head `8cc37ddb5e55` is waiting for workflow approval. On the earlier head `eedbbae4` (run 42437743994), `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failed under the previous whole-tree ceiling, which main itself exceeded at the time (run 42437701964 for another PR on the same base); #197602 replaced that ceiling with a per-PR allowance, and this branch merged main to pick it up.

<summary>Live commands</summary>

prs.body:
## Current repair and validation status

Published head `8c67ab5e26fc741768e84a1dfcaea0f94053d8d1` on frozen main `aa4d490a848b4d96801fd7afcdea6cc01cc80d6e`. **CI snapshot at 19:18:30Z: 66 successful checks, 68 skipped, one neutral and three failures; no active checks. CI is not green.** Independent source review approved this repair for publication. This remains fix-only and open for Vincent's review; it is not a merge request or a claim of green CI.

The actual failing test is `ui/src/e2e/chat-send-ack-ownership.e2e.test.ts:77`: `locator.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded` encountered `Element is not attached to the DOM` in [UI E2E 1/2 job 133536194940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43934378634/job/133536194940). The other two failures are aggregate CI gates: [job 133543839762](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43934378634/job/133543839762) and [run 43936950902](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43936950902). The retained test's static source/config/helper closure is unchanged against `aa4d490a848b4d96801fd7afcdea6cc01cc80d6e`; no deletion-caused dependency or justified restoration was identified. Runtime causality remains **UNKNOWN**: no matching main execution proves inheritance. The requested fixes are published, but the failure is unresolved. This records the root-reported scheduled snapshot, not a new CI poll.

This refresh preserves main's automatic overlap changes and restores both CLI suites exactly from that main revision:

- `src/cli/program/command-registry.test.ts`: grouped lazy registration is exercised through real `parseAsync`, including no duplicate commands and secondary command-name loading.
- `src/cli/program/command-tree.test.ts`: missing names return `false` without removing an existing sibling, alongside name and alias removal.

Main retired `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/post-compaction-loop-guard.test.ts` and its production owner in `3a3eed8695e68e182c4851285a3de90ca2cba0ff`, replacing result-sensitive loop detection with the arguments-only repeat guard. The refresh preserves that deletion; it does not restore the obsolete owner or claim its five-line historical consolidation as a current saving.

The stale WebKit selector for the deleted legacy ModelPicker suite is removed. The retained Solid ModelPicker suite remains selected by the existing `src/components/solid/*.browser.test.tsx` pattern.

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated test setup and overlapping assertions add maintenance cost across CI tooling, agents, gateway, plugins and UI. This preliminary packet consolidates those fixtures while retaining distinct CLI registration and missing-command contracts.

## User Impact

Internal test/support cleanup only. Against frozen main `aa4d490a848b4d96801fd7afcdea6cc01cc80d6e`, the published head adds **2,752** and removes **4,091** lines across **44 paths**: **1,339 net lines removed** (**6,843 gross changed lines**). Production delta is **0**. Four whole-file retirements remove 912 lines; the two CLI suites are retained, not counted as retirements. The original published `5c489a3f` count was 1,470 net lines against its historical `fa40e292` baseline and is not the current diff.

## Why This Change Was Made

Repeated fixtures and equivalent cases share helpers or table rows, with covering suites retained. This preliminary packet has no separate deletion manifest: its actual diff and the four-file coverage map below define its retirement scope. Later campaign manifests do not apply retroactively. Four stale entries in `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` are removed because their mock factories moved from `index.test.ts` into the annotated catalog fixture. No production algorithm or runtime configuration changes are included.

## Evidence

- Signed published head: `8c67ab5e26fc741768e84a1dfcaea0f94053d8d1`; sole parent `aa4d490a848b4d96801fd7afcdea6cc01cc80d6e`.
- Normal repository commit hooks completed successfully, including formatting of 39 source/config files. The targeted pre-commit format check and 36 TypeScript syntax checks passed; the additional UI config syntax/format check and `git diff --check` passed.
- Both CLI files are byte-identical to frozen main. All newly added nonblank main lines in overlapping test files are preserved. The four remaining deleted paths have no surviving exact executable import or selector reference; their named keepers exist.
- No dependency installation, runtime test, typecheck, fresh CI or new main replay ran during this local preparation. The native checkout has no dependency installation; runtime validation remains pending.
- The catalog synthesis mock remains intentionally retained to preserve the existing cold-owner TTS fixture. Prior native cancellation and catalog experiment results below are historical evidence on their recorded source revisions, not validation of this new head.

## Current Coverage Map

| Retired file | Retained owner coverage |
| --- | --- |
| `src/commands/agents.list.dep-warning.test.ts` | `src/commands/channels.list.dep-warning.test.ts`: real agents-list row, asynchronous authentication marker and absence of `DEP_PLUGIN_SDK` warning. |
| `ui/src/components/model-picker.browser.test.tsx` | `ui/src/components/solid/model-picker.browser.test.tsx`: the same ModelPicker/select-picker owner, disabled groups, catalog, unknown model, tooltip and custom-model rows. |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer-height.browser.test.tsx` | `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer-layout.browser.test.tsx`: content-sized height through the same rendering and overflow owner. |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer-width.browser.test.tsx` | `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-composer-layout.browser.test.tsx`: border-width controls through the same width-edge owner. |

| Retained file | Preservation reason |
| --- | --- |
| `src/cli/program/command-registry.test.ts` | Exact-main self-keeper for real grouped `parseAsync` and secondary-name lazy registration. |
| `src/cli/program/command-tree.test.ts` | Exact-main self-keeper for the missing-name `false` result and unchanged sibling. |

The composer layout keeper was created by this packet (659 lines); it is not described as a pre-existing keeper. The Workshop suite remains present; its previous retirement/transfer claim is withdrawn. Other changes consolidate partial test files and fixture setup, not additional whole-file retirements.

## Historical native cancellation and catalog evidence

The following records belong to the original published head and its explicitly recorded bases. References to an actual or then-current main identify those historical SHAs; they do not classify a future CI failure on the published head.

**Validated against the then-current-main baseline for the sole executed failure; raw CI and the required gate remain RED.** [Run 43610042885, attempt 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/attempts/3) reran only the failed large-16 job. [Job 132513350800](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132513350800) again executed the 14-case native-control file: **10 passed and the same four cancellation rows failed**; [aggregate gate 132515407749](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132515407749) failed. The checkout was again `c410968c` (base `20cb257f` plus this head), with the same failure payload, stack and runtime.

The three observed PR-native failures are [the original 299b36e7 run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43582240086/job/132409626919), [this head's attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132507684218), and [the targeted attempt 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132513350800). A separately executed, independently reviewed then-current-main proof now confirms the same failure on [main `d867f1791447e20904bfc2d39c43b1616311035b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d867f1791447e20904bfc2d39c43b1616311035b). Native RUN 13687 ran only `src/gateway/talk/handlers/client-native-control.test.ts`, using the original `gateway-database-workers` isolated group, inner parallelism 1 and no case filter: **14 tests, 10 passed, the same four cancellation rows failed, exit 1** (68.62s test duration). The exact source HEAD and lock hash matched before and after execution; Node `24.22.1` and Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1` matched the PR run. Independent review read the native command, metadata, timing and automatic stdout; stdout SHA256: `89830d6fde9f8044fcc2149bb2f544d5e267dfc44d63e1f01b11639856caf4e8`.

The matching cancellation suffixes are `transcript-first, rejection`, `delegation-first, rejection`, `transcript-first, empty` and `delegation-first, partial`. Each again expected `Real runner consultation completed.` and received `I need a moment to verify that before answering.`, at test `474:78` / support `316:9`. This is **executed then-current-main failure proof**, alongside the [existing actual-base CI proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610133604/job/132493534359) below. The [native provisioning workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43617502605) is a launcher only, not the test result.

The sole executed PR failure is therefore **pre-existing on both its actual CI base and the freshly resolved then-current main**. This establishes baseline equivalence for that failure, not a green required gate, full-suite main success or a flaky passing result. No deletion-caused failure was identified; no restoration or further PR retry is justified by this evidence.

**Catalog mock retention.** The three lines at `src/gateway/talk/handlers/catalog.test-support.ts:76–78` intentionally restore the direct `tts-synthesis` mock, its isolation comment and spacing. The retained cold-owner TTS case in `index.test.ts:327` sets `providerMocks.synthesizeSpeech` at line 388 and checks its call at line 415. Removing that mock in `cb1f` caused an observed zero-call failure in [job 132457376704](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43598130392/job/132457376704); `794fa6` restored it. The native-control file has no import path to this helper. This is intentional fixture wiring, not a claim of a literal byte-for-byte main revert.

**Earlier attempt-2 result: FAILURE.** [Run 43610042885, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/attempts/2) completed with **45 successful jobs, two failed jobs, 27 skipped jobs and zero active jobs**. The failed jobs are [changed-compact-large-16](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132507684218) and its [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132510898410). The sole executed test failure is the four native cancellation rows described below. All UI shards and changed-compact-large-3 passed.

**Raw CI remains RED; the sole executed failure is baseline-equivalent** at historical head `5c489a3fa321a4269ccd94c24e3a75e8ddd74bf4`. On [CI attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/attempts/2), [changed-compact-large-16, job 132507684218](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132507684218) actually executed `src/gateway/talk/handlers/client-native-control.test.ts`: **14 tests, 10 passed and four native cancellation rows failed**. The tested checkout was merge `c410968c` into base `20cb257f`; this is an executed test failure, not a runner-admission failure.

Historical source-boundary review of the 46 changed paths from base `20cb257f` to tested merge `c410968c` found no changes to the failing process's runner, config, setup, test or native fixtures. The group runs `client-native-control.test.ts` alone in a fresh Bun child. The changed Talk support, `catalog.test-support.ts`, is imported only by the catalog/index tests; neither is selected in that child. This source comparison is complemented by the executed same-base result below.

Existing CI on the actual base `20cb257f` also executed the target file: [main job 132493534359 in run 43610133604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610133604/job/132493534359) recorded **14 tests, 10 passed and the same four cancellation rows failed**. Independent review matched the four case suffixes, expected/actual speakable fallback payload, assertion locations `474:78` and support `316:9`, Node `24.22.1`, and Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`. Main checked out `20cb257f` directly; the PR tested merge `c410968c`, whose parents are that base and this PR head.

The main assertions failed **before that job was later cancelled**. This is executed same-base failure evidence, not a successful main job or full-main validation claim. The PR's sole executed test failure is therefore **confirmed pre-existing on its actual CI base**. The PR and required CI gate remain **RED**. No deletion-caused failure was identified, and no restoration or additional CI action is warranted by this result.

Earlier attempt 1 quota failures in [large-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132493405528) and [large-16](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43610042885/job/132493405391) occurred before checkout/tests at the 10,080-start limit. Those are historical admission failures. The earlier job-specific retry request was rejected while the workflow was active; it admitted no new attempt. The user subsequently started attempt 2. Skipped jobs remain outside execution proof; this attempt has no active jobs.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198737

## Other historical validation evidence

Catalog-only CI experiment and repair: `cb1f1508758b30c1c3d0a4f3a5c4859458781a26` restored only the exact frozen `06bfea7` catalog preimage. Its [node-large-15 job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43598130392/job/132457376704) failed on `src/gateway/talk/handlers/index.test.ts` → `talk.speak handler` → `uses the runtime snapshot with cold owner tts`: **84 passed, 1 failed**, `Expected mock call 0` at `index.test.ts:415:26`. The job tested merge `9fd214f29d603117955ada5465fa3c1a5a31504d` into main `13900faa92e1e5e33860ea7a8690d93b444c88d5`. It stopped before the native 14-case group; this run does **not** establish a native cancellation result.

Signed repair `794fa6bdb18ebb2d5fe960ae420ce825e2153ccf` restores only the three annotated synthesis-mock lines in `catalog.test-support.ts`. Independent source review verified that the mock feeds the exact spy used by the failing index case; the complete tree is byte-identical to the earlier `10e4db5` tree. Earlier head `794fa6b` [automatic CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43600220141) has a [script-types failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43600220141/job/132463985346): `scripts/perf/state-read-worker-bench.ts(373,52)` reports TS18048, `entry.tasksCompleted` is possibly undefined. The job tested merge `b1b0b83572eda12a1818913d24f3d5bc7671c6af` of this head into main `7bccde609cbb0eaa054ac07a6d5ccd91ec712a92`. Exact-ref source comparison confirms that the benchmark, diagnostic type and worker owner are byte-identical on both the tested merge and its actual main base. Main commit `d8b6c2838082cca7054fafd47c280051897e0e77` (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198866) made `workerTaskMetrics.tasksCompleted` optional; the unchanged benchmark still sums it without narrowing. GitHub ancestry confirms that commit is in actual base `7bccde609cbb0eaa054ac07a6d5ccd91ec712a92` (two commits ahead, zero behind). The matching blob IDs are benchmark `5442f57315c67a03aa38e41891086da19a495836`, diagnostic type `5c0685a58618377f416e1bce98eb57bf354b261c`, and worker owner `be0892deee832cc769176ba9d1fcd435a461b2ef`. This is a deterministic inherited-main type-contract failure supported by exact source and ancestry, **not a separately executed main typecheck**. Follow-up outside this test-only campaign: the benchmark consumer must narrow pool-only numeric task metrics before summing them; broker metrics deliberately omit this field. No source fix or green result is claimed.

Additional failures on earlier head `794fa6b` observed in run `43600220141`: the [baseline-ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43600220141/job/132463634589) reports a closed `../logging/subsystem.js` mock at `src/infra/worker-idle-gc.test.ts:13`; the [changed-Node job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43600220141/job/132463635025) fails the worker import budget with `agents/identity-file.worker.js: 240 evaluated modules exceeds budget 220`, at `scripts/check-worker-module-budget.mjs:57:9` via `scripts/check-cli-bootstrap-imports.mts:595:5`. Exact-ref source review confirms the logger violation is inherited: actual main base `7bccde609cbb0eaa054ac07a6d5ccd91ec712a92` and tested merge `b1b0b83572eda12a1818913d24f3d5bc7671c6af` have identical test blob `288108c099d660e558eaeb97f4673d47cd2cdc40` and guard blob `5dc9352c64faaea3e743574000129694e50504cf`. Line 13 is the closed mock and line 12 is blank; neither current baseline contains an allowance for this test. The guard scans all current factories, independent of the changed-file base. This is deterministic source proof, not a separately executed main guard result.

The worker-budget review found main-side source growth: main commit `1b3e37b7c6f` adds an eager subsystem logger import/construction in `src/infra/worker-idle-gc.ts`, reachable through identity worker → worker task server → idle GC. This campaign changes no production, build, dependency or budget-guard code on that path. The observed result remains **240 modules versus the unchanged budget of 220**. No main module census was executed and the exact 20-module increase has not been causally measured; no reproduced-main budget failure or green result is claimed. The follow-up belongs to the main-side worker import graph and requires its own proof; retain the 220 budget and do not compensate with a campaign test change. This Node failure is a budget guard, not evidence that the native-control test ran. No source repair is included.

The experiment run also has an inherited-main [baseline-ratchet failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43598130392/job/132457376515): `src/infra/worker-idle-gc.test.ts:13` closes the `../logging/subsystem.js` mock without export preservation or an isolation annotation. Main commit `1b3e37b7c6f` (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198857) introduced it; it is present on actual base `13900faa` and absent from this PR branch. The guard scans all tracked factories; `--base` does not limit it to changed files. Independent source review establishes a pre-existing main guard violation, **not a separately executed main CI reproduction**. No branch repair is applied for that main-only mock. Raw historical failures remain recorded; queued/skipped work is not a pass.

Prior catalog-only counterfactual: diagnostic `2632be5e62480d7e3424873f5a1c9918d54b9c47` replaced only `src/gateway/talk/handlers/catalog.test-support.ts` with its exact frozen `06bfea7` bytes. Independent review verified the sole-file diff, catalog hash, and native RUN 26070 receipt. The complete 14-case native-control file ran on Node 24.22.1 / Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1: **10 passed, the same four cancellation cases failed, exit 1** (88.87s). Line 474 again expected `Real runner consultation completed.` and received `I need a moment to verify that before answering.` Comparison to the earlier PR/main results uses their previously independently verified records; the old main capture had already been disposed after review.

The earlier diagnostic rollback did not improve the failure and was not pushed; that diagnostic checkout was restored byte-for-byte to `10e4db5`. The separate signed `cb1f150` commit now publishes the same catalog-only preimage for the explicitly requested CI experiment. [Workflow 43596561909](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43596561909) provisioned the diagnostic runner only and is **not a CI test result**. Actual test evidence is the independently reviewed native execution receipt. Prior exact-head CI remains **RED**; the new push-triggered run is pending. No manual full-workflow dispatch, old-head rerun, or successful validation is claimed.


**Historical CI status (head `794fa6b`): RED: source-proven inherited-main script-types and closed-logging-mock failures, plus the observed 240/220 worker import-budget failure with main-side source growth identified but no executed-main census. The catalog-only experiment failed an index case before the native group. The four earlier native cancellation failures were independently reproduced on pinned main.** Attempt 1 of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43591273159 failed [changed-compact-large-15](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43591273159/job/132436744396) and [the aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43591273159/job/132440021093). The gate's sole failed dependency was that Node shard; its failure classifier listed only this job. The repaired guard, baseline, lint and other selected jobs passed. Raw CI remains red, not green or fully validated. The single job-specific [attempt-2 rerun](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43591273159/job/132443542444) also failed: the same 14-case native file executed, 10 passed and the identical four cancellation cases failed. The [attempt-2 aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43591273159/job/132446326107) also completed with failure. No further rerun is planned; the independent main reproduction establishes the shared defect.

An independently verified native execution (`RUN63731`) on exact main `18892937f80232a5f7159092e264fb9e44ad6a10` reproduced the same four failures with Node 24.22.1 and Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`. It used the original `agentic-gateway-server-isolated-hosted-5` group, `test/vitest/vitest.gateway-database-workers.config.ts`, and the single included `src/gateway/talk/handlers/client-native-control.test.ts`. Source SHA, lock hash, Bun revision and the failure-name set were independently checked against the original CI receipt. Privacy-safe result excerpt:

```text
main: 18892937f80232a5f7159092e264fb9e44ad6a10
native execution: RUN63731; one group planned, one completed
```

prs.title: fix: accept follow-up chat messages after the previous run finishes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A follow-up message can be rejected when the previous run finishes between input preparation and admission. Preparation retained the old lifecycle, and the first repair refreshed it only on the durable backend; in-memory sessions still had the same race.

## User Impact

Follow-ups use the current session lifecycle on both durable and in-memory sessions. Explicit caller guards, restart recovery, queued-input ownership, and released-actor refusals remain strict. No configuration, schema, permission, or migration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select implicit lifecycle state inside the shared actor transaction, where both backends own ordering. Remove the three preparation-time lifecycle copies and the redundant input snapshot wrapper. A direct admission check preserves the existing typed custody refusal if the actor closes during preparation, so the failure cannot release accepted input to another fallback.

This extends RomneyDa's original fix and regression in this PR, preserving the contributor commits and credit. The final change removes **27 production lines**; tests are counted separately. The Gateway regression now covers stop, resume, then a follow-up after normal completion through a real Gateway and agent with a local HTTP provider.

## Evidence

- Candidate: `b63d1954ef06a192672a905687d0ac564c59d7d3`; frozen integration base: `cd2ae19272a3ee7be456385fa7efc56d6e2109a6`.
- Matching oxfmt 0.74.0 formatting, Node syntax checks, and `git diff --check` passed on the changed files.
- Independent source review and local Codex autoreview completed for the production change at `d87755b1e5399dbad2654fc4f4186facffbc4e5a`, P0–P3, with no actionable findings. The subsequent two-test fixture narrowing has its own independent source review; production is unchanged. The reviewer checked full shared-phase and backend context, including explicit guards, empty completion, custody classification, and receipts. Runtime proof is separate.
- Added durable accept/adopt completion regressions, an in-memory completion regression, and a real queued-input release regression that checks terminal failure classification, retained custody, and zero append.
- Completed Bun checks on final head `b63d1954ef06a192672a905687d0ac564c59d7d3`: memory (9 tests), input concurrency (12), source custody (19), and resident sessions (10) passed. See [memory](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44584535707/job/135775323188), [concurrency](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44584535707/job/135775323154), and [custody/resident](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44584535707/job/135775322970). All production and test typecheck jobs also passed, including the [previously failing shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44584535707/job/135777229835).
- [Real Gateway regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44584535707/job/135775322986) passed in 21.111 seconds: a real Gateway and agent, local HTTP provider, native chat.send, stop, resume, then a third follow-up after normal completion. No external model or live channel was used.


- Aggregate checks are tracked in [current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44584535707). Focused behavior tests, all typechecks, build, and lint passed on the final head. A focused [Testbox attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44581769229) timed out during hydration under the one-minute admission limit, before running any test. Its allocation was stopped. The local task checkout has no qualified runtime dependency install; no local runtime pass is claimed.

The previous local autoreview's concern about empty memory completion was checked against the full phase owner: empty completion explicitly applies its terminal patch before installing state. The final review includes that source and has no findings.

prs.title: fix(update): bridge 2026.11.6 and 2026.11.10-beta.1 updaters
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two OpenClaw releases shipped on 2026-11-19: `2026.11.10-beta.1` on the `beta` channel and `2026.11.6` as `latest`. When their built-in updaters install a newer build, that build needs update bridge files for them, and main doesn't have them yet. On main, `pnpm update:compat:check` fails with "inventory is missing current npm release versions", and updates from these two releases would run without the compatibility bridge every other recent release gets.

## User Impact

People on stable 2026.11.6 or beta 2026.11.10-beta.1 can update to the next build from main with the same compatibility bridge as earlier releases. Nobody needs to do anything.

## Why This Change Was Made

`scripts/lib/update-compat-inventory.json` lists every published release whose updater a new build must bridge. This regenerates it with `pnpm update:compat:gen` over the full registry window: the 32 existing versions plus the two new ones. It follows the same shape as #201309, which added 2026.10.33.

- The diff is additions only (+4225/-0), and all 32 existing entries are byte-identical.
- `2026.11.6`: 78 chunks, commit `06afb10d327`, schemas state 36 / agent 38.
- `2026.11.10-beta.1`: 94 chunks, commit `995f9059b6e`, schemas state 40 / agent 42.
- Both integrities match `npm view openclaw@<version> dist.integrity`.

## Evidence

On Crabbox AWS, at main `6502a5769c0`, after `pnpm install` and `pnpm build`:

- `node scripts/update-compat-inventory.mts --check` fails on base with the missing-release error, and passes after regeneration.
- Installed-tree entries (npm 12 global install of the packed build): base 47,064, with this change 47,205 (+141). That is 295 under the 47,500 soft budget, and the installed-package budget check passes.

Reviews:

- `autoreview` came back scoped-clean at P2.
- An independent `codex exec` review of `e10844ee86c` found nothing.

prs.title: improve(sqlite): distinguish slow transaction completion phases
prs.body:
Related: #183802

## What Problem This Solves

Slow SQLite transaction logs cannot reliably pair a COMMIT step with its transaction hold or distinguish commit preparation from the elapsed COMMIT call.

## User Impact

Operators can correlate slow transaction records without adding session IDs, SQL parameters, or message content, and see which completion boundary needs profiling. This is a diagnostic improvement, **not a fix for the reported 35–61-second stalls**; the incident cause and current-upstream recurrence remain unproven. No durability, admission, schema, busy-timeout, or retention policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing transaction owner gives each outer transaction a random correlation ID shared by BEGIN/COMMIT steps, lock failures, and slow holds. Slow holds report raw `prepareCommitMs` and `nativeCommitMs`, including failed attempts. The latter measures `db.exec("COMMIT")`, including connection wrappers, metadata admission, and scheduling—not isolated SQLite engine or storage time. Existing `commitMs` accounting remains unchanged; it subtracts metadata admission and includes step logging. Post-commit publication remains outside the measured wrapper.

The existing shared label/step logging code moves to a small diagnostics module to keep the transaction executor within its production line limit; there is no new state owner, logging framework, or persistence. The simplification pass removes duplicate success/failure step-reporting logic. Net change: +44 production lines, +76 test lines, +16 documentation lines, and one required wrapper inventory entry.

## Evidence

### Actual shipped CLI: correlated slow BEGIN and hold — passed

The unchanged built product CLI imported **40,001 transcript events** from an **8,026,783-byte** synthetic legacy transcript in a task-owned profile:

```bash
pnpm openclaw --profile issue183802-import doctor --session-sqlite import \
  --session-sqlite-store <owned-state>/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json --json
```

An external native SQLite connection held `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` for 4,000 ms after observing the CLI’s migration spool. The production agent connection retained its existing **5,000 ms busy timeout**, WAL policy, warning thresholds, and synchronous settlement. No source hook, mocked clock, `db.exec` interposer, durability change, or timeout override was used. The CLI exited **0**, reported 40,001 imported events and zero issues, archived its verified inputs, and passed integrity checking. A separate shipped `doctor --session-sqlite inspect --session-sqlite-store <owned-agent.sqlite> --json` invocation independently reported the persisted 40,001 events and `integrityCheck: ok`.

Sanitized records from the actual product file logger share the same transaction ID:

```json
{"message":"slow SQLite transaction step","operation":"session.import.batch","step":"begin","transactionId":"4fc6bb62-44cd-497b-8e53-a6d9d11df991","elapsedMs":3431,"busyTimeoutMs":5000,"beginAdmission":{"nativeAttempts":1,"nativeMs":3431,"serviceCalls":0,"serviceMs":0}}
{"message":"slow SQLite transaction hold","operation":"session.import.batch","transactionId":"4fc6bb62-44cd-497b-8e53-a6d9d11df991","elapsedMs":1742,"phases":{"prepareMs":2,"beginMs":3431,"sqlMs":1723,"hostAdmissionWaitMs":0,"databaseAdmissionWaitMs":0,"commitMs":19,"prepareCommitMs":0,"nativeCommitMs":19}}
```

This proves shipped-entry-point correlation and completion fields during **controlled BEGIN contention plus a bounded multi-row callback**, not a slow COMMIT or a recurrence of the reported 35–61-second incident. The native COMMIT-call time here was 19 ms. All fixture processes and locks were released.

### Regression, build, CI, and review

- Three new native-backed diagnostic cases fail on base because correlation/phase fields are absent, then pass with the change. Transaction diagnostics, transaction safety, and post-commit suites: **52 passed** with `--maxWorkers=1` (3.43 s runner / 2.27 s Vitest). Metadata-relay coverage preserves legacy `commitMs=3` with `databaseAdmissionWaitMs=1000` and raw `nativeCommitMs=1003`.
- Full cold-read consumer suite: **11 passed** (13.32 s runner / 11.17 s Vitest). Wrapper source-closure and eager-import inventory checks pass. Existing concurrent transcript test passes: eight requests settle to one durable idempotent message. Targeted types/lint/format and `git diff --check` pass.
- The authorized `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime` completed exit 0 in **53.0 s**, with normal repository capacity/admission gates. It was not rebuilt for these probes. The entire tracked working tree matches published head `ba2ce18aa725a230a0cc557d8c2b041b03adb195`. The managed guest carrier remains `c232d504`; the unedited dirty-input build stamp records signature `5cda4bb5211e3e608373eca493352390759a8a7ea837e7cc10484fba492c9a8f`.
- **Required exact-head CI is green:** [complete aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43574493099/job/132392924213), every selected dependency successful including PostgreSQL conformance, no known-main-red exception; [security-sensitive and dependency gates](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43576887998) also pass. The bounded PR rollup is truncated; the complete exact-head gate log establishes this result.
- [Completed substantive ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198735#issuecomment-6874308825) covers this head with **no actionable findings** and both prior P1/P2 findings resolved. The subsequent review of the shipped Doctor evidence is also **complete** and explicitly concludes: “Sufficient (logs)”—matching IDs, both completion fields, independent persisted-event counts, and integrity readback. It reports **no actionable correctness or security findings**. The [latest re-review receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198735#issuecomment-6875368255) confirms completion; the original long-COMMIT incident remains outside this diagnostic proof. Local autoreview of the six-file candidate against `06bfea7a5706b8ece40663b878ce839473fa1ea9` was P0-only scoped-clean; it is not a substitute for substantive hosted review.

<details>
<summary>Retained negative control and supplemental native proof</summary>

The first shipped `database restore-migration-backup` probe used a native reader on a task-owned rollback-journal database. Its connection opens without a timeout option or busy-timeout setup, so COMMIT returned `SQLITE_BUSY` immediately (`elapsedMs=0`), rolled back safely, and emitted no slow hold. After the reader released, the same CLI restore succeeded, preserving unrelated data and integrity. This was a negative reproduction, not a permission or build blocker.

A separate native-owner harness produced a matching COMMIT-step/hold pair (1,236 / 1,246 ms); it remains supplemental, not shipped-entry-point proof. The initial 20,001-event import control succeeded but its observer did not acquire contention and it emitted no transaction hold; it is not credited as the paired proof. The bounded contended run above corrected owned-process discovery across all child threads and is the successful product observation.

The local PR-provisioning fixture could not acquire its synthetic operation lock, but its [exact-head CI bootstrap job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43574493099/job/132386232150), [cold-read consumer job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43574493099/job/132386232104), and [wrapper closure job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43574493099/job/132386232235) pass. No failure was masked.

</details>

Contributor credit: Daniil Karpenko (@dankarization).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @dankarization](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/352f46a3-5f77-4787-a96f-85944ce150b8)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/0177f37b-9068-41ab-b49c-5a7e630c510a)

## Worked on by

- @dankarization

prs.title: fix: retain diagnostics for VM-created errors in logs
prs.body:
Related: #200439

## What Problem This Solves

When a subsystem logs an Error created in a Node VM, the file log and console can show `error: {}` instead of the failure message and stack. That leaves operators without the details needed to investigate the failure.

## User Impact

VM-created errors retain the same diagnostic fields as ordinary errors: name, message, error code when present, and stack. File logs keep the full stack; the console keeps its existing six-line limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each VM has its own Error constructor, so the host's `instanceof Error` check misses these native errors. The existing metadata preparation step now also uses Node's native-error check. The fix reuses the current field selection and sink handling without adding a formatter or changing plain-object metadata.

This is a reproduced remaining error shape, not a confirmed explanation of the original reporter's warnings in #200439. That issue should remain open until its actual caught value is identified.

## Evidence

- The new VM case failed on the original implementation while the same-realm control passed. With the fix, all 84 tests across the subsystem, logger redaction, console capture, and console timestamp suites passed on Node 24.22.1/Linux.
- A separate source-level Node process used normal logging configuration, `createSubsystemLogger`, and `flushLogger`, with no logger mocks or overrides. Both the real JSONL file and JSON console changed from `{"error":{}}` to an error record containing `name: "Error"`, `message: "VM operation failed"`, and the stack. prs.title: fix: subagent results delivered after a blocked handoff are no longer reported as lost
prs.body:
Related #201339

## What Problem This Solves

A subagent can finish while its requester is still working. If the requester's turn ends before the result is handed over, the completion is blocked as `permanent_failure`. A few seconds later the requester's pending batch does hand the result over, but the run keeps the `permanent_failure` record. `subagents list` and any monitor then report a lost completion that actually reached the requester.

## User Impact

When the requester's batch delivers a completion that was blocked this way, the run is now recorded as delivered. Completions that were blocked for other reasons keep their block.

## Why This Change Was Made

Blocking a completion after its requester finished keeps the requester's separately owned yield batch, because that batch still carries the result. When the batch settled successfully, the settlement mutation cleared the wake but only updated delivery for pending, retryable or expired completions, so the permanently suspended record was never corrected.

The settlement now also marks delivery when the completion is blocked as a completed-requester failure and its wake is that yield batch. The existing contract from #176145, that a successful receipt does not recover an ordinary `permanent_failure` suspension, is unchanged and its test still passes.

## Evidence

**Owner-level regression.** New test in `subagent-requester-delivery.test.ts`: a completion suspended as `permanent_failure` (`visible_reply_missing`), with its yield-batch wake retained, settles with a delivered outcome. It fails on current `main` (delivery stays `suspended`) and passes with this change (delivery is `delivered`, the suspended fields are cleared, and the wake is removed).

**Existing data from the latest stable release (v2026.11.5).** No schema or serialization change. To check stored rows from a released build:

1. In a v2026.11.5 checkout, the release's own record writer (`bindSubagentRunRecord` + `writeSubagentRunValuesInDatabase`) and schema (user_version 36) stored a blocked completion with its yield-batch wake.
2. This branch opened that database file unchanged, loaded the row, and ran the requester-batch settlement with a delivered outcome.

```
stored by v2026.11.5:
  delivery: {status: suspended, disposition: permanent_failure, suspendedReason: permanent_failure,
             lastDropReason: visible_reply_missing, requesterDelivery: {state: waiting}}
  requesterSettleWake: {status: dispatching, requesterYieldBatch: true, batchRunIds: [xv-run]}

loaded by this branch: identical to the stored row

after settlement, this branch:   delivery: {status: delivered, disposition: delivered, deliveredAt: 95}, wake removed
after settlement, current main:  delivery: {status: suspended, disposition: permanent_failure, ...}, wake removed
```

So rows that are already blocked on an upgraded install load normally and are corrected the next time their yield batch settles. Rows that are blocked for other reasons are untouched (the #176145 contract test still passes).

**Related suites.** Requester delivery, registry lifecycle, requester-wake e2e, sweeper recovery, persistence, steer-restart, the registry suite and all subagent completion admission tests pass (545 tests). `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean.

**Not covered: a live Gateway run.** The reported state only appears when a requester turn ends during restart recovery without visible-reply evidence (the report saw it with CLI-backed runtimes), and then its yield batch settles seconds later. I can't reproduce that race against a live model from my setup, and the mock provider lanes have no scenario that drives restart recovery into this state. If a maintainer can run it against a live runtime, the check is: after the late settle, `subagents list` should show the run as delivered instead of `permanent_failure`.

prs.title: fix(retry): honor nested channel hints behind invalid metadata
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: empty or invalid `parameters.retry_after` metadata on an outer error prevents the shared channel retry runner from honoring a valid hint in its response or nested error. For example, it can retry after the 400 ms backoff despite a nested response requesting one second.

## User Impact

Channel requests using the default hint reader wait for the available provider-requested delay even when an earlier wrapper contains incomplete metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select the first finite hint in the existing root, response, nested-error order. Missing or invalid hints fall through; finite hints, including zero, retain their precedence. The existing runner continues to own retry admission, injected readers, backoff, jitter, and delay caps. No public signatures, configuration, or exports change.

## Evidence

The earlier baseline reproduction had six fake-clock timing failures on the original production code. The repair retains ten distinct cases for invalid outer metadata, nested fallback, finite and zero precedence, and default backoff alongside main's newer coverage.

- Follow-up review removed two duplicate cap tests. The existing table still covers a 45-second hint capped at 30 seconds by default and allowed at 45 seconds with an explicit 60-second retry-after cap.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/retry-policy.test.ts src/infra/retry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 38 tests passed across both owning files, 4.79 seconds wrapper wall time.
- Type-aware test lint, formatting, whitespace, and the documented test-line budget passed after the cleanup. Source-backed core lint from the unchanged production repair also passed. The unique allocation now matches the remaining 76 added test lines; the shared scalar is unchanged.
- Fresh independent reviews found no actionable code findings. Main `3115c80e8` was integrated without rewriting existing PR commits; its current tests and the distinct PR regressions remain.

Validation gaps: no live channel/provider/Gateway trace with real transport, full build/test, or broader production/test type graphs were run. Fake-clock proof does not claim a live provider result. Exact-head CI is pending on the follow-up cleanup.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): SSH sandbox file tools fail with tar errors when calls overlap
prs.body:
Related: #201806

## What Problem This Solves

Overlapping file-tool calls in sessions that share an SSH sandbox can fail with tar extraction errors. Each call clears the shared skills directory before uploading, so one session can delete files another session is extracting.

## User Impact

File operations in the shared workspace wait for an in-progress skills refresh before clearing and uploading again. A canceled operation stops waiting promptly. Separate SSH targets and Crabbox leases can still refresh concurrently.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared remote-shell backend queues clear and upload together per backend, SSH target or provider lease, and remote skills directory. It passes the caller's abort signal to both queue admission and the existing transport operations. An aborted waiter disposes its session promptly, and the active writer keeps its reservation until its upload settles.

This continues @ngutman's original fix on the original branch. The refresh still publishes in place, so a running command that reads skills can see an in-progress refresh.

## Evidence

- **Red on base `138482e6517d`**: the second handle cleared during an active upload, and the canceled call stayed pending. The separate SSH target and Crabbox lease cases passed.
- **Green on candidate tree `abb028ffe2fb`**: 82 focused tests across the remote-shell owner, SSH backend, filesystem bridge, keyed queue, and Crabbox adapter. Targeted lint and formatting and core typecheck passed.
- **Real OpenSSH, loopback**: three SSH backend handles sharing one workspace ran 9 parallel bridge writes and then 9 parallel bridge reads. All 18 operations succeeded, with zero tar errors. All written bytes and 64 uploaded skills matched. [Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44582478643)
- **Autoreview**: no actionable P0–P2 findings in the staged candidate against `138482e6517d`, with SSH, Crabbox, transport, and queue source supplied.

The reporter's full Gateway sequence remains open for verification in #201806.

prs.title: feat(agents): hide picker-hidden agents from user-facing pickers
prs.body:
Related: #166678

## What Problem This Solves

Internal worker agents must be configured as full `agents.entries` entries to stay spawnable as `sessions_spawn` targets, so every user-facing agent picker (sidebar roster, agent switcher, New Session target picker) lists agents that are never meant to be chatted with directly. The only way to remove one from the picker today is to delete its entry, which breaks spawning.

## User Impact

Operators can set `agents.entries.<id>.picker.hidden: true` to keep those agents out of chat-facing agent pickers and switchers. Hidden agents remain valid `sessions_spawn` targets and stay listed by `openclaw agents list`, marked `(hidden)`. Administrative and automation surfaces keep them selectable.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the config flag proposed in #166678. The UI distinguishes the two roster predicates: `listSelectableAgents` and `findSelectableAgent` remain the administrative/automation projection (system rows only), while chat-facing surfaces use the new `listChatAgents`/`chatAgentsList` helpers (`kind === "system"` and `hidden` excluded). That fixes the first review's Settings finding: `SettingsAgentSelector` still offers picker-hidden agents for management. Docs state the scope as the Control UI and the TUI `/agents` picker; native apps (macOS, iOS) do not yet consume this flag. The follow-up round (head `e736f2bda`) added TUI picker filtering, dock-Home resolution for hidden selections, and the roster-mode/default-agent doc notes.

prs.title: fix: warn on small-context manual picks and skip them in automatic setup
prs.body:
Related: #200920 (this PR is the setup safeguard: a warning on manual picks and no automatic selection of small windows; exact first-turn fit and agent creation stay open there) ## What Problem This Solves When you set up a local model with an 8,192-token context window, setup's AI check passes and treats the model as ready. The first real message then fails with "Context overflow: the system prompt, injected context, or tool definitions exceed the model's context window before chat history." The setup check sends a one-line prompt with tools off, so it fits. A real first turn also carries the system prompt and tool definitions, measured at 11.8K to 18.5K tokens. ## User Impact Setup now tells you when the model's effective context window is below 16,384 tokens: - Automatic setup skips such a model and moves to its next candidate. - A model you choose yourself is still accepted, with a warning that names the model, its window, the usual first-turn need and what to raise. The warning shows in onboarding Test & use, in Control UI Model Setup and CLI onboarding (as a note before the model is switched on), in Control UI Add provider (under the success message), and in `openclaw models auth activate` output. Nothing else changes: chat, existing routes, update repair and agent creation keep today's behavior, and utility models (for example Apple's on-device model, minimum 8,192) are not checked. ## Why This Change Was Made The setup check already runs one turn through the real runtime, and the runtime reports the effective context window it used. Setup compares that value with one floor, 16,384, the floor guided Ollama and LM Studio discovery already apply (#112028). That change kept smaller models available through manual selection, so a manual pick warns instead of refusing. A manual pick could instead be checked against the selected route's real first-turn size (system prompt plus tool schemas). That needs the full agent prompt and tool set assembled outside a turn, a much larger change than a warning, and the runtime already reports the exact overflow if a turn does not fit. The warning is the smaller correct change. ## Evidence Control UI, Models > Available models > Test & use on a local llama-server running with an 8,192-token context (real Gateway, real server). Before (base 0c19bcdf293): the model is verified and switched on with no warning. After (54cec6d075c): a `Context window` note appears before the model is switched on. - Real runs on a Mac Studio against a local llama-server (12B GGUF), isolated state and Gateway, same config at base and head: - Control UI Model Setup (`openclaw.setup.activate.start` + `wizard.next`) with the 8,192-window model: the head shows a `Context window` note after the connection test and before the model is switched on; the base goes straight to done. - Direct activation (`openclaw.setup.activate`, the path Add provider and `models auth activate` use): both succeed, and only the head adds the warning line. prs.title: fix(auto-reply): stop leaking NO_REPLY when replies use Windows line endings
prs.body:
Closes #201943

## What Problem This Solves

An agent reply that starts with a standalone `NO_REPLY` control line is supposed to hide that line and keep the rest of the answer. Before this patch the line was only removed when it ended with `\n`; with Windows-style `\r\n` (or a bare `\r`) the control token was delivered to the user as visible text, so they saw `NO_REPLY` before the real answer.

## User Impact

Users on channels fed by CRLF-producing backends now receive only the intended answer instead of the internal `NO_REPLY` token. No config change or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`stripMixedSilentReplyTokens` compared against the exact string `NO_REPLY\n`. It now matches one leading `NO_REPLY` line terminated by `\r\n`, `\r`, or `\n`, case-insensitively, and preserves the remaining text. This mirrors the trailing-token handling already used by the same producer contract.

The streaming directive accumulator had the same delimiter assumption one layer earlier: when `\r\n` was split across chunks (`"NO_REPLY\r"` then `"\nanswer"`), it stripped the leading token early and emitted the orphaned `\n`. It now holds a trailing `CR` until the next chunk arrives, so the delimiter is removed as one unit.

## Evidence

**Behavior or issue addressed:** a leading `NO_REPLY` line with CRLF/CR leaked into visible replies.

**Real environment tested:** Windows 11, Node 24.16.0, source checkout, isolated loopback Gateway on `127.0.0.1`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and the repository's deterministic mock OpenAI provider (`scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs`) configured through `scripts/e2e/lib/fixtures/mock-openai-config.mjs`. The mock returned the exact model text `NO_REPLY\r\nVisible answer`. Synthetic local API key only; no real account, IP, phone number, or internal endpoint is involved.

**Shipped entry point exercised:** `pnpm openclaw agent` (the CLI path that runs the turn through the Gateway; not a direct helper import).

Command after this patch:

```text
pnpm openclaw agent --message "Reply with the proof marker then a visible answer." --session-key agent:main:noreply-display-1 --timeout 120
```

Terminal display output (what the user sees):

```text
Visible answer
```

`--json` envelope from the same Gateway turn:

```text
finalAssistantRawText:     "NO_REPLY\r\nVisible answer"
finalAssistantVisibleText: "Visible answer"
terminalReply:             { "disposition": "visible", "text": "Visible answer" }
```

So the model emitted the marker, and the delivered/displayed reply contains only the answer.

**Regression test is red on the base and green with the fix.** With `src/auto-reply/reply/mixed-silent-reply-tokens.ts` temporarily restored from `origin/main`, `pnpm test src/agents/agent-run-terminal-reply.test.ts` reported `3 failed | 23 passed` — exactly the `NO_REPLY\r\nanswer`, `NO_REPLY\ranswer`, and `no_reply\r\nanswer` cases. With this patch the same file reports `26 passed`.

Streaming accumulator coverage was added to `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts` for four chunk splits of the token line (`["NO_REPLY\r\nanswer"]`, `["NO_REPLY\r", "\nanswer"]`, `["NO_REPLY\r", "answer"]`, `["NO_REPLY", "\r\nanswer"]`); the file reports `37 passed`.

Other checks on the changed files: `pnpm tsgo:core` passed, `oxlint` passed, `oxfmt --check` passed. Related consumer tests (`chat-message-content.test.ts`, `transcript-assistant-delivery.test.ts`) still pass.

**What was not tested:** no real chat channel (Slack/Telegram/Discord) was connected, so this proves the CLI/Gateway delivery path, not a third-party transport's own newline normalization. No live third-party model provider was used; the mock returns the same bytes a CRLF-producing backend would. Full `pnpm build` / `pnpm test` is left to PR CI. This Windows environment lacks `rg`, so `pnpm check:changed` stopped at `spawnSync rg ENOENT` in the database-worker ratchet; that is unrelated to this change.

## Root Cause

`src/auto-reply/reply/mixed-silent-reply-tokens.ts` hard-coded `const prefix = `${SILENT_REPLY_TOKEN}\n`` and compared a fixed-length slice. Any other newline sequence failed the comparison, so `prepareAgentRunTerminalReply`, the streaming directive accumulator, and display readers treated the control line as ordinary visible text.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Unit:** `src/agents/agent-run-terminal-reply.test.ts` covers `NO_REPLY\r\nanswer`, `NO_REPLY\ranswer`, and `no_reply\r\nanswer` alongside the existing `\n` cases. This is the producer boundary that owns terminal reply preparation, and every channel/UI consumer reads its output.
- **Unit:** `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts` covers the streaming accumulator when the CRLF delimiter is split across chunks.
- **Shipped path:** the Gateway CLI run above proves the marker is stripped in delivered output while the model raw text still contains it.

## Scope boundary

Only the leading silent-token line matcher, the streaming accumulator's trailing-CR hold, and their regression tables changed. Trailing-token behavior, whole-reply silence detection, heartbeat handling, and channel delivery are untouched.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted implementation and testing. I read the affected producer contract, reproduced the leak at the shipped CLI/Gateway boundary, confirmed the regression tests fail on the base, and verified the fix and focused tests locally.
