prs.title: fix: let agents publish work from managed worktrees they created
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An agent that does its work in a managed worktree made with `openclaw worktrees create` cannot publish it. `github_publish` tells an unbound conversation to "publish with workspacePath set to the checkout", then the Gateway refuses that exact call with a bare `missing scope: operator.admin`. Subagents never hold `operator.admin`, so every retry fails the same way and finished, reviewed work stays unpublished.

Observed on a live Gateway running 2026.11.5: a subagent retried the same publication three times over 14 hours and got `{"ok":false,"error":"missing scope: operator.admin","code":"UNAVAILABLE"}` each time. Its checkout was a registered managed worktree of a registered project.

## User Impact

User impact: a conversation with `operator.write` can publish a committed managed worktree of an agent workspace or registered project, as long as no session owns that worktree. When a path is still refused, the error now lists the paths that are allowed instead of only naming a scope the caller cannot obtain.

This widens one Gateway authorization check, so it deserves a security read:

- Session-owned worktrees are still refused. A conversation cannot name another conversation's checkout.
- Callers holding only `operator.sessions.write` (guest roles) are still refused.
- Any other Gateway path still requires `operator.admin`.
- The repository rule is the one `worktrees.create` and `worktrees.branches` already apply to `operator.write` callers; both now share one function with the publish path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Local checkout publication reused the `sessions.create` working-directory rule, which only admits folders inside an agent workspace. Managed worktrees live under the Gateway's worktree root, outside every agent workspace, so the one kind of checkout the Gateway creates for write-scoped callers was the one kind they could not publish. A session's own bound worktree already had an exception; unowned (`manual` and Workboard) worktrees have no owning session to publish through, so they need to be selectable as a source.

The publish path now looks the requested path up in the worktree registry and admits it when the record is live, not session-owned, and its repository root passes the existing write-scope rule. Everything after admission is unchanged: a separate publication task with its own checkout, the project and repository match check, and the clean-tree requirement.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and scope</summary>

- Root cause: `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-github.ts` validated `workspacePath` with `prepareSessionCreateRequestedCwd`, which knows agent workspaces only. The branch dates from #184531; #187660 added the bound-worktree exception.
- Owner: Gateway `sessions.github.publish` admission, plus the `worktrees.*` repository-root rule it now shares.
- Production delta: +66 / -10 lines across two files. The growth is the new admission rule and the model-facing refusal text; the extracted `resolveWriteScopedRepoRoot` replaces the inline copy in `resolveAuthorizedRepoRoot`.
- Sibling paths checked and left alone: `sessions.create` cwd, `fs.listDir`, and `sessions.groups.update` keep workspace-only containment. A child session working inside its parent's session-owned worktree still publishes through the parent.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/user-model.md` states the admitted paths.

</details>

## Evidence

The Gateway now publishes a committed managed worktree for a write-scoped System caller (the identity a subagent's tool calls run under), and still refuses the two cases that must stay closed.

- New boundary case `local checkout outcome: unowned managed worktree` in `src/gateway/github-publication-session-access.test.ts` drives the real `sessions.github.publish` handler with a real Git repository and worktree registry. The checkout sits outside every agent workspace. It asserts: a session-scoped guest is refused; a session-owned worktree is refused; the unowned worktree publishes (push and pull request), creates one publication task bound to that checkout, leaves the source untouched, and a retry returns the same result.
- Before/after: against the handler from `main`, that case fails at source admission: both refusals still hold, then the publish returns a refusal where the test expects `status: "published"`. With this change both files pass, 36 tests. The new refusal wording is asserted separately, on the filesystem-root refusal in `publishes an owned checkout outside the default workspace without admin`.
- Existing refusals still hold: an unbound conversation naming a session-owned checkout, the filesystem root, and a `.git` directory all still get `operator.admin`. Only the filesystem-root expectation changed, to also require the new wording.
- `worktrees.create` and `worktrees.branches` authorization tests pass unchanged after the rule was extracted.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes on the final diff (typecheck, lint, import cycles, format, boundary guards) with the dead-export scan skipped. That scan fails on `main` for two exports in files this PR does not touch: `scripts/full-release-validation-policy.mjs` and `src/infra/update-launcher-repair.ts`.
- `pnpm check:changed` ran on the first commit. The second commit changes two expected strings in the test file; it was format-checked and its tests rerun, and PR CI covers the full gate.
- Independent review of the change found no P0-P2 issues. It ran before a one-line type annotation, a test temp-directory helper swap, and the test-assertion commit.
- Live check on the affected Gateway (read-only): a write-scoped `worktrees.branches` call is admitted for the repository root of the refused worktree and refused with `operator.admin` for an unrelated host path, so the refused checkout meets the rule this PR applies.

Not verified: the end-to-end publish from the affected Gateway. It runs a release build without this change, and I did not deploy to it.

Review follow-up: the automated review asked for two things. The baseline now fails at source admission (above). A running isolated Gateway with a real agent is not included: the changed line is the handler's source admission, which the test reaches through the registered `sessions.github.publish` handler with real Git and the real worktree registry, and only the GitHub transport is mocked. The live proof that matters is the affected Gateway publishing after it updates to a build with this change.

<details>
<summary>Commands and runs</summary>

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2 pnpm test src/gateway/github-publication-session-access.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/worktrees.test.ts` on Blacksmith Testbox, final head: 2 files, 36 tests passed. Run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44575346368
- Baseline, same run: `sessions-github.ts` restored from `84bd048423c`, then `pnpm test src/gateway/github-publication-session-access.test.ts -t 'unowned managed worktree'` fails with `expected [ false, undefined, {...} ] to match object [ true, { status: 'published', ... } ]`.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1 pnpm check:changed` on the first commit: exit 0. Run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44539511088

</details>

prs.title: fix: restricted HTTP conversations fail on their second turn
prs.body:
Closes #198678

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a restricted member's second HTTP chat request is rejected when it reuses the same conversation `user` and the role has `sessions.others: "none"`.

## User Impact

Members can continue their own newly created HTTP conversations while other profiles remain unable to access them. Existing unattributed sessions are not assigned to the next caller; this does not recover their historical ownership.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing create-on-run owner now carries the admitted profile on genuinely new rows independently of sandbox requirements. Persistence continues to stamp only new rows, while existing sharing authorization, required sandboxing, and source cancellation/replacement checks remain intact. Both compatible HTTP endpoints share this owner.

No new schema, configuration, authority mechanism, or test-only production seam is introduced. Production is +9/-5 (net +4); those lines express creator attribution independently of optional sandboxing. Tests are +51/-2, extending the existing HTTP/authentication/persistence fixture.

## Evidence

### Current head after resolving the merge conflict

Merged main at `5dea6be4819a4ea7119e113fcc1a91eb6413dcc2` into the existing PR branch. The resolution preserves main's admitted guest identity input and the PR's creator attribution for restricted member HTTP sessions. The complete patch against that base still touches only `src/gateway/operator-session-run.ts`, `src/gateway/server-http.openai-sandbox.test.ts`.

At `9bf1ab2130a8ef3a17fec3b442afaf1a7bd7421c`:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-http.openai-sandbox.test.ts src/gateway/operator-session-run.test.ts src/gateway/openclaw-id/member-sandbox-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 16 tests. The regressions on the earlier named main `2c47052dd994066da28f882fa0d97dc45d52f70d` failed as expected, with both creator second turns returning 403 without the fix.
- Core and affected test typechecks, targeted format/lint, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent P0–P2 review of the identical two-file patch was scoped clean.
- `corepack pnpm build` passed at the current head.
- The current HTTP tests use the real request, authorization, and persistence path with model execution replaced. The standalone Gateway / SSE / local-model proof and fork CI below were executed at the original head `3993aff1b32aeb966150e04065ae1759af491325`. Fresh standalone Gateway proof is pending for the refreshed head.

### Upstream checks and review for the current head

- [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44214003549): `action_required` with 0 jobs.
- [CodeQL](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44214003048): `action_required` with 0 jobs.
- [CodeQL Critical Quality](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44214003217): `action_required` with 0 jobs.

Repository approval is required for runs reporting `action_required`. A fresh ClawSweeper review for this head is pending. The original [durable review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198696#issuecomment-6873467096) accepted behavior proof and had no code findings at `3993aff1b32aeb966150e04065ae1759af491325`. Required upstream checks and author handoff remain pending.

### Evidence retained from the original head

- **Named-base real failure:** at main `11b022e5d9c33a21cfe80886d14475b45be26ee6`, Alice's first HTTP/SSE turn completed with `200` / `FIRST_READY`; her second request with the same `user` returned `403 forbidden` / session not found. Bob's own conversation completed with `200` / `BOB_READY`, and his attempt to access Alice's key was refused. The station recorded exit 1 solely on the required second-turn success assertion.
- **Red → green regression:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-http.openai-sandbox.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'lets a restricted member'` failed at the second-turn assertion for both compatible endpoints against unchanged production code. With the fix, the full affected fixture passes, including different-profile denial and preservation of existing unattributed rows.
- **Focused controls:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-http.openai-sandbox.test.ts src/agents/command/attempt-execution.shared.test.ts src/gateway/session-sharing.creator-namespace.test.ts src/gateway/openai-compatible-agent-run.test.ts src/gateway/operator-session-run.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **51 passed across five files**, 79.69 s wall. The HTTP fixture's 14 cases passed; measured cases and CI timing will remain separate.
- **Checks:** `corepack pnpm tsgo:core`; `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/gateway/server-http.openai-sandbox.test.ts"]' --concurrency 1`; targeted `run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` and `oxfmt --check` for both changed files completed successfully. Test-root budget advisories are retained; no baseline was weakened.
- **Independent local review:** canonical Codex AutoReview, complete uncommitted candidate against the named base, P0–P2, supplied full owner/caller/callee/sharing/provenance context and baseline observations — scoped-clean, no findings. This was static supplied-evidence review; it did not execute tests or access repository files directly.

Formal baseline command: `ocpr prove 198678 --phase pre --sha 11b022e5d9c33a21cfe80886d14475b45be26ee6`, invoking the local `198678-real-http-proof.py --phase pre --sha 11b022e5d9c33a21cfe80886d14475b45be26ee6` driver (local artifact path omitted). It used a real built Gateway and local Ollama model with synthetic trusted-proxy identities and isolated persisted state, not a deployed IdP or external provider. Owned Gateway processes were joined and stopped.

prs.title: fix(a2a): settle steered tasks with the consuming run's outcome
prs.body:
Closes #200646

## What Problem This Solves

With `messages.queue.mode: "steer"`, an A2A `SendMessage` that arrives while a turn is already running gets its own task id, but nothing ever settles it — a peer polling `GetTask` sees `TASK_STATE_WORKING` forever while the run that consumed the message answers on the host task. Steered tasks now settle with the consuming run's terminal outcome, the same signal `chat.send` uses.

- Problem: `extensions/a2a/src/inbound.ts` has a settlement path for followup tasks (queued reply batches, #183803) but none for the `deferredToActiveRun: "steer"` branch; a steered message's dispatch never receives a final reply, so `store.complete`/`store.fail` never run for it.
- Solution: settle the steered task from the consuming run's terminal outcome (completed with the store's status message, failed with the run failure) — the same signal `chat.send` uses.
- What changed: `extensions/a2a/src/inbound.ts` plus two `inbound.test.ts` cases.
- What did NOT change: followup settlement, the non-deferred completion path, the task store, and core reply-runtime observers.

## Why This Change Was Made

The run's terminal outcome is the only settlement signal a steered dispatch will ever receive: `collectRuntimeMetadata` fans every adopted item's `onAgentRunTerminalOutcome` observer into the consuming run, so the extension can settle without new core hooks.

- Status: the review correctly identified that accepted steering does not yet deliver the terminal callback — `runActiveReplySteer` consumes the parked source without transferring its run observers, so the new settlement branch is reachable only when the consuming run does report the outcome. Threading terminal custody through the steering owner is a core reply-runtime change (observer registry on the live reply operation vs. injection-option passthrough); this PR holds the extension-side settlement and the acceptance bar while that seam gets implemented.
- Alternative: mirroring the host task's artifact text would require cross-task plumbing the extension cannot see (the steered dispatch never receives the final payload).
- Risk / non-goals: no behavior change on the followup and non-deferred paths; the completion is a no-op behind the store's terminal guard.

## User Impact

A2A peers that poll `GetTask` until a terminal state get `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` (with a status message naming the run's outcome) or `TASK_STATE_FAILED` when the run fails, instead of waiting forever; the task store no longer accumulates permanent `WORKING` rows.

## Evidence

Focused regression driving the shipped `dispatchA2aInbound` against the real `A2aTaskStore`, with the dispatch result reporting `deferredToActiveRun: "steer"` and the run settling after dispatch resolves (as it does live):

```text
✓ inbound.test.ts > A2A channel inbound dispatch > settles a steered task when the consuming run completes
✓ inbound.test.ts > A2A channel inbound dispatch > settles a steered task when the consuming run fails
```

Before the fix the first case leaves the task in `TASK_STATE_WORKING` with no artifacts (the observed 2h44m probe in the issue); after it the task is `TASK_STATE_COMPLETED` with the store's status message and empty artifacts. The failure case keeps the existing `Agent run failed` status.

What was not tested: `collect` queue mode and the live JSON-RPC peer transport; the settlement logic is transport-independent.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used `git grep` across `deferredToActiveRun` and the reply-runtime observer wiring to confirm the steered observer fires, then implemented the settlement in `inbound.ts` and validated with `vitest`. The implementer understands the code: `collectRuntimeMetadata` fans adopted items' terminal observers into the consuming run, and the store's terminal guard makes double settlement a no-op. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(agents): align tool-free completion relay instructions with tool surface
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #198584

When a subagent completion handoff runs on a degraded path where execution tools are stripped (`!completionRetainsRequesterTools`, including both `disableTools: true` and `["message"]`-only delivery turns), the prompt and `task_completion` internal events still carried `SUBAGENT_COMPLETION_OUTCOME_INSTRUCTION`, which instructs the model to *"require continued work or a follow-up in the kept child session; report a blocker only when progress needs new user authority."*

Because the turn has no execution or delegation tools, models following that instruction literally either attempt blocked tool calls (burning tokens on error round-trips) or report a spurious task failure/blocker to the user for work that already succeeded.

### Changes
- Added `SUBAGENT_COMPLETION_RELAY_ONLY_OUTCOME_INSTRUCTION` and `rewriteSubagentCompletionReplyInstructionForRelayOnly` in `src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-instructions.ts` so relay-only turns are instructed not to attempt tool calls or follow-up runs and to report the captured result truthfully (noting any needed follow-up for a normal turn).
- Added `adaptCompletionRelayTurnForToolSurface` in `src/agents/command/attempt-execution.helpers.ts` (avoiding object spread in `.map(...)`) to rewrite both `prompt` and `task_completion` `internalEvents` when `isSubagentAnnounceHandoff && !completionRetainsRequesterTools`.
- Wired `adaptCompletionRelayTurnForToolSurface` into both the CLI and embedded execution paths in `src/agents/command/attempt-execution.ts`.
- Added unit tests in `src/agents/command/attempt-execution.completion-relay.test.ts` covering relay-only rewriting, `task_completion` event immutability, and preservation when requester tools are retained or the turn is not a completion handoff.

## Evidence

- Verified `adaptCompletionRelayTurnForToolSurface` and `rewriteSubagentCompletionReplyInstructionForRelayOnly` unit tests in `src/agents/command/attempt-execution.completion-relay.test.ts`.
- Verified `attempt-execution.ts` threads the adapted `prompt` and `internalEvents` into both `runCliAgent` and `runEmbeddedAgent` when `isSubagentAnnounceHandoff && !completionRetainsRequesterTools`, while leaving retained-tool handoffs and non-handoff turns unchanged.
- GitHub Actions CI (`checks`, `oxlint`, `vitest`) will validate the full suite on this PR.

prs.title: refactor(gateway): check node plugin approval decisions once
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Plugin node approval re-checked an `isCurrent` predicate at every stage of one approval: when the plugin asked for approval, after the placement-grant resolution, after the decision arrived, a second decision projection after consumption, and once more after grant retention. A started approval could then be refused ("agent runtime approval authority is no longer active") or silently turned into a null decision partway through.

The repo rule (AGENTS.md, "Choose good compromises") is to check authority one time, when work starts. Revocation applies to the next request, and a started request may finish.

## Change

- Deleted: those five approval-stage re-checks in `node-invoke-plugin-approval.ts`, and the `isCurrent` parameter with its construction in `node-invoke-plugin-policy.ts`.
- Kept: the first decision projection (the decision's start check), record-specific allow-once consumption, the placement-owner binding and grant retention.
- What `isCurrent` composed is still refused elsewhere:
  - Plugin currentness, private-owner currentness and the upload/approval gate have their own checks before the transport.
  - The final send checks plugin, private owner, stream, approval and command, plus the session assertion.
  - No refusal point moved.
- The lifetime-check count in `node-invoke-plugin-approval.ts` falls from 2 to 0.

Follows #201887 and #201947.

## User impact

A node approval that has started is no longer cancelled or turned into a null decision partway through by a re-check. Plugin replacement, private-owner closure and a disabled upload still stop the dispatch before it reaches the node.

## Evidence

Proof tier: source (`ocx test`).

- Before deleting, confirmed that each clause `isCurrent` composed (plugin currentness, private-owner currentness, and the upload/approval gate passed by `node.invoke` and computer transport) is still refused at the policy's own pre-transport checks and at the final send.
- 11 test files (node-invoke plugin approval and policy, placement grants, `nodes.invoke*`, computer transport): 204 tests pass on current `main`. That includes two new upload-gate approval-completion cases and the existing `fails closed when the allow-once claim cannot be consumed`.
- `pnpm tsgo`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxlint, format, and the lifetime-check (`node-invoke-plugin-approval.ts` 2 → 0), line-cap, session-identity, mock-export and max-lines ratchets: pass.

Production −15 lines, tests +18 lines.

prs.title: fix: keep subagent cleanup running with large retained tasks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Archiving a backlog of completed subagents can repeatedly kill the state-read worker when the retained runs contain large tasks. Each later sweep reloads the same full payloads and fails again, leaving cleanup stuck.

## User Impact

Subagent cleanup continues across consecutive sweeps even when archived runs contain large retained prompts. Stored run payloads, retention rules, and configuration remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deletion-only mutations now plan from the registry's resident metadata, under the existing FIFO reservation and publication owner. They reject non-null postimages; normal updates still restore full payloads before writing. Both individual cleanup and collector-group archival use this path.

The writer processes `DELETE RETURNING` in groups of 16 within the existing transaction, preserving atomic removal receipts without collecting the entire deleted payload set in memory. No schema or index change is needed.

Worker exit-cause diagnostics are deferred: task-port loss and supervisor termination arrive through separate channels, so preserving the cause requires lifecycle coordination beyond a cheap owner change.

Follow-up for Peter: evaluate whether each retained run needs the full task text. This fix preserves the current storage contract.

## Evidence

The committed regression uses synthetic SQLite state, a real retained native reader limited to 64 MiB, and 108 archive-due collector members with 384 KiB tasks (40.5 MiB total task text).

- Base `2ef6f7bade7`: **1 failed**, with `Native worker task channel closed [task=stateRead.task admittedInputBytes=2541 exchanges=0 stage=running]` during the first tick.
- Fix: **two consecutive ticks succeed**, each archiving all 108 newly seeded rows; durable reads confirm deletion and pending lifecycle processing runs on both ticks.
- Focused recovery, lifecycle, worker persistence, SQLite, and capacity suites: **83 tests passed**. After expanding the rollback fixture to 36 rows across delete batches, the affected SQLite/capacity rerun passed **16 tests**.
- Targeted agents/sessions typecheck, production and test lint, format, and `git diff --check` passed. Worker entrypoints are unchanged; the regression runs the compiled worker closure. PR CI supplies broad build/test proof.
- Net test lines: **0** (+117 / -117). The native regression replaces a cleanup allocation unit test and private clone-call assertions. Stored identity, immutable publication, removal fact, and rollback contracts remain covered. Production net: **+14 lines**.
- `pr-simplify` completed. Isolated Codex autoreview through P2: **scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable findings.

The final regression took 1.99 seconds of test time; the latest two-file run took 50.30 seconds wall time including cold worker compilation (37.52 seconds reported by Vitest). The initial five-file focused command took 66.30 seconds wall time. Exact-head [CI run 44579084342](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44579084342) completed successfully.

prs.title: fix: avoid starting Codex on an unconfigured Gateway
prs.body:
Fixes #201909

## What Problem This Solves

Starting an empty Gateway launches Codex even though no model, credentials, or client requested it. This creates a Codex home and starts native background work on an otherwise unused installation.

## User Impact

An unconfigured, signed-out Gateway no longer starts Codex just to warm its built-in fallback model. Configured primary models, explicit runtime policies, and signed-in defaults retain their existing warmup. Model-picker discovery and native turns remain enabled; no configuration change or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The startup warmup was treating the built-in fallback as configured demand. The existing warmup owner now checks the existing primary-model/runtime selectors and the prepared credential snapshot before acquiring a native catalog. It does not probe credentials or start discovery to make that decision. This fixes the startup decision rather than disabling Codex discovery.

## Evidence

The same isolated Linux Gateway startup was red on main and green with the fix, using the real bundled Codex 0.169.0 and fresh state, HOME, and cache directories. No provider credentials or client connection were supplied during the idle observation.

Main 97a5c372bd115de958b9070b40faf1fb9b3799f0:
  +5s through +40s: 1 Codex app-server; codex-home created — FAIL
Fixed build:
  +5s through +40s: 0 Codex app-servers; no codex-home — PASS
  models.list refresh afterward: 1 Codex app-server — PASS
Configured Codex primary on fixed build:

The final focused file passes all 27 tests, including prepared API-key/native sign-in defaults, explicit runtime-only configuration, existing configured-model warmup, and first-use discovery. The existing startup and model-list lifecycle suites pass another 88 tests.

prs.title: perf(ci): avoid duplicate declaration replay admission
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201675

## What Problem This Solves

The extension-boundary CI job repeats physical filesystem admission for every replayed compiler lookup. This follow-up removes that duplicate work from recording compiler receipts.

## User Impact

No product behavior change. The intended benefit is less work in the boundary checker while retaining containment checks for positive and negative lookups.

## Why This Change Was Made

The declaration filesystem already owns physical admission. Receipt replay now uses that bounded view directly, rather than immediately repeating its admission in a callback. Other filesystem callers and asserted byte reads are unchanged. The existing receipt benchmark loads both cooperating modules from the selected revision so its baseline uses the matching API.

## Evidence

Experiment rejected: the measured median gain is 2.7%, below the predeclared 10% acceptance threshold. Closing without merging. Correctness passed, but the improvement is too small for this performance change.

Acceptance rule recorded before samples: use the full opt-in plugin receipt corpus from one successful candidate boundary build; compare frozen base `cd2ae19272a3ee7be456385fa7efc56d6e2109a6` and candidate in five interleaved fresh-process pairs on the same VM. Measure the instrumented warm receipt-recording phase with the committed `scripts/perf/extension-boundary-receipt-measure.mts`, external process CPU/peak RSS, operation counts, digest, and host load. Accept at least 10% lower median recording time and fewer filesystem admission operations, identical output digests, no slower p95, and no 20% regression in CPU or peak RSS. This does not measure cold compilation or whole CI savings.

### Results

Frozen candidate: `ec7801de499ff224a63fb7a2a3fb3f94652d3c3a`. Boat lease `cbx_d7f2e1da49c9`, observed 8 CPUs and 15,990 MiB RAM, Node 24.22.1. Run `run_fb4e2af70e2c28f0c5fd14ad08b2e3c6`. Five fresh-process AB pairs, 147 real plugin receipts; load averages ranged from 1.01 to 2.75 across reported windows. This was an instrumented warm receipt-recording benchmark, not a full CI comparison.

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Recording median | 36.178 s | 35.216 s |
| Recording p95 (five samples) | 37.570 s | 35.579 s |
| Recording range | 34.637–37.570 s | 34.068–35.579 s |
| Process CPU median | 39.55 s | 38.71 s |
| Process CPU p95 | 41.45 s | 39.21 s |
| Peak RSS median | 1,188,028 KiB | 1,198,144 KiB |
| Peak RSS p95 | 1,190,836 KiB | 1,204,544 KiB |
| existsSync calls | 1,111,859 | 1,007,402 |
| native realpath calls | 1,065,381 | 988,591 |
| other realpath calls | 299 | 299 |

Counted filesystem calls fell 8.3%; median CPU fell 2.1%; median RSS rose 0.9%. All ten receipt digests matched `558c7e7e078ffe93d4af6d66999e60b066985dea6cfcf97bf33fcc94db14b9f0`.

The full boundary check passed: 147 plugins compiled and one canary passed. Both focused integration suites passed (16 tests; three Windows-only cases skipped on Linux), as did the tooling-test typecheck, scoped lint, and oxfmt/Bun format parity. Local ClawSweeper completed a read-only review of `cd2ae19272a3..ec7801de499f` with no actionable correctness or security findings. No hosted broad CI was requested for this rejected experiment.

The diff removes a duplicate caller-side admission while preserving the filesystem owner. No new tests were added; existing boundary regressions cover the preserved behavior. Production diff: two files, net five lines removed; benchmark support: net nine lines added.

prs.title: fix(ci): switch the active WebKit package mirror
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201313

## What Problem This Solves

WebKit setup can spend seven minutes retrying the same slow package mirror. Recovery edits a fixed mirror-list filename, while Blacksmith's APT sources reference a different file. The log says it switched mirrors, but the next attempt still downloads from the original mirror.

## User Impact

A slow first mirror can now recover through the alternatives in the list APT actually uses. Browser coverage, download deadlines and package-installation behavior stay unchanged. No measured cost or runtime reduction is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ask APT for its configured repository metadata after the first download timeout. Use its single local plaintext mirror list for the existing temporary edit and restoration. Do not guess a provider filename or touch inactive lists. Ambiguous and unsupported layouts retain the existing no-recovery path.

## Evidence

- [Observed failed job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44514786893/job/135528901560): both attempts read the provider's mirror list; the second still uses the same slow archive and exits 124.
- Replayed the complete installer in isolated Ubuntu 24.04 with real APT 2.8.4, no network, and a controlled download timeout. Baseline retries the slow active list and exits 124. Candidate selects the fallback and exits 0. Both restore the active/inactive lists and remove the temporary APT option.
- All 11 installer regressions passed. Replacing only the action with the base version makes both new provider cases fail with exit 124; both hosted cases still pass. The candidate action was restored byte-for-byte afterward.
- Targeted tooling typecheck, test-file lint, three-file formatting and workflow validation passed.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed the complete committed range from `cd2ae19272a3ee7be456385fa7efc56d6e2109a6` to `10441e92756d45309263f5125794b1a84f6a8fca` at high reasoning with no priority filter: no actionable correctness or security findings. A separate independent source review also found no actionable issue.
- [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44579901226) for `10441e92756d45309263f5125794b1a84f6a8fca`; merged as `c71022af14dd5f690f62ab07b92fcb44c1dbb81e`. Natural runner failover and any billing benefit remain unmeasured.

prs.title: feat: share an agent as a template from the agent menu
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Turning an agent into a shareable template starts from chat today, so you have to open that agent's main session and know what to ask. The agent menu already lists every agent, but each row only offers Settings, and that Settings icon draws a box on hover that the neighbouring sidebar actions no longer use.

## User Impact

User impact: hovering an agent in the agent menu now shows a Share button next to Settings. Clicking it opens that agent's main session and sends "Create a shareable template of yourself", so the agent starts preparing its template for review. Both row actions now brighten on hover instead of drawing a box.

Share appears only when Templates is turned on and the connection is allowed to create template drafts, the same conditions as the existing Create template action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Template creation already works from an ordinary chat request, so Share sends that request as a normal message in the agent's main session and then opens the session. It does not create a draft itself. If the message cannot be sent, the menu stays where you were and an error toast offers a retry. Retry repeats the same request on the same connection, so a send the Gateway already accepted is not sent twice; after the connection is replaced Retry does nothing and Share starts a new request.

The two row actions share one style so they stay consistent, and the hover rule now changes only the icon color.

## Evidence

Hovering the Research row in the agent menu, dark theme. Before is `main` at 29f26872924, after is this branch. Both use the real Control UI build with the same synthetic mocked Gateway data.

### Clean comparison

Before

![Before: Settings is the only row action and hovering it draws a box](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a9d06277-b1c6-4cda-9e14-2049be14b365)

After

![After: Share sits beside Settings and hovering brightens the icon without a box](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c1b747ca-c817-4a13-ad09-c000041c51f0)

### Annotated comparison

Before

![Before, annotated: the hover box around Settings is outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b7f00337-63bc-41cd-b2e0-0ccc938199e6)

After

![After, annotated: Share and Settings are outlined with no hover box](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82a4cc44-96dc-4e74-b54e-1201fc7b3423)

### After clicking Share

Share hovered, then the result of the click: the Research agent's main session is open with the request sent.

![Share hovered: its icon is brighter and has no box](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d9b311e-3e5b-4f73-8d07-8a18f11ef797)

![After the click: the agent's main session shows the sent message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b87fc25d-65e2-4cd5-a149-2a7b807ea75b)

### What was checked

- A browser test in the sidebar interactions suite hovers each row action and checks that the background stays transparent while the icon color changes, reaches Share then Settings with Tab, clicks Share, and checks that exactly one `chat.send` goes to `agent:research:main` with the message, no template draft is created by the UI, the session opens, and the message is visible in the transcript. It takes about 1.8 seconds.
- Unit tests cover Share appearing only when sharing is available and never on an agent that is still being created. A retry test checks that Retry resends the identical request and does nothing after the connection is replaced; it fails on the first revision of this PR and passes now. They take under 100 ms combined.
- The existing agent menu tests pass unchanged: 202 unit tests across four files, 6 browser layout tests, and all 6 sidebar interaction browser tests. `pnpm check:changed` passes.

Not checked: a live Gateway with a real model. The mocked Gateway confirms the request the UI sends and the resulting navigation, not the agent's reply.

prs.title: fix(templates): keep pre-upload ClawHub failures retryable in draft publication
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #198548. `templates.drafts.publish` can fail **before the artifact is uploaded** — for example when the ClawHub sign-in has expired (`whoami` returns 401), the registry is rate-limiting (429), or the registry is unreachable (a transport error such as a refused connection or timeout). Those failures are raised as `ClawHubRequestError` or a native transport error (not `TemplateProjectError`), which `draftError` treated as unknown. The publish response therefore carried no `templatePublication` metadata, and the Control UI concluded the submission was `unconfirmed` — showing "Submission unconfirmed", blaming the draft's contents, and disabling both Publish and Retry with no recovery short of reloading the page.

The fix makes pre-upload ClawHub failures a **known, retryable, not-published** outcome: the response now reports `templatePublication.effect: "none"` with a named cause, so the UI shows "Not published" and keeps Publish/Retry available.

## Solution

- `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.ts` — `draftError` now treats `ClawHubRequestError` and transient transport errors as known errors. The code distinguishes `clawhub_request_failed` (HTTP response) from `clawhub_unreachable` (transport), and the message names the actual cause:
  - 401 → "Your ClawHub sign-in has expired. Sign in again and retry publishing."
  - 429 → "ClawHub is rate-limiting this Gateway. Wait and retry publishing."
  - other HTTP statuses → "ClawHub returned an error. Check the registry status and retry publishing."
  - transport errors → "ClawHub could not be reached. Check your network connection and retry publishing."
  All of them stay retryable with `effect: "none"`. A failure that starts after the upload request is sent still reports `effect: "unconfirmed"` (the registry may have received the write).
- `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.test.ts` — the publication fixture gains `identity.unauthorized` (whoami 401), `identity.rateLimit` (whoami 429), and `registry.dropWhoamiResponse` (whoami socket destroyed → native transport error). Three regression tests publish after each failure and assert the failure is retryable with `effect: "none"`, the right code and message, zero uploads, and zero registry posts.

## Evidence

- **Regression tests (RED → GREEN):** with the old `draftError`, the new tests fail (they saw `code: "templates_disabled"` and no publication metadata; the transport case took 44s to time out). With the fix, the full `templates-drafts.test.ts` suite passes — 33/33 tests.
- **Behavioral contract:** a pre-upload 401 now yields `{ code: "INVALID_REQUEST", retryable: true, details: { templatePublication: { effect: "none", code: "clawhub_request_failed" } }, message: "Your ClawHub sign-in has expired. Sign in again and retry publishing." }`; a pre-upload 429 yields the rate-limiting message; a pre-upload transport failure yields `{ ... code: "clawhub_unreachable" }` with "ClawHub could not be reached. Check your network connection and retry publishing." Each test asserts `posts === 0` and zero uploads — nothing is ever submitted to the registry in these paths.
- The Control UI already maps `effect: "none"` to the "Not published" state with Publish/Retry enabled (`creator-flow.ts`), so no UI change is needed; this is a protocol/response-contract fix on the Gateway side.
- No credentials, tokens, or private data appear in this PR.

### Real running-Gateway proof (captured trace)

Ran a real local Gateway (templates Labs on, `agents.entries.research` configured) and drove its actual control WebSocket through the full flow — `templates.drafts.create` → `save` → `review` → `publish` — with `OPENCLAW_CLAWHUB_URL` pointed at a stub registry whose `/api/v1/whoami` succeeds during review and then returns **401 on the publish-time identity check**, i.e. a credential that expires before any upload.

Stub registry trace (head revision) — only identity checks, **no `POST /api/v1/packages`**:

```
+13551ms GET /api/v1/whoami (mode=expire-on-publish)
+13617ms GET /api/v1/whoami (mode=expire-on-publish)
+13617ms whoami #2: credential expired -> 401 (pre-upload)
```

**Before the fix** (base `ab5a6d417f7`) — publish returns no publication metadata and no retryable flag, so the UI would lock as unconfirmed:

```
publish -> rejected
{
  "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
  "message": "The Template draft could not be processed. Check its contents and try again."
}
```

**After the fix** (head `e8a28a024dd`) — named cause, `effect: none`, retryable, still zero uploads:

```
publish -> rejected
{
  "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
  "message": "Your ClawHub sign-in has expired. Sign in again and retry publishing.",
  "retryable": true,
  "details": {
    "templatePublication": {
      "effect": "none",
      "code": "clawhub_request_failed"
    }
  }
}
```

I also verified the complementary contract on the same running Gateway: when the stub accepts `whoami` but rejects the upload `POST /api/v1/packages` with 401, publish correctly reports `effect: "unconfirmed"` / `retryable: false`, because a started upload cannot prove the write did not happen.

prs.title: fix: agent roster stays unsorted and hides unread indicators
prs.body:
Closes #198515

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI agent roster stays in configured order when users select **Last updated**, even after another agent's conversation becomes more recent. Agent rows also hide whether one of their conversations is unread.

## User Impact

User impact: unpinned agents follow their latest conversation activity and update as activity arrives, including after a cached sidebar reload. Pins, stable ties, other sort modes, and selecting an agent's main conversation keep their existing behavior. Recency uses the existing shared 300-session window, excluding archived sessions; it is not an all-history ranking.

**Draft:** focused behavior is verified, but UI typecheck and performance-budget proof remain incomplete. This is not a live deployment.

Unread dots now appear on regular and pinned agent avatars when an available non-archived, non-incognito conversation is unread, including after cached sidebar reloads. Reading the main chat does not clear a different unread conversation. This reuses the existing session badge and shared activity facts without new session fetches or polling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing canonical conversation-activity clock instead of metadata update times, apply ordering only in the unpinned roster's Last updated view, subscribe directly to activity updates, and retain display-only recency in cached sidebar snapshots. Existing snapshots without recency remain readable.

## Evidence

- **193 focused tests passed across the latest applicable runs:** activity aggregation (9), sidebar consumers (88), snapshot model (13), snapshot lifecycle (38), shared activity store/transport/message handling (38), unread live/cache regression (1), and Chromium roster behavior (6). Coverage includes public/private unread, pinned rows, live events, cached-to-live hydration, read clearing, sorting, focus, navigation, and existing work/viewport behavior. Final Chromium rerun: 6/6 passed in 40.86 s.
- **Red/green rendering proof:** separate Chromium processes at base `51c2f42a8e029f667829c753d7098af911dd7f70` and the fixed source now committed as `0982e498e8bd9b88389ceeb957bdf0a1a6899f0a`. Selecting Last updated yields `main, recent, working` on base (failing) and `recent, main, working` with the fix (passing). Screenshots below render the production sidebar component with synthetic conversation data, not a live Gateway/model session. Both were inspected and delivered in the originating chat; generated proof media/source copies are not committed.
- **Targeted lint:** 0 warnings / 0 errors across the eight touched TypeScript files. Formatting passed for all nine changed files; `git diff --check` passed.
- **Independent read-only source review:** complete nine-file local diff against the base above (now committed unchanged as `0982e498e8bd9b88389ceeb957bdf0a1a6899f0a`); no actionable findings. Reviewed activity selection, order-neutral aggregation, pin/tie/navigation behavior, owner subscriptions, cache hydration, and the existing session window. Source review only; it did not run tests or establish CI/typecheck success.
- **UI production build:** `node scripts/ui.js build` completed with exit 0; Vite reported 71 s and verified 1,030 finalized sidecars. **This is not a clean performance gate:** it reported eight budget violations (document gzip, largest JS/CSS gzip, total CSS gzip/raw, chat boot JS requests/gzip, and new boot JS gzip). They have not been attributed against an equivalent base build; no thresholds or baselines were changed.
- **Open proof gaps:** the UI TypeScript check hit its 180 s watchdog and was terminated, not passed. No full isolated Gateway/live-model end-to-end run or broad CI proof is claimed. Automatic draft CI skips do not close these gaps; exact-head qualified validation is required before marking ready.

### Before — Last updated leaves the roster in fixed order

![Before: synthetic Harbor remains above the more recently active Scout after selecting Last updated](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/649bf242-1405-496b-bd15-7475a3397983)

### After — Last updated follows conversation activity

![After: more recently active Scout moves above Harbor while the sidebar remains rendered](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dccab4ad-435f-4d87-9424-cf8fe902ba67)

### Unread indicators — reviewed follow-up

Commit `90008fbef77f051a427cf0198cf1d3be89a31e57` adds the seven-file unread follow-up. It retains display-only unread state in snapshots (legacy snapshots remain readable), excludes incognito-only unread from the agent aggregate, and preserves the existing running indicator and sort behavior. Independent read-only review found no remaining actionable findings after reproducing and fixing cached-dot loss. Targeted lint: 0 warnings/errors across six follow-up TypeScript files; formatting passed for seven follow-up files; staged whitespace check passed. Pre-commit hooks passed through the existing task-local Windows pnpm adapter; no checks were disabled.

The production-build result above belongs to the sorting commit. The unread follow-up has not had a fresh production build or successful full UI typecheck; the existing typecheck/performance gaps remain open. This PR stays draft.

The following real-sidebar captures use synthetic conversation data. They were inspected and delivered in chat; no generated media is committed. The running ring is preserved.

#### Before — unread conversations have no agent dot

![Before: Scout and pinned Forge have no agent unread dots despite unread conversations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/130ad97c-b8d4-4758-b266-cda4c82f9977)

#### After — regular and pinned agents show unread dots

![After: Scout and pinned running Forge have unread dots, with the running ring preserved](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/761d0bc2-f13c-45bd-9288-1f49adeb8ba7)


## Running-Gateway activity and supported historical UI compatibility (November 14, 2026)

[Exact-head behavior, captured receipts, and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198644#issuecomment-6886712059): real background activity causes reorder/unread; reload retains both; read acknowledgement and navigation pass. Separately, a real historical 2026.11.3 UI saves v1 cache and Created preference; current exact-head assets retire v1 as designed, reconstruct live v7, retain Created/order through actual reload, and preserve seeded session identity/activity/labels with matching before/after hashes. Same current isolated Gateway throughout: this does not prove a full historical Gateway/database upgrade. Activity inference is explicitly synthetic; the compatibility lane invokes none. Test/outer runners pass; Chromium teardown exit1 after compatibility assertions and build advisory budgets are disclosed. Maintainer navigation-semantics decision remains open.

prs.title: fix(agents): completion relays report spurious failures on tool-free turns
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #198584

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where users would receive "the task failed / I'm blocked" reports for subagent work that actually completed, whenever the completion was relayed on a degraded path (unverified handoff envelope, restart recovery, CLI execution provider, or raw-model run). On those turns every execution tool is disabled by design, yet the announce prompt still instructed the model to "require continued work or a follow-up in the kept child session" — so the model burned tokens on blocked tool attempts and then escalated the relay's own authority loss as a child task failure.
- **Related:** #198584 (this issue); #198204 touched the same instruction builder for a different defect (duplicate delivery) — complementary, no overlap. clawsweeper labels on the issue: `queueable-fix` / `fix-shape-clear` / `source-repro`; its Codex review asked to "qualify shared completion guidance by available tools", which is exactly this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** the completion guidance a relay turn receives matches the tool surface that turn actually resolved. Restricted relays (tools disabled, or allowlist collapsed to `["message"]`) now get relay-only wording: preserve the child outcome, relay it truthfully, state any needed follow-up for a subsequent normal turn, and do not report the turn's own tool restrictions as a task failure. Trusted in-process handoffs that retain the requester's tools keep the existing continuation guidance unchanged.
- The instruction is frozen into the announce prompt at compose time, while the tool-surface decision (`resolveCompletionToolPolicy`) is only made later at run time — so the rewrite is applied at the run seam in `runAgentAttempt`, the single place that authoritatively knows the surface. One condition (`isSubagentAnnounceHandoff && !completionRetainsRequesterTools`) covers both the `disableTools` and message-only cases, for the CLI and embedded paths, across the prompt text and the task-completion internal events (which feed runtime-context fragments).
- **Out of scope:** the tool restriction itself (intentional privilege separation, unchanged); model-free relay for unverified paths (issue's costlier option 2); persisting the capability envelope across restarts (option 3); the settle-into-busy-parent and `sessions_send` A2A paths, which run with tools and keep the original instruction.
- **Highest-risk area:** prompt text substitution on completion handoff turns.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The rewrite is an exact-match `replaceAll` of one frozen constant; text that does not contain it is byte-identical. The trusted-handoff regression test asserts the continuation guidance survives untouched when tools are retained.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** on a restricted completion relay turn, the model-facing prompt and runtime-context fragments contain the relay-only instruction and no longer contain the "require continued work or a follow-up" continuation clause; users stop receiving spurious failure reports for completed child work, and tokens are no longer wasted on blocked tool attempts. Trusted completion handoffs behave exactly as before.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `src/agents/command/attempt-execution.ts` (the `completionRelayOnly` seam after `resolveCompletionToolPolicy`), `src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-instructions.ts` (new relay-only constant + rewrite helpers), and the regressions in `src/agents/command/attempt-execution.completion-relay.test.ts` ("rewrites completion guidance to relay-only on a restricted relay turn", "keeps continuation guidance on a trusted completion handoff turn").

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** isolated worktree at `origin/main` + patch, Node v26.12.1, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and a **real model provider** (`zte/co-claw`, `api: openai-completions`, internal MaaS endpoint; API key read from the local machine config at runtime, never written into any artifact). Two independent levels: (1) a real-model run of the restricted relay turn through the shipped gateway RPC surface, (2) behavioral regressions through the real `runAgentAttempt` seam.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**

  ```bash
  # 1) real-model proof: isolated gateway + real provider, driven through the shipped
  #    `agent` RPC with the unverified-completion-handoff payload. The driver script
  #    lives outside the repository (evidence dir); OPENCLAW_CACHE_TRACE=1 records the
  #    composed prompt, and a loopback passthrough recorder captures the real request
  #    bodies on their way to the real endpoint.
  OPENCLAW_CACHE_TRACE=1 OPENCLAW_CACHE_TRACE_FILE=<evidence>/cache-trace-head-lint.jsonl \
    PROOF_LABEL=head-lint PROOF_SCENARIO=lint PROOF_WIRE=1 \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs <evidence>/restricted-relay-live.mts      # patched head
  git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/agents/command/attempt-execution.ts \
    src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-instructions.ts        # pre-patch sources
  PROOF_LABEL=main-lint … node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs <evidence>/restricted-relay-live.mts
  git checkout HEAD -- <the two files above>                                   # restore

  # 2) regressions + hygiene
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/command/attempt-execution.completion-relay.test.ts \
    src/agents/subagents/completion/subagent-completion-instructions.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxfmt --check <changed files> && pnpm exec oxlint <changed files>
  ```

- **Evidence after fix:**

  ```text
  # real model, patched head, restricted relay turn (run-head-lint.json)
  wire request → https://<internal-maas>/model-cop/co-claw/v1/chat/completions  status 200
  wire request keys: model, messages, stream, stream_options, max_completion_tokens, reasoning_effort
  wire request "tools": <absent>          # the turn really had no execution surface
  prompt sent (OPENCLAW_CACHE_TRACE): "…This turn is a restricted relay: it has no execution,
    file, or session tools and cannot continue work or spawn follow-ups here. Relay the frozen
    child result truthfully and do not report this turn's tool restrictions as a task failure…"
    · contains continuation clause "require continued work or a follow-up": false
  model reply (1 provider call, no tool attempt):
    The lint gate finished: 41 of 44 files are clean. Three in-scope fixable lint errors remain:
    - `src/report/format.ts` — unused import
    - `src/report/summary.ts` — unused import
    - `src/report/csv.ts` — missing return type
    No new authority or user decision is required to fix them. Next step is to clean up those
    three files and re-run the lint gate to confirm everything passes.
  gateway response: status ok · summary completed · durationMs 11438 · provider zte · model co-claw

  # regressions through the real run seam (only the CLI/embedded runners mocked)
  ✓ attempt-execution.completion-relay.test.ts > rewrites completion guidance to relay-only on a restricted relay turn
  ✓ attempt-execution.completion-relay.test.ts > keeps continuation guidance on a trusted completion handoff turn
  ✓ subagent-completion-instructions.test.ts (3 tests)
  Test Files  2 passed (2) · Tests  5 passed (5) · oxfmt --check clean · oxlint clean
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** on the restricted (unverified-handoff) completion relay turn the real model relayed the frozen child outcome verbatim in its own words, recorded the follow-up work for a subsequent normal turn, made **no** tool call, and needed a single provider call. A second scenario (migration dry-run, same harness) shows the same shape: pre-patch the tool-free relay claimed execution it cannot perform (`Once you decide, I can apply it and run the real migration.`), patched it defers (`Let me know your preference and the next normal turn can pick that up and proceed.`).
- **Before evidence (real model, pre-patch sources, same scenario/provider):** the relay turn received the unconditional continuation clause and produced two real provider calls, both attempting an execution tool that the turn does not have:

  ```text
  wire request "tools": <absent>   # same restricted surface as the patched run
  model call 1 → "The lint gate finished with 3 in-scope fixable errors left, so I'll fix them now.
                  Let me inspect the three files.
                  [tool call id=chatcmpltoolb3960701a335ca71 name=exec] {"command":"cd …/workspace && sed -n '1,20p' src/report/format.ts && …"}
                  [tool result id=chatcmpltoolb3960701a335ca71 name=exec] Tool exec not found"
  model call 2 → user-visible payload:
                  Let me check which tools are available for editing and inspect the lint configuration.
                  [tool call id=chatcmpltool96a01a3x56bd1f8d name=exec] {"command":"cd …/workspace && ls -la && cat package.json …","interactive":true}
                  [tool result id=chatcmpltool96a01a3x56bd1f8d name=exec
                  ⚠️ Reply truncated at the model's output token limit. The text above is partial — ask to continue it.
  ```

  The completed child result was never relayed to the user. RED at the seam, same defect: `AssertionError: expected '[Inter-session message] …' to contain 'This completion ends one child run, n…'` — the received prompt still carried the continuation clause while `disableTools: true`.
- **How the restricted turn was produced:** the driver sent the shipped `agent` RPC the exact payload `sendSubagentAnnounceDirectly()` dispatches for an unverified completion handoff — `inputProvenance = {kind: "inter_session", sourceTool: "subagent_announce"}`, one `task_completion` internal event, `message: "Continue the OpenClaw runtime event."`, and **no** in-process delegated tool-policy capability (the shape a gateway restart or missing persisted child lineage produces). The agent config deliberately allowed `bash, read, write, message, sessions_spawn, subagents`, so the empty tool surface can only come from `resolveCompletionToolPolicy()`.
- **Proof boundaries (explicit):** the child's completion event is injected as the `agent` request payload instead of being produced by a live child run; the loopback recorder only observes and forwards every byte unmodified to the real endpoint, so the model call is real; one real-model sample per run, not a statistical claim.
- **Review-driven test trim:** per the ClawSweeper "low-value test" note, `subagent-completion-instructions.test.ts` dropped the constant-substitution and literal-wording assertions already made at the attempt boundary plus the `undefined` passthrough case; it keeps only what that seam cannot show (non-matching text stays byte-identical, the private-completion composer output is rewritable, task-completion event mapping is selective).
- **What was not tested:** no gateway-restart orchestration — the restricted branch is entered through the same unverified-envelope shape a restart recovery produces, asserted at the wire instead of by killing a live process. `pnpm tsgo:core` cannot run on this host at all — its `tsrs` native binary requires `GLIBC_2.32`+ and the host has glibc 2.31 — so type checking is left to CI. One pre-existing test in `attempt-execution.cli.test.ts` ("restricts completion tools for a capability without persisted child lineage") fails identically on untouched `origin/main` on this host (verified by control run); it is unrelated to this change. Repository CI lanes have not executed for this PR yet: the `CI` workflow run is `action_required` (fork PR awaiting maintainer approval), which is why `openclaw/ci-gate` currently reports failure.
- **Proof tier:** L3 (real-model behavior through the shipped gateway RPC surface, wire-captured tool surface and prompt, before/after contrast on the same scenario and provider) plus L2 regressions through the real run seam.
- **Proof limitations:** the child completion event is injected rather than produced by a live child run (see Proof boundaries); single real-model sample per run.
- **Review state:** real behavior proof supplied; awaiting CI approval + maintainer review.

prs.title: refactor(gateway): check forwarded node approvals once at sanitization
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

`node.invoke` re-checked a forwarded approval's liveness several times after the approval had already been accepted: in the policy liveness callback, again just before the raw transport after policy awaits, and in the registry's final `isDispatchAuthorized`. If the approval's retained binding changed while the node command was being prepared, a command that had already started was refused with "approved runtime authority closed before node dispatch".

The repo rule (AGENTS.md, "Choose good compromises") is to check authority one time, when work starts. Revocation applies to the next request, and a started request may finish.

## Change

- A forwarded approval is checked once, when the request starts, by the forwarded-approval sanitizer (`node-invoke-system-run-approval.ts`). That covers the decision's start check, provenance, target node, requester, command binding and allow-once consumption.
- Deleted: `isForwardedNodeInvokeApprovalAuthorityActive`, `resolveNodeInvokeRuntimeAuthorityError`, and their `node.invoke` uses (the policy liveness callback, the pre-raw-dispatch re-check, and the `isDispatchAuthorized` clause).
- Kept: the sanitizer, allow-once consumption, `retainForHandoff`, and the upload gate. `node.invoke` still passes the upload gate to the policy's final send through `isApprovalAuthorityActive`, and the raw-dispatch upload guard stays.
- Not in this PR: the approval-stage re-checks in `node-invoke-plugin-approval.ts` (next PR) and the lifecycle node-invoke completion check (separate chain).

Follows #201887 (node dispatch run authority checked once at caller entry).

## User impact

A node command whose forwarded approval was accepted is no longer refused because the approval's retained binding changed while the command was being prepared. A request whose approval is no longer usable is still refused at sanitization.

## Evidence

Proof tier: source (`ocx test`).

- 12 test files (`nodes.invoke*`, node-invoke plugin policy and private transport, system-run approval, computer transport, placement grants): 238 tests pass on current `main`. The upload-gate tests (disabled before lookup and during preparation) and the forwarded-approval admission test are kept.
- `pnpm tsgo`, `pnpm check:test-types`, oxlint, format, and the lifetime-check, line-cap, session-identity, mock-export and max-lines ratchets: pass.

Production −59 lines, tests −41 lines.
