prs.title: fix(gateway): upgrade state in place at start instead of refusing for copy space
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a new OpenClaw build started on state from an older release, the Gateway upgraded its databases in a private shadow:
1. It copied every migration input of the state directory, which on a real install includes large trees such as Codex session history.
2. It ran Doctor on the copy and swapped the results into place.

That had two costs:
- **Space.** The copy demanded twice its own size in free space. On a replica-shaped install with about 70 GiB to copy and about 100 GiB free, the new build refused to start, and the Git release launcher then switched back.
- **Extra copies.** Doctor inside the shadow also took its own original-state capture and full pre-migration backups.

Separately, if the migration committed and the new build still failed twice, the launcher switched back to a previous release that cannot open the newer schema.

## User Impact

- **No refusal for snapshot space.** The Gateway now upgrades state in place.
- **One image per outdated database, plus the config.** Before migrating, the start keeps each as `<file>.pre-<buildId>`:
  - a copy-on-write clone where the filesystem supports one, which takes about no space;
  - otherwise a byte copy, made only when it still leaves the migration its room;
  - otherwise no image, with a warning. Once that migration commits, the previous release cannot be restored.
- **Revert only on evidence.** A Git release trial that fails twice switches back only on positive evidence that the previous release opens what the revert leaves. Otherwise it stays on the new release, says why, and points to `openclaw triage`.
- **A narrower revert.**
  - It restores the outdated databases and the config from their images.
  - It removes the databases the run created.
  - It stays forward when Doctor moved a legacy source the previous release reads (for example `cron/jobs.json`).
  - It no longer restores other files Doctor changed in place, such as migrated workspace or legacy files. The old copy-and-swap restored those too.
- **Fallback is the only path that replaces a database file.** That is the generic rebuild after a failed Doctor chain. A successful start migrates `state/openclaw.sqlite` in place, so it stays the same file.

## Why This Change Was Made

The owner approved option D in the copy inventory, fix-plan items 8 and 9:
- migrate in place;
- keep a pre-image only for outdated databases (clone or skip);
- never refuse a start for snapshot space;
- revert only onto a build that opens the state.

Every schema step commits in one SQLite transaction with its version bump.

This head also repairs the data-safety findings of the landing round on `d533da100e2`, verdicts below. It holds one rule everywhere:
- delete or replace a file only after its replacement is durable and verified;
- a failure at any step leaves the previous state recoverable;
- the launcher reverts only on positive evidence.

The state machine section lists every file family and step against that rule.

**Boot upgrade (`src/state/state-upgrade.ts`, `state-upgrade-tree.ts`)**
- **Images.** Under the start's exclusive custody, each outdated database is checkpointed through SQLite and imaged by the repository's native clone (`copySqliteFile`, `@openclaw/fs-safe`).
  - A byte copy is made only when it leaves the migration its room.
  - An image that cannot be taken is skipped with a warning, including on a full disk reported through a wrapping error.
  - A leftover image from a finished run is replaced only by renaming the complete new image over it.
  - The config image is written 0600, read through a symlink.
- **Chain.** Doctor runs on the live state. The 2× copy budget, the shadow copy and its code (`copyTree`, `diffTree`, prefix rewriting) are gone.
- **Resume record.** The work directory holds a durable inventory: the files before Doctor, the databases the run started on and the images it published.
  - A start that dies or fails after its migration began keeps the record.
  - The next start reruns the chain on every database the run started on, imaged or not, against the images that run recorded. It never images such a database again or trusts a same-named leftover.
  - An interrupted record is removed only after the new one holds its facts.
- **Fallback.** It rebuilds each outdated database from the live file as the chain left it, so rows Doctor already imported stay; the image stays the rollback baseline.
  - First it folds an imaged database's live WAL in through SQLite. If SQLite reports the checkpoint busy or refuses the mode switch, the start stops with every file in place.
  - It swaps through the durable plan, which now also carries the run's additions.
- **Config refusal.** The state is put back only as a complete set: images of every database the run started on and of an unlinked config, and no legacy source Doctor moved. It is put back through a durable `restore.json` that the next start finishes if this one stops, and the databases the run created are removed. Otherwise the databases stay migrated and the start says why. A linked config is neither imaged nor written through.
- **Additions.** Only databases the run created, and their companions, are recorded for the launcher.
- **No image, no trial.** When a database the run starts on has no image, the start ends the Git release trial (the existing settle operation) before anything migrates. Doctor does the same when it finds a pending store outside the start's discovery, since no launcher restores Doctor's backup of it. This is what makes the first hop safe under an older launcher.
- **Custody.** The start holds schema-maintenance ownership and lends it to the Doctor child. If another process takes it in between, this start stops and leaves the upgrade to that process.

**Doctor (`flows/doctor-health.ts`, `commands/doctor-*.ts`)**
- The boot chain already passes the existing hidden internal handoff `--state-upgrade-live-state-dir`. No new flag, environment variable or config key was added.
- When that directory is Doctor's own state directory, Doctor takes no original-state capture. It takes no version migration backup set either (`preImageOwner: "state-upgrade"`), unless a pending store lies outside the start's own discovery (a configured agent directory); then it takes its normal set.
- The heartbeat retirement backup still runs.
- Standalone `openclaw doctor --fix` keeps its backups.

**Launcher (`src/infra/git-release-launcher.ts`)**

After two failed starts, before changing anything, it reverts only when all of these hold:
1. The previous release declares `openclaw.schemaVersions`.
2. `node:sqlite` is available.
3. The upgrade records and the agent listing are readable, and every database the revert would leave is readable and at or below that release's limit. A restored image with a WAL preserved beside it is read together in a private copy. That is the image it restores, else the live file; for shared state it checks both the header and `state.schema.contentVersion`, the same admission facts that release applies. Databases the revert removes as additions are skipped.
4. After an upgrade ran, an unlinked config has an image.
5. No legacy source the upgrade records (or an interrupted run's inventory) list is gone.

Anything else keeps the service forward, with a message that lists what was not proven. No new `.trial` field.

**Update behavior for published updaters**
- The boot upgrade is new-build code and applies on its first start after any update path.
- The launcher text is written by the installed updater (`publishGitRelease`), so this rule applies from the first update after the updater that ships it.
- **First hop.** The earlier launcher restores every `.pre-<buildId>` file newer than the trial, which includes this start's images, so a first-hop revert lands safely whenever every outdated database was imaged. When one has no image, this start ends the trial before migrating, so the earlier launcher never counts the failed starts and cannot revert onto a refusing release. What the earlier launcher still does not check is a legacy source Doctor moved; on the first hop, a revert after such a move leaves that source archived, as the copy-and-swap upgrade's revert did not (its Doctor ran in the shadow).

**Steps left to a person:** none. A start that cannot fit the migration says so, and resumes once space is free. A trial that stays forward points to `openclaw triage`.
## State machine of the start's upgrade

**Rule held at every step:** a file that may hold committed data is deleted or replaced only after its replacement is durable and verified. A failure at any step leaves the previous state recoverable. The launcher reverts only on positive evidence.

**File families the start touches:**
- Each outdated database `D`, with `D-wal`, `D-shm`, `D-journal` and `D.seal`.
- The config `C`, which can be a symlink.
- The pre-images `D.pre-<gen>` and `C.pre-<gen>`.
- The resume record `.upgrade-<gen>-<pid>-<t>/`. It holds `inventory.json` (`{files, outdated, images}`), `chain.log`, the fallback's `fallback/` builds, `plan.json` (fallback only) and `restore.json` (refusal only).
- The applied record `.upgraded-<gen>.json`.
- Legacy sources Doctor moves into SQLite, and its archives of them (`.migrated`, `.migrated.<n>`, `.migrated-<stamp>-<id>`, by owner). The start never deletes or renames these. A source missing after the run is recorded as a `remove` op, and it blocks every revert.

In the table, "Restart" is what the next start does. "Test" names the test that covers the row: unit tests are in `state-upgrade.test.ts` unless another file is named, the kill sweep is "sweep" and the fallback kill sweep is "fb-sweep".

| # | Step | Creates, replaces or deletes | If killed right after | Restart | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Resume scan | Finishes an interrupted `restore.json` (idempotent). Applies an interrupted durable `plan.json` (idempotent). Reads an interrupted record of this build and keeps it. Deletes other builds' plan-less records (scratch only). | Nothing new. | Same scan again. | `releases retained handles before finishing an interrupted plan`; `records the fallback's additions when its swap is interrupted and resumed` |
| 1 | Create the record | `.upgrade-<gen>-*` (empty); fsync of the state directory | A plan-less record without an inventory. | Resume with nothing changed yet: images are taken or kept, and the chain runs. | sweep `pre\|0` |
| 2 | Image each outdated `D` | Checkpoints `D` through SQLite (never deletes `D-wal`). Writes `D.pre-<gen>.partial-<pid>` and renames it to `D.pre-<gen>`, which replaces a finished run's leftover only by that rename. A full disk, wrapped or not, skips the image. On resume, a `D` the interrupted run started on keeps only the image that run recorded, else none; it is never imaged after it may have changed. | Partial or complete image; `D` unchanged. | No inventory yet, so nothing changed: images are retaken. | `images only the outdated databases…`; `migrates without an image when a copy…`; `skips the image when a copy layer wraps a full disk`; `replaces a leftover image…`; `resumes only with images the interrupted run published…`; sweep `pre\|0/5/20` |
| 3 | Image `C` | `C.pre-<gen>.partial` (mode 0600, exclusive create), fsync, rename, fsync of its directory. A full disk skips it. A linked `C` is never imaged or written: the config writer does not follow a final link. | Partial or complete config image; `C` unchanged. | As in 2. | `images a config privately, and never writes through a linked one`; `keeps a config outside the state directory as a pre-image` |
| 3a | End the Git release trial if any `D` has no image | Removes the trial record of the running release (the existing settle operation), before anything migrates. | Trial ended; nothing migrated. | No launcher counts failed starts, so none reverts onto a release that refuses the state; failures are fixed forward. | `resumes only with images…` (`onUnimaged` called once) |
| 4 | Write the inventory | `inventory.json` (`{files, outdated, images}`) via tmp, fsync, rename, then fsync of the directory. | A record that names the files before Doctor ran, the databases the run started on and the images it published. | Reuses both for the additions and the resume set. | `keeps a database it started on without an image in a resumed run` |
| 5 | Retire interrupted records | Deletes the older records of this build, whose facts are now merged into step 4's record. | One record. | Resume. | `keeps its record when the disk fills mid-chain…` |
| 6 | Normalize text and run the chain (Doctor in place) | Doctor's own SQLite transactions on `D` (each step commits with its version bump), the config rewrite and archives of moved sources. | Each `D` at its old or new version; record present. | Reruns the chain on every database the run started on, against the same images. | sweep `abs\|*`, `wal\|*`; `finishes a chain a kill interrupted…`; `keeps its record when the disk fills mid-chain…` |
| 7 | Validate and check conservation | Reads only. | As in 6. | As in 6. | sweep |
| 8F | Fallback: fold the live WAL of each imaged `D` | SQLite checkpoint plus `journal_mode=DELETE`. A busy or refused fold stops the start with every file in place. | As in 6. | As in 6. | `stops the fallback with the live WAL intact when SQLite cannot fold it in`; fb-sweep |
| 9F | Fallback: rebuild from the live `D` as the chain left it | Writes `fallback/D` inside the record and checkpoints it. The live `D` is unchanged, so Doctor's imports are kept. | As in 6, plus scratch output. | As in 6; the scratch output is discarded with the old record. | `keeps rows Doctor committed before the chain failed…`; fb-sweep `fallback\|*` |
| 10 | Admit the config. On refusal, restore the images. | Only a complete set is restored: every database the run started on and an unlinked `C` have an image, and no file from the inventory is gone. First `restore.json` (files, suffix, created databases) is written durably. Then for each imaged `D` it deletes `D-wal`/`-journal`/`-shm` and renames the image over `D` (fsynced at step 2), restores `C`, deletes the created databases with their companions, and removes the record. | Some `D` restored, the rest still migrated with their images; `restore.json` present. | The resume scan finishes the restore before anything else. | `a start refused for invalid config restores the previous state` (e2e); `keeps the state migrated when Doctor moved a legacy source a refusal cannot put back`; `finishes a refusal's restore that a stop interrupted before anything else`; `keeps a database it started on without an image…`; `migrates in place, keeps the pre-image…` |
| 11 | Record diagnostics | A row in the live state database (or the fallback's output). | As in 6. | As in 6 (one more diagnostic row). | sweep |
| 12F | Fallback: durable plan, then apply it | Fsyncs `fallback/D`, writes `plan.json` (replace ops, companion removals and the run's additions) via tmp, fsync and rename, then applies it. Apply order: link `D-wal` to `D-wal.pre-<gen>` only where `D` has no image (otherwise it was folded at 8F), remove the companions, keep `D.pre-<gen>` (the image, or a hard link of `D`), rename `fallback/D` to `D`. Every step is idempotent. | Durable plan, partly applied. | Applies the same plan to the end and records it (additions included). | `records the fallback's additions when its swap is interrupted and resumed`; fb-sweep `plan\|*` |
| 13 | Write the applied record | `.upgraded-<gen>.json` via tmp and rename. It lists the additions (created databases) and, as `remove` ops, legacy sources that are gone. The plan carries the same ops; removing an absent file is a no-op. | Applied record present; work record still present. | Chain mode: the record is plan-less, so the chain reruns as a no-op and finishes. Fallback: the plan is reapplied (idempotent). | `names only the databases it created as trial additions…`; fb-sweep `applied\|*` |
| 14 | Finish | Prunes older generations' `.pre-*` images (never this build's or a pinned one), older applied records and the work record. | Done. | Current: nothing to do. | `prunes only owned file generations…` |

**Launcher after two failed trial starts** (`git-release-launcher.ts`; this build's launcher only, see the first hop below):
- The revert set is every `<file>.pre-<gen>` with ctime at or after the trial, plus the config image.
- It reverts only when every check below passes. Otherwise the service stays forward, the trial record is removed, and the message lists what was not proven and names `openclaw triage`.
  1. The previous release declares `openclaw.schemaVersions`.
  2. `node:sqlite` is available.
  3. The upgrade records (applied record, plans, interrupted inventories) and the agent directory listing are readable, no legacy source they name is gone, and every database the revert would leave is readable (an image together with the WAL preserved beside it, read in a private copy), at or below the previous release's limit, and, for shared state, has a content version at or below it too. That is the image it restores, else the live file. Databases the revert removes as additions are skipped.
  4. After an upgrade ran, an unlinked config has an image.
- On revert, it restores state first and moves the link last. An interrupted revert reruns from the recorded restore list.
- Tests (`git-release.test.ts`): `stays on the new release when no pre-image…`, `…content version is newer behind an older header`, `…declares no schemas`, `…cannot be read`, `reverts only when the upgraded config has its image`, `reverts when the only newer database is one the revert removes` (also its WAL), `stays forward when Doctor moved a legacy source… (applied record / interrupted inventory)`, `removes a store an interrupted in-place run created when it reverts`, `reads a restored image together with the WAL preserved beside it`, `stays forward when an upgrade record cannot be read`, `switches back and restores the pre-image…`, `stays on the new release when the image it would restore is newer too`, `resumes an interrupted rollback…`, `keeps a family's restored WAL…`.
## Landing round on `d533da100e2`: verdicts

Each "real" verdict comes with a test that fails on `d533da100e2` and passes on this head. The `state-upgrade.test.ts` and `git-release.test.ts` runs were swapped to the `d533da100e2` source to show the failure.

1. **Fallback deleted a live WAL when it could not checkpoint it** (`state-upgrade.ts:600-606` at `d533da100e2`). **Real.**
   - Fix: the fallback folds the live WAL in through SQLite and checks the result. If the checkpoint is busy or the mode switch is refused, it stops and deletes nothing.
   - Test: `stops the fallback with the live WAL intact when SQLite cannot fold it in`. A reader's open snapshot keeps a committed `update_runs` row only in the WAL.
2. **Launcher read only the header** (`git-release-launcher.ts:161-165`). **Real.**
   - Fix: shared state is judged by the header and `state.schema.contentVersion`. Anything unreadable blocks the revert.
   - Tests: `stays forward when the shared content version is newer behind an older header`, `…when a database it would leave cannot be read`, `…when the previous release declares no schemas`.
3. **Fallback from the images dropped rows Doctor had imported** (`:609-619`). **Real**: the rebuild read the image, while Doctor had already archived the moved sources.
   - Fix: the rebuild reads the live databases as the chain left them.
   - Test: `keeps rows Doctor committed before the chain failed in the fallback rebuild`.
4. **A database without an image was forgotten on resume** (`:453-463`). **Real**: the resume set was "still outdated or imaged".
   - Fix: the durable inventory records every database the run started on.
   - Test: `keeps a database it started on without an image in a resumed run`. That refusal now reports that nothing can be restored instead of restoring a partial set.
5. **Config image not private through a symlink** (`:528-533`). **Real**: `copyFileSync` carried the target's 0644.
   - Fix: the image is created 0600 with exclusive create.
   - Test: `keeps the config image private when the config is a link to a shared file`.
6. **First hop is governed by the old launcher** (`:503-515`). **Real for a skipped image; fixed.** The old launcher restores the images, so only a skipped image was unsafe.
   - Fix: when a database the run starts on has no image, the start ends the trial before migrating, through the existing settle operation that a serving Gateway already performs.
   - Test: `resumes only with images…` asserts the hook fires once.
   - Limit: the wiring to the real trial file is not covered by a test.
7. **Launcher counted databases the revert removes** (`git-release-launcher.ts:233-240`). **Real.**
   - Fix: the additions in the applied record and in interrupted plans are skipped.
   - Test: `reverts when the only newer database is one the revert removes`.
8. **Fallback additions lost across an interrupted swap** (`:705-709`). **Real**: the durable plan held only replacements.
   - Fix: the plan carries the additions.
   - Test: `records the fallback's additions when its swap is interrupted and resumed`. It interrupts the swap's first rename, then resumes.
9. **A wrapped full-disk error aborted the start** (`state-upgrade-tree.ts:450-459`). **Real**: only the top-level error was inspected.
   - Fix: causes and aggregated errors are walked, for both full disk and the space admission.
   - Test: `skips the image when a copy layer wraps a full disk`.

Two extra changes, found while writing the state machine:
- A leftover image of a finished run was deleted before its replacement existed. It is now replaced only by rename.
- The inventory was not fsynced before the interrupted records were removed. It now is.

## Rating round on `fa77fc2f102` (this PR's own round): verdicts

That round rated F / F / F with nine findings. Fixed failing-first on `2ab365b0946`, each red against `fa77fc2f102`:

1. **(P1) A refusal or revert dropped Doctor's imported legacy sources** (cron `jobs.json` archived as `.migrated`). **Real.** The fix is described under the next round's item 3, which replaced this round's first attempt (renaming `.migrated` archives back, which missed other owners' archive names).
2. **(P1) First hop with a skipped image.** **Real; fixed** as in item 6 above.
3. **(P1) Doctor's exemption was directory-wide.** **Real.**
   - Fix: Doctor keeps its normal backup set when a pending store lies outside the start's discovery.
   - Test: `copies only when Doctor owns the image (…, outside the start's discovery=true)`.
   - Not changed: the launcher still cannot see an agent database configured outside the state directory. The earlier launcher and the copy-and-swap upgrade had the same gap.
4. **(P1) An image was read without the WAL preserved beside it.** **Real.**
   - Fix: the pair is read together in a private copy.
   - Test: `reads a restored image together with the WAL preserved beside it`.
5. **(P1) Config symlink handling.** **Real.**
   - Fix: a linked config is neither imaged nor written through, and the launcher does not require its image.
   - Test: `images a config privately, and never writes through a linked one (linked: true)`, using a read-only link target.
6. **(P1) Resume trusted a leftover same-build image.** **Real.**
   - Fix: the inventory records the images the run published; resume keeps only those.
   - Test: `resumes only with images the interrupted run published, never a leftover`.
7. **(P2) An unreadable inventory was treated as empty.** **Real.**
   - Fix: an unreadable record, plan or agent listing keeps the service forward.
   - Test: `stays forward when an upgrade record cannot be read`.
8. **(P2) A created database's companions were left behind.** **Real.**
   - Fix: the launcher removes them with the database; the dead companion filter is gone.
   - Test: the WAL assertion in `reverts when the only newer database is one the revert removes`.
9. **(P2) Test-line budget.** **Real.**
   - Shared test helpers were consolidated.
   - The remaining growth is one test per state-machine row and per launcher rule, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/201716-in-place-state-upgrade.txt` with that reason.

## Rating round on `2ab365b0946` (this PR's own round): verdicts

That round rated F / F / F with six findings. Each fix below fails on `2ab365b0946` and passes on this head:

1. **(P1) An interrupted refusal restore consumed images.** **Real.**
   - Fix: a durable `restore.json` is written first, and the resume scan finishes it before anything else.
   - Test: `finishes a refusal's restore that a stop interrupted before anything else`, which stops at the second image rename.
2. **(P1) Configured agent stores outside the state directory were outside the launcher's view.** **Real.**
   - Fix: Doctor, as the start's chain, ends the Git release trial before migrating such a store, and keeps its normal backup set.
   - Test: `settleRunningGitReleaseTrial` is asserted in `copies only when Doctor owns the image (…, outside=true)`.
3. **(P1) Archive names differ by owner** (`.migrated-<stamp>-<id>` for auth profiles). **Real.**
   - Fix: instead of mirroring each owner's archive naming, the start compares its inventory. A file that existed before Doctor and is gone after is a moved legacy source; it blocks the refusal restore and is recorded as a `remove` op that blocks every revert. An interrupted run's inventory is read the same way by the launcher.
   - Tests: `keeps the state migrated when Doctor moved a legacy source…`, `stays forward when Doctor moved a legacy source… (applied record / interrupted inventory)`.
4. **(P2) Stores created before the applied record were missed.** **Real.**
   - Fix: the launcher treats `.sqlite` files absent from an interrupted run's inventory as additions, and a refusal restore removes the run's created databases.
   - Test: `removes a store an interrupted in-place run created when it reverts`.
5. **(P1) Directory entries not synced.** **Real.**
   - Fix: the state directory is fsynced after the record is created, and the config's directory after its image.
   - No test; this is a power-loss property.
6. **(P3) Docs overstated the guarantees.** **Real.** The update guide now states Doctor's remaining backups, the complete-set refusal rule, the revert conditions and which launcher governs the first hop.

**Product question it raised:** boot repair still changes workspace files in place that neither a refusal nor a revert restores. The coordinator accepted this narrower revert for this PR ("state the narrower revert plainly"); it is stated under User Impact and in the docs.
## Evidence

**In-place kill sweep through the real `gateway run` boot**
- Setup: 37 SIGKILLs on the 2026.10.10 release corpus (state v22, agents v27). The corpus holds about 180,000 transcript rows and an updater `update_runs` row written before the restart.
- Kill points:
  - fixed times from 1.25 s to 44 s;
  - 0, 5 and 20 ms after the first image;
  - when the WAL grows and at 30 KB;
  - 0 and 50 ms after the applied record.
- Checks after every kill:
  1. `integrity_check` is ok.
  2. `user_version` equals `schema_meta` and is exactly the old or the new version.
  3. Every pre-existing witness row is unchanged.
  4. A migrated database equals the uninterrupted run.
- Each surviving image is intact at the old version. The rerun serves and equals the uninterrupted run.
- Result on this head: rerun pending on this head (37 of 37 passed on `d533da100e2`).

**Fallback kill sweep (new)**
- Setup: the same corpus. The start's upgrade runs with the real Doctor chain, then an injected `ChainStepError`, so the generic rebuild runs (`fallback-driver.mts` calls `upgradeStateDirectory` with `createDoctorChain` and throws after Doctor).
- Kill points:
  - 0 and 50 ms after the first image;
  - 8 to 36 s inside Doctor;
  - 0 to 4 s into the fallback build;
  - 0, 5 and 40 ms after `plan.json`;
  - 0 and 30 ms after the applied record.
- Checks: the same checks after the kill. Then the real `gateway` start with no fault must finish, serve, reach v40/v43, and keep every witness row.
- An uninterrupted fallback run ends in `mode: fallback`, at v40/v43, with the images at v22/v27, and serves.
- Result: 16 of 16 passed on `9061cf9fc6f`; rerun pending on this head.

**Real updater into this build (macOS launchd Git source checkout install, release mode)**
- Setup:
  - its own profile, state directory and port;
  - a synthetic config with no channels, providers or credentials;
  - a 512 MiB agent database at schema 42;
  - the real `openclaw update --channel dev --yes`.
- Installed side: `6691acae` (the last commit before the 42 → 43 agent-schema bump) + #201463 + #201600 + this PR's launcher, built. The launcher is written by the installed updater, so only an updater that ships it can run the new rule.
- Target: this PR's head, and for the failing-candidate runs, this head plus an e2e-only patch that exits right after the state upgrade.
- Results: rerun pending on this head (busy and idle passed on `d533da100e2`: exit 0, schema 43, trial settled, writer alive, run `succeeded`)

**`update_runs` rows the updater wrote just before the restart** survive:
- the in-place path (sweep witness, unit test);
- the fallback (unit tests `keeps the update run … (fallback)` and `keeps rows Doctor committed …`, and the fallback sweep witness).



## Not proven or not changed

- **Doctor's repair-specific backups.** The credential cutover image for state below v29 and the legacy cron and session repairs still take their own scoped images. Routing them through the same owner decision is a follow-up.
- **First-hop revert with a skipped image** (see "Update behavior").
- **Boot time limit.** The 30-minute chain timeout is unchanged. In-place boot is about 50 s for about 230 MB of databases here; 4 GiB was not measured.
- **Platforms.** PostgreSQL, Windows, and Linux filesystems without clones were not run. Their byte-copy-or-skip path is covered by unit tests.
- **Review tooling.** `autoreview` does not run on this machine; an independent reviewer agent and ClawSweeper rating rounds reviewed the diff instead.

prs.title: improve: reduce repeated prompt estimation before agent replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preparing an embedded agent reply scans the same large system prompt once for context assembly and again for foreground token budgeting when the prompt has not changed. Earlier work shared estimates within each phase, but the fixed-request estimator started too late to connect them.

Related: #190952, #196651.

## User Impact

Agent reply preparation does less repeated CPU work. Token budgets, compaction/preemption decisions, prompt bytes and tool definitions stay identical; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Create the existing attempt estimator during context-engine prompt preparation and carry it through prepared history into the foreground phase. Its existing exact-string and tool-definition checks still re-estimate changed prompts and tools. Engine additions and prompt hooks are therefore safe; unconditional reuse of an earlier prompt estimate would be incorrect.

The rendered-pressure owner now consumes prepared system facts directly, removing the duplicate preemption branch. Production grows by 14 lines for the explicit cross-phase handoff; no new cache or module-level state is introduced.

## Evidence

Five interleaved baseline/candidate owner runs, each with 500 warmups and 1,000 measured preparations: ten synthetic sessions, 360 mixed CJK/tool/image messages per session, 40,600-character instructions, 5,160-character input and 100 frozen tool schemas.

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median main-thread CPU/preparation | 1.969 ms | 1.367 ms (−30.6%) |
| Median within-run p95 | 2.059 ms | 1.469 ms (−28.7%) |
| Sampled allocation/preparation | 622,665 B | 621,896 B (effectively unchanged) |
| Characters scanned/preparation | 127,051 | 86,451 |
| Scans/preparation | 4 | 3 |

Owner A/A median CPU was 1.974600/1.980739 ms (0.31% variation); request-loop allocation A/A varied by 0.41%. All output fingerprints match. A changed-system control retains four scans and identical outputs on both versions. Acceptance required exact numeric parity, fewer scans/lower CPU, stable allocation and no >20% latency regression. Measurements cover the preparation owner, not Gateway startup, provider latency or durable I/O.

`pnpm check:changed` passed. 153 focused tests passed, including prompt-prefix stability, pressure/budgets, replay, assembly/source scopes, history and foreground preparation. The new regression follows assembly into the foreground phase for unchanged and extended prompts. On the exact parent, the unchanged case fails with two scans instead of one while the extended-prompt control passes; the final foreground test file passes all 27 tests. An independent synthetic differential compared 180 complete budget, preemption and fresh-request vectors against the parent implementation, including CJK, images, tool calls, huge prompts and rounding boundaries: exact equality.

Codex autoreview of the local candidate against `697b15678be8b` was scoped-clean through P2; no accepted/actionable findings. The review included the prepared-history and preflight callers. It did not independently run the tests or benchmarks.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs \
  scripts/perf/context-engine-lifecycle-bench.ts \
  --iterations 1000 --long-context --foreground
```

Use `--owner <parent-context-engine-lifecycle.ts>` for the pinned baseline lifecycle owner, `--counts` for separate scan counts, `--allocations` for sampled allocation, and `--system-addition` for invalidation. Shared estimator dependencies are held constant in the owner timing comparison; the differential checks use parent snapshots of all changed estimation owners.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-phase.test.ts \
  src/agents/sessions/context-token-pressure.test.ts \
  src/agents/sessions/compaction/request-budget.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/preemptive-compaction.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/preemptive-compaction.replay.test.ts \
  src/agents/harness/context-engine-lifecycle.test.ts \
  src/agents/harness/context-engine-source-scope.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-history-prepare.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Focused wrapper wall time: 74.52 seconds, including cold compiler generation. CI timing will be available on this PR.
</details>

prs.title: fix(update): keep a launched candidate's restart failure free of a data-risk mark
prs.body:
## Problem

After a migrated update, `finishUpdate` holds `rollbackBlockedReason = state-migrated-no-rollback` for the rest of the run. `completeUpdateCommandResult` stamps any later `status: error` with that block as `dataAtRisk`. The run then ends with "Keep the Gateway stopped: data at risk (state-migrated-no-rollback)".

The commonest error at that point is a restart health failure. The candidate started and answered as the new version, then missed core readiness inside the budget: a slow sidecar, a refused agent database, a plugin reload. That candidate is running on the state it migrated. Nothing shows the state was damaged. Yet the run records a data risk, the guidance tells the operator to keep a running Gateway stopped, and `openclaw update repair` refuses to finish the run, because it never clears a recorded risk. The mark comes from the restart failing, not from anything observed about the data.

The same failure also printed `Rollback: reinstall OpenClaw <previous version> ...` from the restart verifier, even though older code cannot read the migrated state.

This is audit entry 1 ("blanket `rollbackBlockedReason` stamp"), for its highest-traffic producer: the restart.

## Rule

A data-at-risk mark needs positive evidence. After `restart-health-failed`, the block is released only on launch evidence read **after** readiness failed:

- the native service runtime still reports the process that answered. This reuses `readFailedUpdateGatewayState`, which keeps the recorded identity only while the same PID is still running, so a candidate that exited or was replaced during polling is no evidence;
- that process owns **every** listener on the Gateway port (fresh port inspection, the restart inspector's ownership rule). A version answered by another process on any bind address is no evidence, and neither is an unattributed listener;
- that process's recorded version equals the candidate's version, with no build mismatch, and its recorded build equals the candidate's build whenever the update knows it;
- the version it replaced is known and differs.

When it is released:

- the result is the restart-health failure (`readyz-unhealthy`). Restart stays unsafe (`runtime-verification-failed`), with no `dataAtRisk`;
- rollback is not attempted. It would hand the migrated state to a build that cannot read it. `rollbackOutcome` records `not-attempted: state-migrated-no-rollback`, so status and report readers keep the migration fact.

While any rollback block is set, or the recorded rollback outcome is a refusal (the final-recovery pass), the restart verifier drops the reinstall advice. It prints `Rollback: unavailable; update state was migrated, ...` for `state-migrated-no-rollback`, or `Rollback: unavailable; rollback safety could not be verified, ...` for `rollback-state-unverified` (for example, PostgreSQL state with no pre-activation baseline).

Everything else keeps the mark exactly as before:

| Restart observation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Candidate still running with its PID and owning the port, answered as the new version, health failed | data at risk, rollback attempted (and refused by the migration check) | restart-health failure, no data risk, no rollback |
| Restart accepted, but no process ran (queued task, start never happened) | data at risk | data at risk |
| Restart command failed | data at risk | data at risk |
| Candidate answered, then exited while readiness was polled | data at risk | data at risk |
| Another process replaced the one that answered | data at risk | data at risk |
| A different process owns the port that answered | data at risk | data at risk |
| Port busy, listener owner unattributed | data at risk | data at risk |
| Managed PID owns one bind address, another process owns a second | data at risk | data at risk |
| Update knows the candidate build, answer named none | data at risk | data at risk |
| Match flag left by an earlier observation, wrong version | data at risk | data at risk |
| Port answered as the candidate, but no service PID (including after a Gateway-triggered update recorded its own PID) | data at risk | data at risk |
| Same version, different build | data at risk | data at risk |
| Version unchanged by the update, or previous version unknown | data at risk | data at risk |
| Split-root update (original-service compensation) | data at risk | data at risk (unchanged path) |
| Runtime or record unreadable | data at risk | data at risk |

An accepted restart or "start attempted" is not treated as launch evidence. That gap is why #201529 was closed.

## Change

- `update-command-verification.ts`, which owns the recorded activation facts and the restart failure report:
  - `releaseLaunchedMigration` applies the rule above.
  - The health-fact producer now always writes `pid`. Before, a PID-less observation omitted the key, so the merge kept the previous process's PID.
  - The failure advice honors the rollback refusal.
- `update-command-post-update.ts`: passes the refusal to the restart and calls the release after the existing `activationVerified` branch. Net: four lines.
- `update-command-service.ts` and `update-command-service-context-types.ts`: forward `rollbackRefused` to the verifier.
- `scripts/tests/update-restart-module-outcome.mjs`: the vm fixture exposes the new export from the real verification module, as it already does for its siblings.

No config key, stored field, schema value or exit code changes. `rollbackOutcome.reason` is free text, and this reuses the existing reason. The only text change is the verifier's rollback line, shown only when a block is set. None of #201668's files are touched.

## What is left to a person

For the converted case:
- The run ends as a restart-health failure. The existing next step names `openclaw update repair`, `openclaw gateway status --deep` and `openclaw triage`.
- Repair is no longer blocked by a data-risk mark it cannot clear.
- Whatever makes the candidate unhealthy (a channel, an agent database, a plugin) still needs its owner's fix. The readiness report names it.

For the cases that keep the mark, the existing steps remain. They stay manual because no running build has been shown to own the migrated state, and starting one automatically is exactly what the mark exists to prevent.

## Evidence

Exact base `0eb6488cd3c`, head `b1407681922`. The same test files run at both. Only the four product files above are swapped.

- Red, base, finalizer rows: for both launched-candidate rows the finalizer still calls rollback (which the migration check refuses) and stamps the data risk. All thirteen negative controls pass, so they hold the existing behavior. The split-root contract test fails because the owner function does not exist on base. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20422972-71ad-4b40-9ed9-d72fecef60ff
- Red, base, verifier: the stale PID survives a PID-less observation, and reinstall advice is printed while rollback is refused, in the restart pass, the final-recovery pass and the unverified-baseline case. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ecf03a68-8faf-40a2-a18b-4f0d91483413
- Green, head: all 21 pass. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3588d94c-cb49-4794-b3d2-10731f349167

Each guard is mutation-proven. With the guard removed, the named control fails:

| Guard removed | Failing control |
|---|---|
| live runtime re-read (recorded snapshot only) | candidate exited, process replaced |
| listener owned by the managed PID | listener not owned, listener unattributed |
| every listener owned (any one is enough) | listener shared |
| known previous version | previous version unknown |
| candidate build required when known | build not answered |
| version equality (match flag only) | stale match flag |
| `versionMatch !== false` | build mismatch |
| `serviceRunning === true` | candidate exited (recorded) |
| service PID | no service PID |
| version changed | version unchanged |
| split-root exclusion | split-root contract test |
| producer clears `pid` | `clears an earlier process's PID when the running service reports none` |
| refusal-aware rollback advice | `offers the previous version only while rollback is allowed (refusal=restart)` |
| recorded refusal honored in final recovery | `... (refusal=recorded)` |
| refusal-specific wording | `... (refusal=unverified)` |

Checks on head:
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` are clean.
- The line-cap ratchet passes; `update-command-post-update.ts` stays within 700.
- Affected suites, 10 files, 0 failures: `update-command-post-update-repair`, `-post-update-recovery`, `-post-update`, `-verification`, `-service`, `-database-rollback`, `-lifecycle`, `-original-service`, `test/scripts/update-restart-module-outcome`, `test/scripts/eager-import-closure`. These ran on the same product tree before the rebase over unrelated main commits (UI locales, automations, Doctor image candidate, Gateway history, plugins). None of them touch update, port, restart or daemon code.

Review so far:
- An independent review found no blocker. Its findings are addressed: the stale PID merge, keeping the migration fact on record, the split-root path, the unchanged version, and weak assertions.
- ClawSweeper round 1 found two P2s, both addressed. Facts read before readiness polling could describe a candidate that had since exited; the live re-read now covers that. The verifier printed reinstall advice despite the refusal; that is now refusal-aware.
- ClawSweeper round 2 (patch tier C) found three more, all addressed. A version answer was not tied to the managed PID; the listener ownership check now does that. The final-recovery verifier pass still offered reinstall; it now honors the recorded refusal. The base comparison said "rolled back"; it now says the finalizer calls a rollback that the migration check refuses.

- ClawSweeper round 3 (last round) found four. All four are fixed in this head, because each one either dropped the mark on ambiguous evidence or printed a false message. A version answer could come from a non-owned listener on another bind address; every listener must now be owned. An unknown predecessor version passed the "changed" check; it now has to be known. A version answered without a build passed while the update knew the build; the build is now required. "State was migrated" was printed for the PostgreSQL no-baseline refusal; that refusal now has its own wording.

### Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Real-path proof of the restart verifier feeding this check. The finalizer tests fake the restart outcome and write the facts the verifier would record. The producer-side PID behavior and the advice are tested on the real verifier.
- A real Docker cell (see below).
- The remaining audit catch-alls, by owner: migration/rollback (`update-command-rollback.ts` default and catch, `update-command-database-backup.ts` rollback-start and `assertRollbackSafe`), Doctor classifier and preflight (`doctor-maintenance-inspection.ts`), Git legacy pre-Doctor mark (`update-runner-git.ts`), and service recovery admission (`update-command-service-recovery.ts`).

### Not yet proven

There is no real Docker cell yet for package or Git release-mode with a live, write-loaded Gateway where the candidate launches and then misses core readiness. A cell needs a fault that makes the candidate answer as the new version while core readiness stays red, after a real state migration, and only in the candidate. I have not found a deterministic fault for that without a product test hook. The coverage above runs the real `finishUpdate`, rollback selection, ledger, live-runtime re-read, recovery and guidance code, with only the service manager, the restart outcome and the rollback executor faked.

prs.title: fix(ci): keep mixed extension batches off Boat runners
prs.body:
Closes #201663
Related: #201116

## What Problem This Solves

Hourly Extension Tests repeatedly lost a mixed extension batch to Boat memory exhaustion after setup succeeded. The provider reported a process exceeding 7,428 MiB RAM plus 6,143 MiB swap; the test step exited 137.

## User Impact

Mixed extension batches keep their existing Blacksmith runners. Boat remains available for file-bounded extension shards under the same maximum of 20 starts per hourly run. Every test, worker limit, deadline, and hosted manual/retry route is preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider adapter now admits only file-bounded extension shards to Boat. Mixed batches can contain multiple concurrent config groups and are not qualified by the file-shard measurements. Skipped batches do not consume the Boat allowance, leaving it available to later file shards. This restores the established runner placement without speculative memory-size increases or a new configuration option.

## Evidence

- Two observed OOM failures: [04:39 run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44459817245/job/135344291352) and [05:39 run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44466669217/job/135366698620). Both failed during tests with exit 137 and the provider RAM/swap warning. A [recent all-Blacksmith hourly run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44452942906) passed; this is comparison evidence at another head, not exact-head runtime proof.
- Direct execution of the actual workflow admission code: base routed five mixed batches to Boat; the fix routed none. All 25 fixture rows remained present and 20 file shards still used Boat. Zero budget and inactive matrices retained Blacksmith.
- The existing complete-manifest regression now requires mixed batches to stay on Blacksmith and checks that every non-Boat row preserves its original placement and metadata.
- [Exact-head draft CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44471576261) completed successfully, including all five active Node test jobs, workflow/lint checks, typechecking, docs and baseline ratchets. Formatting and diff checks also passed. CI supplied the dependency-backed checks because this code-only worktree has no qualified local installation; no shared dependencies were changed.
- Local ClawSweeper review completed for `11b65598aa4d6b56ce786a611efbb172775a165b..2fe47c7d3a725783cecae992cdd0c6374fcc5525`; no actionable correctness or security findings. Live hourly routing has been observed as detailed below. Merged as `0fee5ad0d21429bb77d6767caf5d72238e6525a2`; merged workflow verified and repository backend restored to `boat`. [Required PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44473240777) passed with 30 successful and 30 skipped jobs. Live routing is now verified in six completed scheduled runs (44516778735 through 44568507741): all retained 55 extension shards, selected 0–20 Boat file shards according to headroom, and placed zero mixed batches on Boat. Five runs passed, including the [latest run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44568507741). The [remaining failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44557207167/job/135677128452) was a Signal assertion in `event-handler.partial-delivery.test.ts` (expected two calls, got three; exit 1), not runner setup or OOM. No quota or OOM failures were observed in this six-run sample.

prs.title: fix(macos): complete OpenClaw ID sign-in inside the app
prs.body:
Related: #144596 (the same popup-host boundary affects session navigation; this PR fixes account sign-in only).

## What Problem This Solves

“Sign in with OpenClaw ID” in the Mac app can do nothing, while the same local Gateway works in a browser. The web flow reserves a popup that the Mac host discards, and an external browser cannot return the sign-in through the app’s separate browser storage.

## User Impact

User impact: local OpenClaw ID sign-in has an app-owned login window and returns to the original Control UI account menu, without moving the chat into an external browser.

**Verification: native compilation, all 8 WebKit cases, and live staging-issuer sign-in in the original app now have reporter-run evidence below. The reporter’s enabled-but-dead real-Gateway before capture is included; a controlled same-environment comparison and the remaining full-app checklist are not claimed.** Both the Mac app and its Gateway-served Control UI need this change. Browser cookies/tokens are not imported: an existing Safari/Chrome login does not automatically authenticate the app.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing Gateway PKCE and code-redemption owner. A reply-capable native bridge presents the Gateway-issued authorization URL in an unprivileged WebKit window and returns the matching callback to the initiating app document. The Control UI then redeems the code and stores its account through its existing owner.

The login window shares the app’s website data store but receives none of the dashboard’s native handlers or injected scripts. Requests are limited to the current dashboard main frame and its callback path; close, document replacement, and timeout settle the pending presentation. Generic popup/link policy, remote device-grant admission, and native claw-enrollment sign-in are unchanged. No configuration, schema, or dependency changes.

Simplification/test audit: removed two redundant mocked popup-helper call-shape checks. Retained independent unsafe-URL, account/menu, sign-out, and browser geometry contracts. Added the native WK transport regression rather than treating synthesized storage events as native sign-in proof.

## Evidence

### Live in-app sign-in — passed

[Jacqueline’s verification report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201642#issuecomment-7015963875) confirms the native app and matching loopback Gateway ran in a disposable Tart VM on **macOS 26.6.2**, using fork source `a466cbebb10c7a9bdee211026b3ea2963eeed415`. Authentication against the **live staging issuer** returned to the original in-app dashboard, which showed **Signed in to OpenClaw ID** and **Sign out of OpenClaw ID** in its account menu. This was not merely a successful external-browser login.

**Before — enabled sign-in action on the reporter’s real Gateway**

![Before: the reporter’s real Mac Gateway shows the enabled Sign in with OpenClaw ID action, with its arrow and no setup-disabled message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/972e6fa6-8395-4fd7-9c22-65b2d61e7507)

Jacqueline reports that clicking this enabled action does nothing on her real Gateway. The screenshot shows web app commit `e69daeb6bc3d` and the enabled menu entry, not the “OpenClaw ID is not set up” state. This is the primary before evidence for the reported bug; the click non-response is the reporter’s observation.

**After — original Mac dashboard following live sign-in**

![After: the original Mac dashboard shows Signed in to OpenClaw ID and Sign out of OpenClaw ID; account identity is redacted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/2508ae0aa06812b0fc381cf7deaa4317b1434f91/pr-evidence/201642/after-sign-in.png)

The real-Gateway before capture and the successful Tart after capture show the reported failure state and the verified outcome in different environments; they are not a same-environment, matched-theme comparison. Both captures were inspected before embedding.

**Separate VM setup state:** the [earlier `428d204…` VM screenshot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2926e47-7f78-455a-8eb5-ce59af57221e) shows an unconfigured, setup-disabled sign-in action. It is retained only as setup context and is **not** the reporter’s dead-button reproduction.

### Native build and WebKit boundary — passed

- [Native build and test job](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/44470547318/job/135378658400): native test bundle built successfully; Swift Testing reports **3 parameterized tests / all 8 cases passed in 11.465 seconds**. The earlier XCTest wrapper’s “0 tests” is not the result being counted.
- The executed cases cover callback code delivery, issuer denial, wrong state, closing the login/dashboard, subframe requests, documents outside the mount, and callbacks outside the mount. They exercise the real WK message transport and callback navigation with a synthetic HTTP issuer, not a JavaScript replacement for the native receiver. The separate live-issuer result is above.
- [Before/after bundle run](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/44470547437): both [before `428d2047b766fcf0e8d426c1d967b0c8697b8625`](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/44470547437/job/135378658632) and [after `a466cbebb10c7a9bdee211026b3ea2963eeed415`](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/44470547437/job/135378658202) app bundles built and were uploaded. Building both bundles is not a live before/after sign-in comparison.

### Revision binding

The [proof workflow revision](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/commit/410ed1a87bb0ee1cfcf091b3f6fcbdf1fd7e61d6) explicitly checks out and verifies fork source `a466cbebb10c7a9bdee211026b3ea2963eeed415`. That source and this PR’s head `0098679b5d71078a259b3915ca4f9b0b651acb84` share parent `fb63d409d0232d417bd297970a334bf878cd7f60` and the same sole one-line correction: `message.world === WKContentWorld.page`. The native presenter, dashboard controller, native regression, UI bridge/account implementation, Swift package inputs, root package manifest, and pnpm lockfile were also compared byte-for-byte and match. These are source-equivalent fork results, **not upstream exact-head CI statuses**; the earlier draft-stage skipped native CI jobs are not counted as passes.

### Existing client-contract checks

- The two native client-routing cases were red against the unchanged production source, then green with this change: a native callback is redeemed and stored in the app’s account owner, and cancellation does not fall back to an external browser. This is client-contract proof, separate from the executed Mac tests.
- 50 focused external-URL, account-menu and account/sign-out tests passed locally (Vitest 2.69 seconds; wrapper 3.57 seconds). UI typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, TypeScript/Markdown formatting, native i18n verification, documentation link audit, and `git diff --check` passed. The later Swift qualification did not change those inputs.
- The earlier [macOS compile failure](https://github.com/jjjhenriksen/openclaw/actions/runs/44468842162) is superseded by the successful native build above. The content-world identity check remains intact.
- Local Auto Review timed out without a report. The [earlier hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201642#issuecomment-7001283648) reported no actionable findings on `fb63d409d0232d417bd297970a334bf878cd7f60`; it predates the qualification and this evidence update.

**Remaining evidence limits:** the real-Gateway before screenshot accompanies the reporter’s click-failure observation; there is no native red-on-base run, controlled same-environment clean/annotated before/after pair, or separately reported full live persistence/relaunch and browser-parity checklist. Native fixture cancellation passed; that does not imply every live cancellation/retry scenario was exercised. No broader provider-method compatibility or merge-readiness claim is made.

[Full Tart, GitHub Actions, red/green and full-app test directions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0098679b5d71078a259b3915ca4f9b0b651acb84/docs/platforms/mac/openclaw-id-sign-in-testing.md).

prs.title: fix(update): build and serve Git releases outside node_modules
prs.body:
## Problem

#201874: on a managed Git install, a Gateway MCP turn fails before replying:

```text
warn mcp-loopback request handling failed: Stripping types is currently unsupported for files under node_modules, for "<state-dir>/git-install/releases/<release>/lib/node_modules/openclaw/extensions/deepseek/web-search-contract-api.ts"
error Embedded agent failed before reply: Claude Code started without the OpenClaw MCP server (status failed).
```

#199706 put each Git release, a full worktree with plugin TypeScript sources, at `releases/<id>/lib/node_modules/openclaw`. Two path rules then meet:

1. `resolvePublicSurfacePath` (`src/plugins/public-surface-runtime.ts`) picks `extensions/<plugin>/<file>.ts` before `dist` when the source exists. Only a Git release has sources; the npm package ships `dist/` only.
2. The plugin loader's Jiti options add `"openclaw"` to `nativeModules` (`src/plugins/sdk-alias.ts`). Jiti 2.7.0 turns that into `node_modules/(openclaw)/` and loads any match natively, even with `tryNative: false` (`src/require.ts:131`). Node then refuses (`lib/internal/modules/typescript.js:188`, `isUnderNodeModules(filename)`).

The updater missed it because it validated a different path than it serves: `buildRelease` built and checked the release at `releases/<id>/build`, then `git worktree move` put it under `node_modules`. The only check at the final path was `openclaw.mjs --version` (`update-runner-git-release.ts`, `git-release-smoke`), which loads no plugin.

Reproduced on a real release tree built by `main` at 18b04f2fd5 (2026-11-19) on this machine, through Jiti with `nativeModules: ["openclaw"]` and `tryNative: false`: `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING` for `extensions/brave/web-search-contract-api.ts`, through both the real path and the link path.

The same class, TypeScript at runtime under `node_modules`, appeared before as #19815 (2026-02-18) and #53953 (2026-03-24).

## Change

Remove the cause in the owner: Git releases no longer live under `node_modules`.

- Layout: `<state>/git-install/openclaw -> releases/<id>/openclaw`. Moving only the tree is not enough: the Gateway names its root by the link (`openclaw-root.ts`), and Jiti matches the link path string too.
- Each release is built and validated where it serves. The build-beside-and-move step (`buildDir`, `git-release-place`) is deleted. A release path that a loader rule breaks now breaks the build before activation.
- `package-release-slot-path.ts` keeps one rule for both layouts: a release keeps the package at the link's path below the prefix (npm `lib/node_modules/<name>`, Git `<name>`). Lease, retention and the switch's deselect stamp use it, not npm-only `dirname` math.
- Retention resolves each retained release at the link's layout or at npm's `lib/node_modules/<name>`, where releases built before the move still live. `update status` keeps listing them, and an open update run that names one still protects it.
- Migration: `servingGitReleaseSlot` reads the old link while it still serves. The first update run by this release rebuilds the serving commit at the new path, publishes the new link, and removes the old link. The old Gateway then sees its installation replaced and restarts through the launcher, which now starts the new link.

No loader exception, no second source/dist rule, no flag.

## Impact

- Managed Git installs load bundled plugin sources again.
- Dev-channel installs on `main` builds since #199706 (they report version 2026.11.5; no published release has the layout) need one more `openclaw update` after the update to this change, because the older updater drives that first hop and still builds under the old path.
- npm, plain checkouts, Docker and package-to-Git switches are unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Regression test** (`src/infra/git-release.test.ts`, "loads a bundled plugin's source contract from the selected release (#201874)"). It copies `extensions/deepseek` into a release made by `createGitReleaseDirs`, publishes it, and loads `web-search-contract-api` through `loadPluginPublicArtifactModuleSync` from the release link path.
  - On `main` (307d9c45): fails. Under Vitest the `tsx` hooks strip the types, so the symptom is `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `openclaw/plugin-sdk/lazy-runtime`: the forced native import resolves the bare `openclaw/...` specifier to the release tree itself. Same cause.
  - On this branch: passes (`git-release.test.ts` 12/12).
- **Migration test** (`update-runner-git-release.test.ts`). A release under `lib/node_modules` is rebuilt at the new path, the new link's real path has no `node_modules` segment, and the old link is gone.
- **Mixed-layout inventory test** (`git-release.test.ts`). After the link moves out, a release still under `lib/node_modules/openclaw` stays listed by `listPackageReleases`, the source of `openclaw update status`.
- **Exact error on a real tree.** A release built by `main` (18b04f2fd5) on a Mac profile, loaded through Jiti 2.7.0 with `nativeModules: ["openclaw"]` and `tryNative: false`: `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING … extensions/brave/web-search-contract-api.ts`, through both the real path and the link path.
- **Mutation proof (build at the final path).** The release build (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts`):
  - In a worktree at `releases/r1/lib/node_modules/openclaw`: fails at once with `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING … scripts/lib/local-check-runtime.mts`.
  - The same commit at `out/r2/openclaw`: passes that stage (`runtime:scripts:check` 4.61 s).
  - So a release path that a loader rule breaks now fails the update before activation.
- **Stable tag unaffected.** A Docker lane run with a real service install of tag `v2026.11.5` (e13cf15): its updater returned `status: ok`, `root: …/git-checkout`, steps `clean-check, git-resolve-target, recovery-artifact-cleanup`. No release link was created. No published release has the release layout.
- **Gates:** `pnpm tsgo:core` exit 0; line-cap check OK (13 files); oxlint and oxfmt clean on changed files.
- **Every test file that reads the release layout:** 21 files. `rg -l 'git-release|gitReleaseSlot|GIT_RELEASE|usesGitReleases|package-release-slot-path|package-release-lease' src --glob '*.test.ts'`, plus `openclaw-root`, `program-args*`, `service-layout` and `stale-install`. All pass.
  - The first batch run (4 workers, load 22–49) timed out 6 update-cli cases. Rerun with 2 workers: 141/141.
  - Four suites did not load in that batch because a parallel scenario edit changed `scripts/` during the run. Rerun alone: 40/40 and 35/35.

## Not proven here

- **Real upgrade from `7db69bedeab6` (the reporter's build) to this change, with a Gateway request that loads the web-search contracts.** A Linux upgrade-survivor `git-release` scenario reached the stable-tag baseline above; the run from `7db69bedeab6` did not finish before landing. The scenario is not in this PR. The reporter is asked to confirm on #201874.
- **Windows.** No Windows host completed a run. On `main`, Windows Git checkouts never use releases (`usesGitReleases` returns false on win32), so they are unaffected by the bug and by this change. That comes from the code, not a run.
- **The old Gateway restarting after the old link is removed.** Before this change the Gateway saw the link move; here the link disappears. INFERENCE: it reads as installation replacement too.

prs.title: fix: agent-authored message buttons reach the agent on every channel
prs.body:
## Problem

A button the agent sends with the `message` tool (`presentation` button with `action: { type: "callback", value }`, or a legacy `value`) has no recorded owner. When no plugin claims the tap, each channel guesses:

- **Slack**: the agent gets a `Slack interaction: {json…}` system event instead of the value.
- **Discord** (registry path): the agent gets only `Clicked "<label>"`; the callback value is lost.
- **Teams**: the agent gets the raw card JSON `{"value":…,"label":…}`.
- **Telegram**: v2026.11.5 and main already deliver `message`-tool buttons through a Telegram-private patch (`tgac1`, backported to stable as `9afcc1b7b29a`), so the plain send/edit path works on stable (E2E below). That patch is set only by Telegram's `prepareSendPayload` hook and its edit path. Paths that skip it still render the plugin envelope `tgcb1:` and expire with "This action is no longer available.": the queue-persistence/`forceCoreDelivery` path, tool-authored source replies and legacy `interactive`. Builds before v2026.11.5 expire every typed agent button. Legacy slash values run as commands.

The main user-visible fixes are the other channels; on Telegram this PR replaces the private patch with the core owner and covers the paths it missed.
- **Feishu / Mattermost / LINE**: legacy values pass through without an owner.

## Root cause

`MessagePresentationAction { type: "callback" }` is "opaque callback value interpreted by the target channel/plugin" (`src/interactive/payload.ts:78-82`), and the SDK dispatcher returns only `{ matched: false }` for an unclaimed tap (`src/plugins/interactive.ts:63-65`). Nothing records that the agent owns the control, so each channel picks its own fallback. Telegram patched this privately with `channelData.telegram.typedCallbackOwner`, which was set on only two producer paths (`extensions/telegram/src/channel-actions.ts:215-249`, `button-types.ts:270-282`).

## Solution

One core owner records ownership **inside the value**:

- `src/interactive/agent-control.ts` (new, core-private codec): `stampAgentControls()` prefixes every callback value that a message action authors with a 2-byte mark (`::`), unconditionally; the decoder removes exactly one mark, so every authored value round-trips (`::pick:a` → `callback_data: ::pick:a`). A leading `:` is an empty namespace, and the plugin registry refuses empty namespaces (`interactive-registry.ts:58-68`), so a plugin can never claim a value by its mark.
- Marking happens where controls **leave core for a channel**, which a delivery reaches exactly once (not at the runner entry, whose params can re-enter through the runner's own Gateway `message.action` hop):
  - `dispatchChannelMessageAction`: the plugin-action leaf, for runner actions and direct Gateway `message.action` callers.
  - `executeSendAction` core branch: right before `sendMessage` persists the payload to the outbound queue, so recovered sends keep the mark. Queue recovery delivers the stored payload without passing a leaf again.
  - `extractToolAuthoredSourceReplyPayload`: tool-authored source replies, which are delivered by the reply pipeline, not by either leaf above.
- `dispatchPluginInteractiveHandler` strips the mark before namespace matching and passes the plain value to the handler. The result type is unchanged.
- Additive SDK exports on `openclaw/plugin-sdk/interactive-runtime`: `agentControlText(data)` returns `callback_data: <value>` for a marked value and `undefined` otherwise; `stampAgentControls(payload)` marks a payload's callback controls (Telegram uses it once, for sends queued by v2026.11.5).
- Channels: an unclaimed tap → `agentControlText(data) ?? <current behavior>`.
  - **Telegram**: marked values travel raw in `callback_data` (62 bytes for the agent's value; the old `tgac1:` envelope left 52). Unmarked typed values keep the `tgcb1` envelope, and an unclaimed one still answers "This action is no longer available." (#116383 semantics).
  - **Slack, LINE, Teams, Feishu (legacy quick envelope), Mattermost (legacy signed context), Discord (registry path)**: decode the mark so it never reaches the agent.

The mark is part of the value, so every encoder, the delivery queue and a Gateway restart keep it without channel cooperation. No state, config, schema, timers or flags.

## What was deleted

- Telegram: `TELEGRAM_AGENT_CALLBACK_PREFIX` (`tgac1:`), `TelegramTypedCallbackOwner`, the `owner` parameter, `hasTelegramAgentCallbackPrefix` / `parseTelegramAgentCallbackData`, `typedCallbackOwner` in `TelegramButtonBuildOptions`, the `prepareSendPayload` mark and its `interactive-fallback` reader, and the router's `tgac1` branches.
- `tgac1` shipped in v2026.11.5 (backport `9afcc1b7b29a`), so a read-only `tgac1` decoder stays in the Telegram router for buttons already in chats (plugin-first on the inner value, then `callback_data: <value>`). Outgoing agent buttons no longer use it; remove the reader once those messages have aged out. Sends still queued by v2026.11.5 carry `channelData.telegram.typedCallbackOwner: "agent"`; Telegram's canonicalize step marks those with the core codec (remove once such queue rows have drained).

## Accepted edges (named, not coded)

- Typed agent buttons delivered as `tgcb1:` by stables before v2026.11.5 are indistinguishable from plugin buttons: they keep their current behavior (unclaimed → unavailable). The agent can resend.
- A plugin installed later can claim older agent buttons in its namespace (plugin-first is kept on the inner value).
- Values starting with `/` now arrive as `callback_data: /…` instead of running as commands. Use `action.type: "command"` for command buttons (docs updated).
- Marking closes a spoof: a legacy raw value could previously mint `tgcmd:` or approval-looking data on Telegram.
- Native passthrough (raw Telegram `reply_markup`, Slack blocks, Discord `components`) is not marked and keeps its current owner. Discord native components/forms keep the registry and `agentComponents.ttlMs`.
- Discord presentation buttons still use the 30-minute registry TTL. Stateless Discord controls are the next PR.
- Slack delivers the tap as a session system event (now the plain `callback_data: <value>` text), not a user message.
- Repeat taps produce repeat turns, the same as typing twice. Telegram still clears the keyboard on tap.
- Third-party channel plugins that forward raw callback values show the 2-byte mark to the agent until they adopt `agentControlText`.
- Teams/Mattermost value size is unbounded (needs a separate decision).
- Taps route to the conversation's session (unchanged for Telegram, Slack, Teams, LINE, Mattermost).

## Plugin SDK impact

- Additive: `agentControlText` and `stampAgentControls` on `plugin-sdk/interactive-runtime` (the focused presentation subpath; `plugin-runtime` is a deprecated broad barrel). No type change; `MessagePresentationAction` and the dispatcher result are unchanged.
- Behavior: message-action callback values reach channel adapters with a leading `::`, and plugin interactive handlers receive the value without it.
- ClawHub static usage (plugin-sdk-impact, 2026-11-19, 2,675 eligible releases, coverage incomplete: 423 partial, 1 failed): `api.registerInteractiveHandler` 10 plugins, `plugin-runtime#dispatchPluginInteractiveHandler` 3, `#createChannelInteractiveDispatcher` 2, `#registerPluginInteractiveHandler` 1. Handlers keep receiving the same `namespace`/`payload`; channel plugins that forward raw values see the mark (degradation, not a break). Bundled source scan not run.

## Tests (red on base `2d9c5d679497`, green on head)

Wire bytes come from a real send through `runMessageAction` → the Telegram plugin → a loopback Bot API (`test/telegram-agent-control-taps.integration.test.ts`); the Telegram tap tests feed those exact bytes through the real callback router.

| Test | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| `test/telegram-agent-control-taps.integration.test.ts` send on the core-forced path (`forceCoreDelivery`, what queue persistence uses; skips `prepareSendPayload`) + edit → `callback_data` | ✗ (`tgcb1:`/`tgac1:` envelopes) | ✓ `::/pick a\|1`, `::pick:b`, 64-byte legacy |
| `bot.agent-callbacks`: unclaimed agent tap → `callback_data: /pick a\|1`, no mark | ✗ | ✓ |
| `bot.agent-callbacks`: plugin claims inner value first | ✗ | ✓ |
| `bot.agent-callbacks`: mention-gated group tap delivered | ✗ | ✓ |
| `bot.agent-callbacks`: agent control with inline buttons off → unavailable | ✗ | ✓ |
| `bot.agent-callbacks`: `tgac1` button already sent by v2026.11.5 → `callback_data: pick:beta` | ✓ (guard) | ✓ |
| `bot.agent-callbacks`: unauthorized tapper ignored; unclaimed `tgcb1` → unavailable | ✓ (guard) | ✓ |
| `message-action-runner.plugin-dispatch`: runner → plugin marked once; authored `::a` → `::::a` | ✗ | ✓ |
| `message-action-gateway`: runner → Gateway `message.action` hop forwards controls unmarked (the Gateway leaf marks once) | ✓ (guard) | ✓ |
| `outbound-send-service`: core send marks once before queue persistence | ✗ | ✓ |
| `message-action-dispatch.registry`: direct Gateway message action marked once; authored `::pick:a` round-trips | ✗ | ✓ |
| `interactive-fallback`: send queued by v2026.11.5 with `typedCallbackOwner` → `::pick:a` | ✗ | ✓ |
| `embedded-agent-messaging-extraction.tool-authored`: source reply marked once (`:pick:a` → `:::pick:a`) | ✗ | ✓ |
| `src/plugins/interactive.test.ts`: decode removes exactly one mark (`::::pick:a` → `callback_data: ::pick:a`) | ✗ | ✓ |
| `src/plugins/interactive.test.ts` dispatcher matches by value, not mark | ✗ | ✓ |
| `embedded-agent-messaging-extraction.tool-authored` source reply marked | ✗ | ✓ |
| Slack `interactions.lifecycle`, LINE `bot-message-context`, Teams `monitor-handler.adaptive-card`, Feishu `bot.card-action`, Mattermost `monitor-interactions.question` + `interactions` | ✗ each | ✓ each |
