prs.title: fix(templates): allow re-adding a deleted template agent
prs.body:
Closes #198475

## What Problem This Solves

Template Add fails with “deletion is in progress” when the same agent ID was previously deleted successfully.

## User Impact

Users can add the template again and receive a fresh agent and chat after deleting its previous agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Chat preparation runs before config publication consumes the completed deletion record. Carry the existing creation claim through session admission and the history reader, so only the current creator can prepare that agent. Keep reader custody and cleanup with their existing owners, including rejection of an ordinary request trying to reuse the creator's warm reader.

The main integration preserves the current session-store source-custody argument and its source-current guard separately from the creation witness. It also retains upstream's reviewed-setup retry controls.

Reported and reproduced by @DonnieFi in the linked issue.

## Evidence

Current validation covers merge commit `9f298accc9129ad2874cbcd40e0ef813e1ea2998` against main `60c112a1bfa94ea4a5d43e4302e18375429d879f` (Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0).

- **Before:** with the same recreation fixture and all eight production files restored to that fixed main, actual Add → production deletion → same-ID Add fails with `Agent fixture-first deletion is in progress; new work is unavailable.` The command exits 1 (253.900 seconds, including cold worker compilation); this is the intended service-boundary failure.
- **After: 13 selected cases passed across five files.** They cover recreation with a fresh session, creator warm-read success and outside-claim refusal, fresh creation, post-commit revocation, pre-commit compensation, reviewed-setup retry, reader cleanup/revocation, source-custody revocation and retargeting in ordinary and inspection modes, and session preemption. Canonical production SQLite workers were compiled by the test wrapper.
- Production core, Template test and session test types passed. Typed lint passed on the eight production files and the Template test. Formatting, whitespace, the nine-file line-cap check and the test-growth check passed; net test growth is 76 lines.
- Fresh independent desktop review through read-only SSH covers the complete nine-file patch and its owning contracts, with no unresolved P0–P2 findings. The merge commit preserves the reviewed tree `4301538ac2bd3f99f3d4253a039cec934f6a8e0f`.

Live Gateway RPC, browser/provider and broad CI validation are not included. The existing real-Gateway evidence gap and maintainer-owned CI/review gates remain pending.

<details>
<summary>Focused commands, cost and limits</summary>

```bash
OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=300000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/templates/gateway-add-pending.test.ts src/infra/agent-database-readers.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks -t 'admitted-recreated$|admitted-reviewed-chat-retry$|admitted-applied$|: revoked$|abort-before-commit$|runs every registered closer and keeps deleted databases closed until revived'
OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=300000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.runtime-config.config.ts src/config/sessions/session-store-reader-preparation.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-transcript-worker-lanes.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks -t 'reuses a live prepared source and rejects revoked custody|rejects a locator retargeted after qualification|revokes readers and joins cleanup.*pending=true, capable=true|retains reads dispatched after cleanup.*capable=true'
OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=300000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/sessions/session-controller.lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks -t '^preempt interrupts a captured subordinate effect before running the mutation$'
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.templates.json --noEmit
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json --noEmit
```

The three test commands completed in 424.190, 85.776 and 89.509 seconds. These are whole wrapper times, including compilation and transforms, not isolated assertion time. The real recreation/cleanup lifecycle needs the production SQLite service boundary; cheaper helper-only assertions would miss the original failure and retained-reader leak. Other cases in these files were intentionally unselected. The finite 300-second wrapper no-output budget was retained; behavioral test timeouts were not increased.

The compiler commands used separate incremental build-info files. Core typed lint's existing root-config route also prepared plugin SDK declarations; no additional check was rerun just to remove that preparation cost. Normal merge hooks retain the content guard and canonically skip formatting/freshness under MERGE_HEAD; the affected-file checks above ran explicitly before committing.

This is isolated production-service/SQLite proof. Live Gateway RPC, browser, vendor/provider acceptance and broad package/CI validation remain outside this local evidence. The existing real-Gateway evidence gap and maintainer-owned CI/review gates remain pending.

</details>

prs.title: fix(browser): answer HTTP auth from the tab's document interception session
prs.body:
Closes #201945

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw browser set credentials <user> <pass>` followed by `open <url>` does not get past HTTP Basic auth:

- managed headless profile (`main` and `2026.11.5`): `page.goto: net::ERR_INVALID_AUTH_CREDENTIALS`
- extension-relay profile (`2026.11.5`): `Protocol error (Fetch.enable): Fetch interception is owned by another session or is being released`

The navigation fence intercepts each guarded tab's documents on its own CDP session but neither asks for nor answers `Fetch.authRequired`, so the challenge falls back to Chromium's default handling, which headless cancels. Playwright's `setHTTPCredentials` handles auth on a second session; on an extension relay that second `Fetch.enable` is refused because the relay grants a tab's Fetch domain to one session only (intended, covered by `relay-bridge.fetch.test.ts`).

## Change

- `pw-session-http-auth.ts` (new): per-`BrowserContext` credentials for the fence, `interception()` (adds `handleAuthRequests` while credentials are set), `answer()` (one `Fetch.authRequired` listener per interception target), `onChange()` (re-enable an already-fenced tab when credentials change), and a relay-browser marker.
- Fence: enables `handleAuthRequests` when credentials exist, forwards `Fetch.authRequired`, answers it. Server challenge → `ProvideCredentials`; the same request challenged again → `CancelAuth` (rejected credentials end as the server's 401 page, no loop); proxy challenge or no credentials → `Default` (unchanged behavior).
- `set credentials`: stores credentials for the fence on every transport. Direct CDP still calls `context.setHTTPCredentials` (tabs the fence never touched, e.g. popups, keep working). Relay connections skip it, so no second `Fetch.enable` is attempted.
- `settleInterception` moves unchanged into `cdp-fetch-interception.ts` so the fence stays under its line cap.

Not changed: credentials are still context-wide and in-memory, as before. Per-origin scope and SecretRef sources are proposed separately in the issue.

## Evidence

Candidate `90943efefd7567fc0f6d460c0bed0b73fab6e4fd` on `main` @ `0eb6488cd3ce5918c4d1fe48d0a4bb4cd2d290a2` (no `extensions/browser` or package changes on `main` since). Built CLI (`pnpm build`, `node openclaw.mjs`), throwaway `HOME`/state, headless Chromium (Linux, Playwright 1.62 image), managed profile `openclaw`, local Basic-auth fixture on `127.0.0.1`:

| Build | Sequence | `open` | `snapshot` |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (`44267df`) / `2026.11.5` | set credentials → open | `net::ERR_INVALID_AUTH_CREDENTIALS` | empty |
| main (`44267df`) / `2026.11.5` | open → set credentials → open | `net::ERR_INVALID_AUTH_CREDENTIALS` | empty |
| this PR | set credentials → open | `opened` | `heading "BASIC-AUTH-OK"` |
| this PR | open → set credentials → open | first `open` fails (no credentials yet), second `opened` | `heading "BASIC-AUTH-OK"` |
| this PR | wrong password → open | `opened`, no loop | `generic: unauthorized` (server 401 body) |

Tests that fail on `main` and pass here:

- `pw-session-navigation-fence.http-auth.test.ts`: fence enables `handleAuthRequests`, answers `ProvideCredentials` / `CancelAuth` on repeat / `Default` for proxy; credentials set after fencing re-enable the existing interception (and clearing turns it off again).
- `pw-tools-core.state.http-credentials.test.ts`: relay contexts never call Playwright's `setHTTPCredentials`; direct contexts call it and also feed the fence.

Without the production change: 4 failed / 4. With it: 97 passed across 7 files (new tests plus the existing fence, state, navigation-guard and relay Fetch suites).

Checks on the candidate tree: `pnpm build` ✅ · `tsgo:extensions` + `tsgo:extensions:test` ✅ · oxlint `--type-aware --deny-warnings` on the changed files ✅ · oxfmt `--check` ✅ · line-cap ratchet ✅ (fence file shrinks) · test-mock-exports, test-timeout-race ratchet, import-cycles ✅. The full `pnpm check:changed` run did not fit the 12 GiB container I have (SQLite worker ratchet), so I ran the steps above individually; happy to fix anything CI reports.

Not verified: a real browser with the OpenClaw extension on the fixed build. The relay path is covered by the unit tests above and the existing relay contract test (`relay-bridge.fetch.test.ts`). The same fence change, applied to a local `2026.11.5` install, also passes with a real Chromium-based browser on macOS over direct CDP (both sequences, wrong password ends on the 401 page).

releases.body:
## 2026.11.10-beta.1

### Highlights

- Agent templates: add agents directly from ClawHub packages, with a single CLAW.md manifest and bundled skill folders checked by the native trust flow. (#195707, #196322, #196348) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @Patrick-Erichsen.
- OpenClaw ID: connect nodes through the ID tunnel, approve them from Access, and link owner devices to your own identity. (#193982, #194007, #197628) Thanks @jalehman.
- Browser handoff: take over the agent’s browser directly from the Browser panel without stopping the agent. (#197928) Related #197902 Thanks @daniel-lxs.
- Chat control: send pending steering messages without stopping a run, edit queued messages, and retain composer drafts across app restarts. (#193665, #197846, #197908) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @vincentkoc and @obviyus.
- Updates: configure automatic update schedules and let the incoming release run its own pre-update rehearsal. (#193713, #197922) Thanks @jacobtomlinson and @fuller-stack-dev.
- State upgrades: migrate Gateway state using copy-and-swap at startup rather than modifying the live store in place. (#198389) Thanks @obviyus.
- Durable execution: keep background commands running across Gateway restarts on macOS. (#197474) Related #197443 Thanks @daniel-lxs.

### Changes

- Access: add a guest member role with sandboxed session tools. (#197748) Thanks @jalehman.
- Tool discovery: offer an opt-in usage-ranked tool index, including MCP tools. (#197128, #198348) Thanks @jalehman.
- Knowledge: find current records when searches use wording from their superseded versions. (#193742) Related #193054 Thanks @daniel-lxs.
- Voice and images: choose the speech-to-text model in Settings → Talk, and let agents review generated images before delivery. (#197906, #198227) Related #197859 Thanks @daniel-lxs and @vincentkoc.
- Providers: support Parallel Decisions both natively and through OpenRouter. (#194537) Thanks @vincentkoc.
- Backups: show stage and byte progress during long-running backups. (#198675) Thanks @vincentkoc.

### Fixes

- Access boundaries: apply OpenClaw ID member permissions consistently to HTTP history and connected-app panels. (#199946, #200070) Thanks @joshavant.
- Queued input: show a visible withheld failure when permission is revoked instead of silently canceling the message. (#200213) Thanks @vincentkoc, @vyctorbrzezowski, and @obviyus.
- Subagents: retain results through Gateway restarts and retry completion delivery after the requester is interrupted. (#199868, #200165) Authored by @steipete.
- OpenAI responses: recover item conflicts across runs and complete replay-safe turns after deferred conflict recovery. (#199896, #200254) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @ZengWen-DT and @obviyus.
- Slack delivery: preserve the final reply when native streams hit a boundary or message-length limit, and keep expired progress from appearing after the answer. (#199849, #200080) Related #200045 Thanks @n1hility, @obviyus, and @atlas-kring.
- Discord: render edited messages consistently with new sends while preserving literal user-mention tokens inside code. (#199958, #200053) Related #190479, #195585 Thanks @obviyus, @yetval, and @saariuslystoned.
- Signal: preserve native mention recipients in quoted messages. (#200058) Related #195074 Thanks @obviyus and @saariuslystoned.
- Chat history: preserve reading position when transcript ranges shrink, load older history after interrupted restoration, and retain pasted text if the clipboard changes mid-paste. (#199747, #200107, #200098) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @vincentkoc and @obviyus.
- Usage display: stop presenting fully unpriced usage as a known zero-dollar cost. (#199711) Related #199710 Thanks @JoshSalomon and @obviyus.
- Update recovery: restrict startup copies and pruning to owned state and preserve successful startup writes for the next Doctor run. (#199929, #200260) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Responsiveness: reduce cold-session compaction CPU and latency regressions, prepare large histories outside the Gateway thread, and shorten write locks during large Knowledge vault scans. (#199561, #200114, #199859) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, and @jalehman.

### Complete contribution record

The full contribution record is available in the tag-pinned [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.10-beta.1/CHANGELOG/records/2026.11.10-beta.1.md#complete-contribution-record).

issues.title: [Bug]: resolve_url_target allows hostnames with NUL bytes (\x00), causing C getaddrinfo truncation
issues.body:
## Description
`resolve_url_target()` in `nanobot/security/network.py` does not reject hostnames containing NUL bytes (`\x00`) or control characters.

On macOS/POSIX, passing a hostname with an embedded NUL byte to `socket.getaddrinfo(hostname, ...)` truncates the hostname at `\x00` in the underlying C call (resolving only the prefix before `\x00`), which can cause `resolve_url_target("http://bad\x00host.example.com/")` to return `ok=True`.

Additionally, when `trust_remote_dns=True` and local DNS raises `socket.gaierror`, the fallback literal checks (`normalized_hostname == "localhost"` and `ipaddress.ip_address(normalized_hostname)`) fail to match inputs such as `localhost\x00.evil.com` or `127.0.0.1\x00.evil.com` and return `(True, "", ())`.

## To Reproduce
```python
from nanobot.security.network import resolve_url_target

# Depending on local DNS/search domain for "bad", this can return (True, '', (...))
print(resolve_url_target("http://bad\x00host.example.com/"))
```

## Suggested Fix
Reject any `hostname` containing `\x00` or control/whitespace characters before `socket.getaddrinfo()` (e.g., return `(False, f"Invalid hostname: {hostname}", ())`).

I asked it to return the call as text without executing tools. When I asked for the exact call again, it drafted another welcome instead of repeating the first one.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python

import asyncio
```

prs.title: fix(webui): confirm linked automation deletion in untimed toast
prs.body:
## Summary

- Replace the blocking `DeleteConfirm` modal with an untimed, persistent confirmation toast when deleting topics that have linked automations.
- Pre-check linked automations via the existing `GET /api/sessions/{key}/automations` endpoint (no backend or API schema changes):
  - Topics without linked automations continue straight into the 8-second undoable pending toast.
  - Topics with linked automations stay visible and show an untimed confirmation toast listing the affected automation(s) with **Cancel** and **Delete** actions.
  - Clicking **Delete** transitions the **same** toast in place into the 8-second undo countdown (avoiding duplicate toasts and the 8-second delayed modal).
  - If an automation is created during the undo window, the gateway's `blocked_by_automations` fallback opens the same untimed confirmation toast instead of a modal.
- Remove the obsolete `DeleteConfirm` component and gallery preview, update `docs/webui.md`, and synchronize localization keys across all 10 supported locales.

prs.body:
## Why

A few internal paths still advertised choices that no caller could make. Some tests also appeared to protect behavior that a regression would not actually break: the old atomic-write test still passed with the writer replaced by a no-op.

## What changed

- Remove the obsolete per-session transcript-tail read and its only helper. Startup recovery already selects unfinished sessions in a batch; live pending-state calculation and paged history stay in place. Remove the unreferenced ISO timestamp utility as well.
- Drop private options that subagent tool construction, channel discovery, and the QQ, Signal and Weixin adapters never receive. Keep the actual workspace binding, policy checks, upload payloads, and retry identifiers. MCP preset actions now construct messages only for actions routed to them; test/import actions already construct their own results.
- Delete the two CSS selectors for the retired composer cache indicator (including their dark variants) and two conditions the update dialog's render guard had already ruled out.
- Remove four duplicate Python cases: empty WeCom filename, memory cursor filtering, model circuit opening, and MCP name sanitization. The retained cases exercise the same input and assertion. Remove the ineffective atomic-write test; the replacement-failure cleanup and compaction readback tests remain.
- Remove eight assertions targeting selectors that the UI no longer renders. Keep all eight interaction scenarios and their assertions on controls, state, or content.

## Scope

Screened tracked Python, WebUI, TUI, shared packages, channel code, and tests, then checked candidates against call sites, registrations, build entries, and test fixtures. Kept dynamic entry points, compatibility APIs, migrations, and helpers that exercise live product behavior. No wire, schema, dependency, or intended user-facing changes.

## Verification

- 787 focused Python tests and 669 WebUI tests passed. Python lint and import boundaries, WebUI lint and production build, and WebUI/TUI TypeScript checks passed.

prs.title: refactor(webui): separate gateway mutations and UI state
prs.body:
## Why
The WebUI gateway converted structured WebSocket writes into synthetic HTTP requests and back. The same paths also mixed disk work, history projection, and UI state ownership into frequently used handlers.

## What changed
- Dispatch allowlisted WebUI writes directly with structured parameters and typed results. HTTP reads keep their auth and cache behavior; the old mutation URLs still reject HTTP writes. Move automation routing, replay/trace projection, and OAuth provider handling into their owning modules.
- Move blocking preview, background, static asset, outbound media, and MCP work off the event loop. Reuse transcript projections and compute replay size metrics only when needed.
- Give gateway credentials, composer voice input, sidebar motion, file preview resizing, scroll anchors, stream batching, and overlay shortcuts explicit owners. Cap unhandled temporary-chat frames and avoid synchronous storage reads on every inbound frame.

## Blast Radius
WebUI and WebSocket gateway internals only. Same-version clients keep the existing action names and response envelopes. Session access, local-only settings, and disconnect-safe mutations are covered by regression tests. No browser host, native updater, or release configuration is changed.

## Verification
- Python WebUI and WebSocket suites: **1,646 passed**, 23 skipped; one subprocess handoff case was left for CI. WebUI Ruff, BasedPyright, and Python import boundaries passed.
- Frontend: **3,945 passed** in the full Vitest run, with 374 focused test passes after the final overlay changes. TypeScript, ESLint, client import boundaries, and the production build passed.

prs.title: feat(agent): integrate mst-python as a metasearch provider
prs.body:
This PR adds the Meta-Search Tool (mst) as a new web search provider for nanobot.

## What it is

MST aggregates results from multiple search engines (DuckDuckGo, Google, Brave, Bing, etc.) simultaneously and merges them using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). This gives richer coverage than any single provider alone.

Inspired by [SearXNG](https://github.com/searxng/searxng) — MST brings the same metasearch concept to Python code directly, without needing a separate web server or Docker container. Package at https://github.com/openmtx/meta-search-tool.

## Changes

- **`nanobot/agent/tools/web.py`** — added `mst` as a new search provider with `_search_mst()` method. Supports:

- **`nanobot/webui/settings_api.py`** — added JSON parsing and validation for `mst_engines` and `mst_weights` in the WebUI settings API
- **`pyproject.toml`** — moved `mst-python` to `[project.optional-dependencies] mst` (optional, not installed by default)
- **`tests/tools/test_search_tools.py`** — 6 new tests covering success, missing package, env vars, config priority, and timeout
- **`tests/webui/test_settings_api.py`** — 4 new tests for MST engine/weight validation in the settings API

```json
{

    "web": {
      "search": {
```

prs.title: feat(webui): continue channel sessions from the sidebar
prs.body:
Resolves [NAN-463](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-463/从-webui-打开并继续原渠道会话)

## Why

A conversation started in Telegram or another channel could not be continued from the WebUI. Starting a new WebUI topic lost that context; sending a reply back to the original channel would surprise the people there.

## What changed

- List saved public channel conversations alongside WebUI conversations. Use the channel name as the title and the existing `@handle` to distinguish chats, topics, and channel instances.
- Open and continue the original conversation without copying its history. Inputs from different entry points run as separate turns, and a reply goes only to the entry that started it. WebUI replies stream; channel replies appear in WebUI history when their turn ends.
- Show shared running state and allow Stop from WebUI, even for a turn started in another channel. Keep the gateway's workspace policy and leave rename, reset, delete, fork, and recovery controls unavailable for channel conversations. Hide private/internal history and label message origin only when it was recorded.
- Show recorded tool calls in channel history by name, without exposing arguments or raw results.

There is no migration, platform backfill, new account linking, or per-user access control. As with the rest of the instance's WebUI, only grant access to trusted operators: saved history can include group messages. Older channel history may lack origin labels or matching tool results.

## Verification

- 1,772 Python tests passed across WebUI, WebSocket, session handles/recovery, and turn routing/concurrency. The new tests cover topic separation, both orders of overlapping WebUI/Telegram inputs, scoped history/media, and stopping an external turn from WebUI.
- Frontend session/sidebar, stream and reconnect tests passed. Production build, TypeScript (including browser fixtures), ESLint, Python lint/type checks, and import boundaries passed.
- Chromium on the built WebUI and an isolated same-version gateway with a simulated Telegram adapter and local model: opened the correct topic, continued it from both entries, checked that only the WebUI reply streamed, confirmed the Telegram reply went to Telegram and appeared in history after completion, and reloaded without duplicate messages. Reviewed desktop and narrow screenshots.
- Tool history follow-up: 1,084 Python tests passed across WebUI and WebSocket session admission. Chromium opened and reloaded saved history from a real WeChat conversation on an isolated test gateway and showed the recorded command and file-read activity.
- Live Telegram and QQ accounts were not exercised. The PR remains a draft for review and remaining live-channel verification.

prs.title: fix(goal): block goals after terminal execution failures
prs.body:
## Why

A sustained goal could remain active after output-limit recovery, repeated empty responses, or another terminal execution failure had already stopped its run. Some refusal and truncated responses were also reported as successful turns.

## What changed

- Settle terminal failures in the gateway's goal execution policy: atomically block only the current active goal, preserve its objective, and record a safe reason and timestamp before notifying clients.
- Preserve terminal runner reasons and report failed model turns, including refusals, content filtering, and exhausted output/empty-response recovery.
- Expose the blocked recap in runtime context so later replies can explain why work stopped.

## Scope

Only terminal-failure state correction. No new goal actions, permission changes, or recovery workflow. Token settings, retry budgets, client protocols, `/stop`, and `/cancel_goal` are unchanged. Retries and recoverable tool errors keep working.

## Tradeoffs

Terminal failures block rather than retry indefinitely. Existing goal tools and recovery behavior remain unchanged; this PR does not add a resume action.

## Blast Radius

Durable goal execution and model-failure reporting use the existing blocked-state projection. Generation checks and an atomic active-state check prevent stale failures from overwriting a replacement session or a closed goal. Hard process crashes and unavailable storage cannot guarantee a persisted transition.

## Verification

- Runner/loop, goal tools, cancellation, sessions, commands, and SDK regression checks: **1136 passed, 3 skipped** on Windows/Python 3.14.
- WebUI goal/wire/background, runtime-context/model-event checks and gateway smoke suite: **59 passed, 1 skipped**.
- Real isolated gateway + local synthetic SSE model: normal completion, `/stop`, exhausted length recovery, reconnect, and status inquiry passed through the public WebSocket interface.
- Full CI lint command, strict BasedPyright, Python import boundaries, and `git diff --check` passed. Full-project/cross-platform CI for the narrowed scope is pending; the running user instance and its configuration were not changed.

Resolves [NAN-455](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-455/执行终止性失败时自动阻塞-goal)

prs.title: fix(session): replay passive history in native continuations
prs.body:
## Why

Fixes #6678. After an SDK import, the updated supplier quote was present in session history but missing from the next Responses request because native continuation replayed only its saved items and pending turn input. Recorded channel notifications, including Heartbeat deliveries, had the same gap.

## What changed

- Add a session-owned passive-history outbox in the existing private SQLite `pending_inputs` table. Imports and recorded deliveries append canonical history and an independently identified replay batch in one transaction, even before the first native continuation exists.
- Stage a finite snapshot of those batches before the next user input when resuming compatible provider state. Without compatible state, use the normal full-history path. Share the existing canonical message projection for sanitization, tools, and media breadcrumbs.
- Acknowledge captured batch IDs atomically with prepared input and continuation state. Checkpoints and turn completion preserve later arrivals; failed writes retain the outbox. Restart preserves pending batches, reset removes them, and forks/SDK exports do not copy their private bookkeeping.

## Scope

Covers SDK `ingest()`/`restore()` and gateway-recorded passive deliveries. Public APIs and provider wire formats are unchanged; Responses reasoning/compaction payloads remain opaque. Passive deliveries do not start a model run or wait on the active run's lock.

## Tradeoffs

The outbox temporarily stores the appended canonical records, rather than introducing message IDs into public history or depending on mutable history positions. Entries are removed when their replay obligation transfers to prepared input. This avoids a schema migration and keeps the journal independent of runner-owned provider state; clearing native state on every append would discard retained reasoning and compaction.

## Verification

- SDK runs against a purpose-built local HTTP/SSE peer verify actual Responses and Chat Completions request bodies: imports before/after an initial run, identical messages in separate batches, restart, ordering, subsequent turns without duplicate replay, retained native reasoning, and canonical tool/media projection.
- The real gateway delivery path is exercised while the first or a later model request is blocked; its notification survives checkpoints and appears once on the next turn. Interrupted prepared requests and failed-write rollback are covered, along with newer arrivals, fork/reset isolation, and private export boundaries.
- Focused SDK/session/provider/delivery suites: **350 passed, 3 skipped** on Windows.
- Additional agent save/recovery/policy/concurrency/governance/subagent suites: **216 passed**.
- Full-repository Ruff, import-boundary checks, strict BasedPyright on changed production sources, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Full-project CI remains pending. These checks use synthetic responses, not a live provider or external messaging delivery.

Reported by @UnZHGPPT; credited as a co-author.

prs.title: feat(provider): support OpenRouter native image generation API
prs.body:
## Reason for the Change

OpenRouter now provides image generation through its native Images API. Nanobot needs to use this API so OpenRouter image generation remains compatible with the current service and can expose more image-generation providers and models through the existing `generate_image` workflow.

## Summary

Update the OpenRouter image-generation client to use OpenRouter's native image API instead of the previous chat-completions image flow.

The implementation:

- Sends generation requests to `POST /api/v1/images`.
- Looks up model capabilities through `GET /api/v1/images/models`.
- Sends `aspect_ratio` and `resolution` only when the selected model advertises the requested values.
- Sends reference images using OpenRouter's native `input_references` format.
- Decodes `data[].b64_json` responses into nanobot image data URLs.
- Preserves a valid response `media_type` when one is returned.
- Keeps provider configuration and the existing `generate_image` tool interface unchanged.

The implementation was tested with these OpenRouter models:

- `openai/gpt-image-2.5-flare`
- `meta/muse-image`
- `bytedance-seed/seedream-5-0-lite`
- `bytedance-seed/seedream-4.5`
- `black-forest-labs/flux.2-pro`
- `x-ai/grok-imagine-image-quality`

## Testing

- `pytest tests/providers/test_image_generation.py -q`
  - Result: 99 passed in 0.82s

The suite covers:
- Native `POST /api/v1/images` requests.
- `GET /api/v1/images/models` capability discovery.
- Supported and unsupported aspect-ratio and resolution values.
- `extraBody` overrides.
- Native reference-image inputs.
- Base64 response decoding and returned media types.
- Capability-lookup failures and responses without images.
- Missing OpenRouter API keys.

## Compatibility and Rollout

Existing OpenRouter provider credentials, image-generation settings, and the `generate_image` tool remain unchanged. Models that do not advertise a requested aspect ratio or resolution receive a request without that optional field, allowing the model to use its default behavior.

prs.title: fix(webui): reconcile running turns on reconnect
prs.body:
## Why

A browser that misses a turn's terminal frame can keep showing an Agent as running after reconnect. A failed history read or a page without the completion ID cannot repair that state. The Gateway already knows which runs are live; reconnect should not depend on recovering the transcript first.

## What changed

- A trusted WebUI attach returns the live named runs for that chat. The client uses absence to clear only previously confirmed runs, not new or unacknowledged submissions.
- Terminal delivery includes sockets that attached during the history write. Retained recovery data no longer reports a finished run as active in attach, hydration, or the session list.
- Check reconnect convergence without a history completion ID in TLA+ and implementation regressions.

## Scope

Previously confirmed named runs in persistent sessions after a healthy reconnect. The snapshot reports liveness, not success or transcript coverage. It does not infer a result while offline or introduce a fixed completion deadline.

## Blast Radius

Same-version WebUI/Gateway reconnect and run indicators. The attach field is additive and only sent to authenticated WebUI sockets; the paginated transcript and its recovery markers keep their existing semantics.

## Verification

- [TLC reproduction and assumptions](webui/verification/turn-sync/ATTACH-RECONCILIATION.md): all 13 default configurations exhausted without a counterexample. The attach model checks up to two losses without completion evidence from history.
- Client and Gateway regressions cover failed reads, missing IDs, preserving newer work, attaching during both successful and failed terminal writes, and excluding retired runs from the session list.
- Ran the built WebUI in Chromium against an isolated Gateway. Dropped the real `turn_end` frame, then injected either HTTP 503 or a fragment without the completion ID. Both the sidebar ring and the Stop button cleared after reconnect, and the answer was recoverable from the real history.

Contributes to [NAN-279](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-279/为-webui-重连建立一致的同步边界与有界缺口补齐)

Queue indicators need to know which inputs a model request is answering. Taking an input from the runner queue is too early: request preparation may still reject it.

issues.title: System-prompt guidance is all accelerator with no brakes — agents loop on failing approaches

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: P3

issues.body:
# System-prompt guidance is all accelerator with no brakes — agents loop on failing approaches

## Summary

The system prompt contains several guidance blocks that push the model to keep working — `TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_GUIDANCE`, `TASK_COMPLETION_GUIDANCE`, the per-family execution blocks — but there is no corresponding universal guidance telling it **when to stop retrying, when to change strategy, and how to report a blocker honestly**. The result is a class of degenerate runs where the model re-executes the same failing command / patch / query many times in a row, re-sending the full conversation context on every attempt. The only "brakes" in the prompt are two coding-specific lines in the coding brief; nothing covers terminal commands, web fetches, install failures, or any non-coding surface.

Line references below are against current `main` (`a72c9ca248`).

## The accelerator blocks (as shipped)

| Block | Location | Keystroke |
|---|---|---|
| `TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_GUIDANCE` | `agent/prompt_builder.py:342` | "Keep working until the task is actually complete... Never end your turn with a promise of future action — execute it now." |
| `TASK_COMPLETION_GUIDANCE` | `agent/prompt_builder.py:396` | "Keep working until you have actually exercised the code or produced the requested result" |
| `OPENAI_MODEL_EXECUTION_GUIDANCE` | `agent/prompt_builder.py:469` ("tool_persistence") | "Keep calling tools until: (1) the task is complete, AND (2) you have verified the result." + "If a tool returns empty or partial results, retry with a different query or strategy before giving up." |
| `GOOGLE_MODEL_OPERATIONAL_GUIDANCE` | `agent/prompt_builder.py:553` | "**Keep going:** Work autonomously until the task is fully resolved." |

These are injected per `TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_MODELS` (`agent/prompt_builder.py:359`) and the config gates, so for families like `qwen`/`deepseek`/`glm` several of them stack in the same system prompt.

## What is missing

1. **No universal stop/change-strategy rule.** Nothing anywhere in the shipped prompt tells the model: "you have now failed twice with the same approach — you must change strategy," or "this call is identical to a previously failed call — do not issue it." The `OPENAI_MODEL_EXECUTION_GUIDANCE` bullet ("retry with a different query or strategy before giving up") is the closest thing, but it only ships to GPT/Codex/Grok-family models and phrases the retry as encouragement, not as a bounded loop with a stop condition.

2. **The only shipped brakes are two coding-specific lines** in `CODING_AGENT_GUIDANCE` (`agent/coding_context.py`):
   - re-read before retrying a failed patch;
   - stop after ~3 attempts on linter/type errors for one file.
   Nothing equivalent exists for the terminal tool, web tools, or any non-coding session — which is where the majority of loop-behavior runs occur (package installs, API calls, scraping, permission errors).

3. **Runtime guards exist but never inform the model.** `agent/iteration_budget.py` / `max_iterations` terminate the loop silently; `agent/repetition_guard.py` only detects verbatim token-level repetition inside a single truncated fragment (#86581), not behavioral loops across turns. There is no signal in the tool-result stream telling the model it is repeating itself, and no prompt instruction defining how to respond to such a signal.

## Secondary issue: enforcement guidance conflicts with confirmation-first user instructions, with no declared precedence

`TOOL_USE_ENFORCEMENT_GUIDANCE` ("Never end your turn with a promise of future action — execute it now... Responses that only describe intentions without acting are not acceptable") directly contradicts a common and legitimate class of user instructions loaded from `SOUL.md` / `AGENTS.md` / context files — e.g. "report the full plan and wait for my confirmation before touching files", "back up before any destructive operation". Nothing in the prompt declares which instruction wins. In practice the model oscillates: it acts, then apologises and asks for confirmation, then acts again — consuming iterations on the meta-conflict instead of the task.

Since SOUL.md/AGENTS.md content is user-provided and loaded into the same prompt, the enforcement block should either explicitly defer to explicit confirmation requirements, or the precedence should be stated.

## Observed failure mode (shape of the problem)

The typical loop run looks like:

```
tool: terminal("pip install X")            -> error (PEP 668)
tool: terminal("pip install X")            -> same error
tool: terminal("sudo pip install X")       -> same error class
tool: terminal("pip install X")            -> same error
... (N times) ...
```

Each retry re-sends the accumulated conversation, so the token cost compounds linearly with loop length. No instruction in the prompt gives the model an exit condition or a reporting format for "I am stuck", so it defaults to retry-or-fabricate (the fabricate half is covered by `TASK_COMPLETION_GUIDANCE`; the retry half is not covered at all).

## Proposal

1. **Add one small universal "execution brake" block** (static text, cache-safe, same tier as `TASK_COMPLETION_GUIDANCE`), roughly:
   - Before starting, state the success criterion in one line (internally or via todo).
   - If the same approach (identical command, identical patch target, identical query) fails twice, the next action MUST use a different strategy; before a third attempt, check whether the call is substantively identical to a previous failed call — if so, do not issue it.
   - After three failures, stop and report: what was tried, the exact errors, the diagnosed cause, and the concrete next options. An honest blocker report is always better than another retry.
   - Explicit precedence line: "Where the user's instructions (SOUL.md / AGENTS.md / context files) require confirmation before an action or impose a stop condition, those instructions win over 'keep working'."

2. **Optional, higher-leverage: runtime loop-guard signal in tool results.** The terminal/dispatch layer already sees consecutive identical failing calls; emitting a marker like `[LOOP GUARD: this exact command has failed N times in a row — change strategy or report the blocker]` in the tool result would make the brake observable rather than advisory, in the same spirit as `repetition_guard.py`. The prompt then only needs to define the response to the marker. This keeps the system prompt byte-stable (the signal rides tool results, not the cached prefix).

3. **Minor, separable:** the coding brief's second brake currently reads "If the same region fails twice, rewrite the enclosing function or file with `write_file` instead of attempting a third patch." This escalates edit conflicts into blind whole-file/whole-function rewrites, which destroys unrelated work. A stop-and-diagnose instruction would be safer than an automatic rewrite escalation.

## What I verified locally

- Disabling `agent.tool_use_enforcement` (config.yaml) removes the oscillation in confirmation-first profiles.
- Adding a brake rule (two-strike stop, identical-call self-check, honest blocker reporting) to `SOUL.md` does not conflict with any shipped block once precedence is stated.
- Removing the rewrite-escalation line from the coding brief passes the existing `tests/agent/test_coding_context.py` suite.

Happy to open a PR for any of the three items if the direction is acceptable.

issues.body:
## Summary

A user provider plugin whose tree is deep (e.g. a model provider whose `tests/` folder has long filenames) never stages on a default Windows host: the gateway prints `Could not stage provider plugin <name>` with `[WinError 3]` for the longest paths and the provider stays unregistered across restarts.

The frozen copy path is `runtime/provider-plugins/<owned-root>/<per-home-module-name>/<plugin-name>/...`. For a plugin named `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` the module prefix alone is long, and the staging copy adds an intermediate `.copy-XXXX` directory. The *published* target fits under 260 chars, but the intermediate staging destination exceeds MAX_PATH, so `shutil.copytree` fails with a bare `FileNotFoundError` (WinError 3).

## Repro

- Windows with `LongPathsEnabled=0` (the default; also the common managed-laptop case where HKLM is locked).
- Install a provider plugin whose `tests/` has long filenames under the deep per-home module prefix.
- Start the gateway: `errors.log` shows `providers.plugin_reload: Could not stage provider plugin ... [WinError 3]` for exactly the files whose destination exceeds 260 chars; `runtime/provider-plugins/owned-*` modules stay empty.

## Expected

The plugin stages and registers regardless of Windows' MAX_PATH, the same as on POSIX.

## Notes

Same failure class as #148588 (pm workspace copy) and #156983 (update dependency-sync), but at a different call site: `providers/plugin_reload.py::_snapshot`.

### Bug Description

On a locally patched macOS install, the Desktop status bar showed `client v0.23.2+1 (update)`. The **client** dialog offered `v0.23.2` under **New update available**, with a **What's new** list and an **Update now** button. The separate **gateway** dialog correctly said **Back to stable release v0.23.2** and **Roll back to v0.23.2**.

Some contributors run local patches they need to keep the client or gateway working while the corresponding PRs are under review. When the offered release predates the installed build, calling it an update makes it easy to miss that the installed build's extra commits may no longer be in use afterward.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a macOS Desktop build one local commit past `v0.23.2`, with the stable client offer targeting `v0.23.2`.
2. Open the `client v0.23.2+1 (update)` status-bar entry and inspect the installed and offered versions and the confirmation button.
3. Compare it with the separate gateway entry when that updater identifies its target as a rollback. No installation is needed to see the copy mismatch.

### Expected Behavior

If the client updater establishes that the offered build is older, the dialog should name the component and show the direction explicitly: **Roll back Desktop client to v0.23.2** (`v0.23.2+1` → `v0.23.2`). Warn that the target may not include local fixes. If the updater won't permit this move, don't present it as an installable update. Genuine forward client updates should keep the normal update copy.

### Actual Behavior

The client offers `v0.23.2` as a new update without saying it is a step back from the displayed client build. The gateway shows rollback copy for its own operation. I did not click either install button, so this report does not claim that the client handoff succeeds or that any patches were lost. Observed on the patched build; not reproduced on an unmodified checkout of `main`.

### Affected Component

Other — Hermes Desktop client update confirmation (not the gateway installer).

### Debug Report

Not uploaded. The visible version labels and confirmation copy are the evidence for this UI report.

### Operating System

macOS

### Hermes Version

Desktop client: `v0.23.2+1`; offered release: `v0.23.2`.

### Proposed Fix

The overlay already renders rollback copy when the selected target's update status supplies a rollback flag and release version. Check whether the client update path can provide an equivalent classification based on the actual installed and offered build identities. Don't infer it from a `+N` suffix alone if the actual build relationship is unknown. Add a regression case for the client ahead of the offered stable tag, independent of the gateway's status.

Related: #137714 / #137780 established rollback wording for the source-check path. #74885 tracks a different problem involving the handling of local commits during an update; this report is about the client confirmation before any install.

AI-assisted drafting and upstream search.

### Bug Description

Title:
Hermes Desktop falsely reports failure when local LLM response starts with an HTTP status code

DESCRIPTION

Hermes Desktop 0.23.1 (0.0.0) incorrectly displays the error message "Hermes couldn't finish this reply" when a local LLM generates a valid response starting with an HTTP status code, such as "HTTP 200" or "HTTP 503".

The response is generated successfully and remains visible in the chat. However, Hermes also displays an error dialog, with the complete generated response appearing in the error details.

The behavior is reproducible with short responses and appears to depend on the content and position of the HTTP status pattern.

ENVIRONMENT

Application: Hermes Desktop
Version: 0.23.1 (0.0.0)
Operating system: macOS 26.7.3
OS build: 25G342
Architecture: ARM64
Hardware: Apple MacBook Air M5
Unified memory: 32 GiB
Inference engine: llama.cpp b11671 (Metal)
Local model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M
Quantization: Q4_K_M
Thinking: Enabled
Thinking effort: Minimal
Model endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:18434/v1

STEPS TO REPRODUCE

1. Open Hermes Desktop.
2. Start a new chat with the local Qwen model.
3. Enable Thinking and select Minimal effort.
4. Submit the following prompt:

Reply with exactly this string and nothing else: HTTP 200. Do not use tools, execute commands, access files, or browse the web.

5. Wait for the model to generate its response.
6. Observe that the model produces "HTTP 200".
7. Hermes displays "Hermes couldn't finish this reply".
8. Expand the error details.

ACTUAL RESULT

The generated response is displayed correctly, but Hermes also reports a failed reply.

The error details contain the exact text generated by the model rather than an explanatory diagnostic message.

EXPECTED RESULT

Hermes should display the generated response without reporting an error.

A model response containing an HTTP status code should be treated as ordinary output text, not as an API or gateway failure.

CONTROLLED EXPERIMENTS

We performed a series of experiments using the same local model and inference configuration.

Generated response                 Result
--------------------------------------------------
LAB_OK_002                         PASS
HTTP                               PASS
HTTP 200                           FAIL
HTTP 200 (OK).                     FAIL
HTTP 503 (Service Unavailable)     FAIL
STATUS 200 (OK).                   PASS
HTTP STRING 200                    PASS
RESULT: HTTP 200                   PASS

PASS = Response generated without a Hermes error.
FAIL = Response generated, but Hermes displayed the failure dialog.

KEY OBSERVATIONS

1. The issue is not limited to HTTP error codes.
   Both HTTP 200 and HTTP 503 trigger the behavior.

2. The word "HTTP" alone does not trigger the error.

3. Replacing "HTTP" with "STATUS" prevents the error in the tested case.

4. Inserting another word between "HTTP" and the numerical status code also prevents the error.

5. Prepending "RESULT:" before "HTTP 200" prevents the error.

6. The issue occurs even with very short responses, so response length does not appear to be the determining factor.

7. In an earlier failed experiment, the backend logs indicated successful model completion:

Turn ended: reason=text_response(finish_reason=stop)

This suggests that at least one affected response completed successfully at the inference/backend level.

SUSPECTED CAUSE

The experiments suggest that Hermes may incorrectly classify a model-generated response beginning with an HTTP status pattern as a technical error.

A potentially related pattern exists in the Hermes Agent source code, in gateway/run.py, within the function:

_looks_like_gateway_provider_error()

The relevant regular expression is:

r"http\s*\d{3}\b"

This pattern appears consistent with several observed test results.

However, the source code also includes handling that bypasses this classification for local platforms. Therefore, the exact failing code path has not been confirmed.

This is a suspected technical lead, not a verified root cause.

IMPACT

The issue creates false failure notifications for otherwise valid LLM responses.

It can also mislead users into believing that inference, local model serving, or the gateway has failed.

This is particularly problematic when using Hermes for software development, API diagnostics, integration troubleshooting, and analysis of HTTP status codes.

WORKAROUND

In the tested cases, adding a prefix such as "RESULT:" before the HTTP status text prevented the error.

For example:

RESULT: HTTP 200

instead of:

HTTP 200

This is only a prompt-level workaround and does not resolve the underlying issue.

ADDITIONAL NOTES

The problem was identified during a controlled local AI benchmarking session.

No tools, shell commands, file operations, or web browsing were required to reproduce it.

Screenshots of successful and failed experiments are available.

The exact root cause has not yet been established.

Please investigate whether response classification, gateway error detection, or Desktop UI error handling incorrectly interprets valid model-generated HTTP status strings as execution failures.

### Steps to Reproduce


1. Open Hermes Desktop.
2. Start a new chat with the local Qwen model.
3. Enable Thinking and select Minimal effort.
4. Submit the following prompt:

Reply with exactly this string and nothing else: HTTP 200. Do not use tools, execute commands, access files, or browse the web.

5. Wait for the model to generate its response.
6. Observe that the model produces "HTTP 200".
7. Hermes displays "Hermes couldn't finish this reply".
8. Expand the error details.

### Expected Behavior

Response generated without a Hermes error.

### Actual Behavior

Response generated, but Hermes displayed the failure dialog.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

On a macOS host with the default multiplexed gateway serving 15 profiles, the gateway's event-loop thread spends most of its wall time waiting for the GIL. Under host CPU pressure the loop then misses three liveness probes, the watchdog exits with code 75, and Desktop `session.resume` requests time out at 30 s while the loop is starved or the gateway is restarting.

This is the macOS, measured version of #149903 and likely the unexplained cause in #137838. It is not one blocking call: the loop is starved, and the individual blockers already filed (#133891, #146507, #145117) are contributors.

### Measurements (2026-11-11, one host)

Sampled with macOS `sample <pid>` for 6–8 s, counting `take_gil` frames per thread.

| | Steady state, before | Steady state, after mitigation | During startup |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gateway threads | 399–401 | 400 | 152 |
| Event-loop thread waiting in `take_gil` | 69% | 76% | 84% |
| Event-loop thread idle in `kevent` | 0% | 2% | 15% |
| GIL-wait, thread-seconds per second (all threads) | 18.7 | 12.3 | n/a |
| On-CPU demand across gateway threads | 1.71 cores | n/a | n/a |

Largest GIL waiters by thread name: `hosted-room-driver-supervisor` (15 threads, one per profile), `AnyIO worker thread` (45), `asyncio_*` executor (50), `hermes-gateway_*`, `hermes-change-watcher`, `gateway-housekeeping`, `hermes-lease-watcher`, `hermes-skill-count`.

Thread makeup: 90 `mcp-stderr`, 44–45 AnyIO workers, 30 `tokio-rt-worker`, 15 `hosted-room-driver-supervisor`, plus executors.

Symptoms on the same day:

- `Gateway event loop missed 3 consecutive liveness probes … exiting with code 75`: 8 times in about 10 hours.
- `tui_gateway.ws: ws write slow (loop stalled >10.0s)`: 224 lines.
- Desktop: `Resume failed: Error: request timed out after 30s: session.resume`.
- A plain `GET /health` on the gateway port got no response for 30 s while a `loop stalled >10.0s` line was logged.
- Two watchdog dumps with an owner stack show the loop blocked acquiring a `threading.Lock` held by a starved worker: `_ENV_FILE_CACHE_LOCK` (`agent/secret_scope.py`, `load_env_file`, reached from `_profile_runtime_scope`) and `_CONFIG_LOCK` (`hermes_cli/config_effective.py`, reached from cron admission).

Host context: 30 logical CPUs, load average 45–125 from unrelated work (iOS simulators, builds). The gateway itself only wants about 1.7 cores, but with one GIL any descheduling of the holder stalls every profile.

### What made it worse, and what helped

1. **Stdio MCP servers are spawned once per profile.** Each of the 15 profiles lists the same stdio MCP servers, so the gateway ran 15 copies of each. One of them (`peekaboo mcp`) uses about half a core per copy reacting to app launch/quit notifications, so 15 copies took about 7.5 cores from the host. Stopping them and setting `enabled: false` moved `/health` median latency from 0.77 s to 0.26 s and stopped the `loop stalled` lines.
2. #133891 (full routing-index rewrite on every Slack thread reply). Three older watchdog dumps show the loop inside `replace_gateway_routing_entries` with 2,481 routing rows. Applying #133897 locally removed that blocker.

### Expected Behavior

One slow or CPU-starved profile should not stall every other profile's turns, Desktop RPCs and the liveness probe. Fifteen mostly idle profiles should not keep a single interpreter's GIL contended at 12–19 thread-seconds per second.

### Suggestions

- Per-profile periodic work (`hosted-room-driver-supervisor`, change/lease watchers, skill counts, housekeeping) polls from 15+ threads. Fewer wakeups, or one shared ticker, would cut GIL demand that scales with profile count.
- Share one stdio MCP server process across profiles that configure an identical command, args and env, or start them lazily per profile on first use.
- The event loop should not take `threading.Lock`s that worker threads hold across I/O (`_ENV_FILE_CACHE_LOCK`, `_CONFIG_LOCK`, `SessionStore._lock`/`_save_lock`). Under GIL starvation the holder can be parked for tens of seconds.
- `gateway.multiplex_profiles` has no opt-out, so a large install cannot spread profiles over processes. An escape hatch (N worker processes, or opt-out per profile) would give big hosts a way to trade memory for isolation.
- Diagnostics: `faulthandler.dump_traceback(all_threads=True)` stops at 100 threads, so on a 400-thread gateway the watchdog dump often has no event-loop stack. 11 of 15 dumps on this host had none. The owner-stack line fixes this where present; please make sure it is always emitted first.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Default gateway with `multiplex_profiles: true` and about 15 profiles, each with Slack, cron jobs and 15–19 MCP servers (several stdio).
2. Load the host to a load average above its core count.
3. `sample <gateway pid> 6` and count `take_gil` on the main thread; watch for `loop stalled >10.0s` and the liveness watchdog.

### Environment

- macOS 27.2 (Darwin 27.2.0), Apple silicon, 30 logical CPUs
- Python 3.14.9
- Hermes v0.23.0 line, multiplexed default gateway, 15 profiles, 804 sessions, `state.db` 9.9 GB
- Desktop app connected to the same gateway

### Related

#149903, #137838, #133891 (#133897), #146507, #145117, #132546, #134889

issues.body:
## Bug: on macOS, `hermes update` cannot auto-respawn a manually launched dashboard — argv capture via `ps -o command=` mangles the launcher's multi-line `-c` script

### Environment
- macOS (darwin arm64), Hermes v0.23.2 → v0.23.3 (detached @ caafe5389a)
- Dashboard launched normally (TUI/desktop shared backend): `<hermes python> -I -c <multi-line bootstrap script> dashboard --no-open`

### Symptom
With a running `hermes dashboard`, `hermes update` stops the process and tries to respawn it. The respawned child dies within the 1s liveness grace window and the update ends with:

```
⟲ Stopping 1 dashboard process(es) (the running backend no longer matches the updated frontend)
    ✓ stopped PID 62874
    ✗ failed to restart (...): child exited during the first 1s (code 1)
⚠ A web dashboard/serve process was stopped during update and could not be auto-restarted.
⚠ Update follow-up 'gateway_restart' did not finish: serve/dashboard process(es) 62874 were stopped during the update and not brought back
```

`logs/dashboard-restart.log` (the respawned child's stderr) shows:

```
  File "<string>", line 1
    import
          ^
SyntaxError: Expected one or more names after 'import'
```

The dashboard UI then sits on "Restarting gateway…" until the dashboard is relaunched manually.

### Root cause
`main_dashboard._dashboard_cmdline_for_pid` (macOS branch) captures the running process's argv with `ps -p <pid> -o command=` and `shlex.split`. The hermes launcher always invokes the backend as `python -I -c <bootstrap script>` where the script is **multi-line**. BSD `ps` renders embedded newlines as the 4-character escape `\012` in its single-line output and does not preserve quote boundaries, so `shlex.split` cannot reconstruct the original argv. Verified live against a running dashboard (PID 63498):

```
$ ps -p 63498 -o command=   (first 200 chars)
/Users/.../python3 -I -c import os, re, sys\012import contextlib, hashlib, io, pathlib, shutil, subprocess\012os.environ.pop('PYTHONHOME'

>>> argv = shlex.split(raw)
len(argv) == 499
argv[3] == 'import'          # <- the entire -c script reduced to its first word
argv[4:8] == ['os,', 're,', 'sys012import', 'contextlib,']
```

`_respawn_dashboard_processes` re-executes that argv via `subprocess.Popen(command)` (no shell), so Python receives `-c import` → `SyntaxError` → child exits immediately → "failed to restart" → the update's `gateway_restart` follow-up is left unfinished.

Because the launcher always passes a multi-line `-c` payload, **every** normally-launched dashboard/serve backend on macOS is unrespawnable after an update. Linux is unaffected (`/proc/<pid>/cmdline` is NUL-separated and exact); this only bites the macOS `ps` fallback.

### Suggested fix
1. In the update's respawn path, never trust a `ps`-captured argv on macOS: when the captured argv is a hermes launcher invocation (argv[0] is a python interpreter and `-c` is present), rebuild it with `runtime_command(project_root, tail)` where `tail` is everything from the first `dashboard`/`serve` argument onward. This mirrors what `_respawnable_command_for_current_install` already does for the `[python, hermes, …]` shape, and matches how `update_serve_resume.py` already rebuilds a clean argv from the ledger entry.
2. Alternatively, persist the exact argv at spawn time (the spawn ledger — `spawn-ledger.json` — already exists) and have the update's respawn path read it there instead of `ps`.

### Workaround until fixed
- Run `hermes update` with no dashboard open, then relaunch `hermes dashboard --no-open`; or
- run the backend under a launchd job — the update path restarts launchd jobs correctly via `launchctl kickstart`.

issues.body:
**Summary**

On macOS, every `hermes update` ends with:

```
⚠ Update follow-up 'gateway_restart' did not finish: serve/dashboard process(es) … were stopped during the update and not brought back
```

`hermes_cli/main_dashboard.py:_dashboard_cmdline_for_pid()` reconstructs a process argv by running `ps -p <pid> -o command=` and passing the result to `shlex.split()`. macOS `ps` cannot round-trip an argv element that contains newlines: it renders them as the literal text `\012`. The PM launcher starts the dashboard as `python3 -I -c "<multi-line bootstrap script>" dashboard …`, so that single `-c` element is both multi-line and full of spaces. `shlex.split` therefore fragments it into hundreds of tokens and the respawned command cannot even parse.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. macOS, Hermes 0.22.6 (upstream `f0d94882`), dashboard running under a launchd job (wrapper → `hermes dashboard --host <tailscale-ip> --port 9119 --no-open`).
2. Run `hermes update`.
3. The updater stops the dashboard backend and tries to respawn it from the captured argv.

**Actual**

```
⟲ Stopping 1 dashboard process(es) (the running backend no longer matches the updated frontend)
    ✓ stopped PID <pid>
    ✗ failed to restart (... dashboard --host … --port 9119 --no-open):
        child exited during the first 1s (code 1)
```

`~/.hermes/logs/dashboard-restart.log`:

```
  File "<string>", line 1
    import
          ^
SyntaxError: Expected one or more names after 'import'
```

**Root cause**

The real argv of the dashboard backend is roughly:

```
[python3, -I, -c, "import os, re, sys\nimport contextlib, …", dashboard, --host, …, --port, 9119, --no-open]
```

`ps` prints that `-c` element with `\012` in place of each newline. `shlex.split` on that text then

- consumes the backslash and leaves the literal `012`, producing `…sys012import…`, and
- splits on every space inside the script.

Confirmed against the live process: the reconstructed argv had **503 elements** (`import`, `os,`, `re,`, `sys012import`, …) instead of ~12, so the child executed `python3 -I -c import …` and died with SyntaxError.

Reproduction snippet (macOS, run against any process whose argv contains a newline):

```python
import shlex, subprocess
out = subprocess.run(["ps", "-A", "-o", "pid=,command="], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
for line in out.split("\n"):
    parts = line.strip().split(None, 1)
    if len(parts) == 2 and parts[0] == "<pid>":
        print(len(shlex.split(parts[1])))   # 503 instead of ~12
```

**Expected**

The respawn should replay the exact argv bytes.

**Suggested fix**

- On macOS, prefer a real argv source — `psutil.Process(pid).cmdline()`, which `dashboard_procs.py` already uses elsewhere — and fall back to `ps` + `shlex.split` only when psutil is unavailable.
- If `ps` must stay, un-escape `\012`, `\011`, `\013` back into real characters *before* splitting (`shlex.split` eats the backslash, so it must happen first).
- Minor: this is currently cosmetic — launchd `KeepAlive` restarts the wrapper anyway — but the update still books the runtime as "not brought back", which is misleading.

**Environment**

- macOS 27.2, Apple silicon
- Hermes Agent v0.22.6 (upstream `f0d94882`), git install
- Dashboard under launchd, job name `ai.hermes.dashboard`

issues.title: Cron: expose the actual claimed scheduled instant to script-only jobs

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: comp/cron
labels.description: Cron scheduler and job management

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
## Current behavior

The built-in recurring scheduler records a UTC scheduled instant for a scheduled execution. A script-only job does not receive that instant. The script can see its start time, but the two differ when a tick is delayed. The current registry cursor may already point to the next occurrence and is not a safe substitute. This was observed on a local source install at `e93b3da9a8062aebee83894ece5cc7206eddc4e1`; the relevant sources are unchanged in the stable and canary commits inspected.

## Requested behavior

Provide a documented, optional way for a script-only job to receive the scheduled instant tied to the execution claim. The value should not come from an inherited environment variable, a mutable next-run cursor, or the process clock. A manual execution must not be represented as a scheduled execution. Please advise whether the existing execution metadata has a supported downstream interface or which scope would be acceptable for a contribution.

## Acceptance

Use an inert script to report the value. Verify the same UTC instant in the scheduled claim, the execution record, and the child. Compare a normal manual script run, a later scheduled run, and a delayed but still eligible tick. Preserve default behavior for scripts not opting in. Related design context: [#105690](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/105690) concerns manual runs incorrectly consuming a future occurrence; it is not the same request.

This note does not propose an unreviewed scheduler replacement, a state migration, or changing provider credentials. No application names, job identifiers, live logs, or private artifacts are included.

issues.body:
## Bug description

In Hermes Desktop, the dotted activity indicator and its live timer continue ticking underneath a visible, completed assistant reply. This is not the static elapsed-time footer. The gateway logs show the reply completed and was sent. Fully quitting and reopening Desktop did not prevent the symptom on a subsequent reply in the same conversation.

## Steps observed

1. Resume an existing conversation in Hermes Desktop on macOS.
2. Send a prompt and wait for the complete answer to appear.
3. Observe that the activity timer below it continues counting after the reply has finished.
4. Fully quit Desktop with Cmd+Q, reopen it, return to the existing conversation, and send another short prompt. The symptom recurred after that reply, too.

This has been observed in one existing conversation. Fresh-conversation behavior is untested.

## Expected behavior

Once a reply has completed, the live activity indicator should disappear. A fixed elapsed-time footer, if shown, should stop counting.

## Sanitized diagnostic evidence

- First observed turn: gateway logged `response ready` and `Sending response`; reported duration was `30.0s`. The answer was already visible while the activity timer continued.
- After quitting and reopening Desktop: gateway reported `response ready` after `12.2s` on a short test reply; the same live-timer symptom was observed after the reply.
- The event or renderer state transition responsible has not been isolated. The gateway logs establish completion; they do not establish which completion events the renderer received.

## Environment

- macOS 26.6.2, arm64
- Source-built Hermes Desktop on stable Hermes Agent v0.23.3, commit `caafe5389a`
- Local gateway connection

Related: #50159 also describes a stale Thinking indicator, but the final answer was missing in that report. Here the complete answer is visible. It is not yet known whether the two share a root cause.
