prs.title: feat(desktop): create, edit and delete routines on the Routines page
prs.body:
Part 11 of 11 · builds on #157894 — merged, routines are created, edited and deleted on the Routines page, in one side sheet, and nowhere else in the redesign. Classic's Scheduled jobs page is unchanged.

| Detail (row action on hover) | Create | Paused, light |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![detail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/ddb1637e092fa99abe2ab1f537dc494e9b9d37d9/apps/desktop/docs/images/routines-detail.png) | ![create](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/ddb1637e092fa99abe2ab1f537dc494e9b9d37d9/apps/desktop/docs/images/routines-create.png) | ![paused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/ddb1637e092fa99abe2ab1f537dc494e9b9d37d9/apps/desktop/docs/images/routines-paused-light.png) |

| Delete confirms in the footer | Held delete with Undo |
| --- | --- |
| ![confirm](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/ddb1637e092fa99abe2ab1f537dc494e9b9d37d9/apps/desktop/docs/images/routines-delete-confirm.png) | ![undo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/ddb1637e092fa99abe2ab1f537dc494e9b9d37d9/apps/desktop/docs/images/routines-deleted-undo.png) |

**List and detail**
- The panel lists every routine grouped Needs attention / Scheduled / Paused. The "All routines" table is gone; the first routine is shown when none is selected.
- Header: Run now ("Run routine" while paused), a pause / resume icon button, and Edit, each with a tooltip on hover and focus.
- One summary card (instruction, frequency, last ran, next run, send results to), a failed-run banner with the plain reason and Retry, and run history whose row actions show on hover, focus and always on touch. History loads in batches as it scrolls.

**One sheet for create and edit**
- Agent picker only with more than one agent; Blank or Template; templates are searchable and grouped by the catalog's categories.
- A template pre-fills name, instruction, schedule and delivery. `/api/cron/blueprints` gains `prefill`: the job a template's defaults would create, or null when a required field has no default. An older backend falls back to title and description.
- The frequency read-back and a "First run" line appear once a frequency is set (`lib/routine-first-run.ts`). Advanced is collapsed, with its two descriptions as info tooltips. The footer is opaque.
- Edit locks the agent with a tooltip saying why.

**Delete with Undo**

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Held: Delete (marker written, routine paused and hidden)
  Held --> Restored: Undo (marker dropped, resumed if it was on)
  Held --> Deleted: dismiss banner / delete another / leave Routines / close window
  Held --> Deleted: next launch, marker unrefreshed for 60s
  Held --> Restored: delete fails (shown again, paused)
```

- A real delete destroys run history, so Delete holds it while the banner is up. Each step is ordered to fail toward not deleting: the marker is written before the pause and dropped before a resume.

**Agent settings**
- Settings › Routines and the Overview's routines section are read-only lists that open the routine, or the create sheet with that agent preselected, on the Routines page. The embedded editor, the table overview and their dialogs are deleted.

**Tests**
- `routine-held-delete.test.ts`: every hold / undo / commit / abandoned path.
- `routines.test.tsx`, `cron/index.test.tsx`: header actions per state, tooltips on focus, sheet create / edit / validation, template prefill, focus return on Esc, read-only agent lists.
- `lib/routine-first-run.test.ts` in three time zones; `tests/cron/test_blueprint_catalog.py` for `prefill`.

**Not verified:** Electron; a real window close or crash during a held delete (store tests only); accents other than blue; a routine whose agent is offline.

prs.title: feat(desktop): onboarding in the redesign: rename splash, first-time splash, starter ideas, sign-up seam
prs.body:
Part 7 of 11 · builds on #157281 · next #157504 — merged alone, users see classic exactly as with part 6; every surface here renders only in the redesign, which part 8 turns on. Two audiences: people who already use Hermes and meet the new names, and first-timers. | Existing user: rename splash | First-timer: welcome splash | | --- | --- | | ![rename splash](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/9b63b51d17f57b7b51046c9cff3e29bf9dfeaf2a/apps/desktop/docs/images/onboarding-rename-splash.png) | ![first-time splash](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/9b63b51d17f57b7b51046c9cff3e29bf9dfeaf2a/apps/desktop/docs/images/onboarding-first-time-splash.png) | | **Notifications tray** | **"Make it yours" (green)** | | ![tray](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/9b63b51d17f57b7b51046c9cff3e29bf9dfeaf2a/apps/desktop/docs/images/onboarding-tray.png) | ![accent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/9b63b51d17f57b7b51046c9cff3e29bf9dfeaf2a/apps/desktop/docs/images/onboarding-accent-green.png) | | **Starter ideas** | **Message held until sign up** | | ![starter ideas](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/9b63b51d17f57b7b51046c9cff3e29bf9dfeaf2a/apps/desktop/docs/images/onboarding-starter-ideas.png) | ![held message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/9b63b51d17f57b7b51046c9cff3e29bf9dfeaf2a/apps/desktop/docs/images/onboarding-held-message.png) | | **A newer build is deployed** | **Phone** | | ![new version](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/9b63b51d17f57b7b51046c9cff3e29bf9dfeaf2a/apps/desktop/docs/images/onboarding-new-version.png) | ![phone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/9b63b51d17f57b7b51046c9cff3e29bf9dfeaf2a/apps/desktop/docs/images/onboarding-phone.png) | ```mermaid flowchart TD Boot["first settled look at the machine"] --> Q{"had chats before the redesign?"} Q -- yes --> Rename["rename splash
old word → new word, spotlight on the nav"] Q -- no --> First["first-time splash
four rows + Make it yours"] Rename --> Tray["bell lights once; tray card reopens it"] First --> Tray First --> Landing["empty chat: greeting + four starter ideas"] Landing --> Send{"sign up required?"} Send -- no --> Run["message sends as usual"] Send -- yes --> Held["held locally, shown with a local reply"] Held -- "signed in, connected" --> Run ``` **Existing users** - `SplashSurface` covers the chat stage; each row maps a classic word to its new name and spotlights where it lives (`NavSpot`, `data-nav-spot`). Counts wait for their source, so a row never shows 0 before it has loaded. - Closes on any nav click (which still navigates), the button or Escape; the bell's tray card reopens it. - ⌘K still answers to the classic words ("cron jobs" → "Routines, formerly Cron jobs"), from one alias table (`lib/old-name-aliases.ts`). - A Webapp tab left open learns a newer build is deployed and offers a refresh; it never reloads itself (`store/new-version.ts`). **First-timers** - First-time splash: no row starts active; "Make it yours" sets light/dark through the theme system and one of five accents (`store/portal-accent.ts`, `html[data-portal-accent]`). Both are native radio groups. - The accent recolours the brand gesture only (fill, ink, tints, focus rings, selections). The navy surfaces and the skin's `--dt-primary` stay as they are. - Starter ideas sit under the composer through a `landing` slot and send through the composer like typed text. They retire after two finished chats or on Hide. | Accent | Fill / dark ink | White on fill | Fill as text, light (worst) | Dark ink (worst) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Blue | #0000f2 / #8585ff | 8.22 | 6.41 | 5.51 | | Violet | #6d28d9 / #b79cff | 6.35 | 5.25 | 7.04 | | Green | #086b36 / #3fd68a | 5.92 | 4.98 | 8.53 | | Orange | #a33f00 / #ff9a52 | 5.74 | 4.82 | 7.67 | | Pink | #b0124f / #ff80b0 | 6.16 | 5.02 | 7.06 | Contrast ratios computed from the shipped token values by `tokens/portal-accent-contrast.test.ts` (AA for text is 4.5). **Sign-up seam** - `lib/visitor-access.ts`: `VisitorAccess = open | sign_up_required{signUpUrl}`. Every page a Hermes backend serves today resolves to `open`; native never asks. ```ts // The hosted page for signed-out visitors injects the target, like the server's other __HERMES_* globals. window.__HERMES_SIGN_UP_URL__ = 'https://…/signup' // startSignUp(from) sends the visitor there with return_to=; // a return with ?hermes_sign_in=failed is read once and stripped. ``` - While sign up is required, `submitText` (the one function the composer, the ideas and the queue send through) holds the latest message in localStorage for up to a day. Nothing reaches the gateway and no conversation is stored. - After sign-in the held message is removed from storage first, then sent as a new chat, so it runs at most once; a failed send puts the text back in the composer. **Metrics** — closed codes on both sides of the shared contract, recorded only behind the usage-sharing gate; anything else collapses to `other`. | Kind | Codes | | --- | --- | | `splash` | `rename_` / `first_time_` × shown, reopened, closed by nav / button / escape / signup | | `splash_row` | first hover or focus of each row per showing | | `starter_chip`, `starter_chips` | which idea was sent; hidden (auto / user), shown again | | `sign_up` | `splash`, `tray`, `chat` | | `theme_pick` | mode and colour | | `alias_search` | which classic word was typed, never the query | **Smaller hubs** — `ChatBar` hands busy input, image requests and file drop to named hooks (`use-composer-busy-input.ts`, `use-composer-image-requests.ts`, `use-conversation-file-drop.ts`) and `ContribWiring` hands the new-project session request to `use-new-project-session-request.ts`, so both stay within their size ratchets. **Classic** — unchanged. The splash, tray, notice, bell and starter ideas mount only in the redesign's routes and rail; the palette aliases are redesign-only. The sign-up hold applies only in the redesign (`$signUpRequired` reads the shell): classic has nowhere to show a held message, so it sends as before. **Not in this PR** - Portal and hosting: injecting the sign-up URL, honouring `return_to` on the same origin, the failure parameter, routing after sign-in. - Booting with no machine at all; machine provisioning; per-account (rather than per-browser) guidance state, which sits behind `store/guidance-ledger.ts`. - An Appearance setting for the accent. **Stack** (integration branch for testing, redesign on: #152168) 1. #157276 2. #157277 3. #157278 4. #157279 5. #157280 6. #157281 7. #157503 ← this PR 8. #157504 9. #157536 10. #157894 11. #157959 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: fix(desktop): list models at once in a new session (seed catalog from profile cache)
prs.body:
## Problem

Creating a new session and opening the model picker shows a loading skeleton for several seconds before any model is listed.

Fixes #151309

The catalog query key carries the session id (`modelOptionsQueryKey(profile, sessionId, owner)`), so every new session starts with a cold cache and waits for a full `model.options` rebuild. Profiled on a real install (`build_model_options_payload`, 8 providers): **~2.9 s warm, ~6 s cold** (imports excluded), while `session.create` builds the agent concurrently.

## Fix

Seed a cold catalog query with the newest catalog the **same profile + registry connection** already holds (`placeholderData`). The session's own fetch still runs and replaces it. The session-specific selection (`model`, `provider`, `is_current`) is dropped from the placeholder so another session's pick never paints in the new one.

Only a cached catalog with at least one selectable model can seed (`hasSelectableModels`, the invariant `model-options.ts` already uses for the live fetch). A cached entry that holds only provider shells with no models is skipped, so the placeholder never swaps the loading state for a false empty picker; with nothing usable cached, the menu keeps loading until the session's own fetch lands. This rule is @kvnloo's commit (`926c12bdaa`); `5c3d2bc7e5` adds the explicit `data &&` guard that `tsc` needs, because `hasSelectableModels` returns a plain boolean and does not narrow `data`.

Applied to every `model-options` query consumer: composer model menu, menu controller, chat bar quick models, full model picker, Edit Models dialog.

Backend latency (credential pool / auth store / `.env` re-read dozens to hundreds of times per call) is out of scope here.

## Verification

- New tests: `cachedProfileModelOptions` picks the newest same-profile catalog, strips the session pick, never crosses profile or connection, and does not seed from provider shells with no selectable models; the menu lists models for a new session while its own fetch never resolves.
- RED: with the menu's `placeholderData` removed, the menu test fails (`Unable to find ... Gemini 3.1 Pro`). On `main` at `1d70b4a489`, `model-options.test.ts` + `model-catalog-menu.test.tsx` fail 4 of 64; the behavioural one, `model-catalog-menu.test.tsx` "lists the profile catalog at once while its own slow fetch is still in flight", times out without `Gemini 3.1 Pro`.
- Head `5c3d2bc7e5` merged with `main` at `1d70b4a489`: the model suites pass 7 files / 114 tests; `src/app/session`, `src/app/chat` and the menu suites pass 376 files / 3,236 tests (`chat/index.test.tsx`'s full module mock gains the new export).
- `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` (apps/desktop) is clean in `src/`, and ESLint is clean on the changed files.

## What does this PR do?

A bot's canonical Bot Chat in the main workspace tab shows the bot's name ("Sylar") until the conversation auto-compresses. After that the caption cycles **Sylar → Untitled session → Bot Chat** and stays on "Bot Chat" until the bot row is clicked again. A long-running companion chat hits this on every compression. One real profile compressed seven times in a day, and every earlier segment ended up with `title = NULL`.

There are two causes, both renderer-side:

1. **The scope is lost on rotation.** A Bot Chat opened `in-place` lands in MAIN, which has no tile. Its bot-mode scope (`workspaceOwnerKey`, `workspaceTabTitle`) lives only in `$botChatScopes[storedId]`. Compression rotates the stored id, and `rekeySessionTile` re-homes tiles only. The new tip has no scope, so `workspaceOwnerTitle` never swaps the stored "Bot Chat" for the bot's label. The persisted `$botChatSessionIds` mark has the same gap: the composer's branch rail comes back on the tip.
2. **Untitled segments fall through to the generic fallback.** The lineage carries "Bot Chat" root → tip only after the rotation publishes (`hermes_state_session_list.py`), so for a while the selected row is untitled. `sessionTitle()` then returns the preview or `'Untitled session'`. That fallback also bypasses the owner caption, which is keyed on the canonical title.

## Related Issue

Fixes #151308

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/store/bot-chat-scope.ts` (new): the bot-chat scope store, moved out of `session-states.ts`, which was already over the file-size ratchet. It adds `carryBotChatScope(prev, next)`, which copies the window-local scope and the persisted mark onto the new tip. The previous id keeps its entry, because main still names it until route-follow re-selects the tip.
- `apps/desktop/src/store/session-states.ts`: `rekeySessionTile` calls `carryBotChatScope` **before** the tile lookup, since main has no tile. The store moved out, so this file shrinks.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/pane-shell/workspace-scope.ts`: adds `workspaceStoredTitle(rowTitle, scope)`. An untitled row under a canonical bot tab takes the canonical title, and the owner caption still applies. It has no opinion outside a canonical bot tab: `+` side threads and Sessions tabs keep the existing fallback. Also adds the shared `WorkspaceTabScope` type.
- Every caption surface now uses it:
  - `app/contrib/controller.tsx` (main workspace tab)
  - `app/chat/session-tile.tsx` (tile tab title and drag payload)
  - `store/browser-tab-title.ts` (web host `document.title`; it now also reads `$botChatScopes`, so a main-held Bot Chat is captioned by its bot)
- Import-only updates for the moved store: `app/chat/composer/index.tsx`, `app/contrib/hooks/use-desktop-integrations.ts`.

The Bot Mode identity contract is unchanged (`apps/desktop/src/AGENTS.md`): the chat is still resolved by `(profile, "Bot Chat")` on every open. Nothing stores or reads a session-id pointer. The carried scope only labels the tab.

### Second commit: the tip loses `hidden` (backend)

Found while verifying this fix against a live install: the caption was not the only thing that broke at
rotation. `_publish_child_session_row` (`hermes_state_compression.py`) copies `pinned`, `archived` and
`auto_archived` onto a compression continuation but not `hidden`, so every segment after the first is
born **visible** under a hidden root. Readers then disagree about the same conversation:

- listings admit a lineage by its ROOT's flag (`s.hidden = 0`), so a lineage whose root stayed hidden
  disappears from the sidebar and the pinned back-fill even though its live tip reads as visible;
- the canonical Bot Chat rename guard (`_set_session_title_in_transaction`) and the desktop keep-list
  (`mergeSessionPage` survivors skip `hidden`) read the TIP's flag, so after one compression the bot's
  chat loses its rename guard and resurfaces in the Sessions sidebar as a raw "Bot Chat" row.

On the reporting install every canonical Bot Chat that had compressed was mixed (one chain: 19 segments,
18 visible). Two had been renamed away from "Bot Chat" (possible only because the tip was unguarded);
Bot Mode then found no registry row, minted a fresh Bot Chat, and the old conversation became
unreachable from the sidebar.

Fix: the continuation takes `MAX(hidden)` over its lineage (`_LINEAGE_CTE_SQL`, the same selector the
lineage-wide setters use) instead of the parent's value, so stores that already hold visible segments
under a hidden root heal at their next compression. Branch/reset children still start visible.
Tests: `tests/hermes_state/test_hidden_lineage_compression.py` (real `SessionDB`, temp `HERMES_HOME`) —
canonical chat stays hidden through two compressions and keeps its rename guard; a mixed legacy lineage
heals; control: a visible chat stays visible. RED on base (`{'mid': 0, 'tip': 0}`, `0 == 1`), GREEN here.
Docs: `website/docs/developer-guide/session-storage.md` lists `hidden` among the inherited flags.
Existing mixed lineages that never compress again stay mixed; a one-shot migration would need a
schema bump, so it is left out.

### Third commit: the caption is lost on relaunch (desktop)

Still reproduced on a build with the two commits above: after the app relaunched, the Sylar tab read
"Bot Chat" again. Both inputs of a bot tab's caption were window-local:

- the owner label (bot -> display name) is published only while the Bots pane renders
  (`roster-pane-lifecycle.ts`), so every restored bot tab read the stored "Bot Chat" until that pane
  was opened;
- the main tab's bot-chat scope (`$botChatScopes`), so a Bot Chat restored into main read "Bot Chat"
  until it was opened from its bot again.

Both now persist, the way tile scope already does: the last-known owner labels (the roster republishes
on every snapshot, so a rename still follows) and the main tab's scopes (validated on read, capped at
200 entries since each rotation adds the tip and keeps the previous id). Nothing is per-bot.
`src/store/bot-tab-caption-relaunch.test.ts` simulates a relaunch (fresh module graph over the same
localStorage): 3 of its 4 tests fail without the change; the 4th (malformed values are ignored) is the
guard.

### Fourth commit: the "New session" gap right after rotation (@kvnloo)

Contributed by @kvnloo (`4a5e95f7e3`). Rotation can select the new tip before its row reaches the session
lists. In that gap `syncWorkspaceTitle` passes the generic "New session" fallback and mounts the draft-title
override, so the tab briefly read "New session" although `carryBotChatScope` had already moved the bot scope
to the tip. `workspaceOwnerTitle` now treats "New session" like the canonical title when the scope is a
canonical bot tab (bot mode, owner key and `workspaceTabTitle` all set), and the controller does not mount the
draft title under such a scope. Ordinary drafts and Sessions tabs keep "New session" (controls in the new
`workspace-scope.test.ts` case).

The follow-up `31f1d729bf` replaced the literal with `NEW_SESSION_TITLE` from `lib/chat-runtime`, and
`5d39651a15` reverts it: `workspace-scope` is loaded by store modules, and importing `chat-runtime` there
creates an import cycle (`transcript-lightbox` reads `$activeSessionId` before it is defined) that broke the
wider desktop suite. The literal `'New session'` stays, with a comment saying why it is not imported.

## How to Test

1. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/store/bot-chat-scope.test.ts src/store/browser-tab-title.test.ts src/components/pane-shell/workspace-scope.test.ts src/store/bot-tab-caption-relaunch.test.ts`
   and `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_state/test_hidden_lineage_compression.py`
2. **RED on base:** applied to the parent commit, the new tests fail. Rotation does not carry the scope or the mark, and the browser tab title reads `Hermes` instead of `Sylar · Hermes`.
3. **Probe on the real controller:** a throwaway, uncommitted test drove `syncWorkspaceTitle` through open → old segment untitled → rotate + select tip (untitled) → tip titled "Bot Chat":
   - base: `Sylar → Untitled session → Untitled session → Bot Chat`
   - this PR: `Sylar → Sylar → Sylar → Sylar`

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass. Ran `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_state/`: the new file and the
  lineage-flag neighbours pass; the other failures there reproduce identically on base on this host (SQLite 3.50.4
  WAL-reset guard, live-writer guards).
- [x] `python scripts/check`: code health is 0 blocking / 0 advisory. The only local failure is `profile-archives`, from gitignored `.cache/desktop-inputs/**.tar.gz` packager downloads that are not part of the diff.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.3.1 (arm64), unit and integration level, plus the live install below.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Docstrings updated; no user docs affected
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`: N/A
- [x] Cross-platform: N/A (renderer state only)
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas: N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

- On `main` at `1d70b4a489` the PR's tests fail: `workspace-scope.test.ts` (`expected 'New session' to be 'Alpha'`) and
  `tests/hermes_state/test_hidden_lineage_compression.py` (`{'mid': 0, 'tip': 0}`). Head `5d39651a15` merged with that `main`:
  the 4 desktop test files pass 28/28, the Python test 3/3, and the neighbouring suites 94 files / 741 tests.
  `tsc -p . --noEmit` and ESLint are clean.
- Full `npx vitest run` on a heavily loaded host (load avg 120–160, another suite running in parallel) reported timeout failures across `electron/`, `scripts/` and 11 `ui` files. None of the `electron/`/`scripts/` files import renderer code. The 11 `ui` files were then A/B'd sequentially against the parent commit (`cabaf053b5`). Run in the same order, the failure sets were **identical**: 5 failed on each side, all 15 s timeouts in `use-keybinds-browser`, `browser-hints` and `terminal-ownership`. `terminal-ownership.test.ts` run alone passed 6/6 on both sides at low load.

**Live install (2026-11-03).** The backend commit runs on the reporting install; the desktop commits run in a
packaged build on a second Mac against it. Mixed lineages already on disk were repaired once (backup first,
`SessionDB.set_session_hidden`), and a scan of every profile DB found none left. Note for anyone verifying this
live: compression runs in whichever process hosts the turn. Desktop sessions run inside the dashboard
(`hermes dashboard --tui`), not the gateway, so **both** processes must be restarted onto this commit. With only
the gateway restarted, the Bot Chat compressed twice more from the desktop and both continuations were born
visible again; after restarting the dashboard as well, the lineage holds `hidden = 1`, and the next desktop-side
compression (16 minutes later) published its continuation with `hidden = 1` and the "Bot Chat" title:
the end-to-end check on the real install.

**Overlap with #148319:** both PRs edit `tileDragPayload` / `tabTitle` in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/session-tile.tsx`
(#148319 skips blank owner-stub rows when naming a tab). The two changes compose; whichever lands second
needs a mechanical rebase: read the title from the non-blank row, then apply `workspaceStoredTitle`.

The earlier "window-local after relaunch" limitation is removed by the third commit.

**Related:** #97527 (open) keeps Bot Chat tab identity across backend restarts and touches the same files
(`app/chat/session-tile.tsx`, `app/contrib/controller.tsx`, `store/session-states.ts`), so a textual conflict is
possible whichever lands second.

Scope note: the reporting install additionally lists each canonical Bot Chat in its Sessions sidebar (captioned by the bot) through a local patch that is not part of this PR and deliberately departs from the Bot Mode contract. It does not interact with this fix: the chat keeps `hidden = 1` there too, and that flag is what this PR keeps consistent across a lineage.

prs.title: fix(desktop): session clicks and New session open in your tab; New session uses the default profile
prs.body:
## Clicking a session should open it where you're looking

Today a plain click on a sidebar session or a Bot roster row doesn't open in the focused tab. It replaces whichever tab holds **main**, a tab users can't see or predict, because main moves when tabs close. Open an untitled tab with ⌘T, click a session, and a *different* tab gets overwritten while yours stays empty. It reads as "the app puts my chat in a random tab."

After this PR, a click behaves the way it does in every browser: **it opens in the tab you're on.**

Fixes #148318

## What changes

- **Focused session tab**: the clicked session takes its slot. The replaced chat goes to the ⌘⇧T stack (a busy one keeps streaming), and an untouched untitled tab is consumed with no undo entry.
- **Bot roster rows** get the same placement and keep their Bot scope. This is a separate commit, so it can be dropped on its own.
- **"New session"** (the sidebar row and ⌘N) had the same flaw: it reset main, so it overwrote whichever tab held main. With a session tab focused, it now opens the fresh chat as a **new tab right after the focused one**; the conversation you were in stays open and untouched, and main is not reset. An untouched untitled tab is kept as is (it already is a new session, so no twin). The tab-strip "+" and ⌘T still stack a new tab at the end. Third commit, separable; the three new-session doors move into `useNewSessionDoors` so `ContribWiring` does not grow.
  - Revised after manual testing: an earlier revision had "New session" take the focused tab's slot (the replaced chat went to ⌘⇧T). Unlike a session click, which names a conversation to show *here*, "New session" asks for a new place to work; swapping out the chat the user was reading read as losing it.
- **A new tab is a new session** (fourth commit). The tab-strip "+" / ⌘T, and "New session" into a focused tab, mint a tile whose session has a row from creation: the owner stub that routes its resume (#102792), with no title, preview or messages. The tab read that stub like a real untitled conversation: captioned **"Untitled session"** and opened as an **empty pane**, because the new-session intro rendered only in the primary chat. A blank row now names nothing (the tab reads "New session" / the composer's live name, also after a relaunch probes the row back), and a tab whose row is blank renders the same intro as main, under the same toggle and transcript rules. An unresolved row is not treated as a draft, so a restored conversation never flashes the intro over its loading transcript.
- **"New session" and ⌘N open the default profile, not a bot** (fifth commit). They are the generic doors, but two things sent them to a bot. (1) A bot chat pins its exact route as the next new chat's owner (`pinNewChatRoute`) and selecting another bot does not unpin it; ⌘N cleared only the profile half of the pin, so the session opened in the *previous* bot. (2) With no saved "Default profile" preference (the out-of-the-box state) they fell back to the ambient profile, i.e. the bot or workspace selected last. Both doors now call `prepareGenericNewSession()` (`app/session/new-session-route.ts`): drop the whole pin, then target the saved preference, else the root `default` profile on the active source. A project scope keeps its own owner; the bot doors ("+"/⌘T in Bot Mode, "New chat with this bot"), "+" outside Bot Mode and `/new` are unchanged.
- **"New session" with the first tab focused opens a new tab too** (sixth commit). The new-tab rule above covered session *tiles* only; with main focused the doors still reset main in place. To the user main is just the strip's first tab, usually holding a conversation, so ⌘N on the first tab swapped out the chat they were reading while the same gesture on any other tab opened a new one. A focused main that holds a chat now gets the new tab right after it. A focused main that already is a blank new session (`mainIsUntouchedDraft`, the predicate the strip "+" uses to reuse a draft) is still reset in place: it is its own twin. A focused page/preview tab is unchanged.
- **Unchanged**: a session already on screen is fronted, never duplicated. ⌘/⌃/middle-click opens a new tab, ⇧⌘-click opens a new window. Clicks (not "New session") with main or a non-session tab focused behave exactly as before. ⌘K and notifications are not touched.

The change is renderer-only: `open-session.ts`, a new `app/chat/focused-tab-open.ts`, and `app/chat/use-new-session-doors.ts` wired from `contrib/wiring.tsx`, plus the caption/intro fix in `session-tile.tsx`, `intro-visibility.ts` and `lib/chat-runtime.ts`, and the generic-door owner in `app/session/new-session-route.ts` (called from `use-new-session-doors.ts`, `use-session-actions` and the ⌘N keybind). It uses the same focus ruler as ⌘T/⌘W.

## Proof

- `focused-tab-open.test.ts` drives the real `openSession` against the real tile and layout stores. **On `main` it fails 7 of 11; with this PR all 11 pass.** The 4 that pass on both are the controls: main focused, already open, ⌘-click, and a Bot Chat already in main.
- The "New session" block (5 tests: opens a new tab beside the focused tile and leaves it and main alone, keeps an untouched untitled tab, opens a new tab beside a focused main that holds a chat (with and without other tabs), and resets a focused main that is already a blank new session) fails without the change and passes with it; against the previous revision (take the focused slot) the first test fails, so it pins the new-tab contract. On the fifth commit the two main-holds-a-chat tests fail (`expected false to be true`) and the blank-main control passes.
- Sixth commit, on top of the full stack with the other open PRs: tsc, eslint, prettier, `scripts/check --only health`, and `vitest run src/store src/app/chat src/app/profiles src/app/open-session.test.ts src/components/pane-shell src/plugins/hermes-bots` (634 files / 5306 tests) pass.
- `new-session-tab-content.test.ts` (6 tests): on the parent commit 5 fail, the first with `expected 'Untitled session' to be 'New session'`; all pass here. The control (a real conversation keeps its title, or "Untitled session" once it has messages) passes on both.
- `generic-new-session-doors.test.tsx` (8 tests): on the parent commit 6 fail (the ambient case opens in `bot-b` instead of `default`); all pass here. The controls (a saved preference wins, a project scope keeps its owner) pass on both. The fifth commit also builds clean in the full stack with the other open PRs (tsc, 5208 desktop tests, `scripts/check`).
- `vitest run --project ui` after the fourth commit: 1522 files / 12769 tests pass.
- Full desktop `vitest run`: every `ui` file passes; the only failures are 11 `electron`/`scripts` files that fail the same way without this branch on my host (a Python helper without `ruamel`, native-dep staging).
- The related suites (open-session, draft reuse, Bot Chat registry, SDK) pass 206/206. `scripts/check`, `tsc`, eslint and prettier are clean.
- Manually verified on macOS 26.3.1 with a packaged build of this branch against a remote gateway (commits 1-3).
  The fourth commit is in the packaged build. The "New session opens a new tab" revision comes from that manual
  testing (the slot-taking behaviour was rejected in use) and was then verified by hand in a packaged build.
  The fifth commit was verified by hand in a packaged build (⌘N and the sidebar row with a bot selected and no saved default).
  The sixth commit was verified by hand in a packaged build (⌘N with the first tab focused and holding a chat opens a new tab beside it; the chat stays).
- Overlap with #148305: both PRs edit `tileDragPayload` / `tabTitle` in `app/chat/session-tile.tsx`. The changes
  compose (the packaged build carries both); whichever lands second needs a mechanical rebase: name the tab
  from the non-blank row, then apply #148305's `workspaceStoredTitle`.

```
cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/app/chat/focused-tab-open.test.ts src/app/open-session.test.ts
```

## Related

#146635 (more untitled tabs make this bug more visible), #148121, #147418.

Who owns a generic new session (fifth commit only). The fifth commit makes the generic doors (sidebar "New session", ⌘N) call `prepareGenericNewSession()`: drop the whole pinned route (profile, route, source), then target the saved Default-profile preference, else the root `default` profile on the active source, so an ambient bot selection no longer captures ⌘N. Open work in the same function:

- **#135660** (open, P2) lets the live profile (`$newChatProfile`, else `$activeGatewayProfile`) win over a saved default in `defaultNewSessionTarget()`. The two rules disagree when a saved default exists and the rail shows another profile: here the saved default wins, there the live profile does. With no saved default #135660 leaves the function as it is, and this PR falls back to root `default`. The branches merge without a textual conflict, but combined, ⌘N with a saved default would follow the gateway's active profile again (a bot's, when a bot is selected), because `prepareGenericNewSession()` clears `$newChatProfile` before asking.
- **#144389** (open, P2, fixes #144386) is about which gateway a generic new session lands on: `clearNewChatIntent()` (profile, route, captured source and the legacy pin), called from `prepareDefaultNewSession()` and the ⌘N keybind, and a `win=secondary` pop-out's launch pair no longer acts as a default. It shares this PR's aim of not letting a stale pinned route steer ⌘N, but with no saved default it lets the draft resolve from the active gateway's live profile, where this PR targets root `default` on the active source. Textual conflicts: the `session.new` keybind in `app/hooks/use-keybinds.ts` (import and body: this PR removes `$newChatProfile.set(null)` and moves the reset into the door; #144389 replaces it with `clearNewChatIntent()`), and `prepareDefaultNewSession()` in `app/session/new-session-route.ts` (this PR splits it into `prepareGenericNewSession()` + `applyNewSessionTarget()`; #144389 adds `clearNewChatIntent()` at its top). Whichever lands second can have `prepareGenericNewSession()` start from `clearNewChatIntent()`.
- **#145996** (issue, open): the main window treats its launch profile (the `?profile=` boot seed) as a permanent new-chat default, through the `windowProfileOverride()` line in `defaultNewSessionTarget()`. This PR does not change that line and still consults `defaultNewSessionTarget()` first, so it neither fixes #145996 nor conflicts with its proposed one-line fix.

The fifth commit (`e8a945ee2e`) is separate: it can be dropped or adapted if maintainers prefer #135660's rule. Dropping it leaves one small textual conflict in `app/chat/use-new-session-doors.ts` when the sixth commit is replayed.

prs.title: fix(desktop): each profile view keeps its own chat tabs
prs.body:
## Your tabs stay where you left them when you switch profile views

On a multi-profile Desktop, the chat tab strip gets reset or swapped whenever you switch profile views:

- **All profiles has no tabs of its own.** Session tiles are saved by the gateway's *active* profile. All profiles shows whichever profile that is, so filtering by `infra` and coming back to All shows a different strip.
- **Opening another profile's chat from All swaps the strip.** On a shared-primary remote, opening an `infra` chat moves the gateway's profile, so the strip changes to `infra`'s tabs.
- **The order and front tab are lost.** The bucket holds the tile list, not the order the tabs had in the pane tree. Returning to a view brings back tabs you dragged or split in a different order, and a different tab is in front.
- **The main tab drops to a fresh draft.** Picking a profile or All profiles from the switcher always opens a new chat, even if that view already had one in its main tab.
- **Relaunch can save tabs to the wrong bucket.** Tiles load into the local bucket and move only after the remote connection publishes. A tab opened in that gap is saved under the wrong scope.
- **Another window can erase the main window's tabs.** The HUD is a full renderer that never shows the strip, but it writes its empty tile set over the main window's. A second window rewrites every bucket, not only the ones it changed.

Fixes #151310

## What changes

Each **view** (All profiles, or one profile) on each connection keeps its own tab set. When you leave a view it saves the tab order, the front tab of each zone and the main tab's chat. Returning to the view, or relaunching the app, restores them.

- `store/session-states.ts`: tiles are bucketed by `$tileViewScope` (the view on screen) instead of the gateway's profile. A view swap saves the strip it leaves and restores the one it enters. Relaunch boots on the last main-window connection. Profile delete or rename drops or moves the deleted or renamed profile's tabs inside All profiles, plus its per-view memory. A rename also moves `ownerProfile`, not only `ownerRoute`, including on the live strip.
- `store/session-tile-storage.ts` (new): tile persistence, moved out of `session-states.ts` (3,094 → 3,023 lines). Writes merge only the buckets that changed. Only the main window writes. The HUD and pop-outs never do. On upgrade, a user who was on All profiles keeps the tabs on screen.
- `store/session-tile-views.ts` (new): per-view memory the bucket doesn't carry: strip order from the pane tree, front pane per zone, and the main tab's chat. A view swap runs inside a store listener, so restored tabs are adopted after the listener returns. The front panes stay pending until those tabs land.
- `store/profile.ts`: `$tileViewScope`, plus `enterAllProfilesView()` for the rail and dropdown. The filter menu's and keybind's All toggle (`toggleShowAllProfiles`) goes through the same path both ways. Picking a view reopens that view's main chat. A view you haven't used yet still starts on a fresh draft, as before.
- `app/contrib/hooks/main-tab-restore.ts` (new), `app/contrib/hooks/use-desktop-integrations.ts`: the **first tab** (the workspace pane) reopens its chat on launch from the same per-view memory (`sessionTiles.viewMain.v1`) as every other tab, instead of a separate memory keyed by the gateway profile and the connection URL. Before, a relaunch often left it on "New session": a chat outside the sidebar's most recent page failed a second check against that list and was forgotten; in All profiles, a chat owned by another profile was never remembered nor restored; a connection whose URL changed under the same id lost it. Now a listed row reopens at once, and an unlisted one goes through the by-id ladder across profiles (`probeStoredSession`), a delegate child reopening as its parent. A chat the backend reports gone is forgotten; an unreachable backend keeps the memory for the next launch; a chat the user opens during the lookup wins. A view whose first tab was a new session stays one, and views with no memory yet keep the old per-profile restore.
- `main-tab-restore.ts` (@kvnloo, `bb57f70ba4`): a lookup still pending from the previous view is dropped when the user has switched view meanwhile (`$tileViewScope.get() !== view`), even if the new view is still a draft, so a stale restore never lands in the view the user picked.
- `store/connections.ts`: each first-tab restore decision writes one `[main-tab]` line to `desktop.log` (ids only), and so does a boot restore that moves to another connection and starts the first tab on a new session.
- `store/windows.ts`: `location?.search` guard. Window stubs without a `location` crashed `isMainWindow()`, which the tile writer now calls.
- Six sidebar and profiles tests that fully mock `@/store/profile` get the new exports. Two of them assert through `enterAllProfilesView` instead of `setShowAllProfiles(true)`.
- `website/docs/user-guide/desktop.md`: a "Tabs per view" entry under *Windows, tabs & panes*.

Renderer-only. No new storage family outside the tile keys, and no backend change.

**Behaviour change, on purpose:** on `main` the strip is keyed by the gateway's active profile by design (`store/session-states.ts`: "Keyed by the GATEWAY profile: the rail's profile switch is a soft swap (`$activeGatewayProfile` moves, no reload)", so a rail switch never leaves the previous profile's tiles registered), which is why All profiles has no tabs of its own today. This PR keeps one tab set per profile view, so that rule still holds for profiles, and gives All profiles its own.

## Proof

Two test files, 21 tests:

- `store/session-tile-views.test.ts` (11 tests) boots a fresh module graph against the real tile store, pane tree and pane mirror. "Relaunch" means the same localStorage with new modules. **On `main`, all 11 fail. With this PR, all 11 pass.** One case is a control ("a profile never visited still starts on a fresh draft"). On `main` it fails only because `enterAllProfilesView` doesn't exist yet.
- `app/contrib/hooks/use-desktop-integrations.main-tab.test.tsx` (10 tests) drives the first tab's cold-start restore through the real hook. On `main` it does not load (`@/store/session-tile-storage` does not exist); with this PR all 10 pass. Without @kvnloo's guard, its race test ("does not restore the old view after the user switches filters during a lookup") fails 1 of 10; with it, 10/10.
- Head `bb57f70ba4` merged with `main` at `1d70b4a489`: the related suites pass 291 files / 2,887 tests, and `tsc` is clean. (An earlier revision also passed `scripts/check`, 14 checks, with eslint and prettier clean on the touched files; not re-run at this head.)
- The full UI project fails the same 5 tests with and without this PR (`prepared-submissions`, `plugin-preview`, `dead-session-prune`, 2× `voice-prefs`). Each of them passes when run alone, on both sides.
- Verified by hand on macOS 26.3.1 with a packaged build against a remote gateway. Switching to `infra` and back to All restores the same strip, order and front tab. The tabs also survive a relaunch.

```
cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/store/session-tile-views.test.ts src/app/contrib/hooks/use-desktop-integrations.main-tab.test.tsx
```

## Out of scope (observed, not changed)

- If a view's remembered main chat was deleted elsewhere, returning to that view tries to open it. The existing gone-session fallback then drops to a fresh draft.
- Right after an upgrade, no view has a remembered main chat yet. Each view starts remembering on first use; until then the first tab keeps the old per-profile restore on launch.

Related: #124520 takes a different approach to the same symptom. It buckets each tile by its *owning* profile, which keeps a cross-profile tab out of All profiles. This PR keys the strip by the *view* instead, so All profiles can hold chats from several profiles. #121983 (per-connection buckets), #141049 (switching profile clears All profiles), #89036.

prs.title: Plugin settings can be viewed and edited from the terminal: hermes plugins config <name>
prs.body:
Plugin settings were only editable from the Desktop app, or by typing hidden keys like `hermes config set plugins.entries.<plugin>.settings.<key>` after digging through a README. Now `hermes plugins config <name>` opens an interactive editor in the terminal that lists every setting the plugin declares, with its current value, and edits them one at a time.

A plugin gets this from its manifest alone. The fields come from its `config_schema` and its `requires_env` list, the same data the Desktop settings form already renders, and edits save through the same writers.

## What changes

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| See a plugin's settings from the CLI | read `plugin.yaml` or the README | `hermes plugins config <name>` lists each one with its value |
| Change one | `hermes config set plugins.entries.<id>.settings.<key> <value>`, unchecked | pick it from the list; choices and on/off come up as pickers, numbers and JSON are type-checked before saving |
| Set a plugin's API key | `.env` by hand, or the install-time prompt once | masked prompt, saved to the profile's `.env` through the same credential route as Desktop; shown only as `set` / `not set` |
| Script or pipe (no TTY) | none | prints each setting, its value and where it is stored |
| `hermes plugins show <name>` | no mention of settings | `Settings: 6 — edit with hermes plugins config <name>` |
| `hermes plugins install` | no mention | `Change its settings any time: hermes plugins config <name>` when the plugin declares settings |

- New `hermes plugins config <name>` (aliases `configure`, `settings`), in `hermes_cli/plugins_settings/cli.py`.
- `hermes_cli/plugins_settings.py` becomes the `hermes_cli/plugins_settings/` package. `fields.py` is the old module unchanged; the facade re-exports its three public names, so `tui_gateway` keeps importing `hermes_cli.plugins_settings`.
- Saves go through `save_plugin_settings` (schema-validated, the `ctx.set_config` writer) and `save_provider_env_credential` (the `PUT /api/env` route). Secrets never reach `config.yaml`.
- Labels without a manifest `label` are humanized with the same rules as the Desktop form (`maps_api_key` becomes "Maps API key"), so both surfaces read the same.
- The full-screen menu clears earlier output, so the result of each edit ("✓ Saved Model to ~/.hermes/config.yaml", "✗ … not saved: 'soon' is not a whole number") is shown in the menu title.
- Docs: user guide command list, `cli-commands.md` reference row, developer guide (plugin authors get the CLI editor for free; give each key a `label` and `description`).

## Live run

A real `hermes plugins config elevenlabs-music` in tmux, against the plugin's actual manifest from hermes-official-plugins main, in a scratch `HERMES_HOME`. Every field type was exercised: a secret, choices, on/off, an int with bad and then good input, and Esc to exit.

| Settings list | Masked secret prompt | After saving the key |
|---|---|---|
| ![list](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/50cf34f948d4aa59115838f73918f86f/raw/362f1ad6780a23f124a34e8d529f098968d09f98/01-list.png) | ![secret](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/50cf34f948d4aa59115838f73918f86f/raw/362f1ad6780a23f124a34e8d529f098968d09f98/02-secret-prompt.png) | ![saved](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/50cf34f948d4aa59115838f73918f86f/raw/362f1ad6780a23f124a34e8d529f098968d09f98/03-after-secret.png) |

| Choice picker | On/off picker | Bad number refused | Good number saved |
|---|---|---|---|
| ![enum](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/50cf34f948d4aa59115838f73918f86f/raw/362f1ad6780a23f124a34e8d529f098968d09f98/04-enum-picker.png) | ![bool](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/50cf34f948d4aa59115838f73918f86f/raw/362f1ad6780a23f124a34e8d529f098968d09f98/06-bool-picker.png) | ![bad](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/50cf34f948d4aa59115838f73918f86f/raw/362f1ad6780a23f124a34e8d529f098968d09f98/08-bad-number.png) | ![good](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/50cf34f948d4aa59115838f73918f86f/raw/362f1ad6780a23f124a34e8d529f098968d09f98/09-after-number.png) |

What the run wrote to disk:

```yaml
plugins:
  entries:
    elevenlabs-music:
      settings:
        music_model: music_v2
        store_for_editing: false
        chat_app_wait_seconds: 45
```

- `.env` gained one key, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`.
- `config.yaml` contains no copy of the secret.
- The refused `soon` left the old value in place.

The no-TTY listing was also run against the Claude subscription plugin's real 10-key schema, and an unknown plugin name gives `Plugin 'nosuch' not found`.

## Tests

- 2 invariant tests in `tests/hermes_cli/plugins_settings/test_cli.py`:
  - Edits land where the plugin reads them, and a secret never reaches `config.yaml`.
  - Without a terminal the editor lists settings and never prints a secret.
- 147 passed across the touched suites: `plugins_settings/`, `tui_gateway/test_plugins_manage_settings.py`, `test_plugin_validate.py`, `test_plugins_cmd*.py`, `ci/test_docs_drift.py`.
- `scripts/check --only health` passes.

## Not covered

- Native Windows has not been run. The editor uses the same curses menus and masked prompt as `hermes setup`.
- Desktop is unchanged. It already renders the same schema.

prs.title: fix(plugins): pin liveness endpoint URL to loopback (salvage #125745)
prs.body:
§3.2 hardening (precondition: an installed, operator-reviewed plugin manifest); not a new boundary.

**Problem:** `liveness.endpoint_path` from an app manifest was appended verbatim to the loopback URL from the vendor's runtime `server.json`, then re-parsed and dialed with that file's bearer token. A path starting with `@host/` rewrites the authority, so the token goes to a manifest-chosen host. The same composed URL + token reaches the MCP transport via `AppResolver.endpoint()`.

**Fix:**
- declaration parse: `endpoint_path` must be a plain rooted path (`[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]`, no `..`); `liveness.path` rooted like `location`; `pid_key`/`url_key`/`token_key` identifier-shaped. Same rules in `tools/mcp_liveness.parse_liveness`.
- resolver: re-parse the composed URL and require http + loopback + same port + no userinfo; `_mcp_initialize` re-checks before sending the token. IPv6 loopback bracketed; runtime pids bounded.
- catalog: unreadable liveness renders `unknown`, not `present`.

Parse-time rejection is defence-in-depth; the dial-site check is what guarantees the token never leaves loopback, even for a directly constructed `AppDef`.

**Tests:** declaration, resolver, liveness and catalog behaviour tests; red on main (39 failures), green with the fix.

Credits: salvaged from #125745 by @beardthelion (authorship kept; rebased onto the multi-location `AppDef`), plus a lint follow-up.

**Compatibility:** third-party manifests whose `endpoint_path` has a query or percent-encoding, or with a relative `liveness.path`, now fail to load (nothing in `plugin-catalog/` or the bundled apps is affected).

Fixes #125744

prs.title: fix(search): refuse search_files roots that span a whole disk
prs.body:
## What

`search_files` rooted at `/`, `$HOME`, or an operator-listed broad root walks the whole disk with `rg` before returning. This refuses such roots, and any path that *contains* one, before a shell starts, and returns a guardrail error telling the model to narrow `path` to the task or project directory.

- `tools/search_root_guard.py`: pure path arithmetic (`os.path.commonpath`), no I/O.
- Broad roots: `/`, `~`, `HERMES_SEARCH_BROAD_ROOTS` (`os.pathsep`-separated), and `file_search.broad_roots` in config.yaml.
- Multi-path `path` strings are checked part by part.
- A root *below* a broad root (e.g. a repo under `$HOME`) still searches normally.

## Why

On an 8 GB host, an agent-issued `search_files` over `/` or `$HOME` read GiBs and starved the gateway and every other process on the disk. The model nearly always meant a project directory.

## Tests

`tests/tools/test_search_broad_root_guard.py` (new, 9 tests).

- Against current `main` without the change: 9 failed.
- With the change, on `main` @ 32dbc1dcda: `pytest tests/tools/test_search_broad_root_guard.py tests/tools/test_file_tools.py` gives 51 passed, 2 skipped.

Searched open and closed PRs and issues for search_root_guard, broad root, and "refusing to search": no existing work found.

prs.title: feat(display): diff-aware tool preview truncation
prs.body:
**Diff-aware tool-preview truncation** — full production path, rebased onto current `main`. Fixes #24298.

Show consecutive tool-call previews under the same ~40-char budget by eliding the shared prefix and revealing the **differing tail** (e.g. `cd /p && alpha` vs `… && beta`), instead of a dumb trailing-`...` head-cut that renders distinct commands identically (and then wrongly collapses them into `(×N)`).

### Before / After
Two consecutive distinct commands sharing a long `cd` prefix, at a ~40-char preview cap:

**Before** (dumb head-cut → identical renders → false repeat):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..."
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..." (×2)   ← looks like a stall
```
**After** (diff-aware → differing tail shown, no false collapse):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/…&& run alpha"
💻 terminal: "…&& run beta"
```
A genuine repeat of the *same* command still collapses to `(×2)` — dedup keys on raw identity, not on the rendered string.

### @teknium1's review — both points addressed on the production path
- [x] **Dedup keys on RAW identity, not rendered-truncation equality.** `_progress_emit` (gateway/run_turn_runner.py) now takes a `raw_key` derived from raw inputs (`tool_name` + raw command / preview / args) and dedups on that; truncation can no longer make two distinct commands collapse into `(×N)`. `truncate_middle()` stays presentation-only.
- [x] **The terminal/code-block path no longer head-truncates + bypasses.** `_progress_terminal_blocks` uses `truncate_middle` with a threaded `prev` (same as the ordinary preview path) instead of `cmd[:cap-3]+"..."`.

### Changes
- `agent/display.py`: `truncate_middle` / `_truncate_around_diff` / `_head_tail_truncate`; `prepare_tool_preview` gains optional `prev=`.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py::format_tool_event` **and** `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` (`_progress_build_message` / `_progress_terminal_blocks` / `_progress_emit`) thread `prev` + the raw dedup key via new `gateway/turn_context.py` fields.
- Tests: `tests/agent/test_display_truncate_middle.py` + `tests/gateway/test_run_progress_diff_aware.py` — distinct prefix-sharing commands must NOT collapse to `(×N)`; true repeats must (incl. on the `supports_code_blocks=True` path); covers a non-terminal preview. Stale expectations updated. All green.

The original branch was ~24k commits behind; this is a clean re-application onto current `main`.

prs.title: fix(gateway): a word holding a key prefix mid-word is not held off the streamed preview
prs.body:
The streamed-reply secret hold treated any trailing word that contained a key-prefix literal anywhere (e.g. AgentMail's `am_` inside `stream_accepted` or `program_id`) as a key still arriving, so that last word stayed off screen until the provider stream ended. The prefix rules only match a literal that does not follow a letter or digit, so the hold now uses that same left boundary; the JWT/base64-PEM/age/Discord-mfa literals, whose rules match glued to a word, keep holding unanchored.

**0.23.2 release blocker** — `Full CI pipeline / Python tests / e2e`, run 43872534262 (job 133317399869): `test_messaging_exactly_once.py::test_crash_between_completion_and_send[stream_accepted_unpersisted-fk_tg]` — "unexpected extra marked copies".

Real-world effect: on Telegram (any edit-streamed platform) a reply ending in such a word sat incomplete while the stream was open; a gateway crash in that window let auto-resume answer again and the delivery ledger posted a labelled "♻️ Recovered reply" copy beside the old preview.

- **First bad commit:** efcf4e1beece "hold unsettled text out of every streamed frame, split and seal" (#154211). Bisect on git-archive trees, single cell: 971e15cd6db5 ok (known-gap xfail), efcf4e1beece FAIL; merge ea24dc721eb4^1 ok, ea24dc721eb4 FAIL.
- **Verdict:** regression, deterministic (3/3 local on origin/main), not a flake. The intended hold behaviour (#56039) is kept for real key starts.
- **Red before:** cell fails 3/3 on main; new `test_a_word_holding_a_key_prefix_mid_word_is_shown_before_the_stream_ends` 4/4 red with main's `stream_consumer_redact.py`.
- **Green after:** cell 3/3 back to its run-time known-gap xfail; whole `test_messaging_exactly_once.py` 61 passed via `scripts/run_tests.sh`; all `tests/gateway/*stream_consumer*`/`*redact*` pass. New companion test keeps `am_…`, `x-sk-…`, `backup_sk-…` held.

prs.title: fix(#64391): skills list --enabled-only can include prompt-ineligible skills
prs.body:
`hermes skills list --enabled-only` claimed to show "exactly which skills will load for that profile" but did not apply the same tool/toolset conditional activation rules as the system-prompt builder. This meant skills like `research-paper-writing` appeared as enabled in the listing even though they would be excluded from the actual session prompt because their `requires_toolsets` conditions were not satisfied.

## Changes

1. **Fix bundled skill** (`optional-skills/research/research-paper-writing/SKILL.md`): Correct `requires_toolsets: [terminal, files]` to `requires_toolsets: [terminal, file]`. Hermes registers the file toolset as singular `file`, not `files`, so the skill was unconditionally excluded from every session prompt.

2. **Store conditions in find-all-skills** (`tools/skills_tool.py`): Store `requires_toolsets`, `requires_tools`, `fallback_for_toolsets`, `fallback_for_tools` in each skill dict returned by `_find_all_skills()`. Condition extraction delegates to `agent.skill_utils.extract_skill_conditions` — the exact helper the prompt builder uses — so listing and prompt can never drift in how they parse conditional frontmatter.

3. **Apply filtering in do_list** (`hermes_cli/skills_hub.py`): When `--enabled-only` is set, resolve the session's effective capabilities through the same runtime path the prompt builder sees: expand the profile's configured toolsets to concrete tool schemas exactly like agent init does (`get_tool_definitions` with the CLI platform toolsets and `agent.disabled_toolsets`), then re-derive toolset availability from those tool names via `get_toolset_for_tool` (mirroring `agent/system_prompt.py`). Both the effective **tool names** and **toolsets** are passed into `_skill_should_show()`, so `requires_tools` / `fallback_for_tools` conditions are evaluated against the session's real tool set. If capability resolution fails, `(None, None)` is passed and `_skill_should_show()` shows everything rather than mis-filtering against empty sets.

4. **Tests** (`tests/hermes_cli/test_skills_hub.py`): Listing tests for all four conditional fields (`requires_tools`, `fallback_for_tools`, `requires_toolsets`, `fallback_for_toolsets`), a resolution-failure no-filter test, a predicate-parity test, and an end-to-end parity test that builds the real `<available_skills>` prompt index from SKILL.md files on disk and asserts listing eligibility matches it for the same tools/toolsets.

Fixes #64391.


---

## Update (2026-11-07) — rebased onto current `main`

This PR sat from 2026-07-14 without ever running CI. It is now rebased onto current `main` (`a776809ad8`); the diffstat is unchanged at 4 files, +321/−2, and the branch is level with upstream.

The bug is still present on `main`:

- `hermes_cli/skills_hub.py` `do_list()` still applies only the disabled-skill filter under `--enabled-only` and never consults `_skill_should_show`, so a skill excluded from the prompt by its `requires_tools` / `requires_toolsets` / `fallback_for_tools` / `fallback_for_toolsets` conditions is still listed as enabled.
- `optional-skills/research/research-paper-writing/SKILL.md:15` still declares `requires_toolsets: [terminal, files]`, and `files` is not a toolset — `toolsets.py` registers `file` and has no `files` entry — so that skill's toolset condition never matches.

### Test evidence on this head

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_skills_hub.py tests/tools/test_skills_tool.py -q
```

→ **88 tests passed, 0 failed.** Reverting only `hermes_cli/skills_hub.py` and `tools/skills_tool.py` (keeping the tests) turns the same run into **14 failed** — every `--enabled-only` conditional-activation case.

`ruff check` (pinned 0.15.22) is clean on all three changed Python files; `ty check` reports no new diagnostics against the base.

prs.title: fix(dashboard): scope the basic-auth password warning to the resolving process
prs.body:
## Problem

On a correctly-configured install whose dashboard authenticates fine, every process
*other* than the dashboard that loads the provider logs:

```
dashboard-auth-basic: dashboard.basic_auth.username is set but neither password_hash
nor password is configured. Provide one of them (password_hash is preferred — compute
it with plugins.dashboard_auth.basic.hash_password).
```

The line is not wrong about what that process resolved, but its wording reads as a global
misconfiguration — "the dashboard has a username and no password" — when the dashboard is
in fact serving behind an enforcing auth gate. It is emitted from any CLI/driver process
that initialises the plugin registry, so the operator sees it constantly and learns to
ignore it.

## Why it happens

`_settings()` resolves `username`, `password_hash` and `password` from the *same*
env-or-config resolver:

```python
username      = setting("HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME", "username")
password_hash = setting("HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD_HASH", "password_hash")
plaintext     = setting("HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD", "password")
```

The password is a secret, and secrets are deliberately kept out of subprocess
environments (the same control as #92144, which blocklists
`HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_SECRET` and its siblings from terminal subprocesses). So
outside the dashboard process the resolver legitimately sees a username with no
password, and the check reports a half-configured credential *by construction* — in
every process except the one that actually serves the gate.

Observed on a self-hosted install: the dashboard process's environment holds
`..._BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD` and `..._SECRET`; the CLI/agent shell holds
`..._BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME` and `..._PUBLIC_URL` but neither secret. Meanwhile
`dashboard-auth.log` shows `Dashboard binding to 127.0.0.1 with auth gate enabled.
Providers: basic`, `/api/auth/providers` returns `basic`, and `/api/sessions` returns
401 without a credential — the gate is enforcing while the warning fires.

## Change

Scope the message to the process that resolved it, and name which source supplied the
username (mirroring the resolution disclosure in #88759):

```
dashboard.basic_auth.username is set (from env) but neither password_hash nor password
is configured for this process: no credential was found in this process's environment or
in config.yaml. Outside the dashboard this is expected — the dashboard holds the secret
in its own environment — so this line alone does not mean the auth gate is off. Provide
password_hash (preferred — compute it with plugins.dashboard_auth.basic.hash_password)
if this process must register the provider.
```

No behaviour change: still a `SkipRegistration(level="warning")`, so registration and the
gate logic are untouched. Only the text changes.

### Alternative considered and rejected

Suppressing the warning in non-dashboard processes. Rejected: there is no reliable way
for the plugin to tell whether it is running inside the dashboard, and silencing it would
hide the case it exists to catch — a genuine half-configured credential.

## Tests

Two cases added to `tests/plugins/dashboard_auth/test_basic_provider.py`:

- `test_password_warning_scopes_itself_to_the_process` — username from env, no password
  anywhere; asserts the message is process-scoped, names the source, and disclaims the
  gate.
- `test_password_warning_names_config_when_username_comes_from_config` — username from
  the config section; asserts the source is named as `config`.

Verified RED then GREEN: with only the source change reverted, both new tests fail and
the captured log shows the old wording; with it, both pass.

```
$ python -m pytest tests/plugins/dashboard_auth/test_basic_provider.py -q
19 passed in 2.52s
$ ruff check plugins/dashboard_auth/basic/__init__.py tests/plugins/dashboard_auth/test_basic_provider.py
All checks passed!
```

(The neighbouring `tests/plugins/dashboard_auth/test_opaque_bearer_not_unreachable.py`
cannot be collected in this environment — it imports `hermes_cli.web_server`, which
exits for want of fastapi/uvicorn. Pre-existing and unrelated: identical failure with
this change stashed.)

## Duplicate check

Searched open and merged PRs and issues for the warning text and for basic-auth warning
reports — nothing covers this. Related work, none duplicated here:

- #88759 — `fix(dashboard): disclose basic_auth config-side resolution`. Same file and
  function, complementary: it discloses resolution on the **success** line and on skip
  reasons. This changes the **warning** message. Textual conflict in `_settings()` is
  possible and trivial to rebase.
- #54610 — `plugins.disabled` containing `basic` breaks the provider. Different cause.
- #92144 — blocklists dashboard auth secrets from subprocess environments. That control
  is precisely why this warning fires outside the dashboard; worth linking.

prs.title: fix(cli): one bad plugin CLI command no longer drops the others
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Stops one bad plugin CLI descriptor from removing every other plugin's top-level command from `hermes`.

`_register_plugin_cli_commands` ran plugin discovery **and** every `add_parser` call inside one `try`, and `_attach_plugin_cli_command` called `cmd_info["setup_fn"](parser)` unguarded. `PluginContext.register_cli_command` explicitly allows a handler-only command — a plugin that dispatches on raw `argv` and passes `setup_fn=None` — so the first such plugin raised `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable`, unwound the loop, and every later command was never attached. The CLI then answered `'<cmd>' is not a hermes command` for all of them, and the exception itself was recorded at DEBUG only, so the symptom reads as "the plugin is not installed".

The same single-`try` shape covers the two other triggers in #130607: a `setup_fn` that raises, and a command name that collides with a built-in registered later (`subparsers.add_parser` raises `ValueError: conflicting subparser`).

### Reproduced

On a host with an enabled plugin that registers `setup_fn=None` (any plugin whose command handler reads raw argv):

```
$ hermes xchat --help
hermes: 'xchat' is not a `hermes` command.
Did you mean: chat?
$ python -c "import logging; logging.getLogger('hermes_cli.main').setLevel(logging.DEBUG); ..."
DEBUG hermes_cli.main: Plugin CLI discovery failed: 'NoneType' object is not callable
```

`dashclaw` — the plugin that registers `setup_fn=None` — and `delegation`, the two commands attached before the offending descriptor, still resolved (dashclaw's own parser is built before `setup_fn` is called, so its help worked); `xchat`, `mcp-serve`, `tokenwatch`, `fish`, `gadget`, `plugin-guard` and `inbox` did not.

After the change all of them attach normally, and the handler-only command is noted rather than called:

```
DEBUG hermes_cli.main_plugin_cli: Plugin command 'dashclaw' registers no setup_fn; attaching it without an argparse setup
```

A descriptor that genuinely fails (a raising `setup_fn`, or a name that collides with a built-in) is named at WARNING with its traceback, and the commands around it still attach.

## Related Issue

Fixes #130607

Overlaps #128648 (manifest-declared CLI commands, and `parent=` for sub-verbs). That PR moves the registration call; it does not add per-command isolation or a name check, so this fix is orthogonal to it — happy to rebase either way.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/main_plugin_cli.py` (new): the registration loop and the two attach helpers, moved out of `hermes_cli/main.py` — `main.py` may only shrink, and the `FILE_LINES` budget rejected the added lines. The facade re-exports `_register_plugin_cli_commands`, so call sites are unchanged.
  - `attach_plugin_cli_command`: skip the argparse setup when `setup_fn` is `None` and keep `handler_fn`.
  - `attach_plugin_cli_command_safely`: per-command guard; on failure the command is named in a WARNING with the traceback (`exc_info=True`) and the loop continues. A parser created before the failure stays in the table without a handler, so it can only print help.
  - `register_plugin_cli_commands`: both loops now go through the guard; the outer catch-all logs its traceback.
- `hermes_cli/main.py`: remove the moved functions, import the sibling.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_cli_command_isolation.py` (new): handler-only command attaches with its handler; a real `setup_fn` still shapes the parser (negative control); a raising `setup_fn` drops only that command; a name colliding with a built-in keeps the built-in and does not break the CLI; end-to-end shape of the report (handler-only command first, every command after it still registered).

## How to Test

1. `just test tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_cli_command_isolation.py tests/hermes_cli/test_startup_plugin_gating.py` — passes.
2. Revert `hermes_cli/main_plugin_cli.py` to the pre-fix body (call `cmd_info["setup_fn"]` unconditionally, no per-command guard) and re-run: 4 of the 5 new tests fail, the negative control still passes.
3. On a host with two plugins, one of which registers `setup_fn=None`: `hermes <other-plugin-command> --help` resolves instead of `'<cmd>' is not a hermes command`.

prs.title: fix(cloud): answer 'not signed in to Nous Portal' with 409, not 401
prs.body:
**0.23.2 release blocker**

## What users see

**Before:** A Webapp user on a no-auth dashboard who isn't signed in to Nous Portal opens Settings ▸ Backup & Transfer (or the Hermes Cloud section of Settings ▸ Gateway). `GET /api/cloud/agents` answers **401** `portal_signin_required`. `apps/desktop/src/lib/browser-transport.ts` reads any 401 on a no-auth dashboard as its own session being refused (`webappSignInRequired()`), so the user is told to sign in to the **Webapp** instead of to Nous Portal. On an auth-required dashboard the 401 also goes through `reauthError()`, which is the session-expiry path.

**After:** The route answers **409** with the same `detail: {code: "portal_signin_required", message: "Sign in to Nous Portal first (…)"}`. The transport passes it through like any other API error. `transferErrorMessage()` (Backup & Transfer) and `notifyError()` (Gateway settings) pull `detail.message` from the body whatever the status, so the user sees "Sign in to Nous Portal". No TS change was needed because none of those consumers branch on the status code.

## Why 409
- 401 is the dashboard session's own status (Webapp transport, `web/src/lib/api.ts` 401 envelope handling, the auth contract e2e).
- 403 is read as auth by `web/src/components/AuthWidget.tsx`.
- 409 already means "this install's state conflicts with the request" across `web_routers` (38 uses) and on this same route for the portal's `org_selection_required`. No auth layer treats it as a session refusal. 424/428 would also work but nothing else in the dashboard uses them.

## The e2e failure it fixes
rc.12-v0.23.2, run 43932903210, job 133532208579:
`tests/e2e/core/dashboard/test_dashboard_auth.py::test_scraped_token_opens_every_get_route` → `routes refuse the dashboard's own token: ['GET /api/cloud/agents']`. The e2e sandbox never has a Nous sign-in, so the new route always answered 401.

## Tests
- Red on origin/main `e2fb450adcf7`: `test_scraped_token_opens_every_get_route` fails with the assertion above (1 failed, 4 passed).
- Green on this branch, `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/e2e/core/dashboard/test_dashboard_auth.py tests/hermes_cli/test_cloud_agents.py`: 8 passed, 0 failed.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_cloud_agents.py::test_signed_out_install_is_told_to_sign_in_not_a_server_error` now asserts 409 and the "Sign in to Nous Portal" message.
- `ruff check` clean.

## Infographic

![Infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab2bbf0/2jQ5qflEr4PeGSh6PJ70A_SrVpUD8S.png)

prs.title: fix(cli): plugin CLI commands never collide with built-ins, and one bad plugin no longer drops the rest
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

In `hermes_cli/main.py`:

1. `_register_plugin_cli_commands(subparsers)` now runs after the last built-in parser. Built-in `--help` order is unchanged; plugin commands are listed last.
2. `_attach_plugin_cli_command` skips a name already in `subparsers.choices` (any built-in or built-in alias, or an earlier plugin's command) with a WARNING naming the plugin.
3. Each command's `add_parser` and `setup_fn` run in their own `try`. On failure the half-built parser is removed from both the parser map and the `--help` listing, a WARNING names the plugin, and the remaining commands still attach. This includes a malformed `help` string (a bare `%`): Python 3.14's `add_parser` raises on it, and on 3.11-3.13 the help is expanded inside the same `try`, because there it would otherwise register and crash every `hermes --help` (found in review by Enough1122). The cleanup only ever removes the plugin's own entry: the name check runs first, so a built-in name never reaches it.

## Compared with #128648

#128648 (nekwo, open feature for #128640: manifest-declared CLI commands and `parent=`) also moves `_register_plugin_cli_commands` after the built-ins, for its own reason (attaching sub-verbs under a built-in). On its own that turns the crash (case A) into the silent drop (case B): it adds no name check against `subparsers.choices` and keeps the single `try` around the whole discovery loop, so a colliding or failing plugin still drops every later plugin's commands. Its new manifest-declared path does wrap its single attach in a `try`. This PR is the bug fix both paths need, and the two compose: the name check and per-command isolation live in `_attach_plugin_cli_command`, which #128648's declared path also calls.

## Related Issue

Fixes #130607

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/main.py`: `_attach_plugin_cli_command` (name check + isolated setup with cleanup); `_build_cli_parser` registers plugin commands last.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_cli_command_clash.py`: two invariant tests through the real `_build_cli_parser()`. The colliding names are read from a plugin-free build (the first and last built-ins), not hardcoded.
- Docs: `website/docs/developer-guide/plugins/index.md` (Register CLI commands: a "Name collisions" caveat, including first-registration-wins between plugins and the malformed-`help` skip) and its zh-Hans mirror `website/i18n/zh-Hans/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/current/developer-guide/plugins/index.md`. `website/scripts/check_doc_links.py` passes.

## How to Test

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_cli_command_clash.py`

- `test_plugin_named_like_any_builtin_never_crashes_or_shadows_it`: a plugin registers the first built-in's name, the last built-in's name and its own command; the parser builds, both built-ins keep their own parsers, and the plugin's own command parses and dispatches.
- `test_failing_or_colliding_plugin_does_not_drop_another_plugins_command`: a colliding plugin and a plugin whose `setup_fn` raises are registered before a good plugin; followed by a plugin whose `help` is `"cuts memory by 30%"`. The good command works, `format_help()` does not raise, both failed commands are gone from `choices` and `--help`, and every warning names its plugin.

Red on `main` (fix reverted): both fail (`ValueError: conflicting subparser: prompt-size`, and the good command missing). Green with the fix. Sabotage, one guarantee at a time: putting registration back mid-build turns test 1 red; dropping the name check turns both red; narrowing the per-command `except` turns test 2 red; dropping the cleanup turns test 2 red (`brokencmd` still in `choices`). Follow-up 5717d8d667: test 2 is red on the previous head (`add_parser` outside the `try`, the good command missing); with only the pseudo-action cleanup dropped it fails with `ValueError: incomplete format` from `format_help()`.
