prs.title: feat(setup): new installs follow the branch they were cloned from
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

A new install follows the update channel of the branch it was cloned from. Setup no longer asks, and never moves the checkout.

- **Problem**: a fresh clone installs the tip of `main` on the default `stable` channel, so once `main` is past the latest release the first `/update-nanoclaw` stops with ahead-of-release.
- **Release branches**: the repository publishes `stable` and `beta` branches next to `main`. `release.yml` moves them to each release as its last step, fast-forward only, and each only to its channel's newest tag, the one the updater picks (`release.mjs branches`). A patch to an older line moves neither.
- **Quick Start**: the README clones `--branch stable`. `beta` and `main` are one line below it.
- **Recorded, not chosen**: `nanoclaw.sh` hands setup the channel of the cloned branch (`stable`, `beta`, or `edge` for `main`) and setup saves it to `.env`. A clone of `main` is told it follows `main` and how to clone releases instead.
- **Explicit choice**: `--update-channel`, `NANOCLAW_UPDATE_CHANNEL`, a channel already in `.env` and the Advanced field work as before and are never overridden. Choosing stable or beta on `main` past its releases prints a hint that the first update waits. A bad env value stops setup unless a flag overrides it; uninstall ignores it.
- **Left alone**: existing installs, forks, other branches, local commits, and a local branch that only shares the name `stable` or `beta`.

**Before this merges**: the `stable` branch must exist upstream, or the new Quick Start fails. Its rulesets are already in place (`channel-branches-no-rewrite`, `channel-branches-locked`). `beta` should be published only from the first release candidate that contains this change: an older one saves no channel, so its first update would stop.

## Related work

Follow-up to #3986. No issue: scoped with the maintainers. See [Upgrading](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/operate/upgrading).

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- CI at `d12ea7ce`: all checks pass.
- `setup/lib/update-channel.test.ts` (29 tests) runs the helper and the real `nanoclaw.sh` in stub official clones of `stable`, `beta` and `main`, including a shallow clone, a fork, an existing install and a local namesake branch. It checks the shell reads `.env` as the updater does, and that the updater resolves `stable` and `beta` from a clone of each branch.
- `scripts/release.test.ts`: 5 new tests for which branches a release moves, against the updater's own tag order, and for the step's behaviour without the app token.
- Not run: an e2e install at this head, and the new `release.yml` step, which only runs in a real release. The branches' ruleset lets only organisation admins move them today, so the step needs an app added to that ruleset's bypass list and its token as a `CHANNEL_BRANCH_TOKEN` secret in both release environments. Without it, the step warns and prints the `git push` for an admin to run. It runs last, so it cannot block a release, and a publish rerun retries it.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
**New installs follow the branch they were cloned from.** `git clone --branch stable` installs the latest release and follows releases; `--branch beta` adds release candidates; a clone of `main` follows `main`. `--update-channel stable|beta|edge` and Advanced setup still set the channel explicitly.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- Setup no longer checks anything out or writes `.env` from the shell. It reads the current branch and the remotes' URLs, and passes a channel name to setup.
- New installs run the code `stable` and `beta` point to. Two rulesets protect them: no force-push or deletion for anyone, and creation or updates only by organisation admins. `release.yml` can move them only once an app is added to that bypass list and its token is stored as `CHANNEL_BRANCH_TOKEN` in the protected `release` and `prerelease` environments; the default Actions token cannot.

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

prs.title: fix(setup): install Node on openSUSE, fail clearly on other non-Debian distros
prs.body:
## Summary

Lets `setup/install-node.sh` install Node on openSUSE, and fail with a clear message on other non-Debian Linux.
- **Problem**: the Linux branch always ran NodeSource's Debian installer, then `apt-get`. On any non-Debian distro it died with NodeSource's "only supported on Debian-based systems" error and no next step.
- **Fix**: pick the install path from `ID_LIKE`/`ID` in `/etc/os-release`. Debian/Ubuntu keeps the NodeSource path unchanged. SUSE (`suse`, `opensuse`, `sles`) runs `zypper install nodejs24 npm24` from the distro's own repos, with no third-party repo and no `curl | sudo`.
- **Other distros**: print which distros are supported and what to install, then exit non-zero.
- **Out of scope**: RHEL/Fedora. The NodeSource RPM branch is in the script, commented out, because it can't be tested yet. Leap 15.6 has no Node that meets the minimum in its own repos; the SUSE branch carries a comment pointing at https://build.opensuse.org/project/show/devel:languages:nodejs. Setup never adds repos itself.

## Related work

Refs #2462. This is a partial fix, so it does not close the issue: it covers SUSE (Option 2's shape) and Option 1's fail-fast message for other distros. RHEL/Fedora remain open.

## Scope note

CONTRIBUTING.md says a fix for one OS version can stay on a fork, and that compatibility work usually belongs in a skill. I think this is still a core fix: openSUSE is a distro family, not one machine's settings, and the Linux branch broke it for anyone on a non-Debian distro with an unclear error. #2462 has been open since 2026-05-13 with no comments or fix, which suggests this isn't a one-off. I searched open and closed issues and PRs for a skill-based or framework approach to suggesting installs on non-Debian distros and found none, so there is nothing to build on or defer to there. If maintainers want that direction, I'm happy to move this into a skill or keep it on a fork.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`

## Validation

- `bash -n setup/install-node.sh` -> passes
- `bash nanoclaw.sh` on openSUSE Tumbleweed -> installer completes; Node comes from zypper (nodejs24 and npm24 24.22.3) (`node --version` -> v24.22.3)
- Official repo check (directory listings of download.opensuse.org): Tumbleweed, Leap 16.0 and 16.1 carry nodejs24 at or above the 24.22.1 minimum; Leap 15.6 does not
- No new automated test: the script shells out to sudo and the system package manager, so there is nothing to run in CI.

## User and release impact

- [x] User-visible change — release note below

```release-note
Setup can now install Node on openSUSE (Tumbleweed, Leap 16) via zypper, and stops with a clear message on other non-Debian Linux distros instead of NodeSource's Debian-only error.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. The SUSE path installs distro-signed packages with zypper and adds no repository. The Debian path is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(add-codex): keep old sign-in folders a process Linux won't show may use
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

On Linux, a Codex sign-in no longer removes an old sign-in folder that a process it can't read might still use.

- **Problem**: before removing a sign-in folder over an hour old, setup reads each listed process's environment from `/proc/<pid>/environ`, looking for that sign-in's id. A failed read counted as "carries no id", so a live login setup couldn't read wouldn't keep its folder (Zvi's note on #4455).
- **Fix**: on Linux each new folder records its boot id and when the setup that made it started, in clock ticks since boot. A process setup can't read keeps an old folder unless it started before that setup. A folder from an earlier boot has no login left. A process that has exited (`ENOENT`, `ESRCH`) or is a zombie counts for nothing. Anything unknown keeps the folder: no record, an unreadable start, or an unknown boot.
- **Why the start**: the user's own `systemd --user` and `(sd-pam)` always have unreadable environments; on Debian 13 they are the only such processes. Without this rule, every Linux install running the NanoClaw service would keep every old folder. Ticks since boot don't step with the wall clock.
- **Also**: folders another user owns are left alone (setup run once with `sudo`), since that user's processes aren't listed.
- **Out of scope**: the stop. It still doesn't wait on a process it can't read, or it would wait on the systemd manager.

## Related work

Closes #4476

Follows #4455 ([review](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4455#pullrequestreview-5973849143)).

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `codex.test.ts` in the composed tree: 100 passed on macOS and on Debian 13 (CT 117, Codex 0.169.0).
- New cases fake a Linux `/proc` and cover reads failing with `EACCES` and `EPERM` for a process that started:
  - after, at, or before the setup that made the folder;
  - at an unknown time.
- Further cases cover:
  - no record, a malformed record, or one from an earlier boot;
  - an unknown boot, or a boot id that isn't one;
  - a zombie;
  - `ENOENT` and `ESRCH`;
  - a folder another user owns.
- A test checks that a new folder records the boot and setup's start.
- On Debian 13 the other tests read the real `/proc`, where `systemd --user` is unreadable.
- `tsc` on the payload shows no new errors, and prettier is clean.
- Each deliberate break of the sweep fails at least one test.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [x] No user-visible behavior change
- [ ] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

This follows #4455, which isn't in a release yet. On Linux, a folder left by main between #4455 and this change has no record, so it stays until removed by hand.

## Security and trust boundaries

A folder may hold a Codex token (`auth.json`). The sweep removes fewer folders when it can't tell who uses them. Folders stay 0700 under the git-ignored `data/`. The record is a 0600 file, `.nanoclaw-made`, in the folder.

## Skill delivery

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

The change touches only the add-codex payload's `setup/providers/codex.ts` and its test.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->
## Summary

Telegram topics become threads, both in forum supergroups and in a bot's private chats (threaded mode), so replies land in the topic they came from and a `per-thread` wiring gets one session per topic.

- **Problem**: the adapter declares `supportsThreads: false`, so every topic of a forum supergroup shares one session and replies go to General. Same for private-chat topics (Bot API 9.3 threaded mode, toggled in BotFather): replies leave the topic.
- **Fix**: `supportsThreads: true`, defaults `threads: true` for groups and DMs. The inbound interceptor normalizes thread ids:
  - forum supergroup (`getChat` → `is_forum`, cached per chat): keep `telegram:<chat>:<topic>`;
  - private chat while the bot has topics enabled (`getMe` → `has_topics_enabled`, cached 5 min, a "disabled" answer re-checked after 30 s): keep `telegram:<user>:<topic>`;
  - a private-chat message outside any topic gets no thread id, so a `per-thread` DM wiring resumes its thread-less session instead of opening a `telegram:<user>` one beside it;
  - anything else (reply chains in ordinary groups) folds back to the chat.
- **Why the is_forum check**: in ordinary groups Telegram also stamps reply chains with `message_thread_id`. Without the check (as in #2892), every reply chain in a plain group would open its own session.
- **getMe failure**: if it can't be read and nothing is cached, the private-chat topic is kept (Telegram only sends a private-chat `message_thread_id` for topics), rather than merging topics into one session.
- **DM sessions**: a DM wiring stays one shared session unless it opts into `session_mode 'per-thread'`; replies go back to the topic either way.
- **Out of scope**: per-topic auto-registration (#1626).

## Related work

Supersedes #2892 (closed; flipped the flag without the non-forum fold). Related: #1699.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `src/channels/telegram-forum-topics.test.ts`: forum keeps the topic; non-forum folds to the chat; chat-level group ids need no lookup; a DM outside any topic gets no thread id; private-chat topic kept while `has_topics_enabled`, dropped when disabled, kept when `getMe` fails; `is_forum` and `has_topics_enabled` cached -> 8 pass. Without the second commit, 4 of them fail.
- `telegram-pairing-interceptor` / `telegram-connect-group` / `channel-defaults` tests pass
- `tsc --noEmit`: no new errors vs. `channels` HEAD. `telegram-registration*` / `telegram-instances-registration` tests need every channel package installed; they fail identically on `channels` HEAD in a Telegram-only checkout (the DM `threads` expectation there is updated)
- Manual: checked against a running bot: forum topics and private-chat topics each get their own session with `session_mode=per-thread`, replies land in the topic, and a private-chat message outside topics resumes the existing DM session

```release-note
Telegram: forum topics and topics in a bot's private chats are now separate threads; replies go back to the topic. Set a DM wiring to session_mode per-thread to get one session per topic.
```

prs.title: fix(add-codex): sign in via the pinned Codex CLI through pnpm dlx, outside /tmp
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Codex ChatGPT sign-in works without a Codex CLI on the host, and no longer warns about `/tmp`.

- **Problem**: with no `codex` on PATH, setup asks for `npm install -g @openai/codex`, which fails with EACCES on a root-owned npm prefix. The throwaway `CODEX_HOME` was in `/tmp`, where Codex refuses its helpers and warns.
- **Fix**: the sign-in runs the image's exact pin from `container/cli-tools.json` through pnpm, the way setup already runs the pinned Bun: `pnpm --package=@openai/codex@<pin> dlx codex login`. pnpm keeps it in its own cache, with no global install and no sudo.
- **Sign-in home**: `data/codex-login/login-<id>`, git-ignored with mode 0700, and never `~/.codex`. The login runs in its own session. Setup gives each sign-in a random id (`NANOCLAW_CODEX_LOGIN`, next to `CODEX_HOME`), names the home for it, and finds its processes by it in their environments (`ps -E` on macOS, `/proc` on Linux), as each inherits it, including Codex in the group pnpm 12 gives it. A process that doesn't show it counts if it is found through its parent, or is in a group the tree already holds (the login runs in a session of its own, so only its processes can join those groups). On a signal, or when the login is killed or ends without signing in, setup stops every group in that tree, using SIGKILL after 3 seconds or on a second signal, and removes the home only once two listings in a row show none left. If it can't list the processes, or couldn't before the first signal, it keeps the home and says so. A later sign-in removes a leftover home over an hour old only once two listings in a row show no process carrying its id; without a listing, the home stays. Ctrl-C while pnpm fetches the CLI stops setup with no error.
- **Fails closed**: a pin that isn't strict semver never reaches pnpm. If the pinned sign-in fails, setup names the API-key option and OpenAI's installer (`… | sh -s -- --release <pin>`, no sudo), with npm second. The installer keeps Codex in `~/.codex/packages`, links it into `~/.local/bin` and adds that to the shell profile, so setup says to re-run in a new terminal. Sign-in still uses the throwaway home.

<details><summary>Alternatives considered</summary>

- **Sign in inside the agent image** (OpenCode): Codex binds its browser callback to `127.0.0.1` inside its own process, so a container's port forward can't reach it. Only device pairing would work.
- **npx** (this PR's first heads): works too, but npx runs any `codex` in its project's `node_modules`, so it needed an empty private project, a binary lookup with a version re-check, and npm error parsing to tell Ctrl-C from a failed fetch. `pnpm dlx` needs none of these and matches Cursor sign-in, skill refresh, lockfile regeneration, the provider check and #4461.

</details>

## Related work

Closes #3791
Closes #4449

Replaces closed #3792.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `codex.test.ts` in the composed tree: 85 passed on macOS and on Debian 13. New cases cover pnpm sign-in, bad pins, a failed or unstartable pnpm and the install commands, the home and its sweep (an old home whose login still runs, one listing missing it, `ps` failing), and Ctrl-C during the probe and during the fetch. The stop tests use real process trees: a wrapper that exits at once on SIGTERM, and a child that outlives it in the wrapper's group or in its own. They cover signals, setup exiting, the wrapper killed from outside, a process without the id, look-alike processes that must survive, `ps` missing, failing, timing out or missing part of the tree once, a second Ctrl-C while `ps` lists it, a large environment, and a wall-clock jump.
- `test-registry-skills.ts add-codex` passes on a fresh clone of HEAD. `skill-pins`, `tsc` and prettier are clean.
- Live test on a Debian 13 LXC with a root-owned npm prefix (`/usr`), no `codex`, and pnpm 10.34.9 through corepack:
  - pnpm fetched the native `@openai/codex@0.169.0-linux-x64` package, and device sign-in showed the URL and code, with no `/tmp` warning
  - Ctrl-C during the download and during device or browser sign-in each exited 130, leaving no process and no home
  - SIGTERM and SIGHUP sent to setup alone during the login, and closing the terminal, each left no process and no home
  - a Codex or pnpm stopped with SIGSTOP kept the home until setup killed it after 3 seconds
  - with pnpm killed from outside, setup stopped Codex before it removed the home
  - `~/.codex` stayed absent
- On macOS, pnpm 12 runs Codex in its own process group. With pnpm and its supervisor killed from outside, setup stopped Codex before it removed the home; the previous head left Codex running.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
**Codex setup no longer needs the Codex CLI installed on your machine.** If `codex` isn't on your PATH, ChatGPT sign-in runs the pinned version through pnpm, from pnpm's cache, with no global install or sudo. It also no longer warns about `/tmp`.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

pnpm fetches the image's exact, reviewed pin with install scripts off (`--config.ignore-scripts=true`), as in the image install; Codex ships none today. pnpm 12 also applies the repo's 3-day `minimumReleaseAge` to this fetch, while 10.34.9 does not. The token goes only to the 0700 home under `data/`, then the gateway vault. If sign-in is killed outright after login but before the token reaches the vault, or setup can't confirm the login stopped, the token can stay in that home until a sign-in an hour or more later finds no process using it, and an `/update-nanoclaw` snapshot taken in that window copies it along with the rest of `data/` and `.env`, on the same machine.

## Skill delivery

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

The change touches only the add-codex payload's `setup/providers/codex.ts`, its test, and two SKILL.md sentences.

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

releases.name: v2026.11.0-rc.3
releases.body:
NanoClaw 2026.11.0-rc.3 is the third release candidate of 2026.11.0: the build we expect to ship as stable unless testing finds a problem, so no more betas come before it. The November release takes the place of 2026.10.1, which never becomes a stable release; its two release candidates stay published, and everything they brought is in this entry. Installs on the `beta` channel get this release candidate; `stable` stays on 2026.10.0 until 2026.11.0 is published. Since 2026.11.0-rc.2, setup on Linux turns on systemd lingering without a polkit prompt, setup shows the provider image rebuild in its progress window, Codex sign-in no longer needs the Codex CLI installed, Slack agent DMs show suggested prompts, `/add-onecli` tells you when OneCLI's database still accepts the default password, and `~/.onecli` can no longer be mounted into an agent container. Since 2026.11.0-rc.1, Codex groups signed in with ChatGPT can use GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, setup on Arch can install jq on a system that has never synced its package lists, `/update-nanoclaw` typechecks agent-runner changes on hosts without Bun, `ncl groups config add-mount` refuses folders NanoClaw keeps for itself, skill-apply and the OneCLI and Iron Proxy scripts start from checkouts whose path contains a space or a symlink, Codex agents on a Slack install keep the ncl and canvas instructions, and Codex agents behind OneCLI can use Codex's built-in image generation. Since 2026.11.0-beta.4, OneCLI installs give OneCLI's database its own password with one command (see below), groups that installed extra packages move to the new agent image on their own, setup asks the hardened-image question again after a sign-in that did not finish and names the real cause when Node or npm is broken, a long reply that fails part-way resumes at the part that failed instead of starting over, `/update-skills` refreshes `slack-agent-flow`, and agents no longer misread a OneCLI `access_restricted` error. Since 2026.11.0-beta.3, fetching the pre-built image works again after a Node upgrade, the WhatsApp link step stops at once when WhatsApp refuses the connection and tells a finished pairing from a requested code, setup keeps using the Node version it checked, Claude agents start fresh when their saved conversation is gone, and a long Slack reply cut through an emoji now posts. Since 2026.11.0-beta.2, gateway approval cards mark anything they shorten, an approval card changes only after NanoClaw accepts the click, long Slack replies are sent as several messages, and installs that set `NANOCLAW_INSTALL_ID` use it in the shell scripts and the installed service. Since 2026.11.0-beta.1, locally built agent images move to Claude Code 2.1.321 and Agent SDK 0.3.321, the first pair that knows Claude Fable 5.2, `/update-nanoclaw` no longer stops on a lockfile conflict at the first update of a default install, setup installs jq when it's missing so channel setup works on WSL and minimal Ubuntu images, setup restarts NanoClaw after it installs a provider, mention-sticky threads no longer wake the agent for chatter it was never mentioned in, answered question cards keep their question text on every channel, and setup warns when a OneCLI gateway on another machine would send your agents to their own machine. Since 2026.10.1-rc.2, a stuck channel send no longer silences a conversation, agents can put KPI fields, a table and charts in cards, setup on Linux and WSL asks for your password in the open before it installs Node or Docker, setup on Linux reaches Docker right after it adds you to the docker group, setup names the NanoClaw account a machine is signed in to and lets you switch it, Discord server messages that @mention someone reach the agent, agent reactions reach Telegram, Mattermost recovers by itself from a short outage at startup, the OneCLI upgrade guide deletes the Dial key only when it has to, and locally built agent images clear every known High and Critical advisory that had a fix. Since 2026.10.0 it moves OneCLI to 1.45, where new agent groups get only their model key and other keys go to the groups you choose, makes the webhook server listen only on this machine by default, applies egress lockdown to agents that were already running, asks for Node's October 2026 security releases, and lets Claude agents read PDFs; Google Chat now checks that its webhooks come from your app. It also lets agents create other agents from templates, adds Cursor as an agent provider, and moves locally built agent images to Claude Code 2.1.321 with Claude Haiku 5.5. Eight changes need action from some installs, among them the OneCLI upgrade, the OneCLI database password, the webhook address and two new Google Chat settings, so check the section below before you update.

### ⚠️ Before you update

- [BREAKING] **Chat SDK channels move to adapter 4.41.1, which fixes Telegram messages with links that were never delivered.** Affected: installs where `grep -o '"@chat-adapter/[a-z]*"' package.json` prints anything (Telegram, Slack, Discord, Google Chat, Teams, WhatsApp Cloud, GitHub, Linear). Fix: `/update-nanoclaw` refreshes installed channels; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-<channel>` for each one. Google Chat: @mentions in spaces now need `GOOGLE_CHAT_BOT_USER_ID=users/<id>` in `.env` (DMs work without it; without it the log says "Google Chat botUserId is not configured" at startup): once the app has replied to you in a DM, list that DM's messages with the Chat API (`spaces.messages.list`), copy the `sender.name` of a message whose sender `type` is `BOT`, and restart the service. Slack agent-to-agent rooms: a sibling bot now arrives as `slack:bot:U…` instead of `slack:bot:B…`, so approve each sibling bot once more. Check: each channel answers a test message. Rollback: `pnpm exec tsx scripts/update-nanoclaw.ts rollback --id <transaction-id>` ([rolling back](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/operate/upgrading#rolling-back)).
- [BREAKING] **Iron Proxy installs that connected Codex with ChatGPT before this release must sign in to Codex again.** Detect, from the NanoClaw folder (works while the service is stopped): `f=data/session-materials/iron-control/codex.json; [ -f "$f" ] && grep -q '"mode":"chatgpt"' "$f" && ! grep -q '"accountId"' "$f" && echo affected`. Once running, an affected install's Codex agents answer only with the failure notice ("Sorry, something went wrong and I couldn't answer") and the agent container log shows `selected workspace missing from routing discovery`. Why: Codex 0.156 and later check the login's workspace id, and older Iron logins never recorded it. Fix: `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth codex`, then check that a Codex agent answers. OneCLI installs are affected only when the vault holds several ChatGPT logins or one without a recorded id; the host log then says "OneCLI login stand-in keeps its placeholder account id": delete the extra or stale login (`onecli secrets list`, then `onecli secrets delete --id <id>`), run the same command, and grant the new secret to each agent that had the old one, as `docs/onecli-upgrades.md` in your install describes. Rollback: return to the previous release.
- [BREAKING] **Forks and hand-made templates: the template code moved and `templates/` is now ignored by git.** Affected: fork code that imports `cloneRegistry`, `listTemplatesFromDir`, `copyTemplate` or `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_SOURCE` from `setup/templates.ts` (it stops compiling), forks that edit the `GROUP_SCOPE_RESOURCES` line or the stamper's `ensureContainerConfig` line, forks that point setup at their own template library, and anyone who keeps a hand-made template in `templates/`. Why: templates fetched by setup or by an agent are install state and must not block `/update-nanoclaw`, and setup now lists a library from its `index.json`. Fix: import `cloneRegistry` and `listTemplatesFromDir` from `src/templates/library.ts` and `await cloneRegistry()`; `copyTemplate` is gone, so call `ensureTemplateLocal`; a fork that changed `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_SOURCE` edits `LIBRARY_REPO` (`owner/repo`) and `LIBRARY_BRANCH` in `src/templates/library.ts` instead; re-anchor fork edits on the new lines; keep a new hand-made template in git with `git add -f templates/<ref>`; give your own library an `index.json` at its root in the same shape as `nanocoai/nanoclaw-templates` (`{ "schema": 1, "categories": { "<category>": [{ "ref": "<folder>", "name": "...", "description": "..." }] } }`). Check: `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` passes and setup's library picker lists your templates ([building templates](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/templates/building)). Rollback: revert this release; fetched templates then show as untracked in `git status`, so delete them or `git add` the ones to keep.
- [BREAKING] **OneCLI installs: upgrade the gateway to 1.45.0 and the `onecli` CLI to 2.11.0, where agents get only the keys you grant them.** Detect: the gateway's `/api/health` reports a version older than 1.45.0, or `unknown` (Iron Proxy installs skip this). Why: OneCLI 1.44 replaced secret modes with per-agent grants, and 1.45 is the last version that converts existing installs, so do not skip past it. Fix: before restarting, follow `docs/onecli-upgrades.md` in your install ([the same guide on GitHub](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-onecli/payload/docs/onecli-upgrades.md)); it backs up the gateway database, stops if the conversion would delete your rules, and covers the CLI binary. If you use `/add-dial-tool`, run the guide's Dial check before you pull; it deletes the Dial key only when the upgrade could hand it to agents you kept away from Dial (see the Dial item below). Existing groups keep what the conversion gives them; new groups get only their model credential, and on a 1.42 gateway new groups still get every key until you upgrade. To give a group a tool, re-run that tool's skill (for example `/add-vercel`) and pick the group; with `/add-tavily-tool`, re-run its Phase 5 so paid-key upgrades attach the key. `/add-vercel`, `/add-tavily-tool` and `/add-dial-tool` refuse a gateway that is not 1.45. If your Claude key in OneCLI is not named `Anthropic` (or your Codex key `Codex` or `openai`), new groups get no key: run that provider's login again after upgrading (`pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step gateway-auth claude`, or `codex`). Check: `/api/health` reports 1.45.0 and a new agent group answers. Rollback: restore the database backup the guide takes.
- [BREAKING] **OneCLI installs: give OneCLI's database its own password. `/update-nanoclaw` does not do this for you.** Detect: `[ -f ~/.onecli/docker-compose.yml ] && { ! grep -q '^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=.' ~/.onecli/.env 2>/dev/null || grep -Eqx "POSTGRES_PASSWORD=[\"']?(onecli)?[\"']?[[:space:]]*" ~/.onecli/.env; } && echo affected`. Remote gateways and Iron Proxy installs are not affected. Why: OneCLI's database still used the fixed default password from OneCLI's compose file. Fix, from the NanoClaw folder: `pnpm exec tsx .claude/skills/add-onecli/scripts/postgres-password.ts`. It saves a random password in `~/.onecli/.env`, sets it on the database and restarts OneCLI once; your data stays. If it prints "Not changed", fix what it names (usually a setting to save in `~/.onecli/.env`) and run it again. Check: a second run prints "OneCLI's database already has its own password", and once the update has finished, an agent answers. Rollback: none needed; the previous release keeps working with the new password.
- [BREAKING] **The webhook server now listens on 127.0.0.1 by default.** Tunnels and reverse proxies on the same machine keep working. Affected: a proxy on another machine, or anything in Docker on Linux that calls back to the host, such as a Mattermost server; webhooks stop arriving, and the log shows `Webhook server started host="127.0.0.1"`. Fix: set `WEBHOOK_HOST=0.0.0.0` (or one interface's IP address; a name such as `localhost` stops the host at startup) in `.env` and restart. Check: a message on that channel gets an answer. Rollback: the same setting restores the old behavior.
- [BREAKING] **Google Chat installs need two new settings, or the channel does not start.** Google Chat now verifies that webhooks come from your Workspace add-on Chat app, using `GOOGLE_CHAT_ENDPOINT_URL` and `GOOGLE_CHAT_PROJECT_NUMBER` (digits) in `.env`; `/update-nanoclaw` brings the new adapter but cannot ask for them. Detect: the log says "Google Chat needs GOOGLE_CHAT_ENDPOINT_URL and GOOGLE_CHAT_PROJECT_NUMBER (digits) in .env to verify webhooks". Fix: re-run `/add-gchat`, which keeps your existing values and asks for the endpoint URL, the project number and the bot user id for @mentions in spaces, or set both values by hand and restart. The Chat app must be a Google Workspace add-on, and converting an app to one cannot be undone. Check: a test message gets an answer. Rollback: `pnpm exec tsx scripts/update-nanoclaw.ts rollback --id <transaction-id>`.
- [BREAKING] **Custom skills and forks: a card's response handler must say what the click did.** Affected: your own skill or fork code that registers a response handler for card clicks, or that calls `finalizeReject` with a reason. Detect: a response handler that returns `true` still compiles, but its card no longer changes and the host logs `legacy_true`; a `finalizeReject` call with a 4th string argument no longer compiles. Why: a card may show only what the host decided. Fix: return `'accepted'`, `'refused'`, `'closed'` or `'ignored'` (or `false` to pass the click on), and pass a reject reason as `finalizeReject(approval, session, userId, { reason })`. Check: `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` passes and a clicked card changes. Rollback: return to the previous release; handlers that return `true` then redraw as before.
- **`/add-dial-tool` users: run the upgrade guide's Dial check before upgrading OneCLI.** It reads only, and says `delete` only when the gateway has not converted yet (1.43 or older) and the upgrade could remove what keeps agents away from Dial, such as `Dial: blocked agents`, or when it cannot read all the rules that decide; a gateway already on 1.44 or later keeps its Dial key and its grants. When it says `delete`, the guide's `--delete` command removes the key; re-run `/add-dial-tool` after the upgrade, which gives the Dial key only to the agent groups you choose, and new groups get Dial only when you add them. NanoClaw's `ONECLI_PROJECT_ID` and the `onecli` CLI's project (`onecli config set project`, or `ONECLI_PROJECT`) must match or both be unset: when they differ, the re-run stops and writes nothing to OneCLI. An agent group name with a line break no longer changes which groups keep Dial.
- **Update Node to its October 2026 security release.** Setup now requires Node 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1 or newer and refuses the end-of-life 23 and 25; locally built agent images move to Node 22.23.5 (Node's November 2026 security release), pinned by digest, and hardened installs get it with a later image. NanoClaw keeps running on an older Node; re-running setup picks a Node that meets the minimum, and stops only when it finds none. After `/update-nanoclaw`, run `bash setup/install-node.sh`, then re-run `bash nanoclaw.sh` so the service uses the new Node. If Node comes from nvm, fnm, volta or asdf, update it there.
- **Egress lockdown now covers agents that were already running when it was turned on**: they restart on the locked network when the host restarts. If the lockdown network exists but is not internal (only a network made by hand, or a setting that points at an ordinary one), agents no longer start and the host log says "Refusing to spawn with open egress". Fix: list what is attached with `docker network inspect nanoclaw-egress`, detach it (`docker network disconnect nanoclaw-egress <container>`), then `docker network rm nanoclaw-egress`; the next agent start recreates it as internal. Iron Proxy installs name it `nanoclaw-egress-<slug>`, and `NANOCLAW_EGRESS_NETWORK` can set another name.
- **Locally built agent images move to Claude Code 2.1.321 and Agent SDK 0.3.321, where Claude Haiku 5.5 replaces Haiku 4.5.** They are the first pair that knows Claude Fable 5.2. On the Anthropic API, Claude Code's background requests and groups set to `haiku` move to Haiku 5.5, which costs a tenth of Haiku 4.5's price for prompts up to 100K tokens. Hardened installs keep Claude Code 2.1.280 and Haiku 4.5 until an image for this release is listed.
- **Hardened installs move to the image built from v2026.10.0.** A pull now takes the image listed in `agent-images.json` on `main` for the newest release in the install's history, so a new hardened image reaches installs without a new release. Betas and release candidates never get an image of their own, so this release candidate uses v2026.10.0's (Claude Code 2.1.280, newer than the old pinned build), and the pull's "agent-runner lock drift" warning is expected. `main` lists a newer build of that image, made on 2026-11-14, so `/update-nanoclaw` pulls it again. Run `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step registry -- --refresh` to move onto it ([hardened runtime](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/guides/echo-hardened-runtime)).
- **Codex groups signed in with ChatGPT can use GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol.** `/add-codex` now pins `@openai/codex` 0.169.0; OpenAI refuses these models to Codex 0.165 and older on ChatGPT logins (API keys already worked). Groups with no model set start new threads on GPT-6.1 Sol with an API key and on GPT-6.2 Sol with a ChatGPT login; existing threads keep their model. To pick one, run `ncl groups config update --id <group-id> --model gpt-6.2-astra`, then `ncl groups restart --id <group-id>`. To stay on the 2026.10.0 default, use `--model gpt-6-astra`.

### ✨ New

- **Agents can create other agents from templates.** Ask for one in chat, pick from `ncl templates list` or the public library, and the agent builds it. Setup's template library list now shows what each template does ([using templates](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/templates/using-templates)).
- **Cursor is an agent provider.** The new `/add-cursor` skill runs Cursor's Agent SDK, and setup offers Cursor in the provider picker; it needs a locally built agent image ([providers](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/extend/providers)).
- **Setup waits for a slow first reply instead of failing.** The first-chat check waits 2 minutes, then asks whether to keep waiting, and shows each stage (sandbox, agent runtime, model) with its time, so local models that take minutes to load no longer fail setup. Runs without a terminal now stop after 2 minutes instead of 30 seconds.
- **Agents on slow local models are no longer cut off mid-turn.** Raise `NANOCLAW_ABSOLUTE_CEILING_MS` (default 30 minutes) or `NANOCLAW_CLAIM_STUCK_MS` (default 60 seconds) in `.env`; the host log names which one fired. Restart the service after a change; installs that set neither are unaffected ([environment variables](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/reference/environment-variables)).
- **Agents can put KPI fields, a table and charts in a `send_card` card.** Slack draws them natively and Teams shows a chart as a table; WhatsApp Cloud doesn't show tables or charts yet, and Mattermost doesn't show charts, so agents put those numbers in text there. The linked-device WhatsApp channel (`/add-whatsapp`) doesn't show cards at all. A card's whole text, title and description included, may be up to about 12,000 characters; `send_card` refuses a longer card with the reason, so the agent can send a smaller one. Channels have lower limits of their own, such as 4,096 characters for a whole card on Telegram, and 150 for the title and 3,000 for the description on Slack; a card over them can be cut off or not posted.
- **Early test builds are now called betas.** They are tagged `vX.Y.Z-beta.N`, and `-rc.N` (release candidate) is kept for the last build or two before a release. The `beta` channel offers the newest beta or release candidate that is newer than stable, and `stable` never offers either. `/update-nanoclaw` reads this rule from `main`, so beta installs on 2026.10.1-rc.2 get this release candidate as they are.

### 🛠️ Fixes

- **Setup tells you when your assistant's first reply failed.** Instead of saying the assistant is ready (for example after a bad API key), it shows the agent's error, names the log files and links the troubleshooting docs; `pnpm run chat` exits with code 4 on a failure notice. When an agent has no error of its own to share, every channel's failure notice now reads "Sorry, something went wrong and I couldn't answer" and links the troubleshooting docs.
- **Setup on Linux and WSL asks for your password up front.** It asks in the open, right before it installs Node or Docker, instead of hiding the sudo prompt behind the progress spinner. On WSL, the docker-group message now tells you to run `wsl --shutdown`.
- **Setup on Linux reaches Docker right after it adds you to the docker group.** The service kept the groups it started with, so it could not open Docker and kept restarting; setup's workaround needs the `acl` package, which stock and minimal Ubuntu lack. Setup now installs `acl` on apt systems, gives your user access to Docker until Docker restarts, and starts the service without a crash wait; a reboot (or `wsl --shutdown` on WSL) makes it last. If it still can't reach Docker, setup prints the commands to run.
- **Setup no longer prints "Failed to execute /usr/bin/pkttyagent" on Linux hosts without polkit.** It enables systemd lingering without a polkit prompt and reports lingering as on only when it is.
- **Setup names the NanoClaw account this machine is signed in to.** At the hardened image and managed Slack steps it asks "Continue as <email>" or "Use a different account", so switching no longer means deleting `account.json`. A first sign-in prints a short code in the terminal: approve only if the sign-in page shows the same code.
- **Setup asks about the hardened image again after a sign-in that did not finish.** If the sign-in code expired or a service was down, setup used to save "build locally" and never ask again, even though it told you to re-run. Now only a real "no" is saved.
- **Channel setup works on WSL and minimal Ubuntu images.** Setup now installs jq when it's missing, so Slack, Discord, Telegram, Teams and Dial setup work there. Slack and Discord setup now stop when the API reply has no id, instead of saving an empty one.
- **Setup restarts NanoClaw after it installs a provider.** `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step provider-auth <provider>` now restarts NanoClaw after installing a provider, so Codex, Cursor and OpenCode work without a manual host restart. The restart runs before sign-in, so an OpenCode install or re-auth that sets a new endpoint needs one more `bash setup/lib/restart.sh`.
- **On an Arch system that has never synced its package lists, setup can now run a whole-system upgrade (`pacman -Syu`, which updates every package) to install jq.** It asks first, No is the default, and it never runs without a terminal. During a provider install, setup also shows "not installed" only once, and keeps the last good build when the host build fails.
- **Setup no longer fills the screen with Docker build output after you pick Codex, Cursor or OpenCode.** The image rebuild shows the same progress window as the first build, and its full log is in `logs/setup-steps/`.
- **Codex setup no longer needs the Codex CLI installed on your machine.** If `codex` isn't on your PATH, ChatGPT sign-in runs the pinned version through pnpm, from pnpm's cache, with no global install or sudo. It also no longer warns about `/tmp`.
- **Setup warns when a OneCLI gateway on another machine would send your agents to their own machine.** They would never reply, so setup prints the `GATEWAY_BASE_URL` line to set.
- **Agents no longer lose or repeat a reply around `send_message`.** An agent that sent something with `send_message` and then left its answer unwrapped is shown what it already sent and asked to finish, and an exact repeat is not sent twice. On streaming providers, a reply sent with `send_message` and followed by plain closing text costs one extra model turn.
- **Agents reply in the language of the message they are answering**, unless you ask for another one. They no longer pick a language from earlier history, other people's messages or the timezone.
- **A stuck channel no longer silences agents.** NanoClaw stops waiting on a send after 60 seconds, logs `Message delivery passed its deadline`, and keeps delivering that conversation's later replies until 3 of its sends are stuck at once; chats wired to share one session (`agent-shared`) count as one conversation. A stuck message is retried if its send fails, and marked failed if there is still no answer an hour later. Other conversations keep going while up to 8 are stuck; with more, their replies can wait a minute or more.
- **Fewer failed agent runs.** On Docker Desktop, a message that arrives while an agent is replying no longer fails the run, and "Permission denied" replies to admin-only commands are sent directly to the chat. On every install, `ncl` and agent tools no longer hit intermittent "database is locked" errors.
- **Mention-sticky threads no longer wake the agent for chatter it was never mentioned in.** A thread keeps going without a mention only after the agent was woken there. A message sent while the thread's first mention is still in its admin-command check (such as `/clear`) no longer wakes the agent: it is dropped under `ignored_message_policy='drop'` (the default) and kept as context under `'accumulate'`. The gap is near zero unless the role lookup is slow, as with a remote database.
- **Approval cards appear where you are waiting and are easier to read.** When an agent in a thread of your own DM asks for approval, the card and its "Reject with reason" prompt appear in that thread. Cards show command arguments and agent-to-agent messages in a code block, and names and the install reason quoted on one line. An approval an agent asks for, or an `ask_user_question`, whose title and question together run over 2,000 characters is refused, and the agent is told the limit so it can shorten it; `ask_user_question` also returns an error within seconds of the host giving up on delivering its card, instead of waiting out its 300-second timeout.
- **Answered question cards keep their question text** on every channel, not just Discord.
- **Gateway approval cards show the action in the card text and mark anything they shorten.** Card text is no longer cut at a fixed length: a shortened value ends with "… N more characters not shown", and left-out details are counted. Card text shows as typed on Slack, Google Chat and Discord. On Telegram, Discord and WhatsApp Cloud a card too long to show whole is refused instead of cut: nothing is approved, and the approver is told the request was not shown. `/update-nanoclaw` brings the channel side; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-<channel>` for each one.
- **An approval card changes only after NanoClaw accepts the click.** A click from someone who can't answer the card leaves its buttons in place. WhatsApp, iMessage and the local web chat confirm an answer only after it is accepted; a refused answer leaves the question open. On Discord, clicks on cards from a durable approval gateway are now recorded (they were ignored), a stalled click acknowledgement no longer holds later events in its channel, and a decided gateway approval card no longer keeps its buttons. `/update-nanoclaw` brings the channel side; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-<channel>` for each one.
- **The background service finds the tools it was installed with.** On macOS it now includes `/opt/homebrew/bin` and the Node.js folder, so Apple Silicon installs using Homebrew or Apple Container no longer crash at start; on Linux it includes the Node.js folder (for example from nvm). Existing installs get it by running `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step service` once.
- **Installs that set `NANOCLAW_INSTALL_ID` now use it in the shell scripts and the installed service.** The shell scripts (image build and pull, restart, skill steps) and the launchd or systemd service that setup installs use the id, and an invalid value stops them with a clear error. On Linux without systemd, `start-nanoclaw.sh` keeps the id too, and re-running setup with a new id replaces the checkout's old service instead of leaving it running. It retires only a service with a name setup writes (`nanoclaw-v2-…`) that starts this checkout and has no `systemctl edit` drop-in, or a service whose program no longer exists. Any other `nanoclaw*` service is left alone. An existing install gets the id into its service and `start-nanoclaw.sh` by running `pnpm exec tsx setup/index.ts --step service` once.
- **`/update-nanoclaw` no longer stops at its validate step on installs with Slack.** The skill refresh now credits each channel import to the skill that adds it, so it stops looking for Slack skills that don't exist. The fix comes with the update itself.
- **When `/update-nanoclaw` cannot refresh an installed skill, the error names each failed skill** and its error, instead of a generic message.
- **`/update-nanoclaw` no longer stops on a lockfile conflict at the first update of a default install.** It now regenerates `pnpm-lock.yaml` and the agent-runner `bun.lock` when they are the only merge conflicts. After a manual merge, take the new lockfile and run `pnpm install --lockfile-only` (for `bun.lock`, `bun install --lockfile-only` in `container/agent-runner`).
- **`/update-nanoclaw` now typechecks agent-runner changes on hosts without Bun**, using the Bun version the image pins. If it cannot run Bun, it says the source was not typechecked instead of claiming the image build would check it.
- **Discord: Approve on an approval card now approves.** Button clicks were misread, so approvals were recorded as rejections and answers to questions came back garbled.
- **Discord: server messages that @mention someone reach the agent.** Chat SDK adapter 4.41.1 dropped every server message with an @mention, including ones that mention the bot; `/add-discord` and `/update-nanoclaw` now apply a patch with the upstream fix. After a manual merge, rerun `/add-discord`.
- **Agent reactions reach Telegram and other Chat SDK channels.** They failed with "message to react not found" and were dropped after three tries.
- **Errors the Chat SDK hits while handling an incoming message show in the NanoClaw log** instead of being dropped silently.
- **Mattermost recovers by itself from a short outage at startup.** When the server, or a proxy in front of it, is unreachable or answers with a server error, it tries 3 more times, waiting 2, 5 and then 10 seconds, instead of staying offline until NanoClaw is restarted; after a longer outage, restart NanoClaw once the server is back. `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-mattermost`.
- **Slack: long replies are sent as several messages instead of failing.** Slack refuses a message over 12,000 characters, so a reply over 10,000 is now split. `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-slack`.
- **Slack: agent DMs now show the three "Get started" suggested prompts**, and new DM threads get a title.
- **Fetching the pre-built sandbox image works again after a Node upgrade.** It failed with "error getting credentials" once Node was upgraded or replaced. The docker credential helper now finds Node on its own, and setup and `/update-nanoclaw` rewrite a helper from an older version.
- **The WhatsApp link step gives a clear answer.** When WhatsApp refuses the connection, the step stops at once, shows the reason and asks you to clear `store/auth/` and try again, instead of waiting two minutes and reporting a timeout. It also tells a finished pairing from a requested pairing code: a rerun after an unused code no longer says "already authenticated", and when the connection drops right after pairing, the step says whether the link was saved and asks you to clear `store/auth/` only when it was not.
- **Setup keeps using the Node version it checked.** An older Node in `~/.local/bin` or npm's global folder can no longer take over `pnpm install` or the background service. When the Node on PATH cannot start or npm is broken, setup names the real cause instead of ending without a message or saying it needs root, and `migrate-v2.sh` finds the pnpm that setup put in `~/.local/bin`.
- **Claude agents start fresh when their saved conversation is gone.** When Claude Code has deleted a chat's saved conversation (after 30 idle days by default), the next message gets a normal reply from a new session, instead of a "No conversation found with session ID" error and a lost message.
- **Codex: agents on a Slack install keep the ncl and canvas instructions.** NanoClaw now caps Codex's AGENTS.md at 64 KiB instead of 32 KiB.
- **Codex agents behind OneCLI can now use Codex's built-in image generation with a ChatGPT subscription**, and the images are sent to the chat. Each agent picks this up the next time it starts.
- **Long replies sent in parts resume at the part that failed.** A retry, even after a restart, picks up after the parts NanoClaw recorded as posted instead of starting over, and a cut no longer splits a single emoji character (on Slack, that stopped the rest of the reply from posting). An emoji built from several characters, such as a flag or a skin tone, can still be split between parts, but each part posts.
- **`ncl groups restart --id <other group>` restarts that group.** Run by a global-scope agent, it restarted the agent's own session instead.
- **`ncl groups config add-mount` now refuses folders NanoClaw keeps for itself** (runner code, skills, plugins, instruction files, keys and certificates) with a clear reason. A container start refused by the mount guard is logged as an error on each attempt. If a group already has one, remove it with `ncl groups config remove-mount`, then restart the group.
- **Setup's verify step says why a background Slack install failed**, and passes again once a later Slack setup has connected and wired a chat.
- **Discord and Matrix: updates and re-runs apply the adapter patch.** `/update-nanoclaw` no longer fails on a Discord install older than adapter 4.41.1, and re-running `/add-discord` or `/add-matrix` on an existing install now applies the adapter patch.
- **`/update-skills` refreshes an installed `slack-agent-flow`**, and re-applying a skill adds the lines an append block gained since the install.
- **Discord: an approval card that times out or closes with nobody clicking no longer keeps its buttons.** `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-discord`.
- **Mattermost: a connection that never finishes opening no longer hangs.** If the server accepts the connection but never finishes the WebSocket upgrade, the adapter gives up after 10 seconds and retries, instead of hanging until NanoClaw restarts. `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-mattermost`.
- **WhatsApp: a voice note is marked as a voice note**, not as an audio file, so the agent can tell the two apart. The file itself still does not reach the agent, as with all WhatsApp media; a fix is in review. `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-whatsapp`.
- **Stopping an agent container no longer logs a false "session realization failed: unknown"** while Docker is still finishing its own removal. A session network that can't be removed keeps the session's claim and is retried, instead of leaking silently.
- **Clearer logs.** Idle containers stopped after 30 minutes log at info, not warn, so the warning log shows only stops that interrupt a message, and a failed container stop logs Docker's own error. GitHub, Linear and Resend log a warning when a message that waited behind a busy conversation is skipped or expires.
- **A refused portal connection is logged right away.** On Node 22 the host waited 10 seconds and logged `handshake_timeout`. It now logs `dial_failed` at once and retries on its normal schedule.
- **The OneCLI docs match OneCLI 1.45.** `/add-onecli` explains what OneCLI 1.45 can allow, ask or block per agent, and the templates guide no longer promises automatic key injection or approval holds on host, method and path. When OneCLI answers `access_restricted`, agents no longer retry a connect link or say the key is stored: they ask an admin to check that the app is connected (another Google app on the same host can cause the error), then connect, attach or reconnect it. `/add-onecli` warns that an Allow tool can let through requests of an Ask tool it covers.
- **Claude agents can read long PDFs you send them.** Installs that build their own agent image get it from the image rebuild in `/update-nanoclaw`. Hardened installs get it with a later image.
- **Groups that installed extra packages move to the new agent image on their own.** After `/update-nanoclaw` or an image rebuild, NanoClaw rebuilds their image in the background when it starts or when the group next runs, and the group's next container uses it, so `ncl groups restart --id <group-id> --rebuild` is no longer needed after an update. If you built a group's image by hand under the group's own tag, give it your own tag and pin that with `ncl groups config update --id <group-id> --image-tag <tag>`, because NanoClaw now rebuilds the group's own tag.
- **Google Chat attachments reach the agent.** On channels whose message ids contain `/`, such as Google Chat, files were dropped and the agent saw only the file name. When someone shares a file from Google Drive, the agent now says it can't open Drive files and asks for the file to be pasted or dragged into the chat.
- **Resend email replies are sent.** Agent replies and the "Connect yourself" hello failed with `Invalid thread ID format`; they now go out, and a reply lands in the email thread the person last wrote in. `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-resend`.
- **Installing extra packages for an agent works when NanoClaw lives in a folder whose name has a space.** Setup and uninstall now stop only this install's own host process.
- **Skill-apply and the OneCLI / Iron Proxy scripts now start from checkouts whose path contains a space or a symlink.** Thanks to @echarrod.
- **Smaller fixes.** An agent reads its own replies from other threads of the same chat as its own, not as another agent's; `ncl groups delete` also removes the group's host bookkeeping rows, and agents that could message it stop listing it right away; creating an agent from a template no longer fails when an agent that has not run yet holds that name; a Slack bot set up for channels only no longer sends you an FYI each time it turns away a DM; `ncl messaging-groups delete` also removes the group's wirings, its own sessions and pending approvals instead of failing with a foreign key error, and removing iMessage uses it; creating an agent refuses a name whose group folder would be invalid (too long, or reserved such as "Global") before anything is written, and says why; setup accepts Anthropic's newer API key types (`sk-ant-usr`, `sk-ant-svc`), which must be scoped to one workspace; Linux Signal setup installs signal-cli 0.14.9, which fixes sends to new contacts hanging (rerun `setup/install-signal-cli.sh`, then restart the service); when `ncl` can't reach the host, it also shows the restart command for Linux without systemd (for example WSL); and the `/add-dashboard` dashboard keeps updating when a transcript grows past about 512 MB and no longer re-reads every transcript each minute (rerun `/add-dashboard` to get it).

### 🔒 Security

- **`/add-resend` installs a Resend adapter with no known advisories.** The pin moves from 0.1.1 (4 moderate findings through `uuid`) to 0.3.0, and `/update-nanoclaw` moves existing email installs to it (after a manual merge, rerun `/add-resend`). The webhook now answers before the message is processed, so a message that fails is not retried, and replies are sent as HTML with a plain-text part that drops link targets.
- **Signal setup checks the signal-cli download's sha256** before installing it.
- **OneCLI setup keeps keys off the command line.** Setup now gives keys to the `onecli` CLI through a private temporary file or stdin, and hides them in error messages. If setup ever failed while saving your Anthropic key or OneCLI API key, rotate that key and delete the old files in `logs/setup-steps/` and `logs/setup.log`.
- **`/add-onecli` now tells you when OneCLI's database still accepts the default password after setup**, and `~/.onecli` can no longer be mounted into an agent container.
- **Dial setup no longer leaves the account token readable by other users on the machine** while it pins the default sender number.
- **Registry sign-in opens your browser only for a plain https link**, and says so when it starts no browser. On WSL without `wslview` or `xdg-open` it no longer tries `cmd.exe`; open the link it prints instead.
- **Text that task scripts and webhooks put in an agent's prompt can no longer pose as text NanoClaw wrote.** Script output, webhook bodies, task prompts and attachment types can no longer close the block they sit in.
- **Locally built agent images move to Node 22.23.5, Node's November 2026 security release.** `/update-nanoclaw` rebuilds the image; hardened installs get it with a later image. Setup's minimum Node stays the same.
- **Approval cards on Google Chat and Discord show request text as typed.** On Google Chat a card's own labels are bold, so a line of request text can't pose as one, and a line in an agent's message that starts like a label, such as `*Action:*`, stays as typed. On Discord, `*`, `_` and `~` in request text show as typed, so they can't turn code into links, mentions or spoilers. `/update-nanoclaw` brings it; after a manual merge, rerun `/add-gchat` or `/add-discord`.
- **Locally built agent images move to Bun 1.4.4, which no longer trusts the revoked eMudhra certificates.** `/update-nanoclaw` rebuilds the image; hardened installs get it with a later image.
- **Locally built agent images clear every known High and Critical advisory that had a fix.** The image ships npm 11, pnpm 10.34.9, a fresh build of its Node base and updated agent-runner libraries. `/update-nanoclaw` rebuilds the image; hardened installs get it with a later image.
- **Re-applying a template to an agent (restamp) can no longer be pointed outside its group folder.** It refuses, with an error, to write a context file or skill through a folder in the group folder that was swapped for a link, and checks template file names more strictly. On a Mac this needs the NanoClaw folder on an APFS or HFS+ disk (the usual Mac disk); on other disks these writes are refused.
- **Hardened how the host opens files in agent folders.**

### 🔧 For custom installations

- **Custom container code that reads `inbound.db`** through `openInboundDb()` or `getInboundDb()` (`mailbox/sqlite/connection.ts`) must use `readInbound((db) => ...)`: `openInboundDb()` is gone, and `getInboundDb()` now works only in tests.
- **Custom mailbox stores that create storage on first write**: a new thread or conversation now gets its earlier context there. The default SQLite store was not affected.
- **`CLAUDE.md` matches the code again.** Coding agents get the right session folder and image tag, and know a group's `CLAUDE.md` is rewritten on every start: standing instructions go in `instructions.prepend.md`.
- **`/add-codex` ships its provider inside the skill**, so installs and forks no longer need the providers branch; on an older core its instructions tell you to update core first. Codex archives pick up core's header fix (the thread-id line no longer renders as a heading).
- **Provider skills can archive exchanges through core.** Use `container/agent-runner/src/provider-contracts/exchange-archive.ts`; refreshing `/add-codex` deletes the old copy in `providers/exchange-archive.ts`, so a custom provider that imports it must switch.
- **Skills can add context when a message wakes an agent, without editing core.** Register a provider with `registerWakeContext` (`src/wake-context.ts`): blocks it returns within a shared 1.5-second budget are written before the waking message, as `<tag about="...">`, a later block rides with the next message, and a slash command gets none. Channel adapters gain an optional `readHistory` (the Chat SDK bridge has it), and the mailbox's outbound reads carry an optional `platformMessageId`. With nothing registered, routing works as before and the agent's prompt gains one line about the `about` attribute.
- **A gateway credential can target one exact path on a host.** The provider credential seam moves to version 2: a custom provider skill that requires exactly version 1 must accept 1 or later, a skill that sets `path` must require 2, and a custom gateway must declare `connectionPaths: true` to accept path-scoped credentials.
- **The agent image no longer installs `cron-parser`** or its `luxon` dependency (about 4.9 MB); scheduling still runs on the host. Custom container code that imported them must add them back.
- **Forks that pointed the `versions.json` agent-image pin at their own mirror** must move that reference to `NANOCLAW_AGENT_IMAGE_REF`, because the `agent-images.json` list now comes first.
- **Forks no longer run the agent-image refresh workflow**, which failed every 6 hours outside `nanocoai/nanoclaw`.
- **OpenCode: `OPENCODE_NATIVE_ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES` and `OPENCODE_NATIVE_ATTACHMENT_MAX_COUNT` are gone**; they never took effect.
- **Forks: keep `@chat-adapter/discord` at 4.41.1.** A newer adapter needs a newer `chat` than core pins, so `pnpm run build` fails. If pnpm stops with `ERR_PNPM_UNUSED_PATCH`, run `pnpm add @chat-adapter/discord@4.41.1` or re-run `/add-discord`; to remove Discord, follow its `REMOVE.md`. `/add-discord`'s troubleshooting now gives the same fix, instead of keeping a newer adapter that doesn't build.

issues.title: youdaonote：API Key 以明文命令行参数传递，安装脚本缺少版本与校验
issues.body:
## 问题

### 1. API Key 进入命令行和对话上下文（主要）

`SKILL.md:18` 要求 Agent 在用户提供 Key 后执行：

```bash
youdaonote config set apiKey <用户提供的Key>
```

明文 Key 会同时出现在模型上下文、命令行参数、shell 历史和进程列表中；`SKILL.md:57`、`SKILL.md:152` 的示例沿用了同样的形式。对一个官方 skill 来说，这是目前主要的凭据暴露面。

建议改为受保护的传递方式（CLI 支持哪种就用哪种）：

- 由用户在自己的终端输入，Agent 不接触明文：

  ```bash
  read -s -p "YoudaoNote API Key: " YDN_KEY
  youdaonote config set apiKey "$YDN_KEY"
  unset YDN_KEY
  ```

- 或从环境变量 / 权限受控的配置文件读取（如 `0600`）。
- 文档中补充 Key 的存储位置与权限说明；若 CLI 只能通过参数接收，至少提示不要在多用户或会记录命令历史的环境中使用。

### 2. 安装脚本直接管道执行，缺少版本与校验（次要）

`SKILL.md:137`：

```bash
curl -fsSL https://artifact.lx.netease.com/download/youdaonote-cli/install.sh | bash -s -- -f -b ~/.local/bin
```

这是官方安装器，自动安装也是产品设计的一部分；问题在于脚本内容不可预知、没有版本固定或摘要校验，而 Agent 又被要求立即执行。

建议保持自动执行，但固定版本并校验：

```bash
curl -fsSLo youdaonote-install.sh <带版本号的安装脚本地址>
echo "<官方公布的 sha256>  youdaonote-install.sh" | sha256sum -c -
bash youdaonote-install.sh -f -b ~/.local/bin
```

并在文档中给出安装脚本的版本号与官方校验值。

## 备注
行号基于 `main@12a300a`（2026-11-16）。

prs.title: feat(cowork): restore subagent sessions on the dsh engine
prs.body:
## Summary

Restore the existing subagent panel on the dsh migration branch. Previously the parent could finish a delegated task and show the output files while the subagent panel stayed empty.

## Changes

- Associate delegated calls and results with dsh child session IDs. Keep the parent subscribed across an early yield so it can receive the children's results and finish its summary.
- Read each child's progress and history through its owning parent. Delegated tools inherit the bound Cowork context and retain the child's dsh permission restrictions.
- Import indexed legacy child transcripts at startup before the old engine directory is archived. Reuse cached messages and materialized child sessions so users can reopen an old parent and delegate new work alongside its existing children.

## Testing

- 87 focused Vitest tests passed. Electron and renderer TypeScript checks and changed-file ESLint passed.
- Verified on Windows by driving Electron with Playwright/CDP and the pinned dsh runtime. A deterministic local model endpoint exercised two and five parallel children, on-disk files, restart, asynchronous parent completion, and new delegations in an upgraded parent session.
- The Windows full suite reported 19 failures. Seventeen also failed on the base commit. The remaining two passed independently on this branch.

prs.title: perf(openclaw): slim the managed AGENTS.md sections and pristine template
prs.body:
## Summary

The workspace `AGENTS.md` is part of every model request, so repeated or unused text costs tokens on each cold start. This trims the parts that were duplicated or never used in LobsterAI, without removing any rule.

- **Office editing**: three per-format sections become one (`buildOfficeAgentPrompt`); each editor only declares what differs. The "answer from the edit reply, do not re-read" wording is kept verbatim.
- **Scheduled tasks**: merge the IM-helper and workaround bans (3,037 -> 1,672 chars for Office, 2,372 -> 2,011 for scheduled tasks).
- **OpenClaw template**: rewrite Group Chats and Tools, drop Related, only when a section hashes to a template shipped by a pinned OpenClaw version (v2026.3.2 - v2026.8.1). Sections the user or the agent edited never match and are left byte for byte.
- **Behavior change**: the proactive template sections ("Heartbeats - Be Proactive", and v2026.8.1's "Automations - Be Proactive", which tells the model to rotate through inbox/calendar/weather checks) are now dropped. The old heading-based strip stopped matching after the v2026.8.1 upgrade, so new workspaces were seeded with guidance that contradicts the heartbeat cost policy. Replaces `stripProactiveHeartbeatSection`.
- Not changed on purpose: Memory Policy, Web Search and the scheduled-task creation bullets. A merged wording changed request counts in A/B runs (create task 3/2/2 vs 2/2/2; remember 6/6 vs 4/5), and one extra request costs more than the ~200 tokens saved.

## Measured (deepseek-flash, local gateway)

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Workspace AGENTS.md | 22,592 chars | 19,573 chars |
| First request | 33,093 tokens | 32,424 tokens |

Regression on the final code: Word / Excel / PPT edit and verify = 3 requests each (read, edit) with correct file contents; scheduled task creation = 2 requests (5 runs).

The saving is small (~2%); the value is mostly removing contradictory guidance and a single place to maintain the Office rules.

## Test plan

- [x] `vitest` for scheduledTask, shared/office, openclawAgentsTemplate, openclawHeartbeatRepair, openclawConfigSync (447 tests)
- [x] ESLint on touched files with CI rules, `tsc --project electron-tsconfig.json --noEmit`
- [x] Local e2e on deepseek-flash as above
- [ ] Not tested: IM group-chat behavior after the shorter Group Chats section
- Full `npm test` has 15 failing files unrelated to this change (known local failures and parallel-run timeouts)

Touches OpenClaw workspace config sync: the managed `AGENTS.md` is rewritten on the next config sync, which breaks the prompt cache once for running sessions.

prs.title: perf(openclaw): defer large tool catalogs behind Tool Search
prs.body:
## Summary
Tool schemas were about two thirds of every model request: 68 tools and ~106k characters sent on each call, for a first-request baseline of ~45k tokens. This PR turns on OpenClaw Tool Search (directory mode) so only core file/shell tools and a few pinned interaction tools are sent directly; everything else is listed in a compact directory or found through `tool_search`.

Measured on deepseek-flash (fresh desktop session, `systemPromptReport` + provider usage): **first request 18,272 input tokens, down from 44.7k–45.8k**; visible tools 68 → 14 (~106k → ~13k characters).

## Related Issue
N/A

## Changes Made
- **Config sync** (`openclawConfigSync.ts`): `tools.toolSearch = { enabled, mode: 'directory', direct: [AskUserQuestion, ask_user, progress_card] }`; deny Control UI tools LobsterAI never renders (`dashboard`, `portal`, `terminal`, `github_identity_status`). `skill_workshop` stays enabled because the opt-in skill review uses it.
- **Managed AGENTS.md**: new "Deferred Tools" section so a tool reachable through `tool_search` counts as available (several sections say "use X if it is available").
- **New patch `openclaw-tool-search-direct-tools.patch`**: adds `tools.toolSearch.direct`. Needed because the delete policy skips confirmation when `AskUserQuestion` is not in the toolset, so it must never be deferred. Plugin `catalogMode: "direct-only"` is not enough (plugin tool descriptors are cached without it). MCP/client tools are never promoted.
- **New patch `openclaw-tool-call-slim-envelope.patch`**: `tool_call` results echoed the full catalog entry (description + input hint) on every call, 1.1k–5.2k characters each. The model now sees `{ tool: { id, name }, result }`; failure `details` and Code Mode keep the full shape.
- **Runtime adapter**: hide `tool_search` / `tool_describe` / `tool_call` events; the deferred tool emits its own events under its real name (plan mode checks that nested event).
- **IM history sync**: read `filePath` from `message` calls wrapped in `tool_call`.
- Patch validators, README sections, and the reviewed patch list updated.

## Type of Change
- [x] Performance improvement

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

- OpenClaw: new `tool-surface-plan` / schema / `tool-search.mcp-error` cases pass; all 94 patches apply in order from a clean tree with strong validation.
- LobsterAI: `openclawConfigSync.runtime` (incl. pinned-runtime `config validate`), `openclawRuntimeAdapter`, `openclawHistory`, `openclawPatches/*` pass; eslint clean on touched files; `npm run compile:electron` OK.
- End to end on the rebuilt runtime through the gateway (desktop session keys): Excel edit and Word edit via the Office editor MCP tools, browser open/read, and scheduled-task creation all succeed through search/describe/call. Results verified on disk; test jobs removed.
- Full `npm test` on Windows: remaining failures (office, git snapshot, qqbot, daily logs, etc.) reproduce on a clean HEAD worktree and are unrelated.

prs.title: perf(openclaw): ship only allowlisted bundled skills
prs.body:
## 问题

Windows 上 OpenClaw gateway 启动时，`starting channels and sidecars` 到 `ready` 要 6–7s。抓 CPU profile 后发现，其中约 75% 是同步的 `fs.access`。

## 原因

- runtime 自带的 51 个 skill（`skills/`）和 4 个 custodian skill（`custodian-skills/`）每次启动都会被检查一遍。LobsterAI 的技能管理界面会跳过它们，用户看不到，但 gateway 照样处理：
  - **检查依赖的二进制：** 每个缺失的命令都要按「PATH 目录数 × PATHEXT 扩展名数」逐个调用 `accessSync`。缺的大多是 macOS 或国外服务的工具（blu、codex、spotify_player 等），一次启动要 12,716 次，同步 IO 5.0s。
  - **写进提示词：** 通过检查的会写进 agent 的提示词，其中包括 clawhub、healthcheck、notion、taskflow，以及会用命令行改 OpenClaw 配置和渠道的 custodian skill，而这些配置是 LobsterAI 在管的。
- 内置 skill 在 `skills.load.extraDirs` 之后加载，同名时内置的胜出，所以 LobsterAI 自己的 `skill-creator`（「创建技能」按钮会按名字调用它）和 `weather` 一直被 OpenClaw 的英文版覆盖，线上版本也是这样。
- `skills.allowBundled` 解决不了覆盖问题：同名冲突在过滤之前就已经决出胜负，把胜出的内置 skill 过滤掉，两个版本会一起消失。

## 改动

- `openclaw:prune` 新增一步：`skills/` 只保留白名单里的 `diagram-maker`，`custodian-skills/` 整个删除。这一步在所有平台的 runtime 流水线里都会执行，在打包之前。
- 和已有的 `BUNDLED_EXTENSIONS_TO_KEEP` 一样用白名单：OpenClaw 升级带进来的新 skill 默认会被删掉。
- 新增测试：白名单的取舍；裁剪行为（custodian 被删、零散文件保留、重复执行没有副作用、目录不存在时不报错）；白名单里不能出现仓库 `SKILLs/` 已有的同名 skill。

## 验证

- 用 win-x64 runtime 和一份真实 state 目录的副本，单独起 gateway 测量（不开 profiler）：

| | 裁剪前 | 裁剪后 |
|---|---|---|
| PATH 探测 | 12,716 次 / 5.0s | 53 次 / 7ms |
| `sidecars.model-runtime` | 6.1–6.8s | 1.2s |
| channels → ready | 6.4–7.2s | 1.4s |

- 查询这个 gateway 实际生效的 skill 列表：共 40 个，LobsterAI 的 37 个可用 skill 都在（`skill-creator`、`weather` 现在用的是 LobsterAI 自己的版本），内置的只剩 `diagram-maker`，clawhub 和 custodian skill 都不在了。
- `/health`、`/healthz`、`/startupz`、`/ready` 照常返回 200。
- `npx vitest run tests/pruneOpenClawRuntime.test.ts tests/openclawRuntimePackaging.test.ts tests/openclawWindowsPayload.test.ts`：68 个测试全部通过。
- 绝对耗时受测试机负载影响较大（当时这台机器内存紧张），上表是同一台机器上交替运行得到的对比。

prs.title: perf(openclaw): ship build-info.json beside the gateway bundle
prs.body:
## Problem

OpenClaw's startup-migration checkpoint keys on `build-info.json` `builtAt`. It looks for `./build-info.json`, `../build-info.json` and `../../dist/build-info.json` relative to its own module. Those paths fit the `dist/` chunk layout, but LobsterAI runs the gateway from `gateway-bundle.mjs` at the runtime root, and only `dist/build-info.json` exists there.

As a result the build identity is `null`, the checkpoint is never recorded, and every gateway start reruns the full doctor preflight: legacy state migrations, plugin convergence, and 4–5 config snapshot reads.

Evidence:
- Installed and dev profiles have only the `primary` row in `state/openclaw.sqlite` `schema_meta`. There is no `startup-migrations` or `state-migrations` row.
- The host logs `startup summary: ... checkpoint=unknown` on every start.

## Change

- Add `dist/build-info.json` → `build-info.json` to `OPENCLAW_BUNDLE_ASSET_TARGETS`. This is the same mechanism `web-tree-sitter.wasm` already uses.
- The electron-builder hook, `finalize-openclaw-runtime` and the payload verification all read that list, so a runtime without the file now fails packaging instead of silently losing the checkpoint.
- The installer resource-recovery checks are unchanged. A missing `build-info.json` only costs startup time; the bundle still works.
- Version, commit and bundled model-catalog stamp lookups in the bundle read the same file. They now resolve as they do in the unbundled runtime.

## Measurements

Windows, dev app on the production renderer, run on a copy of a real profile with `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE=1`:

| | `gateway-run-bootstrap` | spawn → `loading configuration` |
|---|---|---|
| Before (checkpoint never hits) | ~5 s (9–12 s under load) | 6.4–13.8 s |
| After, first start (records checkpoint) | 12.1 s | 14.4 s |
| After, later starts (`checkpoint=hit`) | 1.25–2.2 s | 2.6–3.5 s |

Part of the plugin module-graph load moves from plugin convergence into plugin loading, so the net saving is about 2.5–3.5 s per warm start. In the cleanest interleaved A/B pair, launch-to-gateway-handshake was 11.8 s with the fix and 16.0 s without.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run tests/openclawBundleAssets.test.ts tests/openclawWindowsPayload.test.ts tests/windowsInstallerContract.test.ts`: all pass.
- CI ESLint on the touched test files: clean.
- `node scripts/bundle-openclaw-gateway.cjs` on an existing runtime places the file. Three app starts on a profile copy logged `checkpoint=miss` and then `hit` twice, and the `schema_meta` rows appeared.
- Not checked in a packaged installer build.
