prs.title: perf(openclaw): skip the dreaming startup scrub when dreaming is off
prs.body:
## Summary
memory-core's `gateway_start` hook scrubs `dreaming-narrative-*` session entries and transcripts that interrupted dreaming runs left behind. It runs right after start and again five minutes later, for every configured agent, **whether or not dreaming is enabled**. Even with nothing to remove, its planning step opens each agent database for writing: lease, integrity check, schema contract, index verification and deletion path fence. That's about 130 ms per agent of synchronous work right after the gateway reports ready, and it delays every request, including the desktop client's first handshake.

LobsterAI defaults dreaming to off (`DEFAULT_DREAMING_ENABLED = false`) and always writes `plugins.entries.memory-core.config.dreaming.enabled`, so for most users the scrub never finds anything.

New `zz-openclaw-dreaming-cleanup-only-when-enabled.patch` (`extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming.ts`):
- resolves the startup dreaming config with the same plugin-config fallback as cron reconciliation, but independently of it, so a failed cron reconciliation still scrubs when dreaming is on;
- skips both the immediate and the deferred scrub when dreaming is disabled;
- still scrubs if the config can't be resolved.

Trade-off: leftovers from an earlier period with dreaming enabled are reclaimed on the first start after dreaming is turned back on (changing the memory-core config restarts the gateway).

LobsterAI side: strong validator in `apply-openclaw-patches.cjs`, the patch registered and content-checked in `v20260801UpgradeDecisions.test.ts`, and a README section with rationale, trade-off and measurements.

## Test plan
- [x] OpenClaw `dreaming-startup-cleanup.test.ts`: 12/12 pass, including 2 new cases (disabled → neither scrub runs; re-enabled → leftovers reclaimed on the next start). Both new cases fail without the source change. oxlint clean.
- [x] All 87 v2026.8.1 patches apply from a clean reset with the new validator; the rebuilt runtime contains the guard (`dist/dreaming-*.js`)
- [x] LobsterAI `src/main/libs/openclawPatches/`: 29 files / 104 tests pass
- [x] Gateway CPU profile (4 agents, dreaming off), 1.8 s after ready: idle **160 ms → 851 ms**; the scrub and its SQLite checks (~560 ms) are gone
- [x] Full app, production renderer, 3 warm starts (on top of #3000): ready→handshake **1.16–1.21 s → 0.67–0.71 s** (1.01 s in one run that was slower throughout)
- Note: 5 cases in OpenClaw's `dreaming-phases.test.ts` (session-corpus redaction, concept-tag normalization) also fail without this patch; they're unrelated to the startup scrub.

prs.title: perf(openclaw): connect the gateway client sooner after startup
prs.body:
## Summary
From the gateway reporting ready to the desktop client's handshake took 2.3–2.7 s on Windows, in three serial main-process steps. This PR removes or moves each:

- **Load only the GatewayClient chunk.** `createGatewayClient` required `dist/plugin-sdk/gateway-runtime.js`, a barrel that pulls in 642 modules (7.1 MB) and blocked the main thread for 1.33 s. The new `openclawGatewayClientLoader` reads the barrel's `import { t as GatewayClient } from "../client-<hash>.js"` line and loads only that chunk (142 modules, 0.41 s). If the import can't be resolved or isn't the client class, it falls back to the barrel. Node's compile cache made both slower (1.8 s / 0.56 s), so it isn't used.
- **Prewarm while the gateway boots.** `OpenClawEngineManager` emits `GatewayLoadingConfig` once per process when the gateway logs `[gateway] loading configuration`. The matcher allows the ANSI color codes the gateway puts between the tag and the message. `main.ts` loads the client module at that point, while the main thread is idle.
- **No re-probe right after startup readiness.** `startGateway('channel-sync-ensure-ready')` probed `/startupz` on a gateway confirmed ready under a second earlier. That probe waited ~600 ms on the gateway's post-ready work. The existing-process path now trusts a startup readiness confirmed for the same process within 5 s, as long as the engine is still `running`. Other callers, older confirmations and other processes are probed as before.

## Test plan
- [x] New `openclawGatewayClientLoader.test.ts`: chunk resolution (aliased, unaliased, ignores look-alikes), barrel fallback when the chunk export is wrong, missing or fails to load, duck-typed exports, per-entry caching, retry after a failed load, and a check against the built runtime's real barrel (skipped when no runtime is present)
- [x] `openclawEngineManager.restart.test.ts`: trust only for the same process, within 5 s and while running; `GatewayLoadingConfig` fires once per process for real colored output
- [x] Related suites: 8 files / 476 tests pass; ESLint (CI rules) clean on touched files; `npm run build` (includes full `tsc`) passes
- [x] Full app, production renderer, 3 warm starts each: ready→handshake **2.32 / 2.68 s → 1.16 / 1.21 / 1.17 s**; the existing-process check takes 11 ms instead of 600 ms; `createGatewayClient` takes 5 ms (module prewarmed in ~430 ms during boot)
- Note: on this machine the remaining ~1.2 s is the gateway's own synchronous post-ready work, so the prewarm moves main-thread blocking off the critical path rather than shortening wall time yet. A companion patch skips the largest piece of that work (memory-core's dreaming scrub when dreaming is off).

prs.title: perf(openclaw): read Windows process start times natively
prs.body:
## Summary
- OpenClaw's gateway lock / pid-reuse checks read process start times via `readWindowsProcessStartTimeSync`, which spawned PowerShell (`Process.StartTime`, WMIC fallback). Each gateway start ran it 6 times synchronously (~2.5 s blocking the event loop), and `powershell -Command` spawns are a common EDR/AMSI trigger.
- New patch `zz-openclaw-windows-process-start-native.patch` reads the creation time first through koffi (already shipped on Windows) with `kernel32!GetProcessTimes`:
  - own pid: `GetCurrentProcess`, result cached; other pids: `OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION)`
  - missing pid / exited process → `null` (same as before)
  - koffi unavailable, access denied or call failure → existing PowerShell → WMIC fallback
  - FILETIME truncated to ms, identical to what `Date.parse` produced from PowerShell output, so existing lock records still match
- `apply-openclaw-patches.cjs` adds a strong validator for the patch; `v20260801UpgradeDecisions.test.ts` registers it; patch README documents rationale, fallback and removal condition.
- Patch tests: `readCurrentOpenClawPatch` now normalizes CRLF to LF. Patches are LF in the repo, but Git for Windows defaults to `core.autocrlf=true`, so `planCompletionCheck.test.ts`'s multi-line regex failed on every Windows checkout (CI runs on ubuntu only and never saw it).

## Test plan
- [x] OpenClaw `windows-process-start` / `gateway-lock` / `pid-alive` tests: 70 passed, 1 skipped; Windows-only test confirms native start time equals .NET `Process.StartTime` to the ms for own and parent process, exited child and invalid pid return null, no child process spawned
- [x] All 86 v2026.8.1 patches apply from a clean reset with the new validator; rebuilt runtime contains the change
- [x] `src/main/libs/openclawPatches/`: 29 files / 103 tests pass on Windows (including `planCompletionCheck.test.ts`)
- [x] Full-app E2E (warm): PowerShell spawns 6 → 0, gateway spawn→ready 18.93 → 16.83 s, main process sees ready 23.35 → 21.56 s, client handshake 26.93 → 24.55 s
- [x] Lock contention: second gateway on the same state dir detects the live owner and refuses in 2.2 s (no PowerShell/WMIC); owner stays healthy
- [x] Crash recovery, full app: gateway hard-killed 10 s after ready → LobsterAI auto-restarts it, pre-spawn cleanup removes both stale locks (dead owner), new gateway ready, 0 PowerShell
- [x] Crash recovery, OpenClaw only (no LobsterAI cleanup): stale lock with a dead owner pid is reclaimed and the next gateway becomes ready
- [x] Pid reuse: stale lock pointing at a live unrelated process with a different start time is reclaimed via the native start-time check (LobsterAI's pid-only cleanup keeps such locks); gateway ready, 0 PowerShell

prs.title: fix(openclaw): load Windows plugins natively and cache plugin realpaths
prs.body:
## Problem

On Windows machines with 360 Total Security (common for Chinese users), gateway startup reached 170–250 s, pinned in synchronous fs metadata calls while loading plugins. With 360, each metadata call under `%APPDATA%` / `%LOCALAPPDATA%` costs about 1 ms (`lstat` ≈ 890 µs under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\LobsterAI` vs ≈ 8 µs in a dev folder).

## Root cause

On Windows, OpenClaw never loaded plugins natively:

- `loader-module-runtime.ts` passes `toSafeImportPath(modulePath)` to the plugin loader. On win32 that is a `file:///C:/...` URL, the form ESM `import()` needs.
- `tryNativeRequireJavaScriptModule` hands that URL to `require()`, which rejects it with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. The loader reads that as "target missing" and falls back to jiti with `tryNative: false`.
- So every plugin, including bundled `dist/extensions/*`, was Babel-transformed together with OpenClaw's whole SDK graph, and each import went through jiti's uncached `realpathSync`/`stat` resolver. That is where the ~138k `lstat` calls came from. macOS and Linux pass plain paths and load natively.
- The same URL also made `clearPluginModuleRequireCache`'s `require.resolve` fail silently, so URL-keyed modules were never evicted.

## Changes

Two new OpenClaw v2026.8.1 patches, each with a strong-patch validator in `scripts/apply-openclaw-patches.cjs`, a README section, and an entry in `v20260801UpgradeDecisions.test.ts`:

1. **`openclaw-windows-native-plugin-require.patch`**: converts `file:` URLs to paths before `require()` and `require.resolve()` in `native-module-require.ts`. The URL stays the cache key. Two new tests cover loading and evicting a module through a file URL.
2. **`openclaw-plugin-realpath-parent-cache.patch`**: `pluginCacheRealpathSync` and the installed-plugin index staleness checks cached realpaths by exact path only, so every new file still walked each path component. New `realpath-through-parent.ts` resolves a path as its parent's cached realpath plus its basename after one `lstat` (links and roots still go through `fs.realpathSync`). Cache lifetimes are unchanged. Two existing tests that counted `fs.realpathSync` calls to prove one lookup per path now count the `lstat` too.

This PR first carried a jiti resolver cache. With native loading fixed, jiti is no longer called at startup, so that patch was dropped.

## End-to-end measurements

360 machine. Full `npm run openclaw:runtime:win-x64` build with these patches, copied to `%LOCALAPPDATA%` so it sits on the slow path, gateway run by `LobsterAI.exe` as Node (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`). The baseline is the installed v2026.8.1 runtime (built 2026-10-30), with the same scratch config.

| | installed | built |
|---|---|---|
| `[plugins] loaded 7 plugin(s)` | 124.5 s | 16.0 s |
| HTTP listening | 129.8 s | 18.0 s |
| lstat (7 plugins) | 138,504 | 13,919 |
| All 16 allowed plugins enabled | 270.2 s | 44.7 s |
| jiti cache calls (16 plugins) | 6,508 | 0 |

- Same plugin list and the same `tools.catalog` plugin tools in both; no plugin load errors. lark, nim-channel and netease-bee load natively in the shipped layout.
- `/readyz` is ready with the default 7 plugins. With all 16 enabled it reports `internal` in both runtimes, because channels such as Email are not configured.
- A plugin hot reload applies and re-registers all plugins. A running gateway re-registers from the same module generation by design, so module eviction applies to restarts and CLI flows; the unit tests cover it.
- Patch 2 isolated, by reverting it in the loaded bundle: `lstat` 32,851 → 13,919, process start to plugins loaded 64–75 s → 50–51 s.

## Testing

- New and updated OpenClaw tests pass. Failures in neighbouring files (`plugin-module-loader-cache` path fixtures, one `discovery` case, `channel-entry-contract`, …) fail the same way without these patches on Windows. oxlint/oxfmt are clean; tsgo is clean apart from pre-existing errors in another patch's file.
- All 80 v2026.8.1 patches apply and pass strong validation.
- `v20260801UpgradeDecisions.test.ts` and `openclawReplayDiagnostics.test.ts` pass.
- Plugin staging during the runtime build now logs `failed to load` for openclaw-lark, nim-channel and netease-bee, because their host-peer `node_modules/openclaw` does not export `./plugin-sdk`. Packaging removes that peer, as on macOS where these plugins always load natively, and the e2e above loads them without errors.
- Not yet verified through an installed `dist:win` package.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): recover Windows gateway exits and repair startup
prs.body:
## Summary

Windows gateway restart and one-click repair can fail with `OpenClaw gateway process ... did not exit after SIGKILL` even when the process exits shortly afterward. This change waits for confirmed Windows process termination, and fixes two additional repair blockers found during installed-client acceptance: redirected state roots being rejected as outside the owned directory, and Doctor not receiving the gateway token.

## Related Issue

User-reported Windows gateway restart/repair failures from September 18; no linked GitHub issue.

## Changes Made

- Keep the 6-second graceful shutdown period and allow 30 seconds after forced termination on Windows. A read-only PID probe can confirm termination when Electron's exit notification is delayed; only `ESRCH` proves absence. Permission/query errors remain conservative, and termination still uses the existing ChildProcess handle.
- Validate native lock paths against the same canonical state root. Redirected/junction roots work, while aliases below the owned root and paths outside it remain blocked.
- Pass the persisted gateway token explicitly to Doctor's controlled repair environment, including before the first successful gateway startup.
- Cover delayed notifications, slow termination, permission failures, stale child handles, late close events after replacement, real SQLite lock release, root junctions, and repair token propagation.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing

Validation on September 21 after merging the latest target branch into this branch:

- [x] 173 tests passed across 11 gateway, engine-manager, lock, SQLite/repair and Doctor suites, including the real Electron repair test.
- [x] `npm run compile:electron` passed.
- [x] All 9 changed TypeScript files passed ESLint with `--report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0`.
- [x] `git diff --check` passed.

Installed-client acceptance completed on September 18 for the original fix commit `97735d448547b086fbdf129b842b593426c2d5f9`:

- Actually installed the official 2026.9.4 Windows package, then exercised full NSIS manual overwrite and in-app automatic upgrade to the local unsigned candidate.
- Drove the real packaged client through the Electron main-process Node Inspector and `webContents.executeJavaScript()`; no computer-use or keyboard/mouse control.
- Verified continued conversations, original message IDs/content, model configuration, memory/workspace file hashes, skill toggles, and complete one-click repair on both upgrade paths.
- Injected delayed native termination/exit notifications into the real gateway for the manual repair case, then verified the old late close did not invalidate its replacement. Automatic-path repair also passed without this injection.
- Used a local model fixture and candidate update feed. Resolved the test host's MSIX/native profile mismatch and reran the complete automatic upgrade against one shared physical test profile.
- Full production build and 47 Windows installer contract tests passed for that candidate.

The full installer acceptance is the September 18 run; September 21 reran the target-integration checks above, not a new installer acceptance run.

## Screenshots

Not applicable: no renderer/UI changes.

## Checklist

- [x] Self-reviewed the final diff for unrelated changes and retained upstream changes.
- [x] Changed-file style checks pass without warnings.
- [x] Added and updated regression coverage.
- [x] Documented process lifecycle, repair behavior and validation limits in this PR.

## Electron-Specific Changes

- [x] Changes to main process (`src/main/`): gateway stop confirmation and manual repair environment/path handling.
- No preload, IPC contract, window-management or renderer changes.
- State backup and replacement gateway startup remain gated on confirmed termination; no broad process-name killing is added.

## Additional Notes: target-branch overlap check

Fetched and audited `release/2026.9.21` at `71d1eac882c52c49f03ee776ce519d6ed2fdfa6f` on September 21. None of these three fixes is present there:

| Fix | Existing target behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Windows delayed-exit handling | 2-second forced-stop deadline; no native liveness probe |
| Redirected state-root ownership | Compares native lock paths against the original, noncanonical root |
| Doctor gateway authentication | Repair environment does not explicitly supply `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`; token creation remains private to the manager |

The target includes related Weixin plugin restart-loop/startup-block changes, daily-log discovery work, and [#2728](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2728), which isolates SQLite read-only worker results from stdout noise. These address different paths and are retained. The final diff remains 9 files, 224 insertions and 12 deletions, with the same stable patch ID as the September 18 fix (`0dfeebfd8ad4c9370448948d00e3a7c063dde6fd`).

prs.title: fix(openclaw): snapshot Chrome MCP process trees natively on Windows
prs.body:
## Summary
On Windows the browser tool could become permanently unavailable. The in-app browser (the default display mode) attaches through OpenClaw's `existing-session` Chrome MCP driver. Before trusting a session, OpenClaw proves which processes it owns by listing every process with `powershell.exe Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` under a **2 s timeout**. That list runs twice per attach and at least three times per close.

On ordinary Windows machines the list takes 1.65–2.3 s, and up to 3.1 s under load (measured: bare PowerShell startup is only ~0.33 s, the cost is the CIM module plus enumerating ~420 processes). So most attaches failed with `Chrome MCP process inspection failed`. Our `openclaw-chrome-mcp-process-recovery.patch` then kept the session as `uncertain`, and every later browser command re-ran the same list first and failed the same way. Only a gateway restart recovered it.

This PR replaces the PowerShell list with a native Windows process snapshot (12–19 ms) and keeps PowerShell only as a fallback with a 10 s timeout.

## Related Issue
User feedback: browser tool permanently unavailable on Windows; the precheck enumerates `Win32_Process` through PowerShell with a hard 2000 ms timeout.

Upstream status: still unfixed on OpenClaw `main` and v2026.11.1 (same PowerShell list, same 2 s timeout), and no upstream issue or PR covers it. Upstream fixed the same class of bug in update repair (openclaw/openclaw#183238) via `@openclaw/proc-safe` (openclaw/openclaw#168942), which also removed koffi. When we upgrade past v2026.10.10, this patch should be rewritten on `proc-safe`'s `listProcesses()`.

## Changes Made
- New version-scoped patch `scripts/patches/v2026.8.1/openclaw-chrome-mcp-windows-native-snapshot.patch`, applied after `openclaw-chrome-mcp-process-recovery.patch`:
  - New `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-mcp-windows-processes.ts` reads the process table through koffi (`CreateToolhelp32Snapshot`, `OpenProcess`, `GetProcessTimes`, `QueryFullProcessImageNameW`). Each row's identity is `win32:<creation FILETIME ticks>|<image path>`. Exited and unreadable rows are dropped. A child is detached from a parent pid that now belongs to a younger process, so a recycled pid cannot pull an unrelated tree into `taskkill /t`.
  - The identity source is fixed per gateway run. PowerShell is used only if koffi cannot load or the first native read fails. A native failure after native rows were issued throws instead of switching sources, because mixing identity formats would make live owned processes look exited and skip their cleanup.
  - `chrome-mcp-process.ts` tries the native reader first on Windows; the PowerShell fallback timeout goes from 2 s to 10 s (two attach-time lists still fit the 30 s handshake). macOS `ps` keeps 2 s.
  - Unit tests, a Windows-only real-kernel32 test, and a Windows e2e (`chrome-mcp-windows-processes.e2e.test.ts`).
- `scripts/apply-openclaw-patches.cjs`: strong validator for the new patch.
- `scripts/patches/v2026.8.1/README.md`: cause, measurements, design, verification, and removal condition.
- `src/main/libs/openclawPatches/v20260801UpgradeDecisions.test.ts`: adds the patch to the reviewed set and checks its key lines.

koffi is already kept (real loader, not stubbed) in Windows runtimes for `openclaw-windows-private-directory-native.patch`; the bundled browser chunk resolves it through `createRequire`, the same way it loads `playwright-core`.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [ ] Documentation update
- [x] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

**OpenClaw checkout (Windows 11):**
- 125 tests pass across `chrome-mcp-windows-processes.test.ts`, `chrome-mcp.test.ts`, `server-context.tab-ownership.test.ts`, `server-context.list-profiles.test.ts`. The Windows-only test reads this process, a spawned child, and the child's exit through real kernel32.
- E2E (`--config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts`) with a real `.cmd` launcher → stdio MCP server → long-lived grandchild, and 2.5 s injected into every PowerShell list:
  - Native path: 5 attach/list/close rounds, attach 0.40–0.52 s, close 1.0–1.8 s, **zero PowerShell**, one `taskkill` per root, whole tree gone after each close.
  - Forced PowerShell fallback: every list took 4.7–5.2 s (all over the old 2 s limit) and attach and cleanup still succeeded.
  - Mutation check: with the fallback timeout set back to 2 s, the e2e fails with exactly the reported `Command timed out after 2000 milliseconds … Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`.
- oxlint clean on changed files; tsgo reports no errors in the browser extension or its tests (the remaining tsgo errors pre-exist in files changed by other patches).
- All 92 v2026.8.1 patches apply cleanly to a fresh v2026.8.1 worktree, and the result matches the tested files byte for byte.

prs.title: fix(web-search): run node without the env found on PATH
prs.body:
## Summary
uv's installer adds `~/.local/bin/env`, a sh script meant to be sourced that ignores its arguments and exits 0. When `~/.local/bin` is ahead of `/usr/bin` on PATH, every `env PREFIX node ...` call in the web-search scripts silently runs nothing:

- On Windows bash (Node fetch path), the health check always comes back empty. `search.sh` reports "Bridge Server still unavailable after start" while `/api/health` is healthy.
- On every platform, `build_search_payload` returns an empty payload (the POST falls back to `{}`), `verify_iconv_runtime` always passes, and `nohup env … node server` never starts the server.

Repro: `echo 'console.log(1)' | env node -` prints nothing, while `node -` prints `1`. `command env` does not help, because it still resolves `env` on PATH.

## Related Issue
None. Found during an end-to-end install test on Windows.

## Changes Made
- `search.sh` / `start-server.sh`: add `run_http_node` / `run_node`, which exec the runtime directly and export `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` in a subshell for the Electron case. These replace the foreground `env` calls.
- `start-server.sh`: the background launch exports the prefix in place before `nohup`. A function's subshell would make `$!` a wrapper instead of the server process.
- Test: a no-op `env` ahead on PATH must not make a broken iconv-lite look healthy.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

Tested on Windows Git Bash (bash 5), with the real uv shim first on PATH:
- `bash SKILLs/web-search/scripts/search.sh "test" 1` returns results (before: exit 1, "still unavailable").
- Electron path, with node hidden and a fake Electron that requires `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`: health check, payload and `nohup` launch all work, and the variable does not leak into the caller.
- The `start-server.sh` tests are skipped on win32, so I ran them unskipped under Git Bash: 7/7 pass. With the original script, the new test and the existing "iconv-lite … reinstalled" test both fail on this machine.
- The existing win32 failure "copying resets mtimes …" also fails on the base branch. It is unrelated.
- Not run on macOS. The constructs used are bash 3.2 compatible, and the scripts do not use `set -u`.

prs.title: fix(web-search): keep bundled dist usable after copying and stop npm repairs that cannot work
prs.body:
## Summary
In packaged builds, the bundled `web-search` skill was judged "dist outdated" every time it was copied. Startup then ran `npm install` + `npm run build`, which can never succeed in a packaged copy, so the Web Search bridge server did not start. This PR fixes that check, removes npm repair paths that can't help packaged copies, and stops `WEB_SEARCH_FORCE_REPAIR` from deleting a healthy `iconv-lite`.

Evidence from a real packaged build (macOS, 2026.10.30), in `main-2026-11-02.log`:
```
[SkillServices] Repaired web-search runtime from bundled resources
[SkillServices] Installing/reparing web-search dependencies...
[SkillServices] Compiling web-search TypeScript...
[error] [SkillServices] Failed to start Web Search service: Error: Command failed: npm run build
```

Root causes:
- Copying resets mtimes: packaging (`prepareMacSkills` `fs.cpSync`, electron-builder), `syncBundledSkillsToUserData` and `repairWebSearchRuntimeFromBundled` all copy without preserving them. `readdir` order puts `dist/` before `server/`, so the `.ts` sources always end up newer than `dist/server/index.js`. The shipped `.app` bundle already has this order (~0.19 s), so preserving mtimes in `cpRecursiveSync` would not fix it.
- `npm run build` cannot work in a packaged copy: `electron-builder.json` filters `!**/tsconfig.json` out of `SKILLs`, so `tsc` only prints its help text and fails. Since d4ab92fa, Mac builds also no longer ship `typescript`.

## Related Issue
N/A

## Changes Made
- `skillServices.ts`: new `canRebuildWebSearchDist()` (not packaged, and `tsconfig.json` present). Source mtimes are compared only when it is true. `ensureWebSearchRuntimeReady` now fails fast with a clear error when a packaged copy is still unhealthy after the bundle restore. It no longer falls back to a blocking `execSync` npm install/build on the main process, and no longer runs npm inside `Resources` when the bundle itself is the only copy.
- `start-server.sh`:
  - same staleness rule (`can_rebuild_server`);
  - the build step moved into `ensure_server_build()`, which asks the user to restart LobsterAI instead of running npm in a packaged copy;
  - dependency checks moved into `ensure_dependencies()`;
  - `WEB_SEARCH_FORCE_REPAIR` no longer reinstalls `iconv-lite` unconditionally (that needed npm just to restart, and offline it deleted a healthy package);
  - `verify_iconv_runtime` now decodes once, so missing encodings (the `Cannot find module …encodings` errors that `search.sh` reacts to) are actually detected.
- web-search skill bumped to `1.0.3`, so existing installs get a clean copy with the new `start-server.sh`.
- Dev behavior is unchanged: a source checkout (with `tsconfig.json`) still runs install + build when sources change or `dist` is missing.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [ ] Manual testing performed (not yet run in a packaged app)

Details:
- New `src/main/skills/skillServices.webSearchDist.test.ts` (14 tests). It covers copying through `cpRecursiveSync`, the packaged startup/repair path (no `execSync`), dev rebuild, the legacy dist, and the `start-server.sh` build and dependency steps with a fake npm. Against the unfixed code, the copy, packaged and shell cases fail.
- `skillManager.bundledSync.test.ts`: a newer bundled web-search version clean-copies the skill and keeps `.env`.
- `npm test -- skill`: 280/280. ESLint (CI rules) is clean on the touched TS files. `npm run compile:electron` passes. `bash -n` passes on the script.
- Ran the old and new shell staleness checks read-only on the real installed `.app` bundle and userData copy: old = outdated, new = fresh.

- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

prs.title: fix(media): let visible subagents generate images
prs.body:
## Problem

When the main agent delegates image work with `sessions_spawn` (visible mode), the child runs under `agent:<id>:dashboard:<uuid>`. Every `lobsterai_image_generate` call from that child failed with `Media tool has no authenticated run context`, so no task was created. Main-session generation was unaffected.

## Root causes (stacked)

1. **Hooks dropped by OpenClaw.** `lobster-media-generation` is a non-bundled plugin, and OpenClaw v2026.8.1 blocks its `before_model_resolve` / `agent_end` typed hooks unless `hooks.allowConversationAccess` is set. The run owner was never captured.
2. **Per-registration run table.** OpenClaw calls `register()` once per plugin registry in the gateway process. The hook and tool `execute` could use different `MediaRunContexts` instances, so a call bound in `before_tool_call` was not found in `execute`. Desktop keys hid this because unbound desktop calls are allowed.
3. **No Cowork row for the child.** Dashboard children only have a `subagent_runs` row, so main could not resolve a turn account scope and returned `MEDIA_ACCOUNT_CHANGED`.
4. **No local save.** For the same reason, generated files were not persisted, and the child got no file path.

## Changes

- `openclawConfigSync.ts`: grant `hooks.allowConversationAccess: true` to the media plugin entry.
- `lobster-media-generation/runContext.ts`, `index.ts`: one `MediaRunContexts` per process (`globalThis` + `Symbol.for`); a reload only replaces the bridge sender.
- `openclawLocalSessionResolver.ts`: `resolveSubagentRequesterCoworkSessionId()` maps a spawned child key to its requester Cowork session via `subagent_runs`.
- `main.ts` (media callback): when the child has no Cowork session, use the requester session for account scope, media selection, and saving image/video files into the requester working directory. UI events, status cards and durable task tracking still use the child's own session.

## Electron / OpenClaw notes

- Changes generated `openclaw.json` (plugin hook grant), so the gateway restarts once after upgrade.
- Desktop sessions, `agent:<id>:subagent:` children, IM and cron behavior is unchanged when the session already maps to a Cowork row. IM/cron native runs were likely also affected by cause 2 and should now bind correctly (not separately tested).

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/main/libs/openclawLocalSessionResolver.test.ts tests/openclaw-extensions/lobster-media-generation src/main/libs/openclawConfigSync.runtime.test.ts src/main/libs/lobsterMediaStatusPolling.test.ts`: 201 passed (re-run on the current release base: 198 passed, 3 skipped without the local vendor runtime).
- ESLint on touched files with `--max-warnings 0`: clean. `npm run compile:electron`: passes.
- Verified in `npm run electron:dev`: a visible subagent generated an image in one call, the status result linked a file saved in the requester working directory, and the parent reported it. No hook blocks or `MEDIA_ACCOUNT_CHANGED` in gateway/main logs.

Supersedes #2993, which accidentally included the #2991 commit.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): keep sessions_spawn children off model-picked models
prs.body:
## Summary

Users reported subagents sometimes running on expensive models (e.g. Kimi) instead of the main agent's model.

Root cause in OpenClaw v2026.8.1:
- `sessions_spawn` accepts any `model` the LLM passes, and an explicit value always wins (upstream keeps this by design: openclaw/openclaw#90763, openclaw/openclaw#89522 closed as not planned).
- Same-agent children fall back to the agent's configured model, not the session's active model (`modelSelectionScope: 'session'` keeps session switches local). Upstream fixed only this part in v2026.9.5 (openclaw/openclaw#149036).

## Change

`lobster-model-routing` now rewrites the `sessions_spawn` model in `before_tool_call`:
- Same-agent spawn → the requesting run's selected model (recorded in `before_model_resolve`, before virtual presets resolve, so `yd-fast` children keep the preset).
- Cross-agent spawn → `'default'`, i.e. the target agent's own configured model.
- Unknown requester model → `'default'` (previous 8.1 behavior); ACP spawns untouched.
- Each rewrite logs `[lobster-model-routing] sessions_spawn model A -> B`.

No OpenClaw patch, IPC, storage, or config sync change. Takes effect after the gateway reloads the extension.

## Testing

- `npm test`: 761 files passed.
- ESLint (CI rules) on changed files: clean.
- E2E on a dev gateway: session pinned to `deepseek-flash-YoudaoInner`, LLM told to spawn with `kimi-k3.1-pro-YoudaoInner`:
  - self spawn → ran on `deepseek-flash-YoudaoInner`
  - cross-agent spawn → ran on target agent's `yd-fast`
  - zero Kimi requests in gateway logs.

prs.title: fix(desktop-companion): prevent unintended selection answer cancellation
prs.body:
## Summary

Selection quick answers use independent HTTP requests, but their availability was tied to the OpenClaw gateway. Restarting the gateway could therefore hide an active answer card and cancel its request.

A rapid second click on **Regenerate** could also cancel the answer: the first click removed the previous answer and shrank the window, leaving the original button position outside the card.

## Changes Made

- Keep selection tools available during gateway transitions, with foreground monitoring active while selection remains available. Continue honoring the companion switch, selection preference, snooze, and screenshot state.
- Preserve the card's current minimum height when regenerating, bounded by the available maximum height. Reset it when the selection or action changes, or the card closes, so the second click stays inside the card.
- Add regression coverage for gateway transitions, selection before gateway readiness, foreground changes, and disabling selection.

## Electron-Specific Changes

Updates selection availability and foreground monitoring in the main process, and answer-card sizing in the renderer. Agent task entry retains its gateway readiness checks; clicks outside the card still dismiss it.

## Summary

技能文件的重复通知会触发配置同步，而 OpenClaw 迁移后的 `modelPolicy` 与 LobsterAI 重建的配置不一致，会反复改写配置；配置 RPC 超时又可能把已经生效的配置送入重启兜底。本次稳定策略往返、过滤无效文件变化，并在超时后确认当前配置是否已生效，减少用户遇到的网关反复重启。

## Related Issue

无对应 GitHub Issue；来自 9.20 客户端反复重启问题排查。

## Changes Made

- 保留 `modelPolicy` 和迁移标记，随模型增删更新托管 allowlist，同时保留用户显式策略。配置比较忽略对象键顺序和写入来源信息，保留数组顺序及迁移语义。

prs.title: fix(cowork): keep model selection in scheduled-task conversations
prs.body:
## Problem
On a scheduled-task result page, switching the model appeared to fail: the selector snapped back to 快速 and the next manual reply still used the agent default. The model-change divider also showed the raw id `yd-fast`.

## Cause
Channel polling resolves cron rows (`agent:main:cron:<jobId>[:run:…]`) to the scheduled-task conversation and ran `syncChannelSessionModelOverride` on them. The cron row has no explicit override and matches the agent default, so the local `modelOverride` was cleared right after every switch (`[ChannelSync] synced channel session model override … Model agent/default.`). The channel model sync was meant for IM `/model` switches only.

The divider recorded the agent default `lobsterai-server/yd-fast` without a preset id, so it fell back to the bare model id.

## Changes
- `openclawRuntimeAdapter.ts`: skip cron keys in the channel model sync; manual replies run on the managed key, and the local override owns them.
- `sessionModelChange.ts`: treat `yd-fast` / `yd-ultra` refs as their presets when recording a change (also avoids a "快速 → 快速" notice).
- `ModelChangeDivider.tsx`: same fallback for notices already stored.

## Electron behavior
Main process only changes when the polled OpenClaw cron rows are written to local session state; no IPC, storage schema, or config/restart changes.

## Verification
- New regression test (fails without the guard) plus `sessionModelChange.test.ts`
- `npm test` passes, touched files lint clean, `npm run compile:electron` passes
- Tested manually in the app

prs.title: fix(packaging): stop shipping source maps, tsc output and unused runtime files
prs.body:
## Summary

The installer carries a lot of files the app never loads. This PR removes the ones that can be dropped without changing any dependency or runtime behavior. The largest is every renderer and main-process source map, which was shipped inside `app.asar`.

Root cause for the source maps: `electron-builder.json` lists `"!**/*.map"` at the top level of `files`, but that pattern only applies to the app-root matcher. The `dist` and `dist-electron` FileSets (`from`/`to`/`filter`) use only their own `filter: ["**/*"]`, so all `.map` files were packaged. The 2026.9.17 macOS build had 85 MB of maps in `app.asar`; the current build would ship about 160 MB.

## Changes

- **`electron-builder.json`**
  - `dist` and `dist-electron` FileSets exclude `**/*.map`.
  - `dist-electron` also excludes the tsc-emitted subtrees (`common`, `main`, `renderer`, `scheduledTask`, `shared`). `npm run compile:electron` emits them, but the app runs the Vite bundle `dist-electron/main.js` and nothing loads them.
  - `win.electronLanguages: ["en-US", "zh-CN", "zh-TW"]` drops the other Chromium `locales/*.pak` on Windows.
- **`scripts/prune-openclaw-runtime.cjs`**: new `RUNTIME_UNUSED_PATHS` step.
  - Removes `tree-sitter-bash/src` and `tree-sitter-bash/prebuilds`. OpenClaw only loads `tree-sitter-bash.wasm` through `web-tree-sitter`.
  - Removes the type-only packages `@cloudflare/workers-types` and `bun-types` when present.
- **`src/renderer/assets/startup-credit-poster.png`**: downscaled from 5884×4136 to 1296×911 (5.9 MB → 1.4 MB), sRGB profile kept. It renders at most 432px wide, so 1296px still covers 3× displays.

## Size impact (uncompressed)

| Item | Removed |
|---|---|
| Source maps in `app.asar` | ~160 MB (current build) |
| tsc output tree in `dist-electron` | ~5–9 MB |
| Windows Chromium locales | ~40 MB (estimate, not measured on Windows) |
| `tree-sitter-bash` sources/prebuilds | 18 MB |
| Startup poster | 4.5 MB |

Source maps compress well, so the reduction in the dmg/installer is smaller than these numbers.

## Electron-specific notes

- **Packaging only.** No IPC, preload, storage or OpenClaw config changes.
- **Windows locales**: `app.getLocale()` reports `en-US` when the system locale's `.pak` is missing. First-run i18n only picks Chinese for `zh-CN` (`inferLanguageFromLocale`), so keeping `zh-CN` (and `zh-TW`) preserves the current language choice. A test guards that `zh-CN` stays in the list.
- **macOS locales are intentionally unchanged.** electron-builder only trims `Contents/Resources/*.lproj` on macOS, and those directories are empty. The 47 MB of Chromium locales live inside `Electron Framework.framework`, so `electronLanguages` would save nothing there and would only change `app.getLocale()`.
- **Runtime prune**: `buildScriptHash` changes, so the next `electron:dev:openclaw` may rebuild the runtime.

## Not included

- `typescript` in `SKILLs/web-search/node_modules` (Windows) stays. The runtime recompiles the skill when it thinks `dist` is stale, so removing it is not safe yet. That staleness check is being fixed separately.
- Renderer-only libraries packaged under `app.asar/node_modules` (about 370 MB in the current build, e.g. `@univerjs/*`, `mermaid`, `echarts`, `pdfjs-dist`) are left for a follow-up PR. The main process is bundled and does not require them, but `app.asar/node_modules` is on `NODE_PATH` for agent scripts, so this needs its own smoke test.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run` on `tests/pruneOpenClawRuntime.test.ts`, `tests/electronBuilderAppFiles.test.ts`, `tests/skillMacDependencies.test.ts`, `tests/windowsInstallerContract.test.ts`, `tests/openclawRuntimePackaging.test.ts`, `tests/openclawWindowsPayload.test.ts` and `tests/openclawBundleAssets.test.ts`: 131 passed.
- New `tests/electronBuilderAppFiles.test.ts` runs electron-builder's own file matchers on a fixture. With the old filters the same check ships `.map` files and the tsc tree.
- `npx eslint --ext ts,tsx --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0` on the touched test files: clean.
- Ran `npm run openclaw:prune` on the local mac-arm64 runtime: 18 MB freed. `web-tree-sitter` still loads `tree-sitter-bash.wasm` and parses `ls -la | grep foo && echo ok` without errors.
- Unsigned `electron-builder --mac --arm64 --dir` build: `app.asar` has 0 `.map` files and no tsc subtrees, and `dist-electron/main.js`, `dist-electron/preload.js` and `dist/index.html` are present.
- Not done: launching the packaged app, and a Windows build.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): harden startup recovery and Feishu secret routing
prs.body:
修复 9.18 排查中可复现的启动阻塞与飞书凭据错位，目标分支为 `release/2026.9.18`。schema v1 初始化修复已在基线 `5975a9e33` 中，本 PR 不重复实现。

## 变更

- **Windows 网关生命周期**：Electron 主进程异常退出、IPC 断开后，网关子进程执行现有中断关闭流程；启动期间暂存关闭请求，并限制失去父进程的子进程存活时间。保持已有活跃 owner / Unknown owner 保护，不强杀外部进程、不主动删锁。
- **升级启动兼容**：在旧会话迁移 CLI 校验前，将明确退役的 reload `hot` / `restart` 转为 `hybrid`，仅移除上游明确退役的两个 reload timer；通过原始字节备份和 canonical writer 保留其他配置。marketplace source clone 失败携带类型码，改为可重试提示；仍验证/隔离缺失 payload，未知 owner、插件安全校验失败及用户授权拒绝仍阻塞。auth 迁移失败仅记录字段路径，不记录配置值。
- **飞书多账号凭据**：配置生成与环境密钥导出使用同一账号筛选规则，避免前一个账号缺少 appId/appSecret 时，后一个账号密钥错位；补充默认和显式 Agent 路由及 canonical 配置往返覆盖。

原报告的 PID Unknown 具体成因、最终未知 auth 配置、历史飞书缺失 owner 成因并未全部还原，修复范围限于上述已证实路径。

## 验证

- 网关相关测试 28 通过；实际 SQLite lease 的 IPC 断开红绿验证通过。
- 使用实际 bundled runtime 的 startup/auth helper 两套测试 48 通过；飞书多账号 SDK/canonical writer/Doctor 往返测试通过；改动 TypeScript 的 CI 风格 ESLint 通过。
- 上游 marketplace/update：196 通过、3 跳过；repair 分类与安全边界定向测试 5 通过。post-core 34 通过、1 个原有 Windows 路径格式断言失败；完整 missing-install suite 有原有 Windows 临时目录 EPERM，因此不宣称全量测试通过。
- 44 个版本补丁从 pinned tag 重新应用成功；Electron 编译、renderer/runtime 构建、NSIS 打包通过，installer gate 47 通过。验收包为本地未签名的 `2026.9.18-acceptance.1`，未发布。
- 真实官网 9.4 → 客户端手动检查/下载/重启安装 → 修复版：首启、旧数据核心指纹、冷启动、继续旧会话写文件通过。
- 真实主进程异常终止后，网关 846 ms 退出（code 0）；再次冷启动自行回收旧 owner 锁并在约 119 s 进入 running。独立 MCP 残留另记并精确处理，没有人工删除 gateway 锁。
- 真实客户端命中受控 marketplace clone 故障，确认 clone failed 和 repair 提示，并结合对应源码确认进入缺失 payload 隔离分支；44.336 s 进入 running，随后真实任务完成、核心数据比较无差异。
- 飞书通过 UI 绑定指定 Agent，用户真实消息命中该 Agent 并收到回复。

- CI 最新提交：4,982 项通过、117 项跳过；lint、主进程/renderer 构建及安全检查通过，build-skills 按路径跳过。
- 真实官网 9.4（reload restart）自动检查/下载（source=auto）→ UI 重启安装 → NSIS → 修复版首启通过；配置保留原始备份并迁移为 hybrid，schema 1→15，首启及冷启动数据比较无丢失。异常退出后 gateway 317 ms 退出，随后冷启动能继续旧会话并实际生成验收文件。

用户已合并本 PR，QA 同步人工验收 release；合并树与已通过 CI 的 head 文件内容一致。**本机所列客户端验收已全部完成：用户完整数据归还、最终冷启动、原飞书绑定保留均通过；归还后用户再次发送真实消息，确认指定 Agent 回复正确。** 端侧实际环境为 Windows x64，单个真实飞书账号绑定指定 Agent；多账号凭据矩阵由代码测试覆盖。未发现需要追加产品修复的问题。此结论不替代 QA 的跨平台发版验收。

prs.title: fix(openclaw): compact preset sessions against their selected context window
prs.body:
## Problem

A user reported that in a 快速 (`yd-fast`) chat, after pasting a ~400k-token document with "请只回复：收到。" and then asking about the weather, the context ring stayed at 100%, usage kept growing past the 400k limit, and auto-compaction never ran.

The session selects a 400k window, but the real model behind it (e.g. `deepseek-flash`) accepts 1M, so every request succeeds and overflow recovery never starts. In embedded runs the session's own threshold compaction is disabled (`getCompactionSettings().enabled === false`), so preflight compaction (`runSessionCompactionIfNeeded`) is the only automatic trigger. It resolved the window from provider/model only and used the native 1M window, so it compacted at 980k while the run, the session row and the UI used 400k.

The same mismatch affects:
- the `model_context_bytes` trigger added in #2988: it watched 6.4 MB while a 400k run hydrates at most 3.2 MB;
- 8 server models that declare no native window (kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.5, qwen3.6-plus, qwen3.5-plus, MiniMax-M2.7, glm-5.1, glm-5, doubao-seed-2-0-mini). The run used 400k, but preflight fell back to the 200k default and compacted early, at about 45%.

## Change

One version-scoped OpenClaw patch, `openclaw-session-window-preflight-compaction.patch`. No LobsterAI runtime code changes.

- `resolveMemoryFlushContextWindowTokens` takes the session's `SessionEntry.contextWindow` selection and resolves it from the configured model's `contextWindows` with the run's rule: never exceed a known native window, and use the selection when the model declares none. An unknown option keeps the native value.
- Both preflight callers (`runSessionCompactionIfNeeded`, `runMemoryFlushIfNeeded`) pass the selection.
- Preflight compaction uses the manual planner, which already falls back to the smallest valid tail. A single oversized turn is therefore summarized instead of being skipped as "too small".
- Also adds a strong validator in `apply-openclaw-patches.cjs`, registers the patch in `v20260801UpgradeDecisions.test.ts`, and documents it in the patch README.

## Verification

- New OpenClaw tests: preflight uses the selected window, keeps the native window for unknown or larger options, and uses the selection when no native window is declared. The new preflight integration case fails on the old code.
- The full 89-patch series applies to a clean v2026.8.1 checkout with strong validation passing. `memory-flush.test.ts` 19/19 and `agent-runner-memory.test.ts` 107/107 pass, and LobsterAI patch tests 106/106 pass. Core typecheck shows only the existing `managed-image-replay.ts` errors; oxfmt, oxlint and ESLint are clean.
- All 37 server models from a real local config × `yd-fast` / `yd-ultra` / no selection (111 cases): preflight window equals the embedded run budget.
- Isolated gateway with a mock 1M-window model, three turns (≈410k-token paste, then two short questions):

| Runtime / model class | Turn 1 | Turn 2 | Turn 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before (11-05 runtime) | 110% | 110%, no compaction | 110% |
| After, native 1M | 110% | **8%**, compacted | 8% |
| After, no native window | 110% | **8%**, compacted | 8% |
| After, native 262k | 167% | **11%**, compacted | 11% |

Turn 1 still ends above 100%, because nothing older exists to compact before a single oversized prompt is sent. Compaction runs at the next preflight.

Not covered: real-model in-app runs (needs account credentials and credits), and the overflow-error path for a native window below the paste size (the mock never returns context overflow).

## Behavior notes

OpenClaw runtime change only. 快速/旗舰 sessions now compact around 380k instead of 980k. Models without a declared native window compact at 380k instead of 180k. Ordinary model sessions (no `contextWindow` selection) are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): apply sign-out config shrink without a gateway restart
prs.body:
## Problem

When a user signs out, LobsterAI re-renders `openclaw.json` without the `lobsterai-server` plan catalog (`models`), which is most of the file (e.g. 48 KB → 19 KB). OpenClaw treats a >50% shrink as a clobber:

1. `config.apply` is rejected (`size-drop:` in `io.write-safety.ts`) and LobsterAI retries.
2. LobsterAI falls back to a deferred gateway restart (`config-delivery-fallback:media-entitlement-changed`).
3. The restarted gateway "restores" the same bytes from `.bak` (`size-drop-vs-last-good:`).

Each sign-out costs a 12–60 s gateway restart on Windows. On the reporting machine one cost 58.5 s, with `.rejected.*` / `.clobbered.*` files on 10-30, 11-04 and 11-05.

`config.apply` has no way to pass the size-drop allowance. Keeping a stale plan catalog after sign-out would also have to keep the agent model allowlist, model-compat and thinking profiles consistent, so it was rejected as a contorted workaround. Per the patch policy, this adds a small version-scoped OpenClaw patch.

## Changes

**OpenClaw patch** `scripts/patches/v2026.8.1/openclaw-config-apply-size-drop-allowance.patch` (documented in the patch README):
- `config.apply` accepts an optional boolean `allowConfigSizeDrop`, mapped to the existing `ConfigWriteOptions.allowConfigSizeDrop`. It waives only the size check: `gateway-mode-removed` and unreadable-baseline writes are still rejected. Writers that omit it (Control UI, CLI, doctor, agents) keep the full guard.
- Read-time recovery skips a `.bak` that is byte-identical to the current file. Restoring it only rewrote the same bytes and recorded a false clobber. Clobbers by other writers still restore, because OpenClaw's own writes rotate the previous file into `.bak`. This covers sign-outs persisted while the gateway is stopped.

**LobsterAI** (`src/main/libs/openclawConfigSizeDrop.ts`, `openclawConfigDelivery.ts`):
- Claims the waiver only when the shrink would trip the guard and everything outside `models` still passes it. Large drops elsewhere, including from LobsterAI bugs, keep OpenClaw's protection.
- Measures the gateway's current config from `config.get` `raw`, or from `parsed` when the gateway withholds `raw`. It does that whenever text redaction is unsafe, which LobsterAI's `${ENV}` refs always trigger.
- A gateway without the patch rejects the unknown param. LobsterAI detects that and falls back to the previous restart path instead of treating the config as invalid.

## Verification

- `npm test -- openclawConfig`: 368 passed. CI eslint on touched files clean. `npm run compile:electron` OK.
- OpenClaw: the full 89-patch series applies cleanly. `config.test.ts`, `io.observe-recovery.test.ts` and the gateway-protocol suites pass with 713 tests. 4 `config.openFile` cases fail on Windows with or without this patch (POSIX path expectations). tsgo core reports no errors in touched files.
- Runtime rebuilt from the patched source. End-to-end against real gateway processes, a temp OpenClaw home and a real LobsterAI-rendered config (44.8 KB → 15.3 KB): **23/23**.
  - Live sign-out: waiver claimed, applied, no restart, no `.rejected` file.
  - Restart after sign-out: no auto-restore.
  - Sign-in works.
  - Stopped-gateway sign-out: no restore or clobber; one observe warning, then clean.
  - An unpatched-runtime control reproduces the old auto-restore and exercises the compat fallback.
  - The first E2E run is what caught the `raw: null` case (commit 2).
- Manual desktop test: sign-out at 01:46:19 logged `claiming the size-drop waiver ... 39826->17250 bytes` and `mode=applied` in 826 ms. No `Config write rejected`, no fallback restart, no new `.rejected`/`.clobbered` files.

## Notes

- After the accepted write, OpenClaw still logs one `Config observe anomaly (size-drop-vs-last-good)` line before it promotes the new last-known-good. It restores nothing.
- A `HARD RESTART reason=server-models-updated` during sign-in, in the same manual session, is the existing sign-in path and is unrelated to this change.
- The runtime build fingerprint includes the new patch, so `npm run electron:dev:openclaw` and packaging rebuild the runtime.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): skip integrity checks for cleanly closed agent databases
prs.body:
## Summary

Startup on large profiles was slow because OpenClaw v2026.8.1 runs a whole-file `PRAGMA integrity_check` on every physical agent database open. Quits never closed the gateway cleanly, which made this worse.

- **Clean-close seal (OpenClaw patch).** `openclaw-agent-db-clean-close-seal.patch` backports the upstream v2026.10.10 seal. A database closed cleanly writes `<db>.seal` (dev/inode/birthtime/size/mtimeNs, schema identity, last full-check time, checksum). The next open consumes the seal and skips the whole-file pass while the file is unchanged, no WAL/journal is pending and the last full check is under 7 days old. Anything else falls back to the full check: a crash, a SIGKILL, a modified file, a pending migration or a schema change. Details are in `scripts/patches/v2026.8.1/README.md`.
- **Weixin long-poll abort (plugin patch).** In Weixin plugin 2.4.3 the 35 s `getUpdates` long-poll ignored the channel abort signal. OpenClaw stops channels one by one, so every quit hit LobsterAI's 6 s stop grace and ended in SIGKILL, and no seal was ever written. The patch backports the fix from plugin 2.4.10.
- **Gateway stop grace 6 s → 8 s.** A healthy shutdown measured 5.2–6.2 s; 3.8 s of that is upstream plugin host registry cleanup. 8 s keeps grace plus the SIGKILL exit inside the 10 s `APP_CLEANUP_WATCHDOG_MS`.

## Measurements (macOS, 616 MB main agent DB, 25 agents)

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway ready | 19.2 s | 14.6–16.3 s |
| `startup.maintenance` | 6.5 s | 2.6–3.0 s |
| Main agent DB open | 2.1 s | 51 ms |
| Quit | SIGKILL after 6 s | clean exit (code 0) in 5.2–6.2 s |

The first start after upgrading has no seals yet, so it still runs the full checks.

## Electron-specific behavior

- OpenClaw runtime changes, so the runtime must be rebuilt together with this change.
- The gateway stop grace changes from 6 s to 8 s. This affects quit and hard restarts only when the gateway is slow to exit.
- New `<agent db>.seal` files appear under `userData/openclaw/state/agents/*/agent/`.

## Testing

- OpenClaw: 11 new tests (seal module and agent-db integration). 28 related test files (agent-db, SQLite, backup, snapshot, doctor, migrations) pass: 850 tests. No new oxlint or tsgo errors.
- LobsterAI: `npm test` passes 8321 tests; `npm run compile:electron` passes; ESLint is clean on the changed files.
- Manual: rebuilt the mac-arm64 runtime and ran start → quit → start cycles on the real profile. The logs confirmed seal reuse for all 25 agent databases, an immediate Weixin long-poll abort on stop, and clean gateway exits.

Drop the seal patch when the pinned OpenClaw reaches v2026.10.10.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): improve repair timeout handling and diagnostics
prs.body:
## Summary

一键修复加载完整 OpenClaw CLI 较慢时，配置校验可能在原有 60 秒超时后被终止，导致后续修复无法执行。为显式一键修复增加基于输出活动的有界等待，并保存命令退出诊断，支持慢命令完成并便于定位后续失败。

## Related Issue

无关联 GitHub issue。复用 #2732 已有的旧配置字段和旧安装路径修复逻辑。

## Changes Made

- 修复命令至少等待 5 分钟；stdout/stderr 输出可延长等待，连续静默 5 分钟或单条命令累计 15 分钟时请求终止。
- 请求终止后继续等待进程关闭回调，再结束当前修复步骤。
- 在本次修复备份目录的 `commands/command-*/` 保存 `result.json` 和 `output.log`，记录 PID、耗时、退出码、信号、超时原因及部分输出。
- 阶段异常保留原始 `cause`，超时提示提供中英文说明和诊断文件路径。

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Testing

- [x] 5 组相关 Vitest 测试共 52 项通过；更新异常因果断言后，17 项阶段测试再次通过。
- [x] `npm run compile:electron` 通过，5 个改动 TypeScript 文件的 CI 等价 ESLint 检查通过。
- [x] Windows Electron 实操：通过 renderer CDP 和 main inspector 驱动真实客户端，使用独立 profile。

在重建旧配置及失效安装路径的场景中，为真实 CLI 注入相同的 65 秒启动延迟：基线在约 60.17 秒被 SIGTERM 终止并显示修复失败；修改后两次校验分别约 85.19 秒、83.36 秒正常返回，Doctor 约 222.87 秒完成，完整修复及网关启动成功。随后验证真实模型回复，以及退出客户端、重新启动后的历史续聊；原配置快照逐字节一致，预置历史文件哈希保持不变。

相关测试命令：

```text
npm test -- openclawRepairProcess openclawCompatibilityRepair openclawRepairPreflight openclawConfigSelfHeal openclawStartupCompatibility --maxWorkers=1
```

## Checklist

- [x] 已完成改动自查，改动文件符合 lint 规则。
- [x] 已补充慢命令、静默超时、绝对上限、等待关闭、启动失败和诊断写入失败等测试。
- [x] 已完成 Electron 客户端实操验收。

## Electron-Specific Changes

- [x] Changes to main process (`src/main/`)

新 runner 用于显式一键修复中的校验、迁移、Doctor 和修复辅助命令。常规启动继续使用原 runner，现有退出码、阶段结果及最终网关状态仍决定修复结果。每条修复命令可能等待更久，15 分钟上限按命令计算。

## Additional Notes

端侧确认的是注入延迟后配置校验超时的阻塞机制；现场变慢的具体原因尚未确定。本轮真实客户端的 Doctor 均在 5 分钟内完成，超过基础窗口、静默及绝对上限行为由单元测试覆盖。

prs.body:
## Summary

旧任务中的历史内容块缺失 ID、字段类型错误或为空时，OpenClaw 会在请求准备阶段调用字符串方法并抛错，导致任务反复无法继续。本次在两个历史回放入口增加字段校验，保留可用历史，并提供只读工具定位原始异常记录。

## Related Issue

来自用户反馈，暂无公开 issue。现有日志及界面会话导出能支持本地回放异常的判断，但不足以确认该用户实际损坏的字段或记录。

## Changes Made

- 为 OpenClaw `v2026.8.1` 增加版本补丁，在核心转换及自定义传输入口共用校验器；保留签名内容、提供商扩展块、旧版工具参数及既有结果配对行为。

- 增加补丁应用强校验和回归覆盖；按 `specs/README.md` 规范提供[中文修复设计文档](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/blob/fix/openclaw-transcript-replay-validation/specs/bugfixes/openclaw-transcript-replay-validation/2026-09-15-openclaw-transcript-replay-validation-design.md)。

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Documentation update

- [x] LobsterAI 定向测试：23 项通过，包括使用 CRLF 补丁文件的验证。
- [x] OpenClaw AI 层定向测试：26 项通过；传输层定向测试：40 项通过。合计 89 项。
- [x] 同一异常历史连续两次经真实 Chat Completions SDK 请求本地模拟服务，均成功，输入历史保持不变。
- [x] 补丁通过原始固定版本的应用检查，完整 37 个补丁重复应用验证通过。
- [x] 改动 TypeScript 文件的 CI lint、两个 CJS 脚本语法检查及 `npm run compile:electron` 通过。
- [ ] 重建捆绑运行时后的桌面实机复测。

## Checklist

- [x] 已自查，改动范围限于历史回放校验与定位工具。
- [x] 新增和相关既有回归测试通过，改动文件未产生新的 lint 警告。
- [x] 文档符合 `specs/` 的中文、目录、命名及章节规范。

## Electron-Specific Changes

修改 OpenClaw 捆绑运行时行为，需重建运行时后进入桌面应用。校验只处理请求中的内存历史，定位工具只读访问原始会话；未修改持久化数据格式、IPC、preload 或 UI。

## Additional Notes

用户具体异常记录仍需原始 OpenClaw 会话 JSONL 或 agent 数据库确认。扫描结果包含已存储历史分支中的候选位置，需要结合实际回放窗口核对。本次不包含实时响应的工具调用解析修复。

prs.title: fix(openclaw): prevent large repair snapshots from timing out
prs.body:
## Summary

One-click OpenClaw repair can hit the 15-minute command limit while a large state snapshot is still copying. Size the snapshot's wait from the amount of data it measures and report progress as the copy advances.

## Changes

- Measure snapshot files and bytes before copying. Report progress from large file copies and SQLite online backups to the Electron main process.
- Keep the five-minute idle timeout and cap the measured wait at four hours. Record the latest progress and wait limit in the repair command diagnostics.
- Leave already-imported session archives in place, retain the agent databases in the snapshot, and record the skipped archive paths and restore instructions in the manifest.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): re-render install paths in the no-model config sync
prs.body:
## Problem

LobsterAI installs can share one profile (`%APPDATA%\LobsterAI`) and so one `openclaw.json`. This happens with the installed app plus `npm run electron:dev`, after a reinstall to another directory, or when a macOS app is moved. The config sync that runs while no API model is resolved (`writeMinimalConfig`: app startup before server models load, and logout) copied `plugins` and `mcp` from the existing file unchanged. As a result:

- `plugins.load.paths` kept pointing at the other install's `resources/cfmind/third-party-extensions`, so the gateway loaded that install's third-party plugins.
- MCP stdio servers kept launching the other install's `LobsterAI.exe` / `app.asar/node_modules/...`.
- Sync still reported `changed=false`.

The full sync was not affected, because it already re-renders `plugins.load` and owns `mcp`. The gateway, however, is first started from the minimal config. On a machine with a DLP agent, the dev gateway made about 17.5k sync fs calls into the installed app's folder per start (about 15 s). With corrected paths, plugin loading took about 2.3 s.

## Change

- `openclawPluginRepairPaths.ts`: adds `isRuntimeThirdPartyExtensionsDir()` (the matcher Quick Repair already used) and `rebaseRuntimeExtensionLoadPaths()`. Entries naming a LobsterAI runtime's extensions dir (`resources/cfmind` or `vendor/openclaw-runtime/<name>`) are rebased onto this install's `findBundledExtensionsDir()`, or dropped when it returns null. User-linked plugin paths are kept.
- `writeMinimalConfig`: runs the preserved `plugins` through that rebase. It also renders and owns `mcp` through `buildMcpConfig()`, which is now shared with the full sync.
- `openclawRepairPreflight.ts`: uses the shared matcher. Its behaviour is unchanged.

Behaviour note: with no model configured, `mcp` now follows LobsterAI's MCP state instead of the last file contents, the same as the full sync.

## Verification

- `npm test -- openclawConfigSync openclawPluginRepairPaths openclawRepairPreflight`: 214 passed, 6 skipped.
- New runtime tests cover a profile written by another install, in both no-model and full sync. The two no-model tests fail without the fix.
- CI lint on the touched files and `npm run compile:electron` pass.
- Not manually verified in the running app.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): 插件异常时降级启动并保留基础会话
prs.body:
插件升级或校验失败时，OpenClaw 8.1 会把修复告警升级成整个网关的启动拒绝，导致健康模型也无法对话。本改动移植上游的全局插件可用性策略：隔离失败插件并保留配置，让健康会话继续工作；核心配置、迁移租约和状态迁移错误仍拒绝启动。

- 以版本补丁回移上游 [#150016](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150016)、[#150312](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150312) 及 [#154543](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154543) 的纯配置 hook 隔离，适配固定版本 v2026.8.1。
- 保留缺失/不可检查路径及相关配置，隔离插件 Doctor 注册和纯配置修复异常；不按插件名或报错文本添加豁免。
- 补齐补丁完整性检查、登记测试和 CI 路径条件；提供 Electron CDP 验收驱动。
- Electron 行为变化：插件可用性告警不再阻塞 Gateway ready；IPC 协议与应用数据库结构不变。

prs.title: fix(openclaw): recover invalid generated model policies on upgrade
prs.body:
## Summary

An existing model ID such as `DeepSeek V4 Pro` could prevent the entire gateway from starting after upgrade, even when a different model was selected. The managed policy writer copied every legacy model key into `modelPolicy.allow` and marked migration complete, although OpenClaw rejects some of those keys as explicit policy references. Startup then failed with `Auth migration cannot repair unrelated config errors at: agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow.4`.

Preserve the complete legacy restriction when any reference cannot be materialized, and recover invalid full managed policies already written by the affected release before startup migration validates them.

## Related Issue

Regression following #2742.

## Changes Made

- Match the pinned OpenClaw v2026.8.1 reference grammar, including internal whitespace, ASCII controls, empty path segments, aliases and wildcard placement. Keep supported punctuation, nested model paths and upstream-supported selectors.
- Defer the whole managed allowlist and clear its migration marker when necessary, preserving original model IDs and metadata. Preserve authored policies and intentionally unrestricted migrated configurations.
- Recover generated invalid policies in the minimal-config path when provider credentials are unavailable, without marking fresh empty installations as migrated.
- Add upgrade, repair, idempotence and corrected-ID coverage, plus a 304-reference matrix checked against the actual bundled schema.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Testing

- [x] Related config sync/delivery/application/observation and skill tests: 281 passed before the additional character cases.
- [x] Final focused compatibility tests: 41 unit cases and the real-runtime 304-reference schema matrix passed.
- [x] Real-runtime startup migration test reproduces the original `allow.4` failure, then verifies successful recovery and stable CLI config writes.
- [x] Strict ESLint for all five changed TypeScript files, `npm run compile:electron`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- [x] Real Windows Electron client acceptance via Playwright debugging, with an isolated corrupted profile and a deterministic local model HTTP/SSE endpoint: automatic startup recovery, config.get/config.set roundtrip, two complete chat flows, manual gateway restart, four actual SKILL.md edits without config churn or restart, and corrected-ID migration through the client settings IPC.

During skill setup, one real config delivery timeout entered deferred recovery; the subsequent applied-config check cancelled the restart. The only gateway spawns were initial startup and the explicit manual restart. No computer-use or OS keyboard/mouse automation was used.

## Checklist

- [x] Self-reviewed the scoped diff and followed project style.
- [x] Added explanatory comments for legacy policy and migration-marker semantics.
- [x] Added and ran regression tests; changed files have no ESLint warnings.
- [x] Validated the main-process/runtime behavior in the real Electron client.

## Electron-Specific Changes

- [x] Changes to main process (`src/main/`): OpenClaw config generation and pre-start recovery.

No renderer, preload or IPC contract changes. Existing model IDs and model parameters are retained.

## Additional Notes

Client acceptance used a Windows development build and the pinned runtime with the release patches available at branch creation (`97d21b730`). This does not claim installer/macOS acceptance or validation of the user's remote model service. Runtime-dependent Vitest cases require `OPENCLAW_MODEL_POLICY_RUNTIME` to point to a built runtime.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): reconcile config application before starting tasks
prs.body:
代理端口或模型配置更新后，旧流程可能将 `config.set` 的保存成功当作运行时已经应用，导致新任务继续使用旧配置。本改动将运行中的交付统一为带版本条件的 `config.apply`，确认目标内容及应用版本一致后才放行新任务；待办状态跨越无变化同步、断线和恢复冷却，环境变化则要求真实的新进程。

- 配置先在内存准备，在最新源配置上按字段所有权合并；仅停止子进程后的启动准备允许直接写盘。
- 回迁 OpenClaw #142169 的候选观察缓存失效修复；在 `specs/bugfixes/openclaw-config-hot-reload-delivery/` 和版本补丁 README 保留上游依据及升级移除条件。
- Electron 行为变化：配置未确认时阻止新模型任务；保留活动任务，空闲后继续恢复；原生 shutdown 事件用于识别网关内部重启。

热应用后显式回传收敛状态解除 starting 遮罩；被拒绝的临时会话在恢复后重新创建真实会话，避免 `Session temp-... not found`。

[问题分析、最终方案及上游升级清理说明](https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/blob/fix/openclaw-config-lifecycle/specs/bugfixes/openclaw-config-hot-reload-delivery/2026-09-23-config-lifecycle-design.md) 已合并为单份文档。

验证：宿主定向 Vitest 546 通过 / 3 跳过，补丁清单 19 通过，renderer 回归 48 通过；修改文件 ESLint、Electron 编译和完整构建通过。已通过 Electron 调试接口驱动实际客户端，覆盖三个反馈模型及配置等待、丢回包、校验拒绝、恢复和进程重建。合成模型端点不代表生产套餐服务可用性。上一轮 GitHub CI 全部通过，当前提交状态以 Checks 为准。

上游直接相关测试 13 项通过；扩展 `config-reload` 测试组在本机出现 watcher/journal 断言失败及超时，尚无无补丁对照，未计为通过。截图中的同 run 会话重试约束是独立上游问题，本次消除旧配置这一触发源，不承诺修复任意网络失败后的重试。

prs.body:
## Summary

遗留网关或迁移锁仍引用存活 PID 时，一键修复可能在数据库快照阶段就被维护锁阻断。本次在手动修复的维护屏障内先核验锁所有者、恢复可确认的陈旧锁，再执行原有 Snapshot → Doctor → Recovery → 配置同步 → Plugins → 网关启动与连接流程。

## Related Issue

9 月 16 日反馈第 3 行的网关启动/维护锁故障，无关联 GitHub issue。现场 PID 的实际身份及是否源于自动更新仍不能确认。

## Changes Made

- [x] Documentation update

prs.title: fix(openclaw): compact byte-bounded history instead of sliding it
prs.body:
## Problem

A user reported going from 8,000+ credits to ~800 overnight. Their WeChat DM session (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 1M window) was billed ~60–130 credits per message.

OpenClaw v2026.8.1 hydrates each attempt with at most `contextTokenBudget × 8` stored bytes (8 MB for a 1M window). The bound counts stored event JSON, including inline `view_image` base64, so image-heavy sessions run at 12–20 bytes per prompt token and hit it long before the 980k token compaction threshold. From then on:

- compaction never runs;
- the newest-first reader drops the oldest events every turn, so the first model message changes each turn and the whole ~650k-token prefix misses the provider cache;
- the dropped history is never summarized.

In the user's logs the first full miss happened exactly when `activeTranscriptBytes` crossed 8 MB (7.59 MB → 8.04 MB). Upstream tracks this as openclaw/openclaw#159799 (open); the only merged mitigation, openclaw/openclaw#168157, landed after our v2026.8.1 pin.

## Change

Two version-scoped OpenClaw patches. No LobsterAI runtime code changes.

- `openclaw-bounded-history-chunked-window.patch` (port of #168157) changes the bounded reader:
  - the latest compaction/reset boundary is reserved before the tail is sized;
  - byte pressure is measured from the boundary's retained start;
  - the cut advances in quarter-capacity steps and starts at a user turn.
- `openclaw-bounded-history-compaction.patch` adds a `model_context_bytes` preflight compaction trigger at 80% of the same hydration bound. It is optional: a skip or failure keeps the turn running on the bounded tail, and retries wait for another quarter of the bound. A boundary whose retained tail alone is large does not re-compact every turn. Existing token and `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` triggers are unchanged.
- `apply-openclaw-patches.cjs` gets strong-validator snippets for both patches; the patch README documents the background, behavior and removal criteria.

## Verification

- OpenClaw unit tests:
  - bounded-context tests 12/12 and preflight tests 105/105; the new cases fail on the old code;
  - related session, attempt and caller suites (~260 tests) pass.
- Core typecheck: only the existing `managed-image-replay.ts` errors. oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- The full 80-patch series applies to a clean v2026.8.1 checkout; `npm run openclaw:runtime:host` builds and the runtime starts.
- Standalone gateway + mock model (100k window): turns survive a failing summarizer, retries back off, the window start moves only every quarter step, and the cache recovers after compaction.
- **In-app**, dev app on a real profile, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, ~820 KB of history per turn via `view_image`:
  - turn 8 at 6.55 MB triggered `model_context_bytes` compaction (~9 s), which brought history to 2.46 MB;
  - that turn's first request hit 93%, and turns 9–12 hit 99–100%;
  - 13 turns cost ~12.6 credits in total.

Not covered in-app: the IM (WeChat) channel itself. It shares the gateway and the same preflight function. The chunked window only matters when compaction fails, so it is covered by the mock run and unit tests.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): avoid unnecessary Clawguard startup lease waits
prs.body:
## Summary

The Clawguard startup repair could block gateway startup with `timed out waiting for plugin lifecycle lease core:plugin-lifecycle/global` even when the installed plugin did not need repair. Its 500ms acquisition budget also included synchronous SQLite work, so a slow transaction could fail without another lease owner.

Skip existing legacy installations and unsupported, missing, or malformed replacement packages before acquiring the lease. Allow 5 seconds for applicable checks, and repeat the path/package checks under the lease before any repair.

## Related Issue

Windows gateway startup failure investigated from the September 22 support logs; no linked issue.

## Changes Made

- Filter out irrelevant Clawguard installations before waiting for the shared plugin lease, including the reported 2.5.3 package.
- Increase the startup repair's lease acquisition budget from 500ms to 5 seconds.
- Cover unavailable leases for skipped repairs, changes while waiting for ownership, and acquisition failure for an applicable repair.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Testing

- [x] 71 targeted Vitest tests passed across Clawguard compatibility/install repair and startup compatibility.
- [x] Changed-file ESLint passed with zero warnings.
- [x] `npm run compile:electron`, startup script syntax check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- [x] Rebuilt the actual startup compatibility helper into an isolated temporary runtime and exercised real SQLite state:
  - Unsupported 2.5.3 with an occupied plugin lease: startup preparation succeeded without changes.
  - Existing legacy installation with an occupied plugin lease: startup preparation succeeded without changes.
  - Supported package with a 1123ms delay inside the actual lease acquisition transaction: startup preparation succeeded.

## Checklist

- [x] Reviewed the diff and kept the change limited to three files.
- [x] Added regression coverage and ran the relevant existing tests.
- [x] Preserved lease ownership checks, backup verification, and concurrent-change checks for actual repairs.

## Electron-Specific Changes

- [x] Changes to the main-process startup preparation helper.

The bundled `openclaw-startup-compat.mjs` must be regenerated when packaging this fix. Validation used isolated runtime state; the full desktop UI and the affected user's machine were not exercised.

issues.title: [Bug]: mission CLI duplicates /api prefix for /api/chat/send
issues.body:
## Bug Description

The `qwenpaw mission` CLI passes `/api/chat/send` to `client(url)`, but `client()` already configures `/api` as the base prefix. As a result, mission commands request `/api/api/chat/send` instead of `/api/chat/send`.

This affects all three commands: `mission start`, `mission status`, and `mission list`.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Start QwenPaw with `qwenpaw app`.
2. Run `qwenpaw mission start "Test mission"`.
3. Observe that the CLI sends its request to `http://127.0.0.1:8088/api/api/chat/send`, which does not match the chat API route.

The same duplicated path is constructed by `qwenpaw mission status` and `qwenpaw mission list`.

## Expected Behavior

Mission commands should call `/api/chat/send` exactly once, for example by passing `/chat/send` to the existing API-prefixed client.

## Actual Behavior

They call `/api/api/chat/send`, preventing the Mission CLI from communicating with the intended endpoint.

## Relevant Code

- [`src/qwenpaw/cli/mission_cmd.py:51`](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/main/src/qwenpaw/cli/mission_cmd.py#L51): `mission start`
- [`src/qwenpaw/cli/mission_cmd.py:68`](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/main/src/qwenpaw/cli/mission_cmd.py#L68): `mission status`
- [`src/qwenpaw/cli/mission_cmd.py:85`](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/main/src/qwenpaw/cli/mission_cmd.py#L85): `mission list`
- [`src/qwenpaw/cli/http.py`](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/main/src/qwenpaw/cli/http.py): `client()` appends `/api` to the base URL.

This is present on the current upstream `main`. Issue #5769 concerned a different duplicated-prefix path and does not cover these Mission CLI calls.

issues.title: [Bug]: auto CLI health check uses unsupported HEAD /api/version
issues.body:
## Bug Description

The auto-generated CLI commands perform a daemon health check with `HEAD /version`. Because `client(base_url)` already adds the `/api` prefix, this sends `HEAD /api/version`. A running QwenPaw service responds with `405 Method Not Allowed`, so `_ensure_daemon_alive()` treats the healthy daemon as unreachable and exits with status 2 before executing the requested command.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Start QwenPaw with `qwenpaw app`.
2. Run `curl -I http://127.0.0.1:8088/api/version`; the service returns `405 Method Not Allowed`.
3. Invoke an auto-generated command such as `qwenpaw auto crons-list`.
4. The CLI prints `Error: QwenPaw daemon is not reachable ... Start it with qwenpaw app first.` and exits with status 2 even though the daemon is running.

## Expected Behavior

The health check should use a supported method and endpoint (for example, `GET /version` if that is the intended endpoint), allowing auto-generated commands to proceed when the daemon is healthy.

## Actual Behavior

Every request that reaches `_ensure_daemon_alive()` is rejected by the health check because HTTP 405 is handled as daemon unreachability.

## Relevant Code

- [`src/qwenpaw/cli/auto.py:38-50`](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/main/src/qwenpaw/cli/auto.py#L38-L50): sends `c.head("/version")` and converts all exceptions, including `HTTPStatusError`, into exit status 2.
- [`src/qwenpaw/cli/http.py`](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/main/src/qwenpaw/cli/http.py): `client()` adds the `/api` base prefix.

This was reproduced against a running QwenPaw service and is also present on the current upstream `main`.

issues.title: [Bug]: Daily Paper fails when model digest output is truncated (ToolJSONDecodeError) — no per-paper retry, whole job marked error
issues.body:
Environment
QwenPaw Desktop v2.2.2-beta.4 (Windows 10 x64)
Model: glm-5.3-flash (remote LLM)
Component: ReMe Daily Paper memory cron (reme_daily_paper\analyze.py → agentscope generate_structured_output)
Failed task: 10926114-f4b3-42d9-9bd0-cd5c1a47d27a (2026-10-08 10:20:39 CST)
Problem
In a 3-paper daily batch, 2 papers produced notes successfully (26 KB / 23 KB markdown). The 3rd paper (arXiv 2609.39102) failed: the model emitted the digest as a single tool call whose body argument contains the entire markdown note. For a content-heavy paper the completion was cut off mid-JSON (output token limit), so the tool arguments never terminated:

agentscope.exception._model.StructuredOutputError: Invalid structured output from model glm-5.3-flash: ToolJSONDecodeError: ... JSONDecodeError ... Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 9 (char 8). your_tool_arguments = '{"body":"## ... [never closed]
Consequences:

The note for that paper is silently lost (no partial output, no fallback).
_analyze_one has no retry and no per-paper isolation: the whole job ends status=error even though 2/3 papers succeeded, so the inbox event reports a failure for the entire batch.
On this machine, 5 of the last 8 recorded daily_paper runs ended in status=error (9/5, 9/9, 9/11, 9/13, 10/8; 9/11 was the network issue reported in #7715). Long-output truncation appears to be a recurring failure mode distinct from #7715 (network) and #7199 (surrogate chars).
Log evidence (qwenpaw.log, same run)
09:00:55 [DailyPaperAnalyzeStep] start papers=3 09:09:03 paper done arxiv_id=2610.05608 -> note saved (26 KB) 09:48:53 paper done arxiv_id=2609.38879 -> note saved (23 KB) 09:48:56 paper start arxiv_id=2609.39102 10:20:39 ReMe result pushed: agent=default job=daily_paper event=10926114-... status=error 10:20:39 ERROR | crons\manager.py:1048 | Failed to execute memory cron job daily-paper: Invalid structured output from model glm-5.3-flash: ToolJSONDecodeError ...
Traceback shows the failure surfaces at analyze.py:193 execute → analyze.py:102 _analyze_one → as_agent_wrapper reply → retry_chat_model.generate_structured_output with no recovery step in between.

Root cause
The digest must be serialized as one tool call with the full markdown inside a JSON string argument. Long bodies (~25 KB+ of mixed CJK/escaped text) approach the model's max output tokens; truncation yields invalid JSON and agentscope raises StructuredOutputError.
No resilience layer: no retry (e.g., with a shorter-target instruction), no chunked writing path, and per-paper exceptions abort the whole batch.
Suggested fixes
Per-paper fault isolation — catch StructuredOutputError (and other per-paper exceptions) inside the paper loop in _analyze_one; mark that paper failed, continue the batch; push a partial_success-style event listing which papers failed instead of a blanket error.
Retry with a length constraint — on ToolJSONDecodeError, retry that paper once with an explicit "shorter body" instruction (e.g., cap the note at N characters, or drop to a brief template).
Chunked note writing — allow the digest to be written via several smaller tool calls (append mode) so a single generation never has to serialize a 25 KB+ payload as one JSON string.
(minor) surface per-paper status (done/failed + arxiv_id) in the inbox event.
This would make Daily Paper robust to the same class of failure reported in #7715 (network) and #7199 (crash) — one bad paper should not cost the whole batch.
