issues.title: [Bug]: Mobile full-screen containers render console content under the system status bar (top safe-area-inset missing)
[Bug] Windows: orphaned llama-server.exe processes accumulate across backend restarts, exhausting memory and preventing local model startup
issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, `llama-server.exe` launched by QwenPaw for a local model is **not terminated when the backend exits abnormally** (crash / forced kill / restart). Every subsequent backend start spawns *another* `llama-server.exe` on a fresh random port instead of adopting the one that is already running. After a few restarts the machine runs out of RAM commit, the next server dies silently during `load_model`, and the user only sees:

```
{"detail":"llama.cpp server exited before becoming ready"}
```

## Environment

- QwenPaw **2.3.0.post1**, `pip` install in venv, started with `qwenpaw app`
- Windows 10 (AMD64)
- Local model: `AgentScope/Piccolo-4B-Q8_0` (4.48 GB GGUF)
- Server argv: `llama-server.exe --host 127.0.0.1 --port <random> --model ...gguf --alias AgentScope/Piccolo-4B-Q8_0 --log-file ... --gpu-layers auto --ctx-size 8192 --batch-size 8192 --ubatch-size 8192 --parallel 1 --no-cache-prompt --cache-ram 0 --no-context-shift`
- Machine: 32 GB RAM (commit limit 48.88 GB)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Enable a local model so `llama-server.exe` is running and healthy.
2. Restart / hard-kill the QwenPaw backend (the `atexit` path does not run).
3. `Get-Process llama-server` shows the old process still alive and still `LISTENING` on its old port; the new backend start adds one more process.
4. Repeat a few times: each process holds ~5.18 GB working set.

## Observed

Four successful starts, none reclaimed:

| start time | port | pid |
|---|---|---|
| 08:42:29 | 50442 | 11148 |
| 08:50:12 | 50669 | 13756 |
| 08:52:44 | 50694 | 2412 |
| 08:54:32 | 50711 | 4408 |

Then every subsequent start fails (each on a new port: 50765, 52777, 52782, 52798):

```
INFO | local_models\llamacpp.py:833 | llama.cpp health check returned 503 while waiting for http://127.0.0.1:50765/health
INFO | local_models\llamacpp.py:840 | llama.cpp health check failed for http://127.0.0.1:50765/health:
WARNING | providers\provider_manager.py:1244 | Failed to restore local model server for AgentScope/Piccolo-4B-Q8_0: llama.cpp server exited before becoming ready
```

`local_models/logs/llama-server.log` (446 bytes, overwritten per attempt) ends with **no error at all**:

```
0.00.049.730 I srv    load_model: loading model 'C:\...\Piccolo-4B-Q8_0.gguf'
```

i.e. the child is killed while loading, and the exit reason is lost. Commit charge at that moment: 48.88 GB limit, 6.81 GB free, ~20.7 GB held by the four orphaned servers.

Killing the four orphans (`taskkill /IM llama-server.exe /F`) makes the local model start again immediately — confirming resource exhaustion, not a corrupt model.

## Expected

- When the backend exits (including crash / forced kill), its `llama-server` child should be terminated too.
- At startup, restore should **adopt** an already-running server for the same model instead of spawning a new one.
- When the health check sees a dead child, the error should carry the exit code and the tail of `llama-server.log` instead of a bare "exited before becoming ready".

## Code pointers

- `qwenpaw/local_models/llamacpp.py:266-282` — reuse check is purely in-instance (`self._server_process` / `self._server_port`); no pid/port file, no scan for an existing `llama-server`.
- `qwenpaw/local_models/llamacpp.py:783` `_resolve_server_port()` → `_find_free_port()` — always allocates a **new** port, so old servers are never reused and never conflict. (With a fixed port it would at least fail loudly: `Requested llama.cpp port is unavailable`, `:797`.)
- `qwenpaw/local_models/llamacpp.py:826` — `raise RuntimeError("llama.cpp server exited before becoming ready")` when `returncode is not None`.
- `qwenpaw/local_models/llamacpp.py:301-303` — `start_new_session=True` is applied **only on non-Windows**; on Windows there is no Job Object, so children survive the parent.
- `qwenpaw/local_models/llamacpp.py:85, :890` — cleanup relies on `atexit` + `shutdown_server_sync`, which never runs on a hard kill.
- `qwenpaw/providers/provider_manager.py:1234-1250` — `_resume_local_model()` calls `setup_server(model_id)` unconditionally; on failure it only logs a warning and clears `qwenpaw-local` (`base_url: ""`, `extra_models: []`).

## Suggested fixes

1. On Windows, put `llama-server` in a Job Object with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` so it cannot outlive the backend.
2. Persist runtime state (`local_models/run/llama-server.json`: pid, port, model alias, start time) and, at startup, adopt the running instance if it matches and is healthy; otherwise kill it before spawning a new one.
3. As a cheap pre-flight, stop any `llama-server.exe` whose `--model` matches the one about to be loaded.
4. Improve the error: on `returncode is not None`, include the exit code and the last ~20 lines of the child's log.

## Workaround

```powershell
taskkill /IM llama-server.exe /F
```

then re-enable the local model in the UI.

issues.title: [Bug]: 窄屏下整条消息的文字被剪裁，超宽内容（表格 / 代码块）同样被裁切且无法横向滚动

labels.name: bug

issues.body: ## 环境 - QwenPaw: `v2.3.0.post1`（升级前为 `v2.3.0`，升级后出现窄屏剪裁问题） - 界面: Console（Web UI） - 桌面端: Chrome / Windows 11，视口宽度约 `1903 px` - 移动端: 手机 Chrome，视口宽度 `375 px`（竖屏） - 设置: 设置中心 → 消息展示 → 消息宽度 = **标准** ## 复现步骤 1. 打开 Console，进入任意会话 2. 设置中心 → 消息展示 → 消息宽度选择「标准」 3. 让 Agent 输出以下任一内容： - 列数较多的 Markdown 表格（本次测试 20 列、30 列） - 超长单行的代码块（`text` 或 `css`，约 490~505 字符） 4. 观察消息气泡右侧 5. 用手机浏览器打开同一个会话，观察同样的消息 ## 实际表现 内容宽度超过气泡宽度时，**右侧被直接裁掉，不出现横向滚动条，也没有任何方式查看被裁掉的部分**。 各内容块表现一致。 ### 1. Markdown 表格 20 列表格只渲染到第 13 列（C13 仅显示一半），C14 至 C20 完全不可见。 - 实测表格渲染宽度：`1421 px` - 外层消息区宽度：`990 px` 30 列表格被裁得更早，实测宽度 `1651 px`。 | 截图 1 · 表格 | |---| | | ### 2. text 代码块 单行 505 字符的 `text` 代码块，只能看到前约 100 字符，其后内容全部不可见。块内每 20 字符放置一个 `` 标尺，用于定位裁切位置。 | 截图 2 · text 代码块 | |---| | | ### 3. css 代码块 单行 489 字符的 `css` 代码块（带语法高亮），表现与 `text` 块完全一致，同样从右侧被裁。 | 截图 3 · css 代码块 | |---| | | ### 4. 手机端（窄屏）：不只是表格和代码块，整条消息的文字都会被裁 375px 视口下打开同一个会话，消息区可视宽度只有 `303 px`，而承载内容的容器实测被撑到 `988 px`： - 一个两列的 Markdown 表格渲染宽度 `987 px`，右侧完全看不到，也无法滑动 - **同一条消息里，表格之后的普通段落文字也会一起被裁掉**，因为整块响应内容都被撑到 988px，超出部分被外层 `overflow: hidden` 静默裁掉 - 表现上就是「这条回复右边的字少了半截」，而且没有任何滚动条提示 ![Screenshot_2026-11-18-23-04-21-633_ai.qwenpaw.shell-edit.jpg](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d1a92d9-d241-4ee3-a51a-95835a78e263) ## 补充观察 1. **不是「标准模式特有」**。把「消息宽度」切到「加宽」后，只是可用宽度变大、部分内容刚好能放下；一旦内容宽度超过容器，仍然会被裁且同样没有横向滚动条。标准模式因为容器更窄，所以更容易触发。 2. **同一条消息内的多个内容块全部受影响**。上例中三个块连续排列，每一个都在相同的位置被切断。 3. 通过 Browser 实测，承载消息内容的 `.x-markdown` 元素的实际渲染宽度会被内容撑开（`1651 px`），而外层消息区仍为 `990 px`，超出部分既不可见、也无法滚动到。

issues.title: [Feature]: Isolate agent sessions by Telegram forum topic

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
## Summary

Support topic-scoped agent sessions in Telegram forum supergroups.

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Problem / Motivation

Currently, all messages within a Telegram group share the same QwenPaw session, even when they originate from different forum topics.

For a Telegram group with multiple topics:
 - General
 - Daily Planning
 - Development
 - Research

All incoming messages share: telegram:<chat_id>

Consequently:
 - Different topics share one agent conversation context.
 - Topic-specific discussions contaminate each other's history.
 - Session-scoped memory and Scroll cannot distinguish topics.
 - The Console displays one shared conversation instead of separate topic sessions.

Telegram already supports routing outgoing replies to the correct topic using message_thread_id, but that does not isolate agent sessions.


## Proposed Solution

I propose using message_thread_id as part of the session identifier so that each Telegram forum topic maintains independent conversation history, context, and session-scoped memory.

Use topic-aware session identifiers:
Context | Session ID
-- | --
Private chat | telegram:<chat_id>
Non-forum group | telegram:<chat_id>
Forum topic 201 | telegram:<chat_id>:201
Forum topic 202 | telegram:<chat_id>:202

Only split actual forum topics, not ordinary reply threads.

General-topic behavior should be explicitly defined for updates that contain message_thread_id=1 or omit the field.


## Alternatives Considered

N/A

## Additional Context

Related Issues:
 - #531 — Telegram replies delivered to the General topic
 - #653 — Telegram topic support improvements
 - #8710 — Per-conversation session binding for messaging channels

## Willing to Contribute

- [x] I am willing to open a PR for this feature (after discussion).

## Summary

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Problem / Motivation

Users running Rapid-MLX on Apple Silicon currently need to configure a custom provider and enter connection details manually. A local preset would make that setup discoverable and include a tested model.

## Proposed Solution

Register an `OpenAIProvider` preset with API address `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1`, no required API key, model discovery, and one tested model: `mlx-community/Qwen3.5-4B-MLX-4bit`, with tool-calling capability marked. Reuse the existing adapter and provider settings; users manage their Rapid-MLX server themselves.

Include an English README entry, English and Chinese model documentation, and a registration/persistence regression test. Add no runtime dependencies or managed engine installation. Rapid-MLX is Apache-2.0 and available through `pip install rapid-mlx`; document `rapid-mlx serve qwen3.5-4b-4bit`.

## Alternatives Considered

Users can continue configuring a custom OpenAI-compatible provider. The open managed-MLX work in #8647 installs and manages an inference runtime; this preset instead connects to a server the user already runs.

## Additional Context

Local verification against Rapid-MLX 1.0.4 on Apple Silicon completed a real QwenPaw streaming chat, a `get_current_time` tool call, and a `memory_search` tool call using local embeddings and reranking. The provider suite passed 1,192 tests (one skipped), and provider integration/contract tests passed 27 tests. Commands, responses, and logs are prepared locally under `evidence/`.

This proposal follows CONTRIBUTING's instruction: “If no related issue exists: open a new issue describing your proposal.” No existing Rapid-MLX issue was found on 2026-11-19.

Prepared branch: `add-rapid-mlx`, based on upstream `main`. Nothing has been pushed or posted. If accepted, the follow-up PR will include the required chat screenshot and final check results. The local full test gate currently stops on missing Playwright Chromium; repository-wide Pylint also reports three errors in unchanged Windows sandbox files. Both limitations were reproduced on the pristine base, and changed-file hooks pass.

Reference: https://github.com/raullenchai/Rapid-MLX

## Willing to Contribute

- [x] I am willing to open a PR for this feature (after discussion).

issues.title: [Bug]: Disabling a provider leaves stale agent run-config model — channels fail with ProviderError: Provider is disabled
issues.body:
## 现象

在「模型」页禁用某个 provider（或停用其下模型）后，**智能体「运行配置」里已选定的旧模型不会被联动更新**，仍指向那个已禁用的 provider。此后任何走通道（飞书 / 钉钉 / 企微 / 微信…）发消息，智能体在构建模型阶段直接抛错：

```
qwenpaw.exceptions.ProviderError: Provider is disabled
```

飞书侧对用户只显示一句无信息量的 **「Internal error」**，通道不降级、不回退、也不重试。

## 复现步骤

1. 「模型」页配置 provider A（如下 `kexin_token`，含模型 `glm-5.3-flash`），设为可用。
2. 「智能体」→ 该智能体的**运行配置**里选择 provider A 的模型（写入 workspace `agent.json` 的 `active_model`）。
3. 「模型」页把 provider A **禁用**（`enabled=false`），或全局默认模型改选 provider B。
4. 通过任意 IM 通道给该智能体发消息。
5. → 智能体构建模型即失败，通道返回「Internal error」。

## 实际行为 vs 期望行为

| | 现状 | 期望 |
|---|---|---|
| 禁用 provider 后运行配置 | 仍保留已禁用的 `provider_id`/`model` | 自动回落到全局默认模型，或明确标记为失效并提示用户重选 |
| 构建模型时命中已禁用 provider | 直接抛 `ProviderError: Provider is disabled` | 与「未指定运行配置模型」同等处理：回退到全局默认模型 |
| 通道侧报错 | 笼统的 `Internal error` | 指明「provider X 已被禁用，请为智能体 Y 重新选择模型」这类可操作信息 |

## 根因

模型来源是**两套互斥的优先级链**，「模型」页的禁用状态只作用于第一套：

1. **全局默认模型** —「模型」页的默认选择（`defaultModels` / `defaultChatModel` / `defaultLlm`）。
2. **智能体运行配置** — 各 workspace `agent.json` 的 `active_model`（`provider_id` + `model`）。

`runtime/builder.py:build_model` → `agents/model_factory.py:2446 create_model_and_formatter` 解析到智能体级模型后，去校验 provider 的 `enabled`；被禁用即抛 `ProviderError`。**校验失败时没有任何回落路径**——既不回落到全局默认模型，也不提示「你选的模型已被禁用」。

更关键的是：`model_factory` 的模型选择器只列出 `enabled !== false` 的 provider（`models.list.filter(...)`），所以**用户在运行配置里根本看不到已禁用项**——但**已存下来的旧值会被继续沿用**。用户既看不见、也改不掉（除非主动去改运行配置），于是通道静默坏死。

## 证据

环境：QwenPaw **2.3.0-beta.1** / Windows 11。

**1) 通道构建模型失败（`qwenpaw.log`）**

```
2026-11-04 19:17:06 | ERROR | qwenpaw\runtime\runtime.py:193 | runtime: unhandled error session=76371ed5: Provider is disabled
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "qwenpaw\runtime\runtime.py", line 108, in run
  File "qwenpaw\runtime\builder.py", line 465, in build
  File "qwenpaw\utils\io_utils.py", line 136, in run_sync_io
  File "qwenpaw\runtime\builder.py", line 655, in build_model
  File "qwenpaw\agents\model_factory.py", line 2446, in create_model_and_formatter
qwenpaw.exceptions.ProviderError: Provider is disabled
2026-11-04 19:17:06 | ERROR | qwenpaw\app\channels\base.py:1038 | channel _stream_with_tracker failed: Provider is disabled, session=76371ed5, agent=feishu:sw:76371ed5
```

**2) 智能体运行配置确实指向已禁用的 provider**

```
2026-11-04 14:10:34 | INFO | qwenpaw\app\routers\providers.py:969 | Returning agent-specific model for default: provider_id='kexin_token' model='glm-5.3-flash'
2026-11-04 15:48:25 | INFO | ... provider_id='kexin_token' model='glm-5.3-flash'
2026-11-04 18:50:54 | INFO | ... provider_id='kexin_token' model='glm-5.3-flash'
2026-11-04 19:26:04 | INFO | ... provider_id='kexin_token' model='glm-5.3-flash'
2026-11-04 19:26:47 | INFO | ... provider_id='kexin_token' model='glm-5.3-flash'
2026-11-04 19:26:53 | INFO | ... provider_id='kexin_token' model='glm-5.3-flash'
2026-11-04 19:27:08 | INFO | ... provider_id='minmax' model='MiniMax-M3.1-Flash'   <-- 手工改运行配置后
```

`GET /api/models` 实测 `kexin_token` 为 `enabled=false`（api_key 仍在，只被关掉开关）。provider 总数 42，其中 5 个 `enabled=false`：`opencode`、`ct`、`kexin_token`、`qwen_36`、`qwen_38`。

**3) 时间线完全自洽——报错只在「运行配置仍指向旧 provider」的窗口内出现**

| 时间 | 事件 |
|---|---|
| 19:17:06 | `Provider is disabled`（飞书 `session=76371ed5`） |
| 19:18:18 / 19:18:25 / 19:18:31 / 19:18:36 / 19:18:41 | 同错连发（5 次） |
| 19:23:53 / 19:24:02 | 同错再发（2 次） |
| **19:27:08** | 运行配置改为 `minmax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` |
| 19:27:08 之后 | **再无一次 `Provider is disabled`** |

共 8 次报错（每次在日志里出现 2 行：traceback + 通道侧转发），时间跨度 19:17:06–19:24:02；运行配置一改，通道立刻恢复。

**4) 与本 issue 无关的相邻噪声**（不影响结论）：`feishu get user name api error: code=99991672 Access denied`（缺 `contact:contact.base` 权限）、`Skipping skill 'himalaya' ... CLI binary not found on PATH`、`sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database ... qjYxdu\history.db`（另一 workspace）。

## 建议修复方向

1. **禁用 provider 时级联处理运行配置**：禁用 provider 后，扫描各 workspace `agent.json` 的 `active_model` / `fallback_models`，若指向被禁用 provider → 自动回落到全局默认模型，并在 UI 提示「智能体 X 的运行配置已回退」。
2. **构建模型时兜底**：`create_model_and_formatter` 命中已禁用 provider 时，不要直接抛错，改为回退到全局默认模型（与「未指定运行配置模型」走同一条路径）；若全局默认也不可用，再报错。
3. **可操作的错误信息**：通道侧不应只显示 `Internal error`。至少在错误里带上「provider `kexin_token` 已被禁用，请为智能体 `default` 重新选择模型」。
4. **UI 可见性**：运行配置已选中的模型若被禁用，选择器应把它标为「已禁用」并保留显示（而不是从列表消失），让用户看得到自己正指向一个失效项；禁用 provider 时弹出「N 个智能体正在使用它」。
5. **一致性**：让「模型」页的全局默认与智能体运行配置的禁用状态走同一套 provider 有效性校验，避免两套来源对同一个 provider 给出不一致的可选性。

## 关联

- #8511 — 飞书通道间歇性 `ProviderError: **No active model configured**`。**根因不同**：#8511 是会话路由竞态（消息被 build 进 `active_model` 为空的工作区）；本 issue 是 **provider 被禁用后运行配置的旧模型未联动**，报错本体为 `Provider is disabled`，两者互不覆盖，建议分开处理。

issues.title: [Bug]: Scheduled task conversations show no messages until execution completes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body: ## QwenPaw Version 2.3.0 ## Description While a scheduled Agent task is running in the background, its corresponding conversation in the Web Console shows no messages or execution progress: - The message that triggers the task is not visible. - Model response messages are not visible. - All conversation content appears only after the entire task has finished. This prevents users from following the task’s progress during execution. The task uses dispatch mode `final`. I did not encounter this behavior in the previously used version. It appeared after upgrading, but the exact version that introduced the issue has not been identified. **Related PR(s):** Unknown. **Security considerations:** No credentials, tokens, or sensitive configuration are included in this report. ## Component(s) Affected - [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models) - [x] Console (frontend web UI) - [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.) - [ ] Skills - [ ] CLI - [ ] Documentation (website) - [ ] Tests - [ ] CI/CD - [ ] Scripts / Deploy ## Environment - **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0 - **OS:** Windows - **Install method:** Not confirmed - **Python version (if applicable):** 3.13 ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure a multi-step Agent scheduled task with dispatch mode set to `final`. 2. Let the task trigger and open its corresponding conversation in the Web Console while it is executing. 3. Observe that no trigger message, model responses, or execution progress appear. 4. Wait until the entire task finishes. The conversation content then becomes visible. ## Actual vs Expected - **Actual:** The conversation shows no messages or progress during execution. All content appears only after the task finishes. - **Expected:** The conversation displays the task’s trigger message and subsequent model responses as execution progresses. ## Logs / Screenshots ## Additional Notes Preliminary code investigation identified the following relevant paths, relative to the `qwenpaw` package: - `app/crons/executor.py` registers the conversation and directly calls `workspace.stream_query(req)`, without registering the execution with `workspace.task_tracker`. - `app/chats/api.py` obtains conversation execution status from that TaskTracker. - `app/routers/console.py` relies on `tracker.attach(chat.id)` for stream reconnection. - Cron also sets `suppress_console_push=True`, which causes ConsoleChannel to skip the frontend push queue. These findings suggest a missing connection between cron execution and the Web Console’s live conversation tracking. The complete cause and the release that introduced this behavior still need confirmation.

issues.title: DoomLoopGate never triggers when agentscope accumulates a reply into one assistant message
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0 (Docker image `agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.3.0`). Also reproducible on `main` at `fc1db1a`.

## Description

With the default loop configuration (`window_size=3`, `similarity_threshold=1.0`, stages `after=3 / modify_prompt` and `after=4 / stop`), a turn that repeatedly calls the same tool with identical arguments never triggers either stage.

In a real 9-iteration console session on the default mode (the same failing SQL through `execute_readonly_sql` every round), `--log-level debug` showed `DefaultMode configured 2 gate(s)` and `LoopGate 'doom-loop' activated` on every iteration, but never `Doom loop: sim=`; the turn only ended via `IterationGate`. The persisted `agent.state.context` contained just two messages: the user message and one assistant message with 8 accumulated `tool_call`/`tool_result` block pairs.

**Root cause**

- agentscope 2.0.10 keeps **one assistant message per reply**. `Agent._save_to_context` uses `state.reply_id` as the message id and appends every iteration's blocks (reasoning, tool calls, tool results) to that same message.
- `DoomLoopGate._auto_record_from_ctx` (`src/qwenpaw/loop/gates/doom_loop.py`, around L205) returns as soon as the latest message id matches the last recorded one:

  ```python
  last_msg = context[-1]
  if last_msg.id == state.last_recorded_msg_id:
      return
  ```

  Within a reply the id never changes, so after the first check no further tool calls are recorded, `history_dirty` stays `False`, and `check()` returns `BYPASS` for the rest of the turn.
- Consequence: only a model response whose **first** snapshot already contains at least `window_size` identical tool calls (parallel calls in one response) can trip the window. Even then `consecutive_hits` is seeded to `window_size` and only increments on a later dirty check, so the `after=4 / stop` stage is unreachable in the default mode.

**Related PR(s):** coming in a follow-up PR.

**Security considerations:** none.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0 (`main` at `fc1db1a` also affected)
- **OS:** Debian 12, aarch64
- **Install method:** Docker
- **Python version:** 3.12 (agentscope 2.0.10)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use the default mode (console chat) with the default `agents.running.loop.doom_loop` stages.
2. Ask something that makes the agent call the same tool with exactly the same arguments at least 4 times (for example, the same failing SQL).
3. Observe that no doom-loop warning is injected and the loop is never stopped by the doom gate.

Minimal reproduction without an LLM:

```python
import asyncio
from types import SimpleNamespace

from qwenpaw.config.config import DoomLoopStageConfig
from qwenpaw.loop.gates.doom_loop import DoomLoopGate


async def main():
    msg = SimpleNamespace(id="reply-1", role="assistant", content=[])
    agent = SimpleNamespace(state=SimpleNamespace(context=[msg]))
    ctx = {
        "agent": agent,
        "final_msg": None,
        "iteration": 0,
        "has_tool_calls": True,
    }
    gate = DoomLoopGate(
        window_size=3,
        similarity_threshold=1.0,
        stages=[
            DoomLoopStageConfig(after=3, action="modify_prompt", prompt="warn"),
            DoomLoopStageConfig(after=4, action="stop", prompt="stop"),
        ],
    )
    for i in range(1, 7):
        # Same message id, one more identical tool call per formatting round,
        # exactly like agentscope accumulates blocks into one reply.
        msg.content.append(
            {
                "type": "tool_call",
                "name": "execute_readonly_sql",
                "input": {"sql": "SELECT 1"},
            },
        )
        result = await gate.check(ctx)
        state = gate._ensure_state()
        print(i, len(state.history), state.consecutive_hits, result.action.value)


asyncio.run(main())
```

Actual output on 2.3.0 / `main`:

```
1 1 0 bypass
2 1 0 bypass
3 1 0 bypass
4 1 0 bypass
5 1 0 bypass
6 1 0 bypass
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** `history` stays at 1 for the whole reply; both the warning and the stop stage never fire. The `after=4 / stop` stage is unreachable.
- **Expected:** the third identical call produces `INTERRUPT_AND_CONTINUE` with the configured warning prompt, the fourth produces `TERMINATE` with the stop prompt.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
[DEBUG] DefaultMode configured 2 gate(s)
[DEBUG] IterationGate: 1/100
[DEBUG] IterationGate: 2/100
...
[DEBUG] IterationGate: 9/100
(no "Doom loop: sim=" line anywhere)
```

## Additional Notes

The current unit tests only call `gate.record()` directly (`tests/unit/loop/test_doom_loop_gate.py`), so the `_auto_record_from_ctx` path has no coverage and this regression shipped unnoticed. A fix that consumes the tail of the accumulated message (count of already-recorded `tool_call` blocks) restores the intended 3-warning / 4-stop behaviour and keeps the 2.3.0 improvements (recording every tool call in the message, the `has_tool_calls` guard, and warning injection).

issues.title: [Bug]: XiaoYi channel emits no working/status frames during long turns (blank client for minutes) and drops the WS silently
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2.post1

## Description

**Two related symptoms on the XiaoYi (小艺) channel:**

**1. No downstream frame at all during a long turn.** While a turn is running, the
channel writes nothing to the WebSocket except the 30s protocol-level
`msgType=heartbeat` (constant `HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL = 30` in `xiaoyi/constants.py`).
That heartbeat keeps the TCP/WS link alive but is invisible in the client UI, so
the user sees a completely blank conversation for the whole duration of the turn.

Concrete case (2026-10-20): a short prompt wrote nothing back for ~7m36s. Queue
and consumer were created, the agent was rebuilt and the session was being read
during the turn, but no user-visible message was ever emitted, and the turn was
finally cancelled by an instance restart:

```
2026-10-20 15:43:16 | INFO | unified_queue_manager.py:206 | Created queue: channel=xiaoyi session=<redacted> priority=20
2026-10-20 15:43:16 | INFO | channels/base.py:550 | _consume_with_tracker: chat_id=<redacted> session=<redacted>
2026-10-20 15:43:17 | INFO | runtime/builder.py:574 | builder: built agent for session=<redacted> model=deepseek-v4.1-flash tools=75
2026-10-20 15:44:42 | INFO | chats/session.py:454 | Get session state dict ... successfully.
2026-10-20 15:50:52 | INFO | hooks/error/error_hook.py:90 | cancel_cleanup: cancelled (session=<redacted>): CancelledError
```

**2. Unexpected disconnects, sometimes twice within 40 seconds.** The channel
re‑connects successfully (1s backoff), but nothing in the log says *why* the link
dropped (no close code / reason), and the in-flight turn is not resumed or
replayed.

```
2026-10-22 21:55:11 | WARNING | xiaoyi/channel.py:838 | XiaoYi [primary]: Disconnected
2026-10-22 21:55:11 | INFO    | xiaoyi/channel.py:1089 | XiaoYi: Reconnecting in 1s (attempt 1)
2026-10-22 21:55:12 | INFO    | xiaoyi/channel.py:222  | XiaoYi [primary]: Disconnected
2026-10-22 21:55:28 | INFO    | xiaoyi/channel.py:1101 | XiaoYi: Reconnected successfully
2026-10-22 21:55:48 | WARNING | xiaoyi/channel.py:838  | XiaoYi [primary]: Disconnected
2026-10-22 21:55:48 | INFO    | xiaoyi/channel.py:1089 | XiaoYi: Reconnecting in 1s (attempt 1)
2026-10-22 21:55:49 | INFO    | xiaoyi/channel.py:222  | XiaoYi [primary]: Disconnected
2026-10-22 21:55:49 | INFO    | xiaoyi/channel.py:1101 | XiaoYi: Reconnected successfully
```

**Related PR(s):** none

**Security considerations:** none — no credentials or config values are included
in this report; `agentId`/`session` IDs are redacted.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2.post1 (`qwenpaw-2.2.2.post1.dist-info`)
- **OS:** Linux, kernel 4.19.90-2003.4.0.0036.oe1.x86_64 (openEuler), containerised
- **Install method:** Docker image
- **Python version:** 3.11

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure the `xiaoyi` channel and confirm `XiaoYi: Connected` in the log.
2. From the XiaoYi app, send a prompt that takes more than ~40s to complete
   (one that triggers several tool calls works reliably).
3. Watch the app during the turn: no typing indicator, no progress text, no
   partial output — the conversation stays empty until either the final message
   arrives or the turn dies.
4. Leave the channel connected for a few hours and grep the log for
   `XiaoYi [primary]: Disconnected`; drops occur every few minutes to tens of
   minutes, occasionally twice within 40s (2026-10-22 21:55:11 and 21:55:48).

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** the client shows nothing for the whole turn; on a 7m36s turn the
  user reasonably concludes the bot is hung. Disconnects are silent about their
  cause, and any final message produced while `_ws.closed` is true is dropped —
  `send_json()` returns `False` and no retry/replay follows.
- **Expected:** (a) a user-visible working/status frame at a configurable
  interval while a turn is in flight, so the client never looks frozen;
  (b) the disconnect log carries the WS close code/reason; (c) a final message
  that cannot be delivered because the socket dropped is persisted and replayed
  after `Reconnected successfully`, instead of being silently lost.

## Logs / Screenshots

See the two log blocks under **Description** (turn with no output; repeated
disconnects 37s apart).

Code pointer for the silent-drop case — `xiaoyi/channel.py`:

```python
async def send_json(self, data: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    """Send a JSON payload. Return True on success."""
    if not self._ws or self._ws.closed or not self.connected:
        return False
    try:
        await self._ws.send_json(data)
        return True
    ...
```

`await self._ws.send_json(...)` succeeds as soon as the frame is written to the
local transport; a peer that has already gone away is not detected until the
next receive, so a `True` return is not proof of delivery.

## Additional Notes

**Local workaround already validated on 2.2.2.post1 (not submitted as a PR —
happy to open one if the maintainers want it):**

- emit an immediate ack frame when a turn starts (so the client stops showing a
  blank screen), then a `status-update(working)` frame every 12s for the
  lifetime of the turn;
- interval configurable via `XIAOYI_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL` (set to `0` to disable),
  hard-capped at 1800s per turn;
- all keepalive tasks cancelled on `stop()` / disconnect, so no task leaks.

Result in the log — the same long turn that previously produced silence now
keeps the client refreshed, and the frames are accepted (`ok=True`):

```
2026-10-23 15:56:38 | INFO | xiaoyi/channel.py:1469 | XiaoYi: keepalive(working) session=... waited=12s ok=True
2026-10-23 15:56:50 | INFO | xiaoyi/channel.py:1469 | XiaoYi: keepalive(working) session=... waited=24s ok=True

2026-10-23 15:57:14 | INFO | xiaoyi/channel.py:1469 | XiaoYi: keepalive(working) session=... waited=48s ok=True
```

prs.title: fix(scroll): recognize url-referenced media in tool-result folding
prs.body:
## Description

When a chat session accumulates enough turns to trigger context compression, historical completed tool results are inspected by `ScrollContextManager._tool_result_fold_candidates()` to collapse long or media-carrying results into compact pointer stubs (`[scroll folded] ...`).

Previously, `_tool_result_has_inline_media()` only checked for `source.get("type") == "base64"` or `source.type == "base64"`. URL-referenced media blocks (`source.type == "url"`), such as video, audio, or image outputs generated by `send_file_to_user` and similar tools, were not recognized as inline media. Consequently, these media tool results failed the `has_media` check and, having short text captions (<= 200 chars), were skipped by `_tool_result_fold_candidates()`.

As a result, uncollapsed media blocks were carried over across turns and re-spliced verbatim into rebuilt request payloads after compression. Subsequent model API requests failed repeatedly with errors such as `400: Video count 2 exceeds limit 1 per request`, permanently hanging the session for that channel.

This change extends `_tool_result_has_inline_media()` to recognize `source.type == "url"` with non-empty URL values for both dictionary-based and object-based sources.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8474

**Security Considerations:** None.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Why the issue happens

In `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py`:

```python
    @staticmethod
    def _tool_result_has_inline_media(block: Any) -> bool:
        ...
        for item in output:
            if ScrollContextManager._block_type(item) != "data":
                continue
            source = (
                item.get("source")
                if isinstance(item, dict)
                else getattr(item, "source", None)
            )
            if isinstance(source, dict):
                if source.get("type") == "base64" and source.get("data"):
                    return True
            elif getattr(source, "type", None) == "base64" and getattr(
                source,
                "data",
                None,
            ):
                return True
        return False
```

When a tool output provides a data block with a URL source (`source={"type": "url", "url": "https://..."}`), `_tool_result_has_inline_media` returned `False`.

In `_tool_result_fold_candidates`:

```python
    has_media = self._tool_result_has_inline_media(block)
    if (
        not has_media
        and self._tool_result_text_chars(block) <= _PRE_TRIM_MIN_CHARS
    ):
        continue
```

Because `has_media` was `False` and media tool results generally have little or no text characters (`<= 200`), the block was skipped and never folded. During context compression and payload rebuild, the raw media block remained in the active payload.

## The change

1. In `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py`, `_tool_result_has_inline_media` now also checks:
   - For dict sources: `source.get("type") == "url" and source.get("url")`
   - For object sources: `getattr(source, "type", None) == "url" and getattr(source, "url", None)`
2. In `tests/unit/agents/context/test_scroll_manager.py`:
   - Added `test_tool_result_has_inline_media_recognizes_url_sources` to test both base64 and URL sources across dict and object representations as well as negative cases.
   - Added `test_pressure_fold_recognizes_url_media_independently_of_text_length` to verify that tool results carrying URL media bypass the text length restriction and fold into pointer stubs under context pressure.

prs.title: fix(providers): read a gateway-reported status from the error text
prs.body:
## Description

`extract_status_code()` reads a status from the exception's `status_code`, `code`, `response`, and `body`/`details` fields, and falls back to the message text for one narrow gateway format — `Streaming response failed: [503] ...`.

An OpenAI-compatible gateway that fails mid-stream can instead report the status only inside the message text, for example `status_code=502, 请联系管理员处理！ (request id: ...)`. The OpenAI SDK raises a base `APIError` for such a response: no `status_code`, no `response`. The real status is present in the text, but the fallback does not recognise that shape, so `classify_model_error()` returns `unknown` — no same-model retry, no cross-model fallback, and the turn or scheduled job dies. The same upstream failure wrapped as a real HTTP 502 is `transient` and does fall back, so identical failures behave differently only because of how the gateway phrased them.

This adds one more narrow pattern for gateway error text, keeping the same deliberate narrowness the existing fallback documents: only `4xx`/`5xx` are read, so a success code quoted in a message (`expected status_code=200`) is never mistaken for a failure, and unrelated three-digit numbers in provider messages are still ignored.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8505

**Security Considerations:** None — this only affects how a provider error is classified, never what is sent to a provider.

prs.title: fix(task_tracker): bound the run completion callback and always clean up
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes the **run-cleanup half** of #8173: a chat run whose completion callback hangs or is cancelled never releases its entry in `TaskTracker._runs`, so the run stays `running` forever.

### Root cause

`TaskTracker._producer` clears its `_runs` entry and pushes the end-of-stream sentinel at the end of a `finally` block, *after* awaiting the `on_finished` completion callback. Two paths meant that cleanup never completed:

1. **The callback hangs.** `on_finished` is `ChatManager.mark_chat_finished`, which persists a completion marker under a lock shared with ~24 other manager methods. Lock contention or a stalled repo suspends the producer task *inside its own `finally`*. The task is then not done **and** the entry is still registered, so every status reader reports `running` — workspace reload is blocked and inbound messages are dropped with HTTP 409.
2. **The producer is cancelled mid-callback.** `CancelledError` is a `BaseException`, so it escapes the `except Exception` guard and skips cleanup entirely, leaving subscriber streams without their sentinel.

### The fix

- Run the callback through `asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(...))` bounded by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT`, so a hung callback is logged and given up on rather than holding the run open.
- Move the cleanup into a nested `finally` so it always runs.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8173

Deliberately *not* `Fixes` — see the scope note below.

### Scope — what this does **not** fix

This addresses the cleanup leak only. The other items from #8173 are **not** implemented here: the post-spawn connection health probe, the idle watchdog, `force` semantics on the reload/disable-enable paths, and in-channel hints for `/new` and `/stop` on backends that do not support them. Those are larger design questions and I would rather land the narrow fix first.

Note that the wedge is now **bounded** by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT` rather than eliminated: the run stays `running` while the callback runs, because `test_attach_or_start_reports_completion_before_becoming_idle` pins that ordering deliberately (it asserts `get_status == "running"` from inside the callback). Reordering the pop ahead of the callback would break that contract.

### What the new tests cover

New `tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py` (6 tests) covers a hung callback, a callback that raises, a callback that raises `TimeoutError`, a producer cancelled mid-callback, and `request_stop` against a slow callback. Waits are event-based rather than fixed sleeps.

Against unmodified source these fail on behavioural assertions (`run entry survived a hung completion callback`, etc.), not on import or attribute errors.

### Security Considerations

Not applicable — no change to channel auth, credentials, or config handling.

## Evidence

Verification is a real failure on unmodified source followed by the **same command** against the patched tree. Base is `5c56644a` (`main`), patch is `e2b7b8be`.

**1. Unmodified baseline — the new tests genuinely fail.**

```

=========================== short test summary info ============================

FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_completion_callback_timeout_is_logged_not_raised
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_cancellation_during_callback_still_clears_the_run
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_request_stop_with_a_slow_callback_does_not_wedge_the_run
4 failed, 1 passed in 8.32s
```

**2. Same command with the patch — all green.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py
.......................                                                  [100%]

```

**3. Full `tests/unit/app` with the patch — no regression.**

```

3118 passed, 1 skipped, 12 warnings in 58.77s
```

prs.title: fix(console): keep wide tables and code blocks scrollable in bubbles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Wide Markdown tables and long code blocks are silently clipped at the right edge of the message bubble with no horizontal scrollbar, on both desktop and mobile (#8811). On narrow screens the whole reply is clipped because the same mechanism stretches the entire markdown block past the viewport — users see half a row of text with no way to reach the rest (issue screenshots: 20-column table cut at C13, 505-char `text` block cut after ~100 chars, mobile message clipped at ~1/3 width).

Root cause: `v2.3.0.post1` introduced the `quoteResponse` wrapper (`HostBubbles.tsx`) between the SDK bubble content and the markdown root:

```
bubble-content → .quoteResponse (new, unconstrained) → .x-markdown → pre / table
```

The SDK bubble content sizes itself intrinsically, and a flex child defaults to `min-width: auto`. The markdown root is already capped (`min-width: 0; max-width: 100%`, the #5480 fix), but the new wrapper was not, so the `max-content` width of wide tables (`width: max-content` in the vendor `x-markdown` stylesheet) and long code lines widened the wrapper instead of scrolling inside the block — the bubble then clipped the overflow silently.

## Evidence

- Regression pinpointed with `git diff v2.3.0 v2.3.0.post1 -- console/src/pages/Chat`: the `quoteResponse` wrapper addition is the **only** chat-style change in that release, matching every symptom timeline in #8811 (worked on v2.3.0, broke on post1; desktop table/code clipping, mobile whole-message clipping, both width modes).
- Independent confirmations in the issue: @elain0205 verified the mechanism against the shipped `2.3.0b1/b2` console assets, and @ginohero confirmed the same on Docker `v2.3.0.post1`, including that the `quoteResponse` wrapper "has no `min-width: 0`".
- After the fix, the wrapper is capped like the markdown root, so tables and `pre` keep their own horizontal scroll (`max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto`, the #6852 rules) exactly as in v2.3.0.

## Fix

Give the wrapper the same shrinkability the markdown root already has:

```css
.quoteResponse {
  min-width: 0;
  max-width: 100%;
}
```

One rule covers all viewports; `env()`-free, no effect on normal-width content.

## Verification

- New regression test in `HostBubbles.test.ts`, following the existing source-assertion pattern used for the #5480 / #6852 / #6583 style fixes.
- `vitest run` on `HostBubbles.test.ts`, `index.module.test.ts`, `uiFontSizeCoverage.test.ts`: 53/53 passed.
- `tsc -b` clean; prettier and eslint clean on the changed files.

Fixes #8811

prs.title: fix(crons): persist cron and heartbeat token usage to turn records
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron and heartbeat runs drive `workspace.stream_query` directly instead of going through `Channel.consume_one`, so their token usage was never committed to the session's turn records. The console usage panel undercounts all scheduled task consumption: cron jobs (daily digests, reminders) and heartbeat runs make model calls whose usage never lands in the persisted turn records, even though the session data model already distinguishes cron sessions from chat turns.

Failed runs had a second, subtler problem: staged usage was never dropped, so a failed run's tokens could leak into the next run on the same reused session.

Fixes #8705

## Description

- Extract `commit_turn_usage` / `discard_turn_usage` into `qwenpaw.token_usage.turn_usage`:
  - `commit_turn_usage` resolves and persists one finished turn's usage, never raises
  - `discard_turn_usage` drops staged usage when a run does not finish normally
- `Channel._commit_turn_usage` and `_clear_session_turn_usage` now reuse the shared helpers (no behavior change)
- Cron executor: commit usage after a successful run; discard on timeout / cancel / error
- Heartbeat: same treatment for all three `stream_query` sites

prs.title: feat(console): support runtime base-path deployment
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8714.

Related context only: #1853, #8177, and #8316. This PR does not reopen, comment on, or close those older issues or pull requests.

Add an optional `QWENPAW_BASE_PATH` runtime setting for serving the standard prebuilt Console and API below a reverse-proxy prefix such as `/app/qwenpaw/web`.

#8316 covers custom builds through `VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME`. This PR covers the complementary runtime case: pip/uv/Docker users should not need to rebuild the Console or have a proxy rewrite minified JavaScript. Uvicorn `root_path` alone cannot solve the absolute URLs already present in that prebuilt output.

### What changed

- Add a validated base-path ASGI middleware using standard `root_path` semantics for HTTP, mounted static files, and WebSockets. The bare prefix redirects to a trailing slash; requests outside the prefix return 404.
- Inject only two explicit deployment values into `index.html`: its `<base href>` and a JSON-encoded runtime prefix. JavaScript and CSS response bodies are not rewritten.
- Build default Console entry and module URLs relative to the document base; resolve public assets, API calls, router/login navigation, and chunk-readiness probes against the same runtime prefix.
- Preserve the existing root and `/console` behavior when the setting is empty or `/`. Existing build-time `VITE_CONSOLE_BASENAME` and desktop behavior remain separate.
- Document runtime proxy configuration in English and Chinese. Proxies must preserve rather than strip the configured prefix.

The current login flow uses a Bearer token in `localStorage`, so no authentication-cookie path change is needed.

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

### Components affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Console
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Tests

Backend regression coverage includes prefix boundaries, `root_path`-aware URL generation, HTTP and WebSocket mounting, HTML token replacement, byte-identical static assets, SPA deep links, static containment, response compression, authentication, agent routing, and voice routing:

```text

5 passed in 0.22s (voice)
```


Build and formatting:

```text
Initial bundle: 10.00 MiB raw, 2.58 MiB Brotli across 11 assets.

```

Real Chromium verification applied the review patch to a clean worktree, rebuilt it, and used isolated QwenPaw processes, temporary working directories, and a dedicated test account:

- Opened `/app/qwenpaw/web/login`, loaded the prefixed logo, and logged in through the real form.

prs.title: feat(memory): allow a separate model for ReMeLight memory writing
prs.body:
## Description

`ReMeLightMemoryManager` currently injects the agent's main model into ReMe's `as_llm` component before every memory-writing job (`auto_memory` / `auto_dream` / `daily_paper` / `auto_fin`), so memory writing always consumes the same (often expensive) model used for chatting.

This PR adds an optional `memory_model` slot to `reme_light_memory_config`, so memory writing can run on an independent, lighter model:

- Uses `{"provider_id": "...", "model": "..."}` as the canonical format; a string is treated as a bare model name that inherits the main model's provider, including version-tagged names such as `qwen2.5:7b`.
- When unset, behavior is unchanged (main model is used).
- If dedicated-model construction fails (including non-`ProviderError` SDK exceptions), the manager logs a warning and injects the usable main model. Runtime failures before output can also fall back to that model. Main-model failures still propagate. Image jobs exclude the main-model fallback unless it has confirmed image support.
- The injected model is refreshed before every LLM job, so config changes take effect without a restart.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7664

**Security Considerations:** `memory_model` stores only a provider/model reference; no credentials are written to `agent.json` (API keys stay in the provider store).

prs.title: feat(memory): add reranker model center with service test, multi-query precision history and auto-verify
prs.body:
## Description

**What this PR does:** Adds a reranker model center to the reranker settings (Runtime Config → Memory & Retrieval), mirroring the existing Embedding model center, and upgrades the ranking-precision verification from a single binary smoke test into a multi-query, persisted, and optionally scheduled metric.

**Why:** A misconfigured reranker is currently invisible until retrieval quality degrades. The new center surfaces configuration status, current model, service verification (connectivity + latency) and a meaningful ranking-precision figure (`correct/total`, 10-run rolling average, sparkline) so a bad model is visible at a glance and its trend can be tracked across restarts.

The overview shows four slots: configuration status, current model, service verification and ranking precision.

### Changes

- **Reranker model center**: `RerankerModelCenter` overview on the same 4-column grid and status styles as the embedding card; session-scoped `rerankerVerificationStore` keyed by agent + service fingerprint, invalidated when the service config changes or the agent switches.
- **Service verification**: `POST /workspace/reranker/test` sends a real rerank request with sample documents (one clearly relevant plus two distractors) and returns latency, relevance scores mapped back to request order, and whether the expected most-relevant document ranked first. The outbound call runs under a hard `asyncio.wait_for` deadline, upstream HTML error pages are stripped to plain text, and the API key is masked in returned messages.
- **Multi-query precision**: runs a 5-case multi-domain suite (password / checkout / unit conversion / planet / subscription) and reports `total`, `correct_count`, `precision` and per-case `scores`/`correct`, instead of a single boolean.
- **Persistent history**: new `reranker_history.py` appends each verification to `WORKING_DIR/reranker_history.json`, keyed by a service fingerprint; new endpoint `GET /workspace/reranker/history?fingerprint=`.
- **Trend UI**: the precision slot shows `correct/total = NN%`, a 10-run rolling average and a mini SVG sparkline; history survives restarts and refreshes.
- **Scheduled auto-verification**: `RerankerConfig.auto_verify_interval_hours` (0 = off) plus a background sweep task in the app lifespan that probes due services.
- **i18n**: strings for the overview, verification and precision slots across all 7 locales.

## Type of Change
- [ ] bug fix
- [x] new feature
- [ ] breaking change
- [ ] documentation
- [ ] refactor

## Affected Components
- [x] core
- [x] console
- [ ] channels

- [ ] scripts

## Checklist

- [x] Ran and passed relevant tests: `pytest tests/unit/agents/memory/test_reme_reranker.py tests/unit/agents/memory/test_reme_config.py` → 29 passed.
- [x] Updated documentation where needed (locale strings; no user-facing docs changed).

## Testing
1. Open Runtime Config → Memory & Retrieval → Reranker; the model center shows four slots.
2. Configure a reranker base URL/key and click "Test"; the verification slot returns latency and the precision slot reports `correct/total = NN%` (e.g. `5/5 = 100%`).
3. Re-verify; the precision slot shows a 10-run rolling average and a mini sparkline, and records persist in `WORKING_DIR/reranker_history.json` across restarts.
4. (Optional) Set "Auto verify interval" to e.g. 24h; the background sweep probes due services and appends to history.

## Local Verification Evidence

**pre-commit run (changed files)** — exit code 0, all applicable hooks Passed:

**pytest** — 29 passed in 0.46s:

```
============================== 29 passed in 0.46s ==============================
```

prs.title: chore(deps): bump reme-ai to 0.4.2.3
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QwenPaw pins `reme-ai==0.4.2.0`. On Windows the memory tag index never rebuilds, so `/memory/tags` and `/memory/tag-files` answer 503 (#8580). The root cause was fixed in ReMe by canonicalizing legacy Windows paths instead of failing the rebuild — ReMe #717.

**That fix first ships in 0.4.2.3, not in 0.4.2.2.**

```
v0.4.2.1  has #717 = False
v0.4.2.2  has #717 = False
v0.4.2.3  has #717 = True
          "* fix(tag-index): canonicalize legacy Windows paths instead of failing rebuild
             by @BeiMu-new in https://github.com/agentscope-ai/ReMe/pull/717"
```

So bumping to 0.4.2.2 would install cleanly and still leave #8580 broken. This PR goes to 0.4.2.3, the first release that actually carries the fix.

0.4.2.3 requires `mcp<3,>=1.28.1`. QwenPaw pins `mcp 1.28.1`, which sits inside that range, so the new build resolves without touching any other constraint.

## Scope

Type: A (single-point fix)

Four places spell the version out and they move together:

- `pyproject.toml` — `reme-ai==0.4.2.0` → `reme-ai==0.4.2.3`
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/reme_light_memory_manager.py` — `_REQUIRED_REME_VERSION = "0.4.2.3"`
- `tests/unit/agents/memory/test_reme_start.py` — the monkeypatched `reme.__version__` must equal the constant, otherwise the version check fires before the assertion under test
- `tests/integration/test_reme_watch_contract.py` — the install line in the module docstring

## Self-review

1. **Only the target semantics move** — `git diff --stat` is 4 files, `+4 −4`. Every changed line is a version literal.
2. **Callers of `_REQUIRED_REME_VERSION`** — three uses, all inside `reme_light_memory_manager.py`: the startup comparison, the mismatch message and the reinstall hint. None of them branch on a specific version, so the value change is safe.
3. **`0.4.2.0` left in place where it is a historical statement** — the comment in `reme_tags.py:59` describes what 0.4.2.0 did (why the long-tag fallback exists) and `website/public/release-notes/v2.3.0.*` records what that release shipped. Rewriting either would make the record wrong; neither is the current pin.
4. **Local environment untouched** — the regression run below used a separate venv with 0.4.2.3 installed, so the running instance keeps 0.4.2.0 until this lands.

## Test scope

Run with `PYTHONPATH=src` against a venv where `reme-ai==0.4.2.3` is installed:

- `tests/integration/test_reme_consistency_contract.py` + `test_reme_embedding_contract.py` + `test_reme_tags_contract.py` — **6 passed**
- `tests/integration/test_reme_watch_contract.py` — **1 passed**
- `tests/unit/agents/memory` — **303 passed** (1 pre-existing asyncio warning)
- `pre-commit run --files <the four files>` — all hooks passed

The tag-index contract above is the one that exercises the #717 path on a real ReMe application; it passes on 0.4.2.3.

## Evidence

```
$ python -c "import reme; print(reme.__version__)"
0.4.2.3                      # venv used for the regression run

$ PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/integration/test_reme_*_contract.py -q
6 passed                     # consistency + embedding + tags
1 passed                     # watch

$ PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/unit/agents/memory -q
303 passed
```

Refs #8580, ReMe #717

prs.title: fix(media): enforce the inline budget, rescale after a refusal, and report omissions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The downscale pass added in #8632 judged an image by its longest side alone. Three gaps followed from that, and they are fixed together because they meet on the same path.

**1. The byte budget and the side limit are two independent limits.**
A 2000x2000 PNG is well inside the 8192 px side limit and can still weigh 11.46 MiB, so the pass returned it untouched and the formatter rejected the request on bytes right afterwards. Both limits are now checked, and a formatter that provisions its own limits passes them down, so this pass and the cap cannot disagree about what fits.

**2. PNG has no quality knob.**
Every quality step emitted the same bytes and paid for another full deflate. The quality loop is skipped for PNG; only reducing the side makes it smaller.

**3. A rejection could not name the image it rejected.**
The retry log said "some media" while every image in the request was dropped, which left no way to tell which one the provider objected to. Each wire media block now gets a label (position, media type, decoded size) across the Anthropic `source`, OpenAI `image_url` and Gemini `inline_data`/`file_data` spellings, and the log names them.

**4. A rejection that named the media was replayed forever.**
Non-streaming recovery recognised only `413` / body-size wording. A `400 image dimensions exceed the maximum allowed size` fell through to `raise`, and because the offending block stayed in `state.context`, every later turn sent it again and collected the same rejection. The streaming path did strip media, but only for that one request — the identical loop, one turn later.

Both paths now classify a payload refusal, mark the historical copies as omitted once (`mark_media_omitted_after_overflow`) and retry. The stored message keeps its bytes, so the full-resolution file stays retrievable; only request copies are stripped.

**5. When the refusal is about the active turn, shrinking beats deleting.**
If nothing historical can be omitted, the refusal is about the image the user is asking about. Deleting it would be wrong. The request-scoped limits (`max_image_side`, `max_bytes`) are halved once for a single retry and restored afterwards, so the retry sends a smaller rendition while the stored message is untouched.

**6. Dropped media was invisible to the user.**
When media is replaced by a text placeholder the model answers as if the file had never been attached — indistinguishable from "the model ignored my image". The reply now carries `qwenpaw_media_omitted` (`{count, reason}`), which the Console renders as one system line and non-Console channels send as one extra text line.

## Scope

Type: B (state machine / retry), with a D-shaped surface because the notice crosses agents → channels → console.

- `src/qwenpaw/providers/capping_formatter.py` — `MAX_IMAGE_SIDE` moves here, beside the byte cap, so both media limits have one home; new `max_image_side` field (`ge=0`, default 8192).
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/utils/image_resize.py` — two limits decided independently, `max_side` threaded through, quality loop skipped for PNG.
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/model_factory.py` — reads the formatter's limits and passes them down; new `_describe_wire_media_blocks` / `_wire_media_label`.
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/utils/message_request_normalizer.py` — threads `max_bytes` / `max_side` to the resize pass.
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/react_agent.py` — payload-refusal classification on the non-streaming path, one-shot limit tightening with restore, per-response omission notice.
- `src/qwenpaw/app/channels/base.py` — `_media_omitted_notice`, sent with the existing fallback notice so channels without Console rendering see it too.
- `console/src/pages/Chat/fallbackNotice.ts`, `console/src/pages/Chat/index.tsx`, `console/src/locales/{en,zh}.json` — parse and render the notice.

## Self-review

1. **Callers of `downscale_image_bytes`** — `_rescale_source` is the only intermediate, `normalize_messages_for_model_request_async` the only entry point; both are updated, and both keep the old behaviour when the new keyword arguments are omitted (`max_side=MAX_IMAGE_SIDE`, `max_bytes=MAX_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES`).
2. **`MAX_IMAGE_SIDE` relocation** — `grep -rn MAX_IMAGE_SIDE src/` returns only `capping_formatter.py` (definition) and the modules that import it; no stale constant remains in `image_resize`.
3. **`max_image_side` as a new field** — declared with `ge=0` and the same default as before (8192), so every existing formatter subclass inherits it; `_normalize_messages_for_formatter` reads it with `getattr(..., MAX_IMAGE_SIDE)` so a custom formatter without the field still works.
4. **`_describe_wire_media_blocks`** — used only by `QwenPawAgent._last_wire_media_summary`, which returns `[]` when no formatter is active.
5. **Reversal** — `max_bytes <= 0` keeps its old meaning of "no byte limit" rather than shrinking forever.
6. **Both limits agree** — the resize pass receives `formatter.max_bytes` / `formatter.max_image_side` instead of the module constants, so a provider override cannot make the pass shrink to a different budget than the one enforced a moment later.
7. **Bounded retries** — both refusals share one budget (`max_recoveries`): a retry that is refused again recovers once more from the same budget instead of ending the turn, and a recovery that re-raises its own exception stops immediately. Limit tightening is one-shot per user turn: `_qwenpaw_media_limits_tightened_this_turn` blocks a second shrink after the borrowed pair is restored, so the same request shape is not sent twice, and `_reply()` resets it for the next turn.
8. **Stored history is not rewritten** — the omission pass only writes `qwenpaw_omitted_media_ids` metadata. `test_omissions_survive_resume_and_allow_new_images` verifies the state round-trips and a newly attached image is still sent.
9. **The notice is additive** — with no omission the channel output is byte-identical to the previous string (a single fallback line). An unparsable notice renders nothing rather than an empty system message.
10. **Non-streaming classifier stays narrow** — `is_request_body_too_large` is untouched (still `413` / body-size only); the media branch is a separate condition that additionally requires media on the wire and the existing payload-rejection classifier.

## Test scope

- Targeted: `test_context_overflow_recovery.py` + `test_react_agent_media_strip.py` + `test_media_omitted_notice.py` + `test_message_request_normalizer.py` + `test_image_resize.py` + `tests/unit/app/channels` — **383 passed, 7 failed**. The seven are the pre-existing video cases (`test_video_rejection_recovers_and_next_turn_skips_video`, `test_mixed_media_rejection_uses_media_free_retry`, `test_positive_video_limit_does_not_disable_next_valid_input`, `test_failed_video_retry_does_not_learn_or_mutate_history`, `test_video_cache_expires_and_is_scoped_to_model`); they fail the same way on the base revision, which I re-ran to confirm.
- Adjacent: `tests/unit/agents -k 'media or overflow or omitt'` — **466 passed, 3 skipped, 15 failed**. Seven are the video cases above; the other eight are `test_view_media` audio/video conversions, which fail identically when the suite runs against the PR base source (`8c7c3127`) — local ffmpeg behaviour, not this PR.
- Console: `fallbackNotice.test.ts` — **6 passed**; `sdkHostIntegration.test.tsx` + `ChatPage.coverage.test.tsx` — **196 passed**; `tsc -b --noEmit` clean; `prettier --check` clean
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` — all hooks passed (black reformatted two test files on the first pass, clean on the re-run)

## Evidence

A 2000x2000 high-entropy PNG, well inside the side limit and far over the byte cap:

```
INPUT   side=2000x2000  bytes=12,015,257  (11.46 MiB)
        longest side 2000 <= 8192 -> the old side-only check returned this unchanged
OUTPUT  bytes=596,065  (0.57 MiB)  media_type=image/png  changed=True
        under 2 MiB cap: True

max_bytes=0 -> unchanged=True  (11.46 MiB)
```

The media labels, one per wire spelling:

```
#1 image/png 1.0 MiB      (Anthropic source)
#1 image/jpeg 1.0 MiB     (OpenAI image_url data URL)
#1 image/webp 1.0 MiB     (Gemini inline_data)
```

The refusal path, measured before and after the change:

```
before  marked=0  max_image_side=8192  qwenpaw_media_omitted=ABSENT
after   marked=8  max_image_side=8192 (history had blocks to omit)

active-turn only:
before  marked=0  side=8192 bytes=2097152
retry   side=4096 bytes=1048576
after   side=8192 bytes=2097152 (restored)
```

Removing the new classifier turns two tests red; removing the streaming omission call turns one red — both restored afterwards.

Every fix in this revision was falsified on its own: reverting the recovery loop, the resize-ineffective gate, the audio-count branch, the omit-keeps-active-image condition, the per-turn notice dedupe, or the tool-parameters short circuit each turns exactly its own test red, and the code is restored afterwards.

prs.title: feat(chat): add append-only session storage, paginated history and native Turn forks
prs.body:
## Description

Long conversations previously depended on mutable session snapshots and loading large history windows. That made historical Turn forks, runtime recovery, and reconnect behavior difficult to keep consistent. This branch introduces durable per-session SQLite history with append-only facts and rebuildable projections, and bounds the Console's history and replay work.

This draft covers the complete branch, including:

- Store message/content facts and immutable context revisions separately from current message/runtime projections. Rebuild projections without rewriting historical facts; reuse state component references for usage-only revisions and avoid redundant block events.
- Migrate legacy JSON sessions and history databases, preserve available historical messages, reconstruct legacy runtime where possible, and retain provider session/Turn mappings.
- Fork completed Turns with their historical runtime boundary. Codex/Qoder branches use native provider interfaces and stored Turn mappings rather than rebuilding third-party context. Failed native restoration/reset must not silently create a fresh context.
- Add stable history pagination, bounded rendering, message-directory navigation, streaming/reconnect replay, and safe session switching/deletion.
- Integrate storage with clear/new, compact, dump/load, Scroll/Recall, cloning, backup, checkpoints, statistics, and PawApp/SDK session access. Preserve reset and checkpoint restoration semantics; roll back failed/cancelled compaction.

## Issues addressed

- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/3915 — measured virtual rendering, incremental history loading, scroll anchoring, and bottom-follow behavior.
- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/3923 — bounded Console history reads and windowed rendering address the full-history/full-DOM paths. This does not claim a measured memory result for the reporter's exact dataset or include all optional bundle-size suggestions.
- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8134 — durable display history is independent of the model's compacted context.
- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/6542 — completed turns persist their final messages and session state. This covers the real-time archival proposal, not zero loss of uncommitted output after a forced process termination or external notebook synchronization.
- Fixes https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8744 — durable display history is independent of the model's compacted context.


## PRs superseded after merge

The following PRs can be closed manually as superseded after this PR merges. This is a functional replacement assessment, not a claim that every change from those PRs was incorporated:

- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7361 — history pagination and virtual rendering.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/7542 — access to pre-compaction history through paginated durable transcripts. Retention changes are outside this PR's scope and are not a prerequisite for replacing the pagination implementation.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/6704 — use the completed-Turn Fork implementation, including the latest completed turn, rather than adding a second whole-session fork path.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8091 — route-driven active-chat tracking also covers sidebar navigation and cached sessions.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/1481 — metadata updates exclude messages without mutating the caller's session.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/803 — per-agent last-chat persistence and route restoration replace the older global storage-key approach.
- https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/1489 — backend cancellation, cancellation-state persistence, and history/reconnect handling replace the older cancel-endpoint approach.

Some of these behaviors are inherited from main and retained by this branch; they are not all new contributions of this PR. PR #7413 / issue #7410 are already addressed by main's #8212, and the workspace-owned HistoryStore work in #8471 is superseded by #8482 and subsequent maintenance. Those are independent cleanup items, not closure claims of #8532.

**Security Considerations:** Session ownership and active-session deletion checks remain part of history access. This PR does not include local databases, conversation exports, screenshots, profiling dumps, or environment credentials. Provider contexts remain provider-owned.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Refactoring
- [x] Breaking change (session storage representation changes; legacy data is imported)
- [ ] Documentation

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Console
- [x] Channels (Console streaming/reconnect)
- [x] Tests
- [x] Scripts / Deploy (replay verification tooling)

## Checklist

- [ ] `pre-commit run --all-files` passes (changed-file checks passed; no all-files claim)
- [ ] Full default test configuration is green (see known failures below)
- [ ] Documentation published in this repository
- [ ] Ready for review / merge

## Testing

Focused implementation-audit validation on **2026-11-06**, against HEAD **95bc9c73e8108a7645332087149c209d56a2a14c**:

- Frontend: **111 passed** across 10 files covering measured/history windows, route gates, bottom follow, large-session handling, ownership, transitions, initialization, and replay parsing.
- Backend: **207 passed** across the selected persistence, migration, projection-rebuild, Fork/catalog, replay, task, and lifecycle tests. This includes the regression test from #7413 run from a temporary file, without adding it to this PR.
- These are focused regressions, not a new full-suite run or browser E2E run. No fresh Edge performance measurement, OS-level SIGTERM test, Windows extended-path test, or browser network-disconnect injection is claimed.

Earlier branch validation retained for context (not rerun as a full suite at the HEAD above; groups overlap and should not be summed as unique coverage):

- Chat storage suite: **478 passed** after each of the three storage optimizations.
- Backend combined regression: **2337 passed, 1 platform skip**.
- HTTP integration retry (backup, checkpoints, conversation commands, PawApp context): **54 passed**, using the existing `QWENPAW_INTEGRATION_HTTP_TIMEOUT=180` setting after initial fixture startup timeouts.
- SDK lifecycle: **2 passed** with a 180-second test timeout after a 45-second dependency metadata scan timeout. Other plugin/SDK contracts: **147 passed**.
- TypeScript noEmit, changed-file pre-commit checks, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Frontend full single-worker run: **657 files passed / 2 failed**; **8475 tests passed / 1 failed / 2 expected failures / 9 skipped**. This was not a green default full run.
  - JobDrawer JSON validation did not display its error within `waitFor`; the unchanged complete file passed on isolated retry (**29 passed**).
  - PawApp SDK session routing exceeded the default 10-second initialization hook timeout, also on isolated retry (**45 passed / 9 skipped**). With command-line `--hookTimeout=30000`, all **54 passed**. No source or test configuration was changed to hide this limitation.

## Evidence

Historical terminal results retained from the earlier branch validation:

```text
pytest tests/unit/app/chats/ -q
478 passed

Backend combined regression
2337 passed, 1 skipped

HTTP integration retry
54 passed

SDK lifecycle / other contracts
2 passed / 147 passed

vitest run --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  2 failed | 657 passed (659)
Tests       1 failed | 8475 passed | 2 expected fail | 9 skipped (8487)

Isolated JobDrawer retry: 29 passed
Isolated sessionRouting --hookTimeout=30000: 54 passed
```

Earlier behavior checks (not repeated in the 2026-11-06 focused audit):

- A database generated by the previous implementation containing four `block.committed` events was rebuilt twice: messages, runtime, and original events remained unchanged.
- Eight database command scenarios and sixteen Fork boundaries verified state preservation, with Codex/Qoder native reset failure protection probes.
- Console browser flow: create two Turns, fork the first, continue with the remembered first-Turn marker, fork again, and reload. Both forks closed the dialog, navigated automatically, and incremented the name. Long-history scrolling and the message directory also loaded.
- Synthetic SQLite usage-write benchmark (1000 context entries, about 1 KiB each): median **34.174 ms → 4.975 ms**, SQL statements **2013 → 10**. JSON state reading/parsing remains; this is not a production latency guarantee.

## Additional Notes

This is a large draft covering the whole storage/pagination branch, not just its final optimization commit. Historical legacy runtime reconstruction can be approximate where exact snapshots were never stored. The previously recorded browser smoke used the built-in agent; native-provider behavior was covered by automated adapters/probes, not a fresh five-Turn provider UI run in this validation. Reconnect checks do not claim a new browser network-disconnect injection run.

Local verification artifacts are retained outside the Git diff. The known default frontend timing failures and upstream CI results need review before promoting this PR out of draft.

prs.title: fix(loop): record every tool call appended during a reply so the doom-loop gate can fire
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`DoomLoopGate` is enabled in the default mode (`window_size=3`,
`similarity_threshold=0.5`, `stop` after 4 hits) but it has never fired. A reply
that repeats the same tool call with the same arguments — the case in #8712,
where one `Bash` invocation was approved 14 times in 70 seconds — ran until the
user pressed stop twice.

The gate's auto-recording path de-duplicated on the **message** id:

```python
last_msg = context[-1]
if last_msg.id == state.last_recorded_msg_id:
    return
```

Inside a single reply, every assistant message is written with the same
`state.reply_id`: `agentscope` creates one `ReplyContext(reply_id=…)` per reply,
and `AgentState.append_context` either extends the existing message or appends a
new one with that same id. From the second iteration on, `last_msg.id` already
equalled `state.last_recorded_msg_id`, so the function returned before recording
anything and the history never grew past one entry. A three-entry window can
never fill, `_detect_repetition` can never return true, and no stage is reached.

This is not specific to shell calls: no tool, in any reply, could trip the gate.

## Scope

Type: B (state machine / dedup)

One file of production code plus one test file. `agents/tools/shell.py` is not
touched: the earlier revision of this PR changed `_with_shell_guard` to stop
overriding the result state with `ERROR`, on the theory that the tool result
never reached the model. That theory was wrong — the result does reach the
model — so that change is reverted, and this PR fixes the layer that actually
dropped the repetition.

## Self-review

1. Failure — a block with an unexpected shape cannot raise: the scan skips any
   block whose type is not `tool_call`/`tool_use`, and reads fields defensively
   for both block objects and plain dicts.
2. Timeout — not applicable: the gate has no timeout path; it runs synchronously
   inside `check()`.
3. Skipped — a text-only iteration (`has_tool_calls is False`) records nothing;
   an empty or non-list `content` returns early.
4. Concurrency — one iteration that carries several parallel tool calls records
   every block it contains (`test_blocks_of_one_iteration_are_all_recorded`).

## Evidence

Recorded against the real `DoomLoopGate` with synthetic contexts that mirror
what the agent writes:

| context | history after 8 iterations | gate fired |
| --- | --- | --- |
| same message id every iteration (before) | stays at 1 | never |
| same message id, blocks appended (after) | 8 | iteration 4 |

Production logs agree: `qwenpaw.log` since 13 November contains no
`DoomLoopGate` and no `Doom loop` line at all.

The concrete case from #8712 — 14 identical `Bash` calls inside one reply — now
reaches the configured stop stage instead of running to completion.

## Test scope

- Target: `tests/unit/loop/test_doom_loop_auto_record.py` — **7 passed**.
- Red/green: with the `src` change reverted the same file gives **2 failed**
  (including the three-iteration stop case), and **7 passed** once restored.
- Adjacent: `tests/unit/loop` — **99 passed**.
- Adjacent: `tests/unit/modes` + `tests/unit/agents/tools/test_shell_resources.py`
  — **196 passed, 4 skipped** (the skips are the platform-gated resource tests).
- Lint: `pre-commit run --files` — all hooks passed.

Fixes #8712.
