prs.title: fix(skills): keep rollback backups until every workspace is restored
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Rolling back a multi-workspace skill install had five separate weak points. Each one can lose a skill or keep a user waiting, and they sit on the same code path, so they are fixed together.

**1. A restore failure abandons the remaining workspaces.**
`_restore_workspace_skills` used to run every target inside one `try`, so the first failure skipped the targets that had not been undone yet, and the `finally` cleanup then removed their backups as well. A target whose restore failed now keeps its backup, and every target is attempted before the first error is re-raised.

**2. The restore marker is written after the backup has been consumed.**
`_restore_workspace_skill` renames the backup back into place and only then sets `files_restored`. A process killed inside that window leaves a target that looks un-restored while its files are already back, and the next pass would delete the skill as "nothing to put back". A target with no backup but a present skill directory is now counted as restored.

**3. Overwriting an installed skill waits for the old tree.**
`install_staged_skill_dir` deleted the previous tree inline before installing. `rmtree` cannot be interrupted, so cancelling an overwrite had to wait for every file of the old tree. The old tree is now renamed aside first and reclaimed on a daemon thread; cancellation is honoured before anything is replaced.

**4. Pre-existing defect, not introduced by #8477: deleting a skill can lose all three copies.**
`garbage_collection` of the rollback `finally` removed every backup root unconditionally, including the root of a target whose restore had just failed. After a failed restore that backup is the only copy of the previous version on disk, so the cleanup turned a recoverable failure into permanent loss. It is now kept and marked, so a later sweep does not reclaim it either.

**5. New cleanup logic (not a defect fix): reclaim stale rollback roots.**
Backups now live under `skills/` instead of the workspace root, so a restore is a sibling rename rather than a second copy. That move leaves a root in place when a process is killed mid-install, so the next install sweeps the roots that are neither in use nor marked as retained.

## Scope

Type: B (state machine / cancellation / rollback)

Touches `src/qwenpaw/agents/skill_system/store.py`, `src/qwenpaw/app/routers/skills.py` and three test files.

## Self-review

1. **Failure** — `test_restore_continues_after_one_target_raises` (a restore that raises no longer strands the later targets) and `test_failed_restore_keeps_its_backup` (the kept root survives the cleanup and carries the marker).
2. **Cancellation** — `test_cancelled_overwrite_does_not_wait_for_the_old_tree` (measured 6.4s → 0.013s over 12k files) and `test_install_failure_moves_the_old_tree_back`.
3. **Skip / no-op paths** — `test_missing_backup_with_present_skill_counts_as_restored` (the killed-between-rename-and-marker case) and `test_restore_without_a_backup_removes_the_new_copy`.
4. **Concurrency** — the reclaim runs on a named daemon thread and `test_stale_rollback_roots_are_reclaimed_once` covers two installs in one skills directory; the retained marker is what keeps a failed restore's root out of a later sweep.

## Test scope

- Targeted: `test_staged_install.py` + `test_skills_router_pool_ops.py` + `test_skills_router_helpers.py` — **191 passed**
- Adjacent: `tests/unit/agents/skill_system` — **811 passed**; `tests/unit/app/routers -k skill` — **270 passed**
- `pre-commit run --files <the five files>` — all hooks passed

## Evidence

Before this change, injecting one restore failure across three targets left the later targets on the new content with their backups already deleted. After it, the failing target keeps its backup (marked) and the remaining targets are restored.

Overwriting a 12k-file skill took **6.4s** to cancel (the inline `rmtree`) and **0.013s** after the tree is renamed aside.

```
# cancellation timing, 12k files
before: 6.4s   (rmtree of the old tree inside the request)
after : 0.013s (rename aside + daemon reclaim)
```

Refs #8013

prs.title: fix(console): reserve top and side safe-area insets in full-screen containers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In full-screen mobile containers (PWA installed in standalone mode, home-screen shortcuts, edge-to-edge WebViews), the console renders underneath the system status bar: the clock and battery icons overlap the header and sidebar brand, and the first row of UI becomes partially unreadable and untappable (#8796). `console/index.html` declares `viewport-fit=cover`, which extends the layout viewport into the notch/status-bar area — the app already insets the **bottom** edge (17 `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` usages across the console) but never the top or side edges (`git grep "safe-area-inset-top" -- console/` returns zero matches), so the header and sidebar start at the physical top edge of the screen.

## Evidence

- Reproduction and verification steps on upstream `main` are documented in #8796 (standalone PWA / WebView only — in a normal mobile browser tab the browser chrome occupies the status bar region and `env(safe-area-inset-top)` resolves to `0px`, which is why this only surfaces in full-screen containers).
- The fix mirrors the established bottom-edge pattern: `env()` resolves to `0px` on desktop windows and in normal mobile browser tabs, so both edits are no-ops outside full-screen containers — no visual change for regular desktop/browser users.

## Fix

- **Root layout** (`console/src/layouts/index.module.less`, `.mainLayout`): add `box-sizing: border-box` plus `padding-top/left/right: env(safe-area-inset-*, 0px)`. One rule covers every in-app page (sidebar, header, content) while the page background keeps bleeding behind the notch.
- **Login page** (`console/src/pages/Login/index.tsx`): the login route renders outside `MainLayout`, so its own `100vh` root gets the top/bottom insets in its inline padding, keeping the centered card clear of the status bar.

Scope notes:
- The `100dvh` suggestion from the issue is already implemented on `main` (`@supports` block at ≤768px), so no change was needed there.
- The desktop OS shell (`console/src/os/useOsStyles.ts`, `MENUBAR_H`) is intentionally left untouched: `env()` is constant `0px` in the desktop webview today, so adding the calc would be an unverifiable no-op. Happy to add it if maintainers see an edge-to-edge desktop case.

## Verification

- New regression tests in `layouts/index.module.test.ts` (source-assertion pattern used across the repo's layout tests): 17/17 pass.
- `tsc -b` clean; prettier and eslint clean on the changed files.

Fixes #8796

prs.title: feat(sdk): expand plugin SDK 1.1 APIs, lifecycle management, and developer tooling
prs.body:
## Description

Expand the public plugin SDK to version 1.1 so plugins can implement common features through supported APIs, with identity, permissions, coordination, and resource lifecycle managed by the host.

This PR adds or extends:

- Request identity, model selection, scoped conversation history, and run queries.
- Dynamic prompts, stop conditions, scheduled workflows, and pluggable shell execution backends.
- Skill market language/category filters and cancellation during installation.
- Managed threads and interactive processes, file uploads/downloads, workspace paths, and legacy storage import.
- Draft reading and safe replacement, frontend registration, and checkpoint save/preview/restore APIs.
- Process-based channel drivers, structured messages, approvals, delivery tracking, management operations, and HTTP/WebSocket ingress.
- Public types, SDK version checks, channel templates, and plugin testing tools.

Representative plugins were used for local validation. Their implementations and dedicated acceptance tests are excluded from this PR. Shared SDK regression tests remain self-contained.

**Related Issue:** None linked.

**Security Considerations:** Resource access remains scoped to the applicable plugin, user, workspace, and session. Checkpoint restoration uses host coordination and approval. Stale results cannot overwrite a changed draft. Remote execution failures do not automatically fall back to local execution. Cleanup must not report completion while owned threads or processes remain active.

- [x] New feature

### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.)

prs.title: fix(memory): refresh index after auto memory summary
prs.body:
﻿## Summary
- bump `reme-ai` from `0.3.1.8` to `0.3.1.9`
- update QwenPaw's expected ReMe version guard to match the new release
- drop the previous QwenPaw-side explicit index refresh workaround in favor of the upstream watcher lifecycle fix

## Related Issue
Fixes #4220
Refs agentscope-ai/ReMe#233

## Root Cause / Resolution
Maintainer feedback on this PR pointed to ReMe's file watcher as the better place to fix the stale memory-index timing gap. I followed up upstream in agentscope-ai/ReMe#233, which found that `BaseFileWatcher.close()` left `_stop_event` set and `start()` reused it. After a close/start cycle, the watcher could appear running while the watch loop exited immediately.

That upstream fix has been merged and released as `reme-ai==0.3.1.9`, so this PR now updates QwenPaw to consume that fix instead of carrying a QwenPaw-specific workaround.

## Tests

- `pre-commit run --files pyproject.toml src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/reme_light_memory_manager.py tests/unit/agents/memory/test_reme_light_memory_manager.py` - passed
- `git diff --check` - passed

prs.title: fix(memory): OpenViking follow-up cleanup, compatibility, and shutdown fixes
prs.body: ## Description Follow-up to #7613. This PR applies the plugin-local cleanups suggested during review, adapts automatic-recall budgeting to the host's current `HintBlock` format, and addresses the shutdown edge case accepted as a non-blocking follow-up in #7613. All changes are confined to `plugins/memory/openviking/`. **Related Issue:** Relates to #7613 **Security Considerations:** [If applicable, e.g. channel auth, env/config handling] ### Automatic-recall budgeting - Account for the actual `HintBlock.hint` content when reserving space for the host-generated recall wrapper. - Preserve the complete untrusted-history notice and bound the full injected recall text, rather than only the retrieved body. - Update budget tests to measure the actual hint content instead of fields from the previous message format. - Remove the hard-coded request-budget expectation derived from the old host prompt. Existing boundary tests verify the complete-message budget. - Update the toolkit-builder test's mock configuration to include `coding_mode.enabled`. ### Shutdown lifecycle - Store and reuse a single HTTP cleanup task across repeated and concurrent `close()` calls, rather than treating a cleared client reference as proof that cleanup completed. - Use `asyncio.shield()` so cancelling a caller's wait does not cancel the underlying cleanup. Cancellation still propagates to the caller. - Preserve the actual cleanup result. If HTTP cleanup fails, subsequent `close()` calls continue to return `False` instead of incorrectly reporting success. - Add regression coverage for repeated close after failure, caller cancellation followed by successful or failed cleanup, concurrent close calls, and repeated close after success. Preserve credential redaction in failure logs. ### Review follow-up **Item 1 — Reuse the base automatic-recall flow** The session-aware `auto_memory_search()` override is retained in this PR. I agree that the base flow could serve the current default configuration with query expansion disabled. The retained override passes the current QwenPaw session ID to OpenViking, allowing session-based query expansion when `query_expansion="auto"` is enabled through the documented source change. The READMEs now clarify that query expansion remains disabled by default, requires editing source and redeploying, and depends on available session history or an archive overview. No Console or Agent configuration switch is introduced. **Item 3 — Use one UTF-8 clipping implementation** Reuse `_clip_utf8()` for both automatic recall and explicit search. When truncation cannot retain meaningful text, return an empty string rather than a marker-only result. Preserve the complete untrusted-history notice and multibyte character boundaries. **Item 4 — Flatten persistence filtering** Combine role, persisted-ID, and pending-ID filtering into one pass, and calculate the `every_turn` condition once. Preserve the existing separation between successful append and successful commit progress. **Item 5 — Reduce test coupling** Move shared fixtures into `conftest.py` and centralize manager cleanup. Budget tests measure the complete injected message and check the intact notice and nonempty recalled body, rather than relying on hard-coded values derived from host prompt wording. ### Additional small cleanups - Use a direct relative import in `plugin.py`. - Return `await self._request(...)` directly in the two forwarding client methods. - Catch `httpx.RequestError` alone, since it already includes `TimeoutException`. The explicit-search small-budget guard is retained as a defensive useful-body check if the fixed source limits are reduced, with boundary-test coverage. ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Breaking change - [x] Documentation - [x] Refactoring ## Component(s) Affected - [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models) - [ ] Console (frontend web UI) - [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.) - [ ] Skills - [ ] CLI - [x] Documentation (website) - [x] Tests - [ ] CI/CD - [ ] Scripts / Deploy ## Checklist - [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes - [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks - [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass - [x] Documentation updated (if needed) - [x] Ready for review ### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.) - [ ] I ran `./scripts/check-channels.sh` (or `./scripts/check-channels.sh --changed`) and it passes - [ ] Official channel changes are covered in `tests/unit/channels/test_.py` (startup, shutdown and message delivery) - [ ] Shared host/process changes are covered in `test_channel_host.py` / `tests/unit/plugins/test_plugin_process.py` - [ ] Console changes retain the built-in contract checks in `tests/contract/channels/` ## Testing The tests cover complete-message recall budgets, oversized and multibyte results, intact safety notices, empty-result handling, persistence retries and deduplication, bounded caches, and shutdown lifecycle behavior. Shutdown regression tests verify that repeated or concurrent calls cannot report success before cleanup completes, caller cancellation does not cancel the shared cleanup task, and genuine cleanup failures remain reported as failures. ## Evidence ```bash PYTHONPATH="$PWD/src:$PWD" \ PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \ PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED=1 \ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ -p no:cacheprovider \ plugins/memory/openviking/tests ``` ```text 146 passed in 1.21s ``` ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --all-files git diff --check ``` All applicable hooks passed. ### OpenViking v0.5.2.1 — session-based query expansion For this verification, the request was changed in source to `query_expansion="auto"` and the commit policy was set to `auto`. The user first established the current project, then asked a follow-up using only “它的设备编号和维护窗口是什么？” After switching from R3 to R4, the server’s expansion followed the new project. Selected response fields from the OpenViking v0.5.2.1 query-expansion verification: ```json { "query_expansion": "used", "planned_queries": [ "它的设备编号和维护窗口是什么？请直接回答，不要主动调用工具，也不要读取本地文件。", "升级验收-R4-b610e899 设备编号", "升级验收-R4-b610e899 维护窗口" ] } ``` The corresponding answer returned `OV-UP-B610E899` and Sunday at 20:45. Additional checks confirmed that recall remained functional after a message-count-triggered commit retained recent messages, and a fresh session did not borrow the previous session’s history for query expansion. Long-term memory remains shared across those conversations. The `used` status alone is not treated as proof of query rewriting; the expanded `planned_queries` above provide that evidence. ## Additional Notes 1. The plugin keeps its own automatic-recall method to pass the current session ID to OpenViking. If `query_expansion` is changed from `"off"` to `"auto"` in the source code, OpenViking can use the current conversation's history to expand search queries. 2. Extracting the shared recall-budget helper into `BaseMemoryManager`, and updating both OpenViking and PowerContext to inherit it, is intentionally deferred to a separate follow-up PR.

prs.title: fix(console): prevent adjacent conversation backgrounds from overlapping
prs.body:
## Description

On a mouse-only browser, selecting one sidebar conversation and hovering the next paints a darker overlapping strip between their backgrounds. `SidebarSessionList` allocates 38px per conversation, but the 32px action button plus 6px top/bottom padding makes `SessionItem` 44px tall. The backgrounds therefore overlap by 6px.

Give the conversation background an explicit 36px height and 2px vertical padding, retaining the existing 2px bottom margin. This fits the virtual row, centers the label and 32px desktop action button, and keeps the existing 44px touch target and its negative margin unchanged. The existing touch media rule already produced a 36px background, explaining why this is not visible in every browser environment.

This PR changes one stylesheet only and is independent of the sidebar drag/group PRs.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)

## Testing

- `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`
- `npm run test:run -- src/components/SessionItem/SessionItem.test.tsx src/layouts/SidebarSessionList.test.tsx src/components/SessionGroupDnd/SessionGroupDnd.test.tsx` — 3 files, 54 tests passed.
- `npm run build:prod` — passed, including TypeScript, Monaco CSS, precompression, and initial-bundle checks.
- `npx prettier --check src/components/SessionItem/sessionItem.module.less` — passed.
- `pre-commit run --files console/src/components/SessionItem/sessionItem.module.less` — passed applicable hooks. Full-repository pre-commit was not run.

## Evidence

Real Chrome UI was loaded from both Vite and the production build using three synthetic conversations. The first conversation was selected through its actual button, then the adjacent conversation was hovered with the mouse; no active-class or hover-style injection was used.

Measured browser geometry:

| Input mode | Before background / row | After background / row | After gap | Action target after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mouse | 44px / 38px | 36px / 38px | 2px | 32px |
| Touch emulation | 36px / 38px | 36px / 38px | 2px | 44px |

Eight screenshot/geometry cases passed for mouse/touch × light/dark × 14px/20px UI font settings. Screenshots were captured and visually inspected. Text and button centers align with the row center. The production-build checks also opened the action menu, entered/cancelled inline rename (25px input within a 36px row), and activated/cancelled the real drag preview without saving changes.

The same production assets were additionally loaded in Electron 22.3.27 / Chromium 108 on Windows: mouse/touch × 14px/20px all measured 36px backgrounds in 38px rows, with 2px gaps and unchanged 32px/44px action targets. This was a Windows desktop check, not a physical touch-device or Windows 7 execution test.

Reproduce manually: use a mouse-only browser, open Chat with at least two conversations in the same expanded group, select the first, and hover the second. Before this patch their backgrounds overlap; after it they remain separated. Repeat with touch emulation to confirm that the existing touch layout remains separated.

prs.title: feat(providers): extract local model management into plugin
prs.body:
## Description

Extract local model management into a Plugin Provider. The plugin owns model downloads, llama.cpp installation and service lifecycle. The host keeps model selection and unified inference.

- Preserve existing users' configuration and model files.
- Move download dependencies into the plugin and import them lazily.
- Reuse plugin registration, dependency preparation and lifecycle management.

### TODO / Follow-ups

- **CLI / doctor:** Add shared plugin CLI registration, then restore local model commands and diagnostics. They are deferred even when the plugin is installed. Other core commands and diagnostics remain available.
- **SDK release:** Assign a release version to the contract additions; the SDK version currently remains 1.0.0.

### Advantages

- Makes local model management optional, preserves existing model data, and prevents cloud-only startup from restoring unused llama.cpp services.
- Measured cloud-only initialization: **1 → 0** local managers, **6 → 0** local modules, and **~0.9 MiB lower host RSS** (5-run median, partial startup path). Core no longer requires ModelScope (**~21.7 MiB** of installed package files in the measured environment).

### Note
On macOS 15.7.4, local models can fail to start with the `piccolo-v1` runtime on both `main` and this PR due to a known Metal shader issue, and we'll track the upstream fix separately from the plugin migration. [llama.cpp #31360](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/31360)

prs.title: fix(channels): restore SDK and worker logs after channel isolation
prs.body:
## Description

Restore troubleshooting logs lost after channel isolation (#8187) across all 18 migrated channels and the host-side Console, queue, and delivery paths.

- Preserve SDK and worker log levels and source context, deduplicate Lark output, redact recognized credentials, and keep routine startup traces at `DEBUG`.
- Use bounded queues and separate writer threads so slow log consumers do not block worker IPC or the host event loop. Reserve queue capacity for warnings and errors, and summarize dropped worker logs.
- Restore platform-specific diagnostics, including QQ IP allowlist rejection and streaming fallback, WeChat API return codes, and XiaoYi stream completion.
- Add rate-limited summaries when the shared response route table fills up or attachment-only requests accumulate. Distinguish routes retained after an uncertain inbound ACK, `finish` skipped after a text-merge failure, and `finish` RPCs with an unknown result.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8814. This PR improves diagnosis; it does not change route eviction, retries, or delivery semantics.

prs.title: fix(drivers): persist rotated MCP OAuth refresh tokens
prs.body:
## Description

Persist rotated refresh tokens for remote MCP OAuth authorization-code credentials. The standard exchanger previously returned only the new access token and its lifetime. When the authorization server invalidated the previous refresh token, the following refresh sent that stale value and failed with `invalid_grant`.

The credential provider now saves the replacement refresh token with the new access token. It keeps the stored refresh token when the response omits a replacement and still accepts existing two-value custom exchangers. This follows [RFC 6749 section 6](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6749#section-6).

Related to #7053 and the earlier work in #7066. The regression test exercises the remote MCP driver credential path, which is separate from the ChatGPT subscription provider mentioned in #7066.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Tests

## Testing

The regression test runs two consecutive refreshes against a mock token endpoint and checks both the stored refresh token and the token sent on the next request. It also covers a provider that omits a replacement.

## Evidence

On upstream `main`, the rotation case failed because the credential store held `initial-token` after the response issued `refresh-1`. The case with no replacement passed.

With this patch:

```text
$ python -m pytest -q tests/unit/drivers tests/unit/app/routers/test_mcp_oauth_flows.py tests/integration/test_driver_mcp_oauth_flow.py

prs.title: fix(console): repair CJK emphasis boundaries in chat Markdown
prs.body:
## What problem this solves `**中文。**后面` and `__中文！__后面` never parse: CommonMark only accepts a closing delimiter run that is right-flanking, and a run preceded by CJK punctuation and followed by a CJK letter is neither right- nor left-flanking. The renderer therefore shows the raw markers instead of bold text. The Markdown source is never rewritten. The fix is one instance-level marked tokenizer extension. ## Scope Type: C (new renderer behaviour, no data or protocol change) | Input | Stock | This PR | |---|---|---| | `**甲。**乙` | literal markers | `甲。乙` | | `__甲。__乙` | literal markers | `甲。乙` | | `**甲，**乙` … `**甲？**乙` | literal markers | `甲，乙` | | single `*甲。*乙` / `_甲。_乙` | literal | unchanged | | ASCII punctuation before the closer (`**甲.**乙`) | literal | unchanged | | ASCII follower (`**甲。**b`, `**甲。**1`) | literal | unchanged | | nested or unbalanced runs (`***甲。***乙`) | stock result | unchanged | | CJK punctuation after the closer (`**甲。**，`) | stock result | unchanged | | already-valid emphasis before a CJK span (`**标准** **甲。**乙`) | two spans | two spans | | fenced code, inline code, HTML | verbatim | verbatim | | link label and image alt | verbatim | verbatim | | link `href` / `title`, image `src` / `alt` / `title` | unchanged | unchanged | | tables | literal in cells | emphasis in cells | Where the extension does not take over, the stock tokenizer result is used unchanged. ## How it works `console/src/utils/markdownCjkStrong.ts` registers one `tokenizer.emStrong` override: - it runs only when the source starts with `**` or `__`; - `findCandidate` accepts only the agreed shape — CJK punctuation before the closer, CJK letter after it — and takes exactly one candidate. If the span contains an inline character that may belong to another construct (`` ` ``, `$`, `<`, `~`, `[`, `\(`, a bare URL), it returns `false` at once and the stock tokenizer owns the span. That single guard covers code spans, formulas, HTML, strikethrough, links and images without tracking any of them separately; - when the candidate survives that guard, `findCloserAroundInlineNodes` looks for the closer outside any *complete* inline node, using marked's own `codespan` and `link` tokenizers so a closer inside a code span or a link is not taken; - `indexSuffixBalance` scans the same masked source once, from the end, with marked's own closer rules per delimiter, and records for every offset how many markers the stock parser could still match after it. The extension only takes over when that index proves the native parser cannot close the run; otherwise it returns `false`; - the body is limited to 4096 characters. `console/src/components/ChatMarkdown/ChatMarkdown.tsx` is a local counterpart of the SDK's Markdown component. The SDK builds its `config` internally and never forwards one, so the only way to register an instance-level extension without touching global tokenizer prototypes is to compose the same pieces ourselves: math, footnotes, citations, streaming cursor, media, link handling, HTML sanitisation and the code-block slot are all preserved, and the only difference from the SDK is the extra extension. `AssistantMarkdown` renders through it; `vite.config.ts` inlines the SDK subpaths the wrapper imports so the unit tests resolve them the same way the app does. ## Known limitation The extension does not only recover delimiters the native parser left unconsumed. When it takes over a span that contains a run the native parser *did* consume, it re-pairs: `**甲。**乙**丙，**丁` - stock: `**甲。乙丙，**丁` - this PR: `甲。乙丙，丁` The stock result already bolds `乙`; this PR splits that pairing and bolds `甲。` and `丙，` instead. Recovering more CJK text is not worth changing input the parser renders correctly today, so this revision is held rather than merged. ## Evidence - `console/src/utils/markdownCjkStrong.test.tsx`: 90 tests through the real renderer — `XMarkdown` for the emphasis cases (agreed punctuation family, follower family, protected regions, repeat-render stability, streamed-versus-complete equality, two-span preservation) and `ChatMarkdown` for the formula cases (one KaTeX node with its payload, and a closer inside a formula producing no emphasis), plus cost guards on the scan and on native fallback. - `console/src/pages/Chat/AssistantMarkdown.test.tsx` and `HostBubbles.render.test.tsx`: 22 tests pass, covering the streamed code-block pipeline that this component reuses. - Headless Chrome, 1,000 repetitions of `**状态。**正常
` (measured by the reviewer): | version | time | |---|---| | this PR | ~38 ms | | recovery after native parsing, fast rejection index | 455 ms | | token-only | 874 ms | - `tsc -b --noEmit`, eslint and prettier pass on the changed files. ## Test scope - Target: `console/src/utils/markdownCjkStrong.test.tsx` (90 passed) - Neighbour: `console/src/pages/Chat/AssistantMarkdown.test.tsx`, `HostBubbles.render.test.tsx` (22 passed) - `tsc -b --noEmit`, eslint and prettier pass on the changed files. ## Status Held per review. The focused rendering tests and the three benchmarks (space-, `
`- and colon-separated inputs, including streaming updates) stay in the branch as the record of the problem. Two directions were named in review and neither is in this PR: reducing the repeated scans at the parser layer, and letting the Chat SDK accept Markdown extensions so a local renderer copy is not needed. The first is outside this repository; the second is a separate improvement.

prs.title: fix(agents): fall back to the global default when a run-config provider is disabled
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Disabling a provider on the Models page does not update agent run-configs that still pin a model on it (`agent.json` `active_model`). Every subsequent channel message (Feishu / DingTalk / WeChat / ...) for such an agent fails at model-build time with `ProviderError: Provider is disabled`, and the channel surfaces an unactionable "Internal error" to the end user. Worse, the run-config model selector only lists enabled providers, so the stale selection is invisible in the UI — the user cannot see or fix it without knowing to edit the run-config by hand.

## Evidence

- #8579 documents the full timeline: `kexin_token` disabled → 8 consecutive `Provider is disabled` failures from `create_model_and_formatter` over 7 minutes → run-config manually changed to `minmax` at 19:27:08 → zero errors afterwards.
- Code path: `create_model_and_formatter` only consulted the global default when the agent had **no** run-config model at all (`model_slot or manager.get_active_model()`); a configured-but-disabled slot raised immediately with no fallback and a message that named neither the provider nor the agent.
- New tests reproduce all three behaviors against stubbed providers (fallback, explicit-override error, no-usable-default error); the existing `tests/unit/agents` + `tests/unit/runtime` suites still pass (4869 passed, 8 skipped).

## Fix

In `create_model_and_formatter`, treat a persisted run-config model whose provider is disabled like an unset run-config model:

- Fall back to the global default chat model and log a warning naming the agent, the disabled slot, and the fallback slot.
- Explicit per-request model overrides (`model_slot_override`) still raise — the caller asked for exactly that model — now with an actionable message: `Provider 'X' is disabled; choose another model for agent 'Y'`.
- If no enabled global default exists either, raise an actionable error asking to reselect a model for the agent.

The async wrapper delegates to the sync factory, so both entry points are covered.

Scope note: directions 1 / 4 / 5 from the issue (cascading run-config updates when a provider is disabled, surfacing disabled selections in the UI selector, unifying validity checks) are intentionally left out — they are UI/product decisions; this PR fixes the runtime death path they all build on.

## Verification

- 5 new test cases in `tests/unit/agents/test_create_model_and_formatter_override.py` (fallback asserts the warning text; explicit override asserts the actionable message; no-usable-default is parametrized over missing/empty global slots).
- `pytest tests/unit/agents tests/unit/runtime`: 4869 passed, 8 skipped.

Fixes #8579

## Description

A reply observed on QwenPaw 2.2.2 displayed a table in the Console, but the DingTalk AI card displayed the pipe-table source as a paragraph. The source placed the table immediately after a text line, without a blank line:

```text
Details:
| key | value |
|---|---|
| a | 1 |
```

This patch supplies an explicit block boundary before pipe tables:

- Add `ensure_table_spacing()` to the DingTalk Markdown helpers and regular Markdown normalization.
- Apply only this table-specific transformation to the outgoing `StreamingUpdateRequest.content`, for both streaming and final updates. Keep `last_streamed_content` as the original text, so unchanged higher-sequence deltas remain acknowledged and do not trigger redundant sends or `PLATFORM_SEND_FAILED`.

prs.title: fix(plugins): log unhandled errors in RPC request handlers
prs.body:
## Description

`RpcPeer._dispatch_request` (`src/qwenpaw/plugins/execution/rpc.py`) catches any unexpected handler exception, replies with `-32603 internal error` / `INTERNAL_ERROR`, and then discards the exception (`_ = exc`). Nothing is logged, so a worker-side failure such as the `RESPONSE_SCOPE_LIMIT` error in the linked issue shows up only as a generic "internal error" with no traceback (the reporter had to patch `rpc.py` locally to see it).

This PR adds a module logger and calls `logger.exception(...)` (method name + traceback) in that `except Exception` branch before replying. The reply sent to the caller is unchanged.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8814. This covers only suggested fix 3 (do not discard exceptions in `rpc.py`); the route-eviction problem (fixes 1 and 2) is a design decision left to the maintainers, so the issue should stay open.

prs.body:
## Summary

Shell commands that sent email, made HTTP write requests, or uploaded local files could run without approval in AUTO and SMART modes. Neither Tool Guard nor governance had a detection rule for these operations.

## Changes

Add two `MEDIUM`-severity rules to the ruleset shared by Tool Guard and governance. Both paths use their existing approval logic when a rule matches.

- `TOOL_CMD_OUTBOUND_MAIL` detects `himalaya message send` and invocations of `sendmail`, `msmtp`, `mutt`, and `neomutt`.
- `TOOL_CMD_OUTBOUND_HTTP` detects common write requests and uploads made with curl, wget, and HTTPie, including explicit POST requests, `--data-binary @file`, and multipart file uploads.

## Testing

Added 23 regression cases covering outbound commands, read-only operations, and governance approval decisions. The tests verify that governance returns `ASK` in both AUTO and SMART modes for all three cases reported in the issue.

All 748 related tests passed locally. The tests evaluated approval decisions without sending email or uploading files.

prs.title: fix(channels): hide internal scaffolding at the display boundary
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Assistant text reaches the user through more than one egress, and two
families of model-facing bytes were being forwarded verbatim on all of them:

1. **Framework-injected context** — `<system-info>` / `<system-notification>`
   and the other `system-*` notes the runtime prepends to a turn. They are
   persisted as ordinary assistant text, so the renderer's structured-block
   switches never match them, a live stream shows them, and `GET /chats/{id}`
   shows them again after a reload.
2. **Reasoning a model inlined into plain text** — a `<thinking>…</thinking>`
   block written into the text block, or a truncated tail ending in a bare
   closing tag. Those bytes are in the same text block, so no display switch
   reaches them either.

## Filtering contract

This section is the definition the previous round asked for: what is
filtered, from which sources, and how incomplete input is treated.

### Sources

- `GET /chats/{id}` history playback (`app/chats/utils.py`).
- The channel renderer used by every structured send
  (`app/channels/renderer.py::message_to_parts`).
- The SSE serializer shared by Console and the web UI
  (`app/channels/base.py::_serialize_event_for_sse`), which also covers
  `console/channel.py` because both call the same method.
- The default reply path (`app/channels/base.py::_response_to_text`) used by
  channels that send the extracted string instead of rendering message parts.
- The streaming hooks (`app/channels/base.py::_on_stream_content_delta` and
  `_on_stream_msg_end`): the raw delta feeds a per-message scanner and only
  its output reaches the display buffer handed to `on_streaming_delta` and
  `on_streaming_end`. The event object and `streaming_buffers` stay raw.

### What is removed

- Reasoning blocks delimited by any of `think`, `thinking`, `analysis`,
  `reasoning`, in either case.
- `system-*` notices, closed by their own tag or by a shortened one
  (`</notification>` closing `<system-notification>`).
- A `<parameter …>` tool shell that opens a line and never closes.
- A bare closing tag with no opening tag: text before it was reasoning, text
  after it is the reply.

### What is never touched

- Text inside fenced code (backtick and tilde), indented code, blockquote
  lines, and inline code spans (single and double backticks).
- A closed `<parameter …>…</parameter>` pair.
- A *reasoning* opening tag that never closes, when the whole text contains
  no closing tag at all — every observed sample of that shape was a reply
  *discussing* the tag, and truncating at the opener deleted real replies.
  Injected `system-*` openers are not exempt: a live stream cannot know the
  closer is missing, so they stay hidden until the message ends.

### Incomplete tags

- **Streaming**: one scanner instance is kept for the whole message (message
  id + block index), not only while a block is being suppressed, so the open
  backtick run and the open fence survive between deltas. Injected `system-*`
  blocks are hidden by the same state — an opener starts hiding, its closer
  or a self-closing tag resumes output — and a partial tag prefix is buffered
  rather than emitted. Each delta is filtered exactly once; whole-message
  snapshots take one stateless pass.
- **Non-streaming**: one scan over the whole text. Whether an unclosed opener
  is reasoning or prose is decided once, from whether any closing tag exists
  in the same text.
- **Line endings**: paragraph boundaries use `\r?\n[ \t]*\r?\n`, so CRLF and
  LF behave identically.

## What is covered, and what is not

Covered: the four egresses above, balanced and bare closing tags, `system-*`
under any name, truncated tool shells, cross-chunk and cross-block splits,
LF and CRLF.

Deliberately not covered (separate discussion, as the review suggested):

- a naked closing tag with no opening tag *and* no surrounding prose — the
  current rule keeps the reply and drops the trailing paragraph, but it is a
  heuristic, not a general Markdown/XML inference mechanism;
- reasoning prose with no tag at all — it has no anchor, so separating it
  requires the parser to keep reasoning out of the text block;
- a scaffold block with no closing tag anywhere — left untouched as damaged
  data.

## Evidence

Targeted:

```
tests/unit/app/channels/test_scaffold_round10.py     29 passed
```

The cases are grouped by the two issues named as merge blockers:

```
fence closes, later reasoning still removed   [` and ~]   2 passed
tags inside a fence stay verbatim             [` and ~]   2 passed
unclosed fence keeps the remainder            ```         1 passed
closing fence split across chunks             5 chunks    1 passed
default reply path filters scaffolding                    1 passed
default reply path filters injected notes                 1 passed
```

Both fixes are load-bearing — reverting either one turns its cases red:

```
fence close reverted        -> 3 failed
                            (test_fence_closes_and_later_reasoning_is_still_removed[`]
                             test_fence_closes_and_later_reasoning_is_still_removed[~]
                             test_fence_state_survives_a_chunk_boundary)
default reply path reverted -> 2 failed
                            (test_default_reply_path_filters_scaffolding
                             test_default_reply_path_filters_injected_context)
```

The three cases from the twelfth review are load-bearing too:

```
inject state reverted       -> 1 failed
                            (test_sse_injected_block_across_three_chunks)
display buffer reverted     -> 1 failed
                            (test_streaming_hooks_show_only_the_public_reply)
state lifetime reverted     -> 1 failed
                            (test_sse_code_examples_survive_chunk_splitting)
```

## Test scope

- Target: `tests/unit/app/channels/test_scaffold_round10.py` (29 passed)
- Neighbouring: `tests/unit/app/channels` (214 passed)
- Context/history: `tests/unit/agents/context` + `tests/unit/app/chats`
  (1115 passed, 3 skipped)
- Pre-commit: all hooks passed (black reformatted two files on the first
  run; clean on the second)

issues.title: [Feature]: WhatsApp Web: send agent replies as quoted replies so group members know they were answered
issues.body:
### Affected component

channel (whatsapp-web)

### Summary

In WhatsApp groups, the bot's replies arrive as standalone messages. Because mentions are broken on this channel (#10976 — outbound mentions are sent as plain text with no `mentionedJid`), and replies are never quoted, the member who invoked the bot often cannot tell the bot answered them at all.

A quoted reply would solve the "who was answered" problem without depending on mention rendering.

### Current behavior

`send()` in `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/whatsapp_web.rs` builds the outbound text message as a plain conversation message:

```rust
let outgoing = waproto::whatsapp::Message {
    conversation: Some(markdown_to_whatsapp(&text_content)),
    ..Default::default()
};
```

No `contextInfo` is attached — no `quoted_message`, no `mentioned_jid`. There is also no config option for quoted replies: the WhatsApp channel docs (v0.8.7) do not mention "quote" at all, and no existing issue requests it (searched "quote" / "quoted reply" / "reply-to" before filing).

### Expected behavior

When the agent replies to a triggering group message, attach `contextInfo.quotedMessage` (with the triggering message's stanza ID and participant) so WhatsApp renders the reply as a quoted reply to that message. The invoking user then sees the bot answered *them*, even while mentions are broken.

Ideally behind a channel config option (e.g. quote replies on/off, default on for groups), so deployments that prefer standalone messages can opt out.

Note: the core `SendMessage` type already carries `in_reply_to` / `thread_ts` and a `reply_to()` builder, but those serve email threading and Slack threads — the WhatsApp Web channel does not consume them. Wiring the triggering message's ID through to the WhatsApp send path is part of this request.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Pair a WhatsApp Web session and add the bot to a group with 2+ participants.
2. A member mentions the bot (or replies to it) to trigger a turn.
3. Observe the bot's answer arrives as a new standalone message — no quote, no mention, nothing linking it to the message that invoked it.

### Impact

Affected users: all WhatsApp Web group conversations. Every bot reply in a group is affected. In a busy group the reply is easily missed, and the invoker has no signal they were answered. A quoted reply is also the most robust addressing fallback while outbound mentions remain broken (#10976).

### Related

- #10976 — mentions broken both ways on WhatsApp Web (inbound bare LID digits, outbound plain text). Quoted replies are a complementary fix, not a duplicate: they solve the "who was answered" problem without depending on mention rendering.
- #7032 / #7034 — `mention_only` gating against LID JIDs (fixed).

### ZeroClaw version

Observed on a current self-hosted install; confirmed in `main` source as of 2026-11-20 (the `send()` quoted above is from current `main`).

### Operating system

Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu).

labels.name: topic:identity-access
labels.description: Authentication, OIDC, principal isolation, and authorization; former milestone #17.

issues.body:
### Which RFC trigger does this meet?

Security: a new security layer or material change to the security model.

### Problem

Operators need to authorize an agent to perform a task against a service without disclosing the underlying credential to the model, chat, skill text, or general-purpose tools. Provisioning a credential and authorizing its use are distinct actions. Feature issue #12373 describes the workflow. The catalog and cross-tool authorization contract need a project decision.

### Proposal

Define an opt-in operator-managed credential catalog and a scoped-use contract for trusted consumers. The operator can grant more than one supported consumer access to a credential, with an explicit destination and consumer-specific constraints. The agent handles a reference. A trusted adapter resolves and uses the material only after ordinary tool, principal, and sandbox policy checks. A reference alone is not authorization.

### Agent-scoped grants for operator-managed credentials

Grant each operator-managed service alias to an explicit **agent, trusted consumer, and canonical destination**, with operation or resource restrictions where the consumer supports them. The runtime must supply the effective agent identity. The model can name an alias in a request. It cannot select a different agent identity or grant itself access. For delegated calls, enforce the authority of the effective agent and the applicable delegation policy.

Use the existing authentication and access policy to decide who may invoke an agent. An external identity provider can supply the authenticated caller for authorization and audit. This catalog requires no separate user directory or per-user credential enrollment. Record the caller when verified and available, the agent, credential alias, consumer, destination, operation, and outcome. Keep credential values out of both audit records and model context.

Access to an agent lets a caller request operations that the agent's configured credentials support, subject to ordinary policy and approvals. When operators and ordinary users need different capabilities, give them different agents or separately authorized execution profiles with distinct grants. For example, a CyberOps agent can have a scoped administrative SSH credential for the SIEM, while an investigation agent can have only a read-scoped Wazuh service credential. A user who can invoke the investigation agent cannot inherit the CyberOps SSH grant.

These are proposed grant semantics. The existing HTTP prototype in #12408 currently checks tool access and HTTPS origin. Personal downstream identity remains a separate delegated authorization flow.

### Design sketch

- Metadata-only listing and write-only creation and replacement through authorized administrative surfaces. Support disable and delete, with redacted audit outcomes. Keep existing configured credentials compatible and avoid silently granting new consumers access.
- Credential types and consumer grants are separate. User/password destinations can use a protocol-qualified address with an optional port. The consumer owns canonicalization and protocol-specific endpoint matching. A syntactically valid catalog entry does not enable a protocol or a consumer.
- HTTP authentication must match the configured HTTPS origin. Redirect, authority and header handling must prevent credential forwarding outside the authorized destination. For SSH, bind use to the approved destination, login and host-key verification. Keep the signing socket private to a narrowly scoped task broker, with no agent forwarding or sandbox escape. Define the behavior of already-running operations when a grant is revoked.
- Local encrypted storage and opt-in external backends use the same grant semantics. With an external backend, keep raw payloads out of ZeroClaw persistent storage and avoid fallback to plaintext or a different backend on resolution failure. External service identity and permissions remain deployment configuration.
- A skill may name a reference but cannot resolve it directly. MCP and plugin consumers require explicit typed integrations, their own reviewed trust boundary and opt-in grants. Storing TOTP seeds or other types does not itself authorize use.
- Coordinate the credential classification and enforcement model with #6971 and #7142. Coordinate principal and delegated-task authority with proposed #12131. The scope here is service-secret use, independent of inbound credential renewal.

### External vault provisioning

Use consistent catalog actions across providers. **Add** creates the credential. **Link existing secret** associates an existing provider identifier. **Replace** updates the value explicitly and may leave a blank value to preserve the remote secret. **Delete** removes the catalog entry. Remote destruction requires a separate provider operation. Suggest an editable identifier derived from the configured tree, alias, and credential type. Provider policy remains authoritative for permitted paths.

Keep provider writes opt-in, operator-only, and separate from agent resolution. Prefer short-lived write authority scoped to the configured tree. Send the value directly to the provider over authenticated transport, and store only the reference in the local catalog. Use conditional create and version-aware updates or an equivalent provider mechanism. Preserve siblings when updating structured entries. Keep existing link-only integrations useful while adding provider-specific writers. Cover an unavailable provider, concurrent writes, a completed remote create followed by a failed local save, and safe relinking.

For a configured OpenBao writer, the operator selects OpenBao, enters the credential value and saves. The gateway uses its configured OpenBao identity and the WebUI keeps the suggested reference editable. The operator does not mint, copy, or paste a vault token. Linking an existing secret saves the reference only and requires no vault write. The configured prefix and the OpenBao ACL constrain writes, and the agent still needs authorization to use the resulting credential. This workflow is implemented in #12481 and inherited by #12482.

OpenBao provisioning is tracked in #12481. The cloud writer adapters in #12482 add 1Password Connect, Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, and Google Secret Manager. AWS and Google enforce creation uniqueness at the service. Azure and 1Password check for an existing name and require an operator-managed single-writer scope for name collision safety. Google reports when a resource could have been created before its first version failed. Connect returns stable resource identifiers for future rotation.

### Alternatives considered

Keep per-tool secret configuration only. This is simpler but duplicates provisioning and cannot express a shared operator-managed catalog. Exposing unrestricted secret reads to the model, a shell or a skill would make destination enforcement and redaction unreliable.

### Non-goals

Generic secret retrieval, implicit use of a credential by arbitrary MCPs, and unrestricted browser or shell login. This proposal does not choose an organization-wide secret provider.

### Risks and mitigations

Test authorization across tool, credential, principal, and destination boundaries, including denied redirects, alternate SSH destinations, cancellation, live revocation, rotation, and unavailable backends. Never log payloads, and make failure modes observable through redacted metadata. Document per-platform setup and when external backends can keep secret payloads off persistent host storage.

### Breaking change?

No proposed breaking change. Existing configurations retain their existing behavior. Introduce the new contract opt-in and document rollback by disabling the integration or revoking its grants.

### Decision and revisit surface

Decide this contract here before landing implementation under it. See feature request #12373 and existing implementation prototypes #12402 (plugin TLS UI), #12408 (catalog and permissions) and #12418 (scoped SSH). These prototypes preceded this formal proposal and do not establish acceptance or grant a runtime holding-crate exception. Please identify which slices may proceed under existing authority and which should wait for ratification.

### Data hygiene checks

- [x] Examples, payloads, and logs contain no deployment credentials or personal data.

Drafted with OpenAI Codex assistance at the request of the submitting account, @CastelloBrancoTecnologia. Proposed for discussion.

## Credential ownership and multi-user execution

The operator chooses the secret backend and provisions service credentials that the operator manages. The operator explicitly grants a trusted tool or integration use of a service credential for a configured destination and bounded operation. An alias grants no authority by itself. A user may be authorized to invoke the operation while the secret remains confined to the backend. The agent and the requesting user receive the permitted result and redacted status.

ZeroClaw v0.9.0 supports opt-in OIDC sign-in and scoped dashboard chat for non-admin users. Pairing also remains available. This proposal does not rely on pairing as proof of an individual caller's identity. [Release notes](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/releases/tag/v0.9.0)

There are two independent decisions:

| Decision | Authority |
| --- | --- |
| May this caller invoke this operation against these resources? | Runtime policy and applicable integration policy, using the authenticated caller and agent where available. |
| Which service credential may this integration use at this destination? | Operator-managed catalog grant, restricted to the agent, consumer, destination and operation. |

For example, Alice can read alerts for her assigned Wazuh hosts and Bruno can also read inventory. Both calls can use the same operator-managed, read-scoped Wazuh service identity. The integration needs trusted caller identity for caller-specific enforcement or audit, even when the downstream identity is shared. Tool permission alone must not make an unrestricted privileged credential usable via arbitrary routes, methods or payloads. Use least-privileged upstream identities and enforce narrower operations in the integration. Record caller, operation, destination and outcome without credential values. If an integration requires a caller identity that its runtime path cannot supply, deny that operation rather than guessing from the prompt or inheriting the operator's identity.

[#12441](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12441) proposes passing authenticated caller context into tool execution outside model-visible arguments. Its identity primitive complements this service catalog. The requesting user, agent and backend must never treat a user-supplied identity string as proof of identity. Existing service-alias prototypes have narrower grants today. In particular #12408 currently scopes use through the existing HTTP tool permissions and allowed HTTPS origin; it does not yet provide per-principal or per-operation alias grants.

Personal delegation is a separate integration contract. A prompt such as “POST to https://xyz.example using my credentials” expresses intent only. For a provider that supports personal delegation, the user links their own account through an authenticated flow such as OAuth with consent. The backend binds that authorization to the verified principal, provider, destination and scopes, checks it on use, and supports revocation. Login to ZeroClaw alone supplies no downstream authorization. Passwords and tokens stay out of prompts, and the operator-managed service catalog neither enrolls personal credentials on a user's behalf nor falls back to an operator credential when personal delegation is absent. This RFC does not add a per-user credential vault.

## Proposed merge sequencing

Reviews on #12408 and #12490 ask for the first credential slice to support local API keys and HTTP Basic on a single HTTPS origin, with an explicit operator grant and write-only UI. The Token authorization scheme can follow as a consumer-specific addition. SSH keys, TOTP, directory-service credentials and external providers remain under this RFC. Land each with its consuming integration and a reviewed authorization boundary. External resolution should use the project's secret abstraction.

This sequencing is a proposed response to review. The RFC retains the broader operator-managed credential design for discussion.

prs.title: feat(telegram): configure automatic acknowledgement reactions
prs.body:
## Summary

- Add the optional `ack_reaction_emojis` array to per-bot Telegram configuration. One emoji gives a consistent acknowledgement; multiple emojis replace the default random pool.
- Omitted, empty or whitespace-only arrays retain the built-in pool. `ack_reactions = false` still disables automatic acknowledgements.
- Scope: the immediate Telegram acknowledgement only. Replies and other channels are unchanged. This PR does not include automatic continuations.

### What this does, simply

A bot can consistently react with 👀 to say it saw a message without using an emoji that might read as approval.

## Testing

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, on the Telegram messaging channel, with automatic acknowledgements enabled and 👀 permitted in the chat.
- Set `ack_reaction_emojis = ["👀"]` under `[channels.telegram.<alias>]` and send several messages. On this branch the immediate reaction is always 👀; on `master` there is no pool override. Remove the setting to restore the built-in pool. Disable `ack_reactions` to suppress the immediate reaction in either version.

### How I tested

- At `5f9ad0e`, the four focused channel tests passed (mock Bot API request shape, configured pool, default pool and live alias config), the media-group regression test passed, and the TOML round-trip test passed.
- Test output: `4 passed; 0 failed`, `1 passed; 0 failed`, and `1 passed; 0 failed`, respectively. The committed diff passed the whitespace check.
- Live Telegram rendering and upstream CI are not yet verified. The mock Bot API tests verify the outgoing request, not what Telegram displays.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions, capabilities or filesystem scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Credential handling changed? No.
- PII in the diff, tests, fixtures or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or new untrusted model-visible text? No.

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config surface changed? Yes, one optional per-bot TOML key. No migration is required.
- Rust toolchain floor changed? No.

## Rollback

Remove `ack_reaction_emojis` or set it to `[]` to restore the built-in pool, or revert `5f9ad0e`.

prs.title: feat(config): introduce independent provider registry domain types
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (stacked review; merge after #12448)
- **What changed and why:** Introduce the typed provider registry domain for connections, capabilities, model references, presets, overrides, and fallback validation. Add the model/API resolution primitives that later layers consume.
- **Scope boundary:** This layer owns registry domain types and validation/resolution only. Runtime activation, registry editing RPCs, provider construction, CLI, ZeroCode, and Web consumers remain in later stacked PRs.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-api` capability contracts and `zeroclaw-config` provider-registry types/resolution. No active user-facing consumer is switched in this layer.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12448. Related to #12450. This stacked series supersedes #9809 (closed).

### What this does, simply

A connection describes how to reach a provider, while a model entry describes a concrete model and capability exposed through that connection. This layer gives those concepts typed representations and a single resolver for inherited API options, explicit `null` clearing, model-level wire API selection, capability validation, and provider fallback graph validation. Later layers can build consumers on this canonical boundary without duplicating TOML parsing or provider/model lookup.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; this is a non-user-facing domain layer and the focused resolver/configuration tests exercise the changed boundary.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** GitHub CI runs the workspace format, lint, test, feature, platform, schema, and compatibility matrix for this head. Full builds and tests remain delegated to CI per the stacked-review workflow.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No runtime/network consumer is activated in this layer. Security and source-image checks are evaluated by the current master workflow and are not changed here.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — exit 0.
  - `git diff --check` — exit 0.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Rebuilt the branch from the current #12448 head and retained only the domain-registry commit plus the ASR timeout/endpoint resolution fixes. The incremental diff is limited to the provider registry domain and its API/config resolution surface.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no CLI, web, TUI, or channel surface changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `f1eaca9479`; full behavior validation is provided by the GitHub CI checks on this exact head.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Registry construction now has one typed source for connection/model/capability resolution, including ASR timeout inheritance, explicit timeout clearing, complete endpoint overrides, and per-kind wire API validation. Secret masking/restoration failures are returned to export, gateway, and RPC callers instead of being silently discarded.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace tests and builds are intentionally delegated to GitHub CI because this is a domain-only preparatory layer.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Secret masking and restoration helpers now return and propagate serialization/deserialization errors; credential values and masking behavior are otherwise unchanged.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes; this layer defines the canonical domain and leaves existing loading and consumers unchanged until later stacked layers.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No active surface is switched on by this layer.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk preparatory layer: revert this layer after reverting dependent stacked layers.

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the commits on this PR before reverting dependent registry-consumer layers.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Registry-domain compilation or focused resolution tests fail; later layers cannot resolve canonical model/capability references.

Stack integration: this PR targets upstream `master` and is reviewed incrementally after #12448. Merge the parent first and refresh children. The original #9809 is closed; this is the domain-types layer of the replacement stack.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors: #9809 by @NiuBlibing (replaced collectively by this stacked series).
- Scope materially carried forward: This PR carries only the registry-domain and API/config-resolution slice; activation and UI slices remain in later stacked PRs.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? No.
- If `No`, why: The original PR and this stack have the same author; there is no additional contributor to attribute with a co-author trailer.

---

**Labels** live in the GitHub label UI. Do not add bot/AI attribution footers.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - #11076 adds the `agy_cli` coding-CLI tool. Its implementation lives in `zeroclaw-tools`, but registering it touches three files in this holding crate. Review on #11076 found no exception row covering that wiring, and the maintainer review there [recommended this separate proposal](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11076#discussion_r4463798491) with the scope used here.
  - This adds one pending row at the end of the active-exception table. It covers the `tool-agy-cli` feature forwarding in `Cargo.toml`; the `AgyCliTool` re-export, the `tool-agy-cli` feature in the existing coding-CLI `cfg` gates, its `any_coding_cli_tool_enabled` term, the compiled-out warning, the `select_tool!`/`register_tool!` block and the `agy_cli` cases in the existing coding-CLI registration tests in `src/tools/mod.rs`; and the `tool-agy-cli` and `tool-agy-cli-*` keys in `locales/en/tools.ftl`.
  - Destination: the tool-composition owner in the planned `zeroclaw-kernel` extraction; the implementation stays in `zeroclaw-tools`. Review condition: when application wiring takes over native tool construction (#11187), or before the scope expands.
  - The approval cell says **Pending Core Team review**. If the row is approved, I'll record the approving handle and review link in a follow-up commit on this branch before merge, as #11980 did.
- **Scope boundary:** The table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` only. No code. Every existing row is unchanged. It covers no other coding-CLI tool, and grants no new executor, tool grant, approval or sandbox authority.
- **Blast radius:** Merge eligibility of #11076's runtime wiring under ADR-016.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11076, Related #11187

### What this does, simply

The runtime crate is a holding crate: new work there needs a recorded Core Team decision, and a feature PR can't grant itself one. This row is that record for #11076's registration of `agy_cli`, so reviewers can approve or narrow it here before #11076 merges.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for scope: compare the row's paths with `git diff --name-only master...pull/11076/head -- crates/zeroclaw-runtime`.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** N/A, documentation only.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** One added row with four cells; every existing table line unchanged.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None specific. The docs quality and link gates cover `docs/book/src`, not this file.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `git diff --stat master` shows `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md | 1 +` with no line removed. `git diff --name-only master...388ee8df0 -- crates/zeroclaw-runtime` (the current #11076 head) lists exactly `Cargo.toml`, `locales/en/tools.ftl` and `src/tools/mod.rs`, the three paths the row names.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A, no user-visible interface state changed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No build or tests: no code changes.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes, if Core approves: the row permits the named additions in the holding crate. It grants no runtime authority.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the commit. If #11076 has merged by then, its code stays; reverting withdraws the permission for further additions under this row.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** None; documentation only.

prs.title: fix(docker): keep the installer script the web build embeds
prs.body:
## What
One line in `.dockerignore`: re-include `scripts/install_windows_prebuilt.ps1` after `scripts/`.

## Why
`cargo web` is the alias `run --release -p xtask --bin web --`, so every image build compiles `xtask` in its web-builder stage. `xtask/src/generate/docs.rs:315` embeds `scripts/install_windows_prebuilt.ps1` with `include_str!`, while `.dockerignore` excludes `scripts/`, so the file never reaches `COPY . .` and the build stops:

    error: couldn't read `xtask/src/generate/../../../scripts/install_windows_prebuilt.ps1`: No such file or directory (os error 2)
       --> xtask/src/generate/docs.rs:315:21

`bec292f66` (#12166) added the `include_str!` without the matching exception. This hits every web stage built from this ignore file: `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.debian`, `Dockerfile.alpine` and `Containerfile`.

## How
The exception names only the file the compiler embeds, so `scripts/` still keeps its cache-busting exemption. It is the same pattern this file already uses for `apps/tauri/Cargo.toml` after `apps/*`.

## Verification
- `rm -rf scripts && cargo check --locked -p xtask --bin web` reproduces the exact message above; restoring `scripts/` makes the same command finish.
- `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets` passes with the file present; no Rust source changed, so the docs gates do not apply.

Linked issue(s): None.

prs.title: fix(cli): check the local daemon in builds without a gateway
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch** `master`
- **What changed and why** In a build without the gateway, the four gateway-backed SOP administration commands now direct the operator to the standard build. The CLI-only exit-code health check asks the configured local daemon for its health snapshot and accepts only `components.daemon.status == "ok"`. The request has a five-second deadline.
- **Scope boundary** The changes apply to builds with the agent runtime and without the gateway. Gateway-enabled builds retain their HTTP health probe and SOP administration routes.
- **Blast radius** CLI-only health checks and the `sop pending`, `logs`, `approve` and `deny` commands. The localized `status --help` text explains what a healthy CLI-only daemon means.
- **Linked issue(s)** Closes #12097. Builds on merged #11975 and #11976.

### What this does, simply

These commands used to look for a web gateway even when the installed binary could only run a local daemon. A health check now asks that daemon directly. Commands that need the web gateway tell the operator which build provides it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The CLI-only build job includes the real executable, a loopback listener on the configured gateway port, and on Unix a local IPC fixture that serves healthy and unhealthy replies.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change** The existing CLI-only lane runs binary and component tests without the gateway. Its component checks hold the gateway port open while running all four SOP verbs and checking an absent daemon. The Unix IPC fixture checks which local methods the binary calls and observes both exit codes.
- **Known CI coverage gap** On the signed PR head, the hosted CLI-only build ran both `sop_admin_and_exit_code_status_do_not_contact_the_gateway_port` and `status_exit_code_reads_the_local_daemons_health` successfully. The local runner could not bind its socket fixtures. [CLI-only build](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44245807800/job/134604360145)
- **Commands run and tail output**
  - Built the binary and component tests with `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw --no-default-features --features agent-runtime,plugins-wasm,channel-filesystem --bin zeroclaw --test component cli_only`. From the resulting test executables, the daemon health predicate passed (`1 passed; 0 failed`) and the CLI-only command/status component checks passed (`2 passed; 0 failed`). prs.title: feat(channels/telegram): add trusted_groups group authorization
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Adds `channels.telegram.<alias>.trusted_groups`, a list of negative numeric group/supergroup `chat.id` values. Messages from a listed group are admitted from any member without a peer-group sender entry, so operators do not need to add every member of a trusted group to `peer_groups.*.external_peers`.
- **Scope boundary:** No wildcard or per-topic trust, no per-group sender/tools settings, no DM or pairing changes, and no approval-authority expansion.
- **Blast radius:** Telegram inbound authorization, Telegram config schema/validation, and the Telegram channel factories. Other channels and the shared approval path are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12562. Related #9634 — previous broader attempt; this PR is narrower and does not supersede it.

### What this does, simply

A Telegram group can be authorized as a whole. If its `chat.id` is in `trusted_groups`, any member can talk to the agent without an individual peer-group entry.

```toml
[channels.telegram.home]
mention_only = true
trusted_groups = ["-1001234567890"]
```

`trusted_groups = []` keeps current behavior. `mention_only`, `ignore` denies, DMs, and pairing are unchanged. A trusted-group member can talk to the agent but cannot approve approval-gated tool calls.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes — requires a real bot and a test group.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` (`telegram`), `cli`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Bot token; test group/supergroup; one account in peer groups and one account in no peer group.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Add the group's negative `chat.id` to `trusted_groups`.
  2. With `mention_only = true`, mention the bot from the unlisted account.
  3. Send the same test from a DM.
  4. Trigger an approval-gated tool from the unlisted account.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the unlisted group member gets an agent reply; the DM still gets the unauthorized notice; the unlisted member cannot approve the tool call, while a peer-authorized member in the same group can.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the unlisted group member gets the unauthorized notice.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** required CI covers workspace build, Telegram unit tests, config validation, docs, and lint gates.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** full workspace tests were not run locally; targeted config/channel tests and the full Telegram test module were run. Required CI covers the remaining workspace surface.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo check -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-channels --features zeroclaw-channels/channel-telegram
Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)

cargo test -p zeroclaw-config trusted_group
test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-telegram trusted_group
test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

telegram::tests
test result: ok. 413 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored

cargo fmt --all -- --check
git diff --check
clean
```

Focused tests cover exact match, non-matching group, DM rejection, `mention_only`, `ignore` precedence, attachment/media-group/voice authorization, and approval rejection for a trusted-group-only sender.

Manual Telegram smoke: an unlisted sender in the trusted supergroup reached the agent turn; a non-trusted DM still produced the unauthorized notice.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Group admission, DM unauthorized notice, and approval separation. Telegram media variants were covered by automated tests, not manually.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** commit `3a1caae92`; `channel` (`telegram`) and `cli` config path; local targeted tests plus a real Telegram smoke. No screenshots or viewport dimensions apply.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `N/A` — no visual output; command tails are above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** `N/A` — no interactive UI or transition change.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full workspace test suite skipped locally; required CI covers it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** `trusted_groups` bypasses the sender allowlist for the listed group; every member can drive the agent and its tools within the agent's risk profile.
- New external network calls? **No.**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** More untrusted users can reach the agent in a trusted group. Mitigations: opt-in default-empty field, docs warning, `mention_only`, `ignore` precedence, no approval expansion, and a recommended restricted agent/tool profile.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes.** `trusted_groups` defaults to `[]`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** New Telegram config field; schema-driven `zeroclaw config set` works automatically.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users:

```text
No migration required. Existing configs are unchanged. To use the feature, add the negative group chat.id to channels.telegram.<alias>.trusted_groups and reload/restart the daemon.
```

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback command/path:** remove `trusted_groups` from the channel block, or `git revert <sha>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `trusted_groups = []` disables the grant.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** unauthorized notices in a group that should be trusted, or agent turns from a group that should not be trusted.
