prs.title: feat(mcp): route declared MP4 resources into Qwen video input
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Materialize MCP `resource.blob` items explicitly declaring `video/mp4` as MP4 files and register existing `MarkerKind::Video` attachments, so the provider receives video rather than a document-path description.
  - Reuse the existing materializer, aggregate/item budgets, metadata preservation, and tool-carrier grammar. Resource URIs remain provenance and are never fetched.
  - Pass only declared, current-turn videos to Qwen; preserve tool text, mixed images/documents, native tool-result attribution, and XML external-tool headers. Stop replaying tool videos after a new user turn.
  - Add full MCP HTTP → tool wrapper → native/XML Agent → provider HTTP tests, plus an ignored real-Qwen smoke test.
- **Scope boundary:** Explicit MP4 embedded resources. Other video formats retain document handling. No new MCP tool/content type, camera integration, remote URI fetch, Responses transport, client frame extraction, or shared ACP document-format change.
- **Blast radius:** MCP embedded-resource formatting, shared MP4 header identification, Qwen declared-attachment normalization, and compatible-provider media relocation. Existing image tests remain part of regression coverage.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12578. Related #11383 for tool-body marker trust-boundary concerns.

This is the child of #12578 and is intentionally a draft while the parent is reviewed. Both PRs target `master` as required. The full diff currently includes the parent commit; the child-only comparison is [`016e14f67...f1b5ac448`](https://github.com/wenhaozhao/zeroclaw/compare/016e14f67c187de0684c049fa3489b289b1c1d3c...f1b5ac448248a217fb88ae8c6323cb6c6437aea5). Refresh and revalidate this branch after the parent lands.

### What this does, simply

A tool can return an MP4 using the existing MCP embedded-resource format. ZeroClaw saves it in the workspace and passes the declared video to a supported Qwen model. The tool's descriptive text stays text, including any VIDEO examples it contains. The video remains available during later tool rounds of that user request, and is removed from media replay when another user request begins.

```json
{"type":"resource","resource":{"uri":"evidence://event/clip.mp4","mimeType":"video/mp4","blob":"<base64 MP4 bytes>"}}
```

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; automated end-to-end tests use real MCP HTTP intake, the production tool wrapper and Agent, and captured provider HTTP. The ignored live test provides optional paid provider reproduction.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None at submission time. Upstream CI is pending. Local evidence covers the complete combined stack, resource intake, image compatibility, source attribution, and user-turn lifetime.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Ordinary CI ignores live-model tests. The end-to-end integration test requires `test-util`; its exact command is below. Local platform was macOS/aarch64 with rustc 1.97.1; no local Linux/Windows/MSRV execution is claimed.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers
lib: 2000 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored
integration: 1 passed; 60 passed; 3 ignored

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools
lib: 1399 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored
integration: 4 passed; 1 passed; 3 passed

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features test-util --test mcp_video --config 'profile.test.package.zeroclaw-runtime.opt-level=1' mcp_video_reaches_qwen_http_through_native_and_xml_agent_turns -- --nocapture
1 passed; 0 failed; 1 filtered out
No compiler/linker warnings.

cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime --features zeroclaw-runtime/test-util --all-targets -- -D warnings
Finished dev profile; no warnings.

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- --test-threads=4
6240 passed; 2 failed; 10 ignored

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- --skip relay::local_dial_tests::
6240 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored; 2 filtered out
```

  The two runtime failures are the `relay::local_dial_tests` backlog fixtures: `could not stall a loopback connect: the listener backlog never filled`. Both reproduce on unmodified upstream `master` at `ad4c1f6c3`: `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib relay::local_dial_tests:: -- --nocapture` returned `0 passed; 2 failed; 6249 filtered out` with the same backlog error. They are not counted as passing or attributed to this change.

  The unoptimized macOS runtime test binary exceeds the linker's compact-unwind table size; the same warning reproduces on unmodified master. The runtime-only optimization used in the isolated integration command reduces code size without disabling diagnostics.

  Also passed: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check`, the docs quality gate (0 errors), and the docs links gate (local target check passed). Docs checks used `BASE_SHA=ad4c1f6c3` and both changed Markdown paths; optional HTTP link checking was skipped because lychee was unavailable.
  **Initial upstream CI status:** The Security job currently fails its dependency audit with 8 vulnerabilities and 19 allowed warnings ([job log](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44533093279/job/135591285823)). The submitted heads and upstream `ad4c1f6c3` have identical `Cargo.lock` blobs; this stack changes no Cargo manifest, lockfile, or audit workflow. The existing dependency findings remain a merge blocker; this PR does not suppress them. Other required checks are still running.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The freshly built optimized `mcp_video` test binary ran `mcp_video_agent_to_real_qwen --exact --ignored --nocapture` with explicit test credentials and the public OpenCV eight-second MP4 excerpt. A real Qwen3.8-Flash Agent called the isolated MCP tool exactly once and returned a pedestrian-motion description. `1 passed; 0 failed`; Agent round duration 7.58 seconds. This is transport/inference smoke evidence, not accuracy or billed-cost measurement.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no presentation or rendered interface changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `f1b5ac448`. Final Rust sources were unchanged after the test builds; final edits were documentation. Tests are `embedded_video_tests.rs`, `compatible_mcp_video_tests.rs`, and `zeroclaw-runtime/tests/mcp_video.rs`; the full stack is exercised through `Agent::turn` and MCP/provider HTTP boundaries.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Captured HTTP requires byte-identical video content in the first tool continuation, string-only native tool messages, preserved XML `[Tool results]` attribution, and zero video parts on the next user turn. The real-model test output was `test mcp_video_agent_to_real_qwen ... ok`.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Valid MP4 resources gain declared video attachments. MIME case/parameters and misleading/missing extensions normalize correctly. Invalid Base64/header and over-budget results redact binary with unavailable notices. Metadata and sibling text survive. Missing/unsupported tool videos degrade individually. Body markers stay literal; image/video/document and zero-attachment XML carriers retain provenance.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No full workspace, desktop, Linux/Windows, or MSRV claim; upstream CI supplies its supported matrix. Other real models were not exercised. Live tests stay ignored by default, and optional HTTP link validation requires lychee.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes:** declared MP4 resources gain model-video delivery. Workspace writes use the existing materializer; provider reads use the parent's current-turn policy and bounded no-follow loader. Allowed filesystem roots are unchanged.
- New external network calls? **Yes:** existing Qwen inference requests may include the tool-declared video. No URI dereference, new external endpoint, or extra fetch/upload request is introduced.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No:** runtime authentication is unchanged; the ignored test reuses explicit `ZEROCLAW_TEST_QWEN_*` variables.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No:** committed media fixtures are synthetic; live video and credentials are uncommitted.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes:** explicitly declared external video becomes evidence. The fixed-position carrier separates attachments from untrusted body text; native relocation retains result ordinals and XML retains its tool-result header.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: An untrusted MCP server can supply video evidence, but cannot promote a VIDEO example in its body or trigger a fetch of its resource URI. Existing 10 MiB per-file/aggregate and 64-item limits remain in force, plus the parent's smaller Qwen dispatch budget. Only current-turn declared videos are delivered; stale/invalid/unsupported attachments degrade without replacing sibling text.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes, additive media support:** explicit MP4 resources intentionally gain video-attachment behavior. Other video formats, shared ACP document behavior, existing text/images, and non-Qwen provider request formats are retained.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No:** no new runtime configuration/CLI fields or MCP tool/content types; the live test uses the parent's explicit test variables.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: N/A. MCP producers opt in through the existing `resource.blob` shape with `mimeType: "video/mp4"`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's eventual merge commit first. On the submitted branch the child is isolated in `f1b5ac448`. The parent's independent user-file video input can remain.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added. Producers can return text/image evidence while video delivery is investigated.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Video remains a path description, Qwen returns a video-input error, or a tool-video unavailable notice appears. The MCP Agent capture test exposes missing bytes, lost provenance, and stale-video replay. Saved files remain under the existing workspace upload lifecycle.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. This child depends on #12578 and does not supersede another contribution.

prs.title: fix(web): show a detached chat turn and load its answer when it ends
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - When a dashboard chat socket closes mid-turn and reopens while the turn is still running, the page reloads the transcript once, before the turn is stored, and nothing reloads it again: the answer stays missing until a page reload or a conversation switch (#12107).
  - Hydration now asks `GET /api/sessions/{id}/state` before it loads the stored transcript (asked after it, a turn ending between the two reads would leave its answer unloaded). While the turn is `running` there, the page shows it as running (before the composer unlocks, so it does not offer to send into it) and asks again every 2 s. Once the state leaves `running`, it loads the transcript once more. The gateway sets `idle` or `error` only after it has persisted the turn (`ws.rs`), so that load has the answer, or the stored outcome of a failed turn.
  - The watch ends without a reload on the next hydration, a conversation switch or clear, a model switch (a clear or model switch also stops one that has not started yet, while the first check or the transcript load is still out), unmount, and when its socket closes (the reopen reloads and asks again). A check still in flight when the watch ends is ignored. A failed check, including the 404 of a gateway without session persistence, reads as "not running": the page keeps today's single load and never retries in a loop. So does a check without an answer within 10 s (`STATE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`): each check has its own deadline, and the page stops awaiting it at the deadline or when the watch ends, so a stuck request can neither keep the composer locked nor keep the turn shown as running. A daemon restarted mid-turn settles the abandoned turn to `error` (`recover_abandoned_session_turns`), which also ends the watch.
  - Because the check runs after any hydration, a page loaded while its conversation's turn runs (a reload, or a return from another conversation) also shows the turn and loads the answer when it ends.
  - A stored `running` state can outlive its turn: the gateway ignores errors on its state writes (`let _ = backend.set_session_state(...)` in `ws.rs`), so a failed `idle` write leaves `running` until the next restart. A page watching such a turn would stay locked, and Stop did nothing, because the abort route's `no_active_response` answer was discarded. Stop now reads that answer. The gateway also gives it in the moment between a turn's end (its cancel token removed) and its `idle` write, so the answer alone does not end the watch: two state checks that both start after it must still read the same turn id `running` (a check already out when Stop was refused does not count). Then the watch ends like a finished turn, with one reload, and later loads on this page do not lock on that turn id again. A different turn, or one without a turn id, is never treated as stale. This assumes the gateway's tail from token removal to the `idle` write takes well under one poll interval (2 s); it is a transcript write and a state write.
- **Scope boundary:** Web dashboard only (`web/src`); no gateway or API change: the state route already exists. A turn streaming on the page's own socket is not watched. A conversation switch still does not abort a detached turn (it aborts a live one, as before); Stop aborts a watched turn through the existing abort route, and the watch then loads the outcome. Accounts whose chat goes through the core (one conversation per socket) are unchanged: there is nothing to reload. No partial-answer replay while the turn runs; the answer appears when it is stored. Not covered, as possible follow-ups: an "outcome unknown" notice or tool-card settling across a reload; a deadline on the transcript load itself (`GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages`, unchanged here and signal-less on master); a turn that another client starts in the same conversation, which this page does not see live at any time (a dashboard socket receives turn frames only for its own prompts; the multi-viewer direction is #9002 and #11185), so a turn started while the transcript loads is shown at the next load, as one started just after it would be; and the known limit pinned in `chatHydration.logic.test.ts` (#11571), where a prompt another client committed with identical text hides the same prompt in flight here: transcript rows carry no turn id, so that needs a server change. A stale `running` state is handled per page: a reload, another tab or another device locks again until Stop is pressed there too; settling such a row on the server (for example in the abort route when no turn is registered) is a separate gateway change.
- **Blast radius:** `AgentContext` hydration, the socket close handler, and Stop's handling of the abort answer. One extra `GET /api/sessions/{id}/state` per transcript load (a gateway without session persistence answers it with 404), plus one every 2 s only while a detached turn runs.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12107. Related #9002 (the wider reconnect contract), #11571 (keeps the in-flight prompt on reload), #11965 (introduced the reload on reopen), #11185 (server-side session-owned turns for RPC clients; no dashboard change).

### What this does, simply

The gateway keeps working on a chat turn after the browser loses its connection, but it saves the turn only when it finishes. If the browser reconnected before that, it fetched the conversation too early, got no answer, and never looked again, so the chat sat idle with the answer missing. Now the browser asks the gateway whether the turn is still running, shows it as running if so, and fetches the conversation again as soon as the gateway reports it finished. It stops asking when the turn ends, when the user moves on, or when anything goes wrong, so it cannot loop. If the gateway's record wrongly says a turn is still running, pressing Stop now unlocks the chat after two checks instead of leaving it stuck.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: web`
- **Setup / preconditions:** Session persistence on (the default) and a turn that runs at least ~20 s (for example a shell tool running `sleep 20`).
- **Steps to run:** Send the turn. While it runs, drop the connection briefly (devtools offline for a few seconds, or restart a proxy in front of the gateway) so the socket closes and reopens. Wait for the turn to finish. Separately: reload the page while a turn runs.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** After the reopen (or reload) the turn shows as running and the composer stays locked; when the turn finishes, the answer appears on its own and the composer unlocks. The prompt appears once.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** After the reopen the page stops showing the turn; the answer does not appear until the page is reloaded or the conversation switched.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the web test jobs run `test:contexts`, which includes `sessionLifecycle.test.ts`, where the new tests live next to the existing reopen test.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI has no browser test; the network-drop behaviour is covered by the manual browser check below.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (on this head, Node with the generated API files from an xtask web build)
  - `npm run typecheck`: clean
  - `npm run test:contexts`: `ℹ pass 159` / `ℹ fail 0` (`sessionLifecycle.test.ts`: 91 pass, 28 new)
  - `npm test`: 174 pass, 0 fail; `npm run test:auth`: 247 pass, 0 fail; `npm run test:navigation`: 9 pass, 0 fail; `npm run test:permissions`: 34 pass, 0 fail
  - `git diff --check`, `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` on the changed files: clean
- **Rebased 2026-11-17 onto master `cda933e6b` (head `263acc119`), then server-side onto `1c8f2b59b` on 2026-11-19 (head `f84cfd0d9`, all three commits patch-identical by `git range-diff`) for the advisory fix in #12516.** Two conflicts with master, both in tests: the `/api/config/list` mock in `sessionLifecycle.test.ts` (kept master's `configListEntries` and this PR's abort route), and the runtime mock in master's new `contextMeter.dom.test.ts` (#12074), which lacked this PR's `getState`; it now answers `idle`, folded into the first commit so every commit type-checks. The second commit is unchanged (`git range-diff`). On this head: `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm test` 180 pass; `npm run test:auth` 250 pass; `npm run test:contexts` 169 pass; `npm run test:permissions` 34 pass; `npm run test:navigation` 9 pass; 0 fail in all; `git diff --check` and `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` clean. The browser and gateway results below are from before this rebase.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - The new tests fail against master's `AgentContext.tsx` (same tests, master's production file): the reopen, page-load, Stop, switch and close scenarios fail at the first "shows the turn as running" assertion.
  - Reverting each guard one at a time (live-turn guard; switch keeps a detached turn; close, clear, model switch and unmount end the watch; the abort checks after the wait and after the last check; a failed check reads as not running; the reload when the turn ends; the per-check deadline, the race that stops awaiting a stuck request, the cancellation of a check when the watch ends; a hydration's pending check registered, and cancelled by clear and by model switch; no watch once cancelled before the load) fails at least one test each: 17 of 17.
  - Stale state (third commit): the tests for Stop on a turn the gateway is not running (unlock after two checks, no re-lock on the same turn id, re-lock on a new one), a check already out when Stop is refused, and a turn without an id fail against the previous head `44618fc9d` or the commit's first draft; a refusal followed by another running turn, Stop accepted, and Stop just as a turn ends (its answer still loads) pin the unchanged paths.
  - The tests also assert the prompt shows exactly once while the turn runs and after the answer loads, and that the page never re-sends it.
  - A turn that ends while the transcript loads (the test's gateway flips to `idle` when the snapshot is read) still gets its answer loaded; this fails with the state asked after the load.
  - A state check that never answers: hydration finishes at the deadline with the single load (no watch), and a stuck check during the watch ends it with one reload; the stuck request's signal is aborted in both, and on a conversation switch.
  - **Browser check against a real gateway with a real network drop** (added 2026-11-15; headless Chromium, isolated `zeroclaw gateway` built from this PR's first two commits, patch-id identical, plus unrelated carried changes). A fake OpenAI-compatible model streams a fixed answer over 20 s; a TCP proxy between browser and gateway drops every connection, with no close frames, and refuses new ones for a set time. Each trial opens `/agent/<alias>`, sends a message, cuts the network once the model's first words are on screen, then waits for the complete answer without any reload or navigation. Control: the same tree with this PR's two commits reverted and nothing else.

    | Network outage | Without this PR | With this PR |
    |---|---|---|
    | 3 s (the socket reopens while the turn still runs) | 0/5: one transcript load while the turn runs, the composer back to "Type a message...", the answer never shown | 5/5: "Running…" shown, `/state` polled every 2 s, the answer loaded when the turn ends |
    | 12 s (the turn ends during the outage) | 2/2 | 2/2 |

  - **Gateway side, without a browser:** over 30 drop-and-reopen trials (clean close, close then reopen, abrupt TCP drop), `/state` stayed `running` during the detached turn, and at the first non-`running` read (polled every 50 ms) `/messages` already held the complete answer: the turn is stored before the state reports `idle`, which this change relies on.
  - **Browser scenarios on this head (`7b47bd716`)**, same harness, one run each (the gateway's state row edited by hand for the stale case):
    - socket reopened mid-turn: "Running…" shown, the full answer loaded about 4 s after the reopen, the prompt shown throughout;
    - a second browser opening the conversation mid-turn: the composer locks, the answer loads without a reload; Stop from that browser stops the turn (state `idle`) and both pages unlock;
    - stored state `running` with no turn running: locked on load; after Stop unlocked within 8 s, answer kept, no `/state` request in the next 10 s (the previous head, as deployed, was still locked and polling);
    - gateway killed mid-turn and restarted: state `error`, the page unlocks.
    - Once in 8 runs of the reopen scenario across builds, under heavy host load, the page briefly (about 2-4 s) showed the "conversation started over" notice and hid the prompt before the answer loaded; it did not reproduce in the other runs and is unexplained.
  - Not covered: mobile background-tab timer throttling and tab eviction.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact final-interface output. No new UI: the change only drives the existing running state (`typing`); one test renders the real chat page (`AgentChatInner`) and asserts the composer is disabled while the detached turn runs and enabled once its answer has loaded.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `7b47bd716c61b623cbc55a5cbd448ec358b78c81`, `web/src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts` ("a page that loads while its turn runs shows the turn and loads the outcome once it ends").
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the assertions above, on the rendered `AgentChatInner` textarea's `disabled` prop.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** turn running on the gateway at hydration → composer disabled, running state shown; state leaves `running` → transcript reloaded, answer shown, composer enabled.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** no Rust checks: no Rust file changed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No (an existing same-origin route, with the page's existing auth)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`.

The managed browser runtime, protected autofill, synthetic HTTPS login tests, and Jarvis acceptance are pending. Do not deploy this draft as a working browser consumer.

git diff --check passed. The focused Rust test was started locally.

prs.title: feat(providers): adopt the canonical V5 registry and runtime model bindings
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; merge only after the dependencies below.
- **What changed and why:** Activate canonical registry admission and backend consumers, promote V4 configuration to V5, materialize complete models for routing/fallback/switching, and wire secret-safe registry editing. Registry types, native protocols, chat transport and reflection are prepared in #12454, #12455, #12456 and #12457.
- **Scope boundary:** V5 admission, persistence/editor wiring, canonical model construction and backend consumer/lifecycle cutover. Activation and affected consumers remain together so no intermediate revision clears profiles that active consumers still read. Zerocode and Web follow separately.
- **Blast radius:** Config persistence and secret handling; provider construction; agent/session lifecycle; memory, speech and decision consumers; channel/gateway/RPC dispatch.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related to #9809. Stack part 9; reference implementation `320aa43a62`. Depends on #12457.

### What this does, simply

The preceding layers prepare independent registry types, native capability protocols, chat transport and generic reflection. This layer activates those components: V4 input is promoted at the V5 admission boundary, backend consumers resolve exact model references, and routing, fallback and switching build complete target bindings. Configuration activation and dependent consumers stay together to avoid a partially switched runtime. This remaining cutover is still large; the preparatory layers make their own architectural boundaries independently reviewable.

## Testing (required)


### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes` — the migration or interactive workflow below supplements passing current-head CI.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Requested surface: `cli`. Not exercised interactively at this revision.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Check out this head with its parent commits; use the repository toolchain and existing test fixtures.
- **Steps to run:** Run workspace Quality Gate, migration and registry edit tests, provider protocol tests, runtime route/switch/fallback/refresh tests and feature-matrix checks; exercise `zeroclaw config migrate` with a V4 backup.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** V4 configuration becomes V5 connections/models; internal consumers resolve exact model keys; switching/fallback materializes all target configuration and a failed update preserves the previous binding.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Master stores provider-owned profiles and consumer-specific capability settings, and has no canonical decoupled registry.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Earlier green runs are historical only. Current-head workspace CI is required after the review fixes; no current-head all-green claim is made.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The separate PR-risk evidence now binds deleted-file records to the captured base revision while retaining head binding for every other file. Live CLI/migration verification remains pending; passing CI does not establish the two old-configuration migration restrictions identified in review. Original #9809 CI does not validate intermediate stack revisions.
- **Commands run and tail output:** At `320aa43a62`, `cargo check --offline -p zeroclaw-config --lib` and `cargo check --offline -p zeroclaw-providers --lib` passed. Expanded config unit suite passed 2,085 tests, including the final fallback and timeout regressions. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check` and the changed-line docs quality gate passed. Existing Rust-toolchain deprecation/unused-dependency warnings were not changed.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Addressed previous-head split dependency errors (retained embedding factory, complete timeout helpers, deferred dispatch-dependent sampling, and secret-test trait import). The registry and provider libraries compile on the cleaned head. Compared the integrated provider and UI trees byte-for-byte with the saved pre-split snapshot. Preserved the frozen V4 fixture. Corrected previous-head CI failures caused by unnecessary TOML rewriting; the existing comment-preservation and atomic-save assertions remain intact. Inspected ownership, imports and the incremental diff against the declared parent. Runtime/network behavior remains delegated to CI.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Pending: CLI Quickstart and configuration command output require exact-head verification before interface sign-off.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `1d9e3b4798`; source formatting only.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** No interactive action performed; current-head CI passed, while manual runtime checks remain pending.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local Cargo build/test/clippy were intentionally skipped at the author’s request to use GitHub CI instead of repeated heavy local compilation.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes; existing capability selection is represented in the new registry. Existing admission boundaries remain in force.
- New external network calls? Yes; native capability adapters use the selected connection and protocol. No additional allowlist bypass is introduced.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes; connection credentials and sensitive headers use the existing encrypted persistence and masked edit contracts.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes; shared extraction policy is selected per materialized model.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Migration, registry editing and provider selection cross configuration trust boundaries. Preserve ciphertext, use masked compare-and-swap edits, validate references before installation, and keep the previous binding when construction fails. Provider output remains subject to runtime tool admission.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Older files are converted at the migration boundary; the new internal API and persisted V5 shape replace profile-owned construction.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes; connections, models, presets, fallback references and configuration editing use the V5 shape.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Back up the existing configuration and run `zeroclaw config migrate`. Inspect the resulting connections/models and exact model references. V1-V3 first migrate through the frozen V4 step, then V4-to-V5. Install the dependent clients before the complete interactive rollout; restore the V4 backup for a V4 downgrade.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert merged children before this layer. Restore the pre-upgrade V4 backup when returning to a V4 binary; retain memory identity checks and never downgrade by editing only the version number.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added for staging the stack.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** CI compile errors, configuration load failures, or changed provider behavior in the layer-specific regression tests.

Stack integration: this repository grants this author read-only access. These fork PRs therefore target `master` and have cumulative diffs. Review the incremental layer against its declared parent; merge parents first and refresh each child before merging. Original #9809 is closed; this stacked PR remains the registry/provider layer.

Incremental review: [declared parent to this layer](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/compare/cdf1929c97...f06c998aa1).



### Review fixes (2026-11-17)

- Preserve V4 primary selection and non-strict text tools; strict policy follows named models, routes and fallback targets, with conflicting agent policies refused. Materialize fallback connections even when a canonical model shadows legacy input.
- Preserve non-streaming versus streaming timeout semantics with `api.stream_request_timeout_secs`; keep Grok subprocess deadlines bounded.
- Reject registry saves when disk edits diverge, compare stored references without resolving external secrets, and avoid blocking chat sessions for speech-only edits.
- Compare legacy embedding identity against the actual endpoint digest, and normalize image recovery using the served fallback model policy.
- Follow-up native Azure/Bedrock/Gemini timeout wiring is in #12455 and propagated to descendants. Follow-up `96a2d022fd` regenerates only the V5 fixture and fixes the recovery test setup and Clippy condition; `3e7455f7f0` fixes strict Clippy fixture initialization. Placement exception and fresh head-bound Quickstart evidence remain review items; this update does not claim maintainer approval.





### Latest head validation (2026-11-20)

- The provider registry route now bypasses only the global 64 KiB JSON cap and uses a route-specific 4 MiB cap with the configured gateway timeout; the global cap remains unchanged.

- Current head: `f06c998aa1`; declared parent: `cdf1929c97`.
- The branch was rebuilt from the clean reflection parent; downstream ZeroCode and Web changes are not included.
- Registry model defaults preserve unset reasoning extraction (`None`) outside the documented MiniMax/Groq defaults, so think-only responses are normalized and explicit `false` remains an opt-out.
- Registry edits reject deleting the configured vision model, in addition to the existing embedding reference guard.
- `cargo check --offline -p zeroclaw-config --lib` and `cargo check --offline -p zeroclaw-providers --lib` passed with `RUSTC_WRAPPER=`.
- GitHub CI is the source of truth for the full workspace and feature matrix; baseline dependency-security findings remain outside this PR's scope.


This backend cutover layer supersedes #9809; the original PR remains the historical reference only.

prs.title: fix(infra): preserve created_at of retained rows when replacing a session transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Replacing a SQLite session transcript deleted every row and reinserted them all with one timestamp, so from the second turn on `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` returned the time of the last write for every message. The replacement now aligns the new transcript with the stored rows and lets every row that lines up keep its `created_at`; only genuinely new messages get the time of the write.
  - The alignment is the longest run of stored rows that equals the start of the new transcript (earliest run on a tie, which drops the fewest rows). That covers an appended turn, a trim from the start, a trim plus a new turn, and any of these with a changed last row. The usual per-turn case inserts only the new tail and deletes nothing.
  - The history-trim breadcrumb is identified by the stored and incoming flags, never by its text. A newly inserted breadcrumb takes the time of its first write; a retained one keeps its own. The bare `rewrite_messages` leaves the stored flag untouched and says so by passing no incoming flag (`Option<bool>`), so it cannot disagree with the stored one.
  - The three replacement paths now open their transaction as `IMMEDIATE`, because they read before they write. `last_activity` stays the time of the write, never an inherited message time.
  - Tests cover both SQLite replacement paths, the gateway restore-time trim, the gateway end-of-turn write (with and without a history cap) and the RPC chat restore-time trim. A criterion benchmark covers the write paths.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No backfill: rows that were already flattened are inherited as they are; no historical times are invented.
  - Not changed: the JSONL backend (it stores no per-row times), the ACP store (`acp_messages.created_at` has the same flattening mechanism but a different writer; tracked in #11675), and how channel hydration decides the breadcrumb flag from the text of the first row (a different mechanism, outside this change; it will be reported separately if its analysis confirms it). The API shape, the schema and the configuration are unchanged.
  - Known limits, each pinned by a test: when identical messages cannot be told apart after a trim, the write drops the fewest old rows, so a retained row may inherit the time of an earlier identical one (this is the behavior agreed in the issue thread); and an incoming breadcrumb flag with no breadcrumb row makes the first row inherit the time of the stored first row.
- **Blast radius:** every consumer of SQLite session transcripts: gateway WebSocket chat, RPC chat and channel sessions, and whatever shows the times returned by `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` (the dashboard Sessions view; #11622 reads them in ZeroCode). Channel sessions reach the changed code through `replace_conversation_state` (`crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs`). Every replacement now reads the stored rows before writing; see the measurements below.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11420. Related #11593 (an earlier attempt by the same author, closed without merging). Related #11622. Related #11675 (the same mechanism in the ACP store).

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw keeps each chat session as a list of messages in SQLite, and every message row has a `created_at`: the time it was first saved. At the end of every turn the agent hands the backend its whole current history, and the backend used to delete all the rows of the session and write them again with the time of that moment. Messages from earlier turns therefore all showed the time of the latest turn, and the original times were lost for good.

This change makes the backend compare the new history with what is stored. Messages that are still there keep the time they were first saved, and only messages that are really new get the current time. When the agent trims old turns, the turns it keeps keep their times too. When a turn only adds messages, nothing is deleted. Sessions that were already flattened are not repaired, because the original times no longer exist anywhere.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web` (gateway WebSocket chat and `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages`) and `tui` (RPC chat, `session/new` restoring a session). No channel surface is exercised by an end-to-end test.
- **Setup / preconditions:** a Rust toolchain and a Linux or WSL checkout. Building the `zeroclaw-runtime` tests is memory-heavy: on a 6 GB machine I used `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. On this branch:
     ```sh
     cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra --locked --lib session_sqlite
     cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --locked --lib websocket_turn_end
     cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --locked --lib websocket_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_sqlite_rows
     cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --locked --lib session_new_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_chat_rows
     ```
  2. For the old behavior, put only the two backend source files back to `master` and rerun the gateway and runtime commands (the backend tests live inside `session_sqlite.rs`, so they disappear with it):
     ```sh
     git checkout origin/master -- crates/zeroclaw-infra/src/session_sqlite.rs crates/zeroclaw-infra/src/session_backend.rs
     ```
     Restore with `git checkout HEAD -- crates/zeroclaw-infra/src/session_sqlite.rs crates/zeroclaw-infra/src/session_backend.rs`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** all four commands pass.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the four integration tests fail, each on a time comparison:
  - `websocket_turn_end_keeps_created_at_of_earlier_turns_in_sqlite`: `row 0 of the first turn must keep the time it was first persisted`
  - `websocket_turn_end_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_sqlite_rows`: `turn 2: "[CURRENT DATE & TIME: …]\n\nprompt number 1" must keep the time it was first persisted`
  - `session_new_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_chat_rows`: `retained row "turn two request" must keep the time it was first persisted`
  - `websocket_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_sqlite_rows`: `retained row "turn two request" must keep its original time`

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Format` (rustfmt), `Lint` (`clippy --all-targets` compiles the new benchmark; the comment hygiene gate covers the new comments) and `Test` (runs the new unit and integration tests on the changed crates).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the benchmark is compiled by the lint job but never run in CI, and the performance numbers below are from one machine. The `bench` job only compiles `agent_benchmarks`.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Linux (WSL2, rustc 1.98.1), on the final commit unless noted.

  ```text
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra --locked
  test result: ok. 334 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --locked --lib
  test result: ok. 651 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --locked --lib session_new_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at
  test rpc::dispatch::tests::session_new_restore_time_trim_keeps_created_at_of_retained_chat_rows ... ok
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5699 filtered out

  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-runtime --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings -A clippy::drop-non-drop
  Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s)

  python scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.py <changed files>
  Comment hygiene gate passed.
  ```

  `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on each changed `.rs` file passes (I did not run `cargo fmt --all` because the workspace does not resolve on my Windows host). The runtime test above was run on an earlier commit of this branch whose `dispatch.rs` is identical to the final one.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Regression checks: with the two backend source files from `master`, the four integration tests above fail with the messages listed; with the branch they pass. For the backend, the two original reproduction tests from the issue (`rewrite_keeps_created_at_of_unchanged_rows` and `rewrite_if_exists_keeps_created_at_of_unchanged_rows`) fail on `master` at `ea4a54bb5` and pass on the branch.
  - `t19_replacements_do_not_fail_with_database_is_locked_under_contention` passes 12 of 12 runs and fails 11 of 12 when the `IMMEDIATE` transaction is changed to a deferred one, so it does catch that change (it is a race, not deterministic).
  - Alignment: a standalone copy of the pure alignment functions was checked against an independent oracle on 60,000 random transcripts (append, trim, trim plus append, changed last row, changed last row plus trim, with and without a breadcrumb) with 0 mismatches, and the fast "insert only the tail" path never fired when stored rows differed from the requested ones.
  - Performance, one machine (WSL2), `opt-level = 3` and no LTO through `CARGO_PROFILE_BENCH_*` (the repo's release profile optimizes for size), binaries for `master` and the branch run alternately in rounds with the order rotated, paired by round. Median time per call at 1000 messages:

    | case | messages of ~230 B, `master` → branch | messages of ~20 KB, `master` → branch |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | rewrite, unchanged transcript | 37.5 ms → 0.40 ms | 245 ms → 13.5 ms |
    | rewrite plus one new turn | 32.7 ms → 0.82 ms | 268 ms → 25.2 ms |

    Both improvements were in the right direction in every one of 7 rounds. `append` (unchanged code) and `load_with_timestamps` showed no consistent difference.
  - **Cost:** with messages of ~20 KB, rewrites that drop most of the transcript are slower, because the stored rows are now read before they are replaced. Compaction at 1000 messages went from 83.5 ms to 93.2 ms (median of 11 rounds; the branch was slower in 10 of them, sign test p = 0.012, which does not survive a correction for the five cells I compared). A half trim went from 161 ms to 197 ms (median of 7 rounds; slower in 6 of them, p = 0.125, inconclusive). Peak memory of the unchanged rewrite with a ~20 MB transcript rose from about 39 MB to about 51 MB. Round-to-round variation of the same binary was 1.5x to 2x, so small differences should not be read as findings.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` (no presentation change; the values of an existing field change)
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** N/A (see above)
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** I did not run the full workspace tests, the full `zeroclaw-runtime` lib suite, the `zeroclaw-channels` tests, or anything on Windows or macOS; I did not run a real provider, the dashboard or a browser against this branch. The gateway tests use a real gateway and the SQLite backend with a local provider fixture. `clippy` is run with `-A clippy::drop-non-drop` on the three changed crates because that lint fails today on unchanged code in `zeroclaw-channels` (`crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs`, three `drop(dispatch_ownership)` calls), which is identical on `master`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: none. For the record: `created_at` was already returned by `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages`; this change only makes it return the time each message was first saved instead of the time of the last write. The new SQL statements use bound parameters, and the transcript and breadcrumb flag are still written in one transaction, with the deleted-session guard of `replace_conversation_state_if_exists` unchanged (it still returns `false` and writes nothing).

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes` (no schema change; existing databases work as they are; rows already flattened stay flattened)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: not applicable. The benchmark adds `criterion = "0.8"` as a dev-dependency of `zeroclaw-infra`; `criterion` is already in the workspace, and `Cargo.lock` gains only that one dependency line.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the two commits of this PR. There is no data migration: the stored columns are the same, times written by the new behavior stay valid, and the old code would flatten them again at its next replacement.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `None`
- **Observable failure symptoms:** the gateway log message `Failed to persist authoritative post-turn conversation state` or `database is locked` errors from session persistence; a retained message showing the time of the latest turn again; slower end-of-turn writes in very long sessions with large messages.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose the composition-seam row for bounded-delegation ceiling carriage (#9872, #10391)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - #10391 (the #9872 fix) carries a bounded delegate's tool-name ceiling into the scheduler tools, `sop_execute`, `sop_advance`, `sop_workshop`, `spawn_subagent` and `send_message_to_peer`. To do that through the native registry factory it adds a crate-private `caller_ceiling` input on `NativeRecipeInputs`, forwards it in `src/composition/config_backed.rs` (two added lines), adds one `None` in the owned SOP step assembly call in `src/composition/supplied_only_traps.rs`, adds 15 `bounded-ceiling-*` refusal messages in `locales/en/cli.ftl`, and adds tests.
  - Review on #10391 pointed out that the ceiling-carriage row (#11652) does not list `src/composition/config_backed.rs`, and that threading the ceiling through that factory needs its own Core-approved row before #10391 merges.
  - This adds one row, directly under the #11652 row, for that extension. The approval cell records Audacity88's November 14 Core placement decision ([review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12403#pullrequestreview-5905465683)); the scope, destination and review conditions are unchanged from the version approved at `6162c006ab`.
  - The #11652 row and every other row are unchanged.
- **Scope boundary:** The table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` only. No code. The row does not add a construction, a public API, a capability kind or a tool grant, and does not change approval, admission or budget authority. It does not build a ceiling for sessions narrowed by an RPC principal's tool selector (`src/agent/agent.rs` still passes `None` there; #12232 withholds the tools that need an unrestricted principal from such sessions, see #12394), and it does not cover a recipe or factory that builds those tools itself.
- **Blast radius:** Merge eligibility of #10391's runtime changes under ADR-016.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9872, Related #10391, Related #11652, Related #12394

### What this does, simply

The runtime crate is a holding crate: new work there needs a recorded Core decision. prs.title: docs(adr): propose daemon-held OIDC refresh and Okta/Entra ID support in ADR-017
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Amends proposed ADR-017 with a decision for **device-session continuity**: the daemon holds the IdP refresh token as a sealed *refresh grant* keyed by provider alias + ledger `device_id`; a pre-auth RPC authorized by the device's mTLS certificate (admitted like `cert/renew`) refreshes it, verifies the new access token through the same `oidc.<alias>` provider and same `sub`, and returns only the access token for an ordinary `initialize`. Today a Zerocode session cannot outlive one access token: the gateway discards the refresh token and Zerocode replays the login-time token on every reconnect, so sleep/resume past `exp` ends in `-32010`.
  - Adds a decision for **Okta and Entra ID** (required for v1.0). Neither issues RFC 9068 tokens: Okta access tokens have no `typ` and use `cid`; Entra uses `typ: JWT`, `uti` instead of `jti`, and has no introspection endpoint. The amendment keeps token-purpose separation by requiring audience ≠ every configured client_id when `typ: at+jwt` is absent (an ID token's `aud` is always its client), and admits vendor claim spellings only as named, tested compatibility rules (precedent: the Keycloak `azp` rule). Device-grant scopes become per-provider so Entra can request the API scope that sets the audience.
  - Adds matching acceptance gates (sleep/wake + rotation/revocation tests; real-tenant Okta and Entra verification), consequences (daemon now holds long-lived IdP secrets; partially deployment-side audience invariant; Entra revocation bounded by token lifetime + refresh interval), and standards/vendor references. Updates the ADR index gate summary.
- **Scope boundary:** Docs only. No code, config schema, or behavior changes. Browser dashboard stays refresh-free. Existing docs describing current behavior (`zerocode/remote.md` "no refresh-token cache") are left alone until the implementation lands.
- **Blast radius:** None at runtime. Constrains future work in `auth_provider/oidc.rs`, `auth_provider/enrollment.rs`, `cert_ledger.rs`, RPC dispatch pre-auth methods, and Zerocode's connection/auth path.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8289

### What this does, simply

Signing in to ZeroClaw from Zerocode through an identity provider currently lasts only as long as one access token, often minutes to an hour. If your laptop sleeps longer than that, the session can't resume and you have to restart and sign in again, even though your identity provider would happily keep you signed in. This records the plan to fix that: the daemon keeps the provider's refresh token (never your laptop), and your device certificate lets Zerocode quietly ask the daemon for a fresh token.

It also records how ZeroClaw will accept Okta and Entra ID tokens. Their access tokens are shaped differently from what the verifier accepts today, so Entra cannot sign in at all and Okta only works through introspection. The plan accepts their formats without weakening the check that stops an ID token being used as an access token.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Docs-only ADR amendment with no behavior change.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Docs style and link checks cover the two changed Markdown files.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The links gate runs lychee offline, so the 8 new external links (RFC Editor, OpenID, Microsoft Learn, Okta developer docs) are excluded rather than fetched. The Entra and Okta pages were fetched manually while drafting.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base upstream/master HEAD) scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Linting: 2 file(s)
Summary: 0 error(s)

$ BASE_SHA=$(git merge-base upstream/master HEAD) scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
Collected 9 added link(s) from 2 docs file(s).
Checked 1 local docs link target(s).
👻 Excluded.........8
🚫 Errors...........0
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Checked each technical claim against source: `api_oidc.rs` drops refresh tokens (test `rt-never-relayed`); `apps/zerocode/src/main.rs` snapshots `WssRoute.auth_token` at startup and replays it on reconnect; `rpc/dispatch.rs` `handle_initialize` re-authenticates a live connection and enforces same-principal on bound connections; `oidc.rs` requires `typ: at+jwt`, `jti`, and `client_id`/`azp` in JWKS mode; `enrollment.rs` hard-codes `scope=openid` for the device grant; `cert_ledger.rs` keys rows by fingerprint with a stable `device_id`. Token formats were checked against the Microsoft Entra access-token claims reference and Okta's OIDC overview. Not verified: behavior against real Okta or Entra tenants (now an acceptance gate).

- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** N/A
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No (docs only). The *decision* records a future change: the daemon will retain IdP refresh tokens, sealed through the ADR-013 key source, deleted on every refusal path, revoked at the IdP on sign-out, and never released to clients. Containment is certificate revocation plus IdP session revocation.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No

prs.title: ci(audit): stop the daily advisory scan going quiet behind an open issue
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The Daily Advisory Scan (`daily-audit.yml`) opened an issue only when no open issue had "Advisory scan failed" in its title. #11429, opened by the scan on 2026-10-02 and kept open to track the accepted anymap2 advisory, has matched ever since. So the 14 failed scans after it opened no issue. That includes the 2026-11-19 09:05Z run, which found RUSTSEC-2026-0566 to -0573 on `master` and logged "An open advisory issue already exists — skipping duplicate."
  - It now deduplicates on the set of *failing* advisory IDs. Allowed warnings (unmaintained, unsound or yanked crates the policy accepts; 19 of them in that run) don't count, so the set changes only when a failure does: cargo-audit marks a warning block with a `Warning:` line, and cargo-deny heads each finding with `error[...]` or `warning[...]`. Each issue body carries an `<!-- advisory-scan-ids: … -->` marker and lists the IDs. A run whose set matches an open issue links that issue, and a new set opens a new issue (with the existing maintainer mention). The run fails either way.
  - It now installs the cargo-deny 0.19.9 build that the `Security` job in `ci.yml` uses, instead of `cargo install cargo-deny --locked` (the latest release, built from source on every run). cargo-audit was already the same 0.22.2 build.
  - The maintainer docs entry described only cargo-deny and no dedup. It now matches.
- **Scope boundary:** Report-only, as before: no patch PRs, no lockfile edits. The schedule (daily 09:00 UTC), checks, the scoped webpki policy step and permissions are unchanged. `daily-npm-audit.yml` has the same title-only dedup and is left alone here; it hasn't been silenced by a long-lived issue yet.
- **Blast radius:** this workflow's issue creation only. Existing open scan issues without a marker are never matched, so the first failing run after merge opens a fresh, deduplicable issue.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11429, Related #12577

### What this does, simply

Every morning a job checks the project's Rust dependencies against the RustSec advisory list and opens an issue if something is wrong. It was meant to avoid duplicates, but it treated any open advisory issue as a duplicate. One issue has been left open since October on purpose, to track a known problem, so the job has quietly opened nothing since then, even when new security advisories appeared. Now it only treats an issue as a duplicate when it's about exactly the same advisories, so a new advisory always gets a new issue. It also uses the same tool versions as the regular CI security check.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional, after merge.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** GitHub Actions (`workflow_dispatch` on Daily Advisory Scan).
- **Setup / preconditions:** an advisory failing on `master`, or a branch with an ignored advisory removed from `deny.toml`/`.cargo/audit.toml`.
- **Steps to run:** dispatch the workflow twice.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the first run fails and opens "ci: Advisory scan failed — <date>" listing the IDs, even with #11429 open. The second run fails and links the same issue instead of opening another.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** both runs fail and open nothing while #11429 is open.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Docs Style` covers the changed docs line. No CI job runs this workflow on a PR.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the issue path only runs on a real scheduled or dispatched failure.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ actionlint -shellcheck=shellcheck .github/workflows/daily-audit.yml      # actionlint 1.7.11
2 findings, both SC2016:info "Expressions don't expand in single quotes", for the literal
backticks in the existing printf lines. master's file reports the same two; nothing new.

$ python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/daily-audit.yml'))"   # parses

$ DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/maintainers/ci-and-actions.md BASE_SHA=597f53ba7e scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Linting: 1 file(s)
Summary: 0 error(s)
$ DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/maintainers/ci-and-actions.md BASE_SHA=597f53ba7e scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
No added links detected in changed docs lines.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - **ID extraction**, using the awk program pulled from this workflow file, under mawk 1.3.4 (what Ubuntu's `awk` may resolve to), gawk 5.2.1 and BSD awk:
    - the real 2026-11-19 scan output (8 failing and 19 allowed advisories) gives exactly RUSTSEC-2026-0566 to -0573;
    - synthetic cargo-deny output with one `error[vulnerability]` and one `warning[unmaintained]` gives only the error's ID;
    - a fetch failure gives no IDs.
  - **Dedup**, under the runner's `bash -eo pipefail` with a fake `gh` returning canned issue lists:
    - an open old-format issue (no marker, like #11429) plus a new failure → no match, so a new issue;
    - an open issue with the same IDs → links it;
    - an open issue with only some of the IDs → no match, so a new issue;
    - no IDs → `none` marker, no crash under `pipefail`.

  Not verified: a real run on GitHub, and more than 100 open matching issues (the list limit; there is one today).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** N/A
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No cargo checks: no Rust change.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (still `contents: read`, `issues: write`)
- New external network calls? No. The cargo-deny download replaces a crates.io source build, from the same release URL the `Security` job already uses.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert <sha>` restores title-only dedup and `cargo install cargo-deny`. Symptom to watch after merge: a failing scan whose log ends with "An open issue already reports this set of advisories: <url>" should point at an issue listing the same IDs.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose the owner-plane routing row for bounded delegation (#9872, #10391)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - #10391 (the #9872 fix) makes a bounded delegate's target use the owner's plane when the session has an owner. The target's session memory route is pinned to the owner's plane for that target; the child of the rebuilt `spawn_subagent` runs on it, `sop_execute` and `sop_advance` start and advance runs and write their audit rows through it, and `sop_status` shows the runs of that plane and not the caller's. A hop whose target inherits one of those tools is refused when that plane cannot be opened.
  - Review on #10391 pointed out that `src/tools/sop_status.rs` is not in the path list of the ceiling-carriage row (#11652) or of any other row. `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` says a feature pull request cannot grant itself an exception, so the record has to come from a separate change. #10391 also changes runtime paths that the #11652 row does not list (`src/composition.rs`, `src/composition/config_backed.rs`, `locales/en/cli.ftl` and the tests of the ceiling carriage); those are the subject of #12403, a separate pull request that is still open, and this row does not cover them.
  - This adds one row, directly under the #11652 row, for the owner-plane routing. The approval cell says "Pending Core Team approval on this pull request", the wording the table already uses for a row awaiting its decision. Every existing row is unchanged.
- **Scope boundary:** The table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` only. No code. The row adds no tool, route, delivery path, public API, capability kind or tool grant, and does not change approval, admission or budget authority. It does not cover independent delegation (its registry pins its own route in the native factory, `src/tools/mod.rs`), a delegate with neither a root nor a target configuration (the production registry sets a root configuration, so it does not build one, and such a delegate is not rebuilt: it keeps the caller's instances), the tools of a recipe or factory that builds them itself, or the SOP engine and its storage.
- **Blast radius:** Merge eligibility of the owner-plane part of #10391 under ADR-016. No runtime behavior changes here. This row and the composition-seam row proposed in #12403 both sit under the #11652 row, so whichever lands second needs its placement refreshed.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9872, Related #10391, Related #11652, Related #12403

### What this does, simply

The runtime crate is a holding crate: new work there needs a recorded Core decision. #10391 fixes a lost-binding defect in bounded delegation, and in an owned session that fix also has to keep the work a target starts on the owner's plane for that target: before it, a target's SOP tools wrote their audit rows and read run status through the caller's plane. The change touches `sop_status.rs`, which no row names, and gives `sop_execute` and `sop_advance` a different route than the ceiling-carriage row describes. This row lists those paths and states the behavior, so Core can approve, narrow or refuse it explicitly. If it is narrowed or refused, the matching part of #10391 can be cut back to what the existing rows cover. One cost to know about: in an owned session a hop whose target inherits `spawn_subagent`, `sop_execute`, `sop_advance` or `sop_status` now opens the target's memory before it starts, so a memory source that cannot provide it refuses the hop even if the model would never have called the tool.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for scope only.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** None. This changes a governance table, not a `surface` or `channel`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A checkout of this branch and of #10391's head.
- **Steps to run:** Compare the row's path list with `git diff --name-only master...<#10391 head> -- crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/sop_status.rs crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/sop_execute.rs crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/sop_advance.rs crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/delegate.rs crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/scoped.rs`, and check that each path is named by the new row or by the #11652 row; then read the claims in the row against the code they cite in the next section.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** One added row with four cells; every existing table line unchanged; `src/tools/sop_status.rs` named by the new row.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `src/tools/sop_status.rs` is named by no row, and the #11652 row describes `sop_execute` and `sop_advance` only as ceiling carriage.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Docs Style` runs markdownlint and the em-dash check on the changed file, and the docs link gates; it does not check the claims in the row. `CI Required Gate` for the rest. Live result: see the checks on this pull request.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None after the docs and links gates. The claims in the row are not machine-checked; they are checked by reading, listed below.
- **Commands run and tail output:** on commit `e643cc1d0c` (WSL, `BASE_SHA` = `master` `ad4c1f6c3a`, `DOCS_FILES=crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`):
  - `bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` → rc=0: `No prose em-dashes in changed docs files.`, `Linting docs files: crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, `markdownlint-cli2 v0.20.0 (markdownlint v0.40.0)`, `Summary: 0 error(s)`.
  - `bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh` → rc=0: `Collected 0 added link(s) from 1 docs file(s).`, `No added links detected in changed docs lines.`
  - `python3 scripts/ci/check_internal_docs_links.py` → rc=0: `Checked authored Markdown links in 220 file(s); no broken local targets.`
  - `git diff --numstat ad4c1f6c3a HEAD` → `1 0 crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` (one added line, none removed).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Each claim in the row against #10391's code at head `0f9890b856` (read on 2026-11-19):
  - the route is pinned to the owner's plane for the target: `delegate.rs` `route.pin(plane, …)` and `target_owner_scope = Some(owner_scope)` (~`:5904-5912`);
  - the hop is refused with the existing tool-initialization error and a log record that names the step, not the source's error: `bounded_owner_plane_refusal` (~`:1839`), the reason `"target_memory_unavailable"` (~`:5897`), `sealed_route_refusal` (~`:1850`) and the guard on the sealed registry (~`:6868`);
  - `sop_execute` and `sop_advance` take the target's route through their existing `with_session_memory` (present on `master`); `sop_status` is rebound through a crate-private method added in `sop_status.rs`;
  - `sop_approve` is not rebound: a refusing stub takes its place (`BoundedSopApproveDenied`, ~`:6050`; the stub is part of #10391, not of `master`);
  - the names of the tools that share the route and of those that only read it are two lists in `scoped.rs` (~`:382`, `:390`); the registry's memory-work check uses the first, the pipeline and `sop_approve`, and the hop uses both;
  - the exclusions: the native factory pins its own route (`src/tools/mod.rs:4062-4073`); the production registry sets the root configuration (`src/tools/mod.rs:5544`; it also sets the runtime, `:5524`), and the route is only made when a configuration is in hand (`delegate.rs` `rebuild_config`, ~`:5800`); the sealing pass uses a default config so no pipeline tool is minted (`delegate.rs` ~`:6829-6832`).
  The behavior itself is covered in #10391 by regression tests that were checked by reverting the guarded line. What I did **not** verify: that Core agrees the `sop_execute` and `sop_advance` routing fits the scope of the #11652 row; a skill wrapper around these tools was traced by reading only, not by a test, and the row says nothing about it.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no user-visible interface state changed).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** this branch at `e643cc1d0c` on `master` `ad4c1f6c3a`; the code the row describes is #10391 at head `0f9890b856`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** None of the three docs gates. Not run: the optional HTTP(S) link check, because the row adds no link and `lychee` is not installed on my machine; `cargo` checks, because no code changes.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`

The row is a table entry (the record ADR-016 asks for) that approves code which keeps a target's work on the owner's plane for that target; it grants no runtime capability and changes no file system scope. One behavior the row's code introduces, so reviewers can weigh it: in a session with an owner, a hop whose target inherits `spawn_subagent`, `sop_execute`, `sop_advance` or `sop_status` now asks the caller's memory source for the target's memory, and is refused if the source cannot provide it. That includes a target that inherits only `sop_status`, which starts no memory work itself but shows the runs of the plane the route is pinned to. A target that inherits none of the four opens no plane.
