prs.title: docs(runtime): propose bounded RPC denial reason exception
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** Adds one row to the active-exception table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`, proposing a bounded holding-crate exception for the stable RPC denial reasons and reason-keyed denial records in #11289 (which closes #11005). The crate guide requires the exception to be recorded before the feature merges, and a feature pull request cannot grant itself one, so the row is proposed here on its own. It answers the open review item on #11289 (`src/rpc/auth.rs:97`, 2026-10-12), which found that no recorded exception covers RPC denial reporting.
- **Scope boundary:** Documentation only. The permission covers exactly what #11289 changes in `zeroclaw-runtime` at `8b3ee1e18db30e9e29bf8ac03ce6bf918dcbdf79` against master `afd6cf912e413c36a8ba7b23c55bb66d48e52782` (three files: `src/rpc/auth.rs`, `src/rpc/dispatch.rs` and `locales/en/cli.ftl`): the `RpcDenialReason` identifier type with `as_str`, its private `code` and `message_key` mappings and `From<DenyReason>`; on the existing `AuthDenied`, the private `reason` field and `reason()` accessor, the private `new`, `with_message` and `with_values` builders, the `quoted` helper, the 23 named `pub(crate)` constructors that replace `auth_required` and `forbidden` (with `from_deny_reason` rebuilt on the private `with_message` and the five other `auth.rs` functions named in the row, including the shared `authenticate_checked` implementation, building their denials through them), and `audit_attrs`, which gives the existing `RPC authorization denied` record its `method`, `reason`, `denial_message`, `code`, `principal_id` and `auth_provider` attributes; in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`, `audit_denial` emitting those attributes, `RpcDispatcher::refuse`, the `authorize` gate and the 24 other refusal functions named in the row building their denials through the constructors or refusing through `refuse`, the gate attributing a denial after a failed revalidation to the principal whose binding it drops, the `steering_admission` closure's record changes (its session-ownership, revoked transport-owner and remote local-capability refusals recorded under their own reasons, the latter with that reason's `-32003` on the record while the steer is still answered `-32012`; the refusals its binding checks record themselves recorded once rather than twice, so a steer refused because its agent's policy cannot be resolved leaves no denial record), the selectors' and cron write rechecks' no-binding refusals now recorded, the retired `GLOBAL_STREAM_SCOPED_DENIAL` literal, the fourteen added `rpc-auth-*` keys and their translator comment (including `rpc-auth-session-transport-ownership-changed`; thirteen replacing an inline literal, `rpc-auth-session-local-capabilities` feeding only the record), and reuse of the existing `sop-rpc-principal-ceiling-required` and `rpc-cron-agent-principal-required` keys, and focused tests. `RpcDenialReason`, `as_str` and `reason()` are `pub`; no other crate consumes them. `DenyReason`, the JSON-RPC error codes and the grants stay in `zeroclaw-api`, and the record sink in `zeroclaw-log`, so they need no runtime permission; the root `AGENTS.md` bullet and the `docs/book` section that #11289 adds are outside the holding crate. It excludes any identifier in a client response, recording a refused `initialize` handshake or the other refusals answered without an `AuthDenied`, and any new RPC method, grant source, config key, record kind, record sink, retained runtime state or non-English locale.
- **Blast radius:** Contributor placement guidance only. No runtime behavior changes. The prior enumeration was approved by @Audacity88 on 2026-10-29; its permalink remains in the row. This amendment updates the SOP constructor/helper, adds the cron-principal and revoked transport-owner constructors, and replaces the removed SOP Fluent key with the transport-owner key. @JordanTheJet approved this amended enumeration on 2026-11-09 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12062#pullrequestreview-5821600639); that approval is now recorded in the Approved-by cell. The earlier @Audacity88 decision covers only the prior enumeration.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11005 and #11289 (head `8b3ee1e18db30e9e29bf8ac03ce6bf918dcbdf79` against master `afd6cf912e413c36a8ba7b23c55bb66d48e52782`). #11289 lands after #11326, whose global-stream wording the row's key note reflects. Precedent: #11701, #12058, #11963, and the #11286 row already in the table, which covers `src/rpc/auth.rs` and `locales/en/cli.ftl` but is limited to roster-bound pairing tokens.

### What this does, simply

`zeroclaw-runtime` is a holding crate: new code there is supposed to move to its own crate, and the Core Team records each deliberate exception in a table so the extraction debt stays visible. #11289 gives every RPC authorization refusal built through `AuthDenied` a stable identifier such as `grant_missing` or `agent_not_entitled`, writes that identifier into the denial record the daemon already emits (the refusal text moves to its own `denial_message` attribute), moves the refusals' inline English literals into the Fluent catalogue (the gate's grant refusal and the global-stream, session-environment, upload-ownership and revoked transport-owner refusals as well as the selectors'; SOP and cron-principal refusals reuse their existing Fluent keys), and keeps the principal and provider on the record when a policy change drops a connection's binding. Clients receive the same codes and English text as before (the global-stream refusal takes the wording #11326 gives it), and never the identifier. The set of recorded refusals changes slightly: the selectors' and cron write rechecks' no-binding refusals are now recorded, a steer refused by its agent, workspace or environment check is recorded once rather than twice, and a steer refused because its agent's policy cannot be resolved is no longer recorded. This row asks permission for exactly those changes, with the RPC authorization-gate and inbound-authentication owners in the planned kernel extraction as their destination.

Why placement is right: every one of these additions changes code the crate already holds. On master, `AuthDenied`, with its `auth_required`, `forbidden` and `from_deny_reason` constructors, sits in `src/rpc/auth.rs` next to `RpcInboundAuth`, `AcceptedAuthState` and `AuthorityLease`; `RpcDispatcher::authorize`, `audit_denial` (which already writes the `RPC authorization denied` record, with the message as its `reason`), `current_authority`, the selectors and `still_authorized` sit in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`; and the handshake denials already resolve `rpc-auth-*` keys in `locales/en/cli.ftl`. The reason is set by the code that decides to refuse, so it lives where that decision is made, and it reaches only the log record: `rpc_err(denied.code, denied.message)` still sends the client the code and text alone, so the identifier is not part of the wire contract `zeroclaw-api` owns, and `zeroclaw-log` records whatever attributes the gate hands it. Moving the vocabulary out on its own would split the gate from its refusals ahead of the kernel extraction that owns the RPC boundary, which is the case the exception policy describes. #11005 names `src/rpc/{auth,dispatch}.rs` and the catalogue among the work's likely files.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`; documentation-only change to a Markdown table. Please review the row's scope against #11289 at `8b3ee1e18db30e9e29bf8ac03ce6bf918dcbdf79`: `git diff --stat afd6cf912e413c36a8ba7b23c55bb66d48e52782 8b3ee1e18db30e9e29bf8ac03ce6bf918dcbdf79 -- crates/zeroclaw-runtime` lists the three files it names.

### How I tested

#### Current scope amendment: `3e5321f59e0c9dad7a682eedf3b46482186188f9`

The one-row amendment follows #11289 at `8b3ee1e18db30e9e29bf8ac03ce6bf918dcbdf79` against master `afd6cf912e413c36a8ba7b23c55bb66d48e52782`: 30 reason variants, 23 named constructors, 24 other dispatcher refusal functions, and 14 added `rpc-auth-*` keys. The SOP and cron-principal constructors retain existing Fluent keys. The row records the revoked transport-owner refusal and cites @JordanTheJet's 2026-11-09 approval of the amended enumeration, keeping the note that the earlier decision covers only the prior enumeration.

`git diff --check` passed. Both `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` and `scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh` passed with `BASE_SHA=3e50a4720b1f959d0346390030d0319c347fab27` and `DOCS_FILES=crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`. Markdownlint reported zero errors and the link gate's six tests passed. Its offline HTTP check excluded the unchanged approval URL; the actual review was verified through GitHub. Rust suites were not run for this documentation-only amendment. Hosted checks remain a separate gate.

#### Earlier integration: `3e50a4720b1f959d0346390030d0319c347fab27`

This additive merge brings in master `f87368a6aa53d16b0bd7411b002331a22622c2a7`, including the merged Wasmtime security repair #12129. The complete runtime instruction file remains byte-identical to this PR's preceding head; the owned diff is still the same one-row addition. Approval status and scope are unchanged. Both dependency files exactly match master.

On this exact revision, the docs quality gate and docs links gate passed with `DOCS_FILES=crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` and `BASE_SHA=f87368a6aa53d16b0bd7411b002331a22622c2a7`; the link gate's six tests passed, and `git diff --check` passed. The merge and preserved row were independently checked. Rust/plugin suites were not rerun locally for this docs-only owned delta; #12129 supplies inherited dependency evidence. Hosted checks for the published revision must complete separately.

#### Earlier validation

The following evidence belongs to the earlier revisions named below.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the docs-links and comment-hygiene gates. `Docs Style` lints only `docs/book/src`, so it does not cover this file; markdownlint was run by hand below.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no CI markdown lint for `crates/*/AGENTS.md` (run by hand below). No check can confirm that a row matches the code it covers or that a Core decision exists; that is this review.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
git diff --check                                              passed
BASE_SHA=5d4b18d335 scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh             No added links detected in changed docs lines.
scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh crates/zeroclaw-runtime    Comment hygiene gate passed.
python3 -I scripts/ci/check_internal_docs_links.py
                                                              Checked authored Markdown links in 219 file(s); no broken local targets.
python3 -I scripts/ci/check_internal_docs_links.py --root crates/zeroclaw-runtime
                                                              Checked authored Markdown links in 11 file(s); no broken local targets.
npx --yes markdownlint-cli2@0.20.0 crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md
                                                              Summary: 0 error(s)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The row names every runtime path #11289 changes at `5740f15a35` (`git diff --stat` against master `5d4b18d335`: three files under `crates/zeroclaw-runtime`) and nothing else; every type, function, constructor, Fluent key, record attribute and test it names exists at that head (28 `RpcDenialReason` variants, 21 constructors, 32 constructor call sites in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`, 14 added `rpc-auth-*` keys, and no surviving `AuthDenied::auth_required`, `AuthDenied::forbidden` or `AuthDenied { .. }` literal anywhere under `crates/`); the table still has four cells per row, the new row is the last row directly under the previous one, and the file has no em-dash. No Rust was built: no code changes.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`; no user-visible interface changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `N/A`
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `N/A`
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** `N/A`
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Rust gates do not apply to a Markdown-only change.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`; once approved, the row permits only the named additions in the holding crate and grants no execution or data-access authority.
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`

## Compatibility (required)

prs.title: fix(delegate): keep a bounded delegate's workspace, tool ceiling and command policy bound beyond the turn (#9872)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. The head is `9365b1638d`, taken on 2026-11-19. It contains the current `master` tip `ad4c1f6c3a` (merged by `0f9890b856`), so `master` is not ahead of it; among earlier `master` merges are `ba665d125`, `abf3896e4`, `a3f7fe257` and `236facb0a`. Whether the merge builds is shown by the live CI run, not by this line: an earlier head merged without a textual conflict and did not compile (see *CI*).
- **Problem:** the bounded-delegation contract says the caller bounds what a bounded target can do: its filesystem tools work in the target's own workspace, the caller's tool registry is a ceiling, and the caller's command policy stays authoritative. That bound was applied while the target's turn was assembled and then lost by anything that runs *after* that point, because such work rebuilt its tools or its policy without it. Each escape below is repaired where the bound has to survive, not at the reported symptom.
- **What changed and why:**
  - **Workspace (original scope, #9872).** A bounded delegate's filesystem tools are rebuilt against the target's own policy and workspace. Follow-ups in the same spirit: `git_operations` gets a real command boundary built from the target's sandbox (`DelegateTool::rebuild_target_git_operations_tool`), and `backup`/`data_management` keep the target's policy over `master`'s shared data directory.
  - **Tool ceiling carried into work that outlives the turn.** `SopStepReassembly` carries `caller_allowed`; `all_tools_with_runtime` forwards the ceiling to the scheduler tools and to `spawn_subagent`, which closes the replay of a stored job; `send_message_to_peer` takes a `caller_ceiling` and the entry point it relays through, `process_message_shared_with_live_config_and_admission_and_principal`, an `allowed_tools`, so a relayed peer's turn is capped by the sender's ceiling (including the SOP step that peer starts).
  - **Ceiling derivation.** The sealed ceiling is a set of names, so two stand-ins that report the name of a real capability are excluded at the one place it is sealed: `BoundedSopApproveDenied` (`sop_approve`) and `sub_delegate_tool` (`delegate`). It is sealed after the headless SOP step-scope exclusions.
  - **Deferred shell.** A shell job stores a command, not a tool list, and the scheduler runs it under the owning agent's policy. `require_shell_within_ceiling` refuses `cron_add`'s shell branch, `cron_update`, `schedule` and `cron_run` unless the caller held `shell`; `cron_run` now branches on `job_type`.
  - **Persistence windows.** `cron_update`/`schedule` resume check the ceiling as a `JobGuard` inside the same `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction that commits the write (`cron/store.rs::update_job_inner`), so a concurrent write from another turn of the owning agent cannot land in between. `sop_execute`/`sop_advance` cancel a run they would leave parked (`WaitApproval`, `CheckpointWait`, `Pending`), and so does the live SOP driver at a park it reaches after running a queued step (`QueuedSopAction::bounded_caller`); a cancellation that cannot be persisted is reported, never claimed. The bounded rebind of `sop_execute` records no initiating agent.
  - **Command policy across hops and deferred work (`fe804dd56`).** The maintainer's review of `5758af5b2` asked for this in the PR. The mechanism: *any command a bounded target runs, or leaves behind to run later, under a policy rebuilt one hop below the caller, was judged only by the target's command policy.* The callers' command fields (`autonomy`, `allowed_commands`, `block_high_risk_commands`, `require_approval_for_medium_risk`) now travel inside `SecurityPolicy` as `caller_command_bounds`, root first (`policy.rs:514`, anchor `pub caller_command_bounds: Vec<CallerCommandBound>`), and `validate_command_execution_for_shell` requires a command to clear the policy's own rules and each caller's (`policy.rs:3491`, anchor `for bound in &self.caller_command_bounds`). The chain is attached where the bounded branch of `policy_for_target` already binds budget and cost (`delegate.rs:923`, anchor `target_policy.caller_command_bounds = self.security.caller_command_bounds.clone();`) and inherits the parent's, so hop N is bound by the whole path from the root. Cloning a policy carries it; `ensure_no_escalation_beyond` rejects a child policy that drops one (`policy.rs:4852`, anchor `Err(EscalationViolation::CallerCommandBoundDroppedByChild)`). This replaces the `CallerCommandPolicyShell` wrapper, which gated only the target's direct `shell`.
    - Covered: `cron_add`, `schedule` (`expression`, `delay`, `run_at`), `cron_update` and `cron_run` when a command is written or launched; the STORED command when a job is reused without a command patch (`cron_update` of another field, `schedule` resume), re-judged inside the guarded write (`caller_ceiling.rs:297`, `require_job_within_ceiling`); a `spawn_subagent` child; a second delegation hop, whose "caller" used to be the first target's raw policy.
    - Deferred agent jobs: a bounded registration refuses a stored `allowed_tools` list that keeps `shell`, named or inherited from a ceiling that holds it, at write and at launch or re-arm (`caller_ceiling.rs`, `refuse_deferred_shell` at `:197`). A deferred agent has no command to judge when it is written, so the capability is not deferred.
  - **Review follow-ups after the merge with `master@9cd75ac34`.**
    - *Fail closed on reuse.* `sop_execute`, `sop_advance` and `sop_workshop` leave `SAFE_FOR_BOUNDED_REUSE` for a new `REBOUND_BY_DOWNCAST_TOOL_NAMES` (`tools/mod.rs:620`). A bounded target receives them only as an instance rebound to the sealed ceiling; an instance the downcast cannot resolve (wrapped, or `as_any` not forwarded) is omitted, whether or not a root config is attached, because the name check in `delegate.rs` sits before `reuse_is_earned`.
    - *`sop_workshop`.* Under a caller ceiling it keeps only `list` and `inspect`. `apply` writes a SOP definition and reloads the shared engine, and `propose`, `capture_run`, `reject` and `quarantine` save proposals that a later run consumes, so all five are refused. The ceiling reaches it through the bounded rebuild and through `all_tools_with_runtime`.
    - *`sop_execute`/`sop_advance` in every registry built with a ceiling.* Before, only the bounded delegate rebuild gave them the ceiling, so the park-cancellation described above did not apply to a restricted `agent::run` (and with it a `spawn_subagent` child or a cron-fired job) or a peer relay. A SOP step turn never held them (`SOP_CONTROL_TOOLS` excludes them by name). Under a ceiling `sop_execute` also records no initiating agent, as the bounded rebuild already did, so a run whose cancellation cannot be persisted cannot be resumed as the caller. `all_tools_with_runtime` now passes `caller_ceiling` to both, in the branch with an audit logger and the one without.
    - *`CallerCommandBound`.* `from_caller` destructures, and `overlay` builds, `SecurityPolicy` field by field with no `..policy.clone()`, so a field added later stops them compiling until it is decided which side owns it.
    - *Inventory.* The four `a2a_*` tools capture the caller's `SecurityPolicy`, so they are classified as denied for bounded targets, and the maximal-registry fixture now builds them. A new test walks the compiled inventory (`BUILTIN_TOOLS`), so a tool that fixture forgets cannot stay unclassified.
    - Comments that described the pre-inversion fallthrough were corrected, and `delegation.md` states where the `sop_workshop` and park-cancellation behavior applies and that an `independent` hop below a bounded target carries neither the ceiling nor the command chain.
  - **Review follow-ups after `b2795136a`** (from the automated review of the PR and a cold re-read of the delta).
    - *Nested bounded hop and MCP.* A hop hands its nested delegate only the MCP tools its own bundles grant (`bounded_base_tools` filters with `mcp_tool_is_granted`, `delegate.rs`), so a nested target cannot recover an MCP server its caller was not granted (`e8ebeb34a`).
    - *Audit of a refused SOP run.* When `sop_execute`/`sop_advance` cancel a run they would leave parked, the audit trail (`log_run_start`, `log_step_result`, `log_run_complete`) is written before the refusal is returned; the early return used to skip it (`e8ebeb34a`).
    - *The ceiling describes the turn, not the caller.* A turn given a per-run `allowed_tools` (`agent::run`, and `process_message_inner` for a relayed peer) used to seal that list as it came in. The turn's own policy then removes tools from it, so a job, child or relay created in the turn carried names the turn never received: a peer whose policy has no `shell` could store a shell job because `require_shell_within_ceiling` found `shell` in the raw list. The handle is now created before the tools are built (`pending_for_turn`) and sealed once the registry is assembled, to the intersection of the incoming names and that registry (`seal_to_registry`, `tools/caller_ceiling.rs`; calls in `agent/loop_.rs`; `bddec0914`), the way the bounded delegate assembly already sealed its set.
    - *Deferred MCP tools.* Sealing from the registry alone dropped the MCP tools that only become callable after `tool_search` activates them under `mcp.deferred_loading`, so a job, child or relay lost valid tools. That regression came from the previous bullet and was found by the automated review. `ScopedAssembled::deferred_mcp_tool_names` reports the policy-admitted stubs, only when `tool_search` survives assembly, and `seal_to_registry` adds them, still intersected with the caller's names (`1c679eed9`). When `tool_search` does not survive, the list keeps only the tools a `mode = "always"` filter group activated during assembly, because those stay callable without the helper (`docs/book/src/security/authentication.md`) and the ceiling must keep naming a tool the turn can still call (`2416cd124`). The bounded delegate assembly has no such gap: its target never receives `tool_search`, and a deferred tool the caller already activated is an ordinary MCP wrapper in the target's registry, which the ceiling is sealed from. A test pins that.
    - *Bounded rebuild reads the admitted config.* The rebuild of workspace-, identity-, channel- and autonomy-bound tools (and the target's skills and workspace for the prompt) read `self.root_config`, the snapshot the `DelegateTool` was built with, while the rest of that function prefers the config the delegation was admitted against. It now uses the admitted config and falls back to the snapshot (`rebuild_config`, `delegate.rs`; `bddec0914`).
    - *Fluent.* The refusals this PR adds were bare English literals in seven tool sources. They now come from 15 `bounded-ceiling-*` keys in `locales/en/cli.ftl` with the exact wording they had, and a test pins each key's text. The other locales fall back to English until their catalogs are filled, and existing literals in `tools/*.rs` are untouched (`1a328ea53`).
  - **Merge with `master@be354a7ac` (`abf3896e4`) and review follow-ups after it** ([the maintainer's review of `1a328ea53`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10391#pullrequestreview-5540576446), and a context-free read-only review of the delta).
    - *How `tools/scoped.rs` was resolved.* `master`'s #11473 defers built-in tool schemas behind `tool_search`, in the region where this branch clears `deferred_mcp_tool_names` once `tool_search` is gone. Both rules are kept: the branch's runs first (anchor `deferred_mcp_tool_names.retain(`), then `master`'s block (anchor `let builtin_deferral = `), which runs only when the turn's policy and the caller's set admit `tool_search` (anchor `if builtin_deferral && search_admitted {`) and adds a `tool_search` of its own only when no MCP-backed one exists, built from built-in schemas alone (`ToolSearchTool::for_builtin_schemas`), so it activates no executable and cannot bring back a name the first rule dropped. Pinned by `builtin_deferral_does_not_revive_deferred_mcp_tools_without_tool_search`, which also asserts that the deferral ran where `tool_search` is held and did not where it is not. `delegate.rs` kept both test fixtures (`master`'s `PanickingTool` and this branch's `APPROVAL_PROBE_TOOL_NAME`) and `delegation.md` both sections; the two seals in `agent/loop_.rs` (`seal_to_registry` in `run` and in `process_message_inner`) are intact.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw lets one agent hand a task to another. In the "bounded" mode the second agent is supposed to stay inside three limits set by the first: it works in its own workspace, it may only use tools the first agent had, and it may only run commands the first agent could run. Those limits held while the second agent's turn was running. They were lost by anything that kept going afterwards: a scheduled job it created, a procedure (SOP) run that was waiting for approval, a message relayed to a peer, a sub-agent it started, or a further hop of delegation. In those cases the work ran later with the full authority of whichever agent owned it.

This PR carries the limits along with that work. A job or run created under a limit is capped by it, a procedure run that would wait for an approval nobody in the turn can follow is cancelled instead, and a command has to satisfy the rules of every agent above it. It adds no capability; it only removes authority that leaked.

What stays the same: agents that are not under a limit behave as before, and jobs already stored are not retroactively capped. The limits listed under "Known boundary", "Second declared gap" and "Third and fourth declared gaps" are not closed here. The first has a follow-up issue (#11667); the second, third and fourth are tracked in #12394. What operators will notice: a job or run restricted by `allowed_tools` can no longer leave a SOP waiting for approval, and can no longer write SOP definitions through `sop_workshop`.

```
cargo test -j 1 -p zeroclaw-runtime --locked --test 'bounded_delegate_*' \
    --test restricted_run_sop_execute_ceiling                      # 12 binaries, 49 tests passed
cargo test -j 1 -p zeroclaw-tools --locked --test inventory_source_scan \

cargo test -j 1 -p zeroclaw-config --lib --locked                  # 1802 passed

bash scripts/ci/container_build_inputs_gate.test.sh && bash scripts/ci/container_build_inputs_gate.sh   # pass

# on aa2b45b56:

```

  On `9365b1638d` (WSL, the exact commit): the six tests of the forwarded-environment fix pass; each hop test reads the environment a real shell child receives, and six mutations of the propagation sites each turned a test red. `tools::delegate::` and `tools::tests::` passed in full (453 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored) on the working tree just before the commit, not repeated on it. `clippy` was not re-run locally on these tests; CI `Lint` passes on the head. The owner-plane and child-launch commits are covered by the CI `Test` jobs; this block holds no local command output for them.
  The comment hygiene gate (`scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh`, 58 passed, and `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`) passes on `a126de966`. Not run: `cargo doc` for the whole workspace (it stops downloading `zip 9.0.3`: this WSL cannot resolve `static.crates.io` and the crate is not cached, an environment limit), `scripts/ci/run_clippy.test.sh`, clippy for crates other than the three above, code under `cfg(windows)` and `cfg(target_os = "macos")`, and any docs gate other than `cargo doc`.

  Earlier, on the merge with `master`: the first full `zeroclaw-runtime --lib` run found two deterministic failures that git had merged without a conflict (`execute_background_signs_sub_loop_tool_results_with_the_parent_generator` and `background_delegate_reports_live_progress_while_a_tool_runs`), fixed on the test side in `b2795136a`. A macOS-only test that called `all_tools_with_runtime` with the old argument count was found by an independent review; an arity scan of every call site found no other, and it predates `master@4e82ce46e` (see *CI*). Code under `cfg(windows)` and `cfg(target_os = "macos")` is not compiled locally.
- **Mutations** (each applied alone, the tree restored afterwards, and the expected test or tests seen red; the prediction was written first). `fe804dd56`: the chain loop in `validate_command_execution_for_shell`; attaching the immediate caller's bound in `policy_for_target`; inheriting the parent's chain; the stored-command re-judge and the ceiling signal that gates it; `refuse_deferred_shell`; the check that a child cannot drop a bound; the `approved` plumbing of `schedule` resume. Earlier rounds did the same for their own sites. Review follow-ups: the name-based drop in `delegate.rs`; `sop_execute`/`sop_advance` back in `SAFE_FOR_BOUNDED_REUSE`; the `sop_workshop` refusal and its downcast; a new `SecurityPolicy` field (compile errors in `from_caller` and `overlay`); `overlay` taking a field from the wrong side; the allow-list admitting `apply`; each `with_caller_ceiling(caller_ceiling.clone())` call for `sop_execute`/`sop_advance`; the command chain attached to an `independent` target; `cron_run`'s `new_with_runtime` forwarding `None`; `sop_execute` recording its initiator under a ceiling; `overlay` substituting a default for `sandbox_image`; the MCP grant filter of a nested hop; the audit of a cancelled run in both SOP tools; sealing the raw list, dropping the seal in `process_message_inner`, the rebuild reading only `self.root_config`; sealing without the deferred names, reporting them when `tool_search` is gone, never recording the admitted stubs; an MCP instance never handed to a bounded target and reusing every tool; a key removed from the catalog, a changed word in a pinned message, `spawn_subagent` back to a bare literal and a misnamed argument at a call site. **After the merge with `master@be354a7ac`:** the maintainer's two, run on the tree of `9d7d3ce6b` (the `#[cfg(test)]` `assemble_owned_execution` wrapper passing `None` instead of `caller_allowed`: red `assembling_a_step_agent_applies_the_callers_ceiling`, `turn/mod.rs:7003`; `reassembly.caller_allowed` passed as `None` at the production call: red `a_cross_agent_sop_step_under_a_bounded_chain_runs_within_the_caller_ceiling`, `bounded_delegate_sop_step_ceiling.rs:387`); removing the deferred-name clearing; dropping `&& search_admitted`; neutralizing the whole built-in block; clearing the list instead of keeping the pre-activated names, never recording them, never clearing it; passing `None` for the delegate parent set in the pre-activation call; removing `deferred_section.clear()` from the caller-set block; making either clearing depend on a caller set being present. **On `aa2b45b56`:** replacing the caller-name filter of the background path (`delegate.rs:3467`, anchor `.filter(|tool| self.security.is_tool_allowed(tool.name()))`) with `|_tool| true` turns its new test red (a receipt is signed for `calculator`); tree restored. **Mutations that survive:** passing `None` as the policy to `preactivate_always_filter_groups` keeps the new tests green, because the stubs are already filtered by the same policy before pre-activation (`scoped.rs:557`, anchor `deferred_set.filter_by_policy(mcp_policy.as_ref())`), so that check is redundant at this call site (with both layers removed the new test is red); and `&[]` instead of `&deferred_mcp_tool_names` at either `seal_to_registry` call in `loop_.rs` (the fourth declared gap) stays green in the full `zeroclaw-runtime --lib` run and in the twelve ceiling test binaries, at each site, on `9d7d3ce6b` (not repeated after the merge with `master@4e82ce46e`; those lines did not move).
- **Load-sensitive local failures, pre-existing on `master`:** `rpc::local::tests::reload_replacement_generation_waits_for_durable_session_prompt_local` also fails on a clean `origin/master@0c28d7ce8` checkout. Under the default thread count a full local `zeroclaw-runtime --lib` run fails 1 to 4 `rpc::dispatch::tests` with timeouts; the ones I re-ran pass in isolation, the whole run passes with `--test-threads=1` (5923 on `a126de966`), and they pass in CI. I did not try them on a clean `master`; load on my machine is the likely cause, not something I demonstrated.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** For the peer relay: traced the escape end to end (the two construction sites, `process_message`'s registry assembly, `ScopedAssembly::caller_allowed`) and confirmed it does not reopen the name-based findings, since `sop_approve` and `delegate` are excluded at the ceiling's own derivation. For the cron race: read `update_job_inner`'s call graph: it is the only writer reachable from the scheduler tools that changes a job's `command` or `allowed_tools` after creation. The declarative sync (`sync_declarative_jobs` in `cron/store.rs`, anchor `allowed_tools = ?12, source = 'declarative'`) also rewrites both columns from the operator's configuration without a guard; I did not trace whether a tool can edit that configuration. For the SOP park: read `SopEngine::gate_state` to confirm a cancelled run can never resolve as `Resumed`. For `fe804dd56`: an independent, context-free adversarial pass over the diff, the delegation contract and the review protocol found the boundary above and a `schedule` resume without `approved`, both addressed or declared in this head. For `235b709f6`: a second independent pass over the whole diff found, among other things, two wrong comments (corrected), an unrelated change to the gateway's error handling (reverted to `master`'s), and the principal-session gap above (declared). For the delta after `b2795136a`: I enumerated the places that create a sealed ceiling (`loop_.rs` twice, `delegate.rs` once) and the writers of the delegate parent-tool set (the factory's initial set, eager MCP registration, `always` pre-activation, the activation hook, and the `caller_allowed` retain); both inventories come from searches calibrated against a known site, and none of those writers adds `tool_search`. For the delta after `1a328ea53`: a second context-free review of the whole diff against `master`, by reading only (it ran no code). Its test findings are closed or declared in this head: the pre-activation policy and delegate wiring, and the clearing of the deferred listing for a caller set without `tool_search`, now have tests; the two `&[]` call sites and the SOP step's raw ceiling are declared above. I counted the destructures of `ScopedAssembled` (six, all with `..`) with a search calibrated against `loop_.rs:1718` over `crates/`, `src/`, `apps/` and `xtask/`.
  **What I did NOT verify to completion:** the peer relay and the SOP step under the command chain, end to end (the Known boundary above); `sop_list` and, in an unowned hop, `sop_status` (both `SAFE_FOR_BOUNDED_REUSE`) were assumed read-only from their names and descriptions (in an owned hop `sop_status` is rebound, see above); the park-cancellation in the peer relay is covered by the shared registry-factory test and by reading the call sites that pass the sealed handle (`loop_.rs` twice), not by running that route; a SOP step turn excludes `sop_execute` and `sop_advance` by name (`SOP_CONTROL_TOOLS`, `sop/active_scope.rs:11`), so it never holds them; there is no concurrency test for `SopEngine::cancel_run` itself (the argument is a reading of the code under one `MutexGuard`); whether `advance_headless_deterministic_step` can itself invoke a command, and whether `sop_execute`/`sop_advance` can resolve a checkpoint into `spawn_headless_run_driver` by a path other than the parking one, remain untraced. Also untraced: the principal-session gap above end to end; and whether a relayed peer's turn escapes the caller's action tracker and cost context. An `independent` hop below a bounded target carries neither the ceiling nor the command chain by design: the command-chain half is pinned by `policy_for_target_attaches_the_command_chain_only_for_a_bounded_target`, the ceiling half is read from the registry construction, which passes `None`. The delta after `1a328ea53` had one context-free review that read the code but ran none. That a pre-activated tool stays callable without `tool_search` is read from the dispatcher, which looks the name up in the activated set when no static tool matches (`agent/tool_execution.rs:226`, anchor `activated_tools.get_resolved`), and from `docs/book/src/security/authentication.md:376-379` ("remain callable without the helper"); the new tests assert that the tool is activated and named in the ceiling, not that a model call reaches it. The deferred-MCP loss was reproduced with a stub-level assembly test (`ScopedToolRegistry::assemble` against a mock MCP server), not by running a full delegation or peer relay with `mcp.deferred_loading`. The claim that the bounded delegate has no such gap is read from the code and pinned by one test, not run end to end. I did not trace the live SOP step reassembly path separately for the automated reviewer's remark that later SOP hops could recover names removed from an intermediate turn. `cargo fluent check` was not run (CI does not run it). I did not run a context-free review of `9365b1638d`. The live-environment symptom (a command not found in a real TUI session) was not reproduced; the forwarded-environment tests read the environment a shell child receives. The other tools a bounded target rebuilds were not audited for session settings they might lack.
- **Declared limits of the regressions:** the deferred-shell integration tests stop at the store; they do not run the scheduler or execute a command. The cross-agent SOP step started by a relayed peer has no dedicated composed regression: one was written, hit an intermittent unrelated test-infrastructure race (`"Unknown tool: delegate"`), and was deleted rather than merged flaky; the fix is covered indirectly by `bounded_delegate_sop_step_ceiling`, which exercises the same `SopStepReassembly` mechanism through `spawn_subagent`. The cron-race tests use a raw second `rusqlite::Connection` and a test-only hook (`install_after_read_hook_for_tests`) to make the race deterministic.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**: this only removes capability from bounded targets and their relayed peers.
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes**
- **Risk and mitigation:** the refusal strings are model-visible. Most are static authored text; `send_message_to_peer: refused — a delegated caller ceiling was declared but never published, so the recipient's turn cannot be bounded` fires only on an internal wiring failure, the same fail-closed contract as `spawn_subagent`'s. The two SOP refusals interpolate values the caller supplied in the same tool call (`sop_execute`'s `name`, `sop_advance`'s `run_id`), each validated against a real SOP definition or run before being echoed, the same class as the existing `require_within_ceiling` echo of stored tool names. Their failure branch also echoes the backend `StoreError`, and the live SOP driver's error echoes an engine-generated run id and the same `StoreError`: backend-internal values, so no new injection surface, with the leak risk (a storage path or driver message in a tool result) of the class already accepted for `require_within_ceiling`. `fe804dd56` adds two strings in `caller_ceiling.rs`: the `refuse_deferred_shell` refusal (static text plus the tool's own name and the literal `shell`) and the stored-command refusal `{tool}: refused — {reason}`, where `reason` is the command policy's message and can echo the stored command text (`Command not allowed by security policy: <command>`). That command was supplied when the job was written and is echoed into a tool result, again the same class. `sop_workshop`'s refusal is static text plus the action's wire name, which comes from a fixed enum (`sop_workshop.rs:208`, anchor `bounded-ceiling-sop-workshop-action`; text in `locales/en/cli.ftl`). The 15 refusals this PR adds render from `bounded-ceiling-*` Fluent keys with their previous English wording, pinned by a test, so that change introduces no new model-visible text.
- **Declared gaps:** see the Known boundary, the Second declared gap and the Third and fourth declared gaps under *Declared gaps*: the command chain does not reach a peer relay or a cross-agent SOP step, a principal-narrowed `Agent` session's scheduler tools carry no sealed ceiling, a SOP step's ceiling is the caller's raw list, and the seal's inputs at its two call sites are not pinned by a test. They are limits of what this PR closes; the code before this branch had neither bound.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No**, deliberately.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- **Exact upgrade steps for existing users:** no migration is required for existing stored jobs or running deployments; nothing persisted changes shape (see Rollback). It **does** change public Rust signatures:
  1. `zeroclaw_runtime::tools::all_tools_with_runtime`, `all_tools_with_runtime_and_acp_sessions` and `all_tools_with_runtime_and_execution_capability` (`tools/mod.rs`) each gain a final `caller_ceiling: Option<CallerCeiling>` (`CallerCeiling` is a `pub(crate)` alias of `Arc<OnceLock<Vec<String>>>`): source-breaking for a positional caller; `None` keeps the previous behavior. The cross-crate callers in this tree (`zeroclaw-gateway/src/lib.rs`, twice, and `zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs`) pass `None`. The `process_message*` entry points keep `master`'s public signatures.
  2. `zeroclaw_runtime::cron::update_job_for_agent` and `resume_job_for_agent` each gain a final `guard: JobGuard<'_>` (`cron::unguarded` for a caller with no bound to enforce). Only `zeroclaw-runtime` calls them today, but both are `pub`.
  3. `zeroclaw_config::policy::SecurityPolicy` gains a `pub` field `caller_command_bounds` (source-breaking for an out-of-tree struct literal that does not use `..Default`), a new `pub` type `CallerCommandBound` is added, and `EscalationViolation` gains a variant, `CallerCommandBoundDroppedByChild` (source-breaking for an exhaustive match). `CallerCommandPolicyShell` is removed.
  4. `zeroclaw_runtime::tools::REBOUND_BY_DOWNCAST_TOOL_NAMES` is a new `pub const` (`tools/mod.rs:620`), and `BOUNDED_DENIED_TOOL_NAMES` gains the four `a2a_*` names. `SopExecuteTool::with_caller_ceiling` and `SopAdvanceTool::with_caller_ceiling` are new `pub` builder methods (`SopWorkshopTool` gains `pub(crate)` ones). The classification lists (`FILESYSTEM_TOOL_NAMES` and the other `*_TOOL_NAMES` constants), `DelegateChannelHandles`, `image_info_tool` and `BoundedSopApproveDenied` are new `pub` items of `zeroclaw_runtime::tools`; all of these are additive.
  5. `zeroclaw_runtime::tools::scoped::ScopedAssembled` gains a `pub` field `deferred_mcp_tool_names: Vec<String>`: source-breaking for an out-of-tree struct literal or an exhaustive destructure (the six destructures in this tree use `..`: `loop_.rs:1718` and `:3704`, `agent.rs:3017`, `turn/mod.rs:3801`, `delegate.rs:1556` and `zeroclaw-channels/src/orchestrator/mod.rs:16157`).
  6. `zeroclaw_api::tool::Tool` gains a defaulted method `as_any(&self) -> Option<&dyn Any>` (it returns `None`, so no implementor has to change; the MCP tool wrapper in `zeroclaw-tools` forwards it, and the bounded rebuild uses it to downcast the tools it must rebind), and `zeroclaw_tools::mcp_client::McpRegistry` gains `pub fn server_name_for`.
  The other registry-constructor changes (`send_message_to_peer_tool` and the other registry builders) are `pub(crate)`, so they carry no external burden.

  Behavior changes for bounded delegation:
  - shell-job creation, resume and force-run need `shell` in the ceiling; patches are capped; scheduled jobs store the intersection; `sop_approve` and `delegate` cannot be smuggled into a stored job by omitting `allowed_tools`; a bounded target's action budget is intersected with the caller's; a relayed peer's turn, and a cross-agent SOP step that peer starts, are bound by the intersection;
  - a concurrent write from another turn of the owning agent can no longer land between a bounded `cron_update`/`schedule` resume's check and its write;
  - a bounded caller's `sop_execute`/`sop_advance`, and the live SOP driver after a queued step, cancel a run that would park (approval, checkpoint, unmet dependency) instead of leaving it resumable with full authority; a bounded rebind of `sop_execute` records no initiating agent;
  - a bounded delegation made inside a headless SOP step seals a ceiling that excludes what the step's scope denies;
  - `backup`/`data_management` follow `master`'s shared data directory under the target's policy;
  - every command a bounded target runs, or stores to run later, must also clear the command policy of each caller above it, at every bounded hop and for a `spawn_subagent` child; a command the caller's policy refuses is refused even if the target's profile allows it;
  - a bounded registration cannot store, launch or re-arm an agent job whose `allowed_tools` keeps `shell`, and `schedule` resume reads the request's `approved` like the create routes. A job already stored with `shell` stays stored, but a bounded turn cannot launch or re-arm it;
  - a command denied by both the target's and a caller's policy reports the target's message;
  - any `agent::run` given a per-run `allowed_tools` (a stored cron agent job with its own list, for example) now builds its scheduler tools with a ceiling sealed to the tools that run actually holds (the list intersected with its assembled registry), so a job it stores or launches is capped by it and an agent job that keeps `shell` is refused (`agent/loop_.rs:1735`, anchor `crate::tools::caller_ceiling::seal_to_registry(`, and `cron/scheduler.rs:1180`, anchor `job.allowed_tools.clone()`). Read from the code.
  - `sop_workshop` keeps only `list` and `inspect` under a caller ceiling, and `sop_execute`/`sop_advance` cancel a run that would park in every registry built with one: a bounded target, a restricted `agent::run` (so a `spawn_subagent` child and a cron-fired job) and a peer relay; a SOP step turn never holds these two tools, because the step scope excludes them by name. Under a ceiling `sop_execute` also records no initiating agent. This includes a job whose `allowed_tools` an operator wrote: such a job can no longer leave a SOP waiting for approval or write SOP definitions, so a job that has to do either must not be restricted by `allowed_tools`. An RPC principal session restricted by tool names builds its registry with no ceiling and is not covered (see the Second declared gap).

  - a turn given a per-run `allowed_tools` seals its ceiling to the tools it actually holds (plus the deferred MCP tools it may activate, and, when its set does not name `tool_search`, the ones a `mode = "always"` group already activated), not to the names it was handed: a name its own policy removed no longer counts as held, for example `shell` for a peer whose profile has none;
  - a bounded delegate's rebuilt tools read the config the delegation was admitted against, so a feature switched on or off in that config is seen by the target;
  - a nested bounded hop is handed only the MCP tools its own bundles grant;
  - the 15 refusals added by this PR render from Fluent keys; in a locale without a translation they stay English.

  Jobs already stored under the old, wider ceiling are **not** retro-capped, and a SOP run already left parked before this is deployed is not retroactively cancelled.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the commits on this branch, or revert the PR merge commit. No migration or state cleanup: nothing persisted changed shape.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. The bound is active whenever a ceiling is in force.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a legitimate scheduled job stops being created, re-armed or launched; a legitimate `sop_approve`/`delegate` capability stops surviving into a stored job; a legitimate peer relay stops receiving a tool the peer's own profile grants; a legitimate concurrent job update starts losing to a rival write; a SOP run started by a bounded caller is cancelled instead of resumable; a bounded target's command is refused that its own profile allows. Grep tool results for:
  - `refused — this stores or re-arms a shell job` (`cron_add`, `cron_update`, `schedule`, `cron_run`)
  - `refused — this job's stored allowed_tools reach beyond` and `refused — this job stores no allowed_tools`
  - `refused — this agent job would keep 'shell'`: a bounded registration tried to defer an agent with `shell`; the job has to list its tools without it
  - `<tool>: refused — ... Command not allowed by security policy` from `cron_update` or `schedule` resume: a caller's policy refuses the job's stored command; check the caller's `allowed_commands` before treating it as a regression
  - `refused — this tool was registered under bounded delegation but the caller's tool ceiling was never sealed`, and `send_message_to_peer: refused — a delegated caller ceiling was declared but never published`: fail-closed paths that indicate a sealing bug, not a policy decision
  - `refused — SOP` / `refused — run ... left outside this turn ... has been cancelled` (`sop_execute`, `sop_advance`): the parked-run cancellation path
  - ``sop_workshop `<action>` is not available under a caller tool ceiling``: the `sop_workshop` write refusal (`propose`, `capture_run`, `apply`, `reject`, `quarantine`); `list` and `inspect` are unaffected
  - `could NOT be cancelled ... may still be active - treat it as unresolved, not closed`: the cancellation failed to persist, the run is still parked and resumable; investigate the persistence backend
  - log line `bounded live SOP driver: cancelled a run that would have parked outside the turn`; its unpersisted counterpart `bounded live SOP driver: parked run could not be cancelled` comes with a turn error containing `reached a park that a bounded caller's tool ceiling cannot follow past this turn`
  - a cron job update or resume that fails with no obvious cause: check for a concurrent write from another turn of the same agent; it now surfaces as lock contention or a guard refusal instead of silently winning or losing
  - From `1a328ea53` the refusal strings above come from the `bounded-ceiling-*` keys in `locales/en/cli.ftl`; in a locale without a translation they stay the English text quoted here.

prs.title: test(providers): hold the runtime proxy guard in the tool-round wire fixture
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults` fails intermittently in full `zeroclaw-providers` runs. The cause is shared state, not timing. `responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_config` and `codex_responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_after_construction` point the process-wide runtime proxy at a throwaway server for `model_provider.openai`. They serialise on `RuntimeProxyTestGuard`; the tool-round fixture (`wire_body`) did not take that guard. When it overlapped one of them, its OpenAI clients were built through the proxy, and its request went to the proxy fixture instead of its own server.
  - That gives three failure modes, all of which I've seen locally:
    - a decode error, when the proxy answers with its own JSON
    - "Connection refused", once the proxy test has stopped its server
    - the fixture's 5 s timeout, when a stream never sees its final event
  - `wire_body` now holds the guard for its lifetime.
- **Scope boundary:** test-only. No production code changes. I didn't audit other fixtures for the same pattern.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-providers` tests only. The tool-round test now waits for a running proxy test instead of overlapping it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11467 (added the test)

### What this does, simply

Two tests temporarily switch on a global HTTP proxy for the OpenAI provider, and they take a shared lock so nothing else is affected while they do. One newer test didn't take that lock. prs.title: ci(dependabot): give Rust patch updates their own group
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The cargo entry's single `rust-all` group put every minor and patch update into one Dependabot PR of 35 to 37 updates. Those PRs keep being closed or superseded without merging (#12556 now; #12487, #12420, #12393 and others before it).
  - A patch release that fixes an advisory therefore waits inside a batch nobody can land. The Wasmtime 48.0.9 bump for RUSTSEC-2026-0566 to -0573 had to be done by hand in #12577 instead.
  - This splits the group into `rust-patch` and `rust-minor`, so patch updates arrive as their own smaller PR.
- **Scope boundary:** Only the cargo entry's groups. The schedule, labels, `open-pull-requests-limit`, target branch, the npm, Actions and Docker entries, and Dependabot security updates are unchanged. No workflow changes.
- **Blast radius:** Dependabot PR shape for Rust crates only: up to two grouped PRs instead of one.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12577

### What this does, simply

Dependabot opens one PR a day that bumps every Rust dependency with a new minor or patch release. It's so big that it never gets merged, so small, safe patch releases that fix security problems sit in it unmerged. With this change, patch releases come in their own PR, separate from the riskier minor updates, so they can be reviewed and merged quickly.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: Dependabot reads the file only on GitHub. The first scheduled run after merge shows the two groups.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** none run Dependabot config. Its schema is validated by GitHub when the file is pushed (Insights → Dependency graph → Dependabot shows parse errors).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no local Dependabot validator. Checked by YAML parse and structure below.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ python3 -c "import yaml; d=yaml.safe_load(open('.github/dependabot.yml')); print({k: v['update-types'] for k, v in d['updates'][0]['groups'].items()})"
{'rust-patch': ['patch'], 'rust-minor': ['minor']}
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Each dependency matches exactly one group, because the two groups use disjoint `update-types` with the same `*` pattern, which is how Dependabot assigns updates. Security updates aren't grouped by these entries, since groups default to version updates. Not verified: an actual Dependabot run.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** N/A
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No cargo checks: no Rust or lockfile change.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert <sha>` restores the single `rust-all` group on Dependabot's next run.

prs.body: ## Summary - **Base branch:** master - **What changed and why:** - Accept a JSON array in ZEROCLAW_PLUGIN_REGISTRY_URL so private and public registries can be used together. - Preserve fetched-origin identity through search, caching and selection in install, update and Quickstart so same-name packages cannot silently switch publishers. This does not add durable origin metadata to installed packages. - Carry origin information into suggestions and the web catalog without exposing credential-bearing URLs in catalog responses or display labels. - **Scope boundary:** No changes to plugin execution permissions or package layout. Fork-only validation tooling is not included. - **Blast radius:** Registry/cache consumers, CLI/Quickstart, runtime suggestions, gateway API types and the web Plugins page. - **Linked issue(s):** Related #12109 ### What this does, simply Use multiple plugin registries without losing track of which publisher a package belongs to. Existing single-URL configuration still works. Custom lists replace the default registry rather than automatically adding it. Only one package per name can be installed. ## Testing (required) ### How you can test (when useful) - **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. - **Interface(s) exercised:** cli and web; Quickstart interaction remains unverified. - **Setup / preconditions:** Two reachable registry indexes containing a package named demo. Replace the example URLs below. Use the same fixtures on master and this branch. - **Steps to run:** ~~~sh ZEROCLAW_PLUGIN_REGISTRY_URL='["https://registry-a.example/registry.json","https://registry-b.example/registry.json"]' zeroclaw plugin search demo ~~~ - **Expected on this branch (after):** Results from both registries with distinct publisher labels. - **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The single-registry implementation does not support the JSON list or combined results. Manual A/B confirmation is still pending. ### How I tested - **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Previously recorded focused fork-hosted Linux checks cover registry behavior, compatibility and affected consumers. These are the existing results recorded for revision `645a9ae5fdba6ae9e6026d7d057dfbdfc49ac0d4`, not a fresh CI result for the current head: | Check | Result | |---|---| | [Shared registry](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41557780235) | 10 passed | | [CLI](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41564605521) | 16 passed | | [Runtime suggestions](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41673545578) | 1 passed | | [Gateway catalog/compatibility](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41676472684) | 6 unique tests passed; 7 executions (nonadditive) | | [Frontend helpers](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41682990141) | 4 passed | | [Schema/typecheck](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41683862525) | Export, contract guards and typecheck passed | - **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Current-head required CI is not established by the links above. Standard lint/docs gates, full workspace/default-feature test suites, Windows, MSRV and the full release/feature matrix remain outside the evidence here. The sandbox checks below add actual Linux release CLI/gateway and web coverage, but not Quickstart interaction. - **Commands run and tail output:** The linked historical logs contain the focused CI commands. Frontend output: ~~~sh node --experimental-strip-types --test-reporter=tap --test web/src/pages/pluginCatalog.test.ts ~~~ ~~~text # tests 4 # pass 4 # fail 0 # cancelled 0 # skipped 0 # todo 0 ~~~ The historical schema check ran `cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin web -- gen-api` and `npm run typecheck`, including the generated-file check and `tsc -b`. Three new DTOs passed presence checks in both generated contracts. For the current-head sandbox run, the actual CLI commands included `plugin install tool-fixture@0.0.0 --registry http://127.0.0.1:18281/b.json`, `plugin list --verify` and `plugin info tool-fixture`, using the release binary and an isolated `--config-dir`. Each exited 0; selected output lines: ~~~text Installed plugin tool-fixture v0.0.0 tool-fixture v0.0.0 — (no description) [loads] Loads: yes. The component instantiates against this host's WIT world. ~~~ - **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** On 2026-11-03, exercised the real CLI and paired dashboard/API in an isolated Linux sandbox (Rust 1.98, Node 24.22.2). The PR release CLI/gateway used default features plus `plugins-wasm-cranelift`; the dashboard used the separately built canonical web dist. No source changes were made during validation. - Legacy single-URL search and dashboard/API returned the two expected entries. Two registries returned four rows, including two same-name packages with distinct authoritative origin IDs; publisher-supplied spoof origin metadata was ignored. - Both unpinned and version-pinned duplicate installs rejected ambiguity and required `--registry`. Explicit selection of an origin rejected versions available only from the other origin; request logs showed only the selected index was fetched. - Malformed JSON and connection refusal failed without partial search results or cache publication. Cache bytes, inode and restrictive permissions survived failures; initial mode was `0600`, and a successful refresh preserved deliberately narrowed `0400`. Matching offline cache remained usable; a mismatched explicit source set excluded it. This is failure atomicity and separate offline reuse, not successful-search fallback. - Built the repository's harmless `tool-fixture@0.0.0` for `wasm32-wasip2` and installed it from registry B with normal archive/digest, manifest and host-load checks enabled. B-only index/package requests and matching installed component/manifest hashes proved the selected download. `list --verify` reported `[loads]`; `info` reported `Loads: yes`. Installed metadata does not retain an origin field; this is not a durable installed-origin or signature-authenticity claim. - **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot of the actual paired web Plugins page with all four registry rows and distinct origin IDs. Quickstart screenshots remain unprovided. - **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `342cf3c12683365ee3d1b7f68f9da6fdea86a88f`; actual cli, paired web Plugins page and authenticated catalog API. Current-head evidence is summarized above, with exact CLI output above; the captured dashboard screenshot will be attached separately. Earlier automated evidence is linked separately. - **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** CLI output above. The actual multi-registry dashboard screenshot has been captured; - **Action or changed state and observed result:** Switching the web catalog to Installed hid the uninstalled registry entries; All restored all four rows. The authenticated catalog stayed HTTP 200 with the same four rows after both failed refreshes; unauthenticated access returned 401. The later CLI installation succeeded and the host loaded the fixture; that installation was not a web install flow. - **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Tool invocation/execution was explicitly skipped; no supported safe direct non-provider invocation surface was established. Install/load is not execution. Interactive approval, provider/production integration, Quickstart interaction, an unpatched-master comparison, signature authenticity, timeout behavior and concurrent/crash cache stress were not tested. This was bounded sandbox validation, not a full test/lint or platform matrix. A Google Fonts request blocked by dashboard CSP was observed but did not affect catalog behavior; it was treated as nonblocking for this acceptance run and was not attributed to this PR without a baseline comparison. ## Security & Privacy Impact (required) - New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.** Existing cache location; more restrictive cache writes. - New external network calls? **Yes.** Up to eight configured HTTP(S) indexes, with bounded requests and no partial cache publication. - Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** Catalog responses/display labels use opaque origin IDs; cache writes are private. This is not blanket URL redaction for errors or executable commands. - PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** - Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Registry-backed suggestions retain the fetched origin rather than publisher-declared provenance. Registry metadata remains untrusted. - If any Yes, describe the risk and mitigation: Additional registries expand the publisher trust surface. Ambiguous installs and multi-origin updates require an explicit registry. Source validation and all-or-nothing cache publication prevent silently mixing incomplete results. ## Compatibility (required) - Backward compatible? **Yes**, for existing single-registry configuration and public Rust struct literals. - Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** The existing variable also accepts a JSON array. Ambiguous installs and multi-origin updates require `--registry `. - Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.** - If backward compatibility is No or either surface/floor question is Yes: exact upgrade steps for existing users: No change for single-registry users. To opt in, set ZEROCLAW_PLUGIN_REGISTRY_URL to a JSON array of one to eight HTTP(S) URLs. Include the public registry explicitly if wanted. ## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs) - **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert `. Restore a single registry URL and discard/regenerate the union cache at plugin-registry/registry.json before using the old reader. Installed packages are unchanged. - **Feature flags or config toggles:** No feature flag. A single URL or explicit `--registry ` selects one registry. - **Observable failure symptoms:** Missing catalog entries, unexpected origin-selection errors, cache-source mismatches or failed registry refreshes. ## Supersede Attribution (required only when Supersedes # is used) Not applicable; this PR does not supersede another PR.

prs.body:
<!-- replay-cache-fix-20261110 -->
## TLS replay cache follow-up

Revision `f5b5735eb` classifies new TLS-only message IDs at insertion and evicts only that class. Older and encrypted markers remain in the shared replay table, preserving cross-mode deduplication and reviewed inbox release. The private store recognizes the exact legacy and classified schemas.

The old query reproduces a missing encrypted replay marker after exceeding the TLS retention limit. The new regression drives the real private store and offline review/release command through TLS eviction; fresh TLS-to-OMEMO initialization and earlier socket deadline regressions also pass. Integrated XMPP, formatting and all-target Clippy passed locally. Fresh hosted CI remains authoritative.

<!-- control-write-fix-20261110 -->
## Control-write deadline follow-up

Revision `5e1f62ae7` includes `adbc57d18` and master `a4beef9a6`. Control stanzas now have a 60-second write deadline. A stalled or failed control write returns an error from the connection writer, which releases queued replies and lets the existing listener supervisor reconnect. The writer does not replay uncertain sends.

A regression driving the real writer with a stalled sink fails before the fix and passes after it. Healthy and broken control writes are also covered. Integrated XMPP, HTTP-cache and runtime tests, formatting and all-target Clippy passed locally. Fresh hosted CI on this revision remains authoritative.

<!-- review-fix-20261110:start -->
## Review follow-up (2026-11-10)

Published head: 1d062fc50eb74070a6267b4d838875edf763e892. Updated with master 6877da56d.

Atomic peer-device index cleanup for reviewed offline OMEMO session reset, with index-bound review tokens and an actual encrypted send to the surviving device.

Local integration regression tests, formatting and all-target Clippy passed. Hosted CI for this exact head is pending; earlier CI/approval does not validate the new revision. Detailed boundary evidence is in the reply to the corresponding review thread.
<!-- review-fix-20261110:end -->

## Summary



Base branch: `master`.



Implement feature-gated native Rust XMPP with optional Linux legacy OMEMO. Related #9814. Depends on #12015.



### What this does, simply



The native channel owns encrypted receipts independently of the socket. Reconnect reuses the exclusive store; completed runtime and control receipts can be recorded while offline. First-contact key publication explicitly requests readable public nodes.



<!-- jarvis-validation-update:start -->
## Validation update (2026-11-10)

Updated to master a11a5ce5b at f120f8722. Retained scoped-chat authorization and XMPP policy coverage. Canonical API generation, npm run test:auth (including xmppPolicy.test.ts), and the production build passed. Native XMPP/OMEMO validation remains covered by the published commit's CI. The dependency on #12015 remains.

CI results and maintainer decisions on the published revision remain authoritative.
<!-- jarvis-validation-update:end -->

## Testing (required)



### How you can test (when useful)



Run the `xmpp` and `native_ingress_` channel-library filters with `--no-default-features --features channel-xmpp`; then run `crates/zeroclaw-channels/tests/xmpp_native/managed_server.py` using the documented disposable loopback-only fixture.



### Earlier validation (historical)



Current-head CI Required Gate and all executed checks pass at 47f16954424bcc3787379e5e1d2c21df52daf100, including every source-image build. The inherited master root-fixture packaging fix is confirmed across the current Dockerfile/Containerfile source matrix. Integrated validation passed 69 XMPP tests (4 separately marked ignored), 5 shared-ingress tests, all four real encrypted interoperability scenarios and strict channel/test and root binary Clippy. Fresh-account scenarios remove pre-created bot nodes and verify public key discovery without roster subscription. Offline receipt completion, explicit publication policy/refusal, live admission filtering, queue overflow and deferred authorized ping ordering are covered. Human changes-requested review has not been dismissed; re-review is requested.



Visual interface evidence: this follow-up changes integration, lifecycle or tests; prior feature UI evidence remains linked in the review discussion. No new presentation claim is made from source inspection. Remaining platform/integration gaps are those not covered by current-head hosted CI and the named local checks.



## Security & Privacy Impact (required)



OMEMO identity keys, signed prekeys and ratchet state are stored as JSON in the private omemo.sqlite3 database with mode 0600 and exclusive ownership; they are not encrypted at rest by the vault. The vault is required for new identity creation and encrypts queued ingress payloads. The account password uses the existing secret configuration field. Uncertain admitted work remains unreleasable. Public device lists and bundles request open access; these contain public keys, while live peer allowlists and fingerprint pins still gate message admission. Server publication refusal fails explicitly. No private deployment information, real identities, credentials, or messages are included.



- New permissions/capabilities/filesystem scope: Yes â€” the optional channel owns a private mode-0600 OMEMO database and existing-vault access for identity creation and ingress sealing.

- New external network calls: Yes â€” configured XMPP service and bounded protocol exchanges.

- Secrets/credentials handling changed: Yes â€” the account password is a secret field; queued ingress uses vault ciphertext, while long-term OMEMO keys and ratchet state use the private database described above. Fingerprint pins authorize peer devices; they do not encrypt the local key store.

- PII, real identities or private messages in the diff/tests/docs: No.

- Untrusted model-visible content changed: No â€” protocol content remains inside the existing shared dispatch/policy boundary.



## Compatibility (required)



Feature-gated XMPP; encrypted operation is Linux-only. Legacy OMEMO remains distinct from OMEMO v2. The existing migration and replay-protection boundaries remain documented. Offline administration requires stopping the channel owner, including while its socket is disconnected. Existing nodes with incompatible publication policy require owner reconciliation. No toolchain-floor change.



## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)



Disable the XMPP feature/configuration or revert the code subject to documented state compatibility. Preserve newer ratchets, replay markers and uncertain admitted records. Stop the channel owner before supported offline inspection/release. Observe explicit publication errors, refused admission and unreleasable completed receipts.



## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)



None. Incorporated maintainer commits retain their original authorship.


SQLite scope correction: #12322 remains draft pending a published Matrix storage dependency (matrix-org/matrix-rust-sdk#7456). Its workspace-only bridge was removed from this PR; registry compatibility is preserved and #12320 remains the shared advisory tracker. No SQLite waiver is added here.


<!-- followup-20261110-b:start -->
## Additional review follow-up
The discovery exchange now waits for outbound queue capacity inside its existing 10-second budget; queue admission and response share one deadline. Peer timeout remains a typed inbound rejection. Added regressions cover full queue admission, the shared deadline, and cancellation without a late IQ. Integrated validation: 76 XMPP tests pass (4 lab-only ignored).

Local evidence above is from the integrated candidate. Fresh hosted CI will run on the published branch commit; maintainer architecture/merge decisions remain unchanged.
<!-- followup-20261110-b:end -->

## Security maintenance — remove the XMPP chrono dependency

This PR includes the parser correction directly in its branch, commit f7e041a. The XMPP dependency path is now tokio-xmpp → the locally patched xmpp-parsers → time. Its resolved dependency subtree contains neither chrono nor chrono-tz.

The motivation is RustSec RUSTSEC-2026-0543 and the security-maintenance work tracked in #12505. The former Utc::now()/timestamp() calls are supported APIs. The advisory identifies chrono as unmaintained. This change removes that dependency from the new XMPP transport.

The patch preserves the parser's MPL-2.0 license, copyright notices, source commit and original registry checksum. The imported parser is about 1 MB. Functional changes are confined to its date/time APIs, corresponding parser tests and manifests. PATCH.md documents the public type changes, source provenance, test commands and eventual removal of the local override. Upstream xmpp-rs currently declines AI-assisted contributions, so this correction is carried in this PR.

Validation on Windows / Rust 1.98.1

- Default parser suite passed 640 tests, with 8 existing ignored tests.
- Strict XML (pedantic) suite passed 669 tests, with 8 existing ignored tests.
- cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --no-default-features --features channel-xmpp --tests passed.
- cargo fmt --all -- --check passed.
- Dependency-tree inspection confirmed the tokio-xmpp subtree has no chrono or chrono-tz.
- A channel regression test parses delayed-delivery XML and checks nanosecond precision, negative sub-hour offsets and rejection of malformed dates.

The security gate still audits existing workspace dependencies. Other chrono/chrono-tz consumers and the separate ZIP advisory retain their existing tracking. Production deployment of this parser update remains pending.

## Shared security prerequisite

#12552 has merged into master as 3773cae2d7288f9e6af1ad8414e6d2cd33e90451. This branch incorporates that revision. Hosted CI is rerun on the refreshed head; no separate SMTP policy change is carried in this feature diff.

## Shared HTTP pool prerequisite

Depends on #12323 for the shared Tokio-runtime HTTP pool ownership repair. That repair is intentionally kept in its dedicated approved PR rather than copied into this feature diff. The integrated test deployment composes that PR separately and retains the fix. If master-based pooled-dispatch tests fail before #12323 lands, report/rerun that shared prerequisite failure rather than restoring unrelated cache changes here.

prs.title: fix(channels): preserve completed tool results and reuse bounded recovery
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** retain completed tool results across channel deadlines/failures and reuse bounded turn-local recovery through model switches; interrupted calls receive abandonment and terminal card events before a detector error propagates.
- **Scope boundary:** no SSH owner, progress ticker, HTTP cache or dependency-policy implementation.
- **Blast radius:** shared tool-loop cancellation hooks and channel session history.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11909. Depends on #12267. Related #11868, #11869, #11874 and #12323; these are independent changes, not merge prerequisites.

### What this does, simply

A channel can time out after an operation finishes. Completed results enter retained history before awaited notifications, so the next turn can inspect them without blindly repeating the operation. Recovery shares the original deadline; no automatic crash-resumable job or exactly-once external side-effect guarantee is added.

## Testing

### How you can test

Use an isolated channel fixture to complete one tool, then interrupt via cancellation/deadline, a blocked completion hook or a model switch.
