prs.title: perf(ci): fetch only the history each Quality Gate job reads
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Six Quality Gate jobs cloned the repository's full history. When a clone ran slow, the 5-minute jobs among them were cancelled inside `actions/checkout`, and a cancelled job fails `CI Required Gate`. In run data for 2026-10-18 to 2026-11-17, 54 jobs in 20 runs were cancelled 303 to 305 seconds after starting, inside `actions/checkout`, all on `blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404`. One example is run 42142914074, a push to `master` on 2026-11-06, where `Detect crates.io version bump` was cancelled after 5m04s.
  - #12219 made five change detectors shallow. This does the same for the six jobs that still take full history. Each now fetches only the history it reads:
    - **`history-guard`:** the full commit graph as a treeless clone (`filter: tree:0`). `git merge-base` needs commits only.
    - **`docs-style`:** a blobless clone (`filter: blob:none`). The docs gates need `git merge-base` and a diff, and fetch only the blobs they read.
    - **`check-plugin-backends` and `crates-preflight-changes`:** depth 2, which keeps both parents of the test merge commit, plus a depth-1 fetch of the one base commit they compare against.
    - **`lint`:** the default shallow checkout. Nothing in the job reads history.
    - **`zerocode-rpc-boundary`:** no history. Its gate parses one manifest in well under a second, so it now runs on every event instead of fetching history to decide whether to run.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to what any gate checks, and no change to job timeouts. On `pull_request`, `merge_group` and `push`, each detector selects the same work as before, except that the Zerocode gate now always runs.
- **Trade-off:** the merge-queue paths of `crates-preflight-changes` and `check-plugin-backends` first run for real once a pull request is queued. A mistake there would turn the queue red until reverted; both fail closed rather than skip. A git command added to these jobs later that walks a lot of history would also run slower in a partial clone.
- **Blast radius:** Required Quality Gate jobs: Common Ancestor, Lint, the plugin backend checks, Docs Style, Zerocode RPC Boundary, and Detect crates.io version bump.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12218, Related #12219

### What this does, simply

Several required CI jobs downloaded the project's entire history before doing a few seconds of work, and a job with a 5-minute limit was cancelled whenever that download ran slow. A cancelled job turns the required gate red, which blocks the pull request or ejects it from the merge queue for reasons unrelated to the change. Each job now downloads only what it uses: the commit list, or the two or three commits it compares. The checks themselves are unchanged.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: this PR changes `ci.yml`, so its own Quality Gate run executes all six changed jobs on the `pull_request` path.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** this PR's Quality Gate run. A `ci.yml` change selects the docs and plugin-backend job families, so all six jobs run with the new checkouts.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the `merge_group` and `push` paths of `crates-preflight-changes` and `check-plugin-backends` run only in the queue and after merge. Both were reproduced locally against real refs; see below.
- **Commands run and tail output:** run on `dfe8ab35bd` with this patch applied:

```text
$ actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yml
(no output)
$ bash scripts/ci/common_ancestor_guard.test.sh
common ancestor guard tests passed
$ bash scripts/ci/crates_preflight_trigger.test.sh
crates_preflight_trigger: ok
$ bash scripts/ci/plugin_backend_change_filter.test.sh
plugin backend change filter tests: pass
$ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh .github/workflows scripts/ci docs/book/src/maintainers
Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

  Each new fetch shape, reproduced from a workstation against an open PR's test merge ref (`refs/pull/12323/merge`, base `6e83982340`):

```text
depth 2 + base fetch:   HEAD parents present; crates_preflight_trigger.sh pull_request -> run=false;
                        merge_group (base = master~3) -> run=false; push (no base) -> run=false;
                        plugin_backend_change_filter.sh on the diff -> run=true
treeless, full depth:   common_ancestor_guard.sh origin/master <head> -> "Common ancestor with origin/master: 6e83982340..."
blobless, full depth:   git merge-base origin/master HEAD -> 69ea0ae1ae; content diff against it succeeds
clone of master alone:  full 135 s / 194 MB; blobless 2 s / 11 MB; treeless 1 s / 5.3 MB
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** For each job, which git commands its steps and scripts run, and that the new checkout satisfies them. Not verified: the `tests/architecture` suite was not run locally. CI's Test job runs it, and its one assertion on these jobs (the `crates-preflight-changes` block in `tests/architecture/release_workflow.rs`) matches by substring and still holds.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `cargo test --test architecture` (see above).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No. The added fetches go to the same remote `actions/checkout` already uses.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

`git revert <sha>` restores the full-history checkouts.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** master.
- Add opt-in browser dictation and narration in agent chat, with paired-device voice preferences and a localized guide under Config → Other → Browser Voice and Audio.
- Save microphone, recognition mode, language, voice, speed and automatic narration on the authenticated paired-device record, not browser storage. Operators can select another paired device's record without changing the current browser's identity.
- Add one global `gateway.voice_silence_timeout_secs` setting in that same voice screen: default 15 seconds, accepted range 0–300, with 0 disabling automatic submission. It applies to every device/conversation and uses the existing authenticated configuration property API.
- Speak rendered Markdown text rather than hidden delimiters; omit only a trailing crab signature. Preserve meaningful literal code punctuation. Formatting-only replies do not block the continuous reading queue.
- **Scope boundary:** browser speech APIs, paired-device preferences, one gateway configuration field and normal chat submission. No server STT/TTS backend, microphone-audio upload endpoint, new identity or external service is added.
- **Blast radius:** web Config/chat, existing device-registry migration, gateway configuration and same-origin microphone Permissions Policy.
- **Linked issues:** none.

### What this does, simply

A paired browser can enable microphone and speaker controls next to the composer. Recognition starts only when the user clicks the microphone and grants browser permission. Local recognition is the default and never falls back online automatically; browser-service recognition is an explicit choice.

Dictation appends final recognized text to the draft. After the global silence interval, capture stops and final results are accepted before the normal send path is invoked once. Empty captures, hidden/cancelled chats, disconnected/busy sessions and stale conversation requests do not auto-send. A browser ending recognition early still honors the remaining silence interval. Local slash commands remain for manual submission. Set the global value to 0 for manual sending only.

The speaker reads a reply once, stops it, or enables continuous reading through a hold/Shift+Enter gesture. Automatic reading skips restored history and consumes unreadable formatting/signature-only replies so later responses can play. Changing the speech text never changes the displayed/stored response.

<!-- jarvis-validation-update:start -->
## Historical validation update (2026-11-10)

Updated to master a11a5ce5b at 9a9f6a1be. Combined voice controls with scoped chat while retaining operator-only image uploads. Voice submission honors the existing canSend/first-conversation path. A regression drives the actual voice callback through a restricted account's first WebSocket conversation, verifies exactly one message after session_start, and verifies that file uploads remain unavailable. Canonical API generation, the auth suite, all 31 voice tests, and the production build passed. Five gateway voice authorization tests also passed, including revocation during a write. This update was validated locally; earlier installed-browser evidence below describes its recorded revisions.

CI results and maintainer decisions on the published revision remain authoritative.
<!-- jarvis-validation-update:end -->

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interfaces:** web Config and agent chat; authenticated gateway configuration/device APIs.
- **Preconditions:** HTTPS or localhost, a paired browser, browser/OS speech support; select a locally available voice to test playback.
- **Steps:**
  1. Open Config → Other → Browser Voice and Audio. Enable dictation/narration, select language/voice and try the sample.
  2. Change global silence to 15, dictate and pause: verify exactly one send after the interval. Test 0 (manual only), another value, empty capture, manual stop, conversation switch and hidden chat. Confirm the same value appears on another paired device.
  3. Read a response with headings, emphasis, lists, a link and a horizontal rule. Formatting must not be spoken; code such as `apt-get --yes` must retain literal punctuation. A final crab signature is silent, but a crab in the body remains content.
  4. Enable continuous reading; place `---` or a signature-only reply before another readable answer. The latter must play. Restored history and trim notices remain silent.
  5. Reload settings and switch the device selector: per-device choices remain isolated, while the silence timeout stays global. Revoke a technical device and confirm its voice API refuses access. No voice preference storage key is added to browser storage.
  6. Try unavailable local recognition: no online fallback. Browser-service mode and online voices remain explicit choices.
- **Expected after:** documented opt-in controls, durable per-device voice choices, one adjustable global silence deadline and readable narration.
- **Before on master:** these browser speech controls and preference APIs are absent.

### Earlier validation (historical)

- **Earlier layout revision:** 61aeff4bb (global silence, narration fixes and responsive settings/toolbar spacing); the corresponding integrated candidate uses the same feature changes.
- **Latest checks actually run:** 24 voice tests passed; configuration default/range test passed; canonical `cargo run -p xtask --bin web -- gen-api` passed; integrated TypeScript check and production WebUI build passed. The checks exercise the actual component speech-submission callback, global property save, zero-disable, final-results ordering, activity resets, empty/hidden/cancelled capture, early recognition end, signature filtering and continuous queue progress.
- **Historical baseline checks:** gateway paired-device tests (14), security-header tests (5), auth/session/UI tests and format/diff checks passed at earlier documented revisions. These are not reattributed to the new head.
- **CI status:** current head includes master755bc9a4e. Its SQLite exception was approved and merged by maintainers in#12321; this PR does not introduce its own exception. The functional/layout source and installed bundle remain unchanged by that policy-only merge. Current-head CI is authoritative. The independent PR's shared SQLite advisory remains tracked by #12320; the checkout-only #12322 bridge was removed here after its registry-publication limitation was found. No advisory ignore was added. The preceding head's 32-bit check failed during runner `apt install` timeouts, before checking this code.
- **Coverage limits:** component tests simulate speech APIs. Actual microphone hardware, audible OS voice output, language pack downloads and browser-provider network behavior require device testing. New browser validation/deployment results will be reported separately, not inferred from unit tests.
- **Installed-browser validation:** synthetic microphone transcript, actual WebSocket/model completion, exactly one automatic send after **15,131 ms**, technical conversation deleted, global field verified at 15 in Browser Voice and Audio; a nondefault16-second value was saved, verified on disk/after reload, then restored to15. Actual microphone hardware/audio playback are not claimed.
- **Responsive layout follow-up at61aeff4bb:** label above the numeric input (8px gap), separate help and save row (16px gap), and nonshrinking 40px microphone/speaker buttons. Verified the installed UI at 1280px and 390px wide; both controls remain visible. The layout-only static update preserved configuration and binary and did not restart the daemon.

![Historical desktop voice settings before global controls/themed dropdowns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/0cc369ed976c610335df3a05e7fc6db4bfc0b6c1/.pr-evidence/web-voice-layout-desktop.png)

![Historical mobile layout before the global controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/0cc369ed976c610335df3a05e7fc6db4bfc0b6c1/.pr-evidence/web-voice-layout-mobile.png)

- **Earlier functional-field evidence (before the spacing follow-up):** cropped from the installed UI matching the feature changes at3f70b1efc; the evidence branch adds only this image, without changing the reviewed feature head.

![Global browser voice silence setting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/6423d16e3db0b77a369c815b7839f81bbe79d357/.pr-evidence/web-voice-global-silence-live.png)

- **Visual evidence provenance:** the following captures were originally recorded at 6338a726b3297bd18fa3d3a3cc06f5b6a7d109ae and retained at the evidence revision below. They show the prior device selector, guide and controls; they do not show the newly added global field.

![Paired-device selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-devices-other-desktop.png)

![Settings and usage guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-guide-desktop.png)

[Mobile chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-chat-mobile.png) Â· [Portuguese guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-guide-pt.png)

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- **Permissions:** same-origin microphone/on-device recognition is permitted; microphone and narration default disabled per device. Browser consent and user initiation are still required. Global silence defaults to 15 only after dictation is explicitly started.
- **External calls:** optional browser language-pack downloads, explicitly selected online recognition/voices; no microphone audio reaches the gateway.
- **Credentials:** own-device routes resolve the existing paired bearer under the live pairing guard; other-device management uses existing operator authorization. Global timeout reads/writes use the existing config property API and its authorization/validation. No credential is returned or logged by this feature.
- **Personal data in fixtures/docs:** none; synthetic content only.
- **Model-visible text:** recognized text follows the existing user draft/send path; no approval bypass or additional execution capability.

## Compatibility (required)

- **HTTP/config:** existing paired records receive disabled voice defaults; the new global field defaults to 15 when absent. Its range is validated on configuration writes/load. Rust struct-literal callers may need the new field or `..Default::default()`.
- **Config surface:** `gateway.voice_silence_timeout_secs`; existing device preference routes remain per-device. No new environment variable or transport endpoint.
- **Toolchain floor:** unchanged.
- **Upgrade:** build matching gateway/WebUI, enable desired device controls and adjust the global interval in Browser Voice and Audio. Cookie-only sessions without a paired-device identity cannot edit device preferences.

## Rollback

- Disable automatic sending by setting global silence to 0; microphone/narration/continuous reading can be disabled independently in the voice screen.
- For binary rollback, restore a verified prior binary; remove the new configuration key if rolling back to a version rejecting unknown fields. The nullable device-preference column can remain. Preserve state and credentials rather than blindly restoring an old database after accepted work.
- Observable failures: Config save/load errors, browser capture/playback errors or preference-API refusals. Global-setting load failure disables automatic submission rather than guessing a deadline.

### Localization

The existing voice guide/device strings retain their ten-language translations and English fallback. The six new global-setting strings are provided in English and Portuguese; other locales use the existing English fallback.


<!-- followup-20261110-b:start -->
## Additional review follow-up
Continuous reading now checks readiness, listening and speaking before parsing a queued Markdown answer. Added a regression demonstrating no repeated DOM conversion while the parent rerenders during playback; it fails before the fix and passes after. All 32 voice tests pass; the integrated WebUI production build passes.

Local evidence above is from the integrated candidate. Fresh hosted CI will run on the published branch commit; maintainer architecture/merge decisions remain unchanged.
<!-- followup-20261110-b:end -->

## Authenticated browser evidence

A paired Windows operator completed the real spoken-input, single automatic send and audible-reply check in Chrome and Edge on integrated revision `77c0b647d`. The [operator acceptance](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12269#issuecomment-6880263250) and [screenshots](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12269#issuecomment-6880323951) are available. The settings capture shows local dictation selected. The operator did not record browser build numbers or the recognition mode used for each recorded round trip.


## Earlier mobile interface and playback ownership (historical)

The screenshot below renders the production `BrowserVoiceSettings` component and stylesheet from PR commit `610484335` in a headed Chrome viewport at 390 CSS pixels. Device, voice and API data are synthetic. The image shows the reading-voice selector and the speech-speed row. Historical head `1f331f278` changes only the navigation wording in the book relative to the capture.

For the earlier evidence, integrated build `77c0b647d` used the paired voice changes through `bf0093778`, whose themed-dropdown patch has the same stable patch ID as integrated commit `ec761ae6f`. That build predates `2a70a0f90` and `fec38c9b9`. The older image above is historical. This update removes the nine stale captures from the PR branch and stores the new capture on a separate evidence ref.

```text

✔ manual playback in a second pane shows the playback busy message

```

The headed browser also opened the authenticated settings route on Jarvis and confirmed it remained accessible after reload. The screenshot is from the isolated PR fixture. The production check verified navigation and rendering.

The shared Security findings are tracked in #12505 (chrono and chrono-tz) and #12101 (zip 9.0.5). This voice PR does not alter the workspace dependency graph or advisory policy.



## Earlier evidence follow-up at 21dec7b (2026-11-18)

Head 21dec7b incorporates master bec292f. The actual production settings component was rendered in headed Chrome at 390 x 844 and 1280 x 1000 with synthetic device/API/voice data. The current mobile reading-voice selector and speed row are visible. At that historical head, 34 voice tests passed. Historical build provenance, screenshots and coverage limits: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12269#issuecomment-6978640606 . These screenshots are kept on a separate evidence branch. Real hardware acceptance from the historical integrated build is not reattributed to the current head.



## Current source follow-up (2026-11-18)

The refreshed source includes master 3773cae2d7 (#12552). The shared page capture/playback owners prevent cross-pane echo. They also allow the same pane to switch its cancelled narration to dictation even when the browser reports stale speaking/pending flags. The base component suite passes 38 tests; the separate OIDC extension passes 39. Exact published heads and test tails are recorded in the follow-up comment. Hosted CI must still validate the refreshed revisions.

#12552 has merged; this branch incorporates master 3773cae2d7288f9e6af1ad8414e6d2cd33e90451. Previous SMTP advisory failures require new-head CI; no dependency-policy change is carried in this feature diff.

prs.title: fix(channels): require patched lettre for downstream consumers
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`, including merged #12552.
- **What changed and why:** raise `zeroclaw-channels`' lettre requirement from 0.11.22 to 0.11.24 so downstream consumers cannot retain the vulnerable 0.11.22–0.11.23 releases in an existing lockfile.
- **Scope boundary:** one manifest requirement; no lockfile, SMTP configuration, capability, advisory waiver or feature implementation change.
- **Blast radius:** dependency resolution for published `zeroclaw-channels`; this workspace already locks 0.11.24.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12552. Addresses @tidux's optional downstream-resolver hardening suggestion after that PR merged.

### What this does, simply

The merged security fix protects this workspace through Cargo.lock. Published library consumers choose dependencies with their own lockfiles. Requiring at least the patched SMTP version extends that minimum to those consumers without changing the version built by this workspace.

## Testing

### How you can test

Inspect the manifest and run `cargo metadata --locked --offline --no-deps --format-version 1`. Confirm the existing workspace lockfile needs no update and the lettre requirement is ^0.11.24. Full SMTP interoperability is not changed or independently tested here.

### How I tested

`git diff --check` and the locked/offline metadata command passed on this exact one-line source change. Cargo.lock is unchanged. The current master already compiled and passed its required security/tests with lettre 0.11.24 in #12552. New-head hosted CI remains authoritative.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.**
- New external network calls? **No.**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.**

The minimum excludes versions affected by RUSTSEC-2026-0560 through RUSTSEC-2026-0565, including STARTTLS response injection and SMTP command injection. It adds no exemption.

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible? **Yes:** patch-level requirement in the same API-compatible minor series.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No.**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback:** revert the one-line manifest change; doing so reopens the downstream resolver exposure.
- **Feature flags/config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** downstream resolution fails if another dependency requires an incompatible old lettre release; update that consumer's lockfile to the patched version.

prs.title: feat(tools): route Discord external peers to an explicit destination
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Stacked on #12116: the first commit is #12116's head (`a94d584b5` since the 2026-11-19 rebase onto `ad4c1f6c3`, patch-identical), and this PR's change is the second commit. Review the second commit, or the diff after #12116 merges.
- **What changed and why:**
  - On Discord, an `external_peers` entry is a user ID, but messages are posted to channels and threads. `send_message_to_peer` and `send_via` used that user ID (for `send_via`, the group's *first* entry) as the destination, so sends to a Discord external peer failed with Discord's 404 `Unknown Channel`, and which peer `send_via` picked depended on list order.
  - This adds an operator-chosen per-peer route, `[peer_groups.<name>.routes."<peer ID>"]`, with `destination` (the channel or thread ID to post in) and an optional `mention`, following the decisions in #10926 (comment of 2026-11-06).
  - `external_peers` stays admission data: a route key must already be one of the group's `external_peers` (a Discord user ID), a wildcard cannot be routed, and a peer covered by an `ignore` list is not routable.
  - Routed messages always carry an explicit `allowed_mentions` policy on every chunk and attachment payload: nobody is pinged, or with `mention = true` the peer's mention is prefixed and only that user may be pinged.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Discord only. A route on any other channel type is a config error; Matrix and Signal behavior is unchanged and left to separate slices.
  - No peer selector and no group default for `send_via`: a group or channel target posts only when exactly one eligible routed peer exists. Explicit per-peer sends stay with `send_message_to_peer`.
  - The route is not checked against the Discord channel's `channel_ids`, which keeps its meaning as the listening filter. No `thread` field: `destination` is the ID the sender posts to.
  - Unrouted Discord sends and all non-Discord sends keep their payloads; `allowed_mentions` is omitted unless a policy is set.
- **Blast radius:**
  - `SendMessage` gains `allowed_mentions: Option<Vec<String>>` (default `None`, set by both constructors), so struct-literal sites get one more field. Open #11997 also edits `SendMessage`; whichever lands second adds the other's field at those sites.
  - The cron/announcement `DeliveryFn` gains a final `Option<Vec<String>>` mention-policy argument. `deliver_announcement` keeps its signature and passes `None`; the new `deliver_announcement_with_mentions` carries a policy.
  - The Discord sender builds every chunk through one helper, `chunk_payload`. For plain chunks it produces the same request body as the previous `DiscordOutgoing::text` path (tested).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10926. Depends on #12116.

### What this does, simply

A peer group lists who an agent may talk to on a channel. On Discord, an outside participant (another bot or a person) is listed by user ID, but a bot can't post to a user ID: it posts into a channel or thread, and bots can't DM other bots. So asking an agent to message such a peer failed with a confusing "Unknown Channel" error.

With this change, the operator says where messages for that peer should go:

```toml
[peer_groups.discord_peers]
channel = "discord.main"
agents = ["assistant"]
external_peers = ["111111111111111111"]

[peer_groups.discord_peers.routes."111111111111111111"]
destination = "333333333333333333"   # channel or thread ID to post in
mention = true                       # optional: start with a ping of the peer
```

`send_message_to_peer` to that peer, or `send_via` to that group, then posts in the configured channel or thread. The result names the destination, so the agent knows it posted in a shared place rather than a private message. The route never lets anyone new in, can't be used for an ignored peer, and only applies through groups the sending agent is in. If two of the agent's groups route the same peer to different places, the send fails and names both groups. A routed message can only ping the routed peer, and only when `mention = true`.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional; unit coverage is focused, and a live Discord check shows the end-to-end effect.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `discord` (agent tool calls `send_message_to_peer` and `send_via`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Discord bot in a server with a test channel or thread. An agent on `discord.<alias>`, and a peer group containing that agent with another bot or user ID in `external_peers`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Without a route, ask the agent to `send_message_to_peer` the external peer on the Discord channel ref.
  2. Add the `routes."<peer ID>"` block above with your channel or thread ID, reload, and repeat.
  3. Optionally set `mention = true`, and include `@everyone` or another user's mention in the message text.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Step 1 fails with an error explaining how to add a route. Step 2 posts in the destination, and the tool result names it. In step 3 the message starts with the peer's mention, and only the peer is pinged.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Step 1 fails with Discord's `404 Unknown Channel`, because the user ID is used as a channel ID (#12116 replaces this with an actionable error). There is no way to route.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust lint and test jobs cover the config, tools, runtime, channels, API, and gateway changes; Docs Style and the links gate cover the two Markdown files.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no live Discord API call in CI; the payload shape is covered by unit tests.
- **Commands run and tail output** (aarch64 Linux, on this head `8d3a951c2` before opening; the base was master `2341ab56c`):

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                  -> clean
cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets -> clean
  (run on the first revision; the review follow-ups touch only crates the clippy run below rechecked)
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-tools \
  -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings -> clean
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- route peer_group
  test result: ok. 63 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- send_via
  test result: ok. 30 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- send_message_to_peer cron::scheduler
  test result: ok. 108 passed; 0 failed   (plus the isolated child-process delivery test: ok)
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- discord:: announcement compiled_channel
  test result: ok. 327 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api --lib
  test result: ok. 321 passed; 0 failed
scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh -> Summary: 0 error(s)
scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh   -> Checked 1 local docs link target(s)
scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh -> passed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - I ran a mutation check: each new guard was removed in turn, and a named test had to fail. All 15 were caught:
    - ignored-peer exclusion in route lookup, and in `send_via` across the agent's groups;
    - conflict detection across bare-type and dotted-alias groups;
    - sender-scoped lookup (a route in a group the sender is not in is not used);
    - route keys outside `external_peers`, and non-numeric keys, rejected by validation;
    - `send_via` refusing to fall back to the first peer on Discord;
    - the mention policy on later chunks, on routing instructions, on immediate sends, on announcement delivery, and on the routed `send_message_to_peer` call;
    - agent-only groups keeping their existing rejection.
  - Not verified: a live Discord post from this branch.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (tool results and Discord message payloads only; no UI change).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `8d3a951c2`, unit tests listed above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the tests above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `zeroclaw-desktop` is excluded locally because its GTK system libraries are not on this host (CI excludes it too). The full workspace `cargo test` was not run locally; the focused suites above cover the changed modules.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** A configured route can post outside the Discord channel's `channel_ids` listening filter. It is operator-configured only. It applies only to a peer the sending agent's own groups already admit and do not ignore, and conflicting routes fail closed. The docs state that everyone with access to the destination can read routed messages.
- New external network calls? No. Same Discord message endpoint, to a different operator-chosen channel.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. IDs are synthetic, e.g. `111111111111111111`.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new untrusted input. Routed message text comes from the agent as before, and the explicit `allowed_mentions` policy stops it from pinging anyone except the routed peer.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes, with one Discord behavior change.** `send_via` to a Discord peer group, or to a Discord channel one group covers, that has external peers but no single routed peer now fails with guidance instead of posting to the first external peer's user ID. That post already failed with `404 Unknown Channel`. Groups with no external peers keep their existing rejection, and non-Discord channels are unchanged.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** New optional `[peer_groups.<name>.routes."<peer ID>"]` with `destination` and `mention`. Existing configs load unchanged; an invalid route is a load-time validation error.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: none needed. To deliver to a Discord external peer, add a route as shown above.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert` of this PR's commit. Routes are opt-in config; without them, the only change is the clearer `send_via` rejection described above.

prs.title: fix(providers): cache GPT-6.2 system prompts as developer input
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- Follow [OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 migration guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model#gpt-6.2-astra-update-api-and-model-parameters): send the reusable system prompt once as the first typed `developer` item in `input` and omit top-level `instructions`. Starting with GPT-6.2, the public Responses API appends top-level `instructions` after `input`, beyond [eligible cache breakpoints](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching#how-prefix-matching-works), and reserves that field for guidance specific to one request. The [Hermes wire-format change](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/157705) corroborates the placement on the separate Codex subscription endpoint.
- Both Codex subscription and API-key Responses use the shared builder, including streaming and non-streaming recovery. Older or unrelated models keep their existing wire format. Missing system messages keep the existing default prompt; an explicitly empty prompt still omits it.
- **Scope boundary:** No Chat Completions, auth, configuration, dependency, cache-affinity, persistence, or compaction changes.
- **Blast radius:** Both Responses adapters. Custom Responses endpoints using a matching model ID receive the new shape but were not live-tested.
- **Related:** #11403 (separate cache-affinity work), #11907 (existing parallel proxy-fixture race).

### What this does, simply

An agent sends the same system prompt with each new turn. In our synthetic Codex canary, **0 of 8 requests hit the cache with top-level `instructions`, versus 4 of 8 with a leading `developer` message**. This is a concrete case where placement mattered on the Codex endpoint. In the public API, an earlier conversation prefix can still hit the cache while the trailing `instructions` remain uncached. A separate public Responses API canary on `gpt-6.2-sol` found **0/3 follow-up hits with `instructions` vs. 3/3 with leading `developer` input (99.2% of follow-up input tokens reused)**. Neither canary measures Codex subscription allowance or production latency savings.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: loopback HTTP tests of the Responses request body.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Provider HTTP Responses boundary; no web/TUI/CLI UI changes.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Rust toolchain and locked dependencies. Tests require neither credentials nor external inference.
- **Steps to run:**

  ```sh
  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib -- requests_use_developer_prompt codex_gpt62_non_streaming_retry responses_api_key_empty_system responses_api_key_missing_system --test-threads=1
  ```

- **Expected on this branch (after):** Five tests exercise placement, legacy behavior, non-streaming retry, an explicitly empty system prompt, and no system message. When no system message is supplied, the API-key adapter sends the same default text once as the leading `developer` item for GPT-6.2; GPT-6.1 keeps it in `instructions`. The user message is unchanged in both cases.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The system prompt stays in `instructions`. In the negative control, disabling the placement conditional while retaining the original three placement/retry tests made all three fail. A checkout of unmodified `master` does not contain these new tests.

### How I tested

- **Current head:** `2d259cc39a7141e192ade257e05c1ac9d0e017b7`. This follow-up changes only the provider guide, not source or tests. The five wire tests below, docs lint, and `git diff --check` passed on the documentation revision. The added links were checked against the live OpenAI pages and the merged Hermes PR.
- **Test revision:** `a45426c98654f648f57fc10ed898e0d2f3533ed1`. Local checks on Linux aarch64:

  ```text
  Five-test wire command above:
  test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
  
  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib -- --test-threads=1
  test result: ok. 2001 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored
  
  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
  Finished dev profile
  
  cargo fmt --all -- --check; git diff --check; comment hygiene
  Passed
  ```

- **Prior revision:** `9664dacfdb61e262ff96692f233473d35dd68f99` passed hosted [build](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44573718704/job/135735727562), [lint](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44573718704/job/135735728885) and [tests](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44573718704/job/135735727701). The local serial provider suite passed there (2,000 passed, 4 ignored); the earlier dispatcher integration and docs checks covered identical production source. Hosted [build](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44613301769/job/135875248525), [lint](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44613301769/job/135875248787), and [tests](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44613301769/job/135875248234) also passed on the test revision `a45426c9`. See the Checks tab for the documentation head.
- **Independent review:** The exact-head AGY review on `9664dacf` returned `NEEDS_WORK`. It flagged attribution (being handled separately) and the default prompt on API-key requests with no system message. The base already sent that default in `instructions`; the new HTTP regression pins the same fallback, not a new persona policy. Follow-up verified that the linked Hermes PR is real and merged and that the original targeted command ran all three placement/retry tests. The separate AGY review of the **test-only delta** `9664dacf…a45426c9` returned `READY` with no findings. That was not a new full-PR review or maintainer approval.
- **Shared CI blocker:** On `9664dacf`, [Security](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44573718704/job/135735727930) failed at `cargo audit` on eight Wasmtime 48.0.8 advisories, RUSTSEC-2026-0566 through RUSTSEC-2026-0573. [The base failed on the same advisories](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44490965187/job/135446165077); `Cargo.lock` is unchanged. The test revision also failed in its [`cargo audit` step](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44613301769/job/135875248327). Refresh onto `master` after the separate #12577 remediation lands, then rerun CI. No audit suppression.
- **When this meets #11403:** Its `probe_request` test initializer needs `instructions: Some(String::new())` for the new optional field. Apply the adjustment when the patches meet; this PR does not take a dependency on the unmerged patch.
- **Coverage limits:** The live public API canary called OpenAI Responses directly, not through ZeroClaw’s API-key adapter. The adapter itself is covered by the loopback HTTP tests above. Third-party Responses endpoints were not live-tested. The pre-existing parallel proxy fixture race is tracked in #11907; local provider validation was serial. No full-workspace suite or UI evidence: the change is in the provider HTTP adapter and no interface rendering changed.

### Synthetic live A/B: Codex subscription endpoint

On 2026-11-19, the actual Codex provider sent a fixed synthetic system corpus, changing short user prompts, and identical harmless tool declarations. A loopback relay applied the same cache-affinity mechanism in both arms, with separate stable cache identities and synthetic nonce lines to prevent cross-arm sharing. In the control it mapped the builder's legacy-format model argument back to the same GPT-6.2 wire model; an offline comparison against the unpatched base confirmed the control shape. The relay did not move prompts between fields. Requests ran in `C T T C C T T C` order per model. All 16 requests returned HTTP 200, used the requested model, and followed the synthetic instruction.

| Model | Placement | Input tokens/request | Cached input, request 1 → 4 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `gpt-6.2-astra` | `instructions` | 5,810 | 0, 0, 0, 0 |
| `gpt-6.2-astra` | Leading `developer` | 5,810 | 0, 5,632, 5,632, 0 |
| `gpt-6.2-sol` | `instructions` | 5,809 | 0, 0, 0, 0 |
| `gpt-6.2-sol` | Leading `developer` | 5,809 | 0, 0, 5,632, 5,632 |

The live canary used the non-streaming trait call with an SSE wire response; the streaming trait and true non-streaming retry were exercised by mock HTTP tests. Warm misses remain possible. These measurements do not quantify production latency, subscription allowance, or billing.

### Synthetic live A/B: public Responses API

On 2026-11-19, a direct API-key canary called OpenAI’s public `/v1/responses` endpoint with `gpt-6.2-sol`, `store: false`, no tools, and separate stable cache keys for each arm. Both arms used the same synthetic policy and user inputs: one cold request, one exact repeat, and two append-only follow-ups. All eight calls succeeded and returned the expected marker from the policy.

| Placement | Cold request: tokens written to cache | Follow-up cache hits | Follow-up input tokens reused |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Top-level `instructions` | 0 | 0/3 | 0 / 13,656 (0%) |
| First `developer` item in `input` | 4,499 | 3/3 | 13,547 / 13,656 (99.2%) |

The `developer` arm reported 4,499, 4,499, and 4,549 cached tokens across the three follow-ups. This directly verifies the request format on the public API with `store: false`; the loopback tests verify that ZeroClaw sends that format. It is not a measurement of Codex allowance, billing savings, or production latency.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.**
- New external network calls? **No** in production; the existing Responses request is reused.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.** The existing trusted system text moves to a developer input item; there is no new text source or tool privilege. Wire checks cover placement and exact-once behavior. Custom endpoints may implement these roles differently and were not live-qualified.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes** for configuration and older model wire formats. GPT-6.2+ intentionally changes prompt placement as documented.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No.**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- No migration. Confirm developer input support before using a matching model ID against a custom Responses endpoint.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- Redeploy the previous provider-containing build, or revert this PR (if merged unsquashed, revert the documentation and test follow-ups before the production fix), rebuild, and redeploy through the usual release process. No data migration.
- Feature flags or config toggles: **None.**
- Watch for HTTP 4xx rejecting developer input or missing `instructions`, or changed instruction adherence. Cache misses alone do not establish a malformed request.

prs.title: chore(channels)!: move IRC and Twitch out of the binary into registry plugins
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Remove the compiled-in IRC and Twitch channels. Both now ship as the `irc` and `twitch` WASM plugins, which a stock host installs without a rebuild. Twitch was a thin adapter over the IRC channel, so the two leave together. This takes the raw-TCP IRC channel out of the "retain built-in" list in #8850, now that a compatible, validated package exists.
  - `[channels.irc.*]` and `[channels.twitch.*]` become **retired config keys**, the same mechanism WATI used. Each load drops the section and prints a notice that names the plugin and its install and bind commands. The next save removes it from disk, secrets included.
  - `ChannelKind::Irc` and `ChannelKind::Twitch` stay in the attribution enum so historical records deserialize. They are marked not inbound-capable, so they leave the SOP trigger registry, as WATI did.
  - Keep `OutboundContentFormat::PlainText` for migrated `plugin.<alias>` bindings whose `[channels.plugin.<alias>].package` is `irc` or `twitch` (and fall back to `PlainText` for bare `"plugin"` or unresolved plugin aliases whenever an enabled plain-text plugin binding exists), so Markdown link destinations are still scanned by the outbound leak redactor across drafts, multi-message narration flushes, final replies (including `send_via` redirects), and announcements.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No other channel changes, and no plugin-runtime changes.
  - No automatic conversion of an old section into a plugin binding. The plugin must be installed first, and the encrypted credentials belong to a different config row.
  - The schema version is not bumped (see the reviewer question below).
- **Blast radius:**
  - Release archives never included IRC or Twitch: neither is in the dist feature set. They shipped only in `channels-full` source builds and the `all-features` image. That image and `--preset full` also build the plugin runtime, so every install that had these channels can install the plugins.
  - A plain `cargo build --features channels-full` without `plugins-wasm` loses them, and needs `plugins-wasm` added.
  - Generated installer surfaces (`Containerfile`, `setup.bat`, `dev/ci/docker-tags.toml`) were checked against `cargo generate installers`: no drift.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8850. Depends on zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins#174 (merged and published), which publishes the `irc` and `twitch` 0.2.0 packages this PR points operators to.

### Reviewer decision: `retired_in: 4`, no schema bump

The `RETIRED_KEYS` policy comment asks for a version bump when no pending version covers a retirement. V4 shipped in v0.9.0. I used `retired_in: 4` without a V5 bump because:
- Every load already applies every retired key, whatever version the file declares, so operators see the same thing either way.
- A V5 bump would make every config saved by this binary unreadable by v0.9.0 ("newer than this binary supports"). That's a large side effect for a channel removal, and it would be the first V5 change.

If maintainers prefer the bump, it's a mechanical follow-up: a `MIGRATION_STEPS` entry, `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 5`, and a regenerated fixture.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw used to carry IRC and Twitch support inside its binary, but most installs (every release download) didn't include them, and getting them meant rebuilding ZeroClaw. They are now plugins you install with one command. This PR removes the old built-in copies. If an existing config still has an IRC or Twitch section, ZeroClaw says exactly what to do instead of silently ignoring it, and the rest of the config keeps working.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the upgrade path.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw config`, `zeroclaw plugin`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** a build with `--features plugins-wasm-cranelift,channels-full`, and a config dir whose `config.toml` holds `schema_version = 4`, a provider, `[agents.assistant] channels = ["irc.libera"]`, a `[channels.irc.libera]` section with a `sasl_password`, a peer group on `irc.libera`, and `[plugins] enabled = true`. Both `irc` and `twitch` 0.2.0 are published in the plugin registry (zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins#174).
- **Steps to run:**
  1. `zeroclaw --config-dir D config get agents.assistant.channels`
  2. `zeroclaw --config-dir D plugin install irc`
  3. `zeroclaw --config-dir D plugin bind irc --channel-alias libera`
  4. Set `server`, `nickname`, and `channels` on the printed `plugins.entries.<key>.config.*` paths, and the server on `.egress_hosts`, with `config set --no-interactive`.
  5. `config set --no-interactive agents.assistant.channels '["plugin.libera"]'`
  6. `zeroclaw --config-dir D plugin info irc`
- **Expected on this branch (after):**
  - Step 1 prints `warning: dropped retired config key \`channels.irc\` …: the built-in IRC channel moved to the \`irc\` plugin; run \`zeroclaw plugin install irc\` and …`, with no secret value shown.
  - Steps 2 to 5 succeed even though the agent still references `irc.libera`.
  - After the first save, `config.toml` no longer holds `[channels.irc]` or its secret.
  - Step 6 reports `plugin.libera configuration validates against the package schema.`, `The activation plan admits plugin.libera`, and `Loads: yes`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the built-in IRC channel loads from `[channels.irc.libera]`.

### How I tested

At the CI toolchain (Rust 1.98.0), on Linux x86_64:

```text
$ cargo +1.98.0 fmt --all -- --check                       # clean
$ cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 45s
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config --all-features
test result: ok. 2009 passed; 0 failed   (zeroclaw-config lib)
test result: ok. 323 passed; 0 failed    (zeroclaw-api lib)
test result: ok. 106 passed; 0 failed    (zeroclaw-config tests/migration.rs)
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --all-features --lib
test result: ok. 3870 passed; 0 failed; 6 ignored (+ 1 passed isolated)
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-features --lib -- sop:: quickstart:: i18n:: plugin_runtime::
test result: ok. 919 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --locked --features ci-all --test integration --test component --test architecture
test result: ok. 154 passed / 291 passed / 90 passed
$ cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p xtask feature_matrix
test cmd::mdbook::feature_matrix::tests::parity_join_produces_rows_without_stale_keys ... ok
$ scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh   ->  Summary: 0 error(s)
$ scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh     ->  🚫 Errors...........0
$ scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh  ->  Comment hygiene gate passed.
$ cargo run -p xtask --bin generate -- installers  ->  unchanged dev/ci/docker-tags.toml (Containerfile, setup.bat unchanged)
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:**
  - Lint and the workspace clippy cover the removed features and dead code under `ci-all`.
  - The config migration and fixture tests cover the retirement, including the regenerated `fixtures/v4.toml` (`zeroclaw config generate 4`): the diff is exactly the IRC channel, its agent reference, and its peer group.
  - Channel orchestrator unit and turn tests (`irc_family_plugin_bindings_use_plain_text_outbound_format`, `irc_plugin_outbound_redacts_credentials_in_markdown_link_destinations`) cover plain-text outbound leak redaction for `irc` and `twitch` plugin bindings across replies and announcements.
  - Docs gates and the feature-matrix parity test cover the parity keys, which the docs build treats as a hard error when stale.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known. `scripts/ci/container_build_inputs_gate.sh` fails locally only on an unrelated stray worktree under `.worktrees/`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - The upgrade path above, step by step, with the built binary and the real `irc.wasm`.
  - The plugins themselves were driven through `WasmChannel` against a scripted IRC server and real Twitch (details in zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins#174).
  - Not verified: a daemon soak with both channels running as plugins; the `all-features` container image build.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output (CLI warning shown above, `LC_ALL` default, no width dependence).
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `./dev/ci.sh all` in favor of the targeted crates plus the full CI clippy invocation.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No. Removed: the built-in IRC TLS client, including its `verify_tls = false` path that disabled certificate verification.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. Retired sections, secrets included, are dropped from disk on the next save, as for WATI. The notice carries the key path and reason only, never values. The test fixture's sentinel password was confirmed absent from output and from the rewritten file. Outbound leak redaction continues to treat `irc` and `twitch` plugin bindings as `PlainText` so Markdown link destinations are still scanned.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. The `channel-irc` and `channel-twitch` Cargo features are removed, and `[channels.irc.*]` and `[channels.twitch.*]` are retired.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps:
  1. Note the non-secret settings of each `[channels.irc|twitch.<alias>]` section. Secrets are encrypted in the file, so re-enter them from their source.
  2. Build with a WASM plugin backend if this is a custom source build (`--preset full` already has one).
  3. `zeroclaw plugin install irc` (or `twitch`), then `zeroclaw plugin bind irc --channel-alias <alias>` (Twitch: add `--egress declared`).
  4. Set the config keys `plugin info` lists. For IRC, grant the server on the instance's `egress_hosts`.
  5. Replace `irc.<alias>` or `twitch.<alias>` with `plugin.<alias>` in `agents.<agent>.channels` and in peer groups, with lowercase peer names.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` of the commits on this PR restores both channels and their config sections. A config whose retired section was already dropped by a save needs the section re-entered.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** none.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `dropped retired config key \`channels.irc\`` / `\`channels.twitch\`` on the CLI and `removed retired config key …` in logs at load; `agents.<agent>.channels[...] = "irc.<alias>" but channels.irc.<alias> is not configured` validation warnings until references are updated.

prs.title: feat(tools): add agy_cli coding-CLI tool for Antigravity CLI
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Google has moved terminal Gemini use from Gemini CLI to Antigravity CLI (`agy`), and Gemini CLI has stopped serving most accounts (Google Developers Blog, June 2026). ZeroClaw can delegate coding tasks to Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI and OpenCode, but not to `agy`.
  - Adds `agy_cli`, a peer of `codex_cli` / `claude_code` / `gemini_cli` / `opencode_cli`. It is built on the shared coding-CLI executor, so it inherits the same authorization, working-directory validation, timeout, output bounding and runtime-executor routing.
  - Headless `agy` exits 0 and reports `status: SUCCESS` even when it auto-denies a tool permission, so the exit code alone would report a blocked task as a success. `agy_cli` requests JSON output and decides success from it. A run succeeds only when the process exits 0, `status` is `SUCCESS`, and `denied_actions` is empty. Non-JSON or status-less output fails closed.
  - Tool-owned flags are attached (`--print=<prompt>`, `--model=<id>`, `--print-timeout=<n>s`) and placed after operator `extra_args`. A model-supplied prompt that starts with `-` cannot be parsed as a flag, and the tool's own settings take precedence over operator arguments.
- **Scope boundary:** `gemini_cli` is not changed or deprecated here. There is no `agy` model provider. The shared coding-CLI executor is unchanged apart from recognising the new tool name in the env-boundary helper. The sandbox and permission defaults of `agy` itself are left to the operator's agy settings.
- **Blast radius:** Opt-in only. The new `[agy_cli]` section defaults to `enabled = false`, and nothing changes for existing configs. Shared test fixtures changed in two places: the budget-test fake now returns agy-shaped JSON, which the other adapters pass through unchanged, and the runtime routing test now expects `agy_cli` to fail closed on its plain-text probe.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11075. Related #4879, whose closing comment suggested Antigravity CLI support as the follow-up. Related #10381 (merged): `agy_cli` builds its command through the shared `CodingCliCommand`/`CodingCliExecutor` path, so it inherits that PR's host-launcher resolution before the workspace working directory is applied.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw agents can hand a coding task to an external coding CLI. Google has replaced Gemini CLI with a new tool called Antigravity CLI (`agy`), so Gemini users had no supported way to do that. This PR adds an `agy_cli` tool that works like the existing Codex and Claude Code tools. It stays off until you turn it on in config.

The main difference from the other CLIs is how failure is detected. When `agy` runs without a terminal and wants to do something that needs permission, such as running a shell command, it refuses automatically but still exits successfully. `agy_cli` reads agy's JSON result, reports those refusals as a failure, and tells the user how to allow the action in agy's own settings.

ZeroClaw checks that the requested working directory is inside the workspace, but it does not sandbox what `agy` does once it is running. That is governed by agy's own permission settings. The docs section added in `tools/overview.md` states this plainly.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The behaviour is covered by unit tests with fixtures copied from real agy 1.2.9 output. Manual testing needs an authenticated `agy` install, which most reviewers will not have.

### How I tested

- **Revision (2026-10-11):** one commit, which supersedes `76275ecf6`. It was authored and validated at `34d7aea0825a1e7cd7701135e4dc3f341271a56b` on master `0f8fb9d372a5cf850e87f9464c7f5c216a717fee`. **Rebase note (2026-10-11):** the then-current head `6239f29f26fcbe1e6b520016cb98b9eade20f329` was a base-only rebase of that commit onto master `d03325172eb6c64272f01042b60fd7f66d74c711` with GitHub's update-branch (`git range-diff` shows the commit identical; the local validation and review below were recorded on `34d7aea08`). **Rebase note (2026-10-14):** the then-current head `dc09ad4048d50e3960e9d8c44132a8fec3b4b1cd` was a base-only rebase of `6239f29f2` onto master `329e66f76` with GitHub's update-branch. Master had moved 32 commits and four files this PR touches changed upstream (`orchestrator/acp_server.rs`, `orchestrator/mod.rs`, `config/schema.rs`, `docs/book/src/tools/overview.md`); a trial merge was clean and the rebase applied without conflicts. `git range-diff` shows the commit unchanged apart from one context line in `docs/book/src/tools/overview.md` (the neighbouring heading was renamed upstream); the file set is unchanged (18 files). The local validation and review below were recorded on `34d7aea08`; required CI runs on the current head. **Rebase note (2026-10-17):** rebased again with GitHub's update-branch onto master `4e82ce46e` (32 commits, including the rustls/Wasmtime advisory fix #11755 that the earlier Security failure was waiting on). `git range-diff` shows the commit identical, with no content change; the new head is `91da937b6051c182654f7ba5d0cc240b722cece8`. A trial merge was clean; five files this PR changes were also touched on master (`zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs`, both `tools.ftl` files, `zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs`, `docs/book/src/developing/tool-inventory.md`) without conflict. What changed:
  - Inventory: `agy_cli` is registered in `BUILTIN_TOOLS` as a Host-tier tool, listed in the tier table and prose of `tool-inventory.md`, and enabled in the runtime maximal-config inventory test. This fixes the `matrix_safe_policy_names_only_inventoried_tools` failure that appeared after master's typed tool inventory landed, and Greptile's inventory finding.
  - i18n: the tool description, parameter descriptions and errors are Fluent `tool-agy-cli-*` keys in the canonical English catalogue, with the generated tools-crate mirror regenerated. This addresses Greptile's localization finding.
  - Hardening of `agy_cli`'s own contract: a bare `--` in `extra_args` is dropped from the agy argv and flagged by config validation, so it can no longer turn the tool-owned flags into positionals. The `--print-timeout` margin scales with small timeouts instead of collapsing to `1s`. The attached form `--dangerously-skip-permissions=<value>` now triggers the risky-flag warning (agy only; Codex matching is unchanged). Stderr appended to errors is capped like stdout. `agy_cli` is added to the Integrations-group test.

prs.title: fix(tools): reject send_message_to_peer to Discord external peers with an actionable error
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `send_message_to_peer` hands any known non-agent target (an entry from a
    peer group's `external_peers`) to announcement delivery. On Discord that
    delivery posts to `/channels/{recipient}/messages`, but Discord external
    peers are user IDs, so the send fails with Discord's opaque
    `404 Unknown Channel (10003)` and the agent cannot tell what to do instead.
  - The tool now rejects that case before delivery, using configuration only:
    the target has already been validated as a configured external peer (not an
    agent alias), and the channel ref's type is `discord` (same case-insensitive
    `<type>.<alias>` split that delivery uses). No ID-syntax guessing and no
    network calls; Discord user and channel IDs are both snowflakes.
  - The error explains why (user ID vs channel/thread ID, bots cannot DM bots,
    peer groups carry no channel mapping) and what to do: post in a channel or
    thread shared with the peer and mention the peer there.
- **Scope boundary:** No new config keys, no peer → channel/thread routing, no
  DM path. Peer-agent targets (in-process delivery) and external peers on other
  channel types are unchanged. `send_via` is not changed: it resolves its
  recipient from the first `external_peers` entry through `Channel::send` in
  `zeroclaw-tools`, a separate path whose recipient semantics belong to the
  routing design discussion in #10926.
- **Blast radius:** `send_message_to_peer` calls whose target is an external
  peer on a Discord channel. Those sends could not be delivered before; they
  now fail earlier with a clearer message.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10926 (identity vs. delivery-destination
  design; the Discord evidence for this failure is in
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10926#issuecomment-6511170110).
  This PR does not resolve it.

### What this does, simply

Agents can message configured peers with `send_message_to_peer`. For a human
or bot that is not a ZeroClaw agent, the tool sends through the channel's
normal delivery, which on Discord needs a channel or thread ID. Peer lists on
Discord hold user IDs, so the message went to a "channel" that does not exist
and Discord answered with a bare 404. This PR stops that send up front and
tells the agent to talk to the peer in a shared channel or thread instead. How
peers should be routed on Discord is left to the separate design discussion.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the change is a pre-delivery rejection
  covered by a unit test that exercises `SendMessageToPeerTool::execute`;
  reproducing the live 404 needs a Discord bot pair.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the runtime crate's
  lib tests, clippy and fmt cover the changed file.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no live Discord round-trip in CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - RED on master 5a51398dd with only the new execute tests applied:
    `discord_external_peer_is_rejected_before_channel_delivery ... FAILED`
    (`a Discord user target must not report delivery`: master hands the user
    ID to announcement delivery; in the unit test no live Discord handler is
    registered, so it reports success where production gets the 404).
    `non_discord_external_peer_still_reaches_delivery ... ok`.
  - GREEN, `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- --skip tunnel::tailscale`
    on default features and again with every `tool-*`/`tools-external`
    feature: all three new tests pass and every other `send_message_to_peer`
    test passes. 5846 and 5861 passed respectively, 0 failed, 8 ignored
    (run with `umask 077`; under a group-writable umask, three `rpc::local`
    endpoint-lock tests reject the temp dir, which is unrelated to this change).
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check`,
    `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh <changed file>`: clean.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The original failure was seen
  on one deployment: a `send_message_to_peer` call targeting a second bot's
  Discord user ID returned `404 Unknown Channel (10003)`. The new error path
  was not exercised against live Discord.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `tunnel::tailscale` lib
  tests were skipped locally because they reconfigure the host's Tailscale
  Serve state.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
  (test IDs are synthetic)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No (the
  error echoes the target the model itself passed, already Debug-quoted)

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (the rejected sends could not succeed before)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: fix(providers): retry Codex streams as streams on the default endpoint
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - After a streaming decode failure, `send_responses_request` retried once with `stream: false` (#6668). The default ChatGPT Codex endpoint accepts only streaming requests and rejects that retry with `400 {"detail":"Stream must be set to true"}`, so on the subscription route the recovery could never succeed. A truncated stream became a non-retryable "provider rejected the request" error.
  - On the default endpoint (`!custom_endpoint`), the one retry is now a streaming retry. Custom endpoints (`provider_api_url`) keep #6668's non-streaming recovery unchanged.
  - The final error and log attributes name the retry kind (`streaming retry` / `non-streaming retry`).
- **Scope boundary:** one retry, as before. No change to which failures are retried: API error events and non-success HTTP statuses still are not retried. No config keys, no change to the request shape, `reliable.rs` classification, or other providers.
- **Known limit:** the retry kind follows `custom_endpoint`, which is derived from the configured URL. A custom `provider_api_url` that proxies the ChatGPT Codex backend still gets the non-streaming retry, as on master.
- **Blast radius:** OpenAI Codex provider on the default endpoint (OAuth / ChatGPT subscription) when a stream fails to decode. Custom-endpoint deployments are unaffected.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12072. Related #6668.

### What this does, simply

Sometimes the ChatGPT Codex backend ends a response stream before sending any output. ZeroClaw tried to recover by asking again without streaming, but that backend refuses non-streaming requests outright, so the recovery always failed and the user saw a misleading "request rejected" error. Now ZeroClaw asks again the way the backend accepts, once, and if that also fails the error says what actually happened.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: covered by deterministic mock-server tests. Live reproduction depends on the backend truncating a stream, which is intermittent.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `provider` = `openai-codex`

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The `Test` job runs the `zeroclaw-providers` lib tests, including the new and existing `openai_codex` retry tests; `cargo clippy` CI covers lint.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live ChatGPT Codex call.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
# at eaec11f46, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4, aarch64 Linux
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib -- openai_codex::
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_custom_endpoint_reports_non_streaming_retry_failure ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_default_endpoint_reports_streaming_retry_failure ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_default_endpoint_retries_streaming_after_empty_stream ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_default_endpoint_streaming_retry_http_error_is_not_retried_again ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_does_not_retry_failed_http_status ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_does_not_retry_stream_api_error_events ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_retries_non_streaming_when_stream_contains_malformed_frame_after_text ... ok
# test openai_codex::tests::codex_retries_non_streaming_when_stream_decode_fails ... ok
# test result: ok. 55 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1932 filtered out

cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -- -D warnings
# exit 0, no diagnostics

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/openai_codex.rs
# Comment hygiene gate passed.

cargo fmt --all -- --check
git diff --check origin/master
# both exit 0
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - RED/GREEN: the test module from this branch was run against the production code of unpatched master `99bd353c7`. The three default-endpoint tests fail there with the exact production error, `OpenAI Codex API error (400 Bad Request): {"detail":"Stream must be set to true"}`, because the stream-only mock rejects the `stream: false` retry the way the real backend does. All pass with the fix.
  - The default-endpoint tests give the mock provider an OAuth profile and `custom_endpoint = false`; their mock server rejects `stream: false` with that 400 without consuming a queued reply. The custom-endpoint path is pinned by the existing `codex_retries_non_streaming_*` tests and by `codex_custom_endpoint_reports_non_streaming_retry_failure` (passes before and after: behaviour preserved).
  - The fallback block is identical on master and on the build where the failure was observed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace `cargo test` was not run locally (Raspberry Pi host); the change is confined to one function in `zeroclaw-providers`, covered by the focused run above and by CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No (same single retry, now with `stream: true` on the default endpoint)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. Log text changed: the warning "retrying without streaming" is now "retrying once" with a `retry` attribute (`streaming retry` / `non-streaming retry`), and the final error says "stream decode and retry both failed". Log matches on the old strings need updating.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`; no data or config migration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** On the default Codex endpoint, a turn whose first stream is truncated fails with "streaming retry failed (...)" instead of recovering, or a custom endpoint stops recovering via the non-streaming retry.

## Summary

- Base branch is `master`.
- Add a write-only operator panel under Config → Storage → Secrets for credentials already referenced by a plugin TLS profile.
- Reuse the canonical encrypted plugin configuration and existing host-mediated TLS authorization. The catalog returns instance, property, destinations and configured state.
- This is the first implementation slice of Related #12373. The broader catalog, reversible disable, and references usable by other consumers are open design work. This PR leaves the issue open.

### What this does, simply

An authenticated operator can provision a PEM value for a configured plugin TLS profile without putting the value in a chat. Rotation and deletion use the existing configuration commit path. New connections continue to use the existing instance and destination checks.

## Testing

### How you can test

- Reviewer testing requested. Surface is web.
- Pair the dashboard, enable encryption with an initialized key, and configure a plugin TLS profile referencing a schema-declared secret.
- Open Storage → Secrets → Plugin TLS credentials. Set, replace, refresh and delete a synthetic PEM value. Inspect the responses and verify they contain only metadata or configured state.
- On master, the dedicated panel is absent.

### How I tested

- `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --tests -j2` completed successfully.
- Web TypeScript type checking passed. The four existing read-only configuration UI regression tests passed.
- Rust formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Added a real config-router test for scoped-principal rejection, missing key, encrypted persistence, duplicate creation, replacement and deletion. The gateway test exposed a deletion failure. The follow-up persists only the selected credential and tests that neighboring ciphertext and the TLS profile survive. The current-head gateway test is pending CI. A Chrome walkthrough of the real WebUI with a synthetic API passed create, replace, refresh, delete, and draft clearing on cancel. This browser test did not use a live gateway.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The new route requires a current authenticated administrator. It accepts only existing TLS binding slots.
- New external network calls? No.
- Credential handling changed? Yes. Bounded request bodies carry write-only values. The route requires encryption and an existing key, returns metadata with no-store, and emits mutation metadata without the submitted value.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in the diff or fixtures? No.
- Model-visible inputs or prompt injection surface changed? No.

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config, env or CLI surface changed? No. The API and dashboard gain a panel for existing bindings.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.

## Rollback

Revert this change to remove the panel and route. Values already saved remain standard plugin configuration. Restore a known-good encrypted configuration backup to undo a credential rotation or deletion, and retain the corresponding encryption key. Watch for unexpected 403, 409 or 412 responses on the new route and for connection failures after credential edits.



## Shared security prerequisite

#12552 has merged into master as 3773cae2d7288f9e6af1ad8414e6d2cd33e90451. This branch incorporates that revision. Hosted CI is rerun on the refreshed head; no separate SMTP policy change is carried in this feature diff.
